MARCH 5, 2005
RETREAT
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN RETREAT
MARCH 5, 2005     DOSHER HOSPITAL BOARD ROOM
SOUTHPORT, N.C.   8:00 A.M.
 
BOARD MEMBERS PRESENT:   Mayor Norman Holden
               Aldermen Nelson Adams, Meezie Childs,
               James Brown, Stuart Callari, Jim Powell and
               Paul Fisher
STAFF PRESENT:         Rob Gandy, City Manager
               Regina Alexander, City Clerk
               Bob Grant, Public Services Director
Mayor Holden thanked the Board and staff for their commitment and dedicated
work for the City. He commended City Manager Gandy for his hard work and
management of the city’s finances; and as a result, Southport has received the
best audit since he has been on the Board.
Synopsis of Board items discussed during Board Retreat
Fire Department – Greg Cumbee, Fire Chief
Mr. Greg Cumbee, Fire Chief gave the Board an overview of the statistical data
for the Fire Department including number of incidents for 2004, average
turnout, response time, volunteer hours, training, certifications and fire
prevention contacts. (For additional information handout on file in clerk’s
office) He briefed the Board on the equipment status. Some of the main points
were:
·   Purchased new vest and safety jackets (lime green)
·   Purchased illuminated safety cones for night calls
·   Need to purchase another infra-red camera
·   Acquire land for new facility in 2005
·   Retain architect for new facility
·   Start construction 1st quarter of 2006 (recommended site of North Howe and
East 11th area – NC State Fire Marshall)
·   2012 paid firefighters
·   recruit more city employees as firefighters – need 7
·   update fire hydrants and water lines
·   supplement retired firefighters’ monthly stipend as incentive to reduce
attrition among members (Progress Energy Donation)
·   Goal is to increase $5.00 per call fee to $10.00 per call for structure
fires
Alderman Fisher and Mayor Holden communicated that talks are in the process
with Edgar Haywood of Dosher Hospital. It was stated that the Citiworks
Foundation has not been able to meet their obligation and the hospital needs
additional parking, therefore; it is a possibility that the City will be able
to work out a land trade with the hospital to acquire property across the
street (from the hospital) for a fire station. After discussion, it was the
consensus of the Board to move forward with negotiations with Mr. Haywood,
Administrator of Dosher Hospital.
Alderman Fisher requested a synopsis of the grant report.
Police Department – Jerry Dove, Police Chief
Mr. Jerry Dove, Chief of Police, reviewed with the Board the accomplishments,
goals and objectives of the Southport Police Department.

ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS
PRELIMINARY PLAT – RIDGE AT FOREST OAKS (B. ENGLISH)
Review of the revision for the preliminary plat for the Ridge at Forest Oaks
was tabled until July.
SOUTHPORT CROSSING - CAPE FEAR TRADING GROUP (HYSON)
The Board reviewed with developers and their representatives the sketch plan
for Southport Crossing. Mr. Darryl Guidry, Architect outlined a multi-family
section of a residential/commercial development proposed to be constructed at
the corner of Moore Street and Ferry Road. (ETJ) He stated that the project
will be developed in two phases. Residential homes are proposed in the first
phase and commercial abuts the second phase. Mr. Barker stated if sewer is
unavailable for Phase I, they will consider building a sewerage package plant,
or the developer is willing to help finance some of the sewer extension, if
need be. Mayor Holden recommended the Developer meet with department of
transportation officials to discuss traffic access onto Ferry Road. The Board
looked at the drawing and asked questions about proposed commercial businesses.
Mr. Hyson discussed the possibilities of a retail center and land designated as
open space. Mayor stated that he and the former owner had discussed working
with ADM to obtain access to Price’s Creek Lighthouse in order to open that
area as a tourist attraction. Mayor also asked Mr. Hyson about a boat ramp,
motel and restaurant. No commitments were forthcoming, but Mr. Hyson explained
that they are looking at possibilities and will be glad to sit down in the
future to bring this area in as a part of Southport.
SOUTHPORT NEIGHBORHOOD BUSINESS PROJECT
Mr. Mike Petkauskos, owner of property at 508 North Howe Street presented a
sketch plan proposing to construct a mixed use facility to include a three
story style Charleston structure with an antique shop on the first floor and
residential apartments on the second and third floor. Parking will be in the
rear of the building with a drive thru to allow access. Upon presentation to
the Planning Board, they addressed some concerns and all questions have been
answered i.e. delivery trucks and setbacks. The original plan called for 4 ft
side yard setbacks and the UDO has 0 setbacks and his plans have been modified
accordingly. He will maintain the same front line setback as adjacent
buildings. (15 ft)
For clarification, Mr. Gandy stated the Planning Board minutes addressed the
side yard setbacks, but has since been clarified with the Attorney. The
Ordinance table area yard density and height requirements for Business
Districts specifies front yard of 25 ft. but it does allow for a reduction on
non-conforming lots. Ms. Toth, member of the Planning Board in answer to a
question from the City Manager, stated during discussion at the Planning Board
meeting it was ascertained that this was not a typical lot but could not recall
if the lot was classified as non-conforming. City Manager Gandy stated these
issues will be handled by the Planning Board when Mr. Petkauskos presents his
preliminary plan.
Alderman Fisher invited Mr. Petkauskos to the Parking Committee meeting on July
14, 5:00 p.m. and stated that the Committee is working on a parking lot access
from Atlantic and Howe Streets which is to the rear of his property.
AUDITORS – BROCK, PADGETT & CHANDLER

Alderman Fisher motioned, seconded by Alderman Childs to approve the resolution

Resolution Authorizing Execution of Planning and Management Grant Contract
A regular meeting of the Southport Board of Aldermen was held on June 9, 2005
at 201 East Moore Street, Aldermen Chambers (City Hall) Southport, N.C., and
the regular meeting place of the Board. There were six (6) Aldermen and the
Mayor present.
The Aldermen were advised that a proposed contract between the City of
Southport and the North Carolina Department of Environment and Natural
Resources for the provision of Planning and Management Services was presented
and discussed; that, under the terms of the said contract, the City of
Southport will pay a total of $3500 as its local share of the planning project
costs.
BE IT RESOLVED, by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport:
1.   That the contract between the City of Southport and the North Carolina
Department of Environment and Natural Resources is hereby approved.
2.   That the Mayor and the Clerk are hereby authorized to sign and execute
said contract for and on behalf of the City of Southport and forward same to
the North Carolina Department of Environment and Natural Resources.
3.   That upon final execution, a copy of said contract be filed with the
minutes. Upon motion of Alderman Fisher, seconded by Alderman Childs, said
resolution was unanimously passed.
I, Regina W. Alexander, Clerk of the City of Southport do hereby certify that
the foregoing is a true copy of the proceedings of the Board of Aldermen at a
meeting held on June 9, 2005 as related to the contract between the City of
Southport and the North Carolina Department of Environment and Natural
Resources relative to the planning and management project for the City.

The invocation was delivered by Mayor Pro Tem Brown.
MINUTES
The regular monthly meeting minutes of June 9, 2005 and Special Meeting Minutes
of June 20, 2005 were approved upon motion of Alderman Powell, seconded by
Alderman Callari. The vote was unanimous.
CITIZEN MATTERS
(Non-Agenda Items)
Mr. C. B. Caroon of 416 East Bay Street addressed the Board concerning the
history of the Southport Small Boat Harbor. He stated that he read several
articles concerning this matter and wished to come before the Board to provide
information and give a brief history of the Small Boat Harbor/Marina. He stated
that discussion started in 1962 and “in 1963 with the Board and State Ports
Authority to work out a feasible situation whereby this project could be
completed. Negotiations took place in 1963 and it was agreed that it would be a
Small Boat Harbor for the use of the public and operated by the State.
Construction was completed in the spring of 1965, and opened for public use. He
stated in the early 1980’s, the state became dissatisfied with the operation
and it was leased to a private entity and operated for profit, but still it was
offered to the public for their convenience. He stated during his tenure on the
Board, he compiled documents which included a map of the 42 acres which was
transferred to the state, deed to the property, an agreement that was made by
the Board in the spring of ’63 and the resolution. Between ’89 and ’90, some of
them entered into discussion with the State Ports Authority and the topic was
the appraisal of the 42 acres that the city turned over to the State Ports
authority against the price or the money that they spent for improvements to
that facility. They talked about trading off one for the other and letting this
facility be put back into Authority and ownership of Southport. For
information, he explained the process of this negotiation which he stated is on
record in the Register of Deeds Office. Mr. Caroon explained that “it was
agreed that the City would turn this property over to the State Ports Authority
for the purpose for which it has been used primarily.” He read from minutes
where it was discussed and arrangements made for the transfer of the property.
Two properties were involved, 7.2 acres, and 42 acres. The 7.2 acres was kept
by the city for use as a disposal plant, and 42 acres turned over to the State
Ports Authority for the Small Board Harbor. He then read motions from the
minutes that were made to complete the transfer of property. The Agreement was
put together in March 14, 1963.
“The Board met in regular session, present Mayor J.E. Hahn, Presiding, Alderman
R. N. Hood, C.L Rourk, H.F. Aldridge and D.C. Herring.
“Motion was made by D. C. Herring seconded by C. L. Rourk that the two pieces
of property that the City purchased from Holston Land Company be made available
to the North Carolina State Ports Authority. City excluding any part of this
property that may be needed for sewerage disposal plant. This property to be
made available at total cost of land including engineers surveying cost,
attorney title search fee and any other cost to City.”
Mr. Caroon stated the 7.2 acres was to be excluded from this deal in the event
Southport chose to retain it.
“Motion was made by D.C. Herring seconded by C.L. Rourk that the following
Resolution be adopted.”
Resolution
“IT IS RESOLVED that the Mayor of the City of Southport be and he hereby is
authorized to sell the 7.2 acre and the 42 acre tracts of land adjoining the
present Yacht Basin and lying on the northern side of the Intracoastal
Waterway, recently purchased by the City from the Holston Land Company, to the
North Carolina State Ports Authority with the understanding that the same shall
be used only for the purpose of constructing a small boat terminal, otherwise
said land shall revert to the City of Southport; that the sales price for this
property shall be an amount representing the bare cost to the City for the
property consisting of the purchase price, surveyors’ charges and legal fees
for title search and opinion of title;
FURTHER RESOLVED that this offer to sell the property to the said State Ports
Authority shall if not accepted by said Authority, or this authorization be not
extended by appropriate action of this Board, expire on year from the date of
this resolution;
FURTHER RESOLVED that the Mayor and the Clerk to the Board be and they hereby
are authorized to execute all documents necessary to convey the aforesaid land
to the said State Ports Authority;
Mr. Caroon stated an amendment was made to the resolution dated April 11, 1963.
AMENDMENT
“FURTHER RESOLVED that the Clerk to this Board be and he hereby is authorized
and directed to furnish the said State Ports Authority certified copies of this
resolution.”
Excerpt from Minutes dated March 19, 1963.
(Motion was made by D. C. Herring seconded by H. F. Aldridge that the deed
dated December 20, 1962 from Holston Land Company to the City of Southport, for
the property on the western side of City owned property adjoining present Yacht
Basin. This property consisting of forty-two acres more or less be accepted,
Mayor Hahn be authorized to sign note for same.” Motion carried.)
Mr. Caroon stated selling the land will break the spirit of the agreement and
resolution that was approved by the City and State Ports Authority. If the land
is to be sold, the City should get the greater part of the money. Funds could
be used to update infrastructure and consider alleviating some of the tax
burden.
Mr. John Barbee of 712 E. Moore Street addressed the Board concerning the
marina. He stated for the past 4 years, there has been a public marina in
Southport. He stated various maritime clubs hold functions at the marina i.e.
the Power Squadron, Southport Sailing and Cape Fear Yacht Club. The Chamber of
Commerce has held the U.S. Open King Mackerel Tournament there for the past 26
years. He asked the question, “Where are our children and grandchildren going
to hold tournaments and fundraisers, put their boats in and out of the water if
the marina is sold and the City don’t buy it or own it?”
Mr. Barbee stated that the marina is an asset and is irreplaceable, and
believes a disservice will be done to future generations if the city does not
ask the state for control of the marina.
Mr. Woody Wilson of 502 Brunswick Street stated that citizens do not want to
see private or commercial development of the Southport Marina. It is a public
facility and if the marina gets away from the city, it is a lost that will
never be replaced. Mr. Wilson asked the Aldermen to support the citizens in
taking a stand. He asked the Board of Aldermen to support them in their
endeavor to save the marina. He presented a copy of a petition that is being
circulated in the community.
Mr. John Reinsburrow of 998 Pete’s Camp Drive, S.E. addressed the condition of
Northwood Cemetery and stated “in his opinion” it is declining further into
disrepair and is unkempt. He asked the City to take action to make it
presentable.
Second item addressed by Mr. Reinsburrow was the Lowe-White Park. He stated
that he addressed this issue a year ago and was told that it would be made a
place that the citizens would be proud of. He stated that the area is a “dump”.
Mayor Holden in response told Mr. Reinsburrow the city has a plan for the park.
The city is waiting on the outcome of Fort Johnston, and if the city is able to
obtain this property; plans are to build a park and tennis court.
Mr. Brian English of 102 River Drive referenced property in the ETJ beside
Builders First Source which is being used by the S&W Concrete Plant. He stated
this is not a permitted use, and it is his understanding if the Plant was shut
down six months, it could not re-open. He told the Board when Godwin sold to
APAC concrete was not mixed in hat location for approximately 3 years and now
this is being done in the middle of the night which abuts a neighborhood. He
asked that this matter be looked into by the city.
MARINA
Mayor Holden in clarifying information to the public explained “the marina is
not a public marina; it belongs to the State of North Carolina and is leased to
the Benson Group. During the 1970’s under the Governorship of James E.
Holshouser, the marina was leased and it was no longer public, (“State of North
Carolina”). Mr. Bill Arnold approached the operator of the marina (Smitty),
gave him a copy of the lease and 2 weeks to remove the state’s property. From
that point, it became a leased piece of property which meant that the City of
Southport for the last 40 years has never received property taxes on the
property. Mayor stated that he personally contacted Attorney Generals, Rufus
Edmisten, Lacy Thornburg, Mike Easley and Roy Cooper about the lease by letter
and asked them to review the agreement (which was changed at a later date) to
determine if it could be null and void. Each Attorney General stated it could
not be. The property is up for sale today because of the lease that was started
under Governor Holshouser.”
Mr. Caroon again referred the Board to the resolution dated April 1963 between
the City and State Ports Authority. Mayor stated the City of Southport cannot
sell a piece of property without going through the legislature. Mr. Caroon
referenced the lease agreement and Mayor recommended he obtain a copy of the
lease from 1970’s.
ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS
PUBLIC HEARING
Public Hearing on zoning reclassification request by J. Arthur Dosher Memorial
Hospital, to rezone 823 N. Atlantic Avenue from R-10 (residential) to O & I
(office and institutional). Alderman Callari requested this matter be tabled
until she can obtain clarification on rezoning this small area until the next
regular scheduled meeting (August 11, 2005). Motion seconded by Alderman
Childs. Vote carried.
PUBLIC HEARING
Alderman Childs motioned to enter Public Hearing, seconded by Alderman Powell,
on zoning alignment/reclassification request by Cape Fear Trading Company for
the following parcels: 308 West Bay Street, BD (Business District) and R-10
(Residential) to BD (Business District); 317 West Bay Street, Business District
and R-10 to Business District; 115 Yacht Basin Drive, Business District and R-
10 to Business District; and 319 West Moore Street, R-10 and Business District
to R-10. Vote carried.
Mr. Richard Bandera of 309 Clarendon Avenue, Architect stated his concerns are
about the idea and perception that happens from a reclassification request of a
particular site. The proposal from the applicant is changing from an open space
very low residential to R-10 and to a Business District. He stated Article 9,
of the UDO does not define open space very low density and allowable use. He
questioned open space very low residential district in comparison to an R-10?
Mayor told Mr. Bandera attending the Planning Board meetings will help define
these questions. Attorney Isenberg told Mr. Bandera that a table of permitted
uses is contained in the UDO that explains each district use, density,
setbacks, etc. Attorney Isenberg stated the zoning line actually runs through
the lots, a percentage of each lot is zoned business and a percentage
residential, and a property owner has the right to have their lots zoned one
way or another. The purpose of this request is to have each lot zoned one way.
Mr. Russ Ferris questioned the zoning change. Secondly, he questioned some of
the interest of Planning Board members and their backgrounds, and stated the
need for members who does not have a conflict of interest.
Ms. Susan Toth, member of the Planning Board, clarified that the request was to
rezone all four properties to business district. Lots 1, 2 and 3 as depicted on
the map were mainly business district and as stated by the Attorney, this is an
effort to align the zoning in accordance with the use that it is currently
under. She stated it made sense to the Planning Board to rezone those lots to
business districts which is why the recommendation was made. Lot 4 was
requested to be rezoned to business district, which most of it is residential
and they recommended it to remain R-10.
Mr. Henry Bridger’s of 412 E. Leonard Street stated according to the County’s
tax records, 319 West Moore Street is actually Parcel 237LF00401 whereas it is
listed 237LF004. 319 West Moore Street is the parking lot and the old wooden
boat shop. Parcel 237LF004 is 309 West Moore Street. Staff will look into this
discrepancy.
Mr. Rod Hyson, owner and developer asked the Board to support the
recommendation of the Planning Board.
Mr. John Reinsburrow of 998 Pete’s Camps Drive, S.E. (ETJ) asked the Board to
give careful consideration to rezoning this property and the long term affect
to Southport. If this area is rezoned, the developer and the city are bound to
allow anything that falls into this zoning category be constructed there. He
asked if the rezoning is approved, consideration be given to the area to
whichever the majority use of each parcel.
For clarification, Attorney Isenberg stated the lots in question are being
rezoned to the majority use.
No further comments, Alderman Childs motioned to close the Public Hearing,
seconded by Alderman Powell, vote carried.
REGULAR SESSION

RESOLUTION – MARINA
Alderman Fisher stated that the Mayor will attend a public meeting on July 27
and at that time. he will present the following resolution from the City.
RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, the City of Southport recognizes that the State of North Carolina is
considering selling the Southport Marina; and
WHEREAS, the City recognizes that the existing boat ramps and vessel moorings
are of utmost importance not only to the local areas but the entire state; and
WHEREAS, access to these ramps and moorings positively impacts the economy of
Southport and surrounding areas; and
WHEREAS, during the 30+ years that the Southport Marina has been under lease,
the City has received no property taxes from this facility, and has had no
controls over property; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen supports the sale of the Southport Marina
provided that the considerations noted below are appropriately addressed:
·   That the marina facilities be “user friendly” and “public accessible”,
especially the restroom and showers.
·   That the boat ramp remains available for use by the general public with
adequate boat trailer parking at no cost to the public,
·   That in the event a hotel/motel complex is developed, it shall be subject
to accommodation and sales taxes and all marina property shall be subject to
property taxes.
·   That 40% of present dockage for larger vessels remains open to the public
and at least 20% open to transients.
·   Provision shall be made for the yearly U.S. King Mackerel Tournament. It is
estimated to have a $2 million dollar economic impact on the area. The
tournament is 26 years old and average between 428-555 boats per year.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED, that the City of Southport Board of
Aldermen supports the potential sale of the Southport Marina property subject
to the above referenced considerations being appropriately addressed and
incorporated into any sales agreement entered into by the state and other
parties.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that in the event the Marina is retained by the State,
the City requests that it be paid annually a contribution in lieu of ad valorem
taxes based upon the appraised tax value.
ADOPTED, this the 14th of July 2005 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
S/Norman R. Holden
Mayor
Attest:
S/Regina W. Alexander, CMC, City Clerk
Alderman Adams motioned to approve the aforementioned resolution, seconded by
Alderman Callari. Discussion: Alderman Childs asked that “free use of the boat
ramp” be incorporated in the resolution. Vote carried.
Mayor Holden stated if anyone wants a copy of the lease agreement it can be
obtained from the Chairman of the State Ports Authority or the City Manager may
have a copy of each in his office.
Mayor invited the public to attend the meeting with the State Ports Authority
at South Brunswick High School, 3:00 p.m. on July 27th. Mayor Holden stated
that he met personally with the Chairman of the Board concerning Southport
Marina and he informed him of the conditions that he believes Southport should
get from the sale.

AUGUST 3, 2005
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING
AUGUST 3, 2005    7:30 P.M.
ALDERMAN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N. C.
 
MEMBERS PRESENT:   Norman R. Holden, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Meezie Childs, James Brown,
            Stuart Callari, James Powell and Paul Fisher
MEMBERS ABSENT:   None
STAFF PRESENT:      Rob Gandy, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander-CMC, City Clerk
Mayor Holden called the meeting to order. He announced that this Special
Meeting was called by Aldermen Childs and Callari for an opportunity to discuss
the marina. He explained to the public that this is a Special Called Meeting
for the Board, and not a Public Hearing.
The following statement was made by Mayor Holden and is transcribed verbatim:
“I feel that it is time to set the record straight. The Mayor and the Board of
Aldermen certainly is working to save the marina property and I make reference
to a letter which was faxed Monday morning to Governor Easley and to Chairman
Stewart asking them to donate the Southport Marina to the City of Southport. I
feel the Southport minutes, letters and files in City Hall, newspaper articles
since 1983 will show that I’ve always worked to gain control of the Southport
Marina. (I have evidence of this downstairs.) I have contacted four Attorney
Generals, Governor Hunt, Governor Martin and Governor Easley about the
ownership of the Southport Marina in the past asking always that it be turned
over to the City of Southport. Around 14 or 18 months ago, I was contacted by
Special Legal Counsel Ruffin Poole, that there was going to be some action on
the marina. He informed me that Mr. Kent Mitchell would be contacting me.
Myself, Mr. Mitchell, City Manager and Jim Henry of Bald Head Island, Project
Manager set down to discuss the Southport Marina. As I pointed out, Mr. Kent
Mitchell was the first one I discussed the Southport Marina with and I have 2
other witnesses, one sitting right next to me. At this time, he wanted to know
what we wanted to do with the marina. I specifically told him that the citizens
of Southport and myself wanted the marina. After the meeting, it appeared the
gate opened with subjects calling for appointments or information over the
phone about the sale of the Southport Marina. It appeared due to the fact that
it’s called Southport Marina, that a lot of these people understood that it was
the sale from the City of Southport and I explained to them that the City of
Southport did not own the marina. I received a call from the Wall Street
Journal and I have the gentleman’s name downstairs, that asked me was the City
of Southport for sale. I said, well...not yet, and then I explained to him that
it was the marina. And all along it appears that the plans for the City of
Southport, I have spoken several times with a Mr. Terry Lee, Mr. Jeff Earp &
Associate, Mr. Fred Dietrich, Mr. Homer Wright who phoned me several times, and
gosh knows, how many more individuals about the marina. They all had plans for
Southport Marina. I always advised him that it was up to the State Port’s
Authority and I was of the opinion that the marina should always come back to
the City of Southport and you can call them and verify that. Since 1983, I’ve
always worked towards obtaining the marina for the City of Southport. A meeting
was set up by the Governor during his first term of office between myself,
Aldermen Callari, Fisher and four of his legal staff members, one being Mr.
Ruffin Poole who is his number one staff person and Mr. Joe Henderson. For
those of you who do not know who Joe Henderson is, he is the Director of all
the state properties in the State of North Carolina. He assured me and the
committee that he would be working for the Governor to obtain the marina for
the City of Southport. I was first informed of the buyout of the lease the day
that they had the meeting on July 28 when some of you met with Chairman
Stewart. He called me that day about 9:30 a.m. informing me that he had just
been informed there was a buyout of the lease. I did not know at that time who
the buyout person was nor did he. I have spent all day in Raleigh and I have a
witness that is not associated with the City Board in anyway that I have been
in Raleigh all day, starting in the Governor’s office lobbying for the
ownership of the marina. So for the Board of Aldermen and especially the Mayor,
anyone stating we are not for Southport’s ownership of the marina is certainly
misinformed. We need to forget the hostilities and begin to work together if we
are going to get the marina. I am ready, are you? I met with Senator Soles
today, along with my witness. Senator Soles advised me that until HB 1522 has
cleared his Commerce Committee, that the property. City Marina cannot be sold.
If you want to verify that, you can contact Senator Soles. He personally asked
me, Norman what do you want to do with the marina? I said, Senator, I want the
Southport Marina to come back to the City of Southport. If you don’t believe
me, call and ask him.”
Alderman Childs stated the “Special Meeting” was called to give the Board an
opportunity to take action in regards to the acquisition of the Southport
Marina by the City. She stated that she along with Aldermen Powell and Callari
went to Raleigh (today) and met with Senator Soles, Representative Hill and
Representative Stiller. They received support and their willingness to work
with the city to acquire the marina. Alderman Childs then offered the following
Memorandum of Agreement and Resolution for Board adoption. Alderman Callari
seconded the motion, and the vote of approval was unanimous.
Memorandum of Agreement
In 1963 the City of Southport sold the State of North Carolina the marina
property for $9,000.00. It was the intention of all parties that a public
marina would be established to serve the public for both commercial and
recreational boating.
The Southport Marina has become an integral part of the economy of Southport.
It has indeed become a vital part of the body of Southport and reflects the
Southport spirit of a fully open waterfront community.
Our future and the marina’s future are fully entwined. The people of Southport
feel that the Southport marina belongs to them and is a part of their heritage,
life and community, whether in fact, the City of Southport actually owns the
marina or not.
If the State of North Carolina decides to continue ownership of the Southport
Marina through the State Ports Authority or some other agency, the City of
Southport desires to work closely with that management group to insure that the
Southport marina is a quality facility with outstanding service.
If the State of North Carolina has decided or does decide to sell the Southport
Marina, it is the full intention and commitment of the City of Southport to
pursue all avenues necessary to secure ownership of the Southport Marina from
the State of N. C. through the State Ports Authority.
The City requests the State of North Carolina to set aside a specific time
period of six (6) months in which the City of Southport will have exclusive
rights to pursue ownership of the Southport Marina. The City will pursue all
purchase options with due diligence and speed to plan and implement appropriate
financing programs as needed.
The City of Southport requests that the State of North Carolina, through the
States Port Authority work to agree on a reasonable price for the transfer of
the property.
RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, it is our goal to investigate, plan, negotiate and implement the
necessary steps to achieve that ownership; and
WHEREAS, we will take the needed actions to provide the citizens of Southport,
Brunswick County, and the State of North Carolina with a quality marina
facility that has outstanding service.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport unanimously supports the ownership of the Southport Marina by the
City of Southport.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that we say: Return the Marina to Southport.
ADOPTED by the Southport Board of Alderman in special session this the 3rd day
of August 2005.
S/Norman R. Holden, Mayor
ATTEST:
S/Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND CHAPTER 2 ARTICLE III
CITY OF SOUTHPORT CODE OF ORDINANCES
BE IT HEREBY ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport:
The Code of Ordinances, City of Southport, is hereby amended by adding a
section to be numbered 2-114, which section reads as follows:
Section 2-114 CRIMINAL HISTORY CHECKS
1.   In order to protect the citizens of the city and their properties, the
procedures herein are established to provide for fingerprinting and criminal
history checks on all final applicants for regular full and part-time positions
in the city government. Subject to division (C) of this section, employment
with the city may be denied for those persons convicted of any crime against a
person, or crimes against property where intent is an element, or any drug or
gambling related offense.
(A)   The City Manager, or designee, shall conduct an investigation of any
final candidate for a permanent full-time or part-time position with the city
government and it shall be a precondition of employment that an applicant for
such a position shall upon request, provide fingerprints and all other
necessary personal identification including a birth certificate, social
security number and drivers license, if available, so that the City Manager, or
designee, may cause a thorough search to be made of local and state criminal
records to determine if the applicant has a history of criminal convictions or
the crimes enumerated above by use of the Division of Criminal Information
Network (DCI).
(B)   The Police Department shall provide the findings from the use of the DCI
to the City Manager or designee, provided that all necessary agreements with
the State Bureau of Investigations Division of Criminal Information have been
executed.
(C)   An evaluation of any crime for purposes of employment will take into
account the nature and the circumstances of the offense and the time frame of
the offense as it relates to the essential job functions for the position
applied.
2.   If this ordinance or the application thereof to any person or circumstance
is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or
applications of the ordinance which can be given separate effect and to that
end the provisions of this ordinance are declared to be severable.
3.   Any ordinance or any part of an ordinance in conflict with this Ordinance,
to the extent of such conflict, is hereby repealed.
4.   This Ordinance is adopted in the interest of public health, safety and
general welfare of the inhabitants of the City of Southport, North Carolina,
and shall be in full force and effect from and after its adoption.
This Ordinance adopted this the 11th Day of August, 2005.
S/Norman R. Holden
Attest:
S/Regina W. Alexander-CMC

STEP FAMILY DAY PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, in the City of Southport, North Carolina, Stepfamily Day is enhanced
by our strong commitment to support the stepfamilies of our nation in their
mission to raise their children, create strong family structures to support the
individuals members of the family, instill in them a sense of responsibility to
all extended family members; and
WHEREAS, approximately half of all Americans are currently involved in some
form of stepfamily relationship and it is the vision of Founder, Michigan’s
Christy Borgeld and the Stepfamily Association of America that all stepfamilies
in the ’’’’United States’’ be accepted, supported and successful.
WHEREAS, Southport, and our nation has been blessed by thousands upon thousands
of loving stepparents and stepchildren who are daily reminders of the joy,
trials, and triumphs of the stepfamily experience and of the boundless love
contained in the bond between all types of parents and children; and
WHEREAS, Stepfamily Day is a day to celebrate the many invaluable contributions
stepfamilies have made to enriching the lives and life experience of the
children and parents of America and to strengthening the fabric of American
families and society
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen that they
hereby recognize and designate September 16th, 2005 as “Stepfamily Day” in the
City of Southport to celebrate the stepfamily relationships here and across the
nation.
DULY RESOLVED THIS THE 11th DAY OF AUGUST, 2005.

CADES COVE SUBDIVISION – PRELIMINARY PLAT
Mr. Jerry Haire, Planning Consultant for the CADES Cove project presented a
revised preliminary plat which refined the project by reducing lot sizes and
street amenities with no change to access points, location of streets, but
reduced total number of lots to 105. He stated all necessary construction
permits have been obtained and the project is underway. (Project vested with
the preliminary plan approved August of 2004 to proceed with construction
permits.) The details in the refinement process led to revisions that staff
requested be presented to the Board. All concerns and checklist items have been
addressed per staff’s recommendation with approval from the Planning Board
(July).
In response to question by Alderman Powell, Mr. Haire stated that they can
build 29 (3 bedroom homes) with current sewer allocation. (Phase I)
Mayor Holden asked about the estimated time for Phase IV. Mr. Haire stated this
depends on sewer allocation. Mayor Holden voiced concerns about the traffic
coming out on 14th street. Mr. Haire responded that DOT has asked them to
create a limited access movement at the 14th street intersection. They want to
develop this and open it up for construction access. They propose to rough in
the infrastructure of the roads which is a part of Phase I as they move into
Phase II, depending on the need. DOT recommended they do a limited access via
raised median for a right-in and right-out access at that location. DOT also
asked them to widen and create a left turn-in lane on Robert Ruark Drive. Mr.
Haire stated that he understand concerns about the right-out only access adding
to the downtown congestion and the need for a turn around to go back out of
town. A future option is to connect Caswell Avenue to 14th street that will
come out to a full moving intersection that can provide a right turn coming
into down town.
Mayor stated future development is going to create a terrible traffic area onto
Howe Street and requested they work with DOT to endeavor to reduce traffic
coming onto Howe.
Alderman Adams stated he can not support the preliminary plat with what DOT has
approved for the developer regarding the proposed traffic pattern. He has no
problem with the access points but the design and function.
Attorney Isenberg asked Mr. Haire if he can record the plat with Phase I &
Phase II with access out to Robert Ruark since the Board is having problems
with the access on 14th Street. Mr. Haire stated this can be done, however the
intent is to open up 14th Street access somewhere between Phase II and Phase
III for construction. He stated they do not have a schedule for the future
development on 14th Street. Timing depends on sewer allocation.
Alderman Powell suggested making 14th Street one way going into the
development. Mr. Haire asked as an alternative if the Board will approve the
revised plan with Phase IV approval contingent on further design. They will
agree that Phase IV not be developed until such time that an agreeable design
is made to 14th Street or make it a one way in or eliminate it altogether. Mr.
Haire stated it is a stretch to proceed on just part of a preliminary plan
since it has already been approved and they have permits for the entire
project. They are willing to work with staff and DOT on the design and
function, without holding a portion of the project back.
After much discussion, Mr. Haire stated they will work with staff and DOT to
formulate a workable plan.
Due to sufficient sewer allocation, Alderman Powell motioned to approve the
Preliminary Plan for Phase I and Phase II. Alderman Callari seconded the
motion. The votes were:
      4 ayes: Aldermen Powell, Brown, Callari and Childs.
      2 noes: Aldermen Fisher and Adams

UDO COMMITTEE
Alderman Childs reported on the UDO Committee comprised of Barbara Clewis,
Aldermen Callari, Powell and herself.
·   Purpose of the Committee being appointed was a result of some
misunderstanding between the Board and the people who wrote the UDO. She
related it was her belief that mixed use development was permitted in the
Central Business District (CBD) which is historical to that district. In
working with citizens that is trying to execute mixed use development, it was
found that the Planning Board and the Planner has a different view, therefore a
meeting was held and they met with the Planning Board to address this issue.
Other issues were discussed which included the following:
1)    To impose 1 year time limit for planned building groups and subdivisions
plat approvals. Construction must begin within 1 year after approval.
2)    New District designated as Marina District.
3)    Make single family residential dwellings a conditional use in the O & I,
CBD, BD and HC zoning districts.
4)    Prohibit signs within the ROW or on public property unless the sign
promotes the city.
5)    Parking requirements
6)    Reduce height maximum
7)    Reduce multi-family density requirements from 11 units per acre to lower
8)    Bulk up on landscaping requirements
9)   Require percentage of open space that is in addition to any wetland areas
or storm water ponds
Alderman Childs asked that the Board of Aldermen request the Planning Board to
change the UDO to allow for mixed use in the Central Business District, (CBD)
and to establish a Marina District
Attorney Isenberg stated that in order for the Board of Aldermen to consider
amendments to the UDO, recommendations must be submitted from the Planning
Board and advertised for Public Hearing before Board action.
Mayor Holden recommended the UDO Committee send their recommendation to the
Planning Board for the August 18th meeting and once they have reviewed these,
submit their recommendation to the Board of Aldermen for the September meeting.
He suggested Alderman Childs’s Committee prioritize the changes, ex: place the
central business district as number one and Marina as number two, whichever the
Committee deem is most important.
Alderman Powell communicated that an educational work session will be held on
the section in the UDO regarding storm water August 29, 7:00 p.m., Community
Building with Consultant Jeanette Powell from AMEC International.

AUGUST 29, 2005
JOINT MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN/PLANNING BOARD JOINT MEETING
AUGUST 29, 2005                  7:00 P.M.
COMMUNITY BUILDING               SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
ALDERMEN PRESENT: James Brown, Mayor Pro Tem
            Jim Powell, Stuart Callari and Meezie Childs
PLANNING BOARD:   Barbara Clewis, Chairperson
            Susan Toth, Sandra Spencer, Harley Lemons,
            Dale McPherson, Stephanie VanNoordt and
            Buddy Barnes
STAFF PRESENT:      Robert Grant, Public Services Director
            Wayne Strickland, Building Inspector
            Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
            Michele Windham, Secretary to Planning Board
OTHER:         Jeanette Powell, Consultant, AMEC
The Board of Aldermen and the Planning Board met jointly to hold a workshop on
Storm water Management. Alderman Powell introduced Ms. Jeanette Powell,
Consultant for AMEC International.
Ms. Powell presented a power point presentation on Storm Water Management in
Southport.
·   Storm water is the runoff from rainfall events
·   Storm water problems results from water quantity and quality
·   Problems are addressed by storm water management ordinance, design manuals,
minimum standards, public education, outreach and voluntary programs.
·   Southport’s tool box consist of storm water ordinance, storm water permit
and storm water management plan technical manual
·   Southport’s ordinance protects, maintain and enhance public health, safety
and general welfare. Establish minimum requirements to control storm water from
new development and provide for the issuance of a storm water permit for new
development.
·   Southport’s storm water ordinance protects, maintain and enhance by
minimizing damage to public and private property, ensure a functional drainage
system, reduce effects of development, assist in attainment of water quality
standards, reduce local flooding and drainage problems, maintain pre-developed
runoff characteristics and mitigate flooding and drainage impacts.
·   The minimum requirements for new development are storm water permit,
discharge control plan, access to facilities, inspection of facilities and
facility maintenance.
·   The following are not subject to a storm water permit: Farming and logging,
additions or modifications to an existing house, residential development on a
single existing lot, development or single family residentially zoned parcels,
necessary repairs to a storm water treatment practice.
·   Subject to the storm water permits: development can’t commence until storm
water permit is issued, conditional upon receipt of a state E/SC Permit, must
meet NCDENR State Storm Water Management Program requirements which are valid
for 1 year.
·   Waivers can be obtained for developments that do not impair objectives of
the ordinance, cannot feasibly do on site management, and does not impact
downstream structure, habitat, erosion and flooding. Mitigation is required for
land preservation, retrofits on existing development, free in lieu to fund
storm water studies.
·   Storm water permit non-compliance includes investigation of formal
complaints, written notification of violations and remedies, misdemeanor fine
of $50 and/or 30 days imprisonment. Civil penalty of $25 (Ms. Powell did state
that the state charges $35,000)
·   Storm water permit suspension and revocation includes notice of violation,
stop work order, restoration of lands, and holds on occupancy permits and
property lien for failure to maintain.
·   Performance Bond Security may be required for permit issuance, estimated
construction costs + 25%, released with as-built plans & PE Certification, and
partial pro-rata release at city’s discretion.
·   Southport’s Storm water Management Plan Technical Manual design standards
and guidance for detention and wet retention facilities, infiltration systems,
operation and maintenance of facilities, piped drainage systems, open channels,
constructions standards and inlets.
·   Requirements for storm water discharge control facilities: Provide velocity
control, 25 year peak = existing peak evaluate & address downstream flooding
(25 yr & 100 yr events). Inspect and maintain facilities, dedicate access for
maintenance, designed by appropriately licensed professional. City may add on
to address existing problems.
·   Retention Pond is required for commercial or multi-family development that
is less than 1 acre and greater than 40% developed or greater than 1 acre and
greater than 25% impervious.
·   Design requirements for detention and retention facilities: Design for the
25 year event, downstream flooding check for 100 year event and encouraged as
an Amenity/Visual Enhancement.
During the presentation, attendees asked many pointed questions relating to
maintenance concerns, the North Carolina State Stormwater Plan, retention
ponds, watershed studies, easements, construction, etc. Increasing fines for
non-compliance was emphasized.
After the presentation, comments were made on the Storm Water Ordinance. Ms.
Powell commented that Southport has a good ordinance with a few changes that
she would recommend.
Alderman Powell requested Ms. Powell to submit a proposal to the City
delineating recommended changes to enhance the City’s Storm Water Ordinance.
No further dialogue, the workshop was adjourned.

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been petitioned under G.S. 160A-31 to annex
the area described below; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at Southport City
Hall at 7:30 p.m. on September 8, 2005 after due notice by publication in the
State Port Pilot on August 24 and August 31, 2005, and;
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the petition meets the requirements
of G.S. 160A-31;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, by the Board of Aldermen of Southport, North
Carolina that:
Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-31, the following
described territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City of Southport
effective immediately
Beginning at a nail in the pavement where the Northern line of Stuart Avenue,
having a 66 foot right-of way, is intersected by the Eastern line of North Howe
Street (N.C. Highway 211, 80 foot right-of-way); running thence from said
beginning point North 18 Degrees 00 Minutes West along the Eastern line of
North Howe Street 119.68 feet to an existing iron pipe; thence North 72 degrees
31 Minutes 30 Seconds East 327.09 feet to a new iron rod in the Western line of
S.R. 1542 (60 foot right-of-way); thence South 13 Degrees 59 Minutes East along
the Western line of S.R. 1542 119.45 feet to a new iron rod at its intersection
with the Northern line of Stuart Avenue; thence South 72 Degrees 26 Minutes 41
Seconds West along the Northern line of Stuart Avenue 318.72 feet to the point
of beginning. Described property containing 38570.70 sq. ft. 0.89 Acres
Section 2. Upon and after September 8, 2005 the above described territory and
its citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be entitled to the same
privileges and benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said territory
shall be subject to municipal taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10.
Section 3.  The Mayor of the City of Southport shall cause to be recorded in
the office of the Register of Deeds of Brunswick County, and in the office of
the Secretary of State at Raleigh, North Carolina, an accurate map of the
annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the County Board
of Elections, as required by G. S. 163-288.1.
ADOPTED, this the 8th day of September 2005.

CREDIT CARD POLICY
City Manager stated adopting this policy is a means to improve internal
control. The policy has been reviewed by the City Auditor and is recommended.
Alderman Childs motioned to approve the Credit Card Policy, seconded by
Alderman Callari. Vote of approval was unanimous.
City of Southport Credit Card Policy
SUBJECT: Credit Card Usage in the Performance of City Business
PURPOSE: To establish criteria for the use of credit and purchase cards issued
on behalf of the City in the course of performing City business. To standardize
the documentation and reporting of business expenses, so that all City
employees/officials are guided by a common set of expense guidelines
established by the City of Southport, Local Government Fiscal Control Act and
IRS Regulations.
PROCEDURE:
Business Credit Card: Business Credit Cards will be available for check out not
more than one (1) day prior to their anticipated use from the Finance
Department for the use of the Mayor, Aldermen, the City Manager and City
Employees. The individual to whom the card is issued is responsible for the
card and its proper use. The City Manager will have final approval authority on
credit card issuance. The Finance Director will be responsible for verifying
reconciliation of all credit card usage and charges pursuant to this policy.
The credit card is to be used for approved, official business only.  The City
recognizes that occasionally it will be good business for a City Official to
buy meals when working with existing or potential business investors, agencies
that might purchase City services Such use of the credit card is recognized to
be a legitimate expense of the City whether used locally or while traveling as
long as it is an ordinary and/or necessary expense as regulated by IRS.
For other travel expenses, the credit card will only be used for securing and
confirming lodging and travel reservations. Once the reservation is confirmed,
the employee/official is to submit a Travel Expense Request two weeks in
advance for Lodging, Meals, Mileage, Registration and other related
miscellaneous fees. A check will be issued to that employee/official one (1)
day, prior to departure. In the event, that travel plans are cancelled and an
employee has received an advance, the City must be reimbursed immediately.
The credit card will not be used in lieu of the normal purchasing procedures of
the City of Southport. In the event that a vendor will not bill the City with
the security of purchase order number, an exception will be made. This
exception is made only after the employee follows the correct procedure of
obtaining a purchase order prior to the purchase as required by Local
Government Commission’s. No item over $5,000 will be charged on the City Credit
Card.
Personal use of credit cards is strictly prohibited and subject to disciplinary
actions to include termination of employment.
Reconciliation- Credit card activity must be reconciled as established below:
The Cardholder will submit receipts and/or documentation describing and
appropriately coding each transaction on a purchase order immediately. All
lodging receipts and daily meal expenditures that exceed $75.00 are to be
submitted as required by IRS regulations.
Receipt/documentation should be completed and the card returned to the City not
later than one (1) day after use. In the event of a lost or missing receipt,
the City employee/official will be held personally responsible for the expense
and must compensate the City immediately.
Adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen on September 8, 2005.
S/James Brown, Mayor Pro Tempore

S/Regina Alexander, City Clerk

this issue. As a result of the meeting, the Historical Society drafted a set of
rules to govern firing of the cannon. Recently, he was contacted by a concerned
citizen who is still being disrupted by the noise and requested the city
enforce its Noise Ordinance. It was explained that the Southport Historical
Society use firing of the cannon for private events as a means of raising
funds. The citizen asked that the Historical Society curtail the firing of
cannons for private events. He asked the Board for recommendations and
requested the City Attorney respond to the question of being in violation of
the City’s Noise Ordinance.
Mayor Pro Tem Brown asked about the number of times the cannon is fired for
private events. Mr. Bill Fravel stated this depends on requests, sometimes the
cannon may be fired two to three times over a weekend. They will provide the
Board with a list of scheduled activities. Mayor Pro Tem Brown stated this
matter will be turned over to the City Attorney for review.
Mr. Jim Clary, a resident of East Bay Street expressed concern that the cannon
is being fired every weekend, especially in the summer months. Some of the
residents fear that the momentum is being picked up and they ask that the
cannon firings be reserved for honorary and patriotic events.
HURRICANE KATRINA
Alderman Adams asked if the City has made any plans to aid Katrina Hurricane
victims through disaster relief. City Manager Gandy gave the Board a handout
that governs expenditure of public funds. Alderman Adams suggested the City
establish one day for disaster relief and insure that the public is aware of
it. He suggested water, clothing etc. and the possibility of having a focal
point to drop these supplies off within the City. He also suggested the
possibility of transporting these supplies to a location where supplies are

recommended cleaning supplies be added to the list. City Manager Gandy asked
Ms. Prendeville if she will work with the City through the Inter Church

estimates on repairs.

help supports a structure)
·   3 concrete docks need to be removed, pilings almost non-existent
·   Building that houses the restaurant is in bad shape, ADA non compliant and

·   Dry rack storage building in disrepair, needs to come down
Mayor Pro Tem Brown announced that part time personnel have been hired by the

ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, NC
 
MEMBERS PRESENT:    Norman R. Holden, Mayor
            James Brown, Mayor Pro Tem
            Aldermen Paul Fisher, James Powell, Stuart Callari,
            Nelson Adams and Meezie Childs

            Regina W. Alexander-CMC, City Clerk

order at 7:30 p.m. by Mayor Norman Holden.
Alderman Brown delivered the invocation.
MINUTES
Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Callari to approve the s pecial
meeting minutes of August 29, 2005 and regular meeting minutes of September 8,
2005 . The vote was unanimous.
CITIZEN MATTERS
(Non-Agenda)
For the benefit of the public, Mayor Holden announced that early voting will
begin October 20 at the Board of Elections office in Bolivia and urged citizens
to vote.
Mayor stated having been contacted by several citizens concerning mixed use in
the Central Business District ; this matter will be considered at a special
meeting of the Board on October 25, 2005 at 6:30 p.m.
Mr. Bill Duke of 215 North Caswell Avenue spoke on behalf of the Committee to
save the Southport Marina. He stated that “our Committee remains unified to
honor the request of 7,500 citizens to return the marina to Southport and to
keep it a public facility. At the recent Planning Board meeting Dale Holland
presented and the Planning Board agreed with his proposal concerning the zoning
of Southport Marina. As discussed at this meeting these zoning recommendations
will be in effect if only the ownership of the marina is maintained by the
State of North Carolina or the City of Southport. It was also discussed and
agreed upon that these proposed zoning ordinances should be recommended to the
Board of Aldermen as soon as possible. It was also agreed that additional
proposed zoning requirements would be developed because of any potential
transfer of ownership to a private concern. Our Committee would like to be on
record saying that we believe the Board of Aldermen has a larger responsibility
to the citizens of Southport than to piece meal this approval process. By doing
this the City is only partially empowered with zoning ordinances. With private
ownership, the city will be powerless in any zoning efforts. We recommend the
following: Since the City of Southport has employed Dale Holland; we recommend
that he turn up his timetable for developing zoning proposals for both
government and private ownership. Taxpayers dollars are paying for his
professional counsel and the taxpayers would like a designing proposal
forwarded to the Board of Aldermen yesterday. We accept, why accept only half
of what is truly needed and what we’ve all been working for. Mr. Holland needs
a sense of urgency and you the Aldermen should not accept anything less than
the complete proposal. Thank you very much.”
PUBLIC HEARING
Alderman Childs motioned to enter Public Hearing, seconded by Alderman Callari
to discuss zoning text amendment change, Major and Minor Subdivisions
addressing Section 25-13: Lot Standards, (B) Minimum Dimensions.  The vote of
approval was unanimous. For benefit of the public, Mayor Holden stated the
standards were approved and inserted in the Zoning Ordinance on May 13, 1999
but were inadvertently omitted in the Unified Development Ordinance. The
Planning Board recommends approval of changes.
Attorney Jay Short told the Board that he represents Cape Fear Trading Group
and stated the Board has made several changes to the UDO since its adoption in
June 2004. As the UDO exists at present, in the business district there are no
minimum square footage requirements and no set back requirements for single
family residential which is a permitted use in the Central Business District as
it exists now. Cape Fear Trading Group bought the Yacht Basin property 2 years
ago and has submitted various mixed use plans to the City which has met with
resistance. As a result of perception of those proposals, Cape Fear Trading
Group recognized that single family residential was a permitted use for that
tract of land and has submitted a plan to the City of Southport. During the
process of submitting their plan, it was learned that the City was going to
modify the UDO to make single family residential use a conditional use for the
Central Business District , not a permitted use.  They also   learned about the
change in the minimum square footage requirements and lot dimensions. Cape Fear
Trading Group submitted a plan to the city prior to the September meeting,
however the Board did not vote at this meeting. Cape Fear Trading has met with
staff to get feedback on their plan and changes to be made. They were told by
Mr. Holland and Strickland their changes would be approved. The changes have
been made and the newly revised plan has been submitted with the use that is
permitted within the UDO. Attorney Short asked if the changes are adopted, to
let their plans as submitted proceed through the process and be exempt from any
new changes the Board may adopt tonight.
After a question from Alderman Childs, Attorney Short responded that the plans
were submitted to Mr. Strickland today.
Alderman Adams stated if the plans are submitted and approved they should be
grand- fathered under the UDO as it exists when the plans were submitted.
Attorney Isenberg stated if the plans have been officially submitted to the
city and fees paid, the Board has the authority if the amendments are adopted,
and to make them apply only to developments submitted after adoption of the
changes.
Alderman Fisher stated the UDO was adopted in June, and if changed tonight,
then anything that has been officially submitted to the Building Inspector or
Planning Board prior to that time, should come under the UDO as it existed when
the plans were submitted.
Mr. Henry Bridgers of 412 East Leonard Street stated in allowing the permitting
of residential housing in the Central Business District, Southport will receive
perpetual complaints from new residents about the noise, traffic, parking,
flooding, sewerage, etc. He stated the City has an inadequate sewer system and
if residential construction is allowed in the Yacht Basin with the addition of
more commodes, this condition will not improve. He stated that he witnessed
sewer being washed into the Yacht Basin with the recent rains.
Mr. Dale McPherson of 108 South Rhett stated when the UDO was originally
adopted there were provisions in the document for conditional uses for
residential in the business district. The Planning Board recommended this in
order to have control over how much residential density is allowed in the
business district. He asked the Board why have a business district if it is not
going to be a business district. He stated residential in the business district
will cause more parking problems and believes the Yacht Basin was inadvertently
changed from a   conditional use to a permitted use. He stated they are trying
to protect the Yacht Basin but believes it is slipping under the fence and will
be all residential. He stated if the city is not careful, everything that draws
people to this town will be no more. If the Board decides to change the zoning
to a conditional use, it is of no use to the city because the very thing that
they are trying to protect will slip through.
Mr. Ed McKinnon of 308 West West Street and a government and economic teacher
at South Brunswick High School encouraged the Board not to sell out with
conditional allowances by killing the “golden goose” of Southport. He
encouraged the Board to keep the fishing village that draws people to this area
and not become a Wrightsville Beach in 10 to 20 years. He asked the Board to
make a conscious decision in what they are going to allow to be built on the
waterfront because it will change everything.
Mr. Ed Boguskie of 502 West Brown Street read excerpts from the City’s
Comprehensive Plan that was adopted in May of 2001. “the zoning regulations
shall be made in accordance with comprehensive plan and design to lessen
congestion in the streets, to provide a land use form that reflects the vision
of the city’s residents is unified to avoid conflicting land uses, optimizing
resources, preserves the city’s character and is pleasing, providing open
space, vistas in distinguishable districts.”
Mr. Randy Fullwood stated growing up in Southport around the Yacht Basis meant
a lot to him and seeing the changes that are proposed is incomprehensible. He
encouraged the Board to preserve the business district and not let it become
residential.
Mr. Bill Bruce engaged with Mr. Rod Hyson of Cape Fear Trading stated under
their plan the amount of sewerage disposal in that area will be less for the
proposed 11 residences than the motel and restaurant that is already there.
Their plan has parking underneath the building for each residence in accordance
with the requirements of the UDO. He stated the UDO will require that the
buildings be constructed in a way that they will be elevated to avoid flooding.
If Mr. Hyson is denied approval to construct residential and commercial
construction is allowed in that area, the city will have the same problem with
flooding and possibly more of a parking problem.
Mr. Henry Bridgers explained for point of clarification the parking he was
referring to was delivery trucks discharging food and the people that live in
this area are inconvenienced for several hours.

seconded by Alderman Powell. The vote carried.
ZONING AMENDMENT TEXT CHANGE
Alderman Childs motioned to approve the Zoning Amendment Text Change, Major and
Minor Subdivision, Section 25-13: Lot Standards (b) Minimum
Dimensions.  Discussion: Alderman Fisher asked if plans have been submitted
prior to this text change will they be impacted by the change. Consensus of the
Board was no. Amendment: Alderman Childs amended the motion to make the text
change effective for all plans submitted after date of adoption. Motion
seconded by Alderman Powell and the vote of approval was unanimous.
ZONING AMENDMENT TEXT CHANGE
Article 25. MAJOR AND MINOR SUBDIVISIONS
Section 25-13: Lot Standards
(B)   Minimum Dimensions:
In no case shall any lot have a frontage of less than seventy-five (75) feet,
an average lot depth on land of less than one hundred (100) feet, or a square
footage of less than ten thousand (10,000) square feet in area. Lots located on
the turning circle of a cul-de-sac may have individual minimum frontages of
forty (40) feet per lot provided that the lot shall have a lot width of at
least seventy five (75) feet measured fifty (50) feet from the front property
line and in no case shall any lot less than ten thousand (10,000) square feet
in area.
AMENDMENT TO THE UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
The Board considered an amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance and
table of permitted uses; residential housing types.  This amendment was
recommended by the Planning Board and reflects the change of single family
detached from a permitted use in the Central Business District, Business
District, Office and Institutional District and Highway Commercial to a
Conditional Use in these zoning districts.
City Manager Gandy explained that the Planning Board requested the Board
consider making the above changes. Alderman Childs stated she has a problem
with R-10 setbacks if the lot is non-conforming.
After discussion, Alderman Childs motioned to approve the residential housing
type single family detached entry of the table of permitted uses to conditional
use in the O& I, CBD, BD and HC zoning districts  without the R-10 setback
requirements.    Discussion: Alderman Fisher referenced major and minor
subdivisions and recommended five or more lots should be presented to the Board
of Aldermen for approval, not just the Building Inspector. No further
discussion, motion seconded by Alderman Powell, vote carried.
TRAFFIC CORRIDOR STUDY – SOUTHEASTERN BRUNSWICK COUNTY
The Board acknowledged a written request from May Moore, Brunswick County
Commissioner for a $5,000 appropriation to perform a traffic corridor study for
Southeastern Brunswick County. Mayor Holden stated he has attended meetings
with other Mayors pertaining to this study and it appears that there is some
problem with raising the funds. He recommended if the Board decides to fund the
study, it does so contingent upon other municipalities donating the same
amount. In giving the Board background information this request, Mayor
explained that the idea came from Leland as a result of Commissioner Bill Sue
obtaining funding through the Metropolitan Planning Organization. The City of
Southport is under the Rural Planning Organization.
Alderman Adams stated there is no question that a study needs to be made but
believes the County should use ad valorem tax dollars to fund the study.
Alderman Fisher stated as a member of a County Thoroughfare Committee several
years ago, a plan was developed and submitted it to the County Commissioners
and the Department of Transportation with similar proposals. He recommended
that Plan be implemented.
Mayor Holden communicated that several studies are being implemented by the
North Carolina Department of Transportation with the “Moving Ahead Program” and
if the Board so desires, he will request staff to write a letter to
Commissioner Moore and ask her to revisit and implement the old study. The
Board by consensus agreed with this recommendation. Alderman Fisher stated that
Mr. Walton Willis was also involved in the study.

YARD WASTE PROGRAM
City Manager Gandy reported that staff has looked into the possibility of
providing new roll out carts as part of the city’s yard waste program. He
stated when the city first negotiated the contract with Waste Industries it did
not specify in the contract that Waste Industries would provide replacement
carts. Waste Industries upgraded their carts and the city was allowed to use
the old carts for yard waste, and over a time they were replaced. Approximately
a year ago, Waste Industries stated they could not afford to do this any more
with what they were being paid. City Manager Gandy referenced the Board to
Agenda Item #12 after meeting with Joe McCarthy from Waste Industries. The
company can provide yard debris carts at a cost of $67.50/unit and will
continue to pick up yard debris that is bagged and bundled. In reviewing the
permits issues and account information, the city is adding approximately 12 new
residential accounts each month. If the Board determines to catch up the
accounts initiated since June of 2004 when the cart service was discontinued,
it will cost approximately $12,150. The City currently charges $4.83/month for
solid waste pick-up which includes pick up and not the cart. If the city wants
to go with the carts again, the cost will need to be adjusted to $.675 p/mo to
accommodate cost of the cart, maintenance and replacement costs.
In answer to question from Alderman Powell, City Manager Gandy explained that
the cart service yard debris is not a part of the solid waste contract. This
service is outside of the regular solid waste contract where one cart is
provided for household garbage.
Mayor recommended sending a survey to each property owner to determine if they
want a cart. Alderman Brown suggested the survey ask if there are people that
have a cart and don’t want it, to give it to someone that wants one. After
discussion on whether or not to provide carts to every household, the Board
agreed to place this item on the agenda for the Board’s Retreat in January.
Aldermen Fisher asked the City Manager to provide a recommendation on new
accounts, maintenance and how the contract will be amended. Wants to see this
program continued.
Alderman Brown stated he wishes to see the service continued and the City needs
to make carts available to those people that want them.

FIRE PREVENTION WEEK
Alderman Childs motioned to adopt a Resolution proclaiming October 9-15, 2005
as Fire Prevention Week in the City of Southport. Motion seconded by Alderman
Brown. Vote of approval was unanimous.
Resolution
Proclaiming October 9 - 15, 2005
Fire Prevention Week
WHEREAS, the Southport Fire Department is committed to ensuring the safety and
security of all those living in and visiting our Fire District; and
WHEREAS, fire is a serious public safety concern both locally and nationally,
and homes are the locations where people are at greatest risk of fire; and
WHEREAS, the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) has documented through
its research a significant increase in home candle fires, even as most other
causes of home fires have steadily declined; and
WHEREAS, the Firefighters of the Southport Fire Department are dedicated to
reducing the occurrence of residential and commercial structural fires and fire
related injuries through prevention and protection education; and
WHEREAS, the residents of the Southport Fire District are responsive to public
education measures and are able to take personal steps to increase their safety
from fire; and
WHEREAS, using proper care with candles will have a positive effect on the home
fire problem; and
WHEREAS, each candle fire that is prevented in the Southport Fire District is
an opportunity to prevent painful injury and costly property damage; and
WHEREAS, the 2005 Fire Prevention Week theme, “USE CANDLES WITH CARE: WHEN YOU
GO OUT, BLOW OUT!” effectively serves to remind us all of the simple actions we
can take to stay safer from fire everyday.
THEREFORE, I Norman R. Holden, Mayor of the City of Southport do hereby
proclaim October 9-15, 2005 as Fire Prevention Week through out this City, and
I urge all the citizens of Southport to heed the important safety messages from
the Southport Fire Prevention Team, and to support the many public safety
activities and efforts of the Southport Fire Department.
S/Norman R. Holden, 
Mayor
