REGULAR SESSION
Alderman Fisher moved, seconded by Alderman Callari to approve an amendment to
the Unified Development Ordinance to establish a Marina/Marina District. The
vote of approval was unanimous.
Marina/Marina District
Marinas located on state property under NCGS 160A-392 or city-owned property
shall not allow single-family or multi-family residential usage.
The purpose of this note to the Table of Permitted Uses is to protect the
character of the commercial development of this area and to reserve an area
along the waters edge for maritime uses, water dependent uses, and water
oriented uses. This is consistent with Southport’s historical character as a
working waterfront community open for all the public to use. This note also
provides for certain other non-water dependent uses which are closely aligned
with water oriented uses. Land uses which would wall off or prevent the public
from access to public trust waters are specifically discouraged. Residential or
“dockominium” uses in this area are expressly forbidden.
This area is established to provide land for the use by all of Southport’s
citizens, visitors to the area by land or by water, and to support the city’s
tourist industry. Specifically, on city property or property regulated by NCGS
160A-392 the following shall be allowed:
Bait and tackle shops
Boat and other marine related offices
Boat docks - public and for marina lease only
Boat dry storage
Boat ramps and boat launching facilities (including public)
Boat repair facilities
Boat service areas
Boat safety and towing facilities
Boat storage and boat construction yards
Bulkheads and other shoreline stabilization
Commercial charter or sightseeing water craft facilities
Fishing piers and public boardwalks
Launderette, coin operated laundry for marina users, accessory to marina
operation
Marina
Marine related service and filling stations
Marine equipment stores
Mooring piles
Navigational markers
Parking areas - vehicle and boat trailers
Parks and public use areas
Public utility buildings
Public water access
Restaurant as an accessory use to marina operation
All setbacks must comply with CAMA and Corp of Engineers requirements.
Except for Dock master’s office, roofs, shelters, framing, or other similar
elevated structures are not permitted over dock areas. Temporary, removable
canopies are permitted to provide outdoor dining protection at restaurants.
PUBLIC HEARING – CENTRAL BUSINESS DISTRICT (CBD)
Alderman Callari moved, seconded by Alderman Brown to enter Public Hearing to
receive comments from the public on a proposed amendment to the Central
Business District Mixed Use. The vote was unanimous.
(Please note that comments from citizens are as near verbatim as possible with
a few exceptions)
Ms. Stephanie Van Noordt of 903 E. Leonard Street, an alternate member of the
Planning Board, speaking as a concerned citizen asked the Board not to rush to
redefine the heart of the City referring to the Central Business District. She
presented the following:
(Please note statement is near verbatim as possible)
“Why would residential be permitted within a CBD?
Why is the presented change of the 1 to 1 ratio that is being presented for
mixed use in CBD, why is it not the same as a business owner living on the
site?
What is a hypothetical road map if residential is adopted in CBD?
First question asking myself about residential being permitted in a CBD, I see
certain circumstances that will warrant residential development and would
assume that by introducing this as a permitted use that there could potentially
be a larger problem with our CBD related to revitalization. If there were in
fact declining vitality in our downtown district, I think more than residential
inclusion would warrant discussion at this time. Other reasons that I can think
of for adding to the table of permitted uses are conveniences of travel between
work and home to an extensive CBD area, the lack of housing adjacent to the CDB
area, plus any other factors that I personally would not have insight into
because I am not a Planner. I find that any of these I brought up to be a
stretch to apply them to our downtown.
The second question...the argument presented for a 1 to 1 business residential.
I have heard that shop owners have had in the past the ability to live upstairs
of their businesses and this is something Southportians want to remain
available to business owners. I think that the presented text change, the
ordinance adaptation presented tonight does not address this directly. Although
it does assure that many redeveloped buildings will be torn down. It is simply
a relationship of uses, and by that; business use, residential use. There is a
true disconnect between those proportions because there is no ownership and
will not promote the business owners residing rights within the CBD, but will
continue a promotion of disconnect between the businesses and the residential
parking, and I fear that it could also lead to gated off parking lots for
residential owners in the CBD. I think a better approach is to maybe look at
the business unit with an accessory apartment under a single ownership where
occupancy is more than x number of days, so that occupant is truly living there
and that the parking space then is occupied by the same person. That business
owner and the resident are all under the same ownership. In fact, this is
already included within our ordinance. I think it is more on target towards
finding an avenue for residing and shop keeping in this town.
The third thing is I found myself asking at both of those meetings, why the
rush and push for this zoning change? It is evident and it’s been in the paper
that it clearly reflects the future sale of Mrs. Bette Leggett’s store. I have
to wonder if this is not a zoning issue but a developer issue. I know that we
have project types in town that have 3 commercial units with 3 residential
units above, but they are in multiple locations in Southport and I know that
this is an expanding trend and I have seen this on the beach. Could that then
become a road map for the CBD where residential apartments have the majority
over the business owners, and then it is not a CBD anymore. I would appeal to
the Board to keep the CBD the way that it is and to follow the accessory
apartment usage and see the ability of what Southport has had in the past and
would like very much to continue to have where the shop owner has that right to
live also in a downtown. I also think that articulate professionals are
available and can design for commercial use in the CBD. Thank you”
Ms. Susan Farley of 203 E. Brown Street presented petitions that were signed by
various shop owners in the City. She stated all of them want to see Mrs.
Leggett sell her store because empty businesses are not good for their
business. Their concerns basically follow Mrs. Van Noordt’s theory. They are
not necessarily opposed to mixed use. “I think mix use is wonderful and I think
shop owners living above their stores are wonderful and ideal. I live in one of
the current mix use buildings and the reality of it is all of the residential
is going to be sold before the commercial. As a business owner I am going to
look at that and I’m going to say that without parking provided for those
residents, that’s two cars that is going to sit in front of my store all day.
I’m not going to rent and I’m not going to buy a business in that kind of area.
Therefore I am going to end up with more empty businesses. Then if you end up
with all these cars parked out in front, they are all attached to residences.
You end up with your customer base shrinking. There’s no other way to look at
that. We have all seen what happened to downtown Wilmington. They put in
parking regulations, they did things in parking, and there are constantly
battles between the people that live above with below. The only things that can
survive in that type of area are bars and restaurants. Those are the only
things that have the margin that’s been able to support that and I don’t think
that we want to see downtown ’’Southport’ a row of bars and restaurants. So
those are our main concerns. Now I happen to live in a mixed use building and
we have parking, but I still have a problem. Every week I have people walk in
and say “Susie I drove by but you were full.”
They will come back, because they know I have parking, but I am not sure that
this will happen in the Central Business District and grant it, I am not in the
CBD and you might ask, why do I care, but if Southport starts to die and go on
the down swing, we are all going to be in the same boat, and there are a lot of
towns that are just condominiums but I don’t think that we want that, I don’t
think that’s what we are growing towards, and I don’t think that is what we
need. (Petitions are incorporated as an official part of these minutes)

STORM WATER PROPOSAL
Alderman Powell referenced the workshop that Ms. Jeanette Powell of AMEC
Environmental held on the City’s Storm water Ordinance. Some deficiencies in
the City’s Storm water Ordinance were referenced and should be upgraded. After
the workshop, AMEC Environmentalist Consultant was asked to put together a
proposal to address the areas of concerns so the City can avoid future
problems. He stated some of the areas in the ordinance overlap between the
city, state and federal government and Storm Water is one of the most important
ordinances for the city. The proposal totaled $37,308.
Alderman Adams voiced his support of the Storm water Ordinance and asked that
the new Planner be given the opportunity to review the document for his input
before considering to hire AMEC.
Alderman Powell motioned that the City hire AMEC Environmental to re-write the
City’s Storm water Ordinance at a cost of $37,308.
Alderman Adams again stated Storm water is important, as is traffic but if the
City did not contribute $5,000 to help with a traffic study, he does not want
to spend $37,308 until the Planner has time to review the City’s Ordinance and
make a recommendation.
Alderman Childs asked that the Planner be afforded the opportunity to review
the Ordinance before expending funds and requested the motion be amended to
reflect this.
AMENDMENT: Alderman Powell motioned to hire AMEC Environmental to re-write the
City’s Storm water Ordinance at a cost of $37,308 contingent upon the Planner
reviewing the document and make a recommendation at the December Board meeting.
Discussion: Alderman Fisher recommended the Planner seek grants to cover the
cost of the Storm Water Ordinance modifications. Alderman Powell amended the
motion to ask the Planner to investigate grants to cover the modifications to
the Storm Water Ordinance. Motion seconded by Alderman Callari. No further
discussion, the vote of approval was unanimous.

REGULAR SESSION
In regular session, Mayor Holden called for a vote on Item #5.
City Attorney Isenberg asked that the board defer consideration of this item
until further review by him and Mr. Grant because it appears there may be a
conflict in the UDO where it allows vested rights to last for 2 years for site
specific approval.
Alderman Callari motioned to defer action on the statement “require in planned
building groups and final subdivision plats that construction must begin within
one calendar year following approval of the planned building group by the
Planning Board, and approval of a final subdivision plat by the Board of
Aldermen until further consideration and review by the City Attorney. Motion
seconded by Alderman Childs, vote was unanimous.
Alderman Fisher asked that “construction” be clarified in the definition
section of the UDO. He talked with the building inspector about this and he was
told a building must be started. Alderman Brown and Callari agreed that
construction should be more than clearing a lot.
City Attorney Isenberg stated there are two different issues; planned building
groups refer to buildings and after a final subdivision plat is approved it may
refer to clearing roads and installing infrastructure. Alderman Fisher stated
the Planning Board has been asked to look into this and the surety bond that is
put up for subdivisions, which should be held until complete build out of a
project due to sewer and drainage problems.
Item # 6 – Alderman Fisher motioned to amend the Unified Development Ordinance
Article II, Table of area, yard, density and height requirements as recommended
by the Planning Board. Amendment to building height to change from 40 feet to
35 feet with the following note: “The apex of the main roofline may extend
above 35 feet as long as 2/3 of the roof height falls below 35 feet.” The
motion was seconded by Alderman Brown: Discussion: Alderman Adams referenced
previous discussion where the Board discussed height restrictions not allowing
any construction above 40 ft.
Ms. Susan Toth, member of the Planning Board stated the reason that this matter
was discussed by the Planning Board is because they are trying to maintain the
character of Southport with the variations of rooflines instead of structures
maxing out at 40 ft. The 35 feet height limits allow for structures such as
cupolas and widow walks which will allow variations to rooflines keeping in
with the character of Southport.
Mr. Adams stated his disagreement with the rationale because if a hotel/motel
wants to build in an outlying area, they should not be restricted to 40 feet.
Alderman Adams referenced height restrictions may work in various zoning
districts.
Alderman Callari stated a builder will max out at 35 ft. and if he does go 5 ft
higher it will be for ornamental purposes only.
Mayor Holden called for vote on the motion: Votes were 2 ayes, Aldermen Fisher
and Brown. 4 noes: Aldermen Adams, Childs, Callari and Powell.
Alderman Childs motioned, seconded by Alderman Adams to send back to the
Planning Board for review and recommendation mixed use in CBD and height limit
as a conditional use or possibly in certain zoning districts. The vote of
approval was unanimous.
Item #7 – Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Callari to deny
approval of an amendment to the UDO Article II, Section II-1: Notes to the
table of area, yard, density and height requirements, Note 3. Height
restrictions and modifications as recommended by the Planning Board. Motion
seconded by Alderman Callari, the vote of approval was unanimous.
Item #8 – Alderman Fisher motioned, seconded by Alderman Callari to approve
amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance Article 2, Basic Definition and
Interpretations, Section 2-2: (2) Accessory Apartment to read “a self contained
unit within a new or existing structure for a single family.” The vote of
approval was unanimous.
Item #9 – Alderman Fisher motioned to approve a Conditional Use Permit for
expansion of Kid’s World Learning Center, 713 N. Caswell Avenue for Jock and
Anita Taylor pursuant to the applicant maintaining the legal right to use off
street parking. Motion seconded by Alderman Childs, vote carried.
Item #10 – In response to question from Alderman Childs, Attorney Isenberg
stated the UDO does list as a Conditional Use a residential unit contained
within the principal use within the business district. However, he could not
find a definition in the UDO for a residential unit and does not know how it
would be defined by the Planning Board.
Alderman Childs stated she believed that it was the Board’s intent to make
residential a permitted or a Conditional Use in the Central Business District
when it was developed.
Alderman Brown stated when the UDO was developed; he believed the intent of the
Board was to permit residential use in the CBD. He stated, five years ago he
owned a building downtown and residential use was allowed.
Alderman Childs stated the interpretation given to the Board stated residential
was not a permitted or conditional use in the UDO, however it was discovered
today that residential units are a conditional use in the UDO as listed on page
93 and she sees no reason to change it.
Alderman Adams suggested the Board not rush to action and clarify any
interpretations.
Attorney Isenberg stated it appears it may allow a business owner to have a
residence above their business, but not multiple residences.
Alderman Powell stated a conditional use will need to come before the Board for
a decision on each individual case.
Alderman Fisher recalled that conditional use was put in the UDO because it
already exists in the business district and it was discussed that if something
was demolished and an owner wanted to re-build it would be under a conditional
use. Parking was also a factor during the discussion.
The Board agreed that a more definitive definition of residential unit is
needed. After discussion, there was no formal action, but concurred to send
back to the Planning Board.

DOSHER HOSPITAL PROPOSAL FOR LAND
The Board reviewed the proposal submitted by Dosher Hospital for trade of
property located between the west side of Howe Street and Lord Street for an
equal amount of city owned property located at the corner of Fodale Avenue and

PUBLIC HEARING – ZONING RECLASSIFICATION – (DALE MCPHERSON)
Aldermen Childs motioned to enter Public Hearing on a zoning reclassification
request by Mr. Dale McPherson to rezone 1169, 1175, 1183 and 1191 East Leonard
Street from R-10 (residential) to LI (light industrial). Motion seconded by
Alderman Brown, vote carried.
No comments from the public.
Motion by Alderman Childs to re-enter regular session, seconded by Alderman
Callari, vote carried.
In regular session, Alderman Adams asked if adjoining property owners came to
the Planning Board. Susan Toth stated Mr. McPherson told the Planning Board
that he spoke with the property owners and they were okay with the rezoning.
Mr. McPherson told the Board he had signatures of adjoining property owners.
Alderman Fisher commented that the Planning Board approved the rezoning with a
50 ft. buffer and questioned how the city will insure that this is finite.
David Emilita, Planning Director stated Article 18 of the UDO requires a buffer
where industrial development abuts residential development and in this case it
does on the south side. Section 18-B only requires a minimum 10 ft buffer in
addition to the yard requirement which is less than 50 ft. This then becomes a
matter of being able to condition the zone change with a 50 ft buffer on any
side that abuts residential development, which is within the Board’s power to
effect this change which he would recommend. City Attorney Isenberg stated this
was discussed in the agenda meeting and the rezoning could not be made
conditional on this but the Board could rezone all of the property except for
50 ft.
Alderman Fisher asked about the status of the request to the Planning Board not
to change provisions of the warranty bond acceptance until complete build out
of the project in order to guarantee utilities. Mr. Grant stated that they are
looking into this but may encounter a problem with the state.

            James Powell, Stuart Callari and Paul Fisher

CITIZEN MATTERS
(Non Agenda Items)
Mayor Holden clarified a statement made in a letter to the editor that he read
in the State Port Pilot. Mayor stated he does not have the authority as Mayor
to give the City of Southport away; and if he did, he would have given the
marina to the City of Southport.
The floor was opened for public comments. No citizens to address the Board.
PUBLIC MEETING
Mayor stated that Alderman Adams asked that a public meeting be held to give
citizens an opportunity to express their opinions on the issue of Progress
Energy’s consideration of building an additional nuclear power plant/reactor
possibly at the Brunswick Plant.
Mayor established a time limit of 3 minutes for each speaker.
Mr. Mike McCracken, employee of Progress Energy, Brunswick Plant stated that
Progress Energy is considering numerous sites in the Carolinas and Florida to
build a new reactor. The reason for building a large base load plant is the
need to provide electricity to a growing customer base. The company needs to be
able to provide large amounts of power 24 hours a day 7 days a week. He
communicated that Progress Energy added over 69,000 new customers between the
Carolinas and their Florida operation last year and the projection is an
increase of 600,000 in the next 10 years. Mr. McCracken told the Board since
the 1980’s they have grown by 1 million customers. He explained that nuclear
power has an advantage because it is clean and admit no emissions from burning
fossil fuels and is cost efficient and affordable. Progress Energy is using a
score card to decide where to build the power plant in which technical
consideration, customer concentration, businesses, cost, strategic factors,
environmental impact, socio-economic and community support will be used to
determine the location. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has been informed
that Progress Energy plans to submit a combined construction operating license
as early as 2008, however they will need to announce a location soon as that is
part of the license process. Construction could begin as early as 2010 and on
line by 2016.
Ms. Nancy Harkey, Town of St. James expressed concerns about expanding the
nuclear power plant. She stated she does not understand the evacuation
procedure and asked what triggers the alarm. She stated that nuclear power is
an expensive technology and comes with risks i.e. disposal of spent fuel, the
attraction of terrorists, and referenced damage at Three Mile Island and
Chernobyl. She suggested other measures be explored i.e. windmills being a
technology, jet turbine, hydro-electric. She asked that alternatives be
examined before an expensive catastrophe takes place.
Mayor Holden recommended Ms. Harkey speak with Mayor Lesher about some of her
concerns because she is aware of evacuation procedures.
No further comments from the public, Alderman Callari motioned to close the
public meeting and re-enter regular session. Motion seconded by Alderman
Fisher, the vote carried.
Alderman Adams asked the question “what is the advantage of Southport adopting
a resolution of support?” Mayor stated it is his understanding after discussion
with the Plant Manager, the more support received from citizens and elected
officials, the company would be more inclined to locate in that area.
Mr. McCracken stated as a company they have looked at alternative energy
resources and have come to the conclusion that the only viable way to generate
large amounts of electricity safely and reliable with minimum impact on the
environment is with nuclear power. In answer to Alderman Adams question, Mr.
McCracken stated they will be bringing jobs to the area. They currently employ
1000 people and approximately two-thirds of the workforce is from Brunswick
County.
Alderman Adams asked if the City stands to gain ad valorem taxes, and whether
or not the city can annex the plant if constructed. Mr. McCracken stated their
community involvement, being a good corporate citizen and neighbors add value
to the City.
Alderman Adams asked if Progress Energy is seeking resolutions of support. Mr.
McCracken stated they are not, but there have been resolutions of support from
within the Carolinas and the County of Brunswick. He communicated that other
communities have expressed support to management because they are trying to
attract good clean industry that will provide high paying and reliable jobs. He
explained that production of electricity has to be a local endeavor because it
is a local industry.
Alderman Fisher, a Commissioner on the North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power
Agency (12 years) and recently elected Chairman of 32 cities stated this group
owns 20% of 5 generating plants that are a part of progress energy. Two of the
plants are the Brunswick Plants in which they own approximately 18-20%. The
nuclear plants are the most efficient and generate electricity much cheaper.
NCEMPA gets 50% of electricity from nuclear, 25% from coal, and 25% purchased
on the supplemental market. Alderman Fisher stated when it is purchased on the
market it is more expensive. He stated that nuclear power is the most efficient
and safest. Alderman Fisher then offered a motion that the City of Southport
adopt a resolution supporting the plant because of jobs, taxes and Progress
Energy being a good neighbor with residual benefits, and further request that
one of the plants be constructed at the Brunswick Plant. The motion died for
lack of a second.
Alderman Callari stated she is not against the resolution but believes each
person must make up their own mind and does not believe the city can speak for
everyone in the town.

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been petitioned under G.S. 160A-31 to annex
the area described below; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at Southport City
Hall at 7:30 p.m. on January 12, 2006, after due notice by publication in the
State Port Pilot on December 21st and 28th, 2005, and;
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the petition meets the requirements
of G.S. 160A-31;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, by the Board of Aldermen of Southport, North
Carolina that:
Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-31, the following
described territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City of Southport
effective immediately
EXHIBIT A
From an existing MAG nail at the intersection of Jabbertown Road SR 1526 and
Leonard Street SR 1527 north 74 degrees 05 minutes 44 seconds west 1701.49 feet
to a point on the Northern right of way of Jabbertown Road SR 1526, said point
being the point of beginning. From the beginning point leaving said right of
way, North 07 degrees 05 minutes 26 seconds East 7.09 feet to a point, thence
North 87 degrees 33 minutes 24 west 100.11 feet to a point, said point being a
concrete monument, thence south 07 degrees 39 minutes 12 seconds West 150.60
feet to a point, said point being on the Northern right of way of Jabbertown
Road SR 1526, thence with said right of way South 86 degrees 30 minutes 19
seconds East 51.46 feet to a point, thence continuing with said right of way
South 81 degrees 19 minutes 24 seconds East 49.91 feet to the place and point
of beginning, containing a total of .35 acres more or less.
This being the same property as shown on a plat entitled “Area Annexed by the
City of Southport, NC on January 12, 2006” recorded in Map Cabinet __________
at Page ______ of the Brunswick County Registry.
Section 2. Upon and after January 12, 2006 the above described territory and
its citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be entitled to the same
privileges and benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said territory
shall be subject to municipal taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10.
Section 3.  The Mayor of the City of Southport shall cause to be recorded in
the office of the Register of Deeds of Brunswick County, and in the office of
the Secretary of State at Raleigh, North Carolina, an accurate map of the
annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the County Board
of Elections, as required by G. S. 163-288.1.
ADOPTED, this the 12th day of January 2006.

FUEL ADJUSTMENT CHARGE
Alderman Fisher reported that cities and utilities throughout the southeast
have changed their pricing in fossil fuel and plant costs which has
significantly impacted the North Carolina Easter Municipal Power Agency for
2005. Other increases are projected in 2006. He explained the NCEMPA is seeing
an increase of $16 million above budget costs for 2005, and due to significant
increases in coal cost, natural gas and supplemental energy, and other
operating costs, the projected increase is $31 million for 2006. As stated
earlier, the electricity comes from 50% nuclear which is the cheapest, coal is
25% which doubles the cost of nuclear, and supplemental can triple or
quadruple. (Below is listed the Rate Adjustment Proposal as presented by
Committee) Alderman Fisher outlined the following rate adjustment proposal from
the Committee:
RATE ADJUSTMENT PROPOSAL
1.    Effective on Jan. 1, 2006 the City of Southport received an adjustment of
9.7% on the price of energy purchased from the North Carolina Eastern Municipal
Agency.
a.   A decrease in Southport’s electrical fund revenue of $398,904.00 per year
is projected due to this adjustment.
b.   An average monthly decrease in revenue of $33,242.00 will be seen unless
adjustments are changed.
c.   This adjustment is largely due to the significant increase in the cost of
natural gas and coal.
2.   We are working on ways to reduce our electrical cost such as:
a.   Automatic meter reading could increase the efficiency of our billing
process.
b.   A mechanism to collect back bills is now in place. Customers state income
tax refunds will be collected by the city for back bills.
c.   Further increase emphasis on Load Management program and customer revenue
collection.
d.   Repairing undersized feeders and trimming trees will decrease line loss.
e.   Educate customers on ways to reduce cost by conserving energy. Perform
energy audits to help customers find ways to save.
3.   The City of Southport’s electrical distribution system requires upgrades.
a.   Our substation reached 95% capacity this past summer. There are NEC
concerns that need to be rectified. Rebuilding this facility will cost in the
area of $1,000,000.00 dollars.
b.   Several feeders are undersized and need to be upgraded. Some of these
feeders are being put underground. $ 240,000.00 was budgeted for this project
for 05/06.
4.   The City of Southport absorbed 2% of the last rate adjustment and all of
the previous two adjustments. A proposed energy rider of 0.837 cent per KWH
will be needed to offset the increased energy purchased cost.
a.   This adjustment will produce $398,904.00 per year.
b.   Average household adjustment will be $11.73 dollars per month.
5. Recommended action that Board of Aldermen approves an Energy Cost Adjustment
of 0.837 cents per KWH.
Aldermen Fisher motioned to approve an energy cost adjustment of 0.837 cents
per kilowatt hour. The increase will equate to approximately $12.00 per month
for an average home. Motion seconded by Alderman Powell.  Discussion: Alderman
Adams requested the Board hold a workshop due to questions he needs answered.
He asked that the workshop be scheduled within the next week because he is not
prepared to vote on an increase without discussion. The votes were 3 ayes,
Aldermen Fisher, Callari and Powell, and 3 no votes, Aldermen Adams, Brown and
Childs. Due to a tie vote, Mayor Holden exercised his option and voted no.
Motion failed.
Aldermen Adams motioned to hold a special workshop 6:30 p.m. on January 18,
2006, seconded by Alderman Brown, vote carried.
APPOINTMENTS – PLANNING BOARD
Alderman Childs recommended a Committee be appointed to interview applicants
for the Planning Board due to several people applying. Aldermen Childs, Brown

Board members Callari, Brown and Mayor Holden expressed their gratitude to
citizens for interest shown in the Planning Board and encouraged their

Mayor Holden asked Alderman Childs to schedule the date(s) and inform the
applicants accordingly. Alderman Fisher suggested the Chairman of the Planning
Board and Director be included in the interview process.
RESOLUTION HONORING DR. MARTIN LUTHER KING, JR.
Alderman Childs motioned to adopt the following resolution honoring Dr. Martin
Luther King, Jr., and in support of the celebration scheduled January 15-16.
Motion seconded by Alderman Brown, vote unanimous.
RESOLUTION HONORING DR. MARTIN LUTHER KING JR. CELEBRATION
WHEREAS, the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Committee was formed and
entrusted with the responsibility to plan a community wide celebration to
appropriately honor this great leader; and
WHEREAS, Dr. Martin Luther King Celebration Committee has selected the dates of
Sunday, January 15th and Monday, January 16, 2006 to hold this celebration with
events scheduled to include a march, youth programs and other similar events;
and
WHEREAS,  the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Celebration has established a mission
statement in which its most important goal is to bring people of the community
together for the purpose of promoting good will and harmony for the betterment
of the entire community; and
WHEREAS, it is extremely important that the great works and deeds of Dr. Martin
Luther King, Jr. be duly remembered, honored and recognized in this most
fitting and proper way.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Mayor and Board of Aldermen of
Southport recognizes January 15-16, 2006 as the official dates of celebration
by the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Committee for the purpose of
honoring this great man and encourage all citizens to participate in the
activities scheduled.
THIS 12th day of January 2006.
S/Norman R. Holden, Mayor

POLICE DEPARTMENT – TASER WEAPON
Chief Dove gave the Board a brief over view on the new weapon called a
conductive energy device/Taser which is one of the newest and safest advances
in law enforcement technology in subduing criminals and people who resist
arrest. He explained it been used in situations where deadly force was
authorized. The Wal-Mart Foundation awarded the Southport Police Department a
$1,000 grant to purchase equipment for officer safety. Chief Dove requested
Board approval to purchase 2 Tasers with funds from the Wal-Mart Foundation and
with funds left from their technology program.
Alderman Brown motioned to authorize Chief Dove to expend funds to purchase two
taser weapons and authorized the necessary training for the officers. The
motion was seconded by Alderman Callari, vote carried.

The Board scheduled their annual retreat for Saturday, February 11, 2006, 8:00

OTHER BUSINESS
MARINA COMMITTEE
Alderman Childs reported that the Committee continues to pursue ownership of
the Marina and upon returning from Raleigh (Council of State) they met with the
City Manager and Planning Director to look at the Marina District. She motioned
to hold a Public Hearing February 9, 2006, 7:30 p.m. to discuss changes to the
district. Motion seconded by Alderman Callari, vote carried.
Alderman Childs communicated that the Committee extended the new lessees an
invitation to meet with the Aldermen and community. Mayor Holden suggested a
drop in session and to invite the public. Mayor Holden recommended that
citizens be bussed to the marina via the City Parks and Recreation bus to look
at the proposed plans by the new lessees.
COMMUNITY BUILDING
Alderman Fisher reported that the Committee is working to achieve the goals
assigned by the Board to make the Community Building more accessible and
affordable for all citizens. The Committee recommended a change from $45.00 per
hour for day rate, and $75.00 per hour for the night rate be changed to $100.00
for a four hour block. This amount covers only the expense for the Community
Building and will apply only to non-profit groups Sunday through Thursday. If
more hours are needed, it will cost $20.00 for each additional hour. Alderman
Fisher motioned to approve the new rate schedule. Discussion: Alderman Adams
stated it is his belief that $100 will still serve special interest groups.
Alderman Childs stated she appreciates the rate change and asked the
possibility of entertaining lowering the rates again for local groups, because
she wants it to be a Community Building and affordable for local citizens. The
motion was seconded by Alderman Callari. The votes were 5 ayes, Aldermen
Childs, Fisher, Brown, Callari and Powell. 1 no vote, Alderman Adams.
PARKING COMMITTEE
Alderman Fisher stated the Parking Committee will present a proposal for Board
consideration at the February Board meeting for a Parking Study to be performed
by a Parking Management Firm. The Committee met with a consultant and realizes
the parking in Southport is beyond their capability and comprehension.
NAVASSA MAYOR
Mayor Holden recognized Eulis Willis, Mayor of Navassa and welcomed him to
Southport.
STATE PORT – STATEMENT BY MAYOR
The following statement was read by Mayor Holden:
STATEMENT
“With the announcement of the newly planned international port, the
responsibilities of the Board of Aldermen have increased considerably. The
impact over time of this complex just a few miles from out town certainly makes
our planning, zoning and other activities even more important.
Ensuring the vitality of Southport while maintaining a balance between the
known and unknown during the build up stage of the port will be of immense
importance and we will need to protect the uniqueness, charm, friendliness of
our community and our way of life, which is even now changing daily.
I will be appointing a Committee of Aldermen and citizens to work with me to
address the issues that confront us as we move through this time in our lives.
Also I would like to recommend that the new port facilities take into
consideration, if in fact they build the port to utilize the Southport
electrical service. I would like the Board of Aldermen to work with me and take
the lead for the City of Southport and for Brunswick County from this point on.
Thank you.”
ADJOURNMENT
No further business, the meeting was adjourned upon motion of Alderman Childs,
seconded by Alderman Brown, vote carried.

A special meeting notice was duly posted in accordance with NCGS 143-318.12 for
the purpose of discussing the proposed energy cost adjustment of 0.837 cents
per KWH. The rate adjustment increase is needed because on January 1, 2006, the
City of Southport received an adjustment increase of 9.7% on the price of
energy purchased from the N. C. Eastern Municipal Agency which is due because
of increased cost in natural gas and fuel. The city absorbed 2% of the last
rate increase and the previous two.

ITEM 8.
SOUTHPORT PARKING STUDY (Parking Committee)
Alderman Fisher stated that the Parking Committee has met for years to
determine ways to resolve some of the parking problems within the city, however
the problem is beyond their capabilities and the Committee recommends that the
Board hire a professional parking consultant at a cost of $2500 to develop a
Parking Study. (Steve Hernandez was present to answer questions) Since there
were no questions, Alderman Fisher motioned to hire Lanier Parking Systems to
perform the parking study for the City at a cost of $2500. Motion seconded by
Alderman Callari, vote of approval was unanimous.
ITEM 9.
ELECTRIC RATE ADJUSTMENT
Alderman Fisher stated the Board delayed an energy rider in January on the
electric bills which was passed onto the City from the power agency. The City
lost between $34,000-40,000 because the energy rider was not implemented.
Alderman Fisher stated after talking with Board members, it was determined that
a special meeting is not necessary because the city can not afford to lose
$398,000 this year on over charges and electricity. Alderman Fisher then
motioned to approve an energy cost adjustment of .0837 per kwh which will
equate to approximately $11.71 per month for the average customer effective
February. Motion seconded by Alderman Callari, the vote was unanimous.
ITEM. 10
EAST LEONARD STREET SANITARY SEWER LIFT STATION
Mr. Grant, Public Services Director stated that South Star Development Company
requested the City accept dedication of the East Leonard Street Sanitary Sewer
Lift Station for operation and maintenance. He stated the system has been in
operation for 5 months and monitored by staff. It currently serves Carillon
Assisted Care Development and will eventually serve the Cottages at Prices
Creek and Turtlewood Development. He recommended acceptance subject to a one
year warranty bond representing 10% of the original construction costs to cover
potential defects in workmanship and materials. Upon review and approval of the
bond, the deed will be recorded. (Bond will be in City’s hand by the week of
January 13)
Alderman Powell motioned to accept dedication of the wastewater system subject
to 10% warranty bond being submitted, motion seconded by Alderman Fisher, vote
was unanimous.
ITEM 11.
MIKE PETKAUSKOS – RIGHT OF WAY
The Board acknowledged a request by Mike Petkauskos to improve certain right of
way in the City. Mr. Emilita, Planning Director, stated during review of the
site plan by the Review Committee there were some concerns over emergency
access to the rear of the building. If the City alley way is opened, this would
provide emergency access to the rear of the building and adjacent properties.
Mr. Petkauskos agreed at his expense to open up the right of way from his
property to the city’s parking area to provide a secondary access. Board
approval will be needed to allow Mr. Petkauskos to remove obstructions from the
right of way during construction and a procedure in place that will allow other
owners to remove structures from the city’s right of way. (Note: Alley
referenced is between Atlantic Avenue and Howe behind Ocean Outfitters)
Mayor stated this will be beneficial to the City as well as Mr. Petkauskos
which will make the parking area accessible. Alderman Fisher stated the Parking
Committee has been working on opening up this alley for months which has been a
complicated process. He stated the survey is completed and recommended this
area be included in the parking study. Alderman Fisher moved that the area
referenced above be included in the parking study to be performed by Lanier
Parking Consultants Study. Motion seconded by Alderman Callari, vote was
unanimous.
Mr. Franks stated if alley is opened in one area, then others will be opened.
He stated he lives in this area and was not contacted concerning this proposal.
Mayor stated the City needs to eventually look at the alleys and make a
decision to possibly consider giving alleys to the adjoining property owners.
Alderman Adams stated he is against giving city alleys or city right of ways to
property owners. He stated t city property should remain city property.

ITEM 14.
OTHER BUSINESS
City Manager Gandy stated one week ago, the City had a brown out due to a
problem with a transmission line coming in from Progress Energy. The city
terminated its sub-station so it would not cause major problems within the
city. He explained that this same situation occurred approximately four months
ago on the same day. The transmission line needs to be looked at and possibly
replaced. The city pays a lease facility charge on the line and sub-station to
Progress Energy which averages $9700 per month. He has been in communication
with representatives from Progress Energy and a meeting has been scheduled to
discuss improvements to the line.

proposed plans to the city. (Schematic on file in City Manager’s office)

review of the Storm Water Ordinance he will draft amendment language change to
the Storm Water Ordinance, which will be submitted to members of the Committee,
the Board of Aldermen and Planning Board. These changes will be presented at
the April Board meeting.

outstanding job cleaning Smithville and Northwood Cemeteries, and the Salt
Marsh Board Walk and Waterway Overview. He motioned that a letter of

vote carried.

Mayor Holden called the meeting to order.
1.
Presentation by Brunswick Electric Membership Corporation representatives on
description of basic and non-basic O&M contract, work plan, systems upgrade and
contract price proposal.
·   Mr. Chip Leavitt and Don Hughes presented a power point presentation on
Southport’s electrical system from the point of beginning when BEMC entered
into contract in 2001 to present.
·   Meters were discussed and Mr. Leavitt explained the types of meters i.e.
water and automated electrical meters which he stated works well with the scada
system. He stated electrical system meters are available now and it will be
2007 before water meters are available. Update on invoices and work order
procedures, some changes made and at present is working well for City and BEMC.
·   Solar street lighting at this point not promising due to cost. Will
continue to monitor this.
·   Decorative materials around pad mounted transformers. Need clearance for
access and signage visible, if shrubs are planted they tend to over grow and
cover the warning labels. Alderman Childs asked about fences. Will work on
this.
·   Future research on green power initiatives. Mr. Leavitt stated will work
with City on initiatives, some grants are available. City Manager stated staff
will continue to work with BEMC officials to develop a program for green power
initiatives.
·   Mr. Don Hughes stated Southport provides electricity to approximately 2400
customers. It is their goal to continue providing services to improve and
enhance Southport’s electrical system i.e. upgrades to automated meters,
underground service, experienced technical personnel, 24 hour call system,
scada system, GIS engineering staff for design and planning.
·    A new substation for Southport is needed because the current substation is
below standards and is hazardous. Estimated cost of a new-substation is $1.1
million. Mr. Hughes stated it is more cost effective to locate new sub-station
in same area because of the need to provide power while new sub-station is
being constructed. Mayor Holden asked Mr. Hughes if BEMC would be willing to
contribute monies towards a new sub station.
·   City Manager agreed with BEMC officials that the sub-station has almost
reached capacity and safety is a concern.
·   Board discussed underground utilities and assessing customers. Alderman
Fisher suggested installing underground in phases and calculate the number of
customers in each phase and assess accordingly. Mr. Hughes stated that once the
Board decides what phase and where they want to begin; they will calculate the
cost and proceed from that angle. They are presently working on a contract with
Time Warner Cable.
·   Mr. Leavitt discussed the company’s operation and maintenance contract. He
stated the company has sustained financial loss since 2001 and will propose a
rate increase in their new contract negotiations with the city.
2.
W. K. Dickson, Carter Hubard, Regional Waste Water System
Mr. Hubard in power point presentation outlined the company’s success in
working with the city on the waste water system. He presented a schematic
delineating ETJ line and the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District boundary,
City’s treatment plant, new pump station for Phase I and the District Treatment
Plant. Schematic showed piping routes to get from Southport with the flow and
how pipes will be installed. Continuing to reduce the inflow and infiltration,
pursuing and obtaining funds for capital expenditures, completion of
transmission mains to district, completion of the Southeast Brunswick
expansion, completion of the transmission mains to the reuse site are projects
that will enable the decommissioning of the existing city wastewater treatment
plant. (The South Brunswick Sanitary District will be the treatment plant for
the city’s wastewater.) City Manager stated city is ahead of anticipated
schedule.
3.
Public Services Director-Bob Grant
Mr. Grant presented a twelve month overview of departmental work plans and
accomplishments: Grant from CWMTF in amount of $1,686,000 for acquisition of WW
Effluent Spray Field, Phase I Wastewater Enhancement Project underway which
allows 200 gallons of flow reversal to Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District
which is scheduled for completion by late spring, water line replacement on
Lord, Caswell, Brunswick, and portion of Nash Streets, which electrical
conduits where installed for future underground installations. Completion of
211 interconnect to county water main to enhance water pressure; continued
SCADA system refinement to allow for enhanced remote monitoring of utility
system from the utility office or wastewater plant which has been very
beneficial, installed variable frequency drives at COS WWTP, replaced and/or
installed valves for Water System to allow for improved isolation and fewer
water service interruptions, rehabilitation/pressure wash cleaning of salt
marsh walkway/gazebo, installed concrete median on South Lord Street between W.
Bay and W. Moore, rehabilitation of Franklin Park Gazebo and Well House Sites,
I & I repairs, River Drive, Stuart and Leonard, Harbor Oaks, resurfaced East
11th Street, paved Cottage Lane and resurfaced section of Owens Street,
rehabilitation and cleaning of tank interior, spartina planted at foreshore of
shoreline sill stabilization area at Kingsley Park, coordinated electric
facility upgrades in downtown area for July 4 festivities, underground electric
installed W. Bay, South and North Lord Streets and a portion of Nash, 900,000
lbs of debris remove from streets during hurricane Ophelia response and
recovery efforts, replacement of Indigo and River Drive lift station generators
and trimmings of electric system coordinated with BEMC. Mr. Grant outlined work
plan for fiscal year 2006/07. (Reference material on file in Clerk’s office)
Discussed wastewater package plants, standard manual for developers, electric
system upgrades, continuing underground installation, prioritizing and
replacing supplemental equipment, once the wastewater flow is reversed, the
City will need to look at paying for treatment, possibly sewer rate increases
incrementally. Alderman Brown recommended looking at this during budget
preparation. Alderman Fisher talked about a Capital Improvement Program being
in place to replace equipment. Mandatory hook-up for underground installation
was discussed in order for it to be effected properly. Alderman Brow agreed
that some form of assessment program may be needed in order to make it
affordable.
4.
Fire Department – Chief Greg Cumbee
Chief Cumbee gave the Board an overview of the Southport Fire Department i.e.
number of certified hours of training grant awards for fire prevention,
hydrants painted, meetings and exceeding ISO and OSHA standards. Update on
equipment status, (report given to each board member and on file in Clerk’s
office). Chief stated the Fire Department has the money to move ahead on land
purchase, they have outgrown the building which is inadequate. Goals are to
purchase land this year (2006), retain an architect, submit architectural plans
for new facility and begin construction by 2007. Estimated cost of facility is
$1.5 - $2 million. Many departments are transitioning to compensating
firefighters, and this will need to be looked at in the future. Thus far
retention of volunteers is good. Chief Cumbee stated as a result of growth, the
fire department is not in alignment because of inadequate facilities and the
continual need to upgrade equipment. During discussion, general consensus is
the facility is needed. Alderman Brown gave a brief synopsis of article read
about the growth and the impact to this area.
Mayor Holden stated the facility is needed and the need to move ahead with this
project. Alderman Fisher explained that the City has been negotiating with the
hospital for property, and part of the lot is essential to the fire department.
If the city takes out 150 ft sq for a new sub-station, offer the hospital the
remainder. If the hospital moves the building the negotiated cost was $150,000
but they may accept $75,000. The building was considered with the land
purchase. City had an environmental assessment performed before negotiations
continued. Board agreed the city needs to proceed with negotiations and
determine how much land will be left to offer the hospital. Mayor asked that
the City Manager get with BEMC to determine the exact amount of property needed
for a sub-station. Mayor asked Alderman Fisher to speak with officials of the
hospital to determine amount of land needed and re-negotiate. Board concurred
if exceptions need to be made for height restrictions; they are willing to do
so.
5.
Rescue Squad – Tammie Drew, Chief
Chief Drew reported on 2005 accomplishments: Squad answered 524 calls in 2005,
compensation, increased responses, received matching grant, started AED program
in all city owned building. Discussion on training staff to use AED, Chief Drew
will provide training on the AED for city employees, county funding increased
as a result of increased responses, billing program initiated, painted
building, replaced carpet, updated training records to be in compliance with
County Emergency Services and the State, enacted new policies and procedures to
protect the squad and the City from liability. 2006 goals are to increase
membership, recruitment program, rescue technical training, MR& EMT classes,
incentive for volunteers. Water Rescue: Squad has no need for boat and truck,
will work with county and coast guard for water rescue. Board unanimously
agreed to decommission the water rescue operation and transfer ownership of the
truck that was used to tow the Boat to the Police Department. Chief stated the
need for washer and dryer to wash contaminated uniforms. This will bring them
in compliance with OSHA regulations. Heating unit inoperable, City Manager
asked Chief to seek bids for new unit.
Board recommended line of communication be opened up to bring in volunteers
from St. James. Mayor stated if need be he will present a letter to Mayor
Lesher.
6.
Police Department – Chief, J. V. Dove
Chief Dove outlined Police Department’s goals and accomplishments:
Extended hours of operation 7 days a week from 8:30 a.m. to 12 midnight.,
Detective/Investigative position reinstated, Chaplaincy Victim Advocate program
incorporated as a part of Southport Safe Neighborhoods Program, computer
technology resources improved, 2 new radars, new shotguns given to the Police
Department by Progress Energy, grant received to purchase 2 tasers, grant
received to purchase ballistic vests, Lt. Laughren the In Service Training
Coordinator, fleet of vehicles upgrade by the purchase of 4 at a reduced cost,
3 officers have advanced certification and 2 currently have 4 year degrees, one
has a 2 year degree. 2006 goals are to seek funding from private sector for
Police K-9, develop new policy and procedure manual, field training officer,
expand department by 2 additional officers.

Parks and Recreation – Heather Hemphill
Ms. Hemphill reported on departmental activities i.e. A total of 3700

Major development anticipated is the Lowe-White Park. Based on survey, tennis
courts and playground area was preference to include a bike ramp. Alderman

updated property survey of the Lowe-White Park. Board agreed that the entire
area be cleaned up and the dump area be moved.
Alderman Fisher informed the Board the last conversation with Mr. Hyson is the
ball fields will remain intact for this summer and after this summer; the city

size swimming pool and a new club house as proposed by Mr. Hyson. The City has

City Manager and Ms. Hemphill explained that the stage at Caviness Park is in

Ms. Hemphill asked for part time help to help maintain the parks. (March-

Goals: Obtain Stevens Park, Lowe-White Park, air conditioning in gym, replacing

Park) bike paths to connect through city, employee wellness program.
Mayor recommended Manager contact Supervisor of Elections since they use the

City Manager authorized director to proceed with replacing the sinks in the
gym.

Retreat Minutes
 
Board of Aldermen
Retreat Minutes   February 11, 2006
 
Chief Cumbee reviewed with the Board the condition of the equipment and fire
trucks. Bids will be submitted to replace the 1973 model which will be placed
in reserve.
Mayor Holden referenced the 1964 pumper truck and stated the possibility of
donating it for a tax write off. Chief stated with the condition of the truck,
he does not believe they can sell it. Alderman Childs referenced the fire truck
in town that belongs to an individual that is being driven around. Chief Cumbee
stated it is wrong for individuals to purchase fire trucks and joy ride around
town drinking. He stated every time this happens, he receive telephone calls
from people accusing the Southport Fire of this. The truck looks identical to
the Fire Departments with red lights. He stated he cannot say that it is
illegal, but does not believe that this should be allowed. The Board concurred
with Chief Cumbee. Chief stated he does not believe too many individuals would
want to buy the truck and spend the money to keep it up. They can not find
parts for the truck nor afford them. Mayor asked if any other departments would
be interested in acquiring the truck, perhaps some in the State of Florida.
Chief stated in the past, trucks have been sent to South America. He asked
representatives from E-1 if they knew of a department that would be interested
in the truck to let him know.

ITEM 6.
Resolution supporting continued maintenance of the Atlantic Intracoastal
Waterway, shallow draft inlets and inlet crossings by the U.S. Army Corps of
Engineers.
Alderman Fisher moved to approve the resolution, seconded by Alderman Brown,
and the vote of approval was unanimous.
RESOLUTION SUPPORTING CONTINUED MAINTENANCE OF THE ATLANTIC INTRACOASTAL
WATERWAY, SHALLOW DRAFT INLETS AND INLET CROSSINGS BY THE U.S. ARMY CORPS OF
ENGINEERS
WHEREAS,  the US Army Corps of Engineers has historically maintained the
Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway, 5 shallow-draft inlets and 8 inlet crossings in
North Carolina at an adequate depth for commercial and recreational navigation
purposes; and
WHEREAS, the continued maintenance of these navigable waterways is essential to
the State of North Carolina’s commercial barge traffic, commercial fishing
industry, tourism industry, and quality of life of its residents, property
owners, and visitors; and
WHEREAS,  the approved Federal budget for FY 05-06 does not include sufficient
funding to maintain these crucial waterways at an adequate depth, with only
minimal funding made available that will not realistically begin to meet the
needs that exist; and
WHEREAS, continued neglect of these waterways will only result in further
shoaling and reduced navigability, thereby negatively impacting the companies
that rely on the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway for cost-effective
transportation of goods and materials, the many commercial fishermen who depend
on the navigability of these waterways to reach the open ocean, the thousands
of recreational boaters who contribute to the State’s vibrant tourism economy,
and local residents whose quality of life is greatly enhanced by the
navigability of these waterways; and
WHEREAS, the continue maintenance of these navigable waterways is essential for
protecting the safety of commercial and recreational boaters, and also enables
the US Coast Guard to continue to fulfill its mission of patrolling America’s
coasts, enforcing safe boating regulations, and performing emergency rescue
operations.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
urges the President and the United States Congress to recognize the immense
economic, safety, and quality of life benefits associated with maintenance of
these waterways, and urges them to appropriate sufficient funds in the FY 06-07
Federal budget and beyond to continue maintenance of the Atlantic Intracoastal
Waterway, shallow-draft inlets and inlet crossings by the US Army Corps of
Engineers.
Duly adopted this the 9th Day of March, 2006.
S/Norman R. Holden
Mayor
Attest:
S/Regina W. Alexander, CMC
City Clerk

Resolution extending the current contract between the City of Southport and

fiscal year including the increased contract fee for May and June 2006.
Alderman Fisher moved seconded by Alderman Callari to approve the resolution
extending the current contract with Brunswick Electric Membership Cooperative
including the increased contract fee for May and June 2006. The vote of

RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, the City of Southport entered into a five year contract with Brunswick
Electric Membership Corporation for operation and maintenance of the city’s
electrical system on April 19, 2001; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport is currently in the process of renegotiating
this contract for another five year term; and
WHEREAS, it is the desire of the City of Southport to have the inception date
of the new contract coincide with the start of our new fiscal year July 1,
2006; and
WHEREAS, in order to do so, it is necessary to extend the current contract
through June 30, 2006, which has been agreed upon by Brunswick Electric
Membership Cooperative.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport
that the current contract with Brunswick Electric Membership Cooperative be
extended through June 30, 2006 under the terms and conditions currently
existing except that the monthly fee payable to Brunswick Electric Membership
Cooperative shall be increased to $23,335.50 for the months of May and June,
2006.

ITEM 11.
Proclamation declaring March 17, 2006 as “Arbor Day” in the City of Southport
Alderman Childs moved that the following proclamation be approved declaring
March 17, 2006 as Arbor Day in the City, seconded by alderman Callari, vote of
approval was unanimous.
CELEBRATE ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/
IMAGES/0-0-0-46.jpg]
WHEREAS, in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of
Agriculture that a special day be set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS, this holiday called Arbor Day , was first observed with the planting
of more than a million trees in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS, Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS, trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and
water, cut heating and cooling costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air,
produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for wildlife, and
WHEREAS, trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes,
fuel for our fires, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic
vitality of business areas, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual
renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE,  I Norman R. Holden, Mayor of the City of Southport, N.C. do
hereby proclaim March 17, 2006 as ARBOR DAY in the City and urge all citizens
to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees and woodlands, and
 
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote
the well being of this and future generations.
DATED,  this 9th day of March, 2006.
S/Norman R. Holden, Mayor
ITEM 12.
Proclamation declaring the week of March 13-17 as “Multiple Sclerosis Awareness
Week”
Alderman Powell moved to adopt a Proclamation declaring the week of March 13-17
as Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Week in the City of Southport, seconded by
Alderman Childs, vote of approval was unanimous.
PROCLAMATION
MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AWARENESS WEEK
WHEREAS, MS is a chronic and disabling disease of the central nervous system in
which in progression, severity and specific symptoms cannot be foreseen; and
WHEREAS, every hour of every day someone new is diagnosed with MS, a disease
that can erode a person’s abilities and hopes, halt a career and unravel the
fabric of families; and
WHEREAS, last year in North Carolina more than $8.5 million was raised to find
a cure for MS and develop effective treatments for the disease, as well as
providing a wide range of client programs to improve the lives of the ten
thousand individuals living with MS in our state; and
WHEREAS, according to the National MS Society, $6.3 million has been granted to
North Carolina’s universities over the last fifteen years to find a cure for
MS; and
WHEREAS, this investment is paying off in significant advances in treating MS,
such as new medications which may reduce or delay future disability for people
with MS; and
WHEREAS, research advances have brought us closer to finding the cure, much
remains to be done, and services must continue to be provided to those who live
with the disease; and
WHEREAS, there are public and private agencies available to serve the
constantly changing needs of those with MS and their families living in North
Carolina by extending essential services to all who need them.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that they hereby proclaim March 13-17, 2006 as “MULIPLE SCLEROSIS
AWARENESS WEEK” in the City of Southport, and commend this observance to all
our citizens.
S/Norman R. Holden, Mayor

S/Regina W. Alexander, CMC

Budget Amendment #14

N. C. EASTERN MUNICIPAL POWER ASSOCIATION
Alderman Fisher informed the Board that he was in Washington, D. C. the week of
February 28 thru March 2 representing the N.C. Eastern Municipal Power Agency
at the American Public Power Association meeting. During this time he met with
the North Carolina members of congress. He explained that twelve resolutions
were approved by the Public Power Association for submission to congress. Two
of the resolutions he found most interesting were “Cold ironing” which is
dockside power vs. ship power which should be a service of the new
international port. Second: Plug in hybrid electric vehicles. He asked the
parking consultants to include this in their study for review. Alderman Fisher
stated that he met with eight members of the House including Senator Burr and
Senator Dole’s staff. Four topics briefed for the Power Agency were economic
development, captive rail shipping, telecommunications, and low income home
energy assistance. Yucca Mountains were discussed at the Senate. During the
meeting with Congressman McIntyre, Senator Burr and Senator Dole’s staff, he
discussed the city’s wastewater and electric programs with his pitch being
proactive not reactive federal grants. He stated that he and the City Manager
will be preparing follow up correspondence to submit.

ITEM #5
Mayor asked the Board’s position on Article 24, Storm Water Discharge Control
Ordinance. Discussion: Attorney Isenberg stated in reviewing the changes he
noted some misspellings and asked that they be incorporated.
Alderman Powell moved to approve the Southport Unified Development Ordinance,
Article 24, Storm Water Discharge Control Ordinance and incorporate the changes
noted by Attorney Isenberg. The motion was seconded by Alderman Callari, the
vote was unanimous. (Changes incorporated as recommended)
1.    Redevelopment of Existing Properties:
The wording in Section 24-2 (B) in the second sentence is amended to read
(addition here underlined):
In addition, storm water discharge control measures shall be provided to limit
the 25-year developed peak discharge rates to existing peak discharge rates for
unimproved land (land not having been improved) such as pasture, grassland,
meadow, brush, secondary (old field) growth or forest. Improved property
(property that has the soil surface exposed or a disturbance to the vegetative
cover or topography) that is proposed for redevelopment, whether or not to be
paved, containing or to contain structures, or be regraded, shall include storm
water discharge control measures to limit the two-year, ten-year and 25-year
design storm discharge rates from exceeding that amount discharged in an
unimproved state. For the purposes of this Ordinance, the design storm is the
storm of 3-hour duration as shown on Chart E-6 in the City of Southport Storm
water Management Plan Technical Manual.  
2.    Illegal Discharges:  A new paragraph (F) is to be added to Section 24-
1 to read as follows:
(F)   Illegal Discharges. No person shall cause or allow the discharge,
emission, disposal, pouring or pumping directly or indirectly to any storm
water conveyance, the waters of the State or upon the land in manner and amount
that the substance is likely to reach a storm water conveyance or the waters of
the State or, any liquid, solid, gas, or other substance, other than storm
water; provided that non-storm water discharges associated with following
activities are allowed on the condition that they do not contain potential
pollutants, create erosion, cause sedimentation or impact the existing water
quality of the conveyance or of the waters of the State:
(1)   Potable water line flushing,
(2)   Landscape irrigation and lawn watering;
(3)   Uncontaminated pumped groundwater (not including construction
dewatering);
(4)   Diverted stream flows;
(5)   Naturally rising groundwater and springs;
(6)   Discharges from potable water sources;
(7)   Air conditioning condensation;
(8)   Uncontaminated foundation and footing drains;
(9)   Uncontaminated water from crawl space pumps;
(10)   Flows from riparian habitats and wetlands;
(11)   Dechlorinated (less than 1 ppm total chlorine) swimming pool discharges;
(12)   Street wash waters;
(13)   Flows from fire-fighting;
(14)   Other non-storm water discharges for which a valid NPDES discharge
permit has been approved and issued by the State of North Carolina, provided
that any such discharges to the municipal waste water system shall be
authorized by the City of Southport.
Discharges of hazardous materials released, or having the potential to reach a
storm water conveyance system, shall be contained, controlled, collected and
properly disposed. All affected areas shall be restored to their condition pre-
existing the discharge event.
Persons in control of the hazardous materials immediately prior to their
release or discharge, and persons owning the property on which the materials
were released or discharged, shall immediately notify the City Fire Chief of
the release or discharge, as well as making any required notifications under
State and federal law. Notification shall not relieve any person of any
expenses related to the restoration, loss, damage, or any other liability which
may be incurred as a result of said release, nor shall such notification
relieve any person from other liability which may imposed by State or federal
law.
3.   Illicit Connections: A new paragraph (G) is to be added to section 24-1 
(G) Illicit Connections.
(1)   Any drain or conveyance, whether surface or subsurface, which allows an
illegal discharge to enter the storm water conveyance system, is unlawful.
Prohibited connections include, but are not limited to, any conveyances which
allow any storm water discharge containing sewage, process waste water,
commercial washing machine wastewater including commercial vehicle washing, to
enter the storm water conveyance system. Any connection thereto from indoor
drains and sinks, regardless of whether said drain or connection had been
previously allowed, permitted, or approved by a governmental agency is
prohibited. Any drain or conveyance from a commercial, residential or
industrial land use to the storm water conveyance system which has not been
documented in plans, maps or equivalent records and approved by the City is
prohibited. The construction, use, maintenance or continued existence of
illicit connections to the storm water conveyance system is prohibited.
(1)   Where such connections exist in violation of this section and said
connections were made prior to the adoption of this provision or any other
ordinance prohibiting such connections, the property owner or the person using
said connection shall remove the connection within one (1) year following the
effective date of this ordinance. However, the one (1) year grace period shall
not apply to connections which may result in the discharge of hazardous
materials or other discharges which may pose an immediate threat to health and
safety, or are likely to result in an immediate injury and harm real or
personal property, natural resources, wildlife, or habitat.
(2)   Where it is determined that said connection:
a.   May result in the discharge of hazardous materials, or may pose an
immediate threat to health and safety, or is likely to result in immediate
injury and harm to real and personal property, natural resources, wildlife, or
habitat, or
b.   Was made in violation of any applicable regulation or ordinance other than
this Article, the Public Services Director shall designate the time within
which the connection shall be removed. In setting the time limit for
compliance, the
i.   The quantity and complexity of the work,
ii.   The consequences of delay
iii.   The potential harm to the environment, to the public health and to
public and private property, and
iv.   The cost of remedying the damage.
4.   Post-Construction Maintenance or Warranty Bonds:
A new Section 24-10 is to be added to read as follows:
Section 24-10: Post-Construction Maintenance/Warranty Bond
At the time of the release of the performance bond, a maintenance bond shall be
furnished to the City to guarantee upkeep and the workmanship and materials of
all required storm water management improvements proposed to be dedicated to
the City for a period of one (1) year from the date of the release of the
performance bond/security. The amount of the maintenance bond shall be twenty
(20) percent of the equivalent amount of the performance bond. Thirty (30) days
prior to the end of the one (1) year warranty period, the applicant shall
request in writing to the City Administrator, for an inspection by the Public
Services Director to determine the need for any repair or maintenance work to
be accomplished before the release of the maintenance bond. Following the
inspection, the applicant shall accomplish all required repairs and maintenance
to the satisfaction of the Public Services Director prior to the release of the
bond. If the applicant does not perform said maintenance and repairs, the City
shall declare the bond in default and perform said repairs with the funds of
the maintenance bond.
5.   Upstream Watershed Drainage: A new subsection (6) is to be added to
Section 24-2 (C) to read as follows:
(6)   The post-development discharge for the two-year, ten-year and 25-year
design storm shall not exceed pre-development discharge including runoff from
all upstream flows entering the site under existing conditions.
6.   Language and Ambiguities and Conflicts:
The Ordinance contains four areas of language ambiguity which can cause
conflicting interpretations regarding applicability.
Existing Section 24-1 (C) (3) is to be deleted and replaced by the following :
(3) Residential development of a single family dwelling or a duplex on a single
existing lot, provided that the lot is not part of a larger common development
plan.
Existing Section 24-2 (H) (5) is to be deleted in its entirety, and Section 24-
3(B) (2) is rewritten as follows by adding the wording here underlined to
paragraph (2):
If a responsible party fails or refuses to meet the requirements of the
maintenance covenant, the City, after reasonable notice, may correct a
violation of the design standards or the maintenance needs by performing all
necessary work to place the facility in proper working condition. (The
remainder of paragraph (2) to read as is)
Section 24-7 is to be deleted and replaced with the following wording:
Section 24-7: Retention Pond or Subsurface Facility Requirements
Within areas zoned for commercial, industrial or multifamily uses (CBD, BD, HC,
LI, HI, MF, PUD, and O/I0, retention pond facilities or subsurface drainage
facilities shall be required as follows:
1.   For all development which exceeds forty percent (40%) impervious surface
coverage on a parcel or tract of land whose land area is less than one (1) acre
in size.
2.   For all development which exceeds twenty-five percent (25%) impervious
surface coverage on parcels or tracts of land whose land area is one (1) acre
or more in size.
NOTE: The designed should refer to the NC Department of Environment and Natural
Resources, Erosion and Sediment Control Planning and Design Manual for
supplemental information.
7.   Penalties:  Section 24-4 (E) is to be deleted and replaced with the
following:
Penalties. The penalties for violations of this Article shall be as follows,
the dollar amount penalties contained in Section 7-4 notwithstanding.
(1)   Civil penalties imposed for illegal discharge shall be as follows:
a.   First time offenders will be assessed a civil penalty of one hundred
dollars ($100.00) per violation or per day for a continuing violation if the
quantity of the discharge is less than or equal to five (5) gallons and
consists of domestic or household products. If the quantity of the discharge is
greater than five (5) gallons or contains non-domestic substances, the
offending party shall be assessed a civil penalty of one thousand dollars
($1000.00) per violation or per day for a continuing violation.
b.   Penalties imposed upon repeat offenders willfully committing violations
which are identical or substantially similar to previous violations shall be
double the amount assessed for the prior violation or per day for a continuing
violation, but shall in no event exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) per
violation or per day for a continuing violation.
(2)   All other acts or conditions constituting a violation of this Article
shall subject the offender to a civil penalty of five hundred dollars ($500.00)
per violation or per day for any continuing violation.

2.    Amend Definition (210) OSR (Open Space Ratio)
“(210) OSR (Open Space Ratio). The ratio of all open space as defined in
Definition (209) Open Space, contained in an application for approval to the
total development project area included in the application, expressed as a
percent. For the purposes of calculating the ratio, wetlands, as defined by
CAMA and/or the US Army Corps of Engineers, and water bodies, sediment and
detention basins and storm water retention ponds shall qualify for no more than
fifty (50) percent of the minimum open space requirements of this ordinance as
determined by this calculation.”
