“(147a) Impervious Surface Ratio. The ratio of the total area of impervious
surface as defined in Definition (147) Impervious Surface, in an application
for approval to the total area within the development project property
boundary, expressed as a percent.”
ITEM #7
Attorney Isenberg stated after review with City Staff, some procedural changes
were noted and asked that they be incorporated. Discussion: Alderman Fisher
suggested development plans be completed before submission to the Board and
recommended plans be stamped with approval date. Mr. Emilita explained that it
has been discussed that when a development plan has been voted on for approval,
the plan will be stamped with the approval date, resolution and title of plan
so it will be conclusive as to what plan has been approved in the minutes and
paper documents reflect that approval accordingly. Mr. Emilita stated if this
procedure is adopted, development plans will not be presented to the Board
unless it is deemed completed by staff.
Alderman Childs moved to approve the application review procedure to be
incorporated into the Unified Development Ordinance. The motion was seconded by
Alderman Fisher, the vote was unanimous.
1.   Article 12, Section 12-5 Application Review Procedure
Paragraphs (A) and (B) are to be deleted and replaced by the following
paragraphs.
“(A) Prior to the filing of an application requiring the approval of the
Planning Board and/or the Board of Aldermen, the applicant shall submit to the
Administrator a sketch or preliminary design plan for the proposal. Four (4)
copies of all materials containing the information required by the pertinent
section of the UDO shall be submitted. The Administrator, together with City
staff shall have thirty (30) days in which to determine the completeness of the
submission. It is the intent during this period to outline significant issues
such as access, layout, development constraints, availability of and proximity
to utilities, environmental impacts and/or pertinent zoning regulations.
Missing or incomplete information is to be supplied by the applicant during
this period. The Administrator may extend this period to allow the applicant to
complete the application, and staff to review the material submitted. Upon
determination of completeness, the application will then be placed on the next
available Planning Board agenda. Upon notification of placement on the agenda,
the applicant shall submit to the Administrator twelve (12) copies of all
material required by the Wednesday one week prior to the meeting of said
Planning Board to perfect the application. Failure to timely submit shall be
grounds for tabling of the application.
(B)   At the Planning Board meeting, the applicant should present the proposed
application and receive the Planning Board’s input. The Planning Board may
appoint a Review Committee to report at the next regularly scheduled meeting.
At that meeting, the Planning Board shall adopt and issue a report which shall
determine whether there are any recommendations by the Board which should be
incorporated into the preliminary plat or planned building group application or
the referral to the Board of Aldermen.”
2.   Article 12, Section 12-17: Procedure for Conditional Use Permit
The first paragraph of this section is to deleted and replaced as follows. The
remainder of the section is to read as is.
“Conditional use permits may be issued by the Administrator, after approval by
the Board of Aldermen, for the uses as designated in Section 12-18: Table of
Regulations for Conditional Uses, and after Planning Board review and
recommendations. The petition for a conditional use permit and accompanying
plans shall be submitted to the Administrator in accord with Section 12-5. The
Planning Board shall forward the application and its recommendations to the
Board of Aldermen within thirty (30) days after completing its review of the
application in accord with Section 12-5(B). Upon receiving the application and
recommendations of the Planning Board, the Board of Aldermen shall schedule a
public hearing in accordance with the notice and public hearing provisions of
this Ordinance and State law. The Board of Aldermen shall consider the
application and recommendations of the Planning Board, and may approve or deny
the requested conditional use permit. No vote greater than a majority vote
shall be required for the Board of Aldermen to issue such permits. For the
purposes of this section, vacant positions on the board and members who are
disqualified from voting on a quasi-judicial matter shall not be considered
“members of the Board” for calculation of the requisite majority. When deciding
conditional use permits, the Board of Aldermen shall follow quasi-judicial
procedures. (See also Sections 3-15 and 3-19 of this Ordinance).”
3.   Article 13 Introductory Unnumbered Section
The second paragraph in the introductory unnumbered section of Article 13 is to
be deleted and replaced with the following:
“Planned building groups (inclusive of manufactured home parks) shall be
approved by the Planning Board unless otherwise specified. Planned building
group applications shall be submitted to the Administrator and processed in
accord with Section 12-5 and this Article.”
4.   Article 13, Section 13-1 (E) Sketch Design Plan 
The existing first paragraph is to be deleted and replaced by the following:
“Sketch Design Plan. Prior to the filing of an application for approval of a
planned building group, an applicant shall submit a sketch design plan to the
Administrator to be processed in accord with Section 12-5”.
5.   Article 25, Section 25-5: Major Subdivision Sketch Design Submission and
Review
Delete the existing first two paragraphs, replacing them with the following:
“Prior to the filing of an application for approval of a preliminary plat, an
applicant shall submit a sketch design plan to the Administrator to be
processed in accord with Section 12-5.”
6.   Article 25, Section 25-6: Major Subdivision Preliminary Plat Submission
and Review (A) Submission Procedure.
Delete the second paragraph and replace it with the following wording:
“Twelve (12) copies of the preliminary plat and any supplementary material (as
well as any additional copies which the Administrator determines are needed to
be sent to other agencies) shall be submitted. The review procedure for major
subdivision sketch design shall be followed for the preliminary plan
submission. Preliminary plats shall meet the specifications in Section 25-8 to
be considered complete.”
(C) Review Procedures . Delete the third paragraph and replace it with the
following wording:
“Upon Planning Board recommendation for approval, the applicant shall submit
twelve (12) copies of the plat so recommended and any supplementary material to
the City Manager for consideration by the Board of Aldermen. A complete
submission shall be made by the Monday one week prior to the week of the
regular meeting of the Board of Aldermen in order to be eligible for placement
on the agenda.”
7.   Article 4, Section 4-1 Amending this Ordinance (B) Application.
Existing Section 4-1 (B) is to be deleted and replaced by the following:
“(B) Application . A complete application for any amendment shall contain a
description of the proposed zoning regulation or zoning map amendment. The
application shall state in detail whether the proposed amendment is consistent
with the City Comprehensive Plan, CAMA Core Land Use Plan, and any other
officially adopted plan that is applicable. The application shall also give
detailed evidence that the proposed amendment is in the interest and will
benefit the general public and not solely be of benefit to the applicant; that
the uses within the proposed zoning district are similar or comparable to the
uses in the district as currently zoned, or that none of the uses permitted in
the proposed zoning district may potentially adversely affect property values
or the health, safety, morals, or general welfare of the residents of the
surrounding area. Such application shall be filed with the Administrator to be
processed in accord with Section 12-5.”
ITEM 8.
Review of Sketch Plan for Stevens Park Project
Heather Burchard, Landscape Architect and Community Designer for Steven’s Park
Project introduced members of their team including Brian McAlister with Withers
and Ravenel, Jeff Losey, Legal Counsel, Rod Hyson Sr., Rod Hyson Jr. and Bill
Bruce, Project Coordinator. Ms. Burchard presented a comprehensive plan for the
Steven’s Park Project which includes single family and duplex homes totaling
167 units. Alderman Adams expressed concern over the amount of traffic on 9th
Street. However it appears from the plan that most of the traffic will access
West 11th. Ms. Burchard explained that there is an 11th Street corridor on the
duplex side of the development. She stated that in eighteen (18) months, Bald
Head will relocate its operations to Ferry Road which should alleviate some of
the traffic on 9th Street. Alderman Adams appeared to be of the opinion, if not
Bald Head traffic, that there will be other traffic. Ms. Burchard explained
that they are under contract for a traffic impact analysis (TIA) which will be
submitted with their preliminary plat. Alderman Adams raised the possibility of
requesting DOT to install a traffic light on 11th Street. Ms. Burchard agreed
that this could be a solution. Alderman Powell stated it was his belief during
discussion of the Comprehensive Plan, that it was agreed upon that any
development proposed for this area would include the installation of a traffic
corridor to help relieve traffic congestion, and he is of the opinion that 11th
Street is not the answer. Ms. Burchard stated that this development is part of
a larger plan and in the future, there will be other access points that will
open onto Robert Ruark, therefore traffic will not be concentrated only on
these two streets. The Board expressed appreciation over the concept of the
development and of particular interest were the parks, ball fields and
concession stand.
Mr. Emilita stated the Planning Board has not formally approved the Plan and it
is presented to the Board as an introductory presentation. The Planning Board
after its meeting will present a recommendation at the next Board meeting.
For point of clarification, City Manager Gandy stated part of the development
will be serviced by a package plant as a result of the City not being able to
fulfill its sanitary and sewer needs at this time. He requested a copy of the
construction plans and a meeting be scheduled at some point and time to discuss
maintenance of the plant and whether or not it will be the responsibility of
the developer. He further requested that the developer mirror what is already
in place for compatibility when the time comes to connect to the city sewer
service.
The Board thanked Mr. Hyson for his consideration of Stevens Park.
In related business, Ms. Burchard informed the Board that they have seven non-
conforming lots on 9th Street that are an original part of the development. The
lots are 73 square feet and should be 75. Mr. Gandy explained that this is a
matter for the Board of Adjustment.
ITEM 9.
Presentation by Representatives from Progress Energy
Mr. John Elliott, Manager of Community Relations of the Eastern Region and
Danny Glosson, Operations Manager for the Southport area discussed with the
Board the power outage on January 27, 2006 on Jabbertown Road where the main
feeder line that serves the City failed. He expressed their concerns and
explained that Progress Energy immediately conducted an investigation and root
cause analysis to determine what caused the equipment failure. The equipment
was replaced and Progress Energy implemented a comprehensive plan to ensure
that the feeder was placed in optimal operating condition. A copy of the
comprehensive plan was provided to City Management providing an overview of the
progress and actions taken to ensure safe and reliable power to the City.
Appreciation was expressed by the Board to Progress Energy officials for
effectively addressing the issue.
ITEM 10.
Review of Proposed Modification Regarding the Cape Fear Landing Project East
Side of Yacht Basin Drive – Tom Peterson, Developer
Mr. Emilita, Planning Director explained that this is a proposal to modify the
existing approved subdivision for 6 family dwellings by substituting a mixed
use structure for lots 1-4 on the approved Plan. The mix use structure is
proposed to contain 4 condo units on the top floor, 2 restaurants, 1 on the
second floor and the other a 2 story restaurant and 2 levels of parking
beneath. The proposal is incompliance with parking and height requirements. Mr.
Emilita stated this reintroduces the concept of mixed use and public access to
the waterfront. As explained by the City Manager, the purpose of bringing this
item before the Board is to gauge thoughts on the concept, and if favorable, it
will be presented to the Planning Board as mixed use for a conditional use
permit.
Alderman Adams stated this matter should not be discussed by the Board before
presentation to the Planning Board. Mayor allowed Mr. Peterson to proceed with
the presentation because it was allowed earlier and some members expressed an
interest in the presentation.
Mr. Peterson explained his proposed plans and stated that 1 structure will
contain 5,000 square feet with 2 levels of parking, elevator access to each of
the 4 units which sit above the restaurant, and above that are 4 individual
condo units with their own roof top and deck access. The other side of the
building will house a 2 story restaurant for casual dining. For confirmation,
Mayor asked if the plans were modified from residential to mixed use with some
commercial. Mr. Peterson concurred.
In answer to questions from Mayor Holden concerning water in the streets during
high tide, Mr. Peterson explained that this will be addressed by his engineers.

ITEM 11.
Ordinance for Hire Tours
Mr. Randy Jones presented a draft ordinance to the Board for “Hire Tours”. In
explanation to the Board, it was explained over the past several years there
has been an increase in “for hire tours” being conducted in the Southport area
i.e. walking, Pedi cab, and trolley. This situation was discussed between Mr.
Jones and the City Manager in which ordinances were secured from others towns
with similar situations. Mr. Jones with directives from the City Manager
established a committee with representatives from the Maritime Museum and
Southport Historical Society to review the ordinances and assist in drafting an
ordinance for the city. Mr. Jones explained that the City Attorney reviewed the
ordinance and made some changes and recommended a Tourism Committee. This
Committee is the Director of Tourism, representatives from the Maritime Museum,
Southport Historical Society and a city council member.
Alderman Fisher stated he was not comfortable with a Committee outside of city
staff operating and executing the ordinance because it should be operated by
City staff. He recommended the approval with the change that city staff shall
enforce the Ordinance and recommended the Chief of Police and Code Enforcement
Officer.
Attorney Isenberg stated if the Police Department get involved in enforcement
and administering the ordinance, the application fee should be increased.
Alderman Fisher recommended a $30.00 application fee. After discussion, it was
the consensus of the Board that the Tourism Committee be comprised of the Chief
of Police, Code Enforcement Officer and Director of Tourism. No further
comments, Alderman Fisher motioned to adopt the ordinance with noted changes,
seconded by Alderman Powell, the vote carried.
CHAPTER 10
ARTICLE VII
ORDINANCE REGULATING “FOR-HIRE” TOURS
WHEREAS, traditionally, walking and vehicle tours have been offered by non-
profit organizations in the City of Southport and have not created problems;
and
WHEREAS, “for-profit” businesses are now offering walking and vehicle tours in
the City of Southport, and, as a result of the increase in the number of tours,
the Board of Aldermen finds it is in the best interest of the “City” to study
these types of tours and to consider any appropriate regulations with respect
to such tours; and
WHEREAS, while the matter is under study, the Board of Aldermen determines that
regulation of “for-profit” walking and vehicle tours will maintain, protect and
promote the tourist industry and the economy of the City of Southport, will
manage pedestrian and vehicle traffic on the streets and sidewalks, and will
maintain and promote the aesthetic charm and quality of life of the residents
of the City of Southport;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport as follows:
ARTICLE 1 - GENERAL
Section 10-156 Purpose and Authority
It is the purpose of this ordinance to require that all walking and vehicle
tours operated in the city for profit be licensed and regulated as set forth in
this article. This ordinance is not intended to regulate walking and vehicle
tours conducted by nonprofit organizations such as the Southport Historical
Society, the North Carolina Maritime Museum at Southport or schools.
Furthermore, the provisions of this ordinance shall not apply to tours
conducted entirely off the public streets, sidewalks, rights of way or
municipal property.
Section 10-157 Definitions
The following words, terms, and phrases when used in this ordinance shall have
the meaning described to them in this section, except where the context clearly
indicates a different meaning:
“Amplifying Device” shall mean any equipment or apparatus that broadens or
magnifies the human voice, music or any sound.
“Charter Routes” shall mean the approved route of travel for any tour.
“Person” shall mean a natural person, corporation, company, partnership,
limited liability company, or other organization operating for profit.
“Public Right of Way” shall mean any street, highway, sidewalk, parking lot or
alley that is owned, controlled, maintained or operated by the “City” or State
of North Carolina.
“Tour or Touring” shall mean the conducting of or the participation in
sightseeing on foot or in a vehicle in the “City” for hire or in combination
with a request for donations.
“Tour Guide” shall mean any person who acts or offers to act as a guide for
hire or compensation through any part of the “City” to pedestrians or vehicle
passengers.
“Tour Guide Permit” shall mean the written authority granted by the Tourism
Commission for an individual to conduct a sightseeing tour on foot or by
vehicle within the “City”.
“Vehicle” shall mean bicycles, pedicabs, animal drawn or motorized vehicles
used to transport members of a sightseeing tour.
ARTICLE 2 - TOUR GUIDE PERMIT
Section 10-158 Required
No person shall offer a For Hire Tour within the corporate limits of the “City”
unless such person shall have first applied for and obtained from the Tourism
Commission a Tour Guide Permit. It shall be unlawful for any person to operate
a Tour in any manner contrary to the provisions of this article or without
first having obtained said permit.
Section 10-159 Application
Each applicant for a Tour Guide Permit shall submit in writing an Application
to the Tourism
Commission containing the following information: ( Application Forms available
at the Southport Visitors Center)
(1)   The name, address and telephone number of the owner and operator of the
business. If the applicant is a partnership, the names and addresses of the
general partners; if a corporation the names and addresses of the directors and
officers; if a limited liability company, the names and addresses of the
members and managers.
(2)   The address and phone number from which the applicant will conduct
business operations.
(3)   A description of the Charter Route to be used by the applicant including
starting point and stopping points along the route.
(The Tourism Commission may alter starting location to prevent traffic
congestion)
(4)   A description of the hours of operation of the proposed business and the
hours during which the tours will be conducted.
(5)   A detailed description of the information to be given to the members of
the Tour related to those sights to be viewed within the “City”, including a
copy of any published literature proposed to be provided by the Tour Guide to
any members of the Tour.
(6)   A statement showing that the Tour Guide has sufficient knowledge, skill
and information to conduct said Tours.
(7)   A schedule of the rates and charges proposed by the applicant in the
operation of the business.
(8)   A certificate of general liability insurance in a minimum amount of $
100,000.00 which specifically provides that the same many not be cancelled
without thirty (30) days written notice to the “City”.
(9)   Proof of City of Southport Privilege License.
(10)   Non refundable application fee of $30.00.
Section 10-160 Handicap Accessibility
(1)   All proposed Charter Routes must follow handicap accessible public rights
of way appropriate to tours where walking is utilized by a walking tour or
exiting a tour vehicle.
Section 10-161 Hearing; Approval.
(a)   Upon receipt of the complete Application for a Tour Guide Permit, the
Tourism Commission shall conduct a hearing on the application within seven (7)
business days. The applicant shall be notified of the time, date and place of
the hearing at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of the said hearing. The
Application will be approved if the applicant shows to the satisfaction of the
Tourism Commission that:
(1)   The applicant is able and sufficiently knowledgeable about the history of
the City to perform the proposed service.
(2)   The applicant has not within three (3) years of the date of the
application been convicted of a felony or any crime of moral turpitude.
(3)   The application is complete and sufficient.
(4)   The applicant meets all of the minimum qualifications for the Tour Guide
Permit.
(5)   The applicant is solvent and financially able to furnish adequate service
on a continuing basis and have the necessary insurance required.
(6)   The proposed service will be carried out in a reasonably safe manner so
as not to interfere with the health, safety and welfare of pedestrians, motor
vehicles and the general public and the proposed Tour will not unreasonably
interfere with the use of the streets, sidewalks, parking lots, alleys, parks
and other public properties within the “City”.
(b)   Each Tour Guide Permit granted by the Tourism Commission of the City of
Southport shall include the Charter Route and specific hours of operation. The
Tourism Commission shall have the authority to set other conditions to the Tour
Guide Permit as deemed necessary in the interest of the health, welfare and
safety of the public.
In the event the Tourism Commission denies the applicant’s permit, they may
appeal said decision in writing within forty-eight (48) hours of the
notification to the City Manager.
Section 10-162 Prohibited Acts
It shall be unlawful and a violation of this ordinance and a violation of a
Tour Guide Permit for any Tour Guide or any Tour Guide Permit Holder to:
(1)   Fail to follow the approved Charter Route or move in a manner blocking
entrances to stores, homes, public parks, cemeteries or other places of
business or interfere with street traffic.
(2)   Fail to follow the lawful commands of a law enforcement officer.
(3)   Move on a sidewalk in excess of a column of two persons abreast.
(4)   Solicit members of the public verbally while such member of the public is
on any public street, public sidewalk or public property.
(5)   Operate an Amplifying Device during the course of the Tour without
specific written Tourism Commission approval.
(6)   Fail to comply with all the conditions of the Tour Guide Permit
(7)   Place a permanent sign in a public space to promote the business.
( a temporary sign may be placed one (1) hour before operating hours of the
tour, within one (1) block of the starting location of tour and must be removed
at the end of operating hours if the tour originates on public property
approved by the Tourism Commission )
Section 10-163 Revocation.
The Tourism Commission may revoke a Tour Guide Permit after a hearing conducted
with forty-eight (48) hours notice to the permit holder upon the following
grounds:
(1)   A violation of the terms and conditions of this ordinance or the
conditions of the Tour Guide Permit.
(2)   Upon determining that false information was given on the Application for
a Tour Guide Permit.
(3)   The cancellation or revocation of the Tour Guide Permit Holder’s
liability insurance coverage
(4)   The business closing of the holder of a Tour Guide Permit.
(5)   Conviction of a felony or crime involving the moral turpitude by a Tour
Guide or permit holder.
Section 10-164 Transfer.
The Tour Guide Permit issued pursuant to this article shall not be transferred
by the permit holder except with the prior written permission and approval of
the Tourism Commission.
Section 10-165 Violations
In addition to revocation of a Tour Guide Permit, the violation of any of the
provisions of the ordinance shall subject the offender to a civil penalty in
the amount of $50.00 per violation to be collected by the “City” in the nature
of a debt. Each day a continuing violation shall be deemed a separate
violation.
Section 10-166 Exemptions
Exempt from this ordinance are walking and vehicle tours conducted by non-
profit organizations such as the Southport Historical Society, The North
Carolina Maritime Museum at Southport and schools. Exempt, non-profit
organizations are expected to be guided by this ordinance in all matters
related to health and safety, right of way and public access concerns.
ARTICLE 3 - TOURISM COMMISSION
Section 10-167 Tourism Commission
A Tourism Commission is hereby established to study issues relating to For-Hire
Tours within the City of Southport, to make recommendations after a review and
study and to execute this Ordinance Regulating For-Hire Tours on behalf of the
Board of Aldermen. The Tourism Commission shall consist of three (3) members
and shall include the Director of Tourism for the City of Southport, the Chief
of Police of Southport and the Code Enforcement Officer for the City of
Southport. The administrative activities of the Tourism Commission will be
placed with the Department of Tourism for the City of Southport. The Tourism
Commission will report to the Board of Alderman and make recommendations when
necessary related to the ordinance.
This ordinance is effective upon its adoption this 5th day of May 2006.
S/Mary “Meezie” Childs, Presiding
Alderman
Attest:
S/Regina W. Alexander, CMC
City Clerk

Pursuant to North Carolina General Statute 160A-72, the Board of Aldermen of
the City of Southport hereby states its intention to authorize the exchange of

garage building. This tract is part of tax parcel 237DC023 and this tract is
valued at $105,562.
The land to be acquired by the City from Dosher Hospital is 1.41 acres located
at the northwest corner of Howe Street and 10th Street with 66 feet frontage on
Lord Street. This tract consists of tax parcels 237DC015, 237DC017 and
237DC019. This land is valued at $359,570.
In addition to the exchange of these properties, the City of Southport will pay
the sum of $187,500 to Dosher Hospital.
All persons interested in making this exchange are invited to attend the
meeting of the Southport Board of Aldermen to be held in the Aldermen’s
Chambers, Southport City Hall, 201 E. Moore Street, Southport, NC at 7:30 p.m.
on June 8, 2006. At that time the Board intends to authorize the exchange of
the properties described above.

Resolution
WHEREAS, for many years, the citizens of Southport and surrounding communities
have enjoyed the use of Stevens Park for a wide array of recreational
activities; and
WHEREAS, for many years this park was leased from the Harper Family, but
recently the property was sold and therefore the City of Southport must
relocate part of our recreational facilities to City owned property; and
WHEREAS, one critical facility that we have to move is the 55 and Over club, a
club that has always maintained its membership at the maximum the facility will
accommodate (100) members and;
WHEREAS, to move the 55 and Over Club, picnic and other facilities, it is
estimated to cost approximately $50,000.
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
respectfully requests your efforts in securing a $50,000 grant to assist the
City of Southport in this critical venture.
DULY RESOLVED, this the 11th day of May 2006.

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been petitioned under G.S. 160A-31 to annex
the area described below; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at Southport City
Hall at 7:30 p.m. on June 14, 2006, after due notice by publication in the
State Port Pilot on May 31 and June 7, 2006;
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the petition meets the requirements
of G.S. 160A-31;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, by the Board of Aldermen of Southport, North
Carolina that:
Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-31, the following
described territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City of Southport
effective immediately
EXHIBIT A
Beginning at an iron stake at the intersection of the western right- of- way of
North Howe Street and the northern right-of- way of West 12th Street in the
City of Southport; thence along the northern right-of-way of West 12th Street,
South 68 degrees 42 minutes 58 seconds West, 129.32 feet to an iron stake;
thence North 21 degrees 17 minutes 02 seconds West, 50 feet; thence North 68
degrees 42 minutes 58 seconds East, 129.32 feet to the western right-of-way of
North Howe Street; thence along the right-of-way of North Howe Street, South 21
degrees 17 minutes 02 seconds East, 50 feet to the point and place of beginning
and being all of Lot 20, Block 4, Southport Heights.
This being the same property as shown on a plat entitled “Area Annexed by the
City of Southport N.C. on June 14, 2006 recorded in Map Cabinet ____ at Page
____ of the Brunswick County Registry.
Section 2. Upon and after June 14, 2006 the above described territory and its
citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be entitled to the same
privileges and benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said territory
shall be subject to municipal taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10.
Section 3.  The Mayor of the City of Southport shall cause to be recorded in
the office of the Register of Deeds of Brunswick County, and in the office of
the Secretary of State at Raleigh, North Carolina, an accurate map of the
annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the County Board
of Elections, as required by G. S. 163-288.1.
ADOPTED, this the 14th day of June 2006.
S/ Norman R. Holden
Mayor

S/Regina W. Alexander, CMC

ITEM 6.
Public Hearing pursuant to G.S. 160A-59.24 on the question of approving an
annexation agreement with the Town of St. James allowing the City of Southport
to annex and prohibiting the Town of St. James from annexing certain property
City Manager Gandy explained that this lot is an out parcel located in front of
Lowe’s Home Improvement. The statute governing this type of annexation states
the city with the closest proximity has priority over annexation. After review
through the county’s GIS system, it was determined that the property is closer
to the Town of St. James corporate city limits. The City of Southport was
petitioned and in order for it to go forth an ordinance establishing an
annexation agreement between the Town of St. James and the City of Southport
must be approved. It was explained that state law allows governments with a
common cause to work together to resolve such issues.
Alderman Childs motioned to approve the “An Ordinance Establishing an
Annexation Agreement between the Town of St. James and the City of Southport.”
Alderman Powell seconded the motion and the vote of approval was unanimous.
(Ordinance Incorporated as Attachment #1)

seconded by Alderman Adams to unseal the closed session minutes from June 20,
2004 (Fire Department Land Acquisition), October 14, 2004 (Cameron Property),

(Property acquisition – spray field) and place in the official minute book. The
vote of approval was unanimous.
ITEM 10.
Review and approval of resolution establishing procedures for handling closed
session minutes
A resolution was presented to the Board for consideration establishing
procedures to handle closed session minutes rather than presenting them to the
Board each time. Alderman Childs motioned to adopt the following resolution,
seconded by Alderman Brown, vote carried.
Resolution
Establishing Procedures for Handling
Closed Session Minutes
WHEREAS, General Statute 143-318.10(e) provides that every public body shall
keep full and accurate minutes of all official meetings, including any closed
sessions held pursuant to General Statute 143-318.11; and
WHEREAS, General Statute 143-318.10(e) provides that minutes of a closed
session conducted by a public body in compliance with General Statute 143-
318.11 may be withheld from public inspection so long as public inspection
would frustrate the purpose of a closed session;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that pursuant to General Statute 143-318.10(e), all closed session
minutes are to be sealed against public inspection immediately upon
preparation; and that said sealed minutes shall be presented for approval to
the Board of Aldermen following their preparation; likewise, any revisions
deemed necessary by the Board shall also be sealed against public inspection.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that all sealed minutes shall be reviewed whenever
deemed appropriate by the City Clerk, Manager and Attorney, who shall by
majority opinion be empowered to unseal and release for public inspection any
closed session minutes for which so doing would no longer frustrate the purpose
of having met in closed session.
Adopted this the 14 day of June 2006.
S/Norman R. Holden
Mayor
Attest:
S/Regina W. Alexander, CMC
City Clerk

SECTION VII
TAX RATE ESTABLISHED
An Ad Valorem rate of twenty-seven (.27) cents per $100.00 full valuation is
hereby established as the official tax rate for the City of Southport for the
fiscal year 2006-2007. This is based on an estimated valuation of approximately
$411,852,515 with an estimated collection rate of ninety-eight and one third
percent (98.33%).
SECTION VIII
NEW OR REVISED FEE CHARGES

See Attachment “A”
B. WATER IMPACT FEES
See Attachment “B”
C.   SEWER RATES
See Attachment “C”
D.   WASTEWATER ALLOCATION POLICY & IMPACT FEES
See Attachment “D”
E.   STORMWATER MANAGEMENT PLAN & FEE SCHEDULE
See Attachment “E”
F.   PLANNING & ZONING FEE SCHEDULE
See Attachment “F”
SECTION IX
TRAVEL REIMBURSEMENT POLICY
It is the policy of the City of Southport to reimburse employees for work
related out of town travel. Mileage will be reimbursed for private vehicle use,
when properly authorized, at a rate of .44 ½ cents per mile.
Meals will be reimbursed when necessary to be out of town on business at:
A.   Per diem rate of $45.00 per day without receipts, ($8.00 breakfast, $12.00
lunch, $25.00 dinner), or
B.   The actual cost of meals, including tips, will be paid by the City
provided receipts for such meals are submitted.
Either of these methods may be used, however, only one of the methods may be
used during a business trip not a combination of the two. Everyone is expected
to eat meals he/she would normally eat.
All lodging costs will be paid at the host facility or next closest facility
available. Other costs for seminars, meetings, conferences and programs,
including registration, taxi, baggage handling, etc. incurred as part of the
normal travel will be paid by the City.
SECTION X
SPECIAL AUTHORIZATION - BUDGET OFFICER
The Budget Officer shall be authorized to reallocate departmental
appropriations among the various objects of expenditure and interdepartmental
transfers as said officer believes necessary. The Budget Officer shall be
authorized to effect inter-fund transfers, not to exceed $1,500.00. Notation of
such reallocation and transfers shall be made to the Board on the next
succeeding financial report.
SECTION XI
RESTRICTION - BUDGET OFFICER
The inter-fund transfer of monies exceeding $1,500.00 shall be accomplished by
Board authorization only. The utilization of any contingency appropriation
shall be accomplished only with Board authorization.
SECTION XII
UTILIZATION OF BUDGET & BUDGET ORDINANCE
This Ordinance and the Budget Document shall be the basis of the financial plan
for the City of Southport municipal government during the 2006-2007 Fiscal
Year. The Budget Officer shall administer the budget and shall ensure that
operation officials are provided guidance and sufficient details to implement
their appropriate portion of the Budget. The accounting section shall establish
records which are in agreement with the budget and this ordinance and the
appropriate statues of the State of North Carolina.
Copies of the Budget Ordinance shall be furnished to the Finance Director and
the City Manager of the City of Southport, to be kept on file by them for their
direction in the disbursement of funds.
DULY ADOPTED, this the 27 th day of June, 2006.

WHEREAS, the City of Southport owns that certain tract of land located at the

City Manager Gandy stated that the original plan was adopted in 1997 and DENR

RESOLUTION ACCEPTING AND ENDORSING THE 2006 UPDATE OF THE SOLID WASTE
MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR BRUNSWICK COUNTY
WHEREAS, it is a priority of this community to protect human health and the
Environment through safe and effective management of municipal solid waste; and
WHEREAS, the reduction of the amount and toxicity of the local waste stream is
a goal of this community; and
WHEREAS, equitable and efficient delivery of solid waste management services is
an essential characteristic of the local management solid waste management
system; and
WHEREAS, it is a goal of the community to maintain and improve its physical
appearance and to reduce the adverse effects of illegal disposal and littering;
and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport recognizes its role in the encouragement of
recycled products; and
WHEREAS, involvement and education of the citizenry is critical to the
establishment of an effective local solid waste program; and
WHEREAS, the State of North Carolina has placed planning responsibility on
local government for the management of solid waste; and
WHEREAS, NC General Statute 130A-309.09A(b) requires each unit of local
government, either individually or in cooperation with other units of local
government, to update the Ten Year Comprehensive Solid Waste Management Plan at
least every three years; and
WHEREAS, the Brunswick County Solid Waste Management Department has undertaken
and completed a long range planning effort to evaluate the appropriate
technologies and strategies available to manage solid waste effectively;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that
Brunswick County’s 2006 Update of the Ten Year Comprehensive Solid Waste
Management Plan is accepted and endorsed and placed on file with the City Clerk
on the 13th Day of July, 2006
/s/ Norman R. Holden
Mayor

/s/ Regina W. Alexander

ten (10) days prior to the date of the public hearing.

XII.
Review of Resolution requesting the North Carolina Department of Transportation
to conduct the engineering and environmental studies required for development
of the transportation infrastructure required for the development of the North

Alderman Powell moved to adopt the following resolution and requested a copy be
sent to Representatives Stiller, Hill, Senator R. C. Soles and Lanny Wilson,
DOT Board member. Motion seconded by Alderman Fisher, the vote carried.
RESOLUTON REQUESTING THE NORTH CAROLINA DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION TO CONDUCT
THE ENGINEERING AND ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES REQUIRED FOR DEVELOPMENT OF THE
TRANSPORTATION INFRASTRUCTURE REQUIRED FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NORTH
CAROLINA INTERNATIONAL PORT IN BRUNSWICK COUNTY
WHEREAS, the North Carolina State Ports Authority has acquired in excess of 600
acres of prime riverfront property in Brunswick County, within five miles of
the Atlantic Ocean; and
WHEREAS, the Ports Authority has begun planning the development of a new state
of the art container port serving North Carolina, to be called the North
Carolina International Port, which it desires to be operational as early as
2012 and fully operational no later than 2014; and
WHEREAS, the new port will make North Carolina’s ports competitive with the
ports in neighboring states and will have a profound positive economic benefit
to the entire State; and
WHEREAS, this project should not be designated as a regional project in the
Transportation Improvement Plan but should be recognized as a State project for
the economic benefits it brings to all regions of North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, cargo handling activities at the Ports of Morehead City and Wilmington
drive Statewide economic development by contributing to 84,833 North Carolina
jobs and $299 million in annual State and local tax revenues, and activities at
the North Carolina International Port are forecast to support over 280,000
North Carolina jobs and $674 million in annual tax revenues; and
WHEREAS, it is critical to the development and success of the NCIP and to the
economic development of the State that both rail and highway access be located
so as to provide the most efficient transportation for the containers to be
transported through the NCIP; and
WHEREAS, the Department of Transportation has the expertise and experience
required to complete the engineering and environmental studies necessary for
connection of the NCIP with the major rail and highway corridors in the area;
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
does hereby request that the North Carolina State Department of Transportation:
a.   Move forward with the engineering and environmental studies required to
initiate construction of highway and rail access to NCIP and that such study or
studies be commenced as soon as possible;
b.   Provide for the most efficient connections between the NICP and the
Interstate highway system and to the State’s rail systems;
c.   Study the feasibility of the State assuming responsibility for upgrading,
operating and maintaining the U.S. Federal Railroad to service Military Ocean
Terminal, Sunny Point, the NICP and other enterprises.
d.   Consider an alternative route from NCIP to US Highway 17, which would
parallel NC 87.
e.   Identify and pursue a funding strategy to provide the funding for highway
and rail access to NICP.
f.   “Fast track” this project in order to accommodate a 2012 target date for
completion of Phase 1 of the NCIP development.
The foregoing Resolution was adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen at its
regularly scheduled meeting held on July 13, 2006
/s/ Norman R. Holden. Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk

V.
Public Hearing - to consider revision to the Unified Development Ordinance
Repeal of Section 25-14 “Land Disturbing Activities” and addition of Article I
General Provisions, Section 1-11
Alderman Callari moved to enter public hearing on the above, seconded by
Alderman Childs, vote carried.
Attorney Isenberg noted that there were a few clerical changes but not anything
substantive that would require another hearing. Paragraph 1 under #2-change
word to “matter,” third paragraph added words “prior to the completion of
application.”
No public comments, Mayor called for a motion to close the public hearing and
re-enter regular session. Alderman Childs moved, seconded by Alderman Brown,
vote carried.
Alderman Childs moved to approve the revision of the Unified Development;
Repeal of Section 25-14 “Land Disturbing Activities” and addition of Article 1,
General Provisions, Section 1-11 “Land Disturbing Activities” with the noted
changes. Alderman Callari seconded the motion and the vote of approval was
unanimous.
1.   Section 25-14: Land Disturbing Activities
“Section 25-14 is hereby repealed.”
2.   ARTICLE 1. GENERAL PROVISIONS.
ADD: Section 1-11: Land Disturbing Activities
“It has become a matter of public concern that owners of land under development
application review have prematurely “head started” unregulated land clearing
and pre-construction activities. This is improper for many reasons; not only
procedural but it also could create liability issues, environmental impacts, as
well as cause adverse impacts upon unsuspecting neighbors. The intent of this
section is to prevent this activity on the part of developers awaiting full
approval, but not to prevent the individual homeowner from landscaping
activity, vegetative maintenance, tree trimming or tree removal.
Therefore, from the effective date of this section August 15, 2006 there shall
be no pre-construction activity, including, but not limited to disturbance to
vegetation other than path-clearing by hand for inventorying natural resources
or land surveying activity; or installing vegetative protection or erosion and
sedimentation control measures as approved by the City, for any site under
application review, until such pre-construction activity is authorized by the
City approval agency and until all applicable City, State and Federal approvals
have been obtained and submitted.
The City approval agency shall have the authority to require restoration of the
site to its predevelopment conditions existing at the date of acquisition by
the applicant, but no more than three years prior to the commencement of
application review. The City approval authority may require such environmental
studies, as it deems necessary to establish such predevelopment conditions,
baseline environmental data, and other site information in fulfillment of its
responsibilities of this Ordinance.
This provision shall not apply to final development approvals granted by the
City as of the effective date of this section. The intent of this section is
not to regulate normal landscape and vegetative maintenance by the owner-
occupant or tenant of a residence or commercial building. Activities permitted
under Article 18 of this Ordinance shall not be affected by the section.”
3.   ARTICLE 2. BASIC DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS
Add the following new definitions:
Application Review. The process, by which a submission for proposed
development, construction or reconstruction of a building or site is evaluated,
processed and acted upon by the City approval agency. Application review shall
be considered to have begun on the date of the first submission of an
application with the Administrator.
Pre-construction Activity. Any action taken to disturb land or vegetation for a
site prior to the completion of application review, or other site preparation,
including but not limited to the storage of construction materials, stockpiles,
containers, vehicles or similar items prior to the start of construction
permitted there under.
Alderman Fisher made mention of construction work being performed on Sundays
and asked about the city code governing this. City Manager Gandy and Attorney
Isenberg stated this comes under the Noise Ordinance in the City Code. Mr.
Gandy stated that he asked the Building Inspector to make this a part of the
building permit process and he will discuss this again. Mr. Gandy asked if
anyone sees construction work being done on Sundays to contact the Police
Department.

IX.
Utility Meter Contract
City Manger Gandy explained that the meter-reading contract was entered into
October of 1999, two years prior to approval of the first Operation and
Maintenance contract with Brunswick Electric. He made referenced to discussion
about the possibility of meter reading being done in house, however; it has
been by contract for the past seven years and he did not consider this
possibility. He stated Brunswick Electric actually did it in house and then
they sub-contracted it out. The Finance Director performed an analysis to
determine what it would cost to bring meter reading back in house assuming the
position would be given to someone on staff. It would cost the city $.89 per
meter vs. $.80 per meter on contract. The contract person for BEMC read 4500
meters averaging 20 days per month including electric, water and irrigation.
Alderman Fisher stated this was discussed during a Committee meeting with
Brunswick Electric, why pay the intermediary when the city can contract
directly for the same service and save money, approximately $3,000.
City Manager Gandy informed the Board that Brunswick Electric is running pilot
programs on automated meter reading. At this point, they read only electric
meters. Once this test program is working sufficiently, they will include water
meters. During contract negotiations, the city was asked if it would be
interested in participating when water meters are brought on line. He stated
that there is a possibility that meter reading will be automated in the next 2-
3 years.
Mayor Holden stated if meter reading is brought back in house, the city will
have to pay benefits i.e. retirement, insurance, 401-K, provide a vehicle, etc.
It is more cost effective to contract the meter reading and recommended
approval of the contract. City Manager Gandy stated if city staff read meters,
this would pull from other duties and possibly end up a full time position.
Staff recommended the proposal from Terry Bassett, the current meter reader in
the amount of $43,500 annually ($1,673.08 bi –weekly) with no change in rate
for the first 20 meters and $.80 per meter afterwards. This proposal is $3,880
less than the Coastal Group who submitted a bid. Ms. Bassett’s proposal also
includes provisions for backup meter readers, vehicles, supplying her own
liability and medical insurance, vehicle maintenance and 4% increase each
optional year.
Alderman Adams stated he questioned the contract and his major concern was to
afford an employee on staff the opportunity to have the job. The City already
pays benefits and vehicles are available. He contended that anytime jobs like
this become available, employees in-house should get first preference, and
other people should be given the opportunity to submit bids. City Manager Gandy
stated bids were received from BEMC, Coastal and Terrilyn Bassett, who was the
low bidder. City Manager Gandy reiterated again that the meter reading has been
contracted for seven years; he did not look at it as an in-house position
because the service has been contracted. Alderman Adams concluded his comments
by stating that more than one person should have known about the bidding
process for the meter reader and if others knew, more savings could have been
realized.
No further comments, Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Fisher to
award the contract to Terrilyn Basset for the amount of $43,500. The votes of
approval were five ayes, Alderman Powell, Fisher, Childs, Callari and Brown.
One no vote, Alderman Adams. (Contract Incorporated as Attachment #1)

XI.
Resolution in Support of Oak Island and Sunset Beach Bridge
Alderman Childs moved to adopt the following resolution in support of ensuring
that the Oak Island and Sunset Beach bridge projects proceed without further
delays. Alderman Brown seconded, the vote of approval was unanimous.
RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF ENSURING THAT THE OAK ISLAND AND SUNSET BEACH BRIDGE
PROJECTS PROCEEED WITHOUT FURTHER DELAYS
Whereas, over the past 20 years the growth rate in Brunswick County has been
more than twice the rate of the state as a whole; and
Whereas, the people of Brunswick County have waited patiently for an improved
State Road Network in the County while others parts of the State have had
numerous major highway improvements, some of which have been for convenience or
economic development; and
Whereas, Brunswick County is home to a nuclear power plant and a major military
munitions depot, either of which could necessitate rapid evacuation of our
people; and
Whereas, the County is also prone to natural events, such as hurricanes, which
also can trigger a need for rapid evacuations of people out of the area; and
Whereas, we now learn through a media report that two long delayed bridge
projects in Brunswick County may yet again be delayed; and
Whereas, those two projects link two of Brunswick County’s barrier islands to
the mainland and are critical to the safety and general welfare of the
residents and visitors.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
recognizes the urgency and necessity for expediting the construction of the
above mentioned bridges, hereby respectfully request the Governor, our
delegations to the General Assembly, the Secretary of Transportation, and the
State Board of Transportation give this their highest consideration necessary
to ensure that the Oak Island and Sunset Beach bridge projects proceed without
any further delays.
THIS THE 10TH DAY OF AUGUST 2006.
/s/ Norman R. Holden, Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk

1994 CHEVROLET CAPRICE- CONVEY TO BSL POLICE DEPT.
City Manager Gandy informed the Board several years ago a reserve officer
donated a 1994 Chevrolet Caprice to the City. Grady Sillings who did reserve
work with the City resigned and will be doing reserve work with the Boiling
Spring Lakes Police Department. Chief Richard White asked if he could acquire
the unit to use as a reserve vehicle which can also be used as part of the
City’s mutual aid. City Manager Gandy stated after talking with the City
Attorney, it was determined that since the vehicle was donated, it would
require Board approval to convey the unit to the Boiling Spring Lakes Police
Department.
Alderman Brown moved to convey the 1994 Chevrolet Caprice to the Boiling Spring
Lakes Police Department, seconded by Alderman Childs, the vote of approval was
unanimous.
ROAD CLOSING – HOWE STREET
Mr. Gandy told the Board that a problem was discovered with the Howe Street
right of way as the title work for the property that was negotiated with Dosher
Hospital was being done. Attorney Isenberg said that Attorney Prevatte who did
the title work for the hospital on the property they are getting from the City
found the problem. On an old 1900 map, Howe Street went up to Fodale at one
time, and then from Fodale on it was called Cape Fear Road. The road took a 45º
turn at Fodale and there is an old right of way called Howe Street that runs
through the middle of the city’s property. In order for the City give a good
title to Dosher Hospital, it will be necessary to do a road closing procedure
to close the old road. He explained that it was never opened or used, but
technically, it is on an old recorded map. Dosher has asked the City to call
for the Public Hearing and the Board to consider closing the road.
Alderman Fisher moved to adopt the resolution to close the street and to set
public hearing on September 14, 2006, seconded by Alderman Brown, vote carried.
RESOLUTION TO CLOSE STREET
THAT WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport proposes to
permanently close that portion of the street known as Howe Street as shown on
the Farguson plat recorded in Map Book 1 at Pages 70-70A of the Brunswick
County Registry, said portion being bounded by Lee Avenue on the south, Block
14 of the Park View Addition on the west, the old Wilmington, Brunswick and
Southern Railroad and Jackson Place on the north, and Block 11 of the Park View
Addition on the east; and
WHEREAS, prior to the closing of said street, it is necessary for the Board of
Aldermen to hear all interested persons on the question of whether or not the
closing would be detrimental to the public interest, or the property rights of
any individual;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport pursuant to G. S. 160A-299 as follows:
1.   That the City of Southport intends to permanently close that portion of
the street as described above.
2.   That a public hearing on said closing shall be held at 7:30 p.m. on
September 14, 2006, at the Southport City Hall, 201 E. Moore Street, Southport,
N. C.
3.   That a copy of this resolution shall be published once a week for four (4)
successive weeks prior to the hearing, a copy hereof shall be sent by
registered or certified mail to all owners of property adjoining the public
road as shown on the county tax records, and a notice of the closing and public
hearing shall be prominently posted in at least two (2) places along said
street.
This the 15th day of August, 2006.

by the editorial staff of the star news. He will write a letter to the editor

STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA
ORDER
BRUNSWICK COUNTY
THAT WHEREAS, G. S. 160A-299 requires that when a city proposes to permanently
close any street or public alley that the Board of Aldermen first adopt a
resolution declaring its intent to close said street or alley and calling for a
public hearing on the question; and
WHEREAS, G. S. 160A-299 further requires that the resolution to close the
street or alley be published once a week for four successive weeks prior to the
date of said hearing, that a copy thereof be sent by registered or certified
mail to all owners of property adjoining the portion of the street or alley to
be closed as shown on the county tax records, and that notice of the closing
and public hearing be prominently posted in at least two places along the
street or alley to be closed; and
WHEREAS, on August 15, 2006, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport
passed a resolution proposing to close a certain portion of the street known as
Howe Street as shown on the Farguson plat recorded in Map Book 1 at Pages 70-
70A of the Brunswick County Registry, said portion being bounded by Lee Avenue
on the south, Block 14 of the Park View Addition on the west, the old
Wilmington, Brunswick and Southern Railroad and Jackson Place on the north, and
Block 11 of the Park View Addition on the east, and also calling for a public
hearing on said question; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has complied with all requirements of G. S.
160A-299, including the holding of the public hearing and the giving of all
required notice; and
WHEREAS, no portion of the street or alley to be closed is under the authority
or control of the Board of Transportation; and
WHEREAS, adjoining property owners and other persons were heard on the question
of whether or not the closing would be detrimental to the public interest or
the property rights of any individual; and
WHEREAS, it appears to the satisfaction of the Board of Aldermen after the
hearing that the closing of this road is not contrary to the public interest
and that no individual owning property in the vicinity of the road or in the
subdivision in which it is located would be deprived of reasonable means of
ingress and egress to their property and that the portion of said road
described above should be closed;
NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED pursuant to G. S. 160A-299 as follows:
1.   That the following described portion of Howe Street is hereby closed:
That certain portion of Howe Street as shown in Map Book 1 At Pages 70-70A of
the Brunswick County Registry being bounded by Lee Avenue on the south, Block
14 of the Park View Addition on the west, the old Wilmington, Brunswick and
Southern Railroad and Jackson Place on the north, and Block 11 of the Park View
Addition on the east.
2.   That the City of Southport hereby reserves and retains all right, title
and interest in the utility improvements and easements, if any, located within
said road.
This the 14th day of September, 2006.
CITY OF SOUTHPORT
BY: /s/ Norman R. Holden, Mayor
ATTEST:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander
Clerk

Adoption of Ordinance establishing Annexation Agreement with City of Boiling
Spring Lakes
Alderman Callari moved, seconded by Alderman Brown to approve the following
Ordinance establishing an annexation agreement between the City of Boiling
Spring Lakes and the City of Southport, vote was unanimous.
AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING AN ANNEXATION AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF BOILING
SPRING LAKES AND THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT
THAT WHEREAS, the City of Boiling Spring Lakes and the City of Southport, duly
incorporated municipalities under the laws of the State of North Carolina,
desire to enhance orderly planning by such municipalities , provide for future
development including necessary infrastructure, and eliminate uncertainty in
connection with said planning and future growth; and
WHEREAS, the governing boards of said municipalities also desire to avoid
potential conflict and confusion and to foster good intergovernmental
relations; and
WHEREAS, Chapter 160A, Article 4A, Part 6, of the North Carolina General
Statutes authorizes municipalities to enter into agreements designating areas
which are not subject to annexation by the participating municipalities;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED that the participating municipalities hereby
agree as follows:
1.   This Agreement is executed pursuant to the authority of Chapter 160A,
Article 4A, Part 6, of the North Carolina General Statutes.
2.   This Agreement shall terminate ten (10) years after its effective date.
3.   The City of Boiling Spring Lakes may not annex the following described
area:
   See Exhibit A attached hereto.
4.   The effective date of this Agreement shall be the date of adoption of the
approving ordinance by the last participating municipality to do so.
5.   The City of Boiling Spring Lakes hereby waives all statutory notice
requirements of annexation by the City of Southport during the term of this
Agreement for the areas described in this Agreement pursuant to G. S. 160A-
58.24(a)(5).
6.   This Agreement may be modified or terminated by a subsequent agreement
entered into by the participating municipalities pursuant to G. S. 160A-58.24
(d). Any subsequent agreement shall be approved by ordinance after the required
public hearings.
7.   This Agreement may be terminated unilaterally by a participating
municipality or a participating municipality may withdraw from the Agreement by
repealing the ordinance by which it approved the Agreement and providing five
years’ written notice to the other participating municipality. Upon the
expiration of the five-year period, this Agreement shall terminate.
8.   This writing contains the entire Agreement between the participating
municipalities.
Adopted by the Board of Commissioners of the City of Boiling Spring Lakes on
the ___ day of October 2006.
CITY OF BOILING SPRING LAKES

X.
Review of non-contiguous annexation petition submitted pursuant to G.S. 160A-
58.2 (Section of Dutchman Village property – Jeff Earp)
After review of the petition, Alderman Fisher, a member of the Sewer Committee
stated that the City could not provide sewer at this time and motioned to deny
the annexation petition, seconded by Alderman Childs, vote carried. (On
determination from City Attorney Isenberg, the satellite annexation statute
requires the Board to make a specific finding “that a city must stand ready to
provide sewer services to newly annexed areas on substantially the same basis
and in the same manner in which those services are provided to the rest of the
city.” )

XII.
Main Street Program
Mr. Randy Jones, Director of Tourism and Susan Farley, President of the
Southport Merchants Association, updated the Board on the work being done on
behalf of the N.C. Main Street Program. Mr. Jones explained that the City and
Southport merchants have worked cooperatively to promote the city’s image,
however; the issues facing downtown Southport today is growth, development and
tourism, which is going to affect the quality of life for everyone. In order to
identify, prioritize issues, create, and implement new solutions, they propose
to establish a non-profit membership organization as Downtown Southport Inc. to
accomplish established goals. It was requested that a member from the Board of
Aldermen be appointed to serve on the organizing committee along with
representatives from the Planning and Tourism Departments, and members of the
Southport Merchants Association. The first meeting of the Organizing Committee
is scheduled for Monday, October 2, 5:30 p.m. in the conference room of the
Aldermen Chambers. Alderman Fisher volunteered to be a member of the Committee
from the Board of Aldermen.
XIII.
Review of action plan for Stevens Park/Lowe White Park
Ms. Heather Hemphill, Director of Parks and Recreation, presented a tentative
timeline for redevelopment of Lowe/White Park for Board consideration.
Tentative Timeline for Redevelopment of Lowe/White Park
September through October 2006-Delineation study of wetlands on park property
Week 1 of October 2006- Move current building used to house the senior programs
from Stevens Park to site clearly out of wetland boundaries on Lowe/White Park
(See Note 1)
November 2006- Select and hire an architect to design Lowe/White Park based on
input received from Board of Aldermen, Recreation Committee and Public Survey
December 2006 - Present Architect design to Board of Aldermen for input and
approval
January 2007- Select contractors and begin construction of Lowe/White Park
improvements
June 30, 2007- Lowe/White Park opens to public
Notes
1.   As of September 6, 2006, many items have already been removed from the
Stevens Park property. Examples include the horseshoe pits, shuffleboard
courts, batting cage, and some picnic tables and benches. The basketball goals
and swing sets are the next scheduled equipment to be relocated.
2.   It is the recommendation of staff that remaining structures be demolished
due to the conditions of these structures as well as the costs associated with
moving them. It is our understanding that the structures that will not be moved
will be rebuilt by the developers of the Stevens Park Ball field and Recreation
Complex.
3.   The City of Southport has contacted the Cape Fear Trading Company about
obtaining a one-month extension to accomplish the goals outlined above. We hope
to hear back from the Company by the end of the week of September 15.
Mayor Holden recommended that a new survey be conducted to gauge public input
on the Lowe-White Park. Ms. Hemphill stated it would take at least one month to
get the survey circulated. The Board agreed that a new survey needs to be
conducted. Alderman Fisher suggested the survey inform the public that the
programs offered at Steven’s Park will carry over to Lowe-White to include
baseball fields. Mayor Holden asked Ms. Hemphill to be looking for an
alternative location to Steven’s Park.
XIV.
Complaint filed against a Planning Board Member – Dale McPherson
Mayor stated the matter concerning a complaint filed by three Planning Board
members regarding a conflict of interest was placed on the agenda because of
directives from the August meeting.
Mr. Dale McPherson, Planning Board member stated that he never recused himself
from voting concerning a change to the UDO, only in the case of Cottage Point
because he represents sales and marketing. He stated that Mr. Roy Pender
proposed about a year ago that the Board look at the Planned Unit Development
(PUD) and the amount of acreage required for a PUD. Mr. Pender asked him why
the Board would not consider this and he told him, “Roy, the thing for you to
do if you would like to address that again with the Board is for us not to have
a discussion about it; you go to the Board and talk about it. So Mr. Pender was
an advocate of having a five acre or minimum ten acres or whatever the Board
saw fit to reduce the amount of acreage needed for a PUD in Southport property
not to include the ETJ.” He explained that Mr. Pender came before the Board and
he did participate in the discussion as a Planning Board member. Mr. McPherson
told the Board of an instance where Mr. Terry Lee came before the Board about 5
years ago and discussed the fact that there was no middle of the road between a
33 ft. non-conforming lot and a 10,000 sq. ft. lot. He also tried to affect a
similar type change. Mr. McPherson stated that he has always been an advocate
for some middle of the road acreage for residential. He explained that he
recused himself many times but never in consideration of a change to a PUD. The
Planning Board did invite Mr. Pender to a workshop to give his points of view
and bring information from other areas that had lesser acreage for a PUD. Mr.
McPherson told the Board that Cottage Point did not have an application to be
considered, but may in the future. He referenced the complaint and noted that
he did not have a financial nor personal interest in the matter. “A change was
being considered to the UDO, not an application.” He explained during the
Planning Board’s Workshop, that it was unanimously decided to recommend a
change to the PUD. Mr. Emilita was asked to draft the wording and it would be
placed on the next Planning Board agenda. Mr. McPherson stated that he brought
it up because he thought that it was inadvertently left out of the packet since
Mr. Emilita was out of town. He stated when it came up, one of the Planning
Board members said that she wanted to read the wording and he told her; “we
have a City Attorney, and have a Planning Director who are quite capable of
getting the verbiage together, it is not a big deal; it is just a matter of do
we want to decrease the minimum acreage in the Southport property.” Everyone
had decided that it was a good move and he failed to see where Cottage Point
has anything to do with this except for the fact that they continue to acquire
property and will possibly at some point, give up constructing condo and
develop a PUD. He did not realize that anyone had a problem with the motion
made on July 20, until eight days after the meeting when a complaint was filed
with the City Manager, and he found out eight days later, not realizing that
his character would be challenged.
There being no discussion or questions from the Board, Alderman Powell motioned
to send this issue back to the Planning Board and let them revisit this matter.
If the Planning Board deems a problem, send a recommendation to the Board of
Aldermen. Motion seconded by Alderman Fisher. Six Ayes: Aldermen Fisher, Adams,
Childs, Brown, Powell, and Callari. 0 Nays: Motion carried.
Attorney Isenberg stated that Mr. Emilita completed a draft language for the
PUD minimum required acreage.

RESOLUTION PROCLAIMING OCTOBER 1-7, 2006 AS PUBLIC POWER WEEK IN THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the City of Southport provides reliable electricity to its citizens;
and
WHEREAS, the citizens of Southport are consumers and owners of their public
power Systems and exercise local control over utility operations and policies;
and
WHEREAS, our employees are neighbors serving neighbors; and
WHEREAS, our electric system is a community asset that contributes to the well-
being of citizens by providing safe and reliable power, excellent local
customer service and economic development opportunities; and
WHEREAS, our community is one of more than 70 public power cities and towns in
North Carolina, and more than 2,000 public power systems in the United States.
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport, North Carolina, does
hereby proclaim October 1 through October 7, 2006, as “Public Power Week” in an
effort to promote public power and those who work in our cities and towns to
provide the best possible electric service for our citizens.
DULY ADOPTED this the 14th day of September 2006.

Jones, Director of Tourism, in order to have someone occupying the space per
grant requirement. The Committee will meet with other citizens interested in
helping with the project.

for storm debris, which took them two weeks to do. This was done at no cost to
the city and if anything is left out, he and the Public Services Director will
insure that it is picked up.

their work on the wastewater projects. During Phase I, the city recouped 80,000
gallons from infiltration, which was the first project. On the second project,
the city gained approximately 65,000 to 75,000 gallons towards its goal of
recouping 160,000 gallons.
The reversal project with a goal of 200,000 is operating; he stated that the
city is currently sending approximately 165,000 gallons per day to the Sanitary
District.
Northwood Cemetery – Alderman Fisher complimented staff on the appearance of
Northwood Cemetery.

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
(Non-Contiguous)
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been petitioned under G.S.160A-58.1 to annex
the area described below; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at Southport City
Hall at 7:30 p.m. on October 12, 2006, after due notice by publication in the
Wilmington Star News, September 30, 2006; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the area described therein meets the
standards of G.S. 160A-58.1(b), as modified by act of the General Assembly
applicable to the City of Southport and in accordance with an Annexation
Agreement between the City of Southport and the Town of St. James, to wit:
a.    The nearest point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is not more
than three (3) miles from the corporate limits of the City of Southport;
b.    No point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is closer to another
municipality than to the City of Southport except for the Town of St. James and
the City of Southport and Town of St. James have entered into an annexation
agreement pursuant to G.S. 160A-58.21 et seq. allowing the City of Southport to
annex and prohibiting the Town of St. James from annexing said property;
c.    The area described is so situated that the City of Southport will be able
to provide the same services within the proposed satellite corporate limits
that it provides within the primary corporate limits;
d.    No subdivision, as defined in G.S. 160A-376, will be fragmented by this
proposed annexation, and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the petition has been signed
by all the owners of real property in the area who are required by law to sign;
and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the petition is otherwise
valid, and that the public health, safety and welfare of the City of Southport
and of the area proposed for annexation will be best served by annexing the
area described;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, by the Board of Aldermen of Southport, North
Carolina that:
Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-58.2, the following
described non-contiguous territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City
of Southport effective immediately.
SEE EXHIBIT A
Section 2. Upon and after October 12, 2006 the above-described territory and
its citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be entitled to the same
privileges and benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said territory
shall be subject to municipal taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10
Section 3.  The Mayor of the City of Southport shall cause to be recorded in
the office of the Register of Deeds of Brunswick County, and in the office of
the Secretary of State at Raleigh, North Carolina, an accurate map of the
annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the County Board
of Elections as required by G. S. 163-288.1.
ADOPTED this the12th day of October 2006.
