III.
Action on recommendation by the Southport Planning Board to consider revising
Section 14-1 of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance by replacing in its
entirety as follows: Five (5) acres of net buildable area within the City
corporate limits, on one or more contiguous parcels and: Twenty five (25) acres
of net buildable area in the ETJ, on one or more parcels (this may include
parcels on both sides of the street) (Public Hearing held Thursday, October 12)
Aldermen Childs stated some concerns were presented to her about reducing the
Planned Unit Development (PUD) threshold for PUD’s in the city limit from the
current 25 acres to the proposed 5 acres. Mr. Hicks stated that the 5 acres
were the result of discussion by Planning Board members who received
information from other towns comparable to Southport. The Planning Board came
up with 5 acres due to the limited number of tracts of land in Southport’s
corporate limits. He explained that staff and the Planning Board believes
reducing the size of the PUD will result in better control in determining what
goes into it and will afford more opportunity for PUD’s to be used in the
process. Alderman Childs suggested 7-acre tracts.
Alderman Adams asked why reduce the size of acreage for PUDS within the
corporate city limits and not the ETJ. He stated in some instances, the ETJ may
be five feet from the city line and the same should apply. Mr. Hicks stated, if
it is the Board’s desire, the Planning Board could look at the same for the
ETJ. He explained even if the acreage is reduced, the Board of Aldermen is
under no obligation to grant a PUD. Alderman Adams stated he is not against the
reduction, but believes it should be larger than 5 acres.
Alderman Brown stated he does not have a problem with reducing the number, but
believes that 25 acres is high for the city.
No further discussion, Alderman Powell moved to amend Section 14-1 of the
Unified Development Ordinance, seconded by Alderman Adams. Vote carried.
Section 14-1: Minimum Size
Eight (8) acres of net buildable area within the city corporate limits, on one
or more contiguous parcels.
Twenty-five (25) acres of net buildable area in the ETJ, on one or more parcels
(this may include parcels on both sides of a street)
IV.
Southport Parking Study – Randy Jones of Lanier Parking Systems
Alderman Fisher explained that Mr. Jones would present the results of the
Parking Study performed at the behest of the Parking Committee. He explained
that the Parking Committee will review the recommendations as a Committee and
will present them to the Board for consideration or implementation.
Mr. Randy Jones of Lanier Parking presented a power-point presentation on the
parking situation in Southport. The study area contained 14 blocks surrounding
the intersection of Moore and Howe Streets. He explained that this is the core
parking area where most of the parking activity occurs for City Hall and
downtown businesses. A detailed analysis was conducted on a block level;
inventory of parking facilities conducted for the entire study area, data
collected through a survey of 12 block faces over an eight-hour period. The
parking demand was then calibrated to reflect seasonal variations and future
growth. Seasonal variations were assumed to be +30% while future growth
projected to increase by 7% compounded over a 3-year period. Mr. Jones in his
report stated that based on the survey; there are 172 spaces in the core area
of downtown and another 826 in close proximity. The report contained a table
showing these parking areas. He stated that the city needs to plan for future
parking due to development. He recommended that the 2-hour time limit be
expanded in other areas and enforced. He also enumerated the economic benefits
and losses pertaining to parking. He talked about the possibility of installing
parking meters along Bay Street and charging for use of the city pier. Alderman
Adams stated his opposition to parking meters. Mayor stated that the City Pier
was constructed with grant monies and do not believe the city would be in
compliance with grant requirements if it charged for use of the city pier.  The
report contained additional information and recommendations for Board
consideration. The Parking Study in its entirety is on file in the office of
the Clerk.
The Board thanked Mr. Jones for a thorough and informative report.
V.
Report on Brunswick County Airport – Owen Gardner, Board Member and Howie
Franklin, Airport Manager
Mr. Gardner, member of the Brunswick County Airport Board stated that
approximately one month ago they received an in-kind donation of 15 acres of
land on the west side of the airport which match federal requirements for
expansion of the runway. He stated no local matching funds are due because of
the value of the property. He told the Board at the end of the first quarter of
this fiscal year, jet fuel sales were up 38% over last year.  The airport
website address is www.brunswickcountyairport.net, and citizens may call 457-
1710 to obtain the current weather, temperature, wind velocity and visibility.
The airport’s major concern now is to obtain funding to move the airport road.
This may be delayed but they are working diligently to speed up the process
because the road has to be moved in order to expand the runway.
Mr. Howie Franklin, Airport Manager showed the Board a copy of the Southern
Aviator who in March selected Brunswick County’s Airport as the “best in the
south” and the Atlantic Flyer wrote an article on Brunswick County Airport
stating, “This was a place that once you came here, you may not want to leave.”
Mr. Franklin presented a copy of the “Economic Impact of North Carolina
Airports – 2006 Study” which showed an economic impact of $26,178,600 per year.
The airport also provides the county with a significant source of property tax
revenue with 39 based aircrafts at a calculated value of $12,445,000, which
would result in ad valorem taxes of $67,200 based on the county rate of $0.54
per $100. The study estimated that there were 17,100 visitors to the area who
utilized the Airport. Mr. Franklin stated that Brunswick County is a General
Aviation Airport, which equates to a non-air carrier airport and talked about
the significance of the small GA Airports. Mr. Franklin explained after a
question from Mayor Holden that it is their goal to construct four (4)
additional hangars once the land is purchased. The Airport currently has a
demand for 58 hangars. Board members thanked airport representatives for the
report. In closing, Mr. Franklin announced that October 28 is Black Aviation
Day and the Jack and Jill Corporation of Wilmington will be in attendance.
VI.
Release of contingency funds for relocation of the 55 and over clubhouse and

ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
MEMBERS PRESENT:   James C. Brown, Mayor Pro Tempore’
            Aldermen Mary “Meezie” Childs, Nelson E. Adams,
            Mary “Stuart” Callari and James F. Powell
MEMBERS ABSENT:   Norman R. Holden, Mayor
            Paul Fisher, Alderman
STAFF PRESENT:      Rob Gandy, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, CMC, City Clerk
            Mike Isenberg, City Attorney
            Chad Hicks, City Planner
I.
Call to Order
Mayor Pro Tem Brown called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m.
II.
Invocation
Mayor Pro Tem Brown delivered the invocation.
III.
Minutes
Alderman Callari moved, seconded by Alderman Powell to approve the minutes from
the October 12 and recessed meeting of October 13. Vote carried.
IV.
Citizen Matters (Non-Agenda)
Mayor Pro Tem Brown acknowledged and welcomed Mayor Kinney, City of Boiling
Spring Lakes, Mayor Shelley Lesher, Town of St. James, and County Commissioner
May Moore.
Mr. William Comninaki, Consultant to Tri-City, Inc., Morehead Farms, Inc and
Dilsheimer Communities of North Carolina, LLC requested to speak about a
proposal submitted to the North Carolina Department of Transportation. He
communicated that he does not believe the State is offering many solutions in
what they have proposed for Brunswick County’s needs for roads. He believes
that the proposal for a two-lane connector by the State will only magnify
traffic congestion in and around Southport. They have proposed an alternative
plan for a four-lane parkway that will draw traffic flow north of the current
bottlenecks. He communicated that he has been in contact with DOT
representatives and they appear positive in their response to their proposal.
Handouts were given to Board members i.e. a map. Following are excerpts from
the proposal:
“Brunswick County’s blistering population growth in recent years, along with
its remarkable popularity with summer vacationers, makes proposed plans for the
133 Connector inadequate to current and future needs. There is an alternative
that we believe is more practical, economical and environmentally friendly.
Please find enclosed several mapping images that support this alternative
vision.
The roadways we are proposing as an alternative conforms to the Preliminary
thoroughfare Plan Improvements for Brunswick County dated 9/29/2000; a document
prepared by the N. C. Department of Transportation’s Statewide Planning Branch.
We are confident our plan represents the vastly more sensible alternative based
on the following considerations:
·   Our roadway’s design is that of a four lane connector “parkway,” stretching
from the intersection of Oak island Road and Highway 211 through to Highway 87-
well beyond existing intersections congested by commercial development;
·   The four-lane parkway, with its 300-foot right of way, can safely
accommodate a speed limit of 55 miles per hour.
·   The parkway’s capacity and other design features make it far more effective
as a hurricane evacuation route;
·   The parkway’s design will create no significant impact on existing
commercial and residential development;
·   Property owners along the right of way have expressed receptiveness to this
alternative, reducing the prospects that condemnation will be necessary;
·   The parkway’s design will leave ample space for new highway infrastructure
that may be needed in order to accommodate the proposed North Carolina
International Port complex at Southport;
·   The parkway can be under construction as early as 2007, with no impact on
existing traffic flows; and
·   The parkway represents a considerable cost savings for the State of North
Carolina.
Another key advantage to this alternative is our intention to propose that this
project be front loaded with private funding pursuant to a public private
partnership whereby the State of North Carolina repays investors pursuant to
terms agreed upon by all parties.”
Mayor Pro Tem Brown and the Board thanked Mr. Comninaki for this presentation.
V.
Public Hearing on request by Walter Knott for a Conditional Use Permit for
Mixed Use Development (commercial/residential), Leggett Building renovation,
114 East Moore Street.
Mayor Pro Tem Brown called the motion to enter public hearing. Alderman Powell
moved, seconded by Alderman Callari to enter public hearing for a conditional

RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF A BRUNSWICK COUNTY COASTAL EVENTS CENTER
WHEREAS, the County of Brunswick has many items to be justly proud of, and the
strength of the people merits the display of the talents and abilities of the
residents of the County, coming from diverse places, with differing backgrounds
and different horizons, and
WHEREAS, it is the desire of the County that there be such a place for the
people of the County to gather to view the fruits of the land and of the
people, to congregate, to deliberate, to plan, to exchange views and engage in
commerce and to help in providing for the growth of Brunswick County, and
WHEREAS, the provision of such a place will be expensive, in terms of hours
consumed, in terms of money, in terms of planning, and in terms of providing
the best possible place for the best possible Coastal Events Center that a
County can have, and
WHEREAS, it is the desire of all involved that the Brunswick County Coastal
Events Center be an example for other counties to follow, that the quality and
superlative nature of the Coastal Events Center should befit its namesake, and
outshine all others.
NOW, THEREFORE, the City of Southport Board of Aldermen are hereby resolved to
wholeheartedly support a BRUNSWICK COUNTY COASTAL EVENTS CENTER, one that
deserves and preserves the high quality of the County, and will be a permanent
example of good people working together with good people to retain a history of
a place named Brunswick.
DULY RESOLVED THIS THE 9th DAY OF NOVEMBER 2006.

A resolution was presented to the Board for adoption proclaiming the 3rd Monday

RESOLUTION PROCLAIMING THE 3RD MONDAY IN NOVEMBER OF EACH YEAR AS CITIZENS FOR
JUSTICE VICTIM AWARENESS DAY IN THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the citizens for justice and the North Carolina Victim Assistance
Network are recognizing the Victim Awareness and Victim Rights on this day; and
WHEREAS, of the millions of crimes reported last year in the United States, in
the State of North Carolina 21,200 crimes against people were reported. In the
state of North Carolina there are over 8, 287 reported sex offenders on file.
WHEREAS, by calling attention to the importance victim awareness and the rights
of victims and the surviving family of victims, the legislation and lobbying
for the rights of victims as stated in the North Carolina Crime Victims Rights
Act of 1999 within our state/communities, these groups hope to improve the
quality and availability of such services; and
WHEREAS, the protection of victims are represented and protected depends on the
awareness of the legislators, citizens, and the communities of the State of
North Carolina, the quality service provided to victims and families represent
a worthy commitment to the citizens of Southport, Brunswick County, and the
State of North Carolina.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport, North Carolina does
hereby proclaim the 3rd Monday of November of each year as “Citizens for
Justice Victim Awareness Day” in an effort to promote awareness in our city,
county, and the State of North Carolina; and urge all citizens to recognize
victims, the families of victims, and the advocates who represent, protect, and
defend victims of crimes and their important work.

XIII.
Application for a Public Beach and Coastal Waterfront Access Project
Chad Hicks, Planner and City Manager Gandy briefed the Board on a proposed
beach and coastal access project. They propose to apply for a grant from CAMA
for a boardwalk/river access project at Fort Johnston beginning on the
waterside in front of the Community Building and heading west, tying into the
existing city pier. The project will include two observation platforms with
steps leading down to the river beach. The City in 1990 authorized W.K. Dickson
to sketch a boardwalk plan that linked Southport Pier to the Community Center;
however, the drawing did not contain the information needed to measure
engineering costs involved in constructing the project. In order to submit an
application package to CAMA, the City of Southport must have a detailed site
plan and a construction cost estimate to submit with the grant. W. K. Dickson
agreed to survey the property and provide the detailed site plan. Estimated
engineering costs for the work is $10,000, and this money cannot be counted
towards any match the city will be required to make should the grant be
awarded. City Manager Gandy stated if the Board were in concurrence with
applying for the grant, staff would proceed with the pre-application process.
He stated if DCM believes that this is a viable project, then staff would
continue with the application process. The Board agreed by consensus that staff
proceed with the grant process.
Alderman Adams asked the City Manager to entertain the idea of installing
public restrooms some place on the site. It was stated that the Fort Johnston
Committee is working on this.

XVI.
Electric Rate Reduction
City Manager Gandy presented a rate adjustment proposal submitted by Alderman
Fisher. In memo to the Board, it was stated that the North Carolina Eastern
Municipal Power Agency’s Rate Committee approved a decrease in the energy fuel
rider of 0.121 cents per KWH. This will decrease the city’s energy rider by
1.5%. The rate will take effect on January 1, 2007. The City’s energy rider is
$0.00837 per KWH. The City will be able to reduce this rate to $0.00716 per
KWH, which will equate to a savings of $1.70 per month for the average
customer. The energy fuel rider was put in place to be able to change the rate
as fuel prices vary. This decrease will maintain the present fund balance. City
Manager Gandy reiterated that this is not a rate change, only an adjustment to
the rider. Alderman Callari motioned to approve the rate adjustment to the
rider, seconded by Alderman Childs, vote carried.

IV.
Citizen Matters (Non-Agenda Items)
Alderman Childs invited the Board and citizens to a reception at the Garrison
House immediately after the meeting.
Mr. Terry Lee, property owner in Southport informed the Board that he
originally purchased 50 lots from Mr. Howard Laughlin who was a surveyor in
this area and the lots were originally platted in 1897. Prior to acquiring the
lots, he visited the Building Inspector’s office to insure that the lots were
buildable. Upon acquisition of the property, he has since sold several lots to
Carolina Southern and three of the lots presently have houses under
construction. Carolina Southern has applied for other building permits and been
denied. Mayor asked what was the explanation given by Mr. Strickland for
denial. Mr. Lee stated that he was told that it was not an approved
subdivision. Mayor Holden asked the City Manager to contact Mr. Strickland and
request in writing within ten (10) days for an explanation as to why the
permits were denied.
Administrative Matters
Alderman Childs motioned to enter Public Hearing on Items V, VI, VII, seconded
by Alderman Callari, the vote carried.
V.
Public Hearing on request by staff to strike from the Unified Development
Ordinance Section 15-4 paragraph 1 that requires a 300’ transition area around
a residential cluster development.
There were no public comments. Chad Hicks, Planning Director explained that
staff is requesting that the 300’ transition area around the border of a
residential cluster development be stricken from the UDO because this
transition area is preventing some developers from using the residential
cluster development tool to develop land. This section of the UDO provides both
the developer and the City alternatives to standard development practices.
Alderman Childs motioned to approve the request by staff to strike from the
Unified Development Ordinance Section 15-4 paragraph 1, which requires a 300’
transition area around a residential cluster development. Motion seconded by
Alderman Callari, vote carried.
VI.
Public Hearing on request by staff to strike from the Unified Development
Ordinance Section 11-1 Note2 (C) that presently allows an unenclosed porch to
protrude into the rear yard not more than ten (10) feet.
There were no public comments. Mr. Hicks explained that allowing a porch to
encroach into the required rear yard presents a problem if the homeowner later
wishes to enclose the porch. By avoiding this encroachment altogether, the
problem of denying a property owner a building permit to enclose a porch can be
avoided.
Alderman Childs motioned to approve the requested change in Section 11-1 of the
Unified Development Ordinance. Alderman Childs seconded, vote carried.
VII.
Public Hearing on request by staff to strike from the Unified Development
Ordinance a portion of Article II Table of Area, Yard, Density and Height,
Footnote 1. This note states that, “Non-Conforming lots which are located in
the Southport Historic Area may be granted front, rear, and side yard setbacks
proportionate to the size of the lot”. Staff requests that front setback be
stricken from the proportionate reduction.
Dale McPherson, member of the Planning Board stated that they are trying to
achieve some uniformity and this change will not affect development already in
place.
Mr. Hicks stated in allowing the proportionate reduction of the front yard
setback could allow the placement of buildings ahead of other structures on the
street. Note 4 of Article 11 allow a reduction in front yard setbacks where
adjoining properties have less than the required setback. By eliminating the
proportionate reduction of the front yard setbacks, the streetscape of
Southport can be protected while allowing owners to use property that may not
meet all the requirements of the UDO.
Alderman Childs motioned, seconded by Alderman Callari to approve the
recommendation by staff to strike from the Unified Development Ordinance a
portion of Article II Table of Area, Yard, Density and Height, Footnote 1. Vote
carried.
VIII.
Public Hearing on the question of annexing Tract A non-contiguous property
owned by the City of Southport
Alderman Childs motioned, seconded by Alderman Callari to enter Public Hearing
to received comments from the public on annexing Tract A non-contiguous
property owned by the City. Vote carried.
There were no comments.
Alderman Childs motioned to re-enter regular session, seconded by Alderman
Fisher, vote carried.

“Due to the increase in traffic we have already experienced, I believe it will
continue to become worse especially with the construction of the new Super
Port. I plan to appoint a Southport Traffic Control Committee to begin
immediately to address this serious problem.
The purpose shall be to advise the federal, state, county and local
municipalities of our situation and begin to look at the present and future to
come up with solutions.
I would like to ask the City Manager to place an announcement in the local
paper asking for anyone interested in this problem that has any experience in
traffic situations to submit a resume’ to the City Manager not later than
January 3, 2007.
Four Southport citizens shall be selected by the following city fathers and
staff that will serve with the four.
I would like to appoint City Planner Chad Hicks, who will serve as Chairman.
Public Services Director Bob Grant and Planning Board Chairman Barbara Clewis
will serve as Co-Chairs. I would also like to ask Aldermen Adams, Fisher and
Powell to serve as well.
I would strongly suggest the committee contact the other five municipalities
Mayors for their interest and input.
Last week, myself and the City Planning Director were at the State Department
of Transportation monthly meeting informing Lanny Wilson, our DOT
representative along with Alan Pope, our DOT district engineer of our plan. Mr.
Pope informed us of a contact person at the DOT Wilmington office to assist us
with our task.
As the State DOT Liaison for the 3rd District, I stand ready to assist. Once
the Committee has been appointed, I would hope a meeting would be set as soon
as possible.”

Executive Session
 
Executive Session Minutes December 14, 2006
 
Public Services Director Bob Grant briefed the Board on the following:
The City of Southport has received notice from William A. White, Esquire,
representing a group of 29 electric utility providers self-termed as the
Potentially Responsible Parties (PRP) who have been identified by the EPA as
being potentially liable for an estimated $30,000,000.00 in environmental
clean-up costs of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCB’s) illegally disposed of by
the agents of the former Carolina Transformer, Inc. (CTI) at their site located
in Fayetteville, NC. CTI conducted business from this site from 1959 through
1984. The notice suggests that other electric utilities along the east coast in
addition to the 29 entities (the PRP group) originally identified by the EPA
may have potential exposure and that the City of Southport may in fact, be
among these additional parties. The PRP group has offered to allow the City and
other parties to join them in defending the EPA claim and arriving at an
ultimate settlement at a cost of $10,000.00 to each entity opting to join. The
notice also suggests that the PRP group may ultimately pursue legal action
against these other entities to offset the costs they may incur in their
negotiations with the EPA on a final settlement of this issue.
The notice provided by the PRP group to Southport suggests that CTI accounts
receivable records indicate that Southport appears to have done some limited
degree of business with CTI in 1977 and 1978. From discussions with former
employees and review of available financial records and other documentation,
the City has found no evidence to date of transactions with CTI in the past.
The records we have found and the recollections of the former employees
contacted suggest that the City did business almost exclusively from 1979 until
2000 with Southeastern Transformer located in Dunn, NC.
Even if the City did in fact conduct business with Carolina Transformer in the
years identified in the notice, the PRP has not provided documentation that any
business conducted might have involved the receipt and processing of PCB
related materials by CTI.
The City has two apparent courses of action it can consider. It can join the
PRP group, which on its face, suggests we feel we may have potential exposure
in this issue; or it can decline to participate with the group in its effort to
reach a settlement with EPA. If the latter option is chosen, it is possible
that the PRP group could pursue a separate action against Southport and other
entities identified by them as having possible exposure in order to recoup a
portion of their ultimate settlement costs negotiated with the EPA.
On the basis of the City’s investigation regarding this matter, staff feels
that at this time, any exposure on the City of Southport’s part would appear
minimal given the in light of the limited documentation provided to us to date
by the PRP group and would suggest that we respond back to them in writing
indicating that we respectfully decline to participate at this time, but would
welcome the opportunity to review any additional documentation relating to
transactions between the City and CTI that may be forthcoming in the future.
After due consideration of the information provided in Mr. Grant’s briefing,
the Board agreed with staff’s recommendation and directed city staff to prepare
a letter to that effect to be forwarded back to the PRP group through attorney
White.
There being no further business, Alderman Childs motioned to re-enter regular
session, seconded by Alderman Callari.
Adjournment – 8:57 P.M.
Alderman Childs moved to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Alderman Callari,
vote carried.

VII.
Public Hearing – Cape Fear Trading Group, Conditional Use Permit for a
Residential Cluster Development at Maple and 9th Street (Stevens Park)
Alderman Callari moved to enter Public Hearing, seconded by Alderman Brown to
receive comments on a request by Cape Fear Trading Group to obtain a
Conditional Use Permit for a residential cluster development at Maple and 9th
Street (Stevens Park).
Mayor Holden stated that the City Clerk must swear in the people wishing to
speak on Conditional Use Permits, which is a requirement of the North Carolina
General Statutes.
Mr. Chad Hicks, Planning Director, explained that the Planning Board
recommended Cape Fear Trading Group be granted a Conditional Use permit for a
residential cluster development at 9th and Maple Street. This CUP will allow
the developers to utilize the residential cluster development section of the
UDO in order to develop the Stevens Park property. He communicated that the
residential cluster development will not increase density on the site but will
provide an alternative development option which will preserve the natural
resources of the land. Mr. Hicks stated if the conditional use permit was
approved, the subdivision would still have to go through the standard approval
process.
For clarification after a question by Alderman Callari, Mr. Hicks stated that
there would be more open space due to the houses being closer together.
Alderman Powell asked if the traffic issue was going to be addressed. Mr. Hicks
stated that it will be addressed in the subdivision review process and the
Planning Board will submit a recommendation to the Board of Aldermen.
There being no other comments, Alderman Callari moved to re-enter regular
session, seconded by Alderman Brown, the vote was unanimous.
Attorney Isenberg stated in approving a conditional use permit, the Board and
Planning Board shall find as a specific finding of fact that the permit will
comply with the following four facts:
a)   That the use will not materially endanger the public health, safety, or
general welfare if located where proposed and developed according to the plan
as submitted and approved;
b)   That the use meets all required conditions and specifications;
c)   That the use will not adversely affect the use or any physical attribute
of adjoining or abutting property, or that the use is a public necessity; and
d)   That the location and character of the use, if developed according to the
plan as submitted and approved, will be in harmony with the area in which it is
to be located and in general conformity with the City of Southport Land Use
Plan.
Alderman Callari moved to grant the conditional use permit based on the above
requirements being met. Alderman Brown seconded the motion; the vote of
approval was unanimous.
VIII.
Public Hearing on a request by Southport Marina, Inc. to obtain a Conditional
Use Permit to construct a dry storage boat building greater than forty feet
(40’)
Mayor Holden announced that the City Clerk would swear in those persons wishing
to speak during this Hearing on the Conditional Use Permit.
Alderman Childs moved, seconded by Alderman Callari to enter Public Hearing on
a request by Southport Marina, Inc. to obtain a Conditional Use Permit to
construct a dry storage boat building greater than forty feet (40’) in height
at the Marina site. Motion carried.
Mr. Hicks, City Planner stated the Planning Board recommended that Southport
Marina Inc be granted a conditional use permit to build a dry storage facility
in excess of forty feet (40’). Marina representatives stated that this request
would allow for a more aesthetically looking building to be constructed as
opposed to a box type structure. The height requested by the Conditional Use
Permit is to allow construction up to fifty-five feet (55’). During
presentation to the Planning Board, they were told that the old dry stack
facility was approximately forty-eight feet (48’) in height.
Mr. Hicks stated that it meets the four requirements of the UDO.
Alderman Powell in observation noted that one Planning Board member voted
against the Conditional Use Permit, and others voted in favor. He noted that it
has only been eight (8) months since the Planning Board recommended that height
restrictions be thirty-five feet (35’) in the City, and asked what was going
on. Mayor Holden noted that the Planning Board would need to address this
question.
Mr. Hicks stated if the conditional use is granted, the entire project will
come back to the Planning Board.
Robert Plassman of 5099 Fernwood Drive and Chairman of the Board of
Adjustments, stated as a resident of Southport, he objects to the Conditional
Use Permit because the proposed building does not fit the harmony of Southport
and it goes beyond the recommendation of the Planning Board. If approved, this
will open the door for others.
Mr. Mark Johnson, representing the Southport Marina, stated that they have
spent numerous hours working and repairing facilities at the marina in order to
have a nice updated marina for the citizens. He explained that the overall
ambience of the facility has been neglected and the group that leases the
marina is working diligently to bring the marina up-to-date and in so doing,
they are trying to embrace the essence of Southport. He stated that the
additional height requested is to create warmth and an inviting feeling o
making the building attractive other than a box. He stated the leasee has
complied with every aspect of the City Code. He explained that the dry storage
is for public access and is the largest part of the marina operations and more
people are opting to place their boats in storage rather than hauling them back
and forth. Mr. Johnson stated the height was originally fifty feet (50’). They
requested the Conditional Use Permit to construct the dry storage building
greater than forty-feet (40’) high.
Mr. Ed Boguskie asked the Board if the height limit is changed, will this open
up other areas. He asked the Board to deny the request.
Mr. John Winter stated that he is a tenant in dry storage and has been for the
past 10 years and would like to see a full size dry stack unit.
No further comments from the public, Alderman Childs motioned to re-enter
regular session, seconded by Alderman Callari. The vote carried.
Attorney Isenberg read the criteria for a Conditional Use Permit.
a)   That the use will not materially endanger the public health, safety, or
general welfare if located where proposed and developed according to the plan
as submitted and approved;
b)   That the use meets all required conditions and specifications;
c)   That the use will not adversely affect the use or any physical attribute
of adjoining or abutting property, or that the use is a public necessity; and
d)   That the location and character of the use, if developed according to the
plan as submitted and approved, will be in harmony with the area in which it is
to be located and in general conformity with the City of Southport Land Use
Plan.
Alderman Fisher stated he does not believe the Conditional Use meets criteria C
and D and believes the building should not exceed the height limit of 40 feet.
He moved to deny the Conditional Use Permit, seconded by Alderman Callari, the
vote of approval was unanimous.

Public Hearing – Non-Contiguous Annexation
Alderman Childs moved, seconded by Alderman Callari to enter Public Hearing on

There were no public comments; however, Alderman Fisher explained that this is
the Swain Tract purchased by the city for its WWTP re-use facility. The
Southeast Sanitary District will treat the sewerage and the effluent will then
be pumped to the spray fields at this location. The plan is to sow some type of
crop, possibly sod. They are currently negotiating with companies pertaining to
this matter. He explained that the City is restricted because this is in the
Sunny Point buffer zone and nothing can be built at this location.
Alderman Childs moved, seconded by Alderman Adams to re-enter regular session,
vote carried.
Alderman Fisher motioned to approve the non-contiguous annexation and to adopt
the following annexation ordinance, seconded by Alderman Brown, the vote
carried.
AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has adopted a resolution under G. S. 160A-58.7,
stating its intent to annex the area described below; and
WHEREAS, a public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at
Southport City Hall at 7:30 pm on January 11, 2007, after due notice; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the area meets the
requirements of G. S. 160A-58.1(b), as modified by Act of the N. C. General
Assembly applicable to the City of Southport and as authorized by the
Annexation Agreement with the City of Boiling Spring Lakes and the resolution
adopted by the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners, as follows:
a.    The nearest point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is not more
than three (3) miles from the primary corporate limits of the City of
Southport;
b.    No point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is closer to the
primary corporate limits of another city than to the primary corporate limits
of the City of Southport except for the City of Boiling Spring Lakes and an
Annexation Agreement has been entered into with the City of Boiling Spring
Lakes allowing the City of Southport to annex said area; in addition, a
resolution has been adopted by the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners
pursuant to G. S. 160A-58.24(e) consenting to said annexation by the City of
Southport;
c.    The area is so situated that the City of Southport will be able to
provide the same services within the proposed satellite corporate limits that
it provides within the primary corporate limits;
d.    The area is not a subdivision; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the annexation of the area is
in the public interest;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina that:
Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G. S. 160A-58.7, the
Annexation Agreement with the City of Boiling Spring Lakes and resolution of
the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners, the following described
noncontiguous property owned by the City of Southport is hereby annexed and
made part of the City of Southport as of the date hereof:

XI.
Public Hearing – Zoning Classification of Open Space
Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Brown, to enter Public Hearing to
receive comments on assigning the zoning classification of Open Space (OS) to
city property located between Bethel Church Road and Sunny Point. Motion
carried.
Mr. Hicks stated that the Planning Board recommended the land near Sunny Point
be designated open space (OS). This designation will not permit any structures
to be built but will allow the city to use the land for municipal uses, such as
park space.
Alderman Powell for clarification stated the rezoning would encompass all the
land annexed (440 acres) and 405 acres of this property is in the Sunny Point
buffer zone, and 35 acres is not. He recalled that the fire department
requested to use this land for practice and drying their hoses, but if this
were the case, the city cannot build anything at this location if the property
is zoned OS. He asked about the possibility of zoning the larger tract and
leaving the 35 acres unzoned. City Attorney Isenberg stated if the property is
not zoned, anything could be located there. He stated due to the wording of the
legal notice, the issue is whether the Board wish to zone the property Open
Space (OS).
City Manager Gandy noted that the wording of the notice was advertised in
accordance with recommendation from the Planning Board.
Chief Cumbee stated that the Fire Department requested and talked about
installing a ramp in order to be able to back trucks up to the pond to test the
fire hoses. It was noted that the property in question is not in the blast
zone.
Alderman Adams stated if the city has an opportunity to extract the 35 acres
not located in the blast zone, then it should be considered. City Attorney
Isenberg stated that the Board could rezone this area later.
Alderman Fisher noted that open space is not a permitted use on page 89 in the
UDO. Mr. Hicks explained that the utility section in the UDO covers what the
city proposes to do with the land.
Mayor asked if this property will have any bearing on the grant, Mr. Grant
stated the statutes dictates that the land be annexed and zoned as
expeditiously as possible.
Larry Coble of 700 Leonard Street cautioned the Board about storage building if
crops are harvested. Alderman Powell stated that the city will not need any
buildings at that location, but will install an irrigation system.
No further discussion, Alderman Powell motioned to re-enter regular session,
seconded by Alderman Callari, vote carried.
Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Fisher, to rezone the property
located between Bethel Church Road and Sunny Point to open space (OS). The vote
was unanimous.
Alderman Fisher asked that the Board revisit page 89 of the UDO and add
government use as a permitted use.
XII.
Preliminary Plat – Osprey Landing
Mr. Hicks in presentation to the Board presented the preliminary plat for
Osprey Landing and noted that the Planning Board recommended approval. He
explained that this 121-unit development is located off Robert Ruark Drive and
the developers have committed to an allocation schedule of 20 units per year
due to sewer considerations. All requirements of the UDO have been met in the
site plan with the exception of continuing discussion in regards to the
potential upgrade of the Forest Oak lift station. WK Dickson is working with
staff to finalize the necessary specifications regarding this upgrade. The
developer is awaiting the outcome of this engineering work in order to finalize
the lift station capacity and design of their lift station as well as what will
be expected of them in the way of contribution to the Forest Oaks upgrade. WK
Dickson has indicated that this engineering work should be completed by the end
of January. Once engineering work is completed, staff and WK Dickson will meet
with the developer and their engineers to formulate the final design of the
wastewater components of their system and resolve any remaining issues relating
to the Forest Oaks upgrade.
Planning Board members were concerned about the added traffic on the existing
road system around this development. The traffic study shows that there will be
some intersections that will drop from a level of service of D to F around year
2011. The developer told board members that surrounding projects were taken
into account during the traffic study and that all required NCDOT standards
were adhered to when conducting the study. This plan shows a reduction in
overall density since it first came before the Planning Board. The developer
has been proactive in lowering the number of home sites in an effort to
mitigate traffic impacts.
Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Brown to approve the Preliminary
Plat for Osprey Landing.  The vote of approval was unanimous.
XIII.
Preliminary Plat – Yacht Basin Phase I (Cape Fear Trading Group)
Mr. Hicks stated the developer asked that the preliminary and final plat be
presented for approval. He explained that this could be granted contingent upon
written approval of the storm water plans and a bond guaranteeing completion of
the storm water system. The plan met requirements of the UDO and storm water
issues were addressed. FEMA has given a favorable review of the plan and W. K.
Dickson has approved the storm water management plans, but no formal written
statement of approval was received prior to this meeting, however; City
Engineers spoke with staff by telephone. Mr. Hicks stated staff recommends
approval of the preliminary plat but see no problem with the final plat subject
to a bond being in place guaranteeing improvements to storm water. If the Board
opts for this, staff will with not sign the final plat until a letter of credit
is provided and the engineers for Cape Fear Trading provide a cost estimate.
The city will be protected if the Board decides to approve the final plat based
on these contingencies.
Alderman Adams asked the Attorney about this option. Attorney Isenberg stated
the Board could approve the plat contingent upon the letter of credit and the
city accepting the cost estimate from Cape Fear Trading Engineers. The Board
may require the letter of credit to be in writing. Mayor stated the Board has
always required the letter of credit to be in writing.
Mr. Hicks explained if the Board approves the preliminary plat, construction
can commence immediately, if both are approved, the developer will conference
with City Engineers and the bond will have to be in place, staff will hold the
plat until everything is agreed upon in writing.
Alderman Powell asked if both plats are approved, how this would affect the
remainder of the development. Mr. Hicks stated storm water plans covers Phase I
and II; however, Phase II of Yacht Basin will have to go through the Planning
Board planned building group review and approval process. In answer to a
question from Alderman Powell, it was explained that W.K. Dickson signed off on
the storm water for Phase Phase II and I. Mr. Hicks assured the Board staff
would be vigilant and insure that storm water is in place. He noted that the
warranty bond is for a one-year period. Attorney Isenberg reiterated that the
city does not have to sign off on the plat until all the improvements have been
installed or as long as there is a letter of credit or bond in place. The plat
cannot be signed off until all improvements are completed and accepted by the
City.
City Manager Gandy explained that there is a performance bond, which will run
whatever time it takes to install the improvements. The warranty bond is
enacted once the infrastructure is in place and accepted after complete build
out.
Alderman Childs asked about the property being under water at the foot of Bay
Street and plans for addressing this issue. Mr. Hicks stated FEMA reviewed the
plans and signed off on them.
Mr. Eric Lappela, Engineer and Developer Manager for Cape Fear Trading
addressed the flooding on Bay Street and they will raise the grade of the
street and raise the storm drainage, which will be above the level of the
highest tidal flooding recorded. Alderman Powell stated the drawings previously
received did not show elevations of stated magnitude. Mr. Lappela explained
that those were preliminary elevations and explained the proposed elevations.
Alderman Powell refuted the elevations cited to handle tidal flooding and storm
water.
Mr. Henry Bridger’s of Leonard Street stated that twice in 2006 sewerage was
flowing in the street during the lunar high tide. Mr. Lappela stated this will
be addressed and they propose to eliminate the backflow which caused the
flooding
Ms. Ann Lee Wiggershaw, stated she was one-third owner in the Provision Company
and owner of the Flavors Ice Cream Shop asked that the Board not approve
anything unless it is in writing, she is concerned about the area in question.
Mayor asked the position of the Board concerning the Yacht Basin Project.
Attorney Isenberg advised that the Board can approve the preliminary plat not
subject to the bond, but if both are approved, the final plat should be
approved subject to a bond or letter of credit.
Preliminary Plat – Alderman Adams moved to approve the preliminary plat for the
Yacht Basin Phase I project, seconded by Alderman Childs, the votes of approval
were 5 ayes, Aldermen Adams, Childs, Brown, Fisher and Callari. 1 no vote,
Alderman Powell.
Motion passed.
Final Plat – Mayor Holden noted that the Board did not receive any information
in the agenda material on the final plat, only the preliminary. Alderman Fisher
requested the information from the engineers be submitted in writing for Board
review.
Board declined action on the final plat.

RESOLUTION HONORING DR. MARTIN LUTHER KING JR. CELEBRATION
WHEREAS, the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Committee was formed and
entrusted with the responsibility to plan a community wide celebration to
appropriately honor this great leader; and
WHEREAS, Dr. Martin Luther King Celebration Committee has selected the dates of
Sunday, January 14th and Monday, January 15, 2007 to hold this celebration with
events scheduled to include a march, youth programs and other similar events;
and
WHEREAS,  the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Celebration has established a mission
statement in which its most important goal is to bring people of the community
together for the purpose of promoting good will and harmony for the betterment
of the entire community; and
WHEREAS, it is extremely important that the great works and deeds of Dr. Martin
Luther King, Jr. be duly remembered, honored and recognized in this most
fitting and proper way.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Mayor and Board of Aldermen of
Southport recognizes January 14-15, 2007 as the official dates of celebration
by the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Committee for the purpose of
honoring this great man and encourage all citizens to participate in the
activities scheduled.

Other Business
Alderman Fisher informed the Board that the 55 & Over Club House has to be
moved out of Stephen’s Park by the first week in February. A decision has not
been made on where to locate the building. They have looked at sites on
Atlantic Avenue, the Alternative School, and the only other option is the Lowe-
White Park. A request was received from Cape Fear Trading Group asking to use
the building as a sales office, however; they have not had time to explore this
option. The earliest they can make the club house a part of the Parks &
Recreation Department is December 2007 or January 2008. There is a possibility
the building can be rented with the utilities being paid, possibly negotiating
that they would move it saving $15,000. He stated the only other option is to
move it and leave it until everything is worked out on where to set it up. The
consensus of the Board is to rent the building and if this does not go through,
move it. Mayor asked that the building be re-named and propose that the City
eventually build a new Sr. Citizen facility.
Alderman Fisher reported that the Parking Committee erected signs along Moore
and Howe. They are currently waiting for a redesign of the signs and looking at
the possibility of lowering them due to visibility. He will make a report at
the next meeting.

JANUARY 16, 2007
SPECIAL MEETING/RESCUE
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING/RESCUE
JANUARY 16, 2007  7:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Mayor Norman Holden
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Meezie Childs, Stuart Callari, Jim Powell,
            Jim Brown and Paul Fisher
ABSENT:         None
STAFF:         Rob Gandy, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
            Mike Isenberg, City Attorney
OTHER:         Tamie Drew, Rescue Squad Chief
            Ellen Dorsett
            Other Rescue Squad Members
Pursuant to notice posted in accordance with North Carolina General Statute
160A-71(b), the Board of Aldermen called a special meeting to consider
personnel/rescue squad matters.
Mayor Holden called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and announced the Special
Meeting is being held to consider accusations and comments regarding the Rescue
Squad Chief.
City Manager Gandy explained that the Mayor and Board members including members
from the public brought concerns to his attention pertaining to the Rescue
Squad Chief harassing a city employee and interfering with his duties. He
stated several people in the community had apparently witnessed those arguments
and reported this to Board members.
·   He also cited the golf cart incident that took place in December on the
west side of town, which was a concern to the Board and himself.
·   The lack of supervision from the Rescue Squad Chief by allowing a member to
ride ATV’s in this manner, including the incident on Caswell Street in
December; and an incident recently in Franklin Square Park.
·   City Manager Gandy stated it was reported to the Mayor and Board that
children have been left unattended at the Rescue Squad Building while members
were on calls.
Mayor Holden asked Chief Drew for comments:
Chief Drew stated that most of the incidents occurred by a general member of
the department who is not a paid member. She stated that she could control him
to a certain extent but limited as to what she can and cannot do because he is
not a paid member. She explained, “This is something Bob Redden enacted when he
was the Chief.” She stated on both occasions when the incidents took place, the
individual was not on the time clock and being paid by the department.
She stated as of today she “had not received any confirmed documentation of
what was entailed the night of the golf cart incident or in fact, the ATV
incident. All this was submitted to Rob as of today, and when I received these,
I guess about noon or 11:00 today, by noon I had suspended that member and
provided Rob with documentation.” She stated she did not address this issue,
because she was not aware of it. City Manager Gandy told Chief Drew that the
Officer on duty, who wrote the report, Officer Connelly, notified her that
night in December. Chief Drew stated the officer notified her at midnight. City
Manager Gandy stated he believed that she was given the details and he finds
out now that he was wrong and want it substantiated today, that there was a
non-member also riding on this vehicle and some other things occurred, but when
the individual in question showed back up at the department upon your request,
he was by himself. Chief Drew stated that he was alone, and of course; she
addressed him about his conduct and told him that it was not appreciated. She
informed him that he was no longer allowed on the golf cart, whether it was
during the day or night. She stated that the Police Officer called her at
midnight, and she got out of bed and went to the Rescue Squad Station to
address this issue with the person in question. His name was Tray Rogers, she
told Officer Connelly to take whatever legal actions necessary, and she would
stand behind him 100%.
Chief Drew stated there are only two-squad members who have children, herself
and the Assistant Chief. She explained that the Board may or may not be aware,
Charles (husband) has her children and they live with him and do not reside
with her. She stated that on one occasion, there was a situation where the
Assistant Chief had her children at the station, this was addressed and she was
told if this happened again, there would be disciplinary action. She stated
that she is aware that this is a major liability, and all the children are
legally old enough to baby-sit themselves.
Chief Drew explained that she was unsure of the comment about the argument with
a city employee.
Mayor Holden stated that he personally observed Chief Drew and a city employee
in front of the Fire Department and it appeared that she was arguing; she had
her finger in the City employee’s face or chest. Chief Drew asked who was the
city employee, Mayor Holden responded it was a city employee, which is a
personnel matter, and she will have to see the City Manager. Chief Drew stated
other than her husband, who is a city employee; she is not at liberty to
discuss everything that has happened. Mayor Holden stated that the Board is not
here to listen to that, only to consider her position as the Supervisor and
Rescue Chief. The Board stated that they did not wish to discuss personal
matters because this was not the purpose of the meeting. Chief Drew told the
Board that she had copies of minutes from her business meetings where matters
have been addressed that were brought to her attention, including disciplinary
actions. She explained that anything brought to her attention by the City
Manager on any occasion, has been addressed.
In answer to a question from Alderman Childs, Chief Drew told the Board that
the member in question was suspended from the department. In accordance with
departmental by-laws, she has no recourse of action other than suspension, but
he has the right to appeal the process to the Membership Committee, and this
Committee will decide whether to uphold the suspension or to terminate him from
the department. She stated that he was suspended today (January 16, 2007)
because this was the first time that she had received any documentation as to
what actually transpired.
Mayor Holden asked Chief Drew if the Police Officer advised her the night of
the incident. She stated that she was told on the night in question that her
golf cart was out; the Police Officer stopped him and advised him to return it.
Mayor asked if he told her who had it, Chief Drew responded yes.
City Manager Gandy stated for the record, that he did not receive a copy of the
expanded report until Friday and gave Chief Drew a copy today. (January 16,
2007)
Alderman Fisher asked how does a person becomes a general member.
Chief Drew explained that a majority of squad members’ vote on a general member
in accordance with the by-laws but they are non-certified. The former Chief,
Bob Redden proposed this and it was adopted into the bylaws. She explained that
non-certified members could ride on the units and participate in the city’s
insurance. This person is working on his certification and is 19 years of age.
Alderman Powell stated anytime Rescue Equipment goes out, it should be logged
in a logbook. Chief Drew stated this has not been done in the 12 years that she
has been with the squad; however, this is something that can be implemented.
Aldermen Adams and Childs asked about the number of general members. Chief Drew
responded that she has five who are working on certification and one to two
general members usually work with a team of two certified EMT’s. Alderman
Childs suggested reducing it to one general member per team. Chief Drew stated
that the general members are covered under the City’s insurance (general
liability) because they are members of the department. Alderman Adams asked
about the number of general members the department can carry on their roster at
any one time. Chief Drew stated they can have no more than 40 general members,
but the by-laws do not address general members. They have 27 certified EMT’s
and 32 total Squad members.
Alderman Adams stated that it is a serious matter if vehicles are being allowed
to leave the squad building and not logged in or out. Chief Drew stated if it
is the Board’s desire, she could enact a policy that all vehicles are to be
logged in and out. She explained that she told the City Manager some things she
could perceive and stop before it happens, and some things she addresses after
it happens.
Chief Drew (after consulting with Ellen Dorsett, a member of the squad) stated
that the county keeps a log of vehicles that are called out when they call into
them and the information is on file when the vehicles leave the Rescue
Building. The golf cart is not considered an emergency vehicle and they would
not have it logged. Chief Drew stated after the incident in December, she took
the keys to the golf cart.
Alderman Powell stated the incident that occurred when the young man ran the
stopped sign on 9th Street, if a car had hit him, it could have come back on
the City’s insurance. Mayor Holden stated the individual who was not supposed
to be in the cart could have come back on the City as a liability.
Mayor Holden read a response from Tray Rogers to the Police Officer who told
him, “other city employees do it all the time” and the reason he did it is
because he was bored.
Chief Drew stated this was no excuse and when she received the documentation
today, this was addressed.
Alderman Callari stated that she is concerned about the number of young people
that she noticed running in and out of the building during her walks. She cited
Friday December 1, as being one of the times and she walked across to see what
was going on and questioned the reason for this. Chief Drew stated this has
never been a problem and the kids could have possibly been her children or the
Assistant Chief’s. She stated kids in that area may not be associated with the
Rescue or Fire Department. Chief Drew stated that it is a public building and
sometimes they have had citizens ask to use the restrooms.
Mayor Holden asked Chief Drew how frequently has she and the City Manager been
in consultation since she became Rescue Chief. Chief Drew stated that she has
met with the City Manager several times recently. In May, when complaints were
coming in from the former Chief, she met approximately 15 times, since last
Thursday, three times and a couple of months prior to that, other than to let
him know major things that were going on in the department, once a month. Mayor
asked Chief Drew if she believed that he offered his services as City Manager,
and she responded, “I do”. She stated anything that she has heard of or may be
a potential problem including the ATV incident, the confrontation between
Police Officer and one of her members, she discussed it with the City Manager.
Alderman Childs asked if there were any other undocumented things from the
Police Department. Chief Dove responded no.
Alderman Callari asked when rescue members stay at the building, do they take
their meals or does the Chief cook and feed them and allow other people to come
and eat. Chief Drew stated the squad building has a stove, microwave and
refrigerator and members are welcome to bring their food, cook, or warm it
because some of them are on duty twelve or more hours. Chief Drew stated other
people that are not a member of the squad are not allowed to come in and eat.
She stated in the past twelve months there is not a situation where she can
recall members or city employees eating with the exception that on occasion the
fire department has utilized the refrigerator and vice versa.
Alderman Powell asked why does Rescue Squad members feel that they can bring
their children to work and other city employees do not, “he believes this is an
accident waiting to happen and the captain guidance is not exactly right and
the ship is wavering down the road.” Chief Drew responded that there has never
been a situation where the parent was not present with their child. She stated
on occasion when her children have been present; she was not being paid by the
City. Mayor reiterated that she was on city property.
Alderman Powell stated when an individual takes on a responsibility as Chief of
the Rescue Squad or Fire Department; they are public officials who are visible
to the public and on duty 24 hours a day. Chief Drew agreed and stated she
cannot shut out her family and children because she is on duty 24 seven’s. She
stated that she upholds her position and believes that she has handled herself
in a professional manner concerning any situation that has occurred under her
leadership as Chief of the Rescue Squad. Chief Drew stated she has stressed
professionalism at all times to squad members.
Chief Drew reiterated that she has discussed the situation about the children
with members and her Assistant Chief.
Alderman Fisher asked Chief Drew if there is anything going on in her personal
life that will interfere with her professional job as Rescue Squad Chief. Chief
Drew responded that there are two different situations, but they will not
prohibit her from doing her job. She stated that because of one situation on
Wednesday night, she has taken steps to insure that a confrontation will not
happen again.
City Manager Gandy asked about the general member status and if they are
allowed to respond to calls the same as certified members. Chief Drew stated
no, because they are not allowed to operate red lights. City Manager Gandy
asked if she was positive this had not occurred and Chief stated yes. She
explained that this situation was addressed, and general members are not
allowed to respond with any type of red lights. They have been told that if
they come upon a wreck, that it would be appropriate for them to turn on some
type of hazard light i.e. a flashlight or to put on emergency flashers if they
use their personal vehicles to avoid being hit. City Manager Gandy stated he
does not believe that it would be appropriate for a general member to respond
in their personal vehicles to the Rescue Squad Building with red lights. Chief
Drew explained stated that her vehicle is considered an emergency vehicle
because she has lights and a siren. There are only two people in any emergency
department i.e. fire and rescue that are allowed to operate a siren. She has
expressed to the Police Officers that if any of her people are caught speeding
through the city, she expects them to be stopped. She discourages members from
using their personal vehicles. On occasion, this has happened when they
received a call at the Long Beach intersection near CVS and she has had to use
her personal vehicle to get through the intersection, but primarily has a crew
at the station. Mayor Holden asked Chief Drew if she was stating that, “No
member of the rescue and the blue van has been out of the City of Southport
within the last two to three weeks with the red light on.” She replied not to
her knowledge. City Manager Gandy interjected that he was talking about members
responding to calls by coming into the department to pick up a rescue vehicle.
Mayor noted that he was going to Wal-mart and before he reached the Pantry,
sirens came on and then red lights from the blue van. Chief Drew explained that
this is an ambulance fully equipped as a first response vehicle, but not used
to transport.
Alderman Childs stated that she is glad the Squad has young people interested
in becoming members and it is most important that they have some older adults.
Chief Drew stated that she understands this concern and noted how the
membership has increased.
Chief Drew explained in response to Alderman Child’s observation, that before
general members were added to the bylaws, they were considered probationers,
which are primarily used for new members that may want to come into the
department that need additional training. Rescue has twenty-seven certified and
five general members, and the individual that is out on disciplinary action is
on probationary status.
Alderman Adams asked Chief Drew if she realized the importance of her members
logging out vehicles and not depending on the county for this information.
Chief Drew stated this could be enacted with the exception of emergency calls.
There being no further questions or comments, Alderman Callari moved to suspend
the Chief until the Board has sufficient opportunity to look into deficiencies
more in-depth and recommends that the City Manager compile a list of these
complaints in order for the Board to review and follow up within forty-five
(45) days. 
Amendment: Alderman Callari amended the motion to place the Chief on probation
instead of temporary suspension for 45 days and the City Manager write a letter
detailing the reprimand including the deficiencies and any other infractions
the Board has found under Chief Drew’s supervision of the Rescue Squad. Motion
seconded by Alderman Powell.
Discussion: Alderman Childs asked if another motion could be made to note the
discrepancies and request the Chief report back in 45 days without placing her
on probation. The Attorney ruled if this motion did not pass, a substitute
motion could be made. Alderman Fisher asked what will the Chief be responding
to, and is she going to be sent something in writing that is clear and
documented. Attorney Isenberg replied that the letter from the City Manager
would state the deficiencies that need to be corrected. Alderman Fisher stated
the Board is aware of various situations and want to insure that the Chief’s
personal life will not interfere with the operation of any other department in
the City. His concern is whether the Code Enforcement Officer can do his job
with the restraining order in place; he is also the Captain of the Fire
Department and an employee of the city with certain duties that must be
performed. Chief Drew stated that they have been in proximity since the
restraining order, however; she does not care to address this issue because it
is her personal life. Mayor Holden and the Board agreed that they do not wish
to discuss any personal matters.
City Attorney asked that the restraining order not be brought up again because
a hearing is scheduled for Friday, it will be determined whether the order is
extended, canceled or modified, and no one will know until after the hearing,
however he is certain that it will be modified to the point that the employee
can perform his job.
Chief Drew assured the Board that she is not trying to keep the employee from
doing his job.
Ms. Ellen Dorsett requested to speak; Mayor Holden explained that this was not
a public hearing.
Clarification: Attorney Isenberg explained to Chief Drew, that she is still the
Chief, but has been placed on probationary status for 45 days. The City Manager
is to write a letter detailing the deficiencies that the Board has found to
exist under her supervision of the Rescue Squad, and she is to set forth those
actions to correct the deficiencies the Board believes exist in the department,

Chief Drew in question to the Board asked how this action coincides with any

Mayor then called for the vote: three ayes, Aldermen Callari, Adams and Powell,
three noes, Aldermen Brown, Childs and Fisher. Mayor Holden voted in the
