VI.
Public Hearing on request by Cape Fear Trading Group to obtain a Conditional
Use Permit (CUP) to allow for mix of commercial and residential use for Yacht
Basin Phase II Project.
Alderman Childs moved seconded by Alderman Fisher, to enter Public Hearing on
the above request, vote carried.
Mr. Hicks explained that due to a parking issue that arose after prior approval
of the storm water plans reported at January’s meeting, the storm water control
facility had to be relocated to accommodate the increased number of parking
spaces resulting in the need for further review of the revised plan. WK Dickson
and the City’s staff have reviewed the storm water plans. Bonding for the
required improvements has been submitted and if the Board approves this
request, the plan will have to continue through the review process as a Planned
Building Group.
Attorney Jeffrey Losee of Roundtree, Losee, and Baldwin, representing Cape Fear
Trading Group gave the Board a brief introduction of the presentation on the
Conditional Use. He indicated that two primary issues have been the subject of
questions from City staff i.e. parking and drainage with emphasis on storm
water. Parking has been designed in accordance with UDO standards and they have
provided parking for existing uses and created additional public parking.
Drainage has had extensive review by WK Dickson on behalf of the City and
representatives of FEMA. All the areas have been addressed and a letter has
been issued to that effect from W. K. Dickson to the City.
(Mr. Lappala and Ms. Burkett was sworn in by the City Clerk before their
presentation)
Ms. Heather Burkett explained the illustration, showing in detail proposed
green space, decks, walkways; signage for the history of Southport, an area for
children i.e. gardens along Caswell Street and benches throughout the
streetscape. Mr. Terry Lee asked if parking would block access to his property
located on the corner. Mr. Hicks stated this project will go through the
Planned Building Group process and will not block access to property owned by
him.
Ms. Ann Marie Rickshaw asked about the type of parking.
Professional Engineer, Eric Lappala demonstrated to the Board with three-
dimensional drawings illustrating storm water, buildings and a water model
showing the impact that this development will have on the area. He stated
concerns were raised about the fill and whether it could be done, and in answer
to the question, they hired Dr. Eric Colson, a Coastal Engineer, who performed
the same coastal engineering studies and models that FEMA does to establish
base flood elevations, modifying the site to the fill condition. He concluded
that the base flood elevation that is required to be set, the first floor level
has to meet those elevations. This report was provided and reviewed by the
City’s Engineer, W.K. Dickson, and FEMA. They concurred that filling the site
would have no adverse impact and raise the base flood elevations that FEMA has
set. In summary, they reviewed the tidal flooding issue, designed the site
grading, and storm water controls to eliminate it as much as they can accept
for extreme rare events. He noted that there will be some water in the street
at the highest tide of record, but it is going to be only a few inches.
Alderman Powell noted a few inconsistencies on the pipe size and asked that
those to be corrected on the final plan. He noted for the benefit of the
public, that the pipe is going to be standing in salt water most of the time,
and questioned the type of pipe that will be used. He stated when Bay Street is
filled in and the tide comes in, there is not going to be as much area for the
water to spread and it will cause problems. Alderman Powell stated it was his
understanding that there is a Statute on the books where anything that is done
on the coast that will effect adjoining properties; owners must sign off. Mr.
Lappala noted on the drawing that the area near the Provision Company is
topographically higher than the area along Bay Street. They are not proposing
to do anything along the street within that area because they do not control
the property. Mr. Lappala stated everything would be constructed to City
standards.
Alderman Childs moved, seconded by Alderman Fisher to re-enter regular session.
Motion carried.
Attorney Isenberg stated in approving a conditional use permit, the Board of
Aldermen shall find as a specific finding of fact that the permit will comply
with the following four facts:
a)   That the use will not materially endanger the public health, safety, or
general welfare if located where proposed and developed according to the plan
as submitted and approved;
b)   That the use meets all required conditions and specifications;
c)   That the use will not adversely affect the use or any physical attribute
of adjoining or abutting property, or that the use is a public necessity; and
d)   That the location and character of the use, if developed according to the
plan as submitted and approved, will be in harmony with the area in which it is
to be located and in general conformity with the City of Southport Land Use
Plan.
Mr. Hicks stated the storm water issues have been addressed, the city is
picking up extra parking and the specific use of the building will have to go
before the Planning Board as a Planned Building Group. The Planning Board
recommended approval and W.K. Dickson sent a letter stating it meets the
requirements of the Unified Development Ordinance and recommended approval.
Alderman Powell stated it is his belief that the storm water design cannot
handle some of the problems in that area.
Alderman Fisher moved to approve the Conditional Use for Cape Fear Trading
stating that it meets all four criteria set forth in the UDO. Motion seconded
by Alderman Adams: Discussion: Alderman Fisher stated in 1945 there was water
standing in the street and 2010 there will be water, it is a low area and he
believes the developers have done the best job that can be accomplished in
improving the City in that specific locale. Mayor Pro Tem called for the vote:
4 ayes, Aldermen Fisher, Adams, Childs and Brown. 1 no vote: Alderman Powell.
Motion passed.
VII.
Public Hearing to consider revisions to the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance, Article 8 “Nonconforming Situations, Section 8-2, Nonconforming
Lots,” Paragraph (B)
Alderman Childs moved, seconded by Alderman Fisher to enter Public Hearing to
consider revisions to the Unified Development Ordinance. Motion carried.
Mr. Hicks stated this issue was directed to the Planning Board from the Board
of Aldermen requesting that they address non-conforming lots and an equitable
way for owners to use these lots. The Planning Board recommended the following
language change.
Article 8. Nonconforming Situations, Section 8-2: Nonconforming Lots, Paragraph
(B):
Strike the reference to (1) and replace with: (A)
Add the following text at the end of paragraph (B):
   “but must be instead combined said adjacent land with the nonconforming lot.
Should the nonconforming lots mentioned above have been legally subdivided and
recorded in Brunswick County prior to August of 1973, then this requirement of
combination shall not apply and those lots legally subdivided and recorded
prior to August of 1973 and never voluntarily combined through an action of the
owner shall each be considered a separate, buildable lot subject to other
requirements of this ordinance. Actions of the owner, which shall constitute a
voluntary combination, shall be, but not limited to, building a structure that
encroaches over lot lines, recording an instrument of combination, or recording
a plat that removes the separate lot lines thereby creating one lot.
Nonconforming lots created, subdivided or recorded after August of 1973 cannot
take advantage of this paragraph. In all cases where a property owner wishes to
take advantage of the exception within this paragraph for pre 1973 lots, the
owner shall present documentation to the building inspector or other designated
city staff which shows that no voluntary combination of the lots has occurred
and that the lots were subdivided and recorded prior to August, 1973.”
For explanation, Mr. Hicks explained the lots that most people were concerned
about were the Smith and Weeks section of town that was recorded in the early
1900’s. Southport adopted its first zoning ordinance in 1973 which required
those lots be combined if the owner owned lots next to each other. He explained
that an individual can now build a house on each of their lots, but this would
require a title opinion stating the lots were never voluntarily combined
through an instrument of recombination or other actions of the owner. Mr. Hicks
noted that the Planning Board had pros and cons concerning this change and
requested that he convey this to the Board. (See Below)
Potential Negatives
1.   Increased burden on water, electric, traffic, and sewer infrastructure and
how necessary improvements to these systems will be funded
2.   Increased storm water runoff to neighboring property owners and the
Southport drainage system with no regulatory controls in place at this time
3.   Driveway cuts that are close together
4.   Possible negative impacts to neighbors
5.   Fire safety concerns
Potential Positives
1.   Eliminates hardships on property owners wishing to build or sell existing
lots
2.   Helps build community interaction and strengthens neighborhood bonds
3.   An increase in the supply of lots could reduce acquisition cost and
provide more affordable housing as stated in the Comprehensive Plan
4.   Could lead to preservation of the character of the existing neighborhoods
5.   Clears out overgrown lots where loitering occurs
6.   Increases the tax base through an increase in housing stock
7.   Makes neighborhoods distinguishable as stated in the Comprehensive Plan
Mr. Ed Boguskie of 502 W. Brown Street asked the Board rather than change the
Ordinance, as provided in Section 8-2A of the UDO, each individual case can
come before the Board of Adjustments and then no precedent will be established.
Mr. Cecil Frank, 503 N. Atlantic asked if it was legal to buy a house that is
constructed on three lots, take the house down and then build three buildings.
Mr. Hicks stated at present, an individual can build on a non-conforming lot if
set backs are met. If a person own three lots, they have to combine them and
build one structure. Mr. Frank stated that Mr. Thorsen’s house was taken down,
and three are being built. Mr. Hicks acknowledged some mistakes were made and
the City is trying to correct them.
Ms. Gwen Midyette, 318 Willis Drive explained that the property in question had
three tax parcel numbers that made the property sub-dividable.
Mr. Phil Joyner, 812 North Caswell Avenue asked if the Board was telling the
citizens what they could do with their property whether it is 33 or 66-foot
lots because he owns several pieces of property on Caswell Avenue. He asked if
the Board was changing the ordinance because an individual was unhappy, and why
the sudden change.
Attorney Isenberg stated the change would make it easier for an individual to
use their thirty-three (33) foot lots. The ordinance currently provides 33 ft
lots to be combined in order to build. The change will provide for an owner to
build on each lot if they have never been combined, in actuality making it
easier to use their property.
Mr. Hicks stated there are approximately 150 thirty-three (33) foot lots in the
City according to County tax data. Mr. Yost asked if the City had
infrastructure in place to handle the construction and growth. Mayor Pro Tem
explained this is one of the negatives cited by the Planning Board and will be
looked into by the City.
Mr. Dale McPherson, 108 South Rhett Street for clarification stated that in
1976 the County for the convenience of tax billing combined properties.
No other comments, Alderman Childs motioned to re-enter regular session,
seconded by Alderman Fisher, vote carried.
Alderman Childs moved to approve the revisions to the Unified Development
Ordinance, Article 8, Non-Conforming Situations, and Section 8-2, seconded by
Alderman Powell. Discussion: Alderman Fisher stated he has reservations about
the change because it does not only effect the Smith and Weeks Subdivision
because most of the property in Southport was developed as 33.3-foot lots. He
explained that he has four 33.3 lots, one on each side of his house, even
though the ordinance states you must have 10,000 square feet to build,
according to this change he could build a house on each lot. He stated that he
want people to use their land but the City’s sewer program is based on usage
per gallon and the City has committed itself to a $13 million sewer program, $2
million upgrade for electricity, and these things should be considered. After
further discussion, by the Board. Mayor Pro Tem Brown called for the vote. 4
ayes, Aldermen Childs, Powell, Adams and Brown. 1 no, Alderman Fisher. Motion
passed
Article 8. Nonconforming Situations, Section 8-2: Nonconforming Lots, Paragraph
(B):
Strike the reference to (1) and replace with: (A)
Add the following text at the end of paragraph (B):
   “but must be instead combined said adjacent land with the nonconforming lot.
Should the nonconforming lots mentioned above have been legally subdivided and
recorded in Brunswick County prior to August of 1973, then this requirement of
combination shall not apply and those lots legally subdivided and recorded
prior to August of 1973 and never voluntarily combined through an action of the
owner shall each be considered a separate, buildable lot subject to other
requirements of this ordinance. Actions of the owner, which shall constitute a
voluntary combination, shall be, but not limited to, building a structure that
encroaches over lot lines, recording an instrument of combination, or recording
a plat that removes the separate lot lines thereby creating one lot.
Nonconforming lots created, subdivided or recorded after August of 1973 cannot
take advantage of this paragraph. In all cases where a property owner wishes to
take advantage of the exception within this paragraph for pre 1973 lots, the
owner shall present documentation to the building inspector or other designated
city staff which shows that no voluntary combination of the lots has occurred
and that the lots were subdivided and recorded prior to August, 1973.”

X.
Mr. John Monaghan, Community Relations Manager of Piedmont Natural Gas Company
– Introduction of Company and discussion of a possible franchise arrangement
with the City of Southport
Mr. John Monaghan, Regional Communications Manager for Eastern North Carolina
introduced Rodney Myers, Regional Executive and Dennis Ergent, Manager of the
Wilmington Operations Center. Mr. Monaghan in presentation introduced Piedmont
Natural Gas, its history, benefits to the City and its citizens, and the
request for a franchise. He stated granting a franchise would allow the company
to run its lines in public rights of way within the City welcome them to the
community and stated that the price for terms of service is regulated by the
North Carolina Utilities Commission and i.e. safety standards. Benefits to the
City would be to receive one-half of piped natural gas excise tax revenues on
utility sales, property tax on facilities, new energy choice for residents and
businesses, and environmentally friendly energy source. Mr. Monaghan stated
they would like to proceed with the formal process of the franchise, and then
the company can advise residents whether they can serve them.
Mayor Pro Tem Brown thanked Mr. Monaghan for the presentation and advised him
that the Board would consider his request and asked that he contact the City
Manager. Mr. Monaghan stated the City Manager was provided a draft franchise
document.
Alderman Fisher referenced Section 2.05 “The company shall not be obligated to
the City or any of its departments or agencies for any tax, license fee, other
fee, or any other payment whatsoever, relating to the rights granted herein
this franchise other than that which is levied by state law.” Monaghan
explained this provision does not mean that if the Board has statutory
authority that it cannot levy fees and taxes provided in the franchise or in
the NCGS.

Alderman Fisher moved, seconded by Alderman Powell to approve the amendment to
the Rescue Squad Ordinance. Vote carried.
PROPOSED EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT
Secs. 6-36-6-40. Reserved.
ARTICLE III. RESCUE SQUAD
Sec. 6-41. Organization
This organization shall be known as the Southport Rescue Squad, and the purpose
of this squad shall be to operate and serve as a volunteer rescue squad in all
ways, means and methods, including but not limited to, training and furnishing
of first aid, protection of lives and properties, search and rescue operations
and the providing of ambulance service to the Southport area on a non-profit
basis.
Sec. 6-42 Officers.
The officers of the rescue squad shall consist of a chief, assistant chief and
other officers as shall be called for in the bylaws of the organization. The
officers shall be elected by the members of squad according to the bylaws of
said squad, and shall serve a term of one (1) year. The results of the election
of officers shall be reported to the board of aldermen for the city at their
regular December meeting of each year. Officers of the Rescue Squad are subject
to the control and supervision of the Board of Aldermen and may be removed from
office at any time by the Board of Aldermen at its discretion.
Sec. 6-43 Bylaws.
The members of the Rescue Squad shall adopt bylaws for the operation of the
squad. The bylaws shall be submitted to the Board of Aldermen for approval and
shall not be effective until approved by the Board of Aldermen. In the event
that the bylaws conflict with state law or local law, the terms of the state or
local law shall govern and prevail.
Sec. 6-44 Duties of the Chief.
The chief shall have general control over all squad apparatus, personnel and
equipment.
The chief shall, at least once a month, arrange for suitable drills or
instruction in the operation and handling of equipment, first aid, rescue work,
and all other matters generally considered to be essential to proper rescue
work and providing for the safety of life. The chief is to see that complete
records are kept of all rescue calls and ambulance calls, condition and
inventory of all vehicles and equipment, personnel and other information about
the work of the squad. The Chief is responsible for the formulation of the
department’s annual operating budget and is responsible for maintaining such
budget.
Sec. 6-45 Assistant Chief.
In the absence of the Chief of the Rescue Squad from the city, or in the event
of his/her being prevented from attending to his/her duties by sickness or
otherwise, the assistant chief shall perform all duties required of the chief,
and shall be clothed with the same authority as the chief.
Sec. 6-46 Duties of other officers.
Other officers of the squad shall assume those duties as designated by the
chief of the squad and they shall perform those duties to the best of their
ability and in a manner upholding their office.
Sec. 6-47 Membership.
The total membership of the squad shall be designated in the bylaws of the
squad. At the time of becoming an active member of the squad, the person must
be at least eighteen (18) years of age and be a resident of the Southport area.
A member must possess a sound mind and body, be a good citizen, and be of good
moral character. A prospective member shall obtain an application form from the
department, and shall have a valid driver’s license. He/she may also be
required to take a physical examination that will be paid for by the
department.
Sec. 6-48 Meetings.
Meetings of the squad shall be held on a regular basis, at least once per
month. Attendance requirements for the squad shall be established in the bylaws
to assure that squad members remain aware of proceedings of the squad and
periodically update their training.
Sec. 6-49 Operations.
Provisions for the operation of the squad shall be established through the
bylaws of the squad and day-to-day operation shall be controlled by a written
set of rules and regulations, which shall be available to all squad members.
The bylaws, rules, and regulations of the squad shall be subject to review of
the Board of Aldermen of the city.  
Attorney Isenberg told the Board he and the City Manager discovered a few
discrepancies in the Fire Department’s Ordinance and will submit those changes
later.

Resolution in support of USS N.C. Submarine Commissioning in Wilmington,
The Board acknowledged a request from Mayor Saffo of Wilmington asking for
support by adopting a resolution endorsing the efforts of the City of
Wilmington to have the official commissioning of the USS North Carolina
Submarine in Wilmington in 2008.
Alderman Powell moved to adopt the following resolution, seconded by Alderman
Childs, vote of approval unanimous.
RESOLUTION ENDORSING EFFORTS TO HAVE THE OFFICIAL COMMISSIONING OF THE USS
NORTH CAROLINA SUBMARINE IN THE CITY OF WILMINGTON IN 2008
WHEREAS, the USS North Carolina (SSN-777) is a Virginia class submarine that
will be the fifth to be named for the 12th State, North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, this ship is presently under construction at Northrop Grumman in
Newport News, Virginia, with construction to be completed in 2007; and
WHEREAS, the citizens of the State of North Carolina are very proud of its deep
and rich heritage in support of a strong military and national defense, and
proud of its service provided by the citizens of North Carolina in support of
the defense of our Country; and
WHEREAS, it would be desirable and appropriate that the commissioning of the
newest submarine carrying the name of the great State of North Carolina be held
in the Port City, Wilmington, whose significant historical and military stature
is unsurpassed.
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:
THAT, the City of Southport Board of Aldermen officially endorses efforts to
have the commissioning of the Virginia Class Submarine, the USS North Carolina,
in the Port City of Wilmington, North Carolina in 2008.
DULY RESOLVED THIS THE 8th DAY OF FEBRUARY, 2008.

Proclamation – Arbor Day
Alderman Childs moved to adopt the following proclamation proclaiming March 16,
2007 as “Arbor Day” in the City of Southport, seconded by Alderman Callari, the
vote was unanimous.
ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/IMAGES/0-0-0-46.jpg]
WHEREAS, in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of Agriculture that a special day be
set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS, this holiday called Arbor Day , was first observed with the planting of more than a million trees
in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS, Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS, trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and water, cut heating and cooling
costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air, produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for
wildlife, and
WHEREAS, trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes, fuel for our fires, and
beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic vitality of business areas, and
beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE,  I Norman R. Holden, Mayor of the City of Southport, N.C. do hereby proclaim March 16, 2007
as ARBOR DAY in the City and urge all citizens to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees and
woodlands, and
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote the well-being of this and
future generations.
DATED, this 8th day of March, 2007.
S/Norman R. Holden, Mayor
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/IMAGES/0-0-0-
48.jpg]                                       [https://export.amlegal.com/media/
199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/IMAGES/0-0-0-50.jpg]

Alderman Callari moved to adopt the following resolution, seconded by Alderman
Childs, the vote was unanimous.
2007 ELDER ABUSE AWARENESS RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, Elder Abuse is the broad term used to identify mistreatment of elder
and disabled adults, and abuse and neglect of elderly and disabled adults is
one of most under-recognized and under reported social problems in this
country; and
WHEREAS, the magnitude of the problem is likely to increase for several
reasons, especially with the anticipated rise in the number of elderly
population; and
WHEREAS, mistreatment can take many forms: physical abuse, emotional abuse,
sexual abuse, neglect by caretaker, self-neglect and exploitation, financial
exploitation; and
WHEREAS, between 500,000-5 million people suffer elder abuse every year; and
WHEREAS, it is estimated that approximately only one out of every 14 cases of
elder abuse is reported; and
WHEREAS, elder abuse is preventable.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport recognizes the month of
June as Elder Abuse Awareness month and encourages all residents and other
jurisdictions to become more aware of this problem and join in the prevention
of Elder Abuse.
DULY ADOPTED THIS THE 8TH DAY OF MARCH 2007.
/s/ Mayor Norman R. Holden
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, Clerk

V.
Public Hearing on the Unified Development Ordinance text change. The purpose of
the language change is to adjust sections of the UDO that were affected when
the Planned Unit Development land area requirements were reduced.
Mayor Holden called for a motion to enter Public Hearing on the above language
change to the Unified Development Ordinance. Alderman Callari moved to enter
Public Hearing, seconded by Alderman Childs, vote carried.
Mr. Chad Hicks stated language changes to the Unified Development Ordinance are
necessary to clean up sections of the UDO that still refers to old acreage
requirements in which the change will make residential cluster developments a
conditional use. He stated that Section 15-1: Residential Cluster Development
has always been handled as a conditional use, but it is not worded as such in
the UDO.
The second change is regarding the Planned Unit Development requirements for
land inside the city limits that was reduced to eight (8) acres. Some places in
the UDO still refer to the 25 acres inside and outside of the city limits,
Section 15-2: Residential Cluster Developments.
There were no comments from the public. Alderman Childs moved, seconded by
Alderman Callari to close the Public Hearing and to re-enter regular session,
vote carried.
Alderman Childs moved to approve the changes to the Unified Development
Ordinance as presented. Motion seconded by Alderman Callari, the vote was
unanimous.
ARTICLE 15. RESIDENTIAL CLUSTER DEVELOPMENT
Section 15-1: Purpose and Intent; Definition
For the purposes of this section, a residential cluster development is defined
as:

VI.
Airport Commission
Mr. Owen Garner, member of the Brunswick County Airport Commission told the
Board that Congress last year stopped funding special projects, which included
the airport expansion, and that this places the airport in a dilemma. Their
plans are completed to extend the runway, permits are in hand, and land
purchases complete. The Commission cannot let a contract without funds. The
state has made a formal request to the County Commissioners to advance some
funds to get the project back on track.
Mr. Howie Franklin, Airport Manager, stated that the Aeronautical Council for
the State of North Carolina met in Brunswick County for the second consecutive
year. He stated one of their priorities is the Brunswick County Airport, and
the entire state believes that Brunswick County Airport is poised to make an
economic impact on the local economy. The last economic impact study presented
to the Board showed that the airport is bringing in $26 million a year. He
explained that the Aeronautical Council is appointed by the Governor to develop
aviation and airports across the state. The Council believes that if the
Brunswick County Airport expands its runway to 5,500 feet, it will quadruple
the number of dollars into the economy. He stated people in Raleigh are
lobbying for transportation monies, and the Department of Aviation has stated
if transportation monies were received, then they would fund the remainder.
Therefore, many people are working towards this end, including the county. If
they do not receive funding, the Airport will stay as is for the next 8 to 12
years. Mr. Franklin stated that $6.3 million is needed; $2.3 million will build
the road, and $4.2 million to install the runway. The entire project will cost
over $10 million. If the runway is constructed, they believe the rest will take
care of itself. Mr. Garner explained that the federal funds derives from the
aviation trust fund which is a result of ticket taxes and aviation fuel tax,
etc. and can only be used for aviation. Mr. Garner asked the Board if they
believe in this project, to put in a good word to the County Commissioners.
Mayor stated that he would have the City Manager contact Mr. Garner.

Mr. Chad Hicks stated Steven’s Park Phase I preliminary and final Plat reviews
have been completed. The City received the storm water comments from W. K.
Dickson, City Engineers and everything is in order. If the preliminary plat is
approved, the developer is also asking for final plat approval. The bond amount
has been set and reviewed by City Engineers. The bond is not in place, but Mr.
Hyson stated that it would be, if the final plat is approved.
Mr. Hicks explained in response to a question from Mayor Holden, that Stevens
Park is the name of the overall development, but on the plat that was dedicated
to the City; it is called the Stevens Park Municipal Recreational Property. Mr.
Hicks stated the municipal parkland has been separated from the development and
the land donated to the City has been deeded and recorded. Alderman Fisher
asked if the construction of the ball fields is in this phase. Attorney
Roundtree replied yes, and that they do not intend to develop the residential
area without completing the ballparks in a manner that the city will be proud.
Alderman Powell asked about Stevens Park Boulevard and if the developer has any
intention to let the boulevard go through and exit near Robert Ruark. He
explained the initial drawings that were presented, they discussed another
access and it is not showing on the plans that he reviewed. Mr. Hicks explained
that it would be shown on Phase II.
In response to Alderman Adams question concerning bonds being in place, Mr.
Hicks replied that City Engineer, W. K. Dickson reviewed the amount of $4.5
million, which was deemed sufficient. He stated the preliminary plat may be
approved without the bond being in place, and if the final plat is approved,
the City will not sign off until the bond is received. (City Manager Gandy
noted the construction bond guarantees that the city will have the resources it
needs in place should something happen and the surety bond will be issued to
the developer who will actually install the utilities and guaranteed for one
year).
Alderman Fisher asked about the date for construction of the ball fields.
Attorney Roundtree stated during discussion with members of the LLC, they
intend to have the fields ready by early 2008.

the assurance in writing, which stated April 2007, but in no event, no later
than August of 2007. The vote was unanimous for final plat approval. Passed

Dosher Hospital – Abandonment of Certain Right of Way – Fodale Avenue
City Attorney Isenberg stated the City was contacted by Dosher Hospital because
the property that they acquired in exchange with the city for parking, the
surveyor determined that part of the pavement of Fodale Avenue is outside of
the city’s right of way. Dosher has asked the city to consider closing a
portion of Fodale Avenue so the title can revert to them and they can add it to
the land acquired, which will give them the necessary footage needed to
finalize their construction plans. A map was shown depicting the right of way
including pavement.
City Manager Gandy stated if the Board wishes to pursue this, a Public Hearing
is required and the notice posted. City Attorney Isenberg stated that before
the Board votes; he wants the deed in hand conveying to the City the part of
the land that is outside of the city’s right of way, so the city will not lose
any rights of way. City Attorney Isenberg stated the Board may adopt the
resolution calling for the Public Hearing in June to consider the matter, but
no action on the order closing the road until the City secures the deed for the
other part.

RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN RELATING TO THE AWARD AND

WHEREAS, The City of Southport is a qualified grant recipient as defined under

WHEREAS, the Southport Board of Aldermen are extremely pleased and grateful to
the Trustees of the Clean Water Management Trust Fund for providing prior
funding assistance to allow for the acquisition of a 406 acre site (CWMTF
2005B-513) that will provide for the environmentally conscious management of
highly treated effluent, and

$3,000,000 grant that will allow the City to ultimately decommission its

fostering the anticipated reopening of an estimated 625 acres of shellfish
waters presently closed to shellfish harvesting, and

above referenced grant at its meeting of August 14, 2006 in acknowledgement of

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED BY THE SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN THAT:

with the conditions, terms and stipulations of the Agreement and applicable
Exhibits as forwarded by the Clean Water Management Trust Fund to the City for
execution. The Board of Aldermen hereby designate Robert W. Grant, AICP, Public
Services Director for the City of Southport and Patty D. Miller, Finance
Director for the City of Southport as representatives of the City fully
authorized to execute any and all documents or transactions relating to CWMTF
Grant Agreement 2006A-529 on behalf of the City and the Board of Aldermen.

EARTH DAY PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, our home, this planet earth, is getting smaller and more crowded as
its population grows and its resources are abused; and
WHEREAS, since the first Earth Day in 1970, the Clean Air Act has made the
nation’s air cleaner, the Clean Water Act has improved water quality; and the
Endangered Species Act has attempted to preserve ecosystems to maintain the
variety of species; and
WHEREAS, following the principals of reduce, repair, reuse and recycle,
residents can improve their environment; and
WHEREAS, preservation is easier and less expensive than restoration; and
WHEREAS, Earth Day provides an opportunity for members of the community to
study, learn and teach local activities which will contribute to protecting our
planet’s ecosystem.
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport hereby proclaims Sunday
April 22, 2007 Earth Day, to be observed by all citizens in ways to better
understand, appreciate, and preserve the resources of our earth, and especially
the resources of this area.

MAY 7, 2007
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING
MAY 7, 2007       4:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:          Norman R. Holden, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, James C. Brown, Jim Powell, Meezie Childs,
            Stuart Callari and Paul Fisher
STAFF:         Rob Gandy, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, Clerk
            Mary Russ, Tax Collector
            Patty Miller, Finance Director
Pursuant to notice duly advertised and posted, a Special Meeting was held at 4:
00 p.m., Aldermen Chambers, 201 E. Moore Street, Southport, N. C. for the
purpose of receiving a report and recommendations from the Tax Committee.
Alderman Fisher, Chairman of the Committee, informed the Board that two public
meetings were held, one at the ILA Hall located at 211 W. 10th Street on
Friday, April 27, and Monday, April 30, the Garrison House. The purpose of the
meetings was to receive comments from citizens on the 2007 tax revaluation, and
the effect that it will have on their property. The Committee comprised of
Aldermen Fisher, Adams, Brown, Rob Gandy, City Manager, Patty Miller, Finance
Officer and Mary Russ, Tax Collector, met with several citizens and received
comments and information. The Committee formulated three (3) resolutions for
Board consideration:
RESOLUTION CONCERNING THE BRUNSWICK COUNTY 2007 PROPERTY REVALUATION AND THE
CURRENT RATE OF THE DOSHER HOSPITAL TAX
WHEREAS, North Carolina counties are responsible for the valuation of property
for use in applying property tax rates in all local government jurisdictions;
and
WHEREAS, counties must undertake revaluation of property at least every eight
years according to State law, and
WHEREAS, the intent of revaluation of property on a periodic basis is to ensure
a fair system of property taxation; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick County has chosen to conduct revaluation of property on a
four-year cycle as permitted by State law; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick County has conducted a revaluation to be effective in 2007;
and
WHEREAS, property owners in the City of Southport and other municipalities in
Smithville Township have raised questions concerning the fairness of the
revaluation, including methods used to determine values; and
WHEREAS, the fairness in applying values to individual property is the
cornerstone of the property tax system as determined by State law, and all
necessary steps should be taken to ensure the fairness of the property
valuation process; and
WHEREAS, the 2007 revaluation is fraught with numerous errors and used
antiquated data invalidating the fairness of the system and was based on sales
figures from two years ago, which were higher than they currently are; and
WHEREAS, the system does not allow for changes in the market value and sales
between revaluation periods; and
WHEREAS, the current tax laws do not allow for a homestead exemption for all
citizens of North Carolina and current senior exemption is outdated and
unrealistic; and
WHEREAS, the current property tax system is regressive, outdated and not fair
to all citizens of North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, this revaluation will place an undo tax burden of the citizens of
Southport and Smithville Township who will also be responsible for paying the
four cents tax to Dosher Hospital that will only add to their tax burden; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Hospital stands to receive an unanticipated increase of
approximately $1.7 million in revenues at the four cents tax rate with the new
revaluation figures from the county; such windfall to be financed by the
residents of Smithville Township; and
WHEREAS, the Dosher Hospital tax rate was first established years ago to
support and maintain the operation of the hospital and was used to finance the
bonding debt and therefore should be used to retire the bonds and not for the
purchase of equipment or general expenses; and
WHEREAS, local governments, by law, must begin their budget preparation efforts
by establishing a revenue neutral property tax rate, and we believe Dosher
Hospital should use the same method as it applies to their current tax rate.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen that
the Dosher Hospital Board of Directors closely examine the current tax rate of
four cents and the increased amount of revenues expected to be generated by the
county revaluation and see if this amount can be reduced or eliminated to help
ease the tax burden for the citizens of Southport and Smithville Township as
these citizens have helped support the Hospital for many years and now is the
time for the Hospital to assist those citizens by reducing or eliminating the
current four cents tax rate.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Dosher Hospital Board of Directors join the
efforts recommended by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen to participate
in a task force to work with our state representatives, county commissioners
and municipal elected officials to prepare changes to the property tax system
for the 2008 session of the General Assembly to find ways to reduce the tax
burden on our citizens. Such changes and considerations should be, but not
limited to, a new system to replace the antiquated taxing system, the expansion
of the tax base to include a land transfer tax, homestead exemption on primary
residences for all North Carolina citizens, a realistic elderly exemption and
the establishment of a floating rate tied to the bond for Dosher Hospital.
DULY RESOLVED, by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen this the 7th Day of
May 2007.

RESOLUTION CONCERNING BRUNSWICK COUNTY 2007 PROPERTY REVALUATION
WHEREAS, North Carolina counties are responsible for the valuation of property
for use in applying property tax rates in all local government jurisdictions;
and
WHEREAS, counties must undertake revaluation of property at least every eight
years according to State law; and
WHEREAS, the intent of revaluation of property on a periodic basis is to ensure
a fair system of property taxation; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick County has chosen to conduct revaluation of property on a
four-year cycle as permitted by State law; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick County has conducted a revaluation to be effective in 2007;
and
WHEREAS, property owners in the City of Southport and other municipalities in
Smithville Township have raised questions concerning the fairness of the
revaluation, including methods used to determine values; and
WHEREAS, the fairness in applying values to individual property is the
cornerstone of the property tax system as determined by State law, and all
necessary steps should be taken to ensure the fairness of the property
valuation process; and
WHEREAS, the 2007 revaluation is fraught with numerous errors and used
antiquated data invalidating the fairness of the system and was based on sales
figures from two years ago, which were higher than they currently are; and
WHEREAS, the system does not allow for changes in the market value and sales
between revaluation periods; and
WHEREAS, the current tax laws do not allow for a homestead exemption for all
citizens of North Carolina and the current senior exemption is outdated and
unrealistic; and
WHEREAS, the current property tax system is regressive, outdated and not fair
to all citizens of North Carolina.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen that
Brunswick County give strong consideration to the following suggestions and
recommendations:
1.   to put aside the 2007 tax revaluation until the tax system can be studied
by our state legislators, county commissioners, municipal officials and the
Dosher Hospital Board.
2.   that the county take the lead in establishing a task force to rework the
current system and recommend changes to the appropriate levels of government.
The task force, working with our state representatives, county commissioners,
municipal elected officials and Dosher Hospital Board prepare changes to the
tax system for the 2008 session of the General Assembly.
3.   the considerations to be studied by the task force are, but not limited
to:
a.   an updated system to replace the antiquated taxing system.
b.   expansion of the tax base to include a land transfer tax, homestead
exemption on primary residences for all citizens of North Carolina, a realistic
elderly exemption, a new fair system to conduct revaluations, and the
establishment of a floating rate tied to the bonds for Dosher Hospital.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the local representatives to the General Assembly
support this effort and support any bills currently in the legislature that
will reduce the property tax burden on the citizens of North Carolina.
DULY RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen this the 7th Day of
May, 2007.

RESOLUTION CONCERNING BRUNSWICK COUNTY 2007 PROPERTY REVALUATION AND REQUEST
FOR STATE ASSISTANCE IN REVAMPING CURRENT TAX SYSTEM
WHEREAS, North Carolina counties are responsible for the valuation of property
for use in applying property tax rates in all local government jurisdictions;
and
WHEREAS, counties must undertake revaluation of property at least every eight
years according to State law; and
WHEREAS, the intent of revaluation of property on a periodic basis is to ensure
a fair system of property taxation; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick County has conducted a revaluation to be effective in 2007;
and
WHEREAS, property owners in the City of Southport and other municipalities in
Smithville Township have raised questions concerning the fairness of the
revaluation, including methods used to determine values; and
WHEREAS, the fairness in applying values to individual property is the
cornerstone of the property tax system as determined by State law, and all
necessary steps should be taken to ensure the fairness of the property
valuation process; and
WHEREAS, the 2007 revaluation is fraught with numerous errors and used
antiquated data invalidating the fairness of the system and was based on sales
figures from two years ago, which were higher than they currently are; and
WHEREAS, the system does not allow for changes in the market value and sales
between revaluation periods; and
WHEREAS, the current tax laws do not allow for a homestead exemption for all
citizens of North Carolina and current senior exemption is outdated and
unrealistic; and
WHEREAS, the current property tax system is regressive, outdated and not fair
to all citizens of North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, the current system relies too much on property taxes and needs to be
studied and the tax base expanded.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen and
other municipalities request that the 2007 revaluation be put aside until the
system can be studied by our state representatives, county commissioners,
elected municipal officials, and the Dosher Hospital Board. Additionally, it is
requested that the county take the lead in establishing a task force to rework
the current system and recommend changes to the appropriate levels of
government. The task force, working with our state representatives, county
commissioners, municipal elected officials and Dosher Hospital Board prepare
changes to the system for the 2008 session of the General Assembly.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the local representatives to the General Assembly
support this effort by recognizing the current property tax system is outdated
and study ways to expand the tax base to include a land transfer tax, a
homestead exemption on primary residences for all citizens of North Carolina, a
realistic elderly exemption, a new fair system to conduct revaluations, the
major overhaul of the Machinery Act, and the establishment of a floating rate
tied to bonds for Dosher Hospital.
DULY RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen this the 7th Day of
May, 2007.

VII.
Public Hearing to amend Article 9, Section 9-1 “Open Space District” of the
Unified Development Ordinance (Open Space Permitted Uses)
Alderman Powell motioned to enter Public Hearing to receive comments on Article
9, Section 9-1 “Open Space District” of the Unified Development Ordinance, to
read “Area of special public interest that should be placed in a zone protected
from any development other than improvements or uses undertaken by the City of
Southport,” seconded by Alderman Fisher, vote carried.
Mr. Hicks explained that the Unified Development Ordinance does not allow the
City of Southport to use land zoned open space. In order to avoid future
issues, the Planning Board and staff recommends that the Unified Development
Ordinance table of permitted uses be modified to allow the City of Southport to
use any land zoned open space for improvements or uses that the Aldermen deems
necessary.
There were no public comments.
Alderman Adams motioned, seconded by Alderman Fisher to close the Public
Hearing and to re-enter regular session, vote carried.
Alderman Fisher moved to amend Article 9, Section 9-1 “Open Space District”,
seconded by Alderman Powell, vote was unanimous.
ARTICLE 9. ZONING DISTRICTS AND ZONING MAP
Section 9-1: Establishment of Zoning Districts, and the Purpose Thereof
(L) OS Open Space District.
Amend as follows: Areas of special public interest that should be placed in a
zone protected from any development other than improvements or uses undertaken
by the City of Southport.
VIII.
Public Hearing to amend Article II, Table of area, yard, density and height
requirements note 3” of the Unified Development Ordinance, to read “Shall be
determined based upon the requirements of Conditional Use Permit issued by the
Southport Board of Aldermen, and the addition of note 6 to read: eight (8)
acres in the City limits, 25 acres in the extraterritorial jurisdiction.
Alderman Powell moved to enter Public Hearing to receive public comments on
amending Article II, Table of area, yard, density and height requirements. Note
3” of the Unified Development Ordinance to read “Shall be determined based upon
the requirements of Conditional Use Permit issued by the Southport Board of
Aldermen, and the addition of note 6 to read: eight (8) acres in the City
limits, 25 acres in the extraterritorial jurisdiction.” Motion seconded by
Alderman Adams, vote carried.
Mr. Hicks stated the Planned Unit Developments are critical to the management
of growth in Southport. In using Planned Unit Developments, developers and the
City can work together to design and build developments that are assets to the
community. When the Unified Development Ordinance was written, the ability to
negotiate with developers on area, yard, density and height requirements was
removed. He believes in some instances, PUD’s are beneficial to the city and
the residents of the developments if more area is given to open space or
preservation of on site wetlands. If the Board approves this language change,
protections will be in place to prohibit a poor plan from being approved. He
stated the Board of Aldermen must approve all developments and lot standards,
and the current restriction of six dwelling units per acre in a PUD will remain
in place. The purpose of this change is to allow more room to collaborate with
developers to ensure that projects in Southport are designed to a standard that
fits Southport.
Addition of Note 6
Note six needs to be added to the table in Article 11 to account for the PUD
acreage requirement change that was previously adopted, which is a housekeeping
matter and will not change the substance of the UDO.
Mr. Ed Boguskie member of the Zoning Board of Adjustments addressed several
questions to Mr. Hicks and he responded accordingly. Mr. Hicks explained that
amending this article would allow more flexibility and each situation will
stand on it own and the density will not be affected.
Alderman Powell moved to close the Public Hearing and to re-enter regular
session, motion seconded by Alderman Fisher, vote carried.
Alderman Fisher moved to amend Article 11 as recommended by Planning Board and
staff, seconded by Alderman Powell, vote carried.
ARTICLE 11. TABLE OF AREA, YARD, DENSITY, AND HEIGHT REQUIREMENTS
Amend note 3 as follows:   Shall be determined based upon the requirements of
Conditional Use Permit issued by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
Add note 6:    8 acres in City limits
      25 acres in Extraterritorial Jurisdiction

Unified Development Ordinance by striking the sentence, “The applicable yard
setback requirements for single-family structures shall be based upon the
square footage of the lot.

Resolution – Clean Water Act of 2007
Alderman Fisher moved to approve a resolution of support for the Clean Water
Act of 2007, seconded by Alderman Powell. The vote was unanimous.
RESOLUTION OF SUPPORT FOR THE CLEAN WATER ACT OF 2007
WHEREAS, North Carolina’s continued prosperity depends on protecting the
State’s water resources for current use and future generations; and
WHEREAS, North Carolina is expected to grow by 3.5 million people to exceed 12
million by the year 2030, placing pressures on the State’s water resources and
local water providers; and
WHEREAS, North Carolina’s businesses, traditional and emerging industries all
depend on reliable supplies of clean water, reasonable utility costs, well
maintained water infrastructure and an attractive natural environment; and
WHEREAS, the 1998 Clean Water Bonds delivered significant benefits to North
Carolina communities and citizens, supporting 1,103 projects in 97 counties,
which
>   helped create or retain 42,000 jobs
>   corrected major regulatory violations in 97 communities
>   addressed failing septic systems and contaminated wells in 59 counties
>   resulted in 50 communities receiving sewer service for the first time
>   encouraged regional efficiencies, sound planning and conservation
practices; and,
WHEREAS, North Carolina’s public water, sewer and storm water utilities will
require Investments totaling $16.63 billion to keep pace with necessary
improvements and population growth over the next 25 years, including $6.85
billion in investments within the next five years.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
urges the North Carolina General Assembly to enact the “Clean Water Act of
2007”, which provides for a $500 million bond issue to be expended over the
next five years, and an annual appropriation of $50 million in recurring
funding to address urgent needs.
DULY ADOPTED THIS THE 10th DAY OF MAY, 2007
/s/ James C. Brown, Mayor Pro Tem
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk

Proclamation – Motorcycle Safety Awareness Month
Alderman Fisher moved, seconded by Alderman Adams to adopt the following
Proclamation designating the month of May as Motorcycle Safety Awareness Month.
Motion seconded by Alderman Adams, vote carried.
PROCLAMATION
Motorcycle Safety Awareness Month
May 2007
WHEREAS, motorcycling is a popular mode of transportation and recreation for
thousands of citizens across Brunswick County, the State of North Carolina and
the United States; and
WHEREAS, North Carolina has 146,041 registered motorcycles, including 1,944 in
Brunswick County, and 260,000 licensed drivers with motorcycle endorsements or
motorcycle learner’s permit; and
WHEREAS, it is important that the citizens of Brunswick County, its cities and
municipalities, be aware of motorcycles on its 2,023 miles of roadways, and
recognize the importance of sharing the road with motorcycles; and
WHEREAS, the safe operation of a motorcycle is enhanced through a combination
of rider training and experience, good judgment, and a knowledge of traffic
laws and licensing requirements; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick County Concerned Bikers Association/ABATE of NC is committed
to increasing the safe operation of motorcycles by promoting rider safety
education programs; their goal is to alert the motorists of Brunswick County,
its cities and municipalities to “Look Twice and Save a Life”; and
WHEREAS, Motorcycle Awareness Month is designed to increase public awareness
about motorcycles and to encourage their safe and proper use among motorcycle
riders.
NOW, THEREFORE, the Southport Board of Aldermen, do hereby proclaim the month
of May 2007 as Motorcycle Awareness Month in entity and urge all citizens to
call this observance to the attention of all our citizens.
THIS, the 10th Day of May 2007

            Mike Isenberg, City Attorney
            Chad Hicks, City Planner

The Board acknowledged a request from Mr. Ed Boguskie of 502 West Brown Street
on behalf of the Southport Historical Society and the Cape Fear River Pilot’s

V.
Public Hearing on request by Dosher Hospital to close permanently a portion of
the western end of Fodale Avenue at its intersection with the eastern line of
Howe Street.
Alderman Childs moved seconded by Alderman Powell to enter Public Hearing, vote
carried.
Attorney Isenberg explained that it was determined during survey of property
for the City and Dosher Hospital, that a portion of the pavement for Fodale
Avenue near the terminus of Howe Street was misaligned and partially out of the
City’s right of way. A portion of the pavement is owned by Dosher Hospital,
they have provided the city a deed that will give the City the pavement located
on their property, and they in turn request that the City close a similar
portion on the North side of Fodale Avenue. Attorney Isenberg communicated that
he has the deed, which has been executed by hospital officials. Mayor Holden
asked if this action would close Fodale Avenue, and Attorney Isenberg responded
that the pavement would not change at all.
There were no questions from the public.
Alderman Childs moved, seconded by Alderman Adams to close the Hearing to re-
enter regular session, vote carried.
Alderman Fisher moved, seconded by Alderman Callari to adopt the order closing
permanently a portion of the western end of Fodale Avenue at its intersection
with the eastern line of Howe Street. Vote carried.
STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA
ORDER
BRUNSWICK COUNTY
THAT WHEREAS, G. S. 160A-299 requires that when a city proposes to permanently
close any street or public alley that the Board of Aldermen first adopt a
resolution declaring its intent to close said street or alley and calling for a
public hearing on the question; and
WHEREAS, G. S. 160A-299 further requires that the resolution to close the
street or alley be published once a week for four successive weeks prior to the
date of said hearing, that a copy thereof be sent by registered or certified
mail to all owners of property adjoining the portion of the street or alley to
be closed as shown on the county tax records, and that notice of the closing
and public hearing be prominently posted in at least two places along the
street or alley to be closed; and
WHEREAS, on April 17, 2007, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport
passed a resolution proposing to close the following described portion of
Fodale Avenue ,and also calling for a public hearing on said question:
Beginning at the point where the northern line of Fodale Avenue intersects the
eastern line of Howe Street and run thence South 70 degrees 06 minutes 48
seconds East 154.78feet with the northern line of Fodale Avenue to an iron
stake; run thence South 30 degrees16 minutes 46 seconds East 46.88 feet to a

VI.
Public Hearing on the City of Southport’s Wastewater Master Plan – Carter
Hubard, W. K. Dickson
Alderman Childs moved to enter Public Hearing, seconded by Alderman Powell, the
vote of approval was unanimous.
Mr. Carter Hubard, Engineer with W.K. Dickson, presented a power point
presentation on the Wastewater Plan; he outlined the project summary, funding
and schedule and selected alternatives including the grant/loan amount. In
presentation, he stated that the City’s WWTP was originally built in the 1960’s
and expanded in the 80’s discharging into the Intracoastal Waterway at the
mouth of Cottage Creek. He stated the facility is in compliance but may not be
re-permitted due to regulations and it is costly to maintain and does not
satisfy the long-term needs. Mr. Hubard elaborated further on the wastewater
disposal site, projections for the future i.e. growth trends, transmission
facilities, regional wastewater treatment i.e. expansion of SBDSD WWTP from 0.5
to 2.0 MGD with interlocal agreement and infiltration of treated effluent.
Funding will come through the Clean Water Management Trust Fund grant of $1.8
million for the disposal site, and $3 million for subject wastewater project.
Grants and loans in the amount of $8,952,000, impact fees and user rates, which
would help to reduce the loan and monthly rates.
Mr. Gene Hart of 822 Memory Lane asked about solid waste and sending treated
water to Sunny Point.
Ms. Suzanne Dorsey of 808 Indigo asked about testing of the aquifer.
Mr. Hubbard responded to all questions.
Mr. Ed Boguskie of 502 Brown Street asked Mr. Hubard the following questions:
·   Will treated water be sent to Sunny Point? Mr. Hubbard responded yes.
·   What will happen to the sludge: Sludge will be handled under a separate
contract
·   Will the groundwater aquifer be monitored: Mr. Hubbard responded that these
types of facilities usually have groundwater monitoring.
No further discussion, Alderman Callari moved to close the Hearing and re-enter
regular session, seconded by Alderman Childs. Vote carried.
VII.
Presentation by Dr. Suzanne Dorsey, Executive Director of Bald Head Island
Conservancy on barrier islands research and environmental issues.
Alderman Brown introduced Dr. Suzanne Dorsey, who spoke on research the
conservancy is doing on Bald Head about barrier islands and other environmental
issues.
Dr. Dorsey did a presentation on the barrier islands and their importance to
the mainland (Southport). She stated that her goal is to form a network of the
barrier island communities and to inform people about the importance of these
islands. They have established a private non-profit organization that is
working to protect the islands. She informed the Board that she is available to
assist and share information about her work to save the barrier islands.

XVI.
Review of Resolution supporting efforts of Brunswick County – Smithville
Township Hospital tax issue
Mayor Holden stated that he supports the two-cent tax reduction, however; if
the County Commissioners and the Hospital Board does not agree on the
Committee’s recommendation, he will support presenting this matter to the
legislature by January. However, he trusts that the Hospital will take the
initiative to work with the City. The City and Hospital has had a good
relationship in the past and has always been able to work amicable i.e. closing
a street for the hospital expansion, paying their electric bill amongst other
things the city has contributed.
Alderman Fisher moved to approve the following resolution, seconded by Alderman
Callari, the vote of approval was unanimous.
Mayor Holden asked that a copy of the resolution be sent to Senator R. C.
Soles, Representatives Bonner Stiller and Dewey Hill.
RESOLUTION
RESOLUTION SUPPORTING EFFORTS OF BRUNSWICK COUNTY-SMITHVILLE TOWNSHIP HOSPITAL
TAX ISSUE
WHEREAS, a four-cent tax is levied on property in Smithville Township for
support of the J. Arthur Dosher Memorial Hospital located in Southport; and
WHEREAS, Smithville Township includes areas governed by Brunswick County and
the municipalities of Bald Head Island, Caswell Beach, Oak Island, Southport
and St. James; and
WHEREAS, a revaluation of property in Brunswick County, including Smithville
Township, has taken place with new, substantially increased, property values
effective in the 2007-08 fiscal year; and
WHEREAS, government entities in Smithville Township have been approached by
property owners in Smithville Township concerning the impact of increased
property values and its effect on the four-cent tax levied on property in
Smithville Township for support of J. Arthur Dosher Memorial Hospital; and
WHEREAS, the dramatically increased property values were not anticipated at the
time of the most recent ballot questions in May, 2000; and
WHEREAS, there is a need to achieve a financial solution to the Smithville
Township property tax issue brought by escalating property values without
harming the J. Arthur Dosher Memorial Hospital or Brunswick County’s bond
rating; and
WHEREAS, the government entity best able to address the Smithville Township
property tax issue is the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
hereby fully encourage and support the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners
in its efforts to secure a reasonable solution to the Smithville Township
property tax issue; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the City of Southport hereby agree to fully
participate as a partner with Brunswick County in efforts to secure a
reasonable solution to the Smithville Township property tax issue.
This the 14th day of June, 2007.
/s/ Norman R. Holden
Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, Clerk
City Manager will send a copy of resolution to Commissioner May Moore and
ascertain their next move.

City Manager Gandy made reference an editorial written in the Wilmington Star
with a misleading headline “Southport Secret Meeting Cheats Public.” The
meeting was not called by the City of Southport, it was a tax meeting held by
Brunswick County representatives and their legal department determined whether
it should be an open meeting without consulting city staff. He has attempted to
contact the editorial staff at the Wilmington Star, but has not received a
response. Alderman Callari agreed that the Star News owe the City an apology.
She stated her elation by seeing people downtown on Wednesdays at the Farmer’s
Market.

to have one committee.

Rescue Squad – Mayor Holden stated that he received a letter from Mayor Shelly
Lesher of St. James with reference to one of the Southport Rescue Squad members
speeding through the town, disregarded posted speed limits and instructions
from Security to stop. Because of this action, he requested the City Manager to
direct Chief Drew to relieve the young man of his duties immediately, and if
she does not follow through with this action, he will then request the City
Manager to remove her as Rescue Chief. Once the budget has been adopted, he
requested the City Manager and the County EMS meet to begin negotiations to
place the City Rescue Squad under the County EMS. He stated that citizens are
being double taxed; this is evidenced by the Rescue Squad budget and the amount
of taxes being paid to the county. Mayor Holden stated he is ashamed of what is
happening with the Rescue Squad and believes the City is running a nursery
school and strongly suggest that the City go with the County. He referenced the
recommendation submitted by the City Manager several years ago, recommending
this action. He believes the response time will be quicker and City can save
money. He vowed to stay involved until the City and County Rescue Squad is
merged.

V.
Dosher Hospital Tax - Discussion
Mayor informed the Board that he talked with Commissioner Moore about Dosher
Hospital and the requested tax reduction. He asked Alderman Fisher to comment
on his conversation with Commissioner Moore.
Alderman Fisher stated that on June 28, 2007, May Moore, County Commissioner
called him to ask for a position from the city regarding the Dosher Hospital
tax. The County Commissioners and the municipalities in Smithville Township
proposed on June 26, 2007 to Dosher Hospital Board that the current tax be
reduced from $.04 to $.02 (cents). Commissioner Moore advised him that the
Chairman of the Hospital Board (Sizemore) made a counter offer to reduce from
$.04 to .03 (cents) Commissioner Moore wanted to know Southport’s position
regarding this proposal. He stated she was of the opinion that the $.02 cents
is appropriate to service the bond and to keep Dosher Hospital an excellent
care facility. Alderman Fisher stated it is his belief that the Board should
continue to support cutting the tax by $ .02 (cents). He stated that Alderman
Adams supports the $ .02 tax cut.
Today (later) June 28, 2007, Commissioner Moore called to say that the Hospital
Board in an emergency meeting had withdrawn their offer to negotiate the rate
from $.04 to .03. Alderman Fisher motioned that the Board of Aldermen supports
the County Commissioners and recommend a referendum in November to cut the tax
rate from $.04 to .02. Alderman Powell seconded the motion and the vote of
approval was unanimous.
Alderman Fisher also complimented staff on an excellent budget that meet the
needs of the city in addition to reducing the tax rate below revenue neutral
and retaining a fund balance, and he stated his pleasure at being able to give
city employees a 5% across the Board cost of living, where most cities only
give 2 to 3%.
He asked that the City watch the CAMA Grant for Fort Johnston, and in the event
the City does not receive the grant, funds (budgeted) be allocated to other
projects.
VI.
Southport Rescue Squad
Mayor Holden stated that the City has had problems with the Rescue Squad over a
period of time and he referred to a proposal presented by the City Manager in
2003, asking Brunswick County EMS to provide options for the provision of
emergency services within the City of Southport, however since this time the
figures have changed. He asked the City Manager to contact Mr. Randy Thompson
of Brunswick Emergency Services to schedule a meeting with Aldermen Callari,
Powell, City Manager and himself and to invite the Rescue Chief. He stated it
is his belief that rescue services can be combined and bring the level of
services up by being as progressive as other municipalities who have gone under
the County EMS; this will save monies and increase the response time.
Alderman Callari stated the Board a few years ago recommended that the
Southport Rescue Squad become self sufficient, and this has not been
accomplished.

Administrative Matters
Review and approval of amendment to the existing contract between the City of
Southport and W. K. Dickson authorizing additional hydrology analysis of the
City’s spray field area.
In memo to the Board from Bob Grant, Public Utilities Director, he asked that
the Board consider approval of a request to amend the contract with W. K.
Dickson for the Phase II Wastewater Master Plan. If approved, this will
authorize additional work by the hydrologist to analyze the city’s effluent
management site off Sunny Point Road for rapid infiltration, which involves the
use of ponds to contain and allow for the effluent infiltration. This is an
alternative concept to utilize the site other than an irrigated crop management
site. Mr. Hubard had previously recommended that the city analyze the site’s
potential for an alternative technology. Alderman Fisher stated that the
Wastewater Committee recommends approval of the contract amendment. He then
moved to approve the amendment to the existing contract between the City of
Southport and W. K. Dickson authorizing additional hydrology analysis of the
city’s spray field area. Alderman Powell seconded the motion and the vote of
approval was unanimous. (Copy of Contract Amendment on file in the Clerk’s
Office, Finance and Public Utility Department)

Alderman Childs moved, seconded by Alderman Powell to adopt the following
Resolution honoring the Cape Fear River Pilots and proclaiming Saturday, August
18, 2007 as “Cape Fear River Pilots Day” in the City of Southport.  The vote of
approval was unanimous.
RESOLUTION IN HONOR OF THE CAPE FEAR RIVER PILOTS
WHEREAS, the City of Southport and the Southport Historical Society have joined
together to honor all our Cape Fear River Pilots, both past and present and;
WHEREAS, Saturday, August 18, 2007 has been selected as the day to honor those
in this profession and the men who carry out the commission of the Cape Fear
River Pilot’s Association “ To make certain that the passage of ships between
the Atlantic Ocean and Sunny Point or Wilmington via the Cape Fear River is
safe and expeditious” and;
WHEREAS, on this day, the River Pilots who went to sea and returned no more
will also be properly honored and will be foremost on the minds of all that
knew and loved them.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen that
they hereby proclaim Saturday, August 18, 2007 as “Cape Fear River Pilots Day”
in the City of Southport and ask that our citizens join in the festivities of
this day that will include a ceremony at Fort Johnston, tours of the Pilot
Boat, a memorial service at the Lost Pilots Monument and an exhibit at Fort
Johnston.
DULY RESOLVED THIS THE 12TH DAY OF JULY, 2007
/s/ Norman R. Holden

V.
Public Hearing on request by Cameron Smith to rezone a 33-foot portion of
parcel #238GA023, 708 East Moore Street from R-10 (residential) to BD (business
district).
Alderman Childs moved to enter public hearing on the rezoning request, seconded
by Alderman Brown, vote carried.
Mr. Chad Hicks, City Planner presented a request from Mr. Cameron Smith to
rezone a portion of a 33-foot strip on Moore Street that currently borders
property that is zoned business district (BD). The property in question is
zoned R-10. Mr. Smith has requested that 33 feet be subtracted from R-10 and
added to BD. (Business District)
Mr. John Barbee, 712 E. Moore Street stated the property in question has been
zoned residential for approximately 50 years and the City’s Land Use Plan shows
the property as residential and stated he does not see the need to expand the
business district.
Mr. Dana Stutz, 703 East Moore Street stated his concerns about the amount of
traffic flow and the type of business Mr. Smith is proposing.
Mr. Chad Hicks, City Planner, stated the property in that locale is currently
zoned R-10 (residential) and BD (business district). The extension would give
them 33 foot more in the BD (business district). The Planning Board recommended
the property be rezoned, however, the future Land Use Plan has the entire area
zoned residential including the area that is presently zoned commercial.
No further comments, Alderman Childs moved to re-enter regular session,
seconded by Alderman Powell. Vote carried.
Alderman Adams stated that 145 feet of the property is zoned business, and he
posed a question asking how would rezoning a 33’ strip allow the developer to
do anymore with 33 ft than he can with the 145 feet lot.
Mr. Cameron Smith of Harbor Oaks explained that he currently has two
residential lots which are odd shaped and as a result, unable to sell. He
wishes to convert it back to one lot, which will be 100 feet wide on the road
frontage and 70 feet on the river. He is proposing to take the 33-foot strip,
which was originally access for the second lot, and use it with what he already
has which will make it a 100 x 70 lot.
Alderman Fisher stated that Mr. Smith has always done a credible job with his
projects; however, he is concerned bout the business district closing in on
residential. If rezoned to Business District. The UDO provides for 150
permitted uses for the lot in question. However, there are many uses in that
provision he does not believe should be included and it needs to be changed to
Conditional Use so that the Board can view what is going to be constructed. He
stated if the property was sold and did not violate the rules, the Board would
have no reason for rejection. He moved to deny the rezoning request, seconded
by Alderman Adams. The vote of approval was unanimous. Alderman Fisher asked
that the Planning Board review this matter between commercial and residential,
and present a recommendation to the Board.

board, all plans and documents must be final and ready for actual construction.
All engineering, survey, building, and civil plans must include a signed and

effective immediately:
SEE EXHIBIT A

citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be entitled to the same
privileges and benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said territory
shall be subject to municipal taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10.
Section 3.  The Mayor of the City of Southport shall cause to be recorded in
the office of the Register of Deeds of Brunswick County, and in the office of
the Secretary of State at Raleigh, North Carolina, an accurate map of the
annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the County Board
of Elections, as required by G. S. 163-288.1.

XVI.
Review of Resolution in support of the Cigarette Litter Prevention Program
Alderman Fisher moved to adopt the following resolution in support of the
Cigarette Litter Prevention Program, seconded by Alderman Brown, vote
unanimous.
RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, Brunswick County and the City of Southport have laws against
littering, including cigarette litter defined as partially smoked cigarettes,
cigarette butts and filters, matches, lighters and packaging; and
WHEREAS, Keep Brunswick County Beautiful, an affiliate of Keep America
Beautiful, has enacted a vigorous program to reduce cigarette litter in our
community; and
WHEREAS, there is a general lack of public awareness that cigarette butts are
litter; and
WHEREAS, there is a legitimate concern that cigarette litter, because of its
size and light weight, is often carried with storm water runoff into our local
surface waters, thus polluting our environment; and
WHEREAS, most cigarette filters are made of plastic cellulose acetate – which
is neither biodegradable nor digestible – lasts for many years and is often
consumed by wildlife which kills the bird, reptile, fish, and turtle eating it;
and
WHEREAS, the remaining tobacco in a discarded cigarette contains several
residual alkaloids, including nicotine, and, if consumed, poses a health hazard
to small children and animals; and
WHEREAS, smoldering cigarette litter increases the risk of fire; and
WHEREAS, the various community clean-up groups in our town find thousands of
cigarette butts at each periodic clean-up event.
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen goes on
record in support of the Cigarette Litter Prevention Program and urge our
citizens not to litter in any manner or form.
DULY RESOLVED THIS THE 14th DAY OF AUGUST 2007.
Attest: /s/ Regina W. Alexander, Clerk   /s/ Norman R. Holden, Mayor

Such signs shall not exceed thirty-two (32) square feet in area display face
and no more than ten (1) feet in height. Construction signs shall not be
erected prior to the issuance of a building permit and shall be removed within
seven (7) days of the issuance of a certificate of compliance. The vote of
approval was unanimous.
