XIV.
Amendment to the City’s Cemetery Ordinance (Bond)
Mr. Strickland, Building Inspector per memo to the Board addressed concerns
about Northwood Cemetery. He communicated that some of the funeral homes are
using grave digging machines and he fear that they may disturb adjacent
gravesites. If this occurs, the city has no mechanism in place to recoup
damages to properties and recommended a $500 bond be imposed to assure that the
sites will be protected.
Mayor Holden suggested an agreement between the City and funeral homes be
written in order to protect each other. Alderman Adams talked about the
condition of the roads in Northwood Cemetery and people getting bogged down due
to the sandy conditions and the City needs to do something about the roads. He
stated that he asked Bob Grant, Public Services Director, to get proposal(s) on
the cost of paving the first two roads, and if need be, pave another next
fiscal year. The proposal totaled $21,350. Alderman Callari asked that the
excess sand from grave digging not be placed in the roads, which contributes to
the problem.
Alderman Fisher motioned, seconded by Alderman Child, to approve the $500 bond
and amend the ordinance as recommended by the Building Inspector. The vote was
unanimous.
Chapter 5
CEMETERIES
Sec. 5-1. Definitions.
Lot shall refer to the entire tract or piece of property purchased for the
purpose of burial consisting of one (1) or more individual plots or gravesites.
Plot shall refer to one (1) individual gravesite within a lot.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-2. Lot sales.
(a)   All sales of lots in city-owned cemeteries shall be made only by the city
at prices approved and set by the board of aldermen from time to time. All
persons desiring to purchase a lot in a city-owned cemetery shall apply to the
city cemetery superintendent who shall be authorized to issue a deed for said
lot upon payment of the purchase price therefore in full. Lots may be purchased
on installment plans approved by the board of aldermen. In the event that any
installment due under an installment plan remains unpaid for ninety (90) days
after the due date, the purchaser, without notice, shall forfeit all rights to
said lot and said lot shall be made available for sale by the city to another
party.
(b)   Resale of a lot in a city-owned cemetery is hereby prohibited except as
specifically provided herein. In the event that a person owning a cemetery lot
desires to relinquish ownership of the same, the person shall notify the city
cemetery superintendent and the city shall repurchase the cemetery lot at the
current price as set by the board of aldermen.
(c)   No interment or burial of a body or other disposition thereof, in a city-
owned cemetery, shall be made until the purchase price for the cemetery plot
has been paid in full.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-3. Permits.
No interment or burial of a body, or other disposition thereof, shall be made
in a city-owned cemetery until a permit is issued by the city. In applying for
a permit hereunder, the applicant shall furnish the city with the following
information concerning the deceased: name, date of death, home address,
birthplace, date of birth, next of kin, and address of next of kin.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-4. Time of interment.
All local and non-local funeral directors or other persons in charge of any
funeral shall be required to pay a ten dollar ($10.00) fee determined by the
Southport Board of Aldermen  to the city before a permit is issued for an
interment for Mondays through Fridays. Before a permit will be issued for an
interment on Saturdays, Sundays or legal holidays, the funeral director must
notify the City of Southport at least twenty-four (24) hours, or one (1)
working day, prior to the time of burial, or pay a seventy-five dollar ($75.00)
fee equal to three (3) times the regular fee  to reimburse the city for
overtime salaries and other costs incurred by the city in connection with
weekend interments. The city shall have an appropriate employee on call and
available every weekend for this service, if interment is allowed on Saturdays,
Sundays and legal holidays. (Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-5. Record of interments and removals.
A complete record shall be maintained by the city of all interments,
disinterments and removals from any city-owned cemetery. The record shall give
the name of the cemetery, section, lot number, size and location of graves on
the lot, and the names of all persons buried on said lots. Records shall be
permanently preserved by the city.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-6. Opening of graves.
No grave within a city-owned cemetery shall be opened or otherwise disturbed
nor shall any body be removed from any grave without a permit from the county
health director and the consent of the lot owner and immediate family of the
deceased.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-7. Depth of graves.
All graves shall be dug at least four and one-half (4 1/2) feet in depth to the
pit. The width of graves above pit level shall be not less than four (4) inches
greater than the box width, on the side. All graves shall be made approximately
level with the lot and all extraneous material shall be removed from the lot
premises.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-8. Maintenance of lots.
No person shall place, or cause to be placed, on any lot in a city-owned or
city-operated cemetery, any stone or other object, other than an approved
marker or monument. Boundaries of all lots shall be marked by corners which
shall be set by the city at no additional cost to the lot owner. Mowing and
maintenance of the common areas of city-owned or city-operated cemeteries shall
be the responsibility of the city. The common are is hereby defined for
purposes of this section as all areas of said cemeteries other than those lots
or gravesites which have been sold or conveyed by the city, or registered to an
owner thereof in the city records, or in which interment or burial of a body
has taken place. As to these lots and gravesites, it shall be the
responsibility of the owners thereof to mow and maintain the same.
(Ord. of 12-3-91; Ord. of 11-13-03)
Sec. 5-9. Vaults or liners.
Due to the sandy soil conditions within the area, and the fact that markers
cannot be prevented from sinking or being covered by sand, vaults or liners
shall be required for all burials and interments in city-owned cemeteries.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-10. Removal of debris.
All materials and other debris shall be removed from a gravesite  and the
surrounding area raked and leveled  immediately upon completion of interment by
the funeral director. Dead flowers, tents, and other such items shall be
removed within three weeks of the burial. A bond of Five Hundred Dollars
($500.00) shall be required of all funeral directors and shall be refunded on
request after a final inspection by the City.  (Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-11. Erection of foundations.
All foundations for monuments and footstones shall be erected and installed
under the supervision of the city cemetery superintendent and shall not be
erected without prior written approval from said city cemetery superintendent.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-11.1. Cremation.
(a)   Each lot in a city-owned or city-regulated cemetery which is used for the
burial of cremains shall be no less than three (3) feet by eight (8) feet in
size. Each lot may contain up to three (3) plots per gravesite for the burial
of cremains.
(b)   There shall be only one (1) above-ground monument for each lot used for
the burial of cremains which above-ground shall not be larger than twenty-four
(24) inches in width and sixty (60) inches in length.
(c)   Monuments marking individuals plots or gravesites within the lot shall
not exceed three (3) feet by two (2) feet and shall not extend above ground
level.
(d)   Cremation remains must be buried no less than three (3) feet in depth.
(Ord. of 9-14-00(1))
Sec. 5-12. Northwood cemetery.
The following regulations shall apply to Northwood Cemetery, Section G, and H
only:
(1)   Only one (1) family monument shall be permitted on any one (1) lot.
(2)   All monuments shall be set even with the property lines and shall not
extend over the property lines in any direction.
(3)   All foundations of monuments shall be no less than eight (8) inches in
depth and shall not rest on the liner cover.
(4)   All monuments shall not exceed twenty-four (24) inches in depth nor sixty
(60) inches in height.
(5)   For a single plot or single gravesite, monuments shall not exceed twenty-
four (24) inches in width.
(6)   For lots consisting of two (2) or three (3) plots, monuments shall not
exceed forty-eight (48) inches in width.
(7)   For lots consisting of four (4) plots, monuments shall not exceed sixty
(60) inches in width.
(8)   For lots consisting of five (5) or more plots, monuments shall not exceed
ninety (90) inches in width.
(9)   Footstones shall conform as to material with the material comprising the
monuments on the lot. Foundations for monuments and footstones shall be
composed of a hard course aggregate, sand and cement in proportions not less
than 1:3:5, and well-compacted in place. Foundations shall be at least as wide,
and as long as, the base stone of the monument with footstone resting upon it
and must not project above the lot surface.
(10)   The placing of glass vases on cemetery plots or lots is hereby
prohibited. In addition, the planting of flowers or shrubs, except at the plot
or lot corners, is hereby prohibited. Metal receptacles for cut flowers placed
within twelve (12) inches of the centerline of the marker and buried to allow
mowing are allowed and encouraged.
(11)   The placing of a coping or other enclosure around lots or plots is
hereby prohibited, except when the coping or enclosure is ground level and will
not interfere with maintenance of the cemetery.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-13. Violation; penalties.
In addition to being a misdemeanor pursuant to G.S. 14-4, the violation of this
chapter shall subject the offender to a civil penalty pursuant to section 1-6
(c) of this Code of Ordinances.
(Ord. of 12-3-91)
Sec. 5-14. Regulation of penalties.
(a)   All lots or squares properly registered or established within the City of
Southport Old Smithville Burying Ground prior to April 13, 1989 are hereby
recognized as valid by the city provided that (1) said lots, squares or
gravesites do not encroach upon any lot, square or gravesite registered or
established prior to the registration of said lot, square or gravesite and (2)
there are no remains or other evidence of burial whatsoever contained within
said lot, square or gravesite.
(b)   That each person or family claiming a lot, square or place of burial in
Old Smithville Burying Ground is responsible for having a qualified
professional archaeologist determine and certify to the city that no remains or
other evidence of burial are located within the desired lot or square. Said
qualified archaeologist shall obtain a permit from the city prior to
investigation. Such certification shall be made before issuance of a burial
permit or before December 31, 2000, whichever occurs sooner. This certification
shall be at the expense of the lot owner.
(c)   In the event that any lot, square or gravesite is determined to encroach
on a prior lot, square or gravesite, all encroachments shall be removed within
forty-five (45) days of such determination and notification by the city at the
sole expense of that party encroaching upon the other lot, square or gravesite.
(d)   No person shall be buried in Old Smithville Burying Ground unless a
burial permit is first obtained from the city and no burial permit shall be
issued prior to certification that said site is available as set forth herein.
(e)   All burials within Old Smithville Burying Ground shall comply with all
other applicable local or state statutes or ordinances.
(Ord. of 5-11-00(2), §§ 1--10; Ord. of 7-13-00, §§ 1--5; Ord. of 4-13-02, §§ 1-
-5)

SEPTEMBER 26, 2007
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN  SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 26, 2007 5:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS  SOUTHPORT, NC
 
PRESENT:          James C. Brown, Mayor Pro Tempore’
            Aldermen Stuart Callari, Nelson Adams, Jim Powell and Paul Fisher
STAFF:         Regina W. Alexander, Clerk
            Mike Isenberg, Attorney
            Chad Hicks, Planning Director
            Bob Grant, Public Services Director
ABSENT:         Norman Holden, Mayor
            Meezie Childs, Alderman
            Rob Gandy, City Manager
Pursuant to notice duly advertised and posted, the Southport Board of Aldermen
met in special session on the above date to discuss a natural gas franchise
ordinance with piedmont natural gas and to explore options for land
acquisition.
I.
Call to Order
Mayor Pro Tem Brown called the meeting to order at 5:10 p.m.
Mr. R. L. Willoughby, Vice President of Power Services, attended the meeting at
the request of staff to consider a study to determine the financial and
operational impact Piedmont Natural Gas Ordinance would have on the city if a
franchise were granted. Board members voiced concerns that granting a natural
gas franchise would affect the city’s electric fund. Alderman Fisher stated $19
million is stilled owed on the current debt and the City needs to know the
implications natural gas would have on the electric sales i.e. tax receipts,
the company’s short and long range business plans and whether or not they will
seek new or existing customers.
Alderman Adams stated concerns about the company being selective with larger
customers. Some of the City questions have not been answered. The City could be
left with loss of electric sales.
Attorney Isenberg stated that he and the City Manager requested specific
language on certain aspects of the agreement, but to no avail.
Mr. Willoughby stated it appears the issue is loss in electric sales; his
company is prepared to assist the City. He presented the following primary
issues to be evaluated with an estimate range from $7,500 to $15,000.
1.   Piedmont business plan (what areas of the city will be served)
2.   Impact on electric sales
3.   Possible gross receipt tax implications
4.   Franchise language and
5.   Opportunities to utilize open trenching for other utilities for future
underground
6.   Evaluation of negotiated issues by city to date
7.   Enhancements to long-term municipal under grounding program and other
negotiated concessions available.
Alderman Adams questioned why hire a consultant until the Board can gauge
whether or not citizens want natural gas and suggested a Public Hearing.
Mayor Pro Tem Brown stated the city needs more than a financial study.
Attorney Isenberg stated that he and staff reviewed other franchises before
writing the draft for the city.
Mr. Willoughby stated once the scope of the work is defined, this would
determine the cost of the study.
Alderman Fisher told the Board that he requested funding from ElectriCities to
assist in financing the study.
The consensus of the Board was to hire Mr. Willoughby’s Company to: 1) review
Piedmont’s business plan, 2) the impact on electric sales and, 3) gross receipt
tax implications. Alderman Fisher motioned to contract with Power Services
Management for Utilities at a cost up to $7500 to study the three areas
specified, seconded by Alderman Callari. The votes were 4 ayes, Mayor Pro Tem
Brown, Aldermen Fisher, Callari and Powell. One no, Alderman Adams.
II.
Exploring Options for Land Acquisition (317 West Bay Street)
Mayor Pro Tem Brown asked the Board if they wished to pursue exploring options
to acquire land that is in foreclosure at 317 West Bay Street.
Alderman Callari motioned that the City pursue exploring options to acquire the
land at 317 West Bay Street, seconded by Alderman Fisher, vote carried.
Alderman Fisher stated the City could use the additional waterfront access and
possibly pursue some type of park through the state’s program. He told the
Board that he spoke with individuals about the possibility of buying the
property. He stated if an individual purchases the land, then the City could
negotiate the purchase for a tax write off.
Alderman Adams asked if much work and cost would be involved in making the land
suitable for a park or waterfront access. Mr. Grant stated he believes the land
is useful. Alderman Callari stated she walks by the property often and have not
seen standing water and it is worth pursuing.
Chad Hicks, Planner stated the tract in question is listed at $4 million and
the tax value is $2,278,400. The two lots combined have a road frontage of 243
feet.

OCTOBER 11, 2007  7:30 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N. C.
 
PRESENT:         Norman R. Holden, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Meezie Childs, James Powell,
            Stuart Callari, Paul Fisher and James Brown
ABSENT:         None
STAFF PRESENT:       Rob Gandy, City Manager
            Mike Isenberg, City Attorney
            Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
            Chad Hicks, City Planner
I.
Call to Order – 7:35 p.m.
Mayor Holden called the meeting to order at 7:35 p.m.
II.
Invocation
Alderman Brown delivered the invocation.
III.
Approval of Minutes
Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Callari to approve the regular
meeting minutes from September 13 and the special meeting minutes of September
26. The vote was unanimous.
IV.
Petitions from the floor (Non-Agenda Items)
There were no petitions from the floor.
Mayor Holden reported that during the Mayors meeting in August he was asked as
liaison with the N. C. Department of Transportation to assist in scheduling a
meeting with DOT representatives and municipal officials. Meeting was held and
those in attendance were: Mayor of Bald Head, POA President of BHI,
representative for the developer;, Lanny Wilson, DOT Board member, Allen Pope,
Division Engineer, the Director of the Southern end of the North Carolina Ferry
Division and his representatives. They discussed the possibility of changing
Bald Head or the State Ferry System schedule because both ferries were meeting
at the same time, which was causing a conflict. He requested that the state
look into the possibility of installing new turning lanes at the end of ferry
road or a stop light. He explained when Bald Head opens up its new marina;
there will be an excessive amount of traffic coming off ferry road. Mayor
Holden stated several years ago, the City wanted to direct the traffic to exit
to the east around the loop and come back to Jabbertown Road, but the downtown
merchants association wanted the ferry traffic business and the idea was
dismissed. It has been discussed with developers about paving Yaupon Avenue
Extension, which will re-route some of the traffic. The Captain of the Ferry
System during a meeting in Raleigh stated that they would consider the ferry
service. Mayor stated he does not believe that the State of North Carolina is
going to change the ferry schedule. His recommendation is that Bald Head Island
Ferry makes some adjustments. For information, Mayor reported that he has a
copy of Brunswick County’s Transportation Improvement Plan (TIP) and it is
available for review. He stated that he would continue as the liaison with DOT
and maintain the Governor’s Southeastern office after he leaves office as Mayor
in December.
V.
Adoption of the City’s CAMA Core Land Use Plan -Resolution
Mayor Holden announced that a Public Hearing was held during the September
meeting on the Land Use Plan. There being no comments from the Board, he called
for the vote. Alderman Powell moved to approve the CAMA Core Land Use Plan and
to adopt the following resolution, motion seconded by Alderman Callari. The
vote of approval was unanimous. Board members commended Mr. Holland on the Plan
and stated changes may need to be made periodically. In response to a question
by Mayor Holden, Mr. Holland stated the Plan should be updated every 6-7 years.
(Land Use Plan on file in the Office of City Planner)
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NC ADOPTING THE
CITY’S CAMA CORE LAND USE PLAN
WHEREAS, the City’s CAMA Core Land Use Plan was financed in part through a
grant provided by the North Carolina Coastal Management Program through funds
provided by the Coastal Zone Management Act of 1972, as amended, which is
administered by the Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management, National
Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; and
WHEREAS, from July 1, 2004, through October 11, 2007, the City drafted a Land
Use Plan with the assistance of its consultant, Holland Consulting Planners,
Inc., and conducted a series of public workshops and meetings as part of a
comprehensive public participation program under the leadership of the CAMA
Land Use Plan Committee; and
WHEREAS, on July 19, 2007, the Planning Board recommended adoption of the draft
CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, at a duly advertised Regular Meeting on September 13, 2007, the Board
of Aldermen held a public hearing on the draft CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, at the Regular Meeting on September 13, 2007, the Board of Aldermen of
the City of Southport, North Carolina found the policies in the draft CAMA Core
Land Use Plan to be internally consistent; and
WHEREAS, at the Regular Meeting on September 13, 2007, the Board of Aldermen of
the City of Southport, North Carolina found the policies and Future Land Use
Map in the draft CAMA Core Land Use Plan to be consistent with the City’s
desired vision for the future and unanimously approved to adopt the draft CAMA
Core Land Use Plan as amended; and
WHEREAS, at the Regular Meeting on September 13, 2007, the Board of Aldermen of
the City of Southport, North Carolina found that policy statements and the
Future Land Use Map have been evaluated, and determined that no internal
inconsistencies exist; and
WHEREAS, the adopted Plan will be submitted as required by state law to the
Wilmington District Planner for the Division of Coastal Management under the
North Carolina Department of Environmental and Natural Resources and forwarded
to the Coastal Resources Commission; and
WHEREAS, a presentation by the City to the Planning and Special Issues (P&SI)
Committee of the Coastal Resources Commission will be scheduled; and
WHEREAS, the P&SI Committee will decide on a recommendation to the Coastal
Resource Commission (CRC) at the meeting; and
WHEREAS, the P&SI Committee chairman will submit the recommendation to the CRC
and the CRC will then vote on certification of the City’s Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, a certified City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan will be
forwarded to the Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management (OCRM) for
federal approval.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina, has unanimously adopted the draft CAMA Core Land Use
Plan; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Planning Director of the City of Southport is
hereby authorized to submit the adopted CAMA Core Land Use Plan to the State
for certification as described above.
Adopted this 11th day of October 2007.
/s/ Norman R. Holden
Mayor, City of Southport

X.
Stray Cats – Denise Moore
Ms. Denise Moore, Director of Kids World Learning Center, Mr. and Mrs. Antwan
Taylor, the owners, and Mary Jo Willis, resident and business owner came before
the Board to discuss the problem of stray cats. Ms. Moore gave the board a
packet of information, which included pictures of stray cats. She stated that
their problem began in 2003, when Mrs. Taylor contacted the City Manager and
Code Enforcement Officer. Mr. Drew conducted an investigation and it was
determined that their concerns were valid. He has trapped some cats, but for
every trapped cat, a stray gives birth to a new litter. Ms. Moore stated until
an ordinance is adopted and enforced, this problem would continue to escalate.
She presented a petition with signatures showing that others are experiencing
similar problems. She told the Board that the owner of the Center located an
ordinance from another town regarding enforcement of stray cats and shared it
with staff. She alluded to a similar problem that Mrs. Mary Jo Willis, a
Southport business owner is having. Ms. Moore told the Board that they have had
to close their business, bring in engineers, medical professionals and teachers
having to take time off from work to pick up their children. She asked the
Board to help rectify this problem by amending the pre-existing Animal Control
Ordinance to include cats. She explained that at any given time, there are
thirteen cats on the neighbors’ porch; however, her personal cats are kept
inside. The strays are not vaccinated, spayed or neutered. The exterminator
bombed the inside of their building and sprayed the outside; in addition, cats
are dying on their property. In conclusion, Ms. Moore stated that true animal
lovers are responsible people; they advocate neutering, spaying, and are
responsible for their pets.
Attorney Isenberg explained that the only law the City has states that all cats
once they reach a certain age must be vaccinated. The City does not have laws
prohibiting cats from running at large or restrict the number of cats on
property. However, the state statute does provide the same powers to regulate
cats as dogs.
Mrs. Mary Jo Willis of Herring Drive told the Board that she has had problems
with stray cats for the past three months, which has plagued their boat storage
business. She cited problem with fleas, blood, urine, tearing of upholstery and
allergic reaction from one of her customers, sleeping on cars, porches and
porch furniture. She spoke with Charles Drew, Code Enforcement Officer and the
City is in the process of buying 20 more cages. Due to the significant
increase, some residents have used their personal cages, which have not been
returned. Ms. Willis stated that some enforcement should be in place to make
pet owners responsible. The stray cats should be picked up before they become
wild and rabid. She asked that the Board implement and enforce a Cat Ordinance
for the City.
Alderman Adams stated it is his understanding that the problem is not the pet
owners, it is stray cats. He questioned if the City should punish cat owners
and impose an ordinance, or should the City implement rules to control the
feral cat population. He stated the issue should be clarified, because nobody
owns a stray cat, and he believes this is the problem.
Alderman Callari stated she has also had a problem with feral cats and had to
replace chair cushions on her porch. Alderman Brown agreed that something
should be done, because an ordinance would only identify pet owners.
Mayor Holden requested Attorney Isenberg review the State Statutes and bring a
proposal to the November meeting. Alderman Callari recommended asking the Code
Enforcement Officer what he believes it would take to perform a mass round up
of feral cats. Mayor Holden stated if cat owners purchase a tag, the same as
dog owners, then the owners could be identified.

EXECUTIVE SESSION
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN OCTOBER 11, 2007
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION
The Board entered executive session for the purpose of giving staff directives
in negotiating the position the Board wishes to take and to authorize specific
terms of an offer for land acquisition.
Attorney Isenberg stated the property at 317 West Bay Street went to
foreclosure and Cooperative Bank bid on the property. In order to upset the
bid, the price must be raised by 5%. It will cost $1.795 million for the
property including court cost and attorney fees.
Alderman Childs asked if the City wish to upset the bid, would sufficient time
be allowed to raise the monies. Attorney Isenberg told the Board if no upset
bids were filed within 10 days, then Cooperative would own the property and the
City could negotiate with the bank. The City has until October 22 to file an
upset bid with the Clerk of Court.
Mr. Chad Hicks, City Planner informed the Board that he spoke with a
representative from Cooperative Bank and they will entertain the idea of
negotiating with the City for a tax write off. City Manager Gandy stated it is
his belief that the City should negotiate with Cooperative Bank after October
22, once the 10 days have lapsed to file an upset bid.
It was the consensus of the Board to direct staff to negotiate with cooperative
Bank after the 10-day time period has lapsed for the property at 317 West Bay
Street.
No further business, Alderman Callari moved to re-enter regular session,
seconded by Alderman Brown, vote carried.

ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A CAPITAL PROJECT FUND:
SOUTHPORT WASTEWATER SYSTEM ENHANCEMENT – PHASE II
WHEREAS, the City of Southport is committed to providing superior wastewater
collection and treatment to its citizens; and
WHEREAS, the City is further committed to providing such service in the most
efficient, economical and environmentally appropriate manner practicable; and
WHEREAS, the elected approach to achieving these goals is through a partnership
with the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District (SBSD) that will ultimately
result in the SBSD assuming all wastewater treatment responsibilities for the
City; and
WHEREAS, it is appropriate that a Capital Project Fund be established for Phase
II of this venture that will result in all of the City’s wastewater flow being
redirected to the SBSD for treatment; and
WHEREAS, a Capital Project Fund is hereby determined to be the most appropriate
manner in which to account for revenues and expenditures associated with Phase
II;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen:
1.   A Capital Project Fund is hereby established for Phase II of this project.
2.   The total budget for the project, subject to amendment by action of the
Aldermen as necessary to implement the project, shall be as follows:
Revenue
CG&L Revolving Fund Loan         $ 8,952,000.00
CWMTF Grant            $ 3,000,000.00
City of Southport Grant Match      $ 878,000.00
Total Revenue            $12,830.000.00
Expenditures
Construction                $ 9,800,000.00
Contingency (10%)            $ 980,000.00
Professional Services            $ 1,345,000.00
Legal/Administrative            $ 70,000.00
Easement/Land Acquisition         $ 439,000.00
CG&L Closing Costs (2% of Construction)   $ 196,000.00
Total Expenditures            $12,830,000.00
3.   The City Manager and Finance Officer are hereby authorized to make any
Fund or accounting adjustments necessary to establish, implement and maintain
this Capital Project Fund.
4.   The City Manager, Finance Officer and Public Services Director are hereby
authorized and empowered to execute on behalf of the City of Southport all
contracts, agreements and other documents necessary to administer this
ordinance and Phase II of the Southport Wastewater System Enhancement Project
and all prior actions of said officers consistent herewith are hereby ratified.
Duly adopted, this 8th day of November, 2007.

City’s Treated Effluent Management Site off of Sunny Point Road
Mr. Grant referenced the Board to the October meeting where Alderman Powell
briefed the Board on an opportunity for the City to have some clearing and site
preparatory work performed on the property at Sunny Point with little or no
cost to the City. He submitted request for proposals (RFP’s) to various
contractors and received one response from Barnhill Contracting. The company
agreed to perform the scope of the work for the value of the salvage earthen
material to be removed from the site, (Approximately 100,000 cubic yards).
Staff recommends that the Agreement be awarded to Barnhill with the stipulation
that there is no monetary cost to the City. Alderman Powell moved to award the
contract to Barnhill and to authorize the City Manager to execute the
Agreement, seconded by Alderman Brown, the vote carried. Thanks were extended
to Alderman Powell in negotiating this deal.

representatives from Sunny Point to review the work to be performed. Motion
seconded by Alderman Callari, vote carried. Alderman Adams asked that something
be provided in writing as to the scope of the work that is permissible in the
buffer zone. Alderman Fisher stated that this is the purpose of the meeting;
Sunny Point will provide the City with a written letter.
XII.
Proposed Fire Department Headquarters
Chief Cumbee thanked Mayor Holden and Board members for their support of the
fire department. He also thanked the Fire Station Committee comprised of his
Sr. Officers, Al Trunnel, Paul Fisher, Nelson Adams and Robert Howard. He
stated that they met several times to discuss and review plans for the proposed
fire station. Chief Cumbee stated it is his hope that the Board will approve
the conceptual drawing and then proceed to the next step. He explained that the
current fire station was built in 1963 and is inadequate for their needs. The
Fire Department has an ISO rating of four (4) which speaks for itself. The new
station is needed so that they can move out of the busy downtown area and be
centrally located, and the new station will be able to house all of their
equipment.
Chief Cumbee introduced Mr. Scott Garner and Neil Brown of Garner and Brown
Architects of Charlotte, North Carolina. Mr. Garner presented the conceptual
drawing of the proposed fire department. He explained that the building was
designed to meet the needs of the city. He stated that the typical life of a
fire station is approximately 50 years and the city is on target. Mr. Garner
gave a detailed description of the station and how it will be used for the
firemen, function of various offices, housing equipment and trucks. The
building was designed reminiscent of Southport and would be a positive addition
to the City.
Mayor Holden and the Board thanked Mr. Garner for the presentation. Mayor
Holden stated it is his hopes that the newly elected Mayor-elect and Aldermen-
elect will look favorably at the new Fire Station. Mr. Garner stated the
proposed building houses 21,000 square feet with an approximate cost of $4 -
4.5 million. Alderman Fisher stated that the Committee is looking at a
financial plan and options are being considered for funding. Congressman
McIntyre’s office has been contacted for assistance.
Chief Cumbee stated the next step is approval from the Board on the conceptual
drawings and once received, he can authorize the architects to go forth with
the plans. Mayor Holden recommended that a financial plan be compiled showing
how they plan to fund the construction and present it to the new board in
January.

connector roadway (TIP #R-3324), and requests the State of North Carolina to
take all necessary steps and action to implement the plan, design and
construction of said alternative. Alderman Powell moved to adopt the resolution
and requested that it be forwarded to Secretary Lyndo Tippet, NCDOT. Motion
seconded by Alderman Callari, vote carried.
RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport recognizes the traffic
congestion existing at the intersection of Oak Island Road and Highway 211
which causes traffic flow and safety problems for the entire area; and
WHEREAS, the Board also recognizes the need to remedy this problem as
expeditiously as possible in order to increase traffic flow and reduce safety
hazards; and
WHEREAS, the Board supports the concept of a public/private four-lane connector
roadway alternative to the planned NCDOT connector roadway (TIP #R-3324) for
the following reasons:
1.   The roadway’s design and capacity make it a much more effective and direct
evacuation route in case of a hurricane or other disaster;
2.   The roadway’s design will create no significant impact on existing
commercial and residential developments;
3.   The roadway’s design will have minimal environmental impact as adequate
lands are available for use in mitigation and preservation;
4.   The roadway’s design will leave ample space for any new highway
infrastructure that may be added in the future to accommodate the proposed
International Port in Southport;
5.   The roadway’s developers are working with the City of Southport to upgrade
and accommodate the city’s sewer needs resulting in less costs for the City;
6.   The roadway can be built sooner and at a significantly lower cost per mile
than the planned NCDOT roadway;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport
that the City of Southport supports the proposed public/private four-lane
connector roadway alternative from the intersection of Oak Island Road and
Highway 211 through to Highway 87 to the planned NCDOT connector roadway (TIP #
R-3324) and hereby requests the State of North Carolina to take all necessary
steps and action to implement the plan, design and construction of said
alternative.
This the 8th day of November, 2007.
City of Southport
By:
/S/ Norman R. Holden, Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, Clerk

XI.
Modification of Appendix A of the Sewer Allocation Schedule relating to
reduction in residential flow amount per bedroom
Mr. Grant, Public Services Director informed the Board for the past two years
the city has been compiling data and working with the Division of Water Quality
to provide a reduction in the amount of flow per bedroom that must be reserved
for each new residential unit. DWQ notified the City in September that this was
approved which will allow the city to reserve 80 gpd of flow for bedroom versus
the former 120 gpd that had been reserved. This modification would increase the
residential per gallon impact fee from $20/gallon to $30/gallon. (See attached
sheet)
Appendix A
Wastewater Allocation Impact Fee Schedule
Wastewater flow allocated for residential purposes shall be calculated based
upon the number of bedrooms contained within the units. No less than two
bedrooms shall be considered in the calculation of flow for a residential unit.
Existing SFD development on a single lot abutting a wastewater utility line
suitable for connection shall pay a wastewater impact fee of $30/gallon. This
charge shall also apply to any existing residential developments for which
impact fees have not previously been paid if full.
For proposed new subdivided development (including the division of existing
lots platted at the time of the initiation of this schedule) duplex or multi-
family development, or any other development where a wastewater utility system
extension permit is required where plans are approved by the City subsequent to
the adoption of this schedule, the following shall apply:
3 or fewer dwelling units/acre            = $30/gallon
4-8 dwelling units/acre            = $35/gallon
Over 8 dwelling units/acre            = $40/gallon
For mixed use development, each 750 ft.² of non-residential space, or fraction
thereof, shall be considered as one residential two bedroom unit for the
purpose of meeting the density calculation prescribed above.
For non-residential development, usage shall be calculated on the basis of the
attached schedule identified as Appendix B. A wastewater impact fee of $20/
gallon per calculated gallon shall be applied with the exception of the
following uses:
Food Service Uses***               = $25/gallon
Laundromats                  = $25/gallon
Car Washes                  = $25/gallon
Motels/Hotels with cooking facilities in room   = $25/gallon
Campgrounds with water/sewer hook-ups      = $25/gallon
Any use requiring pretreatment of waste      = $40/gallon
**** Food Service Uses shall include, but are not strictly limited, to
restaurants, hospitals, day cares, rest or nursing homes, motels, hotels with
separate restaurants, etc, where food is prepared in house and by products of
the activity are handled on site. Where food service is in addition to another
primary use, flow calculations shall be determined on the basis of both the
primary and any related ancillary uses.

XII.
Water Emergency Policy
Mr. Grant presented a proposed Water Emergency Policy for consideration. He
informed the Board that the policy mirrors the County’s, which has been
modified to meet the City of Southport’s needs, and stated the importance of
having it in place to implement measures that are necessary to protect the
city’s water sources in the case of drought, since this has been an extremely
dry season. Aldermen Fisher asked if the City had to implement the policy,
would it be done in stages and monitored. Mr. Grant responded that the City can
and will work with Brunswick County.
No further questions, Alderman Fisher moved to approve the Emergency Water
Policy, seconded by Alderman Brown, the vote of approval was unanimous.
WATER EMERGENCY POLICY
A.   INTRODUCTION.
The City’s Public Services Department henceforth referred to as the
“Department” and the Board of Aldermen, henceforth referred to as the “Board”
shall have the charge to protect the City’s public water supply and to ensure
that the benefactors of this system are assured an adequate supply of water
even in times of water shortage. Water shortage can be the result of climatic
conditions causing drought or it may be the result of a physical breech in the
City’s water supply system (i.e., mechanical failure, cut or broken water main,
etc.) impeding the flow of potable or raw water supply.
B.   WATER EMERGENCY RESPONSE AND MANAGEMENT.
1.   DECLARATION OF WATER EMERGENCY.
The Mayor, after consultation with the City Manager, Public Services Director
and Brunswick County Utilities Director is authorized to declare that a water
emergency exists. Depending on the severity of the emergency, voluntary (Stage
1) and mandatory (Stage 2 and Stage 3) staged water use restrictions as
described in this ordinance shall be imposed upon all water customers.
2.   STAGED WATER USE RESTRICTIONS.
a.   STAGE 1 – WATER CONSERVATION ALERT.
A Stage 1 water shortage emergency may be declared in the event of an immediate
water shortage, as so declared by state and/or local officials, or when there
are three (3) consecutive days when water demand exceeds eighty percent (80%)
of the water production capacity. Water production capacity shall be defined as
the maximum volume of water that meets or exceeds state and federal standards
that the water treatment process can produce during a twenty-four (24) hour
period. Water production capacity can vary depending on system component
reliability and/or raw water conditions. During a declared Stage 1 water
shortage emergency the following voluntary water conservation practices shall
be encouraged.
1)    Inspect and repair all faulty and defective parts of faucets and toilets.
2)    Use shower for bathing rather than bathtub and limit shower to no more
than five (5) minutes.
3)    Do not leave faucets running while shaving, brushing teeth, rinsing or
preparing food.
4)    Limit the use of clothes washers and dishwashers and when used, operate
fully loaded. Operate dishwashers after the peak demand hours of 6:00 PM to 10:
00 PM.
5)    Limit lawn watering to that necessary for plant survival. Water lawns
before the peak demand hours of 6:00 AM to10:00 AM
6)    Water shrubbery the minimum required. Water shrubbery before the peak
demand hours of 6:00 AM to 10:00 AM.
7)    Limit vehicle washing to a minimum.
8)    Do not wash down outside areas such as sidewalks, drive-ways, patios,
etc.
9)    Install water saving showerheads and other water conservation devices.
10)    Use disposable and biodegradable dishes where possible.
11)    Install water saving devices in toilets such as early closing flappers.
12)   Limit hours of water-cooled air conditioners.
13)   Do not fill swimming or wading pools.
b.   STAGE 2 – WATER SHORTAGE WARNING.
A Stage 2 water shortage emergency may be declared in the event of an immediate
water shortage, as so declared by state and/or local officials, or when there
are two (2) consecutive days when water demand exceeds ninety percent (90%) of
the water production capacity. Water production capacity shall be defined as
the maximum volume of water that meets or exceeds state and federal standards
that the water treatment process can produce during a twenty-four (24) hour
period. Water production capacity can vary depending on system component
reliability and/or raw water conditions. During a declared Stage 2 water
shortage emergency the following activities shall be prohibited:
1)   Watering lawns, grass, shrubbery, trees, flower and vegetable gardens
except by hand held hoses, container, or drip irrigation system. A person who
regularly sells plants will be permitted to use water on their commercial
stock. A golf course may water their greens. State and City licensed landscape
contractors may water any plants by hand held hose or drip irrigation under a
written warranty.
2)   Filling swimming or wading pools, either newly constructed or previously
drained. Make up water for pools in operation will be allowed.
3)   Using water-cooled air conditioners or other equipment, in which cooling
water is not recycled, unless there are health or safety concerns.
4)   Washing any type of mobile equipment including cars, trucks, trailers,
boats or airplanes. Any person involved in a business of washing motor vehicles
may continue to operate.
5)   Washing outside surfaces such as streets, driveways, service station
aprons, parking lots or patios.
6)   Exterior washing of office buildings, homes or apartments.
7)   Using water for any ornamental fountain, pool, pond, etc. unless recycled.
8)   Serving drinking water in food establishments such as restaurants or
cafeterias, unless requested to do so by a customer.
9)    Using water from a public or private fire hydrant for any reason other
than to suppress a fire or other public emergency or as authorized by Director
or his authorized representative.
10)    Using water to control or compact dust.
11)    Intentionally wasting water.
12)    Commercial and industrial water customers shall achieve mandatory
reductions in water usage through whatever means are available. A minimum
reduction of twenty percent (20%) shall be the target, however, a greater
target reduction percentage may be required depending on the severity of the
water shortage emergency. Compliance with the reduction target shall be
determined by the Director or his authorized representative. Variances to the
target reduction may be granted by the Director or his authorized
representative to designated public health facilities.
c.   STAGE 3 – WATER SHORTAGE DANGER.
A Stage 3 water shortage emergency may be declared in the event of an immediate
water shortage, as so declared by state and/or local officials, or when there
is one (1) day when demand exceeds one hundred percent (100%) of the water
production capacity. Water production capacity shall be defined as the maximum
volume of water that meets or exceeds state and federal standards that the
water treatment process can produce during a twenty-four (24) hour period.
Water production capacity can vary depending on system component reliability
and/or raw water conditions. During a declared Stage 3, water shortage
emergency the following activities shall be prohibited, in addition to
activities prohibited under Stage 2:
1)     Watering lawns, grass, shrubbery, trees, and flowers.
2)    Washing motor vehicles at commercial car wash establishments.
3)    Watering any vegetable garden except by hand held hose, container, or
drip irrigation.
4)   Commercial and industrial water customers shall achieve mandatory
reductions in water usage through whatever means are available. A minimum
reduction of fifty percent (50%) shall be the target, however, a greater target
reduction percentage may be required depending on the severity of the water
emergency. Compliance with the reduction target shall be determined by the
Director or his authorized representative. Variances to the target reduction
may be granted by the Director or his authorized representative to designated
public health facilities.
5)   In the event that the prohibition of the activities listed above is not
sufficient to maintain an adequate supply of water for fire protection, all use
of water for purposes other than maintenance of public health and safety shall
be prohibited. Residential water use shall be limited to the amount necessary
to sustain life through drinking, food preparation and personal hygiene.
3.   COMPLIANCE PLAN DURING STAGE 2 AND STAGE 3 EMERGENCIES.
The Director or his authorized representative may require that commercial and
industrial water customers prepare plans detailing measures to be taken by them
to achieve mandatory reductions in daily water usage during Stage 2 and Stage 3
emergencies. Such plans shall be completed within sixty (60) calendar days
after receipt of notice to prepare them.
4.   PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION OF MANDATORY RESTRICTIONS.
Any user who is found to have failed to comply with any of the mandatory
restrictions set forth in these Regulations may be fined in accordance with
NCGS 160A-175(c1) with a civil penalty of Five Hundred dollars ($500.00), to be
recovered by the City in a civil action in the nature of debt if the offender
does not pay the penalty within 15 days of being cited for the violation. Each
day’s continuing violation shall be a separate and distinct offense.
5.   AUTHORITY TO DISCONTINUE SERVICE.
Pursuant to the provisions of NCGS 160A-175 and 160A-312(b), water service may
be temporarily discontinued for failure to comply with the mandatory
restrictions in this ordinance. All applicable penalty fees may be applied in
the event of such service suspensions. In the event of continued non-compliance
with this ordinance, removal of meter and service will be deemed proper and
service will be discontinued and tap fees and account deposits shall be
forfeited.
6.   APPEALS BY CUSTOMERS OF PENALTIES AND TERMINATION OF SERVICE.
Any user who receives a penalty and/or has service terminated as a result of
violations of the mandatory restrictions in this ordinance may appeal upon
notification to the Director. The Director shall be the final decision maker
for appeals and shall transmit a written copy of the final decision by
registered or certified mail within three (3) days after notification.
7.   TERMINATION OF RESTRICTIONS.
A water emergency declaration shall be terminated by the Mayor after
consultation with the City Manager, Public Services Director and Brunswick
County Utilities Director upon a determination that the condition that caused
the emergency has abated. The expiration or cancellation of a water shortage
emergency declaration shall be promptly publicized.
2007-Water Emergency Policy-Final-110807

and Dr. Bill Rabon. Mayor Spencer stated that she was advised that the
Veterinary Medical Association states that the only effective program is to
spay, neuter and adopt. She explained that one female cat can be responsible
for 8,000 kittens over a lifetime and encouraged responsible pet ownership.
Mayor asked that the Committee meet and select its own Chairperson.

New Business
Planning Board-Public Hearing on Southport Crossing Zoning Reclassification.
Mayor stated the property owner requested that the rezoning be postponed
because they did not receive notification. Mr. Chad Hicks stated the Planning
Board on December 20 recommended the rezoning to R-20 and the property is
currently zoned multi-family and business. He explained that addresses of
property owners were taken from the County’s website. Staff discovered that the
property was not deeded until December 27. Attorney Isenberg explained that the
property was in foreclosure and receivership. The state court assumed
jurisdiction, however, the receiver did not receive notification either. The
law requires that the owner be served, but staff was unaware that the property
had been sold. He recommended the public hearing be postponed and send notices
to appropriate parties for February.
Alderman Fisher stated via telephone, Alderman Adams asked him to convey to the
Board know that he was against rezoning the property.
Alderman Boguskie asked if the Board could proceed with the hearing since
citizens had attended the meeting for this purpose. It was the consensus the
Hearing should be postponed. Alderman Brown moved, seconded by Alderman Frink
to postpone the rezoning until February. The votes were 3 yes votes: Aldermen
Brown, Frink and Fisher. 2 no votes: Aldermen Boguskie and Potter.
Zoning Reclassification for properties located north of 9th Street, South of
Fodale Avenue, East of Howe Street to Atlantic Avenue and abutting the East
side of Atlantic Avenue North of 8th Street and South of 9th Street from
Business District, Residential and Multi-Family to office/institutional.
Mr. Hicks stated this request deals with properties near Dosher Hospital. The
Planning Board and the petitioner believe the O and I zoning classification is
better suited for these properties rather than the current zoning. The
properties are mostly used for hospital projects. Mr. Hicks stated Mr. John
Sledge, owner of lots 5 & 6 requested his property not be rezoned, which is
currently zoned residential.
Public Hearing- Alderman Brown moved, seconded by Alderman Fisher to enter
Public Hearing on the above referenced. Vote carried.
Mayor asked for public comments.
Mr. Randy Fullwood of 109 East 8th Street stated that his father owns the
adjacent property and they were not notified of the rezoning. Mr. Hicks stated
notification was sent to the address on the county tax records.
Herman Floyd of 619 Fodale Avenue spoke against rezoning; however he was told
that his property was not in the rezoning.
Mr. John Sledge of 815 N. Atlantic Avenue stated he does not object to the
rezoning; however he request that his property remain residential.

City Code – Auxiliary Police Officers
Ms. Miller, Finance Officer presented the following amendment to City Code
explaining that no benefits are involved, however this ordinance needs to be in
place to insure that volunteers are covered under the city's workmen
compensation policy. Alderman Brown moved to approve the amendment, seconded by
Alderman Fisher, vote carried.
Amendment to Section 14-10 of the City Code – Auxiliary Police Officers
Section 14-10 Auxiliary Police Division
The Police Department of the City may establish an Auxiliary Police Division.
The auxiliary police division shall be a volunteer organization, whose members
shall serve without compensation, composed of as many members as may from time
to time be determined by the Chief of Police and approved by the City Manager.
Auxiliary Police, while undergoing official training and while performing
duties on behalf of the city pursuant to orders or instructions of the Chief of
Police of the City, shall be entitled to benefits under North Carolina Workers
Compensation Act and to any fringe benefits for which such volunteer personnel
qualify. (Ord. of 1-10-2008)
Adopted by the Board of Aldermen on January 10, 2008.

JANUARY 15, 2008
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
JANUARY 15, 2008  1:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, NC
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Donnie Potter, James Brown,
            Jwantana Frink, Ed Boguskie and Paul Fisher
STAFF:         Regina W. Alexander, CMC
            Patty Miller, Finance Officer
            Shaaron Aldridge, Payroll Clerk
OTHER:         Lee Hinnant, State Port Pilot
            Hartwell Wright, Human Resources, NCLM
            Lisa Kinsey, Member Services and Marketing Representative
The Board of Aldermen met in special session pursuant to notice duly advertised
and posted to discuss the process of hiring a City Manager. Mr. Hartwell
Wright, Human Resources/Employee Relations Consulting Manager of the North
Carolina League of Municipalities and staff member Lisa Kinsey, Member Services
and Marketing Representative were present to brief the Board in the selection
process of hiring a City Manager.
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order. Mr. Wright gave the Board a handout
on the selection process for a City Manager. He noted the steps in acquiring a
manager.
·   Recruitment
·   Assessment
·   Selection
He stated since the City has advertised; the Mayor or Board should determine
who would handle the next phase of the process by contacting applicants,
scheduling interviews, etc. He recommended that names be kept confidential due
to personnel privacy laws, and suggested the Board contract with a third party
to perform background checks.
Alderman Fisher asked about the cut off date for ads, and whether or not the
City should continue accepting applications. Mr. Wright stated the Board should
decide if they wish to extend the application process until the position is
filled because there is no law stating a cutoff date must be placed in the ad.
Mr. Wright suggested the Board meet as a body to identify the criteria for a
City Manager and compare resume to the profile. He stated between $80,000 and
$90,000 as a possible starting salary, which he compared to other beach towns
of similar size. Alderman Adams countered by stating one cannot compare a
seaport town to a beach town when comparing salaries. Mr. Wright reiterated
that the salary is commensurate with experience and education. He stated the
process could take as long as six (6) months. He gave the Board a list of
possible questions to ask applicants and encouraged the Board to make the
process welcoming by considering travel pay and lodging expenses. He suggested
using teleconference or video conferencing for out of state applicants. Once
the applicant is selected and offered a job, the candidate may expect an
employment contract, which is the norm and recommended the City Attorney draft
a letter of offer/contract including salary and fringe benefits.
In answer to questions, Mr. Wright stated Managers do not have probationary
periods because most often, they have a contract, which protects both parties.
There is no statute requiring them to live within the City limits, but the
Board may establish policy or make this a part of the employment contract.
No further questions, Mayor Spencer and Board members thanked Mr. Wright for
the presentation.
Mayor Spencer asked the Board to consider two (2) additional items realizing
that the meeting was advertised as a Special Meeting . The City Attorney
advised her that this could be done if the Board agreed.
Alderman Potter moved to add the items, seconded by Alderman Boguskie, the vote
carried.
Mayor Spencer stated that she met with Mr. Bill Comninaki of Morehead Farms who
has proposed to the North Carolina Department of Transportation the concept of
a public/private four-lane connector roadway alternative to the planned North
Carolina Department of Transportation connector roadway providing private funds
to assist in building the roadway sooner than what DOT planned. Senator Soles
is aware of this proposal but request confirmation from the newly elected Board
in support of the project. Alderman Potter motioned to adopt the following
resolution, seconded by Alderman Fisher with copies forwarded to Senator R. C.
Soles, Representatives Stiller and Hill including a copy of the resolution
adopted on November 8, 2007. The vote of approval was unanimous.
RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport recognizes the traffic
congestion existing at the intersection of Oak Island Road and Highway 211
which causes traffic flow and safety problems for the entire area; and
WHEREAS, the Board also recognizes the need to remedy this problem as
expeditiously as possible in order to increase traffic flow and reduce safety
hazards; and
WHEREAS, the Board supports the concept of a public/private four-lane connector
roadway alternative to the planned NCDOT connector roadway (TIP #R-3324) for
the following reasons:
1.   The roadway’s design and capacity make it a much more effective and direct
evacuation route in case of a hurricane or other disaster;
2.   The roadway’s design will create no significant impact on existing
commercial and residential developments;
3.   The roadway’s design will have minimal environmental impact, as adequate
lands are available for use in mitigation and preservation;
4.   The roadway’s design will leave ample space for any new highway
infrastructure that may be added in the future to accommodate the proposed
International Port in Southport;
5.   The roadway’s developers are working with the City of Southport to upgrade
and accommodate the city’s sewer needs resulting in less costs for the City;
6.   The roadway can be built sooner and at a significantly lower cost per mile
than the planned NCDOT roadway;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that the City of Southport supports the proposed public/private four-
lane connector roadway alternative from the intersection of Oak Island Road and
Highway 211 through to Highway 87 to the planned NCDOT connector roadway (TIP #
R-3324) and hereby requests the State of North Carolina to take all necessary
steps and action to implement the plan, design and construction of said
alternative.
This the 15th day of January, 2008.
City of Southport

MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AWARENESS WEEK 2008
BY THE MAYOR AND BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPIORT NC
PROCLAMATION
Whereas, MS is a chronic and disabling disease of the central nervous system in
which the progression, severity and specific symptoms cannot be foreseen; and
Whereas, every hour of every day someone new is diagnosed with MS, a disease
that can erode a person's abilities and hopes, halt a career and unravel the
fabric of families; and
Whereas, the North Carolina Chapters of the National Multiple Sclerosis Society
reports that in our state more than 10,000 people are affected by this
devastating disease, and multiple sclerosis generally strike young adults aged
20 through 40, attacking them in the prime of their lives; and
Whereas, the North Carolina Chapters of the National Multiple Sclerosis Society
have been committed throughout the years to heightening public knowledge and
insight about this devastating and disabling disease, and raising more than $8
million to find the cure for MS and develop effective treatments for the
disease, as well as provide a wide range of client programs; and
Whereas, research advances have brought us closer to finding the cure, much
remains to be done, and services must continue to be provided to those who live
with the disease; and
Whereas, finding the cause and developing a method of prevention for multiple
sclerosis is an important task that all Americans and North Carolinians should
support;
Now, Therefore, I Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor of the City of Southport do hereby
proclaim March 10-17, 2008 as "MULTIPLE SCEROSIS AWARENESS WEEK" in the City of
Southport and commend this observance to all our citizens.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, CMC

BOARD RETREAT
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN BOARD RETREAT
FEBRUARY 23, 2008 ALDERMEN CHAMBERS
SOUTHPORT, NC     8:00 A.M.
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Donnie Potter, James Brown, Paul Fisher
            Jwantana Frink and Richard "Ed" Boguskie
STAFF:         Chad Hicks, Interim Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, Clerk
            Patty Miller, Finance Officer
            Greg Cumbee, Fire Chief
            Randy Jones, Director of Tourism
            Heather Hemphill, Parks & Recreation
            Tammie Drew, Rescue Chief
            Ralph Cardwell, Interim Director of Public Services
OTHERS PRESENT:     Chip Leavitt, CEO-BEMC
            Don Hughes, Operations Manager
            Nicky Nance
            Debra Fish
            Kim
            Rob Michel, Financial Analyst
I.
Call to Order – 8:00 a.m.
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order at 8:00 a.m.
II.
Invocation by Alderman Brown.
III.
Departmental Reports
1.   Fire Department
Chief Cumbee in presentation to the Board stated that the Fire Department
responded to 386 fire calls; there are 31 firefighters on the roster, 80% NC.
Certified, ISO 4 rating, and the goal is to replace the 4-wheel drive pumper
truck. Discussed the new fire department, which is needed due to growth. Fire
Department current need is to relocate the Nash Street Station to the area of
North Howe Street and East 11th Street. If the City continues to add hydrants
or buildings in the county district, a station should be located in the area of
Highways 211 and 133. An Executive Committee was formed for the new fire
department headquarters. The architect conceptual drawings have been presented
to the Board, architectural plans for the facility in progress, groundbreaking
and bids slated for 2008. They are exploring potential land purchase for a
substation to be located on Hwy 211. He recommended that financial incentives
be increased to retain firefighters, increase their share of retirement, and
maintain a life insurance policy for members and retirees. Chief Cumbee stated
that Southport is the only municipality without paid personnel. Firefighters
receive a $17 supplement for structural fires and $10 for other calls and fire
fees fund the fire department.
2.   BEMC
Mr. Chip Leavitt, Don Hughes, Nicky Nance and others were present to discuss
the City's contract and the electrical system. Mr. Hughes explained that the
City along with BEMC must be:
·   Environmentally responsible
·   Require input from staff and city officials on what the city want and how
to be environmentally responsible.
·   Don Hughes reviewed with the Board 2007 accomplishments in working with the
City including automated meter reading, improving overhead to underground,
accessibility to internal audit to determine if everyone is billed for street
lights, currently have 2,573 customers in Southport, revenue cost down and
power outages are down compared to previous years and improvement in overall
electrical operations.
3.   Planning and Administration
Chad Hicks, Interim Manager and Ralph Cardwell, Interim Public Works Director
discussed sewer reversal and told the Board the City cannot allocate sewer
because the Sanitary District is treating only `40,000 gpd. Board discussed the
situation; Alderman Adams suggested placing a moratorium on sewer. Chad Hicks
stated placing a moratorium on sewer would place the City at a disadvantage.
County water was discussed which would cost an additional $250,000 per year.
Staff will provide a rate schedule. City will maintain its well for emergency
use. Board discussed the old lines along 9th street and the quality of water
and the need to shutdown the 9th street well.
·   CAMA Grant for Boardwalk, total projected cost was $680,000. $400,000
grants award, $280,000 City's match with an estimated cost overrun of $150, 000
to $200,000 due to shoreline stabilization.
·   Elevator for City Hall (Alderman Fisher recommended applying for a grant)
·   Lack of space for employees
·   Expansion of Building Inspector's Office

BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING
MARCH 6, 2008     7:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Donnie Potter, James Brown,
            Ed Boguskie, Jwantana Frink and Paul Fisher
ABSENT:         None
STAFF:         Chad Hicks, Interim City Manager
            Mike Isenberg, City Attorney
            Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
Mayor Spencer called the Special Meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. pursuant to
notice advertised and posted.
Alderman Brown delivered the invocation.
Mayor Spencer announced that the Special Meeting was called to discuss
personnel and deferred to Attorney Isenberg. Mr. Isenberg stated the Board
could only go into closed session "to consider the qualifications, competence,
performance, character, fitness, conditions of initial employment or an
individual public officer or employee or prospective public officer or
employee; or to hear or investigate a complaint, charge or grievance by or
against an individual public officer or employee. General personnel policy
issues may not be considered in a closed session. A public body may not
consider the qualifications, competence, performance, character, fitness,
appointment or removal of a member of the public body or another body and may
not consider or fill a vacancy amongst sits own membership except in an open
meeting in accordance with G.S. 143-318.11."
Alderman Brown stated he called the meeting to discuss personnel. Attorney
Isenberg stated that the Board could enter closed session to receive legal
advice from Counsel, but not to discuss its own Board members.
7:05 pm - Closed Session
Alderman Fisher motioned to enter closed session to request legal advice from
the City Attorney, seconded by Alderman Brown, vote unanimous.
(Closed session minutes will remained sealed until public inspection no longer
frustrates the purpose of the executive session.)
Regular Session Reconvened – 8:00 p.m.
Alderman Brown moved to re-enter regular session, seconded by Alderman Adams,
vote carried.
In regular session, Attorney Isenberg stated that the purpose of the closed
session was to provide legal counsel on the Board's rights and responsibilities
as Aldermen and as a Board.
Adjournment – 8:05 p.m.
Alderman Adams motioned to adjourn, seconded by Alderman Fisher. Vote was
unanimous.

Executive Session
 
Executive Session Minutes March 6, 2008
 
Attorney Isenberg explained that the City's Charter authorizes the Board to
hire and fire only the City Manager, Clerk and Attorney. The City Manager has
supervisory authority over all other employees. He explained that if a Board
member believes that there is a problem with an employee, they should report
this to the City Manager and he should investigate the matter. Attorney
Isenberg stated that no one Board member has individual authority, only as a
Board.
Alderman Brown stated if a Board member has a problem with employees or any
staff concerns, it should be addressed to the City Manager, which has always
been his policy.
Alderman Fisher reiterated for point of clarification, that an individual board
member has no authority to go to any department head or city employees
representing themselves as a Board, unless the Board of Aldermen gives them
that authority.
Alderman Potter stated that he ran on a platform to do whatever he could to
investigate and help combat drugs in the City. After he was elected, there were
rumors circulating that the Chief would be fired, which he believes came from
the outgoing Board. He stated that he went to the Chief to discuss some
concerns that were addressed to him. During their conversation, he promised the
Chief that if he heard anything about the Police Department that he would come
to him as a friend and brother. He stated that he did receive complaints about
cases not being solved, drugs in the City, and the disillusionment by some of
the department's officers. He met with the Chief to let him know what was being
said, and during their discussion, the Chief offered to resign. Alderman Fisher
asked Alderman Potter if he told the Chief that he had four board members that
wanted him to resign. Alderman Potter answered in the affirmative. Alderman
Potter was asked to name the Board members, which were Aldermen Frink,
Boguskie, Mayor Spencer and himself. Alderman Fisher stated that the Mayor is
not a Board member. Alderman Frink stated that she did talk with Alderman
Potter and told him, if he had an issue to take it before the entire Board.
Alderman Potter acknowledged if he did anything wrong, or acted inappropriately
he would apologize.
Alderman Adams stated that he has been in law enforcement 30+ years and
investigations takes time. He stated if drugs are to this extent in the City,
then the City should hire another Police Officer.
Mayor Spencer stated that the people elect the Board, and the Board should act
as professionals.
Alderman Adams stated the Board should work together as a body.
Alderman Brown explained that he called the meeting to bring unity and to
clarify the Board's role.
Attorney Isenberg suggested the Board direct the Interim City Manager to meet
with each Police Officer in order to determine the morale and needs of the
Police Department.
In other business, Mayor Spencer asked for the Board's approval to proceed with
background checks on applicants for the position of City Manager. Alderman
Brown moved to authorize the Mayor to proceed with background checks, seconded
by Alderman Frink, vote carried.
__________________________________
Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
___________________________
Regina W. Alexander, CMC
City Clerk

b)   Annexation Ordinance-Alderman Fisher moved to adopt the following
annexation ordinance, seconded by Alderman Brown, the vote of approval was
unanimous.
AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
(Contiguous)
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been petitioned under G.S.160A-31 to annex
the area described below; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at Southport City
Hall at 7:30 p.m. on March 13, 2008, after due notice by publication in the
State Port Pilot on February 20 and 27, 2008, and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the petition meets the requirements
of G.S. 160A-31;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, by the Board of Aldermen of Southport, North
Carolina that:
Section 1.   By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-31, the following
described territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City of Southport
effective immediately:
EXHIBIT A
METES AND BOUNDS DESCRIPTION
(LOTS 11B, 12B AND 13B, HIGHLAND PARK AVENUE)
BEGINNING at an existing iron pipe in the Eastern right-of-way of Highland Park
Avenue, City of Southport (80' right of way), which iron pipe is located in the
Southwestern corner of Lot 11B, Highland Park Avenue as appears on map recorded
in Map Cabinet 18, page 523, Brunswick County Register of Deeds; from said
Point of Beginning runs thence South 70 degrees 00 minutes 00 seconds East with
the dividing line of Lot 11B and Lot 10B, Highland Park Avenue, 184.90 feet;
runs thence with the back lot line of Lots 11B, 12B and 13B North 20 degrees 00
minutes 00 seconds East 245 feet to the Northeastern corner of Lot 13B,
Highland Park Avenue; runs thence with the Northern line of Lot 13B North 70
degrees 00 minutes 00 seconds West 108.90 feet to a point; runs thence South 20
degrees 00 minutes 00 seconds West 18.80 feet to a point; runs thence North 70
degrees 00 minutes 00 seconds West 76 feet to the Eastern right of way of
Highland Park Avenue also being the Northwestern corner of Lot 13B, Highland
Park Avenue; runs thence with the Eastern right-of-way of Highland Park Avenue
South 20 degrees 00 minutes 00 seconds West 226.20 feet to the place and point
of BEGINNING and being Lots 11B, 12B and 13B of Highland Park Avenue as
recorded in Map Cabinet 18, page 523, Brunswick County Register of Deeds.
This being the same property as shown on the plat entitled “Area Annexed by the
City of Southport, N. C. on March 13, 2008, recorded in Map Cabinet _____at
Page _____________of the Brunswick County Registry.
Section 2.   Upon and after March 13, 2008 the above-described territory and
its citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be entitled to the same
privileges and benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said territory
shall be subject to municipal taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10.
Section 3.   The Mayor of the City of Southport shall cause to be recorded in
the office of the Register of Deeds of Brunswick County, and in the office of
the Secretary of State at Raleigh, North Carolina, an accurate map of the
annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the County Board
of Elections, as required by G. S. 163-288.1.
ADOPTED, this the 13th day March 2008.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer
Mayor

ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/IMAGES/0-0-0-46.jpg]
WHEREAS, in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of Agriculture that a special day be
set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS, this holiday called Arbor Day , was first observed with the planting of more than a million trees
in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS, Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS, trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and water, cut heating and cooling
costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air, produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for
wildlife, and
WHEREAS, trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes, fuel for our fires, and
beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic vitality of business areas, and
beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE,  I Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor of the City of Southport, N.C. do hereby proclaim March 14,
2008 as ARBOR DAY in the City and urge all citizens to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees
and woodlands, and
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote the well-being of this and
future generations.
DATED, this 13th day of March, 2008.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor

He stated this necessitates adopting a resolution of intent, which does not
annex anyone but is required by state law of the intent to take in new areas. A
map is available for review in the office of the City Clerk. He stated that he
