RESOLUTION OF CONSIDERATION
A RESOLUTION IDENTIFYING THE AREA DESCRIBED HEREIN AS BEING UNDER CONSIDERATION
FOR ANNEXATION AND NOTIFICATION TO CERTAIN PROPERTY OWNERS OF THEIR RIGHTS OF
DELAYED ANNEXATION OF QUALIFIED PROPERTIES
BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that:
Section 1. Pursuant to G. S. 160A-37(i), the following described area(s) is/are
hereby
Identified as being under consideration for future annexation by the City of
Southport, under the provisions of Chapter 160A, Article 4A, Part 2 of the
General Statutes of North Carolina:
Those certain areas identified as “Areas under Consideration for Annexation” on
that certain map attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. A large
scale copy of this map is on file in the office of the City Clerk of the City
of Southport and is also incorporated herein by reference.
Section 2. Owners of agricultural land, horticultural land and forestland
within the area(s) under consideration for annexation as described in Section 1
above are hereby notified that they may have rights to a delayed effective date
of annexation. G.S. 160A-37(f1) and (f2) provide that land being taxed at
present-use value qualifies for delayed annexation, and land that is eligible
for present-use value taxation but which has not been in actual production for
the time period required by G. S. 105-277.3 may qualify for delayed annexation
by making application to the Brunswick County Tax Assessor for certification.
For qualified tracts, the annexation will not become effective for most
purposes until the last day of the month in which the tract or part thereof
becomes ineligible for present-use value classification under G.S. 105-277.4 or
no longer meets the requirements of G. S. 160A-37(f1)(2). Until annexation of a
tract becomes effective, the tract will not be taxed by the City and will not
be entitled to services from the City.
Section 3. A copy of this resolution shall be filed with the City Clerk.
Section 4. This resolution shall remain effective as provided by G.S. 160A-37
(i).
Adopted, this 13th day of March 2008.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer
Mayor

MARCH 25, 2008
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING
MARCH 25, 2008    3:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, NC
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson E. Adams, Donnie Potter, James Brown,
            Ed Boguskie, Jwantana Frink and Paul D. Fisher
ABSENT:         None
STAFF PRESENT:      Chad Hicks, Interim City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
            Mike Isenberg, City Attorney
            Ralph Cardwell, Interim Public Services Director
OTHERS:         Louis Roberti, Chairman, Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District
            Tom Spivey, SBSD District Manager
            Don Loosley, SBSD Commissioner
            David Pond, Engineer, W.K. Dickson, Representing the Southeast
Brunswick Sanitary District
            Carter Hubard, Engineer, W.K. Dickson, Representing the City of
Southport
I.
Call To Order – 3:00 p.m.
Mayor Sandra Spencer called the Special Meeting to order pursuant to notice
duly advertised and posted.
II.
Invocation
Invocation delivered by Alderman Brown.
III.
Purpose of Meeting
Mayor Spencer stated the purpose of the Special Meeting is to discuss the
City's plans for wastewater treatment because changes are underway with SBSD
and the Board needs to discuss its options. She asked Aldermen Potter and
Boguskie, members of the Wastewater Committee to report.
Alderman Potter informed the Board that they attended one meeting with the
Sanitary District and plans were discussed to handle the City's Wastewater
Treatment. The State has mandated that the City close its Wastewater Treatment
Plant by 2011. The City has a contract with SBSD to treat the City's wastewater
and they propose to expand the facility to include 900 mgpd. The expansion
project was discussed at a possible cost of $16 up to $18 million (dollars). He
and Alderman Boguskie asked staff to look for other alternatives, including the
County. Staff will present their options from the County at the April meeting.
He explained that the City is at a point with sewer problems regarding
allocation.
Mr. Carter Hubard of W. K. Dickson discussed O & M for a cost of $250,000 per
year. Staff evaluated the cost and estimated it to be at $500,000 for O & M,
which includes staff, building and equipment.
Alderman Potter stated that SBSD is looking for a commitment from the City but
the City has not received actual numbers. If the capital cost is estimated at
$16 million, the City has to pay it back and the plan calls for a 40-year
period. He is not convinced that the SBSD is the answer. He realizes the City
has a current contract with SBSD, however; Southport may be the only
municipality that has partnered with the SBSD, along with South Harbor and the
Long Beach Road communities. He is concerned that 30 years down the road, SBSD
may cease to exist. It is his belief that the City should look at other
options. He is concerned about the citizens and the affordability of sewer.
Mr. Hubard gave the Board a handout with variables showing payment terms with
the SBSD. He cited $11.5 million for capital and additional cost of $5-
6 million. The City looked at impact fees for new construction, etc. The
initial amount was $47.50 for an average residential customer. The new proposed
rate will be $70-$87.00 based on capital cost of SBSD with participation in
disposal facility.
Alderman Fisher asked if the estimated numbers were based on the 2004 Agreement
between the City and Sanitary District, which outlines the fee structure. He
stated that it was never the city's intent for the SBSD to use the city's
disposal area, and if they wish to use it, they would have to pay the city. He
stated in his last discussion with the SBSD it was his understanding if the
city sent 1000-gallons for treatment, and the SBSD sent 1000 gallons to the
city's disposal site, that it would be a wash. He does not understand the SBSD
not planning to use the city's spray fields when they cannot take the 200,000
gallons per the agreement, they did get up to 170,000 and SBSD could not handle
this and now the City's at 40,000 gpd. His belief is that they should adhere to
the 2004 contract agreement until they can prove to the city that they can do
better.
Alderman Boguskie asked the Engineer at what point does the City want to
increase capacity from 950,000 to 1.5 million. Mr. Hubard stated it depends on
the ETJ, population density, and projected flow and other factors.
Mr. Hicks stated in response to a question from Mayor Spencer, that the SBSD
over allocated for their treatment plant and before they can handle sewer
expansion, it has to be cleared through the Division of Water Quality.
Alderman Fisher stated Southport has not exceeded its allocation; the city was
locked in with the SBSD, which reduced the City's allocation. The concept plan
at the time the 2004 contract was entered into with everything completed, the
rate would have been between $35 and $39. For the benefit of the public,
Alderman Fisher explained the relationship between the City and SBSD. The Food
Lion Complex was on a package plant, it did not operate properly and the state
closed it down. The City was approached about treating their effluent if they
ran a six-inch line. The SBSD could not handle their effluent at this
particular time, and the city agreed to raise it to an eight-inch line in
anticipation of doing 200,000 p/day flow reversal. This started the City's
relationship with the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District.
Alderman Brown stated at the time the City entered into contract with the SBSD,
the county was not an option and the city attempted to do the right thing at
the right time.
In response to questions from Board members, City Attorney Isenberg explained
if the SBSD does not adhere to the terms set forth in their contractual
obligations, the City could look at other options.
Mayor Spencer stated that the City has an existing contract, the SBSD cannot
honor it, and therefore they have asked the City to re-negotiate the terms of
the contract. Attorney Isenberg recommended staff get cost estimates from the
Engineer and compare to the County. Alderman Potter asked that staff put all
the data together and present to the Board in order that citizens may be aware
of what is going on.
Alderman Adams asked about a Special Meeting with the county in order to ask
questions and get answers in to be prepared for the regular meeting in April.
No further discussion, Mayor Spencer called a recess at 4:05 to reconvene at 4:
30 p.m. with representatives from the Sanitary District.
Reconvened Meeting – 4:30 p.m. (Alderman Adams excused)
Mayor Spencer called the meeting back to order. Those present representing the
South Brunswick Sanitary District were Louis Roberti, Chairman, Tom Spivey,
Manager, David Pond, Engineer, W.K. Dickson and Don Loosley, District
Commissioner.
Mr. Pond, Engineer, stated it is his understanding this meeting was held to
receive information and clarification in order that a decision can me made in
the interest of both entities and their customers.
Mayor referenced the following letter from the Sanitary District requesting a
decision from the Board by March 30. Mr. Pond explained that the letter was
asking for a decision based on a schedule developed by the engineers because of
environmental assessments and reports that must be submitted in a timely manner
in order to proceed with plans by a designated date. However, they realize the
City does not want to make a decision within the thirty (30) day period
requested. He asked that the Board evaluate the agreement including costs, and
asked about other issues of interest to the City. (See letter below)
SOUTHEAST BRUNSWICK SANITARY DISTRICT
"WORKING FOR THE PEOPLE OF SOUTHEAST BRUNSWICK SANITARY DISTRICT"
March 19, 2008
Mayor Sandra Spencer, City of Southport
201 E. Moore Street
Southport, NC 28461
Dear Mayor Spencer:
We need to come to closure, by March 31, 2008, on your commitment to the
District to continue its treatment of Southport's wastewater and the required
plant expansion. As we know treatment of the City of Southport wastewater will
enable the City to close its treatment plants so it can eliminate disposal of
its reclaimed water into the Intracoastal Waterway.
March 31, 2008 is a critical date since the engineers will be submitting, April
1, 2008, Environmental Assessments (EA) and Preliminary Engineering Reports
(PER) to the USDA in support of funding requests to them for the City and the
District. They will not allow us to go ahead without both of our commitment to
our agreement.
We will also need to amend the agreement to reflect today's environment. Since
2004, wastewater treatment costs and expansion costs have increased.
The District will be ready to accept the 200,000 gpd (currently 70,000 gpd) in
April/May. We ask that the City verify that they can send us that amount, or
what amount, without causing City plant operational problems.
Total City gallons treated by the District will be 1,000,000 gpd.
Any delays past March 31, 2008 can cause increases to our costs and therefore
increases in rates to the City.
To move this project forward, we suggest a meeting next week to discuss this
and resolve any open issues. We have asked David Pond, PE, executive vice
president of WK Dickson, to facilitate this meeting. Mr. Pond was instrumental
in the planning for this District and City project. Dates that are available
are next Tuesday the 25th and Wednesday the 26th in the morning.
Since this will be a policy and procedural meeting I suggest that we limit the
meeting attendees to you, Alderman Boguskie and Potter and Interim City Manager
Chad Hicks. The District will have me, Commissioner Loosley and District
Manager Tom Spivey attending. WK Dickson will have Mr. Pond and our Project
Managers.
If you need any further information or have any questions, please contact me.
Respectfully,
/s/ Louis Roberti, Chairman
Southeast Brunswick
Sanitary District
Cc: Ed. Boguskie, City Alderman
D. Potter, City Alderman
C. Hicks, Interim City Manager
D. Pond, WK Dickson
D. Loosley, SBSD Commissioner
T. Spivey, SBSD District Manager
Mayor Spencer stated that the Board is concerned about the monthly charge to
its customers.
Attorney Isenberg stated that the City has a contract with the SBSD that has
set forth terms of the agreement and the SBSD proposes to modify the contract.
The Board has concerns about the proposed cost to the City.
Mr. Roberti, Chairman of the SBSD stated that both parties agreed that the
contract needed to be modified and he has notes attesting to this. He explained
that this matter has been discussed over the course of two years and
representatives from the City were aware of the cost to expand the treatment
plant. Alderman Fisher stated that he was on the Wastewater Committee and he
was opposed to the requested modifications. Mr. Roberti explained that things
have changed in terms of costs. He asked Mayor Spencer to appoint a Committee
to work with them because the SBSD does not want to break the agreement; they
are ready to propose rates and move forward. It is their belief that the rates
represent equitable costs for the District and City.
Mr. Hicks, Interim Manager stated staff has not been given numbers on the
proposed rate changes by the SBSD. Attorney Isenberg stated any changes to the
contract with have to be approved by the Board of Aldermen.
Mr. Pond stated the contract allows for modifications. Attorney Isenberg
responded only if both parties agree that the contract should be modified.
Alderman Boguskie stated that it his belief that the SBSD is not capable of
handling the 200,000 gpd. Mr. Roberti replied that if the City has 200,000 gpd
of effluent, that they are ready to accept it.
Mayor Spencer stated the cost per customer as proposed would change to $88.00
per month. She referenced a letter that was sent to the Sanitary District on
November 7, 2007 from the City stating that some of the rates were not
acceptable, and it requested the Sanitary District accept the allocation as
originally proposed.
Mr. Roberti explained that the District had a spill in November and was not
able to accept 200,000 gpd of effluent and the City worked with them. Alderman
Potter stated he is not convinced that the City needs to approve the current
agreement because there are some gray areas that need to be addressed. Mr. Pond
asked that these items be addressed, realizing that the rates are an issue.
(Below is the letter given to the Mayor with proposed rates from SBSD)
SOUTHEAST BRUNSWICK SANITARY DISTRICT
"WORKING FOR THE PEOPLE OF SOUTHEAST BRUNSWICK SANITARY DISTRICT"
March 25, 2008
Mayor Sandra Spencer, City of Southport
201 E. Moore Street
Southport, NC 28461
Dear Mayor Spencer:
We are proposing the following rate structure for the treatment of the City of
Southport's wastewater at the District's plant. The rates are based upon
current cost and financial estimates for the plant expansion, reflecting impact
fees paid and the CWMTF grant as well as the City's share of the District's
expenses for wastewater treatment. As such, the rates are subject to change.
The plant will be expended to 2.0 m gpd and the City will have 1.0M gpd
wastewater treatment capacity.
All rates are based upon the premises that the City and the District complete
their plans by June 30, 2010.
Rates for the period ending June 30, 2010:
Base Sewer Rate will be $7.50, one time monthly charge.
Variable Change will be $4.23 per 1000 gallons
Impact Fees will be $20,500 per month
Interest fee on the City's share of the borrowed money will be $18,400 per
month.
Rates beginning July 1, 2010:
Base Sewer Rate will not be charged:
Variable Charge will be $5.53 per 1000 gallons
Capital Cost Fee will be $42,500 per month until June 30, 2030.
If you have any questions or comments, please contact me.
Respectfully,
/s/ Louis Roberti

Mr. Roberti stated the Sanitary District is prepared to move forward with the
Agreement, but if the City wants to re-examine the contract, they are in hopes
of receiving an answer by March 31. Attorney Isenberg stated the City is not
ready to make a decision on the Agreement and need to examine other
alternatives.
Mr. Hicks asked for a period of 60-90 days. Mr. Roberti responded that they
will do all they can to assist the City.
Mr. Pond explained that he recognizes the perception since W. K. Dickson
represents the SBSD and the City. If either party wishes a second engineering
opinion, he would be glad to offer his assistance.
Mayor asked that the Utility Committee meet with representatives from the
Sanitary District. (Aldermen Boguskie, Potter, Hicks and Cardwell)
Alderman Fisher stated that the City raised its impact fees to cover the cost
of the system so customers would not have to pay more. The revenues from the
impact fees went into capital improvements, which was the original concept of
the City.
Mayor Spencer questioned how the cost doubled and requested a cost analysis.
Both parties established June 12 as the date for a decision to determine if the
City wish to continue with the project.
No further discussion, the meeting was adjourned at 5:35 p.m. upon motion of
Mayor Brown, seconded by Alderman Potter, vote carried.

APRIL 10, 2008
REGULAR MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN REGULAR MEETING MINUTES
APRIL 10, 2008    7:30 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Donnie Potter, James C. Brown,
            Richard "Ed" Boguskie, Jwantana Frink and Paul Fisher
ABSENT:         None
STAFF PRESENT:      Chad Hicks, Interim City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, CMC- Clerk
            Mike Isenberg, City Attorney
            Ralph Cardwell, Interim Public Services Director
I.
Call to Order – 7:30 p.m.
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m.
II.
Invocation
Rev. Charles Drew, Pastor of Lighthouse Pentecostal Church delivered the
invocation.
III.
Approval of Minutes
Alderman Brown moved, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to approve March 13 regular
meeting minutes and special meeting minutes of March 6 and 25th. Vote carried.
IV.
Approval of Agenda
Mayor Spencer requested that an executive session be added to the agenda under
Item IX for the purpose of personnel. (City Manager) Alderman Potter moved to
amend the agenda to include the requested item, seconded by Alderman Adams,
vote carried.
V.
Committee Reports
There were no Committee reports.
VI.
Departmental Reports
Reports placed in Board's agenda packet.
VII.
Old Business
None to be presented.
VIII.
New Business
a.    CUP request for Southport Marina (Public Hearing)
b.    CUP request for Jeff Ward Bed and Breakfast (Public Hearing)
Alderman Potter moved to enter Public Hearing to receive public comments on the
above referenced Conditional Use Permit requests. Motion seconded by Alderman
Brown, vote carried.
Mayor Spencer read the requirements for granting a Conditional Use Permit.
(Clerk swore in citizens wishing to speak on the Conditional Use Permits)
Mr. Robin Rose, representative for Southport Marina stated Southport Marina
requested a conditional use permit to maximize the space available by
constructing a first class dry storage building which can house up to 76
additional boats. Mr. Rose explained that the design would be first class and
quality in keeping with other construction that has been done at the marina and
the citizens of Southport will be proud of it. He stated the facility would not
devalue adjoining property and would have a positive impact on the economy.
Mrs. Stephanie Van Noordt, Architect stated the building is designed with a
pitch, which is typical for the design of the proposed structure. In answer to
a question from Alderman Boguskie, she stated that 40 ft would be a hardship,
as any developer wishes to maximize the use of their property. The requested 50
ft structure can house an additional 76 boats. She explained that they met the
four points of the criteria as enumerated in the UDO.
Mr. Hicks, Planner and Interim Manager stated (March 20) the Planning Board
made a recommendation to approve a height extension for a proposed dry storage
building at the Southport Marina. In addition to the requirements of the UDO,
the Planning Board recommended that as a condition of approval, the Southport
Marina make a curb out between the main parking area and the boat ramps to aid
drivers using the facilities.
The Marina has requested a CUP that would allow them to construct a 50'
building. The UDO regulations state that if a height extension is requested, a
CUP must be issued. The Board must decide if the following conditions are
satisfied prior to granting a CUP.
1.   That the use will not materially endanger the public health, safety, or
general welfare if located where proposed and developed according to the plan
submitted.
2.    That the use will meet all required conditions and specifications.
3.   That the use will not adversely affect the use or any physical attribute
of abutting or adjoining property, or that the use is a public necessity.
4.   That the location and character of the use, if developed according to the
plans submitted and approved, will be in harmony with the area in which it is
to be located and in general conformity with the City of Southport Land Use
Plan.
Alderman Adams talked about granting CUP's circumventing the height
restrictions in the UDO and he does not want to see a hotel or motel chain come
in and ask for a CUP. Mr. Hicks explained that the four criteria must be met.
Alderman Brown interjected that each request should be considered on its own
merit. Alderman Potter stated that it is his belief that granting a CUP for
height change could open up "a can of worms." Attorney Isenberg stated that the
Board may wish to consider removing height exception as a requirement for a
CUP.
Mr. Woody Wilson of 502 W. Brunswick Street read the City's mission statement
and stated if the Board approved the CUP, this will establish a precedent and
he asked that the Board support the UDO 40 ft. height restriction because the
UDO is a tool that provides guidance for growth.
Mr. Phillip King of 520 Brunswick Street stated opposition to raising the
height limit to 50 ft. because he believes that this action will set a
precedent.
Mr. Gene Holyfield stated his support of the marina. He commented that the old
building was 48 ft. and what difference will two feet make. The marina is a
first class operation with first class people.
Mr. Paul Swenson of 207 E. Brown Street stated the marina is an asset and first
class, but may be sold one day and the new owners may not have the same
consideration for the citizens. He asked if the Conditional User Permit is
granted, that the Board require perpetual public access.
Mark Johnson told the Board that he is a proponent of boating and every
facility up and down the coast is full. If the Council limits dry storage, then
they limit public access to the water.
Mr. Russ Ferris of 406 West West asked that the Council think about public
input before they act on matters.
There were no further comments on the Conditional Use Permit for Southport
Marina.
b)     Mr. Jeff Ward, Bed & Breakfast CUP request.
Mr. Jeff Ward told the Board that he propose to make the Robert Ruark House at
119 North Lord Street into a Bed and Breakfast. He stated that there is a need
for this type of accommodations in Southport especially near the downtown area.
He stated that sufficient parking is available and there would be no signs or
lights to bother the neighbors.
Mr. Hicks noted that the Planning Board recommended approval of the B&B, which
will house four bedrooms and baths for guest occupancy. No new impervious
surface will be added to the site and pervious grass pavers will be used for
guest parking. He read the conditions that must be satisfied before granting a
Conditional Use Permit.
1.   That the use will not materially endanger the public health, safety, or
general welfare if located where proposed and developed according to the plan
submitted.
2.   That the use will meet all required conditions and specifications.
3.   That the use will not adversely affect the use or any physical attribute
of abutting or adjoining property, or that the use is a public necessity.
4.   That the location and character of the use, if developed according to the
plans submitted and approved, will be in harmony with the area in which it is
to be located and in general conformity with the City of Southport Land Use
Plan.
Mr. John Eide of 208 W. Nash Street stated his opposition to a Bed & Breakfast
in their neighborhood. He explained that he leases the house next door and they
were not notified of the request for a Conditional Use Permit. He stated
bringing commercial enterprise into a residential neighborhood would lower
their property values and the comfort of the neighbors will be affected.
Mr. Ward in answer to questions from Alderman Boguskie stated a manager would
be in residence and meals would be prepared on site.
Mr. Carl Taylor, resident of Arbor Creek, told the Board that he operates a Bed
& Breakfast in New Bern, NC. He stated that this business would enhance the
area and there is a need for this type of accommodation in the City.
No further comment, the Public Hearing was closed at 8:35 p.m. upon motion of
Alderman Brown, seconded by Alderman Potter. Vote carried.
Attorney Isenberg explained that the law states the applicant is entitled to a
Conditional Use Permit if they have complied with the criteria set forth in the
Unified Development Ordinance; however, the burden of proof is on the opponents
to prove these conditions do not exist. He stated if a motion to approve is
presented, the criteria must be identified; and if not, facts must be
established as to why the CUP is denied. He explained that general assertion is
not competent evidence. If the Board wishes to defer consideration, they may
not talk to the general public except in an open Board meeting. However, if any
of the member's spoke to the proponents prior to the Hearing, it should be
brought to the attention of the Board.
For the record, Mayor Spencer stated that she and Alderman Frink visited the
marina. Alderman Brown, Fisher and Adams also noted that they spoke with Mr.
Rose.
Alderman Fisher stated it is his belief that the Southport Marina will one day
be returned to the City and when it does, he wants it to be the best marina. He
stated if the City currently owned the marina that it would be leased. He
explained that the City has an active request in the Governor's office and the
legislature, requesting that the Marina be returned to the City of Southport.
Alderman Fisher motioned to approve the Conditional Use Permit for a dry
storage boat building with a curb cut between the main parking area and the
boat ramp to aid drivers using the facilities. Motion seconded by Alderman
Brown. (Alderman Brown stated the marina is first class and he wants to insure
that everyone has access to the water and it is accessible to the public.)
Discussion: Alderman Adams stated approving the CUP would set a precedent.
Attorney Isenberg stated the opponent must prove by setting forth facts that
the criteria have not been met. A CUP is allowable in the UDO for the marina
zoning district.
Alderman Potter stated that he and Mr. Boguskie did not visit the marina
because visiting the site could have prejudiced their opinion.
Alderman Fisher stated that he and Alderman Brown visited the marina to be
familiar and knowledgeable in order to make the right decision.
No further discussion the votes were: 2 ayes; Aldermen Fisher and Brown.
4 noes, Alderman Adams, Potter, Frink and Boguskie. Motion failed.
Alderman Adams motioned to deny the Conditional Use Permit for Southport Marina
dry storage boat building because it does not meet criteria #3 " that the use
will not adversely affect the use or any physical attribute of abutting or
adjoining property, or that the use is a public necessity." He stated that the
proposed 50 ft. building would obstruct the area view and decrease the value of
city property from the East. Alderman Potter seconded the motion, the votes
were 4 ayes: Alderman Adams, Potter, Boguskie and Frink. 2 noes, Alderman Brown
and Fisher. CUP denied.

Lowe White Park
Mr. Hicks told the Board that the City is ready to begin work on the Lowe-White

City's share is $241,351. He stated that it is staff's belief that the project
can be completed by year end and recommended the Board approve the extra cost
and proceed with constructing the park per grant application. He stated if the
park is re-designed, the City may risk losing the grant. He stated that there

Franklin Square Art Gallery
Mr. Hicks reported that the Associated Artists have requested the City pay to
build a platform landing (fire escape) at the base of the newly installed
elevator.  The building belongs to the City and is leased by the Associated
Artists. In order to meet building code, a fire escape must be built at the
elevator base. The platform will cost $4,150. Mrs. Stephanie VanNoordt, present
for another agenda item and Architect for this project, told the Board the
elevator cannot be used until compliant with code. She stated the platform is
required in the event of an emergency where people escaping from the second
floor can remain on the fire escape (platform) until rescued. It must be large
enough to comply with State Code. Alderman Brown stated the City owns the
building and if someone got hurt, the City would be liable. Alderman Adams
suggested this be considered during the new budget. Alderman Fisher moved to
approve $4,150 from fund balance, seconded by Alderman Brown. Vote was
unanimous.

VIII.-G.
Resolution of Support State Tourism
Alderman Potter moved seconded by Alderman Boguskie, to adopt the following
resolution of support for additional funding for State Tourism. Vote carried.
RESOLUTION SUPPORTING ADDITIONAL FUNDING OF THE NORTH CAROLINA DIVISION OF
TOURISM, FILM AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT
WHEREAS, in 2007, tourism generated $16.5 billion in travel expenditures,
$1.344 billion in state and local taxes, $4 billion in payroll and employed
more than 190,000 North Carolinians, and
WHEREAS, although consistently ranking among the top 10 states in visitation,
North Carolina's travel marketing budget ranks only 21st among the 50 states
and 8th among peer southern competitors, and
WHEREAS, South Carolina has increased its budget to approximately $46 million
for 2008-09 and will be investing in domestic marketing and advertising at a
more than 3:1 advantage over North Carolina, and
WHEREAS, North and South Carolina draw visitors from the same states and
markets and South Carolina stands to increase its market share at the expense
of North Carolina if the state does not respond to this threat immediately, and
WHEREAS, independent research conducted by Longwoods International reported
North Carolina receives $185 in new visitor spending and more than $15 in state
and local tax revenues for every dollar invested in paid advertising, an
impressive ROI of more than 15:1 on the state's investment, and
WHEREAS, based on Longwoods findings and the 2007 TIA Economic Impact of
Tourism Study on North Carolina's Economy, an additional $5 million for the
Division's statewide marketing efforts would generate $925 million in new
visitor spending and more that $75 million in new state and local tax revenues,
and
WHEREAS, tourism provides public and private sector benefits in all 100
counties. In 2006, Brunswick County ranked 9th among the 100 counties in
visitor spending with $367.87 million in expenditures, $75.41 million in
payroll, nearly 5000 people employed, and $23.97 million in local tax receipts.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Brunswick County Tourism Development
Authority does hereby urge Governor Easley and the North Carolina General
Assembly to increase the Division of Tourism's statewide marketing program by
$5 million.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Brunswick County Tourism Development Authority
does hereby encourage the tourism industry of Brunswick County to contact
Governor Easley and our legislators in support of said additional funding.
Adopted this 10th day of April, 2008
               ATTEST:
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor      /s/ Regina Alexander, City Clerk

IX-A.
Other Business - Power Services Inc.
The Board heard from Mr. Willoughby of Power Services, Inc. who performed an
evaluation of the request from Piedmont Natural Gas for a franchise to install
a natural gas system in the City and to determine the benefit or impact to the
electrical system. He gave the Board a written report and stated the
impossibility of giving an exact estimate on the potential impact that natural
gas would have on the electrical systembecause they do not know who would buy
into it. He stated of the 1,937 customers, the city could lose $21 a month from
residential customers (hot water heaters) and for an entire house $32. He
stated the City might have an advantage by requiring the company to put in
underground cables. He stated it is in the Board's best interest to work out
the best franchise for the City. City Attorney Isenberg stated the former City
Manager negotiated an Agreement to control what Piedmont Natural Gas does. He
stated if it was the Board's desire he would proceed with the Agreement. It was
the consensus that the Attorney continue negotiations with Piedmont Natural Gas
on a Franchise Agreement to include underground cables.

A.    Resolution closing out Southport Wastewater System- (Patty Miller,
Finance Director)
Alderman Fisher motioned, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to approve the
following resolution closing out Southport's Wastewater System Enhancement
Phase I Capital Project Fund. Vote carried.
RESOLUTION CLOSING OUT SOUTHPORT WASTEWATER SYSTEM ENHANCEMENT – PHASE (I)
CAPITAL PROJECT FUND
WHEREAS, the Wastewater System Enhancement, Phase I Project has been completed;
and
WHEREAS, it is appropriate to close out the Fund accounting for this project in
accordance with the State Statutes and generally accepted accounting
principles;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen, that
the Wastewater System Enhancement Phase I Capital Project Fund is hereby
completed and that the Fund accounting for revenues and expenditures concerning
this project is closed out in accord with the following provisions:
1.   The fund will be closed upon receipt of any revenue outstanding as of
today’s date.
2.   Any excess revenue over expenditures will be automatically transferred to
the Water/Sewer Fund.
3.   Capital assets acquired or constructed as a result of this Capital Project
will be transferred to the Water/Sewer Fund for recording of fixed assets in
accordance with appropriate statutes and standards.
4.   The Finance Director is hereby authorized to make any Fund or accounting
adjustments necessary to effect the closing of this Fund.
Adopted this the 8th day of May, 2008.
/s/Mayor Sandra P Spencer

PROCLAMATION
ANNUAL MUNICIPAL CLERKS WEEK
MAY 4 - MAY 10, 2008
WHEREAS, the Office of the Municipal Clerk, a time honored and vital part of
local government exists throughout the world; and
WHEREAS, the Office of the Municipal Clerk is the oldest among public servants;
and
WHEREAS, the Office of the Municipal Clerk provides the professional link
between the citizens, the local governing bodies and agencies of government at
other levels; and
WHEREAS, the Municipal Clerk serves as the information center on functions of
local government and community; and
WHEREAS, Municipal Clerks continually strive to improve the administration of
the affairs of the Office of the Municipal Clerk through participation in
education programs, seminars, workshops and the annual meetings of their state,
province, county and international professional organizations; and
WHEREAS, it is most appropriate that we recognize the accomplishments of the
Office of the Municipal Clerk;
NOW, THEREFORE, I Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor of the City of Southport, does
recognize the week of May 4 through May 10, 2008 as “Municipal Clerks Week”,
and further extend appreciation to our Municipal Clerk Regina W. Alexander, and
to all Municipal Clerks for the vital services they perform and their exemplary
dedication to the communities they represent.
ADOPTED, the 8th day of May 2008.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor

EXECUTIVE SESSION
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION MAY 14, 2008
 
Attorney Isenberg referenced a statement made by Alderman Fisher on assessments
and explained to the Board that it cannot adopt a resolution of intent and
change its policy and begin assessing property owners. The Board policy must be
in effect at least 180 days if the Board wishes to consider levying assessments
for sewer. The city currently does not have such a policy in effect. The
planner, Mr. Holland, recommended obtaining a copy of the sanitary district
policy. Attorney Isenberg advised the Board that if the city decides to assess
an area, they must revise its current policy. If the Board wishes to establish
a policy and wants to wait 180 days before a resolution of intent is passed,
the Board can do it, but he believes 180 days is too long to wait.
Next Attorney Isenberg asked Mr. Holland to present possible annexation
alternatives for the Board to review and consider. Although other options were
briefly discussed, there were three main alternatives presented by the city
planner: (1) Commercial along Hwy 211, (2) Area along 211 to the Progress
Energy canal, and (3) Including Southgate and/or Carolina Lace in the
annexation areas. While these options were presented, Mr. Isenberg discussed
the legal issues related to these options and whether or not each alternative
safely satisfied the legal criteria and requirements for involuntary annexation
such as the contiguity, subdivision and use tests.
Attorney Isenberg asked the board for guidance as to which alternative it
favored and he told the board that the city is not bound until they pass a
resolution of intent, which is a declaration by the Board and can be adopted at
any meeting. He stated once a resolution of intent is adopted, you cannot add
to it, but you can subtract. The board asked Isenberg legal questions regarding
these alternatives and he advised the Board concerning the various issues,
including crossing the Progress Energy Canal.
Alderman Potter stated he favored taking in as much commercial as possible.
Attorney Isenberg asked the Board to give himself and Mr. Holland directives as
to which way the city want to proceed. Motion by Alderman Potter to direct the
City Attorney and Dale Holland to prepare and present a proposed resolution of
intent in June to the Board on options 1 and 4 for its consideration. Alderman
Boguskie seconded, the votes were 3 ayes Aldermen Potter, Boguskie and Brown. 1
no, Alderman Frink.
Motion by Alderman Potter to re-enter regular session, seconded by Alderman
Brown, vote carried.

SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N.C.
MAY 29, 2008      5:00 P.M.
 
PRESENT:           Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Donnie Potter, Ed Boguskie, Jwantana Frink,
            James Brown and Paul Fisher
ABSENT:         Alderman Nelson Adams
STAFF:         Regina Alexander, Interim Manager/Clerk
            Patty Miller, Finance Director
            Ralph Cardwell, Interim Director Public Services
            Dale Holland, Planner
I.
Call to Order
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.
II.
Invocation by Alderman Brown
III.
Presentation of FY 08-09 Budget
Ms. Patty Miller, Finance Director presented the City's proposed operating
budget for FY 2008-09. The Board scheduled June 6, 9:00 am as a special meeting
for the budget workshop.
IV.
Wastewater Options
Mr. Carter Hubard, Engineer with W. K. Dickson reiterated the projected costs
for residential customers under the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District's
(SBSD) proposal which is $84 under Option 1, County rate $62. Option 2 if the
city and county constructed a plant, the rate would be $42.50 per month but
increase to $75 after completion of the plant by 2012. Mr. Hubard told the
Board that the City's current permit to discharge into the Intracoastal
Waterway (ICWW) would expire 2011.
Mayor Spencer stated the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District needs an answer
by June 12. Clean Water Management Trust needs to know the Board's decision by
mid July. She stated that the City Attorney sent a letter to the District
asking them to honor the 2004 contractual agreement, but no answer has been
received as of this meeting.
In answer to question by Alderman Fisher, Mr. Hubard stated if the 2004 rate is
acceptable to the SBSD; the projected cost for residential customers is $74.
Alderman Boguskie stated SBSD cost totals $11,683,000, which is the City's
share of the facilities. Mr. Hubard stated that $682,000 is actual construction
costs, $55,000 O&M per year for the City, and $2.7 is the capital costs
associated with the disposal site.
In response to a question by Alderman Potter, Mr. Hubard stated when the
Professional Engineering Report was submitted May 2007; the agreement was based
on Southport and the SBSD using the disposal facility. He stated the costs were
favorable at this time; however, with the current analysis, Option #1 is better
with the County. He stated that the county's proposal would need the final
details worked out, i.e. ownership of force mains, transfer of ownership,
ability of county to receive Southport's flow and the best use of the property
near the Military Ocean Terminal at Sunny Point.
Mr. Jerry Pierce, Public Utilities Director for Brunswick County, stated the
county would support Southport's choice. If the City decided to join with the
County, it would be a partner and their books would be audited and available
for inspection. He stated that they meet quarterly with all partners. Mr.
Pierce stated the county would own the facilities. He stated if the City
decided to collaborate with the county and send their sewer, they would plan
for expansion of the Supply Plant or build a new plant near Sunny Point.
Mr. Ralph Cardwell, Interim Public Services Director, told the Board that the
city is linked with the SBDS and they will have to treat the City sewer. The
city can't stop sending flow to the SBSD. Clean Water Management Trust wants
sewer out of the ICWW. Option 1 is the only timeline in which the city can
achieve this goal. He told the Board that a private individual is willing to
pay a pumping station to transport wastewater to St. James, which will be
needed. He stated this would be a savings to the City of approximately $1
million. He recommended the Board consider Option 1 which would require minimum
staff.
Alderman Potter stated it is his belief that Option 1 is best for the City.
Alderman Adams asked that the Board schedule a workshop to review the options
discussed. The Board agreed to have a special meeting on Tuesday, June 10 at 6:
00 p.m.
Alderman Fisher asked staff and Mr. Hubard to submit the information in
summation prior to the meeting for review.
Adjournment – 6:40 p.m.
No further business, the meeting adjourned upon motion of Alderman Boguskie,
seconded by Alderman Frink, vote carried.

IV.
Discussion of City's Proposed Operating Budget FY 08-09
Ms. Patty Miller, Finance Officer presented the proposed fiscal year 08/09
operating budget. City's overall budget is $14,926,496, general fund balance
$4,753,792. Proposed ad valorem rate is $0.17 per $100 valuation of
$893,327,500 with a collection rate of 98%, which represents $0.02 cents tax
rate increase. $238,402 of fund balance appropriated as the City's portion of
Lowe White Park project. The other portion of fund balance appropriated is for
the cost in completing the Jaycee Building, replacing the porch railings on the
Community Building, construction cost for addition to Building Inspections and
computer equipment purchases.
Alderman Brown read the following statement:
To: Board and Department Heads
"I think the City should be runned as a business not on a profit and loss basis
but should be operated efficiently. Our primary goal is not to just keep the
tax rate down; of course, no one wants to pay more taxes than necessary. We
must consider the tax rate but more importantly, we must consider the health,
safety and welfare of our citizens. Providing more than adequate services in
all areas of our city government, maintaining all city property, equipment and
public facilities in the best possible condition, insuring that Southport is in
a clean and safe condition to welcome all visitors. We must govern to insure
that we leave Southport to our successors in number one condition. Therefore,
considering the tax rate while it is important, I have had a number of citizens
tell me that they would prefer to pay a little more taxes to have the streets
in better condition and to keep the facilities looking better. I know that when
I went on the Board in '85, everything was runned down. All the equipment,
everything that we had, we had to replace and we were working off yellow
tablets. So, those times are past, thank goodness, but while I think the tax
rate is important, I think that we need to look at the other areas as well."
Mayor agreed and stated, "That the duty is to the citizens to provide the best
services that we can and this is one of the reasons the Board is looking at
annexation. If Southport stays in its present configuration, taxes will
continue to increase but there comes a time that they will have to stop because
people simply cannot afford to pay more and the choice comes down to reducing
services, and she does not want to do that."
Mayor expressed her concern at using fund balance to balance the budget but
expressed appreciation to staff.
Mr. Thornton, City Manager stated he reviewed the proposed budget and financial
summaries. He asked for directives from the Board in accomplishing tasks within
the budget and will work towards that goal. He cited some areas in the current
budget of uncollected revenues of $1.4 million and $650,000 appropriation out
of fund balance in this budget year that has not been appropriated. CAMA Grant
for the Fort Johnston Boardwalk, money to meet city's obligation for PARTFF
Grant for Lowe-White Park, which can be implemented over a three (3) year
period, Police Department requests five new officers to accommodate annexation,
which can be implemented over a two year period from the date the annexation
becomes effective to provide services. He explained that there are areas in the
budget that needs to be examined including questions about expenditures and
revenues. He stated that he would compile additional budget information and
present to the Board, explaining that a budget is a planning document and can
be revised.
Alderman Fisher stated he supports the 5% COLA for city employees. He
recommended Mark Southerland, a 20 year employee be given a 10% increase
because he has saved the City money by doing work especially in the Jaycee

and Recreation.

Executive Session
 
Executive Session Minutes June 6, 2008
 
Attorney Isenberg told the Board that the Town of Oak Island adopted two
resolutions of intent to annex the Oakwood Glen Subdivision off Airport Road,
and 600+ acres on Long Beach Road that turns onto NC 211 and stops at Lowe's
Home Improvement, including one lot past Lowe's on the opposite side of the
road. City staff reviewed the map and resolutions of intent and they appeared
to be in order. He related that the annexation report must be approved thirty
(30) days before the public information meeting. Attorney Isenberg told the
Board that an engineering consulting firm worked on the project for
approximately three (3) years and according to Chad Hicks, City Planner, their
figures were conservative.
Attorney Isenberg told the Board that he talked with David Lawrence, Professor
at the School of Government, and he stated the first town that passes a
resolution of intent acquires that area unless a mistake is made in their
calculations. However, this will not be known until Dale Holland reviews Oak
Island's annexation report. The City still does not have an answer from
Progress Energy on the land request, but Mayor Spencer was told that
representatives from Raleigh would be coming down to meet with the local Plant
Manager and the Manager would contact City officials. Professor Lawrence agrees
with the City that if Progress Energy agrees to the subdivision test, the City
can legally jump over the canal; however, if they do not, the City will have a
legal argument by going down the road. He believes it may be worth trying to do
this, but there are no assurances. There is a case that would permit this
because the canal is manmade and it is not a natural waterway. The annexation
is still preferable if the city can use the Progress Energy property to go
across the canal.
Alderman Brown asked if there was anything that would preclude Lowe's and
others petitioning Southport for voluntary annexation. Attorney Isenberg stated
only if the petition was received prior to approval of the resolution of
intent.
Alderman Fisher asked if there was a law that precluded the City from adopting
a resolution of intent for the same area. Attorney Isenberg stated the city
could adopt a resolution of intent that includes some of the area, but unless
the city can show a mistake or legal error in Oak Island's report, they have
priority. Alderman Fisher explained that the City had to get permission from
the Town of St. James to annex the property known as Rivermist, and from the
City of Boiling Spring Lakes to annex property belonging to the City near Sunny
Point. Attorney Isenberg stated this was satellite, whereas a town cannot annex
anything that is closer to another town without a resolution of annexation
agreement between the respective towns. He explained that Oak Island's
annexation is contiguous.
Attorney Isenberg presented a map showing the annexation Southport has proposed
which includes some of the area Oak Island has proposed; including food lion,
cinema theatre and West Trace on the opposite side. This is a new combination
of option 1 and 2, which the City's resolution of intent is proposing. Attorney
Isenberg stated if Oak Island's annexation is upheld, the City might not be
able to go up to their boundary because it will not be able to meet the tests.
However, in the meantime, the City could work out an annexation agreement with
Oak Island, which could preclude them from going any further. The Attorney
showed various scenarios on the annexation map the City could pursue. Alderman
Fisher suggested adopting a resolution of intent for the same area and if a
mistake is found in their annexation plan, Southport will be on the books to
proceed.
City Manager Thornton apprised the Board of conversation with Dale Holland and
explained that Mr. Holland's preliminary review found everything appeared to be
in order. He wished to review the city limits boundary because during
preliminary review; the city limit did not appear to match GIS and he wished to
compare the map. Mr. Holland asked the Board for directives in proceeding with
the process.
Attorney Isenberg suggested the Board consider a resolution that directs him
and staff to perform the necessary paper work to challenge Oak Island's
annexation.
Alderman Fisher stated the City could potentially lose money because of the
Fire District extending to the area Oak Island proposes to annex. Attorney
Isenberg told the Board Brunswick County has a local act and if one town takes
property from another's fire district, they are required to pay one-half of the
fire fees for three years. Mr. Holland has prepared Resolutions of Intent, one
proceeding down both sides of the road (Hwy 211) to get across Progress
Energy's canal, and the other includes the Progress Energy Canal contingent
upon their approval.
There being no further discussion, Alderman Boguskie motioned to re-enter
regular session, seconded by Alderman Potter, vote carried.

Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor

Regina W. Alexander, CMC

JUNE 10, 2008
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
JUNE 10, 2008     6:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, NC
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Donnie Potter, James Brown,
            Richard "Ed" Boguskie and Paul Fisher
ABSENT:         Alderman Jwantana Frink
            Mike Isenberg, City Attorney
STAFF PRESENT:      Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
            Ralph Cardwell, Interim Director of Public Services
            Patty Miller, Finance Director
I.
Call to Order – 6:00 p.m.
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
II.
Invocation
Alderman Brown delivered the invocation.
III.
Wastewater Issues
Mayor Spencer gave council members a letter from Mr. Lou Roberti, Chairman of
the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District. She stated that Attorney Isenberg,
Mr. Thornton, City Manager and herself met with Mr. Roberti, Chairman of the
Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District, Attorney Prevatte and Mr. Ken Anderson.
She stated that the District had made some concessions and the information was
given to Carter Hubard, Engineer.
City Manager Thornton reported that he met with the City's Utility Committee
and they considered the revised rates in preparing the recommendation with the
understanding, what the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary would do if the City of
Southport chose to further its relationship with them.
Mr. Carter Hubard in his presentation gave staff and the Board a summarization
enumerating Wastewater Transmission Facilities, Reclaimed Water Transmission
Facilities and Reclaimed Water Site including a detailed analysis of Brunswick
County's proposal for wastewater treatment in comparison to service by the
Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District. The summarization included updates on
the project cost, sample rates, net present worth analysis, schedule including
advantages and disadvantages and recommendation to the Board. (Information
Incorporated as Attachment #1)
Mr. Hubard stated the three options were compared and the proposals evaluated.
His letter is a summary of the information presented on May 7, 2008
Mayor Spencer asked if the potential loss of the grant was considered in the
options. Mr. Hubard stated whatever option the city selects, a request should
be made to the Clean Water Management Trust to utilize the funds because the
goal is still to get the discharge out of the waterway. The timing is
different, the project may change, but there will be a request to use the funds
for city facilities to get the discharge out of the ICWW. The grant is
considered in the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District's proposal; however,
the grant funds are diminished in Options 1 & 2.
In answer to questions from Alderman Boguskie, Mr. Hubard stated $3 million in
CWMT grant has been set aside for transmission, pump station and disposal
facilities, and some of these funds have been used for professional services,
but there is still money under contract. Alderman Boguskie questioned if the
money is set aside, why go through the extension process. Mr. Hubard explained
one of the stipulations in the contract states if the schedule is revised,
there must be a request for an extension. Alderman Boguskie stated the schedule
with the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District was not met and questioned the
difference. Mr. Hubard stated when he contacted CWMT they requested a reason
for the schedule change be submitted, but they did not indicate funds would be
reduced based on the schedule. They will review the plans before the funding
amount is changed; potentially those monies may carry over to the options, but
he is not certain. Alderman Boguskie stated if the city elects to collaborate
with the county, they would get out of the waterway quicker which would be a
good reason.
Alderman Fisher asked about a timeline, and Mr. Hubard stated the removal of
discharge SBSD 2011, Brunswick County-Option 1, 2010 and Brunswick County
Option- 2, 2012. He asked about the grant under Phase II and what has been
engineered that pertains to SBSD including Options 1 and 2. Mr. Hubard stated
with SBSD the grant and site will be used according to plan. Funds expended
today are for high rate infiltration basins on the site. Option 1 with
indication from the county, the wastewater from the City would go to the Supply
plant. When capacity is reached and expansion is needed, which is projected to
be 10 years, they will evaluate a new facility, possibly the east plant near
Sunny Point or the west plant. The plan under Option 2 is to build a plant near
Sunny Point and Southport's disposal facility could be used to dispose of the
water from the treatment plant. The option 1 and the period presented in the
proposal is not committed to where the expansion would occur and how the site
would be used. He suggested if the City pursue this option, to make this part
of the agreement that the eastern facility be the location for the expansion
and use of the disposal site.
Mr. Hubard reviewed with the Board other details contained in the summary. In
concluding, it was recommended that the City pursue Brunswick County Option 1.
(See Option 1, Attachment # 1) See attachment # 2 with revised numbers
Alderman Adams asked that Attorney Isenberg explain the legalities to the Board
at the next regular scheduled meeting.
Garrison House
Mr. Thornton presented an estimate on the Garrison House bathroom renovations.
Alderman Fisher asked if the renovation included a changing station, which was
in the original plan. It was stated that the restrooms have to meet ADA
standards, i.e. ramps, window, locks and security lights. The Board consensus
was to award the contract to the lowest bidder R. L. Jones & Sons for
$2,018.24. (Other bidder was Wayne Smith & Son, Inc., $4,600.00)
No further business, motion by Alderman Boguskie to adjourn, seconded by
Alderman Adams, vote carried.

VII.
Presentation by Roger Globatt of the Federal Communications Commission
Mr. Globlatt of the FCC informed the Board and public that the Wilmington area
is a pilot program for the country in digital transition. The deadline for
conversion in Wilmington and surrounding counties is September 2008. The FCC is
attempting to get the word out through ads, media and public appearances to let
people know that if they have old technology, i.e. analog and antennas, they
will need to purchase converter boxes. Cable, satellite and digital TV's will
not present a problem. They are asking that people prepare for the conversion.
Public Hearing – Alderman Brown moved to enter Public Hearing to receive
comments on text revisions to the Unified Development Ordinance Amendments to
Articles 6, 11, and 12, Amendments to Section 14-8 and Amendment to Section 11-
1, Note 3. Motion seconded by Alderman Frink, vote carried
Attorney Isenberg stated the amendments are to set up procedure where the Board
of Adjustment rather than the Board of Aldermen will be responsible for the
issuance of conditional use permits. Most changes delete word "Board of
Aldermen" and replace with Board of Adjustment; the Planning Board recommended
adding church steeples to Note 3 of Article 11, Table of Area, Yard, Density
and Height Requirements.
Alderman Fisher asked when would a person apply for a conditional use permit
and noted with the proposed changes, there is no way an individual can apply
for a CUP. Attorney Isenberg stated only through a variance. Alderman Fisher
stated that he could envision in years to come the possibility that buildings
may exceed the 40 ft. requirement.
Alderman Frink asked about the possibility of hotels locating in this area and
the effect the height restriction may impose. Attorney Isenberg explained that
the Board could modify the height requirements.
Mr. Strickland, Building Inspector, stated the Planning Board deleted the
height requirement, however; they will hold a series of workshops to review all
conditional use designations in the UDO Table of Permitted Uses. Realizing that
a hotel could be located in Southport, the Planning Board will revisit the
height requirements to insure if there is a conditional use for height, the
conditions and location are specified.
Mayor asked that a letter from Steven Coggins be placed on file.
Woody Wilson of 502 Brunswick Street supports the Board of Adjustment ruling on
conditional use permits, which he stated would free the Aldermen to carry out
their normal duties and responsibilities.
No further discussion, Alderman Adams moved to re-enter regular session,
seconded by Alderman Brown, vote carried.
In regular session, Alderman Boguskie motioned to adopt the proposed amendments
and that the Board finds that the proposed amendments are consistent with the
City's Comprehensive Land Use Plan and that the amendments are reasonable and
in the public's interest by clarifying the City's Conditional Use Permits,
hearing procedures, and making the City's procedures conform to applicable law.
Motion seconded by Alderman Potter, the votes was five ayes: Alderman Boguskie,
Potter, Brown, Frink and Adams. One no, Alderman Fisher.

Old Business
a)   Second reading of an ordinance granting a franchise to Piedmont Natural
Gas Company, Inc.
Alderman Fisher motioned to approve the ordinance granting a franchise to
Piedmont Natural Gas Company, Inc., seconded by Alderman Boguskie, the vote of
approval was unanimous.
AN ORDINANCE GRANTING A FRANCHISE TO PIEDMONT NATURAL GAS COMPANY, INC.
BE IT ORDAINED BY THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT as follows:
1.   DEFINITIONS.
As used in this Ordinance, the following terms, words and phrases shall have
the meanings respectively ascribed to them in this section:
COMPANY shall mean Piedmont Natural Gas Company, Inc.; a corporation organized
under the laws of the State of North Carolina and authorized to do business in
the State of North Carolina and any successor in interest to Piedmont Natural
Gas Company, Inc. under this franchise Ordinance.
CITY or SOUTHPORT shall mean:
The City of Southport, a municipal corporation located in Brunswick County,
North Carolina, or
The area now or hereafter within the territorial City limits of the City of
Southport to the extent it may be lawfully included as presently or hereafter
fixed by law or ordinance, or
The Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport or any officer or agent duly
authorized and acting on behalf of the City as a municipal corporation, as
indicated by the context by which the term is used;
Board of Aldermen shall mean the governing body of the City of Southport;
Gas when used as an unqualified term shall mean either natural or artificial
gas, by whatever process or processes derived or manufactured, or both such
gases either separately or a mixture of them admixed as allowed by the proper
regulatory authorities.
2.   FRANCHISE GRANTED
Subject to the laws of the State of North Carolina and of the City of
Southport, and subject to the provisions of this ordinance, CITY hereby grants
the permission, right, privilege and franchise to COMPANY to supply, sell,
furnish and distribute gas to the inhabitants and consumers of SOUTHPORT, and
to construct, operate and maintain a gas utilities system, and for that purpose
to lay, install, construct, operate, repair and maintain the necessary gas
lines, pipes, conduits, devices and other facilities in the public streets and
alleys in the City of Southport for the furnishing, distribution and sale of
gas to the inhabitants and consumers in the City of Southport. It is mutually
understood and agreed that this franchise is non-exclusive.
3.    TERRITORY. 
The area to be covered by this franchise shall include the present corporate
limits of the City of Southport and any future areas which may be annexed to
the existing corporate limits.
4.    DURATION.
The duration of this franchise shall be for a period of 20 years from and after
the enactment of this ordinance upon and after its second reading at a regular
meeting of the Board of Aldermen.
5.    OBLIGATION TO FURNISH GAS.
COMPANY hereby covenants and agrees, at its own cost and expense, to extend its
piped gas distribution system and to deliver and distribute gas to customers as
required and governed by COMPANYS North Carolina Service Regulations, Sections
7, 8 & 13, as approved by the NCUC, and any other applicable governmental laws
and regulations, and subject to COMPANYS determination of economic feasibility
in accordance with the criteria set forth in those regulations.
6.    COMMENCEMENT OF SERVICE.
COMPANY shall, upon enactment of this ordinance, proceed with due diligence and
good faith to secure such rights of way, easements, permits and licenses which
are necessary for extending service hereunder. Service hereunder shall be
available to customers in the City of Southport within two years from the
granting of this franchise; if not, SOUTHPORT may declare this franchise null
and void.
7.    COMPLIANCE.
COMPANY shall comply with all applicable rules and regulations of the NCUC and
any other governmental agency having jurisdiction over the work and products of
COMPANY as well as all applicable rules, ordinances and regulations of
SOUTHPORT which are not in conflict with the rules of the NCUC or the U. S.
Department of Transportation. COMPANY shall comply with all provisions of this
franchise where the same can be done without violating the rules of the NCUC or
any other governmental agency having jurisdiction over the work and products of
COMPANY.
8.    QUALITY & PRESSURE; METERS
The quality and pressure of the gas to be furnished and supplied within the
City of Southport shall conform to or exceed the quality standards and conform
to the pressure standards set by appropriate regulatory authorities. Meters
shall be installed, inspected and maintained by COMPANY in accordance with the
standards promulgated by the NCUC or other applicable regulatory authorities.
9.    TIME OF WORK.
Except in the case of an emergency or other similar situation requiring
immediate repairs in order to protect the health and safety of the public,
construction, installation, maintenance or repair work to be undertaken on the
COMPANYS natural gas distribution system in the public streets or alleys of the
City of Southport may only be performed during the times allowed therefor in
the permit issued by SOUTHPORT to COMPANY pursuant to Paragraph 11 below,
excepting, however, that no such work may be performed on any legal holidays
observed by the CITY.
10.   USE OF STREETS.
The construction, operation and maintenance of COMPANYs gas system shall be
done in a manner which minimizes to the greatest extent practicable (within
reasonable economic costs) interference with the public use of the streets,
alleys, public ways and other public places of SOUTHPORT and damage to the area
disturbed. No gas pipes or mains shall be laid in the same trenches in which
water, sewer or electric lines are laid except as allowed by permit and by
applicable state and federal regulatory standards. COMPANY shall construct,
install , locate and maintain its mains and pipes so as to be compatible with
the construction, location and maintenance of existing water, sewer, cable,
underground electric service or electrical connections, laterals or mains.
COMPANY and SOUTHPORT agree to evaluate and consider the feasibility of joint
trenching in circumstances where COMPANY and SOUTHPORT mutually determine that
the application of such technology is appropriate. In circumstances in which
SOUTHPORTs and COMPANYs facilities are installed in the same trench, or
otherwise in close proximity to each other, each party shall install its
facilities in a manner that will not interfere with the construction, location
and maintenance of the facilities of the other party.
11.   EXCAVATION.
Except in the event of emergencies in which the public health and safety
require immediate excavation to make repairs, COMPANY shall not excavate in the
public streets, alleys or other public property of the City of Southport until
it shall have obtained from SOUTHPORT a permit approving and setting forth the
location and times allowed for the proposed excavation, and any other
appropriate conditions. A reasonable fee may be charged for this permit. All
excavation, backfilling and paving shall be subject to inspection by SOUTHPORT
and such work shall be made in compliance with all rules, laws and regulations
of SOUTHPORT. In the event of emergency repairs, however, COMPANY shall obtain
a permit as soon as practicable under the circumstances. CITY agrees to act
upon a permit application within a reasonable time.
In all cases where a public street, alley or other public way is excavated,
altered, disturbed or encumbered by COMPANY, it shall take all precautions
necessary or proper for the protection of the public and shall maintain
adequate warning signs, barricades, signals and other devices necessary to give
adequate notice or warning to the public of the existence of all conditions and
hazards present. COMPANY shall undertake every reasonable option available to
prevent creating a hardship to adjoining properties.
12.    RESTORATION.
COMPANY shall, promptly after installing or repairing mains, pipes or other
facilities, refill the trenches in which the pipes are located according to the
standards and requirements set by SOUTHPORT and shall keep the excavated area
in a safe condition. In addition, COMPANY shall promptly restore, repair and
replace pavement, sidewalk, curb, gutter, streets, alleys, water and sewer
infrastructure, underground electrical service and components, and stormwater
collection and conveyance facilities or other property of SOUTHPORT destroyed
or damaged by such excavation or other work to their approximate former
condition with like materials. In the event that COMPANY cuts or disturbs a
section of sidewalk paving, COMPANY shall restore the whole section by a new
section rather than only replacing the cut-out area. All repair, replacement
and restoration work shall be subject to inspection and approval by SOUTHPORT
and shall be completed within 21 days from the date of damage unless such work
requires immediate attention (such as damaged water, sewer or electrical lines)
in which case it shall be repaired, replaced or restored within 8 hours of the
time of damage. In the event that the restoration work is not acceptable to
SOUTHPORT or is not completed within said time period, CITY may do all or part
of such work at the sole cost or expense of COMPANY. COMPANY agrees to
reimburse CITY for said costs and expenses within 30 days of demand therefore
by CITY.
13.    INSPECTION.
SOUTHPORT shall have the right, but not the duty, to inspect all excavation,
construction, backfilling and paving work performed by COMPANY pursuant to this
franchise and to perform such other inspections as it deems necessary to insure
compliance with the franchise.
14.    REGRADING.
In the event that any of COMPANYS facilities are within the public streets ,
alleys or other public property of the City of SOUTHPORT and work to such
public streets, alleys or public property necessitates the movement, removal or
relocation of the COMPANYS facilities affected by such work, the COMPANY shall
promptly move, remove or relocate its facilities upon notification by SOUTHPORT
and COMPANY shall bear the cost of moving, removing or relocating such
facilities; provided, however, that SOUTHPORT will reimburse the COMPANY for
such costs if the COMPANYS right of occupancy in its existing location is other
than by virtue of this franchise and SOUTHPORT has not succeeded to the
interests of the party granting COMPANY its right of occupancy.
15.    REPAVING.
If SOUTHPORT decides to pave, repave or otherwise improve a street or public
way , it shall give 90 days prior notice to COMPANY of its intention with
regard to the paving or repaving. COMPANY shall use its best efforts to perform
such work as it deems necessary for the planned extension of new lines or
repair of existing lines within the street or public way prior to the time that
SOUTHPORT begins paving, repaving or otherwise improving said street or public
way. If COMPANY fails to perform such work prior to the paving, repaving or
other improvements by SOUTHPORT, but later performs such work within one year
from the date that SOUTHPORT completes the paving, repaving or other
improvements to that portion of the street or public way, COMPANY shall at its
own expense repave the section of the street or public way disturbed by
COMPANYS work to the reasonable satisfaction of SOUTHPORT or the N. C.
Department of Transportation. If COMPANYs work occurs after this period,
COMPANY shall comply with Section 12 hereof.
16.    TREES.
COMPANY shall preserve and protect all trees and shrubs located within the
public ways from damage by COMPANY and its agents and shall comply with all
local ordinances concerning tree preservation and protection. In the event that
the treatment, removal or replacement of such trees or shrubs is necessitated
by the actions of COMPANY or its agents, COMPANY shall pay to SOUTHPORT the
reasonable cost of treating, removing and replacing any trees or shrubs which
have been so damaged or destroyed. These costs and expenses shall be determined
in good faith by SOUTHPORT, and COMPANY shall reimburse SOUTHPORT within 30
days from demand for reimbursement.
17.    INDEMNIFICATION.
COMPANY shall at all times indemnify and save harmless SOUTHPORT, its officers,
employees and agents, for each and all such nuisances, damage, injury, loss,
cost or expense (including reasonable attorneys fees )caused, occasioned or
contributed to by any act or failure to act by the COMPANY, its officers,
agents and employees, in the construction, installation, repairing, maintaining
or operation of its mains, pipes or any of its facilities or equipment used for
the sale, transportation and distribution of gas hereunder, including making
cuts, disturbances and excavations in the public streets and public ways,
except for loss, cost or expense caused by the negligence of SOUTHPORT. COMPANY
shall file with SOUTHPORT certificates for liability insurance in the amount of
at least $1,000,000.00.
By acceptance of this franchise, COMPANY hereby holds SOUTHPORT, its officers,
agents and employees, free and harmless from all damages and claims for damage
and from all personal injuries and deaths, which may arise or in any manner
grow out of or result in any way from its installation, operation, maintenance
or repair of its mains, pipes, conduits or any of its facilities, except for
damages and claims for damage caused directly by the negligence of SOUTHPORT.
18.    ASSISTANCE IN LOCATING COMPANY FACILITIES.
In the event of an emergency situation in which SOUTHPORT requires information
or assistance in locating COMPANYS lines or other facilities, COMPANY agrees to
make its best effort to furnish a competent person at SOUTHPORTS designated
location to locate said lines or facilities within one hour of such request by
SOUTHPORT.
In the event of a non-emergency situation in which SOUTHPORT requires
information or assistance in locating COMPANYS lines or other facilities,
COMPANY agrees to furnish a competent person at SOUTHPORTS designated location
to locate said lines or facilities within 48 hours of such request by
SOUTHPORT.
19.    INTERRUPTION OF SERVICE.
In the event of an interruption of service to its customers or the failure to
supply gas for reasons beyond the control of COMPANY, COMPANY shall comply with
Sections 21 & 31 of COMPANYS North Carolina Service Regulations as approved by
the NCUC and any other applicable regulatory authority in restoring service and
notifying its customers.
20.   ACCESS TO BOOKS & RECORDS.
During the period of this franchise, SOUTHPORT shall have the right to review
at reasonable times the books and records of COMPANY relating to its property
and business transactions in the City of Southport for purposes of conducting
an excise tax audit. SOUTHPORT shall have the right and privilege, at its own
expense, to examine, audit and copy such books and records. COMPANY shall also
allow SOUTHPORT to review or inspect maps of its transmission and distribution
system within the city which shall be maintained up to date by COMPANY.
21.    RATE INCREASE.
If COMPANY files any notice, application, petition or request to increase its
rates or make any change which would have the effect of increasing its rates,
COMPANY shall comply with all rules, regulations and requirements of the NCUC
regarding the giving of proper notice to SOUTHPORT and its customers of said
request or filing. Upon request of SOUTHPORT, COMPANY agrees to provide a
representative to meet with the Board of Aldermen or designated staff member to
explain the reasons for the rate request.
22.    ASSIGNMENT OF FRANCHISE.
COMPANY shall not sell, transfer, assign or lease its system within the City of
Southport, or a substantial part thereof, or transfer any of its rights under
the franchise to another person or entity, without the prior written approval
of SOUTHPORT. Furthermore, no sale, transfer, assignment or lease shall be
effective until the purchaser, assignee or lessee has filed with the City Clerk
an agreement acceptable to the City reciting the terms of the transfer and
accepting and agreeing to be bound by all the terms and conditions of the
franchise. This provision does not apply to the creation of a security interest
in COMPANYs system for the purpose of securing financing nor to an assignment
or transfer to a surviving entity in a corporate reorganization.
23.    REVOCATION.
This franchise shall be effective from the date of final adoption by SOUTHPORT
and acceptance by COMPANY. It may not be revoked by SOUTHPORT unless COMPANY
violates any of the terms, covenants or conditions hereof or fails to comply
with the regulations of the NCUC and COMPANY fails to remedy such violation or
noncompliance within 30 days from notice by SOUTHPORT of such failure ,
violation or noncompliance.
24.    CHANGES OR AMENDMENTS.
No agreement, term or condition not set forth herein shall have any efficacy or
validity. No change or amendment hereto shall be effective until lawfully
adopted by CITY and agreed to by COMPANY.
25.    ACCEPTANCE BY FRANCHISEE. 
Unless this ordinance is executed and accepted by COMPANY within 30 days after
its final passage by SOUTHPORT, it shall not become effective and shall be null
and void anything herein to the contrary notwithstanding.
Finally adopted this 12 day of June, 2008.
