RESOLUTION REGARDING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT APPLICATION #08-0212-01
THAT WHEREAS, the requisite legal procedures required by state and local law
were not followed by the City in the hearing and consideration of Conditional
User Permit Application #08-0212-01 filed by Southport Marina, Inc. on or about
February 12, 2008; and
WHEREAS, as a result thereof, there has not been a legally valid decision
regarding said application; and
WHEREAS, the applicant is entitled to a valid hearing and decision on said
application pursuant to state and local law;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen as
follows:
1.   That the applicant is entitled for the above-referenced application to be
heard de novo by the City under the procedures of its Unified Development
Ordinance in effect at the time of said hearing.
2.   That the applicant is entitled for the substantive provisions of the UDO
in effect as of February 12, 2008, to be applied at said quasi-judicial hearing
including (1) building height limits allowing for consideration of a
conditional use permit application in order to exceed the forty foot height
requirement and (ii) the four criteria set forth as Section 12-17 (A)-(D).

e)   Resolution in support of Dialysis Center to be located in Southport
Alderman Fisher motioned to approve the resolution in support of a Dialysis
Center, seconded by Alderman Frink, vote carried.
Resolution
Whereas, 26 million Americans have Chronic Kidney Disease, and
Whereas, 20 million more people are at risk, and
Whereas, many millions of Americans suffer from diseases that contribute to
kidney failure, and
Whereas, we all have relatives or know of someone that is on dialysis, and
Whereas, citizens in Southport and surrounding communities have expressed an
interest in having a Dialysis Center located in Southport, and
Whereas, we realize that many people are traveling from Southport and
surrounding communities to take dialysis treatment in Wilmington, NC and other
areas, and
Whereas, we the Mayor and Southport Board of Aldermen ask Dosher Hospital staff
and the Hospital Board of Trustees to support and make every effort possible to
help establish a Dialysis Center in Southport,
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Southport Board of Aldermen will
support the Hospital Board of Trustees and staff to encourage the establishment
of this facility that will benefit many of our citizens.
ADOPTED, this the 12th day of June 2008.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer
Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, CMC
City Clerk

EXECUTIVE SESSION
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION MINUTES SOUTHPORT
June 12, 2008             BOARD OF ALDERMEN
 
The Board of Aldermen met in closed session to consult with and receive legal
advice from the City Attorney on legal issues related to annexation and the
Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District's contract.
Attorney Isenberg informed the Board regarding the legal issues facing the
Board in its attempt to annex property across the Progress Energy canal.
Isenberg told the Board about the various alternatives and options which the
Board should consider. He briefed the Board about discussions with the Progress
Energy Plant Manager and attorney related to these legal issues and how the
city might solve the problems. He reported that Progress Energy may be willing
to assist the city in crossing the canal by subdividing a parcel of property,
but that Progress asked for assurances that the City will not annex the Plant.
Isenberg reported that he would discuss an agreement concerning this with the
Progress Energy attorney. The Board reviewed the alternatives and expressed its
desire to proceed up 211 as far as possible.
Next, the Board discussed the Southeast Sanitary District situation with
Attorney Isenberg. He informed the Board that he had met with the districts
attorneys and it is the Sanitary District's contention that it will be entitled
to damages if Southport goes with the county due to rising construction costs
and increased engineering fees, which resulted from its reliance on Southport
partnering with it. After discussion with Isenberg regarding the districts
claims, the Board expressed its general desire for the city manager to still
talk to the county about the county alternatives.
No further discussion, motion by Alderman Boguskie, seconded by Alderman Adams
to re-enter regular session.

Wastewater Discussion
City Manager Thornton stated the purpose of the meeting is for the Board to
give staff directions with wastewater issues and to clarify to the public the
Board's intent regarding this issue.
Alderman Potter stated he believes the Southeast Brunswick Sanitary District
(SBSD) is vague in the direction they want to proceed. He explained during
meetings with SBSD, County and staff, it has been his contention that the city
should negotiate with the County because it is his belief that it is in the
City's best interest and he supports negotiating with Brunswick County to
provide sewer.
Alderman Boguskie stated a decision needs to be made because the city does not
have any sewer allocation, which is a pressing issue with some projects. The
city is under a moratorium and needs direction in order to give the Clean Water
Management Trust information in a timely manner. He supports negotiating with
the County.
Alderman Frink agreed since the City does not have any sewer allocation to
collaborate with the County.
Alderman Fisher stated it is time to move; the SBSD proposed to raise the rates
and their plan was rejected; and if it is Board consensus, he agrees to
negotiate with the County and requested the City Manager contact the County for
the best offer.
Alderman Adams stated the Sewer Committee worked hard and the Board should
accept their recommendation; he sees no other alternative but to pursue Option
1 with Brunswick County.
Alderman Brown stated if the City elects to collaborate with Brunswick County;
it should pursue the Eastern Plant near Sunny Point so the city can use its
spray fields. He believes this is an advantage in seeking the best price for
Southport.
Alderman Boguskie motioned, seconded by Alderman Potter, that the Board of
Aldermen authorize and direct the City Manager to enter into discussion and
negotiation with Brunswick County for the purpose of reaching an agreement with
the county to provide wastewater treatment services to the city in accordance
with the proposal by the county heretofore identified as Brunswick County
Option 1. The vote of approval was unanimous.

Chapter 3 Code of Ordinances
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that the
following sections in Chapter 3 of the Code of Ordinances are hereby amended or
enacted to read as follows:
Section 3-0. Owner .
For purposes of this chapter, an owner is hereby defined as any person, group
of persons, firm, partnership, corporation or other entity owning, keeping,
having charge of or taking care of an animal or allowing an animal to remain on
his premises or property for more than 72 hours.
Section 3-1. Vaccination of Dogs and Cats.    
The owner of every dog or cat shall have the animal vaccinated against rabies
between 12 and 26 weeks of age, again one year later and then every three (3)
years by a licensed veterinarian or by a certified rabies vaccinator with a
rabies vaccine approved by the United States Department of Agriculture and
approved by the North Carolina Commission for Health Services for use in this
State.
Section 3-2. Registration.
Every owner or keeper of a dog or cat over four (4) months of age shall
register the dog or cat at Southport City Hall on or before July 15 of each
year and shall pay the annual license tax as set by the Board of Aldermen for
the privilege of keeping said dog or cat within the city limits.
Section 3-3.Collars and Tags.
(A)   The owner of a dog or cat must be able to produce a current rabies
vaccination certificate issued by a licensed veterinarian or certified
vaccinator. Every owner or keeper of a dog or cat shall see that his dog or cat
is wearing a collar with a current vaccination tag and city license tag
attached thereto regardless of whether or not the animal is on or off the
owner’s property. Rabies tags cannot be transferred from animal to animal. If a
rabies tag is lost, destroyed or stolen, a duplicate tag must be promptly
obtained from the veterinarian and attached to the animal’s collar.
(B)   If a dog or cat is observed not wearing a valid rabies vaccination tag
and the owner is unknown and cannot be found after a reasonable effort to
discover and locate the owner, the animal control officer or his designee may
seize the animal. The animal shall be transported to the Brunswick County
Animal Shelter to be impounded and redeemed in accordance with the regulations
and ordinances of Brunswick County. If the owner is found before impoundment,
the owner shall pay the civil penalty for failure of his animal to wear a valid
rabies vaccination tag. The owner may also be subject to other appropriate
penalties described herein, plus a civil penalty if the animal is being at
large.
Section 3-4.1. Nuisance by Cats.
(A) The owner or keeper of a cat shall be responsible for any cat(s) owned or
kept which creates a nuisance. The commission on more than one occasion of any
of the following qualifying act(s) or conditions described in numbers 1 through
8 shall be deemed prima facie evidence of a cat creating a nuisance:
(1)   gets into or turns over garbage pails or cans; or
(2)   walks on and sleeps in or on automobiles of another; or
(3)   damages gardens or other foliage or other real or personal property; or
(4)   defecates off of the owner’s premises unless said defecation is
immediately cleaned up and removed by the owner or keeper; or
(5)   is maintained in an unsanitary condition or lack of cleanliness so as to
be offensive to sight or smell or a danger to the public health; or
(6)   in estrus is not confined to a building or secure enclosure; or
(7)   while unprovoked, chases or approaches a pedestrian, bicycle rider or
other vehicle in a menacing fashion;
(8)   habitually and repeatedly makes noises sufficient to interfere with
neighboring residents reasonable use of their property.
It shall be a violation of this Ordinance for an owner to allow his cat(s) to
engage in any of the acts listed above on more than one occasion.
(B )   Upon receiving a first complaint regarding a cat or cat owner, and after
finding probable cause to believe that the cat or cat owner has committed one
or more acts listed in Subsection (A) above, the animal control officer may
issue a written or verbal warning to the owner. If Animal Services receives a
second complaint about a cat and after investigating said complaint determines
there is probable cause to believe that the cat or the owner has again engaged
in one or more acts described in Subsection (A) above, the animal control
officer may issue a written Declaration of Nuisance to the owner. If, while
Animal Services is investigating the second complaint, the cat is physically
caught on the property of another, it may be returned to its owner, if known,
if the owner can be located. No civil penalty shall be issued for the cat or
the owner allowing the cat to be a nuisance at this time. The Declaration of
Nuisance shall inform the owner that a civil penalty will be issued if the cat
or any other cat owned by him is found to be in violation of this Section
again. If the owner is known but can not be located or if the owner is unknown,
the cat may be seized and transported to the Brunswick County Animal Shelter to
be impounded and redeemed in accordance with the regulations and ordinances of
Brunswick County.
Section 3-8. Dogs & Cats in Heat.
 It shall be unlawful for the owner or keeper of any dog or cat which is in
estrus (commonly referred to as “heat”) to permit such dog or cat to be off the
property of its owner or keeper unless it is within a vehicle being driven on
the street. While on the owner’s property such dog or cat must be kept in a
building or other secure enclosure.
Section 3-11.1. Unlawful to trap dogs and cats .
(A)   It shall be unlawful for any person, organization or agency to trap, by
cage or other device, a dog or cat without a permit issued by the animal
control officer.
(1)   The animal control officer shall have the sole authority and discretion
to issue a permit for this purpose which shall be valid for 10 days. Any dog or
cat trapped pursuant to a permit shall be treated humanely and promptly turned
over to the animal control officer.
(2)   It shall not be unlawful for a person to apprehend a dog or cat on his
property by hand, provided, however, the person must notify the animal control
officer within 24 hours of catching the animal. Any dog or cat trapped pursuant
to a permit shall be treated humanely and promptly turned over to the animal
control officer.
Section 3-12. Cleaning up after dogs and cats.
Any person owning, keeping or harboring any dog or cat shall promptly remove
and dispose of all feces left by the dog or cat on public property and on any
private property not owned or lawfully occupied by such person within the city.
Section 3-13.1. Strays.
(A)   A stray is defined as “An animal within the city wandering at large or
lost without evidence of the identification of an owner, or any animal within
the town wandering at large whose owner, if determinable, has failed to pay for
and procure a license or vaccination tag.
(B)   It shall be unlawful for any person to harbor, feed, keep in possession
by confinement or otherwise maintain any stray animal which does not belong to
him or her, unless he or she has, within seventy two (72) hours from the time
such animal came into his or her possession, notified the animal control
officer.
(C)   When the Animal Control Officer or an Animal Services Officer has
determined that a person has violated Subsection (B) above, he may issue a
written Notice of Violation and Civil Penalty to the person in violation. Any
stray animal may be seized and transported to the Brunswick County Animal
Shelter to be impounded and redeemed in accordance with the regulations and
ordinances of Brunswick County.
(D)   It shall be unlawful for any person to refuse to surrender a stray animal
to Animal Services upon demand.
Adopted by the Board of Aldermen on July 10, 2008, upon motion of Alderman Paul
Fisher, seconded by Alderman James Brown. The vote was unanimous. (6 ayes,
Aldermen Fisher, Brown, Adams, Potter, Boguskie and Frink.)

screened porch into a sunroom. The Building Inspector and the Zoning Board of
Adjustments did not approve the request because the porch encroaches on City
right of way. Mrs. Rogers stated the porch is an integral part of the house and
she has been paying taxes on the house including the porch. The house was built
in 1884 and closing in the porch would not result in appreciable change. She
believes by disallowing her to use her home to the full potential results in a
handicap for her. Attorney Isenberg told the Board legally that they cannot
permit someone to build on property they do not own, and the Board of Aldermen
cannot overrule the Board of Adjustments decision.
Mr. Strickland, Building Inspector explained that the Board of Adjustments
upheld his ruling. They told Ms. Rogers that the Board of Aldermen would have
to abandon that portion of right of way that her house sits on. He recommended
the Board not abandon right of way because of other similar situations in the
City, which could result in the City losing a lot of right of way. It was
explained that City Council elected years ago not to sue anyone encroaching on
the City's right of way, nor make anyone tear down their existing structure;
however, they would not permit any expansion or improvements to those non-
conforming uses. It was stated because City Council elected not to make
citizens tear down structures for encroaching on city right of way does not
mean that citizens own the property.
Mayor Spencer thanked Ms. Rogers empathizing with her dilemma, and reiterated
that the Board of Aldermen could not over rule the Board of Adjustments.

WHEREAS, the citizens of the City of Southport and all those who visit,
appreciate and enjoy the unique history, charm and appeal that the Southport
area offers; and
WHEREAS, the safe use of State roads and highways is of utmost importance to
not only the citizens of Southport, but also to our visitors from this great
State and other states and countries; and

dependent upon that of travel and tourism to generate significant tax revenues,
jobs and economic opportunity for residents of this area; and
WHEREAS, the condition of the State maintained roads within the City of
Southport and the greater Southport area are of significant concern;

respectfully request and call upon Governor Mike Easley, Secretary of
Transportation Lyndo Tippett, Division 3 Board of Transportation member Lanny

Law to take the action necessary to restore and maintain the condition and
integrity of Leonard Street (SR 1527), East Moore Street (NC 211) and

a)   N. C. DOT presentation on roundabout project at E. Moore Street and Ferry
Road
Anthony Law, District Engineer for New Hanover and Brunswick Counties,
explained that a public information meeting was held April 2008. DOT
representatives were asked to provide additional information related to the
function of a roundabout.
Other DOT staff members present were John Rhone, Assistant District Engineer,
Danny Cumbo, Division Traffic Engineer, and Ben Hughes, Assistant Division
Traffic Engineer. A power point presentation on locations with roundabouts was
shown. The United Stated began using roundabouts in the 1900's because they are
safer compared to regular intersections. Mr. Cumbo explained that roundabouts
have eight conflict points that causes reduction in fuel use and emissions.
There is not as much stop and go, better capacity for traffic flow, delay is
lower compared to other intersections with DOT designs accommodating truck
traffic, which has more flexibility. Other benefits include traffic calming and
speed reduction, pedestrian and bicycle, easy to determine gaps with vehicles
coming from one direction and fewer lanes to cross. Studies were conducted
which resulted in this data.

Attorney Isenberg presented the following resolution to call for Public Hearing
to consider closing a public alley. In his review of the sketch plan, he
believes the alley will need to be closed to meet setback requirements to

unanimous.

IX.
New Business
a)   Consideration of Resolution of Intent to Annex
Attorney Isenberg explained that this is the first step in the annexation
process. All parties have signed the Agreement and the plat has been recorded.
Mr. Holland prepared two options; 1A includes fewer lots than option 3, which
picks up 11 lots on Jabbertown Road. The purpose of the resolution of intent is
to inform the public that the City is considering annexing property.
Mr. Holland stated if the Board adopts the resolution, the annexation plan and
report must be approved thirty days before the public information meeting. The
plan must be delivered to the County thirty days prior to, which results in the
Board scheduling a special meeting on Friday, September 26 to approve the
annexation plan and report. The Plan and report will describe the basis of the
annexation, why the area qualifies and define the services to be provided, the
circumstances under which they will be provided and it will be a financial
statement as to the impact, revenues and expenses.
Discussion: Mr. Holland stated that Option 3 has stronger qualifications to
satisfy the statutory definition of an urban area and meets the subdivision
test. Alderman Adams stated it is unfair to annex a few property owners when
there is more lucrative property that can be annexed. He reiterated his support
for Option 1A.
Mr. Holland and Attorney Isenberg agreed that if less is taken in, the City
might not qualify for annexation. The City meets the minimum requirement for an
urban area but the subdivision test is very critical. The lots in area 1A are
at 61.03%, which has a small margin of error. They added 11 parcels as a minor
adjustment to strengthen the City's position on the subdivision test at 63.43%.
No further discussion, motion by Alderman Fisher to adopt the Resolution of
Intent approving Option 3 for annexation, and to schedule a Special Meeting
Friday, September 26, 9:00 a.m., motion seconded by Alderman Potter. The votes
were 5 ayes: Aldermen Fisher, Potter, Brown, Frink, and Boguskie. 1 no vote,
Alderman Adams. Motion passed.
RESOLUTION OF INTENT
A RESOLUTION STATING THE INTENT OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT TO CONSIDER ANNEXATION
OF THE AREA DESCRIBED HEREIN AND FIXING THE DATE OF A PUBLIC INFORMATIONAL
MEETING AND A PUBLIC HEARING ON THE QUESTION OF ANNEXATION
BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that:
Section 1. It is the intent of the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport
to consider annexation of the following described territory pursuant to Chapter
160A, Article 4A, Part 2 of the General Statutes of North Carolina:
(See Attachment A, property description).
Section 2. A public informational meeting on the question of annexing the
territory described in Attachment A and as shown on attached map (Attachment B)
will be held at Southport City Hall at 1:00 p.m., on October 29, 2008, at which
time plans for extending services to said territory will be explained and all
residents and property owners in said territory and the City of Southport will
be given an opportunity to ask questions and receive answers regarding the
proposed annexation.
Section 3. A public hearing on the question of annexing the above-described
territory will be held at Southport City Hall at 6:30 p.m., on November 20,
2008, at which time plans for extending services to said territory will be
explained and all residents and property owners in said territory and all
residents of the City of Southport will be given an opportunity to be heard.
Section 4. A report of plans for extending services to the above-described
territory shall be made available for public inspection at the office of the
City Clerk at least thirty (30) days prior to the date of the public
informational meeting. The statement of financial impact contained in the
report shall be delivered to the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners at
least thirty (30) days prior to the date of the public informational meeting.
Section 5. A legible map of the area to be annexed and a list of persons
holding freehold interests in property in the area to be annexed who have been
identified shall be posted in the office of the City Clerk at least thirty (30)
days prior to the date of the public informational meeting.
Section 6. The effective date of the annexation shall be not less than one year
following the date of adoption of the annexation ordinance.
Section 7. Notice of the public informational meeting and public hearing shall
be given by publication and by first class mail, as required by G.S. 160A-37.
Adopted this 11th day of September 2008.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer
Mayor

(g)   Paul Swenson
Mr. Swenson of 207 E. Brown Street told the Board that the Provision Company
has been in business for 15 years, and in the past two years, they have had
storm water runoff on two occasions in their business. It is his contention
that development activities on Bay Street (previously Charlie Perry's and Port
Charlie Restaurant) where fill was deposited raising the level of the road to
five inches is causing the water to run down Bay Street into their place of
business. Prior to this, the runoff ran into the river and marsh. He asked the
City to consider storm water issues before the property is fully developed and
compound problems.
Mr. Swenson stated when Cape Fear Development built the residential building
next to Provision, Yacht Basin Drive was raised. The Developer told him that
the elevation had not been raised. He explained that he owns the slip adjacent
to the property and hired a surveyor to shoot the elevation. It was raised
approximately 10 inches and they now have a drop off onto their property that
was level. He consulted with the Developer and was assured the situation would
be addressed. Since this time, he hired an Attorney who sent a letter to the
Developer, but to no avail. Mr. Swenson spoke with the City Building Inspector
and inquired whether he could hire a contractor to bring the level of the road
back to the original elevation. Mr. Strickland told him that he would have to
address this matter to City Council. Mr. Swenson asked the Board to consider
letting them bring Yacht Basin Drive back to its previous level at his expense.
Alderman Adams stated the Board did not authorize the Developer to perform work
on City right of way. Mr. Strickland stated the former Manager and Public
Services Director authorized the work.
Alderman Potter questioned if the Developer elevated the road that causes storm
water runoff onto private property, should they be held responsible. Attorney
Isenberg stated it depends on whether or not the portion raised is City right
of way, because City property does not run the entire length of the road. City
Attorney Isenberg stated if the City permitted, the Developer to do the work,
the City may be responsible for some of the work.
The Board agreed with recommendation of Alderman Potter to hire a surveyor to
determine where the City right of way begins and ends including the elevation
of the property. It was Board consensus to authorize the City Manager to hire a
surveyor.
h)   Proclamation proclaiming the week of September 17-23 as Constitution Week
Alderman Fisher motioned to approve the resolution seconded by Alderman Brown,
vote carried.
NORTH CAROLINA SOCIETY DAUGHTERS OF THE AMERICAN REVOLUTION
BRUNSWICK COUNTY
CHAPTER
Bonnie K. Beemer, Chair
DAR Constitution Week
PROCLAMATION
CONSTITUTION WEEK
September 17 – 23, 2008
WHEREAS, It is the privilege and duty of the American people to commemorate the
two hundred twenty first anniversary of the drafting of the Constitution of the
United States of America with appropriate ceremonies and activities; and
WHEREAS, Public Law 915 guarantees the issuing of a proclamation each year by
the President of the United States of America designating September 17-23 as
Constitution Week.
NOW, THEREFORE, I Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor of the City of Southport, North
Carolina do hereby proclaim the week of September 17-23, 2008 as
CONSTITUTION WEEK
And urge all citizens to study the Constitution, and reflect on the privilege
of being an American with all the rights and responsibilities which that
privilege involves.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand and cause the seal of the City
of Southport, North Carolina to be affixed this the 11th day of September of
the year of our Lord two thousand eight.
/s/ Sandra. P. Spencer, Mayor

Annexation Plan – Mr. Dale Holland, Consulting Planner
Mr. Holland presented the annexation report for Board approval. This would
authorize him to move forward with the next step in the process. He explained
that the purpose of the public informational meeting is to discuss the
financial implication of the annexation to the residents and the City.
Mayor Spencer stated the report included Stevens Park but those facilities no
longer exist. However, the City has acquired seven (7) acres that will include
public recreation amenities. It was also noted that no reference was made to
Fort Johnston and the Community Building. Mayor Spencer stated that the City
owns the building where the Art Gallery is housed, but do not own the artwork.
Mr. Holland explained that the references were placed in the report because
they were included in the City's Land Use Plan. Mayor Spencer also questioned
the calculations of water cost on page 10. Mr. Holland stated that he would
review the calculations and correct the figures, and the report would be
revised with changes.
Alderman Fisher questioned if there is a discrepancy in the right to service
sewer, water and electricity. Mr. Holland stated the services would remain the
same, and he perceives no discrepancy.
Mr. Holland stated after questions from Alderman Fisher, that the annexed area
did not go any farther down Jabbertown than what was required to satisfy the
definition of an urban area. Mayor asked about the Yaupon Drive area. Mr.
Holland stated the original charge by the Board was to look at the area along
North Howe, and explained that it would be difficult to connect these areas to
the current resolution of intent.
Alderman Fisher stated that this is the first involuntary annexation imposed by
the City. He questioned if residents are annexed, would they be required to
connect to City sewer. If not, he believes that it should be required through
assessment. Mr. Holland stated the Sewer Policy adopted in 1988 applies to
areas within the corporate limits, which is a policy decision by the Board.
Alderman Adams reiterated his objection to annexing the eleven parcels on
Jabbertown Road.

approve the annexation report with changes referenced by Mayor Spencer. The
vote of approval was 5 ayes, Alderman Brown, Potter, Frink, Boguskie and
Fisher. 1 no, Alderman Adams. (Report on file in the office of the City Clerk)
Public information meeting scheduled October 29, 2008 at 1:00pm, Aldermen
Chambers.
IV.
Comprehensive Plan and CAMA Core Land Use Plan
City Manager Thornton presented a recommendation from the Planning Board dated
January 17, 2008 concerning the Land Use and Comprehensive Plans. The
recommendation discussed the similarities between the Plans and recommended
that the CAMA Land Use Plan be used as the Comprehensive Plan. It was stated
that the Land Use Plan is more comprehensive, it contains guidelines charting
growth, and requires frequent updates by the State.
Mr. Holland concurred that the present Land Use Plan is more comprehensive. He
stated the City of Southport developed its own Land Use Plan instead of being
under Brunswick County. He explained that the City's current CAMA Land Use Plan
has been certified by the State of North Carolina, and submitted to the Federal
Government for certification.
Mr. Thornton explained having one Comprehensive Plan would simplify matters for
staff and developers.

Chief Cumbee gave historical data on the process that began in 2002, with a
recommendation from the State on the need to locate a fire station further
north. The current station was built in 1958-59 and does not have sufficient
space to accommodate the fire trucks, firefighters, or house equipment with
sufficient apparatus.
Mr. Howard reiterated that the present facility has outlived its functional
life. Handouts were presented showing two options with projected costs, i.e. a
potential capital funding plan by increasing tax rate by 3.8 or pay one-half
from general fund, borrow $1.3 million and the firefighters will raise one
million dollars from the community. (Information on file in the Office of the
City Clerk)
Mr. Scott Garner, Project Architect, stated the new building is energy
efficient and designed for future needs. It is their belief that eventually the
volunteer department will transition to full time paid firefighters and this
station will be equipped to accommodate the growth. An emergency operations
center is included in the plans.
Alderman Potter thanked the firefighters for their work and willingness to
raise monies to help fund the new station. He also noted that the Southport
Fire Department currently holds an ISO rating of four (4) which can be a factor
in homeowners' insurance premiums. He stated if the department was to lose this
rating, the cost of insurance could possibly exceed the difference in tax
dollars to the City.

Resolution
Adopting a Comprehensive Transportation Plan For Brunswick County, North
Carolina
WHEREAS,  Brunswick County, the Municipalities of Brunswick County, and the
Transportation Planning Branch, North Carolina Department of Transportation
actively worked to develop a comprehensive transportation plan for Brunswick
County; and
WHEREAS, the County, the Municipalities and the Department of Transportation
are directed by North Carolina General Statutes 136-66.2 to reach agreement for
a transportation system that will serve present and anticipated volumes of
traffic in and around the County; and
WHEREAS, it is recognized that the proper movement of traffic within and
through Brunswick County is a highly desirable element of the comprehensive
plan for the orderly growth and development of the County; and
WHEREAS, after full study of the Plan, and following a Public Hearing on
October 9, 2008, the Southport Board of Aldermen believes it to be in its best
interest to adopt a plan pursuant to General Statutes 136-66.2;
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Brunswick County Comprehensive
Transportation Plan, as shown on a map dated November 5, 2007, be approved and
adopted as a guide in the development of the transportation system in Brunswick
County and the same is hereby recommended to the North Carolina Department of
Transportation for its subsequent adoption by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
ADOPTED, this the 9th day of October 2008.

STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA
ORDER
BRUNSWICK COUNTY
THAT WHEREAS, G. S. 160A-299 requires that when a city proposes to permanently
close any street or public alley that the Board of Aldermen first adopt a
resolution declaring its intent to close said street or alley and calling for a
public hearing on the question; and
WHEREAS, G. S. 160A-299 further requires that the resolution to close the
street or alley be published once a week for four successive weeks prior to the
date of said hearing, that a copy thereof be sent by registered or certified
mail to all owners of property adjoining the portion of the street or alley to
be closed as shown on the county tax records, and that notice of the closing
and public hearing be prominently posted in at least two places along the
street or alley to be closed; and
WHEREAS, on September 11, 2008, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport
passed a resolution proposing to close the following described public alley,
and also calling for a public hearing on said question:
Being that certain public alley which runs from the northern line of 10th
Street in a northerly direction to its terminus in Block 7A of the Smith &
Weeks Addition to the City of Southport as shown on a map recorded in the Book
of Division of
Lands and Dowers at Page 10 of the Brunswick County Registry, said alley
running parallel with Howe Street and Lord Street and between the two streets;
and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has complied with all requirements of G. S.
160A-299, including the holding of the public hearing and the giving of all
required notice; and
WHEREAS, no portion of the street or alley to be closed is under the authority
or control of the Board of Transportation; and
WHEREAS, adjoining property owners and other persons were heard on the question
of whether or not the closing would be detrimental to the public interest or
the property rights of any individual; and
WHEREAS, it appears to the satisfaction of the Board of Aldermen after the
hearing that the closing of this public alley is not contrary to the public
interest and that no individual owning property in the vicinity of the alley or
in the subdivision in which it is located would be deprived of reasonable means
of ingress and egress to their property and that said alley described above
should be closed;
NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED pursuant to G. S. 160A-299 as follows:
1.   That the following described public alley in the City of Southport is
hereby closed:
Being that certain public alley which runs from the northern line of 10th
Street in a northerly direction to its terminus in Block 7A of the Smith &
Weeks Addition to the City of Southport as shown on a map recorded in the Book
of Division of Lands and Dowers at Page 10 of the Brunswick County Registry,
said alley running parallel with Howe Street and Lord Street and between the
two streets.
2.   That the City of Southport hereby reserves and retains all right, title
and interest in the utility improvements and easements, if any, located within
said alley as described above.

[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/

CITY OF SOUTHPORT
IDENTITY THEFT PREVENTION POLICY
Subject:   New Identity Theft Prevention Program for the City of Southport
Purpose:    The creation and implementation of an Identity Theft Prevention
Program at the City of Southport that will identify, detect, mitigate, and
update Red Flags that signal the possibility of identity theft in connection
with the opening of a covered account or any existing covered account.
Effective Date: October 9, 2008
TABLE OF CONTENTS
PART 1    DEFINITIONS   8
PART 2   IDENTIFICATION OF RELEVANT RED FLAGS   8
PART 3   DETECTION, PREVENTION AND MITIGATION   10
PART 4   PROGRAM UPDATES   11
PART 5    ADDITIONAL LEGAL REQUIREMENTS (IF NECESSARY)   11
PART 6    ADMINISTRATION   12
PART 7    POLICY APPROVAL   13
PART 1
DEFINITIONS
1.   For purposes of this Policy, the term "Covered Account" means an account
that the City of Southport offers or maintains, primarily for personal, family
or household purposes, that involves or is designed to permit multiple payments
or transactions and any other account that the City of Southport offers or
maintains for which there is a reasonably foreseeable risk to customers or the
safety and soundness of the City of Southport from identity theft, including
financial, operational, compliance, reputation, or litigation risks.
2.   For purposes of this Policy, the term "Identity Theft" means a fraud
committed or attempted using the identifying information of another person
without authority.
3.   For purposes of this Policy, the term "Red Flag" means a pattern,
practice, or specific activity that indicates the possible existence of
identity theft. Part 2 provides a specific description of which Red Flags are
applicable to this policy.
PART 2
IDENTIFICATION OF RELEVANT RED FLAGS
After careful examination of our accounts, including the methods by which we
open access and past experience with identity theft, the following events/
occurrences reasonably indicate the potential for identity theft and should be
considered "Red Flags" for purposes of this policy:
A.   Alerts, notifications, or other warnings received from consumer reporting
agencies or service providers, such as fraud detections services. For the
purposes of this policy the City of Southport will be utilizing the ONLINE
Utility Exchange as their service provider to identify the “Red Flags” listed
below:
1.   A fraud or active duty alert is included with a consumer report.
2.   A consumer-reporting agency provides a notice of credit freeze in response
to a request for a consumer report.
3.   A consumer-reporting agency provides a notice of address discrepancy (See
Part 5).
4.   A consumer report indicates a pattern of activity that is inconsistent
with the history and usual pattern of activity of an applicant or customer,
such as:
a.   A recent and significant increase in the volume of inquiries;
b.   An unusual number of recently established credit relationships;
c.   A material change in the use of credit, especially with respect to
recently established credit relationships; or
d.   An account that was closed for cause or identified for abuse of account
privileges by a financial institution or creditor.
B.   The presentation of suspicious documents, such as:
5.   Documents provided for identification appear to have been altered or
forged.
6.   The photograph or physical description on the identification is not
consistent with the appearance of the applicant or customer presenting the
identification.
7.   Other information on the identification is not consistent with information
provided by the person opening a new covered account or customer presenting the
identification.
8.   Other information on the identification is not consistent with readily
accessible information that is on file with the financial institution or
creditor, such as a signature card or a recent check.
9.   An application appears to have been altered or forged, or gives the
appearance of having been destroyed and reassembled.
C.   The presentation of suspicious personal identifying information, such as a
suspicious address changes:
10.   Personal identifying information provided is inconsistent when compared
against external information sources used by the City of Southport. For
example: a. The address does not match any address in the consumer report; or
b. The Social Security Number (SSN) has not been issued, or is listed on the
Social Security Administration's Death Master File.
11.   Personal identifying information provided by the customer is not
consistent with other personal identifying information provided by the
customer. For example, there is a lack of correlation between the SSN range and
date of birth.
12.   Personal identifying information provided is associated with known
fraudulent activity as indicated by internal or third party sources used by the
City of Southport. For example:
a.   The address on an application is the same as the address provided on a
fraudulent application; or
b.   The phone number on an application is the same as the number provided on a
fraudulent application.
13.   Personal identifying information provided is of a type commonly
associated with fraudulent activity as indicated by internal or third party
sources used by the financial institution or creditor. For example:
a.   The address on an application is fictitious, a mail drop, or a prison; or
b.   The phone number is invalid, or is associated with a pager or answering
service.
14.   The SSN provided is the same as that submitted by other persons opening
an account or other customers.
15.   The address or telephone number provided is the same as or similar to the
account number or telephone number submitted by an unusually large number of
other persons opening accounts or other customers.
16.   The person opening the covered account or the customer fails to provide
all required personal identifying information on an application or in response
to notification that the application is incomplete.
17.   Personal identifying information provided is not consistent with personal
identifying information that is on file with the City of Southport.
18.   If the City of Southport uses challenge questions, the person opening the
covered account or the customer cannot provide authenticating information
beyond that which generally would be available from a wallet or consumer
report.
D.   The unusual use of, or other suspicious activity related to, a covered
account:
19.   Shortly following the notice of a change of address for a covered
account, the City of Southport receives a request for a new, additional, or
replacement card or a cell phone, or for the addition of authorized users on
the account.
20.   A new revolving credit account is used in a manner commonly associated
with known patterns of fraud patterns. For example:
a.   The majority of available credit is used for cash advances or merchandise
that is easily convertible to cash (e.g., electronics equipment or jewelry); or
b.   The customer fails to make the first payment or makes an initial payment
but no subsequent payments.
21.   A covered account is used in a manner that is not consistent with
established patterns of activity on the account. There is, for example:
a.   Nonpayment when there is no history of late or missed payments;
b.   A material increase in the use of available credit;
c.   A material change in purchasing or spending patterns;
d.   A material change in electronic fund transfer patterns in connection with
a deposit account; or
e.   A material change in telephone call patterns in connection with a cellular
phone account.
22.   A covered account that has been inactive for a reasonably lengthy period
of time is used (taking into consideration the type of account, the expected
pattern of usage and other relevant factors).
23.   Mail sent to the customer is returned repeatedly as undeliverable
although transactions continue to be conducted in connection with the
customer's covered account.
24.   The City of Southport is notified that the customer is not receiving
paper account statements.
25.   The City of Southport is notified of unauthorized charges or transactions
in connection with a customer's covered account.
E.   Notice from customers, victims of identity theft, law enforcement
authorities, or other persons regarding possible identity theft in connection
with covered accounts held by the City of Southport:
26.   The City of Southport is notified by a customer, a victim of identity
theft, a law enforcement authority, or any other person that it has opened a
fraudulent account for a person engaged in identity theft.
PART 3
DETECTION, PREVENTION AND MITIGATION
A.   Detection
In an effort to ensure proper detection of any Red Flags, all customers
(consumers) must provide at least the following information/documentation
before any new covered account will be opened:
1.   Full Name;
2.   Date of birth (individual);
3.   Address, (a residential or business street address for an individual; for
an individual who does not have a residential or business street address, an
Army Post Office (APO) or Fleet Post Office (FPO) box number, or the
residential or business street address of next of kin or of another contact
individual; or for a person other than an individual (such as a corporation,
partnership, or trust), a principal place of business, local office, or other
physical location; and;
4.   Identification number, which shall be: (i) For a U.S. person, a taxpayer
identification number; or (ii) For a non-U.S. person, one or more of the
following: a taxpayer identification number; passport number and country of
issuance; alien identification card number; or number and country of issuance
of any other government-issued document evidencing nationality or residence and
bearing a photograph or similar safeguard.
For any account holder of a covered account for which the above information is
not already on file at the City of Southport, the customer will be contacted
within a reasonable period of time after discovering the missing information to
obtain the necessary information.
To assist with detection of Red Flags, the City of Southport will implement the
appropriate computer programs tailored to the City of Southport business needs
to help authenticate customers, monitor transactions, and change of address
requests. The following programs are being used and the City of Southport
continued use thereof is incorporated and made part of this policy:
1.   Logics Utility Software
1001 Navaho Drive, Suite 204
Raleigh NC 27609
B.   Preventing and Mitigating Identity Theft
In the event a Red Flag is detected, the City of Southport is committed to
preventing the occurrence of identity theft and taking the appropriate steps to
mitigate any harm caused thereby. In order to respond appropriately to the
detection of a Red Flag, the City of Southport shall consider any aggravating
circumstance(s) that may heighten the risk of identity theft. After assessing
the degree of risk posed, the City of Southport will respond to the Red Flag in
an appropriate manner, which may include:
1.   Monitoring a covered account for evidence of identity theft;
2.   Contacting the customer;
3.   Changing any passwords, security codes, or other security devices that
permit access to a covered account;
4.   Reopening a covered account with a new account number;
5.   Not opening a new covered account;
6.   Closing an existing covered account;
7.   Not attempting to collect on a covered account or not selling a covered
account to a debt collector;
8.   Notifying law enforcement; or
9.   Determining that no response is warranted under the particular
circumstances.
In an effort to mitigate the damage caused by identity theft, the following
programs/software are being used, and the City of Southport’s continued use
thereof is incorporated and made part of this policy: Logics Utility Software
For the protection of our customers, all service providers hired by the City of
Southport to perform any activity in connection with any covered account must
also take appropriate steps to prevent identity theft. To this end, the City of
Southport will only contract with service providers that have implemented and
follow a similar identity theft prevention policy.
PART 4
PROGRAM UPDATES
The City of Southport is committed to maintaining an Identity Theft Prevention
Policy that is current with the ever-changing crime of identity theft. To that
end, the City of Southport will reassess this policy on a periodic (annual)
basis. In reassessing this policy, the City of Southport will add/delete Red
Flags in Part 2, as necessary, to reflect changes in risks to customers or to
the safety and soundness of the City of Southport from identity theft. The
determination to make changes to this policy will be within the discretion of
the responsible parties, identified in Part 6 of this policy, but after careful
consideration of the following:
1.   The City of Southport's past experience(s) with identity theft;
2.   Changes in methods of identity theft;
3.   Changes in methods to detect, prevent, and mitigate identity theft;
4.   Changes in the types of accounts that the City of Southport offers or
maintains; and
5.   Changes in the business arrangements of the City of Southport, including
mergers, acquisitions, alliances, joint ventures, and service provider
arrangements.
PART 5
ADDITIONAL LEGAL REQUIREMENTS (IF NECESSARY)
A.   Consumer Addresses
1.   Address Confirmation
The City of Southport shall furnish the consumer's address that the City has
reasonably confirmed is accurate to consumer reporting agencies as part of the
information that the City of Southport regularly furnishes for the reporting
period in which the City of Southport establishes a relationship with the
consumer. In an effort to ensure that the City of Southport maintains accurate
address information for its consumers and to ensure the City of Southport
provides accurate address information of our consumers to reporting agencies,
at least one of the following steps must be taken prior to providing the
consumer's address to the consumer reporting agency:
a)   Verify the address on file with the consumer;
b)   Confirm the address being sent to the consumer reporting agency matches
the address the City of Southport has on file for that particular consumer;
c)   Compare the address with information received from any third-party source;
or
d)   Verify by other means that are reasonably available at the time.
2.   Address Discrepancies
Because the City of Southport is a user of consumer reports, at least one of
the following steps must be taken when the City of Southport receives notice
from any consumer reporting agency that a substantial difference exists between
the address for the consumer that the City of Southport provided and the
address (es) in the consumer reporting agency's file for that particular
consumer:
a)   Compare the differing address with the City of Southport 's file, by
either (1) confirming that the address information provided by the City of
Southport to the consumer reporting agency is the same information the City
obtains and uses to verify the consumer's identity in accordance with the
requirements of the Customer Information Program (CIP) rules (31 USC 5318(1)
(31 CPR 103.121»; or (2) comparing the differing addresses with the City of
Southport’s records and files, including applications, change of address
notifications, other customer account records, or retained CIP documentation;
or (3) comparing the differing addresses with information the City may have
received from a third-party source; or
b)   Verify the information in the consumer report provided by the consumer-
reporting agency with the consumer.
B.   Other requirements should be addressed below based on entity type
Examples:
(a)   For financial institutions and creditors that are subject to 31 U.S.C.
5318(g), filing a Suspicious Activity Report in accordance with applicable law
and regulation;
(b)   Implementing any requirements under 15 U.S.C. 1681c-l(h)regarding the
circumstances under which credit may be extended when the financial institution
or creditor detects a fraud or active duty alert;
(c)   Implementing any requirements for furnishers of information to consumer
reporting agencies under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, for example, to correct or update
inaccurate or incomplete information, and to not report information that the
furnisher has reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate; and
(d)   Complying with the prohibitions in 15 U.S.C. l681m on the sale, transfer,
and placement for collection of certain debts resulting from identity theft.
DISCLAIMER: There may be additional requirements, such as the examples provided
above.
However, the above examples are not intended to be an exhaustive list.
PART 6
ADMINISTRATION
By signing below, (I/this) individual(s)/committee/board1 of the City of
Southport acknowledge(s) that (I/we) will be responsible for overseeing the
implementation, management, and updating of this new policy and shall have the
following responsibilities:
1.   Assign specific responsibility for the Program's implementation, including
appropriate training for staff;
•   At least annually, the assigned person/staff must report to the individual
(s)/committee/board and provide an update on the policy's effectiveness, any
service provider arrangements, significant incidents involving identity theft
and the City of Southport’s response, and recommendations for ways to improve
the program.
2.   Review reports prepared by staff to ensure that the City of Southport
remains compliant with its legal responsibility to maintain an Identity Theft
Prevention Program; and
3.   Approve material changes to this program as necessary to address changing
identity theft risks.
1 Rules require oversight by the board of aldermen, an appropriate committee of
the board, or a designated employee of management.
PART 7
POLICY APPROVAL
This Identity Theft Prevention Program is hereby made a Policy of the City of
Southport effective October 9, 2008, as authorized by the Board of Aldermen.

J.    Tax Resolution
Alderman Fisher motioned to adopt the tax resolution and to request the County
Commissioners appoint a Task Force with municipal representatives to study the
County Tax System, and make recommendations to the General Assembly in order to
correct the inadequacies in the state tax system. He asked that copies of the
Resolution be forwarded to municipalities in Brunswick County, i.e. Senator
Soles, Representatives Stiller and Hill. Alderman Brown seconded the motion.
Vote unanimous.
Resolution Concerning Brunswick County Property Tax
WHEREAS, a series of unprecedented events in the national and international
financial markets has impacted individual property owners; and
WHEREAS, all levels of government have concerns for an individual's ability to
pay bills and taxes; and
WHEREAS, the property tax burden has shifted to single family homeowners; and
WHEREAS, the North Carolina tax system is antiquated and needs updating.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
request that the Brunswick County Commissioners form a Tax Task Force
consisting of county and municipal representatives to study the property tax
system and make recommendations to the County Commissioners for implementation.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the recommendation not within the authority for
implementation by the County Commissioners be forwarded to the local
representatives in the N. C. General Assembly for appropriate action.
DULY RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen this 13th day of
November 2008.

CELL PHONE POLICY AND PROCEDURE
M. Alan Thornton
City Manager
Adopted December 11, 2008
Introduction
This policy is being initiated in order for the City to comply with Internal
Revenue Service (IRS) rules regarding the taxability of employee cell phones
and devices.
Under IRS Code Section 274 (d), the IRS considers cell phones to be “listed
property” and as such requires detailed record keeping including (a) the amount
of the expense; (b) the time and place of each call and to whom it was made.
The IRS can declare that all undocumented use is personal and should be taxed
as wages, even if the cell phone or device were mostly used for business
purposes.
Purpose
To establish guidelines for the issuance and usage of City owned cellular
telephones as well as procedures for monitoring and controlling costs related
to cellular telephone use in conjunction with City Business. This policy
outlines the cellular phone option supported by the City, guidelines for
appropriate use and other administrative issues related to cellular phone
acquisition and reimbursement. This policy was created in order to enhance
employee safety, limit City liability, help manage telecommunications costs and
comply with IRS Code Section 274 (d).
Definitions
Cellular equipment – City provided cellular telephones, wireless telephones
that transmit communication via tower antennas, cellular data transmission/
receipt equipment, and radio-cellular telephones.
Business related calls – Calls necessary to conduct City Business.
Landline phone – Any communication device that initiates and completes phone
connections via the regular telephone system.
Acceptable Personal Calls – From time to time staff may need to use the City
owned cellular phone to notify family of change in work plans. Staff is
encouraged to use landline phones as much as possible, and use the City owned
cell phones as a last resort. Emergency calls will be considered acceptable
personal calls if a landline phone is not available at the time.
Policy
City cell phones are provided to improve customer service and to enhance
business efficiency. Cell phones are not a personal benefit and should not be
used as a primary mode of personal communication.
Using a cell phone while operating a motorized vehicle is strongly discouraged.
Employees should plan to allow placement of calls prior to driving or while on
rest breaks. When an employee must use their cell phone while driving, they
should keep conversations brief, avoid unnecessary calls, and no calls should
be made if driving is hazardous. If it is necessary for the employee to read or
write while taking the call, the employee should pull off the road.
All employees should take time to become familiar with the various cell phone
functions. The cell phone should be placed where it is easy to see and reach.
Employees should bear in mind that cell phone calls can be intercepted and
should take proper precautions when discussing confidential information.
Procedures
Each Department Director must determine which positions require a cell phone or
other device by identifying those employees who have demonstrated a business
need. Other communication means such as land-line phones, network access,
email, etc. should be used instead of cellular equipment whenever possible.
The City Manager will evaluate the Department Director’s recommendation for
number of cellular telephones requested; number of minutes needed and required
service area in determining the service plan for the City of Southport.
Whenever possible, one plan will be used for all departments.
City Issued Cell Phones:
Employees are provided a City issued cell phone or device. Employees are
responsible for the care and maintenance of the device. The device must be
secured at all times. Employees are required to immediately report the loss or
theft of the City-owned device to their supervisor. City-owned cellular
services are not for personal use for calls made or received except in an
emergency. According to the Internal Revenue Code, any personal use of a City
issued cell phone or device may be considered taxable income and subject to
withholding taxes or the employee may reimburse the City for personal phone
calls.
The employees must review their cell phone monthly invoice and identify
personal calls. All personal calls are to be highlighted and the City is to be
reimbursed by the employee on a monthly basis by completing the reimbursement
form attached. In the event the employee fails to reimburse the City, the
Finance Department will deduct the amount of personal cell phone usage from the
employee's wages.
The following is an example of the calculation of personal usage that is
reimbursable to the City:
Total Monthly Phone Fee               $ 20.15
Pooled Minutes Fees                  $170.49
Total Fee and Pooled Minutes Fee (20.15 + 170.49)      $190.64
Total Department Pooled Minutes            3,000
Per Minute Charge ($190.64 / 3,000)            .063547 cents/minute
Personal Minutes Highlighted On Bill           17
Monthly Phone Fee Due
County for Personal Use (.063547 X 17)          $1.08
Personal Cell Phone – Reimbursement for Business Use
Employees conducting business on personal cell phones are entitled to
reimbursement. If reimbursements are requested, the cell phone number will be
considered public information. The amount of reimbursement will be determined
by the City Manager.
Penalties
Violation of this policy shall result in disciplinary action and may be a cause
for termination.
Department Directors are responsible for reviewing cell phone bills for their
staff for reimbursement of personal calls and the Finance Department will rely
upon the Department Director’s authorization for accuracy of personal vs. work-
related calls.

Executive Session
 
Executive Session Minutes December 11, 2008
 
The Board discussed securing property from the Blake Family to construct a
sewer pumping station off highway 211. City Manager Thornton advised the Board
that staff has been working to acquire an easement and property for the new
pump station. Staff met several times with Blake family representatives and
they agreed not to charge the City for the land and easement contingent upon
the City providing sewer allocation of 75,000 gallons per day for the next ten
(10) years.
Upon discussion, the Board believed this to be a workable solution, which would
result in a savings to the City and agreed to provide sewer capacity per
staff's discussion with the Blake Family.
Personnel: City Manager Thornton stated that Ralph Cardwell has been serving as
Interim Director of Public Services. He offered the permanent position to Mr.
Cardwell and he agreed to accept the position for an annual salary of $60,000.
He explained that he could not approve the requested salary without Board
authorization. He and Mr. Cardwell also discussed hiring someone to fill the
position of Load Management Coordinator. Board consensus was that Mr. Cardwell
had done a good job and stated their support of the recommended salary.
No further discussion, motion made to re-enter regular session by Alderman
Potter, seconded by Alderman Fisher, vote carried.

RESOLUTION HONORING DR. MARTIN LUTHER KING JR. CELEBRATION
WHEREAS, the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Committee was formed and
entrusted with the responsibility to plan a community wide celebration to
appropriately honor this great leader; and
WHEREAS, Dr. Martin Luther King Celebration Committee has selected the dates of
Friday, January 16, Sunday, January 18 and Monday, January 19, 2009 to hold
this celebration with events scheduled to include youth programs, march and
roundtable breakfast, and
WHEREAS,  the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Celebration has established a mission
statement in which its most important goal is to bring people of the community
together for the purpose of promoting good will and harmony for the betterment
of the entire community; and
WHEREAS, it is extremely important that the great works and deeds of Dr. Martin
Luther King, Jr. be duly remembered, honored and recognized in this most
fitting and proper way.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Mayor and Board of Aldermen of
Southport recognizes January 16,18,19 2009 as the official dates of celebration
by the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Committee for the purpose of
honoring this great man and encourage all citizens to participate in the
activities scheduled.
Adopted the 8th day of January 2009.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor      Attest: /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
Committees: Mayor Spencer stated that several people have requested to be
appointed to Committees; however, she would like to discuss the City's
Committee structure during the Board's Retreat before making the appointments.

Adjournment – 8:12 pm

seconded by Alderman Frink, vote carried.

Finance Department – Patty Miller
Taxes
The Finance Director asked the Board to determine if they wished the County to
collect the City's ad valorem taxes or continue to bill in-house. She explained
if the City elects not to join the county; the City needs to upgrade its
software to accommodate the change in the new tax law circuit breaker and
provide training for staff. The new tax law circuit breaker is a tax relief for
the permanently disabled, individuals 65 years of age or older and based on
income limit of $37,500. The County will qualify individuals as well as the
calculations to insure compliance with the law. Ms. Miller stated the City
would still have a designated tax collector. The cost of the county
implementing the circuit breaker is 0.75%.
The Board asked Ms. Miller to provide a cost analysis comparing the County
collecting taxes to the City, including cost of operation to the City, effect
on the finance department, level of responsibility with the new tax law and the
impact on the City's levy.
Cash Investment Policy
The Board discussed investments, return on the dollar and where monies are
invested. Ms. Miller stated she would present a formal cash investment policy
to the Board.
She requested that Integrated Credit Card software with utilities be placed
back in the budget, which will allow the City to post recurring credit card
payments and online payments, once the website is updated.
Ms. Miller and City Manager Thornton discussed the provision in the ABC law,
which provides 30% of its gross receipts to the schools, and 5% to Dosher
Hospital as shown in the Audit report. Staff is looking into this provision
because some municipalities had this local provision changed. City Manager
Thornton stated that he would research this further and look at the possibility
of the distribution formula being revised, which would net additional revenues
for the City.

JANUARY 22, 2009
PUBLIC HEARING (ANNEXATION)
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN PUBLIC HEARING (ANNEXATION)
JANUARY 22, 2009  ALDERMEN CHAMBERS
6:30 P.M.         SOUTHPORT, NC
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Paul Fisher, Nelson Adams and Richard "Ed" Boguskie
ABSENT:         Aldermen Jim Brown, Jwantana Frink and Donnie Potter
STAFF PRESENT:       Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, Clerk
            Dale Holland, Holland Consulting Planner
OTHERS PRESENT:    Earl Clewis, Linda Pasulka, Hal Bolin, Rod Hatcher,
            Lois St.George, Tom Griffin, Louise Mead, David McVeigh
I.
Call to Order – Mayor Spencer
Pursuant to notice duly advertised and posted, Mayor Spencer called the Special
Meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.
II.
Invocation
Alderman Adams pronounced the invocation.
III.
Public Hearing – 6:34 p.m.
Mayor Spencer stated that the purpose of the meeting is to receive public
comments on the proposed annexation for the North Howe Street corridor.
Alderman Boguskie motioned to enter Public Hearing, seconded by Alderman Adams,
the vote carried.
Mr. Dale Holland of Holland Consulting Planners explained that Southport under
North Carolina General Statute 160A-34 proposes to annex 174 acres along North
Howe Street. The Board adopted a Resolution of Intent November 13, 2008, which
notified residents of the City's intent. The resolution included the date of
the public information meeting and Public Hearing. Mr. Holland stated the City
has up to 90 days to adopt the ordinance, and upon adoption; one year to
implement the annexation.
Mr. Joe Pasulka of 1014 Captain Adkins Drive (Smithville Woods) told the Board
that he owns eight acres of undeveloped land behind the former Wilson's Roses
Shopping Plaza. He stated that a potential developer made an offer to purchase
the land contingent upon rezoning by the City to construct affordable housing.
The Planning Board denied the rezoning twice. He stated the City is proposing
to annex undeveloped land increasing his property taxes, but he is not allowed
to rezone and develop his property. He asked the City to work with him to
resolve this issue.
Mrs. Barbara Clewis of 1648 Howe Street, owner of a mobile home and RV Park
explained that her park houses some permanent residents. In a prepared
statement, she explained that being a small business; they cannot afford sewer
impact fees estimated at $180,000 and the required sewer connection that would
be imposed by annexation. She stated that they would be forced to close and
dislocate her residents. She asked the Board to be sensitive to the economic
impact that annexation will impose on citizens.
Verbatim Statement
Hi, I am Barbara Clewis of 1648 Howe St… Earl and I own and operate the
Woodside Trailer park. It is a small family oriented park.
We’re extremely worried because of the likelihood that we may be forced to
close our park if you enforce the current policy of the impact fees and
mandatory sewer hook up, which we’ve been led to believe that the fees would be
$180,000.00. In addition to that expense, we’d be faced with hiring an engineer
to develop a plan to run sewer lines to every lot and then have a contractor
install them. When annexation was considered in the late 80’s, we had an
estimate to have that done and it was approximately $300,000. I’m sure it would
be much more today. In addition to that, expense, we’d be required to have
every septic tank pumped out, broken up and filled with sand.
Waste Industries currently charges $250 to pump a tank. I don’t know what it
would cost to have the tanks filled with sand. Another major consideration is
our abundance of trees.
We didn’t cut down trees to make lots; we situated the lots between the trees.
Thus, some lots are bigger than others, but almost all of them have several
very old trees.
The majority of the root systems of these trees stand a chance of being damaged
and we’d possibly lose a lot of these trees. Our roads would also be damaged.
Repairing them would be another expense. We will be faced with about a half
million dollars expense.
I’ve heard some say that maybe the city could finance their fees. Financing
wouldn’t really be helpful, because it’d only make the actual cost higher.
Financing the city fees and the cost to install the sewer would actually double
or triple the original costs depending on the finance rate and the length of
the financing. This is a small park; we don’t have income like Walmart. We
wouldn’t have enough profit in our lifetime to pay this expense. It would not
be a wise financial move on our part to go forward with the park under these
circumstances. However, if we’re forced to shut the park down, we’d lose our
income. This is something we’ve worked with for 40 years. We built our home
there in 1967 and began the park shortly after that. The income from the park
was to be our retirement income.
I would respectfully ask each of you to ask yourselves if someone told you that
you would have to pay one half million dollars just to keep what you already
have, what would you do? How would you feel?
Or even place yourself in the predicament of the single-family homeowners in
the proposed area. They are going to be severely affected by this action, too,
especially the ones living on fixed incomes. In addition to the sewer impact
fee of over $8.000, they’ll have the cost of pumping and dismantling their
septic tanks and the cost of having the sewer lines run to their homes. So they
are probably facing close to $10,000 in costs just to remain living in their
home in addition to having to pay annual city taxes.
I’d just like to ask that you consider each parcel as being owned by people and
not just as a cardboard puzzle piece. I truly don’t believe that any of you
want to devastate anyone.
I understand that you are currently looking at your policies and we are
grateful that you realize that this annexation would put a burden on many of
the people involved.
We have a lot of residents in our park that are elderly and have been with us a
very long time; several of them have been here over 30 years. The closing of
our park would devastate them and the majority of our other residents. We’ve
provided a safe, happy, clean affordable place for a lot of people over the
years. If we’d asked them, (the past or current residents) they would be
storming city hall tonight with their fears, but I didn’t want to alarm them
unnecessarily. So with the exception of a few that read about the annexation in
the paper, most aren’t aware of the problems we’re facing.
If they’d be forced to leave, most of their mobile homes -because of their age-
wouldn’t be allowed in other parks in the county under the new county UDO. Can
you imagine what this would do to them? Who would pay their relocation
expenses? And as for the RV’s, there isn’t another park around this area for
them either.
We think the city wouldn’t be damaged by NOT requiring sewer connections to
existing structures. You could just require them for any new construction. Or
give everyone a choice. I don’t imagine any new construction would opt for
installing their own septic systems now if they can use city sewer.
There are many cities in N.C. that do not require mandatory sewer connections
to involuntarily annexed areas regardless of whether the lines run past their
property. Ayden is one example. The people have a choice.
People have commented to us that we should just sell out and not worry about
the annexation. We’d worry about all our residents and how it’d affect them.
We’d worry about the need for rv spaces and affordable places for people that
don’t have the means to buy a condo or home in Southport.
I ask you to remember what happened to Tom Jones when the SE Sanitary District
took his park into their district. His park was on Hwy. 211 across from the
Catholic Church. The fees and mandatory sewer hook up costs drove him out of
business. He closed his park. He was in the exact situation that we are facing.
Folks said, no worry, he can sell it. Well, it’s been for sale for a long time-
---and is still unsold.
We do have a question about the garbage collection. Currently we have a
dumpster at each end of the park. They are picked up twice weekly. I understand
that the city only offers once a week pickup. I thought that an annexation is
supposed to give us additional services, but in actuality, no one will be
getting anything they don’t already have.
Now, in probably the worst economic climate this country has faced since the
depression, I think our government should be especially sensitive to the
economic impact that every action you take will make on each individual. I
believe that you-our local government- are a governing body that is for the
people and not against the people-and that you will work to find a solution for
all of us.
We’re sensitive to your desire to expand the city limits and we ask that if you
go forward with this annexation, that you please find a way to do it without
devastating consequences to anyone in the proposed annexed areas.
Thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak.
Mr. Donald Reavis, resident of Dosher Cutoff, again questioned the reason for
annexation. He stated that there are only three houses on Dosher Cutoff that
will be affected and it is his belief that the Board should set up funds to
relocate people if the City continues with the proposed annexation.
There being no further comments, the Public Hearing was closed upon motion of
Alderman Adams, seconded by Alderman Boguskie, vote carried.
Board Comments
Alderman Adams thanked the citizens for their comments and stated the Board
understands their concerns and is sensitive to their needs.
Alderman Boguskie stated that the Board would consider all comments, and
thanked citizens for their input.
Alderman Fisher stated that he did not vote to support the annexation because
it is his belief that other areas should have been included.
Mayor Spencer stated the City needs to grow in order to survive and annexation
was not intended to be a financial burden. Staff is working to alleviate some
of the financial burden from the citizens regarding sewer impact fees.
City Manager Thornton stated annexation is never popular, but the City is
trying to establish orderly growth. Staff is working on proposals to provide
the Board with information for consideration to help relieve some of the
financial impact off the citizens.
Adjournment – 7:01 p.m.
No further business, the meeting was closed upon motion of Alderman Adams,
seconded by Aerman Boguskie, vote carried.
