a)   Electric Committee Recommendation(s)
Alderman Fisher presented the following for consideration on behalf of the
Electric Committee:
The Electric Committee met on January 7, 2009 and reviewed several options to
offset and pay for the increase from NCEMPA on the demand portion of the City’s
electric bill. This will be an overall increase of 4%, which will result in
approximately $17,000 per month. We reviewed residential and customer base
fees, customer area lighting, service charges, demand excess charges on large
commercial accounts and load management monitoring.
We make the following recommendation to the Board for approval and to become
effective February 1, 2009.
1.   Increase Residential Base Fee from $2.52 to $6.00 and increase commercial
base fee from $3.49 to $7.00. This fee is for making electric service available
to our customers and maintaining it. The City’s cost for operation &
maintenance is $25,850 a month. The availability base fee on customer meters,
with the increase, will generate revenue of $15,862. The difference is paid by
sales of electricity, service charges and area lighting fees.
2.   Increase customer area lighting fees. Majority of customers that are
paying $8.14 for a 100-watt area light will have an increase to $10.14. The
revenue generated from this is approximately $3500 a month, which assists in
the cost of the operation, & maintenance cost that the City pays, minus the
cost for kilowatts (kw) used. The monthly cost for kw for each light is
approximately $3.15.
3.   Increase Demand Excess charge from $1.00 to $4.00 on large commercial
demand accounts and impose a $2.00 excess charge on all other commercial demand
accounts. This increase helps brings the demand cost closer inline to the
actual cost the City is paying.
4.   Management and enforcement of load management customers. Making sure that
all load management switches are connected on all customers that are
participating and the proper rate is being charged. After a week of load
management audits on the R12 rate, 79% of our customers had switches that were
disconnected. This percentage will result in approximately $4,000 of recovered
loss revenue.
The overall increase in fees that the City is proposing will generate 3% of the
4% increase by the NCEMPA. The other 1% will be offset by closely monitoring
and managing the load management program.
The City will continuously review all rates, fees and the progress of the load
management audits in the Electric Fund for the next four (4) months and
recommend adjustments (-/+) as necessary.
Alderman Fisher motioned to approve the recommendations of the Electric
Committee, seconded by Alderman Boguskie. The vote was unanimous.
b)   Resolution Altering the Distribution of Southport's ABC Store Revenues
City Manager Thornton stated for 51 years, 35% of ABC revenue net profits have
been given to the three area schools: Southport Elementary -10%, South
Brunswick Middle – 10%, South Brunswick High – 10%, and 5% to Dosher Hospital,
which totaled $93,163 for FY 07-08. He explained that the City is looking at
various sources for additional revenues due to major projects that will impact
the City financially. Because of the economic slow down; the City will be
affected by a decrease in the property tax collections, state sales tax
distribution, building permits and other areas. City Manager Thornton thanked
parents and representatives from Southport Elementary School and Dosher
Hospital for being present due to their concerns about the proposed
redistribution of ABC revenues. He acknowledged that he has a vested interest
in the schools, but as City Manager, he must look out for the financial well-
being of the City in order to continue operating and providing services to the
citizens. He presented a resolution asking the Board to consider redistribution
of ABC revenues, the same as other municipalities have done including Boiling
Spring Lakes, Oak Island, Ocean Isle Beach and Shallotte.
Alderman Boguskie questioned if the City receives 100% of the net ABC proceeds,
could the City provide funds to Southport Elementary School. City Manager
Thornton stated the Board could consider allocations during the budget process.
Alderman Fisher motioned to adopt the "Resolution of the Southport Board of
Aldermen Altering the Distribution of ABC Revenue"  with the City of Southport
receiving 100% of the net profits, and to add:  2) that during the budget
process each year, the Board of Aldermen shall consider an appropriation to
Southport Elementary School to be earmarked for supplies. Alderman Brown
seconded the motion.   Discussion: Alderman Potter suggested establishing an
amount for the school. Alderman Adams stated he does not believe the governing
body should lock in a set amount because it may be contingent upon monies
received. No further comments, the vote of approval was unanimous.
RESOLUTION OF SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN ALTERING THE DISTRIBUTION OF ABC
REVENUE
WHEREAS, Section 6(a) of Chapter 819 of the 1957 Session Laws, as amended by
Chapter 456 House Bill 680 of the 1971 Session Laws and Chapter 1400 Senate
Bill 1472 of the 1973 Session Laws, provide for the distribution of the net
profits derived from the operation of the City of Southport ABC store; and
WHEREAS, G.S. 18B-805(e) provides that the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport may alter the distribution of net profits as established in said
local acts by the adoption of a resolution setting forth a new distribution
formula; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the best interests of the City of Southport, the
Board of Aldermen now desires to adopt a resolution providing for a new
distribution formula for the net profits of its ABC store;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED as follows:
1.   That pursuant to G.S. 18B-805(e), the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
hereby alters the distribution of the net profits of its ABC store to provide
that one hundred percent (100%) thereof shall go to the general fund of the
City of Southport.
2.   That during the budget process each year the Board of Aldermen shall
consider an appropriation to Southport Elementary School to be earmarked for
supplies.
3.   That this resolution shall become effective July 1, 2009.
This the 12th day of February, 2009.

RESOLUTION OF SUPPORT
N.C. Maritime Museum
WHEREAS, we appreciate the support and confidence given to the Southport Branch
of the North Carolina Maritime Museum, and
WHEREAS, the N. C. Maritime Museum at Southport has created a facility that
contributes to the educational and economic growth of Southeastern, N. C., and
WHEREAS, this historic association has expanded its development, and Friends of
the N. C. Maritime Museum, Inc. at Southport which is a non-profit support
organization which works diligently to provide financial support to the museum
for programs and exhibits, and
WHEREAS, the Maritime Museum at Southport was established in 1992, and became a
state agency in 1999, an agency of the North Carolina Department of Cultural
Resources directly under the Division of State History Museums, a component of
the Office of Archives and History, and
WHEREAS, the Maritime Museum at Southport is a teaching facility for area
schools and organizations, with 30,000+ visitors a year, and
WHEREAS, the Southport Maritime Museum is the only center in the southeastern
coastal area of N. C. that collects, preserves and displays the artifacts and
images indigenous to the maritime history and culture of the people of the
Lower Cape Fear Region.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Southport Board of Aldermen request the
State of North Carolina and the N. C. Department of Cultural Resources to do
everything within their power to keep this facility open and operating for the
enrichment of the public.
ADOPTED, this the 12th day of February 2009.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer

b)    Resolution to establish a sewer policy for prospective properties annexed
into the City
Attorney Isenberg stated that the City Code of Ordinances requires connection
to public sewer within sixty (60) days; however, there is a provision in the
City Code for special circumstances in which the Board may extend the time for
compliance or waive the provision. The Resolution to establish sewer policy for
prospective properties to be annexed because of City initiated annexation is a
special circumstance and the Board may alter the requirements. The Board
discussed the Resolution and established an installment plan for paying impact
fees upon connection to the City's Wastewater System with an interest rate of
4% annum. (See Resolution below) Attorney Isenberg stated the policy may be
amended if necessary.
Alderman Boguskie motioned, seconded by Alderman Potter to adopt the following
resolution establishing a sewer policy. Vote of approval was 5 ayes: Aldermen
Boguskie, Potter, Adams, Frink and Brown. 1 no, Alderman Fisher.
Alderman Brown motioned that one single availability fee of $40 be paid in
accordance with City policy for minimum three thousand gallons of sewer,
seconded by Alderman Potter. Vote unanimous.
RESOLUTION OF SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN ESTABLISHING A SEWER POLICY FOR
PROPERTIES ANNEXED INTO THE CITY BY CITY-INITIATED ANNEXATIONS
That Whereas, Section 19-99(b) of the Southport Code of Ordinances provides
that:
When a public sewer becomes available to a property served by a private
wastewater disposal system, a direct connection shall be made to the public
sewer within (60) days. Under unusual and/or special circumstances the Board of
Aldermen may extend the time of compliance or waive this provision; and
Whereas, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds and declares that a city-initiated
annexation is an unusual and special circumstance pursuant to Section 19-99 for
which the Board of Aldermen should extend the time of compliance for mandatory
sewer connection for properties involuntarily annexed into the City of
Southport which properties are already connected to a private wastewater
disposal system;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
following policy is hereby adopted for properties annexed into the City by
city-initiated annexation, which are connected to a private wastewater disposal
system at the time of the effective date of said annexation:
1.   Any improved property which is annexed into the City of Southport by a
city-initiated annexation proceeding and which is already connected to a
private wastewater disposal system on the effective date of said annexation
shall be allowed to continue to utilize a currently functioning and permitted
private wastewater disposal system until such time as the first of the
following events occur: (i) the private wastewater disposal system fails, or
(ii) the use of property changes to a use which would require significant
modification of the existing private system, or (iii) the ownership of the
property changes, or (iv) any environmental issue arises resulting in a
determination of private wastewater disposal system closure by the State of
North Carolina, federal government or Brunswick County. Upon the occurrence of
the first of said events, the City shall notify the property owner and said
property shall be connected to the city sewer within 60 days from notification
by City that connection is required. Connection shall be made in accordance
with the City’s policies and ordinances existing at the time of connection, and
the property owner shall pay all charges and fees in effect at said time except
as otherwise provided herein.
2.   During the period of time beginning with the effective date of annexation
(provided that city sewer is available) until such time as the annexed property
is connected to the city sewer in accordance with City policy, the owner of
said property shall be required to pay a monthly availability fee of the
minimum monthly sewer charge as established by the City.
3.   The owner of a property which is connected to a private wastewater
disposal system on the effective date of a city-initiated annexation which
requires payment at the time of connection of an impact fee of $10,000 or less
shall be allowed to pay the required impact fee for said property together with
interest at 4% annum in not more than 5 annual installments with the first
being due at the time of connection and subsequent installments being due
annually thereafter until paid. The owner of a property which is connected to a
private wastewater disposal system on the effective date of a city-initiated
annexation which requires payment at the time of connection of an impact fee of
more than $10,000 shall be allowed to pay the required impact fee for said
property together with interest at 4% per annum in not more than 20 annual
installments with the first installment being due at the time of connection and
subsequent installments being due annually thereafter until paid. The amount of
the impact fee, tap on fee and all other connection charges shall be determined
as of the city fee schedule applicable on the day of connection. The tap on fee
and any and all other connection charges shall be due and payable in full at
the time of connection.
This the 12th day of March, 2009.
City of Southport
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer
By: Mayor
ATTEST:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC

Alderman Boguskie stated when he spoke in support of the Museum, it was
understood that he was not speaking for the Board of Aldermen.
Alderman Brown stated he supports the Museum and will work to save it, but
would like every avenue explored i.e. the Governor's, Senate and House budgets
to continue funding for the Museum.
Alderman Adams stated he supports the Museum, but will not vote to displace the
Parks and Recreation Department's programs or employees.
Mayor stated if the Board decides that it will lease the property, the City
would need a commitment from the State that the Museum will continue to
operate. Consideration needs to be given to relocating employees and programs
that serve children in the community, a commitment from the Museum or Friends
of the Museum and the State, that all renovations would be paid for by them
including operating expenses and insurance. The Senior Citizen Building may be
available but not in time to accommodate the needs of the City. She stated that
all factors must be considered including permission from the Federal Lands to
Parks Program to lease the building.
Mayor Spencer presented a letter from the Southport Oak Island Chamber of
Commerce in support of the Maritime Museum.
Alderman Frink stated her support of the Museum; however, as a member of the
Parks and Recreation Committee she supports their programs and believes the
Board should discuss this more in-depth before making a decision.
The City Manager added that blame is being placed on the City because of a
fiscal issue that the City has no control over and the Department of Cultural
Resources will make the final decision. The City supports the Museum, however
time is needed to make decisions and develop plans. He explained that the Parks
and Recreation Department has its programs scheduled for the summer. He
reiterated that the Maritime Museum is an asset to the City, but whatever
directives the Board gives, staff will adjust.
Alderman Potter stated his support, realizing also that the Parks and
Recreation programs are scheduled. He stated that his preference would be to
pass a resolution of support with the Maritime Museum remaining in Southport,
not naming a specific location while an alternative solution is explored.
Alderman Boguskie motioned to adopt a resolution of the Board's intent to
authorize the lease of Davis Street apartments at $1.00 annually for a term not
to exceed ten (10) years at the next regular meeting of the Board, seconded by
Alderman Potter. Discussion: Attorney Isenberg stated before property can be
leased; a ten (10) day notice must be given in the newspaper. Alderman Brown
suggested the resolution state that the Board is in favor of the museum and
will investigate all avenues and work toward finding the best solution for
location of the museum, while contacting the Department of Interior about
leasing the building. Alderman Fisher stated the budget is being worked now, if
delayed for thirty (30) days, nothing is being accomplished. If the Friends of
the Museum and others go to Raleigh or invite legislative officials to a town
meeting and write letters, nothing has been accomplished.
Mayor Spencer called for the vote: 5 ayes, Aldermen Adams, Potter, Brown, Frink
and Boguskie. 1 no, Alderman Fisher.
Alderman Adams asked that an informational meeting be held before April's
meeting.
d)   Resolution Supporting Legislative Initiative to Delay Implementation of
Beach Plan/Fair Plan Coastal Insurance Increases
Mr. Thornton explained that the Department of Insurance has considered
increasing homeowners insurance in coastal areas up to thirty percent (30%). He
asked that the Board adopt a resolution establishing the City's position by
joining with others to request the General Assembly to delay a decision on this
matter until additional information is compiled.
Alderman Brown motioned to adopt the Resolution supporting legislative
initiatives to delay implementation of the Beach Plan/Fair Plan Coastal
Insurance increases, seconded by Alderman Boguskie. Amendment: Alderman Fisher
asked that the resolution be amended to include, if the Plan does go into
effect that the homeowners be allowed to make installment payments. The vote
was unanimous.
RESOLUTION
In Support of Legislation Delaying The Implementation of the Rate Increases in
Home Insurance
Whereas, recent actions by the North Carolina Insurance Commission has resulted
in disproportionate rate increases under the Beach and the F.A.I.R. Plans, and
Whereas, the swift inception of rate increases does not provide adequate notice
or time to adjust to the increases, and
Whereas, the rate payers in coastal counties are perplexed as to the
justification of these rate hikes, and
Whereas, issues of this magnitude could be examined for underlying reasons that
may be related to the history of loss, anticipation of loss or the real reasons
for loss, and
Whereas, looking into the issues for the real reasons of the acute increases
would be to our advantage.
Now, therefore the Southport Board of Aldermen resolves to join in with the
Brunswick County Board of Commissioners in efforts seeking a postponement of
the rate increases until such time as explicit and credible evidence becomes
available showing that the rate increases are based upon factual loss in the
coastal regions.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that if these rate increases go into effect that
homeowners be allowed to make installment payments on their homeowners'
insurance premiums.
Adopted this the 12th day of March 2009.
/s/Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
Attest:
/s/Regina W. Alexander, MMC

h)   Arbor Day Proclamation
Alderman Fisher motioned, seconded by Alderman Frink to adopt the following
Proclamation in recognition of Arbor Day. Vote carried
ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/IMAGES/0-0-0-46.jpg]
WHEREAS, in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of Agriculture that a special day be
set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS, this holiday called Arbor Day , was first observed with the planting of more than a million trees
in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS, Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS, trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and water, cut heating and cooling
costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air, produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for
wildlife, and
WHEREAS, trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes, fuel for our fires, and
beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic vitality of business areas, and
beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE,  I Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor of the City of Southport, N.C. do hereby proclaim March 20,
2009 as ARBOR DAY in the City and urge all citizens to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees
and woodlands, and
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote the well-being of this and
future generations.
DATED, this 12th day of March, 2009.
/S/ Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor

MARCH 21, 2009
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING
MARCH 21, 2009    ALDERMEN CHAMBERS
SOUTHPORT, NC     8:00 A.M.
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Donnie Potter, Ed Boguskie,
            Jwantana Frink, James Brown and Paul Fisher
ABSENT:         None
STAFF:         Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
            Heather Hemphill, Parks and Recreation Director
            Ralph Cardwell, Director of Public Services
I.
Call to Order
Mayor Spencer convened the meeting at 8:04 a.m.
II.
Invocation
Alderman Brown pronounced the invocation.
III.
Discussion of the NC Maritime Museum in Southport
Mayor Spencer acknowledged a letter from Stuart Callari and requested that it
be incorporated in the minutes.
Mayor Spencer stated that she was informed that the Governor's budget includes
funding for the Southport Maritime Museum, but there were no monies allocated
for a location.
Mr. Walter Madsen, Friends of the Museum, told the Board he spoke with Mr. Joe
Schwartzer, State Director of the NC Maritime Museums and explained the time
frame that the Board was under due to the summer schedule of the Parks and
Recreation Department. He stated if the Board of Aldermen elected to approve
the Friends of the Maritime Museum's Plan, the Parks and Recreation Department
could stay in place through the month of September.
Alderman Boguskie informed the Board of a meeting scheduled April 1 with
Senator Soles, Secretary of the Department of Cultural Resources, and Friends
of the Museum. He stated representatives from the City should attend.
Alderman Fisher recommended the Board invite Senator Soles, Representatives
Stiller and Hill to Southport for a Town Hall meeting.
Wayne Strickland, speaking on behalf of the Friends of the Museum asked that a
timeline be provided as to what is expected if the City allows use of the
property. Friends of the Museum have received a guarantee from the Department
of Cultural Resources that they would not need to relocate until the end of
summer, which would give the Recreation Department sufficient time for their
summer programs.
Alderman Adams questioned whether the Friends of the Museum contacted
legislative representatives to ask for support, and questioned whether they
looked for alternative locations. He stated his opposition to a ten-year lease
and relocating the Parks and Recreation Department.
Mr. Strickland stated that they have looked at other locations, but their
desire is to remain downtown. He communicated that the Department of Cultural
Resources does not wish the Museum to remain in a storefront facility.
Heather Hemphill, Director of Parks and Recreation shared with the Board that
she is concerned about the summer programs. She stated losing the Davis Street
facility would affect her programs and some of these programs cannot be placed
in another location. The Senior Citizen Building that was discussed will
require renovations. The department needs a facility with more than office
space. She expressed concern that the City gym is not air-conditioned.
Alderman Fisher questioned the State's plan for the Museum and explained the
City developed a long-range plan for Ft. Johnston, which was based on Lowe-
White Park being completed, which has been pushed back three years.
Mr. Strickland questioned why the Davis Street apartments at Fort Johnston are
the best location for Parks and Recreation with no handicap accessibility.
Mayor Spencer stated the Board called this meeting to discuss the possibility
of leasing the Davis Street apartments to the Maritime Museum. The City needs
to focus on helping the Maritime Museum survive and to keep the Parks and
Recreation programs viable.
Alderman Brown stated the Board should first contact the Department of Interior
to ascertain if leasing the facility is viable, schedule a meeting with
legislative officials to investigate funding for the Museum, and to receive
comments from the citizens of Southport. He cited some relocation options that
can be explored, i.e. fire station and visitor's center. The Board needs time
to look at options, because the City cannot displace one department for another
agency.
Alderman Boguskie suggested City representatives attend the meeting in Raleigh
on April 1 and afterwards, schedule a public meeting.
Alderman Potter stated both the Museum and Recreation Department benefits the
City and hope a decision can be forthcoming to satisfy everyone.
Mayor Spencer asked the Board to consider directives or alternatives for the
next meeting.
Ms. Roberta Dosher, member of the Parks and Recreation Department stated that
she is in favor of the Maritime Museum; but the City should abide by the
agreement that was approved when Fort Johnston was acquired by the City.
Pursuant to a question from Alderman Fisher, Mr. Strickland stated that they
prefer to stay in the present location, but the State does not want the Museum
in a storefront building. A permanent site is preferable. Alderman Fisher spoke
about the fund raising strategies that were used to raise monies for the
Community Building and the same mechanism could possibly work to assist the
Maritime Museum, but everyone must work together.
Alderman Boguskie motioned, seconded by Alderman Potter to follow-up with
Senator Soles and the Department of Cultural Resources concerning the April 1
meeting in Raleigh. Votes were 5 ayes Alderman Boguskie, Potter, Brown, Adams
and Frink. 1 no, Alderman Fisher.
Alderman Frink motioned, seconded by Alderman Brown to schedule a Town Hall
meeting April 3, 6:00 p.m. subsequent to the meeting in Raleigh on April 1, and
to invite Senator R. C. Soles, Representatives Stiller and Hill. The vote was
unanimous.
IV.
Clean Water Management Trust Fund Proposed Amendment #1 to Project No. 2006A-
529
City Manager Thornton stated the City received two grants from CWMTF, $1.68
million to purchase the spray irrigation site near Sunny Point. Second grant
was for the infrastructure to get wastewater out of the waterway by 2011. When
the City decided to join with the County, the State realized that the site
would not be utilized as originally planned; however, the City did discuss use
of the site by the County, which will possibly take place in the future, but
not soon enough for the CWMTF Board. The Clean Water Management Trust Board
sent an amendment to the City stating that in order for the City to receive the
remainder of the $3 million grant, the City will need to pay back the $1.68
million.
City Manager Thornton stated approximately $2.5 million remains of the $3
million because a portion of the money has been spent for design drawings and
surveys. Staff requested directives from the Board because the City has 365
days from the date that the Board agrees to the terms of the amendment to remit
the money. If the $1.68 is not returned, then the City will not receive the
balance of the $2.5 to complete the sewer reversal project.
City Manager Thornton stated the City owns the 400-acre site near Sunny Point,
which is ideal for a spray irrigation complex, and when the county builds the
Southeast Wastewater Treatment Plant, the City could possibly negotiate with
the County to use its site and recover some of the costs.
City Manager Thornton in answer to questions stated the City needs the money to
continue with the sewer reversal project; however, the City will request to pay
it back in installments because there is the possibility the property will be
used for its intended purpose.
Ralph Cardwell, Public Services Director stated the City has two valuable
pieces of property, the 400-acre tract near Sunny Point and the land where the
Waste Water Treatment Plant is located at the end of West West Street. He
stated once the WWTP is dismantled, the Board could sell the land with an
option to lease it back. He stated that he has been contacted about the land.
The Board discussed various options and what could be done i.e. considering
selling property to raise monies to pay back the grant.
Alderman Potter motioned, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to direct staff to
contact the Clean Water Management Trust to pursue options to pay the $1.68
million back in installments, and to request an extension of time, and further;
to investigate options to sell land with the understanding that the City will
have options to lease the property, however the City would retain the 400 acres
near Sunny Point. Discussion: Alderman Fisher recommended staff continue to
negotiate not having to repay the $1.68 million. The vote of approval was
unanimous.
V.
Other Business
City Manager Thornton announced that Town Hall Day is May 6, Raleigh, NC.
City Manager Thornton stated that staff would explore options and make every
effort to provide services when a decision is made regarding the Maritime
Museum.
Mayor Spencer stated the Senior Citizen building will soon be vacated and the
City needs to decide the best use for the building.
Mayor Spencer announced that Relay for Life is the first weekend in May 1. She
and her family will be having a Yard Sale April 18 to raise funds in support of
this worthy cause.
By consensus, the Board agreed to hold a public meeting on April 3, 6:00 p.m.
and to invite Representatives Hill, Stiller and Senator R.C. Soles.
Alderman Fisher suggested the Board look at developing a strategic plan for the
City because of the number of outstanding projects that are pending.
Alderman Adams requested the City Hall restroom upstairs be remodeled i.e. new
fixtures.
Mayor Spencer informed the Board that McClure Design and Building Contractor of
Acworth, Ga. was the low bidder for the fire station in the amount of
$3,293,000.
Alderman Potter stated a proposal should be presented from the Fire Committee
before the Board votes on the bids in order to determine financing options and
a repayment plan.
Alderman Fisher noted that the City gym was built in 1951-52 and only one-half
of the gym remains.
VI.
Adjournment – 10:45 a.m.
No further business, meeting adjourned upon motion of Alderman Potter, seconded
by Alderman Brown. Vote carried.

Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor

Resolution – Federal Stimulus Monies
City Manager Thornton asked the Board to adopt a resolution because the City is
making application for funding through the American Recovery and Reinvestment
Act. He stated that the City needs to be "shovel ready" when funding becomes
available. The City is applying for stimulus funds for its sewer reversal
project. If funds were awarded to the City, it would be a 50% grant and 50%
loan. Of the $2.8 billion in requests for stimulus monies, there is only $76
million available for wastewater projects. The first round of funds in category
one will be issued on or about June 1, and the second round in the July-August
timeframe.
Carter Hubard, Consulting Engineer stated the projected schedule is to begin
construction in the fall of 2009 and the project will take approximately one
year to complete.

resolution and to authorize the City Manager and Mayor to sign it. The vote of
approval was unanimous.

to sign resolutions for stimulus monies if the need arises, since the timeframe
is tight when applying for these funds. Mayor Spencer and City Manager Thornton
stated that they did not see the need for the resolution at this time.

APRIL 3, 2009
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
APRIL 3, 2009     ALDERMEN CHAMBERS
SOUTHPORT, N.C.   6:00 P.M.
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Alderman Donnie Potter, Ed Boguskie, Paul Fisher,
            Nelson Adams, James Brown and Jwantana Frink
ABSENT:          None
STAFF PRESENT:      Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, MMC-City Clerk
I.
Call to Order
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m.
II.
Invocation
Alderman Adams pronounced the invocation.
III.
Town Hall Meeting
Mayor Spencer stated the purpose of the meeting is to address issues regarding
the Maritime Museum.
City Manager Thornton briefed the Board on the meeting in Raleigh, which was
attended by him and four (4) members of the Board with Senator R. C. Soles,
Representative Stiller, Secretary Carlisle, Department of Cultural Resources
and others. Mr. Thornton stated that the legislative representatives support
the Maritime Museum and expressed that it remains open. Secretary Carlisle told
them that Governor Perdue expects vertical cuts in State departmental budgets
and she is seeking ways to comply; therefore ultimately proposing to cut $50-
$60,000 from the Southport Maritime Museum. Mr. Thornton stated in gleaning
information from the meeting, the Department of Cultural Resources is not an
advocate one way or another as to whether the Maritime Museum locates in the
Fort Johnston barracks; or if they remain downtown in their present location.
The Department of Cultural Resources are looking at ways to cut their budget
and are open to options. The State is looking for the best long-term solution,
which is to have a State owned facility in Southport. It was his belief that
those in attendance were advocating for a nice Museum comparable to those in
Beaufort and Cape Hatteras, and that the level of support be consistent and
equal amongst the three Maritime Museums. Once the Department of Cultural
Resources formulates a long-term goal, then supporters of the Museum should
contact legislators asking for support and request appropriations in future
budgets.
Representative Stiller stated that all Museums should share the reduction, not
only Southport. Tommy Harrelson proprietor of the building where the museum is
currently housed, stated his willingness to work with the Museum and make some
concessions regarding the rent. City Manager Thornton stated those in
attendance demonstrated a willingness to do what they could to keep the doors
of the museum open. Secretary Carlisle informed them that no decisions would be
made until September. This should allow sufficient time to develop a plan. Mr.
Thornton stated that it is his belief that the barracks are not a permanent
solution; however, the Museum is intrinsic to Southport and nobody wants to see
it gone.
Mayor Spencer stated the legislators were in support of the Museum remaining in
Southport and she expressed this to Secretary Carlisle.
Alderman Fisher stated that there is no operational plan in place and believes
that there should be one developed by the State to keep the Museum open.
Supporters should continue lobbying the State for funding.
Alderman Frink agreed that a plan is needed and use of the barracks will only
be a band-aid fix.
Alderman Boguskie stated that Dr. Crow, made it known that one of his long-
range plans is to acquire a building for the Southport Museum. He agreed that a
plan is needed at the State level, but in the interim, something needs to be
decided to help the Museum.
Mayor Spencer stated that 78% of the artifacts contained in the Museum are
ready to be turned over to the State, which has been an issue, in addition to
the State not owning the building.
Stuart Callari of 106 W. Nash Street voiced her support of the Maritime Museum.
She asked if the Maritime Museum is placed in the Davis Street Barracks, where
will the City place the Parks and Recreation Department. It is her belief that
a plan needs to be developed by the State for the Museum. If the Museum is
placed in the barracks, it will set a bad precedent because Southport deserves
a first-rate State Museum. She encouraged the Friends of the Museum to lobby
Raleigh for funding because after all, the Southport Maritime Museum is a State
facility.
Mr. Jim Carey of 3437 Members Club Blvd, St. James, and representing Friends of
the Maritime Museum stated that they have a plan in place, but the State does
not. It is their belief that the band-aid fix will work until plans are
developed by the State, which will take longer to develop. The Friends
currently have a plan for renovations to the barracks. They need the help of
the City to find a location for the Museum until a long term Plan is developed
by the State. If a location is not found prior to Labor Day, the Museum may
cease to exist.
Alderman Adams reiterated his support of the Museum; however, he stated that
the Board needs to be aware of problems it will incur to help another agency
including financial responsibility when their first obligation should be to the
City and its departments. He stated that ten (10) years is a long time to enter
into a lease with any agency. He asked the Board to be careful of problems that
will be placed upon the City when trying to help another agency.
Alderman Boguskie stated ten years is the maximum for a lease and the State can
sever a lease. He agreed that the City must look out for the Parks and
Recreation Department, but this should be a decision by the City Manager since
City employees work for the Manager.
Alderman Adams stated the City Manager works for the Board, which gives him
directives and a decision of this significance, should be a Board decision.
Alderman Frink questioned why the Museum could not remain in its present
location if the proprietor is willing to work with them regarding the rent.
Alderman Fisher stated that the Parks and Recreation Department has been in
transit for the past four years. The youth are the backbone of the City and
questioned if the barracks are the best location for a Museum. He suggested
asking the County for financial support.
Mayor Spencer explained that the States does not want to pay rent; Secretary
Carlisle indicated that if someone were willing to pay the rent, the Department
of Cultural Resources would continue to pay staffs' salaries.
Alderman Brown stated that apparently, the State desires a first class Museum,
and it is his belief that the City should not displace people.
Alderman Potter stated the State is responsible for the Museum and believes
what is happening with the Museum is a disservice to the Community. He stated
until the State acknowledges to what extent it is willing to make a commitment,

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNDER THE
AUTHORITY GRANTED BY CHAPTER 160A, ARTICLE 4A, PART 2 OF THE NORTH CAROLINA
GENERAL STATUTES
WHEREAS, all of the prerequisites to adoption of this ordinance prescribed in
Chapter 160A, Article 4A, Part 2 of the North Carolina General Statutes have
been met; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has taken into full consideration the statements
presented at the public hearing held on January 22, 2009, on the question of
this annexation; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has concluded and hereby declares that
annexation of the area described herein is necessary to the orderly growth and
development of the City of Southport;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that:
Section 1. From and after the effective date of this annexation, the following
territory shall be annexed to and become a part of the City of Southport, and
the corporate limits of the City of Southport shall be extended to include said
territory more particularly described by metes and bounds as follows:
See Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference.
Section 2. The Board of Aldermen hereby finds and declares that the above-
described territory meets the requirements of G.S. 160A-36, in that:
Contiguity Test:
1.   The area is adjacent and contiguous to the existing municipal boundary, as
defined by G.S. 160A-36(b) (1), as of the 13th day of November, 2008, the date
upon which this annexation proceeding was begun.
2.   The aggregate external boundary line of the area to be annexed is
41,506.74 linear feet. The portion of this boundary that coincides with the
City of Southport’s boundary is 11,151.18 linear feet. Therefore, 26.9% of the
external boundary coincides with the City of Southport’s boundary, in excess of
the one-eighth (12.5%) contiguity requirement.
3.   No part of the area to be annexed is included within the boundary of
another incorporated municipality.
Subdivision Test:
1.   The area to be annexed is developed for urban uses as defined in G.S.
160A-36(c) in that 69.9% of the total number of lots and tracts in the area are
used for residential, commercial, industrial, institutional, or governmental
purposes, in excess of the required 60%, and 66.3% of the total of residential
and undeveloped acreage consists of lots and tracts three acres or less in
size, also in excess of the required 60%, all of which is demonstrated as
follows:
a.   Total Number of Lots and Tracts         =   113
Number of Lots and Tracts Used for Residential,
Commercial, Industrial, Institutional, or Governmental   =   79
Lots used for specified purposes            =    79
Total number of lots and tracts   113   =   69.9%
Statutory Requirement:   60%
b.   Total Residential and Undeveloped Acreage      =   73.93 acres
[total acreage, not counting acreage used for commercial, industrial,
governmental, or institutional purposes]
Residential and Undeveloped Acreage in Lots and
Tracts Three Acres or Less in Size          =   48.98 acres
Res. & Undev. Acreage in Lots/Tracts < 3 Acres   =   48.98
Total Residential & Undeveloped Acreage         73.93   = 66.3%
Statutory Requirement:   60%
Section 3. It is the purpose and intent of the City of Southport to provide
services to the area being annexed under this ordinance, as set forth in the
report of plans for services approved by the Board of Aldermen on November 13,
2008, and filed in the office of the Clerk for public inspection on November
13, 2008, and as amended on April 9, 2009.
See Exhibit B attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference.
Section 4. The Board of Aldermen hereby finds and declares that, on the
effective date of annexation prescribed in Section 8 hereof, the City of
Southport will have sufficient funds appropriated to finance the estimated cost
of construction of water and sewer facilities found necessary in the report of
plans for services to extend the basic sewer and water system of the City of
Southport into the area to be annexed under this ordinance.
Section 5. From and after the effective date of this annexation, the territory
annexed and its citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws,
ordinances and regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be
entitled to the same privileges and benefits as other parts of the City.
Section 6. The newly annexed territory described above shall be subject to City
taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10.
Section 7. The Mayor of the City of Southport shall cause an accurate map of
the annexed territory described in Section 1 hereof, together with a duly
certified copy of this ordinance, to be recorded in the office of the Brunswick
County Register of Deeds and in the office of the Secretary of State of North
Carolina. Such a map shall also be delivered to the Brunswick County Board of
Elections as required by G.S. 163-288.1.
Section 8. This ordinance shall become effective on April 9, 2010.
As to qualified tracts of agricultural land, horticultural land and forestland,
the annexation will become effective on the last day of the month in which the
tract or part thereof becomes ineligible for present-use classification under
G.S. 105-277.4 or no longer meets the requirements of G.S. 160A-37(f1)(2).
Adopted this 9th day of April 2009.

IV.
MAJOR SERVICES AND EXPENDITURES
This section of the annexation report provides the basis for plans to extend to
the proposed annexation area all applicable major services currently provided
in Southport on a non-discriminatory basis. North Carolina general statutes
require that all services including police, fire, infrastructure, and
administration be provided within the annexed area at levels comparable to that
provided within the existing corporate limits. The City of Southport, through
these annexation procedures, will aim to accommodate this requirement while
minimizing the financial impact on residential and non-residential property
owners.
A.   Administration Overview
The city operates under the Mayor-Aldermen-Manager form of government in
accordance with G.S. Chapter 160A, Article 7, Part 2. The Mayor and Board of
Aldermen are the governing body of the city. The Board is composed of six
members representing two voting districts who are elected at-large. The members
are elected for four-year terms. The Mayor is elected at large and serves a
two-year term.
The City Manager is appointed by the Board, and is responsible for the
administration of all departments of the city government and the implementation
of Board policy. The Board also appoints a City Attorney to represent the city
and provide legal counsel to city officials. The Board appoints citizen
representatives to serve on a variety of advisory committees who advise the
Board of various issues such as beautification, forestry, planning, and others.
The City Clerk maintains a City Code that codifies ordinances pertaining to the
administration and operations of the city.
The city administration is comprised of ten departments (Administration, Public
Services, Police, Building Inspections, Planning, Parks and Recreation,
Tourism, Code Enforcement, Water and Sewer Utility, Finance, Animal Control,
and Fire and EMS (Volunteer)) functioning under the direction of the City
Manager. A department head is appointed by the City Manager to manage each of
these departments.
B.   Police Protection
The Southport Police Department is located on the first floor of the City Hall
Building at 201 East Moore Street. The department’s full-time staff is made up
of a chief, one lieutenant, two sergeants, seven patrolmen, and a records
clerk. The city also has six part-time office personnel and one K-9. The
department responds to approximately 600 calls per month and maintains its own
Records Management System. Response calls are received through the Brunswick
County 911 Call Center. The following vehicles are available for use by the
department:
•   1 - 2005 Crown Victoria
•   1 - 2004 Crown Victoria
•   2 - 2002 Crown Victorias
•   1 - 1999 Chevy Lumina
•   2 - 1998 Crown Victorias
•   1 - 1998 Chevy Lumina
•   1 - 1997 Crown Victoria
•   2 - 1996 Crown Victorias
•   1 - 1994 Chevy Caprice
•   1 - Harley Davidson Motorcycle
•   1 - Speed Monitor Trailer
1.   Staffing Recommendation Statistics
According to the United States Department of Justice as of 2007, the average
number of law enforcement employees, including both full time sworn in officers
and civilians, for cities located in the south is 3.4 per 1000 population. The
national average for all cities is also 3.0 per 1000 population. Currently, the
Southport Police Department exceeds these minimum staffing levels with 4.2
full-time sworn officers and civilians per 1000 population. The population used
to make this determination is 2,860 as reported by the NC Department of Revenue
Sales and Use Tax Distribution.
As noted earlier in the report, it is estimated that Southport’s population
will increase by an estimated 229 persons subsequent to annexation. This will
result in a staffing level of 3.9 police department employees per 1000 in
population. The resultant staffing level for the Southport Police Department
subsequent to annexation will be above both the southern and national averages.
The city will closely monitor this issue to ensure that adequate police
protection is provided. If it is determined that additional staffing is
required, the Board of Aldermen will take appropriate measures to accommodate
this need.
C.   Code Enforcement and Animal Control Operations
The Southport Code Enforcement Department has the main responsibility of
enforcing all city codes recorded in the Southport General Code of Ordinances.
The Department has several different divisions in which the duties of code
enforcement are grouped:
Animal Control
Fire Prevention
Health/Sanitation
Minimum Housing
Solid Waste
Miscellaneous/Other Duties
The Code Enforcement Officer is responsible for the enforcement of the animal
control code, which is outlined in Section 3 of the Southport Code of
Ordinances. Along with the enforcement of this code, the City of Southport
provides several services dealing with domesticated animals as a benefit to
city residents. They are as follows:
Rabies Education
Free Adoptions
Low Cost Rabies Clinics
Pet Responsibility Education
City Licensing Program
Stray/Abandoned Animal Capture
The Code Enforcement Officer also performs several investigative functions.
Under the Animal Control Division, the code official is a North Carolina State
Certified Animal Cruelty Investigator. All animal cruelty/neglect cases are
investigated through this department. Noise violations pertaining to animals
are also investigated when a complaint is received. All animal bites/attacks
must be reported and investigated according to the North Carolina General
Statues. Any and all animal related matters can be forwarded to the Code
Enforcement Department for a prompt response.
The proposed annexation will not have any significant impact on the current
staffing levels for the provision of code enforcement and animal control
services.
D.   Public Services
The City of Southport Public Services Department is currently staffed by an
administrative staff of seven individuals. This staff is comprised of a Public
Services Director, Assistant Director, Wastewater Operations Supervisor,
Systems Coordinator, Buildings and Grounds Supervisor, Public Works Supervisor,
and Garage Supervisor. These individuals are charged with maintaining the
city’s infrastructure including the electric system, water and sewer services,
city maintained streets, and governmental facilities.
The proposed annexation will not necessitate a need for additional public
services personnel; however, there will be cost tied to the provision of
comprehensive infrastructure services. The following provides a detailed
breakdown of each function of the public services, and what cost will be
incurred to insure statutory compliance with the provision of services to the
annexation area. Within this section of the report, the following will be
addressed: streets, electric services, water services, and sewer services.
1.   Streets/Lighting
A majority of the streets located within the annexation area are currently
paved, and are either maintained by the North Carolina Department of
Transportation (NCDOT) or the City of Southport. As noted within the revenue
section of the report, the city will assume maintenance of an additional 1.8
miles of right-of-way within the annexation area. The city will utilize
increased Powell Bill revenues to provide street and shoulder maintenance for
these streets. The remainder of streets located within the annexation boundary
will continue to be maintained by NCDOT.
There are three street segments within the proposed annexation area that are
either currently unopened or not paved. These include a portion of North Lord
Street (unopened/602 linear feet), a portion of North Atlantic Avenue (not
paved/948 linear feet), and Dutch Street (not paved/785 linear feet). As with
other unpaved right-of-ways within the city, streets will be improved upon the
request of those property owners served by a respective right-of-way. There is
a landowner cost share associated with this process. Each street will be
addressed independently upon request of said property owners. Upon annexation,
property owners along North Lord Street, Dutch Street, and North Atlantic
Avenue may request improved road service through the City of Southport Board of
Aldermen.
Within the city’s primary corporate limits, there are streetlights located
along city-maintained right-of-ways at an approximate rate of one light per 500
linear feet. In order to maintain this standard within the annexation area, the
installation of an additional ten (10) streetlights will be required. The
installation of one streetlight is estimated to cost $1,200, resulting in a
total cost of $12,000. The city contracts with Brunswick Electric Membership
Corporation for the installation of all new streetlights, and will utilize
these services to install all required lighting proposed within this report.
2.   Electric Service
The City of Southport provides electric service through its Public Services
Department, and is responsible for the maintenance of all transmission lines
and service connections. Electric service is provided on the basis of
districts, and most of the properties located within the proposed annexation
area are currently served by the city’s system. Due to this fact, no impact
regarding either expenditures or revenues is anticipated as a result of the
proposed annexation.
3.   Water Service
As discussed within the revenue summary portion of this report, all properties
within the proposed annexation area are currently served by either the county
or the city water systems. It has been noted that a reduction in water sales
revenue is anticipated as a result of this annexation process; however, no
additional expenditures are anticipated to provide public water to the proposed
annexation area. The city’s public services department will continue to provide
maintenance to this portion of the water system at current staffing and budget
levels.
4.   Sewer Service
A detailed account of current sewer service within the annexation area was
discussed within the revenue section of this report. Additionally, Map 3,
Appendix I, provides an account of where infrastructure services are available.
The Board of Aldermen will provide central sewer service consistent with the
city’s sewer service policies.
Installation of all required sewer improvements will be installed in
conjunction with the capital project proposed by the city to connect its city-
wide sewer system to BrunswickCounty. The city is currently in the planning
stages of a project to reverse the flow of wastewater to the Brunswick County
Public Utilities treatment system. By mandate from the North Carolina
Department of Environment and Natural Resources, the city must close its
existing wastewater treatment plant no later than November of 2011. In order to
comply with this mandate, the city has negotiated with Brunswick County to
accomplish a flow reversal project that will facilitate closure of the city
plant and connect the city system to the Brunswick County system.
The proposed project involves running a force main from the existing system to
a point of connection to the county’s system along NC 211 in the vicinity of
St. James. This project will involve the installation of transmission lines and
a large pump station to be located on property across N. Howe Street from the
current Wal-Mart property. The cost of this project is estimated to be $4.5
million dollars. This project and expenses associated with it will not be
considered a factor regarding this annexation report because the connection to
the county system will occur with or without annexation. It should also be
noted that city has received a $3 million dollar grant from the Clean Water
Management Trust fund to assist in the planning and development of this
substantial capital improvements effort.
The city will complete the connection to the county system by the end of 2010.
The proposed pump station and transmission lines associated with this system
will assist in providing ready access to a large portion of the proposed
annexation area. In order to address the remainder of the properties currently
not served, the city will need to acquire one pump station. The required pump
station may be acquired from Wal-Mart, and is already in place and functional.
The estimated cost of taking over this pump station and upgrading the facility
to required standards will be approximately $50,000.
Once these sewer improvements have been established, the only other improvement
required to provide the entire annexation area with central sewer service is
collection lines. The city estimates that the impact fee revenue outlined in
the previous section of the report will cover a substantial portion of this
cost, assuming service is extended to the entire annexation area. Any cost
balance will be paid out of the City of Southport Water and Sewer Fund.
Construction contracts on required lines must be let and construction begin
within one year after the effective date of annexation, and the City will so
comply. Lines will be constructed in accordance with current city policies for
sewer services.
The city maintains an independent water and sewer fund that will serve to
finance any required improvements required as a result of the proposed
annexation. Additionally, the city currently has adequate sewer capacity to
support additional connections that will result from annexation. Connection of
the city to the county sewer system in 2010 will ensure adequate sewer
capacity. The annexation is expected to have a minimal impact on demand with
respect to the water or wastewater treatment systems.
5.   Sanitation
Sanitation curbside solid waste removal services will be provided in accordance
with Section IIIF, outlined above. There is not expected to be any impact on
revenues or expenditures relating to these services. The city will continue to
provide curbside yard waste and recycling services (currently contracted with
Waste Industries). Brunswick County will continue to provide weekly curbside
solid waste pickup services.
E.   Fire Department
The City of Southport Volunteer Fire Department currently serves the city as
well as a surrounding Fire Protection Service District established through
Brunswick County. The fire department is funded by a fire fee collected by the
county, and disbursed among the county’s defined fire districts. The fee is
calculated based on the type of use and size of a particular property.
The Southport Volunteer Fire Department will continue to serve the annexed area
in the same capacity as it served prior to annexation. Property owners will
continue to pay the same fire fee as they paid prior to annexation. There will
be no change in the level of service provided or the cost of providing/
receiving service. There are no rural fire departments currently providing
service within the proposed annexation area.
According to the Insurance Services Office of North Carolina, the current fire
insurance classification of the area served by the Southport Volunteer Fire
Department is 4, conditioned upon the property being located within 1,000 feet
of a fire hydrant.
The area to be annexed is currently served by the Southport Volunteer Fire
Department, and is located within 1,000 feet of a fire hydrant. There will be
no change in fire insurance rates or services as a result of annexation.
F.   Parks and Recreation
The City of Southport maintains six parks.
Waterfront Park, located on Bay Street between Howe and Davis Streets, is a 1-
acre park overlooking the Cape Fear River. The park has a public fishing pier,
shelters, benches, picnic tables, water fountains, swings, lights, and
walkways.
Lowe-White Memorial Park, located on the corner of Leonard Street and Willis
Drive, is a 1.5-acre park with plans for renovation. Plans for renovation
include a playground, a walking track, 2 tennis courts, and restrooms.
Franklin Square Park is located off Howe Street between Nash and West Streets.
The 1-acre park has a large gazebo and stage, a small playground, park benches,
and picnic tables.
Keziah Park is located on the corner of Moore and Lord Streets. The 1/4-acre
park is best known for its Indian Trail Tree and is used for picnicking and
passive activities.
Alvin C. Caviness Park is located on Owens Street between Clarendon Street and
Caswell Avenue. The 3/4-acre park has one full and one half court basketball
arena and children’s playground equipment. Stevens Park is located in the
city’s ETJ on 9th Street. This is a 7-acre property which is being cleared for
a ball field.
In addition to the parks mentioned above, the city maintains an Art Gallery, a
City Gym , the community center, a city dock, a multi-purpose building (Jaycee
Building), a Senior Citizens Center (located behind the Jaycee Building), a
visitor center (located adjacent to Keziah Park), and Fort Johnston, which is
used as a multi-purpose building. The park services outlined above are all
available for use to city residents and visitors free of charge. The City of
Southport maintains a proactive parks and recreation department, and will
continue to research new recreational opportunities. The proposed annexation is
not expected to have any impact on revenues or expenditures regarding the
provision of recreational services.
G.   Planning and Building Inspections
The mission of the Planning Department is (1) to work with the City Manager and
the City Board of Aldermen to plan for the growth and evolution of the city;
(2) to manage the land use controls (land use plan, zoning code, subdivision
code, sign code, etc.); (3) to promote the health, safety, and welfare of
property owners and the general public through effective building code
inspections; (4) to assure the efficient communication between zoning and
inspection activities through vigorous code enforcement; and (5) to support the
activities of the city's Planning Board and Board of Adjustment.
The Building Inspection Services Department is charged with providing
inspection services, plan review and customer service to every architect,
engineer, developer, contractor, business and property owner that resides or
works within the City of Southport. The Building Inspection Services Department
is responsible for ensuring safety and the safeguard of property through the
enforcement of the North Carolina Building Code, Plumbing Code, Mechanical
Code, Electrical Code, and Fire Code.
Before commencing construction, repair or making any alterations, property
owners must confer with the Planning and Building Inspections Department to
make certain that the project conforms to current building and zoning codes and
that the proper permits are obtained. Thus, there will be no impact on
development standards or staffing levels for the Planning and Inspections
department.

APRIL 27, 2009
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING
APRIL 27, 2009    6:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen James Brown, Donnie Potter, Nelson Adams, Ed Boguskie
            and Jwantana Frink
ABSENT:         Alderman Paul Fisher
STAFF PRESENT:       Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
I.
Call to Order – 6:00 p.m.
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m.
II.
Invocation
Alderman Brown pronounced the invocation.
III.
Purpose of Meeting
Mayor Spencer announced the purpose of the Special Meeting was to discuss the
Maritime Museum. She asked Aldermen Boguskie and Frink for an update on the
meeting held with the Friends of the Museum and representatives from the
Department of Cultural Resources on April 16.
Aldermen Boguskie, Frink and the City Manager briefed the Board on the meeting:
·   Museum will stay open through September
·   Discussed location of Museum, where it could and should be located
·   Thirty-day notice to get logistics in order to prepare for closing.
·   Looking at concession agreement for the other barrack on Moore Street
·   Talked about options, if the Landlord would lower the rent and have a plan
in place.
·   Time is limited, Department of Cultural Resources looking for assistance
from the City. They are seeking options and solutions because the State does
not have the money. Department of Cultural Resources budget will be reduced by
33% in fiscal year 09-10. Paying $65,000 in rent is not an option.
·   Mr. Thornton stated there is not sufficient time to provide another option
because staff was told that the Museum would close in September. He explained
the importance of the Museum to Southport's economic survival. The City asked
for a commitment by the State to develop a long-range plan for the Maritime
Museum existence in Southport, but Cultural Resources staff could not guarantee
anything because of the financial condition of the State. They all agreed that
the solution presented is not the best, but a viable option to continue
operating the Museum. The State does not have the money to purchase property
and construct a new Museum. However, the Board should continue to push for this
when the economic situation improves.
·   Alderman Frink communicated that the State's major concern is paying rent,
which has not been discussed in detail.
Alderman Adams stated the Maritime Committee has not approached Mr. Harrelson
about negotiating the rent and he is amenable to negotiation, if the Museum
staff wishes to remain in their existing location. He stated the Maritime
Committee should be given the opportunity to talk with Mr. Harrelson.
Mayor Spencer stated that she spoke with Mr. Harrelson and he indicated a
willingness to reduce the rent with the City paying $30,000 and the County
$30,000. She also spoke with the Chairman of the County Commissioners about
funding for the Museum and was told the request would be considered in their
budget deliberations.
Alderman Adams stated the City would possibly have some available funds and
vacant buildings. It is his belief that these options should be explored. If
the City can help the Museum to remain in place for one year, this will give
the Board sufficient time to explore other options.
Alderman Brown stated he wished to explore other options and to seek funding to
assist with rent. Once the fire station is constructed, it will leave a vacant
building, which is a more suitable location for the museum.
Mayor Spencer stated that the City wants the Museum to remain open and the
Board is exploring every available option to assist.
Alderman Boguskie restated the time constraint and encouraged the Board to make
a decision because of the thirty-day time period.
Alderman Potter stated the immediate need of the Museum should be addressed. He
does not deem it a problem leasing another barrack to the Maritime Museum,
since they already have a concession agreement for one. The renovations and
expansion will save the City money in maintenance and upkeep. It appears the
only choice is to find a location or assist in the payment of rent. He stated
his support of Parks and Recreation and the Museum, but the Board needs to make
a decision.
Alderman Frink reiterated that she does not want the Museum to close; however,
as a member of the Parks and Recreation Committee she stated that they had not
been invited to the table to discuss this matter with the various factions. No
one on the Parks and Recreation Committee wants to see the Museum closed.
After discussion, Board consensus was that the Maritime Committee appointed by
the Mayor meet and bring a recommendation to the Board no later than Tuesday,
May 12, 2009 at a Special Meeting.
Alderman Potter motioned, seconded by Alderman Adams that the Maritime Museum
Committee meet with the necessary parties and make a decision prior to the May
14 regular Board meeting, and to place this item on the Board's agenda for a
vote. The vote of approval was unanimous.

Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor

The vote of approval was unanimous.
RESOLUTION OF SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN AMENDING SEWER POLICY FOR PROPERTIES
ANNEXED INTO THE CITY BY CITY-INITIATED ANNEXATIONS
BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that Section 1 of the sewer
policy for properties annexed into the city by city-initiated annexations
adopted on March 12, 2009, is hereby amended to read as follows:
1.   Any improved property which is annexed into the City of Southport by a
city-initiated annexation proceeding and which is already connected to a
private wastewater disposal system on the effective date of said annexation
shall be allowed to continue to utilize a currently functioning and permitted
private wastewater disposal system until such time as the first of the
following events occur: (i) the private wastewater disposal system fails, or
(ii) the use of property changes to a use which would require significant
modification of the existing private system, or (iii) the ownership of the
property changes, provided, however, that a transfer of ownership by conveyance
or operation of law without consideration to immediate family members shall not
be deemed to be a change of ownership under this provision, or (iv) any
environmental issue arises resulting in a determination of private wastewater
disposal system closure by the State of North Carolina, federal government or
Brunswick County. Upon the occurrence of the first of said events, the City
shall notify the property owner and said property shall be connected to the
city sewer within 60 days from notification by City that connection is
required. Connection shall be made in accordance with the City’s policies and
ordinances existing at the time of connection, and the property owner shall pay
all charges and fees in effect at said time except as otherwise provided
herein. Notwithstanding the above, nothing herein shall be construed to require
mandatory connection to the city system for a private wastewater disposal
system which is functioning and permitted on the effective date of a city-
initiated annexation for routine repair and maintenance which does not involve
significant modifications or improvements to the existing system as determined
by the appropriate permitting agency or authority.
Adopted May 14, 2009.

h)    Consideration of Resolution opposing the transfer of all State Secondary
Roads within Municipal Boundaries from the State to Local Governments
Alderman Fisher motioned, seconded by Alderman Frink to approve the following
Resolution, vote was unanimous.
RESOLUTION OPPOSING THE TRANSFER OF ALL STATE SECONDARY ROADS WITHIN MUNICIPAL
BOUNDARIES FROM THE STATE TO LOCAL GOVERNMENTS
WHEREAS, the State of North Carolina's rapid growth has placed an increased
strain on the State's current transportation infrastructure; and that growth is
expected to continue with North Carolina projected to have more than 12 million
residents by 2030; and
WHEREAS, due to the increases in construction costs for steel, concrete, and
asphalt, the North Carolina Department of Transportation has experienced a
significant funding shortfall over the past several years; and
WHEREAS, the North Carolina Department of Transportation has identified a $64
billion funding shortfall in regards to statewide transportation needs through
the year 2030 and additional funding sources are needed to construct important
local, regional and statewide transportation projects; and
WHEREAS, traditional transportation funding sources have proved inadequate to
address the multi-modal transportation needs of the State, especially highways,
transit, rail, bicycle, and pedestrian facilities as well as the safety and
economic development needed in rural areas; and
WHEREAS, current Powell Bill funding allocations to municipalities is
inadequate to address current municipal street maintenance and construction
needs; and
WHEREAS, the 2007 North Carolina General Assembly established the 21ST Century
Transportation Committee to study the transportation infrastructure needs of
the State; and
WHEREAS, the 21ST Century Transportation Committee was asked to report on
several important topics related to addressing these challenges, including
innovative funding methods, local funding options, urban congestion relief, the
division of transportation infrastructure between State and local governments,
multi-modal needs, and energy conservation with its report due on or before
December 31, 2008.
NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that the City of Southport urge the Governor and
the North Carolina General Assembly to consider the following:
The current process for transferring roads from the State to local governments
through mutually approved street and highway system responsibility agreements
that recognize the relative importance of all roadways --- not just state and
federal highways --- to the integrity of the major thoroughfare system works
well and should be maintained with enhancements as may be deemed beneficial.
Any wholesale unilateral transfer of all state secondary roads within
municipalities from the state to local governments is contrary to this
principle, would result in denigration of the roadway network in North
Carolina, and is strongly opposed. Any transference of maintenance and
construction responsibilities for highways or secondary roads from the State to
the local governments must provide continuing dependable funding sources for
those roadways at a level acceptable to local governments, including at a
minimum, adequate reimbursement schedules based on roadway lane-miles rather
than center-line miles.
ADOPTED, the 14th day of May 2009 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
/s/Regina W. Alexander, MMC
City Clerk
