MAY 21, 2009
BUDGET WORK SESSION
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN BUDGET WORK SESSION
MAY 21, 2009      9:00 A.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Mayor Sandra P. Spencer
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, James Brown, Ed Boguskie,
            Jwantana Frink and Paul Fisher
ABSENT:         Donnie Potter
STAFF PRESENT:       Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina Alexander, City Clerk
            Patty Miller, Finance Officer
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order at 9:10 a.m.
Alderman Brown delivered the invocation.
City Manager Thornton presented the proposed budget for FY 2010-2011. City
Manager Thornton discussed the revenue projections. He stated the sales tax is
projected to come in at 5%-6% lower this year. The projected tax collection
rate is 95% based on an estimated valuation of $912,693,227 with an $.18 tax
rate. He explained that the budget:
·   Maintains the current level of services
·   Includes a Capital Improvement Plan
·   Vehicle replacement program to lease purchase vehicles for the Police
Department.
·   2% cost of living adjustment for employees.
·   Electric Fund Budget - City purchase makes up larger percentage of the
electric fund budget i.e. operation and maintenance with BEMC. Salaries are
proportional on a cost-sharing basis.
The Board discussed the following matters:
·   Alderman Fisher recommended the Automatic Meter Reading Program be included
in the budget.
·   Alderman Fisher and Brown asked about the donation to Southport Primary
School. Alderman Frink requested South Brunswick Middle and High Schools be
considered.
·   Alderman Frink asked about the accommodations tax. City Manager Thornton
stated that he reviewed the local bill and the Board by Resolution can effect
this change. Alderman Fisher differed in opinion stating that a Commission
would have to be established in order to increase the accommodations tax. City
Manager Thornton stated he would clarify this matter with the City Attorney.
·   Alderman Adams recommended asking Progress Energy to increase their
monetary donation to the City. He stated that the City is in the process of
building a modernized fire station with updated technology and a command center
for the benefit of everyone, including Progress Energy. City Manager Thornton
stated that he would check into this; however, he did not balance the budget
based on anticipated donations. Alderman Brown and Boguskie agreed that the
City should ask for an increase; however, the Board is cognizant of the
projects that Progress Energy has constructed and donated around the City.
·   Mayor Spencer asked about providing yard debris cans to new residents. The
finance officer stated that this service has been discontinued, but yard debris
can be placed in large trash bags and placed curbside.
·   Alderman Fisher asked a question about Rescue Squad expenditures  vs
 revenues. He stated whatever monies are received from billing should offset
volunteer fees. City Manager Thornton stated that he is seeking to modify some
of the calls being responded to by the Rescue personnel and if some of the
calls are appropriate or necessary. He stated that he spoke with the County's
Emergency Management Director and Chief Cumbee about this matter. Alderman
Fisher stated if the Rescue Squad is transporting patients, this is good
because of their prior history with response time.
·   Alderman Fisher encouraged the Board to consider renting the Garrison
House, which would generate revenue.
·   The Board agreed if the City is going to repair the City dock, fees should
be increased. City Manager Thornton stated monies are included to enlarge the
dredging area, electrical upgrades and repairs. He suggested fees be increased
after repairs and upgrades are made to the facilities.
·   Alderman Fisher stated that he would like to see the Boardwalk project re-
submitted. City Manager stated staff has been talking with a local architect to
look at the Bay Street/Yacht Basin area to improve the overall appearance i.e.
Ft. Johnston Boardwalk. He will need additional discussion on a streetscape
design and involve the residents, property and business owners in that locale.
·   The upkeep of Northwood Cemetery was mentioned and the Manager stated funds
are included in the budget.
·   Christmas tree and lighting was discussed for Bay Street
·   Alderman Adams (general fund) asked about the $75,000 budgeted in Code
Enforcement for office building. He does not see the need to expend the monies
with departments being shifted and buildings becoming available.
·   It was noted that funds are in the budget for software and computer
upgrades
·   Alderman Adams requested another road be paved in Northwood Cemetery. Mr.
Thornton advised that Powell Bill Funds could not be used.
·   A part time worker was recommended for Buildings and Grounds for the
summer.
·   Alderman Adams asked about the accrual of vacation, stating that new hires
only get 3.3 hours per month and this needs to be reviewed.
·   Caswell Avenue was discussed as a connector road for the benefit of the
community. City Manager Thornton stated this is something that can be
considered under the Capital Improvement Program. The Board discussed
prioritizing streets, i.e. sidewalks, all city streets paved before re-
surfacing.
Aldermen Fisher and Brown stated the Board made a commitment to the primary
school to consider a donation during budget deliberation. Alderman Frink asked
that the other schools be considered. City Manager Thornton told the Board that
the schools are getting stimulus monies to help offset their budget. He stated
the first payment for the Fire Department and Sewer Reversal Project will begin
in 2010-11 and asked the Board to be cautious when considering large donations,
which will affect the budget by reducing expenditures in other areas.
Alderman Fisher suggested waiting until the first quarter revenues are received
and determine at that time if the City can donate funds to the school. If the
City donates money, it should be earmarked for school supplies only.
Insurance: It was noted that health insurance is a major expense at $610 p/mo
for each employee, retirees and Board members. Some of the Board members stated
that their primary insurance is equivalent to the City benefits through Cigna
and they get no additional coverage. City Manager Thornton stated staff could
talk with individual Board members and if the City's insurance is not a benefit
to them, they may elect to discontinue the coverage. Mayor Spencer suggested
additional information be compiled. Alderman Fisher suggested an insurance
workshop.
Powell Bill: Revenues down due to gas tax. City Manager recommended resurfacing
some City streets.
Electric Department: No abundance of revenue to offset anticipated
expenditures. 17% increase from NCEMPA this year. City increased the base rate
and looked at ways to increase fees i.e. conducting load management audits,
increased pole fees. Revenues in the budget are based upon underground service
from anticipated projects. City Manager Thornton stated that he would like to
start the automated meter-reading program and hire an Assistant Utility
Services Director working in the Electric Department to understand the workings
of the electric system whenever the monies are available. They also discussed
line lost, under grounding, the cost of meters new vs. refurbished, and the
cost to implement the automatic reading program i.e. software and training.
Alderman Fisher stated the plan was to increase rates and build the fund
balance to offset capital improvement for automatic meter reading. He
recommended that this program be implemented in FY 2010-11 by taking $200,000
from fund balance. City Manager Thornton stated the substation cost came in
lower than expected and some of those funds can be used towards the automatic
meter-reading program.
Mayor Spencer stated if the fund balance is available, this is the year to
implement the program. City Manager Thornton stated the money is available in
fund balance and revenues may exceed expenditures this year. It was Board
consensus to implement the automatic meter-reading program in FY 2010-2011. The
Manager stated that he would provide a revised budget with this change.
Water and Sewer Fund: Revenues and expenditures balance. Closure of sewer plant
will not take place in this fiscal year. Water tank contribution will need to
be increased because of DWQ rule requiring that the City have one-half of the
maximum amounts of daily distribution in storage. Board discussed operators
being licensed and proper certification. City Manager stated overtime has been
monitored and only in necessary circumstances.
Capital Improvement Plan: City Manager Thornton stated that the automated meter
reader will be placed in the CIP program. Alderman Fisher asked about the
Public Works Building, and the Parks and Recreation Complex i.e. gym. Mayor
Spencer stated that she received a proposal for suggested improvements at the
Waterfront Park. City Manager Thornton stated he would give the suggestions to
the Parks and Recreation Director to explore.
Mosquito Spraying: Alderman Adams stated the City does not need to purchase a
new truck but request to see the equipment operable. City Manager Thornton
recommended that he explore working with the County because they will provide
this service at no cost in addition to insuring that the City's mosquito
spraying system is operable.
Adjournment – 12:17 p.m.
No further discussion, Alderman Brown motioned for adjournment, seconded by
Alderman Boguskie, vote carried.

Mr. Robert Howard of 114 N. Atlantic Avenue, expressed concern regarding the
sixty-five (65) year Agreement entered into by the City of Southport and
Progress Energy during the annexation process. He stated in approving the
Agreement, the City has waived the right to zone or include Progress Energy's
property in the City's Land Use Ordinances, including future use of the
property. Progress Energy will not pay ad valorem taxes or personal property
taxes. He stated the Board of Aldermen agreed without conditions to oppose
efforts by the N.C. General Assembly and any other entity including the courts
to annex properties owned by Progress Energy into Southport regardless to what
they propose to use the land for within the sixty-five year period. He
explained that the City further agreed to seek that legislation be enacted and
made into law that authorizes, ratifies and makes the Agreement and its terms
enforceable and binding. Mr. Howard stated if the Board did not act
immediately, the Bill would be enacted into law and the only way that it can be
removed is if the Board of Aldermen adopts a resolution requesting
Representative Stiller and Senator R.C. Soles to remove the Bill from the final
reading. However, the Board signed the Agreement; agreeing that they would not
do this. If the Board rescinds its action, the City may be subject to a
lawsuit. The Board should do what is necessary to instruct legislative
representatives to remove the Bill from the House, reconsider its position, and
adopt a resolution opposing this Bill. (SB 315 and HB 347)

VIII.
Public Hearing
a)    City of Southport 2009-2010 Proposed Budget
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Frink to enter Public Hearing,
the vote was unanimous.
There were no citizens wishing to speak on the budget. Alderman Brown moved,
seconded by Alderman Boguskie to close the Hearing and to re-enter regular
session, the vote was unanimous.
IX.
New Business
a)    Adoption of FY 2009-2010 Annual Budget
City Manager Thornton explained that the budget provides for no tax increase,
the schedule of fees remains the same i.e. electric, water and sewer rates. The
Automatic Meter Reading program has been included in the budget. The level of
services will be provided.
City Manager Thornton explained, per request of Alderman Adams, that the Board
had expressed a desire to provide some funding to Southport Elementary School.
He projected ABC revenues in the budget; however, once the revenues are
received and if there is an overage of what is projected in the budget, the
Board will make a decision to provide some funding to Southport Elementary
School.
Alderman Fisher stated that it was his understanding that the proceeds would be
reviewed quarterly. City Manager Thornton stated as the monies come in
quarterly, that he would provide the information to the Board.
The Board commended the City Manager and staff on the budget.
Alderman Fisher asked that the Capital Improvement Plan  include non-funded
projects in order to plan for the future, i.e. fire sub-station, Park Avenue
Extension, road joining Leonard Street to Highway 87 for the east side of the
City, new public service area and location, extension of the Community Building
and board walk.
Alderman Brown motioned, seconded by Alderman Fisher to adopt the Budget for FY
2009-2010. Discussion: Alderman Boguskie asked about the funding for the
Automatic Meter Reading (AMR) program. Mr. Thornton stated monies would come
from the Enterprise Fund (Electric Fund Balance). He also asked about property
at Rivermist, it was explained that the City was in negotiation with the
developer, but since this time, ownership has changed. The vote of approval was
unanimous. 2009-2010 Budget adopted.

SECTION VI
TAX RATE ESTABLISHED
An Ad Valorem rate of eighteen (.18) cents per $100.00 full valuation is hereby
established as the official tax rate for the City of Southport for the fiscal
year 2009-2010. This is based on an estimated valuation of approximately
$912,693,227 with an estimated collection rate of ninety-five percent (95.00%).
SECTION VII
SPECIAL AUTHORIZATION - BUDGET OFFICER
The Budget Officer shall be authorized to reallocate departmental
appropriations among the various objects of expenditure and interdepartmental
transfers as said officer believes necessary. The Budget Officer shall be
authorized to effect inter-fund transfers, not to exceed $1,500.00. Notation of
such reallocation and transfers shall be made to the Board on the next
succeeding financial report.
SECTION VIII
RESTRICTION - BUDGET OFFICER
The inter-fund transfer of monies exceeding $1,500.00 shall be accomplished by
Board authorization only. The utilization of any contingency appropriation
shall be accomplished only with Board authorization.
SECTION IX
UTILIZATION OF BUDGET & BUDGET ORDINANCE
This Ordinance and the Budget Document shall be the basis of the financial plan
for the City of Southport municipal government during the 2009-2010 Fiscal
Year. The Budget Officer shall administer the budget and shall ensure that
operation officials are provided guidance and sufficient details to implement
their appropriate portion of the Budget. The accounting section shall establish
records that are in agreement with the budget and this ordinance and the
appropriate statues of the State of North Carolina.
Copies of the Budget Ordinance shall be furnished to the Finance Director and
the City Manager of the City of Southport, to be kept on file by them for their
direction in the disbursement of funds.
SECTION X
ADOPTION
Copies of this Budget Ordinance shall be furnished to all appropriate officials
of the municipality and kept on file for the proper recordation of receipts and
disbursement of funds.
All passed by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport upon proper motion
of Alderman James Brown, seconded by Alderman Paul Fisher. This 11 June 2009.
The vote of the Board was recorded, as six yes, zero no with none absent.

b)   Consideration of Resolution Authorizing Lease of City Property and
Concession Agreement
City Manager Thornton presented the Resolution authorizing lease of City
property (Davis and Moore Street Apartments) and upon adoption of the
resolution; it authorizes the City Manager to lease the property. The
Concession Agreement for the North Carolina Museum at Southport.
Alderman Fisher recommended the word " same term " be changed to "renewable by
mutual agreement of both parties hereto."
Alderman Boguskie motioned to adopt the Resolution Authorizing Lease of City
Property as amended , seconded by Alderman Potter. Discussion:  Alderman Fisher
stated it was his understanding that the Sr. Citizens' Building was to be
available by June 30, but there is some discussion that the Pottery Studio was
not informed of this move, at the present time, they do not have a place to
relocate. City Manager Thornton stated in discussion with Heather Hemphill,
Parks and Recreation Director, at this time, the Parks and Recreation
Department with its current level of programs, do not have the need to utilize
the rear of the Sr. Building. He stated that he requested Ms. Kimberly Caroon
to provide him with a schedule showing when the Pottery Studio anticipates
their move to college annex, realizing that they are behind schedule with the
facility.(Southport Annex) Alderman Adams stated that Parks and Recreation
should be prepared to start expanding its programs and utilize the entire
building. City operations should not be stifled to accommodate other programs.
City Manager stated that there is no formal agreement with Brunswick Community
College to provide the Pottery Studio a place to operate, but the City has no
current plans to ask them to relocate. Mr. Thornton advised that they were made
aware of the possible move. Ms. Hemphill stated that they would be moving
within this fiscal year. No further discussion on the motion, the vote of
approval was six ayes, no opposition. (Unanimous)
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING LEASE OF CITY PROPERTY
WHEREAS, the City of Southport owns the Ft. Johnston Davis Street barracks
which site the Board finds is currently surplus to the city’s needs; and
WHEREAS, the City and the N. C. Department of Cultural Resources have agreed
upon a lease under which the N. C. Department of Cultural Resources will lease
the City’s property described above for a term of 2 years beginning July 1,
2009; and
WHEREAS, in consideration of leasing this property, the N. C. Department of
Cultural Resources has agreed to pay the sum of $1 per year and to make all
necessary improvements, additions and alterations to the property and be
responsible for all repairs, maintenance, insurance and expenses; and
WHEREAS, N. C. G. S. 160A-272 authorizes the City to enter into leases of up to
10 years upon resolution of the Board of Aldermen adopted at a regular meeting
after 10 days public notice; and
WHEREAS, the required notice has been published and the Board is convened in a
regular meeting;
NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN RESOLVES that the Board hereby approves
the lease of the city property described above to the N. C. Department of
Cultural Resources for 2 years and directs the City Manager to execute any
instruments necessary to the lease.
Adopted June 11, 2009.
City of Southport
By:
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer
Mayor

CONCESSION AGREEMENT
THIS CONCESSION AGREEMENT is entered into this 11th day of June, 2009 by and
between the CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA (City), whose address is 201 East
Moore Street, Southport, North Carolina 28461, and the NORTH CAROLINA
DEPARTMENT OF CULTURAL RESOURCES operating as the NORTH CAROLINA MARITIME
MUSEUM-SOUTHPORT, (“NCMMS”), Division of State History Museums, Office of
Archives of History, whose address is 4605 Mail Service Center, Raleigh North
Carolina 27699-4605.
WHEREAS, on August 30th, 2006, the United States of America, acting by and
through the Southeast Regional Director, National Park Service, under and
pursuant to the power and authority contained in the provisions of the Federal
Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (63 Stat. 377), as amended,
and particularly as amended by Public Law 485, 91st Congress, and regulations
and orders promulgated thereunder, conveyed by quitclaim deed (“the Quitclaim
Deed”) to the City, its successors and assigns, subject to certain
reservations, exceptions, restrictions, conditions and covenants contained in
the Quitclaim Deed, all of its right, title and interest in and to that certain
land and improvements therein described in the deed recorded in Deed Book 2634
, Page 0269, Brunswick County Register of Deeds Office, a copy of which is
attached hereto as Exhibit “A” and made a part hereof; and
WHEREAS, the Quitclaim Deed requires that the Property be used and maintained
for public purposes and that the City conform to certain requirements with
respect to the Property contained in the Quitclaim Deed; and
WHEREAS, the NCMMS desires to use a portion of the Property for programming
consistent with the terms of said quitclaim deed;
NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the mutual terms, covenants and
conditions contained herein, and other good and valuable consideration, the
receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, it is mutually agreed
between the City and the NCMMS as follows:
1.   RECITALS . The above recitations are true and correct.
2.   TERM . The City agrees to grant an exclusive Concession Agreement for the
use of the Property commonly referred to as 103-B Davis Street across from the
Southport City Hall for the purposes set forth herein, consistent with the
provisions of the Quitclaim Deed, for a two (2) year term beginning July 1,
2009, renewable by mutual agreement of both parties hereto upon terms and
conditions to be agreed upon for up to four additional two year terms, all
subject to the right of termination contained herein. This agreement shall
automatically be renewed unless either party gives the other party 60 days
written notice of its intent not to renew in which case this agreement shall
terminate at the end of the then existing term. The parties hereto acknowledge
that the term of this Concession Agreement is subject to the legal authority of
the City of Southport to enter into an agreement of such term and duration as
set forth herein; in the event that a court of competent jurisdiction should
determine that the authority of the City is exceeded, then the terms of this
Agreement shall be rendered null and void, in which event the NCMMS shall have
no claim for damages or recourse against the City.
3.   RESTRICTIONS . No interest in the Property is conveyed hereunder that
would violate any of the provisions of the Quitclaim Deed. Where the terms
herein conflict with those contained in the Quitclaim Deed, those in the
Quitclaim Deed shall govern.
4.   NO AGENCY . Services performed by the NCMMS hereunder shall be at no cost
to the City. The NCMMS shall not have the power or right to obligate the City
in any respect for any purpose without the prior written approval of the City.
5.   RENT; UTILITIES . The NCMMS shall pay to the City $1.00 (One Dollar) per
year as rent which shall be paid on the date hereof and on or before each
anniversary date of this agreement. All rentals payable under this Concession
Agreement shall be paid to the City at 201 East Moore Street, Southport, North
Carolina, 28461, or such other address as may be designated in writing by City
to NCMMS. The NCMMS shall pay all utilities for the duration of the Concession
Agreement beginning on July 1 ,2009. The NCMMS shall maintain all utility
accounts in its own name and shall pay all charges and shall indemnify and hold
the City harmless against all utility expenses.
6.   MODIFICATIONS TO PREMISES. It is contemplated by the parties hereto that
NCMMS will renovate and refurbish the subject property. All modifications and
improvements shall conform to the provisions of the Quitclaim Deed and Section
106 of the National Historic Preservation Act and be approved by the North
Carolina Department of Cultural Resources, Historic Preservation Office, prior
to the beginning of said renovations. Any and all contractor’s or mechanic’s
liens placed upon the property as a result of work ordered by the NCMMS shall
be removed by NCMMS within thirty (30) days of the filing of such lien or liens
in the public records of Brunswick County, North Carolina. The NCMMS covenants
not to make any changes, alterations, or additions about the said building or
premises without first obtaining the written consent of the City and in no
event do anything that shall weaken or damage the building or structure now on
the premises.
7.   USE OF PREMISES . The NCMMS further covenants that the premises shall be
used only and exclusively for public use and any and all activities and
purposes reasonably related thereto, and no part of the premises shall be used
in any manner whatsoever in violation of the laws of the United States, the
State of North Carolina, or the ordinances and regulations of the City of
Southport or Brunswick County, including all federal, state and local laws and
regulations with reference to hazardous waste and environmental protection. To
the extent permitted by law, the NCMMS shall indemnify and hold the City
harmless for any such violation. It is understood and agreed that the NCMMS
shall be entitled to enter into sub-concession agreements with vendors and/or
providers who provide services and/or sell and/or exhibit items which are
consistent with the purposes of NCMMS and the City of Southport Parks and
Recreation Department. It is further agreed and understood, consistent with the
policy of the National Parks Service that all revenues generated on the subject
premises must be utilized on the subject property for additional development,
operation, and/or maintenance. Under no circumstances may revenues generated
from or upon the premises be utilized by the NCMMS for purposes which are
inconsistent with the terms and conditions of the Quitclaim Deed to the City of
Southport.
8.   USE OF THE PREMISES; CONTINUOUS OPERATION . After the renovation of the
subject property is completed, NCMMS agrees, as a material covenant to this
Concession Agreement, to operate the building as an extension of the Maritime
Museum and specifically as the North Carolina Maritime Museum at Southport and
to support the City of Southport Parks and Recreation programs continuously
(with the exception of holidays, weekends, and other normal closing dates) via
mutually agreed upon use of the leased premises. In the event that the NCMMS
fails to comply with this covenant, the City shall be entitled to terminate
this Concession Agreement by giving 60 (sixty) days written notice to the
NCMMS. NCMMS hereby agrees to and understands that no additional use of the
Fort Johnston property is implied nor agreed to in this Agreement. Use of any
property or space by the NCMMS outside of the Davis Street Apartment Building
located at 103-B Davis Street, must receive prior written approval from the
City of Southport.
9.   ACCOUNTINGS . The NCMMS shall deliver to the City annually, or at other
times within two (2) weeks of a written request of the City, an accounting of
its activities including financial records.
10.   ACCESS . The City and its authorized officers, agents and employees,
shall have access to the Property at reasonable times, and anytime in case of
an emergency.
11.   MAINTENANCE . The City of Southport shall be responsible for maintenance
of the Fort Johnston grounds. The NCMMS agrees to accept this leased facility
as is and the NCMMS is responsible for all other repairs and maintenance except
as specifically set forth herein.
12.   ADDITIONAL COVENANTS . The NCMMS further agrees that it shall be
obligated to:
a.   Keep the facilities clean at all times and free of hazardous plagues by
means of adequate extermination systems.
b.   Provide reasonable access to City inspection personnel and provide access
to the United States of America, and any representative it may so delegate,
including the right of entry upon the Property at any time to conduct
inspections.
c.   Use its best efforts to assure that its employees are persons of good
moral reputation, respectable and willing to provide the public a service of
excellence.
d.   Not place, or allow to be placed, temporary or permanent advertisements or
commercial propaganda in the facilities granted under this Concession
Agreement, except those necessary and convenient for the efficient operation of
its activities in accordance with its mission statement. Prior approval from
the City is required for the placement of any advertisement, commercial
propaganda or signage.
e.   As a State Agency, the NCMMS shall provide general liability insurance and
insurance on the contents owned by the NCMMS contained in the granted area of
the building.
f.   Operate the granted area competently, professionally, and in compliance
with the provisions of the Quitclaim Deed.
g.   In the operation of the Property, as well as in the employment or
contracting of services, the NCMMS shall observe federal norms prohibiting
discrimination under title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1969, as amended, and
the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. In other words, it shall abstain from
discriminating against any person or group due to its race, sex, color,
national origin, religion, political affiliation, or physical, mental, or
sensory disabilities.
13.   INDEMNITY . To the extent permitted by law, the NCMMS shall indemnify and
save and hold the City harmless from and against all liability, claims and
demands on account of personal injuries (including, without limitation of the
foregoing, workers’ compensation and death claims) or property loss or damage
of any kind whatsoever, which arise out of or are in any manner connected with,
or are claimed to arise out of or be in any manner connected with, the
operation of the Property by the NCMMS, or any agents or employees of the
NCMMS, pursuant to this Concession Agreement. The NCMMS shall not be
responsible for liability, claims or demands for personal injury, property loss
or damage unrelated to the performance of this Concession Agreement.
14.   DEFAULT . The NCMMS understands and agrees that its failure to comply
with any of the provisions of this Concession Agreement shall constitute an
event of default. The default shall exist at the time of the failure to comply
with the provisions of this Concession Agreement, whether or not either party
has notice. The NCMMS also understands and agrees that the City may elect, at
the City’s option, any single remedy or penalty or any combination of remedies
and penalties, as available.
15.   REGULATIONS . The NCMMS agrees to adhere to and comply with any and all
federal, state and local safety laws, regulations, and ordinances, including by
not limited to, all building and fire codes established to ensure safety of
occupants as well as secure the building prior to or during storm events. The
NCMMS shall within thirty (30) days of the completion of the renovation of the
property provide written copies of its safety policy statement regarding its
intent to assure compliance with the safety regulations and laws. If the plan
is not in compliance with the aforementioned federal, state and local safety
laws, regulations and ordinances, the NCMMS shall be given thirty (30) days to
produce a compliant safety policy and program. If the NCMMS fails to comply,
the City may terminate this Concession Agreement immediately.
16.   REMOVAL OF HAZARDS . The NCMMS shall be responsible for keeping the
Property clear, safe and free from hazards that could result in personal injury
or property damage and for reporting hazards to the City.
17.   TERMINATION PROVISION . In addition to any other termination provision
contained herein, the failure of the NCMMS to observe any of the provisions of
this Concession Agreement shall constitute a breach of the Concession Agreement
for which the City may terminate the Concession Agreement upon providing the
NCMMS (60) sixty days written notice. In addition, City may terminate this
Concession Agreement upon 60 days written notice in the event that the NCMMS
fails to adequately budget for or fund the operation of the museum or in the
event that the museum ceases operations for a period of 30 days or more. In the
event of termination pursuant to this section, City may take immediate
possession of the premises and NCMMS shall comply with its obligations set
forth in Section 18 below. The NCMMS shall be entitled to terminate this
Concession Agreement at any time upon giving 180 days written notice to the
City.
18.   END OF TERM . The NCMMS agrees at the end of any Concession Agreement
term, should no new Concession Agreement be reached between the parties, to
vacate the Property within (30) thirty days without any demand and without any
notice, removing all equipment of a temporary nature, necessary for the
operation of the NCMMS and leaving the property in as good a condition as it
was at the time of entry thereon by the NCMMS, except for reasonable use and
wear thereof, acts of God, or damage by casualties beyond the control of the
NCMMS, and on vacating shall leave the Property free and clean of all rubbish
and debris. If the NCMMS fails to perform its obligation set out herein, the
City has the option of doing so at the expense of the NCMMS and NCMMS agrees to
reimburse City for said expenses within 30 days of receipt of written demand
therefor.
19.   FUTURE AGREEMENTS . Any executory agreement hereafter made between the
parties hereto shall be ineffective in changing, modifying, or discharging this
Concession Agreement in whole or in part unless the executory agreement is in
writing and signed by the party against whom the enforcement of the change,
modification, or discharge is sought.
20.   DEED RESTRICTIONS . The NCMMS shall do nothing with respect to the
Property that would violate any of the provisions of the Quitclaim Deed, or
cause title to the Property to revert to the United States of America.
21.   CONDEMNATION . Should the building upon the leased premises be totally
destroyed by fire, condemnation, or other cause, or so damaged that rebuilding
or repairs cannot be completed within (1) one year from the date of the fire or
other cause of damage, this Concession Agreement shall terminate.
22.   CONTINGENCY . Neither party shall have any obligation under this
Concession Agreement until the consent contained below is duly executed by an
authorized agent of the United States of America, acting by and through the
Secretary of the Interior.
23.   EXECUTION OF LEGAL INSTRUMENTS . The NCMMS shall, at the request of the
City, execute all legal instruments necessary to permit the City to complete
any financial arrangements which may be required from time to time by lending
institutions wherein the leased premises are required to be used as collateral
for said financing, but NCMMS shall not be required to sign any instrument
which increases or decreases NCMMS’s obligations as set forth herein.
CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA
/s/ Sandra Spencer
BY: SANDRA SPENCER, MAYOR
/s/Regina W. Alexander

Resolution Authorizing the Disposition of Certain Personal Property by Private
Sale and Negotiation
Whereas, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport desires to dispose of
certain surplus property of the City of Southport; and
Whereas, said personal property is valued at less than $30,000 for any one item

X.
Other Business
a)   Power Point Presentation on Signs
City Manager Thornton explained that the purpose of the power point
presentation on signs is to discuss the illegal proliferation of signs in the
City. Staff is not advocating eliminating the signs; however, in accordance
with the existing City Code, the majority of the signs are illegal, which has
become an issue. Staff is trying to determine how to address the situation,
which has become a liability and is dangerous in public rights of way.
Amy Nelson, City Planner gave a power point presentation on illegal signs that
currently exist. She explained that some of the signs are a public safety issue
and signs in the City rights of way are illegal. She cited Section 17-3 noting
signs that are prohibited. Downtown Southport Inc. (DSI) is putting up a kiosk
at BB&T with a map that will list members with their location marked on the
map. She is currently doing research on off premise signs better known as way
finding signs which guide people to attractions, businesses, and points of
interest that are not on the main thoroughfare. She stated Moore and Howe
Streets are state maintained roads and the state does not allow signs on their
rights of way and will remove them. Staff is seeking ways to remove some of the
clutter while being aesthetically pleasing. Sandwich Board signs are legal, but
should be located on the person's property.
Alderman Fisher stated the City must be judicious in looking at this issue
because of the City's design. He stated that some homes are located in the City
rights of way. City Manager Thornton noted that this is a delicate issue and
the purpose of bringing this to the Board's attention is to let the public know
that there are restrictions currently in place.
Alderman Adams recommended a sign workshop. Alderman Potter suggested the
Planning Board continue with its study, the Board agreed by consensus.

Executive Session Minutes June 11, 2009
 
The City Attorney advised the Board of the status of the lawsuit with South
Brunswick Sanitary District particularly the City's motion for summary judgment
to be heard on June 29, 2009.
Attorney Isenberg advised that the City's annexation had been challenged. The
City has fifteen (15) days to respond; however, he would file an extension to
give staff sufficient time to pull together the documents. Attorney Isenberg
then reviewed several different alternatives, which the Board should consider
in defending this lawsuit, and he further advised the Board that he would
consult with them later after he had the opportunity to talk to the attorney
for the challenging parties.
Attorney Isenberg discussed the Progress Energy Agreement with the Board and
advised them as to the City's obligations under the Agreement. He advised the
Board that withdrawing their support for the local bills would be contrary to
the terms of the Agreement but he could not tell them at that time what
remedies Progress Energy might pursue.
The Board discussed the Agreement with the City Attorney and the possible
effect on its annexation if it would withdraw support for the local bills. The
members expressed a general desire not to bind future boards for 65 years.

JUNE 22, 2009
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
JUNE 22, 2009     4:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, NC
 
PRESENT:          Mayor Sandra P. Spencer
            Aldermen Nelson E. Adams, Donnie Potter, James Brown,
            Ed Boguskie, Jwantana Frink and Paul Fisher
ABSENT:         None
STAFF PRESENT:      M. Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, MMC, City Clerk
            Patty Miller, Finance Director
            Carter Hubard, Engineer, W.K. Dickson
I.
Call to Order – 4:00 p.m.
Mayor Spencer called the meeting to order at 4:06 p.m.
II.
Invocation
Alderman Boguskie pronounced the invocation.
III.
Purpose of Special Meeting
City Manager Thornton explained that the Clean Water Management Trust Fund
Board of Trustees requested that the City accept an amendment to reimburse the
Clean Water Management Trust Fund $1.686 million. These funds were designated
to purchase a 400-acre tract of land near Sunny Point for a spray irrigation
system for wastewater that was to be treated by the Brunswick Sanitary
District. The contract with SBSD was terminated and the City entered into an
Agreement with Brunswick County; therefore, plans changed. The land is not
being used for a spray field, but staff has been in negotiations with the
County for use of the site, but not within the timeframe originally proposed.
The City in June requested the Clean Water Management Trust Fund forgive the
debt, but that request has been denied. The City has made application for
stimulus monies for other projects, and if the $1.686 million is not repaid, it
will have a negative impact on additional funding. City Manager Thornton stated
Southport is in a good position to receive stimulus monies for other sewer/
water projects contingent upon the amendment being approved by the Board. The
amendment must be signed before consideration of the City's application. The
Clean Water Management Trust Board will meet with Construction Grants and Loans
on June 24 to discuss the City's project and make a decision on the potential
distribution of stimulus funds.
Alderman Fisher recommended waiting until July 1 before repaying the money.
Alderman Adams favored repaying the money and the City will own the land
without restrictions.
Mayor Spencer noted that the financial climate is different from the time the
grant was received.
Alderman Potter motioned, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to approve the amended
agreement to repay Clean Water Management Trust the $1.686 million. The votes
were five ayes , Aldermen Potter, Brown, Boguskie, Adams and Frink. One no
vote, Alderman Fisher. Motion passed.
IV.
Adjournment – 4:55 p.m.
No further business, Alderman Brown motioned to adjourn, seconded by Alderman
Potter. The vote was unanimous.
____________________________
Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
__________________________
Regina W. Alexander, MMC
City Clerk

SOUTHPORT, N. C.  7:30 P.M.

V.
Public Comments
Mr. John Elliott, Eastern Regional Manager for Progress Energy, expressed the
Company's disappointment with the decision made by the Board to breach its
annexation agreement . He stated that the Agreement was initiated by the City
of Southport. Based on Progress Energy's long-standing relationship with
Southport, they were supportive, responsive, and the arrangement was negotiated
in good faith to help Southport achieve its growth objectives. The company is
evaluating its options pertaining to Board action, and the City will be
notified when the company decides on a course of action. He stated that
Progress Energy would continue to work with the City to restore its
relationship, which is essential in a community with one of its largest
corporate citizens. He asked that the City repeal its Annexation Ordinance for
the Brunswick Nuclear Plant property, which will restore the collaborative
process that will lead to a consensus and long term decisions that will be
important to insure that everyone who has a stake in this issue are on board in
the process. In conclusion, he stated that the company's relationship with
Southport has been forged over decades and they remain committed to the
relationship.

Reports included in agenda packet.
VIII.
Public Presentations
a)    Center for Municipal Solutions – Rusty Monroe
Amy Nelson, City Planner introduced Mr. Rusty Monroe from the
telecommunications industry. She requested that he speak before the Board
because of an issue that came before the Planning Board concerning the City's
Telecommunications Ordinance. Ms. Nelson stated that changes are taking place
in the telecommunications industry and the City needs enhanced control over
what companies propose to do when they come in to provide a service. She stated
that Mr. Monroe travels the country educating local government on the future of
telecommunications.
Mr. Rusty Monroe, Founder and Owner of the Center for Municipal Solutions, told
the Board that he represents local governments in the regulation of cellular
towers and wireless facilities, which are becoming a frequent infrastructure
issue. He presented a power point presentation and stated a balance needs to be
reached with the industry, public sector, and the Cities in regards to revenue
and economic development. The location of towers is a technical issue with the
effects being visual in regards to location, sighting and construction of the
facilities. He stated within the next several years, 40,000 more towers and
wireless sites would be located in the State of North Carolina because of
wireless internet and high-speed data. He reviewed the City Ordinance and
recommended that it be updated to protect the City and to regulate towers.
Board members were given a copy of the Table of Contents from a model ordinance
that is being used in other areas.
b)    Brunswick Community College – Dr. Stephen Greiner
Dr. Stephen Greiner, President of Brunswick Community College, discussed plans
for an off campus center in Southport (Lord Street). He stated that the
Architect proposes to renovate sections of the existing historic building with
more square footage than if a new facility were constructed. The college will
offer off-campus courses in continuing education and regular curriculum and the
renovations will be made in phases.
John Thompson and Chris Lowman gave an overview by way of power point
presentation on the site plans and architecture design for renovation of the
Brunswick Community College Campus located at 717 North Lord Street.
In response to City Manager Thornton, Mr. Thompson stated the Arts and Crafts
building is in the first phase and the timeline for completion is eight to ten
months contingent upon acquiring the necessary documents.
Dr. Greiner stated in order to move beyond the design phase, Trustees of the
College asked their Attorney James Prevatte to work in a cooperative effort
with the City to insure zoning compliance and acquire a resolution to obtain
Caswell Avenue right of way. He explained that according to a structural
engineering report, the gymnasium is structurally sound and can be renovated in
another phase of the project when funds are available.
Alderman Adams questioned whether staff had informed Dr. Greiner that the City
is proposing to open Caswell Avenue. He reiterated that he is obligated to
citizens of Southport, and will not vote to give City right of way to any
organization. City Manager Thornton stated that Caswell Avenue is a part of the
Capital Improvement Plan.
Alderman Frink questioned what effect opening Caswell Avenue would have on the
college. Mr. Thompson stated that it could prohibit expansion because the City
Ordinance would require onsite parking and a portion of their funds would be
spent on construction of a parking lot.
Dr. Greiner stated the land on Lord Street is approximately 3.5 acres. Alderman
Fisher advised if additional acreage is needed, that land is available near the
primary school and the proposed City Park. John Thompson, Architect, stated
renovation of the building on Lord Street has cultural significance and can be
restored with additional square footage for the dollar compared to construction
of a new building.
Attorney Isenberg stated the correct procedure to close a road is to submit a
formal request to the Board of Aldermen.
City Manager Thornton asked that staff be allowed to meet with Dr. Greiner, the
architect and other interested parties to review plans to explore options that
would be mutually agreeable to both parties.
IX.
New Business
a)    Discussion of potential reimbursement plan to Clean Water Management
Trust Fund Project #2005B-513
City Manager Thornton stated that the Clean Water Management Trust Fund is
seeking reimbursement of $1,686,000 in grant monies that was allocated to the
City in 2006 to purchase a 400-acre tract of land near Sunny Point for a spray
irrigation site. The City opted to join with the County to treat its
wastewater, and the existing need was not present for utilization of the site
as a spray field by Brunswick County as it was with the Sanitary District.
Because of not utilizing the land at this time for a spray field, the Clean
Water Management Trust Fund Board of Trustees requests that the funds be
repaid. In exchange, the City would own the 400-acre tract including mineral
and timber rights with no encumbrances upon the property. Staff has been in
discussion with the County regarding utilizing the land as a spray irrigation
site. Mr. Thornton stated as of June 30, the City has a fund balance of $1,607,
252 in the Water and Sewer Fund, of which $900,000 is restricted for capital
use. He recommended the Board make the first one-third payment from the
available fund balance and finance the remaining two-thirds with an outside
financing source.
Alderman Adams suggested the City re-negotiate the terms of the repayment
schedule with CWMTF after the first payment is remitted. Alderman Fisher stated
the original agreement was made in good faith and he does not agree with
repaying the funds. He suggested that a meeting be held with the Clean Water
Management Trust Board, City Engineer, Aldermen and County Representatives to
work out a resolution so that the City will not have to repay the money. City
Manager Thornton cautioned that the Board approved on June 22, 2009 Amendment
No. 1 to the Clean Water Management Trust Fund Grant Agreement, DENR Contract
No. GA07126, CWMTF Project No. 2006A-529 that: 1) The City will reimburse the
fund for Grant 2005B-513 within 365 days of signing the amendment, and 2) no
additional engineering fees will be paid as a result of the scope change. The
City has committed to this amendment; it has been signed and submitted to the
CWMTF.
Alderman Brown recommended utilizing the three-year repayment schedule and if
the City needs to borrow money later to meet its obligation, it will do so. He
then motioned to approve the three-year annual installment plan effective one
year from this date. (July 9, 2010). Motion seconded by Alderman Adams. The
votes were 3   ayes Aldermen Brown, Frink, and Adams. 1 no vote, Alderman
Fisher.
b)    Municipal Records Retention and Disposition (2009)

Municipal Records and Disposition Schedule in accordance with the provision of
Chapters 121 and 132 of the General Statues of North Carolina. The vote of

c)    Lowe-White Park Project (Bids)
City Manager Thornton stated sixteen (16) bids were received for the Lowe-White
Park. The low bid totaled $505,300.00. The City Engineer and staff consulted
with the low bidder to discuss cost saving reductions. $447,230 is budgeted for
the project and the City has sixty-days to accept or reject the bid.
Mr. Carter Hubard, Engineer stated they looked at ways to reduce cost but to
accomplish the grant requirements for the park, they proposed deleting the roof
for the overlook structure, reduce the footage of the trail, job built
restrooms instead of prefabricated, change landscape plan from asphalt trail to
stone base, and reduce width of trail to five feet. City could assist with the
landscape plan or have it done outside of the contract. Approximate cost
reductions totaled $65,000.
Mr. Hubard recommended testing the concrete and timber piles during the project
to insure that the backfill is compacted properly. He stated this cost was not
included in the contractor's bid, but was listed in the specs. The cost ranges
from $12,000-$18,000.
Alderman Fisher asked if the testing was required. Mr. Hubard stated that the
testing is to insure that there are no potential material issues and to insure
the integrity of the park. Alderman Fisher stated if the testing is not a legal
requirement that he is prepared to vote to build the park without the testing.
Attorney Isenberg stated the City has three options:
·   Award the low bid as bided $505,300
·   Award the low bid with the modifications negotiated, or
·   Reject all bids and to re-bid
It was stated that the grant has been extended one time, and the City has until
June 2010 to complete the park to comply with grant requirements.
Alderman Adams motioned to reject all bids and to re-bid the project. Motion
failed for lack of a second. (Motion failed)
Attorney Isenberg stated that two voting members are absent, and to authorize
the contract, four members must vote in the affirmative.
Alderman Fisher motioned, seconded by Alderman Brown to award the contract for
Lowe-White Park to B & K Coastal dba  as Cape Fear Paving with modifications
and reductions totaling $64,380. The vote of approval was 3 ayes, Alderman
Fisher, Brown and Frink. 1 no, Alderman Adams. (Board will have to re-vote)
The Board agreed to hold a special meeting on Monday, January 27, 2009 at 6:00
p.m. to discuss the Lowe White Park.
d)    ABC Board

Jones to a three-year term on the ABC Board. The vote was unanimous.

Executive Session
 
Executive Session Minutes July 9, 2009
 
Attorney Isenberg advised the Board regarding the possible settlement
alternatives for the annexation challenge filed by the petitioners in
connection with the annexation ordinance passed on April 9, 2009. He informed
the Board as to the legal issues involved in the Board voluntarily amending the
annexation ordinance before it became effective as well as the procedure
involved in reaching a settlement agreement with the petitioners in the court
action. He informed the Board as to the advantages and disadvantages of each
method. Isenberg then advised the Board as to the possible legal consequences
resulting from the Board's withdrawal of support for the local bills and the
possible effect of said action on the annexation ordinance.

seconded by Alderman Brown, vote carried.

Mr. Charles Drew, Code Enforcement Officer
3.   Rules under which this meeting will be conducted:
a.   All those wishing to speak will be sworn in.
You do not have to speak if sworn, but must be sworn to speak.
Attorneys, as members of the Court, do not have to be sworn.
b.   All presented evidence will be retained.
c.   Anyone wishing to speak will be heard subject to the following:
1)   All comments are to deal with the issues before us.
2)   Owner and complainant (or their attorneys) are to have five (5) minutes
each to speak. (Time to be monitored.) Speakers are to give any cross-
examination that they have to the Board to ask of the opposite party.
3)   The Committee will approve the credentials of expert witnesses
Any expert testimony given will be for no more than five (5) minutes with a
total of no more than ten (10) minutes for all expert testimony for both owner
and complainant.
4)   Others who wish to speak for either the owner or complainant will have
three (3) minutes each with a total of ten (10) minutes for all to speak.
5)   Cross examination is the function of the Committee and will have no time
limit. Cross-examination questions should be submitted to the Committee by the
owner, complainant, or attorney(s).
6)   Staff or Code Enforcement Officer presentations will have no time limit.
7)   There will be no interrupting of those speaking. All provided testimony
and comments shall be given in a normal voice.
8)   Anyone being disruptive will be asked to leave.
9)   Emotions will/should be under control, but if they interfere with your
presentation, you will be asked to let someone else speak.
10)    Once all testimony is heard, the Hearing will be closed and no more
comments will be accepted unless the Committee asks a specific question of an
individual.
There is no rebuttal or cross-examination allowed for these specific fact-
finding questions.
11)   The Committee will then discuss the case.
* There will be open discussion amongst the Committee.
* A decision will be made tonight, unless more information is required.
* Even if there is a rendering to Superior Court, the animal in question must
abide by the City Ordinance and State Law regarding dangerous dogs.
* The owner and dog address must be known at all times by the Office of Code
Enforcement for the City of Southport.
* Owner of the animal in question is called OWNER, and the person or animal
injured or menaced is called a COMPLAINANT.
* Both the OWNER and COMPLAINANT are to remain for paperwork at the end of the
proceedings.
4)   Ready to proceed:
* Swear participants in.
* Officer to make report.
* Complainant.
* Owner
* Rebuttal
* Final questions by/from Committee
* Committee to discuss and render decision.
Duly adopted on this the 27th of July, 2009 by the City of Southport Board of
Aldermen.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
City Clerk
Alderman Potter moved that Alderman Frink be appointed Chairman of the Appeals
Board, seconded by Alderman Boguskie. The vote was unanimous.
V.
Adjournment
There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned upon motion of
Alderman Brown, seconded by Alderman Boguskie and the vote was unanimous.

EXECUTIVE SESSION
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION MINUTES AUGUST 13, 2009
 
Attorney Isenberg advised the Board of the status of the pending annexation
suit and his discussions with the petitioner's Counsel. In addition, Isenberg
advised the Board that he believed that Progress Energy would be filing suit if
the City did not take some action to remove the Progress property from the
annexation area. Isenberg then told the Board that he believed that they had
the following options in relation to the pending annexation suit and possible
suit by Progress Energy:
1)     Litigate both suits in order to uphold the entire annexation.
2)    Try to enter into a settlement agreement with the petitioners, which
would remove the petitioners' property, Progress property and possibly others
from the annexation area.
3)     Repeal the annexation ordinance; or
4)     Attempt to amend the annexation report and annexation ordinance to
remove the petitioners and Progress property from the annexation ordinance. The
Board discussed each of the alternatives with the City Attorney, but no action
taken in closed session.
No further discussion, motion made by Alderman Boguskie, seconded by Alderman
Potter to re-enter regular session. Vote unanimous.

Carolina that:

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the City Planner has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
proposed amendments to Article 2, Section 2-2, Article 10 and Article 12,
Section 12-18, of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
these proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed , was held on September 10, 2009, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that these proposed amendments to
the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with the Southport CAMA Land
Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) this type of use or business
is not addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance and should be, (ii) these
amendments are necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the
Highway Commercial District, and (iii) regulation of these uses is necessary to
promote the public safety and general welfare of the community by restricting
the hours of operation and proximity of said businesses to residential areas,
schools, churches etc;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments and additions to the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted.

AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
TEXT AMENDMENT # 09-08-20-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With
Respect to Conditional Uses
AMEND:
1)    Article 2, BASIC DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS
Section 2-2 “Definitions of Basic Terms” is hereby amended by adding the
following definition in alphabetical sequence:
Electronic Gaming Operations.
Any business enterprise, whether as a principal or an accessory use, where
persons utilize electronic machines, including but not limited to computers and
gaming terminals, to conduct games of chance, including sweepstakes, and where
cash, merchandise or other items of value are redeemed or otherwise
distributed, whether or not the value of such distribution is determined by
electronic games played or by predetermined odds. This term includes, but is
not limited to internet cafes, internet sweepstakes, beach sweepstakes or
cybercafés. This does not include any lottery approved by the State of North
Carolina.
2)    ARTICLE 10: TABLE OF PERMITTED USES:
The Table of Permitted Uses is hereby amended by adding “Electronic Gaming
Operations“and by placing a “C” entry in the HC (Highway Commercial) column.
3)    ARTICLE 12: ZONING & CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT APPROVAL
Section 12-18: Table of Regulations for Conditional Uses
“Table of Regulations for Conditional Uses”, is hereby amended by adding a new
section, to be inserted in alphabetical sequence, to read as follows:
Use: Electronic Gaming Operations, Conditional Use District: HC
Use – Electronic Gaming Operations. The following specific provisions shall be
met as minimum standards prior to the approval of any business engaging in
electronic gaming operations as a conditional use in the Highway Commercial
(HC) zoning district.
(A)   Days/Hours of operation: businesses engaging in electronic gaming
operations activities may operate from 8:00 am until 12:00 midnight each day,
seven (7) days per week.
(B)   The maximum number of machines/ terminals/ computers for any electronic
gaming operations business is 20.
(C)   Minimum paved parking spaces:
(1)   One (1) space per every two (2) terminals or one (1) space per every one
hundred (100) square feet of total floor area, whichever is greater;
(2)   One (1) handicapped space per every twenty five (25) or fewer spaces;
(3)   One (1) in every eight (8) accessible spaces, but not less than one,
shall be served by an access aisle ninety six (96) inches wide minimum and
shall be designated "van accessible";
(4)   One (1) additional space per each (1) employee.
(D)   All applicable permits must be issued to the applicant prior to the
issuance of the conditional use permit and the opening of business.
(E)   If food or beverage is served, the establishment must meet the
requirements of the Brunswick County Health Department, including any and all
necessary permits and/or licenses.
(F)   The establishment must be a minimum of five hundred (500) feet from any
building being used as a dwelling or any residential zoning district.
(G)   The establishment must be a minimum of one thousand (1,000) feet from any
other organization engaged in an electronic gaming operations business or any
adult or sexually oriented business.
(H)   The establishment must be a minimum of one thousand (1,000) feet from any
established religious institution/synagogue, school, daycare center/home;
library, public park, recreation area or motion picture establishment where “G”
or “PG” rated movies are shown to the general public on a regular basis.
(I)   A current certificate and straight-line drawing prepared within thirty
(30) days prior to application by a registered land surveyor depicting the
property lines and the structures containing any existing electronic gaming
businesses within one thousand (1,000) feet of the property to be certified;
the property lines of any established religious institution/synagogue, school,
daycare center/home; library, public park, recreation area or motion picture
establishment where “G” or “PG” rated movies are shown to the general public on
a regular basis that is within one thousand (1,000) feet of the property to be
certified. For purposes of this Section, a use shall be considered existing or
established if it is in existence at the time, an application is submitted.
(J)   Measurement of distance separation shall be in a straight line from the
closest point of the buildings at which the internet café/ sweepstakes business
is located.
(K)   No alcoholic beverages will be served or consumed on the premises of
electronic gaming operations.
This ordinance is effective upon the date of adoption, September 10, 2009.

j)    Proposal to place wind turbine at Municipal Waste Water Treatment Plant
City Manager Thornton presented a request from Mr. Richard Holloman, President
of Carolina Wind Turbines asking to place a less than 10 kw vertical axis wind
turbine on City property at the Wastewater Treatment Plant. In a letter from
Mr. Holloman, he states, "the unit is a low RPM turbine that produces energy at
lower wind speeds than traditional horizontal units and the energy generated
would be available to the City. It will be less than 35 ft. tall and a 14 ft.
diameter, making very little noise."
City Manager Thornton explained that this is an experimental wind turbine and
part of the growing green initiative at no cost to the City. He stated that the
turbine needs to be located in an area with consistent wind and Southport's
proximity to water was the most likely location. The structure will be shielded
from public view and is a short-term experiment, and will be removed at the
City's request. City Manager Thornton stated that the North Carolina Eastern
Municipal Power Agency (NCEMPA) and ElectriCities do not have an issue with the
experiment. He stated if it is the Boards' desire to consider this, staff will
prepare an agreement protecting the City's interest i.e. liability.
Attorney Isenberg asked about the permitted use under the UDO. Alderman Adams
suggested the company look for other property since the WWTP is situated on
prime property and he believes this is not the best use of the land. Alderman
Fisher clarified that it is a single device wind sail at no cost and liability
to the City. However, it may establish precedent in determining whether wind
can be used for green power, which will be required in the future. Mr. Thornton
asked the Board if they desired to explore the concept, and if so, staff would
begin discussion with Progress Energy, ElectriCities, and NCEMPA. Board members
concurred to explore the concept.
Alderman Fisher moved, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to direct staff to explore
the concept subject to contract approval. The votes were 4 ayes, Aldermen
Fisher, Boguskie, Brown and Frink. 1 no, Alderman Adams. (Motion passed)

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, proposed amendments to Article 18, Section 18-4(B)(1) & (C)( 2), of
the Southport Unified Development Ordinance have been prepared and submitted to
the Planning Board; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
these proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public hearing,
properly noticed, was held on October 8, 2009, before the Board of Aldermen
regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that these proposed amendments to
the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with the Southport CAMA Land
Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) industry standard plant size
is not addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance and should be, (ii) this
amendment is necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the
landscaping standards, and (iii) regulation of these uses is necessary to
promote the public safety and general welfare of the community by ensuring that
all commercial installations are governed by the same set of rules;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments and additions to the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted.
This 8th day of October 2009.

City Manager Thornton recommended the Board request the Army Corps of Engineers

Erosion Protection Project under Section 14   of the Emergency Streambank and
Shoreline Erosion Protection for Public Facilities. Adopting a resolution would
be the first step towards the Corps developing and establishing an Emergency
Streambank and Shoreline Erosion Protection project for the West Bay Street
pumping station.
He also discussed the potential involvement of the City in a Section 206
Aquatic Ecosystem Restoration Project  requesting the Corps to investigate the
feasibility of a project along the waterfront in the area of Kingsley Park and
the Small Boat Basin on West Bay Street. The City's responsibility would
include funding a portion of the plans, specifications and construction costs
for projects under Section 14 and 206, if approved.

investigate the scope of the 206 project.    The vote of approval was
unanimous.
Resolution
Be it resolved, that the Southport Board of Aldermen request the U. S. Army
Corps of Engineers to conduct investigations and studies to determine the
feasibility of developing an Emergency Streambank or Shoreline Erosion
Protection Project at Southport under the authority provided by Section 14 of
the 1946 Flood Control Act, as amended.
It is understood that, if it is found feasible and advisable to develop an
Emergency Streambank or Shoreline Erosion Project at Southport, the Board of
Aldermen would be required before construction commences to enter into a
contractual agreement that it will provide such local cooperation as may be
prescribed by the Secretary of the Army.

d)   Resolution Requesting Southport's Hazard Mitigation Plan to be merged with
the County of Brunswick's Plan
Ms. Amy Nelson, City Planner, and Mr. Chris Crew, State Hazard Mitigation
Officer of the North Carolina Emergency Management Office, told the Board that
Hazard Mitigation Plans must be updated every five years; FEMA and Homeland
Security propose more regional plans. The City Planner stated that she is
working to merge the City's Plan with Brunswick County, which will be
beneficial to everyone. Mr. Crew stated it is the federal government and
state's desire to consolidate Hazard Mitigation Plans. If Plans are not in
place, towns will not be eligible for public or individual assistance funds in
the event of a state disaster declaration. If a federal disaster declaration is
made and the Plan is not in place, the town would not be eligible for hazard
mitigation funds. He explained that the City will not lose funds and will have
its own annex in the joint Plan, which will describe hazard threats to the City
and include mitigation measures appropriate for Southport. As a party to the
Plan, the City will be eligible to apply for its own funds. In conclusion, he
stated in order for the City to join Brunswick County's Plan, the State Hazard
Mitigation Office must have a document from Brunswick County agreeing to
Southport becoming a part of their plan. If the Board does not act at this
meeting, the City will be on its own for the next five years.
Alderman Fisher moved , seconded by Alderman Boguskie to adopt a resolution
requesting action by the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners to merge the
City of Southport's Hazard Mitigation Plan with the County. Vote of approval
was unanimous. (Motion passed)
A RESOLUTION REQUESTING ACTION BY THE BRUNSWICK COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS
TO MERGE THE HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN FOR THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA,
WITH THE BRUNSWICK COUNTY HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN
THAT WHEREAS, on October 30, 2000, the President of the United States signed
into law the Disaster Mitigation Act of 2000 to amend the Robert T. Stafford
Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act of 1988 to reinforce the
importance of pre-disaster mitigation planning to help reduce disaster losses;
and
WHEREAS, North Carolina Senate Bill 300 requires all local governments to have
an approved Hazard Mitigation Plan in order to receive state public assistance
funds (effective for state-declared disasters after November 1, 2004); and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport Hazard Mitigation Plan (Plan) was approved on
November 5, 2004 by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and the
North Carolina Division of Emergency Management (NCEM);
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been working with Brunswick County on the
Hazard Mitigation Plan update and the planning process involved since the
spring of 2009; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport now desires to merge said Plan with the County
of Brunswick in accordance with the guidance provided to the City of Southport
by FEMA, NCEM, and the County of Brunswick;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina in session assembled this 8th day of October 2009:
SECTION 1. That the attached “Hazard Mitigation Plan for the City of Southport”
is hereby forwarded to the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners for adoption
as a merge to the Hazard Mitigation Plan for the County of Brunswick, said plan
attached hereto as (Exhibit A).
SECTION 2. That upon adoption, said plan shall continue to serve as a guide for
the various departments of the City of Southport Government in pre-disaster
planning and post-disaster recovery.
SECTION 3. That said plan will be reviewed annually or immediately after a
natural disaster.
SECTION 4. That all reports and changes shall be submitted to the North
Carolina Division of Emergency Management and the Federal Emergency Management
Agency every five years.
Adopted this 8th day of October 2009.
/s/ Sandra Spencer, Mayor

OCTOBER 13, 2009
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
OCTOBER 13, 2009  4:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, NC
 
PRESENT:         Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor
            Aldermen Donnie Potter, James Brown, Ed Boguskie, Paul Fisher
            and Nelson Adams
ABSENT:         Alderman Jwantana Frink
STAFF:         M. Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, MMC, Clerk
            Amy Nelson, Planner
            Wayne Strickland, Building Inspector
            Dale Holland, Consulting Planner
I.
Call to Order – 4:00 p.m.
Mayor Spencer called the special meeting to order at 4:00 p.m. and announced
the purpose of the meeting is to discuss recommended changes to the Unified
Development Ordinance.
II.
UDO Amendments - Mr. Dale Holland, Consulting Planner
Mr. Dale Holland stated that the recommended changes to the Unified Development
Ordinance includes; 1) definitions under Article II, which is a minor
modification for home occupations. 2) A revised table of permitted uses to
incorporate changes to conditional use permits i.e. clarifications and
conditions. 3) Article 10, denotes the table of permitted uses. 4) Article 11
denotes the table of yard, area and height requirements. The only change in
Article 10 and 11 is reconstructing the table of permitted uses i.e. the order
and numbering. 5) Section 12-18 includes supplemental regulations incorporated
in the table of permitted uses. He stated that the most significant change to
supplemental regulations and the table of permitted uses is the recommendation
by the Planning Board that accessory apartments, including attached and garage
apartments be deleted as separate categories and replaced with accessory
dwelling unit residential, and accessory dwelling unit commercial. He explained
that the Planning Board went through the process to take the responsibility of
conditional use permits from the Board of Aldermen and place it with the Board
of Adjustments. However, there were some concerns by the Board that some of the
requirements imposed for conditional use permits should be strengthened and
others expanded by specifying where they may or might not occur. The next step
in the process is a Public Hearing.
The Board discussed with Mr. Holland various aspects of the recommended
changes.
There being no further discussion, Alderman Fisher moved, seconded by Alderman
Brown to schedule a Public Hearing on November 12, 2009 for public comments on
the recommended changes to the Unified Development Ordinance. The vote of
approval was unanimous.
Alderman Potter extended appreciation to the Planning Board for their diligence
and work as volunteer members.
III.
Adjournment
Alderman Brown moved to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Alderman Boguskie.
Vote carried.

Mayor
_________________________
Clerk

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENTS TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the City Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning
Board proposed amendments to Article 2, Section 2-2, Article 10, Article 11,
Section 11-1, and Article 12 of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance;
and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
these proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to the NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on November 12, 2009, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that these proposed amendments to
the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with the Southport CAMA Land
Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) in order to bring the Unified
Development Ordinance up-to-date after careful review, adjustments to
conditional uses were necessary, including the addition of community colleges,
(ii) these amendments are necessary to promote orderly growth and development
in the City of Southport and its extraterritorial jurisdiction, and (iii) these
changes and additions are necessary to promote the public safety and general
welfare of the community by modernizing the City’s ordinances;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments and additions to the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted.
This 12th day of November 2009.
/s/ Sandra P. Spencer
Mayor

b)    Resolution in support of Veterans Medical Clinic in Brunswick County
Alderman Fisher motioned, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to adopt a resolution

be located within Brunswick County. The vote of approval was unanimous.
