Resolution in Support of a Veteran's Medical Clinic In Brunswick County
WHEREAS, veterans deserve and merit the best medical care available, and
WHEREAS, veterans have made many contributions and sacrifices in the line of
duty for the United States of America and its citizens, and
WHEREAS, some veterans have problems traveling long distances and it is only
fitting that veterans deserves a medical facility within close proximity
without traveling hundreds of miles, and
WHEREAS, there is a critical need for a Veteran's Clinic within Brunswick and
Columbus counties; and
WHEREAS, according to statistics from the Veteran's Administration, Brunswick
County has a veteran's population of 12,656, and Columbus County 4,394.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Southport Board of Aldermen go on
record in support of the Veteran's Administration converting the old Brunswick
Community Hospital into a much-needed Veteran's Medical Clinic to serve the
veterans population of Brunswick and Columbus Counties.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a copy of this resolution be forwarded to the
appropriate persons.

d)   Resolution to Endorse the City's Application for NCDOT Bicycle and
Pedestrian Planning Grant Initiative
City Manager Thornton explained that the City is applying for an 80/20 program
in 2010, which will result in the development of a comprehensive municipal
bicycle and pedestrian plan. Mrs. Amy Nelson, City Planner stated the City does
not have a plan for sidewalks or bike paths and the City is in the process of
applying for a grant for sidewalks. Adopting the resolution is a component of
the plan and once in place, the City can apply for other grant funds i.e.
transportation enhancement. Alderman Adams noted that the City has had requests
for sidewalks. City Manager Thornton explained that this Plan would allow the
City to perform a comprehensive review of existing sidewalks and those that the
City wishes to put into place; however, it does not preclude the City from
installing sidewalks if other monies are available i.e. power bill funds.
Alderman Fisher moved, seconded by Alderman Potter to adopt the resolution
endorsing the application for the NC DOT bicycle and pedestrian planning grant
initiative. The vote of approval was unanimous. (Aldermen Fisher, Potter,
Adams, Frink and Boguskie) Motion passed 5-0.
RESOLUTION TO ENDORSE THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT’S APPLICATION FOR THE NORTH
CAROLINA DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION’S BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN PLANNING GRANT
INITIATIVE
WHEREAS on December 4, 2009, the NCDOT Division of Bicycle and Pedestrian
Transportation will conclude the 2010 Call for Proposals to encourage the
development of comprehensive municipal bicycle plans and pedestrian plans; and
WHEREAS the Bicycle and Pedestrian Planning Grant Initiative is a state program
set up for municipalities all across the state of North Carolina; and
WHEREAS the City of Southport has an opportunity to apply for this 80%-20%
matching grant program in 2010; and
WHEREAS there is a strong desire in the City of Southport to enhance the
transportation planning by providing more choices in order to make the
community more pedestrian-friendly, bicycle-friendly, and a better place to
live; and
BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport,
North Carolina in session assembled this 12th day of November 2009 endorse the
NCDOT Division of Bicycle and Pedestrian Transportation’s Bicycle and

North Carolina.

A RESOLUTION ADOPTING THE BRUNSWICK COUNTY MULTI-JURISDICTIONAL HAZARD
MITIGATION PLAN FOR THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT NORTH CAROLINA
THAT WHEREAS, on October 30, 2000, the President of the United States signed
into law the Disaster Mitigation Act of 2000 to amend the Robert T. Stafford
Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act of 1988 to reinforce the
importance of pre-disaster mitigation planning to help reduce disaster losses;
and
WHEREAS, North Carolina Senate Bill 300 requires all local governments to have
an approved Hazard Mitigation Plan in order to receive state public assistance
funds (effective for state-declared disasters after November 1, 2004);
WHEREAS, the City of Southport Hazard Mitigation Plan (Plan) was approved on
November 5, 2004 by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and the
North Carolina Division of Emergency Management (NCEM);
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been working with Brunswick County on the
Hazard Mitigation Plan update and the planning process involved since the
spring of 2009; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has merged said Plan with the County of
Brunswick in accordance with the guidance provided to the City of Southport by
FEMA, NCEM, and the County of Brunswick;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen in
session assembled this 12th day of November 2009 that the Brunswick County
Multi-Jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan is hereby adopted as the official
hazard mitigation plan of the City of Southport, North Carolina.
Adopted this 12th day of November 2009.

k)   Ordinance Establishing a Capital Project Ordinance Fund: Southport
Wastewater System Enhancement – Phase II
City Manager Thornton stated adopting the above referenced ordinance would
rescind the existing ordinance, which reflects the project as it existed prior
to the City establishing the agreement with the County of Brunswick to treat
its wastewater.  The ordinance shows where the monies come from including the
ARRA funding and how it is to be expended.
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Fisher to approve the Ordinance
Establishing a Capital Project Ordinance Fund for the Southport Wastewater
System Enhancement – Phase II. The vote was unanimous. (Aldermen Fisher,
Potter, Adams, Frink and Boguskie) Motion passed 5-0.
ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A CAPITAL PROJECT FUND:
SOUTHPORT WASTEWATER SYSTEM ENHANCEMENT- PHASE II
WHEREAS, the City of Southport is committed to providing superior wastewater
collection and treatment to its citizens: and
WHEREAS, the City is further committed to providing such service in the most
efficient, economical and environmentally appropriate manner practicable: and
WHEREAS, the elected approach to achieving these goals is through a partnership
with Brunswick County that will ultimately result in Brunswick County assuming
all wastewater treatment responsibilities for the City: and
WHEREAS, it is appropriate that the pre-existing Capital Project Ordinance be
rescinded and a new Capital Project Ordinance be established for this venture
that will result in all of the City’s wastewater flow being redirected to
Brunswick County for treatment: and
WHEREAS, a Capital Project Fund is hereby determined to be the most appropriate
manner in which to account for revenues and expenditures associated with the
project.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen:
1.   The pre-existing Capital Project Ordinance with SBSD is rescinded.
2.   The Capital Project Fund is amended and established with Brunswick County
for Phase II of this project.
3.   The amended total budget for the project, subject to amendment by action
of the Board of Aldermen as necessary to implement the project, shall be as
follows.
Revenues

d)    Resolution in Support of Retaining Existing Funding Method for
Distribution of Sales Tax Revenues in Brunswick County
Mayor stated that this is an issue with the beach communities, as they want to
redistribute sales tax revenues. City Manager Thornton stated that out of 18
municipalities within Brunswick County, the current tax distribution method is
on a per capita basis and the county must reaffirm this method each year. The
majority of municipalities wish the county to continue the method on a per
capita basis. If the distribution were changed based on the ad valorem method,
Southport would lose one-half of its sales tax distribution. City Manager
Thornton recommended the Board adopt the resolution to oppose the change in the
distribution method.
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Frink to adopt the following
resolution. Vote unanimous. Motion passed 6-0
RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF RETAINING THE EXISTING FUNDING METHOD FOR THE
DISTRIBUTION OF SALES TAX REVENUES IN BRUNSWICK COUNTY
WHEREAS, the City of Southport is a municipality in Brunswick County, North
Carolina, and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport has a strong and
mutually beneficial working relationship with its fellow municipalities of
Brunswick County, and
WHEREAS, the City's portion of sales tax revenue distribution is vital to
maintaining a strong and vibrant community and meetings its obligations to the
citizens, and
WHEREAS, the citizens of Southport have elected its officials to serve and
protect the best interests of the City and to take action when activities which
potentially impair the future prospects for growth occur, and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen unanimously agree that a change in the
distribution method of sales tax revenues is not in the best interest of the
City and would result in a significant tax increase to our property owners, and
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Board of Aldermen request the Brunswick
County Board of Commissioners to retain the current distribution method on a
per capita basis, and direct the City Clerk to send a copy of this resolution
to each Commissioner of Brunswick County and each municipality.
ADOPTED this the 10th day of December 2009 in regular meeting of the Southport
Board of Aldermen.
/s/Sandra P. Spencer, Mayor

/s/Regina W. Alexander, MMC

b)    International Port Project and Southport's Status
Mayor Howard referenced the resolution that was adopted July 2006 with
conditions supporting the proposed international port. He recommended that the
resolution be rescinded and the Board with hold all resolutions until studies
are completed. He invited organized groups to appear on the Board's agenda if
they wish to address this matter.
Alderman Adams suggested that this item be discussed at the retreat in order to
acquire a better understanding why the Mayor proposes to rescind the
resolution. He stressed the Board working as a unit when making a decision on
the Port.
Alderman Karn explained that the Board is not speaking for or against the Port
and concurred that it should be discussed in-depth and to get the State Ports
Authority to engage the City in their discussions.
Alderman Potter motioned, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to rescind the 2006
resolution requesting the North Carolina Department of Transportation to
conduct the engineering and environmental studies required for development of
the transportation infrastructure required for the development of the North
Carolina International Port in Brunswick County, and to discuss the proposed
Port at the Board's Retreat in January. Discussion: Alderman Adams reiterated
that the Board should discuss the matter as a Board since there are new Board
members and his belief that the Board should be united on this issue and not
convey a negative message to the public. Alderman Karn recommended public input
be received; stating that he is in favor of rescinding the resolution, but do
not believe one month will make a difference. Alderman Poole stated rescinding
the resolution would signify the City's neutral position. Mayor Howard stated
that he recommended rescission of the resolution because the official position
of this administration should be neutral until all studies are completed in
order to make informed decisions. He will propose to Governor Perdue, Speaker
of the House and Mayor Pro Tem of the Senate to appoint someone from Southport
to serve on the State Ports Authority in order to be a part of the process.
Mayor Howard called for the vote on the motion. The vote was 3 ayes, Aldermen
Potter, Poole and Boguskie. 3 noes, Aldermen Adams, Frink, Karn, Mayor Howard.
Motion failed 3-4.
Mayor Howard requested the Port matter be placed on the January 14 regular
meeting agenda and January 16 retreat agenda.

and space planners to perform an assessment and inventory all city facilities
by assessing the condition of the facilities, and to conduct a space planning

Alderman Karn motioned to authorize the City Manager to request proposals for a
municipal facilities assessment. Motion seconded by Alderman Frink. Discussion:
Alderman Poole agreed that the Board's meeting room is not accessible for all
persons and stated that technology is needed so the public can have access to

d)    Pre-agenda Meeting Discussion
Alderman Boguskie motioned, seconded by Alderman Karn beginning January 2010,
that the Southport Board of Aldermen will hold a pre-agenda meeting 10 days
prior to the regular Board meeting that will be determined by a majority vote
of the items that will be on the agenda for the regular meeting. After this
meeting, no new items will be brought to the table unless it requires a vote
prior to the next regular meeting of the Board, and when this happens, the City
Manager will immediately notify all Board members and the Mayor of the agenda
addition. Discussion: Alderman Boguskie explained the reason for this action is
due to materials being placed before Aldermen at regular meetings without prior
knowledge. Alderman Adams asked that this be discussed at the retreat,
believing that there is another way to handle this without a second meeting.
Alderman Karn stated the advantage of a pre-agenda meeting is to make the
regular meeting more efficient and it should not be more time consuming. Mayor
Howard stated that it may be justifiable to defer the motion for 30 days until
January 14 meeting and if someone request it on the retreat agenda, it could be
considered. Mayor Howard stated the motion would prohibit an Alderman's ability
to place an item on the agenda unless it met with approval of a majority of the
members, and he believes that is inappropriate, because Aldermen should have
the right to have items considered for the agenda. Aldermen Potter asked if the
motion could be deferred and get the City Manager's input.
Alderman Boguskie withdrew the motion, seconded by Alderman Karn. Vote carried.
Passed 6-0
ElectriCities Board: Alderman Boguskie asked about the appointment to the
ElectriCities Board. Mayor Howard stated that this item would be deferred to
the retreat agenda in January. At present, the City does not have an alternate,
but is represented.
Planning Board ETJ Member: Attorney Isenberg asked about the ETJ appointment to
be made by the County and if the Board is standing behind its resolution, with

submitted to the County, and it is his belief that they need to fulfill their

General Statute, which states the County, has forty-five days to make a
decision and if delayed longer, it will revert to the City. The City has
received no official word from the County; however, staff will make contact
with the County to ascertain their position on the appointment.

Frink
            and Ken Karn

IV.
Approval of Agenda
Mayor Howard announced that because of a new law enacted, a Code of Ethics is
required to be adopted by January 1, 2011. Upon receipt of the model policy,
which is being written by the School of Government staff, the Board of Aldermen
will review and adopt one of its own. In the interim, Mayors were requested to
inquire at each meeting if any member of the Board knows of any conflict of
interest or the appearance of a conflict of interest with respect to matters on
the agenda, and if so; to state it. This statement will become a regular part
of the agenda until the Board adopts an ethics policy. No conflicts of interest
were stated by Board members.
Mayor Howard requested to amend the agenda to discuss items XI. a, b, c
immediately after the Public Hearing(s).
Alderman Karn motioned to approve the agenda as amended, seconded by Alderman
Poole. Vote unanimous. Motion passed 5-0
Alderman Adams questioned why X. a) Resolution of Support for the proposed
International Port Project, and b) Fort Johnston was placed on the agenda when
it was consensus of the Board to discuss these matters at the retreat. Alderman
Karn stated he requested the items be placed on the agenda because a majority
of the public attends the regular meetings. Alderman Frink stated the Aldermen
need to discuss the Port collectively as a Board. Alderman Adams motioned to

c)    City of Southport Zoning Amendment Text change ZA 12-09-09-01
Mrs. Nelson presented a text change for Article 3. Administrative Mechanisms
Part 1. Planning and Zoning Board, Section 3-1 Membership and Vacancies:
Extraterritorial representatives shall have equal rights, privileges, and
duties with the other members of the board to which they are appointed,
regardless of whether the matters at issue arise within the City or within the
extraterritorial area.
Attorney Isenberg stated that this text change will clear the ambiguous
language in the City Code, however; ETJ members have voted on all matters
before the Planning Board. State law is specific about ETJ members and
clarifying the language will make the ordinance more specific.
No further comments from the public, Alderman Adams moved to re-enter regular
session, seconded by Alderman Karn. (9:19 p.m.) Motion passed 5-0.
Regular Session Reconvened
Attorney Isenberg told the Board that they should consider if the property is
rezoned, whether it is suitable to change from R-20 to R-10 zoning.
Alderman Adams noted that the Planning Board did not provide a recommendation
on the rezoning, however; staff did and he suggested the rezoning request be
sent back to the Planning Board for a recommendation. He motioned accordingly,
seconded by Alderman Boguskie. Discussion: Alderman Karn stated that he had
sufficient information to make a decision and believes that it is beneficial to
have an R-20 zoning district. Alderman Poole stated she attended the Planning
Board meeting when this was discussed and they declined to make a
recommendation. The vote on the motion was 3 ayes, Aldermen Adams, Frink and
Boguskie, 2 noes, Aldermen Poole and Karn. Motion passed 3-2.
Alderman Adams motioned, seconded by Alderman Karn to approve the text change
to Article 3. Administrative Mechanisms Part 1. Planning and Zoning Board,
Section 3-1 Membership and Vacancies: Extraterritorial representatives shall
have equal rights, privileges, and duties with the other members of the board
to which they are appointed, regardless of whether the matters at issue arise
within the City or within the extraterritorial area. Discussion: Alderman
Boguskie stated the text change is not required by state statute and ETJ
members should only vote on ETJ matters. Alderman Karn noted that the Planning
Board is an advisory board, not legislative and he does not have a problem with
the language change. In answer to Alderman Poole’s question, Amy Nelson noted
that there are no decisions by the Planning Board that the Alderman does not
review. Alderman Karn noted that recommendations regarding conditional uses are
reviewed by the Zoning Board of Adjustments. Mayor Howard called for the vote
on the motion, which was 3 ayes, Aldermen Adams, Karn and Poole. 2 noes,
Aldermen Boguskie and Frink. Motion passed 3-2.

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the City Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning
Board a proposed amendment to Article 3, Section 3-1, of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to the NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on January 14, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) in order to bring the Unified
Development Ordinance up-to-date after careful review, occasional adjustments
are necessary, including those associated with the City’s Extraterritorial
Jurisdiction, (ii) this amendment is necessary to clarify when ETJ members can
vote on City of Southport issues in the City of Southport and its
extraterritorial jurisdiction, and (iii) it concurs with the rights, privileges
and duties allowed by NC General Statute § 160A-362.;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 14th day of January, 2010.
By:    ________________________

Alderman Poole referenced compensation and benefits for the Board totaling
$32,500 in the budget, which includes a monthly salary of $250 per Alderman,
$350 Mayor, and $25 for special meetings, if members elect to get paid. The
City is also expending $60,000 for insurance which includes health, life,
dental and vision. Alderman Poole recommended the Board seek ways to cut cost,
the same as expected of other departments. She asked the Board to consider
reducing their salary and health benefits.
Alderman Adams stated Board members are available 24 hours a day and deserve

the guidelines with Medicare vs. CIGNA.

but other Boards/Committees do not and she has been asked this question.
Personnel System Improvement Objectives:
City Manager Thornton stated that a portion of the insurance is for retirees
pursuant to a personnel policy amendment adopted in 2003. He stated that
benefits will be evaluated and possibly modified based upon years of service.
In the past, employees were required to have a number of years with the City
before they received health insurance until the age of 65. Ms. Miller explained
that the existing policy states if you have years of creditable service with
the N.C. Retirement System and become employed by the City of Southport, they
can retire and receive health insurance from the City with as little as one
year of service. This has caused the City's liability to increase approximately
$4,000,000 which includes existing employees.
Mrs. Miller stated the Board will need to adopt a resolution if it chooses to
pay as you go with the OPED benefits. She stated that a resolution would be
prepared to present to the Board.
City Manager Thornton stated the need for the City's Personnel Policy to be
updated and Chris May of the Cape Fear Council of Governments submitted an
estimate of $3,000 to update the policy and job descriptions. In answer to
question by Alderman Karn, Mr. Thornton noted that there is no provision in the
budget for merit pay, however cost of living increases has been given annually.
He discussed retention of employees and incentives. Mayor Howard stated that
the Board is not in a position to consider merit pay because the city is just
implementing performance evaluations, and this will take a few years to
benchmark.
Alderman Boguskie motioned, seconded by Alderman Karn, to employ Cape Fear
Council of Governments to review and update the City's personnel policy i.e.
job descriptions. The vote was unanimous. Motion passed 5-0

a)    Zoning Amendment RZ 09-1110-01
Mrs. Nelson, Planning Director presented staff's evaluation on the rezoning
request and explained that staff recommends approval of the request to rezone
10.17 acres at 412 Stuart Avenue from R-20 (residential) to R-10 because:
∙   Staff believes that the proposed request is consistent with the intent and
purpose of the CAMA Land Use Plan
∙   Impact on City services will be negligible
∙   Traffic impact on Stuart Avenue will be minimal, traffic on Howe Street
will be impacted slightly
∙   The requested rezoning to R-10 is compatible with the City of Southport's
regulatory documents and would not have an unreasonable impact on the
surrounding community and will enhance the public health, safety, and general
welfare for the reasons stated in the evaluation.
∙   The Planning Board recommended approval of the rezoning.
Alderman Karn referenced Article 4, Section 4-1, (B) Application asking if the
proposed amendment was in the interest of the public and not the property owner
pursuant to this section of the UDO.
Attorney Isenberg stated the application does not have to specifically state
those words but the application must show evidence where staff and the Board
can find that it is beneficial to the public.
(B) Application. A complete application for any amendment shall contain a
description of the proposed zoning regulation or zoning map amendment. The
application shall state in detail whether the proposed amendment is consistent
with the City Comprehensive Plan, CAMA Core Land Use Plan, and any other
officially adopted plan that is applicable. The application shall also give
detailed evidence that the proposed amendment is in the interest and will
benefit the general public and not solely be of benefit to the applicant; that
the uses within the proposed zoning district are similar or comparable to the
uses in the district as currently zoned, or that none of the uses permitted in
the proposed zoning district may potentially adversely affect property values
or the health, safety, morals, or general welfare of the residents of the
surrounding area. Such application shall be filed with the Administrator to be
processed in accord with Section 12-5. (Revised 4/13/06)
Mr. Joey Brouchard representing Southport Development, LLC (Dr. Mintz and Mr.
Aughenbach) stated rezoning the property would benefit the public in several
ways and cited drainage and flood control since this area is subject to
flooding.
Alderman Adams stated the Planning Board and staff did what was asked of them
and he was satisfied with their recommendation.
Alderman Boguskie referenced a traffic impact study performed by Greene
Transportation in 2007 which cited the traffic pattern where Stuart intersects
with Howe Street, River Road, Hwy 211 and Robert Ruark. He stated that Stuart
being in close proximity to this area has a lot of traffic particularly with
the opening of a new restaurant. Ms. Nelson stated a traffic impact study was
not performed, but will be considered during the site plan review.
Alderman Adams motioned to accept the Planning Board and staff's recommendation
to rezone 10.17 acres at 412 Stuart Avenue from R-20 (residential) to R-10and
to adopt the Resolution. Motion seconded by Alderman Frink. Discussion:
Alderman Adams stated if this request is denied, it will place the Board in a
position to tell Brunswick Community College that they cannot expand because of
traffic. Alderman Poole stated she considered the nine (9) adjoining lots which
are zoned R-20, which is one of the few areas in the City that has larger lots.
Alderman Potter stated if the UDO is incorrect, it needs to be fixed and stated
support of staff's recommendation. Mayor Howard called for the vote: 3 ayes,
Aldermen Adams, Frink and Potter, 3 noes, Aldermen Poole, Karn and Boguskie.
Mayor Howard voted in the affirmative to break the tie. Motion passed 4 -3

RESOLUTION APPROVING A REZONING REQUEST FROM R-20 (RESIDENTIAL AGRICULTURAL
DISTRICT) TO R-10 (RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT) FOR 10.17 ACRES LOCATED AT 412 STUART
AVENUE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other land
use ordinances, and a zoning map that control land development within both the
City's incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city's zoning map; and
WHEREAS, Mr. Robert Aughenbaugh has filed an application for a zoning map
amendment requesting that 10.17 acres located at 412 Stuart Avenue be rezoned
from R-20 to R-10; and
WHEREAS, the City Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning
Board a favorable staff recommendation; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed rezoning be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to the NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on January 14, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed rezoning is
consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) the overall size of the tract of land
proposed for rezoning is reasonable when compared to the size of the zoning
district in which the subject property is located, (ii) the proposed rezoning
is consistent with the CAMA Land Use Plan, (iii) the impact to the adjacent
property owners and the surrounding community is reasonable, and the benefits
of the rezoning outweigh any potential inconvenience or harm to the community,
and (iv) the allowed uses within the proposed zoning district are similar or
comparable to uses permitted as currently zoned;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
rezoning request for 412 Stuart Avenue and alteration to the Southport Zoning
Map is hereby approved and adopted.
This, 11th day of February, 2010.
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor

AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE

An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With

Part I. PLANNING AND ZONING BOARD

Extraterritorial representatives shall have equal rights, privileges, and

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City's
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city's land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the City Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning
Board a proposed amendment to Article 3, Section 3-1, of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved, and
WHEREAS, pursuant to the NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on January 14, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Core Land
Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) in order to bring the Unified
Development Ordinance up-to-date after careful review, occasional adjustments
are necessary, including those associated with the City's Extraterritorial
Jurisdiction, (ii) this amendment is necessary to clarify when ETJ members can
vote on City of Southport issues in the City of Southport and its
extraterritorial jurisdiction, and (iii) it concurs with the rights, privileges
and duties allowed by NC General Statute § 160A 362.;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 11th day of February, 2010.
By:
/s/ Robert Howard, Mayor

RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF CONVERTING THE BRUNSWICK COMMUNITY HOSPITAL TO A
VETERAN'S AFFAIRS CLINIC AS A LONG TERM COST EFFECTIVE OPTION TO MEET THE
MEDICAL NEEDS OF AREA VETERANS
WHEREAS, Brunswick County is one of the fastest growing counties in America and
the veteran population has increased significantly over the last decade
reaching an estimated 12,656 today; and
WHEREAS, there is a significant need for an additional Veterans Affairs Clinic
or Medical Center in southeastern North Carolina to serve the medical needs of
over 77,000 veterans; and
WHEREAS, the Brunswick Community Hospital, currently operated by Novant will be
vacated in 2011 when the new Novant Hospital is opened for operation; and
WHEREAS, the Brunswick Community Hospital is a full-service facility that
includes approximately 111,096 square feet and 60 beds and is centrally located
in Brunswick County on US Highway 17 near the intersection of NC Highway 211
and is accessible to all areas of southeastern North Carolina and northeastern
South Carolina and is currently served by all of the necessary utilities and
infrastructure, and
WHEREAS, the County Commissioners are willing to negotiate a competitive lease
or sale arrangement for the property to be used for a Veterans Affairs medical
facility and the renovation costs associated with the facility would pale in
comparison to the proposed costs of leasing the site and constructing a new
facility in New Hanover County; and
WHEREAS, the 100,000 square foot facility proposed for the Wilmington super
clinic has an exorbitant project construction budget of $95 million and an
unfavorable recurring annual site lease of over $200,000 per year; and
WHEREAS, federal dollars should be spent as strategically as possible to
provide the best possible facilities and care to area veterans at the lowest
possible cost; and
WHEREAS, the preliminary project information provided does not appear to meet
the test of cost effective capital facilities planning and frugal utilization
of federal dollars and it appears that there is at least one viable lower cost
option in Brunswick County that has not been equitably evaluated.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen do
hereby respectfully request that the United States Senate, House of
Representatives and the Veterans Affairs Officials evaluate the feasibility and
potential for converting the Brunswick Community Hospital in Supply, North
Carolina for use as a Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic as a more cost
effective capital and operating cost option to provide high quality medical
services to area veterans who deserve a convenient facility.
Adopted on this the 11th day of February, 2010.
/s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
/s/Regina W. Alexander, MMC, Clerk

ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/
IMAGES/0-0-0-46.jpg]
WHEREAS, in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of
Agriculture that a special day be set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS, this holiday called Arbor Day , was first observed with the planting
of more than a million trees in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS, Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS, trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and
water, cut heating and cooling costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air,
produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for wildlife, and
WHEREAS, trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes,
fuel for our fires, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic
vitality of business areas, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual
renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE , I , Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, N.C. do
hereby proclaim March 19, 2010 as ARBOR DAY in the City and urge all citizens
to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees and woodlands, and
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote
the well being of this and future generations.
DATED, this 11th day of March, 2010.
/s/ Robert D. Howard

MARCH 2, 2010
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
MARCH 2, 2010     7:30 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, NC
 
PRESENT:         Robert D. Howard, Mayor
            Aldermen Nelson Adams, Ed Boguskie, Donnie Potter, Kenneth Karn,
            Mary Ellen Poole and Jwantana Frink
ABSENT:         None
STAFF:         M. Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, MMC, Clerk
OTHERS:          Amy Nelson, Director of Planning
            Wayne Strickland, Building Inspector
            Jerry Dove, Chief of Police
A.
Call to Order - 6:00 p.m.
Mayor Howard called the special meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
1)    Welcome - Mayor Pro Tempore Poole
Mayor Pro Tempore Poole gave words of welcome.
2)    Invocation
Chief Jerry Dove pronounced the invocation.
3)    Local Elected Officials' Ethics Statement
Mayor Howard cited the following for the benefit of Board members.
"If any members know of any conflict of interest or the appearance of a
conflict of interest with respect to matters on the agenda, please so state at
this time."
4)   Adoption of Agenda
Alderman Boguskie motioned, seconded by Alderman Frink to approve the agenda,
vote carried. Motion passed 6-0
B.
Board of Aldermen Comments
Mayor Howard stated that the appearance of signs in the City is an unresolved
issue. The Aldermen, Planning Board and staff have reviewed the language in the
Sign Ordinance i.e. community surveys and public meetings in order to gauge
public input. He explained that it is necessary that the City regulates the
type, size, and location of signs to encourage their effective use as a means
of communication, to provide quality and equity among sign owners and for those
businesses that wish to use signs. He stated that the City wants to insure that
there is reasonable sign control, aesthetic enhancements and that the City's
Ordinance promotes signage that is orderly, appropriately sized, illuminated
and located. Good sign management improves the ability of the public to locate
businesses by reducing sign clutter, enhancing the aesthetics, and creating a
place where people want to spend time and money. He explained that the Board
must decide to direct staff to enforce the current ordinance or recommend
viable alternatives for consideration by staff, Planning Board and the Board of
Aldermen.
Alderman Poole stated that she was a member of the Planning Board when the sign
survey was conducted. Public comments were received and a work session held
with citizens and business owners regarding signage. She asked after citizen
input that the Board consider a solution for the aesthetics of the City, safety
issues regarding illegal signage, and the needs of the business community to
advertise their location and merchandise.
Alderman Boguskie stated the signs are a problem which affects the citizens,
visitors and businesses. The Board must support the Unified Development
Ordinance and be in compliance with ADA and NCDOT requirements. The City needs
to develop a workable plan and stay within those guidelines, and support the
businesses.
Alderman Karn told the Board that he contacted the Department of Transportation
and was told that enforcement along the state right of way is complaint driven.
However, if DOT sees a violation, the signs can be removed without notifying
the owner. He also spoke with Angela Massey at the Division 3 right of way
office and she explained how the width of rights of way is calculated. Utility
poles are the guidelines that they use and it is just inside their right of
way; therefore, anything that is in between the building and utility pole line
is considered not in the state right of way. He spoke with Robert Murphy at the
NC. Department of Commerce who works with the N.C. Main Street Program and a
former Planning employee with the City of Wilmington who wrote the regulations
in Wilmington for the use of "A" frame signs which gives specific regulations
and recommend that all signs be permitted. He stated the City is not attacking
merchants, but trying to address the aesthetics of the City while supporting
the businesses.
C.
Comments by City Manager
City Manager Thornton reiterated the importance of the business community to
the City and working with the merchants. He stated that there are liability
issues concerning signs on public rights of way which are illegal and the City
cannot ignore these because of safety factors.
D.
Power Point Presentation on Signs - Amy Nelson, Director of Planning
Ms. Amy Nelson, City Planner presented a power point presentation showing the
various signs in the City and the obstruction of public rights of way which is
illegal in accordance with City Code Section 16-8. She also noted that under
Section 17-2, General Provisions, and (B) Permit Requirements where sign
permits are required and failure to apply for one is in violation of City Code.
Ms. Nelson showed signs of various cities and noted that staff is currently
working on an update to the sign ordinance with input from the public while
attempting to retain the visual beauty of Southport. She also noted that the
City is seeking to purchase and install way finding signs.
E.
Public Comments
The following persons addressed the Board on the sign issue:
Mr. Frank Vacirca, 3898 Timber Stream Drive (Harbor Oak), asked that the best
interest of the community be served including support of businesses.
Rita Sanders, Live Oak Nutrition, spoke in support of having a sign on Howe
Street for visibility because their business is not on the main street and the
sign directs citizens to their place of business.
Emily Humphreys, Port City Java, Howe Street stated the trees cover most of her
signage and the sign in front of her store directs customers to her business.
She asked that the ordinance revision allow "A" frame signs.
Carol Baker, Waterfront Gifts, 117 S. Howe Street stated the ordinance on the
books has not been enforced. The signs and clutter on state and city rights of
way prohibits the flow of pedestrian traffic and poses a danger. The City
should enforce the current ordinance and make amendments if necessary.
Judi Zorich, Cape Fear Jewelers, 102 E. Moore Street, stated she has witnessed
worse problems than signs. The drive ups to the ATM machine across the street
from their place of business blocks access for citizens in wheel chairs which
should be addressed.
Kathy Rebeck, 1306 N. Atlantic (Acupuncturist) stated that there are no street
signs at 13th Street and she is unable to give people directions to her office.
Since Southport is a town with small businesses, signs are an inexpensive way
to let people know that they are in business. She agreed that the signs should
look nice and be in a safe location. She asked the Board to consider the small
businesses and allow them to attract customers by use of these signs
D. Crews owner of a former business stated that some of the businesses depend
on signs to advertise and asked that enforcement of the sign ordinance be
placed on hold for at least 30 -60 days to gauge where merchants are
economically because many small businesses are closing their doors.
Katie Stewart, 821 Memory Lane, owner and operator of Old South Tour Company
stated businesses depend on tourism and she uses an "A" frame sign. She only
places her sign out when she is working and removes it once her day is
completed. She asked the Board to keep businesses in mind when making its
decision.
Pamela Sexton, 122 Howe Street, owner of Cattail Cottage, stated that it is her
belief that sandwich board/ A frame signs add charm to the City and she has
never received a complaint from her customers. She has an "A" frame sign in
front of her business because the large trees block visibility. She stated
trees, trashcans, utility poles; etc should be taken care of before signs are
addressed. She asked that business owners be included in the dialogue with the
City before erecting way finding signs.
Penny Watkins, 715 N. Howe Street, owner of Boo & Roo's Gift Store (Town Gate)
stated that she purchased a custom made "A" frame sign to draw customers to her
store. The sign is effective because it brings in customers and is taken down
at night. The sign is placed in a grassy area and does not pose a hazard or
obstruct public safety. The guidelines should be written to pertain to each
block or section of the City on an individual basis, because no two areas in
the City are the same. Disposing of the signs will be devastating to the
businesses, and urged the Board not to take this action.
Michelle Archangelo, of Elkton Md. and a visitor to the area stated she would
not know that many of the businesses exist without the signs.
Rebecca Funderburk, 416 N. Howe, owner of Rebecca Fabrications and a Massage
Practice at 1306 N. Atlantic spoke in support of the signs because of their
uniqueness and the character they bring to the City. She stated with the
economic climate, that this is the wrong time to tax businesses about signs.
Nancy Clookie, 3488 Members Club, states Southport is a wonderful place to live
and urged the Board to carefully weigh their decisions because whatever actions
taken will affect the businesses when they are trying to survive.
Brian Kimball, Loco Jo's Bar & Grill on Howe Street.  Stated signs are vital to
his business survival. The sign ordinance has been on the books for years and
it is his belief that this is the wrong time to enforce it because businesses
need all the help that they can get to survive.
Richard Bandera, 309 Clarendon Avenue, business owner, and a member of the
Planning Board. Mr. Bandera, representing the Planning Board explained that the
Planning Board has been working to understand sign limitations under the UDO,
how to address violations that exist with signs in the rights of way i.e.
differences on the state right of way, safety and visual issues for the
business district. The Planning Board is seeking ways to separate this from
City managed streets to determine if anything can be done for the businesses.
He stated it is difficult for the Board to advise the Aldermen when they do not
know how the right of way on a state road is defined i.e. beginning and end.
They want to treat the businesses fair and having this information would help.
The Planning Board recommends that the UDO be revisited on City managed streets
to allow signage types supported by the merchant survey. The survey showed that
68% of the participating merchants believed that the "A" frame signs are good
for the business district. Ms. Nelson, City Planner is researching various
municipalities that allow "A" frame signs on public sidewalks under a special
permitting process.
The Planning Board hopes that this could apply to Southport which would be a
win situation by managing safety accessibility, visual concerns and promote
area businesses. The Planning Board recommends consideration of way finding
signs which are allowed to be constructed in the state right of way. The
Planning Board further supports way finding signs because they will address
some concerns and direct visitors to some of the underserved business
districts, historic sites and recreational opportunities in the City. However,
the signs do not allow business advertisement but point visitors and citizens
in the right direction. Mr. Bandera noted that Downtown Southport, Inc. has
been active in pursuing matching grants through the Main Street Program and he
asked if they are available that they be made public.
Mayor Howard thanked the public for their input and stated the City is working
in the best interest of Southport and the businesses. He encouraged all to work
together and provide input.
Alderman Boguskie noted that the UDO can be changed, however if signs were not
permitted, they are illegal and ADA rules must be adhered to by the City.
Alderman Adams stated his support of the merchants and recommended a Task Force
be established with merchants, Planning Board member(s) and staff to make
revisions to the sign ordinance.
Alderman Karn presented a section of the Carolina Beach Ordinance addressing
signs i.e. indemnification, size, etc. He stated the City needs to be protected
and agreed to the establishment of a Task Force.
Alderman Frink stated the City needs neat, safe and attractive signs. She also
agreed to the establishment of a Task Force.
Alderman Potter stated the City does not want to penalize businesses but needs
to secure liability for the City. The Board understands and supports the
businesses.
Alderman Poole agreed with establishing a Task Force.
Alderman Adams motioned to establish a Task Force comprised of staff, Planning
Board member(s) and merchant representative(s) and to table action on the
removal of signs until April, seconded by Alderman Poole. Discussion: Alderman
Potter expressed concern about liability to the City and asked the City Manager
to consult with the Attorney on this issue. Mayor Howard stated this effort can
work only if everyone involved works together and participate in the process.
Mayor Howard stated that he will meet with the City Manager, staff and Planning
Board to develop a Task Force and he requested three (3) names be provided to
him by the merchants to representative them on the Task Force. Notification
will also be given of the meetings. Alderman Adams stated that the liability
issue had been discussed and the City is reaching out to the merchants; if some
of them are not willing to cooperate, the City will need to give a directive
that all liability signs be removed. Mayor reiterated that all signs be taken
in at night. No further discussion, the vote was unanimous. Passed 6-0
F.
Adjournment - 7:38 p.m.
No further business, motion by Alderman Boguskie, seconded by Alderman Frink to
Adjourn. Vote unanimous. Passed 6-0

e)   Amendment Chapter 16, Section 16-4, House Moving
Alderman Potter motioned, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to adopt the amendment
to Chapter 16, Section 16-4 of the House Moving Code. The vote of approval was
unanimous. Motion passed 6-0
AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT CODE OF ORDINANCES
TEXT AMENDMENT # 10-0208-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Code of Ordinances
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Chapter
16, STREETS AND SIDEWALKS, Article I. IN GENERAL, Section 16-4 "House moving"
is hereby amended by replacing the original section with the following:
(a)   APPROVAL AND BOND REQUIRED.
No person shall move any house, building or other structure along, upon or
across the public streets or sidewalks without a written permit issued by the
Building Inspector, and a deposit to cover damage done to any street or
sidewalk or to any property of any person or the City. This deposit shall be in
the sum of $5,000 and shall be delivered to the City at least one City business
day prior to moving any structure within the City limits or its
extraterritorial jurisdiction. Such deposit may be cash, certified or cashier's
check, or a bond issued by a surety licensed to do business in North Carolina.
This deposit may be used by the City to pay for any damage done to any street
or sidewalk or to any property of any person or the City resulting from the
moving of any house, building or other structure. After completion of the move,
the Building Inspector and Public Services Director shall make an inspection to
determine if any damage occurred as a result of said move, and any portion of
said deposit not required in order to pay for damages shall be returned to the
applicant.
(b)   LICENSE REQUIREMENT.
No person may move a house, building or other structure along, upon or across
the streets, sidewalks or other public ways of the City without first being
licensed as a house mover by the North Carolina Department of Transportation or
its successor agency as provided in G.S. Ch. 20, Art. 16 as it presently exists
or shall be hereafter amended. Provided, however, that such license shall not
be required for individuals moving their own buildings from or to property
owned individually by those persons. This section shall not relieve an
individual of the requirement of posting a deposit, or obtaining a permit as
hereinafter provided, nor shall it relieve an individual of the requirement
that the applicant prove their financial responsibility as hereinafter
provided.
(c)   PERMIT REQUIREMENTS AND PROCEDURES.
No person may move a house, building or other structure along, upon or across
the streets, sidewalks or other public ways of the City without first obtaining
a permit from the City Building Inspector. Any person wishing to obtain a
permit shall apply to the Building Inspector on a form approved by the City for
a permit at least two weeks prior to the date that the person wishes to move
the structure. The Building Inspector may reduce the two week period for good
cause shown. The application shall be completed in its entirety and shall be
accompanied by an application fee to be set by the Board of Aldermen and also
by the following: (i) a travel plan. The travel plan shall show the proposed
route, the time estimated for each segment of the move and a plan to handle
traffic so that no one delay to other roadway users shall exceed 20 minutes. In
addition, the travel plan will show all intersections, traffic lights and other
locations where a bottleneck of traffic could potentially be created; (ii)
proof that the applicant has made satisfactory arrangements with any person or
other entity whose power, telephone, cable television or other lines will be
affected by the move; (iii) a list and description of all utilities, trees and
other equipment, poles, structures and appurtenances which will need to be
altered or moved along the route of the travel plan; (iv) a list of all
services required from the City with regard to police personnel, personnel of
the Public Services Department, and other personnel of the City, including but
not limited to the number of personnel needed, manpower hours estimated to be
used, and such other information as may be required by the City in order to
estimate the cost of the move to the City.
(d)   PROOF OF FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY.
In addition to the other requirements set forth in subsection (c) above, the
applicant must file documentation of their financial responsibility. All
applicants shall possess motor vehicle insurance for bodily injury to or death
of one or more persons in any accident, and for injury to or destruction of
property of others in any one accident with a minimum coverage of $350,000
combined single limit of liability. Additionally, the applicant shall have in
effect comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum coverage of
$350,000 combined single limit of liability, including coverage of operations
on state streets and highways that are not covered by motor vehicle insurance,
and Workers' Compensation insurance complying with the requirements of G.S.
Chapter 97. Proof of all insurance coverage effective through the date of the
proposed move issued by the insurance carrier(s), equivalent to that required
for licensed house movers by G.S. § 20-359.1 as it presently exists or may be
hereafter re-codified, shall be considered satisfactory proof of financial
responsibility and the fact that an applicant is licensed as a house mover by
the department of transportation shall be sufficient to prove his compliance
with this section. In the case of an individual moving their own structure to
or from their own property and not required to be licensed as a house mover,
the applicant must provide documentation satisfactory to the Building Inspector
that the applicant has appropriate and adequate insurance coverage and a copy
of this documentation shall be kept on file in the Building Inspector's office
until the move is completed. The adequacy of the insurance coverage shall be
determined in the reasonable discretion of the issuing officer or City Manager
based upon all circumstances disclosed in the application and supporting
documentation.
(e)   ISSUANCE OF PERMIT.
The applicant shall review their travel plan with the Building Inspector and
the Chief of the Police Department or his designee and if the route cannot
accommodate the move due to roadway weight limits, or will cause undue
interruption of traffic flow or will otherwise create an unduly hazardous
condition, the permit shall not be issued. Approved travel plans are required
before obtaining a permit. Permits will not be issued for holidays, weekends or
evening hours unless there are extenuating circumstances approved by the
Building Inspector, Police Chief and Public Services Director. The Building
Inspector shall review the application with the Director of the Public Services
Department to determine that the applicant has made satisfactory arrangements
for the disconnection of all public utilities under the control of the City and
that the disconnections can be accomplished in an appropriate manner. Nothing
contained herein shall be interpreted to require the Building Inspector to
issue a permit if, in his judgment, the proposed move cannot be made safely, or
if, in his judgment, the applicant has not made appropriate arrangements with
power, telephone, cable television or other utility suppliers, or if, in his
judgment, the applicant has not made appropriate arrangements with the City for
the disconnection of public utilities under the control of the City.
(f)   CONDITIONS FOR VOIDING PERMIT.
The permit may be revoked by the Building Inspector or any police officer of
the City if any conditions of the permit are violated. Upon any violation, the
permit must be surrendered upon demand of the Building Inspector or a police
officer and a new permit obtained before proceeding. Misrepresentation of
information on application to obtain a permit, fraudulently obtaining a permit,
alteration of a permit or unauthorized use of a permit will render the permit
void.
(g)   APPEAL.
An applicant shall have the right to appeal the denial of his application to
the City Manager within ten days of the mailing of notification of the denial
of the permit to the address given in the application. Any such denial shall be
without prejudice to the applicant's rights to submit another application with
alternate plans until an acceptable route is determined, if such an acceptable
route exists. In addition, the applicant may appeal the revocation of the
permit to the City Manager within ten days of notification of revocation.
(h)   LIABILITY OF MOVER.
The permittee shall be responsible for injury to persons or damage to property
of any kind resulting from his acts or omissions and by accepting the permit
agrees to indemnify and hold the City harmless for any claims arising out of
his conduct, actions or omissions.
(i)   REMOVAL AND REPLACEMENT OF OBSTRUCTIONS.
All obstructions or impediments, including traffic signals, signs, poles and
utility lines, will be removed immediately prior to and replaced immediately
after the move at the expense of the mover, subject to the approval and
satisfaction of the City, provided that arrangements for and approval from the
owner of such signals, signs and lines is obtained by the applicant.
This ordinance shall be effective upon the date of adoption, this 11th day of
March, 2010.
City of Southport
By:
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor

Regina W. Alexander, MMC

g)    Fleet Fueling System
City Manager Thornton explained that the City has an underground fuel storage
tank and the state will monitor these more closely and eventually require a
licensed operator. As a result of changes, staff is recommending a fleet
fueling card system.
Mr. Cardwell, Public Services Director stated during the inspection in
December, the State Inspector requested the fuel tanks be dugged downward to
the hose connection to verify that the City has a European style suction
system. The cost to remove the concrete and tank is $4200. If the City does not
pass inspection, an employee will have to attend and pass a class in Raleigh to
become a designated operator of the City tanks. He will then have to train a
Class C Operator who will need to be present anytime a vehicle is filled. The
fuel pumps will have to be shut off when the garage closes unless a scada
control system is installed which will notify an employee at home when a
vehicle is being filled.
Alderman Potter motioned to authorize the City Manager to proceed with the
fleet fueling card system, seconded by Alderman Poole. Vote unanimous. Passed
6-0

the end of Moore Street between Caswell and Bay, and allow parking down Caswell
towards Bay.

Committee met April 7. Johnny Faulk and David Fox made a presentation on
Southport's Grease Control Ordinance. The ordinance requires cooking
establishments to have an oil and sand interceptor in place. With 42 cooking
establishments, only five are non-compliant and staff will work to bring them
into compliance. This is a county requirement and must be enforced. Mr.
Cardwell gave an update on the sewer reversal project which is on schedule.
Impact fees were discussed and it was decided that the Utilities Director and
the City Manager would review the fees and submit figures to the Board in order
to have a track record with the county. The City does not sell sewer outside of
the City limits, but as a result of meter location and the new line, the City
can accept additional clients. Costs will need to be addressed along with Board
approval for this change.
Sign Task Force: Alderman Karn reported that the Sign Task Force met twice and
discussed changes that will be recommended to the Board. DOT provided

presented to the Planning Board.

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City's
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the city's land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
a proposed amendment to Article 10 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on April 8, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) this type of use or business is not
sufficiently addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance and should be, (ii)
this amendment is necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the
Central Business and Business Districts, and (iii) regulation of this uses is
necessary to promote the public safety and general welfare of the community by
allowing walk up style restaurants in the more pedestrian-oriented areas of the
City;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 8th day of April, 2010.
City of Southport

e)   Discussion of Absenteeism Policy for Planning and Board of Adjustment
Alderman Karn read Article 3, Administrative Mechanisms, Part 1, Planning and
Zoning Board, Section 3-1 Membership and Vacancies which states "faithful
attendance at the meetings of the Board is considered a pre-requisite for
maintenance of membership on the Board. A vacancy shall exist on the Board if a
member is absent from twenty-five (25%) or more of the Board's meetings within
a twelve month period, and said vacancy may be declared and filled by the Board
of Aldermen." He explained that the Unified Development Ordinance makes no
provision for excused absences. It was the consensus of the Planning Committee
that it would not add a provision for excused absences. He stated that as a
member of the Committee, he attempted to communicate his concerns to the
Planning Board member but he was not receptive. Planning Board Chairmen,
present and past told him that they did not receive notification of this
member's absences. Alderman Karn stated that Aldermen are tasked with enforcing
the city ordinances and this is not a personal attack. Alderman Karn motioned,
seconded by Alderman Boguskie to remove James Powell from the Planning Board
due to excessive absences and to direct the Clerk to advertise the vacancy.
Discussion: Alderman Poole stated the UDO and City Code needs to correlate. She
explained during her tenure as Chair of the Planning Board, she was not
notified of absences; which could have been the result of the agenda packet
that is provided to each member stating if they are unable to attend meetings
to contact the Board Clerk. As a result of these instructions, the Chairman was
not notified. She stated that this will be addressed in the new procedures.
Alderman Potter stated if the Ordinance/UDO is going to be amended to include
new provisions, he suggested postponing action. Mayor Howard stated the
attendance rule has never been enforced and there are alternate members on the
Planning Board to take the place of members that are absent. He likened this to
the Sign Ordinance which has not been enforced; however the City has allowed
signs to stay in place until the ordinance is modified. He stated that the
Southport Community is built on volunteers and encouraged the Board not to
proceed with this removal.  Alderman Boguskie stated that he is in favor of
enforcing ordinances in the City Code; if not, they should be removed from the
book. Alderman Adams questioned the timing. Mayor called for the vote: 2 ayes
Aldermen Karn and Boguskie. 4 noes , Aldermen Adams, Poole, Frink and Potter.
Motion failed 4-2

City Manager Comments
Mr. Thornton informed the Board that the urban centers (five metropolitan
areas) of North Carolina are seeking a change in the funding equity method in
North Carolina. These monies are used to fund roads in the state. The urban
centers propose to change the formula in order to get more funding as they have
been the recipient of transportation improvements i.e. loops, four lane roads,
etc. for the past 20 years. If the formula is changed by the N. C. General
Assembly, it will delay projects especially in rural areas. City Manager
Thornton asked the Board to adopt a resolution to send to congressional
representatives opposing the formula change. It was Board consensus that the
Manager draft a resolution for Board review and it will be acted upon at the
May meeting.
City Manager Thornton thanked Mayor Howard for speaking before a legislative
committee in Raleigh on behalf of the City to maintain local control of its ABC
system. He explained that making local Boards regional would take away
revenues.
City Manager Thornton informed the Board that they should receive a draft
budget in May.

Board Comments
Mayor Howard stated that he spoke before a joint legislative study committee
asking them to carefully consider and deliberate reasonable reforms while
perpetuating the integrity of local controlled ABC systems. He explained that
the City of Southport's Act was approved in the legislative session on May 24,
1957 with voter approval and Southport received the first revenues in 1959. He
provided some facts to the Committee about Southport's ABC Board and store,
which has excellent management and sound business principles with cost controls
in place. The ABC Store returns 12.23% of revenues to the City from sales. He
stated that local municipalities and Brunswick County are unified on
maintaining local control of its ABC stores.

procedures in place for the City Manager and Clerk. He and Mayor Pro Tem Poole
reviewed several evaluation forms from other areas including the League and
developed a process for evaluating the City Manager. They selected questions
that best identify Southport for the evaluation. The process allows the
employee to perform a self evaluation and written narrative which will be
returned to the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem. Upon receipt of the City Manager's
self evaluation and narrative, copies will be given to Board members and each
Alderman will complete their individual performance evaluation. The results of
the evaluation will be compiled and the Board will meet in closed session for
discussion. Alderman Poole reviewed the seven step process with the Board.

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City's
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the city's land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
proposed amendments to Articles 10, 12 and 16 of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered these matters and has recommended
that these proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance be
approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on May 13, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding these issues; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that these proposed amendments to
the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with the Southport CAMA Land
Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) this type of use or business
is not addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance and should be, (ii) these
amendments are necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the
Highway Commercial District, and (iii) regulation of this use is necessary to
promote the public safety and general welfare of the community by allowing RV
Parks in the City;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 13th day of May, 2010.
City of Southport
By:
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
