AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
TEXT AMENDMENT # 10-0318-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With
Respect to Conditional Uses
AMEND:
1) ARTICLE 10: TABLE OF PERMITTED USES:
The Table of Permitted Uses is hereby amended by adding "Recreational Vehicle
Parks, Private", and by placing a "C" entry in the HC (Highway Commercial)
column.
2) ARTICLE 12: ZONING & CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT APPROVAL
Section 12-19: Supplemental Regulations
"Regulations for Conditional Uses", is hereby amended by adding a new section,
to be inserted in alphabetical sequence, to read as follows:
Use: Recreational Vehicle Parks, Private, Conditional Use District: HC
Use - Recreational Vehicle Parks, Private. The following specific provisions
shall be met as minimum standards prior to the approval of any private business
engaging in recreational vehicle parks, hereinafter referred to as RV Park, as
a conditional use in the Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. For the
purpose of this chapter, Recreational Vehicle Park, RV Park and Travel Trailer
Park have the same meaning.
(A)    Design Standards
(1)   An RV Park shall require minimum gross land area of three acres.
(2)   A minimum of 8% of the total land area shall be devoted to accessible
common open spaces intended for recreational use. These open spaces are
separate from the individual RV sites, hereinafter referred to as campsites,
and shall be grouped and of character suitable for active and passive
recreation and shall be reasonably located for safe and convenient access to
residents. Sufficiency of size of each open space shall be determined by the
Zoning Board of Adjustment.
(3)   A buffer strip of at least ten feet in width shall be maintained along
all public road frontages and along the perimeter of the RV Park (see Section
18-1). These buffers shall be free of all encroachment by campsites, buildings
or structures, parking areas or impervious coverage.
(4)   An RV Park shall contain at least 15 individual campsites.
(5)   All campsites shall be located on land with elevations that are not
susceptible to flooding. Campsites shall be graded to prevent any water from
ponding or accumulating within the park. Each campsite shall be properly graded
to obtain a reasonably flat area and to provide adequate drainage away from the
space. This requirement is not intended to circumvent FEMA regulations or the
City of Southport Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance (Section 21).
(6)   Each campsite shall be located at least 30 feet from the edge of any
publicly-maintained street or road.
(7)   RV Park shall be designed to prevent overcrowding, fire hazards, and to
provide sufficient light and air. In no case shall an individual campsite be
less than 1,250 square feet in area or have a minimum average width of less
than 25 feet. In no case shall an RV be parked closer than 15 feet to another
RV.
(8)   No campsite shall have direct vehicular access to a public road.
(9)   Each campsite shall be identified by a permanent number which may not be
changed. The appropriate number of each campsite must be permanent and visibly
displayed on each space. Each number shall be placed on a concrete, wood,
metal, or any permanent post and conspicuously located on the campsite.
(10)   Each RV Park and any future additions thereto must meet the minimum
standards and requirements set forth in the International Building Codes with
North Carolina Amendments for sanitation and plumbing installations,
accommodations, use and any associated parking. These structures may also
contain a retail sales counter and/or coin operated machine for the RV Park
residents' use, provided there is no exterior advertising. Vending machines
also may be permitted in a sheltered area provided there is no exterior
advertising on the structure. All service structures shall be maintained in a
clean and sanitary condition and kept in good repair at all times. Structures
shall be safely and adequately illuminated. Facilities shall be easily
accessible and conveniently located to all users of the RV Park. All structures
shall be constructed in accordance with the International Building Code with
North Carolina Amendments, and shall meet Building Code and/or UDO setback
requirements.
(11)   In addition to the prohibition on advertising on vending structures, the
sign regulations for the base zoning district in which the RV Park is located
shall apply.
(B)   Parking and Streets
(1)   Parking shall be provided in compliance with Article 16, Off-Street
Parking and Off-Street Loading Requirements. Parking within the RV Park shall
take place off an internal street within designated parking areas only.
(2)   No campsite within an RV Park may directly access a public street. Access
to all campsites and accessory structures within the RV Park shall be made
using internal streets.
(3)   Internal Street Standards
(a)    One or two-way streets shall be used throughout the RV Park. Such
streets shall be well-maintained and clearly identified. All streets within the
RV Park shall be privately owned and maintained. Each campsite shall abut an
internal street within the RV Park.
(b)    Streets shall have a minimum width of 20 feet for two-way streets and 14
feet for one-way streets.
(c)    Any dead-end shall be provided with a permanent turnaround with a
minimum radius of 40 feet.
(d)    All internal streets within the RV Park shall be surfaced with a minimum
of six inches of compacted stone and shall be capable of supporting the imposed
load of fire apparatus in accordance with the Fire Apparatus Access Roads
Standard in the North Carolina Fire Code (NC Fire Code Section 503, fire
apparatus weighing at least 75,000 pounds) and be equipped with adequate and
suitable drainage facilities.
(e)    Maintenance of all internal streets and drainage facilities shall be the
responsibility of the owner of the RV Park. Such streets shall be maintained in
a manner to be free from pot holes, breaks in the pavement, rough surfaces,
ponding of water and associated problems which would impede or cause hazards to
motor vehicles. Speed reduction bumps on paved internal streets are
permissible, but they shall be painted and appropriate signs indicating the
bump must be placed along the street.
(f)    All internal streets shall be subject to annual inspections by the City
of Southport Code Enforcement Officer or Building Inspector per Section 106 of
the North Carolina Fire Code.
(4)   External Access
(a)    An RV Park shall not be located on through lots. RV Park roads shall be
designed to slow traffic.
(b)    An RV Park with only one point of external access shall provide at least
one permanent turnaround within the campsite. All external access must be
approved by the Southport Public Services Director or the North Carolina
Department of Transportation if the connecting street is a state-maintained
road.
(c)    Any proposed electronic vehicular access gates or barricades must be
siren-activated for Emergency Vehicle access.
(C)   Utilities
(1)    Water
(a)    An accessible, adequate, safe and potable supply of water shall be
required. Where public, municipal, or community water systems exist within
1,000 feet of the park, the developer shall connect to such system.
(b)    When a public water supply is not available, a community water supply
may be developed and its supply used exclusively in accordance with local and
state regulations and standards of the Division of Environmental Management, NC
Department of Environment, Health, and Natural Resources codified in 15A NCAC
2C. Each water supply well shall be located so as to maintain a minimum
pollution-free radius as specified in N.C.G.S. 15A-18C-0203. Siting of well
locations should be discussed with the Brunswick County health authority.
(c)    Internal water distribution systems shall be installed in accordance
with minimum City Standards.
(2)   Sewer
(a)    Approval by the Brunswick County Health Department shall be required for
any installation, alteration or use of a sewage disposal system. All sewage
wastes from each park, including wastes from toilets, showers, bathtubs,
lavatories, wash basins, sinks, and water using appliances not herein
mentioned, shall be disposed of by an approved sewage disposal system.
(b)    Adequate and safe sewage disposal facilities shall be provided in all RV
Parks. Where public, municipal, or community sewer systems exist within 1,000
feet of the RV Park, the developer shall connect to such system.
(c)    When a public, municipal, or community system does not exist within
1,000 feet, a centralized sewage disposal and treatment system complying with
the requirements of the North Carolina Department of Environment, Health and
Natural Resources shall be provided. Individual septic tank systems may be
allowed in accordance with the requirements of Title 15A - Department of
Environment, Health and Natural Resources - Chapter 18 - Environmental Health
Subchapter 18A - Sanitation Section .1900 - Sewage Treatment And Disposal
Systems.
(d)    Each RV Park shall provide at least one sewage dumping station for each
100 campsites which are not equipped with individual sewer and water
connections. Sewage dumping stations shall be approved by the Brunswick County
Health Department or the North Carolina Division of Water Quality.
(D)   RV Park Operation
(1)    General
(a)    The person to whom an operating permit for an RV Park is issued shall
operate the RV Park in compliance with this Ordinance and shall be responsible
for maintaining the RV Park, its facilities and equipment in good repair and in
a clean and sanitary condition.
(b)    The RV Park owner shall notify its visitors of all applicable provisions
of this Ordinance and inform them of their responsibilities under this
Ordinance.
(c)    The RV Park owner shall be responsible for refuse collection. Storage,
collection, and disposal of refuse shall be so managed as not to create health
hazards, rodent harborage, insect-breeding areas, accident, fire hazards, or
air pollution. Any refuse storage devices shall be enclosed on three sides by
opaque fencing material. The method of garbage disposal shall be noted on the
plan and approved by the City of Southport Zoning Board of Adjustment.
(d)    Swimming pools or bathing areas shall be installed, altered, improved,
and used in compliance with applicable County and State Health Services
regulations. Any bathing area shall require the approval of the Brunswick
County Health Department.
(e)    Except as specifically permitted by this paragraph, it shall be unlawful
to locate a mobile home in an RV Park. Two mobile homes shall be permitted to
be located within a RV Park to be used as residences of persons responsible for
the operation and/or maintenance of the RV Park.
(f)    No more than one RV camper may be parked on any one campsite. RV campers
shall not be permitted on parcels, lots, or spaces other than those approved
through these regulations.
(g)    The transfer of title of campsites, either by sale or by any other
manner shall be prohibited within an RV Park as long as the RV Park is in
operation.
(h)    All RV campers must be placed individually on approved campsites where
all design standards and utilities have been completed.
(i)    Junked or wrecked vehicles shall be prohibited in an RV Park.
(2)   Inspection
The Brunswick County Health Department, the City of Southport Building
Inspector, the City of Southport Code Enforcement Officer and the Public
Services Department are hereby authorized and directed to make such inspections
as are necessary to determine satisfactory compliance with this Ordinance. It
shall be the duty of the owners of RV Parks to give these agencies free access
to such premises at reasonable times for inspections.
3)    ARTICLE 16 OFF STREET PARKING AND OFF-STREET LOADING REQUIREMENTS
Section 16-3: Minimum Parking Requirements
"Minimum Parking Requirements", is hereby amended by adding a new section, to
be inserted in alphabetical sequence, to read as follows:
Recreational Vehicle (RV) Parks, Private   Two (2) parking spaces at each
campsite + 1 per 500 SF of enclosed area for offices, maintenance facilities,
etc. within the park.
This ordinance is effective upon the date of adoption, May 13, 2010.

b)    Resolution opposing revising the N. C. Transportation Equity formula
City Manager Thornton presented a resolution for Board consideration. He
explained that the Metropolitan Mayors Coalition is seeking to change the North
Carolina Equity Formula which has worked well in the past; and if changed, the
smaller counties/municipalities would receive less funding. Mayor Howard stated
his support of the resolution.
Alderman Karn motioned to adopt the resolution in opposition to revising the
North Carolina Transportation Equity Formula, seconded by Alderman Frink. Vote
unanimous. Passed 4-0
Resolution in Opposition to Revising of the North Carolina Transportation
Equity Formula
WHEREAS, the North Carolina General Assembly implemented the Transportation
Equity formula twenty years ago as a result of the 1989 Highway Trust Fund law;
and
WHEREAS, the Transportation Equity Formula provides a fair means of
distributing the various types of transportation funds; and
WHEREAS, the North Carolina Metropolitan Mayors Coalition has requested that
MPO's, RPO's, municipalities and counties endorse resolutions supporting the
evaluation and revision of the Transportation Equity Formula; and
WHEREAS, it is expected that the Cape Fear Area Rural Planning Organization's
member local governments would be adversely impacted by any changes to the
Transportation Equity Formula.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Southport Board of Aldermen opposes the
efforts of the North Carolina Metropolitan Mayors Coalition in seeking to re-
evaluate and modify the Transportation Equity formula.
ADOPTED, this the 13th day of May, 2010 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:
s/Regina W. Alexander, Clerk

MAY 22, 2010
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
MAY 22, 2010      8:00 A.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N C
 
PRESENT:         Robert Howard, Mayor
            Aldermen Mary Ellen Poole, Kenneth Karn, Jwantana Frink, Ed
Boguskie
            and Donnie Potter
ABSENT:         Alderman Nelson Adams
STAFF:         M. Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, MMC, City Clerk
            Neal Sage, Chief of Southport Rescue Squad
            John Young, Volunteer Rescue Squad Treasurer
I.
Call to Order - 8:08 a.m.
Mayor Howard called the meeting to order and delivered the invocation.
II.
Proposed Budget FY 2010-2011
Mayor Howard asked the Board to be cognizant of providing sufficient revenue to
carry on the City's functions and to provide sufficient monies to perpetuate
the infrastructure and beautification of the City while adopting a budget that
the citizens can live with.
Mayor Howard communicated that he attended a meeting in Elizabeth City with
Mayors of ElectriCities members. Discussed were concerns about ElectriCities
ability to borrow money at will. As a result, member cities financial
obligations have been extended and part of this is due to mismanagement and
real estate bonds investments. Mayor Howard stated that member cities need to
work collectively with legislators and municipal power agencies to place
restrictions on borrowing money except that which is authorized by the Boards
of member cities. He noted that a number of cities transfer monies from their
electric enterprise fund into the general fund to offset taxes.
Mayor Howard advised the Board, when he was in Raleigh that he spoke with
legislators about the need to appoint a representative from this area to the
Ports Authority Board.
Mr. Thornton advised that the proposed budget was compiled with no rate
increase in the electric, water and sewer funds, nor proposed tax increase, but
delivering the same level of services. (See budget message)
Budget Message
The Budget for Fiscal Year 2010-2011 reflects a continuation of strong fiscal
conservativism that management believes is necessary to insure the delivery of
essential and desirable public services to the citizens of Southport. The
continued economic instability and market volatility necessitates a very
conservative approach in calculating anticipated revenues and budgeting desired
expenditures. Essentially, the City of Southport FY 2010-2011 Budget is a hold
the line budget in terms of utility fees, taxes and to a great extent,
expenditures.
The FY 2010-2011 Budget reflects the continuation of the current municipal ad
valorem tax rate at that of .18 per $ 100 of valuation. In spite of the overall
State and National trend, the City's Ad Valorem tax base and subsequently its
property tax revenues continues to experience slow growth. Water, Sewer and
Electric utility rates are not proposed to be increased in the FY 2010-2011City
of Southport Annual Budget. Fiscal year 2010-2011 will be a transitional year
for the City of Southport's wastewater operations as the reversal project is
completed, our wastewater treatment plant is shut down and the City begins
sending its wastewater to the County of Brunswick for treatment. Management
stresses that close scrutiny and diligence continue to be paid to the Water and
Sewer Fund in coming years as rate adjustments may likely be necessary to
offset the anticipated impact and treatment fees that the City will experience.
Management also stresses that close scrutiny be paid to the City's Electric
Enterprise Fund. While this Fund has continued to 'hold its own', the level of
capital necessary to perform system enhancements, upgrades, replacements and
the placement of the system underground, is not being realized. The City's
electrical distribution system continues to age and with that age comes the
need to perform greater levels of maintenance and upgrades. The City of
Southport needs to review the methodology involved with creating appropriate
levels of capital reserves in this Fund to meet the needs of a municipally
operated electric distribution system.
Proactive foresight and continued diligence in terms of reducing departmental
expenditures, conservative revenue projections and Board and staff support have
provided the City of Southport with growth in all three of its funds over the
last two fiscal years. Since June of 2008, the Total Available Fund Balance has
grown from $ 2,850,000 to more than $ 4,350,000 with nearly $ 1.1 million of
that growth being realized in the General Fund.
Overall, the proposed FY 2010-2011 City of Southport Annual Budget seeks to
maintain a high level of delivery of desirable public services while
responsibly taking into account the needs for future programs and service
improvements.
In spite of the national and state economy and the budgetary challenges it
presents, it is expressly understood that citizens demand and expect more from
their local government than ever before. With this in mind, every effort is
being made to respond to these needs by the City of Southport. The public
services provided by the City of Southport remain responsive and of the highest
quality in spite of the ever rising expense of providing them.
General Fund
The General Fund is the basic operating fund of the City. It is used to account
for all financial resources except those required to be accounted for within
another specific fund. The primary revenue sources of the General Fund are Ad
Valorem property taxes and State-shared revenues. Primary expenditures within
the General Fund are for Police, Fire, Streets & Sidewalks, Solid Waste
Collection, Recreational Services and Facilities, Public Property Maintenance,
Planning, Zoning and Code Enforcement as well as other General Governmental and
Administrative services. The total proposed General Fund budget for FY 10-11 is
$ 4,091,500 which amounts to a $ 266,800 decrease from last year's budget of $
4,358,300 and a $ 527,205 decrease from FY 2008-2009 year's budget of $
4,618,705.
The proposed budget for FY 2010-2011 maintains the property tax rate of .18
cents per $100 valuation. In the face of increasing fuel, utility, personnel,
economic uncertainty and other related costs, it is a testament to diligent
oversight by the Board, management and staff that the City continues to provide
high quality public services in these challenging financial times.
Water & Sewer Fund
The FY 2010-2011 budget for this Enterprise Fund reflects a period of
transition from the City of Southport operating its own wastewater treatment
facilities to that of partnering with the County of Brunswick for wastewater
treatment and the future decommissioning of the City's wastewater treatment
facility. The construction of the necessary infrastructure to complete the
reversal of wastewater flow from the City of Southport to the treatment
facilities of the County of Brunswick will be completed during FY 2010-2011.
The closure of the City's wastewater treatment facilities will also take place
in FY 2010-2011 upon completion of the flow reversal project. All of this has
been necessitated by the State Division of Water Quality's ruling that the City
of Southport eliminate the discharge of its treated wastewater into the
Atlantic Intercoastal Waterway by November of 2011. The City will continue to
purchase potable water from the County of Brunswick for the course of FY 2010-
2011. Currently, this Fund is in secure financial position. Diligence will be
required over the course of the next few years to continue to maintain this
position. There are no proposed rate increases in FY 2010-2011 as staff will
continue to monitor the overall costs and effects of this transition in the
treatment of municipal wastewater and make recommendations to the Board.
Electric Fund
The Electric Fund continues to be a budgetary challenge in FY 2010-2011. The
significant cost of purchasing electricity for distribution to the customers on
the City's system remains as the primary challenge for the City as we strive to
provide reliable and affordable public power. The purchase of electricity and
the contract for maintenance that the City has with Brunswick Electric Company
represents 87% of the entire Electric Fund expenditures for FY 2001-2011. When
you also factor in the expense of customer underground installation work that
the City pays BEMCO to perform, those three expense line items comprise 91% of
the Electric Fund expenditure budget for FY 2010-2011. Of the total $ 6,781,900
of proposed Electric Fund expenditures for FY 2010-2011, the purchase of power,
BEMCO maintenance contract and customer underground installation make up $
6,120,000. This leaves only $ 661,900 within the Fund for everything else
including proportional salaries and benefits, dues, vehicles, load management
program, capital outlays for improvements, meter reading expenses, etc. There
is an Assistant Public Services Director's position funded in the FY 2010-2011
Budget as the City would find itself in a very precarious position should the
services of the current Director be lost for any reason. Continued close
scrutiny must be paid to this Fund to continue to keep it fiscally responsible.
Further increases in the cost of purchasing electricity remain a possibility
and a concern as any increase in this expenditure significantly impacts this
Fund.
Revenue Outlook
The property tax rate of .18 cents based upon the current tax levy is expected
to generate $1,550,000. Property taxes comprise roughly 36% of the anticipated
General Fund revenue. No increase in the City of Southport property tax rate is
proposed in the FY 2010-2011 City of Southport Proposed Budget. The remainder
of General Fund revenues are comprised primarily from State-collected and
State-shared sources. Sales tax revenues are reflective of the condition of the
overall economy and should continue to be closely monitored. The Budget Officer
has very conservatively estimated anticipated sales tax revenues as the
volatility in the economy continues. Total sales tax receipts for FY 2010-2011
have been estimated at $ 625,000. This represents a decline of $ 25,000 from
current fiscal year budget level of $ 650,000 and a $ 95,000 decline from the
budgeted level in FY 2008-2009. This decline in anticipated sales tax revenues
is based upon the overall state of the economy and a desire by management to
budget conservatively in light of the lingering national recession and
unanticipated financial challenges it may present. Franchise taxes on power,
natural gas, cable television, and telecommunications make up another $ 275,000
in estimated revenue. It is through stable anticipated income from the status
of the local economy, retention of all net ABC operations profits, fees
generated from the use of public assets, a recommended increase in the local
Occupancy Tax along with the Board, management and staffs continued diligence
in conservative fiscal practices that the continued growth in expenses of
public service provision is accommodated in the proposed budget for FY 2010-
2011. There is no transfer from the unappropriated general fund balance
recommended to balance the proposed FY 2010-2011 Proposed Budget.
Departmental Budgets
General Fund
1)   General Administration: Administrative expenses are proposed at $ 706,900.
This figure represents an increase from last year's $ 466,350. The increase is
due to a new line item being added to the budget of this department to reflect
the first year of a 20 year payment plan on the new Fire Station. The first
payment for the financing of this project will be $ 241,000. The FY 2010-2011
City of Southport proposed budget currently reflects no salary increase in pay
for all employees.
2)   Police Department: The Police Department is budgeted at $ 927,050 this is
up slightly from $ 901,900 last year. The increase is largely due to the
expense associated with the provision of health insurance. The need for
continued vehicle replacements in this upcoming fiscal year and into the future
is being continued by again funding the Vehicle Replacement Plan. Under this
Plan, Police vehicles will be acquired via a public financing or lease purchase
program with an outside financial institution. This Plan is resulting in Police
vehicles that are more fuel efficient, last longer and require less maintenance
than the arrangement of purchasing used, former Highway Patrol cruisers.
3)   Planning, Inspections and Code Enforcement: This Department is budgeted at
$ 264,000 for FY 2010-2011. This represents a decrease of $ 71,200 over the
level of funding provided for FY 2010-2011. The decrease is due to the
elimination of $ 75,000 for a renovation to or a replacement of the Inspections
and Code Enforcement office building. In light of the Facilities Assessment/
Spatial Analysis to be performed on all of the City's buildings and the decline
in building and construction activity in the City, the Board and staff may wish
to further evaluate the necessity of this requested expenditure.
4)   Public Services: Total Public Services General Fund operations are
budgeted at
$ 652,550 which is broken down as follows:
a.   Public Services-Streets: $ 188,500
b.   Public Services - Sanitation: $ 98,500 (Includes specific expenses
associated with the collection of residential wastes and garbage)
c.   Public Services-Bldg. & Grounds: $ 197,700
d.   Public Services-Garage: $ 167,850
5)   Parks & Recreation: The Parks and Recreation Dept. reflects a decrease in
the funding level in comparison to FY 10-11. This decrease is due to the
completion of construction of Lowe-White Park and the renovation to the former
Senior Center on Atlantic Ave. in FY 2009-2010.
6)   Tourism: The Southport Tourism Department level of funding reflects a
slight decrease from that of FY 2010-2011 level. The replacement of a
department head and general belt tightening is to be credited for the decrease
within this department.
Water & Sewer Fund
The Water and Sewer fund of the City of Southport for FY 2010-2011 reflects a $
531,450 increase in funding level from that of FY 2010-2011. This is largely
due to the addition of the first repayment to the NC Clean Water Management
Trust Fund for the formerly targeted spray irrigation property. The first
payment will be in The amount of $ 562,000.
Electric Fund
The Electric Fund remains the single most expensive department for the City of
Southport to operate. The fund total for FY 2010-2011 is budgeted at $
6,781,900.
This amount reflects a very slight decrease from last year's funding level. As
a result of the cost of the provision of electric power coupled with an express
desire of the Board to pass on as little of an increase to City of Southport
customers as is possible, the Electric Fund departmental budget contains no
funding for any capital improvements or capital outlays for equipment or
service enhancements.
As stated earlier in this Message, continued diligence must be paid to this
Fund as the City must be mindful of the obligations and expenses associated
with the continued ownership of a public power enterprise.
Executive Summary
Based upon the goals and objectives established by the City of Southport Board
of Aldermen to maintain and enhance the quality of life for all of the citizens
of Southport, a conservative yet forward-looking budget and Capital Improvement
Plan has been drafted that solidifies the City's commitment to the provision of
and the improvement to high quality public services. Such provision and their
improvements, however, require adequate funding on the operational side while
maintaining a close scrutiny on balances and reserves. This budget proposal
strives to achieve that continued high level of public service provision while
maintaining current the level of the property tax and water and sewer and
electric rates and fees. Staff has proposed and recommends that the City of
Southport Board of Aldermen accept and implement the proposed municipal
operations budget for FY 2010-2011. Continued conservative management of the
City's finances is critical to the fiscal health of the City. In weighing the
goals, objectives, needs and expectations of the City of Southport and the
associated need for additional revenue, the current budget proposal, I believe,
strikes a balance that improves service levels while respecting the financial
health of the City government and its growing needs and objectives for years to
come.
Respectfully submitted,
M. Alan Thornton
City Manager

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
a proposed amendment to Article 2 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public hearing,
properly noticed, was held on June 10, 2010, before the Board of Aldermen
regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) an updated, more extensive definition of
this type of establishment is needed for the Unified Development Ordinance,
(ii) this amendment is necessary to promote orderly growth and development in
the Highway Business District, and (iii) this amendment is necessary to promote
the public safety and general welfare of the community by better defining
Electronic Gaming Operations in the City;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 10th day of June, 2010.
By:
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor

c)   Adoption of Proposed Budget FY 2010-2011
The Board discussed the merits of approving an Assistant Public Services
Director which is proposed in the FY 2010-2011 budget. Mayor Howard suggested
the position be placed on hold until needed.
Mr. Cardwell, Public Services Director justifying the request stated that City
facilities are not being maintained. The City needs a person that can develop a
Facilities Management Program which is required in order to apply for various
grants, maintain City facilities i.e. load management, sewer system, lift
sites, etc.
Other areas discussed:
·   Alderman Karn asked the Board to consider funding for way finding signs.
·   Alderman Adams asked if consideration had been given to making a donation
to the schools from ABC revenues. City Manager stated that the consideration
was to be based on ABC revenue projections but they have been decreased.
·   Mayor Howard asked that capital monies not be spent in VRS until a
feasibility study is performed and to insure availability of funds for a
document control system. Manager stated that appropriate funds are available to
begin a document control system program.
Alderman Boguskie motioned to adopt the budget FY 2010-2011 as recommended by
the City Manager, seconded by Alderman Karn. Discussion: Aldermen Adams, Frink
and Poole stated that they could not vote on the budget as presented and needed
further justification i.e. job description for the position. Alderman Karn
stated if the position is deleted, it can pose a problem because the City needs
a public facilities maintenance plan for its facilities. The votes were: 3
ayes, Aldermen Boguskie, Karn and Potter .  3 no votes, Aldermen Adams, Frink,
Poole. Mayor Howard voted no, breaking the tie. Motion failed 4-3
Alderman Poole motioned to approve the budget excluding the Assistant Public
Service Director, seconded by Alderman Frink. Discussion: Alderman Adams stated
the Board should establish criteria for the position when it decides to hire an
individual. Alderman Boguskie for clarification insured that no new positions
were in the budget and questioned the standby salary in the Fire Department’s
budget. Alderman Poole noted the budget can be amended. Alderman Karn
reiterated the importance of hiring an individual to be trained. The votes were
4 ayes, Aldermen Poole, Frink, Adams, and Potter. 2 noes, Aldermen Karn and
Boguskie. Passed 4-2

SECTION VI
TAX RATE ESTABLISHED
An Ad Valorem rate of eighteen (.18) cents per $100.00 full valuation is hereby
established as the official tax rate for the City of Southport for the fiscal
year 2010-2011. This is based on an estimated valuation of approximately
$925,751,174 with an estimated collection rate of ninety-five percent (95.00%).
SECTION VII
SPECIAL AUTHORIZATION - BUDGET OFFICER
The Budget Officer shall be authorized to reallocate departmental
appropriations among the various objects of expenditure and interdepartmental
transfers as said officer believes necessary. The Budget Officer shall be
authorized to effect inter-fund transfers, not to exceed $1,500.00. Notation of
such reallocation and transfers shall be made to the Board on the next
succeeding financial report.
SECTION VIII
RESTRICTION - BUDGET OFFICER
The inter-fund transfer of monies exceeding $1,500.00 shall be accomplished by
Board authorization only. The utilization of any contingency appropriation
shall be accomplished only with Board authorization.
SECTION IX
UTILIZATION OF BUDGET & BUDGET ORDINANCE
This Ordinance and the Budget Document shall be the basis of the financial plan
for the City of Southport municipal government during the 2010-2011 Fiscal
Year. The Budget Officer shall administer the budget and shall ensure that
operation officials are provided guidance and sufficient details to implement
their appropriate portion of the Budget. The accounting section shall establish
records which are in agreement with the budget and this ordinance and the
appropriate statues of the State of North Carolina.
Copies of the Budget Ordinance shall be furnished to the Finance Director and
the City Manager of the City of Southport, to be kept on file by them for their
direction in the disbursement of funds.
SECTION X
ADOPTION
Copies of this Budget Ordinance shall be furnished to all appropriate officials
of the municipality and kept on file for the proper recordation of receipts and
disbursement of funds.

g)   City of Southport Water Shortage Response Plan
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Potter to adopt the resolution
approving the Water Shortage Response Plan which was created by the state for
public water distribution systems. Vote carried. Passed 6-0
Resolution for Approving Water Shortage Response Plan
WHEREAS,  North Carolina General Statute 143-355(l) requires that each unit of
local government that provides public water services or plans to provide such
services shall either individually or together with other such units of local
government, prepare and submit a Water Shortage Response Plan; and
WHEREAS, as required by the statute and in the interests of sound local
planning, a Water Shortage Response Plan for the City of Southport has been
developed and submitted to the Board of Aldermen for approval; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the Water Shortage Plan is in
accordance with the provisions of North Carolina General Statute 143-355 (l)
and that it will provide appropriate guidance for the future management of
water supplies for Southport as well as useful information to the Department of
Environment and Natural Resources for the development of a state water supply
plan as required by statute;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that the Water Shortage Response Plan entitled, Water Shortage
Response Plan dated June 10, 2010 is hereby approved and shall be submitted to
the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Division of Water
Resources; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Board of Aldermen intends that this plan shall
be revised to reflect changes in relevant data and projections at least once
every five years or as otherwise requested by the Department, in accordance
with the statute and sound planning practice.
This the 10th day of June 2010
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander
Clerk
Water Shortage Response Plan
City of Southport, North Carolina
May 24, 2010
The procedures herein are written to reduce potable water demand and supplement
existing drinking water supplies whenever existing water supply sources are
inadequate to meet current demands for potable water.
I.    Authorization
The Southport City Manager shall enact the following water shortage response
provisions whenever the trigger conditions outlined in Section IV are met. In
his absence, the Public Services Director will assume this role.
Mr. M. Alan Thornton
Southport City Manager
Phone: (910) 457-7988
E-mail:alan_thorton@southportnc.org
Mr. Ralph Cardwell
Southport Public Services Director
Phone: (910) 457-7936
E-mail: ralph_cardwell@southportnc.org
II.    Notification
The following notification methods will be used to inform water system
employees and customers of a water shortage declaration: employee e-mail
announcements, notices at municipal buildings, notices in water bills. Required
water shortage response measures will be communicated through PSA announcements
on local radio, cable stations and on the City website (http://
www.cityofsouthport.com). Declaration of emergency water restrictions or water
rationing will be communicated to all customers by telephone through use of
reverse 911.
III.    Levels of Response
Five levels of water shortage response are outlined in the table below. The
five levels of water shortage response are: voluntary reductions, mandatory
reductions I and II, emergency reductions and water rationing. A detailed
description of each response level and corresponding water reduction measures
follow below.
 
Stage Response                Description
                              Water users are encouraged to reduce their water
1     Voluntary Reductions    use and improve water use efficiency; however, no
                              penalties apply for noncompliance. Water supply
                              conditions indicate a potential for shortage.
                              Water users must abide required water use
                              reduction and efficiency measures; penalties
2     Mandatory Reductions I  apply for noncompliance. Water supply conditions
                              are significantly lower than the seasonal norm
                              and water shortage conditions are expected to
                              persist.
3     Mandatory Reductions II Same as in Stage 2
                              Water supply conditions are substantially
4     Emergency Reductions    diminished and pose an imminent threat to human
                              health or environmental integrity.
                              Water supply conditions are substantially
5     Water Rationing         diminished and remaining supplies must be
                              allocated to preserve human health and
                              environmental integrity.
 
In Stage 1, Voluntary Reductions, all water users will be asked to reduce their
normal water use by 5%. Customer education and outreach programs will encourage
water conservation and efficiency measures including: irrigating landscapes a
maximum of one inch per week; preventing water waste, runoff and watering
impervious surfaces; watering plants deeply to encourage root growth; washing
only full loads in clothes and dishwashers; using spring-loaded nozzles on
garden hoses; and identifying and repairing all water leaks.
In Stage 2, Mandatory Reductions I, all customers are expected to reduce their
water use by 10% in comparison to their previous month’s water bill. In
addition to continuing to encourage all voluntary reduction actions, the
following restrictions apply: irrigation is limited to a half inch per week
between 8PM and 8AM; outdoor use of drinking water for washing impervious
surfaces is prohibited; and all testing and training purposes requiring
drinking water (e.g. fire protection) will be limited.
In Stage 3, Mandatory Reductions II, customers must continue actions from all
previous stages and further reduce water use by 20% compared to their previous
month’s water bill. All non-essential uses of drinking water are banned and
garden and landscape irrigation must be reduced to the minimum amount necessary
for survival. Additionally, in Stage 3, a drought surcharge of 1.5 times the
normal water rate applies.
In Stage 4, Emergency Reductions, customers must continue all actions from
previous stages and further reduce their water use by 25% compared to their
previous month’s water bill. A ban on all use of drinking water except to
protect public health and safety is implemented and drought surcharges increase
to 2 times the normal water rate.
The goal of Stage 5, Water Rationing, is to provide drinking water to protect
public health (e.g. residences, residential health care facilities and
correctional facilities). In Stage 5, all customers are only permitted to use
water at the minimum required for public health protection. Firefighting is the
only allowable outdoor water use and pickup locations for distributing potable
water will be announced according to Southport’s Emergency Response Plan.
Drought surcharges increase to 5 times the normal water rate.
IV.    Triggers
Southport is provided water by purchase from the Brunswick County. When
Brunswick County declares a water shortage Southport is required to do so as
well. During this time Southport Public Services Director will stay in close
contact with Brunswick County and follow their triggers.
Return to Normal
When water shortage conditions have abated and the situation is returning to
normal, water conservation measures employed during each phase should be
decreased in reverse order of implementation. Permanent measures directed
toward long-term monitoring and conservation should be implemented or continued
so that the community will be in a better position to prevent shortages and
respond to recurring water shortage conditions.
V.    Enforcement
The provisions of the water shortage response plan will be enforced by City of
Southport Public Services department and police personnel. Violators may be
reported to the City’s dedicated water conservation hotline. Citations are
assessed according to the following schedule depending on the number of prior
violations and current level of water shortage.
 
Water Shortage Level First Violation Second Violation Third Violation
Voluntary Reductions N/A             N/A              N/A
 
Mandatory Reductions (Stages 2 and 3) Warning $250 Discontinuation of Service
 
Emergency Reductions $250 Discontinuation of Service Discontinuation of Service
 
Water Rationing $500 Discontinuation of Service Discontinuation of Service
 
Drought surcharge rates are effective in Stages 3, 4 and 5.
VI.    Public Comment
Customers will have multiple opportunities to comment on the provisions of the
water shortage response plan. First, a draft plan will be will be available at
City Hall for customers to view. A notice will be included in customer water
bill notifying them of such. Also a draft plan will be published on the city
website.  All subsequent revisions to the draft plan will be published at least
30 days prior to an adoption vote by Southport’s City Aldermen.
VII.    Variance Protocols
Applications for water use variance requests are available from the City Public
Services Office. All applications must be submitted to the Public Services
Office for review by the Public Services Director or his or her designee. A
decision to approve or deny individual variance requests will be determined
within two weeks of submittal after careful consideration of the following
criteria: impact on water demand, expected duration, alternative source
options, social and economic importance, purpose (i.e. necessary use of
drinking water) and the prevention of structural damage.
VIII.    Effectiveness
The effectiveness of the Southport water shortage response plan will be
determined by comparing the stated water conservation goals with observed water
use reduction data. Other factors to be considered include frequency of plan
activation, any problem periods without activation, total number of violation
citations, desired reductions attained and evaluation of demand reductions
compared to the previous year’s seasonal data.
IX.    Revision
The water shortage response plan will be reviewed and revised as needed to
adapt to new circumstances affecting water supply and demand, following
implementation of emergency restrictions, and at a minimum of every five years
in conjunction with the updating of our Local Water Supply Plan. Further, a
water shortage response planning work group will review procedures following
each emergency or rationing stage to recommend any necessary improvements to
the plan to Southport’s City Aldermen. The City of Southport Public Services
Director is responsible for initiating all subsequent revisions.

j)    Discussion of Southport’s Petition Regarding the Proposed Port
Alderman Karn motioned to adopt a resolution opposing construction and
operation of the proposed International Port based on the communication and
lack of a response from State Port representatives to hold public meetings in
the City. Mayor Howard ruled the motion out of order due to the lack of
notification to Board members and the public that a resolution would be placed
on the floor for a vote, and asked that it be put on the July agenda. Alderman
Karn appealed the Mayor’s decision stating that any member of the Board can
make a motion, and since it is procedural, the Board can decide by vote to
consider the motion.
Alderman Karn then placed a motion on the floor to appeal the Mayor’s ruling,
seconded by Alderman Boguskie. 5 ayes, Aldermen Karn, Boguskie, Poole, Potter
and Frink, 1 no, Alderman Adams. Passed 5-1
Alderman Potter asked to be recused from voting on the Port due to the advice
of legal counsel and his employment. Alderman Boguskie motioned to recuse
Alderman Potter, seconded by Alderman Karn; the vote of approval was unanimous.
Passed 6-0
Alderman Karn restated the motion that the Board of Aldermen approves a
resolution opposing the construction and operation of the N.C. International
Terminal at Southport, seconded by Alderman Boguskie.  Discussion: Alderman
Adams cautioned the Board about changing its position from in favor, to neutral
and now against. He cited potential jobs that the Port could bring, and that
there are many residents in the City who supports the Port. He stated if a
resolution is adopted opposing the Port, he believes that it will be a dire
decision. Alderman Frink stated that it is too early for the City to take a
position. Alderman Poole stated her vote is not against the Port, but there are
other ways to bring in jobs. The votes were: 3 ayes, Aldermen Karn, Boguskie
and Poole. 1 no, Alderman Adams, 1 abstention, Alderman Frink, Alderman Potter
was recused from the vote. Motion passed 4-1. (Alderman Frink abstention
counted as an affirmative vote)

10 June 2010
Honorable Mayor
Fellow Board Members and Staff
Citizens and Friends
1.   Serving the citizens of Southport has been an honor and pleasure. I have
been overwhelmed by the support of the community and the hospitality of the
City staff. I am very proud of the progress this Board and staff have made and
applaud their continued commitment to Southport
2.   I have volunteered for temporary duty outside of the Wilmington area on a
tour that could last one year or longer. As the business of running this City
continues, the uncertainty associated with this assignment will render me
ineffective in the role of Alderman. Because of this action, it is with a heavy
heart that I submit my resignation from the position of Alderman for the City
of Southport effective 12 June 2010.
3.   I want to thank everyone that made this experience possible and especially
Vickie and Josh for their support past, present and future as I refocus my
service elsewhere. To maintain stability on the Board, I would like to
recommend that Vickie be considered to fill this term. I am confident she will
be a diligent public servant and serve this community well.
Respectfully,
/s/ Donnie
Donnie Potter

Resolution in Opposition to the Construction Of the North Carolina
International Terminal next to the City of Southport, NC
WHEREAS, the North Carolina State Port Authority has failed, despite numerous
requests, to meet with the citizens and Aldermen of Southport in a public
setting to provide information and answer questions about the proposed Port,
and
WHEREAS, the economic benefits of the proposed Port to Southport, Brunswick
County and the State of North Carolina have been grossly exaggerated and
discredited by a number of authorities, and
WHEREAS, this development will create serious problems related to public
safety, traffic congestion, reduction in tourism, and adverse environmental
impacts, and
WHEREAS, the cost to taxpayers for this project will exceed two (2) billion
dollars at a time when government resources are scarce and the shipping
industry is at a historical low point, and
WHEREAS, competitive ports in Charleston, SC, Savannah, Ga and Hampton Roads,
Va. have approved expansion projects, existing infrastructure and natural deep
water harbors, and
WHEREAS, the majority of the citizens of Southport are opposed to the proposed
port, and
WHEREAS, government officials want to know if the local municipalities are in
favor of or opposed to the proposed Port
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, THAT THE City of Southport is opposed to the
construction and operation of the proposed container shipping terminal, named
the North Carolina International Terminal next to the City of Southport.
This resolution was adopted by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport
at its regularly scheduled meeting held on June 10, 2010
/s/ Mary Ellen Watts Poole
Mayor Pro Tem

/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC

City Attorney Isenberg addressed the board regarding the question which had
arisen concerning the validity of the appointment of Aldermen Vickie Potter on
June 10. Isenberg stated that he had reviewed state law, the city charter and
section 2-61 of the Code of Ordinances, and that he had also conferred with the
Institute of Government. Based upon his review of the law and consultation with
the Institute, Isenberg stated that in his opinion the appointment of Mrs.
Potter was legal and the City had complied with all legal requirements for the
appointment.
Mayor Howard read the following statement into the record:
“Mr. Potter told me during a breakfast meeting several weeks earlier that he
may resign at some point in time due to job commitments. At that time he
stressed that a decision had not been made and asked me to hold that
information in confidence. I respected his request for confidentiality. He did
mention to me that if he decided to resign he wanted to recommend his wife to
fill his unexpired term and asked for my support. I told Mr. Potter, that while
I have much respect for him and Mrs. Potter that I could not commit to his
request for support prior to going through an open dialog with the Board
members and constituent involvement. I suggested that the filling of Aldermen
positions was a Board decision after receiving public input.
It was and continues to be my feeling that because our citizens just identified
their choices for the Board during an election only several months ago, the
results of that election should be one of the considering factors. During the
November election only 38 votes separated three candidates for two seats.
Clearly in respect for our citizens this fact should have been given
consideration. Additionally their action places Mrs. Potter in the position of
being the only Alderman that has not received public scrutiny or input; truly
an injustice to those we represent.”

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City's
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the city's land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
a proposed amendment to Article 8 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on July 8, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) this aspect of nonconformities is not
properly addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance and should be, (ii)
this amendment is necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the
City of Southport, and (iii) it is necessary to promote the public safety and
general welfare of the community by allowing for the adjustment of certain
property lines in the City.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 8th day of July, 2010.
City of Southport
By:
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
ATTEST:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, Clerk
AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
TEXT AMENDMENT # 10-0212-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With
Respect to Nonconforming Lots
AMEND BY ADDITION OF:
ARTICLE 8: NONCONFORMING SITUATIONS
Section 8-2: Nonconforming Lots
(C) Contiguous nonconforming lots owned by the same person, which were legally
subdivided and recorded in Brunswick County prior to August of 1973, may be
combined with a contiguous conforming lot which is oversized and also owned by
the same person, for the purpose of re-positioning lot lines as long as all of
the net resulting nonconforming lots are less nonconforming. The conforming lot
may not be made nonconforming. No additional lots may be created through this
process, as the number of lots resulting from the reconfiguration must be equal
to or less than the number of lots originally involved in the recombination.
The resulting lots must be more conforming to all City standards than they were
prior to undertaking this process. Any structure in existence on any of these
contiguous lots at the time of reconfiguration cannot create new
nonconformities or increase the extent of existing nonconformities with respect
to yard size and setback requirements.
b)    Consideration of Resolution Authorizing Concession Agreement for City
Property (Maritime Museum)
City Manager Thornton presented a resolution authorizing the Concession
Agreement for City Property (Maritime Museum). The lease agreement was formally
approved May 14, 2009 and was sent to the Department of Interior Regional
Office in Atlanta. The Agreement has been revised and is presented for review
approval. Attorney Isenberg noted changes made were basically in the
terminology. Mayor Howard questioned some of the language in the Concession
Agreement and the obligation of the City including potential liability because
some of the language is ambiguous. In reviewing the document, Attorney Isenberg
stated he does not believe that the City has to worry about liability issues.
No further discussion, Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to
approve the resolution authorizing Concession Agreement for City Property. The
vote of approval was unanimous. Passed 6-0.
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING CONCESSION AGREEMENT FOR CITY PROPERTY
WHEREAS, the City of Southport now owns the Fort Johnston Barracks located at
103-A and 103-B Davis Street and 204-A and 204-B East Moore Street, having
acquired said property pursuant to the terms of that certain quitclaim deed
from the United States of America recorded in Book 2634 at Page 269 of the
Brunswick County Registry; and
WHEREAS, the City, State of North Carolina and The Friends of the North
Carolina Maritime Museum at Southport have agreed to enter into a Concession
Agreement whereby the City will grant unto the State an exclusive concession
agreement for the use of said property; and
WHEREAS, the United States of America, acting by and through the Southeast
Regional Director of the National Park Service, has approved and consented to
the terms and provisions of said agreement; and
WHEREAS, N. C. G. S. 160A-274 authorizes the City to enter into this Agreement
with the State of North Carolina for the use of said property upon such terms
and conditions as it deems wise; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
Board hereby approves the attached Concession Agreement and authorizes and
directs the Mayor or City Manager to execute said agreement on behalf of the
City.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 9-38 OF THE CODE OF ORDINANCES
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Section
9-38 of the Code of Ordinances is hereby amended to read as follows:
Sec. 9-38. Notice to abate nuisance.
Upon a determination that such conditions constituting a public nuisance exist,
the city Manager or his designee shall notify, in writing, the owner, occupant
or person in possession of the premises in question of the conditions
constituting such public nuisance and shall order the prompt abatement thereof
within fifteen (15) days from receipt of such written notice.

3rd Edition, written by A. Fleming Bell, II of the North Carolina School of

of Procedures will be incorporated as Attachment #1)
Note: Page 12- Rule 5. Public Address to the Council
City Manager Thornton requested a policy be established for persons wishing to
address the Board. Consensus was 10 day requirement and staff asked to draft
wording specifying length of time, etc. and present back to the Board.
The Board discussed posting all Committee meetings notice in accordance with
the open meeting law at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to the meeting.
Notice should be provided to the Clerk and she will insure that the notice is
posted. Mayor Howard asked the Manager to draft a directive to all committees,
staff liaisons and chairpersons apprising them that notice of committee
meetings must be posted and minutes kept of their meetings and a copy provided
to the Clerk to be kept on file.
B)    Code of Ethics
The Model Code of Ethics was reviewed by the Board. Mayor Howard noted that the
policy can be amended whenever a change is needed. He also suggested any Board
or Committee under the Board's authority follow the ethics policy unless a
different one is approved by the Board. City Manager Thornton noted that a code
of ethics was recently adopted for ABC Boards and the requirements possibly
follow the same tenets as the one for local elected boards.
The Board discussed the proposed policy and made few changes. Alderman Boguskie
motioned that Section 6 (see policy) be stricken from the code, seconded by
Alderman Karn. 1 yes vote, Alderman Boguskie, 5 noes, Aldermen Karn, Adams,
Poole, Potter and Frink. Motion failed on 5-1.
Alderman Frink moved to adopt a Code of Ethics for the Southport Board of
Aldermen making it applicable to all Boards under the authority of the
Aldermen. The vote of approval was unanimous. Passed 6-0 (Copy of Code
Incorporated in the record)
City Manager Thornton in answer to questions by members of the Board stated the
Personnel Policy should include a section on ethical behavior for employees.
When the revised policy is presented to the Board, and if it is not
sufficiently addressed, the Board can make changes to the policy before
approval.

JULY 21, 2010
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
JULY 21, 2010     6:30 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS SOUTHPORT, N. C.
 
PRESENT:         Robert Howard, Mayor
            Aldermen Mary Ellen Poole, Kenneth Karn, Ed Boguskie,
            Vickie Potter, Nelson Adams and Jwantana Frink
ABSENT:         None
STAFF:         M. Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, MMC, City Clerk
I.
Meeting called to order – 6:30 p.m.
The meeting was called to order at 6:30 p.m. by Mayor Howard.
II.
Invocation
The invocation was pronounced by Mayor Howard.
III.
Ethics Statement
Mayor Howard asked “if any member of the Board knows of any conflict of
interest or the appearance of a conflict of interest with respect to matters on
the agenda, to please state it at this time .”
IV.
Approval of Agenda
Alderman Frink moved, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to approve the agenda. Vote
unanimous. Passed 6-0
V.
Agenda Matter
a)   Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.12 a special meeting was called to consider
enforcement of City ordinances regulating obstructions in the public rights of
way and sidewalks.
Public Comments:
Alan Pascucci stated the initial problem was A-frame signs blocking traffic and
inhibiting the flow of pedestrians. He suggested the City either ban all
obstacles in accordance with the ordinance or to allow obstacles with “letters”
if the issue is culpability on the City’s behalf. He questioned whether the
City has on file with the Department of Transportation letters of insurance or
proof of indemnification. He suggested this issue be resolved because it can
tear the City apart.
Ernest Long told the Board that the source of the complaint should have been
considered before acted upon. He stated if obstructions are a danger to
pedestrians, they should be removed. He asked that the City engage public
opinion about the benches as he has done, because they provide a public service
and contributes to the ambience of the City.
Karen Taylor, owner of Taylor’s Restaurant and President of the Chamber of
Commerce, stated the timing is not right to enforce the ordinance. She told the
Board that she moved to Southport because of the City’s ambience and beauty.
She encouraged the Board to read the letter from the Chamber of Commerce and
consider what the businesses are dealing with in hopes that the issue can be
resolved.
Woody Wilson, 502 Brunswick Street encouraged the Board to enforce what is on
the books or tweak it to make it work. He added that the benches are used by
the public and they add to the ambience of the town. However, if the ordinance
is fixed then staff can enforce Board directives.
Mayor Howard commented that he does not support the approach to enforcing the
sidewalk obstruction ordinance. It is his opinion that the downtown area should
be user friendly. Merchants should be able to place benches and flower planters
in front of their businesses subject to application and approval by the Code
Enforcer, however; if anything obstructs safe pedestrian passage on sidewalks,
it should be removed. He believes that the ordinance is sufficient but a matter
of interpretation and enforcement. He asked the Board to declare a moratorium
on the enforcement of the City Code as it relates to benches, planters and
displays in the downtown area until review by staff, Board of Aldermen and
Beautification Committee. Upon completion of evaluation by the Beautification
Committee a report be presented to the Board with recommendations. Further to
request the City Attorney to provide a legal opinion regarding the ability of
the City Code to allow convenience benches, flower planters and flower displays
on the sidewalks in the downtown business area i.e. the liability issue for the
City.
Alderman Boguskie stated he does not take his oath of office lightly, he has a
job to do as an elected official and the ordinance is explicit. He explained
that he is not against benches; however, the ordinance is on the books and it
can be changed with a majority vote of the Board, not a committee.
Alderman Karn presented pictures of various situations in the downtown business
area. He stated that the City Planner and Code Enforcer took measurements of
the sidewalks. He noted that the existing ordinance is definitive and the need
is to define safe passageway i.e. the dimensions and what constitutes an
obstruction and compliance with the American Disabilities Act. He would like to
see the benches and flower planters remain if the City can write an ordinance
that is enforced fairly. He stated that this should be a decision by the Board.
Alderman Poole stated under the City Code of Ordinances; benches and flower
pots, display of goods prohibited (16-7), obstructions of public rights of way
and existing encroachments on rights of way need to also be reviewed.
Alderman Adams stated the ordinance needs to be fixed and he would like to seek
input from the Beautification Committee, merchants and advice from the City
Attorney. He supports a moratorium and input from anyone.
Alderman Potter voiced support for the benches and planters but wish to see
them against the buildings. She agreed that the ordinance needs to be worked as
soon as possible.
Alderman Boguskie motioned that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen declare
a moratorium on enforcing City Code Section 16-7, 8-10 for forty-five (45)
days, seconded by Alderman Karn. Discussion: Alderman Potter questioned what
would happen if someone got hurt. Mayor noted that the City has liability
insurance. Motion carried unanimously. Passed 6-0
Adjournment 7:10 p.m.
Motion by Alderman Boguskie to adjourn, seconded by Alderman Frink. Vote
unanimous.

Dear Mr. Thornton;
The Southport-Oak lsland Area Chamber of Commerce Board of Directors,
representing over 540 businesses is very concerned about your letter dated June
L6, 20L0 sent to Southport Business Owners. Our specific concern is the
definition of obstructions... "Obstructions include but are not limited to:
benches, tables, chairs, displayed merchandise and other non-permitted signs."
We understand the Southport Board of Alderman's desire to use the City Unified
Development Ordinances to implement a "vision" for Southport. We respectfully
submit the removal of items deemed as "obstructions" is by no means in the best
interest of the businesses, residents and visitors to Southport. lf you
continue down this path of sterilization of the Southport business district you
will be losing what makes Southport unique and welcoming - its individuality.
This individuality sets the Southport business district apart from its
competitors in the region and state
We support the removal of items that are "obstructing the free passage of
persons and vehicles." We do not support the removal of items from the
sidewalks and rights-of-way just because benches, tables, chairs, displayed
merchandise exist in the sidewalks or rights-of-way. We submit for
consideration that the Board of Alderman charges the City Manager with the task
of reviewing its interpretation of an obstruction and when doing so consider
what makes Southport has character.
We hope you will consider a broader and more favorable definition of
"obstructions" that will allow Southport's individuality to shine.
Sincerely
/s/ Karen Sphar
