AUGUST 23, 2010
SPECIAL MEETING
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN             SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
AUGUST 23, 2010               6:30 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS (CITY HALL) SOUTHPORT, N. C.
 
PRESENT:            Mayor Robert D. Howard
            Aldermen Nelson E. Adams, Richard “Ed” Boguskie, Mary Ellen Poole,
            Ken Karn, Jwantana Frink and Vickie Potter
ABSENT:              None
STAFF PRESENT:      M. Alan Thornton, City Manager
            Regina W. Alexander, MMC-City Clerk
I.
Call to Order – 6:30 p.m.
Mayor Howard called the Special Meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. pursuant to
notice duly posted and advertised, the purpose of the special meeting was to
discuss the establishment of a Tourism Development Authority, increasing the
occupancy tax from 3 – 5%, adopting a resolution calling for a Public Hearing
and proposed Unified Development Ordinance changes.
II.
Invocation
The invocation was pronounced by Reverend Charles Drew, Pastor of New Light
House Pentecostal Church, Bolivia, N.C.
III.
Agenda Approval
Alderman Frink motioned to approve the agenda with the addition of public
comments, seconded by Alderman Karn. Vote unanimous.
IV.
Public Comments
Mrs. Kendall Crews of 211 River Drive told the Board about her quest to obtain
public records and a copy of the August 12 agenda packet which did not include
the revisions recommended by the Planning Committee and Board. A written
statement was given to the Clerk and she requested that it be made a part of
the public record. (Statement placed on file)
Mr. Fred Guerrina of 710 Dale Avenue and a member of the Planning Board
questioned why the Board proposes to give up its executive power for a written
rule to dismiss an individual from a Board which will limit the Boards’
authoritative power. The Planning Board is an autonomous board operating at the
discretion of the elected board in an advisory capacity and should have the
power to act independent and make recommendations in conjunction with City
staff.
Mr. Buddy Barnes, 425 West West Street and a member of the Planning Board,
suggested the Board not make changes to the Code and asked that they review
carefully the changes being proposed. He confirmed that there has been
miscommunication between staff and the Board, but believes the situation has
been resolved. The Planning Board did make some recommended changes and he
presented the minutes with the changes to the Clerk.
Mr. Jim Clary resident of Bay Street stated concerns about disbanding the
Planning Board which is an important City Board. He stated concerns about
increasing the occupancy tax by 2% with the down turn in the economy.
Mr. David McVey of 216 Willis Drive and a member of the Tourism Committee
stated his opposition to raising the occupancy tax. He stated that it appears
that the City is anti-business and believes that it should be mandatory that
Aldermen schedule time to meet with citizens.
Mr. Dale McPherson of 108 South Rhett Street and a member of the Planning Board
referenced Section 3-10 Public Facilities of the Unified Development Ordinance
in which the Planning Board Liaison Committee proposed to take this out of the
Code and it is his belief that this section should not be deleted. He stated if
Board decisions are not considered carefully, staff will be made responsible
for the wishes of the people. He explained that Planning Board members have
expertise in various areas and the Board is beneficial to the City.
Alderman Poole noted that minutes of the Planning Board were received. She
explained that the Planning Board Operations Procedure Committee is presenting
procedural changes for Board of Aldermen review. She stated that there is no
proposal to dissolve the Planning Board. The procedure still requires the
Planning Board to make recommendations. The discussion is whether or not they
will have the option of holding additional meetings i.e. review committees.
Alderman Adams asked if the changes were recommended by the Planning Board or
the Planning Board Operations Procedure Committee. Alderman Poole noted the
changes include options for consideration and the Planning Board Operations
Procedure Committee and the Planning Board did not agree on all options,
therefore; no consensus was met. The document along with the Planning Board
minutes gives options if the Board of Aldermen proposes to make changes.
Alderman Karn explained that there are two places on the document where members
were not in accord and the options are enumerated by the Committee and Planning
Board. He explained that the Committee believes the Planning Board would
operate more effectively if the changes recommended by the Committee were
approved.
Mayor Howard asked about Article 4: Amendments in the Unified Development
Ordinance which explains how the Unified Development Ordinance can be amended
under 4-1 (a) and 4-2  Alderman Poole noted that this is the policy for the UDO
and any changes made will require a vote of the Board.
V.
Tourism Development Authority/Adoption of Resolution
Alderman Boguskie explained that a Tourism Development Authority is established
by the Board of Aldermen who may appoint five (5) members with staggered terms.
Funds are generated from tourism and channeled through the Tourism Development
Authority. The City is currently using general fund monies to support tourism
and the occupancy tax would help offset this cost. He referenced the job
description included in the packet for a Director of Economic and Tourism
Development. Alderman Karn added that the TDA is pro business and every dollar
invested in tourism is a three dollar return which would benefit the City
economically. (Statistics from Congressman McIntyre)
Alderman Adams voiced opposition to creating a governmental entity where the
City does not have control of the monies.
The Board discussed approximate revenues that would be generated with a 2%
increase in the occupancy tax. Mayor Howard questioned the cost to operate a
Tourism Development Authority. Alderman Boguskie in explanation stated there
would be no administrative expenditures involved in the Tourism Development
Authority with the exception of expenditures for tourism unless the Board of
Aldermen decide to pay members a stipend. Alderman Boguskie referenced the
Board to number 5 of the resolution which read  “the authority shall report
quarterly and at the close of the fiscal year to the Southport Board of
Aldermen on its receipts and expenditures for the preceding quarter and for the
year in such detail as required by the Board.”  Mayor Howard stated it is
currently costing $167,000 to operate the Tourism Department i.e. salaries and
promotion. It is estimated the City will take in $75,000 from the occupancy tax
which will go to the Tourism Development Authority, therefore the revenue
portion of the City budget will be reduced by $50,000. He questioned where the
additional funds would come from to fund the budget. City Manager Thornton
stated the budget will be reduced based upon what the Tourism Development
Authority will do under its authority for travel and tourism promotion. Mayor
Howard stated it is his belief that the citizens will spend more funds to
operate the Tourism Development Authority.
Alderman Adams suggested that more definitive information be submitted before
Board action due to the level of discussion and questions raised from the Board
about the budget and cost for the Tourism Development Authority.
Alderman Karn stated the taxpayers currently fund the entire tourism budget of
$167,000 which will be offset this year by a projection of $50,000 in occupancy
taxes. He cited as a reference that Myrtle Beach’s tourism budget is equivalent
to the entire tourism budget for the State of North Carolina. He explained if a
Tourism Development Authority is established in Southport, it will generate
more revenues which would save money and not cost the citizens. Mayor Howard
stated that this matter should be deferred and tax dollars not expended until a
cost benefit analysis is compiled.
In answer to a question by Alderman Frink, City Manager Thornton stated that
travel and tourism is the largest industry in Southport and anything done by
way of marketing and promoting tourism would benefit the City. If the Board
decides to pursue this, a Public Hearing is required to be held. Staff can
provide projected revenue numbers if requested by the Board.
Alderman Frink motioned that the Board not adopt the resolution creating a
Tourism Development Authority, seconded by Alderman Adams. The votes were: 2
ayes, Aldermen Adams and Frink. 4 nays: Aldermen Potter, Poole, Karn and
Boguskie. Motion failed 4-2.
Alderman Boguskie stated that the information was presented for discussion not
Board action because there are several things to be considered.
Alderman Karn motioned to adopt the resolution to levy an additional room
occupancy tax and create a tourism development authority and fill in the blanks
under number one (1) as follows: “There is hereby created the Southport Tourism
Development Authority, which shall be a public authority under the Local
Government Budget and Fiscal Control Act. The Authority shall be comprised of 4
members who shall be appointed by the Southport Board of Aldermen. Initially 2
members shall be appointed for a term of 3 years each and 2 members for a term
of 2 years each. Thereafter, each member shall serve a term of 3 years.”
Alderman Boguskie seconded the motion; the votes were 4 ayes Aldermen Poole,
Karn, Boguskie and Potter. 2 nays, Aldermen Frink and Adams. Motion passed 4-2
VI.
Discussion of a Proposed UDO and Code of Ordinance Revisions
Mayor Howard asked if the Planning Board submitted a recommendation pertaining
to revisions. Alderman Poole acknowledged that the Planning Board written
minutes serves as their recommendations. (Reference June 7, 2010 Planning Board
Minutes)
Alderman Poole stated there are discrepancies in the City’s Code and Unified
Development Ordinance i.e. text changes, who has authority, whether or not all
applications should be sent to review committees and attendance issues. The UDO
addressed missing 25% of meetings and the City Code stated 30%, and whether to
use the verb “shall” or “may.”
Alderman Adams questioned the purpose of review committees and prolonging the
application process. It is his belief that the City Planner should make the
decision. Alderman Poole explained that the Planning Board reviews the
application(s) in its entirety and may elect to send them to a review
committee.
Alderman Karn referenced Article 12. Zoning and Conditional Use Permit Approval
Section 12.5 (b)   stated the change is the Planning Board may with the
approval of the Administrator (Planning Director) appoint a review committee to
report at the next regularly scheduled meeting. Change being the Planning Board
is to get the approval of the Administrator for an item to go to a review
committee. The Aldermen on the Committee voted that the Administrator should
give the approval for a review committee. The Planning Board members believed
that the Planning Board should give the approval to appoint a review committee.
The Planning Board however recommended that a vote be held of the Board to
determine if a review committee should be appointed. The question is who
decides whether a review committee is appropriate.
Mr. Buddy Barnes, member of the Planning Board stated a review committee’s
purpose is to review applications and/or make a recommendation to assist the
applicant in meeting the UDO requirements so the Planning Board can make a
recommendation to the Board of Aldermen. Their goal is not to prolong the
process because they operate on a sixty (60) day schedule. The Planning Board
needs to be independent in selecting whether or not they can go to a review
committee.
Alderman Karn noted that he has attended several meetings and in some instances
committee reviews have worked and other things have not been in the purview of
a Planning Review Committee, citing storm water as an example.
City Manager Thornton stated that the table of permitted uses allows specific
uses in each zone which is handled at staff level. PUD’s and subdivisions
should go before the Planning Board, and if necessary appoint a review
committee.
Alderman Potter questioned if applications meet UDO requirements, why go before
the Planning Board? Mr. Thornton stated that Section 12-5 was placed in the UDO
when the City had no Planning Director.
Alderman Potter stated if an item goes before the Planning Board, then they
should have the right to vote on whether or not it should go to Committee, but
if an item meets the requirements of the UDO, this should be handled by staff.
The Planning Board should review the larger projects and be able to decide if a
committee review is needed.
Mayor Howard asked who makes the determination on what should go before the
Planning Board. Amy Nelson, City Planner stated Article 12: Section 12-
5 Application Review Procedure describes the process.
Ms. Tish Hatem, Chairperson of the Planning Board during pre-agenda meetings
with staff, it is recommended whether or not an item should be sent to
committee.
Mr. Fred Guerrina, member of the Planning Board stated some of the Planning
Board members have expertise in many areas and as a result, can be an asset in
assisting staff.
Alderman Karn and Poole reiterated that items can still go to review committee
if recommended, but believes every project does not need to go before a review
committee.
Mr. Dale McPherson stated that the Planning Board is trying to insure that
everything coming into the City is in compliance with the Unified Development
Ordinance
Alderman Poole stated the Planning Board did not agree with either option and
developed its own recommendation; the Committee’s vote was divided.
Alderman Karn motioned, seconded by Alderman Poole to accept text changes to
Section 12-5 Application Review Procedure and change the wording in 12-5(a) by
deleting approval and inserting recommendation of the Planning Board and/or
approval by; and 12(b) insert with approval of the administrator going to
review committee. The votes were 3 ayes ; Aldermen Karn, Boguskie and Poole. 4
nays : Aldermen Adams, Frink, Potter and Mayor Howard. Motion failed 4-3
Article 3, Section 3.1 Membership and Vacancies 
Alderman Poole explained under Article 3, Section 3-1 Membership and Vacancies,
the UDO states a vacancy shall exist on the Planning Board if a member is
absent from 25% or more of the Board’s regular meetings. The Planning Board
Operations Procedures Committee included special meetings, workshops and
committee meetings. The vacancy “may” be declared and filled by the Board of
Aldermen instead of “shall.” (Planning Board recommended the verb “may” and to
eliminate special meetings and committee meetings from the attendance
requirements. The Committee recommended “shall” and special meetings and
workshops should be included.
Alderman Adams motioned to accept the Planning Board’s recommendation, seconded
by Alderman Frink. Discussion: Alderman Karn read an excerpt from the UDO which
stated “faithful attendance at the meetings of the Board is considered a
prerequisite for the maintenance of membership on that Board. A vacancy shall
exist on the Board if members are absent from 25% of the meetings.” The
Committee members believe workshops and committee meetings should be included.
Discussion: Alderman Adams and Frink opposed dismissing members without
consideration due to sickness/work. Alderman Potter stated all meetings should
be included. Alderman Adams amended the motion to include regular, special,
workshops and committee meetings to be included in the 25%.  The vote was 4
ayes, Aldermen Adams, Frink, Potter, and Mayor Howard. 3 nays, Aldermen Karn,
Poole, Boguskie. Motion passed 4-3
Alderman Poole recommended the same language in Section 3-1 for Section 3-2,
Rules of Conduct which will make it consistent. Alderman Potter motioned,
seconded by Alderman Frink to use the same language in Section 3.1. The vote
was 4 ayes, Aldermen Potter, Frink, Adams, and Mayor Howard. 3 nays, Aldermen
Poole, Karn, Boguskie. Motion passed 4-3
Alderman Poole stated in Section 3-2 (a)  the call for applicants to fill the
vacancy will be made immediately after the offending member is dismissed. The
dismissed member may apply for reinstatement by submitting an application for
the vacant position . Motion by Alderman Poole to include this change, seconded
by Alderman Potter. Vote unanimous
Section 3.3 (a) Meetings: Alderman Poole stated these procedures will
be followed “in the event that a quorum will not exist, the Chairperson in
consultation with the administrator will advise board members and the public
accordingly.” Alderman Karn motioned to accept the change, seconded by Alderman
Poole. Vote unanimous.
Section 3.3 (f) Alderman Poole noted changes which accommodate computer files.
Motion to approve by Alderman Boguskie seconded by Alderman Poole. Vote
unanimous.
Section 3-5 Basic Studies referenced release of information from all City
officials to Planning Board. Change verb from shall to “may.” Alderman Boguskie
noted there are some records that cannot be released. He motioned to approve
the word “may”, seconded by Alderman Karn. Vote unanimous.
Section 3-7 Zoning Ordinance (b) deleted from “time to time” which is an
editorial change. Alderman Karn motioned to accept deletions 3-7 (b) and 3-7
(a) from time to time, seconded by Alderman Boguskie. Vote unanimous.
Section 3-9 Urban Renewal, no change.
Section 3-10 Public Utilities, Committee recommended deleting due to the
ambiguity this is not a state requirement. Alderman Karn stated deleting this
section does not exempt the City from going before the Planning Board on
projects. Alderman Karn motioned to delete Section 3-10, seconded by Alderman
Poole. Vote unanimous.
Section 3-11(c) Miscellaneous Powers and Duties, Committee recommended
deleting employees because Planning Board does not have employees. Alderman
Poole motioned to delete the word “ or employees ,” seconded by Alderman
Boguskie. Vote unanimous.
Section 3-12 Planning Board Procedures for Reporting to the Board of Aldermen.
added “ working days” and “after approval by the Planning Board.”  Motion to
approve changes as written by Alderman Boguskie, seconded by Alderman Poole.
Vote unanimous
Section 3-13 Advisory Council and Special Committees, editorial change to last
sentence to “duties and responsibilities” Motion by Alderman Poole, seconded by
Alderman Frink, vote unanimous. Vote unanimous.
Section 3-13 (b) the terminology was clarified. No motion required.
Alderman Poole will re-write the wording and present it to the Board for Public
Hearing at the September meeting.
TDA Resolution - City Manager Thornton asked the Board to re-consider the
resolution to establish a TDA because a Public Hearing must be held prior to
adopting the resolution. Mayor Howard stated text changes had been made to the
resolution and the changes will be presented September 9 and Public Hearing
held.
ADJOURNMENT – 9:49 P.M.
Alderman Boguskie motioned to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Alderman Frink.
Vote unanimous.

VIII.
Public Presentation
a)   Report from the 2010 Fourth of July Festival Committee- Don Parker
Mr. Don Parker, Chairman of the 2010 N. C. Fourth of July Festival Committee
reported July 2010 marked the 39th year of the festival since incorporation in
1972. He stated that the economic impact was difficult to assess but
conservative estimates showed that out of town visitors spent $5.2 million in
Southport and other areas. He stated that the City of Southport gains sales tax
revenue from vendors who generated over $51,000 for the budget. The Festival
Committee has 50 Committee Chairs, hundreds of volunteers, Board of Directors
i.e. City Managers of Southport and Oak Island. The Committee did not receive
any input or feedback that they were doing anything other than what the City
wanted them to do. He asked if there are other issues to be addressed that they
be presented to the Festival Board through the City’s membership.
Alderman Potter referenced the administrative agreement in 1999 with the
Chamber and questioned approval if Southport did not have any administrative
duties. Mr. Parker stated his understanding is when the Fourth of July Festival
was incorporated everything was inclusive in the Board’s responsibilities.
Mayor Howard explained that the Southport Fourth of July Festival was begun at
the urging of the Board of Aldermen in the 1960’s which was a partnership with
the town and community. In 1971-72 it became more regional and was incorporated
as the N.C. 4th of July Festival under Lt. Governor James B. Hunt. He stated
that the City always gave its blessings and participation because they saw the
value of the festival occurring in Southport. However, he was not aware of the
City having any specific administrative responsibilities, and the City
initially assigned staff to help in various areas of the event in the early
1960’s. Mayor Howard stated the Board minutes from this time may reference the
agreement in question, but he was not aware of any administrative functions.
Alderman Potter stated that there is some contention concerning the 4th of July
Festival because of the way merchants are being treated by vendors who are the
life blood of the City.
Alderman Boguskie suggested a meeting be held with the merchants and the 4th of
July Committee as previously discussed with Mr. Parker to address concerns. Mr.
Parker asked that ground rules be established and fair representation from
merchants in town. Mayor Howard stated that Aldermen Poole and Potter are
formulating a Committee with appointments forthcoming. Alderman Poole shared
with the Board that she had received calls from merchants who had some issues.
She and Alderman Potter discussed setting up a committee and will formulate the
purpose to have available at the next regular City Council meeting. They will
also meet with the merchants to find out what their issues are and schedule a
meeting.
Mayor Howard thanked the 4th of July Committee for their report and commended
the volunteers for their service.
Mayor Howard stated that some of the citizens in the audience were present due
to the Tourism Development Authority and occupancy tax being on the agenda but
removed. He asked if Board members wished to explain to the public why the item
was removed from the agenda.
Alderman Poole stated she voted for the motion initially. However, once the
information was reported in the media more citizens became aware of what was
being considered. She received several calls. It is her belief that more
information should be researched and reviewed before further consideration by
the Board.

Amy Nelson, City Planner explained the current zoning of Fort Johnston and the

use.

a)   Consideration of Southport Minimum Housing Code Ordinance Text Amendment;

MINIMUM HOUSING CODE
SECTION 3-305
If, after notice and hearing, the Hearing Officer determines that the dwelling
under consideration is unfit for human habitation, he shall state in writing
his findings of fact in support of that determination and shall issue and cause
to be served upon the owner thereof an order.
1.    If the repair, alteration or improvement of the dwelling can be made at a
reasonable cost in relation to the value of the dwelling (the ordinance of the
city may fix a certain percentage of this value as being reasonable), requiring
the owner, within the time specified, to repair, alter or improve the dwelling
in order to render it fit for human habitation or to vacate and close the
dwelling as a human habitation; or habitation. The order may require that the
property be vacated and closed only if continued occupancy during the time
allowed for repair will present a significant threat of bodily harm, taking
into account the nature of the necessary repairs, alterations, or improvements;
the current state of the property; and any additional risks due to the presence
and capacity of minors under the age of 18 or occupants with physical or mental
disabilities. The order shall state that the failure to make timely repairs as
directed in the order shall make the dwelling subject to the issuance of an
unfit order under subdivision (4) of this section; or
2.    If the repair, alteration or improvement of the dwelling cannot be made
at a reasonable cost in relation to the value of the dwelling (the ordinance of
the city may fix a certain percentage of this value as being reasonable),
requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to remove or
demolish such dwelling. However, notwithstanding any other provision of law, if
the dwelling is located in a historic district of the city and the Historic
District Commission determines, after a public hearing as provided by
ordinance, that the dwelling is of particular significance or value toward
maintaining the character of the district, and the dwelling has not been
condemned as unsafe, the order may require that the dwelling be vacated and
closed consistent with G.S. 160A-400.14(a).
Adopted this the 9th day of September 2010.

RESOLUTION APPROVING A REZONING REQUEST FROM R-10(RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT) TO OS
(OPEN SPACE DISTRICT) FOR 3.81 ACRES LOCATED AT 204 E. MOORE STREET, 103 S.
DAVIS STREET, 223 E. BAY STREET, AND PARCEL NUMBER 237LH048
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other land
use ordinances, and a zoning map that control land development within both the
City’s incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s zoning map; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has filed an application for a zoning map
amendment requesting that 3.81 acres located at 204 E. Moore Street, 103 S.
Davis Street, 223 E. Bay Street and parcel number 237LH048 be rezoned from R-10
to OS; and
WHEREAS, the City Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning
Board a favorable staff recommendation; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed rezoning be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to the NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on September 9, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed rezoning is
consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) the proposed rezoning is consistent with
the intent of the CAMA Land Use Plan, (ii) the impact to the adjacent property
owners and the surrounding community is reasonable, and the benefits of the
rezoning outweigh any potential inconvenience or harm to the community, and
(iii) the allowed uses within the proposed zoning district are comparable to
the site’s current land uses;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
rezoning request for 204 E. Moore Street, 103 S. Davis Street, 223 E. Bay
Street and parcel number 237LH048, and alteration to the Southport Zoning Map
is hereby approved and adopted.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 16, STREETS AND SIDEWALKS, OF THE CODE OF
ORDINANCES OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Sections
16-8 and 16-10 of the Code of Ordinances are hereby amended to read as follows:
Sec. 16-8. Obstruction of public rights of way.
(a)   Except as specifically set forth in subsection (b) herein, it shall be
unlawful for any person to place or cause to be placed on any public street,
road, alley, sidewalk or other public right of way within the City any wall,
fence, gate, brick, stone, wood, rock, vegetation or other structure, material
or substance above the horizontal plane of the existing ground. In addition, it
shall be unlawful for any person to take any action whatsoever within any
public right of way which creates a hazardous condition or safety hazard or
which otherwise interferes with or obstructs in any manner the passage of
persons or vehicles upon or within said public rights of way or which
obstructs, interferes with or hinders lawful parking within any public right of
way.
(b) Nothing herein shall prevent any business or other legal entity located in
areas zoned CBD and BD from (i) placing objects which are not otherwise
prohibited under the Southport Code of Ordinances on that portion of a sidewalk
which is directly abutting the building occupied by such business or entity,
provided that said items do not extend more than 36 inches into the sidewalk
and do not violate Section 16-7 of the Code of Ordinances prohibiting the
display of goods, or (ii) placing A-Frame signs on a sidewalk or right of way
where specifically allowed under the Southport Unified Development Ordinance .
Notwithstanding this, however, no business or other entity may place or cause
to be placed any object on a sidewalk so as to violate the provisions of the
ADA regarding unobstructed clearance.
Sec. 16-10. Existing encroachments on rights of way.
In the event that the Southport code enforcement officer determines that there
exists any encroachment, obstacle, vegetation, wares, goods or other condition
within a public right of way or sidewalk in violation of Section 16-7 or
Section 16-8 of this Code or which interferes with the free passage of persons
or vehicles within said right of way or sidewalk, or which otherwise creates a
hazard to the public, said code enforcement officer shall attempt to identify
the person(s) responsible for said obstacle or encroachment. Upon
identification, the code enforcement officer shall notify in writing said
responsible person(s) who shall have seventy-two (72) hours from the date of
notification to remove said encroachment or condition. In the event that the
responsible party fails to remove said obstacle or encroachment within the time
allowed, and in addition to other remedies as allowed by law, the city may
promptly remove said obstacle or encroachment and shall charge the cost of said
removal to the party responsible for said obstacle, encroachment or condition.
In the event that the code enforcement officer is not able to identify the
responsible party, or if the condition or encroachment creates an imminent and
immediate danger to the public, the city may summarily remove said encroachment
or other condition within the right of way without notice.
This ordinance shall take effect on the 9th day of September, 2010.
City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard

II.
Invocation
The invocation was delivered by the Mayor.
III.
Rules and Procedures for the Board of Aldermen
Alderman Karn referenced the Rules of Procedures adopted by the Board on July
31, 2010 setting forth rules in the manner meetings should be conducted. He
discussed rule #9 as referenced below:
Rule 9. When the Presiding Officer Is in Active Debate
If the mayor or other presiding officer becomes actively engaged in debate on a
particular proposal, he or she shall designate another council member to
preside over the debate. The mayor or other presiding officer shall resume
presiding as soon as action on the matter is concluded.
Comment: Good leadership depends, to a certain extent, on not taking sides
during a debate. On a small board this may not always be feasible or desirable;
yet an unfair advantage accrues to the side whose advocate controls access to
the floor. This rule is designed to insure even-handed treatment to both sides
during a heated debate. Ordinarily if the mayor is leading the meeting, he or
she should ask the mayor pro tempore to preside in this situation, but if that
person also engaged in the debate, the mayor should feel free to call on some
other council member in order to achieve the purpose of this rule.
Alderman Karn stated that any decision by the Presiding Officer can be appealed
by the Board. He stated an appeal motion and point of order cannot be denied
and cited rule 18.
Rule 18. Procedural Motions
(a)   Certain Motions Allowed. In addition to substantive proposals, only the
following procedural motions, and no others, are in order. Unless otherwise
noted, each motion is debatable, may be amended, and requires a majority of the
votes cast, a quorum being present, for adoption. Procedural motions are in
order while a substantive motion is pending and at other times, except as
otherwise noted.
Comment: Rule 18 reflects substantial departure from the rule in RONR. Each
procedural motion in RONR was reviewed to determine whether it was appropriate
for use by a small board; substantial modifications and deletions were the
result. The following enumeration of procedural motions is exhaustive; if a
procedural option is not on the list, then it is not available.
Procedural motions are frequently used to “act upon” a substantive motion by
amending it, delaying consideration of it, and so forth. They are in order
while substantive motions are pending as well as at other times.
In addition, as in RONR, several procedural motions can be entertained in
succession without necessarily disposing of the previous procedural motion. The
order of priority establishes which procedural motion yields to which—that is,
which procedural motion may be made and considered while another one is
pending.
The procedural motions are summarized in table form in the appendix. Note that
the appended table is intended only to provide a quick reference guide to the
motions; this rule and its comments should be consulted for a discussion of how
each procedural motion is used.
(b)    Order of Priority of Motions. In order of priority (if applicable), the
procedural motions are
Motion 1. To Appeal a Procedural Ruling of the Presiding Officer. A decision of
the presiding officer ruling a motion in or out of order, determining whether a
speaker has gone beyond reasonable standards of courtesy in his or her remarks,
or entertaining and answering a question of parliamentary law or procedure may
be appealed to the council, as specified in Rule 7. This appeal is in order
immediately after such a decision is announced and at no other time. The member
making the motion need not be recognized by the presiding officer and the
motion, if timely made, may not be ruled out of order.
Comment: Rule 7 allows the ruling of the presiding officer on certain
procedural matters to be appealed to the council. This appeal must be made as
soon as the presiding officer’s decision is announced, so this motion is
accorded the highest priority. See Rule 7 and its Comment for further
discussion of this motion.
Alderman Karn read the following comment by Fleming Bell from the School of
Government and noted that the Board’s own rules were violated by the Presiding
Officer in accordance with the rules and procedures adopted by the Board.
Comment: Good leadership depends, to a certain extent, on not taking sides
during a debate. On a small board this may not always be feasible or desirable;
yet an unfair advantage accrues to the side whose advocate controls access to
the floor. This rule is designed to insure even-handed treatment to both sides
during a heated debate. Ordinarily if the mayor is leading the meeting, he or
she should ask the mayor pro tempore to preside in this situation, but if that
person also engaged in the debate, the mayor should feel free to call on some
other council member in order to achieve the purpose of this rule.
Alderman Karn referenced Section 2. Of the Code of Ethics  “treating other
board members and the public with respect, and honoring the opinions of others
even when they disagree,” citing the manner in which his motion was refused. He
stated that it is important that Board members know the rules and follow them
and the presiding officer not minimize the amount of involvement in a debate.
IV.
Elimination of Street Access Existing Curb Cut at 102 South Caswell Avenue
Mayor Howard referenced the minutes from the Traffic and Transportation
Committee in the Board’s packet from the August 30th meeting. He read an
excerpt from a letter written by Terry Lee, owner of property at South Caswell
Avenue to the City asking that his two curb cuts be restored which allowed him
access to his property on Caswell and Moore, which was blocked by the City’s
new parking spaces. Mayor Howard stated he read the City codes, visited the
property and did not deem any conflict with honoring Mr. Lee’s request. He
asked the Board to give favorable consideration to Mr. Lee’s request to re-
establish the curb cuts.
Alderman Boguskie stated that the lots have been vacant for ten years. In his
opinion, one cut is sufficient until Mr. Lee decides to build on the property.
Alderman Karn stated one curb cut gives the owner adequate access to his
property.
Alderman Adams stated due to the size of the lot, the property would be more
desirable with two curb cuts.
Attorney Isenberg advised the Board that property abutting a public road is
entitled to legal access. Submittal of a site plan determines the number of
curb cuts required. Legally Mr. Lee is entitled to one curb cut, however;
submittal of a development plan will determine where the cuts are to be located
and the number that is legally entitled, but there is nothing that prohibits
the Board from giving him two cuts.
Alderman Boguskie motioned that the City provide one driveway cut at the corner
of Caswell and Moore. Motion died for lack of a second vote.
Alderman Karn moved to grant Mr. Lee both curb cuts, seconded by Alderman
Adams. No discussion, the votes were 4 ayes, Aldermen Karn, Adams, Potter and
Poole. 1 nay vote, Alderman Boguskie. Motion passed

VI.
Annexation Feasibility Report
City Manager Thornton stated that there are two approaches for the annexation
initiative:
·   The comprehensive approach is the option to get across the discharge canal
and take in Smithville Woods Subdivision.
·   The phased approach would end on this side of the canal and not take in
Smithville Woods Subdivision.
City Manager Thornton referenced the annexation report prepared by Benchmark
CMR and stated if it is the Board’s desire to move forward with annexation, the
Board needs to select the option it wishes to consider. Staff looked at
revenues vs. expenditures and wastewater would be the most expense. There are
393 parcels within the comprehensive annexation area and 168 parcels identified
within the phased approach. Statistical data was given to the Board for review.
Alderman Karn asked about the resolution adopted May 14, 2009 amending the
sewer policy for properties annexed into the City by City initiated annexations
and who determines whether or not a septic system is functional. City Manager
Thornton responded that the County Health Department is responsible for
permitting and inspecting septic systems.
Attorney Isenberg stated the Board may change its policy on what the annexed
persons will pay, but if it is more, the policy would have to be in effect 180
days before the resolution of intent is passed.
Mayor Howard noted the City can gain up to $350,000 in revenues annually by
annexing.
In answer to question from Alderman Boguskie, City Manager Thornton responded
that the City has to make sewer available to annexed areas at an approximate
cost of $4.5 million.
Attorney Isenberg stated if the Board decides on annexation, the first step is
to adopt a resolution of intent which must contain 1) complete description of
the property to be annexed, 2) the date of public informational meeting, 3)
date of public hearing and 4) if the city’s current resolution of consideration
does not cover the entire area to be annexed, a statement that the annexation
cannot become effective until at least one year after the annexation ordinance
is adopted.
City Manager Thornton asked members of the Board to discuss and consider the
information presented because the Board must decide what is best for the future
of Southport including planned growth.
VII.
Adjournment
No further business, motion by Alderman Boguskie, seconded by Alderman Adams to
adjourn the meeting.

VIII.
Public Hearing
Alderman Frink moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to enter Public Hearing for a
Zoning Amendment Text Change ZA 10-0907-01. Vote unanimous.
Amy Nelson, City Planner and the Planning Board recommended an amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance which alters the current wording to provide more
houses for a property owner where empty lots exists next to a lot in question.
The change also makes provision for the protection of City easements so that
utility access is not compromised.
Proposed wording:
Note 4. Reduction of Minimum Front Yards In Residential Districts Where Lots
Along Block Face Have Less Than The Required Minimum. Where the front yards of
lots along the block face containing a subject lot are less than the minimum
front yard setback of the district, the average front yard setbacks of the lots
along the block face containing a subject lot shall be the minimum front yard
for such lot, with the exception that no house may be constructed over city
utility easements, including sidewalks.
Mr. Buddy Barnes, Planning Board member acknowledged support of the amendment.
No more comments, Alderman Poole moved to close the Hearing, seconded by
Alderman Potter. Vote unanimous.

a)   Consideration of Zoning Amendment Text Change ZA 10-0907-01
Alderman Boguskie moved to adopt the resolution amending the Unified

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
a proposed amendment to Article 11 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on October 14, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) this aspect of setbacks is not properly
addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance, (ii) this amendment is
necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the City of Southport,
and (iii) it is necessary
to promote the public safety and general welfare of the community by allowing
for the adjustment of certain front yard setback lines in the City.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 14th day of October, 2010.
City of Southport
By:
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
ATTEST:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander
Clerk

AMEND:
ARTICLE 11: TABLE OF AREA, YARD, DENSITY AND HEIGHT REQUIREMENTS
SECTION 11-1: Notes to the Table of Area, Yard, Density and Height Requirements
Note 4. Reduction of Minimum Front Yards In Residential Districts Where Lots
Along Block Face Have Less Than The Required Minimum. Where the front yards of
lots along the block face containing a subject lot are less than the minimum
front yard setback of the district, the average front yard setbacks of the lots

   c) Annexation - City Manager
   The Board discussed the proposed annexation and its options. City Manager
Thornton encouraged the Board to consider what is best for the future of
Southport and growth. The options presented were the comprehensive approach to
get across Progress Energy’s discharge canal and take in Smithville Woods
Subdivision, and the phased approach which would end on this side of the canal
excluding Smithville Woods.
   Mayor Howard stated in his opinion the comprehensive plan is the most
feasible. He recommended the annexation process and a cost feasibility study be
a mutual effort with the people in the affected areas, the City keep impact
fees at a minimum, provides a grace period where reduction in fees will be
provided if people connect and abandon their current system.
   City Manager Thornton explained that the City has a standard residential
sewer impact fee schedule based on the number of bedrooms. Alderman Karn asked
about incentives to hookup to the system. Mayor Howard noted that the average
impact fee for a three bedroom house is $7200.
   Alderman Boguskie noted that W.K. Dickson provided an estimated cost
projection of $4.5 million to construct a gravity feed sewer system with
estimated payments of $334,000+ annually for twenty (20) years.
   Alderman Adams expressed concern that the annexation proposal did not
continue to East Leonard Street and divided Jabbertown Road. City Manager
Thornton stated he would discuss this with the consultant. Alderman Poole asked
if a lift station was included in the feasibility study for Jabbertown. City
Manager Thornton noted that two lift stations were included in the Smithville
Woods area and one for Jabber town Road.
   Alderman Karn asked if the policy adopted May 14, 2009 (see below) would
change with an incentive program. City Manager Thornton acknowledged that it is
the policy currently in place and would require discussion by the Board;
however as the policy stands if residential property is sold, the new owner
must connect regardless to the status of their private wastewater disposal
system.
   Attorney Isenberg explained the policy was written so that it would be known
and taken into consideration during the contract sale. In answer to a question
from Alderman Adams, Attorney Isenberg stated the Board could announce that
anyone in the City not connected to wastewater have a certain number of days to
connect at a reduced price.
RESOLUTION OF SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN AMENDING SEWER POLICY FOR PROPERTIES
ANNEXED INTO THE CITY BY CITY-INITIATED ANNEXATIONS
    BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that Section 1 of the
sewer policy for properties annexed into the city by city-initiated annexations
adopted on Year2009Day12Month3lstransMarch 12, 2009, is hereby amended to read
as follows:
1. Any improved property which is annexed into the City of Southport by a city-
initiated annexation proceeding and which is already connected to a private
wastewater disposal system on the effective date of said annexation shall be
allowed to continue to utilize a currently functioning and permitted private
wastewater disposal system until such time as the first of the following events
occur: (i) the private wastewater disposal system fails, or (ii) the use of
property changes to a use which would require significant modification of the
existing private system, or (iii) the ownership of the property changes,
provided, however, that a transfer of ownership by conveyance or operation of
law without consideration to immediate family members shall not be deemed to be
a change of ownership under this provision, or (iv) any environmental issue
arises resulting in a determination of private wastewater disposal system
closure by the State of North Carolina, federal government or Brunswick County.
Upon the occurrence of the first of said events, the City shall notify the
property owner and said property shall be connected to the city sewer within 60
days from notification by City that connection is required. Connection shall be
made in accordance with the City’s policies and ordinances existing at the time
of connection, and the property owner shall pay all charges and fees in effect
at said time except as otherwise provided herein. Notwithstanding the above,
nothing herein shall be construed to require mandatory connection to the city
system for a private wastewater disposal system which is functioning and
permitted on the effective date of a city-initiated annexation for routine
repair and maintenance which does not involve significant modifications or
improvements to the existing system as determined by the appropriate permitting
agency or authority.
   Adopted May 14, 2009.
   Alderman Poole motioned, seconded by Alderman Frink to recuse Alderman Adams
from the vote due to property ownership in the proposed area. The vote of
approval was unanimous.
   Alderman Karn moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to authorize the City
Manager to move forward with the comprehensive option for annexation and to
consider including the property between Jabber town and East Leonard in the
plan. The vote of approval was unanimous.
   d) Double Taxation
   Mayor Howard acknowledged Rescue Squad members and the EMS Director of
Brunswick County. He read a written report about double taxation and the need
to look at the duplication of services. Mayor Howard stated that citizens are
paying twice for some of the same services. He stated that his report is not an
attack against the Rescue Squad and the City will be looking at other areas to
cut back due to difficult economic times. He recommended a task force be
created by the City and County to look at double taxation issues.
(Excerpts from prepared statement below)
“Property tax duplication is a complex issue for city residents; which can
occur in several ways to include where city taxpayers who pay city and county
taxes are either denied, or charged extra for, certain county services.
Hopefully we can come together with the county to establish ways for the County
to reimburse cities for services they provide that would otherwise be provided
by the county. To this point the state has not recognized the importance of
double taxation. Do we need to ask our representatives who serve us in the
North Carolina General Assembly to pass a State Tax Duplication Law?
It seems prudent for the County to create a new City/County Double Taxation
Task Force to consider a reimbursement program for Brunswick County to prorate
to cities to partially offset the cost of duplicated services, particularly
regarding police, parks and recreation, rescue, capital for infrastructure such
as water & sewer and for road maintenance. Such an undertaking has been
successful with providing Fire Services throughout Brunswick County with the
development of Fire Districts. The task force could be composed of professional
staff from the county and the affected cities with responsibility to conduct a
feasibility study. Hopefully that study would demonstrate the need for and
provide that cities would be reimbursed based on what the county would have
spent if it performed the service in the municipality, tied to the county’s
actual, net, expenditures derived from property taxes. As an example, if the
county said it would spend $50,000 on a particular service, but Southport spent
$75,000 on that same service, the City would only receive a $50,000
reimbursement.”
“Serious consideration should be given to consolidating selective services with
Brunswick County. There’s an economy of scale to be had rather than services
being replicated by the city and the county especially when our citizens are
paying double for many services.
   Mayor Howard asked the Board to authorize him as Mayor to begin
conversations with Brunswick County officials using the expertise of other
Board Members and staff as needed. Alderman Potter recommended other Board
members be included in the meeting. Alderman Adams suggested the entire Board
attend the initial meeting in support of the Mayor and recommended Mayor Howard
take the lead. Alderman Boguskie volunteered to work with the Mayor. The Board
agreed by consensus that Mayor Howard move forward with his recommendation.
   Mayor Howard suggested that another Committee be established in December to
keep several issues running concurrently. Alderman Poole asked about the survey
referenced in the Mayor’s report and when it will be conducted. Mayor Howard
suggested areas be identified and prioritized in December and afterwards, send
out a survey to the citizens.
   e) Board Information

Raleigh Convention Center.

   Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Frink to enter Public Hearing for

   a) Zoning Amendment Text Change ZA 10-1011-01
   Amy Nelson, City Planner explained that this change would alter the current
wording from the previous version of the UDO to allow more flexibility in
locating accessory structures by placing back some of the original wording to
allow accessory buildings within five square feet of property lines. Staff and
Planning Board recommend this action.
Remove the following:
(G) Accessory Structures. The total area of accessory structures shall not
exceed 75% of the rear yard area of the lot and shall meet all rear and side
yard setbacks of the district. No accessory structure shall be constructed
beyond the rear building line of the primary structure. A maximum of two (2)
accessory structures shall be permitted within the rear yard of any R-10, R-20,
MF, PUD, O-I, CBD, BD or HC zoned property.
Detached garages with a second floor accessory residential dwelling may not
exceed a ground level building footprint area of five hundred-thirty (530)
square feet.
Replace with:
(G) Accessory Structures. The total area of accessory structures shall not
exceed 75% of the rear yard area of the lot and shall meet all rear and side
yard setbacks of the district. However, accessory structures 530 sq. ft. or
smaller in any district may have setbacks of five (5) feet to a side or rear
property line. No accessory structure shall be constructed beyond the front
building line of the primary structure. A maximum of two (2) accessory
structures shall be permitted within the rear yard of any R-10, R-20, MF, PUD,
O-I, CBD, BD or HC zoned property.
Detached garages with a second floor accessory residential dwelling may not
exceed a ground level building footprint area of five hundred-thirty (530)
square feet and may be constructed behind the front building line provided they
are located no closer than 5 feet to any adjoining lot line.
   No public comments.
   b) Zoning Amendment Text Change ZA 10-1014-01
   Mayor Howard stated this agenda item was removed but the Public Hearing will
be held.
   Ms. Nelson stated that the text change is a correction to the wording in the
UDO where Holland Planning Consultants in error by their own admission had a
phrase in the definition that should have been removed under Article 13:
Planned Building Group Regulation.
Remove the following:
Planned Building Group. A residential project containing nine (9) or more
attached dwelling units, a residential project with attached dwelling units for
individual ownership; a commercial and/or institutional project located in an
O-I, BD, HC, or PUD zoning district; a commercial and/or office-institutional
project located within an O-I, BD, HC, or PUD zoning district involving the
construction of a building greater than seven thousand (7,000) square feet; a
commercial and/or office-institutional project within an O-I, BD, or PUD zoning
district involving the construction of more than one (1) building; or a
manufactured home park.
Replace with:
Planned Building Group. A residential project containing nine (9) or more
attached dwelling units, a residential project with attached dwelling units for
individual ownership; a commercial and/or office-institutional project located
within an O-I, BD, HC, or PUD zoning district involving the construction of a
building greater than seven thousand (7,000) square feet; a commercial and/or
office-institutional project within an O-I, BD, or PUD zoning district
involving the construction of more than one (1) building; or a manufactured
home park.
   Mr. Buddy Barnes, Planning Board member residing at 425 West West Street,
stated that he and former Mayor Sandy Spencer was on the Planning Board when
the UDO was written and he does not believe the current wording is a mistake.
Holland wrote three other town UDO’s and the wording is the same. Staff
proposes to have a Technical Review Committee (TRC) and there is no law or
statute that makes the TRC accountable to the public.
   Mr. Fred Guerrina, 710 Dale Avenue and member of the Planning Board
encouraged the Board to leave the wording as is to insure an open process.
   Ms. Sandy Spencer, 410 West Brunswick Street, former Mayor and Planning
Board member did not recall the section of the UDO that was in question.
   No further comments from the public, Alderman Karn moved, seconded by
Alderman Poole to close the Public Hearing and re-enter regular session. The
vote of approval was unanimous.
   a) Zoning Amendment Text Change ZA 10-1011-01
   Alderman Karn motioned, seconded by Alderman Adams to adopt the resolution

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning
Board a proposed amendment to Article 11 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended
that this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved;
and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on November 10, 2010, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to
the Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land
Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) this aspect of setbacks is
not properly addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance, (ii) this
amendment is necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the City of
Southport, and (iii) it is necessary to promote the public safety and general
welfare of the community by allowing certain accessory structures to have
decreased setback requirements in the City.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.

AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
TEXT AMENDMENT # 10-1014-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With
Respect to Basic Definitions and Interpretations, and Planned Building Group
Regulation
AMEND:
ARTICLE 2: BASIC DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS
Section 2-2: Definitions of Basic Terms
Planned Building Group. A residential project containing nine (9) or more
attached dwelling units, a residential project with attached dwelling units for
individual ownership; a commercial and/or office-institutional project located
within an O-I, BD, HC, or PUD zoning district involving the construction of a
building greater than seven thousand (7,000) square feet; a commercial and/or
office-institutional project within an O-I, BD, or PUD zoning district
involving the construction of more than one (1) building; or a manufactured
home park.
ARTICLE 13: PLANNED BUILDING GROUP REGULATION
Planned Building Group. A residential project containing nine (9) or more
attached dwelling units, a residential project with attached dwelling units for
individual ownership; a commercial and/or office-institutional project located
within an O-I, BD, HC, or PUD zoning district involving the construction of a
building greater than seven thousand (7,000) square feet; a commercial and/or
office-institutional project within an O-I, BD, or PUD zoning district
involving the construction of more than one (1) building; or a manufactured
home park.
ARTICLE 13: PLANNED BUILDING GROUP REGULATION
Section 13-3 (A): Business Planned Building Group Regulations
Construction or Expansion of Planned Building Group. The following planned
building group regulations shall apply to a commercial and/or office-
institutional project located within an O-I, BD, HC, or PUD zoning district
involving the construction of a building greater than seven thousand (7,000)
square feet; a commercial and/or office-institutional project within a O-I, BD,
or PUD zoning district involving the construction of more than one (1)
building. Mixed uses are allowed in approved Business Planned Building Groups.

    AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
TEXT AMENDMENT # 10-1118-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With
Respect to Conditional Uses
AMEND:
1) ARTICLE 2: BASIC DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS
Section 2-2 “Definitions of Basic Terms” is hereby amended by adding the
following definitions in alphabetical sequence:
Hospital Emergency Air Ambulance Helipad
The word helipad is short for helicopter landing pad, a landing area for
helicopters. While helicopters are able to operate on a variety of relatively
flat surfaces, a fabricated helipad provides a clearly marked hard surface away
from obstacles where a helicopter can land. Helipads are usually constructed
out of concrete and are marked with a circle and/or a letter "H", so as to be
visible from the air. A helipad does not have fuel and service facilities and
does not maintain an air traffic controller. A helipad is for the sole purpose
of facilitating emergency medical transport via air ambulance.
2) ARTICLE 10: TABLE OF PERMITTED USES:
The Table of Permitted Uses is hereby amended by adding “Hospital Emergency Air
Ambulance Helipad”, and by placing a “C” entry in the O&I (Office and
Institutional District) column.
3) ARTICLE 12: ZONING & CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT APPROVAL
Section 12-19: Supplemental Regulations
“Regulations for Conditional Uses”, is hereby amended by adding a new section,
to be inserted in alphabetical sequence, to read as follows:
Use: Hospital Emergency Air Ambulance Helipad, Conditional Use District: O&I
Use – Hospital Emergency Air Ambulance Helipad. 
The following specific provision shall be met as minimum standards prior to the
approval of any business engaging in the establishment and use of a Hospital
Emergency Air Ambulance Helipad as a conditional use in the office and
institutional (O&I) zoning district.
(A) Compliance with federal regulations and standards.
The establishment of any helipad and the operation and flight of helicopters
within and above the corporate limits of the city shall at all times comply and
be in conformity with at least the minimum of all pertinent regulations and
standards promulgated from time to time by the Federal Aviation Administration
and other applicable federal agencies, with particular reference to applicable
federal air regulations, civil air regulations, and advisory circulars or
successor publications.
(B) Minimum altitude for helicopter flight.
Except when necessary for take-off or landing, no person may operate a
helicopter below the following altitudes:
(1) Generally.  An altitude allowing, if a power unit fails, an emergency
landing without undue hazard to persons or property on the surface. In
addition, each person operating a helicopter shall comply with the routes,
altitudes and other directions and regulations specifically prescribed for
helicopters by any rule or ordinance pertaining to the same. At no time shall a
helicopter be below 500 feet without special permission granted by the city
manager pursuant to authority and for cause described in this Article.
(2) Over congested areas.  Over any congested area of the city or over any open
air assembly of persons, an altitude of 1,000 feet above the highest obstacle
within a horizontal radius of 2,000 feet of the helicopter.
(3) Over other than congested areas.  An altitude of 500 feet above the surface
of open fields or areas upon which there are no trees, buildings or other
obstacles; provided, however, the helicopter shall not be operated closer than
500 feet to any person, vehicle, vessel, tree, tower or structure.
(C) Permit to operate helipad--Required; application; issuance; terms and
conditions.
(1) No helipad shall be established or used unless an application for the
establishment of the same shall have first been filed in writing with and
approved by the Board of Adjustment. Such application shall contain a
description of the proposed location, dimensions, obstruction clearance planes,
proximity and height of nearest buildings, trees, towers or other structures,
characteristics of the immediate area of such helipad and such other
information as the Board of Adjustment may require.
(2) If the Board of Adjustment finds and determines that the public safety and
convenience will be preserved and a nuisance or other burdensome condition will
not be created and that the public interest will not be adversely affected by
the establishment and use a helipad at such site and under such conditions and
that such use at such site will be in accord with pertinent zoning regulations,
it may issue a permit for the establishment and use of such helipad and the
operation of helicopters to and from the same. The Board of Adjustment may
impose such terms and conditions in the issuance of such permit as it
determines to be necessary in the promotion of the public safety, convenience,
health and welfare.
(3) No helipad shall be established or used unless such permit therefore has
been granted under the provisions hereof and the required insurance has been
issued and is in effect as required in this article.
(D) Same--Revocation.
In addition to any other remedies, the Board of Adjustment shall have the right
and authority to revoke any permit which may have been issued to establish and
operate a helipad within the city upon a finding, after notice, that any of the
provisions and requirements of this article have been violated or that the
public liability and property damage insurance required to be carried at all
times by the permittee has been canceled or for any reason has ceased to be in
full force and effect or if the operations at the helipad are performed in such
a manner as to become unduly hazardous or to constitute a nuisance or create
conditions which the Board of Adjustment may find to be contrary to the public
safety, health, convenience and welfare. Before any such permit may be revoked,
however, notice of at least ten days shall be given to the permittee and an
opportunity to be heard before the Board of Adjustment upon any charges shall
be given to such permittee.
(E) Insurance requirements.
(1) As a condition precedent to the issuance of a permit to establish and use a
helipad, the applicant for such permit shall first secure public liability and
property damage insurance in an insurance company licensed and authorized to do
business in the state in limits of not less than $250,000.00 for personal
injuries or death occasioned to one person, and, subject to that limitation for
one person, insuring against injuries or death in any one accident in limits of
at least $500,000.00 and for property damages in the sum of $500,000.00 for any
one accident; such applicant shall cause a certificate to be issued by such
insurance company certifying that such policies, as herein required, have been
issued and are in force and effect.
(2) This section shall not apply to the United States of America or any
military branch thereof, nor shall this section apply to the state, the North
Carolina National Guard, or any branch thereof.
(F) Compliance with safety and fire prevention standards.
As a further condition precedent to the issuance of a permit to establish and
use a helipad and to land and take-off helicopters from such helipad, the
applicant for such permit shall first secure written certification from the
City Manager that the helipad being considered complies with all safety and
fire prevention standards necessary for the safety of the operation and
adjacent properties and with the other provisions in this Article.
(G) Area and location of heliports and helipads.
(1) The minimum dimension of the area which describes an approved helipad shall
be equal to not less than 1 1/2 times the diameter of the rotors of the
helicopter.
(2) Approved helipads shall be so located that at least two obstruction
clearance planes are available which are compatible with the flight
characteristics of the helicopter. Obstruction clearance planes shall be
selected with due regard to the safety and convenience of persons and to the
safety of property on the surface.
(H) Prohibited acts generally.
It shall be unlawful to operate a helicopter within or above the corporate
limits of the city or to operate a helipad within such corporate limits:
(1) In a negligent or reckless manner so as to endanger the lives or property
of the operator or others.
(2) When the operator of such helicopter is under the influence of intoxicating
beverages, drugs, barbiturates or other stimuli or depressants.
(3) In violation of any of the provisions set forth in this section.
(4) Unless there is then outstanding and in full force and effect a valid
airworthiness certificate issued for such helicopter by the Federal Aviation
Administration or other federal agency with appropriate authority to issue such
certificate.
(5) Unless the operator flying such helicopter shall then and there have a
valid airman's certificate in full force and effect with the appropriate
aeronautical ratings issued by the Federal Aviation Administration or other
federal agency with appropriate authority to issue such certificate.
(6) To operate a helipad or a helicopter after the permit to do so has been
revoked.
(7) To operate a helicopter to or from any property or place within the city
other than a helipad in such location, with such dimensions and obstructions
clearance planes and such other safety provisions as comply with the federal
air regulations and the terms and conditions set forth in the permit issued by
the governing body of the city as hereinabove provided; provided, however, this
provision may be varied by the city manager in emergencies in which helicopter
operations at places other than at an approved helipad are necessary in
connection with the immediate extending of help because of a disaster or civil
disturbance or in performing an emergency errand of mercy or when the chief of
police or sheriff of the county certifies to the city manager that the use of
such helicopter in a special flight operation is urgent and immediately
necessary in aiding law enforcement or where there exists a special and urgent
necessity for the use of a helicopter at a place other than a helipad in the
preservation of the public peace, health, safety and welfare; but in no case,
emergency or otherwise, shall such helicopter be operated in violation of any
federal air regulations or upon the property of any person except after having
first obtained the permission and consent of such person owning or in control
of such premises that the same may be so used.
(I) Helicopter Operation
(1) No persons shall operate any helicopter within the limits of the City of
Southport unless there is outstanding for such helicopter a valid air-
worthiness certificate issued by the Federal Aviation Administration of the
United States of America.
(2) No person shall operate any helicopter within the limits of the City of
Southport unless there is outstanding for the person flying such helicopter a
valid airman’s certificate with appropriate ratings issued by the Federal
Aviation of the United States of America.
(J) Construction
Any person may construct, build, or designate space for a helipad in any area
of this municipality, where such use is permitted by the zoning ordinance,
subject to the following restrictions:
(1)   That if such helipad is to be elevated in any manner by being constructed
on a platform or on the roof of a building, such platform or building shall be
inspected and approved as structurally safe for use by a certified structural
engineer at the expense of the applicant.
(2)   That if such helipad is to be at ground level it shall either: (a) be
located in an enclosed area which does not permit access by the public at will,
or (b) be completely enclosed by a fence or wall, either temporary or
permanent, designed so as to provide safety for persons, vehicles or other
things in the area.
(3)   That the design, construction and physical characteristics of any such
helipad shall conform to applicable standards, rules and regulations of the
Federal Aviation Administration. That the plans and specifications of any such
helipad shall be submitted to the City Manager of the City of Southport for
examination and determination whether they conform to any applicable provisions
of the existing building code, and the necessary permits, if any are required
pursuant to such code, shall be obtained before any construction is begun.
(4)   Landing Pad. Every helipad located above ground level shall be provided
with a landing pad constructed in accordance with applicable Building Codes
and/or FAA Regulations.
(5)   Dust-Proof Cover. All helipad landing areas shall be composed of asphalt.
(6)   Lighting. Any helipad intended to be used for night landing or take-off
shall be provided with flood lights which are directed toward the ground and
windsock only, and with linear perimeter lighting of fluorescent or cold
cathode type, or by amber lights spaced around the helipad pad, not less than
20 feet apart.
(7)   All elevated helipads shall be restricted to helicopters not exceeding
the gross weight or load rating stated in the application for permit or
permits.
(8)   All helipads shall be marked in accordance with FAA criteria.
(K) Fencing
Every ground level helipad shall be fenced and protected to prevent entrance of
unauthorized personnel with a fence, a minimum of 36 inches in height, entirely
surrounding the minimum helipad area as established by the FAA; except that the
minimum fence height may be increased 12 inches for each 10 feet that the
landing area is extended beyond the minimum area required. Other fencing shall
be in accordance with applicable Building Code requirements, if any. Each side
of this fence shall be marked with an appropriate warning sign, two (2) feet by
two (2) feet in size.
(L) Minimum Area
No permit shall be issued for a helipad which does not meet the minimum area
standards of applicable FAA regulations.
(M) Safety Features Required
No permit for the operation of helipad shall be approved by the Chief of the
Southport Fire Department until the following fire prevention equipment is
provided at the site of the proposed helipad:
A set standpipe not less than two and one-half inches in diameter shall be
provided at each helipad landing site. This standpipe shall be provided with a
hose sufficiently long to reach the landing pad. This hose is to be equipped
with a spray nozzle and a water supply sufficient to efficiently operate same.
(1)   When a set standpipe cannot be provided, a Badger 50 lb. wheeled A,B,C
extinguisher unit: 50lb.A/B/C wheeled (30- A, / 160-B,C ) 1/2' hose 25' long w/
quick release handle and tires of hard rubber. shall be provided.
(2)   A telephone, other than a pay phone, shall be provided at each helipad
for emergency purposes.
(3)   Any elevated, or roof-top landing area shall be provided with two exits
as remote from each other as practical; at least one of the exits shall be a
stairway exit. The other exit may be an emergency exit leading from the area by
means of a ladder or a stairway on any landing area.
(4)   No smoking shall be permitted on any landing area.
(5)   No fueling or major repairing of helicopters shall be permitted at any
helipad.
(6)   Fire protection and other required emergency equipment shall be properly
shelter from weather.
No permit shall be approved by the Board of Adjustment until they are
sufficiently satisfied that no inordinate danger to the public will be created
by operation of helipads or by external load or temporary landing operations.
(N) Inspection
The Fire Chief, Police Chief or the Building Inspector, or any of their
authorized personnel, shall have authority to make periodic inspections of the
helipad to determine that all the requirements of a permit issued are complied
with.
(O) Revocation of License
The City Manager may revoke any permit issued herein if after investigation by
the Fire Chief, the Police Chief, or the Building Inspector, it is determined
that alteration of the physical profile of the area surrounding any helipad
renders its continued operation unsafe, or for the violation of any provisions
of law thereto pertaining, he may take appropriate action to suspend such
operation or impose such conditions upon continued operations as he may deem
fit.
(P) Proof of Aircraft Operation Liability Insurance or Bonding of Aircraft
Operator.
All operators of all aircraft using these facilities shall file proof of
possession of adequate insurance or other surety in the amount of
$1,000,000.00, in case of accidents, fires or personal or property damage
resulting from operation of their facility or aircraft.
(Q) Notice of Construction, Alteration or De-activation Required by Federal
Law.
All applicants shall give proper notice to the United States of America of
construction, alteration or de-activation as required by Federal Law on FAA
Form 7480-1. Proof of this notice shall be submitted with the application.
(R) Approach Zone
A helipad shall provide at least two approach lanes at least 90 degrees apart
for landing or takeoff, sufficiently clear of obstructions to provide a slope
of 1:8, approximately 7 degrees measured from the horizontal. Any curved
approach necessary due to the obstruction of buildings or structures shall
provide a turning radius of 600 feet. The flight approach to a helipad shall be
over open area and along major transportation corridors to the extent possible
