   d) Discussion of City of Southport TDA/Tourism and Economic Development
   Alderman Boguskie asked the Board to make a decision on the position of
tourism director because the City has been without one since April. The
position has been budgeted for ten (10) years and is needed to promote tourism
for Southport. As a result of the slow economy local businesses are hurting
financially and he referenced news articles from other areas experiencing
similar issues but they are pooling their resources to promote tourism.
Alderman Boguskie expressed uncertainty as to whether a Tourism Development
Authority was required when the 3% occupancy tax was initially instituted.
However, if an increase in the occupancy tax occurs, a TDA will be required and
the monies must be spent on tourism. The primary concern is to make a decision
on a Tourism Director.
    Alderman Karn emphasized comments by Alderman Boguskie and stated the
purpose of a Tourism Development Authority is to administer the occupancy tax.
The TDA was previously taken off the agenda so that the Board could determine
the effect a TDA would have on local businesses. He stated economic developer
was added to the job description so that the individual could work to retain
local businesses and bring in new ones. The Tourism Development Authority does
not need to be considered until the Board determines if it will increase the
occupancy tax.
   Alderman Karn then moved, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to authorize the
City Manager to hire a Tourism/Economic Development Director based on criteria
established by the Tourism Committee. Discussion:  City Manager Thornton
acknowledged that the position of Tourism Director had been advertised but
recommended re-advertisement because economic developer was added to the job
description. Alderman Adams stated he was not prepared to vote on the motion
because the agenda referenced discussion. Alderman Poole stated that she
requested to review how a non-profit organization handled tourism years ago,
and after research; it was her opinion that this is not the best to way to
handle tourism for the City.
    Alderman Karn withdrew the motion and asked that this issue be placed on
the January agenda, seconded by Alderman Boguskie. The vote of approval was
unanimous.

Sec. 6-42. Officers
The officers of the rescue squad shall consist of chief, assistant chief and
other officers as shall be called for in the bylaws of the organization. The
officers shall be elected by the members of squad according to the bylaws of
said squad, and shall serve a term of one (1) year. The results of the election
of officers shall be reported to the board of aldermen for the city at their
regular December meeting of each year. Officers of the rescue squad are subject
to the control and supervision of the board of aldermen and may be removed from
office at any time by the board of aldermen at its discretion.
(Ord. of 2-10-77; Ord. of 2-8-07)

squad members on the roster, one-third constitutes a quorum. Thirteen (13)
members were present and the valid election results were 7 for Neal Sage and 6
for Tammy Drew.

   a) Consideration of Resolution in support of North Carolina’s Current Public
ABC System
   City Manager Thornton explained if the ABC system is privatized, it would
affect approximately $236,238 in revenues generated annually by the City’s
local ABC System. He encouraged the Board to adopt the following resolution in
support of the current ABC System.
   Alderman Frink moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to adopt the succeeding
resolution. The vote of approval was unanimous. Passed 6-0 (Copy of resolution
will be sent to congressional representatives)
                Resolution In Support of North Carolina’s Current
Public Alcoholic Beverage Control System
WHEREAS, Chapter 18B of the North Carolina General Statues addresses the
regulation of alcoholic beverages in our state, and
WHEREAS, current North Carolina law establishes a uniform system of control
over the sale, purchase, transportation, manufacture, consumption and
possession of alcoholic beverages in North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, local government control is central to the current alcoholic beverage
control system; it is a local decision to establish and operate ABC stores, and
local government, acting through an appointed local ABC Board, balances the
control, profits and availability of spirits in its jurisdiction; and
WHEREAS, when local voters approved liquor sales for off-premises consumption,
the voters did not vote to allow liquor to be sold in private retail
establishments, but only through publicly controlled local ABC stores; and
WHEREAS, current law provides that profits from ABC store sales are returned to
local government, and this revenue stream is a critical source of local
government funding; and
WHEREAS, it is a priority to maintain current sources of revenue, especially in
the current challenging economic times; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport does hereby support
the continuance of the Alcoholic Beverage Control System, and opposes any
efforts to privatize the ABC system, diminish local control or to diminish the
local government revenue stream afforded from local ABC store profits.
Adopted, this the 13th day of January 2011.
                  /s/ Robert D. Howard
                  Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
City Clerk

RESOLUTION OPPOSING PROPERTY INSURANCE RATE INCREASE
WHEREAS, recent information indicates that property insurance rates are
expected to increase substantially in coastal North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, information indicates that the increase proposed will be
disproportionately higher for coastal property owners than others affected by
the rate increases; and
WHEREAS, coastal property owners have recently been affected by double-digit
insurance rate increases in the prior year; and
WHEREAS, further disproportionate increases will have an adverse impact on the
coastal economy, coastal property owners and communities;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the City
of Southport is opposed to the pending anticipated property insurance rate
increases and will take any necessary action in opposition to the increases.
This the 13th day of January, 2011.
                  /s/ Robert D. Howard

   City of Southport UDO, ARTICLE 3. - ADMINISTRATIVE MECHANISMS
PART I. - PLANNING AND ZONING BOARD
Section 3-1: Membership and Vacancies (revised 2-11-10)
The planning board shall consist of seven (7) members and two (2) alternate
members. Five (5) members and one (1) alternate member shall be citizens and
residents of the city and shall be appointed by the Board of Aldermen. Two (2)
members and (1) alternate member shall be citizens and residents of the extra-
territorial jurisdiction of the city as described pursuant to G.S. § 160A-360
et seq. and shall be appointed by the county Board of Commissioners. The City
Clerk will advertise for vacancies when they occur. All candidates, including
board members whose terms are expiring and who are seeking reappointment, must
have a current application [no older than ninety (90) days prior the date of
vacancy] on file with the City Clerk’s office and must inform the Clerk they
wish to be considered for the vacant position. All applicants must be
interviewed by a committee, selected by the Board of Aldermen, consisting of
two (2) Board of Aldermen members and the Chairman of the Planning Board. If
the Chairman’s term is expiring and he/she wants to apply for reappointment,
another member of the planning board will be chosen for the committee by the
Board of Aldermen. The committee will make recommendations to the Board of
Aldermen for the vacant position(s). Any citizen who has filed a current
application and completed the interview shall be eligible for nomination.
Citizens who have not met these requirements are not eligible for nomination to
the planning board. The City Clerk will place the applications of all
candidates who meet these requirements in the agenda packets prior to the
meeting in which the selection(s)are made.  Alternate members shall not be
entitled to vote on matters before the planning board except when a regular
planning board member is absent from a duly called meeting. In that situation,
the alternate shall have the same privileges as the regular members and may
count for quorum purposes and vote if a regular member is absent. Vacancies
occurring for reasons other than expiration of terms shall be filled as they
occur for the period of the unexpired term. Faithful attendance at the meetings
of the board is considered a pre-requisite for the maintenance of membership on
the board. A vacancy shall exist on the board if a member is absent from
twenty-five (25) percent or more of the board’s meetings, special, workshops
and committee meetings within a twelve (12) month period of time and said
vacancy may be declared and filled by the Board of Aldermen. Extraterritorial
representatives shall have equal rights, privileges, and duties with the other
members of the board to which they are appointed, regardless of whether the
matters at issue arise within the city or within the extraterritorial area.
   Attorney Isenberg noted when the UDO was adopted, Chapter 13-26 of the City
Code should have been repealed which is why repetitiveness is apparent. Mayor
Howard asked Attorney Isenberg to work with Alderman Karn on the text changes
prior to submittal to the Planning Board. Mayor Howard asked that procedure be
established as to how a member will be selected if the Chairman applies for
reappointment to the Board.

electrical usage..
Attorney Isenberg explained that the agreement includes a certification which
will be signed and notarized as an affidavit. Dosher will pay the City of
Southport $125,786.80 within five days of execution and certification. He
explained that the City billed Dosher Hospital in the amount of $1,035,000 for
2004-2010 electrical usage. Due to a special provision in the general statutes,
Dosher Hospital qualifies as a government entity because it is supported by tax
dollars and has an elected Board of Trustees. Therefore the statute of
limitation is two years. The original amount of the bill did not contain a load
shed which affects the rates. Dosher staff certified that it load shedded
during this time period and the amount of $125,786.80 is the correct amount
owed the City for this two year period.
   Alderman Karn stated that the error did not cost the taxpayers because the
difference came out of surplus funds.
   Alderman Adams moved to authorize execution of the Settlement Agreement with
Dosher Hospital in the amount of $125,786.80, seconded by Alderman Poole. The
vote of approval was unanimous. Passed 6-0 (Settlement Agreement Incorporated
as Attachment #1)

IV.   Southport Visioning for 2011
a) Annexation Initiative
City Manager Thornton informed the Board that the proposed annexation plan as
initially discussed cannot be done because some of the land is not contiguous,
and does not meet the annexation requirements. Options A&B must be completed
before option C&D are considered. He informed the Board of proposed legislation
that could possibly place a moratorium on City initiated annexations and he
proposed to proceed with option A&B before this is implemented. If legislation
is enacted, it could have an impact on option C&D. The Board discussed in
detail the annexation process and the best way to proceed including the
provision of services. Within two years of the effective date of annexation the
City is required to provide services to the annexed areas at the Citys expense.
Capital costs will be involved in extending wastewater into the areas of A&B
where none currently exists. Mayor Howard stated once the City begins the
process and determines the costs and numbers, the City could possibly offer an
incentive for early hook-up. City Manager Thornton stated as staff works
through the process, the City can determine what options are available because
impact fees are factored into the overall costs of operation and maintenance,
extension of services, debt service, etc. which is a part of the annexation
report.
Alderman Karn stated the number one priority was annexation during the Advocacy
Goals Conference sponsored by the League of Municipalities.

is allocated for conceptual drawing in the CIP. The Boards liaison will convey

discussed the structural challenges with the City gym and asked the City

f) Clean Water Management Trust Fund (CWMTF)
Mayor Howard explained that the City has two payments left on the grant
agreement with Clean Water Management Trust Fund of approximately $561,000.00
which a payment is due in July, and the last July 2012. The repayment agreement
for the wastewater plant was collaterized by the Citys grant proceeds of
$3,000,000. He stated that when the City started drawing down funds, it placed
the City within the collateral limit, freezing further advances. This was not
realized until the request for payment was denied and it was brought to the
Citys attention. The City also had a reduction in the cost of the project which
was originally $5,132,700. When the City changed from the Sanitary District to
the County it reduced the cost to $4,404,695.00. The CWMTF agreed to fund
$3,000,000 of the $5,132,700 which was 58.45% of the total cost of the project.
The City would fund through loans and other sources 41.55%. The City sent a
letter requesting the CWMTF fund $2,891,733 of the $4,404,695.00 total and the
City fund $1,512,962 which would increase the CWMTF funding from 58.45% to 65%
which would lower Southports funding request from 41.55% to 34.35%. Mayor
Howard stated that the City is actually requesting the CWMTF to increase the
Citys grant match by $317,189,000. He explained that the Board of Trustees for
the CWMTF is the only one that can change the collateral provision.   
Mayor Howard stated that he and the City Manager will appear before the CWMTF
Board and ask them to increase the grant request percentage by $317,189,000.
They will also request the collateral provision of the agreement be released to
free up $742,000.
g) Rescue Squad
Mayor Howard reported that he and Alderman Boguskie will meet with staff from
the County to discuss transition of the Southport Rescue Squad to the County,
providing the same services to Southport as other areas.
h) Audit
Mayor Howard suggested a workshop be held with the Citys Auditor to answer
questions and he briefly discussed separation of duties.
i) Countywide Curbside Recycling
City Manager Thornton stated the County is discussing curbside recycling and if
funded on July 1st, all City residents would receive a 96 gallon blue recycling
container which would reduce City cost by $3.41 per home. However, if the
county does not go through with this, the City will continue its bi-weekly
recycling program.
j) Personnel Policy
It was Board consensus to review the Citys updated Personnel Policy during a
workshop.

No further business, the Board Retreat was closed upon motion of Alderman
Boguskie, seconded by Alderman Frink. Vote unanimous.

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the Citys
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area, and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the citys land use ordinances, and
WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
a proposed amendment to Section 3 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance, and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved as
modified by the Planning Board; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to N.C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on February 10, 2011, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance as modified by the Planning Board is consistent
with the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) in order to bring the Unified
Development Ordinance up-to-date after careful review, occasional adjustments
are necessary, (ii) this amendment is necessary to clarify Planning Board
vacancies and other administrative procedures, and (iii) it is necessary to
promote the public safety and general welfare of the community by clarifying
appointment to the Planning Board;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attachment amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance is hereby approved and adopted.
This 10th day of February, 2011
City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard

AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
Section 3-1: Membership and Vacancies
Add the bold text:
The planning board shall consist of seven (7) members and two (2) alternate
members. Five (5) members and one (1) alternate member shall be citizens and
residents of the city and shall be appointed by the Board of Aldermen. Two (2)
members and (1) alternate member shall be citizens and residents of the extra-
territorial jurisdiction of the city as described pursuant to G.S. 160A-360 et
seq. and shall be appointed by the county Board of Commissioners. The City
Clerk will advertise for vacancies when they occur. All candidates, including
board members whose terms are expiring and who are seeking reappointment, must
have an application no less than thirty (30) days prior to the Board of
Aldermen meeting in which the selection(s) are made and [no older than ninety
(90) days prior to the date of vacancy] on file with the City Clerks office and
must inform the Clerk they wish to be considered for the vacant position. All
applicants must be interviewed by a committee, selected by the Board of
Aldermen, consisting of two (2) Board of Aldermen members and the Chairman of
the Planning Board. If the Chairmans term is expiring and he/she wants to apply
for reappointment, the Vice-Chairman of the planning board will be selected for
the committee. The committee will make recommendations to the Board of Aldermen
for the vacant position(s). Any citizen who has filed a current application and
completed the interview shall be eligible for nomination. Citizens who have not
met these requirements are not eligible for nomination to the planning board.
The City Clerk will place the applications of all candidates who meet these
requirements in the agenda packets prior to the meeting in which the selection
(s) are made. Alternate members shall not be entitled to vote on matters before
the planning board except when a regular planning board member is absent from a
duly called meeting. In that situation, the alternate shall have the same
privileges as the regular members and may count for quorum purposes and vote if
a regular member is absent. Vacancies occurring for reasons other than
expiration of terms shall be filled as they occur for the period of the
unexpired term. Faithful attendance at the meetings of the board is considered
a pre-requisite for the maintenance of membership on the board. A vacancy shall
exist on the board if a member is absent from twenty-five (25) percent or more
of the boards meetings within a twelve (12) month period of time and said
vacancy may be declared and filled by the Board of Aldermen. Extraterritorial
representatives shall have equal rights, privileges, and duties with the other
members of the board to which they are appointed, regardless of whether the
matters at issue arise within the city or within the extraterritorial area.

Southport

anticipated to provide an economic boost to Southport.

c)   Public Private Partnership Initiatives
City Manager Thornton reported he had contacted the Resource Institute (RI),
the City of Mt. Airy and visited their web site and provided the link to the
website to Board members. Extensive information about Mt. Airys project with
the Resource Institute on the Ararat River Greenway Project is posted on the
website. The Resource Institute functions as an administrative, coordinating,
clearing house agency for the city that enlists their services. They would
handle all coordinating activities including grant writing, hiring consultants,
etc. If entered into project, would be multi-year with funding spread out over
time. Funding provided in Mt. Airy project was 20% of total cost, roughly 80%
grant funding. RI would receive 10-15% of the total cost which is reasonable
and available to municipalities and because of their capabilities, would be an
arm of the City.
Mayor Howard reported he, the City Manager and Mt. Airy city staff toured the
Mt. Airy project, spoke with Mt. Airy staff and received positive feedback.

f)   Discussion of Walgreens Sign Concerns
Mr. Joseph Mendola representing the owner, Fair Enterprises, and the Walgreen
Corporation stated he had been meeting with City Planner, Amy Nelson since
October, 2010. Negotiations were made on 13 different points, i.e., smaller
signs in compliance with the City Ordinance with the exception of the logo W
above the entrance. Mr. Mendola pointed out the tax dollars lost with a delay
in the project due to the sign. He requested assistance in resolving the issue.
Mayor Howard asked Mrs. Nelson to explain why the sign request was denied. Mrs.
Nelson stated the ordinance allowed two (2) signs per lot and three (3) signs
per corner lot. Her interpretation was the location is not a corner lot. Mrs.
Nelson proposed a UDO text amendment to clarify the issue.
In reply to a question by Alderman Frink, City Attorney Isenberg stated
possible options; property owner had the right to apply for a text amendment
and appeal the Planning Directors determination to the Board of Adjustment.
Request placed on the February 17, 2011 Planning Board Agenda for text
amendment consideration. A special meeting of the Board of Aldermen will be
called if necessary.
g)   Resolution Accepting and Endorsing the 2009-2010 Update of the Solid Waste
Management Plan for Brunswick County
City Manager Thornton reported adoption of the resolution meets statutory
requirements of participation in the Comprehensive Solid Waste Management Plan.
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to adopt the resolution
Resolution Accepting and Endorsing the 2009-2019 Update Of the Solid Waste
Management Plan for Brunswick County
WHEREAS, it is a priority of this community to protect human health and the
environment through safe and effective management of municipal solid waste; and
WHEREAS, the reduction of the amount of toxicity of the local waste stream is a
goal of this community; and
WHEREAS, equitable and efficient delivery of solid waste management services is
an essential characteristic of the local solid waste management system; and
WHEREAS, it is a goal of the community to maintain and improve its physical
appearance and to reduce the adverse effects of illegal disposal and littering;
and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport recognizes its role in the encouragement of
recycled products; and.
WHEREAS, involvement and education of the citizenry is critical to the
establishment of an effective local solid waste program; and
WHEREAS, the State of North Carolina has placed planning responsibility on
local government for the management of solid waste; and
WHEREAS, N.C. General Statutes 130A-309.09A(b) requires each unit of local
government either individually or in cooperation with other units of local
government, to update the Ten Year Comprehensive Solid Waste Management Plan
at least every three years; and
WHEREAS, the Brunswick County Solid Waste Management Department has undertaken
and completed a long range planning effort to evaluate the appropriate
technologies and strategies available to manage solid waste effectively;
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, by the Southport Board of Aldermen that
Brunswick Countys 2009-2019 Update of the Ten Year Comprehensive Solid Waste
Management Plan is accepted and endorsed and placed on file with the City Clerk
on this the 10th day of February 2011.
_______/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC

h)   Consideration of Resolution and grant application forms for Infiltration
and Inflow Reduction with DENR - Mr. Carter Hubard, W.K. Dickson
City Manager Thornton reported staff is recommending adoption of the resolution
as part of the funding application package for the Citys inflow and
infiltration source detection program.
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to adopt the resolution. The
vote of approval was unanimous; motion carried.
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING FUNDING APPLICATION
TO THE NC DENR - CONSTRUCTION GRANTS & LOANS SECTION
FOR CITY OF SOUTHPORT
SEWER SYSTEM REHABILITATION AND REPLACEMENT PROJECT
WHEREAS, The Federal Clean Water Act Amendments of 1987 and the North Carolina
Water Infrastructure Act of 2005 (NCGS 159G) have authorized the making of
loans and grants to aid eligible units of government in financing the cost of
construction of wastewater treatment plant improvements; and
WHEREAS, The City of Southport has need for the reduction of inflow and
infiltration in the sewer system and the City intends to complete a
rehabilitation and replacement of aged publicly-owned wastewater collection
infrastructure in order to ensure effective and efficient treatment of
wastewater and protect the quality of the water in the receiving stream; and
WHEREAS, The City of Southport intends to request funding assistance from the
High Unit Coast Grant Program, the State Low-Interest Loan Program or the State
Revolving Loan (SRF) Program for the project.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, BY THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT:
That the City of Southport will arrange financing for all remaining costs of
the project, if approved for funding.
That the City of Southport will adopt and place into effect on or before
completion of the project a schedule of fees and charges and other available
funds which will provide adequate funds for proper operation, maintenance, and
administration of the system and the repayment of all principal and interest on
the debt.
That the governing body of the City of Southport agrees to include in any
funding agreement a provision authorizing the State Treasurer, upon failure of
the City of Southport to make scheduled replayment of the loan, to without from
the City of Southport any State funds that would otherwise be distributed to
the City of Southport in an amount sufficient to pay all sums then due and
payable to the State as a replayment of the loan.
That City of Southport will provide for efficient operation and maintenance of
the project on completion of construction thereof.
That M. Alan Thornton, City Manager, and successors so titled, is hereby
authorized to execute and file an application on behalf of the City of
Southport with the State of North Carolina for a (loan or grant) to aid in the
construction of the project described above.
That M. Alan Thornton, City Manager, and successors so titled, is hereby
authorized and directed to furnish such information as the appropriate State
agency may request in connection with such application or the project: to make
the assurances as contained above; and to execute such other documents as may
be required in connection with the application.
That the City of Southport has substantially complied or will substantially
comply with all Federal, State, and local laws, rules, regulations, and
ordinances applicable to the project and to the grants pertaining thereto.
Adopted this the 10th day of February, 2011 at Southport, North Carolina
/s/ Robert D. Howard

XII.   Board Comments
$   Alderman Boguskie reported he reviewed the contract with the Clean Water
Management Trust Fund(CWMTF) and it states; The grant agreement may be
rescinded, modified or amended only by written agreement executed by all
parties. Alderman Boguskie contended an agreement should be provided from
CWMTF. Mayor Howard pointed out that when the cost of the project was reduced,
from $5,132,700.00 to $4,695,000.00, CWMTF criteria dictated a proportionate
reduction which is standard operating procedure. The Citys request is a
contribution reduction from $4,169,000.00 to $3,465,000.00. Attorney Isenberg
concurred a modification must be in writing and executed by all parties. He
recommended that CWMTF clarify where in the contract it is stated the funds can
be reduced proportionately. Mayor Howard suggested Alderman Boguskie contact
Mr. Rogers, CWMTF, directly. Alderman Karn noted the Board needed to determine
how the situation would be approached. Mayor Howard suggested a Board member
represent the City at a February 20, 2011 CWMTF Board committee meeting
regarding contractual obligations and to receive an explanation of proportional
reduction.
Alderman Karn moved to direct the City Manager and Alderman Boguskie to obtain
information regarding matched funding from the CWMTF Board and reconvene to
make a final decision. Alderman Boguskie seconded the motion. Unanimous vote;
motion carried.
$   Alderman Karn requested clarification and status of the planning board/City
staff relations issue as discussed at the Board Retreat. Mayor Howard reported
he had a time line of the issues involved, had met with Aldermen Poole and
Potter, planning board liaisons, and would be meeting with staff and planning
board members

   h) Consideration of Arbor Day Proclamation
      Alderman Adams moved, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to adopt the

ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/
IMAGES/0-0-0-1454_1282x1296.jpg]
 
WHEREAS , in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of
Agriculture that a special day be set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS , this holiday called Arbor Day, was first observed with the planting
of more than a million trees in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS , Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS , trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and
water, cut heating and cooling costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air,
produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for wildlife, and
WHEREAS , trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes,
fuel for our fires, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic
vitality of business areas, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual
renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE, I Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC, do
hereby proclaim March 18, 2011 as ARBOR DAY in the City and urge all citizens
to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees and woodlands, and
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote
the well-being of this and future generations.
DATED, this 10th day of March, 2011.
/s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Regina W. Alexander

USDA Forest Service, Southern Region will conclude the Request for Proposals to
assist in the comprehensive management of trees, forests and related natural
resources in populated areas for the physiological, sociological, economic, and
aesthetic benefits trees provide to society; and
WHEREAS the City of Southport has Tree City USA status; and
WHEREAS the City of Southport has an opportunity to apply for this 50%-50%
matching grant program in 2011; and
WHEREAS the grant available through the NC Division of Forest Resources and the
USDA Forest Service, Southern Region will provide the basis for preserving and
protecting the trees of Southport that help give the City its special
character;
NOW, BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina in session assembled this 10th day of March 2011
endorse the 2012 Urban and Community Forestry Grant Program application for the
City of Southport, North Carolina.
Adopted this 10th day of March 2011.

      City Planner, Amy Nelson introduced Mr. Marc Page, Brunswick County Land

Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to adopt the resolution.

RESOLUTION TO ADOPT THE BRUNSWICK COUNTY
MULTI-JURISDICTIONAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN
WHEREAS, the City of Southport is vulnerable to an array of natural hazards
that can cause loss of life and damages to public and private property; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport desires to seek ways to mitigate situations that
may aggravate such circumstances; and
WHEREAS, the development and implementation of a hazard mitigation plan can
result in actions that reduce the long-term risk to life and property from
natural hazards; and
WHEREAS, it is the intent of the Board of Aldermen to protect its citizens and
property from the effects of natural hazards by preparing and maintaining a
local hazard mitigation plan; and
WHEREAS, it is also the intent of the Board of Aldermen to fulfill its
obligation under North Carolina General Statutes, Chapter 166A: North Carolina
Emergency Management Act and Section 322: Mitigation Planning, of the Robert T.
Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to remain eligible to
receive state and federal assistance in the event of a declared disaster
affecting the County; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick County, in coordination with Belville, Boiling Spring Lakes,
Bolivia, Calabash, Leland, Navassa, Northwest, St. James, Sandy Creek,
Shallotte, Southport, and Varnamtown, has prepared a multi-jurisdictional
hazard mitigation plan with input from the appropriate local and state
officials;
WHEREAS, the North Carolina Division of Emergency Management and the Federal
Emergency Management Agency have reviewed the hazard mitigation plan prepared
for Brunswick County for legislative compliance and has approved the plan
pending the completion of local adoption procedures;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport hereby:
∙   Adopts the Brunswick Multi-jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan; and
∙   Agrees to take such other official action as may be reasonably necessary to
carry out the proposed actions of the Plan.
Adopted on March 10, 2011.

Alderman Frink moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to adopt the resolution.

RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF TRANSPORTATION IMPROVEMENTS IN
EASTERN BRUNSWICK COUNTY
WHEREAS, Brunswick County continues to have very serious transportation
impediments that hinder safe travel and timely evacuations for residents; and
WHEREAS, over 20,000 residents live in the area comprised of Southport, Oak
Island, Caswell Beach, Bald Head Island, Boiling Spring Lakes and St. James;
and
WHEREAS, the area population increases to over 45,000 during the summer season;
and
WHEREAS, there are four state roads serving the area to include NC 133, NC 87,
NC 211 and Midway Road; and
WHEREAS, the area is home to the Progress Energy Nuclear Power Plant and the
Sunny Point Military Ocean Terminal, and
WHEREAS, all of the access/egress routes are prone to flooding during major
rain events, hurricanes and tropical storms, prohibiting safe and timely
evacuations and isolating a major portion of Brunswick County often for several
days; and
WHEREAS, the North Carolina Transportation Plan should be expanded to address
the immediate needs for road and bridge improvements.
WHEREAS, the majority of the current NCDOT improvements are volume and not
safety related;
NOW, THEREFORE, be it ordained by the Southport Board of Aldermen that we
request the North Carolina General Assembly and the North Carolina Department
of Transportation to initiate action to improve the integrity of these four
highways to better insure safe passage during and after major rain events.
Adopted this the 10th day of March, 2011.
      By: /s/ Robert Howard, Mayor

/s/ Regina W. Alexander

APRIL 4, 2011
WORKSHOP MEETING MINUTES
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN            WORKSHOP
APRIL 4, 2011                MEETING MINUTES
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS(CITY HALL) SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:      Mayor Robert D. Howard
         Aldermen Ed Boguskie, Vickie Potter, Ken Karn
         Mary Ellen Poole, Jwantana Frink
ABSENT:      Nelson Adams
STAFF PRESENT:   Regina Alexander, Interim City Manager/City Clerk
         Michele Windham, Deputy Clerk
         Ralph Cardwell, Public Services Director
         Patty Miller, Finance Director
I.   Call to Order - 6:00
Mayor Howard called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
II.   Invocation
Mayor Howard pronounced the invocation.
III.   Proposal from Brunswick County to extend a wastewater line to the
Rivermist Pump Station and use of a City wastewater transmission line to St.
James.
Alderman Boguskie reported on a meeting with Brunswick County Public Utilities
on March 22, 2011 attended by himself, Mr. Cardwell, Interim Manager Alexander,
and Mr. Marty Lawing, Mr. Jerry Pierce, and Mr. John Nichols of Brunswick
County.
(Report on file in Clerks office and attached as Exhibit A.)
Alderman Boguskie explained that Brunswick County Public Utilities is in the
process of providing Boiling Spring Lakes with a wastewater collection system
and would like the City of Southport to allow the County to run a wastewater
transmission line across City of Southport Wastewater Service Area, utilization
of the Rivermist Pump Station and 3 miles of a City wastewater transmission
line. The proposal from the County is to have an agreement with the City
sharing in the cost of operating the Rivermist Pump Station and a cost for
using the wastewater transmission line.
Alderman Boguskie provided Board members with the Memorandum of Understanding
between the City and Brunswick County providing for the County to treat up to
500,000 gallons a day of wastewater at the West Brunswick Regional Water
Reclamation Facility.
(Memorandum of Understanding on file in the Clerks office and attached as
Exhibit B.)
Mr. Cardwell pointed out Oak Island and other communities have partnered with
the County in the West Brunswick Regional Water Reclamation Facility and have
purchased sewer allocation. He indicated the City is not a direct partner and
leases sewer allocations from the County partnership at $2.98/per thousand
gallon. He suggested future purchase of unused allocations from the partner
cities.
There was discussion about current and projected sewer allocation needs.
Consensus was allocation concerns are not a part of the proposal for running
the pipeline. Allocation will be addressed at a future date.
Recommendation was made by Mr. Cardwell and Alderman Boguskie that a meter be
installed at the edge of the City of Southport Wastewater Service Area as shown
on a September 18, 2008 drawing by W. K. Dickson and incorporated as part of
Exhibit B.
Mr. Cardwell recommended the agreement stipulate the County provide for
maintenance and expansion of the Rivermist Pump Station and maintenance of 3
miles of wastewater transmission line.
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to proceed with a mutual
agreement of understanding by both parties for the County to run a wastewater
transmission line across the City of Southport Wastewater Service Area, utilize
the Rivermist Pump Station and 3 miles of wastewater transmission line subject
to all conditions discussed. Motion passed 5-0.
Adjournment - 6:50 p.m.
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to adjourn. Unanimous vote.

PROCLAMATION
NATIONAL DAY OF PRAYER
WHEREAS, civic prayers and national days of prayer have a long and venerable
history in our constitutional republic, dating back to the First Continental
Congress in 1775; and
WHEREAS, the Declaration of Independence, our first statement as Americans of
national purpose and identity, made the Laws of Nature and Natures God the
foundation of our United States of America and asserted that people have
inalienable rights that are God-given; and
WHEREAS, the Supreme Court has affirmed the right of state legislatures to open
their sessions with prayer and the Supreme Court and the U.S. Congress
themselves begin each day with prayer; and
WHEREAS, in 1988 legislation setting aside the first Thursday of May in each
year as a National Day of Prayer was passed unanimously by both Houses of
Congress and signed by President Ronald Reagan; and
WHEREAS, the National Day of Prayer is an opportunity for Americans of all
faiths to join in united prayer to acknowledge our dependence on God, to give
thanks for blessings received, to request healing for wounds endured, and to
ask God to guide our leaders and bring wholeness to the United States and her
citizens; and
WHEREAS, it is fitting and proper to give thanks to God by observing a day of
prayer in the City of Southport when all may acknowledge our blessings and
express gratitude for them, while recognizing the needs for strengthening
religious and moral values in our State and Nation; and
NOW, THEREFORE, I Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, and Board
of Aldermen do hereby proclaim May 5, 2011 as A DAY OF PRAYER IN SOUTHPORT and
urge all citizens of Southport to observe the day in ways appropriate to its
importance and significance.
This 14th day of April 2011.

City of Southport
2City of Southport
2011 Earth Day Proclamation
WHEREAS, the first Earth Day was celebrated on April 22, 1970, and was founded
by the late Senator Gaylord Nelson with the goal of inspiring environmental
awareness and encouraging the conservation, protection and appreciation of our
nations natural resources; and
WHEREAS, it is the responsibility of each of us to safeguard the environment,
by recognizing that all human life depends upon the Earth and upon one another
for our mutual existence, well-being and development; and
WHEREAS, the steps we can take to protect and preserve our natural environment
through education, partnerships and positive actions should be encouraged; and
WHEREAS, the citizens of Southport are committed not only to the protection and
preservation of our environment, but also to the restoration of ecosystems and
habitat; and
WHEREAS, in furtherance of this objective the City of Southport supports
organizations that participate in Earth Day 2011; and
WHEREAS, the City commends all who participates in Earth Day, for their
dedication in taking a proactive role in shaping the future of our environment
and in protecting the earths precious natural resource;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of
Southport, do hereby proclaim April 22, 2011, as
EARTH DAY
and urge all our citizens to be mindful of local, state and national laws which
protect our environment and to join in efforts to preserve the beauty and
wonder of the lands, skies and water of the Earth in all its diversity.
This the 14 th day of April 2011
/s/  Robert D. Howard, Mayor

MAY 2, 2011
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN            WORKSHOP MINUTES
MAY 2, 2011                  6:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS(CITY HALL) SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
WORKSHOP MINUTES
PRESENT:      Mayor Robert D. Howard
         Aldermen Ed Boguskie, Nelson Adams, Ken Karn
         Vickie Potter, Mary Ellen Poole
ABSENT:      Jwantana Frink
STAFF PRESENT:   Regina W. Alexander, Interim City Manager/MMC-City Clerk
         Michele Windham, Deputy Clerk
         Patty Miller, Finance Director
         Neal Sage, Chief VRS
I.   Call to Order - 6:00 p.m.
   Mayor Howard called the workshop to order at 6:00 p.m.
II.   Invocation
   Mayor Howard welcomed citizens and pronounced the invocation.
III.   Purpose of Workshop
   Mayor Howard stated the purpose of the workshop was to receive public input
relating to the Rescue Squad, discuss the relocation of City departments during
renovation of City Hall and to receive an update on the 2011-2012 Budget. He
stated each person wishing to make comments would have three (3) minutes to
speak
IV.   Public Comments
   Mrs. Diane Boguskie, 502 West Brown Street, shared a personal experience
with the rescue squad and she spoke in support of keeping the squad.
   Mr. Larry McCracken, 4004 Norsemen Loop Road, Unit 1, Rivermist Subdivision,
spoke in support of the rescue squad and discussed raising funds and applying
for grants.
   Ms. Alvina Landkamer, 231 N. Caswell Avenue, told of the rescue squad saving
her life.
   Ms. Ruth Law, resident of Southport since 1985, shared her numerous
experiences with the rescue squad and offered to help raise money.
   Mr. Chris Grace, Boiling Spring Lakes Fire Chief, spoke in support of the
rescue squad and noted the different response times of county ambulances
depending on where they are located at any given time.
   Ms. Margaret Connaughton, 94 year old resident of Southport, told of her son
Patrick serving on the rescue squad and about her experiences with the squad.
   Ms. Fiona Boatram, West Nash Street, expressed her support of the rescue
squad.
   Ms. Catherine Fravel, 311 Yaupon Drive, just outside the City limits, shared
an experience with the rescue squad and she speculated on the response time
during the busy 4 th of July holiday.
   Mr. Doug Ledgett, 312 Stuart Avenue, told of serving on the Fire Department
for 39 years. He expressed support for the rescue squad and disputed that the
citizens are being double taxed for the service.
   Mr. Tom Florkiewicz, 1014 Bonner Bussells, stated he had multiple medical
problems and he supported the rescue squad.
   Ms. Ellen Dorsett, resident of Airport Road, stated she has been a member of
the rescue squad for 33 years. She talked about the multiple roles the squad
performs in caring for a patient and their family. She discussed the addition
of a golf cart for the quick response team during the 4 th of July Festival.
   Mr. John Dahill, Chief of the St. James Fire Department shared his
experiences answering questions people have asked about the duplication of
rescue services provided by both the County and St. James. He emphasized the
importance of public safety and encouraged the Board to retain the Southport
Rescue Squad.
   Mr. Keith Keller, 410 Yaupon Drive Extension, spoke in support of keeping
the rescue squad, pointing out the squad makes up 3.8% of the Citys budget.
   Dr. Billy Sherrod, 224 River Drive, spoke in support of the rescue squad and
offered to help raise money.
   Neil Sage, 604 N. Fodale Avenue and Rescue Squad Chief, addressed the Board.
He pointed out the rescue squad has received no operational funds from the City
for the 2010-2011 budget year but does need assistance with capital
expenditures. Chief Sage indicated application for a FEMA grant is in process,
specifications have been prepared for replacement of the Chevy Suburban, a
used, demo or rebuilt ambulance is being considered, new monitors will be
required to stay inter-linked with the County, and station improvements are
needed. Chief Sage questioned if the County would bring a unit into Southport
at no cost; if a charge by the County, what would the charge be and what would
be the best system for the citizens of Southport.
   Mr. John Barr, resident of Oak Island, spoke in support of the Southport
Rescue Squad and challenged the Board to manage the City budget to keep the
squad and provide the needed equipment.
   Ms. Ann Price spoke in support of the Rescue Squad.
   Mrs. Karen Sage, wife of Neil Sage and former school principal, spoke about
the invaluable service the Rescue Squad provided to the entire community.
V.   Agenda Items
   a. Rescue Squad
      Alderman Karn moved, seconded by Alderman Potter to keep the rescue
squad.
Discussion
   Alderman Karn stated it is his opinion that the rescue squad is an essential
service.
   Alderman Poole stated she had more questions and would like time to review
and consider the comments given and the information provided. Alderman Adams
agreed and pointed out that Alderman Frink was absent.
   Aye: Aldermen Karn, Boguskie and Potter. Nay: Aldermen Nelson and Poole.
Motion passed 3 - 2.
   b. City Hall Relocation
   The Board agreed to proceed with Option 1 & 2 of the Space Needs Assessment
relating to City Hall and that City Hall would be vacated and departments would
utilize other City buildings during the renovation.
   Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to authorize the City
manager to issue RFPs for design, development, schematic, construction drawings
and project completion for City Hall renovations and to have those documents be
ready for possible award of a contract during the 2010-2011 budget year.
Unanimous vote
   c. Budget Update
   Manager Alexander stated the 2011-2012 budget will be presented to the Board
during their May 12 regular meeting. She indicated the budget is revenue
neutral, there will be a change in the health care benefits, water and sewer
rates may increase, options are being considered for the City owned property
located near Military Ocean Terminal Sunny Point, and staff is requesting an
increase in rental fees for City buildings and boat slips. She praised the hard
work of Finance Director, Patty Miller.
   Manager Alexander stated money is in the 2011-2012 budget for the City Hall
renovation architectural design. The Board agreed to solicit RFPs and award a
contract prior to the end of budget year 2010-2011.
VI.   Other Business
   Mayor Howard stated concerns were raised about the cost of providing sewer
to the proposed annexed areas during the April 26 public informational meeting.
Mayor Howard stated the three methods by which sewer lines may be extended:
   1.   By petition of at least fifty (50) percent of all property owners who,
combined, own at least fifty (50) percent of the linear footage of the land.
   2.   Petition by a property owner to the City for the extension of one or
more lines to benefit their individual property.
   3.   By the action of the Board of Aldermen, who may determine that a line
extension is beneficial to the public.
Consensus of the Board was to hold discussions until the May 12 regular
meeting.
..............................
A workshop was scheduled for Wednesday, May 25 at 6:00 p.m. to meet with
Resource Institute on a possible master plan for the waterfront.
..............................
Manager Alexander announced there will be evening filming taking place between
May 23 and June 10.
VII.   Adjournment
   Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to adjourn the meeting at
8:08 p.m. Unanimous vote

   b) Consideration of recommendation from the Water & Sewer Committee
   Alderman Boguskie reported on the sewer partnering options submitted by
Brunswick County:
Option #1 - County provide operation and maintenance, city allows conveyance of
county sewer through city system;
$   City expands the transmission system within its service area at no capital
cost to the City.
$   City continues to provide retail sewer service in the service area.
$   City has no operation and maintenance costs for the Rivermist pump station
and downstream 16" force main.
Option #2 - Regional transmission system expansion
$   City expands the transmission system within its service area at no capital
cost to the City.
$   City remains the retail sewer service provider in the service area.
$   City has no operation and maintenance costs for these major pump stations
and force mains. (Rivermist, Sandy Lane, Downstream 16" force main from Sandy
Lane pump station to the tie-in point at St. James)
$   City is not responsible for Sanitary Sewer Overflows at these major pump
stations and transmission mains.
$   Allow for more effective management of the major pump station and force
main transmission system.
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to accept Option #2,
Regional Transmission System Expansion, of the Sewer Partnering Options for the
City of Southport from Brunswick County and to lower the sewer impact rate from
$25/gal per. seat for a restaurant to $5/gal. per seat; rate effective this
date. Unanimous vote.
   c) Consideration of recommendation from the Tourism Committee for
advertisement promotional in Our State Magazine
   Board consensus to explore advertising options in Our State Magazine and to
promote merchant participation.
   d) Consideration of sewer options in proposed annexation area
   Mayor Howard stated the three options for providing sewer service to the
proposed annexation area.
      1.   By petition of at least fifty (50) percent of all property owners
who, combined, own at least fifty (50) percent of the linear footage of the
land.
      2.   Petition by a property owner to the City for the extension of one or
more lines to benefit their individual property.
      3.   By the action of the Board of Aldermen, who may determine that a
line extension is beneficial to the public.
   Mayor Howard indicated it is the Boards intention, further in the annexation
process, to adopt Option 1.

MAY 19, 2011
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN            PUBLIC HEARING MEETING MINUTES
MAY 19, 2011                 6:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS(CITY HALL) SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PUBLIC HEARING MEETING MINUTES
PRESENT:      Mayor Robert D. Howard
         Aldermen Ed Boguskie, Nelson Adams, Ken Karn,
         Mary Ellen Poole, Jwantana Frink, Vickie Potter
STAFF PRESENT:   Regina W. Alexander, Interim City Manager/MMC-City Clerk
         Michele Windham, Deputy Clerk
I.   Call to Order - 6:00 p.m.
   Mayor Howard called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
II.   Invocation
   Mayor Howard pronounced the invocation.
III.   Public Hearing
   Mr. Vagn Hansen and John McHenry, Benchmark CMR, Inc., explained Annexation
Area A and B Reports as required by North Carolina statutes.
   Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Frink to go into Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote.
   Mr. Michael Rice, 2012 Bonner Bussells, provided a booklet to each Board
member and made a PowerPoint presentation in opposition to the proposed
annexation.
   Mr. Ken Stewart, 603 N. Fodale Avenue and owner of Stewarts Hardware at the
intersection of Jabbertown Road and Rt. 87, talked about the information
provided by the consultants and the qualifying factors for a property to be
deemed urbanized.
   Ms. Judy MacMurdo, 1019 Captain Adkins Drive, read resolutions by the
Brunswick County Board of Commissioners In Support of Legislation Against
Involuntary Annexation and the Brunswick County Republican Party urging the
North Carolina General Assembly to adopt annexation reform legislation.
   Mr. Lew Cabral, 937 E. Leonard Street, expressed his opposition to the
proposed annexation.
   Ms. Jan Mousley, 6005 Robert Ruark Drive, spoke about the property damage
that would occur if sewer service was installed to the proposed annexation
area.
   Mr. David Morgan, 1006 Pilot Circle, spoke in opposition to the proposed
annexation.
   Ms. Carol Kirby, Robert Ruark Drive, talked about the water table in her
yard and the economic effects the annexation could have on fixed income people,
lower income families, and unemployed and under employed individuals.
   Mr. Joe Pasulka, 1014 Captain Adkins Drive, expressed his opposition to the
proposed annexation.
   Mr. Jay Royal, business owner at 1320 N. Howe Street, spoke in opposition to
the proposed annexation.
   Mr. Fred Gann, veteran and resident of Woodside Trailer Park, spoke about
the impact an annexation could have on the nearly 50 residents of the trailer
park.
   Mr. Adam Bingel, 1016 Bonner Bussells Drive, spoke in opposition to the
proposed annexation and stated North Carolina was one of only four States that
allow forced annexation.
   Mr. Bill Fairley, 101 Live Oak Turn, expressed his opinion annexation would
not provide any benefits to the proposed area of annexation.
   Mr. Reese Swan, resident of Woodside Trailer Park, spoke in opposition to
the proposed annexation.
   Mr. Roy Tucker, 1017 Captain Adkins Drive, expressed his belief forced
annexation is inconsistent with US principals and the City could have worked
with residents for a voluntary annexation.
   Mr. Sonny Hickman, 1028 Captain Adkins Drive, talked about his experiences
with installation of sewer service to his home on Oak Island. He stated he
would like to be annexed at some point in the future.
   Mr. Keith Keller, 410 Yaupon Drive Extension, read from the Area B
Annexation Report regarding sewer connections to the proposed annexation area.
He urged those residents attending in the audience to be prepared to challenge
the annexation.
   Mr. Dwight Flanagan, 226 Captain Adkins Drive, spoke in opposition to the
proposed annexation.
   Mr. Earl Clewis, 1648 N. Howe Street and owner of Woodside Trailer Park,
stated his opposition to the proposed annexation.
   Mr. John Bruton, 1308 N. Atlantic Avenue, spoke about his experiences living
previously on N. Ninth Street, foreclosure notices in the newspaper, bank owned
houses, struggling businesses and his opposition to the proposed annexation.

MAY 25, 2011
RESOURCE INSTITUTE PRESENTATION
TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN
MAY 25, 2011
6:00 P.M.
PRESENT:       Mayor Robert D. Howard
         Aldermen, Ken Karn, Vickie Potter, Mary Ellen Poole, Jwantana Frink
ABSENT:       Aldermen Adams, Boguskie
STAFF PRESENT:     Regina Alexander, Interim City Manager/City Clerk
         Michele Windham, Deputy Clerk
         Amy Nelson, Planning Director
         Heather Hemphill, Parks & Recreation Director
Mayor Howard called the Special Meeting to order for the purpose of hearing a
presentation by Resource Institute for a potential master plan development of
the Citys Waterfront.
Mayor Howard pronounced the invocation.
Mayor Howard spoke about Southport being a tourist destination, the natural
beauty of the Cape Fear River and the opportunities to enhance the river front
to bring people and businesses into the community. He talked about the City of
Mt. Airy hosting an event showcasing their Ararat River project. He noted the
City has ownership of strategic property that would be advantageous to
development and that such an undertaking could not be realized without private
involvement.
Mayor Howard introduced Michael Squeak Smith, Chairman of Resource Institute.
Mr. Smith stated Resource Institute is a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization
incorporated in 2001 with a Mission to provide an avenue of support to other
organizations, cities and nonprofit groups to address natural and human
resource opportunities to enhance the quality of life.  Mr. Smith introduced
Mr. Charles Anderson, Project Developer and they talked about Resource
Institutes:
Objective:   Put relationships to work.
Goal:      Facilitate and manage each project in full partnership with sponsor.
Process:   Secure high quality firms, do project within budget, seek grant and
funding resources, provide project support from start to finish and reduce
sponsor staff requirements.
Mr. Smith and Mr. Anderson displayed before and after pictures of several river
projects and talked in depth about the Mt. Airy Ararat River project;
   $   Donation of the land many years prior.
   $   Desired project:
      - Water quality enhancement
      - Promote water based recreation
      - Infrastructure issues addressed
      - Creation of a new environmental park
      - Creation of a greenway park
      - Upgrade to the soccer park
      - Economic development
   $   Project partners
      - 54 easements from landowners
      - Clean Water Management Trust Fund
      - Division of Water Quality
      - CAMA
Mr. Smith and Mr. Anderson discussed the challenges encountered during the
Ararat project and the multitude of benefits realized.
Mr. Smith and Mr. Anderson exhibited pictures of many Southport waterfront
locations; Wastewater treatment plant, Cape Fear Restaurant, Fort Johnston,
Yacht Basin, flooding at Fishy/Fishy Restaurant, erosion issues at the central
pump station, rip rap areas along the river and they discussed the impact each
has on the waterfront. They talked about the waterfront walkway developments in
Beaufort, North Carolina and Georgetown, South Carolina and the steps that
could be taken to achieve a showcase waterfront for Southport. They emphasized
the importance of creating a community vision with input from citizens,
business owners, City staff and a City formed task force.
Mr. Smith and Mr. Anderson answered questions about the project scope
(anticipated from Kingsley Park to the Southport Marina), how Resource
Institute secures funding for projects, their relationship with other
government agencies, Southports financial investment, and the total project
percentage Resource Institute charges a sponsoring organization.
There was discussion among Aldermen and audience members about including
Stevens Park in a plan, issues with stabilizing the river bank along Bay
Street, and the preservation of Southports uniqueness. Mr. Cliff Pender,
encouraged the City to be proactive.
Alderman Poole thanked the public and Resource Institute.
Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to adjourn the meeting.
Unanimous vote.

SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES

         Aldermen Ed Boguskie, Nelson Adams, Jwantana Frink
         Vickie Potter, Mary Ellen Poole

         Mike Isenberg, City Attorney

III.   New Business
Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Frink to adopt an amendment to
Chapter 19, Article IV, Water & Sewer Policy, Code of Ordinances, City of
Southport. Vote unanimous.
AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 19, ARTICLE IV, WATER AND SEWER EXTENSION POLICY,
OF THE CODE OF ORDINANCES OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Section
19-137 of the Code of Ordinances is hereby amended as follows:
(1)   The introductory sentence to Section 19-137 shall read as follows:
Inside the corporate limits, there are two (2) methods by which water and sewer
extensions can be accomplished.
(2)   Subsection 19-137(3) is hereby repealed and deleted.
This the 2 nd day of June, 2011
City of Southport
ATTEST:                  /s/ Robert D. Howard
/s/ Regina W. Alexander            Mayor
Clerk
Mayor Howard asked for comments from Board members.
The Deputy Clerk read into the record a statement submitted by Alderman Karn:
This has been an arduous and emotional process for all of us: current
residents, those in the areas proposed for annexation, and  the Board of
Aldermen. I will not go into great detail as all of the points, both pro and
con, have been covered. But it is important to understand that the board has
heard all concerns raised by residents in the proposed annexation areasas well
as those of our own citizens and considered them in reaching a decision
tonight.
For me, the major benefits of approving these annexations are:
. To establish a stable tax base within the scope of the services provided by a
municipality of our size.
. To maintain and improve services and development that will substantially
benefit all citizens in our areaincluding those in the proposed annexation
zones.
. Fairness to our current taxpaying citizens.
Annexation helps balance the costs of city benefits among those benefitting
from them. The annexation maps show the division between Southport and the
areas in the county proposed for annexation are arbitrary. The city itself
makes the properties located in close proximity more valuable. As such, any
expenditure to make Southport better--or even to maintain it as it is--should
be shared by all citizens in the area. Southport has been here for over 200
years. Maintaining everything that is Southport comes at a price, but those who
are virtually surrounded by our city limits do not currently contribute to this
support.
The nearby unincorporated residents claim to have county equivalents for
emergency services provided by Southport, but the fact is that Southports
squads are invariably the first responders. Response times for police and
emergency medical services would be much longer if the county were the sole
provider. Annexation area residents currently pay nothing to support those
critical services provided by the taxpayers of the City of Southport.
Southport will incur additional expenses if the areas are annexed into the
City, but in the long term the additional income will enable a higher quality
of services to all. If the annexations are abandoned or rejected, Southport
will have difficulty providing even the basic services to our current residents
in future years without raising taxes. Or, we will be forced to substantially
reduce services over the next few years and everybodyincluding those in the
annexation areaswill lose.
Annexation area residents support our community by shopping in Southport.
However, while 70% of local option sales tax revenues are generated in cities,
we receive only about 29% of that revenue. Many other state- and federally-
allocated funds come to us based on population. Those outside the city
limitseven though they benefit from these fundsare not considered when the
allocations are made.
The only caveat regarding the annexations before you this evening is the
provision in our current city ordinances which allows the Board of Aldermen to
extent sewer service based on what it perceives to be the public good. I feel
strongly that sewer extension should not be forced upon the property owners in
the annexation areas. If changes can be made to the city ordinances and the
annexation report to eliminate that option I would recommend you give it strong
consideration.
One issue that has not been raised in public is that the annexations currently
being consideredif approvedwill enable Southport to annex the business corridor
across the Progress Energy Canal. This will substantially increase the Citys
tax base and ease the pressure to either raise taxes or eliminate services. It
will also enable Southport to make improvements such as the waterfront plan,
replacing old city buildings, building more parks and public spaces while
improving and maintaining those we already have, and much more that Southport
has needed for many years.
If we all pitch in we can create a vibrant community, increase economic
development, and have a high quality of life well into millennium 2000.
I urge my fellow board members to demonstrate vision for our beautiful city by
approving both annexation ordinances before you this evening.
While it may not be a popular decision, it is the best one for Southport
Alderman Poole discussed her deliberations of the annexation issue and her
mission as an elected official to ensure the health, safety and financial
responsibility of the City of Southport for its citizens and future
generations.
Alderman Boguskie spoke about his struggles with the involuntary annexation
issue, concerns of the cost burden for sewer services to the annexation areas,
long standing State statutes, current legislative initiatives and the trust the
citizens of Southport have placed on him.
Alderman Frink shared her experiences with annexation since 2007, her vision
for the future and to see Southport grow.
Alderman Adams stated his respect for both sides of the annexation issue and
his intention to vote for what he believes is the best for the City.
Alderman Potter stated her questions about annexation had been answered.
Mayor Howard thanked the citizens of Smithville Woods and Jabbertown Road for
their comments. He thanked the Board members, the current and previous City
Manager and City staff for their hard work during the process. Mayor Howard
shared the Boards journey through the process that started in January 2010, the
State Statutes in place since 1959 that the Board has been operating under, and
assured the citizens that the City is not in financial trouble.
Alderman Frink moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to adopt the Resolution
Amending Annexation Report for Area A. Vote Unanimous
RESOLUTION OF SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN AMENDING ANNEXATION REPORT
WHEREAS, after a full and thorough review and discussion regarding the report
of plans for extending services to the area being considered for annexation,
the Board of Aldermen did on March 24, 2011, approve the Annexation Report for
Area A; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to and in furtherance of said report and in accordance with
state law, the City did hold a public informational meeting on April 26, 2011,
and a public hearing on May 19, 2011, to hear comments and questions regarding
said report and the proposed annexation; and
WHEREAS, after careful consideration of all questions and comments received and
after further discussion and deliberation regarding said report, it now appears
to the Board of Aldermen that said report should be amended to reflect the
repeal of Section 19-137(3) of the City of Southport Code of Ordinances, which
has the effect of removing the Water and Sewer Extension Policy option of City
initiated water and sewer extensions, and amended to include the addition of a
portion of Robert Ruark Road that is not maintained by NCDOT to the list of
roads, or portions thereof, that may be eligible for maintenance by the City of
Southport following the effective date of the annexation;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED that the Annexation Report for Area A
adopted on March 24, 2011, be and is hereby amended as follows:
1. In Section 5 of the report, the description of the level of service to the
annexation area for street maintenance services on page 8 is hereby amended to
add the following to the enumerated list of streets that the City anticipates
assuming maintenance of upon the effective date of the annexation:
11. Robert Ruark Drive SE (portion not under NCDOT maintenance)
2. In Section 5 of the report, the description of the level of service to the
annexation area for street maintenance services on page 8 is hereby amended to
accurately reflect that a portion of Robert Ruark Road is not maintained by
NCDOT by amending the second sentence in the paragraph immediately following
the enumerated list of streets that the City anticipates assuming maintenance
of upon the effective date of the annexation to read:
Streets in the area proposed for annexation that the City will not assume
maintenance responsibility for following the effective date of the annexation
are the portion of Robert Ruark Drive (SR-1852) that is maintained by NCDOT,
and Fairley Street SE, which is noted as a private street on the associated
subdivision plat.
3. In Section 5 of the report, the description of the current level of service
in the City for water service on page 10 is hereby amended to reflect the
repeal of Section 19-137(3) of the Citys Water and Sewer Extension Policy by
amending the third paragraph under said description to read:
All water service connections and water line extensions are governed by the
Citys adopted water supply and extension policies. All developed properties
inside of the City that are located adjacent to a water distribution line are
required to connect to the Citys water system within thirty (30) days of the
installation of the water line, in accordance with Section 19-5 of the Citys
Code of Ordinances. The Citys water extension policy provides two methods by
which water lines may be extended within the corporate limits. These two
methods are outlined in Section 19-137 of the City Code of Ordinances, and
explained briefly herein (for a full explanation, please refer to the City Code
of Ordinances). The first method for accomplishing the extension of water lines
is by petition of at least fifty (50) percent of all property owners who,
combined, own at least fifty (50) percent of the linear footage of the lands
abutting the proposed line extension. In the case of a successful petition
through the first method, the City will complete the project, and finance the
cost of such extensions through a one hundred (100) percent assessment of the
benefitted property owners. The second method of extension is through the
petition by a property owner to the City for the extension of one or more lines
to benefit their individual property. In the case of an extension by this
method, the petitioning property owner is responsible for the full cost of the
proposed line extension and associated costs. In the case of both service
connections and line extensions, additional tap fees and impact fees will apply
to each customer in accordance with the Citys adopted fee schedule.
4. In Section 5 of the report, the description of the current level of service
in the City for sewer service on page 11 is hereby amended to reflect the
repeal of Section 19-137(3) of the Citys Water and Sewer Extension Policy by
amending the third paragraph under said description to read:
All sewer service connections and sewer line extensions are governed by the
Citys adopted sewer use and extension policies. All developed properties inside
of the City that are located adjacent to a sewer collection line are required
to connect to the Citys sewer system within thirty (30) days of the
installation of the sewer line, in accordance with Section 19-5 of the Citys
Code of Ordinances. The Citys sewer extension policy provides two methods by
which sewer lines may be extended within the corporate limits. These two
methods are outlined in Section 19-137 of the City Code of Ordinances, and
explained briefly herein (for a full explanation, please refer to the City Code
of Ordinances). The first method for accomplishing the extension of sewer lines
is by petition of at least fifty (50) percent of all property owners who,
combined, own at least fifty (50) percent of the linear footage of the lands
abutting the proposed line extension. In the case of a successful petition
through the first method, the City will complete the project, and finance the
cost of such extensions through a one hundred (100) percent assessment of the
benefitted property owners. The second method of extension is through the
petition by a property owner to the City for the extension of one or more lines
to benefit their individual property. In the case of an extension by this
method, the petitioning property owner is responsible for the full cost of the
proposed line extension and associated costs. In the case of both service
connections and line extensions, additional tap fees and impact fees will apply
to each customer in accordance with the Citys adopted fee schedule.
5. In Section 5 of the report, the description of the proposed level of service
for the annexation area for sewer service on page 12 is hereby amended to
reflect the repeal of Section 19-137(3) of the Citys Water and Sewer Extension
Policy by amending the final sentence in the third paragraph under said
description to read:
Upon the effective date of the annexation, the City may begin considering
petitions for sewer line extensions into the annexation area in accordance with
the Citys water and sewer extension policy.
This the 2 nd day of June, 2011.      City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
ATTEST:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
Clerk

g) Consideration of a Resolution Establishing Fund Balance Policies as Required
by Governmental Accounting Standards Board 54
Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to adopt a Resolution
Establishing Fund Balance Policies as required by GASB 54, vote unanimous.
A Resolution Establishing Fund Balance Policies as requried by GASB 54
WHEREAS, the Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) has
adopted Statement 54 (GASB 54"), a new standard for governmental fund balance
reporting and governmental fund type definitions that becomes effective for the
fiscal year ending June 30, 2011; and
WHEREAS, the City desires to be in compliance with BASB Statement 54;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southprot hereby adopts the
following policy:
FUND BALANCE POLICY
Fund balance measures the net financial resources availble to finance
expenditures of future periods. To maintain the Citys credit rating, meet
seasonal cash shortfalls, economic downturns f a local disaster, the City shall
maintain and present fund balance for the general fund in accordance with the
requirements of GASB 54.
The Board of Aldermen shall take formal action to commit the use of fund
balance for projects or purposes in any current year or future years budget.
Where an expenditure is incurred for which restricted and unrestricted fund
balance is available, the restricted fund balance, to the extent feasible,
should be used first.
When expenditure is incurred for which there is an unrestricted fund balance
available, funds should be spent in the following order: committed, assigned
and unassigned.
a.   Committed fund balances are amounts that can be used only for the specific
purposes determined by a changed or lifted only by the government taking the
same formal action that imposed the constraint originally.
b.   Assigned fund balances are amounts intended to be used by the government
for specific purposes and so expressed by the governing body or by an official
or body to which the governing body delegates the authority.
c.   Unassigned fund balance is the residual classification of the general fund
that includes all amounts not contained in other fund balance classifications.
Unassigned amounts are technically available for any purpose.
The Citys revenue spending policy for programs with multiple revenue services
shall be in the following hierarchy: bond proceeds, federal funds, State funds,
local non-City funds, City funds.
The Finance/Budget Officer has the authority to deviate from this policy if it
is in the best interest of the City.
The above resolution is adopted this 9th day of June, 2011.
The City of Southport
Attest:                     /s/ Robert D. Howard
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC       Mayor
Clerk

at Dosher Memorial Hospital and a request to County Commissioners to expand the
