Resolution of Support for Dosher Hospital Tax Rate Request
Whereas, in a widely publicized election conducted in May, 2000, the Smithville
Township voters approved a tax for the exclusive benefit of Dosher Hospital of
4 cents per $100 valuation through tax year 2031; and
Whereas, in 2007, Dosher Hospital entered into an agreement with Brunswick
County to voluntarily reduce the approved 4 cent tax rate to 2.25 cents to
provide tax relief associated with the extraordinary increase in Smithville
Township property values documented by the 2006 property revaluation; and
Whereas, the 2010 revaluation resulted in dramatic reductions to Smithville
Township property values; and
Whereas, the 2007 agreement calls for budget neutral adjustments to the tax
rate to coincide with each additional revaluation; and
Whereas, the estimated budget neutral adjustment required by the 2010 valuation
is approximately .75 cents; and
Whereas, the 2007 agreement further allows Dosher Hospital to request
additional tax funding for specific capital improvements, provided the funding
does not require a tax rate exceeding the 4 cent per $100 rate authorized by
the Smithville Township voters; and
Whereas, the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners promised in the 2007
agreement to seriously consider such a request; and
Whereas, Dosher Hospitals inpatient rooms were constructed in the late 1970s
and do not meet current handicap accessibility, fire safety, patient privacy,
and security requirements; and
Whereas, amortization of the estimated cost to renovate Dosher Hospitals
inpatient care wing requires an approximate 1 cent increase to the Dosher tax
rate;
Now, Therefore, Be It Resolved that the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport does hereby support Dosher Memorial Hospital in its request to the
Brunswick County Board of Commissioners that the Dosher Hospital tax rate be
set at 4 cents per $100 valuation beginning in the 2011-2012 tax year.
This the 11th day of June, 2011.
City of Southport
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard
Attest:  /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC       Mayor
   Clerk
RESOLUTION REQUESTING THE BRUNSWICK COUNTY COMMISSIONERS TO EXPAND THE
BOUNDARIES OF SMITHVILLE TOWNSHIP
THAT WHEREAS, Smithville Townships Dosher Memorial Hospital is a true community
hospital serving the citizens and residents of Smithville Township including
the citizens and residents of Caswell Beach, Oak Island, Southport, Bald Head
Island and the Players Club area of St. James ; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Hospital is supported by an additional ad valorem tax on the
citizens and property owners within Smithville Township; and
WHEREAS, the hospital has long been an asset to not only the residents in
Smithville Township, but also those who live in the other areas of the Town of
St. James and in the City of Boiling Spring Lakes, which lie outside the
Townships boundaries; and
WHEREAS, the municipalities in the Township were recently asked for their
support of the Hospitals request to resume a 4-cent per $100 of assessed value
tax rate, the maximum allowed, in order to pursue needed improvements to better
serve the community; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport has endorsed the
Hospitals request, recognizing Doshers importance to the community; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Hospital also serves and provides critical medical care to the
citizens and residents of the remainder of St. James and the City of Boiling
Spring Lakes and surrounding areas; and
WHEREAS, amending the boundaries of Smithville Township to include the
remainder of St. James and the City of Boiling Spring Lakes can only enhance
operations of our community hospital; and
WHEREAS, including those areas within the Township will bring equity among the
base of local users of the Hospital;
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport hereby requests that the Brunswick County Commissioners expand
Smithville Township to include the entire Town of St. James and the City of
Boiling Spring Lakes and intervening areas within its borders.
Adopted this the 11th of June, 2011.
City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC

STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA
COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK
AGREEMENT
THIS AGREEMENT, made and entered into this 11 day of June 2011  by and between
the County of Brunswick, a body corporate and politic with its county seat
located in Bolivia, North Carolina, Party of the First Part, hereinafter
referred to as County and  Southport, NC , a body and corporate and politic
situation in Brunswick County, North Carolina, Party of the Second Part
hereinafter referred to as Town.
WITNESSETH
WHEREAS Brunswick County Citizens will enjoy improved customer service from a
single source for billing, information and paying property taxes; and,
WHEREAS Town has requested that County bill and collect the ad valorem taxes of
Town; and,
WHEREAS, County has agreed to bill and collect the ad valorem taxes of Town as
hereinafter set forth;
NOW, THEREFORE in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein, the
parties hereto agree as follows:
1.   County shall bill and collect the ad valorem taxes due the Town for the
tax year 2011 in conformity with Chapter 105 of the General Statutes of North
Carolina.
2.   County shall deduct from all sums collected by it, whether in the form of
full or partial payment, three-quarters of one percent (0.75%) thereof as a
collection fee.
3.   County shall remit to Town all remaining sums collected by County on Towns
behalf on a monthly basis. In the event a taxpayer makes a payment direct to
Town, it must be immediately forwarded to County for proper posting of the
taxpayers account.
4.   County shall not undertake foreclosure proceedings independently on Towns
behalf, and all such foreclosure actions shall be undertaken in conformity with
Countys policies regarding the same as adopted from time to time by the
Brunswick County Board of Commissioners.
5.   Town shall provide County with its tax rate, building permits, zoning
changes, and all other information and/or documentation required to fulfill the
provisions of this Agreement, in a timely manner.
6.   Town will be responsible for the collection of all delinquent taxes for
tax years prior to the starting tax year stated in 1 above.
7.   Town will provide staff resource(s), and may maintain a position with the
title of Tax Collector, to assist with delinquent tax collections after January
5 th each year (statutory delinquent date). The amount of time and effort
expended will be directly proportionate to the desired % collection goals set
by the Town. The Town will be responsible for the provision of office space,
telephone, long distance calling access, and access to a computer, for the
resource(s) assisting with delinquent collections.
8.   County shall provide all normal hard costs of collection, including bill
and notice printing, postage, advertising, delinquent remedy enforcement, and
software maintenance. County will also provide reasonable training and
assistance to the Town delinquent resource(s).
9.   Town may undertake annexations according to statutes. The County will
collect first year city taxes on all annexations that are effective on July 1
st . The Town will bill and collect the first years prorated taxes for all
taxpayers in annexation areas when the annexation is not effective on July 1 st
.
10.   This agreement shall be valid for a period of one (1) year from the date
hereof, but shall be automatically renewed thereafter for a period of one year
until this Agreement is rescinded by resolution adopted by either the Brunswick
County Board of Commissioners or the governing board of Town. Any such
termination will be effective as of June 30 th of the fiscal tax year in
effect, but notification of such resolution must be delivered by May 31 st of
the final year.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties hereto have caused this instrument to be signed
by their proper governmental officials pursuant to formal action of their
governing boards and properly attested as by law provided.
COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK
/s/ William Sue
Brunswick County Board of Commissioners

b)   Wastewater
Alderman Boguskie reported meeting with Jason Glazener, Corps of Engineers, on
the erosion protection project for the Bay Street pump station. It has been
found that the erosion rate is 4 foot per year and will be undermined in 4-
5 years. The projected cost, 2.5 million, to save the pump station is a 65/35
split; Army Corps of Engineers 65%, City 35% ($500,000). It is anticipated the
study will be completed by November.
Alderman Boguskie explained the Sewer Transmission Facilities Agreement with
Brunswick County:
- The Service areas agreed to in the Memorandum of Understanding between the
City and County dated November 17, 2008 shall remain in force.
- The County will construct a sewer force main through the Citys service area
and connect to the city-owned Rivermist Pump Station and the city-owned 16"
transmission force main along Highway 211.
- The County shall allow the City to make one pump station connection to the
Countys proposed force main within the Citys service area.
- The City agrees to lease to the County, for $1/yr, for the term of the lease,
its rights, title, and interest to the Rivermist Pump Station, Sandy Lane Pump
Station, all transmission Force Main downstream of the Sandy Lane Pump Station.
- The County guarantees sewer capacity up to 500,000 gallons per day.
- The City agrees to grant the County unrestricted access and use of easements,
lands, interests, and rights in lands required for the operation and
maintenance.
- The County shall operate and maintain the transmission facilities.
- Additional sewer connections, additional wastewater flow and modifications
shall be made by the County.
- Agreement may be terminated or modified at any time by written consent of
both parties.
Mr. Ralph Cardwell, Public Service Director, agreed with the recommendation to
accept the agreement. Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to
accept the Sewer Transmission Facilities Agreement with Brunswick County.
Unanimous vote.

Use of the Garrison House Lawn
___________________________________________
The following are provisions for use requirements of the Garrison House lawn at
Fort Johnston, including restrictions and requirements as detailed in the
agreement with the US National Parks Service Lands to Parks program signed by
the City of Southport on
September 5, 2006:
General Use of the Garrison House Lawn:
1.   The lawn may be used by any person, public entity, or organization which
allows an individual from the general public to be a member, subject to
approval by the City of Southport Director of Parks and Recreation.
2.   All activities must be open to the general public with no restrictions
based on gender, race, color, creed, or religious beliefs. Activities may be
limited to children of specific ages with adult supervision.
Permission to Use the Garrison House Lawn
1.   All use of the Garrison House lawn must be approved in writing by the City
of Southport Director of Parks and Recreation.
2.   Requests for use of the lawn must include the name of the person,
organization or entity; date(s) and times of the proposed use (including set-up
time); and a complete description of the specific activities that will take
place on the lawn.
3.   A specific contact person must be identified in the request. This person
is responsible for compliance with this agreement by the requesting party.
4.   Electrical and other utility needs must be arranged and approved in
writing by the City of Southport Director of Parks & Recreation and the
Director of Public Works.
5.   The City of Southport Director of Parks & Recreation, City Manager, Code
Enforcement Officer, or Police and Fire & Safety officials may revoke
permission to use the lawn at any time for violation of this agreement or any
local, state and federal laws.
6.   Applicants must apply for permission each time the lawn is used. In the
case of use in a series of events (farmers market, etc) one application for the
entire series within the same calendar year is sufficient.
7.   All requests for use of the Garrison House lawn will be cross-checked
against any bookings for the Community Building as simultaneous events in both
venues may create a conflict. All conflicts will be resolved by the Director of
Parks & Recreation or his/her designee.
Specific Restrictions, Limitations and Fees
1.   Vehicles or heavy equipment are not permitted on the Garrison House lawn.
If there is a compelling need to do so, permission must be approved in writing
by the City Manager.
2.   Users cannot drive a stake or embed anything into the ground on the lawn
that will be deeper than 6 inches.
3.   Use of chemicals or other substances directly on the surface of the lawn
is prohibited. Report any problems that may require chemicals (herbicide,
insecticide, etc.) to the market coordinator, the Director of Parks &
Recreation or the City Manager.
4.   Open flame or other heat sources are not permitted on the lawn.
5.   All users of the lawn must have it inspected within 2 days after use to
determine if damage has been done. Damages, or lack thereof, must be noted on
the agreement form and filed with the Department of Parks & Recreation.
6.   The name of the person, organization or entity on the request for lawn use
is responsible to repair at their cost any damage to the lawn during use.
7.   If the event or activity will result in income generated by the user, a
fee will be charged and paid to the City of Southport Department of Parks &
Recreation. This fee will be determined by the City Manager based on the nature
of the event, the expenses related to the event or activity to the party
requesting use of the lawn, and any city services that may be requested. All
income from use of the lawn must be used for the maintenance and/or improvement
to Fort Johnston and the surrounding areas within its borders.
Adopted this 14th day of July, 2011
City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
ATTEST:  /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
      Clerk

Alderman Karn moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to go out of public hearing.
Unanimous vote.
Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Adams to adopt an Amendment to the
City of Southport Code of Ordinances, Chapter 4: Buildings and Building
Regulations, Disaster Recovery Emergency Permitting. Unanimous vote.
AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT CODE OF ORDINANCES
TEXT AMENDMENT # 11-0615-01
An Ordinance Amending the Southport City Code of Ordinances, With Respect to
Buildings and Building Regulations
AMEND BY ADDING:
DISASTER RECOVERY
EMERGENCY PERMITTING
Purpose
It has been established that there are a significant number of structures
within the City that are nonconforming to the current ordinances. The City has
realized that due to the large number of nonconforming structures, in the event
of a disaster it may be impractical to require all structures which sustain
significant damage to rebuild in compliance with the current ordinances.
Furthermore, the community's economy will depend on the ability of all property
owners to repair, reconstruct, or rebuild and become operational as quickly as
possible following a disaster. These procedures are intended to allow a
property owner to obtain approval to repair, reconstruct, or rebuild any
structure that is damaged or destroyed as a direct result of a disaster to the
state or condition that existed prior to the disaster without the necessity of
a full review as may otherwise be required under the City Code of Ordinances or
the Southport Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). These structures would be
rebuilt on their original footprint, but not increasing the nonconformity.  Any
application to repair, reconstruct or rebuild a structure that does not comply
with the following procedures shall only be reviewed and acted on pursuant to
other applicable sections of the Citys ordinances. Building permits are
required for all repairs and reconstruction.
Definitions
Damage Assessment Survey: a field survey to determine levels of damage for
structures and identify the condition of said structures.
Disaster: any natural or human-caused catastrophe (including any hurricane,
tornado, tsunami, earthquake, or related), or, regardless of cause, any
widespread fire or flood, or large-scale impacts from an explosion. The
disaster will be declared an emergency by the Mayor of the City of Southport.
Emergency: a local emergency, as defined by the City Code, which has been
declared by the Mayor of the City of Southport for a specific disaster and has
not been terminated.
Reconstruction: the rebuilding of permanent replacement housing, construction
of large-scale public or private facilities badly damaged or destroyed in a
major disaster, addition of major community improvements, and full restoration
of a healthy economy.
Planning Review Not Required
A. Any structure that sustains damage as a direct result of a disaster and
receives a lawful occupancy permit after a damage assessment may be repaired to
the state or condition that existed prior to the disaster without the necessity
of obtaining planning approval. The work must be completed within 18 months of
when the Board of Aldermen declares the City is ready to begin receiving
applications for permits after the declared disaster.
B. If a structure receives a lawful occupancy permit after a damage assessment
and the repair is delayed through litigation or other cause beyond the control
of the owner, then the owner shall apply for an extension.
C. The requirements of the UDO and the City Code of Southport shall be met,
except as specifically provided herein.
D. For applicants who do not meet the time period set forth by paragraphs A and
B, any repair that occurs must comply with all requirements of the UDO and the
City Code of Southport.
Manufactured Homes
Manufactured homes that are damaged or destroyed may be repaired, replaced, or
changed to stick built construction using the following:
A. If the structure receives a lawful occupancy permit after damage assessment,
the structure may be repaired compliant with this Section.
B. If the structure is declared restricted use or unsafe to enter or occupy
after damage assessment, the structure may be repaired, replaced, or changed to
stick built construction.
1. The structure may be repaired provided the requirements of the UDO and the
City Code of Southport are met.
2. The structure may be replaced pursuant to the terms and conditions of this
ordinance.
3. The structure may be removed and a stick built home may be constructed under
the current regulations for review and approval. This would be considered a
change to the existing condition so the benefits of this ordinance would not
apply.
Planning Emergency Permitting
In order to be reviewed under the provisions of this ordinance:
A. A structure that sustains damage or is destroyed shall be repaired,
reconstructed, or rebuilt to the state or condition that existed prior to the
disaster.
B. A structure that sustains damage or is destroyed must receive a declared
restricted use or unsafe to enter or occupy and require an emergency
construction building permit after a damage assessment.
Planning Emergency Permitting Application
The planning emergency permitting application must be submitted within six
months of when the Board of Aldermen declares the City is ready to begin
receiving applications for permits. At their discretion, the Board of Aldermen
may extend the application period by resolution.
Planning Emergency Permitting Affidavit
The planning emergency permitting affidavit must be submitted as part of the
planning emergency permitting application. The affidavit, to be signed by the
owner of record and notarized, must certify that all structures are being built
back to the height, density, setbacks and other such requirements that legally
existed prior to the disaster. However, if any local, state, or federal
regulations require any changes to the structure with regard to height or
square footage, the affidavit will allow the owner to build back with changes
to comply with those regulations.
Single Family or Duplex Dwelling
A. Any single family or duplex dwelling unit that sustains damage or is
destroyed must submit a complete planning emergency permitting application in
order to be reviewed under this ordinance. The application shall include such
information and documentation as may be reasonably required by the
Administrator, including all the following items:
1. If the structure sustains damage amounting to less than 50% of the fair
market value:
a. A planning emergency permit and permitting affidavit as described.
b. Elevation drawings previously approved by the City showing the height of all
four elevations of all structures on the site prior to the disaster or pre-
disaster photos showing all four sides of each structure on the property.
c. Pre-disaster photos of the entire property layout including front, rear and
side yards.
2. If the structure sustains damage amounting to 50% or more of the fair market
value:
a. A planning emergency permit and permitting affidavit as described.
b. Two copies of an as-built survey or such other documentation or information
as required by the Administrator.
B. The requirements of the UDO and of the City Code of Southport shall be met,
except as modified herein.
C. For applicants who cannot meet the requirements of paragraph A and for all
applicants who do not meet the time period set forth, any repair,
reconstruction, or rebuilding that occurs must comply with all requirements of
the UDO and the City Code of Southport.
Non-Single Family Structures (Commercial, Industrial, Multi-Family, etc.)
A. Any structure, other than a single family or duplex dwelling unit, that
sustains damage or is destroyed must submit a complete planning emergency
permitting application in order to be reviewed under this ordinance. The
application shall include such information and documentation as may be
reasonably required by the Administrator, including all the following items:
1. A planning emergency permit and permitting affidavit, available in the
Planning Department and Building Inspections Division.
2. Two copies of all approved plans OR two copies of an as-built survey.
3. Any other documentation as required by the Administrator.
B. The requirements of the UDO and the City Code of Southport shall be met,
except as modified herein.
C. For applicants who cannot meet the requirements of paragraph A and for all
applicants who do not meet the time period set forth, any repair,
reconstruction, or rebuilding that occurs must comply with all requirements of
the UDO and the City Code of Southport.
Landscape and Tree Standards
Non single-family properties that sustain damage or are destroyed as a direct
result of a disaster must meet the current requirements of the UDO in Article
18 for landscaping and comply with an approved landscape plan. The time frame
for meeting this requirement shall be extended to three years, with one third
of the required planting to be done in each of the three years. The three-year
time period will begin when the property is issued a Certificate of Occupancy
by the City.
Applications under Review at the Time of a Disaster
A. All action on applications for development, subdivision, or other approvals
or permits that are reviewed and acted on by the Administrator that are
submitted during or are in progress at the time of a State of Emergency due to
a disaster declaration by the Mayor shall be suspended for such time as the
Administrator deems necessary, provided that such suspension shall not exceed
18 months. The time frames established for reviews as set forth elsewhere shall
be suspended during this period. All such applications shall be reviewed and
acted on based on the provisions in effect at the time the application was
deemed complete.
B. All applications for approvals or permits that are reviewed and acted on by
the Board of Adjustment, the Planning Board, or the Board of Aldermen that are
submitted during or are in progress at the time of a State of Emergency due to
a disaster declaration by the Mayor shall be suspended until such time that the
Board can reasonably schedule any required public hearings and meetings to
review and act on such applications, provided that such suspension shall not
exceed 18 months. All such applications shall be reviewed and acted on based on
the provisions in effect at the time the application was deemed complete.
TEMPORARY SINGLE FAMILY USES
Purpose
The purpose of this Section is to allow single family dwelling owners to place
a temporary dwelling on the property where the damaged or destroyed dwelling is
located, while the existing single family dwelling is being repaired or
rebuilt.
Applicability
A. This Section shall apply in all cases where any single family dwelling, as
defined in the Southport UDO, is damaged or destroyed as a direct result of any
event that has been declared a State of Emergency due to a disaster, as defined
in the City Code of Southport. In such cases where these provisions conflict
with other provisions, the provisions here shall take precedence.
B. These provisions shall be in effect for six months from the date the Board
of Aldermen declares the City is ready to begin receiving applications for
permits. At their discretion, the Board of Aldermen may extend this time period
by resolution.
Provisions
A. Single family dwelling owners shall place the temporary dwelling within the
legal limits of the property where the damaged or destroyed dwelling is
located.
B. Each single family property is limited to one temporary dwelling.
C. The dwelling shall be travel ready.
D. Basic sanitation facilities shall be in place prior to placement of the
temporary dwelling.
E. The location of the temporary dwelling shall comply with health and safety
regulations as stated by the Building Inspector and the Fire Marshal and as
approved by the Administrator.
TEMPORARY NON-RESIDENTIAL USES
Purpose
The purpose of this Section is to allow permitted non-residential uses to place
a temporary non-residential unit on the property where the damaged or destroyed
non-residential use is located, while the existing non-residential use is being
repaired or rebuilt.
Applicability
A. This Section shall apply in all cases where any non-residential use, as
defined in the UDO, is damaged or destroyed as a direct result of any event
that has been declared a State of Emergency due to a disaster, as defined in
the City Code of Southport. In such cases where the provisions of this Section
conflict with other UDO or City Code provisions, the provisions of this Section
shall take precedence.
B. These provisions shall be in effect for six months from the date the Board
of Aldermen declares the City is ready to begin receiving applications for
permits. At their discretion, the Board of Aldermen may extend this time period
by resolution.
Provisions
A. Non-residential uses shall place temporary unit(s) within the legal limits
of the property where the damaged or destroyed non-residential use is located.
B. Temporary non-residential units shall be travel ready.
C. Basic sanitation facilities shall be in place prior to placement of the
temporary non-residential units.
D. The location of the temporary non-residential units shall comply with health
and safety regulations as stated by the Building Inspector and the Fire Marshal
and as approved by the Administrator.

ORDINANCE NO: 2011
AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING AND IMPLEMENTING A PROGRAM TO CHARGE MITIGATION RATES
FOR EMERGENCY AND NON-EMERGENCY SERVICES PROVIDED/RENDERED BY THE SOUTHPORT
RESCUE SQUAD
WHEREAS, the emergency and non-emergency services response activity to
incidents continues to increase each year; Environmental Protection
requirements involving equipment and training, and Homeland Security
regulations involving equipment and training, create additional demands on all
operational aspects of the rescue services; and
WHEREAS, the rescue squad has investigated different methods to maintain a high
level of quality of emergency and non-emergency services capability throughout
times of constantly increasing service demands, where maintaining an effective
response by the rescue squad decreases the costs of incidents to insurance
carriers, businesses, and individuals through timely and effective management
of emergency situations, saving lives and environmental damage; and
WHEREAS, raising real property tax to meet the increase in service demands
would not be fair when the responsible party should be held accountable for
their actions; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport desires to implement a
fair and equitable procedure by which to collect said mitigation rates and to
establish a billing system in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and
guidelines;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT:
SECTION 1: The Southport Rescue Squad shall initiate mitigation rates for the
delivery of emergency and non-emergency services by the rescue squad for
personnel, supplies and equipment to the scene of emergency and non-emergency
incidents. The mitigation rates shall be based on actual costs of the services
and that which is usual, customary and reasonable (UCR), which may include any
services, personnel, supplies, and equipment and with baselines established by
addendum to this document.
SECTION 2: A claim shall be submitted to the responsible party and filed
through their insurance carrier. In some circumstances, the responsible party
will be billed directly.
SECTION 3: The Board of Aldermen may make rules or regulations and from time to
time may amend, revoke, or add rules and regulations as it may deem necessary
or expedient in respect to billing for these mitigation rates or the collection
thereof.
SECTION 4: It is hereby declared and determined that all formal actions of this
Board of Aldermen concerning and relating to the adoption of this Ordinance
were adopted in open meetings of this Board of Aldermen, and that all
deliberations of this Board of Aldermen and any of its committees that resulted
in such formal actions were in accordance with all legal requirements, and the
Codified Ordinances of the City of Southport.
SECTION 5: This ordinance shall take effect thirty days (30) from the date of
adoption.
SECTION 6: Mitigation rates will only apply to persons who are not residents of
the City of Southport. Residents within the City of Southport currently
subsidize these emergency service costs through their property taxes. For
purposes of this section a resident is defined as: (a) any person who maintains
his or her full time residence within the City of Southport; or (b) is the
majority owner of a business that operates from real property owned by the
business located within the City of Southport. (For purposes of this section a
business includes any joint stock company, corporation, association, joint
venture, limited liability company, club or partnership).
Passed:  7-14-2011          /s/ Robert D. Howard

b) Consideration of Resolution Opposing New N.C. House District 18
Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to adopt the Resolution
Opposing New North Carolina House District 18. Unanimous vote.
RESOLUTION OPPOSING NEW NORTH CAROLINA HOUSE DISTRICT 18
THAT WHEREAS, the new proposed House District 18 includes portions of
Wilmington, Leland and Southport; and
WHEREAS, Wilmington is an urban center, Leland a rapidly developing rural
comunity and Southport a coastal community with each area having different
needs and interests in regard to economics, development and traffic; and
WHEREAS, proposed House District 18 includes approximately 60% of Southport
with the remaining portion of Southport in a different district; and
WHEREAS, it would be inefficient and confusing for Southport officials to have
to work with more than one representative in reference to issues affecting
Southport; and
WHEREAS, having all of Southport in one district and all of Leland in one
district would promote the best interests of both communities;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport hereby requests the North Carolina General Assembly to include all of
Southport in one House District and one Senate District.
Adopted this 11th day of August, 2011      City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the Citys
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the citys land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
a proposed amendment to Article 16 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on August 11, 2011, where public comment
was heard and considered before the Board of Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) this aspect of parking is not properly
addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance, (ii) this amendment is
necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the City of Southport,
and (iii) it is necessary to promote the public safety and general welfare of
the community by allowing for the use of boat slips as parking spaces in the
City where applicable.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.

Article 16: Off-Street Parking and Off-Street Loading Requirements
Section 16-2: General
Addition to this section:
(F) Utilization of boat slips as required parking. A boat slip is defined
herein as a space
designed for the mooring of a single watercraft and usually projecting from a
dock.
Eating and drinking establishments and water-oriented retail businesses may
utilize
boat slips to meet off-street parking requirements subject in accordance with
the
following standards:
1) All slips must be under the ownership or long-term control of the subject
business.
2) Boat slips must be available on a first come, first served basis, with no
fee
assessed for use.
3) Boat slips must be reasonably designed to accommodate customer boats.
4) The dock facility must be properly accessible in accordance with the
regulations
governing the maneuvering of watercraft on the adjacent waterway.
5) Boat slips must only be used for transient mooring of customers frequenting
said establishment and no extended storage of vessels shall be allowed.
6) Boat slips are allowed to meet off-street parking requirements strictly on a
one parking space per 20' linear dockage.
This ordinance shall be effective upon the date of adoption.

Taxicab
Alderman Frink moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to amend the City of Southport
Code of Ordinances as recommended by staff. Unanimous vote.
AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT CODE OF ORDINANCES
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen that Section 10-111 of the Code of
Ordinances is amended to read as follows:
ARTICLE V. TAXICABS*
Sec. 10-111. Definition.
The word "taxicab," when used in this article, shall be defined as any motor
vehicle seating nine (9)  fifteen (15) or fewer passengers, operated upon any
street or highway on call or on demand, accepting or soliciting passengers
indiscriminately for hire between such points along streets or highways as may
be directed by the passenger so being transported, and shall not include motor
vehicles or motor vehicle carriers as defined in G.S. 20-376.

RESOLUTION BY CITY OF SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMEN TO APPROVE AND ADOPT THE
LOCAL WATER SUPPLY PLAN
WHEREAS, North Carolina General Statute 143-355 (I) requires that each unit of
local government that provides public water services or plans to provide such
services shall, either individually or together with other such units of local
government, prepare and submit a Local Water Supply Plan; and
WHEREAS, as required by the statute and in the interests of sound local
planning, a Local water Supply Plan for the City of Southport, has been
developed and submitted to the Board of Aldermen for approval; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the Local Water Supply Plan is in
accordance with the provisions of North Carolina General Statute 143-355 (I)
and that it will provide appropriate guidance for the future management of
water supplies for the City of Southport, as well as useful information to the
Department of Environment and Natural Resources for the development of a state
water supply plan as required by statute;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that the Local Water Supply Plan entitled, PWSID#04-10-010 dated
2010, is hereby approved and shall be submitted to the Department of
Environment and Natural Resources.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Board of Aldermen intends that this plan shall
be revised to reflect changes in relevant data and projections at least once
every five years or as otherwise required by the Department, in accordance with
the statute and sound planning practice.
This the 11th day of August 2011.
/s/ Robert D. Howard

AUGUST 22, 2011
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN  SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
AUGUST 22, 2011    6:00 P.M.
COMMUNITY BUILDING SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
PRESENT:      Mayor Robert D. Howard
         Aldermen Ed Boguskie, Nelson Adams, Ken Karn
         Vickie Potter, Mary Ellen Poole, Jwantana Frink
STAFF PRESENT:   Regina W. Alexander, Interim City Manager/MMC-City Clerk
         Michele Windham, Deputy Clerk
I.   Call to Order - 6:00 p.m.
Mayor Howard called the special meeting to hear public comment on Fort Johnston
to order at 6:00 p.m.
II.   Invocation
Alderman Nelson welcomed citizens and pronounced the invocation.
III.   Public Comment
Ms. Shirley Wilson, 502 Brunswick Street, and a volunteer at the Visitor
Center, spoke about involving the volunteers in discussions, the accommodations
that would need to be made in Fort Johnston to make space for pictorial
displays, and security concerns.
Ms. Pat Kirkman, 119 Park Avenue, Acting President of Southport Historical
Society, spoke in opposition of using Fort Johnston as the Visitor Center.
Mr. Larry Maisel, 114 W. West Street, talked about the Historical Societys
experiences using the Fort Johnston Garrison building.
Mr. Paul Fisher, 110 River Drive, stated he was on the advisory committee that
developed a comprehensive concept plan that included Fort Johnston being used
as a visitor center, the tennis court developed as a parking lot contingent on
completion of Lowe-White Park, expansion of the Community Building, relocation
of the playground, and a riverwalk. Mr. Fisher cited a recent State Port Pilot
newspaper poll result of 52% in favor of the Visitor Center moving into the
Fort Johnston Garrison.
Mr. Phil Fravel, 311 Yaupon Drive, representing Mr. Sandy Toth discussed the
items; books, t-shirts, tickets for community events, etc. sold in the Visitor
Center and he questioned how the regulations governing Fort Johnston would
affect those sales.
Ms. Barbara Stockbridge-Davidson, 518 Brunswick Street, and volunteer at the
Visitor Center, suggested Fort Johnston be used as a historical museum
Ms. Cornelia Rogers, 319 Atlantic Avenue, encouraged the Visitor Center
volunteers and the Board to have an open dialogue and work together.
Ms. Karen Mosteller, 310 N. Atlantic Avenue, spoke in opposition to moving the
Visitor Center.
Ms. Becky Felton , 230 Caswell Avenue, suggested the Fort Johnston Committee
provide the public with a detailed business plan for use of the Garrison
building and questioned where the money would come from for renovations.
Mr. Rick Johnstone, 110 Willis Drive, recalled his wifes family history
enjoying the tennis court, he questioned the need for additional parking spaces
and spoke in support of leaving the Visitor Center in its present location.
Ms. Martha Johnson, 227 E. 11 th Street, recommended Fort Johnston be used as a
historical site.
Ms. Cindy Brochure, the Citys new Tourism & Economic Development Director
introduced herself and welcomed working with the Historical Society and Visitor
Center volunteers.
Ms. Becky, Captain Adkins Drive, spoke about the availability of restroom
facilities at the current Visitor Center on the west side of town and she spoke
in support of leaving the Visitor Center in its present location.
Dr. Sylvia Beck, Brunswick County resident, spoke in favor of moving the
Visitor Center to the Fort Johnston Garrison.
Ms. Joan Willey, 111 Ft. Johnston Place and Ms. Dora Loflin, 410 Bay Street,
spoke in opposition to removing the tennis courts and playground.
IV.   Questions
Mayor Howard opened the floor for questions.
Ms. Rogers asked if the contract between the City and Department of Defense was
flexible and if the City was obligated to put the Visitor Center in the
Garrison. Alderman Boguskie advised the contract is flexible as long as the
building is used for public use.
Ms. Rogers asked if a mold study had been performed in the building. The Mayor
responded the Citys insurance company commissioned an air quality study, no
major problems were found, it is not unhealthy, and it was determined having
the building closed up perpetuated the growth of mold.
It was asked if the cost had been determined for renovations to the Garrison
for use as a visitor center. Alderman Frink stated a 2009 estimate was $25,000
- $30,000 but the cost would depend on the actual renovations undertaken.
It was asked if there were plans for the current building housing the Visitor
Center. Mayor Howard indicated no plans had been made for the building.
V.   Board Comments
Alderman Boguskie pointed out the 200 year old Garrison had been altered
several times, only the interior can be changed, and the outer walls are
considered historical.
Alderman Frink and Alderman Karn discussed the Fort Johnston Committee
considerations and deliberations made to reach a recommendation for use of the
Garrison.
Alderman Frink pointed out the new Maritime Museum, located adjacent to the
Garrison, has become the most centralized place in Southport.
Alderman Boguskie pointed out the City has owned the property for five years,
he suggested establishing an advisory committee, the U.S. Parks Service wants
the property used for the general public and he did not want the Garrison to be
solely a visitor center.
Alderman Poole discussed the importance Fort Johnston has played to the
military in the area and suggested creating a Friends of Fort Johnston group.
She agreed with Alderman Boguskie and recommended further discussions with the
public and visitor center volunteers.
Alderman Potter expressed her opinion the Committee and former Board had spent
a great deal of time and effort addressing the issue and she was in favor of
using the Garrison as a visitor center.
Alderman Karn expressed his hope the preservation of the historical aspects of
the Garrison and the Visitor Center can work hand in hand, the volunteers will
be an integral part of the process, an interactive video room will be
established and security issues addressed.
Mayor Howard expressed his concerns the public did not want to move the Visitor
Center, remove the tennis courts and playground, a historical use for the
Garrison had not been reached and the public had not been assured a viable plan
for the use of the Garrison had been met.
Alderman Adams commended the committee for addressing a controversial issue.
Alderman Adams motioned, seconded by Alderman Potter to accept the
recommendation of the Fort Johnston Committee to move the Visitor Center into
the Garrison, develop a parking lot where the tennis court is located and move
the playground.
Ayes:   Aldermen Adams, Potter, Frink & Karn
Nay:   Aldermen Boguskie & Poole
Motion Passed 4-2
Adjournment
Alderman Boguskie motioned, seconded by Alderman Adams to adjourn the meeting
at 8:14 p.m. Unanimous Vote

a)   U.S. Army Corp of Engineers, Jason Glazener
Consideration of options to protect the pump station located at the end of Bay
& Lord Streets
Mr. Jason Glazener, U.S. Army Corp of Engineers provided a handout of two (2)
options to protect the Bay Street pump station from further shoreline erosion.
Option 1:   Sloping Rock Revetment
∙   Would replace the existing concrete rubble
∙   Would be roughly in the same footprint
∙   Meets objective of protection
∙   Does not protect beach in front of revetment
∙   Federally preferred plan
∙   Cost: $ 480,000; 65% Fed/ 35% City
Option 2:   Offshore Stone Sill
∙   Would be 20 yards offshore, mostly submerged
∙   Would be several hundred feet in length
∙   Would closely resemble the offshore sills near Kingsley Park
∙   Provides aquatic habitat
∙   Better preservation of beach behind sill
∙   Preferred by environmental agencies
∙   Cost: $ 710,000; 65% Fed/ 35% City
Mr. Glazener informed the Board that due to budget cuts, Federal funding for
Section 14 projects nationwide will be pulled at the end of September. The cut
will place the Southport project on hold until more funding becomes available.
Mr. Glazener discussed the work completed to date on the project and the
remaining work to complete the study.
Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Potter to accept Option 1, Sloping
Rock Revetment as the preferred option. Unanimous vote.

Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Frink to approve the proclamation as

Proclamation Recognizing
The 10th Anniversary of 9/11 As A National Day of Service and Remembrance
On September 11, 2001, the security of our nation was shattered by cowardly
terrorist attacks that killed nearly 3,000 innocent people at the World Trade
Center towers in New York City, the United States Pentagon, and in the pristine
fields of Shanksville, Pennsylvania. The terrorists goal was to strike a
powerful blow to the hearts of all Americans and tear at the fabric of our
nation. As a result of this tragedy, came a remarkable spirit of unity,
compassion and determination that will never be forgotten, just as we will
never forget those who were lost and injured and the people who rose in service
during the rescue and recovery effort and in defense of our nation at home and
abroad.
In observance of the 10 th anniversary of September 11, 2001 which killed
citizens from 92 countries, we hereby adopt the following Proclamation in
tribute to those lost and injured and the many who gave of themselves in
service to their communities and to American in the aftermath of the attacks:
WHEREAS, people of all ages and walks of life across America and around the
world, collectively witnessed an event of immense tragedy on September 11,
2001; and
WHEREAS, the events of that day instantly transformed everyones lives, some
through personal loss, and many others through an unfamiliar sense of
individual and national vulnerability; and
WHEREAS, Americans arose from the shock, unifying the country in national
spirit, pride, selflessness, generosity, courage and service; and
WHEREAS, many brace people tirelessly and courageously participated in an
extraordinarily difficult and dangerous rescue and recovery effort, and
WHEREAS, September 11 th should never be just another day in the hearts and
minds of all American; and
WHEREAS, September 11, 2011 will be the 10 th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks
on America;
WHEREAS, many citizens may wish to memorialize September 11 by engaging in, or
making a plan to engage in personal and individual acts of community service,
or giving activities, as part of a solemn day of remembrance and tribute; and
WHEREAS, on March 19, 2009, the United States Congress passed legislation
authorizing the establishment of September 11 as a federally recognized
National Day of Service and Remembrance, which was signed into law by President
Barrack Obama on April 21, 2009; and
WHEREAS, President Obama on September 11, 2009, issued the Patriot Day
Proclamation officially designating September 11 as a National Day of Service
and Remembrance, and calling upon all interested Americans to participate in
this observance through moments of silence, flying the flag of the United
States at half-staff, as well as community service and charitable activities as
a tribute to these victims.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport asks all citizens to
observe September 11, 2011 and mark the 10 th Anniversary of 9/11, as a
Voluntary Day of Service and Remembrance by all citizens and organizations.
ADOPTED, this the 8 th day of September, 2011
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
ATTEST:  /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
      Clerk
j)   Consideration of Proclamation for 2011 Lyme Disease Awareness Month
Alderman Boguskie moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to adopt the Proclamation
for 2011 Lyme Disease Awareness Month. Unanimous vote.
Proclamation for 2011 Lyme Disease Awareness Month
WHEREAS, infected ticks carrying the bacteria, borrelia burgdorferi which
causes Lyme disease, continue to spread throughout North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, the total numbers of both suspected and confirmed Lyme disease cases
reported to our state health department, co0ntinues to rise each year with over
nearly 900 case events reported in 2010. Additionally, the Center for Disease
Control estimates that Lyme disease may be under-reported by a factor 10 to 1
over actual cases, and
WHEREAS, the North Carolina Division of Public Health now encourages physicians
and health care professionals to consider the diagnosis of Lyme disease in
patients who present the symptoms of infections, even if the patient has no
travel history outside of North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, Lyme disease is difficult to diagnose because it imitates other
conditions and no reliable laboratory test can prove who is either infected or
bacterial-free, which often leads to under-diagnosis or misdiagnosis; and
WHEREAS, early indicators of infection include flu-like symptoms, characterized
by chills, headache, fatigue, muscle and joint aches and swollen lymph nodes;
and
WHEREAS, weeks or months later, patients with untreated or under-treated Lyme
disease can suffer from permanent and sometimes life-threatening damage to the
brain, joints, heart, eyes, liver, spleen blood vessels and kidneys. For this
reason it is imperative that all who may be exposed by Lyme disease receive
immediate treatment; and
WHEREAS, the best solution to reduce the risk of contracting Lyme disease is
awareness and education about the seriousness of the illness and the need for
residents, especially children, to practice personal preventive techniques when
engaging in outdoor activities - such as frequent tick checks, use of tick
repellant and proper removal; and
WHEREAS, the warm summer months are considered the most active time for ticks
and when the majority of residents are exposed to ticks during outdoor
activities.
Adopted this the 8th day of September, 2011.
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor

characteristics of a successful candidate.
∙   City Manager Position Description

responsibilities.

Vision Awareness Month Proclamation
Southport Lions Club
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club is working to increase vision awareness,
especially among the youth through vision screening at local schools; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club collected over 1,500 pairs of glasses in the
past twelve months and provides assistance to those needing but unable to
afford eye tests and the purchase of glasses; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club will conduct vision screening once a month,
September through December at the Brunswick County Resource Center and
conducted screenings at the Brunswick County Health Festival on September 17th
and 18th ; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club works in conjunction to support vision
screening with the New Hope Clinic that provides free health care to uninsured
citizens; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club, continues to keep with the challenge Helen
Keller issued to the association in 1929, to become knights of the blind in the
crusade against darkness; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club, established in 1945, is composed of men and
women volunteers who dedicate their time to the betterment of our community and
aiding those in need; and
NOW THEREFORE, I, Robert Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC in
recognition of this important service, sponsored by the Southport Lions Club,
do hereby proclaim October as Vision Awareness Month.
ADOPTED, this 13th day of October 2011 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor

and Interpretations
Ms. Amy Nelson, Planning Director, explained that the requested text amendment
to Article 2 will change the definition of what constitutes a minor subdivision
and will allow for staff approval of subdivisions that are five acres or less
in size. The text amendment has been recommended by the Planning Board. There
were no comments from the public.
e)   Public Hearing; Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment, Article 17,
Regulations for Signs
Alderman Potter reported the Board had tasked the Planning Board with review
and revision of the Unified Development Ordinance Regulations for Signs.
Ms. Tish Hatem, Planning Board Chairman, reported the Planning Board, City
staff, merchants, and citizens held many work sessions to develop clear
guidelines for signs. She displayed a proposed Citizens Guide to Signs
brochure. Ms. Hatem stated the consensus among all involved found the revised
ordinance meets the citys needs. Ms. Hatem pointed out that many supportive
phone calls were received and several of the merchants and citizens were
present in the audience. She thanked Alderman Poole and Potter for their
guidance through the process and urged the Board to adopt the proposed
ordinance.
Ms. Martha Johnson, newest member of the Planning Board, shared her experience
researching various sign ordinances in order to contribute to the revision
process.
Mr. Jay Royal, local merchant, commended everyone involved and expressed
support of the proposed text amendment.
Mr. Buddy Barnes, Planning Board member, emphasized that everyone involved in
the sign regulations review process did their due diligence and over 300 hours
were spent in review committees.
No further comments from the public, Alderman Adams moved to re-enter regular
session, seconded by Alderman Potter. ( 8:19 p.m.) Motion passed 6-0.

f)   Consideration of Resolution for text Amendment, Article 2, Basic

Alderman Potter motioned, seconded by Alderman Poole to adopt the Resolution
for Text Amendment, Article 2, Basic Definitions and Interpretations,
Subdivision Definitions (332). Motion passed 6-0.
RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the Citys
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the citys land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Director has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board
a proposed amendment to Article 2 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance at the request of the Planning Board; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
the proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public hearing,
properly noticed, was held on October 13, 2011, where public comment was heard
and considered before the Board of Aldermen regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Core Land
Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) the aspect of minor subdivision is
sufficiently controlled by the size of the tract to be subdivided, (ii) this
amendment is necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the City of
Southport, and (iii) it is necessary to promote the public safety and general
welfare of the community by allowing staff to review minor subdivisions as
determined by the size of the tract, rather than the number of lots.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 13th day of October, 2011.      City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
Attest: /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
      Clerk

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the Citys
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the citys land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered these matters and has recommended
that these proposed amendments to Article 17 of the Unified Development
Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public hearing,
properly noticed, was held on October 13, 2011, before the Board of Aldermen
regarding these issues; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that these proposed amendments to
the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with the Southport CAMA Core
Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) considering the current
economic situation, revisions to the City sign ordinance were necessary, (ii)
these amendments promote orderly growth and development in the City, and (iii)
regulation of signs is to promote the public safety and general welfare of the
community;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 13th day of October, 2011.      City of Southport

RESOLUTION TO ENDORSE THE CITY OF SOUTHPORTS APPLICATION FOR THE NORTH CAROLINA
DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATIONS BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN PLANNING GRANT INITIATIVE
WHEREAS on December 2, 2011, the NCDOT Division of Bicycle and Pedestrian
Transportation will conclude the 2012 Call for Proposals to encourage the
development of comprehensive municipal bicycle plans and pedestrian plans; and
WHEREAS the Bicycle and Pedestrian Planning Grant Initiative is a state program
set up for municipalities all across the state of North Carolina; and
WHEREAS the City of Southport has an opportunity to apply for this 80%-20%
matching grant program in 2012; and
WHEREAS there is a strong desire in the City of Southport to enhance the
transportation planning by providing more choices in order to make the
community more pedestrian-friendly, bicycle-friendly, and a better place to
live; and
BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport,
North Carolina in session assembled this 13th day of October 2011 endorse the
NCDOT Division of Bicycle and Pedestrian Transportations Bicycle and Pedestrian
Planning Grant Initiative application for the City of Southport, North
Carolina.

V.   Public Comments
Ms. Kendall Crews, 215 Rive Drive, requested her comments be entered into the
public record:
I became concerned after reading the recently revealed August 20, 2010 report
from WK Dickson regarding levels of hydrogen sulfide at the Burrington Avenue
Central Pump Station and the potential of associated health risks with levels
that high. Research from many sources such as the CDC, EPA and the North
Carolina Division of Air Quality reveal that chronic exposure to relatively low
levels of hydrogen sulfide gas could pose health risks. My concern was for
residents living in that area who have frequently complained of a strong sewer
odor over the course of many months. I decided I would conduct a survey of the
residents in that area of the pump station regarding possible health complaints
and shared my intention to do so with a local physician who also holds a
Masters Degree in public health policy. He advised me to conduct the survey
over a large area for a more representative sample. I then visited the
residents in 15 homes within a three (3) block area of the pump station. Eight
(8) of the ten (10) residents within one block of the site reported symptoms
consistent with the exposure to hydrogen sulfide gas. There were various
complaints such as burning eyes, eyes infections requiring medical treatment,
throat irritation, persistent cough, skin lesions and breathing problems
requiring two (2) trips to the ER, sinus problems, lethargy and sleep
difficulty. In all cases the time frame reported for either initial onset or
worsening of these symptoms was starting or since this summer. When I reported
back to my physician advisor, he expressed deep concern at the concentration of
symptoms reported. I hope it is clear why my concern goes beyond that of a
nuance odor. As a citizen and a licensed registered nurse, I am compelled to
advocate for the welfare of my neighbors.
Dr. Joe Pat Hatem, Dosher Memorial Hospital physician, discussed the public
health risks associated with the central pump station. He supported Ms. Crews
comments and conducting of the survey. He thanked the Mayor for his efforts to
find a solution to the problem.
Ms. Irena Sedivy, 119 N. Davis Street, talked about her fears her home could be
damaged by an apparent dead Live Oak tree in the Citys right-of-way. City staff
and Forestry Committee to re-examine the condition of the tree.

VIII.   Old Business
1)    Presentation of recommendation(s) for Central Pump Station
Carter Hubard, W.K. Dickson, and Public Service Director, Ralph Cardwell
reported:
A significant amount of FOG (fats, oil, grease) was observed throughout the
system. FOG in collection systems is typically from cooking oil and grease from
disposal of kitchen waste and food scraps in sink drains. The source of FOG is
liquefied animal fats and vegetable oils that are poured down the sink drains.
The liquefied fats and oils solidify in the system causing accumulation in
pipes, manholes, and pump station wet wells. The accumulation of the FOG
results in sewer line backups, manhole overflows, and limits venting. The
reduction in flow increased the retention time and presents conditions suitable
for condition H 2 S formation. FOG in wet wells creates an anaerobic condition
at the liquid surface and at the walls.
The heavy build up in the gravity sewers flowing to Bay Street and in the Bay
Street Pump Station indicates that commercial properties are a major
contributor of FOG. The FOG build-up in Park, Leonard, Cottage Point, and 9 th
Street pump stations which serve mainly residential areas indicates that
residences are also contributors.
Corrosion in the system is more severe where force main discharges into
manholes. The odor and H 2 S readings were higher at the Central pump station
in the afternoon. We reviewed pump station history log to check on any patterns
that may indicate why the odor increases in the afternoon but the results were
inconclusive.
A review of the pumping rates indicates force main retention times for The
Landing, Turtlewood, Deep Point, and Indigo pump stations more than 1 day in
the system. Reportedly there are 30 grinder stations in the system. Small
grinder type pump stations typically pump only once a day so they are prone to
create septic wastewater conditions.
A review of the pumping rates from Indigo pump station and 9 th Street pump
station indicate low velocity in the 10-inch force main (less than 2 ft/s). Low
velocity in the force main can lead to sediment build up that can result in
blockages and biological activity.
Recommendations
Immediate Recommendation Actions
1.   Monitor H 2 S with recording meter.
2.   Evaluate the H 2 S readings to inform the staff and neighborhood of the
environmental hazards.
3.   Increase enforcement of FOG ordinance by routine inspection of restaurants
and schools.
4.   Clean the gravity sewer by jetting and removing solids from manholes.
5.   Clean wet wells of trash and FOG.
6.   Clean wet well walls with pressure washer.
7.   Remove sealant from vent holes in manhole cover at Bay Street and Caswell
Avenue.
8.   Solicit bids from chemical suppliers for system additives to reduce odor
and corrosion in the Central Pump Station.
9.   Evaluate H 2 S readings to size an air scrubber.
Program Recommendations 
1.   Increase FOG education by a presentation to board and education program in
schools.
2.   Procure air scrubber for Central Pump station to reduce odor.
3.   Develop chemical additive performance contract.
4.   Develop maintenance program of the sewer system with video tracking of
areas cleaned.
5.   Update Sewer Use Ordinance.
6.   Increase the velocity in the 9 th Street force main to promote scour and
reduce retention time.
Staff will be installing H 2 S meters at the central pump station in the wet
well and at the vent to the outside. This will enable real time data collection
to ensure that levels do not exceed acceptable limits for public health and
odor concerns. It will also detect wet well levels of H 2 S consistent with
corrosion of the wet well walls and pump station machinery.
Complete report included as Attachment 1.

c)   Consideration of a Resolution Recognizing the Importance of the Lower Cape
Fear River, The Modern City of Southport and Fort Johnston in the War of 1812
Manager Alexander read into the record the Resolution Recognizing the
Importance of the Lower Cape Fear River, The Modern City of Southport and Fort
Johnston in the War of 1812.
Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Boguskie to adopt the resolution as
presented. Motion passed 5-0 .
A RESOLUTION RECOGNIZING THE IMPORTANCE OF THE LOWER CAPE FEAR RIVER, THE
MODERN CITY OF SOUTHPORT AND FORT JOHNSTON IN THE WAR OF 1812.
WHEREAS, The North Carolina Department of Cultural Resources has established a
team of staff and citizen members to plan for the commemoration of the 200 th
anniversary of the War of 1812; and
WHEREAS, The North Carolina War of 1812 Bicentennial Committees mission is to
develop events, activities, and materials to educate the public about Americas
Second War for Independence and the role of North Carolina and North
Carolinians in that war;
and
WHEREAS, The lower Cape Fear River was of vital importance to the defense of
North Carolina in the War of 1812 and Fort Johnston, in modern Southport, North
Carolina, was one of two United States fortifications that guarded Eastern
North Carolina against British attack during the War of 1812; and
WHEREAS, Fort Johnston was the site of a large buildup of both United States
Army regular troops and North Carolina militia called up to defend the lower
Cape Fear River against British attack during the War of 1812; and
WHEREAS, The North Carolina War of 1812 Bicentennial Committee has sponsored a
committee to host a symposium and living history program on October 20, 2012
entitled The Lower Cape Fear in the War of 1812; made up of members from North
Carolina Division of State Historic Sites, the North Carolina Maritime Museum
at Southport, the Daughters of the War of 1812, Downtown Southport, Inc. and
Southport Tourism and Economic Development;
BE IT RESOLVED, The North Carolina War of 1812 Bicentennial Committee, the City
of Southport and the Lower Cape Fear War of 1812 Symposium Committee will
commemorate the importance of the lower Cape Fear River and Fort Johnston
during the War of 1812 with a week long commemoration from October 15-20, 2012;
ending with a symposium and living history program on the grounds of Fort
Johnston on October 20, 2012.
ADOPTED, this the 10 th day of November, 2011
/s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC, Clerk

b)   Water/Sewer Committee
Alderman Boguskie entered into the record:
This will be the last report from the Water/Sewer Committee as it will be
rolled into the Utilities Committee. Members to be announced. Water from the
County was acquired and the Southport wells, which were problems, were shut
down. The Leonard Street well is classed as an irrigation well but could be
activated in the case of a disaster. Ralph Cardwell, Utilities Director, saved
the city several thousand dollars in the handling of the Leonard Street well.
The sewer reversal to Brunswick County went well. We now send our waste water
to the Brunswick County Plant in Supply where the waste water is treated and
the effluent is used on their spray field. During the shutting down of the West
West Treatment Plant there was a small spill. The spill was recorded, according
to the state regulation, but not reported because of the small amount of
spillage, again following the State regulations. After the reversal, the
Central Pump Station on Burrington Avenue is now handling almost twice the
waste water it handled when the West West plant was in operation. This has
caused some concern because with the increase of waste water came an increase
of odor from the pump site. The odor is a rotten egg smell known as Hydrogen
Sulfide (H 2 S). The human nose is so sensitive to this odor that it can detect
it in 0.0001 parts per million, much like sharks and blood in the water.
Because of this problem, a Waste/Water Committee meeting was held with W.K.
Dickson in trying to reach a solution to the odor problem. Suggestions were
adding chemicals to the treatment sites that did not produce enough flushes per
day to keep the lines moving, this would eventually come to the Central Pump
site cutting down on the odor. Another suggestion was to place a scrubber at
the Central site, where at that time we were treating the odor with a masking
agent, similar to your bathroom spray can. When this was brought to the Board
of Aldermen a citizen brought to the board information on a company in
Greensboro, NC that could help at a much lesser cost. Another special meeting
was held so we could hear from this company.   No one from the company was in
attendance, as they were working a trade show. A retiree from the Greensboro
sewer system was in attendance to tell us how the additive worked for
Greensboro. It did work in reducing the rotten egg smell in some pump sites but
not in all. After this meeting it was decided that staff and W.K. Dickson Co.
come up with a plan of action and they did. We were notified by email that we
needed the intervention of the County Health Department. Mr. David Stanley and
some of his staff did visit the pump site and found nothing that bothered them
as to safety issues. Mr. Stanley shared his information with the state agencies
and they also found nothing out of compliance.
While this was happening two Southport citizens in the medical field conducted
a survey among some of the residents in the area asking about health issues
that might be attributed to H 2 S. They felt the problem was of a severe nature
while Mr. Stanley talking with some of the same group received a satisfactory
report and so stated in an email to the Mayor. The survey was flawed. When
taking this type of survey you draw a radius from the point of the problem, in
this case the Central Pump Station, for at least three blocks. This gives the
same coverage east to west and north to south and all points in between. Staff
takes H 2 S readings in manholes or cleanouts in this area. You finish with a
smoke test of the lines, both city and in house lines. When smoke appears in
ones house you have a plumbing problem, dry traps, no traps or exhaust pipe not
going through the roof.
Some asked that we get other agencies involved. OSHA was one mentioned. OSHAs
interest is the well being of the city staff and has guidelines for them to
follow when entering an area that might have a gas collection of more than 5
parts per million. This comes under the OSHA Confined Space Regulation, which
the Southport staff follow to the letter. We also have found that there are few
regulations concerning H 2 S in the atmosphere around a plant or pump site.
The chemical additive will help as will a scrubber, but nothing will completely
clear out the odor. We can flush the lines with potable water but this is
causing treatment of potable water as an expense to our tax paying citizens and
is not the most acceptable practice by the State. I believe if we let staff,
our engineering firm W.K. Dickson and input from the County and State agencies
do their job, this problem can be alleviated as much as possible. H 2 S is
inherent in the sewer collection system.
Respectfully submitted
Ed Boguskie (Chair)
December, 8, 2011

c)   Website Update
Alderman Karn submitted the Website Report dated December 1, 2011:
I am continuing to load content and have started going to each department to
make sure their page has the information they need. I will also be training
someone in each department so they can add content and update their department
info themselves. This will save us money in that we wont have to pay an IT
person to perform that function.
This system is far more powerful than our existing site. As a result, the
technical specs required by the program exceed the capabilities of the
inexpensive web hosts. When we began I contacted Network Solutions, our current
web host. They told me that they could handle our website, but it might cost us
more money per month.
When I went back to them this week with the exact specifications, the tech said
that they could not accommodate us. I have been exploring other options to see
if we can get the best price. I contacted several web hosting companies and
compared the services and price offered by Vision Internet, our site designers,
which is $200/month. Most actually charge more than that to meet the exact
specs. We can compromise on the specs (slower speed, less security, do back-ups
ourselves, and more) but the best price I could get for that is $130/month.
Current budget items that correspond to this expense are in the General Fund:
1800   Computer software upgrade   $ 9,000
2601   Equipment purchases      $12,000
3500   Repair/Maintain Equipment   $15,000
As of the date on this report I do not have the activity for the 2011-12
expenditures for these items, but I will have them by the meeting date,
December 8, 2011.
The amount needed for the remainder of this fiscal year is $780 - $1,200.
This expenditure will save us money in the long term due to reduced IT
consultant expense and it will improve communication with our citizens
immensely. Amy Nelson and I will be making a presentation to the Board in
January when we expect the site to launch. But we need to solve the web host
situation before the site can go live.
Alderman Karn reported he had met with the Finance Director and there is a
budget line item, Contracted Services, that can be used towards the monthly
fee. Board consensus further discussion and possible action will be taken at a
future meeting.

Mr. Ed Boguskie, 502 W. Brown Street, requested the following be entered into
the record:
   Since the last Board of Aldermen meeting in December, I have heard too often
the words, mandated by the Board. A mandate from the Board requires that it be
done in an open session and would be in the minutes of that meeting. Mandates
or board action, which ever you choose, cannot be done via phone calls among
the board members and then call that board action. The board has to, by statute
and city charter, make all action items in open meetings with notice of the
meeting. Notice is a standing, published meeting schedule or a 48 hour notice
posted in city hall. If the board chooses to hire a consultant, be it an
engineering firm or other type of consulting firm, action has to be taken in
open public session and under only a few exceptions the board can hire a city
employee.
   Board members cannot put in place work orders. These are done by city
managers, city supervisors or director of city departments. I once received an
email that said, let staff do its work, not a bad thing for board members to
remember.
   W.K. Dickson is on the agenda tonight for two (2) task orders. (Task Order 4
& Task Order 5). Southport has to use an engineering firm as we have no
engineer on staff. The former Utilities Director was not an engineer, the
interim director is a planner and the utilities committee has no engineer as a
member. I am concerned about the cost that will be incurred for these two (2)
orders. The cost for engineering work is public record and can be seen.
Engineering cost are among the highest dollar items spent on the running of a
city. All engineering work should be scrutinized as to need versus dollars
spent. We are in one of the worst economic downturns of our life time. One day
good news the next three (3) days bad news and this has an impact on Southport
and Brunswick County. Keep this in mind when spending taxpayers dollars.
   Lastly Southport is a City Manager Board type of government. The City
Manager handles the day to day running of the city, while the board works on
the needs and wants of our citizens. In this form of government the board will
pass on to the city manager things it would, collectively, want to see happen.
Be statute and charter the Mayor is given mainly ceremonial powers. This type
of government serves its citizens well. You as board members need to understand
your duties, as elected officials, and carry them out without hesitation,
reservation or coercion. When in doubt contact the city attorney or the North
Carolina School of Government at Chapel Hill, neither will lead you in the
wrong direction.
Respectfully submitted Thursday, January 12, 2012
Ed Boguskie
