RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENTS TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the Citys
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the citys land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered proposed amendments to Articles 2
and 13 of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance and has made a
recommendation that these proposed amendments to the Unified Development
Ordinance be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to the NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on January 12, 2012, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding these issues; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public comments and
recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby finds that these proposed
amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with the
Southport CAMA Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) these changes are necessary
in order to clarify a definition in the Unified Development Ordinance, (ii)
these amendments should promote efficiency in plan review, and (iii) they
should promote the public safety and general welfare of the community by
better-defining a type of development with the potential for a major impact on
the community.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments and additions to the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted, this 12th day of January, 2012.
City of Southport
By: /s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC

c)   Consideration of Resolution Adopting a Policy for Mutual Assistance with
other Law Enforcement Agencies
Police Chief, Jerry Dove, stated the North Carolina Attorney Generals office
requires an updated policy for mutual assistance. Attorney Isenberg stated the
agreements are standard wording of General Statutes and allows the Board to
authorize the Chief of Police to enter into mutual assistance agreements.
Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Coring to adopt the Resolution
Adopting a Policy for Mutual Assistance With Other Law Enforcement Agencies.
Motion carried 6-0.  
RESOLUTION ADOPTING A POLICY FOR MUTUAL ASSISTANCE WITH OTHER LAW ENFORCEMENT
AGENCIES
WHEREAS, pursuant to North Carolina General Statutes 160A-288, the governing
body of a town may adopt appropriate guidelines for the purpose of mutual
assistance with other municipal and county law enforcement agencies; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to said laws, the law enforcement assistance to be rendered
authorizes lending officers to work temporarily with officers of the requesting
agencies, including in an undercover capacity, and lending equipment and
supplies; and
WHEREAS, it is deemed to be in the best interest of the citizens of the City of
Southport to adopt a reasonable policy and set of guidelines whereby reciprocal
law enforcement assistance can be both rendered to and obtained from other
governmental jurisdictions; and
WHEREAS, such reciprocal assistance is necessary for effective law enforcement
for the protection of the citizens of the City of Southport.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT THAT:
1.   The Chief of Police is hereby authorized to enter into mutual assistance
arrangements with other municipal and county law enforcement agencies, provided
that the head of the requesting law enforcement agency makes such a request in
writing.
2.   The Chief of Police is hereby authorized to permit officers of the
Southport Police Department to work temporarily with officers of the requesting
agency, including in an undercover capacity, and the Chief of Police may lend
such equipment and supplies to requesting agencies as he deems advisable.
3.   All such request and authorizations shall be in accordance with North
Carolina Statutes 160A-288, as applicable.
4.   While working with a requesting agency, an officer shall have the same
jurisdiction, powers, rights, privileges and immunities (Including those
related to defense of civil actions and payment of judgments) as the officers
of the requesting agency in addition to those the officer normally possesses.
5.   While on duty with the requesting agency, an officer shall be subject to
the lawful operational commands of the officers superior officers in the
requesting agency, but the officer shall for personnel and administrative
purposes, remain under the control of the officers own agency, including for
purposes of pay. An officer shall furthermore be entitled to workers
compensation and the same benefits to the extent as though he were functioning
within the normal scope of the officers duties.
6.   The Chief of Police is hereby authorized to enter into mutual assistance
agreements with other low enforcement agencies in accordance with such
reasonable arrangements, terms and conditions as may be agreed upon by the
respective heads of the law enforcement agencies.
Adopted this the 12th day of January , 2012
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor
Attest: /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
Clerk

g)   Consideration of Proposals for the Old Smithville Burying Grounds
Ms. Muzette Steck, Southport Historical Society, presented the following
proposals for The Old Smithville Burying Grounds:
1.   The Southport Historical Society (SHS) asks for permission to remove all
Christmas wreathes and flowers from grave sites within two weeks before Easter.
Remove all Easter flowers between Thanksgiving and Christmas.
2.   SHS asks permission to remove glass containers as well as all portable
containers which hold water and breed mosquitoes.
3.   SHS asks permission to attach letters and numerals on wooden plaques along
the inside of the fence which will enable visitors to find any grave. The style
of the sign will be similar to the routed sign and colors of the sign at the
corner of Moore and Rhett Streets.
4.   SHS asks the City to continue to mow the areas outside the fence and only
the larger grass areas inside the fence. Over the years, many foot stones have
been chipped or broken because the riding lawnmower is too wide to safely mow
most of the interior areas. However, the week trimming of individual plots, as
was done by the City in November, improves the overall appearance.
5.   SHS will continue to apprise the City Manager, the Aldermen and Mr.
Strickland of perceived needs and possible solutions. It would be helpful to
have one Alderman to whom SHS could present problems such as trees which are
uprooting massive family headstones and other trees which are in danger of
falling on tombstones.
Board consensus to hold implementation of policy pending a Public Hearing
during the February regular meeting.

Alderman Barnes motioned, seconded by Alderman Powell to adopt the Resolution

.  Motion carried 6-0.
RESOLUTION
HONORING DR. MARTIN LUTHER KING JR. CELEBRATION
WHEREAS, the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Committee was formed and
entrusted with the responsibility to plan a community wide celebration to
appropriately honor this great leader; and
WHEREAS, Dr. Martin Luther King Celebration Committee has selected the date of
Sunday January 15 and Monday January 16, 2012 to hold this celebration with
events scheduled to include youth programs, a march and roundtable breakfast,
and
WHEREAS, the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Celebration has established a mission
statement in which its most important goal is to bring people of the community
together for the purpose of promotion good will and harmony for the betterment
of the entire community; and
WHEREAS, it is extremely important that the great works and deeds of Dr. Martin
Luther King, Jr. Be duly remembered, honored and recognized in this most
filling and proper way.
NOW, THERFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Mayor and Board of Aldermen of Southport
recognizes January 15-16, 2012 as the official dates of celebration by the Dr.
Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Committee and encourages all citizens to
participate in the activities schedules.
Adopted the 12th day of January 2012.
/s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

2.   RESOLUTION TO ENDORSE EARTH HOUR in Southport March 31, 2012, 8:30 - 9:30
p.m.
RESOLUTION TO ENDORSE EARTH HOUR
Southport, North Carolina depends on the planet for resources and, likewise,
the health of the planet depends on good stewardship. Good stewardship of our
land, water, air, beaches, flora and fauna contributes to a healthy environment
in which to live, work and play. It also creates a desirable destination for
visitors and tourists. This contributes also to financial health.
WHEREAS, to focus the Citys attention on positive actions for the environment,
residents, governments, businesses, and organizations are hereby asked to join
together to celebrate Earth Hour 2012, and;
WHEREAS, Earth Hour 2012 participants commit to switching off all non-essential
lights from 8:30 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. to raise awareness of earths challenges,
and;
WHEREAS, participants come together to create activities in support of the
environment during Earth Hour, and;
WHEREAS, participants commit to going beyond Earth Hour to reduce their
environmental impact and find solutions to our environmental challenges by
adopting environmentally sustainable lifestyle habits and business practices on
an ongoing basis, and;
WHEREAS, official support of the Board of Aldermen qualifies Southport as an
official Earth Hour city, and;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that Saturday, the 31st of March, 2012, from 8:30 PM to 9:30 PM, is
hereby proclaimed as: EARTH HOUR IN SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA;
This the 9th day of February, 2012
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor

5.   Agreement between Downtown Southport, Inc. (DSI) and City of Southport for
use of the Garrison Lawn for their Annual Farmers Market
AGREEMENT
CITY OF SOUTHPORT AND DOWNTOWN SOUTHPORT, INC.
This Agreement made and entered into this 9th day of February, 2012 by and
between the City of Southport and Downtown Southport Inc. (DSI)
1.   The City of Southport agrees that DSI may use the Fort Johnston Garrison
lawn for its Farmers Market on Wednesdays beginning May 2012 until it concludes
October 2012.
2.   It is mutually agreed upon that DSI will pay the amount of $25 per week
for use of the Garrison Lawn.
3.   It is also agreed upon that this Agreement is in effect until the end
October 2012 and will be re-negotiated for 2013.
4.   It is further agreed that DSI will contribute funds to the City of
Southport to assist with beautification projects for use of the Garrison lawn.
5.   It is hereby mutually agreed that DSI shall be responsible for any damage
to the Fort Johnston Garrison Lawn resulting from its use thereof.
6.   DSI does hereby agree to indemnity and save harmless the City of Southport
and its officers, officials, employees and agents from and against any and all
suits, claims, loss, cost, injuries, damages, charges, liability or expense
whatsoever, including court costs and attorney fees, which they may sustain or
be put to by reason of this agreement and DSIs use of the Garrison Lawn for the
Farmers Market or other purpose.
Now, therefore in consideration of the mutual terms set forth, it is hereby
agreed to these terms and conditions by Downtown Southport Inc. and the City of
Southport, N.C.
CITY OF SOUTHPORT
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
Interim City Manager
DOWNTOWN SOUTHPORT INC.
/s/ Peggy Popelars
DSI President

b)   Utility Committee
Alderman Powell reported the Utility Committee met January 11, 2012:
$   Discussed the Central Pump Station meter readings of Hydrogen Sulfide;
readings are down from 200 parts per million December 8, 2011 through February
2, 2012 to 6 parts per million currently.
$   Held discussion regarding the Sacred Heart Catholic Church.
$   Committee supported issuance of a letter from the Public Service Director
to restaurants about grease traps.
$   Mr. Cecil Rhodes, ElectriCities met with committee members and provided an
update. Mr. Rhodes reported no changes would be made to rates until 2015.
$   Committee reviewed the Highland Park Subdivision proposed sewer; individual
home grinder pump system. Committee recommended system be redesigned to a
gravity feed system as the grinder pump system has not been used in Southport
for over 30 years and the risk of an overflow in a storm situation is
unacceptable.
$   Committee discussed heavy truck traffic on Jabbertown Road and recommended
opening a new dialogue with involved parties to determine if a separate access
road could be put in place.
$   Committee recommends purchase of portable scrubbers; $7,500 each, can be
tested for 120 and if not satisfied can be returned.
Alderman Powell motioned on behalf of the Utility Committee to authorize
expenditure of up to $15,000 from the Public Services capital expenditure fund
for the purpose of purchasing two scrubbers. Motion carried 6-0.
c)   Rate Committee
Alderman Barnes gave the committee report. The committee met to discuss rates
charged for rental of the Community Building. The committee recommended:
1.   No change in current published rates for rentals.
2.   Addition to the rates:
   A.   Each rental must be accompanied by a $200 cleaning deposit
   B.   A charge of $150 flat fee per event to use the kitchen. Fee will cover
kitchen water and electricity, maintenance, upkeep and replacement of kitchen
appliances. Committee also recommended installing locks on the kitchen doors
3.   Request City Manager acquire pricing for new kitchen appliances:
commercial grade, 2 door, stainless steel refrigerator; icemaker; commercial
grade microwave oven.
4.   Appointment of a committee to study the feasibility of making the
Community Building a stand-alone segment of City government.
Alderman Barnes motioned on behalf of the Rate Committee to adopt the committee
recommendation for Item 4 above; appointment of a committee to study the
feasibility of making the Community Building a stand-alone segment of City
government.
Ayes:   Aldermen Barnes, Powell, Coring, Poole
Nay:   Aldermen Karn, Adams
Motion carried 4-2

Alderman Karn motioned, seconded by Alderman Poole to amend the Code of

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 11-13. CONCEALED HANDGUNS OF THE CODE OF
ORDINANCES
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Section
11-13(a) & (b) of the Code of Ordinances is hereby amended to read as follows:
Sec. 11-13. Concealed handguns.
(a)   Pursuant to G.S. 14-269, G.S. 14-415.11 and G.S. 14-415.23, it shall be
unlawful for any person willfully and intentionally to carry a concealed
handgun for which a permit has been issued pursuant to G.S. 14-415.11 into and
onto all municipal buildings and their appurtenant premises and the following
recreational facilities: Fort Johnston Playground, Lowe-White Park and Caviness
Park.
(b)   An appropriate posting of this prohibition shall be posted on all
buildings and recreational facilities designated above.
This is the 9 th day of February, 2012.
      City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard

1)   Discussion and possible Board action on Southport Rescue Squad Referendum
Alderman Poole motioned, seconded by Alderman Barnes to adopt a Resolution
Pursuant to G.S. 160A-209(e) Calling for Referendum for Approval of Property
Tax Levy to Support Southport Rescue Squad and to establish a committee to
provide public information in reference to the referendum.
Ayes:   Alderman Poole, Barnes, Coring, Powell, Karn
Nay:   Alderman Adams
RESOLUTION PURSUANT TO G. S. 160A-209(e) CALLING FOR REFERENDUM FOR APPROVAL OF
PROPERTY TAX LEVY TO SUPPORT SOUTHPORT RESCUE SQUAD
THAT WHEREAS, G. S. 160A-209(e) authorizes cities to call for a referendum
regarding the approval of a property tax levy for those purposes set forth in
G. S. 160A-209(c); and
WHEREAS, ambulance services, rescue squads and other emergency medical services
is such a purpose set forth in G. S. 160A-209(c); and
WHEREAS, the Southport Board of Aldermen wishes to allow the citizens of
Southport to vote on the approval of a property tax levy for the purpose of
supporting the Southport Rescue Squad;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen as follows:
1. That the Board of Aldermen hereby calls for a referendum on the following
issue:
Shall the City of Southport be authorized to levy annually a property tax at a
rate not in excess of that which will produce $ 124,000.00 for the purpose of
providing ambulance services, rescue squads and other emergency medical
services?
2. That, pursuant to G. S. 163-302, absentee voting in this referendum shall be
permitted.
3. That the City hereby requests the Brunswick County Board of Elections to
conduct said referendum in accordance with G.S. 160A-209 (e) on August 7, 2012,
or as soon thereafter as possible.
4. That the Mayor of the City of Southport shall confer with the Board of
Elections to schedule and coordinate said referendum pursuant to North Carolina
law.
This the 9 th day of February, 2012.
City of Southport
/s/ Robert D. Howard
Mayor

   A)   Menton Padgett, City Auditor
   Attendance of auditors cancelled.
   B)   Paul Fisher, ElectriCities Update
   Mr. Paul Fisher, City appointed ElectriCities representative, explained the
North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency (NCEMPA); 32 cities, including
Southport, own a portion of five (5) electric generating plants - three (3)
nuclear, two (2) coal fired; the current debt is 2.9 billion, 1.5 billion paid
since 1993; Southport’s share of debt is 15 million which will be paid in 2026;
the average monthly residential electric bill is $110.30. Mr. Fisher encouraged
Southport to endorse the three (3) “E’s”: environment, economy and energy
revolution. He proposed goals for consideration; i.e., establish program to
conserve energy, keep system in top shape, put system underground, switch to
alternative sources of energy.
   In response to concerns raised by Mayor Howard, Mr. Fisher indicated the
Agency has voted not to enter into any further debt and any increase in the
debt of the Agency would have to be voted on by all 32 cities. The Agency is
required to maintain a capital fund, not less than 5 million, for a
catastrophic event. The fund is currently 55 million.
   The potential impact of the merger of Progress Energy and Duke Power was
discussed by the Board.
   Manager Alexander explained an invitation was extended to Brunswick Electric
Membership Corporation (BEMC) to attend the retreat but BEMC representatives
had a scheduling conflict. A meeting with BEMC will be scheduled after arrival
of the new City Manager.
   Mayor Howard recommended the Rate Committee review the City’s electric rate
structure and reduce the number of rates. He emphasized the City setting an
example by being conservative and the importance of updating the 10 year plan.
The Board discussed development of an underground master plan, natural gas
availability and the load management program.
IV.   City Departments’ Visioning, Goals and Mission
a)   Finance Department
   Finance Director, Jim Philyaw, gave an overview of fiscal year 2012-2013
goals and objectives, purchase order and credit card policies and procedures,
and enterprise funds (detailed information provided in Board agenda packet).
Mr. Philyaw presented a financial summary for the periods ending February 17,
2012. He stated the unaudited General Fund balance is $1,604,189, Electric Fund
$2,434,086, Water/Sewer Fund $2,204,760.
   Mr. Philyaw indicated the property tax collection rate is projected to be
behind last years’ collection rate, 95.48%, due to the County performing
collections. He noted that cities historically do a better job collecting taxes
than counties. Manager Alexander pointed out having the County collect the
taxes was an initiative of the Board during the 2011 Retreat and a
recommendation of staff to try for one year to determine if it was best for the
City. Manager Alexander stated staff will analyze the County versus City
collection and report back to the Board during budget deliberations.
   Mr. Philyaw discussed the City’s purchasing power, projection of revenues
not anticipating a budget shortfall, and all departments being within budget.
He is working on a cost allocation for all departments in order to determine
what it costs to run each department. He commented on several goals and
objectives:
   •   Cross train department employees,
   •   Credit card use for small purchases, emergency basis when a vendor will
not accept invoicing,
   •   Finance department have complete control over purchase orders,
   •   Purchase of a new laser printer,
   •   Determine feasibility of connecting all departments to financial
software to view and monitor their budget,
   •   Modify the utility billing collection system to allow reading of all
meters monthly for all active and inactive customers to assure electricity,
water and sewer are not being acquired illegally,
   •   Develop procedures to require all contracts be issued on a fiscal year.
   The Board discussed and reached a consensus to direct staff to pursue a
zero-based budget during the 2012/2013 budget process.
   Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Karn to authorize the
expenditure of $16,000 including shipping and handling for purchase of the

a)   City of Southport Facilities Assessment and Spatial Analysis
   Mayor Howard updated the Board on the facilities spatial analysis. He
presented a 2,400 sq. ft. conceptual plan, prepared by City employee and
licensed North Carolina Architect Connie Keller, that recommends housing the
Police Department in the old fire department on Nash Street, expansion of the
Rescue Squad Headquarters, and addition to the Code Enforcement building. The
plans calls for a connected facility and facade.
   Mayor Howard presented conceptual plans for the redesign of both floors of
City Hall to take better advantage of space, re-align Board chambers to
facilitate flow to office space and make City Hall ADA compliant.
   Mayor Howard discussed the planned phasing and relocation of employees to
other city buildings, i.e. old visitor center and jail annex, during
construction. He estimated $1.2 - 1.5 million to bring the buildings up to
standards. He noted the proposed plans did not take into consideration the
needs of the Public Services Department.
   Alderman Poole suggested addition of public restrooms behind the Code
Enforcement building and next to the Police Department to deter vandalism.
   Ms. Keller pointed out the space analysis was determined through in depth
interviews with City staff and their individual needs.
   Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Barnes to proceed with the
proposed projects as presented, including development of construction drawings.
Motion carried 5-0.
b)   City Dock Repair and Maintenance
   Alderman Barnes discussed repairs needed to the City dock; unstable walking
surface, slips in disrepair, deteriorating pilings and water levels during low
tide. He pointed out that two accidents had occurred on the dock in the past
year. He stated he had researched grant opportunities contingent on providing
transient boat slips and he suggested adding transient boat slips and applying
for a Boating Infrastructure Grant.
   Alderman Barnes motioned, seconded by Alderman Karn to direct staff to
research grant opportunities and the feasibility of adding transient boat slips
with an emphasis on safety.
Motion carried 5-0.
c)   Opt Out Option for the City’s Health Insurance Program
   Alderman Powell suggested consideration of an opt out option for the City’s
health insurance program and used his situation as an example. Mr. Thomas
discussed several scenarios when an opt out option may be advantageous to the
City; employees on Social Security, spouse has insurance, insured under a
military insurance program, and he pointed out some jurisdictions offer the
option at a fractional level.
   Board consensus to direct staff to prepare a policy recommendation on the
feasibility of insurance opt out program and present during budget
consideration.
l)   Attorney Agreement
   Mayor Howard proposed establishing a procedure and designating a point
person for authorizing consultation with the city attorney. Mayor Howard noted
the attorney charges the City every time a Board member calls him. Mayor Howard
pointed out there are many options, i.e. City Clerk, City Manager and North
Carolina League of Municipalities for getting legal advice. Finance Director,
Jim Philyaw, stated the City had spent $67,000 for all attorneys fees during
the current fiscal year and $32,000 the prior year. Board consensus that staff
get itemized billing from the City Attorney. City Manager Alexander explained
that most of this cost was attributed to a contract Attorney representing the
City in a lawsuit.
d)   Resolution to Create a Tourism Development Authority   (TDA)
   Consideration of the resolution was withdrawn. Mayor Howard and Alderman
Karn pointed out that Senator Rabon was drafting legislation to bring the
city’s TDA in line with other cities and designation of occupancy tax funds for
a specific purpose.
h)   Equipment cost for Community Building and Rate Committee Proposal on fee
(s)
   Alderman Barnes presented a recommendation from the Rate Committee for
purchase of a commercial grade refrigerator, microwave oven and ice maker for

   Alderman Barnes motioned, seconded by Alderman Poole to appropriate up to
$7,500 to purchase a commercial grade refrigerator, microwave oven and ice
machine for the Community Building. Motion carried 5-0.
   Alderman Barnes presented a Rate Committee recommendation to adopt a per
event kitchen rental fee for the Community Building to provide for maintenance
and renewal of equipment. The committee also recommends installation of locks
on the kitchen doors.
   Alderman Barnes motioned, seconded by Alderman Powell to adopt a per event
$150 kitchen fee to the rental rate of the Community Building effective upon
arrival of new kitchen equipment.
Aye:   Aldermen Barnes, Poole, Powell and Coring
Nay:   Alderman Ken
Motion carried 4-1.
j)   Riverfront Study
   Mayor Howard discussed undertaking a study and implementing a master plan
for the riverfront from Kingsley Park to the Yacht Basin. He indicated there is
the potential to get Federal or State matching funds.
   Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Barnes to allocate up to
$50,000 matching funds in the 2012-2013 budget for the purpose of conducting a
Riverfront Master Plan. Motion carried 5-0.
n)   Health Emergencies Plan
   Alderman Karn expressed his understanding that there is a procedure that has
not been put into place to deal with community wide health emergencies. He
recommended the in-coming City Manager and staff address the issue.

2.   ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
      ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
[Image]
 
WHEREAS, in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of
Agriculture that a special day be set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS, this holiday called Arbor Day, was first observed with the planting of
more than a million trees in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS, Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS , trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and
water, cut heating and cooling costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air,
produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for wildlife, and
WHEREAS , trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes,
fuel for our fires, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic
vitality of business areas, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS , trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual
renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE, I Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC, do
hereby proclaim March 16, 2012 as ARBOR DAY in the City and urge all citizens
to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees and woodlands, and
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote
the well-being of this and future generations.
DATED, this 8th day of March, 2012.   
                  /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

AN ORDINANCE FINDING THAT A DWELLING LOCATED IN THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT VIOLATES
THE MINIMUM HOUSING CODE AND DIRECTING THAT SAID DWELLING BE DEMOLISHED
WHEREAS, the Southport Board of Aldermen finds that the building on property
described herein is classified as unfit for human habitation in accordance with
the minimum housing standards included in the City of Southport Minimum Housing
Code Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, all hearings and orders, notifications, and other actions prescribed
in said Minimum Housing Code Ordinance and in N.C.G.S 160A-443 have been
accomplished prior to adoption of this ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the owners of the dwelling located on the property described herein
have been given reasonable opportunity to bring the dwelling into conformity
with the Minimum Housing Code; and
WHEREAS, the dwelling located on property described herein can not be repaired
at a reasonable cost relative to its value, and should therefore be demolished.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA:

authorized and directed to demolish the dwelling located in the City of
Southport at the following location:
   Property Owner Name   Location of Property      Parcel Number
   James F. Clemmons Jr.   607 North Caswell Avenue   237EC017
Section 2: That this ordinance shall be recorded in the Office of the Register
of Deeds of Brunswick County. This ordinance shall become effective on March 8,
2012.

5.   City of Southport Volunteer Appreciation Week Resolution
RESOLUTION
CITY OF SOUTHPORT
VOLUNTEER APPRECIATION WEEK
WHEREAS, to encourage an environment in which volunteers can flourish, the City
of Southport Board of Aldermen have adopted the goal of continuing a program
that promotes community organizations and encourages volunteerism; and
WHEREAS, City of Southport is often called the community of volunteers; and
WHEREAS, our City could not function without volunteers who serve the Southport
Visitor’s Center, Dosher Hospital, NC Maritime Museum, Ft. Johnston/Southport
Museum, and many other Southport boards, commissions, task forces and
committees; and
WHEREAS, everyday, volunteers help shape the policies that keep our City
heading in the right direction and their impact can be felt throughout the
community; and
WHEREAS, there are thousands of volunteers in our community who give their time
and effort to help others through their church, community organizations,
service clubs, schools, hospitals, charitable organizations and other worthy
endeavors; and
WHEREAS, volunteers are motivated by the simple satisfaction of helping their
fellow citizens and making their community a better place to live.
NOW THEREFORE, I, Robert Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, North
Carolina, in the county of Brunswick, do hereby resolve and proclaim March 18 -
March 24 as “Volunteer Appreciation Week” in the City of Southport to honor the
hard work and selfless dedication of the thousands of volunteers who serve the
city and the community.
ADOPTED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen this 8th day of March, 2012.
                        s/ Robert D. Howard

   Mr. Ed Boguskie, 502 W. Brown Street, read a statement into the record:
   Tonight I would like to address two (2) areas concerning the performance of
your duty as an alderman or mayor. The NC general assembly passed a law in 2009
requiring all NC cities, counties, local boards and etc. to adopt a resolution
or policy containing a code of ethics to guide their actions as a governing
board. This resolution had to be adopted by January 1, 2011.
   Southport did adopt a code of ethics per state statute. The guide
specifically pointed out five (5) areas that the code must address. The statute
left local boards a good deal of leeway in deciding on their code but made it
plain the five (5) areas had to be addressed. 1. The need to obey all
applicable laws regarding official actions taken as a board member. 2. The need
to uphold the integrity and independence of the board member’s office. 3. The
need to avoid impropriety in the exercise of the board member’s official
duties. 4. The need to faithfully perform the duties of the office. 5. The need
to conduct the affairs of the governing board in an open and public manner.
Under #1 If a board member is ever in doubt about what course of conduct is
legal in a particular situation the official should seek the advise of the
local government attorney. If the action is ethical seek the council of other
board members or a trusted advisor.
   The Southport Board of Aldermen also adopted the Suggested Rules of
Procedure for a City Council. These rules are based on Robert’s Rules of Order
Newly Revised. 1. The council must act as a body. 2. The council should proceed
in the most efficient manner possible. 3. The council must act by at least a
majority. 4. Every member must have an equal opportunity to participate in
decision making. 5. The council’s rules of procedure must be followed
consistently. 6. The council’s actions should be the result of a decision on
the merits and not a manipulation of the procedural rules.
   At the retreat on Saturday, February 25, 2012 do you feel the board followed
the Ethics Code or the Suggested Rules of Procedure? If you, as a board member,
do not have a copy of these two (2) publications ask Regina and she will
procure them for you. When you receive a copy of (A Model Code of Ethics for NC
Local Elected Officials) look under the acknowledgments, check the committee
members and you will see the name of Regina Alexander, city clerk, city of
Southport. This was not a paying job and it required many hours from start to
finish.

1)   Renovation to the Whittlers Bench and placement of a 20 ft. Cedar Tree
   Ms. Kendall Crews, 211 River Drive read a statement into the record:
   According to an interview several years ago with then Southport long time
resident Leilia Pigott, a cedar tree was planted in 1954 by the Southport
Garden Club within the perimeter of the Whittlers Bench. It was the replacement
for two Poplars that had been destroyed by Hurricane Hazel that same year. It
stood for over four decades serving as welcome shade for those wishing to sit a
spell. For almost 42 years it stood not as an obstruction to the view but as a
focal point to draw ones eyes to the artistic beauty of the magnificent Cape
Fear at its back. Then on July 12, 1996, the cedar tree like its predecessors
was ravaged by an act of God named Bertha. Many mourners gathered around its
remains after the storm grieving over the loss of a significant piece of
Southport’s history and character. Had the cedar tree gone unscathed by this
violent storm, it would in all likelihood still be standing. I can’t imagine if
that were the case that there would be a need for a public hearing tonight to
consider removing it because it blocks the view. Why such heartfelt passion
over a tree? Because to quote a comment on Facebook, “The tree is like New York
Times Square or the Statue of Liberty.” We are not New York but what an umbel
yet mighty symbol of Southport that little ole tree has been. Circling it has
been a rite of passage to many upon their return to Southport whether they were
gone for a day or many years. So important was that scruffy tree to the very
essence of Southport that pieces of it along with its story are displayed in
the Maritime Museum. An excerpt from the Sunday Star News July 14, 1996
edition, report on the damage from the storm reads, “In Southport residents and
visitors, some a bit teary-eyed, picked up pieces of the cedar tree at
Whittlers Bench to keep as souvenirs. Some posed for pictures in front of the
landmark tree split in two during the storm.”   I was one of those teary-eyed
people the story referred to. To this day a few splinters from that tree remain
one of my most treasured possessions.  Tonight I have shared a little piece of
it with each of you. A request has been made by a passionate group of
volunteers, many of whom grew up hanging out around that tree hearing stories
of old, stories of their ancestry. Their request is to replace the cedar tree
and fix the aging bench at no cost to the city. Finally, after almost 16
years, since its destruction, you are simply being asked to bestow your
blessings on the restoration of an iconic symbol that has defined decades of
Southport’s history.
   Mr. Bob Thorsen, Southport resident, read a letter from Mary Strickland:
   We went down the Howe Street hill to the waterfront to eat lunch today. We
do this often, a lovely hour in the middle of a long summer workday. At times a
Spring tonic, a Fall respite, or a Winter haven. But today something was
different. Suddenly the heat was stifling, the air humid and the waterfront
vista could not invite us to stay awhile. What was wrong? We wondered aloud and
suddenly knew. The cool, tranquil and protection of the beautiful Whittlers
Bench tree at the foot of Howe Street was missing. But we knew that. We knew
that when Hurricane Bertha torn it away and we grieved that same day with
others of our community loss. Today we must be caught in a warp of time. Time
to relive a moment, the unannounced eight year anniversary of that very sad
day. Today the Whittlers Bench is not inviting. It’s hot, sultry, no shade to
cool are native sons and guests, how can this be? What would have been so very
ugly and so very distasteful about that old familiar tree that would keep us
from rushing in to put up another in its place? And why didn’t we instantly act
to share with others the joy of what we once had. This town was built on the
dreams of people seeking spiritual peace, refreshment of body and soul. Our
memorial founder Joshua Potts once toasted, “May the tree of liberty take root
in the center of the earth and its branches spread from pole to pole.” The
living branches of our Whittlers Bench tree afforded protection for many
throughout the years. Joshua Potts would have been pleased. We could use
another tree of liberty right now to unify, to help heal. We could find a tree
that would be a symbol of our faiths and the strengths of this homeland. We
could plant a tree for all to see at the foot of a long gentle hill to the
river. Our founders would understand and we would once again be refreshed in
many ways.
   Thank you,
   Wayne and Mary Strickland
   Southport, North Carolina
   River Road

IX.   Old Business

Section 16-3: Minimum Parking Requirements
   Special situations wherein the property owner cannot comply with the above
requirements due to pre-existing, undersized lots in the Business District (BD)
shall be handled by the Planning Board. The Planning Board may alter the number
and location of parking spaces to be required, but shall in all cases give due
consideration to the needs therefor.
RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the City’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to Article 16 of the United Development Ordinance be
approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public hearing,
properly noticed, was held on March 8, 2012, before the Board of Aldermen
regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) many older lots in the Business District
are not able to meet modern-day parking requirements, (ii) this amendment
promotes orderly growth and development in the City, and (iii) allowance of
parking flexibility promotes the public safety and general welfare of the
community.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This 8th day of March, 2012            City of Southport
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard
                        Mayor

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 11 OF THE CODE OF ORDINANCES TO PROHIBIT
DANGEROUS WEAPONS ON CITY PROPERTY
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Chapter
11 of the Code of Ordinances is hereby amended by adding the following section:
Section 11-13.1 Dangerous Weapons
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to carry, possess or have within
his immediate access any dangerous weapon while in or upon city property.
   (b)   For purposes of this section, the following words have the meaning
indicated:
City property means any building, park, recreational facility, cemetery,
garage, parking lot or other public property owned by or controlled by the
City.
Dangerous weapon includes, but is not limited to, any firearm, rifle, pump gun,
air rifle, air pistol, bowie knife, dirk, dagger, slingshot, loaded cane,
metallic knuckles, razor, stun gun, switch blade knife, black jack, nightstick,
explosives or any other devise or object designed to or intended to be used to
inflict injury upon persons or property.
   (c)   This section shall not apply to:
      (i)   Sworn law enforcement officers
      (ii)   Members of the armed forces or national guard while on duty
      (iii)   Any person possessing a firearm in a cemetery for the purpose of
conducting a military funeral pursuant to a permit obtained from the city.
      (iv)   Any person possessing a firearm in a city park for ceremonial
purposes
         pursuant to a permit obtained from the city.
This the 8th day of March, 2012         The City of Southport
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard
                        Mayor

PROCLAMATION
NATIONAL DAY OF PRAYER
WHEREAS, civic prayers and national days of prayer have a long and venerable
history in our constitutional republic, dating back to the First Continental
Congress in 1775; and
WHEREAS, the Declaration of Independence, our first statement as Americans of
national purpose and identity, made “the Laws of Nature and Nature’s God” the
foundation of our United States of America and asserted that people have
inalienable rights that are God-given; and
WHEREAS, the Supreme Court has affirmed the right of state legislatures to open
their sessions with prayer and the Supreme Court and the U.S. Congress
themselves begin each day with prayer; and
WHEREAS, in 1988 legislation setting aside the first Thursday of May in each
year as a National Day of Prayer was passed unanimously by both Houses of
Congress and signed by President Ronald Reagan; and
WHEREAS, the National Day of Prayer is an opportunity for Americans of all
faiths to join in united prayer to acknowledge our dependence on God, to give
thanks for blessings received, to request healing for wounds endured, and to
ask God to guide our leaders and bring wholeness to the United States and her
citizens; and
WHEREAS, it is fitting and proper to give thanks to God by observing a day of
prayer in the City of Southport when all may acknowledge our blessings and
express gratitude for them, while recognizing the needs for strengthening
religious and moral values in our State and Nation; and
NOW, THEREFORE, I Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, and Board
of Aldermen do hereby proclaim May 3, 2012 as “A DAY OF PRAYER IN SOUTHPORT”
and urge all citizens of Southport to observe the day in ways appropriate to
its importance and significance.
This 12th day of April 2012.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard
                        Mayor
Attest: /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
      Clerk
City of Southport
2012 Earth Day Proclamation
   WHEREAS, the first Earth Day was celebrated on April 22, 1970, and was
founded by the late Senator Gaylord Nelson with the goal of inspiring
environmental awareness and encouraging the conservation, protection and
appreciation of our nation’s natural resources; and
   WHEREAS, it is the responsibility of each of us to safeguard the
environment, by recognizing that all human life depends upon the Earth and upon
one another for our mutual existence, well-being and development; and
   WHEREAS, the steps we can take to protect and preserve our natural
environment through education, partnerships and positive actions should be
encouraged; and
   WHEREAS, the citizens of Southport are committed not only to the protection
and preservation of our environment, but also to the restoration of ecosystems
and habitat; and
   WHEREAS, in furtherance of this objective the City of Southport supports
organizations that participate in Earth Day 2012; and
   WHEREAS, the City commends all who participates in Earth Day, for their
dedication in taking a proactive role in shaping the future of our environment
and in protecting the Earth’s precious natural resource;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City
of Southport, do hereby proclaim April 22, 2012, as
EARTH DAY
and urge all our citizens to be mindful of local, state and national laws which
protect our environment and to join in efforts to preserve the beauty and
wonder of the lands, skies and water of the Earth in all its diversity.
   This the 12th day of April 2012.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
   Clerk
PROCLAMATION
SOUTHPORT SPRING CLEAN UP 2012
Whereas, the City of Southport annually organizes a spring clean up to insure
clean and beautiful streets in the City; and
Whereas, the Spring Cleanup will take place April 17-21, 2012, and encourage
local citizens, businesses, civic groups, churches, schools, families,
individuals and professional groups to participate in this effort by organizing
cleanups in their neighborhoods; and
Whereas, Southport Code Enforcement Department is collecting debris and refuse
at the intersection of 8th Street and Caswell Avenue; and
Whereas, the great natural beauty of Southport and a clean environment is a
source of pride for all citizens and attracting tourists; and
Whereas, the cleanup will increase awareness of the need for cleaner roadsides,
streets and neighborhoods, and emphasize the importance of not littering, and
encourage recycling of solid waste, and
Whereas, the 2012 spring cleanup is an annual event coordinated by the Code
Enforcement Officer, and is utilized by our residents and citizens as a service
to keep Southport clean and beautiful, and
Whereas, the “Southport Spring Cleanup” will be a part of bringing awareness to
the citizens of this Great City regarding the importance of a clean environment
to the quality of life in Southport, North Carolina.
NOW, THEREFORE, I ROBERT D. HOWARD, MAYOR OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA, do hereby proclaim April 17-21, 2012 as “SPRING CLEANUP” time
in Southport and encourage citizens to take an active role in making our city
cleaner.
This 12th day of April 2012      
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

   “I have, for sometime, had reservations about the number of closed sessions
or executive sessions that the Southport Board of Aldermen have entered into.
Each of you are aware of the permitted purposes for a closed session and any
thing beyond these permitted purposes is not legal. I am having trouble with
closed sessions being added to the agenda at the board meeting with little or
no explanation as to why. At the March meeting Alderman Karn had to ask why the
closed session was being added. This is not acceptable. If there is a real
reason (falling under the 9 guidelines) a reason should be given and unless, of
a vital nature, should not be added at a board meeting.
   When you, the aldermen, feel a closed session is not valid or the
conversation during a closed session goes beyond what the session was called
for, you may leave the session and go back to your board seat at any time. This
will say a lot to those in the audience. Think this over, it is important or
the State would not have addressed it as it has done. North Carolina is very
strong on open meetings and the open meeting laws.”
   Alderman Coring reported he had received 69 comments in favor of keeping the
tennis courts.
VI.   Committee Reports
a)   Emergency Services Committee
   Alderman Poole stated the committee report:
   Members: Aldermen Coring and Poole, Chiefs Cumbee, Dove and Sage, and City
Manager
   1.   The Emergency Services Committee was appointed by Mayor Howard with the
purpose of making a recommendation to the Board of “What Official Position
Should the City take in regard to the Vote of the Citizens concerning Emergency
Services.”
   2.   The following is an interim report with the final report being provided
at the May meeting.
   3.   Considerations of the committee included the desires and wishes of the
citizens, costs involved and the citizen population of 2800 versus the services
population of 9,200. In consideration of the 2800 vs 9200, it is noted that
there was and is no effort to compare Fire to Rescue or vice versa, but only to
acknowledge this for financial and economic purposes.
   4.   For an interim report, the Committee recommends that
      a.   The primary focus should be ambulance services. The city requires a
new ambulance and a dependable back up. At this time it is estimated that the
cost would be approximately $200,000.00. It is noted that Chief Sage is very
proactive in reviewing available equipment with different options for
purchasing to get the best equipment for the least amount of money. It is noted
that in order to focus on the mission of this committee, the costs involved in
renovation to the building were not discussed. However, it is noted that once a
decision is made, the approximately $200,000 estimated cost for renovations
would need to be placed in the Rescue Squad Budget.
      b.   Departments Should Train Together: With continuing of Rescue
operations with Fire Department Back up.
      c.   Review Emergency Plans and update as necessary.
      d.   Update Master Plan
      e.   Complete Matrix covering responsibilities - Fire, Police, Rescue
   5.   For the May meeting, request that information be provided to the Board
by the City Manager and the Finance Officer concerning information on the
Rescue Squad to include but not limited to all revenues and expenditures.
   6.   We request that no discussion or decisions be made until the next
meeting when the Board has had appropriate time to review the interim report
and obtain all of the information available from Staff.
b)   Shop to the Beat
   Alderman Poole reported that Shop to the Beat has been renamed to “Southport
Beat” and would be held the third Friday of each month, 5:00 to 8:00 p.m.
beginning June 15.
c)   Website Committee
   Alderman Karn reported the committee met April 4 and changes were made to
the site based on recommendations made at that meeting. Alderman Karn presented

   Planning Board chairman Tish Hatem updated the Board on a proposed Unified
Development Ordinance (UDO) text amendment to allow ice-vending machines. She
stated a Planning Board subcommittee met March 28, and will be reporting to a
full Planning Board during the April 19 meeting with a recommendation:
   •      Remove restrictions to distance from residential zoning areas
   •      Remove size restrictions
   •      Add language for removal of machine within 30 days if main business
ceases to operate
   •      Retain as a conditional use in Business District (BD) and Highway
Commercial (HC) zoning districts
   •      Retain as an accessory use
   Ms. Hatem indicated the review committee felt permitting the units as a
stand alone business would not fit with the small shop theme of the city.

the use as a stand alone business.

TEXT AMENDMENT # 12-0308-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With
Respect to Off-Street Parking and Off-Street Loading Requirements
Statement of Present Regulation
ARTICLE 10.   Table of Permitted Uses (revised 12-13-07)
Section 10-1, Note 4: Accessory Uses
Swimming pools as an accessory use in R-10, R-20, MF, MH, O-I or PUD districts
shall be enclosed by protective fencing not less than five (5) feet in height
and should be setback five (5) feet from the existing property line.
Statement of Proposed Amendment:
Swimming pools as an accessory use in R-10, R-20, MF, MH, O-I or PUD districts
shall be setback five (5) feet from the existing property line and enclosed by
protective fencing meeting the requirements of the NC Residential Building
Code.
RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the City’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to Article 10 of the Unified Development Ordinance
(UDO) be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public hearing,
properly noticed, was held on April 12, 2012, before the Board of Aldermen
regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) in this instance Southport’s UDO should
be in alignment with the State of North Carolina Building Code, (ii) this
amendment promotes orderly growth and development in the City, and (iii)
allowance of a lower pool fence height does not hinder the public safety and
general welfare of the community.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance is hereby
approved and adopted.
This 12th day of April, 2012            City of Southport
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard
                        Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Regina W. Alexander, MMC
      Clerk

TEXT AMENDMENT # 12-0229-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With
Respect to Off-Street Parking and Off-Street Loading Requirements
ARTICLE 16.   OFF-STREET PARKING AND OFF-STREET LOADING REQUIREMENTS (revised
12-13-07)
Statement of Present Regulation:
Section 16-3: Minimum Parking Requirements
The following off-street parking space shall be required and maintained:
 
Storage, Self-Service One (1) space for each 225 square feet of gross floor
                      area, plus one (1) space for each employee.
Statement of Amendment Proposed by Staff: 
Section 16-3: Minimum Parking Requirements
The following off-street parking space shall be required and maintained:
 
Storage,     Minimum five (5) spaces or one (1) space for each 100 storage
Self-Service units, whichever is greater, plus one (1) space for each employee
             and two (2) spaces for manager’s quarters, if present.
RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and
to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for the
Southport Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate
revisions, modifications and additions to the City’s land use ordinances; and
WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended that
this proposed amendment to Article 16 of the Unified Development Ordinance
(UDO) be approved; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public hearing,
properly noticed, was held on April 12, 2012, before the Board of Aldermen
regarding this issue; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed amendment to the
Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use
Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) some current parking requirements in the
UDO use an unnecessary amount of impervious surface, (ii) this amendment
promotes orderly growth and development in the City, and (iii) allowance of
parking flexibility in this instance promotes the public safety and general
welfare of the community through protection of natural resources.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
amendment and addition to the Southport Unified Development Ordinance is hereby
approved and adopted.

RESOLUTION APPROVING FINANCING TERMS
   WHEREAS : The City of Southport, North Carolina (the “City”) has previously
determined to undertake a project for one Spartan Aerial Platform Fire Truck
(the “Project”), and the Finance Officer has now presented a proposal for the
financing of such Project.
   BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED, as follows:
   1.   The City hereby determines to finance the Project through Branch
Banking and Trust Company (“BB&T”), in accordance with the proposal dated April
4, 2012. The amount financed shall not exceed $400,000.00, the annual interest
rate (in the absence of default or change in tax status) shall not exceed  1.77
%, and the financing term shall not exceed  five (5)  years from closing.
   2.   All financing contracts and all related documents for the closing of
the financing (the “Financing Documents”) shall be consistent with the
foregoing terms. All officers and employees of the City are hereby authorized
and directed to execute and deliver any Financing Documents, and to take all
such further action as they may consider necessary or desirable, to carry out
the financing of the Project as contemplated by the proposal and this
resolution. The Financing Documents shall include a Financing Agreement and
Deed of Trust and a Project Fund Agreement as BB&T may request.
   3.   The Finance Officer is hereby authorized and directed to hold executed
copies of the Financing Documents until the conditions for the delivery of the
Financing Documents have been completed to such officer’s satisfaction. The
Finance Officer is authorized to approve changes to any Financing Documents
previously signed by City officers or employees, provided that such changes
shall not substantially alter the intent of such documents or certificates from
the intent expressed in the forms executed by such officers. The Financing
Documents shall be in such final forms as the Finance Officer shall approve,
with the Finance Officer’s release of any Financing Document for delivery
constituting conclusive evidence of such officer’s final approve of the
Document’s final form.
   4.   The City shall not take or omit to take any action the taking or
omission of which shall cause its interest payments on this financing to be
includable in the gross income for federal income tax purposes of the
registered owners of the interest payment obligations. The City hereby
designates its obligations to make principal and interest payments under the
Financing Documents as “qualified tax-exempt obligations” for the purpose of
Internal Revenue Code Section 265(b)(3).
   5.   The City intends that the adoption of this resolution will be a
declaration of the City’s official intent to reimburse expenditures for the
project that is to be financed from the proceeds of the BB&T financing
described above. The City intends that funds that have been advanced, or that
may be advanced, from the City’s general fund, or any other City fund related
to the project, for project costs may be reimbursed from the financing
proceeds.
   6.   All prior actions of City officers in furtherance of the purposes of
this resolution are hereby ratified, approved and confirmed. All other
resolutions (or parts thereof) in conflict with this resolution are hereby
repealed, to the extent of the conflict. This resolution shall take effect
immediately.
   Approved this 12th day of April, 2012.      City of Southport
                        /s/ Robert D. Howard
                            Mayor                  
   By: Regina W. Alexander, MMC
       Clerk

RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has for many years supported Brunswick Community
College and its programs; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has allowed the use of city facilities for
various functions and activities, including the Senior Citizens’ Building
located at 209 N. Atlantic Avenue; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick Community College Pottery Studio was located in this City
facility as City records indicate from January 30, 1988 until August 6, 2009;
and
WHEREAS, Brunswick County relocated the Senior Citizens program and the City of
Southport Parks and Recreation offices were moved to this location; and
WHEREAS, since the Pottery Studio did not have a facility, the City allowed
Brunswick Community College to use the Old Fire Station from December 7, 2010
through June 7, 2011 pursuant to an agreement between the City and Brunswick
Community College; and
WHEREAS, Brunswick Community College campus was not completed and the City
extended the offer to the college to let them continue to use the old fire
station with the agreement that the City would provide a 30 day notice if the
building was needed; and
WHEREAS, the pottery class will be relocated to the Brunswick College Campus on
Lord Street upon completion of renovation; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport is in the process of preparing for renovation of
City facilities and has need to relocate the Police Department in the old fire
station;
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Southport Board of Aldermen requests
Brunswick Community College to open a portion of the Lord Street Campus for use
by the Pottery Studio;    
This 12th day of April 2012            /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

APRIL 30, 2012
SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
APRIL 30, 2012    2:00 P.M.
CITY HALL         SOUTHPORT, N. C.
 
PRESENT:   Robert D. Howard, Mayor
      Aldermen Todd Coring, Nelson Adams, Jim Powell, Buddy Barnes and Ken Karn
ABSENT:   Alderman Mary Ellen Poole
STAFF
PRESENT:     Pat Thomas, City Manager
    Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk
      Amy Nelson, City Planner
OTHERS:   Senator Bill Rabon
      Representative Frank Iler
      John Elliott, Representing Progress Energy
      Don Eggert, AICP, Cape Fear Rural Planning Organization
      Karen Fussell, NCDOT Division 3 Engineer
      Jackson Provost, NCDOT Division 3 Construction Engineer
      Gary Lovering, NCDOT Roadway Project Engineer – Eastern Region
      Kevin Moore, NCDOT Roadway Project Design Engineer – Eastern Region
      Jay McInnis, NCDOT – PDEA Project Planning Group Supervisor
      Kim Gillespie, NCDOT – PDEA Project Planning Engineer
   The meeting was called to order at 2:10 p.m. by Mayor Howard. He introduced
Karen Fussell, North Carolina Department of Transportation Division 3 Engineer
and she introduced other staff members. Other attendees were acknowledged by
Mayor Howard.
   The invocation was delivered by Alderman Karn.
   Mayor Howard stated the purpose of the meeting is to open a dialogue with
DOT representatives, Senator Rabon and Representative Iler for consideration in
developing an alternate access road in and around Southport. Mayor Howard
stated the seriousness of the gridlock became evident during DOT highway
construction in March which caused major traffic delays and congestion, which
could have ultimately resulted in an emergency. He explained that a second
access road is critical to Southport and its citizens which could also serve as
an evacuation route while relieving truck traffic off of Jabbertown Road. The
proposed road would connect Leonard Street to Rob Gandy Boulevard over to
Highway 87 & 133, while diverting truck traffic off of Jabbertown Road.
   He explained that City representatives talked with Howard Lee and Cameron
Smith, both property owners near the proposed route. Mr. Lee is willing to sell
property for a right of way at fair market value, while Mr. Smith will grant a
60 ft easement. The City is prepared to assist the State to make this happen.
   Senator Bill Rabon stated that another road is needed but questioned the 60
ft easement. He suggested extending the road to East Moore to get traffic over
to Dosher Cutoff which is designated as an evacuation route. He explained that
the State would need to know costs and future plans. He stated that it would be
prudent to request DOT to perform a feasibility study. He asked about wetlands
in the proposed area as did Representative Iler while expressing environmental
concerns and the impact of the proposed road. Alderman Powell noted that the
area in question is dry land and does not cross wetlands.
    Ms. Fussell also referenced environmental concerns and suggested a
feasibility study be performed. She explained that projects are determined by a
cost ratio analysis and this project may need to be considered for the
Transportation Improvement Plan program (TIP).
   Mr. Don Eggert, of the Cape Fear Rural Planning Organization (COG) told the
Board that a letter was written in October 2005 to former Mayor Norman Holden
in support of an Eastside Connector Road and they supported the City’s request
for DOT to perform a feasibility study on the need for a new connector road,
but he was not aware of the results.
   Mayor Howard reiterated the City’s position, while asking for assurance that
DOT, Senator Rabon and Representative Iler understand the City’s position and
will commit to assisting in the development of this road, realizing that the
City will continue to pursue this project. Senator Rabon mentioned that the
State will be pursuing public-private partnerships for future projects.
   Ms. Fussell suggested the Board adopt a resolution asking DOT for a
Feasibility Study which will begin the initial process to look at preliminary
costs.
   City Manager Thomas stated that he would work with the State and DOT on this
project. Mayor Howard noted that the Resolution would be submitted after the
May 10 meeting.
   Mr. George McCracken of 556 Jabbertown Road asked if the speed limit could
be reduced on Jabbertown Road due to the high volume of traffic i.e. speeding
trucks. Ms. Fussell stated that this was an enforcement issue and speed limits
are established according to percentiles. Alderman Adams voiced concerns about
truck traffic speeding, pot holes in the road and shoulders broken due to the
high volume of traffic and suggested DOT look at this situation.
   Chief Dove stated that this area was not in the corporate city limits and
could not be enforced by the Police Department.
   Ms. Carolyn Hankins, property owner on Jabbertown stated due to the weight
of the trucks and high volume of traffic, it is her belief that homes have been
damaged.
    Ms. Fussell suggested a resolution be submitted to DOT requesting a speed
limit reduction. Mayor Howard noted that this area is not in the City limits
and reiterated that the residents are neighbors and need help.
   Mr. Patrick Connaughton asked about the palm trees in the triangle at the
intersection of Highway 87 and 211 and suggested removal or the trees be
trimmed back for more visibility.
   No further comment, the meeting was adjourned upon motion of Alderman Adams,
seconded by Alderman Barnes. Vote unanimous.

City of Southport
A RESOLUTION REQUESTING NCDOT STUDY OF AN ADDITIONAL ACCESS ROAD INTO THE CITY
OF SOUTHPORT
WHEREAS Department of Transportation construction work at the intersection of
NC 211 and NC 87 during the week of March 19-23, 2012, caused major traffic
delays and congestion and brought to the City's attention in a very forceful
manner the potential public safety hazards that could arise from obstruction of
the sole route of access in and out of Southport; and
WHEREAS obstruction ofthe single highway in and out of Southport (NC 211)
prevents emergency vehicles from providing essential life-saving and property
protection functions in a timely manner, causes major traffic delays and
congestion, and creates serious hardships on citizens and businesses in the
community; and
WHEREAS the Jabbertown Road community adjacent to Southport, an area zoned and
developed for residential use, is also experiencing serious safety concerns
related to high levels of truck traffic (up to 250 tractor trailers daily)
traveling to and from industrial locations; and
WHEREAS these significant threats to public safety can be alleviated by the
development of an alternative access route that bypasses the NC 211/NC 87
intersection;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina:
1. The City respectfully requests that the North Carolina Department of
Transportation undertake a feasibility study, as well as engineering studies,
to determine an appropriate means of constructing an alternative route of
access into Southport that would (a) bypass the NC 211/87 intersection and (b)
provide an alternate route for industrial h·uck traffic that is currently
utilizing SR 1526 (Jabbertown Road);
2. The City requests that the feasibility study and related engineering work be
conducted in an expeditious manner and that the study include careful
consideration of a potential roadway corridor for which the City has received
tentative right-of-way commitments;
3. The City requests that, in the future, any Depmtment of Transportation
construction work along the city's sole route of highway access (a) be preceded
by adequate advance notification to the City and to affected area public safety
agencies, (b) be conducted primarily at night to avoid peak traffic hours, and
(c) be conducted in off-season periods to avoid conflicts with high traffic
levels during the tourist season.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this resolution shall be provided in an expeditious
manner to Senator Bill Rabon, to Representative Frank Iler, to the Department
of Transportation board member for NCDOT Division 3, and to the Division
Engineer for NCDOT Division 3.
Adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen on May 10, 2012.

2. Lighting Adjacent to Dosher Memorial Hospital
City Manager Thomas told the Board that the City was approached by
representatives from Dosher Hospital regarding the four decorative post lights
on Howe Street adjacent to Dosher Hospital. According to research, the lantern
lights were installed by the hospital and electrical power provided by the
City. The overhead power was cut during renovation of the hospital and the line
removed. The hospital has since installed a new yard light over a decorative
light to provide security to a parking and dock area at the southwest comer of
Howe. He presented a sketch showing location of other lights but stated there
is no street light at the intersection of Fodale Avenue and Howe Street. The
hospital requested the City consider re­establishing the agreement under which
the hospital provided the light fixtures and the City supplied the power. The
hospital will pay the cost of installing new underground wiring and lighting
fixtures, if the City supply the power and Brunswick Electric Membership
Corporation estimated the monthly power cost at $3.00 monthly to operate two
lights. Three options were presented for Board consideration:
Options
   o   Advise the hospital that the City has no need for additional lighting in
the area of concern and that any new lighting must be requested by and paid for
by the hospital as yard lights (at a cost of approximately $15 per month each)
   o   Agree to resume the previous arrangement in which the hospital paid for
the installation and the City paid for the power, but place only two taller
decorative fixtures, one in the location of the two closely spaced fixtures and
one near the entrance walkway.
   o   Agree to resume and continue the previous arrangement, installing only
two replacement fixtures, and also place a street light at the intersection of
Howe Street and Fodale Avenue.
Discussion:
Alderman Powell suggested a street light be installed at Howe and Fodale,
possibly located on the same pole when the state installs the traffic signal.
City Manager Thomas stated the design is unknown as to the type of traffic
signal that will be installed, but could be a possibility.
Aldennan Adams stated citizens pay for their own security lights and the same
policy should apply to the hospital.
Alderman Barnes noted that the location is a City sidewalk and complaints have
been registered about the darkness and possible danger. He stated $3 a month is
not unrealistic to pay for the safety of citizens on a public sidewalk.
Alderman Adams moved to adopt Option 1 and to advise the hospital the City does
not have need for additional lighting and any new lighting must be requested
and paid for by the hospital as yard lights at a cost of approximately $15 per
month. Motion seconded by Alderman Karn. Discussion: Alderman Coring asked what
precipitated this discussion and noted the lights between Moore and the
waterfront do not work i.e. the bench area at Waterfront Park is dark. Mr.
Thomas explained that the Hospital Facilities Manager approached the City and
reported of a recent accident. No further discussion, the votes were 5 ayes,
Adams, Kam, Coring, Poole and Powell. 1 no, Alderman Barnes. Motion passed 5-1.
3. Emergency Medical Services Committee Recommendation
Alderman Poole presented the following recommendations from the Emergency
Medical Services Committee comprised of Aldermen Coring, City Manager Thomas,
Chiefs Sage, Dove, Cumbee and Alderman Poole as Chairperson. Alderman Poole
moved that the following recommendation be approved, seconded by Alderman
Coring. The vote of approval was unanimous.
1.   Primary Ambulance Replacement. Appropriate sufficient funds in the FY 13-
14
City budget to replace the old ambulance unit with a new unit, financed over a
five year period so that the squad can continue to meet the significant needs
for emergency medical responses in the Southport area. (Specification, bidding,
and delivery of a unit, which would take place in FY 12-13, will probably take
six to 9 months, and the first payment would likely not be due until 12 months
thereafter.)
2.    Cardiac Monitor. (a) Appropriate funds in the FY 12-13 budget to provide
funding for replacing one cardiac monitor. (b) Also pursue a North Carolina
Department of Insurance OFM grant and/or other grants to help provide funding
in lieu of the city funds.
3.    Other Equipment Replacement. (a) As soon as the first cardiac monitor is
replaced, begin annually placing moneys in a capital reserve fund to help fund
replacement of the second monitor, the second ambulance, and the QRV unit. (b)
Encourage the rescue squad auxiliary to contribute funds derived from the
squad's annual fundraising efforts for the same purpose. (c) Continue to apply
for AFG funding to potentially help with vehicle replacement.
4. Extrication Equipment. Create a small task group - composed of rescue and
fire department members selected by the two chiefs - to explore the feasibility
of transferring the extrication equipment to the fire department at some point
in the foreseeable future. The feasibility study should include required
training for utilization of the equipment, available means of transport,
potential compensation of the rescue squad, and the potential impact on
eligibility for rescue-related grants
5.   Sale of Equipment. Ask the Rescue Squad to explore sale of the 1991
International rescue truck-preferably to another Brunswick County emergency
services unit- in order to raise funds to help with the replacement of the
second ambulance (for which re-chassis should be considered) and the Quick
Response Unit.
6.    Referendum. Rescind the resolution requesting that a tax levy referendum
be conducted in August.
7.    Business Plan. Encourage the squad to continue preparing- and updating
annually its business plan, which has helped identify ways and means or
providing service and has helped improve the squad's degree of self-support.
8.    Grants. Encourage the squad to continue its efforts to pursue appropriate
grant opportunities to help fund essential equipment needs.
9.    Recognition. Identify an appropriate and public means of recognizing the
squad 's members and leadership for the significant progress that the volunteer
squad has made in rebuilding and sustaining an emergency medical service that
responds in a rapid and reliable manner to community needs.
Alderman Powell motioned to rescind the resolution requesting that a tax levy
referendum be conducted in August, seconded by Alderman Kam. Vote unanimous.

XIV.    City Attorney
City Attorney Isenberg explained to the Board that House Bill 848 of the
General Assembly's 1983 session converted all 99 year leases made by the Town
of Smithville into fee simple deeds. The bill recited that an attempt to
convert the leases into fee simple title was first done in 1812-1 813 but that
the commissioners of Smithville continued to issue 99 year leases until 1900
assuming that the 1812-1813 act automatically converted them to fee simple. The
purpose ofthe 1983 bill was to clarify this. He explained in 1983 when the
General Assembly voted the act was approved which the City of Southport
supported.
Mr. Dale McPherson asked if City records were researched showing where the City
supported this action. City Clerk Alexander attested that the records were
researched checked and she did not locate anything on this matter. Attorney
Isenberg noted that there is nothing that can be done at this time because
people rights are vested.
