CITY OF SOUTHPORT FILMING POLICY AND GUIDELINES
A. Statement of Policy
   The City of Southport welcomes and encourages film production activity in
the community, for the purposes of marketing the community, supporting tourism,
attracting investment and employment by the film industry, and providing unique
recreational interest for residents and visitors. The City of Southport
considers itself to be a “filming-friendly community”. However, because filming
often alters normal activities in the community and can involve exceptional or
unusual events and activities, the City has enacted this policy to insure that
filming activity is conducted with adequate notice, with suitable preparations
and protections, and with appropriate consideration for the effects on
residents and businesses in the community. This policy is designed to support
filming, to promote cooperation and collaboration between the City and the film
industry, to balance the needs of filmmakers and of the community, and to
protect the health, safety, and general welfare of residents, businesses, and
property owners in Southport.
B. General Principles and Conditions
The basic principles that this policy sets forth, and which it contemplates
should be observed by both the administrators of the policy and the film
industry, are as follows:
1. Film production companies shall be consistently extended the welcome and
courtesies of a desired business investment.
2. Film companies should remember at all times that they are guests in both
residential and business areas, that their presence in these areas is dependent
on the goodwill of the occupants, and that they should be courteous and
considerate of occupants and property owners.
3. Filming activities shall be accommodated and assisted, whenever reasonable
and within the resources of the City to provide such support.
4. Permit applications and similar requests by film production companies shall
be reviewed and acted upon in a reasonably expeditious manner, taking into
account the City’s resources.
5. Good communication is considered an extremely important factor in
maintaining positive relations between production companies and the community.
Adequate notification shall be provided at all times to persons, businesses,
and organizations affected by filming activities.
6. The scheduling of filming activities should be arranged in a manner, both
with respect to days of the week and times of day, that minimize adverse
effects on residents, businesses, and transportation.
7. If high impact activities (such intensive or extensive filming or special
effects) are likely to significantly affect residents, businesses, or other
entities, film productions shall make timely and reasonable efforts and
arrangements to mitigate these effects for the affected persons, businesses, or
other entities.
8. In order to insure that costs and inconveniences to residents and taxpayers
are appropriately off-set, the City shall be compensated for the use of
resources and facilities required to accommodate filming activity.
9. In order to protect residents and taxpayers from unnecessary liability, film
production companies shall provide insurance and indemnification of the City
against claims of loss arising from filming activity.
10. The name, insignia, logo, and other symbols of the City of Southport shall
be not used in a disrespectful or derogatory manner or without permission at
any time.
11. The laws and regulations of the city, state, and federal government shall
be fully observed at all times by persons engaged in filming activities.
12. Filming activities that require the approval of non-city agencies (such as
the NC Department of Transportation, the NC Division of Coastal Management, the
NC Division of Water Quality, the U.S. Coast Guard, the County of Brunswick, or
others) are solely the responsibility of the film production, and such
permissions – some of which may require significant lead times – should be
sought in a timely manner in order to avoid delays in production.
C. Definitions
The following terms have the meaning indicated, as used in these guidelines:
1. “Film liaison” is the person specifically designated by the city manager for
coordination of filming activities. The film liaison may be a city staff
member, a person hired or contracted by the city for the specific purpose of
coordinating filming activities, or the city manager.
2. “Filming” is film production activity, regardless of the recording media,
including production of feature films, television programs, documentary films,
commercials, instructional or training films, or other commercial film
production activity intended for use in broadcasting to- or viewing by the
public or specific audiences. “Filming”, for purposes of this policy, does not
generally include limited, non-intrusive filming by individuals intended for
purely personal or family viewing in private settings without an admission
charge.
3. “Film productions” are the companies, organizations, owners, or projects
engaged in commercial, governmental, or non-profit filming. For purposes of
these guidelines, “film companies” and “production companies” have the same
meaning as “film productions”.
4. “Intermittent traffic [or pedestrian] control” is limitation of use of
public vehicular or pedestrian routes for brief periods of time, normally not
exceeding five minutes.
5. “Low impact filming” is filming activity with all of the following
characteristics:
(a) Filming that takes place outside of regular business hours in a business
district; and/or
(b) Filming that has a minimal impact on parking, vehicular and pedestrian
traffic, and access to businesses that are open; and/or
(c) Allows uninterrupted flow of pedestrian and vehicular traffic, utilizes no
more than two on-street parking spaces in a block, produces minimal noise and
lighting between 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., does not obstruct passage on
sidewalks or in alleys, and provides off-street areas for all cast crew,
extras, support vehicles, catering, and other support activities.
6. “High impact filming” is filming that has one or more of the following
characteristics:
(a) Involves filming outside of the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.; and/or
(b) Displaces more than a minor amount of parking in a block; and/or
(c) Involves street closures, traffic detours, or alternative routing or flows
of traffic; and/or
(d) Impedes pedestrian access to normal walkway areas or customer access to
businesses; and/or
(e) Involves significant night-time lighting, loud noises, special effects,
fire, pyrotechnics; and/or
(f) Involves intermittent traffic or pedestrian control for a significant
length of time:
(g) Involves extensive set dressing, large numbers of extras, or large base
camps or equipment staging areas; and/or
(h) Involves potentially dangerous stunts, vehicle stunt activity, rolling
roadblocks, or other activities that require significant safety perimeters or
tend to impede traffic flow; and/or
(i) Impedes public access to shopping areas, public parks, or public facilities
that are customarily open to the public.
D. Pre-Production Conferences
A pre-production conference is required between the city film liaison and the
film location manager at least two weeks prior to application for any filming
permits. This conference may also include other city officials, such as the
city manager, police chief, and public services director. The film production
company is also encouraged to include in the conference other representatives,
such as producers or directors, who may help provide a complete and
authoritative description of desired filming activities, locations, and time
periods. The film production is asked to provide, at the time of this
conference, as much information as possible regarding anticipated filming
activities, including a general description of the production, locations,
dates, and any “high impact” or special effects activities. The film liaison
will share and discuss with the production company representative(s) the City’s
filming policy and guidelines and any available information regarding
anticipated community activities, other filming taking place at the same time,
municipal resource issues, or other factors that need to be considered in
planning of film production in Southport. The city manager shall be notified in
advance of all such pre-production conferences, notes of the meeting shall be
kept by the film liaison, and the conference shall be reported to the governing
board by the manager.
E. Filming Permits
1. Applications 
a. Content. A permit is required for any and all filming activity that takes
place within the boundaries of the City of Southport. Permit applications shall
be made in a form approved by the city manager, shall be submitted to the
City’s designated film liaison, and all necessary information shall be
provided, including maps, diagrams, illustrations, or other information
required by the film liaison to adequately explain the content of the
application. All applications shall be complete and legible, and illegible or
incomplete applications will not be accepted. The location manager or other
film production representative is encouraged to review each application with
the film liaison in person upon submission and shall participate, in a timely
manner, in any conferences requested to clarify applications.
b. Separate Applications. A separate film permit application should be
submitted for each filming location for each day of filming, unless the film
liaison elects to accept, for the City’s convenience an application for multi-
day low impact filming in a specific location. Multiple locations will not be
accepted on the same application.
c. Traffic Detours. Production companies who wish to detour traffic within the
City and who request street closures that require that traffic be detoured
shall submit a plan in writing, preferably in map form, no less than 10 days
prior to the proposed re-routing, showing the proposed detours(s) and all
traffic control re-routing measures, including signage, barricades, personnel,
and/or advance publicity planned to effect the necessary detours. The plan is
subject to the approval of the film liaison and the Southport Police
Department, including any required modifications. If the needed detour(s)
involve one or more state-maintained roads, the applicant must submit, prior to
approval of the permit, written evidence that the proposed detour plan has been
approved by the North Carolina Department of Transportation.
d. Rain Dates. Alternative filming dates may be requested for filming that may
be delayed by adverse weather or other unforeseeable circumstances. Requests
for alternative dates should be reasonably limited, however, and should not
include “shotgun” requests that may tend to undermine the permitting process
and to make it difficult for city departments, the public, and/or businesses to
reasonably anticipate the actual scheduling of filming.
2. Licenses
In order to be eligible for the issuance of filming permits, film productions
must possess any privilege license(s) required by the city.
3. Deposits
Prior to the issuance of any filming permit, the film production company is
required to provide a basic assurance of its financial responsibility for fees
that will become due and payable to the City in the form of a cash deposit or
in the form of a letter of credit or performance or security bond, in a form
approved by the City, listing the City of Southport as the payee. The amount of
the deposit or bond shall be approved by the city manager and shall be
represent a preliminary estimate of 50 percent of the amounts expected to be
due to the City – based on the duration of the filming, the estimated extent of
resources and facilities required, and previous experiences with film
production. This deposit may be waived or modified in circumstances involving
minor or limited filming activity. The financial responsibility deposit or bond
will be returned or released after the production company has paid all bills
due to the City in association with the film production, and is not be used by
the film production as a draw-down amount for any such obligations.
4. Insurance and Indemnification.
All film productions are required, prior to the issuance of any filming
permits, to maintain and provide evidence of liability insurance policies, with
the City named as an additional insured, in the following minimum amounts:
General Liability Insurance            $1,000,000 per occurrence; $2,000,000
aggregate
Automobile Liability Insurance         $1,000,000 per occurrence; $2,000,000
aggregate
Workers Compensation and Employer Liability    $1,000,000
In addition, film production companies shall be required, prior to the issuance
of a permit, to execute (by an authorized officer) an agreement to indemnify,
defend, and hold harmless the City and its officers, agents, and employees from
and against all claims, suits, actions, damages, liability, and expenses for
bodily or personal injury, loss of life or property, or other damages arising
from or out of any occurrence associated with the filming activity.
5. Processing and Approvals
a. Review and Issuance. From the date and time at which applications are
complete and all necessary information is available, the City will endeavor to
review and act on low impact filming applications within 48 hours (occurring on
business days) and on high impact filming applications within 72 hours
(occurring on business days) whenever possible. Approved permits may be in the
form requested or may include modifications or conditions considered by the
film liaison to be necessary for compliance with these guidelines and the
protection of the public interest.
b. Conditions. Filming permits may, when issued, include conditions or
requirements designed to clarify the permission being granted and/or to insure
that adequate consideration is given to affected residents, businesses, and/or
organizations in the community. Any requirements included in these guidelines
shall be considered a condition of all permits issued.
c. Comments. Permits are subject to modification if the City receives
significant comments after notification of affected persons. The City will
issue any necessary modifications at least 24 hours in advance whenever
possible.
d. Extended Hours. High impact filming between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00
a.m. shall require that the film production obtain the approval of residents in
the affected areas as follows:
- For extension by one hour, 51 percent approval is required;
- For extension by two hours, 66 percent approval is required;
- For extension for more than two hours or all night, 90 percent approval is
required.
6. Impact Level Determinations. Determinations of filming impact levels will be
made by the film liaison, subject to review by the city manager.
7. Restrictions
The following limitations will, apply, in general, to the issuance of filming
permits:
a. Downtown District. Due to high levels of shopping and tourism activity in
the downtown area, coupled with related traffic and parking issues, filming in
the downtown area should be planned, as much as possible, for Sunday or outside
normal business hours.
b. Holiday Season. Due to the importance of the holiday shopping season, high
impact filming will not normally be allowed in concentrated business areas from
Thanksgiving Day to December 31 without the approval of affected businesses.
c. Sales and Special Events. High impact filming will not normally be allowed
within two blocks of a planned sales event or special community event if the
event is an annual event, if the event has received approval from the city,
and/or if expenses have been incurred prior to application.
d. Location Spacing. A minimum three blocks separation must be maintained
between any two filming locations (including base camp, equipment parking, and
other support activities) that occur on the same date.
e. Multiple Permits. No more than two film permits will normally be issued
within any business district or residential neighborhood for any given date.
f. Location Stress. The City reserves the right to restrict high impact filming
on streets or in neighborhoods, business districts, or parks, which have
experienced significant stress due to heavy filming, seasonal festivals or
events, natural disasters, construction activity, or similar circumstances.
g. Emergencies. In the event of natural or civil disasters or infrastructure
emergencies, the City reserves the right to cancel any and all filming permits
on both public and private properties within the city. If evacuations related
to public safety emergencies require the use of a particular street, area, or
district, all permits for such areas become null and void. Permits vacated for
these reasons will be re-issued as soon as possible after emergency conditions
have ended and appropriate safety evaluations have been conducted.
h. Public Safety and Convenience. The City reserves the right to change,
modify, update, or waive provisions of permits or these guidelines when
necessary for the public safety and/or convenience.
i. Policy Compliance. The City reserves the right to cancel and/or modify
filming permits when necessary to insure adherence to these guidelines or
public laws or ordinances.
8. Permit Limitations, Revocations, and Penalties
Film production companies shall limit the activities at each location to those
described in the filming permit. Failure of the production company to comply
with the terms and conditions of a permit, failure to comply with the
requirements in these guidelines, conducting filming activity without a permit,
and/or violation of public laws and ordinances may result in the immediate
revocation of a permit and/or penalty fees of up to $200 per hour or $1,000 per
day, as determined by the city manager. Such penalties may be deducted from the
film production’s deposit.
F. Notifications
1. General. Adequate communication and notification is an essential factor in
maintaining positive relations between film productions and the community.
Adequate notification shall be provided at all times to persons, businesses,
and organizations affected by filming activities.
2. Responsibility. The film production is entirely responsible for notifying,
in a timely and complete manner and in a form considered satisfactory by the
City, all residents and businesses affected by filming activity.
3. Notification Form and Content. Filming notifications shall be in writing and
shall include sufficient information to allow residents and businesses who may
not be familiar with filming activity to understand, in layman’s terms, the
days, hours, nature, and full extent of the filming activity, including any
impacts on access to properties, on use of streets and pedestrian ways, and on
normal and peaceful use of properties. Notifications shall also include any
significant conditions that have been issued in association with the permit.
The City reserves the right to determine whether the content of such
notifications adequately communicates to affected residents and businesses the
nature and extent of the planned filming activity and to require that the
notification include the filming permit and the full content of any related
conditions if it considers this additional information to be advisable.
Notifications shall include the name, telephone, and e-mail contact information
for at least two representatives of the film production (including the location
manager) and the name and contact information for the city film liaison.
4. Timing of Notifications. Notifications of affected areas shall take place
after the City’s review and approval of each permit and shall be made no less
than three business days prior to any filming activity. Earlier notification
may be required, in the discretion of the film liaison, in instances involving
business districts or certain high impact filming. Notification periods may be
reduced in some instances of low impact filming if the film liaison determines
that significant advance notification is not warranted.
5. Area of Notification. The area of notification (affected areas) may vary
based on the level (impact) of filming activity, but should include an area at
least one block in every direction from the filming activity. High impact
filming activity may require notification of a significant larger area,
especially if significant traffic controls, high levels of noise, special
effects, or lighting, or other major impacts will be associated with the
filming activity. Determinations with regard to “affected areas” will be made
by the film liaison, in consultation with the city manager.
6. Re-Notifications. If the schedule and/or nature of filming activity changes
after a permit has been issued and notifications have been distributed, the
film liaison may, in his or her discretion, require that re-notifications be
made to the affected area. The film liaison may also require re-notifications
if a determination is made that the initial notification was improperly made or
insufficient with respect to content.
7. Notification Documentation. In addition to other notification requirements
listed above, high impact filming requires that film productions obtain proof
of notification, in the form of signatures and legible names from affected
residents and/or businesses. Proof of notifications must be provided to the
film liaison at least 24 hours in advance of the filming activity, and failure
to provide notification shall be grounds for revocation of a filming permit.
The film liaison shall be notified if occupants could not be reached, including
the dates and times (normally at least two) when notifications were attempted.
The film liaison may waive the documentation requirement in instances when
occupants could not be reached after reasonable attempts, but notification
shall be left at the property in every instance.
8. Community Meetings. Film productions are encouraged, in order to foster
understanding and promote good community relations, to provide one or more
opportunities, prior to- or early in the production, for residents and
businesses to attend an announced meeting, learn about the upcoming film
activity, and meet representatives of the production (and actors, if
available). Film productions are also encouraged to utilize public meetings to
help the community or specific areas understand the nature and extent of
planned high impact filming activity. In certain instances of major impacts on
businesses or residential neighborhoods, the film liaison may require that a
meeting opportunity be provided, prior to filming activity, for residents or
businesses to ask questions of film production representatives and offer
comments about proposed filming activity.
9. Extended Hours Notifications. As noted in the Filming Permits section,
special conditions apply to high impact filming between the hours of 11:00 p.m.
and 7:00 a.m. If the consent thresholds are met for extended hours filming,
this information (including the level of consent obtained) shall be conveyed to
affected residents, either within the regular notification or by separate
notification.
10. Reservation of Rights. The City reserves the right to deny or revoke
permits when insufficient time has been allowed for proper notification or when
the notification process has been improperly or insufficiently carried out.
G. General Filming Requirements
The following guidelines apply to filming in all areas of the city, unless
limited by reference to specific areas.
1. Base Camp Placement. Whenever possible, base camps and dressing room
trailers should be parked away from nearby residences and noise from
generators, engines, doors, and other sources should be limited in the hours
between 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Base camps shall be located in areas zoned for
commercial use whenever possible.
2. Equipment Placement. Equipment and support vehicles that are not in
immediate use shall be parked or stored in areas that do not interfere with
pedestrians or vehicular traffic and shall not utilize more than 50% of on-
street parking in blocks where residents necessarily and customarily depend on
on-street parking. Any exceptions must be approved by the film liaison and will
normally require consent of the affected residents.
3. Access Protection. Production vehicles and equipment must not block fire
hydrants, driveways, or other access routes or ramps unless specifically
authorized by the City and/or property owner. Ten feet of clearance should be
left on each side of driveways, unless otherwise specifically authorized.
4. Sight Distances and Parking. Production vehicles and equipment must be
parked or placed in a manner that does not impede safe lines of vision at
intersections and must comply with all city ordinances regarding on-street
parking. Any exceptions must be approved by the Police Department and will
require the presence of one or more law enforcement officers to help maintain
safe traffic movement.
5. Private Property. Filming activity, production equipment placement, and/or
production staging shall not take place on private property without the consent
of property owner(s).
6. Lighting. Lighting for filming, both during day and night hours, should be
oriented away from residences whenever possible and should not be directed in a
manner that interferes with the safe movements of vehicular or boat traffic.
7. Moving and Transition. Production companies are responsible entering and
vacating filming locations with as little noise and disruption as possible at
the beginning and end of each shooting day. Base camps and equipment trucks
moving into residential areas shall not do so before 6:00 a.m. or after 11:00
p.m. without special permission from the film liaison.
8. Waste Collection. Production companies that are being allowed to hold
traffic on streets that are scheduled for solid waste or recycling collection
shall either (a) allow collection trucks access to those areas for normal
pickup or (b) relocate all waste and recycling containers that have been placed
out for collection in an accessible location for collection trucks and return
all containers to their correct locations following pickup. If access to such
containers is inappropriately impeded, the production company will be
responsible for the prompt collection and proper disposal of the solid waste
and recycling materials that could not be collected.
9. Right-of-Way Use. Occupants and property owners may not charge production
companies for the use of public rights-of-way, nor prohibit the use of such
right-of-way without the concurrence of the city. A film permit that authorizes
the use of a specific right-of-way area shall constitute a temporary license
for the use of that area.
10. Clean-Up and Restoration. Unless permission has been granted for continuing
use, production companies shall clean and restore site locations on public
property to their original condition at the end of each shooting day.
Production companies are responsible for returning any public rights-of-way or
public property used for filming, base camp, or other support purposes to their
original condition promptly after use and for satisfactorily repairing any
damage to grass, foliage, pavement, or other public property or improvements.
All sets and related materials shall be removed within seven days after the
conclusion of filming; if sets and other materials are not removed within seven
days, the City may remove same, and the film production shall be responsible
for the costs of such removal.
11. Noise and Fumes. Production companies should make a conscientious effort at
all times to limit and control noise and fumes from generators, engines, and
other equipment, particularly when located in close proximity to residences,
parks, or outdoor facilities open to the public. Film productions may be asked
to relocate equipment that creates nuisance conditions for nearby residents.
Unless specifically incorporated in a film permit, film productions are
separately responsible for compliance with city noise ordinance requirements.
12. Traffic Control 
a. Approvals. Approval must be obtained from the City (and, if applicable,
NCDOT) at least three business days prior to any film activity that will
disrupt the normal flow of traffic, including both full street closures and
intermittent traffic control. Requests and approvals will be coordinated by the
film liaison as part of the film permit process, and, for traffic control
requests, requires the approval of the Southport Police Department.
Interruption of traffic on State-maintained streets also requires approval of
the North Carolina Department of Transportation, which must be obtained by the
production company and provided to the City at the time of application.
b. Street Closures and Detours. Street closures during normal business hours in
business districts are strongly discouraged. Production companies are
encouraged, instead, to schedule filming in such areas outside business hours
or on Sundays whenever possible. When street closures are approved, property
owners and occupants shall be allowed reasonable access to and from their
properties. Production companies that wish to close streets and/or detour
traffic within the city must submit a plan at least 10 working days in advance
to the film liaison, with copies to the Police Department and, if applicable,
NCDOT. The City (and NCDOT if applicable) must approve the plans for alternate
routing of traffic, informational and directional signage, and law enforcement
personnel needed to appropriately divert and route traffic. Production
companies are advised that adequate provision for movement of truck traffic to
and from local industries is important and that the alternatives to use of NC
211 and NC 87 for routing of this traffic are very limited.
c. Rush Hours. Holding of traffic on primary thoroughfares will not normally be
permitted during morning or afternoon “rush” hours or on streets significantly
affected by school traffic during school opening and closing hours.
d. Intermittent Traffic Control. Intermittent holding of traffic shall not
normally exceed three minute intervals and shall not exceed five minute
intervals except when specifically approved by permit.
e. Control and Direction of Traffic. Any filming activity that involves the
holding, delaying, or re-routing of traffic must be accompanied by an
appropriate number of law enforcement personnel, which shall be determined by
the police chief or his designee. All traffic control must be handled by off-
duty city police officers, scheduled through the Police Department and paid
directly by the production company. The police chief may also approve, at his
or her discretion, the use law enforcement officers from other jurisdictions if
an insufficient number of off-duty Southport police officers are available. The
Police Department may approve and establish special traffic flow or direction
measures if necessary to accommodate permitted filming activity, provide access
to properties for the convenience of occupants or owners, and/or to protect
public safety. Except when street areas are closed or special traffic control
measures are approved, production companies and their personnel and contractors
shall comply, at all times, with traffic laws and ordinances.
13. Public Facility Protection. The City reserves the right to require the
presence of a police officer or officers at any filming activity that takes
place on or near public parks or other public properties, in order to provide
security for public facilities and in order to protect the public.
14. Use of Alleys and Fire Lanes. No parking or placement of production
vehicles or equipment of any kind shall take place in alleys, fire lanes, or
other fire response access areas without written permission from the Southport
Fire Department, the film liaison, and the consent of any affected property
owners.
15. Building and Electrical Safety. The film production company shall obtain
all required permits for the construction of structures and for the
installation and use of electrical facilities. Each separate location that
utilizes electrical generation equipment, cabling, or other significant
electrical equipment shall be inspected by a city electrical code inspector and
appropriate fees for such inspections shall be paid by the production company.
16. Pyrotechnics, Explosives, Fires. Film activities that involve the use of
explosives, pyrotechnics, fire, smoke, or similar special effects require
specific approval by the Southport Fire Department, and the fire department may
require such measures that it considers necessary to protect persons and
properties from any potential hazards associated with such activities. Any use
of explosives, pyrotechnics activity, or burning shall require that any film
production personnel involved in such activities provide evidence of any
required certification and/or training to undertake such activities and shall
require that any local or state laws or regulations governing such activities
must be observed. The City will advise the film production company any
requirements of which the film liaison may be aware, but the production company
has primary responsibility for compliance, and the City’s approval of a film
permit does not indicate or imply any determination of compliance with the laws
or regulations of non-city governments or agencies.
17. Protection of Resources. Film productions should endeavor at all times to
insure that water, soil, air, plants, and other natural resources are protected
from damage, particularly in areas where dirt, sod, or hazardous materials are
used in close proximity to environmentally sensitive areas. Removal, damage, or
alteration of vegetation on public property or public rights-of-way is
prohibited unless specific permission is granted in writing by the city manager
or his designee. Any permits required by state or federal resource protection
agencies are the responsibility of the film production. The City will advise
the film production company regarding any such permits or regulations of which
the film liaison may be aware, but assumes no responsibility for such
notifications, and any permits issued by the City do not indicate or imply
compliance with the laws and regulations of non-city governments or agencies.
18. Use of City Name or Symbols. The name, insignia, logo, and other symbols of
the City of Southport shall be not used in the film production or in marketing
for the production without written permission, following appropriate reviews of
script information and the approval of the Board of Aldermen.
19. Location Manager Availability. The film production location manager shall
provide the film liaison with a means of immediate contact (such as a cell
phone or pager number) for the location manager and at least one additional
location representative throughout the duration of the production.
20. Releases and Agreements. Any releases by- or agreements of the City
requested by the film production shall be reviewed by the city attorney prior
to execution by any city official, and the legal costs of such reviews shall be
borne by the film production. The city manager is the only person authorized to
execute releases or agreements.
H. Filming Fees
A. Fee Schedule. The following fees are hereby established for various services
and privileges associated with filming in Southport. Partial days shall
normally be considered full days for purposes of billing. If services are
requested for which a fee has not been established, fees for such services
shall be determined by the city manager based on the cost of time, equipment,
and material. The City reserves the right to require that film productions
acquire certain personnel, equipment, or materials from a non-municipal source
if such resources are not readily available or are needed to carry out other
municipal functions.
[Schedule of Fees – see separate chart]
B. Billings. Unless otherwise delegated by the city manager, recordkeeping of
billable services and privileges and the preparation of billings shall be the
responsibility of the film liaison. Interpretations of billable fees shall be
made by the film liaison, subject to review by the city manager. Billings shall
be prepared and issued, through the City finance department, at least monthly
and shall be payable within 30 days of issuance. Any billings that are not paid
within 30 days shall be subject to a late charge of five percent per month.
I. Reports. The film liaison shall provide regular reports to the city manager
about anticipated filming activity, in order that the Board of Aldermen (and,
if necessary, the general public) may be kept aware of upcoming filming
activity.
J. Policy Review. This policy shall be reviewed at least every three years
following its adoption.
C) Cemeteries Care Study
   Mayor Howard stated the Board discussed in previous work sessions the
establishment of a foundation for perpetual care of cemeteries. Alderman Poole
provided information to the Board for review.
   Alderman Barnes moved, seconded by Alderman Powell to establish a Study
Committee to review cemetery issues for perpetual care and funding, and the
Committee will report to the Board. Discussion: Alderman Coring noted that all
plots with the exception of nine have been sold in Northwood Cemetery and
questioned the long-term goal of care and maintenance funding. He asked if the
City was trying to avoid funding money for the care of cemeteries for which
people have already paid. Mayor Howard noted that the City is not obligated to
fund anything; however, the City has maintained the cemeteries with the help of
volunteers. The purpose is to establish stability for the operation and
maintenance of the cemeteries and provide a vehicle where this could be done by
having a perpetual care trust fund, endowment or other legal means where funds
can be contributed voluntarily, that would insure that care is given to the
cemeteries. Alderman Powell noted that all monies are now being placed in the
general fund, and the Board is trying to establish the means where monies will
be earmarked for care and maintenance of cemeteries. No further discussion, the
vote of approval was unanimous. Motion passed.
    Mayor Howard asked the Board for recommendations and encouraged civic
organizations and the public to participate.

E) Building Improvements Committee Report
   Alderman Powell reported that the Building Improvements Committee discussed
several options when the City begun the process of exploring City building
renovations. It was decided not to tear down the Code Enforcement Building
because of the need for public restrooms. The City Manager located the building
at 1029 North Howe Street, which is located on seven-tenths (7/10) of an acre
and the parking lot will hold 30 cars. He stated when discussion occurred about
the building and its availability, a new vision was formed to centralize City
government. The building is located near the center of town, with hopes in the
future to acquire the entire block for a government center. The City began
negotiations to acquire the 1029 building including closing date, then the 300
building became available. The Committee wanted to be fair and put off
purchasing the 1029 building before the end of the year in order to look at the
300 building. He stated according to the county tax records, the 1029 building
is 10,000 square feet and the 300 building is 8100 square feet. The 300
building sits on seventeen- hundredths of an acre and has only 10-12 parking
spaces with no room to grow. The street right of way on 11th street is sixty-
six feet (66 feet) wide and some of this could be turned in to parking spaces.
The Building Improvements Committee hired an architect and structural engineer
to check out the building and the report was excellent. With the vision to
centralize government, the Committee voted 2-1 to recommend the purchase of the
1029 North Howe Street building.
   Alderman Karn stated that he looked at both buildings including cost
breakdown. The difference in the cost between the two buildings is a savings of
$419,000 if the City selects the 300 Howe option, but it does not meet the
needs of the City. Acquiring the facility will not place all departments under
one roof and it may end up costing the City more if one department is left at
the current City Hall with major upgrades needed. The 1029 building is
sufficient to place all departments under one roof, more cost effective, and is
the best use of City resources.
   Mayor Howard answered a question posed by Alderman Barnes stating that
$75,000 was included in the financial analysis to upgrade the Police Department
depending on which option the Board selected.
   Alderman Poole stated that she weighed various scenarios realizing the Board
must be prudent. She stated that the best use of space is to acquire the 300
North Howe Street building that will allow three departments to move and
upgrade services. She stated that she is not sure whether the City needs to
plan for growth since Southport is a finite number of people with finite
services. Acknowledging that Southport recently received the second place award
for best downtown area in the State; it is important that facilities remain
downtown. Citizens want the City to maintain the current City Hall. If the City
purchases the 300 building, then it will have money to refurbish City Hall. She
asked the Board to consider purchasing 300 North Howe. (Security Building)
   Alderman Adams stated he favored the 1029 North Howe Street Building and the
Board was solidified in this decision with financing from the sale of the
property on West West Street. If the Board pays less and departments remain
fragmented, it defeats the purpose of what is trying to be achieved by placing
all departments under one roof. He stated that the 1029 building is sufficient
to house all departments and has sufficient parking and he supports this
option.
   Alderman Coring stated the City has done its due diligence. The City keeps
moving farther North as a result of annexation. Ten twenty-nine (1029) North
Howe is more centralized for all citizens and it will meet the needs of the
City including parking. He looked at the 300 Building, but believes the City
needs to plan for growth and not gridlock itself. He prefaced his remarks by
stating the Police Department is about community and public service.
   Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Karn to deny the contract on
the 300 North Howe Street Building (SSB) and to move forward to exercise the
contract for purchasing the 1029 North Howe Street Building.   Discussion:
Alderman Poole asked Mayor Howard for his view because of his knowledge and
experience with commercial real estate. Mayor Howard stated that both buildings
were good options, but he looked at the feasibility and need to operate both
buildings. He stated that City Hall and the 300 building would essentially use
the same amount of square footage to accommodate City departments. Due to the
furniture and updated telephone system, significant value has been added to the
300 building. The City will have to buy furniture for the 1029 building and a
new telephone system. While both facilities provide for availability and
utilization, the 300 building will enhance the downtown municipal complex. He
explained, regardless of which building is acquired, not all of City government
will be under one roof. He stated that the current City Hall needs to have a
viable use and whatever department remains will not be disadvantaged with
quality of space. Acquisition of the 300 building ($420,000) will equate to 20%
savings in taxpayers’ dollars, with approximate 6.45 per $100 evaluation
assessment in ad valorem taxes. Ten twenty-nine (1029) North Howe will cost per
square feet including furniture $184, and the 300 building $137.50. A vault
exists in the 300 building and one will have to be constructed in the 1029
building. He stated most importantly is the viable use of City Hall. He
explained that when it came to the public’s knowledge that the City was looking
to purchase a building rather than build one, he was told that the Security
Savings Building was available. When contacted, he presented the option to the
Building Improvements Committee for consideration. Upon review of the options,
he favored the 300 Building which he deemed would be in the best interest of
the taxpayers. In conclusion, Mayor Howard stated whatever building is
selected, the Board will move forward and continue to work together.
       Discussion: Alderman Barnes asked if the space analysis study performed
by John Sawyer Architect proposed options for location of City Hall. Mayor
Howard stated that one of the options suggested was to construct a new public
services building further north. Alderman Powell called for the vote on the
motion. The votes were 4 ayes, Powell, Coring, Adams and Karn. 2 no votes,
Aldermen Barnes and Poole . Motion passed 4-2 in favor of the 1029 building.
IX.   Other Business
   1) Audit Contract Amendment
   City Manager Thomas stated that the City auditors need additional time to
complete the audit because documentation from City staff was not completed. The
Local Government Commission requires that the contract be amended when
additional time is required.
   Alderman Karn moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to approve the Audit
Contract Amendment, authorizing Mayor Howard to execute it. Vote unanimous.
(Copy of Contract Amendment Incorporated As Attachment #2)
   2) City Dock Lease
   Mayor Howard reported that Mr. Ivey Gaskell’s boat had been docked at the
Yacht Basin 20 plus years. The lease was in Son McKeithan’s name but they
shared the dock. Mr. McKeithan no longer has a boat at the City dock and he was
in the process of transferring the lease to Mr. Gaskell, which was not complete
before the passage of new city regulations. He was contacted about this matter
and referred it to Alderman Barnes, Chair of the Rate Review Committee for
investigation.
   Alderman Barnes stated it was not the intention of the Committee to make
anyone leave the boat dock. He stated the way the City’s ordinance is written,
the contract is in Mr. McKeithan’s name and if he gives it up, then Mr. Gaskell
would have to apply for a boat slip which would place him at the bottom of the
waiting list. He does not believe that this is fair to Mr. Gaskell, who is part
of the nautical history of Southport and has been for years. He has used his
own resources to work on the dock and slip at his own expense. Alderman Barnes
motioned, seconded by Alderman Poole to direct the City Manager to transfer the
lease from Son McKeithan’s name to Mr. Ivey Gaskell. Discussion: Alderman Poole
stated that Mr. Gaskell is the defacto leasee because he has been paying a
portion of the rent for years. Alderman Coring stated that he previously
requested a list of the slip owners and this is an example of what can happen
when decisions are rushed. The vote of approval was unanimous. Motion passed.
X.   City Manager Comments
   None
XI.   Board Comments
   Alderman Karn stated he does not believe the Board intends to abandon the
City Hall building regardless of the vote on acquiring another building. If the
project proceeds as outlined, the citizens will decide on what happens to City
Hall. Both options include expenditures to stabilize City Hall.     Alderman
Coring reiterated that the City has no plans to demolish or abandon City Hall.
    Alderman Powell stated in 30-60 days, Mayor Howard will appoint a Citizens’
Committee to look at options and plans for City Hall.
XII.   Adjournment – 7:50 p.m.
   No further business, meeting adjourned upon motion of Alderman Barnes,
seconded by Alderman Poole. Vote unanimous.

staff and those involved in the refurbishment of the tennis courts at Fort
Johnston.

drove into the river at the foot of Bay Street.
III.   Purpose of Meeting
   Mayor Howard stated the purpose of the meeting is to proceed with the
legalities for closing on the property at 1029 North Howe Street, which will
require Board approval.
   Mayor Howard cited the terms of the Novant lease payout with Novant agreeing
to pay 50% of the remaining rent in consideration of the early termination of
its lease. The Board agreed to the terms of the termination of Novant’s lease.
Attorney Isenberg stated that he is waiting on the estopple certificate and
termination agreement, however; the Board may wish to extend the term of the
purchase contract, but all paper work is in order. Alderman Barnes, moved,
seconded by Alderman Karn to extend the due diligence date until February 14,
2013, and the closing date to February 21, 2013, and to accept Novant’s offer
of early termination. Vote unanimous.
   City Manager Thomas reported that Wells Fargo lease ends in 2016, but they
have the option for two five-year renewals. The total due on the initial lease
is $327,478, which includes maintenance fees of $40,958. Wells Fargo offered to
terminate its lease early without any money. Mr. Thomas explained that the City
would get at least $70,000+ per year in rent from Wells Fargo, which would be a
benefit to the City with this additional revenue.
   Alderman Powell motioned, seconded by Alderman Barnes to move forward with
due diligence and continue with the closing up to February 21, and to decline
the Wells Fargo offer to terminate their lease without compensation to the
City. The vote was unanimous.
   Mayor Howard announced that the City is near to closing on the 1029 North
Howe Street Building. Surveys, paperwork and due diligence have been completed.
Upon closing, the downstairs portion of the building is clear. When the closing
is completed, some office relocations will begin after repairs and retrofitting
the building for occupancy. City Manager Thomas will decide where offices will
be located on the first floor.
   The Board agreed to hold a budget goals workshop January 31, 6:00 p.m.
   Alderman Barnes communicated that the Tourism Department sold 300 tickets
for the Safe Haven Premiere, February 14.

   Mr. Fred Guerrina, 710 Dale Avenue, encouraged the Board when considering

before making changes.

bins, making the decision to relocate all departments in the current City Hall
and asked that good judgment continue to prevail when making decisions about
what is placed on the Fort Johnston garrison lawn, while continuing to make
Southport a safe haven for everyone.
   Mrs. Shirley Wilson, 502 Brunswick Street, thanked Cindy Brochure, Tourism
Director and the City for the events planned around the release of Safe Haven,
with excellent publicity for the City. She asked the Board to consider a film
policy because an ordinance can be too restrictive, complicate the overall film
production process, and deter film companies from wanting to film in Southport.
   Mr. Paul Genovese asked the Board to insure that a surety bond or deposit is
posted prior to film companies receiving a permit to film in Southport. He
discussed policy vs. ordinance. An ordinance, which is law, allows the Board to
make decisions rather than negotiate policies. He encouraged the City to
consider its citizens and give then the same consideration as film companies.
   Mr. Johnny Griffin, representing the Wilmington Regional Film Commission,
stated his job is to recruit the film industry to 11 counties in southeastern
N.C. along with the State of North Carolina. Last year the film industry spent
$230 million in Southeastern North Carolina, which was an economic boost to the
economy. He asked that whatever document is adopted, that it has flexibility
and allows individuals from the film industry and the City to be able to
negotiate due to the nature of the movie business.
   Ms. Nancy Clookie told the Board that she worked in the film industry for
many years and is now in retail. She stated that she is not promoting change
and whatever decision is made, that it be made with flexibility due to the many
changes that are made in a moment’s notice during filming. Safe Haven brought
in wonderful, polite people, it was a boom to the retail businesses, and she
encouraged the Board to be mindful of this.
   Mrs. Carol Baker, owner of Waterfront Gifts, stated that she has been
overwhelmed with positive comments about the filming and the people. The City
has an ordinance in place, which is a good guideline, although it may require a
few changes. She stated that the City has efficient and qualified staff to
negotiate and make decisions. She encouraged the Board to do whatever it can to
encourage filming in Southport and everyone will benefit.
   Mr. Sandy Mitchell, 513 North Atlantic, stated he read the new proposed
guidelines and they are okay with him. He has been involved with the movies on
different occasions. However, he was disturbed because of the fireworks with
Safe Haven. He does not care for the provision in the guidelines under 5(d)
extended hours where a percentage of the neighbors can vote to allow extended
hours for filming. This should be changed to 100%. If not, it appears that the
sanctity of his home is being sold if the new guidelines are adopted as
written.
   Toby Bronstein of Caswell Beach noted that Safe Haven filmmakers estimated
to have spent between $15 and $20 million in Southeastern, N.C. Southport had
an advantage because the book was set here. However, it is her belief that this
will not happen again and Southport must not allow the temporary inconvenience
of a few to outweigh the benefits to many. She asked that the Board consider
not ruling by ordinance and choose to embrace the guidelines that will welcome
future film production. She encouraged accommodating the production companies
and creating an environment where Hollywood and Southport can both prosper.
   Michael Rice of 2012 Bonner Bussells, stated his position is that the
proposed guidelines should be adopted which are modeled after Wilmington and is
film friendly. He cited revenues generated by the filming of Safe Haven and the
number of visitors that will come to the City. Because of the movie, this could
raise real estate taxes in Southeastern, NC and the City must create a film
friendly environment. Competition for film projects is intense in State and
out. Southport will be in competition with other areas for film projects and
must be on even terms with other localities. He encouraged adoption of the film
guidelines because of the flexibility. In closing, he stated the essence of
Southport is hospitality, which should be extended to the film industry and
encouraged adoption of the proposed film guidelines

on five areas of cost.

   A. Public comments from Southport citizens on the proposed Film Policy
   Mr. Woody Wilson of 502 West Brunswick Street stated that he went through
the entire filming process of Safe Haven and he is part of the 96% that enjoyed
the filming, and has no problem with the film industry coming back to
Southport. He encouraged the Board not to restrict the ability of the movie
industry to film in Southport while protecting the rights of the citizens. The
City has a City Manager and Tourism Director that can work with the film
industry without having an ordinance where the Aldermen will need to meet to
make a decision. He concluded by encouraging the Board to let staff manage the
day-to-day business.
   Mr. Chris Schnell of 422 West Brunswick Street stated that he and his wife
welcomed the film industry with southern hospitality. The only thing that he
asked in return was respect and consideration of their rights to enjoy their
home in peace. He stated that consideration was given during the filming of
Safe Have with the exception of fireworks going off 200 yards from their front
door five nights, which interrupted their sleep. He told the Board that nobody
from the film industry discussed any aspect of the filming with him or his
wife. He further communicated that the existing film ordinance has been in
place since 1997, and he sees no need to change the ordinance because there is
not a mandate to repeal the existing ordinance. All city ordinances and
policies are in place to protect the rights of the citizens and he asked that
the Noise Ordinance be enforced. He reiterated that they are proud citizens of
Southport and are in support of the film industry filming in the city. He
encouraged the Board when casting their vote, to place the well-being and
protecting the rights of the citizens first, and to consider retaining what has
worked well for the past sixteen years.
   Mayor Howard told citizens that the Board has received all their comments,
i.e. e-mails, and letters that will be considered when making a decision.
   B. Cannon Placement Request – Fort Johnston Property
   Retired General Don Parker, a member of the Foot Soldiers of Fort Johnston
gave a power point presentation on the proposed placement of a Civil War 10-
inch Columbiad replica cannon on Fort Johnston. In the presentation, it was
noted that Fort Johnston is an historic icon that defines the earliest origins
of the City, but there is no recognizable symbol on the grounds of its historic
past. It was proposed that their non-profit organization acquire non-firing
cannon like those at the Fort during the Civil War period. They will work with
the City, local and regional historical organizations, as well as State
entities in facilitating the long-term enhancement, presentation and
interpretation of the site in a holistic manner.
   Alderman Karn, Chair of the Fort Johnston Committee, stated he and Alderman
Barnes looked at the proposal and was favorably impressed. He received staff
feedback, but no public input. It was realized that there was no master plan
for Fort Johnston, which posed some questions of where the cannon would be
placed. They proposed to wait for a master plan, but since the proposal has
been presented to the Board, it does not have to be brought back to the
committee and stated that it is a good idea.
      City Manager Thomas stated under City policy regarding installations on
Fort Johnston property, it states that there will be a first reading on any
proposed installation. The proposed use is to be provided, described, and/or
illustrated in detail and in written form at a regular meeting. The
presentation and description shall constitute the first reading of the proposed
use. If the Board agrees by majority vote, upon first reading, that it desires
to consider the proposed use, then the proposed use shall be sent to any
appropriate agencies – including the State Historic Preservation Office for
review and comment. After comments, second reading for public comments, and
third reading for Board approval.
      City Manager Thomas posed the following questions to General Parker and
they were answered accordingly:
·   Type of cannon is 10” Columbiad replica
·   Cannon would be mounted on 10x10 brick foundation with cannon on wooden
carriage
·   Proposed site preferred is center because best enhancement
·   Site preparation would require excavation of a 10 ft. footprint that will
be 3 ¾ inches deep, which would take place within the six-inch limitation of
fill dirt (Reference letter from Stephen R. Claggett, State Archaeologist)
·   No cost to the City, monies will be raised.
      Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Poole that the presentation
constitutes the first reading and direct staff to prepare for a Public Hearing.
Vote unanimous.
      Mayor asked the City Manager to provide his recommendation.
      C) Use of City Hall - Filming “Under the Dome”
      City Manager Thomas told the Board that the Location Manager, Brooke
Barnhill for CBS-TV series “Under the Dome,” has expressed an interest in the
potential use of City Hall in the production, and wanted to know:
·   If the inside and outside of the City Hall, including the Board Chambers
can be used for filming?
·   Can the Board Chambers and/or the exterior of the City Hall be painted?
·   If the Board Chambers can be used, can the pews be removed and replaced
with chairs for purposes of filming?

reasonable filming inside most areas of City Hall, with the exception of the
north end (Finance and Police areas). However, the City Facilities Policy
adopted by the Board September 24, 2012 indicated that the Board Chambers is
not available for rental.

benefit the City, including charges. City Manager Thomas stated that charges
would be comparable to other areas, and the potential benefits could be the
painting of City Hall, which may be to the Board’s liking and a possibility
that the chairs may be left. Alderman Powell concurred with Alderman Karn,
having a new paint job with a leaking roof is not prudent, asking if the City
may be able to negotiate for a new roof. City Manager Thomas stated the user
fees could be applied for that purpose. No further discussion, the vote of
approval was unanimous.

BUDGET AMENDMENT #8 FISCAL 2012-2013
NORTH HOWE STREET BUILDING OPERATIONS FUND
   WHEREAS the City of Southport has purchased property at 1029 North Howe
Street for the purpose of serving current and future building space needs for
municipal operations; and
   WHEREAS the property will be occupied, for the foreseeable future, both

   Film Issue –Mayor Howard affirmed the Board’s support of the film industry
and other events that are staged in Southport, while insuring the safety and
concerns of the citizens without unnecessary interruptions to their daily
lives. He alluded to the frustration and misleading information that has been
circulated, while acknowledging that it was the intent per Board minutes of
August 2, 2012 to review and tweak the existing ordinance as needed in
accordance with the annual review that is required. He did not anticipate
repealing the existing ordinance but was aware that the Committee was working
along those lines. The current ordinance was adopted in 1997 and some of the
same issues emerged by some of those who have expressed concerns now. In light
of the rising controversy, which he stated promulgates dissatisfaction
regardless of the position the Board may take, he asked the Board to consider
keeping the existing ordinance by reaffirming its existence, rather than
adopting a document that has not been tried. He stated since 1997, many films
have been shot in Southport and the ordinance has never been an issue and he
does not see it as an issue now, but the matter needs to be resolved while
appreciating the work of the Committee.
   Alderman Powell motioned to reaffirm the existing film ordinance and that it
be reviewed annually, seconded by Alderman Poole. Discussion: Alderman Karn
stated the object is to regulate, not restrict which can be done by ordinance
or guidelines. City Attorney Isenberg stated guidelines are more flexible than
an ordinance and adopted differently. Alderman Karn noted that other film
friendly cities have guidelines rather than ordinances, and in the film
industry, sometimes impromptu decisions need to be made and guidelines would
allow this, with an ordinance, it would require Board approval. While putting
the document together, other ordinances were evaluated. The guidelines are film
friendly and fill in the holes from the existing City ordinance. They did not
make it more restrictive, but put in place additional restrictions for
notifications and protecting the rights of citizens. He asked that the document
be considered the first reading.
   Alderman Barnes, a member of the Film Committee acknowledged that a lot of
work went into the proposed guidelines, but he does not believe that it is
ready for adoption because of issues with some of the wording. He does not
believe that it should be thrown out, but he is in favor of keeping the current
ordinance because it was not the ordinance not working, but City management.
   Alderman Adams suggested to continue operating under the current ordinance,
and if there is additional critiquing, place it on the retreat agenda.
   Mayor Howard stated that he wished the matter be resolved. Alderman Coring
stated that the Committee did its due diligence with developing guidelines that
address all issues that was brought to the their attention and he is in favor
of the guidelines.
   The vote on the motion by Alderman Powell was 4 ayes, Aldermen Powell,
Poole, Adams and Barnes. 2 noes, Alderman Karn and Coring. Motion passed 4-2
   Mayor Howard announced that the Committee’s task was completed and directed
that filming be a topic at the Board’s Annual Retreat
   Sandy Lane – The Board asked at a previous workshop that this road be
maintained which is in the City limits. Alderman Powell stated that this is a
60ft designated right of way and the intersection is dangerous, and a school
bus travels this road everyday.
   Attorney Isenberg stated legally Sandy Lane is a 10 feet wide dedicated
right of way. When the city purchased the property for the pump station, it was
granted a 30 feet utility easement for access to the pump station. Within the
30 ft. utility easement, it allows the city to run their lines from the pump
station up 211 and access right to get to and from the pump station with the 30
ft. This is not a public right of way, and the city can maintain enough to get
to the pump station. In answer to a question, Mr. Isenberg stated the roadbed
is within the right of way. If it was not for the easement, the City would not
have any right to maintain.
   Robert Tucker, Director of Public Services noted that the easement runs from
211 down to the pump station. The school bus turnaround is beyond the City’s
easement on private property.
   Alderman Adams stated if the city has the right to maintain the road, it
should be done and believes the City is getting too involved in technicalities.
   Hankinsville Alley – Alderman Adams asked that the holes be filled in and
the road scraped.
   Rural Transportation Advisory Committee- Mayor Howard announced that Mayor
Betty Wallace, Town of Oak Island, and Bruce Maxwell, Town of St. James were
appointed

entries.

auditors because the audit is ultimately the responsibility of the Board.

Board needs to discuss appointment of an Interim City Manager in accordance
with G.S. 143-318.11 (6) as soon as possible.

resignation while commending Mr. Thomas for his professionalism, leadership and
dedication to the City.

continue to work to insure a smooth transition.

   F. Southport Market Agreement Renewal
AGREEMENT
CITY OF SOUTHPORT AND DOWNTOWN SOUTHPORT, INC.
This Agreement made and entered into this 14th day of March, 2013 by and
between the City of Southport and Downtown Southport, Inc. (DSI)
1. The City of Southport agrees that DSI may use the Fort Johnston Garrison
lawn for its Waterfront Market on Wednesdays beginning May 1, 2013 until it
concludes September 25, 2013.
2. It is mutually agreed upon that DSI will pay the amount of $25 per week for
use of the Garrison Lawn. There are 22 total weeks in the 2013 season.
3. It is also agreed upon that this Agreement is in effect until the end of
September 2013 and will be re-negotiated for 2014.
4. It is further agreed that DSI will contribute funds to the City of Southport
to assist with beautification projects for use of the Garrison lawn.
5. It is hereby mutually agreed that DSI shall be responsible for any damage to
the Fort Johnston Garrison Lawn resulting from its use thereof.
6. DSI does hereby agree to indemnity and save harmless the City of Southport
and its officers, officials, employees and agents from and against any and all
suits, claims, loss, cost, injuries, damages, charges, liability or expense
whatsoever, including court costs and attorney fees, which they may sustain or
be put to by reason of this agreement and DSI’s use of the Garrison Lawn for
the Waterfront Farmers Market or other purpose.
Now, therefore in consideration of the mutual terms set forth, it is hereby
agreed to these terms and conditions by Downtown Southport Inc. and the City of
Southport, N. C.

   B. Maritime Museum Expansion Concept – Friends of Museum
   Mr. Walt Madsen, Board member, Friends of the Maritime Museum and Connie
Keller, Architect, presented a 3-D power point presentation showing a
preliminary concept for expansion of the Maritime Museum. They propose to
expand into the area that is currently used for storage space by the City’s
Parks and Recreation Department. The conceptual drawing is to make the Board
aware of plans and begin the process of meetings to get the land allocated.
   Mr. Madsen answering questions, stated if the concept is approved, plans are
to raise the funds, the same as they did before. At this time, they are not
asking for financial support from the City. Alderman Powell asked about storage
containers on site, which is used by the Museum and others by the Parks and
Recreation Department. Alderman Adams commented about previous contributions
from the City and they keep asking the City for more when the grounds have to
be utilized by all entities i.e. City.
   Alderman Barnes referenced the resolution and board policy adopted January
10, 2013 stating that three readings must be held for any proposed use of the
Fort Johnston property, which involves installation of structures or additions.
Mayor Howard stated that the policy would apply for this request. Alderman
Barnes asked if the Museum would be asking the City for funding. Mr. Madsen
acknowledged until they put the plan together, he will not say that they will
not come back to the City for assistance. They are asking for 10 ft. off Moore
Street, and 22 ft. off Davis Street. The space is concrete where they propose
to expand.
City Manager Thomas informed the Board in his report, that this is preliminary
information and feedback is not intended to constitute a “first reading” within
the meaning of the Fort Johnston Installation Policy.
Mr. Madsen in response to a question posed by Alderman Coring stated that they
met with the Parks and Recreation Director, Ms Hemphill and City Manager
Thomas. There were no further questions or comments.

   I. Personnel Policy Amendment – Retiree Health Insurance
   Mr. Thomas stated during the FY 12-13 budget review process, it was noted
that the City has incurred a significant financial obligation for payment of
employee retirement benefits under its policy. These benefits are expected to
cost over $150,000 in the current fiscal year – the equivalent of about 2.4
cents ad valorem tax levy.
   Concern was expressed by the Board about the financial sustainability of the
retiree health insurance program. Indications were given that the Board would
like to curtail or eliminate this benefit program for persons who have not yet
entered city employment.
   A resolution was presented for Board consideration, which will not affect
any current retirees or current full-time employees.
   Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Powell to adopt the following
resolution amending the Personnel Policy with regard to retiree health
insurance effective immediately.
A RESOLUTION AMENDING THE PERSONNEL POLICY
WITH REGARD TO RETIREE HEALTH INSURANCE
   WHEREAS the City of Southport Personnel Policy, Article IX, Section 3,
provides for certain health, life, and dental insurance benefits to be paid to
retirees, and
   WHEREAS the Board of Aldermen has determined that the cost of such benefits
is not financially sustainable in the future; and
   WHEREAS the Board of Aldermen desires to discontinue such benefits for
persons who are hired or become creditable service employees going forward, but
to leave unchanged such benefits as they may apply to current retirees or
creditable service employees;
   BE IT RESOLVED that the Personnel Policy of the City of Southport is amended
by adding the language shown below, underlined, to Article IX, Section 3, of
the Personnel Policy:
Section 3. Retirement Insurance
The City shall provide membership in the North Carolina Local Government
Employees Retirement System for all regular employees who will be eligible
under the rules and regulations of the system. The City and the employee will
share the costs for membership at a ratio determined by General Statute and the
LGERS.
The City will offer contribution of health, life, and dental coverage to
employees retiring from the City with total creditable service and eligibility
as defined and accepted by the North Carolina Local Government Employees
Retirement System.
Employees retiring with five (5) years of creditable service may continue in
the City’s group health, life and dental plans, if allowed by the plan
provider, at the employee’s expense. Employees retiring with ten (10) years of
creditable service may continue in the City’s group health, life and dental
plans, if allowed by the plan provider, with the employee’s coverage paid at
50% by the City and 50% paid by the employee. Family or spouse coverage
premiums shall be paid 100% by the employee. Employees retiring with 20 years
of creditable service may continue in the City’s group health, life and dental
plans with the City paying 100% of the premium for the employee’s coverage and
the employee paying 100% of the premium for family or spouse coverage. When the
employee becomes eligible for Medicare, such coverage in the City’s group plans
will be the Medicare supplement, if offered by the group provider.
The second and third paragraphs of this section, relating to the payment of
health, life, and dental insurance coverage for retired employees, shall not
apply to any employee who begins creditable service in the retirement system as
a City of Southport employee after March 14, 2013 or who is hired as a City
employee after March 14, 2013.
Adopted in regular session by the Southport Board of Aldermen, March 14, 2013.
                                 s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:
/Regina Alexander, Clerk

   City Manager Gandy reported that the City has several sections that can be

concerning the installation of natural gas lines, it was understood that if
they came in and cut ditches, they would install conduit for the City to run
electric lines. They started boring and installed lines, but this was not done.
The City should seek an avenue for enforcement because Southport does not
recoup anything for natural gas. Mr. Fisher stated that this was written into
the documents that if a trench was cut, it had to be wide enough for conduit.
He did state that some conduit is installed in the Yacht Basin area.
   Alderman Adams suggested the City contact Brunswick Electric Membership
Corporation (BEMC) about retiring the City’s debt before 2026. Mayor Howard
stated that this item would be added to the City goals.
4.   Fire Department - Chief Cumbee
   Chief Cumbee reported that the Viper Radios have been received.
·   Substation on Hwy 211 near River Mist Subdivision should be pursued. The
original developer promised land to the City. (Jeff Earp)
·   Howe Street emergency light installed in front of fire department
·   City awarded a $70,000 FEMA grant to purchase gear.
·   Review of contract between the City and Duke Power is ongoing.
·   Fire Fee – Chief Cumbee discussed with the Board a proposal by Brunswick
County to change the funding source for County Fire Services. It their idea
that the fire fee revenue does not match needs within some districts. The
Policy Committee recommended to the Commissioners that the existing fire fee
supported district plan be abandoned and a countywide tax system be
implemented. The rationale is fire fees are based on the size of a residential
structure, commercial structure or acreage tract calculated on an inclining
scale as opposed to ad valorem property taxes, which are based on value of the
structure or parcel. In most cases, if the fire tax were levied at the same
rate in each district, the revenue disparity would be similar. The current fire
fee has been in effect eleven years, and Southport has always operated within
its budget. Some departments have paid firefighters and volunteers, which cost
about $53,000 annually per firefighter. He stated if the City of Southport had
to implement this process, the budget would increase approximately $600,000.
Most fire chiefs are opposed to the fire tax, which could have a tremendous
effect on departments and services, particularly volunteer fire departments.
Chief Cumbee asked that the Board send a letter or resolution opposing the fire
tax and to retain the current method to collect fire fees. Mayor Howard agreed
that this could have a major impact for years to come and asked that a letter
be written to the County Commissioners opposing a fire tax be placed on the
April 11 agenda for consideration.
5.   Public Services – Robert Tucker, Director
   At the March meeting, the Board of Aldermen authorized a contract with
Southern Asphalt, Inc for resurfacing city streets. The project will be funded
by Powell Bill funds. The amount of the contract is $146,143.25, which will
provide for repairs. The Board will need to adopt a budget amendment at its
April meeting before a notice to proceed can be issued. The construction time
is 60 calendar days. Construction is anticipated to occur late April through
May with the initial work to occur on the Howe Street segment.
·   North Atlantic Avenue from East Leonard to East West Street
·   Fodale Avenue from Mitchell to East Nash Street
·   North Lord Street from West Nash to West Brown
·   Long Leaf from Fodale to Herring
·   Kingsley from South Rhett to East Moore
·   Howe Street from Moore to Bay Street
   The City currently has 29 miles of City maintained streets. At the current
rate of expenditure, all streets would be resurfaced every 25 years and with
the rate of funding at $100,000 annually, the City could resurface its streets
every 33 years.
   Mayor Howard expressed concern that the paving had not commenced and noted
the Board approved this action at their last meeting and if the matter was a
budget amendment, he could have called a special meeting and as it stands, the
project is 30 days late beginning.
   Alderman Barnes asked about the status of Bay Street, Yacht Basin and Short
Streets. Mr. Tucker explained that the Board established the paving priorities
in 2012. There has not been a formal study of paving needs in the city for
several years and his goal is to conduct a study of all city streets and
conduct a paving rating survey using DOT methods. Upon completion, this will be
submitted to the Board with a recommended list of streets based on the survey.
He will inspect the streets referenced and determine if some intermediate work
can be done to repair them temporarily.
