   Mr. Tucker stated that the City has been working cooperatively with the
Corps of Engineers to permit and construct a stone revetment along the
waterfront at the Bay Street pump station to reduce erosion. The Corps has
completed their design and the City Manager is conducting negotiations for the
required permanent easements from the affected property owners. They anticipate
being able to secure the required easements as an in-kind contribution to the
project. The City’s current projected share of the funding is estimated at
$180,000. The total cost is anticipated at $540,000 and it is proposed to bid
and award the project by September 1, 2013 for construction.
   Alderman Barnes asked about the impact to neighbors from the trucks. City
Manager Gandy stated they will be cognizant of this and neighbors will be
notified when work begins.
   Proposed Wastewater Planning Study
   Mr. Tucker stated that the city receives routine requests from property
owners and developers in areas that are within the city’s designated sewer
service area that are not serviceable by the current wastewater collection
system. A significant number of these requests have come in along the Howe
Street corridor and in the area near Dosher Cutoff. The city and county have
agreed to make transfers of ownership and operation of the existing Rivermist
and Sandy Lane Pump Stations from the City to the county while reserving some
additional wastewater flow capacity to serve future growth. One element of the
agreement is that the city is granted a single force main connection to the
Boiling Springs Lake force main that is currently under construction. In order
that the city may develop its future wastewater collection infrastructure in an
orderly and efficient manner, staff recommends that the Board of Aldermen give
favorable consideration to funding a wastewater planning study of the remaining
service area to determine the best feasible location for future pump stations
and interceptor lines. Mayor Howard asked that the Utility Committee discuss
this issue.

6.   Finance – Bonnie Bray, Finance Director
   FY 2011-2012 Audit
   FY-12 audit is nearly complete, with the help of Art Cottrell, an outside
auditor that was hired to assist her with accounting to correct financial
statements that will be submitted to Berry, Padgett & Chandler by April 10.
Related fieldwork and testing to verify the integrity of the data will be
performed by the outside audit team over the following month, while work
continues in house on related full accrual documents, including depreciation,
the Management Discussion & Analysis, disclosure notes and required
supplementary information. She stated that financial data has been uncovered
that occurred in FY 13 while trying to get FY 12 corrected. She went from
eighteen months of no bank reconciliations down to five with outside
assistance, but confident that the information provided to the Auditor is
correct.
She stated that Menton has provided a revised contract, which identifies
completion of the audit by May 31, 2013. Interim City Manager Rob Gandy has
been in phone contact with Sharon Edmundson, of the NC Local Government
Commission, regarding the extended schedule. A letter of explanation is being
prepared for transmittal with the contract after review by the Board of
Aldermen during the April 11 meeting.
   FY 2013-2014 Budget
   Ms. Bray told the Board that she has been unable to provide monthly
financial data because of the financial records and the inaccuracies. Once all
bank statements are reconciled and financial records are updated, she will
provide a complete history of the City’s finances.
Finance staff has been working closely with department heads since January to
ensure the financial data they need to develop their FY14 budgets was properly
recorded and accessible to them. However, the accuracy of FY12 records has been
in doubt until just recently, and the accumulated data for FY13 has not yet
been verified. Consequently, they have been operating without a vital piece of
budget machinery, i.e., a complete picture of the City’s fiscal history.
   Mayor Howard asked when could the Board expect to know the financial
condition of the city and what is needed to expedite the work. Ms. Bray told
the Board because her staff does not have an accounting background, she
recommended Mr. Cottrell continue as an outside resource for the next month
working around his availability. Mayor Howard asked if she had any other
options. Ms. Bray told the Board that Mr. Cottrell’s hourly rate is $60 an
hour, but he    understands the accounting and know what to look for. Another
factor is the City’s accounting software is DOS based, and not user friendly.
   Alderman Poole suggested that the problems be identified i.e. dates
initiated, completion and the cost involved. Aldermen Coring, Barnes and others
expressed their dismay at the financial condition of the City records and
reiterated getting it correct is a priority. Alderman Coring stated that the
Board could not establish goals for the city if they do not know the financial
condition. Mayor Howard and the Board agreed before it can move forward with
planning for FY 13-14, they must have correct financial data.
   Budget Amendment: Alderman Barnes motioned, seconded by Alderman Powell to
approve a budget amendment to appropriate up to $10,000 and to authorize the
City Manager to use the funds to assist the Finance Director in getting the
financial accounting up to date. The vote was unanimous. Motion passed.
(Budget Amendment #12)
Ms. Bray told the Board that she expected to overcome this deficiency
comprehensively in the near future, when examination of both FY12 and FY13 data
is complete. In the meantime, as departments continue to identify their needs,
finance staff will meet specific challenges on a case-by-case basis, applying
resources as needed and available. A good deal of work has already been
accomplished.
In addition, legislative actions currently being discussed in Raleigh are
shifting the landscape for predictions of future resources. Outcomes of the
following two, in particular, could have a significant impact:
·   Unemployment Insurance – The current pay go arrangement used by
municipalities to fund unemployment benefits would be replaced by advance
funding of a share of anticipated future claims
·   Tax reductions – Eliminations of privilege license, electric franchise, and
beer and wine taxes would be replaced by corresponding increases in other local
tax revenues
In answer to questions by Alderman Powell, City Manager Gandy stated that he
cannot budget until he has solid figures, but preliminary budgets have been
received from department heads, and if need be, he would consider an interim
budget.
   Powell Bill
At the end of June 2012, the city had approximately $300,000 in the Powell Bill
fund balance. During FY13, the city planned to use approximately one-half of
that, or $154,800, to pay for street-related expenditures of $250,000,
including $110,000 in work ordinarily performed by the street department. In
addition, the city budgeted $96,000 from the State in new Powell Bill revenue
during FY13.
Proposed Budget Amendment #14 is on the April 11 board meeting agenda and would
appropriate another $60,000 for expanded street work approved during the March
14 board meeting. That would leave approximately $86,200 in the Powell Bill
fund balance, with the city having spent a total of $310,000 on related street
repairs during FY13. Because we actually received $7,000 more than was budgeted
in new revenue from the State this year ($103,000 vs. $96,000), the additional
income will potentially increase the Powell Bill fund balance to $103,200 at
year-end assuming the current level of planning.
   Visitor’s Center Store
The Visitor Center has sold approximately 150 t-shirts since the beginning of
the year. Tourism Director Cindy Brochure estimates the center could double or
triple these sales from now until June 30, between normal summer traffic and
the expanded flow brought on by “Safe Haven.” However, the t-shirt stock is
currently exhausted and the expenditure budget to purchase more is depleted, so
capitalizing on this opportunity will require a budget amendment. A relatively
small amount -- less than $3,000 -- would be needed to buy sufficient stock for
the projected target. Sales would replenish the General Fund appropriation in
full and return a nice profit. Mrs. Brochure recommended increasing the revenue
and expenditure lines for this activity in the FY-14 budget. They are currently
$15,000 and $10,000, respectively.
Mayor Howard told the Finance Director that it was the Board’s intent to use
the $10,000 as seed money and the profit would be used to replenish the
inventory rather than be placed in the City’s general fund, the same as an
enterprise fund. Ms. Bray stated that she would do some research as whether the
store is making money and check with other entities on how they handle matters
such as this. The Board concurred that it is their desire that the store be
self-supporting.
Budget Amendment:  Alderman Karn motioned, seconded by Alderman Poole to
approve a budget amendment to temporarily increase the revenue and expenditure
line from $10,000 to $13,000 from the general fund balance to restock
merchandise in the Visitor’s Center Store.
The vote of approval was unanimous. Motion passed.
7.   Future Use of Former Visitor’s Center
      Mr. Gandy discussed with the Board the best use of the former Visitor’s
Center building. Mr. Gandy stated an option is to convert it to a public rental
facility for smaller functions because it has adequate parking. He asked the
Finance Director to gather comparable rental rates for a building of this size.
      Alderman Barnes stated that the City has a special rate for non-profits
for use of the Community Building and if smaller groups could be moved to this
facility, it would not cost as much for utilities. Mayor Howard noted that the
July 4 Committee gave the building to the City and the City in turn donates use
of the Community Building for two weeks during July 4, and sometimes most of
the building is not needed. Rental of this facility could be used to
accommodate some of these smaller groups, and be an annex of the Community
Building. Staff can create a policy and procedure for rental.
      Alderman Coring asked if the City would need use of the facility during
the relocation of offices. Mayor Howard stated the City owns the building and
can use it any time.
      Alderman Barnes moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to assign the old

RESOLUTION APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENT TO UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, Mr. Richard Bandera has prepared and submitted to the Planning
Board proposed amendments to Article 11, Section 11-1(G) of the Southport
Unified Development Ordinance, dealing with the location of accessory
structures; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended
that the proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance, as amended
by the Planning Board as hereinafter set forth, is consistent with the City
Comprehensive Plan and CAMA Core Land Use Plan and should be approved; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on April 11, 2013, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that these proposed amendments
to Section 11-1 of the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with the
Southport Comprehensive Land Use Plan and CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) due to the location of houses
on riverfront lots in the R-10 district, property owners would be unable to
have accessory garages without this amendment, and (ii) the amendment is
necessary and reasonable to support increased accessibility and enjoyment of
Southport’s waterfront while providing reasonable regulation of the location of
these accessory structures for neighboring properties.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments and additions to Section 1-1 (G) of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted.
      This 11th day of April 2013.

A RESOLUTION TO MAINTAIN AND SUPPORT THE CURRENT INTEGRITY AND FUNDING FOR THE
PARKS AND RECREATION TRUST FUND (PARTF)
WHEREAS, North Carolina is known for its unique and scenic natural resources
and opportunities for recreation with a long tradition of its citizens and
visitors enjoying parks, mountains, rivers, greenways, beaches and more.
Generations of residents and visitors have delighted in these landscapes and
park facilities; and
WHEREAS, The Parks and Recreation Trust Fund (PARTF) was established with bi-
partisan support on July 16, 1994 to fund improvements in the state's park
system, to fund grants for local governments and to increase the public's
access to the state's beaches and coastal waterways; and
WHEREAS, since its inception The Parks and Recreation Trust Fund has provided
$161 million via 722 grants to 370 local governments in 99 counties and has
been matched with $312 million of local and private dollars for the purchase of
local park land, building and renovation of facilities and development of
greenways and trails; and
WHEREAS, North Carolina’s population has grown to make it the 10th most
populous state in the nation with projections for the significant growth to
continue in the coming decades, and more state and local parks are needed to
meet the increased demands; and
WHEREAS, parks are identified as key contributors to North Carolina’s tourism
industry that generates nearly $20 billion in annual economic impact; and
WHEREAS, parks in North Carolina are experiencing record visitation levels
including over 14.25 million to state parks in both 2011 and 2012; and
WHEREAS, The Parks & Recreation Trust Fund has leveraged funds that allowed our
State to acquire land for state parks and state natural areas and protected
nearly 83,000 acres and made major additions to the Mountains-to-Sea State
Trail; and
WHEREAS, The Parks & Recreation Trust Fund has funded capital improvement
projects in the state parks such as visitor centers and exhibit halls which
provide tremendous opportunities to educate students and all citizens about
North Carolina’s outstanding natural resources, and other capital projects
including campgrounds, picnic areas, boating facilities, trails and swimming
beaches; and local capital projects including construction of community
centers, athletic fields and greenways; and
WHEREAS, the annual economic impact to local economies of all tourists visiting
the state parks system was estimated at more than $400 million in sales and
income, as well as nearly 5,000 jobs according to a 2008 study.
WHEREAS, a portion of The Parks & Recreation Trust Fund is designated for the
Public Beach and Coastal Waterfront Access Program to improve access to beaches
and coastal waterways by funding public boat ramps and public beaches accesses;
and
WHEREAS, access to parks, recreation facilities and open space provides cost-
effective opportunities for citizens of all ages to participate in health and
wellness activities thereby reducing costs associated with obesity, heart
disease, diabetes and high blood pressure; and
WHEREAS, research has documented that structured park and recreational
opportunities in local communities can prevent crime and provide positive
activities and directions for young people; and
WHEREAS, dedicated, recurring funding of the Parks & Recreation Trust Fund
allows for structured and objective planning and efficient management of the
system at both the state and local levels for today and future generations; and
WHEREAS, the success of The Parks and Recreation Trust Fund is due to the
dedicated funding source provided by a portion of the deed stamp tax, and is
recognized nationally as a model for efficiency and accountability; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport does call on the
members of the General Assembly to maintain dedicated revenues generated by
seventy-five cents of the deed stamp tax for The Parks and Recreation Trust
Fund.
This the 14 day of April 2013 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
                        s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:
s/Regina W. Alexander, Clerk

ALDERMEN CHAMBERS (CITY HALL) SOUTHPORT, N.C.

         Aldermen Ken Karn, Mary Ellen Poole, Buddy Barnes,

1. Call to order – 4:00 p.m.
   Mayor Howard called the meeting to order at 4:00 p.m. He announced that the
meeting was duly posted pursuant to North Carolina General Statute 160A-71(b)
and in accordance with Board of Aldermen Rules of Procedures. The special
meeting is being held for the purpose of discussing the possibility of selling
fill dirt from the 435-acre tract owned by the City near Sunny Point.
   Mayor Howard stated that he received a call from Mr. Balfour Beatty,
contractor for the Long Beach Road extension project for the North Carolina
Department of Transportation. He inquired about purchasing fill dirt from City
owned property. Mayor Howard stated he contacted Alderman Powell who met with
company representatives along with Mr. Gandy, City Manager.
   Alderman Powell reported that they met with the company representatives and
they need approximately 419,000 cubic yards of material. The City previously
sold fill dirt from the property that was used in the construction of the
second Oak Island Bridge and he noted that it is excellent material. If sold,
the City could realize a substantial amount of revenue generated from the sale.
   The Board acknowledged that the land cannot be developed commercially
because it is inside of the blast zone of Sunny Point but can recoup monies
from selling some of the material.
   Attorney Isenberg stated the City has three ways in which it can sell the
fill dirt; public auction, sealed bids or negotiated offer with advertising and
upset bid.
   Alderman Adams stated his support of moving forward with negotiations
because this is an opportunity for the City to recover monies from the land.
   Alderman Barnes moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to authorize Alderman
Powell and City Manager Gandy to negotiate the sale of the fill dirt for a
minimum of $2.50 per cubic yard. Vote unanimous. Motion passed
    City Manager Gandy reminded the Board that the Water and Sewer Fund monies
paid for the Sunny Point property and any proceeds from the sale should be
placed back into that fund.
Adjournment – 4:20 p.m.
   No further business, meeting closed upon motion of Alderman Powell, seconded
by Alderman Poole.  Vote unanimous.  Motion passed

MUNICIPAL CLERKS WEEK

WHEREAS, the Office of the Municipal Clerk, a time honored and vital part of

WHEREAS, the Office of the Municipal Clerk is the oldest among public servants;

WHEREAS, the Office of the Municipal Clerk provides the professional link
between the citizens, the local governing bodies and agencies of government at
other levels; and
WHEREAS, the Municipal Clerk serves as the information center on functions of
local government and community; and

11. Resolution – N.C. Film Industry
Alderman Karn moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to approve the following
resolution in support of the N.C. Film Industry. Vote unanimous. Motion passed.
Resolution to Support the North Carolina Film Industry
WHEREAS, the Film and Television Industry has been an important clean industry
in North Carolina for over 30 years, and
WHEREAS, North Carolina seeks and wishes to attract clean, knowledge-based
industries that position the state well for 21st century job expansion, and
WHEREAS, the Film and Television Industry has contributed to jobs and increased
economic activity in over 50 North Carolina counties, and
WHEREAS, over 4,000 families depend on this industry for well-paying jobs and
the industry workforce has multiplied in each of the last three years, and
WHEREAS, this industry will provide more highly skilled jobs and opportunities
in the future and contribute significantly to workforce earnings potential, and
WHEREAS, our skilled crew base, well-trained talent, excellent facilities and
diverse scenery make North Carolina an excellent place to film, and
WHEREAS, every level of public education trains technical employees for this
industry and post-secondary job placement in the industry is very strong, and
WHEREAS, film over the last five years has exceeded one billion dollars in
gross domestic product for the state, and
WHEREAS, the current North Carolina tax structure encourages productions from
around the world to economically produce movies and television series in our
state, and
WHEREAS, films and TV series produced in North Carolina attract destination
tourism to filming locations, contributing to the state’s travel economy, and
WHEREAS, this Board supports job growth of high skilled, high wage industries.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, the City of Southport Board of Aldermen does
hereby declare our support for both the North Carolina Film and Television
Industry and the current state tax policy that has caused this industry to
grow. We call upon our representatives in the North Carolina General Assembly
to continue support of this important industry.
Duly Resolved, this the 9th Day of May, 2013
s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
s/ Regina Alexander, City Clerk

11. Review of Resolution supporting the preservation of affordable financing
through tax-exempt financing
   In memo to the Board, it was explained that Congress and the President have
offered changes to the tax code that would limit or eliminate tax-exempt
financing. The American Public Power Association, ElectriCities and others are
opposed to this change, which would limit the ability to access affordable
financing and encouraged local governments to adopt resolutions opposing the
changes.
   Alderman Karn moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to adopt the resolution
supporting the preservation of affordable financing through tax-exempt
financing. Vote unanimous. Motion passed.
A Resolution Supporting the Preservation of Affordable Financing through Tax-
Exempt Financing
WHEREAS, municipal bonds are the means by which state and local governments and
school districts finance critical infrastructure, including roads, bridges,
hospitals, schools and utility systems; and
WHEREAS, under current law, the owners of municipal bonds are not required to
pay federal income tax on the interest income they receive from the bonds; and
WHEREAS, the federal tax exemption provides a significant difference between
public sector and private sector debt financing; and
WHEREAS, municipalities benefit from this tax exemption through substantial
savings on the interest cost of borrowed money; and
WHEREAS, the benefit of lower capital costs attributable to tax-exempt
financing are passed on to citizens through reduced rates and greater local
investments; and
WHEREAS, periodically Congress and the President have proposed legislation to
tax or alter the federal tax exemption of interest on municipal bonds; now,
therefore, be it
RESOLVED, that the City of Southport opposes any and all efforts to eliminate
or limit the federal tax exemption on interest earned from municipal bonds.
DULY ADOPTED, this the 13th Day of June, 2013.
                                                                                                              
s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:
s/ Regina Alexander, City Clerk
12. Review of Resolution approving an exception to the contracting prohibitions
in NCGS 14-234
   (Alderman Barnes recused due to interest in the topic of discussion))
The Board acknowledged that Wildwood Landscaping, owned by Alderman Barnes had
a contract on maintenance of the grounds at 1029 North Howe Street prior to the
City assuming ownership. City Manager Gandy explained that G.S. 14-234
prohibits contracting with public officials in the same jurisdiction, but make
exceptions for officials in jurisdictions under 15,000 population. The statute
in subsection d1 allows contracting with public officials in communities fewer
than 15,000 with certain conditions.
·   The undertaking or contract must be approved by specific resolution of the
governing body adopted in open and public meeting with the amount not exceeding
$40,000 in a twelve-month period.
·   The official entering into contract cannot participate in the vote
·   The total amount of contract with each official must be noted in the
audited financial statement of the local government.
·   The governing board must post, in a conspicuous place in City Hall, a list

   A RESOLUTION APPROVING AN EXCEPTION TO THE CONTRACTING PROHIBITIONS IN NCGS
14-234
   WHEREAS General Statute GS 14-234 generally prohibits contracting with
public officials in the same jurisdiction, but makes some potential exceptions
for officials in jurisdictions under 15,000 population; and
   WHEREAS the City of Southport is under 15,000 in population; and
   WHEREAS Alderman Floyd (Buddy) Barnes, the owner of Wildwood Landscape
Contracting, Ltd., has offered to perform certain landscaping maintenance
services at a recently-purchased municipal property located at 1029 North Howe
Street at a cost of $375.00 per month or $4500.00 per year; and
   WHEREAS the Board of Aldermen desires to contract with Alderman Floyd
(Buddy) Barnes and Wildwood Landscape Contracting to provide said landscaping
services for Fiscal Year FY 13-14
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport:
Section 1. The Board of Aldermen hereby approves contracting with Floyd (Buddy)
Barnes, an alderman of the City of Southport, and his company Wildwood
Landscape Contracting, Ltd., for landscaping maintenance at 1029 North Howe
Street for Fiscal Year 13-14 at a cost of $375.00 per month or $4500.00 per
fiscal year.
Section 2. The record of this contract approval shall be entered in the minutes
of the June 13, 2013 Board of Aldermen meeting, shall be noted in the annual

13. Update on Audit FY 11-12 and FY 13-14 budget preparation situation
   Ms. Bray, Finance Director, presented a preliminary report from the Auditors
and stated that the management letter would be presented later. Ms. Bray
reported that the preliminary data show that the numbers are very good and
there is $1.6 million in the general fund balance. She reported that staff has
sufficient financial data to begin work on FY 13-14 budget, however in
communication with the North Carolina Local Government Commission, it has been
recommended that an interim budget be adopted which will shift FY 13-14 budget
by one month to August.
   Mayor Howard and the Board expressed appreciation to staff for their
diligence in getting the City financials in order. He stated that the Board has
been transparent with the City finances
and staff worked to meet self-imposed deadlines. He announced that a special
meeting would be called to receive the audit and to adopt an interim budget
before June 30.
   Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to authorize the City
Manager to close out the capital projects. The vote of approval was unanimous.
Motion passed.
14. Brunswick Community College Gym - Lord Street
   Mayor Howard noted that Alderman Adams had been called to work but asked
that this matter be placed on the agenda.  Mayor Howard communicated that Mr.
Jerry Thrift from Brunswick Community College contacted the City to gauge its
interest in leasing the gym on Lord Street. Mayor Howard stated that the City
cannot totally fund the project and suggested a public private partnership be
formed, and appoint a task force to study the issue. Alderman Barnes stated his
support of retaining the facility with community involvement, and to seek
grants to assist with renovations.
   Alderman Barnes motioned, seconded by Alderman Poole to authorize Mayor
Howard to appoint a Task Force to study the feasibility of a public-private
partnership to determine use of the existing gym and report its findings back
to the Board.  Discussion:  Alderman Karn stated he would not want to see the
City lease the facility and make upgrades when it belongs to the college. He
would rather the City own the gym, but deemed it a worthwhile project because
of the historical significance to the community. He stated grant funds might be
available to assist with renovations. Alderman Coring stated the City currently
has a gym that need upgrades and prefer to see the City focus on that gym and
cautioned the Board about taking on another project. The vote on the motion was
unanimous. Motion passed to establish Task Force.
   Mayor Howard appointed Alderman Adams, Richard Bandera and Donnie Joyner to
the Lord Street Gym Task Force and others may be appointed later.
15. Executive Session- property acquisition (GS-143-318.11 (5)
   The Board entered closed session to discuss the proposed terms for property
acquisition of the Chirico property located at the Yacht Basin owned by First
Bank upon motion of Alderman Poole, seconded by Alderman Barnes. Vote
unanimous.
   Alderman Coring motioned to re-enter open session, seconded by Alderman
Barnes, vote carried. (Closed session minutes will remained sealed for a period
of time)
   Mayor announced in closed session that the Board was given information
concerning contract negotiations for the Yacht Basin property owned by First
Bank and discussed procuring an easement for Hankinsville Alley.
16.   Other Business
   a) The Board discussed purchase of the necessary equipment and appropriation
of funds in FY 13-14 budget to allow the City Clerk to restore and digitize
City records, and provide the necessary office space. City Manager Gandy was
requested to provide the adequate office space in the space analysis plan.
Alderman Barnes suggested additional help to assist the Clerk.
   b) Northwood Cemetery Paving and removal of poles
   The Board approved the paving of two additional roads in Northwood Cemetery
at a cost of $7,000 and the posts be cut down to monument level while still
identifying the graves. Alderman Powell moved to approve the contract and
budget amendment, seconded by Alderman Karn. Vote unanimous. Motion passed.
    Mayor Howard stated that he would continue to work towards an endowment or
perpetual fund to assist with maintenance of the cemeteries.
   c) John N. Smith Cemetery - Mayor Howard reported that Brunswick Electric
Membership Corporation had installed the light at the John N. Smith Cemetery.
   d) Wooden Boat Show - Mayor Howard announced with consensus from the Board
that the City would provide the same services for the Wooden Boat Show
scheduled 2013 as it did in 2012.
   The Board expressed the need to bring part-time employees back to assist
with mowing rights of ways, cemeteries and other work needed around the City.
17. Other Comments
   Alderman Barnes commented on the recently acquired brush truck (Fire
Department). He also noted that the City has received additional donations to

   Alderman Poole stated she attended a recognition service for Ms. Carolyn
Pryor who was the State winner for the Senior Service Award. $500 was received

   Mayor Howard and the Board congratulated Alderman Coring on his promotion to
Lieutenant in charge of the Uniform Patrol, Sheriff Department.
   The Board encouraged support for the North Carolina Fourth of July Festival.

Coring, the vote was unanimous.

for the Police vehicles. The Board discussed in detail with chief Dove the need
for part time civilian desk clerks. Mayor Howard asked Alderman Poole as Chair
of the Emergency Operations Committee to work with Chief Dove to ascertain if
these positions are cut, the effect it would have on the department and
services, while acknowledging that the additional revenues can be placed where
needed, ex. computers.
Building & Grounds - The Board acknowledged a request for an additional skilled
laborer position but did not see the justification and agreed 5 to 1 not to
fund the new position. Alderman Karn stated his support of the position.
Finance – The Board discussed with Ms. Bray funds ($6,000) in the budget to
outsource payroll and explained the outdated payroll software. She stated that
payroll takes 30% of the employee’s time and there have been times when it was
questionable whether the payroll would be produced. The Board asked that Ms.
Bray look at other software options and directed that payroll remain in house.
Alderman Poole suggested payroll and human resources be placed under the City
Manager. Mayor Howard acknowledged that this should be the Board or City
Manager’s decision.
Administration – The Board expressed the need to preserve City records and
appropriated $14,100 for a document retrieval system (Laser fiche) which would
be used to scan and digitize records.
Alderman Karn stated that video streaming ($10,600) should be delayed until the
logistics are worked out and a person identified to operate the system, in
addition to having the correct lighting in the Council Chambers. Mayor Howard
suggested the monies be placed in the Board contingency fund.
Tourism – The Board asked that justification be provided for the requested
position.
South Brunswick High School Booster Club - Melissa Hinnant, member of the South
Brunswick High School Booster Club asked the Board for a one-time donation to
have the City’s name placed on a banner as one of the sponsors for athletic
activities at South Brunswick High School. The Board unanimously agreed to the
$500 donation.
Other Business - Mayor Howard asked that City Manager Gandy initiate the
process for bid procedures to purchase an ambulance for the Rescue Squad and to
proceed with purchase of the Laser fiche system. He asked that Heather
Hemphill, Parks and Recreation Director, compile costs including square footage
for relocation of the three storage buildings behind the Maritime Museum.
No further business, the meeting was recessed until 4:00 p.m., Tuesday, July
30, 2013.

JULY 30, 2013         RECESSED SESSION          4:00 P.M.
Present: Mayor Howard, Aldermen Karn, Powell, Barnes, Adams, Coring and Poole
Staff: City Manager Gandy, Regina Alexander, Clerk and Bonnie Bray, Finance
Director
Mayor Howard called the meeting back to order.
Mr. Ed Boguskie, 502 West Brown Street, commented on the parking along Bay
Street and around the Whittlers Bench. He told the Board that visitors
understand about parking between the lines and the newly designed parking
brought order to the parking in addition to much needed parking spaces. He
suggested to the Board that the sign be removed and leave parking as designed
with the lines.
Police Department – discussion resumed concerning part time clerks in the
Police Department. Chief Dove presented a proposal effective September 5
stating that the hours of operation will be from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Monday
through Friday, and from 8:00 a.m. to 12 noon on Saturdays, Sundays and
holidays. This will save approximately $26,000 in wages. The new hours will
enable the department to continue providing We Care calls and to check on
citizens who participate in the program.
Alderman Karn expressed concern about customer service if the positions were
cut back.
Alderman Adams expressed concern about the City moving backwards instead of
progressing forward and acknowledged that citizens should, if the need arise,
be able to come to the Police Department and speak with someone on duty.
Mr. Gandy stated that Chief Dove was asked to review his departmental budget
and look at ways that he could reduce it and presented this proposal.
RECESS – 4:30 P.M.  Mayor Howard recessed the meeting to ride over to 11th
Street to formally re-open the Hankins Alley by removing the mound of dirt that
was placed at the mouth of the alley/road. (Hankinsville Alley)
RECONVENED MEETING: Budget Workshop 5:12 P.M.
The meeting reconvened and Mayor Howard announced that the mound of dirt had
been removed from Hankinsville Alley and the citizens were pleased.
Cost of Living Adjustment – The Board briefly talked about the 3% COLA that was
proposed in the budget. It was the consensus of the Board that the COLA be
based on a tier system as recommended by Alderman Poole. Mayor Howard asked
that it be placed on the workshop agenda to be held in August and to remove the
salary increases from the budget to a discretionary fund. Alderman Poole
motioned accordingly, seconded by Alderman Barnes. Discussion: Alderman Coring
asked if the salary increase would include those employees who received a
salary adjustment or bonus under the former City Manager before he resigned.
Alderman Adams asked if the COLA would be retroactive. Mayor Howard noted that
these decisions could be addressed during the workshop.
City Manager Gandy stated that he would develop a tier chart and provide it to
the Board.
Community Building:  Alderman Barnes stated that the Director of the Community
Building should be full time. It was his understanding when the department was
separated in FY 2012-2013 that the position would become full time. The
director will soon be out of hours because part time employees are only allowed
to work 1000 hours in a calendar year.
Alderman Karn questioned the need for making the position full time when the
City Manager did not make this recommendation in the budget and believes that a
full time position is not justified or needed.
Alderman Coring stated that all excess revenues generated from rental of the
building should be put into Phase II of the Community Building to enlarge the
facility as originally proposed. He further stated that the building is not
large enough to hold some functions and the City is possibly losing revenues.
Alderman Barnes motioned to make the Community Building Director full time
excluding overtime pay, seconded by Alderman Powell. Discussion: Mayor Howard
stated that it is premature to solidify the full time position and recommended
it be considered in the workshop. Amendment: Alderman Barnes amended the motion
to place the full time position in the budget and after study by the Board, a
full time position would be considered. Alderman Powell seconded the motion.
Discussion:  Alderman Adams questioned the cost of adding a full time position.
Alderman Karn stated that the Board should be prudent, investigate the need for
the position because the City Manager did not recommend it for this budget
year, and recommended the Board focus on the actual needs of the City.
Mayor Howard recommended that this the matter be deferred to the workshop.
Alderman Barnes then withdrew the motion.
Building and Grounds: Alderman Adams moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to
place the position request on the workshop agenda. Vote unanimous.
Tourism/Economic Development:  Handouts with justification for a new position
and Tourism Director job description were given to Board members.  Alderman
Adams moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to place this item on the workshop
agenda. Discussion:  Alderman Karn acknowledged receipt of the justification
and list of job duties from the Tourism Director as the Board requested. The
vote on the motion was unanimous.
City Manager Gandy reaffirmed his recommendation to add a new position to the
Tourism/Economic Development Department. He also told the Board that he and
Chief Dove would implement the change recommended by the Chief and reduce the
Police Department budget accordingly. The Board concurred with the purchase of
four new computers for the Police Department and requested Chief Dove purchase
them from funds within his departmental budget.
Filming: Mayor Howard stated that this topic would be discussed at the August
meeting.
Adjournment – 6:15 p.m.
No further business, the meeting was adjourned upon motion of Alderman Karn,
seconded by Alderman Poole. Vote unanimous.

PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, on Saturday, September 28, 2013 the Southport Wooden Boat Show will be
held at the Old Southport Yacht Basin; and
WHEREAS, the 4 th Annual Southport Wooden Boat Show, sponsored by the SWBS
Committee in Conjunction with Downtown Southport, Inc. A 501 3 organization
will be held from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m.
WHEREAS, boats will be displayed in and around the historic Old Yacht Basin;
and
WHEREAS, visitors can meet and talk with wooden boat makers and owners; and
WHEREAS, visitors will be able to vote for their favorite boat entrant for the
Peoples Choice Award, and
WHEREAS, other awards will be given in various categories; and
WHEREAS, wooden boat shows across the country are popular with boat builders
and restorers; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Wooden Boat Show Committee encourages people to preserve
the wooden boat and nautical history for which Southport is known.
NOW THEREFORE, I Robert D. Howard by the power vested in me as Mayor of
Southport, North Carolina proclaim September 28, 2013 as Southport Wooden Boat
Show day in the City and invite citizens and surrounding communities to help
make this day a success.
Dated this the 8 th day of August 2013.
Robert D. Howard, Mayor

8.   Stevens Park Two Year Ball Field Lease with Bald Head Island, Limited
Mayor Howard presented a two (2) year lease with Bald Head Island Limited for a
3.27 acre tract of property located in Stevens Park. Addition of the 3.27 tract
with property currently owned by the City would allow the reopening of the
ballfields. Mayor Howard noted the lease is temporary and Bald Head Island is
drafting a master plan for future use of the property.
Attorney Isenberg confirmed the lease would be for $1 per year and can be
terminated as an agreement by both parties.
Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to accept the lease with
Bald Head Island Limited for a period of 24 months effective immediately. Vote
unanimous.
9.   Presentation by Ms. Kimberly Thompson on the Southport Community Garden
Ms. Kimberly Thompson, executive director of Keep Brunswick County Beautiful
spoke about a planned community garden on North Caswell Avenue behind the
Brunswick Community College Southport Center. The garden will have thirty 4' x
8' planter beds, two keyhole gardens, a compost area, two sources of water and
bench seating. The project is funded by a $20,000 Lowes Keep American Beautiful
community improvement grant and $10,000 Waste Management Think Green grant. She
stated the plans for the garden have been prepared, work is ready to begin and
the garden space will be available to the public for a small rental fee during
the growing period. Unrented spaces will be maintained by volunteers to support
local food banks. An informational meeting will be held Tuesday, August 13,
2013 at 7:00 p.m. at the International Longshoremen Association (ILA) Hall,
North Lord Street.
10.   Presentation by Ms. Katie McKee, Extension Agent, 4-H Youth Development
regarding the possible establishment of a community based 4-H club in Southport
Ms. Katie McKee discussed the pursuit by Brunswick County 4-H to develop
community based 4-H clubs in each town and city in the county. She outlined
results of recent research showing that young people who join 4-H are more
likely to go to college; likely to pursue careers in science, technology,
engineering, mathematics; less likely to use drugs and alcohol; and become
civically engaged. Ms. McKee requested assistance in recruiting individuals who
would be interested in leading a 4-H club. Ms. McKee provided an informational
handout and announced that a volunteer orientation meeting would be held at 6:
00 p.m. August 21 at the Bolivia County Center, Building N and a 4-H Fair would
be held September 30 through October 5.
11.   Report by Paul Fisher; Annual Conference of the North Carolina Eastern
Municipal Power Agency
Mr. Paul Fisher, the citys representative to the North Carolina Eastern
Municipal Power Agency, gave a report of the agencys annual conference held
July 31 through August 3 in Asheville, North Carolina. He gave a brief
historical overview of the agency and highlights of the keynote speakers and
their messages. He emphasized the economic impact of tourism, the importance of
cyber security and continuation of moving the electric system underground.
(Full report on file in the Clerks office)
12.   Review and approval of final plat for Phase II, Section VII of the Cades
Cove Subdivision
City Manager Gandy reported the final plat of Cades Cove subdivision, Phase II,
Section VII was reviewed and recommended by the Planning Board. Aldermen Barnes
and Poole praised the Planning Board for the thorough review process of the
submittal. Alderman Poole moved to approve the final plat for Cades Cove Phase

AUGUST 22 - 26, 2013          6:00 P.M.
ALDERMEN CHAMBERS (CITY HALL) SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:      Mayor Robert D. Howard
         Aldermen Todd Coring, Ken Karn, Mary Ellen Poole, Buddy Barnes,
         Jim Powell, Nelson Adams

         Regina W. Alexander, MMC, NCCMC

         Jerry Dove, Chief of Police
         Cindy Brochure, Tourism/Economic Development
         Vickie Potter, Director of Community Center

Mayor Howard called the meeting back to order at 6:00 p.m.
Alderman Adams welcomed everyone; Chief Dove gave the invocation and Alderman
Adams led the Board in the Pledge of Allegiance.
Mayor Howard noted the purpose of the meeting was to discuss several budget
matters and asked that the City Manager selection process be added to the
agenda. Alderman Poole moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to amend the agenda to
add discussion of City Manager selection process. The vote was unanimous.
1. Position(s) request in FY 2013-2014
Tourism – Alderman Barnes acknowledged the importance of tourism to the City
and recommended the requested position be funded as recommended by the Interim
City Manager. Alderman Powell agreed and acknowledged recent information he
learned during an ElectriCities Conference concerning the tourism industry and
the monies brought into North Carolina. Alderman Poole acknowledged that the
scope of tourism has changed. Alderman Karn noted the millions of dollars that
it brings to the local economy. Alderman Karn then moved, seconded by Alderman
Coring to fund the assistant tourism position. The votes were 6 ayes, Karn,
Coring, Poole, Barnes, Powell, and Adams. (Adams did not vote, but was counted
affirmative)
Community Center Director - Alderman Barnes stating during FY 11-12, this
position was separated from the Tourism Department and at that time, it was
stated that 90% of the employee’s time was spent coordinating and facilitating
use of the Community Center. It is his belief that making the position full
time would benefit the City by marketing, more hours spent on customer service
and availability to show the facility, and to make better use of the City’s
website as a marketing tool. He believes that the full time position is
justified. Alderman Barnes moved to make the part time director full time,
seconded by Alderman Powell. Discussion: Alderman Poole stated that the old
Visitor’s Center has been added to this department and the mission has changed.
The votes of approval were 5 ayes, Barnes, Powell, Poole, Coring, Adams. 1 no,
Alderman Karn. (Adams did not vote, but was counted affirmative)
Public Services – Mayor Howard stated that there was no unanimous support for
the requested assistant labor position and City Manager Gandy asked that it be
reconsidered at the September meeting.
Mr. Gandy told the Board that $130,000 surplus was placed in the Board’s
contingency and the positions will be funded from out of this lien item.
COLA – City Manager Gandy proposed a 3% cost of living adjustment, however, the
Board was concerned about lower level salaried employees and proposed that a
tier plan be designed to make the adjustments more equitable. Ms. Bray, Finance
Director presented the following tier chart for Board consideration plan for
Board consideration:
                         $70,000 - 100,000 - 1%
                             55,000 - 70,000 - 2%
                             40,000 - 55,000 - 2.5
                                               25,000 - 40,000 - 4%
Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to approve the tier chart
and cost of living increases to be effective August 1, 2013. The vote was
unanimous.
Rescue Squad Ambulance –City Manager Gandy asked for clarification on
directives to proceed with the process to acquire a new ambulance for the
Rescue Squad. After brief discussion, motion by Alderman Coring, seconded by
Alderman Karn to direct staff to begin the process of acquiring a new ambulance
in accordance with the proposal submitted by Chief Johnson, for one new Taylor
made 170” module 2012 GMC G4500 diesel chassis at a cost of $121,985.00 with
first payment to begin July 14-15. The vote of approval was unanimous. (Note:
This price is valid if ordered by July 28, and subject to prior sale, 6 months
build time)
City Manager Selection Process – Alderman Poole asked the Board to review
applications for the City Manager’s position and each Alderman select ten
applicants for consideration. (Applications located in the Mayor’s office) The
Board will recess the meeting to August 26, 6:00 p.m. at which time the
applications will be reviewed.
Police Department Computers – The Board discussed computers for police
vehicles, which were taken out of the budget. City Manager Gandy stated that
four computers could be paid from the contingency fund. Chief Dove told the
Board that the computers would speed up processing and locating stolen
vehicles, etc. Alderman Coring stated the need for the computers in the Police
vehicles.
Alderman Barnes moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to allocate $8,541.52 to
purchase four computers for the Police Department and the monthly charge for
the wireless cards be taken from the Police Department communications fund.
Vote of approval was unanimous.
Maritime Museum – Mayor Howard referenced the proposal to expand the Maritime
Museum, in which the City needs to relocate the storage units located behind
the museum. He previously asked Ms. Hemphill, Director of Parks and Recreation
to come up with a proposal and costs associated with the relocation. She
advised that it would be more cost effective to build a storage facility at a
cost of $5200. Alderman Barnes questioned who would disassemble the old units.
Alderman Adams recommended contacting Sunny Point and suggested Alderman Poole
make the contact.
Alderman Coring stated that he did not want to see storage units placed behind
the City Gym because children use that area and the Art Gallery is located near
that vicinity. City Manager Gandy stated that staff would look for another
location.
Alderman Karn moved, seconded by Alderman Poole to approve up to $5200 for a
storage facility and the location to be approved by staff. Vote unanimous.
Surplus Equipment – City Manager Gandy and Robert Tucker, Director of Public
Services told the Board of the proposal to work with the State Surplus Division
to dispose of City surplus property for an 8% auction fee. Mr. Tucker explained
that this was recommended because of the specialized equipment from the
Wastewater Treatment Plant and being in a larger auction pool will give more
visibility and a better chance of selling the equipment.
Alderman Adams and Coring opposed paying an 8% fee when the City has held its
own auctions in the past.
Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to accept the recommendation
of staff and authorized using state surplus for an 8% fee. Votes were 4 ayes,
Aldermen Powell, Karn, Poole and Barnes. 2 noes, Alderman Coring and Adams.
Recycling – City Manager Gandy gave the Board additional information on
expanding curbside recycling and the associated costs.
Employees Benefit Package – Mayor Howard stated the Board might wish to have a
meeting later to review the employees benefit package. City Manager Gandy noted
that the health insurance costs is up to 28%.
Death - The Board acknowledged the passing of Ms. Cathy Fravel, a long time
City volunteer.
Recess - 7:35 p.m. Mayor Howard recessed the meeting until Monday, August 26,
2013, 6:00 p.m. at which time the Board will meet and review applications for
the position of City Manager.

·   Resolution honoring S. Ellis Hankins upon his retirement from the League as
Executive Director
RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT
WHEREAS, S. Ellis Hankins, Executive Director of the North Carolina League of
Municipalities, a leader in municipal government and leadership for nearly
thirty years, has announced his retirement; and
WHEREAS, S. Ellis Hankins began his career with the League in October, 1982 as
Assistant General Counsel and was promoted to Associate General Counsel; and
WHEREAS, S. Ellis Hankins was promoted to General Counsel and chief legislative
lobbyist in 1987 and served in that position until departing the League staff
in 1994; and
WHEREAS, S. Ellis Hankins returned to the North Carolina League of
Municipalities as its Executive Director in 1997; and
WHEREAS, S. Ellis Hankins is only the fifth full-time Executive Director of the
North Carolina League of Municipalities in the 105-year history of the
membership association representing nearly every municipality in the State of
North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, the work of S. Ellis Hankins benefitted the citizens of the cities and
towns in the State of North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, S. Ellis Hankins has worked to promote good government in North
Carolina through the League’s offering non-partisan advocacy, insurance, and
other services as directed by the membership.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that they hereby honor S. Ellis Hankins, of the North Carolina League
of Municipalities for faithful service and lasting contributions to municipal
government.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this resolution be made a part of the permanent
records of the City of Southport and that copies be forwarded to S. Ellis
Hankins.
DULY RESOLVED THIS THE 12 th Day of September 2013.
                                                                                                                                        
/s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander
City Clerk

·   Proclamation recognizing September 2013 as National Senior Center Month
National Senior Center Month
Proclamation
Whereas, older Americans are significant members of our society, investing
their wisdom and experience to help enrich and better the lives of younger
generations; and
Whereas, the Brunswick Center at Southport has acted as a catalyst for
mobilizing the creativity, energy, vitality, and commitment of the older
residents of Southport, North Carolina; and
Whereas, through the wide array of services, programs, and activities, senior
centers empower older citizens of Southport and surrounding communities to
contribute to their own health and well-being and the health and well-being of
their fellow citizens of all ages; and
Whereas, the Brunswick Center at Southport affirms the dignity, self-worth, and
independence of older persons by facilitating their decisions and actions;
tapping their experiences, skills, and knowledge; and enabling their continued
contributions to the community;
Now, Therefore, I Robert D. Howard, Mayor and the Southport Board of Aldermen
of the City of Southport, North Carolina proclaim September 2013 as National
Senior Center Month; and
Whereas, we   call upon all citizens to recognize the special contributions of
the Senior Center of Southport, its participants, and the specials efforts of
staff and volunteers who work every day to enhance the well-being of the older
citizens of Southport and surrounding communities.
ADOPTED, this the 12th day of September 2013.
                      /s/ Robert D. Howard
                           Mayor

·   Proclamation of Support in Honor of the 2013 Warrior Ride.
PROCLAMATION
Of Support in Honor of the 2013 Warrior Ride
Whereas, Warriors helping Warriors is an organization to foster the most
successful, well-adjusted generation of wounded service members in our nation's
history, and
Whereas, this organization was established to raise awareness and enlist the
public’s aid for the needs of injured service members, and
Whereas, the Warriors Organization help injured service members aid and assist
each other; and
Whereas, Warriors help to provide unique programs and services to meet the
needs of injured service members; and
Whereas, the Warrior Ride is a non-profit 501(c) 3 organization that uses
adaptive bicycling and other morale building events as a tool for recreation
and rehabilitation for our wounded heroes, and
Whereas, the 2013 Warrior Ride is slated for arrival in Carolina Beach, NC on
October 2, 2013, and
Whereas, October 3rd at 10:00 a.m. the cyclists will board the N.C. Ferry to
Southport N.C., and
Whereas, the Warrior riders will make a brief stop at the Southport Waterfront
Park and soon afterwards will journey to other towns and communities in
Brunswick County.
NOW THEREFORE, I Robert D. Howard, Mayor of Southport, NC and the Board of
Aldermen proclaim “The Warrior Ride 2013 Day”  in the City of Southport and
encourage citizens to come out in support of these brave service members.
This 13th day of September 2013.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina W. Alexander, Clerk
5. APPROVAL OF AGENDA
   Alderman Karn moved to approve the agenda with the following amendments:

NEW BUSINESS
Second Reading – Southport Maritime Museum Expansion Project
   Alderman Powell stated that tourism is a $14 billion industry in North
Carolina and cited the number of tourists who visited the museum during the
height of the tourist season and believes the city should form a partnership
with the Friends of the Maritime Museum.
   Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to approve the second
reading of a proposal by the Friends of the Maritime Museum to allow the
expansion of the existing museum facility by 2,079 square feet. The vote was
unanimous.
   Attorney Isenberg stated the third reading would grant final approval for
the expansion project.
Review and approval of FEMA disaster prepositioning contracts: Phillips &
Jordan Inc., and Johnston Environmental & Disaster Consulting
   Mr. Tucker, Public Services Director told the Board that in order to
expedite cleanup after a major disaster. Bids were solicited in accordance with
FEMA guidelines for prepositioning service contracts for Disaster Debris
Clearance and Removal Services and Disaster Debris Monitoring Services. Request
for proposals were solicited from 22 firms. Six (6) firms responded and one
proposal received for Debris Monitoring Services. Staff recommended that the
prepositioning contract be awarded to Phillips and Jordan, Inc., Robbinsville,
NC for Debris Clearance and Removal and to Johnston Environmental & Disaster
Consulting Services, Wilmington NC for Disaster Debris Monitoring Services. The
recommendation was based on the capability of each firm to perform i.e. scope
of services, personnel, equipment and financial strength. Mr. Tucker noted in
the case of a natural disaster, it would be written in their contract that
local contractors would be hired.
   Alderman Powell stated he is familiar with the company and they are a FEMA
approved contractor.
   Alderman Adams voiced opposition to hiring outside contractors when local
contractors are capable of performing the same work.
   Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Karn to accept staff’s
recommendation to hire Phillips and Jordan, Inc., of Robbinsville, NC for
Debris Clearance and Removal and Johnston Environmental & Disaster Consulting
Services,   Wilmington NC for Disaster Debris Monitoring Services.  Votes: 4
ayes, Aldermen Powell, Karn, Coring and Poole. 2 noes, Aldermen Adams and
Barnes. Motion passed    (Contracts Incorporated as Attachment #1)
Drainage, Site Distance and Parking Improvements to the 100 block of South
Davis Street
   Mr. Tucker explained by showing a schematic of the several drainage issues
in the 100 block of Davis Street where water runs off and does not drain
properly, which erode the driveways. He also stated parked cars along the
street have created access problems for residents. He proposed to cut shallow
swales in areas where there are driveways, post no parking signs, which would
give the residents some place to park, and make parking along East Bay and
Davis Street intersection parallel parking to alleviate site distance at the
intersection.
   Mayor Howard stated eliminating parking is suspect, No Parking Signs have
been erected in that area and the major traffic is on East Bay. Mr. Tucker
stated that the proposed configuration would not alleviate any parking.
   Alderman Adams stated that there are drainage problems in Ward II between
Lord, Owens and Leonard Streets. Mr. Tucker explained that the drainage is
stopped up from Clarendon and they are currently working on this situation.
   Alderman Karn moved to approve the project per staff’s recommendation,
seconded by Alderman Powell. Discussion:  Alderman Adams reiterated that Ward
II be given the same consideration as projects in Ward I. Alderman Poole stated
that she would like more time to review the project to get a better
understanding. Votes were 4 ayes, Karn, Powell, Barnes and Coring. 2 noes,
Poole and Adams. Motion passed

Film Industry: Alderman Poole reported that she attended a meeting in

towns. They discussed film incentives and the economic boost derived from the

film incentives not being supported by the North Carolina General Assembly and
the effect it would have on jobs and the economy. She reported that Senator
Rabon and Representative Iler attended the meeting and Senator Rabon supports
the film industry and incentives.

2.   Review and approval of Resolution authorizing the purchase 0f a 2012
Taylor made GMC 4500 Ambulance through the North Central EMS cooperative
purchasing program
Alderman Coring moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to adopt the resolution
authorizing the purchase of a 2012 Taylor made GMC 4500 Ambulance through the
North Central EMS cooperative purchasing program and to authorize the City
Manager to solicit bids from a financial institution for a five-year
installment financing agreement. Vote unanimous. Motion passed
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE PURCHASE OF A 2012 TAYLOR MADE GMC 4500 AMBULANCE
FROM FIRST CLASS OF MONROE, NORTH CAROLINA FOR $119,985 THROUGH THE NORTH
CENTRAL EMS COOPERATIVE PURCHASING PROGRAM AS AUTHORIZED UNDER NORTH CAROLINA
GENERAL STATUE 143-129(e)(3)
WHEREAS, The City of Southport has determined that its current 2002 E-450 has
surpassed its anticipated lifespan and is in need of replacement; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport desires to purchase a replacement ambulance in
order to continue providing life-saving emergency and rescue services to the
citizens and residents of the area; and
WHEREAS, N.C. General Statute 143-129 (e) (3) provides an exception to the
requirements of Chapter 143, Article 8, for purchases made through a
competitive bidding group purchasing program which is a formally organized
program that offers competitively obtained purchasing services at discount
prices for two or more public agencies; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has contacted THE NORTH CENTRAL EMS COOPERATIVE,
a competitive purchasing program as authorized under General Statute 143-129
(e)( 3), seeking their assistance in acquiring an ambulance using
specifications to meet the City’s needs; and
WHEREAS, NCEMSC has completed the bidding process with manufacturers and Taylor
Made offering a 2012 and
WHEREAS, the Southport Board of Aldermen has determined that it is in the best
interest of the City of Southport to waive the normal formal bidding
requirements of NCGS 143-129 in order to purchase said equipment in accordance
with these cooperative purchasing programs.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen,
that:
1.   The City waives the formal bidding provisions of N.C.G.S. 143-129; and
2.   The Board authorizes the City Manager to execute documents required to
purchase one Taylor
Made ambulance per submitted specifications from First Class through THE NORTH
CENTRAL
EMS COOPERATIVE Purchasing Program in the amount of $119,985 pursuant to
N.C.G.S. 143-129(e) (3) and
3.   The Board authorizes the City Manager to solicit for and accept bids from
qualified financing institutions prior to the completion of the build process
for a 5 year installment financing agreement for the full $119,985 purchase
price in FY 2013-2014, with the first annual installment payable in FY 2014-
2015; and to bring the suggested finance package back to the Board for final
approval.
DULY ADOPTED THIS 30th DAY OF SEPTEMBER, 2013
/s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:
/s/ Regina Alexander, City Clerk

5.   Other Business
   Powell Bill - Mayor Howard asked for a financial accounting of Powell Bill
funds from the Finance Director.
   Fire Department Funds: Mayor Howard and the Board discussed transferring
approximately $190,000 from the Fire Station Construction fund for the purpose
of City Hall renovations. Chief Cumbee told the Board that there is
approximately $80,000 worth of work that remains to be completed at the fire
headquarters. Mr. Cumbee stated that it is his understanding that the fire fee
money can only be used for matters pertaining to fire departments. He
acknowledged that the Board may wish to seek a legal opinion on whether the
monies can be used for purposes other than fire department matters.
   Alderman Coring stated that it is his opinion the funds should be used for
the fire department or apply it towards paying off the debt.
   Mayor Howard stated perhaps the monies should be used to pay down the City’s
debt and borrow the money for City Hall renovations since there may be a legal
question of how and what the money can be used for.
   Alderman Karn moved, seconded by Alderman Powell to allocate $189,952 (as of
8/31/13 financial report) from the Fire Station Construction fund minus the
$80,000 that will be used to complete the remaining work at the fire
department, and to apply $109, 952 towards reducing the City’s debt on the Fire
Department. Vote unanimous.
   Lord Street Gym Funding: Mayor Howard informed the Board that the Lord
Street Gym Committee was appointed to discuss the feasibility of the gym and
its use. The Committee, chaired by Alderman Adams is requesting $2200 in seed
money plus reimbursable expenses to hire a licensed engineer to determine the
feasibility and structural integrity of the gym.
   Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to allocate $2200 and
reimbursable expenses to the Lord Street Gym Committee for the purpose of
hiring an engineer to perform a study on the gym and to authorize the City
Manager to work with the Committee. (Funds to be disbursed from Board
Contingency) Discussion: Alderman Karn stated the money would put the program
in a good place. The vote was unanimous.

6.   Proclamation –Vision Awareness Month October 2013
   Proclamation read by Alderman Barnes and presented to Lions Club members by
Mayor Howard and Aldermen.
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/
IMAGES/0-0-0-1581_1271x1119.jpg]
 
Vision Awareness Month
Proclamation
Southport Lions Club
  WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club is working to increase vision awareness,
especially among the youth through vision screening at local schools, and
  WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club collected over 1,500 pairs of glasses in
the past twelve months and provides assistance to those needing but unable to
afford eye tests and the purchase of glasses, and
  WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club will conduct vision screening the fourth
Thursday of each month at the New Hope Clinic and the Brunswick County Health
Festival in September, and
  WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club continues to keep with the challenge Helen
Keller issued to the association in 1929 to become “knights of the blind in the
crusade against darkness,” and
  WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club, established in 1945 is composed of men and
women volunteers who dedicate their time to the betterment of our community and
aiding those in need, and
  NOW THEREFORE, I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC and
the Board of Aldermen in recognition of this important service sponsored by the
Southport Lions Club, do hereby proclaim October as Vision awareness month.
Adopted October 10, 2013.
                                                         S/Robert D. Howard
                        Mayor, City of Southport, NC
Attest:
S/Regina W. Alexander, City Clerk

10. Review and approval of Ordinance approving text amendments to the Unified

   Alderman Barnes motioned, seconded by Alderman Karn to approve the Ordinance
with text amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance as findings set forth
in the Ordinance. The vote of approval was unanimous.
AN ORDINANCE APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENTS TO THE UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, City Staff, in conjunction with the Planning Board, has prepared
proposed amendments to Article 2, Article 10 and Article 12 of the Southport
Unified Development Ordinance; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and find
the proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance to be consistent
with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommend their
approval; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on October 10, 2013, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby find that these
proposed amendments to Articles 2, 10 and 12 of the Unified Development
Ordinance are consistent with the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) these amendments are
necessary in order to promote efficiency in the administration of the Unified
Development Ordinance, and (ii) the amendments are reasonable and necessary to
correct and/or clarify inconsistencies that presently exist within the Unified
Development Ordinance.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments to Articles 2, 10 and 12 of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted.
      This, the 10th day of October 2013.
                     City of Southport
                     By: S/ Robert D. Howard
