Section 1.   ARTICLE 2. BASIC DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS, Section 2.2
“Definitions of Basic Terms” is hereby amended by adding the following
definition in the appropriate alphabetical sequence.
   Modular Unit. A factory built structure that is designed and built in one or
more components or sections that are transported to a site. Plans and
specifications shall bear an engineer’s seal and a third party inspection
certification and/or meet any successor regulations as may be established under
the N.C. State Building Code.
  Section 2.   ARTICLE 10. TABLE OF PERMITTED USES
(a)   The Table of Permitted Uses is hereby amended by replacing the Table
heading, “Business Services, Not elsewhere classified” with the heading
“Business, commercial or other non-residential use, not elsewhere classified”;
 and deleting the Table headings “Business services, not elsewhere classified,
without outside sales or storage and its accompanying supplemental regulations
in Section 12-19 (B) (4); “Amusement and Recreational Services, not elsewhere
classified”; “Social Services, not elsewhere classified” and “Retail Stores,
not classified elsewhere” and its accompanying supplemental regulations in
Section 12-19 (B) (36), in their entirety.
(b)   The Table of Permitted Uses is further amended by adding in the
appropriate alphabetical sequence under the “Residential Housing Types” section
of the Table, “Residential Cluster Development” and by placing a “C” in the R-
20, R-10 and PUD columns and by placing the following language in the
Supplemental Regulations column “Refer to Article 15”.
(c)   The Table of Permitted Uses is further amended by placing a “C” under the
Table heading “Research and Development” within the CBD column.
(d)   The Table of Permitted Uses is further amended by replacing the Table
heading, “Manufactured Home (individual) for Office or Exhibition” with the
heading “Modular Unit”.
Section 3.   ARTICLE 12. ZONING AND CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT APPROVAL, Section
12-19, “Supplemental Regulations” (4) and (26) are hereby amended as follows:
   (4)  Business services, commercial or other non-residential use, not
elsewhere classified. The business service must be an accessory use of the
property and not the principal use.
(a)   The Board of Adjustment must find that the proposed use will be similar
in character and intensity to other permitted or conditional uses provided for
within the district in which it is proposed. Such determination shall be noted
as a finding of fact and shall be included in the record of the final
disposition of the application.
(b)   The property shall be located on a collector or higher classified street
as designated on the City of Southport Thoroughfare Plan.
(c)   Any proposed outdoor operations, inventory display and/or storage must be
specifically approved by the Board of Adjustment who may establish any
additional conditions as may be determined necessary. Such conditions may
include, but shall not be limited to: screening, buffering, increased setbacks
or other appropriate conditions up to and including denial of such proposed
outdoor use for the location sought for due cause in order to protect, maintain
or promote the general public, health, safety and welfare. Such due cause shall
be noted as a finding of fact and shall be included in the record of the final
disposition of the application.
(d)   Parking and/or loading requirements shall be those noted for the use most
closely associated with the proposed use as listed in Section 16-3 as
determined by the Board of Adjustment in conjunction with staff review and
recommendation.
(e)   The Board of Adjustment shall reasonably consider and may require the
establishment of appropriate hours of operation for the proposed use should
they determine such limitation to be appropriate in order to protect, maintain
or promote the general public health, safety and welfare.
(f)   The Board of Adjustment shall consider and may require any additional
relevant time, place and manner conditions or restrictions as may be deemed
appropriate for the location sought for due cause in order to protect, maintain
or promote the general public health, safety and welfare. Such due cause shall
be noted as a finding of fact and shall be included in the record of the final
disposition of the application.
   (26)   Manufactured Home (Individual)   Modular Unit; for Office and/
or Exhibition.   Permanent/Temporary Placement Standards.
                   Modular units to be utilized for office or classroom use
must have been originally constructed for such use and shall not be a renovated
or modified manufactured home. Plans and specifications shall bear an
engineer’s seal and a third party inspection certification. The modular unit
must have a permanent foundation and conditional use approval if it is meant to
be located on site as a permanent fixture.
         (a)   Parking. One (1) space for each person employed in the office at
any given time during a twenty-four (24) hour period plus four (4) spaces for
visitors.
         (b)   Requirements. A temporary certificate of occupancy/compliance,
allowing manufactured homes   modular units   to be  used solely as offices or
for purposes of exhibition to be temporarily parked, maintained, and/or
occupied   for permanent stand-alone office space and to be located  on a
designated lot or land location, may be issued by the supervisor of inspection
services or his authorized agents where the Board of Adjustment finds as a fact
that the use of such manufactured home   modular unit  does not violate the
city or state building, electrical, or plumbing codes, or health regulations
and will comply with the provisions of this ordinance in all other respects.
  All such certificates of occupancy/compliance shall be valid for a period of
twelve (12) months, after which they may be renewed upon similar evidence of
use of such manufactured home.
         (c)   Notwithstanding the foregoing, a temporary certificate of
occupancy/compliance may be issued for a manufactured home  modular unit for
use as a temporary field office for contractors by the Administrator or his
authorized agents without approval of the Board of Adjustment, if the
manufactured home  modular unit :
            (i)   And the structure under construction are located on the same
property;
            (ii)   Is not moved to the site more than 30 days prior to
construction and is not removed not  later than 30 days after construction has
been completed;
            (iii)   Is not used for any other purpose other than that connected
with on-site construction;
            (iv)   Is justified by the size and nature of the construction
project;
            (v)   Is to be used for a period not to generally  exceed 18
months; with subsequent annual renewals permissible upon demonstrated continued
need;
            (vi)   Is utilized only incidental to on-site construction during
daylight hours and not for residential living quarters;
            (vii)   Is parked in a location approved in advance by the
Administrator or his authorized agents;
            (viii)   Sanitary facilities are connected with an approved sewer
system unless an on-site port-a-john is provided ;
            (ix)   Electrical facilities are connected in compliance with
regulations as set forth in the North Carolina State Building Code.
         (d)    Also notwithstanding the foregoing, a certificate of occupancy/
compliance may be issued for a manufactured home   modular unit  for use as a
manufactured classroom by a public or private school, for a school
administrative manufactured office, and  or for a manufactured home sales
office without approval of the Board of Adjustment, if the manufactured home 
following requirements are met :
            (i)   Sanitary facilities are connected with an approved sewer
system;
            (ii)   Electrical facilities are connected in compliance with
regulations as set forth in the North Carolina State Building Code;
            (iii)   Provisions pertaining to a manufactured home  modular unit
foundation and anchorage of the manufactured home to the foundation, as
contained in the State of North Carolina Regulations for Manufactured Homes,
2004 edition, are adhered to. shall be as provided in the NC State Building
Code or its successor document.
11. Discussion regarding the vendor portion of the Charles Dickens Festival
   Mayor Howard informed the Board that three business owners expressed concern
about vendors during the Charles Dickens Festival and he asked staff, with
concurrence from the City Manager, to conduct a poll of area businesses to
gauge their input.
   Ms. Cindy Brochure, Director of Tourism reported that 38 businesses were
polled and two questions asked. Eighty-seven (87%) acknowledged that they had
seen an increase in revenues in 2012 and 13% stated there was no increase. The
second question was whether events benefit Southport businesses including those
events that rely on vendor participation. 82% yes, 18% no because of issues
with the City not having festival guidelines.
   Alderman Barnes stated that Southport is beautiful at Christmas and he does
not want to see festivals turned into the Fourth of July with food vendors.
Mayor Howard stated that vendors would locate only in Franklin Square Park.
Alderman Coring stated it is his opinion what is done for one festival, should
be done for all. The festival had a few vendors last year in Franklin Square
Park and he does not believe that it was a big cost to the City because
Brunswick Electric brought in generators. Alderman Adams stated that he has not
seen an event held in the City where it did not cost money. Mayor Howard noted
that an e-mail was sent to the Board and City Manager stating that 60 vendors
would locate in Franklin Square Park. Alderman Karn suggested that the City
might consider writing a policy governing festivals so that everything can be
spelled out specifically as to what is taking place. Mayor Howard stated that
the festival is functioning on the authority previously given.
   Attorney Isenberg informed the Board that the City has an ordinance, which
requires vendors to apply for permits. (Article IV, Section 16-98) Charles
Dickens Festival would be governed by the same ordinance as other festivals.
The Board concurred that staff proceed with the Charles Dickens Committee as
before. Alderman Adams stated the Board might wish to look at how festivals are
governed, since there is some ambiguity concerning this festival. Mayor Howard
stated that e-mails were sent to the Board and City Manager. Chief Dove in
answer to Alderman Barnes question stated that the festival would provide its
own security.
12. Update from Robert Tucker on disposal of surplus equipment
   Mr. Robert Tucker, Public Services Director told the Board that Donna Boyan
had been trained on the state surplus system and upon entering data, it was
discovered that the exchange of vehicle titles needed to occur before the state
would list the items for sale. It was also discovered that three vehicle titles
were missing and the City is in the process of applying for replacement titles.
The State was given a directive to proceed with auctioning items where the
paper work is in order. He stated that everything should be posted by October
9, and the auction concluded by October 23.
   Mayor Howard asked that the surplus disposition update be placed on the
November agenda.
13. Presentation by Ms. Mary Friend, Beautification Committee
   Ms. Mary Friend, Chairperson of the Beautification Committee proposed a once
a month cleanup program to be held the first Saturday in each month from 9:00
a.m. until 12 noon, titled “ this is our Town” and asked for Board endorsement.
She asked for $100 seed money for bags, gloves, and to purchase plants. City
Manager Gandy announced that a $100 donation had been made and the City will
provide the gloves and bags. Announcements will be placed on the utility bill
and City’s website.
14. Appointment – Southport Beautification Committee
   Alderman Barnes moved to appoint Harry Burrell to the Beautification
Committee, seconded by Alderman Karn, vote unanimous.
15. Other Business

and recommended the following streets be re-surfaced. (Estimated cost: $175,000
/ Powell Bill balance of 10/10/13, $192,000)
·   Clarendon Ave from Hankins Dr to 9th Street
·   E. Stuart from Holly to Highland
·   E. Stuart from Highland to Atlantic
·   W. Leonard from Lord to Caswell
·   E. Nash from Frink to Willis Dr

·   N. Atlantic from Nash to West
·   N. Lord from 11th to 12th Street
·   Caswell between 8th & 9th
·   E. Nash from Howe to Atlantic (excluding parking)

Coring, Powell and Karn. 1 no, Alderman Barnes
   Alderman Powell told the Board that he was approached by some citizens about
resurfacing 9th street, which is a state road. The Committee will submit a
request asking the State Department of Transportation to include 9th Street in
their resurfacing program.
    Alderman Adams asked that sidewalk recommendations be placed on the
November agenda for consideration.

advertise for bids, which should be no more than a three-month process.
   Alderman Adams commented that Short Street was taken off the list, which was
recommended by Alderman Barnes and asked for an explanation. Alderman Powell
explained that Nash was pulled from the list last year but was placed back on
because it is heavily traveled by postal customers and citizens. He stated that
there were other roads/streets that needs re-surfacing and there is the
possibility that they can be picked up with the next round of resurfacing
16. Other Comments
      Mayor Howard explained that the City Hall project was closed in late
February 2013 and the City Manager was directed to move forward with the
project. Mr. Gandy was hired as Interim City Manager and his priority was the
budget and audit. June 2013, Mr. Gandy informed the Board that he would not
seek the full time position of City Manager, therefore; the Board charged the
Building Committee to move forward with the project. Connie Keller was employed
to perform the space analysis in late July, which was approved at the September
meeting. The City Manager is in the process of getting the interior offices
painted and the furniture needs are being completed to move into the building.
This project has not caused any expense to the City because the buildings are
owned by the City. The City does receive approximately $84,000 - 85,000
annually in rental income for the 1029 building. The process has not moved as
expeditiously as it should have and moving should begin in November.
      Interim City Manager Gandy reported that the leaky roof on the current
City Hall is being repaired.

   Alderman Adams moved to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Alderman Powell,
vote unanimous.

12.   Public forum with representatives from Bald Head Island
    Mayor Howard announced that representatives from Bald Head Island were
present to give a presentation and answer questions concerning the waterfront
and wakes caused by the BHI Ferry boats, which is a contributor to erosion of
the waterfront.
   Present were Chad Paul, CEO of Bald Head Island Ltd., Claude McKernan,
Manager Bald Head Island Transportation, Inc. and Joyce Fulton, Director of
Communications, Bald Head Island Limited, LLC. A power point presentation was
shown addressing wake concerns. It was noted that all boats create wakes
depending on the size of the vessels, but BHI captains are usually blamed for
creating the wakes. Mr. McKernan explained that passing vessels also create
wakes while stating that most erosion occurs naturally. The shore along
Southport from Deep Point to the City pier is stable; but has eroded and
accreted many times over the years, while explaining that the lift station
beach was more vulnerable to wakes from their ferry operations out of Indigo.
He stated that they operate the same or greater speeds passing Caswell and no
erosion is apparent. He stated that Bald Head Island wants to continue being
good neighbors and shared with the Board their mitigation efforts: 1) Vessel
Masters know that they are responsible for their wake. 2) Route planning takes
wake into classification; a) current factors, flood or ebb, b) distance, stay
across river, 600 yards, c) approaches, effective, d) speed, balance schedule,
wake, fuel, 3) fuel consideration efforts aid in reducing wake and schematic
and explanation of their route.
   Several people spoke about the erosion and cited their bulkheads as examples
of erosion over the years, which the wakes from the Bald Head Island Ferry has
caused much of the problem. Nancy Crouch, 234 River Drive, Mary Ann Powell
(Landing), Robert Bach (Landing), Dora Loughlin, East Bay Street, Paul Fisher,
River Drive stated the City has been requesting assistance since 1987 and he
has lost 40-60 feet of marsh grass. Erosion is a problem in the City, some of
it can be controlled and some cannot. He cited three things for the Board to
consider; encourage organizations to get involved, follow-up with the Corp of
Engineers on completing a study of erosion along the riverfront, seek help from
the North Carolina Beach and Inlet Waterway Association, which the City is a
member of the organization. Julie Simpson of the Landing spoke about the waves
crashing around her bulkhead and she can pinpoint the time of day the ferry is
passing. Bill Herring stated rip rap should be placed along the waterfront, Al
Wilson of the Landing, stated catamaran wake causes erosion, and Dr. Brad
Hilaman of 612 River Drive addressed his concerns with the wakes from the
Ferry. Wayne Strickland stated that the Cape Fear Pilots should take some of
the blame because it is not only Bald Head Island Ferry causing the problems
and the City should press the Corp of Engineers for assistance.
   Mr. Roy Daniels of West Bay Street presented a power point presentation with
visuals on the course of erosion over the years along the waterfront.
   Alderman Powell stated that Bald Head Island also gets erosion from ship
traffic and the City needs to join forces to work with the Corp to find a
solution for its waterfront erosion.
   Mayor Howard noted that this situation is serious enough to warrant looking
at positions in City Government the first of the year to determine its
priorities and to consider the waterfront erosion problem.
Executive Session pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11 (6) – 9:10 p.m.
   Alderman Coring moved to enter closed session, seconded by Alderman Powell,
vote unanimous.
Regular Session Reconvened – 9:30 p.m.
   Alderman Powell moved to re-enter regular session, seconded by Alderman
Childs, vote unanimous.
   Mayor Howard announced that the Board gave City Manager McDuffie directives
to proceed with contract negotiations. The Board discussed and unanimously
agreed to give City Clerk Regina Alexander a $15,000 salary adjustment
effective January 1 through December 2014 due to special projects, she has
committed to complete before retiring the end of 2014.
   Salary Adjustment:  Alderman Powell moved, seconded by Alderman Barnes to
approve the $15,000 salary adjustment for City Clerk Regina Alexander. The vote
of approval was unanimous.
   Employee Christmas Bonuses: Alderman Barnes motioned, seconded by Alderman
Powell to give full time City employees $175 and part time employees $125
Christmas bonuses. The vote of approval was unanimous.
   Board Retreat: The Board scheduled January 18, 2014, 8:00 a.m. for the
annual board retreat. (Fire Department headquarters – EOC Room)
   Waterfront Project: Mayor Howard stated that the Board would need to hire a
professional to work on the waterfront project and recommended a meeting with
the Corp of Engineers’ representative because the project needs to move
forward.
   ElectriCities CEO Bonus: Alderman Barnes stated opposition to the CEO of
ElectriCities (Graham Edwards) being given a $50,000 bonus and do not believe
the citizens of Southport supports this decision by the ElectriCities Board.
Alderman Barnes moved, seconded by Alderman Adams to adopt a resolution
opposing the $50,000 bonus. Discussion:  Alderman Powell noted that Mr. Graham
was rewarded for doing an outstanding job and saving millions of dollars by
stabilizing rates. Alderman Coring stated that he needed more information
before voting on a resolution. Votes were 4 ayes, Aldermen Barnes, Adams, Poole
and Childs. 2 noes, Aldermen Powell and Coring. Motion passed.  City Manager
McDuffie was asked to draft a resolution opposing the $50,000 bonus.

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been petitioned under G.S. 160A-58.1 to
annex the area described below; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at Southport City
Hall at 6:00 pm on January 9, 2014 after due notice by publication on December
25, 2013 and January 1, 2014; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the area described therein meets the
standards of G.S. 160A-58.1(b), to wit:
a.   The nearest point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is not more
than three
(3) miles from the corporate limits of the (City/Town/Village);
b.   No point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is closer to another
municipality than to the City of Southport;
c.   The area described is so situated that the City of Southport will be able
to
provide the same services within the proposed satellite corporate limits that
it
provides within the primary corporate limits;
d.   No subdivision, as defined in G.S. 160A-376, will be fragmented by this
proposed
annexation;
e.   The City of Southport has a modification to the 10% limitation on the
total amount of satellite area by virtue of an act of the General Assembly; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the petition has been signed by all
the owners of real property in the area who are required by law to sign; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the petition is otherwise
valid, and that the public health, safety and welfare of the City of Southport
and of the area proposed for annexation will be best served by annexing the
area described;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina that:
Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-58.2, the following
described non
contiguous territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City of Southport,
North Carolina, as of the date hereof:
DESCRIPTION OF 1222 NORTH HOWE ST., SOUTHPORT, NC.

POINT BEING LOCATED N-20-25-56-W 125.65’ FROM A REBAR ON THE SOUTHERN RIGHT OF

AN ORDINANCE APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENTS TO THE UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
RELATING TO THE POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, City Staff, in conjunction with the Planning Board, has prepared
proposed amendments to Article 3, Article 5, Article 6, Article 7 and Article
12 of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance to promote and ensure
consistency with recent changes to the North Carolina General Statutes; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and find
the proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance to be consistent
with the North Carolina General Statues and the City of Southport CAMA Core
Land Use Plan and recommend their approval; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on January 9th, 2014, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby find that these
proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with
the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) they are necessary in order
to ensure consistency with recent changes to North Carolina General Statutes
related to the powers and duties of the Board of Adjustment, and (ii) the
amendments are reasonable and necessary to correct and/or clarify
inconsistencies and redundancies that presently exist or would exist within the
Unified Development Ordinance if not corrected concurrently with the proposed
amendments.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments to Articles 3, 5, 6, 7 and 12 of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted.
This, the 9th day of January 2014.            
                     City of Southport
                     By: S/Robert D.
Howard                                    Mayor
ATTEST:
S/Regina W. Alexander, Clerk
Section 1.   Repeal Sections 3-16 and 3-17 of Part II, of Article 3,
“ADMINISTRATIVE MECHANISMS” of          the UDO in their entirety.
Section 2.   Amend Article 5 of the UDO as follows:
ARTICLE 5.   APPEALS, VARIANCES, INTERPRETATIONS
Section 5-1:   Appeals
(A)   An appeal from any final order or decision of the administrator  official
may be taken to the Board of Adjustment by any person aggrieved party who has
standing under G.S. 160A-393(d).    The official who made the decision shall
give written notice to the owner of the property and the party who sought the
decision, if different.   An appeal is taken by filing with the administrator
official and the Board of Adjustment a written notice of appeal specifying the
grounds therefor. A notice of appeal, specifying the grounds therefor, shall be
considered filed with the administrator  official  and the Board of Adjustment
when delivered to the planning department  city clerk , and the date and time
of filing shall be entered on the notice by the planning staff clerk .
(B)   An appeal must be taken within   The owner or other party shall have  30
days after  from  the date of the decision or order appealed from  receipt of a
written final, binding determination by the official to file an appeal. The
written notice shall be delivered by personal delivery, electronic mail, or by
first class mail. Any other person with standing to appeal shall have 30 days
from the receipt of any source of actual or constructive notice of the decision
to file an appeal.
(C)   Whenever an appeal is filed, the administrator  official shall forthwith
transmit to the Board of Adjustment all the papers, documents and exhibits
constituting the record relating to the action appealed from, with a copy
provided to the appellant and land owner, if the landowner is not the appellant
.
(D)   An appeal stays all actions by the administrator official seeking
enforcement of or compliance with the order or decision appealed from, unless
the administrator official certifies by affidavit to the Board of Adjustment
after an appeal has been filed that (because of facts stated in the
certificate) because of the facts stated in an affidavit, a stay would, in his
opinion, cause imminent peril to life or property or because the violation is
transitory in nature a stay would seriously interfere with enforcement of the
ordinance. In that case, proceedings shall not be stayed except by order of the
Board of Adjustment or  a restraining order, which may be granted by a court,
issued on application of the party seeking the stay, for due cause shown, after
notice to the administrator.. If enforcement proceedings are not stayed, the
appellant may file with the official a request for an expedited hearing of the
appeal, and the Board of Adjustment shall meet to hear the appeal within 15
days after such a request is filed. Notwithstanding the foregoing, appeals of
decisions granting a permit or otherwise affirming that a proposed use of
property is consistent with the ordinance shall not stay the further review of
an application for permits or permissions to use such property; in these
situations the appellant may request and the board may grant a stay of a final
decision of permit applications or building permits affected by the issue being
appealed.
(E)   The official who rendered the determination that has been appealed shall
appear at the hearing as a witness.  The Board of Adjustment may reverse or
affirm (wholly or partly) or may modify the order, requirement, decision, or
determination appealed from and shall make any order, requirement, decision, or
determination that in its opinion ought to be made in the case before it. To
this end the board shall have all the powers of the officer from whom the
appeal is taken. The board shall continue the hearing if new issues are
presented at the hearing that were not in the notice of appeal and immediate
consideration might unduly prejudice a party of interest or the city.
(F)   When hearing an appeal pursuant to G.S. 160a-400.9 (e) or other appeal in
the nature of certiorari, the hearing shall be based on the record below and
the scope of the review shall be as provided in G.S. 160A-393(k)
Section 5-2:   Variances
(A)   An application for a variance shall be submitted to the Board of
Adjustment by filing a copy of the application with the administrator in the
planning department. Applications shall be handled in the same manner as
applications for permits in conformity with the provisions of Sections 12-3 and
12-4.
(B)   When unnecessary hardships would result from carrying out the strict
letter of the UDO  A  a  variance may  shall  be granted by the Board of
Adjustment if it concludes that strict enforcement of the Ordinance would
result in practical difficulties or unnecessary hardships for the applicant and
that, by granting the variance, the spirit of the Ordinance will be observed,
public safety and welfare secured, and substantial justice done. It may reach
these conclusions if it finds that   upon a showing of the following :
(1)   If the applicant complies strictly with the provisions of the Ordinance,
he can make no reasonable use of his property; Unnecessary hardship would
result from a strict application of the ordinance. It shall not be necessary to
demonstrate that, in the absence of the variance, no reasonable use can be made
of the property.
(2)   The hardship of which the applicant complains is one suffered by the
applicant rather than by neighbors or the general public;   The hardship
results from conditions that are peculiar to the property, such as location,
size or topography. Hardships resulting from personal circumstances, as well as
hardships resulting from conditions that are common to the neighborhood or the
general public, may not be the basis for granting a variance.
(3)   The hardship relates to the applicant’s land, rather than personal
circumstances;  The hardship did not result from actions taken by the applicant
or property owner. The act of purchasing property with knowledge that
circumstances exist that might justify a variance shall not be considered as a
self-created hardship.
(4)   The hardship is unique, or nearly so, rather than one shared by many
surrounding properties;   The requested variance is consistent with the spirit,
purpose and intent of the ordinance, such that public safety is secured and
substantial justice achieved.
(5)   The hardship is not the result of the applicant’s own actions; and 
(6)   The variance will neither result in the extension of a nonconforming
situation in violation of Article 8 nor authorize the initiation of a
nonconforming use of land.
(C)   In granting variances, the Board of Adjustment may impose such reasonable
conditions as will ensure that the use of the property to which the variance
applies will be as compatible as practicable with the surrounding properties.
The concurring vote of four-fifths of the Board of Adjustment shall be
necessary to grant a variance. The majority of the members shall be necessary
to decide any other quasi-judicial matter or to determine an appeal in the
nature of certiorari. For these purposes, vacant positions on the board and
members who are disqualified from voting on a quasi-judicial matter shall not
be considered members of the board for calculation of the requisite majority if
there are no qualified alternates available.
(D)    Appropriate conditions, which must be reasonably related to the
condition or circumstance that gives rise to the need for a variance, may be
imposed on any approval  variance  issued by the Board of Adjustment.
(E)   No change in permitted uses may be authorized by variance.
(F)   A variance may be issued for an indefinite duration or for a specified
duration only.
(G)   The nature of the variance and any conditions attached to it shall be
entered on the face of the zoning permit, or the zoning permit may simply note
the issuance of the variance and refer to the written record of the variance
for further information. All such conditions are enforceable in the same manner
as any other applicable requirement of this Ordinance.
Section 5-3:   Interpretations
(A)   The Board of Adjustment is authorized to interpret the zoning map and to
pass upon disputed questions of lot lines or district boundary lines and
similar questions. If such questions arise in the context of an appeal from a
decision of the Administrator official , they shall be handled as provided in
Section 5-1 and Section 6-2.
(B)   An application for a map interpretation shall be submitted to the Board
of Adjustment by filing a copy of the application with the administrator
official in the planning department. The application shall contain sufficient
information to enable the board to make the necessary interpretation.
(C)   Where uncertainty exists as to the boundaries of districts as shown on
the Official Zoning Map, the following rules shall apply:
(1)   Boundaries indicated as approximately following the centerlines of
alleys, streets, highways, streams, or railroads shall be construed to follow
such centerline;
(2)   Boundaries indicated as approximately following lot lines, city limits,
or extraterritorial boundary lines, shall be construed as following such lines,
limits, or boundaries;
(3)   Boundaries indicated as following shorelines shall be construed to follow
such shorelines, and in the event of change in the shoreline shall be construed
as following such shorelines.
(4)   Where a district boundary divides a lot or where distances are not
specifically indicated on the Official Zoning Map, the boundary shall be
determined by measurement, using the scale of the Official Zoning Map;
(5)   Where any street or alley is hereafter officially vacated or abandoned,
the regulations applicable to each parcel of abutting property shall apply to
that portion of such street or alley added thereto by virtue of such vacation
or abandonment.
(D)   Interpretations of the location of floodway and floodplain boundary lines
may be made by the administrator  Floodplain Administrator  as provided in
Section 21-13(K).
Section 5-4:   Requests to be Heard Expeditiously within a Reasonable Time
As provided in Section 12-14, the  The  Board of Adjustment shall hear and
decide all appeals, variance requests, and requests for interpretations as
expeditiously as possible  within a reasonable time , consistent with the need
to follow regularly established agenda procedures, provide notice in accordance
with Article 6, and obtain the necessary information to make sound decisions.
Section 5-5:   Burden of Proof in Appeals and Variances
(A)   When an appeal is taken to the Board of Adjustment in accordance with
Section 5-1, the administrator  the official who rendered the binding decision
shall have the initial burden of presenting to the board sufficient evidence
and argument to justify the order or decision appealed from. The burden of
presenting evidence and argument to the contrary then shifts to the appellant,
who shall also have the burden of persuasion.
(B)   The burden of presenting evidence sufficient to allow the Board of
Adjustment to reach the conclusions set forth in Section 5-2(B), as well as the
burden of persuasion on those issues, remains with the applicant seeking the
variance.
Section 5-6:   Board Action on Appeals and Variances   Schedule of Fees
With respect to appeals, a motion to reverse, affirm, or modify the order,
requirement, decision, or determination appealed from shall include, insofar as
(A)      practicable, a statement of the specific reasons or findings of facts
that support the motion. If a motion to reverse or modify is not made or fails
to receive the four-fifths vote necessary for adoption (see Section 3-17), then
a motion to uphold the decision appealed from shall be in order. This motion is
adopted as the board’s decision if supported by more than one-fifth of the
board’s membership (excluding vacant seats).   
(B)      Before granting a variance, the board must take a separate vote and
vote affirmatively (by a four-fifths majority-see Section 3-17) on each of the
six required findings stated in Section 5-2(B). Insofar as practicable, a
motion to make an affirmative finding on each of the requirements set forth in
Section 5-2(B) shall include a statement of the specific reasons or findings of
fact supporting such motion.   
(C)      A motion to deny a variance may be made on the basis that any one or
more of the six criteria set forth in Section 5-2(B) are not satisfied or that
the application is incomplete. Insofar as practicable, such a motion shall
include a statement of the specific reasons or findings of fact that support
it. This motion is adopted as the board’s decision if supported by more than
one-fifth of the board’s membership (excluding vacant seats).     
   A schedule of fees to help defray the administrative expenses, notice
requirements and other related costs shall be maintained by the City of
Southport related to any application filed requiring Board of Adjustment
action. The schedule of fees may be modified from time to time by the City and
a current schedule shall be maintained on file with the City Clerk and the
Planning and Inspections Department.
Section 3.   Amend Article 6 of the UDO as follows:
ARTICLE 6.   HEARING PROCEDURES FOR APPEALS AND APPLICATIONS  (revised 6-12-08)
Section 6-1:   Hearing Required on Appeals and Applications
(A)   Before making a decision on an appeal or an application for a variance or
conditional-use permit, or a petition from the planning staff to revoke a
conditional-use permit, the Board of Adjustment shall hold a hearing on the
appeal or application  within sixty (60) days of the submittal of a completed
appeal or application in accordance with Section 5-4 unless an expedited
hearing is requested by an appellant in appeal situations where a stay of
enforcement is denied. All applications for a conditional use permit shall be
referred by the Administrator to the City of Southport Planning Board for
review and comment. All comments prepared by the City of Southport Planning
Board shall be submitted presented by the Planning Board Secretary Chairman, or
his or her designee, to the Board of Adjustment as evidence at the public
hearing required by this section. This representative of the Planning Board
shall attend the hearing and  be subject to the same scrutiny as other
witnesses. Review of the conditional use application by the City of Southport
Planning Board shall not be a quasi-judicial procedure but the hearing
conducted by the Board of Adjustment shall be. The City of Southport Planning
Board shall include in its comments a statement as to the consistency of the
application with the City of Southport Comprehensive Plan. Comments of the City
of Southport Planning Board shall be considered with other evidence submitted
at the public hearing.
(B)   Subject to Subsection (C), the hearing shall be open to the public and
all persons interested in the outcome of the appeal or application  with
standing under G.S. 160A-393(e)  shall be given an opportunity to present
evidence, and arguments and testify  arguments and testimony.
(C)   The Board of Adjustment may place reasonable and equitable limitations on
the presentation of evidence and arguments and the cross-examination of
witnesses so that the matter at issue may be heard and decided without undue
delay.
(D)   The Board of Adjustment may continue the hearing until a subsequent
meeting and may keep the hearing open to take additional information up to the
point a final decision is made. No further notice of a continued hearing need
be published unless a period of six weeks or more elapses between hearing
dates.
(E)   Except as provided in Section 12-13, the Board of Adjustment may not
rehear a quasi-judicial matter previously denied.
(F)   The required application fee and all supporting materials must be
received by the Administrator before an application is considered complete and
a hearing scheduled.
Section 6-2:   Notice of Hearing
The administrator or his designee  shall give  cause  notice of any hearing
required by Section 6-1 to be provided as follows:
(A)   Notice shall be given to appellant or applicant  the person or entity
whose appeal, application or request is the subject of the hearing , to the
owner of the property that is the subject of the hearing if the owner did not
initiate the hearing, to the owners of all parcels of land abutting the parcel
of land that is the subject of the hearing  and any other person who makes a
written request for such notice. by mailing to such persons a written notice
not later than 10 days before the hearing.   In the absence of evidence to the
contrary, the county tax listing shall be utilized to determine owners of
property entitled to mailed notice. The notice must be deposited in the mail at
least 10 days, but not more than 25 days, prior to the date of the hearing.
Within that same time period, the city shall also prominently post a notice of
the hearing on the site that is the subject of the hearing or on an adjacent
street or highway right of way.
(B)   Notice shall be given to neighboring property owners by mailing a written
notice not later than 10 days before the hearing to those persons who have
listed for taxation real property any portion of which is located within 150
feet of the lot that is the subject of the application or appeal. Notice shall
also be given by prominently posting signs in the vicinity of the property that
is the subject of the proposed action. Such signs shall be posted not less than
seven days prior to the hearing.
(C)   In the case of conditional-use permits, notice shall be given to other
potentially interested persons by publishing a notice one time in a newspaper
having general circulation in the area not less than seven nor more than
fifteen days prior to the hearing.
(D)(B)   The notice required by this section shall state the date, time, and
place of the hearing, reasonably identify the lot  property  that is the
subject of the application or appeal, and give a brief description of the
action requested or proposed.
Section 6-3:   Evidence/Presentation of Evidence
(A)   The provisions of this section apply to all hearings for which a notice
is required by Section 6-1.
(B)   All persons who intend to present evidence to the Board of Adjustment,
rather than arguments only, shall be witnesses to any matter coming before the
board shall be sworn by the board chair or any member acting as chair or by the
clerk to the board . The chair, or anyone acting as chair in the chair’s
absence, may subpoena witnesses and compel the production of evidence. To
request issuance of a subpoena, persons with standing under 160A-393 d) may
make a written request to the chair explaining why it is necessary for certain
witnesses or evidence to be compelled. The chair shall issue subpoenas he or
she shall determine to be relevant, reasonable in nature and scope and not
oppressive. Decisions regarding subpoenas made by the chair may be appealed to
the full board of adjustment. Any party failing or refusing to obey a subpoena
may be subject to application to the General Court of Justice for an order
requiring that the subpoena be obeyed and the court shall have jurisdiction to
issue such notices after notice to all proper parties.
(C)   All quasi-judicial decisions  findings and conclusions necessary to the
issuance or denial of the requested permit or appeal (necessary findings) shall
be based upon reliable  competent, material and substantial  evidence in the
record . Competent evidence (evidence admissible in a court of law) shall be
preferred whenever reasonably available, but in no case may necessary findings
be based solely upon incompetent evidence unless competent evidence is not
reasonably available, the evidence in question appears to be particularly
reliable, and the matter at issue is not seriously disputed.
(D)   The Board of Adjustment has the authority to limit testimony that is
irrelevant.
(E)   The entirety of a quasi-judicial hearing and deliberations shall be
conducted in open session.
(F)   Parties to a quasi-judicial hearing have a right to cross-examine
witnesses.
(G)   Factual findings must not be based on hearsay evidence which would be
inadmissible in a court of law.
(H)   If a Board of Adjustment member has prior or specialized knowledge about
a case, that knowledge should be disclosed to the rest of the Board of
Adjustment and parties at the beginning of the hearing. A member of the board
shall not participate in or vote on any quasi-judicial matter in a manner that
would violate affected persons constitutional rights to an impartial decision
maker. Impermissible conflicts include, but are not limited to, a member having
a fixed opinion prior to hearing the matter that is not susceptible to change,
undisclosed ex parte communications, a close familial, business, or other
associational relationship with an affected person, or a financial interest in
the outcome of the matter. If an objection is raised to a member’s
participation and that member does not recuse himself or herself, the remaining
members shall by majority rule on that objection.
Section 6-4:   Modification of Application at Hearing
(A)   In response to questions or comments by persons appearing at the hearing
or to suggestions or recommendations by the Board of Adjustment, the applicant
may agree to modify his application, including the plans and specifications
submitted . However, in the case of an appeal, the board shall continue the
hearing if new issues are presented that were not in the notice of appeal and
immediate consideration might unduly prejudice a party of interest or the City.
(B)   Unless such modifications are so substantial or extensive that the board
cannot reasonably be expected to perceive the nature and impact of the proposed
changes without revised plans before it, the Board of Adjustment may approve  
the application with the stipulation that the permit will not be issued until
plans reflecting the agreed upon changes are submitted to the planning
staff.   
Section 6-5:   Record
(A)   A tape recording shall be made of all hearings required by Section 6-1,
and such recordings shall be kept for at least two years. Accurate minutes
shall also be kept of all such proceedings, but a transcript need not be made.
(B)   Whenever practicable, all documentary evidence presented at a hearing as
well as all other types of physical evidence shall be made a part of the record
of the proceedings and shall be kept by the city for at least two years.
Section 6-6:   Written Decisions
(D)   Any decision made by the Board of Adjustment regarding an appeal or
variance or issuance or revocation of a conditional-use permit shall be reduced
to writing and served upon the applicant or appellant, and all   other persons
who make a written request for a copy .    
(A)   Decisions and voting by the Board of Adjustment regarding variances and
quasi-judicial matters shall be in accordance with Article 5, Section 5-2 (C).
Every quasi-judicial decision shall be reduced to writing and reflect the
board’s determination of contested facts and their application to the
applicable standards. The written decision shall be signed by the chair or
other duly authorized member of the board. A quasi-judicial decision is
effective upon filing the written decision with the clerk to the board. The
decision of the board shall be delivered by personal delivery, electronic mail,
or by first class mail to the applicant, property owner and to any person who
has submitted a written request for a copy prior to the date the decision
becomes effective. The clerk to the board shall certify that proper notice has
been made.
(B)   Every quasi-judicial decision shall be subject to review by the superior
court by proceedings in the nature of certiorari pursuant to G.S. 160A-393. A
petition for review shall be filed with the clerk of superior court by the
later of 30 days after the decision is effective or after a written copy is
delivered in accordance with the immediately preceding paragraph. When first
class mail is used to deliver notice, three days shall be added to the time to
file the petition.
Section 4.   Amend Section 7-6 of Article 7, “ENFORCEMENT AND REVIEW” as
follows:
Section 7-6:   Judicial Review
   Every final decision of the Board of Aldermen granting or denying a
conditional-use permit and every final decision of the Board of Adjustment
shall be subject to review by the Superior Court of Brunswick County by
proceedings in the nature of certiorari in accordance with the provisions of
Section 6-6. of Article 6.
(B)   The petition for the writ of certiorari must be filed with the Brunswick
County Clerk of Court within 30 days after the later of the following
occurrences:
(1)   A written copy of the board’s decision (see Section 6-6) has been filed
in the office of the planning department, and
(2)   A written copy of the board’s decision (see Section 6-6) has been
delivered by personal service or certified mail, return receipt requested, to
the applicant or appellant and every other aggrieved party who has filed a
written request for such copy at the hearing of the case.
(C)   A copy of the writ of certiorari shall be served upon the City of
Southport.   
Section 5. Amend Section 12-17 of Article 12, “ZONING AND CONDITIONAL USE
PERMIT APPROVAL as follows:
Section 12-17: Procedure for Conditional Use Permit Granted by the Board of
Adjustment (revised 6-12-08)
Conditional use permits may be issued by the Administrator, after approval by
the Board of Adjustment, for the uses as designated in Section 12-18:
Regulations for Conditional Uses. The petition for a conditional use permit and
accompanying plans shall be submitted to the Administrator in accordance with
Section 12-5. If determined to be complete, the application shall be processed
in accordance with provisions pertaining to quasi-judicial hearings contained
in Article 6.   The Board of Adjustment shall consider the application and may
approve or deny the requested conditional use permit. A four-fifth majority of
the entire Board is required to find in favor of an applicant for a conditional
use permit. For the purposes of this section, vacant positions on the board and
members who are disqualified from voting on a quasi-judicial matter shall not
be considered “members of the Board” for calculation of
the requisite majority. When deciding conditional use permits, the Board of
Adjustment shall follow quasi-judicial procedures. (See also Sections 3-15,3-
19, and Section 6-1 of this Ordinance).   
The conditional use permit, if approved, shall include approval of plans as may
be required. In approving the permit, the Board of Adjustment shall find as a
specific finding of fact and reflect in their minutes that the permit will
comply with the following four facts:
(A)   That the use will not materially endanger the public health, safety, or
general welfare if located where proposed and developed according to the plan
as submitted and approved;
(B)   That the use meets all required conditions and specifications;
(C)   That the use will not adversely affect the use or any physical attribute
of adjoining or abutting property, or that the use is a public necessity; and
(D)   That the location and character of the use, if developed according to the
plan as submitted and approved, will be in harmony with the area in which it is
to be located and in general conformity with the City of Southport Land Use
Plan.
In approving the conditional use permit, the Board of Adjustment may designate,
such conditions in addition and in connection therewith as will, in its
opinion, assure that the use in its proposed location will be harmonious with
the area in which it is proposed to be located and with the spirit of this
Ordinance. All such additional conditions shall be entered in the minutes of
the meeting at which the conditional use permit is granted and also on the
conditional use permit approving, and on the approved plans submitted
therewith. All specific conditions shall run with the land and shall be binding
on the original applicant for the conditional use permit, the heirs,
successors, and assigns. In order to ensure that such conditions and
requirements for each conditional use permit will be fulfilled, the petitioner
for the conditional use permit may be required to enter into a contract with
the City of Southport providing for the installation of the physical
improvements required as a basis for the issuance of the conditional use
permit. Performance of said contract shall be secured by cash or surety bond
which will cover the total estimated cost of the improvements as determined by
the City of Southport; provided, however, that said bond may be waived by the
City Board of Aldermen within its discretion.
If the Board of Adjustment denies the permit, it shall enter the reason for its
action in the minutes of the meeting at which the action is taken.
In addition to the conditions specifically imposed by the Board of Adjustment,
conditional uses shall comply with all minimum standards contained in this
ordinance, and with the height, area, and parking regulations of the zone in
which they are located.
In the event of failure to comply with the plans approved by the Board of
Adjustment or with any other conditions imposed upon the conditional use
permit, the permit shall thereupon immediately become void and of no effect. No
building permits for further construction nor a certificate of compliance under
this conditional use permit shall be issued, and the use of all completed
structures shall immediately cease and such completed structures not thereafter
be used for any purpose other than a use-by-right as permitted by the zone in
which the property is located.
Where plans are required to be submitted and approved as part of the
application for a conditional use permit, modifications of the original plans
may be authorized by the Board of Adjustment after review  during the quasi-
judicial proceeding.

RESOLUTION OF SUPPORT
   WHEREAS, the problem of crime touch and affect all segments of our society,
while eroding the moral and economic strength of our citizens; and
   WHEREAS, we live in a world where everyone is concerned about safety, the
law and their moral existence; and
   WHEREAS, the Southport Police Department for years has dedicated itself to
keeping our citizens and residents safe, while sacrificing their own lives,
   NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Board of Aldermen have the utmost
confidence in the integrity of our Chief of Police, officers and staff; and
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that we recognize and appreciate the valuable service
provided by the Southport Police Department and the Board of Aldermen
wholeheartedly supports our Police Department and staff.
This 13 th day of February 2014.

Alderman Poole read a Proclamation in recognition of Regina W. Alexander
WHEREAS, on March 11, 2002 Regina W. Alexander began her distinguished career
with the City Of Southport as City Clerk; and
WHEREAS,  Regina is a lifelong resident of Southport, who has selflessly and
graciously been an extraordinary community volunteer, focusing her life's work
on improving the quality of life for all the Citizens; and
WHEREAS, for 12 years, the citizens of Southport benefitted greatly from
Regina's service as City Clerk; additionally she served twice as Interim City
Manager; and
WHEREAS, through her tireless efforts Regina has provided faithful and
professional service to three Mayors and seven City Councils in the performance
of their duties; and
WHEREAS, Regina W. Alexander MMC, NCCMC has demonstrated her commitment to, and
knowledge of the office of City Clerk, by attaining the certification of Master
Municipal Clerk and North Carolina Certified Municipal Clerk; and
WHEREAS, Regina is an active member of the North Carolina Association of
Municipal Clerks, in cooperation with the International Institute of Municipal
Clerks, School of Government at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
and the North Carolina League of Municipalities in Raleigh.
NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved throughout the City of Southport, on this
occasion of her well-earned retirement, and for the honor she has given to the
City and its citizens, that March 1, 2014 will be proclaimed as “Regina W.
Alexander Day” throughout the City of Southport.
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that this Proclamation and a Key to the City be bestowed
in recognition of her many outstanding contributions to the community and be
presented to Regina W. Alexander as an expression of the Board of Aldermen’s
appreciation for her dedicated service to the City of Southport, North Carolina
and its citizens.

City Attorney Isenberg discussed recently enacted State statutes allowing for
options to proceed with renovations to the former City Hall;
Design-Build
∙   Request for proposals/qualifications from a team of architects/contractor
∙   Interview design/build team, prioritize choices
∙   Negotiate with #1 choice and #2, #3 if needed
∙   Enter into one contract with designer & builder for entire project
∙   Not limited to awarding a contract to the low bidder; can choose best
qualified
Design, Build & Bridge Contract
∙   Hire an engineer/architect; oftentimes an employee to design 35% of
project, and then put out for bids with a design/contractor team.
Board consensus to consider the options as presented by the city attorney for
renovations of 201 E. Moore Street.

Mr. Gerald Donaldson, 5990 Dutchman Creek Road, commented on the Southport
Comprehensive Pedestrian Plan. (Comments included in their entirety):
The proposed Southport pedestrian plan in the second appendix defines
wayfinding or guide signage as: “Wayfinding or guide signs give notice of
traffic laws or regulations that pedestrians, cyclists, and motorists are
required by low to follow.” At B-11. However, this is not illuminating, is
largely inaccurate, and in fact, replicates the definition of Regulatory and
Warning Signs found at the start of the ensuing subsection. At B-12. Although
the Manual of Uniform Traffic Control Devises (MUTCD)* indexes the following
guide sign characteristics to application on freeways and expressways, the
traffic engineering function and purpose of wayfinding or guide signs supplied
by Sec.2E.02 of the MUTCD is applicable to the function and purpose of all
wayfinding or guide signage:
Guide or Wayfinding signs __
A.   Give direction to destinations, or to streets or highway routes, at
intersections or interchanges;
B.   Furnish advance notice of the approach to intersections or interchanges;
C.   Direct road users into appropriate lanes in advance of diverging or
merging movements;
D.   Identify routes and directions on those routes;
E.   Show distances to destinations;
F.   Indicate access to general motorist services, rest, scenic, and
recreational areas; and
G.   Provide other information of value to the road user.
These crucial features of wayfinding or guide signs should supplant the lead
sentence of the section defining these terms on p. B-11.
∙   The narrative throughout the Southport pedestrian plan, as well as the map
of proposed pedestrian enhancements found at 3-4/5, does not appear to address
existing or prospective bicycle paths and currently designated or any
anticipated bicycle routes. As a result, it is difficult to determine whether
some or all of the existing bike paths and routes will be maintained or
extended by interconnection with any planned bike path project or other road
and street improvements that would facilitate bicycle traffic.
*I was a member of the National Committee on Uniform Traffic Control Devises
from 1975-2010, and over the years I helped author many sections of the current
edition of the MUTCD.
Mrs. Molla Donaldson, 5990 Dutchman Creek Road complimented the City and
Brunswick Electric Membership Corp. (BEMC) for keeping the electric service up
during the recent Winter storms.

RESOLUTION GRANTING APPLICATION FOR ZONING MAP AMENDMENT
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other
land use ordinances and a zoning map that control land development within both
the City’s incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s zoning map; and
   WHEREAS, Mr. Brian Quinn has filed an application for a zoning map amendment
requesting that tax parcel 221MA00109, consisting of one acre, be rezoned from
PUD to Business District; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and has
recommended that the application for this zoning map amendment be granted; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed , was held on March 13, 2014, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that the application for zoning
map amendment filed by Mr. Quinn requesting that the above-referenced parcel be
rezoned from PUD to Business District consistent with the Southport CAMA Core
Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the granting of this
application is reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) the tract in
question is no longer a part of the original PUD designated as Cades Cove and
accordingly, the continuing designation of PUD is no longer appropriate for
this parcel (ii) the requesting rezoning is reasonable in that the majority of
the parcels surrounding the parcel in question are zoned Business District;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
application for the zoning map amendment filed by Mr. Brian Quinn is hereby
granted.
      This 13th day of March, 2014.

COMMITTEE REPORTS
11.   Emergency Services Committee
Alderman Poole provided Board members with draft meeting minutes of the
Emergency Services Committee meeting held February 26, 2014 (report included in
its entirety);
The meeting of the Emergency Services Committee was held on 26 February 2014 at
1600 hours at the Southport Fire Department.
The primary purpose of the meeting, as requested by Mayor Howard, was to
revisit the major repair of the Rescue Squad Building for feasibility.
The meeting was called to order by Alderman Poole, Attendees were Alderman Todd
Coring, City Manager Kerry McDuffie, Fire Chief Charles Drew, Rescue Chief
Tyler Johnson and Asst. Chief Brandon Gray and Police Chief Jerry Dove.
The topic of the meeting was brainstormed by the group. Options discussed
included the use of the Public Works location for a Rescue Squad Building.
After detailed discussion, the committee agreed unanimously to recommend to the
Board to delay remodeling of the current building and pursue building a Public
Safety Building in the RiverMist area. The building would house the Rescue
Squad and one bay would be needed for the option of Fire Department use and an
office for the police Department (approx. 200 sq. ft.). It was acknowledged
that it was not acceptable to wait beyond two years to begin action.
The benefits for the new location were identified as:
-   Reduction of response time
-   Going into Southport is quicker than going out
-   Moves the building out of the potential flooding area during hurricanes and
storms
-   More centrally located as Walmart is identified as the central landmark of
calls
-   Growth in Rivermist area
-   Ancillary benefits to Fire Department and Police Department
It was agreed that purchase of new appliances would not be placed on hold, and
that appliances could be moved to a new structure when/if needed.
If approved the Committee would like to be a part of the blueprint design.
The committee requests that this Committee be continued by Mayor Howard and it
is recognized that it has been instrumental in the cohesiveness of all
emergency services working together. Plans for the future were identified as
review of emergency processes and plans and monuments in old Fire Dept. area.
Chief Dove identified that he would be requesting during budget time the
request to replace the Water Rescue Truck with a Tahoe to be issued out as
equipment.
Submitted in draft by Mary Ellen Poole
Alderman Poole stated the topic of establishing a public safety building in the
Rivermist Subdivision was discussed in depth. The Committee concluded that the
need for a station to house the Rescue Squad, a bay for the Fire Department and
space for a Police Department office should be pursued within two (2) years.
The Committee cited the growth in the Rivermist area, a reduction in response
time, and the central location as aspects meriting consideration of the
station.
Alderman Poole identified additional projects the Committee would like to
pursue; i.e., emergency processes and plans and monuments for the former site
of the fire department to recognize the history of the area.
Alderman Coring, member of the Emergency Services Committee, pointed out that
Fire Chief Charles Drew also attended the Committee meeting and supported the
recommendation.
Alderman Coring stated the Committee studied the condition of the current
rescue squad location, location of calls responding to, and response time. He
pointed out that the Fire Department response time shortened after relocation
to the N. Howe Street location.
Mayor Howard asked how the proposed relocation of the Rescue Squad would affect
their response time into the main area of Southport. Aldermen Coring stated he
did not foresee an increase in response as, according to Rescue Chief Johnson,
the ambulance is often out of the station when taking calls. Additionally, the
Rescue Station is staffed at all times so personnel do not have to travel to
the station prior to responding to an incident as is the practice for the
volunteer fire department.
Mayor Howard noted this was the first instance the Board had heard the
recommendation and he suggested each Committee member submit a report to the
Board of discussion during the April meeting. He emphasized the need for
multiple opportunities for public input.
Alderman Barnes asked how the Committee concluded a station in Rivermist would
be more economical to build than to renovate the current rescue station. He
emphasized the squad has a four (4) minute response time and questioned that
time remaining if responding from Rivermist. Alderman Coring reported the
estimate to bring the existing station up to code was $ 330,000. An option to
the major renovation would be construction of a new station at Rivermist as
originally recommended by former Fire Chief Greg Cumbee.
Alderman Adams critiqued the proposal by contending that Brunswick County EMS
should be responding to the Rivermist area and the Southport Rescue Squad
should be move centrally located to the core of the community, similar to the
Fire Department’s centralized location.
Mayor Howard noted the Emergency Services Committee is looking at long term
options for the City’s public safety needs.
Board consensus to put continued discussion and consideration of the issue on
the April agenda and to provide opportunities for public input. The Mayor
pointed out there are two (2) recommendations; 1. Build a new facility in lieu
of renovating the existing rescue headquarters. 2. Determine the location of a
new facility.
12.   Closed Session; Personnel – 7:41
Alderman Adams moved, second by Alderman Poole to go into closed session
pursuant to G.S.143-318.11(a)(6) to discuss a personnel matter. Unanimous Vote;
motion carried.
Regular Session Reconvened – 8:14
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to come out of closed
session. Unanimous vote; motion carried. 
Mayor Howard stated the purpose of the closed session was to discuss a
personnel situation and to review the City Manager’s performance to date.
Alderman Powell moved, second by Alderman Barnes to increase the City Manager’s
salary to $85,000 annually. Vote of approval unanimous; motion carried.
City Manager McDuffie reported he is preparing Requests for Proposals (RFP) for
the Waterfront Restoration project and will provide them to the Board prior to
distribution.
Manager McDuffie provided the Board with a proposal to reduce costs for the
sewer system lift stations odor control, currently an annual contract of
$48,000. He stated that city staff can perform the work in-house at a cost of
$19,211 annually with an initial outlay of $6,460 for a scrubber, resulting in
an annual savings of $22,000 the first year and $28,000 each year thereafter.
BOARD COMMENTS

Alderman Childs stated she too had received calls. She shared pricing Mr. Clay

   Alderman Coring praised the response of multiple fire departments during

City of Southport
2014 Earth Day Resolution
WHEREAS, the first Earth Day was celebrated on April 22, 1970, and was founded
by the late Senator Gaylord Nelson with the goal of inspiring environmental
awareness and encouraging the conservation, protection and appreciation of our
nation’s natural resources; and
WHEREAS, it is the responsibility of each of us to safeguard the environment,
by recognizing that all human life depends upon the Earth and upon one another
for our mutual existence, well-being and development; and
WHEREAS, the steps we can take to protect and preserve our natural environment
through education, partnerships and positive actions should be encouraged; and
WHEREAS, the citizens of Southport are committed not only to the protection and
preservation of our environment, but also to the restoration of ecosystems and
habitat; and
WHEREAS, in furtherance of this objective the City of Southport supports
organizations that participate in Earth Day 2014; and
WHEREAS, the City commends all who participates in Earth Day, for their
dedication in taking a proactive role in shaping the future of our environment
and in protecting the earth’s precious natural resource;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of
Southport, do hereby proclaim April 22, 2014, as EARTH DAY and urge all our
citizens to be mindful of local, state and national laws which protect our
environment and to join in efforts to preserve the beauty and wonder of the
lands, skies and water of the Earth in all its diversity.
This 10th day of April 2014.
    s/Robert D. Howard
    Mayor
s/Michele Windham
City Clerk
A RESOLUTION RECOGNIZING THE NATIONAL DAY OF PRAYER
WHEREAS, civic prayers and national days of prayer have a long and venerable
history in our constitutional republic, dating back to the First Continental
Congress in 1775; and
WHEREAS, the Declaration of Independence, our first statement as Americans of
national purpose and identity, made “the Laws of Nature and Nature’s God” the
foundation of our United States of America and asserted that people have
inalienable rights that are God-given; and
WHEREAS, the Supreme Court has affirmed the right of state legislatures to open
their sessions with prayer and the Supreme Court and the U.S. Congress
themselves begin each day with prayer; and
WHEREAS, in 1988 legislation setting aside the first Thursday of May in each
year as a National Day of Prayer was passed unanimously by both Houses of
Congress and signed by President Ronald Reagan; and
WHEREAS, the National Day of Prayer is an opportunity for Americans of all
faiths to join in united prayer to acknowledge our dependence on God, to give
thanks for blessings received, to request healing for wounds endured, and to
ask God to guide our leaders and bring wholeness to the United States and her
citizens; and
WHEREAS, it is fitting and proper to give thanks to God by observing a day of
prayer in the City of Southport when all may acknowledge our blessings and
express gratitude for them, while recognizing the needs for strengthening
religious and moral values in our State and Nation; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of
Southport, and Board of Aldermen do hereby proclaim May 1, 2014 as “A DAY OF
PRAYER IN SOUTHPORT” and urge all citizens of Southport to observe the day in
ways appropriate to its importance and significance.
This 10th day of April 2014.
                     s/Robert D. Howard
                        Mayor
Attest: s/Michele Windham
      Clerk
PROCLAMATION
SOUTHPORT SPRING CLEAN UP 2014
Whereas, the City of Southport annually organizes a spring cleanup to insure
clean and beautiful streets in the City; and
Whereas, the Spring Cleanup will take place April 11-15, 2014, and encourage
local citizens, businesses, civic groups, churches, schools, families,
individuals and professional groups to participate in this effort by organizing
cleanups in their neighborhoods; and
Whereas, Southport Code Enforcement Department is collecting debris and refuse
at the Taylor Field off of East Nash Street; and
Whereas, the great natural beauty of Southport and a clean environment is a
source of pride for all citizens and attracting tourists; and
Whereas, the cleanup will increase awareness of the need for cleaner roadsides,
streets and neighborhoods, and emphasize the importance of not littering, and
encourage recycling of solid waste, and
Whereas, the 2014 spring cleanup is an annual event coordinated by the Code
Enforcement Officer, and is utilized by our residents and citizens as a service
to keep Southport clean and beautiful, and
Whereas, the “Southport Spring Cleanup” will be a part of bringing awareness to
the citizens of this Great City regarding the importance of a clean environment
to the quality of life in Southport, North Carolina.
NOW, THEREFORE, the Mayor and Board of Aldermen encourage citizens to take an
active role in making our city cleaner.
Adopted this 10th day of April 2014.

   City Manager McDuffie explained that city staff is recommending in house

savings to be realized; $20,000 the first year, $26,000 each year after the
first year. Additionally, he noted a one-time purchase of a scrubber for
$6,460.
