Resolution Endorsing the Negotiation of Sale of Generating Assets Owned by
NCEMPA to Duke Energy Progress, Inc.
Mayor Howard stated the Board had met April 3, 2014 in closed session with
representatives of the North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency (NCEMPA)
regarding the publicized consideration of sale of assets of the Power Agency.
The Mayor pointed out that Southport is a member of the Agency along with 31
other communities and approval of the resolution provides endorsement of the
on-going negotiations.
Mayor Howard stated his hopes that the sale will leave the City free and clear
from debt and with the ability to buy electricity, sell the City’s electric
grid and do what is in the best interest of the citizens, without contractual
encumbrances.
Alderman Childs motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to approve the Resolution
Endorsing the Negotiation of Sale of Generating Assets Owned by NCEMPA to Duke
Energy Progress, Inc. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Resolution of the Southport Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport
Endorsing the Negotiation of Definitive Agreements for the Sale of Certain
Generating Assets Owned By North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency to
Duke Energy Progress, Inc. and for Power Supply
WHEREAS, the City of Southport (the “Municipality”) and North Carolina Eastern
Municipal Power Agency (“Power Agency”) heretofore have entered into an Initial
Project Power Sales Agreement, as amended, and a Supplemental Power Sales
Agreement, as amended, pursuant to which, among other things, the Municipality
purchases from Power Agency and Power Agency sells to the Municipality all of
the Municipality’s All Requirements Bulk Power Supply, as such term is defined
in the Supplemental Power Sales Agreement; and
WHEREAS, a portion of the All Requirements Bulk Power Supply sold by Power
Agency to the Municipality and purchased by the Municipality from Power Agency
is derived from the Power Agency’s undivided ownership interest in the
following electric generating units jointly owned by Power Agency with Duke
Energy Progress, Inc. (“DEP”): Brunswick Units Nos. 1 and 2, Harris Unit No. 1,
Mayo Unit No. 1 and Roxboro Unit No. 4 (collectively, the “Joint Units”); and
   WHEREAS, The Southport Board of Aldermen of the Municipality (the “Governing
Body”) has been advised by representatives of Power Agency that Power Agency
has been authorized by its Board of Directors and by the Board of Commissioners
of the Power Agency to negotiate with DEP on an exclusive basis definitive
agreements pursuant to which (i) Power Agency would sell and DEP would purchase
all of Power Agency’s ownership interests in the Joint Units, and (ii) Power
Agency and DEP would enter into a full requirements power purchase agreement
pursuant to which DEP would sell and Power Agency would purchase all of the
power and energy required by Power Agency to provided full requirements power
supply services to the City of Southport and to all other members of Power
Agency (the “Proposed Transaction”); and
   WHEREAS, representatives of Power Agency also have advised the Governing
Body that if the Proposed Transaction is consummated the proceeds to be derived
from the sale of the Joint Units, when combined with other funds available to
Power Agency, may not be sufficient to pay or provide for the payment of the
principal of and premium, if any, and interest on all revenue bonds heretofore
issued by Power Agency to finance the acquisition of the Joint Units; and
   WHEREAS, representatives of Power Agency confidentially presented to the
Governing Body the confidential results of the preliminary financial analyses
of the Proposed Transaction undertaken by and at the request of Power Agency to
determine the projected effect of the Proposed Transaction on Power Agency and
its participants; and
   WHEREAS, the Governing Body, having taken into consideration the
confidential information concerning the Proposed Transaction presented to the
Governing Body by representatives of Power Agency.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen of the
City of Southport:
   1.   Governing Body has given due consideration to the confidential
information concerning the Proposed Transaction presented by representatives of
Power Agency at this meeting and hereby finds and determines that it is in the
best interests of the Municipality for representatives of Power Agency to
negotiate a definitive agreement with DEP concerning the Proposed Transaction.
   2.   The Governing Body hereby endorses the action of the Board of Directors
and Board of Commissioners of Power Agency authorizing representatives of Power

Resolution Expressing Opposition to Seismic Testing as Proposed in Bureau of
Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement
(PEIS) Alternative A and Alternative B
   Alderman Barnes shared information he had researched concerning the harmful
and deadly effects to all marine mammals when seismic testing is utilized in
the exploration of gas under the ocean floor. He explained the testing is done
by towing an array behind a boat. The array emits a pulse of air under water
that then explodes sending dangerously high decibels through the water that can
be heard up to 5 miles from the originating site. He talked about the large
volume of information he found opposing the practice, likely number of deaths
of dolphins, whales, fish and sea turtles and changes to marine mammals
breading habits and migration. He noted that many scientific organizations are
urging the federal government to postpone permitting the practice until
additional studies is completed and alternative methods of gas exploration can
be defined. He also shared reports of beached dolphins in Louisiana after
seismic testing. He offered to share the information he had gathered.
   Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Coring to place consideration
of the Resolution Expressing Opposition to Seismic Testing on the May regular
meeting agenda. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF SENATE BILL TO CLARIFY SOUTHPORT OCCUPANCY TAX
    THAT WHEREAS, in 1989 House Bill 615 was enacted which authorized the City
of Southport to levy an occupancy tax of no more than 3%; and
   WHEREAS, in 2001 House Bill 1668 was passed which authorized the City to
levy an additional occupancy tax of 2%; and
   WHEREAS, House Bill 1668 required the City to “remit the net proceeds of the
occupancy tax to the Southport Tourism Development Authority” whether or not
the City imposed the additional 2% tax; and
   WHEREAS, the City feels as though the requirement to remit the net proceeds
to a TDA was in error and should have applied only if the City levied the
additional 2% tax; and
    WHEREAS, other towns in Brunswick County were also authorized to levy the
additional tax without having to create a TDA at all; and
   WHEREAS, Senator Rabon has been requested to sponsor a bill to clarify the
City’s occupancy tax authority; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen feels that it is in the best interests of the
City and its’ citizens and taxpayers that the attached Senate Bill be adopted;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that it hereby expresses its’ full support for Senate Bill ___ and
hereby requests that said bill be adopted and enacted in order to clarify the
intent of said prior bills.
   Adopted this 10th day of April, 2014, by a vote of 6-0.

City of Southport
A RESOLUTION OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA OF THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN EXPRESING
OPPOSITION TO SEISMIC TESTING AS PROPOSED IN BOEM PEIS OPT A AND OPT B
WHEREAS,  seismic testing as proposed in the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management
(“BOEM”_ Programmatic Environment Impact Statement alternative A and
alternative B has the potential to harm marine life; and
WHEREAS, seismic testing as proposed in BOEM Programmatic Environmental Impact
Statement alternative A and alternative B has the potential to impact
recreational and commercial fishing; and
WHEREAS,  the City of Southport is a municipality in Brunswick County where a
major economic force is tourism related to the coastal environment; and 
WHEREAS, the City of Southport endeavors to be a good steward of the coastal
environment and its resources; and 
WHEREAS, the full impacts of seismic testing as proposed in BOEM Programmatic
Environmental Impact Statement alternative A and alternative B are not yet
fully understood by scientists, the Oil & Gas industry, or BOEM, and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport believes that more research should be done to
fully understand all impacts of seismic testing and options for mitigation of
those impacts; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport does not believe seismic testing as currently
proposed in alternative A or alternative B of BOEM’s Programmatic Environmental
Impact Statement is the safest way to map oil & gas deposits in the mid-
Atlantic region. 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, the Aldermen of the City of Southport, North
Carolina, is opposed to seismic testing as proposed in alternative A or
alternative B of BOEMS’ Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement until such
time as all testing options are evaluated and proper assurances for the
protection of marine life are established.
                     s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest: s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

   Alderman Barnes read the Resolution into the record.
A RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF NATIONAL SAFE BOATING WEEK
Whereas, recreational boating is fun and enjoyable, and we are fortunate that
we have sufficient resources to accommodate the wide variety of pleasure
boating demands. However, our waterways can become crowded at times and be a
place of chaos and confusion. While being a marvelous source of recreation,
boating, to the unprepared, can be a risky sport. Not knowing or obeying the
Navigation Rules or the nautical “Rules of the Road,” drinking alcohol or
taking drugs while operating a boat, or choosing not to wear your life jacket
when doing so is clearly NOT the smart thing to do, are all examples of human
error or a lack of proper judgment. One particular behavior that can reduce the
number of boaters who lose their lives by drowning each year by is the wearing
of a life jacket. It is a simple task that has the potential to reduce terrible
loss in lives.
Whereas, knowledge and skills are important in reducing human error and
improving judgment. If people are aware of the risk, they are likely to take
the precautionary measures to protect themselves and their friends and family.
That is why we must continue to spread the messages of boating safety not only
during National Safe Boating Week but also throughout the entire year.
Whereas, on average, 700 people die each year in boating-related accidents in
the U.S.; approximately 71% of these are fatalities caused by drowning; and
Whereas, the vast majority of these accidents are caused by human error or poor
judgment and not by the boat, equipment, or environmental factors; and
Whereas, a significant number of boaters who lose their lives by drowning each
year would be alive today had they worn their life jackets; and
Whereas, today’s life jackets are more comfortable, more attractive, and more
wearable than styles of years past and deserve a fresh look by today’s boating
public.
Therefore, I, Robert D. Howard, do hereby support the goals of the North
American Safe Boating Campaign, the United States Coast Guard and the Coast
Guard Auxiliary and proclaim May 17 – 23, 2014, as National Safe Boating Week
and the start of the year-round effort to promote safe boating.
In Witness Thereof, I urge all those who boat to Wear It!  and practice safe
boating habits.
Adopted this the 8 th day of May, 2014.                        
                     s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest: s/Michele Windham

Presentation by Tyler Johnson EMS Building Needs
   Chief Tyler Johnson, Southport Rescue Squad, made a presentation of the
conditions of the 40 year old rescue squad headquarters located at 111 E. Nash
Street;
∙   Medical Supply Room is very narrow and has very limited storage space.
∙   Bathroom Ceiling has been leaking for years and a repair technician has
stated all structural members must be replaced before putting on a new roof.
∙   The bathrooms are small, not gender separated, have only one shower and the
plumbing is old.
∙   Bunk Room is very small, there is no gender separation and the carpeting
had to be removed due to flooding.
∙   Office Space; there is one very small office with minimal storage for
required equipment and documentation and there is no separate office space for
the chief or members to complete run reports or have conferences.
∙   Flooding is an issue into the bays and into carpet in the entire building
∙   There is no room separation between the kitchen, training room and day
room.
∙   The building is poorly insulated, not energy efficient, old cinder block
walls and has cast iron drainage plumbing.
∙   Bays are poorly heated with old heaters and have no air conditioning;
medications required to be kept on vehicles are not to fluctuate temperatures.
Chief Tyler indicated he had consulted with his officers and their
recommendation would be to construct a new station vs. remodeling the current
structure at an estimated cost of $300,000.

PURPLE HEART PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, The Purple Heart is the oldest decoration in present use and was
initially created as The Badge of Military Merit by George Washington in 1782;
and
WHEREAS, the Purple Heart was the first American service award or decoration
made available to the common soldier and is specifically awarded to any member
of the United States Armed Services wounded or killed in combat with a declared
enemy of the United States; and
WHEREAS, the mission of the Military Order of the Purple Heart, chartered by an
act of Congress, is to foster an environment of goodwill among the combat
wounded veteran members and their families, promote patriotism, support
legislative initiatives, and most importantly, make sure we never forget; and
WHEREAS, there are several combat wounded veterans who live within our
community; and
WHEREAS, The City of Southport pledges to support those who serve their nation
through which, together, we build strong communities;
NOW, THEREFORE, I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, North
Carolina, do hereby proclaim the City of Southport as a:
“Purple Heart City in the State of North Carolina”
And encourage the citizens of the City of Southport to show their appreciation
for the sacrifices all Purple Heart recipients have made.
Adopted this the 8th day of May, 2014

SPECIAL RECOGNITION
Police Chief Jerry Dove recognized and honored 1st Sgt. Michael Simmons and
Officer Paul Rockenbach with a Life Saving Merit Badge;
   On the evening of May 21, 2014 at 11:02, Officer Paul Rockenbach of the
Southport Police Department responded to 211 North Lord Street concerning a
citizen having a heart attack. Upon his arrival the citizen was sitting in a
chair on the front porch and was unresponsive. The officer immediately placed
the individual on the floor and within seconds Officer Rockenbach started CPR.
Moments later 1 st Sgt. Simmons arrived and together they performed two man CPR
until the Southport Rescue Squad arrived. The two officers and members of the
rescue crew performed CPR for the next fifty minutes and the patient was
brought back to life. On this occasion the two officers exemplified the
dedication and devotion to duty of professional law enforcement officers.
   For distinguishing themselves in saving and preserving human life and
exceptional performance of duty and service to the citizens of Southport they
are awarded this day the City of Southport Police Department Life Saving Merit
Badge.
s/ Robert D. Howard               s/ J.V. Dove
Mayor, City of Southport            Southport Police Chief

and Duke Power and the committee recommends a rate of 6.65 cents per kilowatt
hour. Alderman Barnes pointed out a by back policy is required by state law.

the endeavor. Board concensus to set the rate at 6.65 cents per kilowatt hour

15.   Golf Carts Ordinance
   Manager McDuffie presented an ordinance drafted by himself, Police Chief
Dove and city attorney Mike Isenberg, for regulating golf carts. He pointed out
the ordinance would not apply to those golf carts that have been licensed by
the state as slow speed vehicles. Chief Dove noted that warnings have been
issued to quite a few carts that are not registered with the state. He added
that an officer will be assigned the responsibility for inspecting those carts
registering with the city.
   Alderman Adams stated he would not support an ordinance that required
purchase of a $50 annual registration sticker.
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Poole to adopt the ordinance
with an annual registration fee of $25.
   Ayes:   Aldermen Coring, Poole, Childs, Barnes
   Nays:   Alderman Adams
   Motion Carried 4-1 (Ordinance included as Attachment #2)
16.   Set Rates for Community Center
   Alderman Barnes presented a proposed new rate structure, recommended by the
Rate Review Committee, for rental of the Community Building that is believed
will increase rentals and get the building closer to being self-supporting. He
stated the out of town rate will remain at $500 per hour with a six hour
minimum rental; the rate for residents once a year will be $50 per hour with a
six hour minimum rental; non-profits will be able to rent the building for $150
per hour on weekends and $25 per hour Monday through Thursday. An additional
rental during the year by a resident will be at a a rate of $250 per hour.
Alderman Barnes added that the Committee also recommended establishing a deck
rental rate for rental Monday through Thursday only without access to the
building’s restrooms; $125 per hour with a four hour minimum for residents,
$150 per hour with a four hour minimum for non-residents. The committee
furthermore recommended the city manager and community building director have
the ability to negotiate rates for special events.
   Alderman Poole expressed her support for the recommendation noting that the
changes will result in a better financial situation for the operation of the
building.
   Alderman Adams supported the recommendation but questioned renting the
outside deck without access to restrooms.
   Alderman Childs motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to adopt the
recommendation of the Rate Committee and asked that a restroom rental rate be
considered and brought back during the July meeting. By the uplift of hands, a
unanimous vote; motion carried.
17.   Fire Department request to bill insurance companies for wreck calls
   Manager McDuffie presented a proposal to bill for fire department services
for those incidents covered by insurance. Chief Drew indicated the fire
department was investigating additional revenue opportunities noting that many
agencies in the county are charging for services. He added that city residents
would not be billed because they are already supporting the department through
taxes and fire fees.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Childs to adopt the ordinance
based on the fire department request to bill insurance companies for wreck
calls. By the uplift of hands, a unanimous vote; motion carried.

sooner.
   Alderman Barnes noted that Mr. Stiller’s bill went back down to normal when

4.   Employee Health Insurance
Mr. Grant provided an overview/recommendation of the Health Insurance Committee
meeting; report included in its entirety:
   Task at Hand
Per the request of the Board of Aldermen, a Committee consisting of Alderman
Mary Ellen Poole and Alderman Todd Coring, retirees Johnny Faulk and Bob Grant,
current F/T employees Heather Hemphill and Charles Drew, City manager Kerry
McDuffie and HR Specialist Teresa Parker met Monday, June 16 at 3 PM in the
Aldermen’s Chambers to review Health Care Insurance options for the coming
fiscal year.
Alderman Poole opened the meeting and welcomed the attendees. City manager
McDuffie addressed the task at and provided the members with additional options
that might be available in lieu of the HDHP/HAS plan proposed within the
current proposed FY 14/15 budget. Committee members voiced concerns over the
potential negative impact the current HDHP/HAS Plan might have on various staff
members who are experiencing some rather serious health challenges at present.
It was noted that the proposed HDHP/HAS plan might be well suited for younger
entry level employees just entering the job market but would present different
challenges for the more mature, seasoned work force Southport presently
possesses.
As the group reviewed the various options proposed, each appeared to present
issues that would be problematic for current plan participants. Discussion then
moved to what steps might be taken to maintain the current MIT plan presently
in place and still maintain a reasonable rate while not negatively impacting
the upcoming budget. Various options were reviewed in detail by the Committee
including employee contribution, elimination of the proposed COLA for FY 14/15
and other possibilities to help offset program costs.
Committee Recommendation
In consideration of all relevant factors, it was the consensus of the Committee
that the measures to be taken to maintain the current MIT plan with the least
impact to the overall COS workforce and upcoming budget would be to forego the
proposed 1.5% COLA increase for FY 14/15. This measure coupled with the funds
the Manager had recommended that the City appropriate for the $1200 initial
contribution and the $100 monthly contribution to the individual’s proposed HAS
should bring costs substantially in line to maintain the current plan. City
Manager McDuffie calculated funding would still be short by approximately
$7,000. The Committee suggested that this shortfall could possibly be met by
sweetening revenues in certain line items (an increase of revenues related to
new construction permits might be one example) And modest cuts in line items
within the general and enterprise fund budgets.
Summary
In putting forth this recommendation, the Committee acknowledges that the
health care landscape is evolving and suggested that the group be constituted
as a standing Committee that would meet regularly throughout the course of the
next fiscal year to monitor the continuing impact of the ACA and other factors
on the health care environment while exploring options that might be considered
in the coming years (cafeteria plans, reasonable individual contributions and
educational opportunities geared to possible modification of individual
behavior pertaining to plan use to potentially lessen the claims history impact
as it relates to the City’s health care programs). In closing, the Committee
expressed their appreciation to the Board for allowing them the opportunity to
participate in this process regarding the vitally important issue.
Mayor Howard commended the committee for doing exactly what the Board tasked
them to do and the employees for foregoing a COLA to help offset the deficit
between the two plans.
Alderman Poole echoed the wish of the committee to meet regularly for further
review of health care options for coming years.
Manager McDuffie reported a meeting of employees was held and employees voted
on two options; current plan and no COLA or a HAS, results totaling 25 in favor
of keeping the current plan.
Mayor Howard acknowledged the emotional aspect of the health care issue and he
discussed the duty of the Board to consider practical and affordable health
care alternatives for city employees. He noted the annual budget expenditure
for health care is nearly $600,000.
Alderman Adams shared his opinion the proposed move to a HAS was not presented
to the employees in a timely manner. He expressed appreciation for Manager
McDuffie’s efforts and endorsed the continued review of options by the Health
Insurance Committee.
Alderman Barnes discussed the dynamics of making changes and he made a motion,
second by Alderman Powell to accept the committee’s recommendation. Alderman
Barnes added his opinion the employees are deserving of a COLA.
Discussion
Alderman Powell stated his support of the committee.
Alderman Childs pointed out there would still be a funding shortfall. Manager
McDuffie stated a budget amendment would be needed from discretionary funds.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

6.   2014-2015 Budget
Manager McDuffie presented the 2014-2015 FY budget stating there would be no
tax change; two amendments would be needed to address health care and the
increase for yard debris and recycling collection. Manager McDuffie pointed out
there had not been an increase in water rates since 2006 and the State had
increased the sales tax rate.
Responding to Alderman Barnes, the city manager advised that privilege license
fees can be collected through the 2014-2015 fiscal year; fees cannot be
increased and cannot be collected from businesses that are not physically
located in Southport.
Alderman Coring questioned a capital outlay from the Electric Fund for the
Public Services Department. The city manager explained that Brunswick Electric
Membership Corp (BEMC) has requested a new tower used for transmitting the
signal for the load management system be installed to replace the deteriorating
tower currently in use. The cost, $23,200, will include all materials and
cabling and was within $300 of the cost to refurbish an existing tower.
Ms. Bray pointed out that additional revenue of $10,000 was added to the budget
for services the Fire Department can now bill for.
The Board discussed city employees’ salary history and proposed salaries for
the 2014-2015 fiscal year. The city manager noted the proposed 1.5% COLA would
be removed from the budget because of the Board’s action on Item 4. Answering a
query by the mayor, the city manager explained salary adjustments for employees
completing probationary periods. The mayor questioned an 11% increase for a new
Finance Department employee. Ms. Bray explained the employee was promoted to
the Tax Collector position.
Other minor inconsistencies were noted in the salaries budget and Alderman
Adams recommended staff clarify the information and resubmit to the Board.

street from Bay Street to Old American Fish Company in front of two privately

authorize the city manager, at his discretion, to close the street subject to
approval by the affected property owners. Unanimous vote; motion carried .
Manager McDuffie proposed shortening the operating hours of the Police
Department during winter months, October through March and keeping the hours
unchanged April through September.
Answering a concern raised by Alderman Barnes to the 11:00 p.m. scheduled shut
down of the city’s water system, Manager McDuffie apologized for the lack of
forewarning to the affected citizens of Southport. He stated the news media had
been notified, notice was posted on the city’s web page and it is anticipated
the system will be back on at 5:00 a.m. Friday, June 20. Alderman Powell noted
a system shut down is normally announced in advance via customers’ utility
bills.
Alderman Barnes suggested appointment of a committee, or directing the Planning
Board or city manager, to designate an area of the city for the operation and
advertising of tours. Board consensus for the Tourism Commission to consider
the request and report back to the Board.
Alderman Barnes asked for the status of additional public restrooms. Manager
McDuffie stated bids had been received to demolish the former Code Enforcement
office on East Nash.
Motion to recess the meeting until Thursday, June 26, 7:00 p.m., to Fire
Department Headquarters, 1011 N. Howe Street, passed with a unanimous vote.
                        /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:   /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

SECTION VI. TAX RATE
There is hereby levied, for fiscal year 2014-2015, a tax at the rate of $0.2456
on each one hundred dollars ($100) of assessed valuation of property located
within the City of Southport for the purpose of raising revenue in the General
Fund.
SECTION VII. BUDGET OFFICER AUTHORITY
The city manager (budget officer) is hereby authorized to transfer
appropriations within a fund and between funds under the following terms:
A.   He may transfer amounts between objects of expenditures (line items)
within a departmental appropriation.
B.   He may transfer amounts between appropriations within the same fund,
provided that a report of such transfers shall be made no later than the next
regular financial report to the Board of Aldermen.
C.   He may approve un-budgeted inter-fund transfers, up to $5,000, provided
that a report of such transfers shall be made no later than the next regular
financial report to the Board of Aldermen.
D.   He may transfer and/or utilize appropriations contained in contingency
appropriations within a fund (except for contingency amounts within the
governing board appropriation) or in emergency fund appropriations.
E.   He may authorize temporary transfers of cash among funds as necessary to
meet cash flow needs.
F.   He may transfer funds from capital reserve funds, up to $20,000 per
purpose, to meet current needs for the purpose for which such funds are being
held in reserve, provided that a report of such transfers shall be made no
later than the next regular financial report to the Board of Aldermen.
All other transfers of funds between appropriations or budget funds shall be
accomplished by Board amendment of this ordinance.
SECTION VIII. CONTINUING AUTHORIZATION
Previously-adopted capital project budgets, grant project budgets, and special
reserve funds are hereby re-authorized, and revenues and appropriations made
for all such funds shall remain authorized on an ongoing basis until such
projects are completed and/or all funds are utilized. At the conclusion of such
capital projects or grant projects, any residual, unexpended local funds shall
be transferred to the general government or enterprise fund with which the
project is associated.
SECTION IX. BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION
This ordinance and the supporting budget document shall be the basis of the
financial plan for the City of Southport municipal government for the 2014-2015
fiscal year. The budget officer shall administer the budget and shall insure
the finance officer and department heads of the city are provided with
sufficient guidance to properly implement this plan. Copies of the budget
ordinance shall be furnished to the city manager and the finance officer for
their use and direction in the disbursement of funds and to the city clerk for
the official records of the city.
SECTION X. ADOPTION
This ordinance has been adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen in special
session on June 26, 2014, upon the motion of Alderman Childs and the second of
Alderman Poole, with a vote of          6 ayes and  0 noes, and shall be
effective July 1, 2014.
                  s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

Resolution of Appreciation
WHEREAS, for over 200 years the City of Southport has celebrated our nation’s
independence; and 
WHEREAS, the North Carolina 4th of July Festival was incorporated in 1972 and
the patriotic spirit is alive and well, and has established the City of
Southport as one of the most patriotic towns in the State of North Carolina;
and
WHEREAS, the 4th of July festival draws an estimated 40,000 to 50,000 people to
Southport and its surrounding communities; and
WHEREAS, the festival highlights over 150 arts and craft vendors, food vendors,
a parade, freedom run, veteran’s recognition, naturalization ceremony, children
games, firefighters’ competition, flag retirement ceremony, fireworks and more;
and
WHEREAS, the N.C. 4th of July festival could not be realized without the
Festival Board of Directors, Committees and hundreds of volunteers that work
year round to promote and organize this event.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport recognizes and thanks
each and every individual who tirelessly gave of their time and energy to put
on one of the best 4th of July Festivals ever.
ADOPTED this the 10th day of July 2014.

4.   Public Hearing; Rezoning 109 and 113 W. Moore Street
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Childs to go into Public Hearing.

   City Manager McDuffie reported that staff had made a request to change the

Planning Board had reviewed the request and submitted a recommendation to the
Board for a zoning reclassification of Central Business District (CBD) except
for a classification of Open Space for Keziah Park and to extend the Parking
Overlay District.
No one from the public spoke.
Alderman Childs motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to come out of Public
Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
5.   Board Action on rezoning of 109 & 113 W. Moore Street
Alderman Childs motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to approve the zoning to
CBD for 109 & 113 W. Moore Street and Open Space for Keziah Park and extend the
parking overlay district.
Discussion
Alderman Coring questioned why a Planning Board member had recused herself from
voting on the zoning request.
Alderman Poole explained that Ms. Meehan had recused herself because, if the
building became available for lease, she may be interested in leasing it.
Alderman Adams stated his opinion the zoning reclassificiation was for the
primary reason of leasing the former Visitors Center building. He stated his
opposition to leasing the building and he noted the City’s need to retain the
building for use by the Police Department during planned renovations to 201 E.
Moore Street. He stated his support for the zoning change to the park.
Mr. B. Wayne Strickland, Building Inspector, explained that the current zoning
creates the non-conforming uses at 109 & 113 W. Moore Street and does not allow
for inclusion of the park as open space classification in the Community Rating
System. He stated the zoning reclassification would correct that situation.
Ayes:   Aldermen Barnes, Poole, Childs
Nays:   Alderman Coring & Adams
Attorney Isenberg advised that four votes were needed to pass a zoning
reclassification as an ordinance requires a majority of the board. Motion
fails.

13.   Noise Ordinance Discussion
   Police Chief Jerry Dove explained the difficulties his officers are
experiencing when answering complaints of loud music on the Yacht Basin. He
noted that the ordinance regulates amplified noise being audible at a distance
of 1,000 feet during certain hours and those venues playing music are located
closer than 1,000 feet to peoples homes.
Attorney Isenberg discussed the specific language of the ordinance. He pointed
out the distance criteria was added in 2002. He remarked that many communities
used to measure decibels but have gotten away from doing so.
Alderman Coring stated his understanding that Brunswick County is in the
process of rewriting the County Noise Ordinance and he suggested the attorney
review the county’s ordinance and parallel it with the City’s ordinance.
Alderman Barnes shared his experience hearing loud music in front of Mr.
Bruton’s home and he identified with Mr. Bruton’s frustration.
Mayor Howard stated his support of police officers in the matter.
Board consensus for the city attorney to review the County ordinance and to
revisit the topic at a future meeting.

contract with Berry, Padgett & Chandler, PLLC. Unanimous vote by an uplift of
hands; motion carried. (contract on file in the Clerk’s office)   
Board Comments
Alderman Coring made the following comments:
“Over the course of the last week, there have been some critical comments
brought to our attention concerning some purchases of equipment of the
Southport Fire Department. I would like to take this opportunity to clarify
some things:
1.   SFD operates its budget totally from a DISTRICT wide FIRE Fee, this fee is
paid by citizens in the city and all citizens in our rural fire district.
2.   The SFD is very fiscally responsible and operates within its budget, and
keeps a revolving fund balance for large capital outlay purchases. Recently we
paid $400,000 down on the tower truck, and paid for the brush unit, outright
without financing options.
3.   We currently have approximately $233,000 in reserves, not inclusive of
what was left over this year. We also remain very strong in our Fireman’s
Relief Fund with nearly $80,000 and over $40,000 in our Fireman’s Fund at New
Bridge Bank.
4.   The SFD does not operate off of wants, but rather needs, the current
equipment purchases of a Polaris and a Utility Truck were budgeted items last
year, and will greatly serve the citizens in our fire district.
SFD remains a fully volunteer department, bringing the savings to our citizens
of at least 1 million dollars a year in personnel costs. We strive to remain
very conservative in our spending and budgeting matters. Questions can always
be directed to the Fire Department Administration. Thank you.”

ALDERMEN CHAMBERS (201 E. MOORE STREET) SOUTHPORT, N.C.

Mayor Howard read a prepared statement:
“An exciting time for Southport is now underway; we have come together today to
finalize contracts, agreements, to announce the first phase of the City’s
Decongestion Plan and to thank our participants in this truly amazing Public
Private Partnership.
The Aldermen behind me and our staff saw the rising traffic levels as an
endangerment to our Citizens. We have signaled an end to the talking and now
confirm that relief is on the way.
Everyone in this room is aware of the dangers caused by the increased traffic
congestion here in the City, this coupled with the fact there is only one
roadway leading into and out of a major portion of our community has placed our
citizens and visitors in an untenable danger in the event of an emergency
evacuation. Tangible evidence is
·   Road way construction at the Sawdust Trail Intersection a few years back
·   Truck accident a few weeks back
We have the potential of being trapped when on the inside, similar to being
“under the Dome.”
The Board of Aldermen is announcing today the resulting effect of a Public
Private Partnership in a second roadway into the Historic Section of our
Community will become a reality immediately.
A second entrance into Southport has often been talked of over the years; as
everyone knows it would deliver the radical improvement needed to get traffic
moving.
Rather than just talk about it, this Board is going to make it happen!
We understand that this will not be the perfect solution, but it will go a long
way to improve our current situation.
The planned extension of Rob Gandy Blvd. from E. Leonard Street to River Road,
where there is currently vacant land, will facilitate a second roadway into the
community with completion expected within the next few months. The completion
of this additional roadway will provide relief for our City and our friends
living on Jabbertown Road.
Several years ago, we called a Summit Meeting by and between our State
Legislative Delegation, the Department of Transportation and the Board to
address this danger to our Community. At that time we discussed
·   The construction of the Beach Road Extension
·   The planned improvement to Highway 211 and 87 expected to take place, I
believe around 2017.
We voiced our concern that we as a community could develop additional roadways
out of town, but that if the State does not improve the feeder routes then and
in that event we could not maximize the benefits of the additional roadway.
When we discussed specifically the essential need for a 2nd roadway, DOT
representatives listened intently, understood and agreed with the need but told
us that it would be 2021 or 2022 before this roadway could become a reality
under the current T1 Plan. They offered their assistance in any way possible
under their operating and budget constraints but were clear that we could not
look to the State for a second roadway in the near future.
Realizing that it was not acceptable to expose our Citizens for another Decade
to the dangers and congestion, this Board invited several business leaders to
consider the situation with us and to partner with the City to provide some
relief.
We had originally hoped to attain an easement from Duke Progress Energy over
their property to maximize the distance from the Sawdust Trail intersection.
When this effort did not materialize, we met with Mr. Cameron Smith a local
developer who owns the property fronting on Leonard Street and backing up near
Rob Gandy. Mr. Cameron Smith, managing partner of Smith-Hill Group, was
instrumental in getting this project off the ground by offering to donate the
60’ right of way to the state that extends approximately 2800’ through their
property. This got us approximately 80% of the way to Rob Gandy. In viewing the
map we found that Mr. Howard Lee and Ms. Aleah McKenzie Muhammad_ had property
between the Cameron Smith property and the end of Rob Gandy.
When we met with Mr. Lee, we immediately found a willing partner. With his
coordination of family members we have obtained approximately an acre of land
over their property.
Then we contacted Ms. Muhammad who also saw the need for her community and
agreed to cooperate with this effort.
Only one industry stepped up to the plate; this was Capital Power; Dave Groves
the plant manager has been sympathetic to our dilemma and supportive of the
fix. Capital Power is stepping up to assist our Community by providing more
than $1M to assist in developing this roadway. Mr. Groves and his Company will
provide a press release immediately following this meeting.
Mr. Groves on behalf of all Southport Citizens we thank you and your Company
for coming to our aid. As a result of your good works and contribution, we can
now look forward to the completion of this roadway within the next few months.
In addition to providing an additional ingress and egress this road will allow
the City in conjunction with the State to reroute the truck traffic through the
community. Thank you sir.
On behalf of all Citizens we want to thank Mr. Cameron Smith, Mr. Howard Lee
and his family and Ms. Muhammad for their willingness to partner with the City
and for their cooperation.
With these properties we had the need, the desire, the property but not the
funding to connect the new roadway to River Road. We then turned again to our
Legislative Delegation. Senator Bill Rabon graciously made this happen for us,
he walked with us every step of the way and without his leadership and
contributions this project would not be a reality today. It is impossible for
us to say how very instrumental Senator Rabon has been with this and other
projects.
Representative Frank Iler gave us his support as well; he always made himself
available to assist our efforts and for this we are grateful to him.
With the assistance of our Legislative delegation we contacted Ms. Karen
Fussell, Division Engineer for DOT’s Division 3. The DOT has awarded the City a
Grant of $180,000.00 towards the $196,000.000 intersection cost, with a promise
from Senator Rabon to attempt to find the remaining balance within this year.
On behalf of the Board, we thank Michael Lee, DOT Board Member, Ms. Fussell and
her associates for their participation and contributions to assist us with this
project including but not limited to assisting us in fast tracking this project
through the regulatory process, clearly we have a wonderful person who
understands people and situations, and this comes through and is impressive.
We firmly believe that our efforts around this corridor will be yet another
reason for those who live in Southport to love and to enjoy Southport even
more.
This Board together with our staff has facilitated an effort of positive change
in our Community. And with this announcement, I want to thank this Board for
their long and untiring work and effectiveness in bringing this project to
reality. Each member of this Board has contributed greatly to this project and
for their efforts we thank them. I do want to single out Aldermen Nelson Adams
and Jim Powell for their untiring efforts that far exceed expectations.
When excites me most about this project is how proactive the community was in
coming together with State and Local leaders to partner with our Businesses to
make Southport a better place to live and to work.”
Mayor Howard introduced Mr. Dave Groves, Capital Power. Mr. Groves acknowledged
the long journey undertaken by a public private partnership to realize a much
needed road. He read an official press release:
Capital Power contributing to new road project in the City of Southport
SOUTHPORT, North Carolina – July 15, 2014 – Capital Power, the owner of the
Southport bio-mass power generation facility located on Powerhouse Drive is
fully financing the extension of Rob Gandy Boulevard approximately one mile
east to East Leonard Street.
Once complete, the public road will eliminate the truck traffic that currently
utilizes Jabbertown Road to transport fuel to the power generation facility.
“This project is a responsible and safe alternative to divert truck traffic
from a residential street while assisting the City of Southport develop a new
road, which was already scheduled to be extended in the future,” said Dave
Groves, Plant Manager Southport Facility. “Traffic and road safety is a
priority for Capital Power and it’s important to use to minimize disruptions to
our neighbors, that’s why we’re developing this new road.”
The new double-lane road will be constructed to standards appropriate for heavy
truck traffic. Capital Power is paying for construction costs and once accepted
by the state, the NCDOT will be responsible for maintaining it. As part of the
project, the existing intersection at Highway 87 (River Road SE) will be
upgraded and a new intersection will be constructed at East Leonard Street.
All necessary permits to construct the road have been received and Thompson,
Corder & Co has been awarded a contract to complete the work. Construction is
expected to begin shortly and is estimated to take approximately 60 days, to
complete weather permitting.
Ms. Fussell expressed her appreciation of the Board’s vision, tenacity and
feats in bringing all parties together. She stated her excitement to see the
project completed.
Mayor Howard emphasized the roles of the attorneys involved and he extended the
Board’s appreciation to Mike Isenberg.
Alderman Powell praised the team effort of those involved.
Alderman Poole thanked Mayor Howard for his leadership through the process and
she expressed admiration to those citizens that donated property noting their
contributions would leave a lasting legacy to the community and their families
for generations.
Alderman Adams expressed gratitude to the unified efforts of all involved.
Attorney Isenberg explained the three (3) agreements for the Board’s
consideration:
1.   Agreement with Dr. Brian Satterwhite for conveyance of a right-of-way
easement to the North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT) for
intersection improvements at Rob Gandy Boulevard and St. Rt. 87.
2.   Construction agreement between the City and NCDOT for intersection
improvements at Rob Gandy and 87.
The City is responsible for obtaining funding for construction.
The City is responsible for intersection improvements at Rob Gandy and 87.
NCDOT has agreed to reimburse the City for $180,000.
3.   Agreement between the City and Capital Power for construction and
reimbursement.
Capital Power is the responsible party to build the entire road on the City’s
behalf. The City reimburses Capital for the construction of intersection
improvements only, which is reimbursed to the City from the State.
The road is built to NCDOT standards and dedicated to the State.
Capital Power has agreements with all property owners. Capital will indemnify
the City for all work and plans.
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Nelson:
That the Board of Aldermen approve the terms of the following agreements:
1.   State small Construction Agreement between the City and NCDOT
2.   Construction Commitment and Reimbursement Agreement between the City and
Capital Power
3.   Agreement for acquisition of an easement between the City and the
Satterwhites
And that the Board authorizes the Mayor to execute the agreement with DOT at
this time and the Capital Power & Satterwhite agreements at such time that all
plans, specifications and contract documents have been approved and authorized
by the NCDOT. By an uplift of hands, a unanimous vote; motion carried.
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Alderman
Poole, second by Alderman Childs. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

Mr. John Keiffer, 404 Clarendon Avenue, spoke in opposition to any future
changes to the noise ordinance citing the impact changes could have on
Southport’s vibrant music scene. He talked about the contributions musicians
have made to the community; New Hope Clinic, individuals in need, and non-
profit groups. He stated his opinion that local venues have made every effort
to adhere to the current noise ordinance.
Mr. Jim Chirico, 111 Caswell Avenue and proprietor of Fishy Fishy Café, pointed
out that Fishy Fishy is a dining destination, employs 80 people in the summer,
40 people in the off season and having music has contributed to keeping the
restaurant open all year. He stated his restaurant’s willingness to work with
the City to find a solution to noise issues and he stated his opinion that
changes to the current ordinance could adversely affect businesses on the
waterfront.
Mr. Eric Lappala, 215 W. Moore Street, stated he had hosted parties at his
residence with local musicians and had never heard any complaints from
neighbors.
Ms. Sherol Lappala, 207 N. Lord Street, stated her support for Southport’s
music scene and her opinion the current noise ordinance is reasonable.
Mr. Daniel Guetschow, 211 River Drive, stated he had measured decibel levels
and found the volume only slighter higher than normal conversation.
Ms. Jill Brown, 122 Yacht Basin Drive, and owner of Yacht Basin Eatery agreed
with prior comments made by her colleagues. She stated she felt the music scene
is enriching the community and the current noise ordinance should remain
unchanged.
Mr. Guy Phillips, Oak Island resident and musician at Fishy Fishy Café, spoke
in opposition to changing the noise ordinance.
Ms. Hope Kennedy High, 610 W. Brown Street, addressed the Board about the
acceptance of water and sewer in Olde Southport and her belief that the
utilities had been accepted by the City in 2003.
Mr. & Mrs. Paul & Maria Swenson, 107 N. Atlantic Avenue, endorsed the comments
made regarding the noise ordinance.

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been petitioned under G.S.160A-31 to
annex the area described below; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
   WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at Southport City
Hall at 6:00 p.m. on July 28, 2014, after due notice by publication on July 16,
2014; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the petition meets the
requirements of G.S. 160A-31;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina that:
   Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-31, the following
described territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City of Southport as
of July 28, 2014:
DESCRIPTION OF TAX PARCEL 2210002707, SOUTHPORT, NC.
To arrive at the point of beginning commence at the right of way intersection
of the west side of Maple Leaf Drive and the north side of Robert Ruark Drive
as shown on Map Book 50 Page 68 recorded in the Brunswick County Registry.
Thence crossing Maple Leaf Drive North 52 degrees 34 minutes 14 seconds East a
distance of 32.93 feet to a point within the right of way. Thence along and
with a curve having a radius of 663.87 feet and a chord bearing of North 60
degrees 59 minutes 06 seconds East a distance of 194.30 feet to a point in the
northern right of way of Robert Ruark drive and the POINT OF BEGINNING.
Thence from said POINT OF BEGINNING, North 53 degrees 12 minutes 18 seconds
East a distance of 39.51 feet to a point. Thence North 53 degrees 12 minutes 18
seconds East a distance of 57.62 feet to a point. Thence North 52 degrees 10
minutes 14 seconds East a distance of 55.63 feet to a point. Thence North 52
degrees 10 minutes 14 seconds East a distance of 56.39 feet to a point. Thence
North 19 degrees 58 minutes 39 seconds West a distance of 22.58 feet to a
point. Thence North 69 degrees 58 minutes 38 seconds East a distance of 70.30
feet to a point. Thence South 71 degrees 09 minutes 03 seconds East a distance
of 141.91 feet to a point. Thence South 70 degrees 36 minutes 33 seconds West a
distance of 380.48 feet to the POINT OF BEGINNING.
   The above described parcel contains 0.40 acres (17,341 sq. ft.)
   Section 2. Upon and after July 28, 2014, the above described territory and
its citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be entitled to the same
privileges and benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said territory

annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the County Board

3.   Waterfront Project Agreement With Criser Troutman Tanner (CTT)
City Manager McDuffie stated that CTT had been provided with past development
plans, the current Southport Comprehensive Pedestrian Transportation Plan and
2015-2020 Parks, Recreation and Open Space Master Plan for their review. He
introduced Mr. Mark Arcuri of CTT.
Mr. Arcuri, discussed the useful information he found in the various plans
provided by the city, the pros and cons of including the City Dock in the
Master Plan, possible cost savings options and public engagements. Responding
to concerns raised by Alderman Childs about duplication of services by CTT and
consultants working with property owners on flood zone designation changes, he
explained the data collected for that purpose will be property specific and
CTT’s data will be more taylored, in a different format and more costly to
incorporate. He pointed out that all wetlands will be located in the project
area and any disturbances avoided.
Alderman Childs motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to authorize the city
manager to execute the contract with CTT in the amount of $138,850 (contract on
file in the City Clerk’s office). Unanimous vote; motion carried.

City Manager McDuffie reported that accepetance of the water and sewer in Olde

ORDINANCE GRANTING APPLICATION FOR ZONING MAP AMENDMENT
    THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other
land use ordinances and a zoning map that control land development within both
the City’s incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s zoning map; and
   WHEREAS, the city staff has filed an application for a zoning map amendment
requesting that 109 and 113 West Moore Street be rezoned from R-10 to CBD; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and has
recommended that the application for zoning map amendment be approved with the
following modifications : (1) that the Parking Overlay District be extended on
both sides of W. Moore Street to the intersection of W. Moore St. and Lord
Street, and (2) that the Keziah Park portion of the property be assigned an
Open Space designation; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on July 10, 2014, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
    WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that the recommendation of the
Planning Board that the property be rezoned from R-10 to CBD, except for the
portion of the property known as Keziah Park, is consistent with the Southport
CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the granting of this
application is reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) the tracts in
question are a non-conforming commercial use in residential zoning, (ii) the
requested rezoning is reasonable in that the majority of the parcels
surrounding the parcels in question are zoned Central Business District;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that 109
and 113 West Moore Street, except for the portion known as Keziah Park, are
hereby rezoned from R-10 to CBD.
   This 28th day of July, 2014.
                     City of Southport
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk

hearing, properly noticed, was held on July 10, 2014, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
    WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that the recommendation of the
Planning Board that the Parking Overlay District be extended on both sides of
W. Moore Street to the intersection of W. Moore Street and Lord Street is
consistent with the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the granting of this
application is reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) the tracts in
question are a non-conforming commercial use in residential zoning, (ii) the
requested rezoning is reasonable in that the majority of the parcels
surrounding the parcels in question are zoned Central Business District;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
Parking Overlay District is hereby extended on both sides of W. Moore Street to
the intersection of W. Moore Street and Lord Street.
   This 28th day of July, 2014.

12.   Insurance
Mayor Howard announced that he had disbanded the Insurance Committee noting his
decision was based on the Board and others being too involved in the duties of
the City Manager.
Alderman Adams and Barnes expressed their appreciatoin to the committee for the
task they undertook and the work they did.
Alderman Coring expressed confusion at the disbanding of the committee and he
read into the minutes the following statement:
“A conversation of emails began on Tuesday July 22 at 1:27 pm in regards of the
scheduling of an insurance meeting as the July meeting had been cancelled. The
emails were between the various members of the committee. After seeing the
conversations back and forth I too chimed in stated that yes we needed to have
a meeting asking the manager to arrange. The emails soon stopped.
It was the next day Wednesday July 23 at 6:24am that I received a reply in
reference to the requrested meeting. I was alarmed once I opened same to see
that it wasn’t from the manager but from Mayor Howard. The Mayor told me that
he had asked that the manager not set a meeting as he wished to discuss it with
the board. The email went on to read that he planned to tell the baord that the
committees work had been done and was complete and that the sole responsibility
be given back to the manager. The Mayor continued to remind me that insurance
comes under the manager and his responsibilities and we as a board are in many
ways interfering with that or “usurping” his duty. The Mayor closed to say he
hoped we could all work together in carrying ouf the Board’s statutorily duties
giving our manager support to manage. Later in the afternoon I called the
manager to discuss the content of the email. The manager listed and without
reciting every word as I cannot recall I can sum up the conversation by saying
this. One of the highlights was me being reminded that the Mayor sets
committees and that he said the committee’s job was done. I asked when that was
decided and at what meeting then I just ended the conversation to say that this
would need to be discussed before the full board.
So to sum this all up let me just say this.
·   I do not appreciate the way the decision to end the committee was made and
has been handled. I feel it should have been handled by way of proper
notification and discussion to the committee chairperson/head and vented down
properly to its members and to the Board of Aldermen. The reason I asked that
the committee be formed was due to the fact that employees felt they had been
walked on and not heard by the manager – who now is being handed back sole
power and responsibility to carry on. One might look at other Committees we
have and question if they are under or carrying out the same “statutorily
duties” you are so quick to mention here. Is that or is that not the Manager’s
roles and duty?
·   If I recall (and I have the copied meeting minutes to show) – the committee
had FULL SUPPORT of this board and a VOTED on MOTION for the committee to be a
“standing committee” throught the year – meeting as a team to work towards the
future of the city’s insurance.
·   Lastly I want to make this clear. I ran for and was elected to this office.
I have attended the required trainings by law and received the same personnel
policy, rules of procedures and charter that each of you did. I do not feel
like I need to be reminded in such ways when it comes to ideas and discussions
such as the manager telling me “the Mayor sets committees” and “reminders” that
we as board members are in many ways usurping the managers responsibilities and
preventing him from duty – then closing to say “thanks” and I’m always
available. When exactly are you available? Wish such harsh words and regards
I’m just not sure anymore.”
Concerned
Alderman Todd Coring
Alderman Coring motioned to keep the committee intact. Motion died for lack of
a second.

11.   Electrical Connection Policy
   City Manager McDuffie explained the proposed revisions to the Electrical
Service Connection Policy and Fee Schedule;
·   If a basic overhead temporary service or new underground service requires
upgrade to electrical facilities within City or Department of Transportation
right-of-way, the City will pay the cost for the upgrades.
·   When primary is extended to provide service to a property, new subdivision
or recombination of properties, the requester will pay the entire cost of the
extension. The requester will pay the entire cost to move primary and secondary
if the requester is recombining lots or asking that the utility be moved for
their aesthetics.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to adopt the revisions to
the Policy & Fee Schedule as presented. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Alderman Adams suggested making reimbursement to those customers who have
incurred costs for transformer upgrades.
The City Manager was directed to provide the cost of reimbursements for one,
three and five years past to the Board at the September regular meeting.
12.   Load Management on New Construction
Manager McDuffie talked about the success of the Load Management Program and he
presented a proposed ordinance amendment to Chapter 19, Article V. Electrical
Service which would require installation by the building contractor or plumbing
or electric sub-contractor of a Load Management switch on all electric water
heaters 40 gallons or larger and all compressor and heat strip circuits on all
standard 240V electric heat pumps or HVAC units in new residential structures.
Alderman Powell spoke in favor of the proposed amendment noting that Apex,
North Carolina has adopted a similar policy and has the lowest electric rate of
all the communities in the Eastern Power Agency.
Alderman Adams stated his opinion the choice to have Load Management switches
should be elective for a homeowner and not mandatory. Alderman Poole agreed.
City Manager McDuffie estimated that approximately 27% of electric customers
have the switches. He pointed out that the switches can be programmed by city
staff to be on or off. He stated the switches cost $150 for water heater and
$175 for AC or heat strips.
Mayor Howard asked Building Inspector Strickland how requiring the switches
would affect issuance of permits. Mr. Strickland indicated he had spoken with
building contractors and the installation of the switches during the time of
construction would be easily integrated and less expensive. He speculated the
cost of labor would be negligible, for a maximum total cost for purchase of the
switch and installation less than $400. He estimated the switches could be
purchased in bulk at a reduced cost by city staff.
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Childs to table the item until the
September regular meeting. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

   Mayor Howard explained a resolution to North Carolina Department of

community, improve public safety, and offer relief to that congested area.

Unanimous vote; motion carried.
A RESOLUTION REQUESTING AN ADDITION
TO THE LONG BEACH ROAD EXTENSION PROJECT
   
   WHEREAS the North Carolina Department of Transportation is undertaking the
construction of the Long Beach Road Extension (R-3324) from NC 87 to NC 133;
and
   WHEREAS J. Swain Boulevard, a collector road in Southport, extends from a
point 2100 feet south of the NC 211/Long Beach Road intersection to a point
within 650 feet of the planned Long Beach Road Extension; and
   WHEREAS the extension of this collector road would significantly facilitate
the flow of northbound traffic from NC 211 and the Dutchman’s Village
development to the Long Beach Road Extension; and
   WHEREAS the City has requested and the property owner has indicated his
willingness to extend J. Swain Boulevard to the Long Beach Road Extension;
   BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport, North
Carolina, that the City of Southport requests that the Department of
Transportation include, in the design for the Long Beach Road Extension, fund
and construct the curb cut and any needed acceleration, deceleration and
turning radius to connect J. Swain Boulevard to Long Beach Road Extension.

18.   Termination of the Insurance Committee
Alderman Coring raised concerns regarding the termination of the insurance
committee stating his opinion that the committee was Board appointed and its
termination was not justified.
After reading the minutes from the meeting in which the committee was
appointed, Attorney Isenberg stated his opinion the motion and second was
unclear to whether the Board was establishing the committee or it was a request
for the Mayor to establish the committee.
Mayor Howard stated he assumed that when the motion was made that he would
appoint the committee from the recommendation made by Alderman Coring.
Alderman Adams stated his support of the recommendation for the committee while
also questioning if the committee should be working under the direction of the
city manager.
Alderman Powell stated his opinion that insurance business is the city
manager’s job.
Attorney Isenberg stated that regardless of who appoints a committee, the
committee is under the direction of the Board unless the Board designates
someone else and the committee does not have any authority unless given
authority by the Board.
Alderman Coring noted that the committee was working alongside the city
manager.
Alderman Coring motioned to keep the insurance committee in force with the same
members. Motion died for lack of a second.
Alderman Poole expressed her opinion the committee was a Mayor appointed
committee. She pointed out that the city manager is the Human Resources Officer
per State statute and that insurance is an HR issue.

20.   Riverfront
Mayor Howard recommended establishing a Riverfront Steering Redevelopment
Committee to help draft a plan for the Southport riverfront evaluation and
development. He suggested the committee report to the Board on the following
points:
   a.   What shall be included in future riverfront development?
   b.   Should the City of Southport incorporate a quasi-public, not-for-profit
riverfront development corporation?
   c.   What types of zones/land use issues should be considered and/or
implemented and how will those affect economic development goals identified by
the task force?
   d.   What, if any, changes to existing street patterns will be required to
responsibly develop riverfront property and how can Southport best interact
with DOT, Corps, Brunswick County and State of NC to ensure desired results?
   e.   What level of site control should the City have over parcels with
potential for development? Should the City identify parcels of land for
acquisition to guarantee a specific end use?
   f.   Which recreational features should be included to complement the
overall plan of development and lead to enhanced quality of life, including but
not limited to: an outdoor amphitheater, walking trails, open space, water
features, plantings, a boardwalk, hotel(s), and any others considered by the
committee or offered by the public.
   g.   Should the City seek conveyance of private land or parcels of
contiguous land and what should be done with such space as it relates to our
riverfront?
   h.   Should the riverfront development be tied in to further development at
the Boat Harbor, Marina, City Property (including former sewer plant) and what
is the most effective way to link riverfront development to Main Street and the
entire historic district?
   i.   What are other successful models for riverfront development throughout
the United States of America and which features from those would work
appropriately for Southport?
   j.   Any other questions identified as appropriate by the Task Force.
Mayor Howard proposed publicizing for residents to make applications to serve
on the committee.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Childs to publicize for applicants
to serve on the committee.
Ayes:   Aldermen Poole, Childs, Powell, Adams
Nay:   Alderman Coring
Motion passes 4-1

“Late last week we received a public records request regarding the upfit of the
City’s administrative offices at 1029 N. Howe Street.
In addition I received an unrelated comment and request for response that there
is chatter in the community that the City’s construction work is being awarded
to Jim Powell’s son-in-law.
Normally, I do not address these type requests or perceptions in public
meetings, however when this Board’s credibility is called into question, we
will step up face them directly, be transparent and disclose all issues and
facts.
The following request for information was received from former City manager Rob
Gandy; all relating to the up fit of the 1029 Building:
1.   The total amount of funds spent
2.   If project exceeded $30K a copy of advertisement for request of formal
bids as

3.   A copy of vendor names of quotes received
4.   A copy of the BOA minutes containing the vote to award the project to the
successful bidder
5.   A copy of scope of services for this project which is required by law
6.   The name of the Construction Company along with the principals of the
company
We don’t want the reality or the perception that we are less than transparent;

make full disclosure.
Mr. Gandy as Interim City Manager was asked by this Board to complete the up
fit of the 1029 administrative offices. It goes without saying Mr. Gandy was a
wonderful City Manager and did an effective and great service as Interim City
Manager last year.
Upon receipt of Mr. Gandy’s request we began assembling the information, then
on Monday morning Mr. Gandy withdrew his request for this information.
The most important thing to me individually and as Mayor is credibility,
honesty and integrity; when there is a question, even a perception, I want to
make sure all information is made available to the public.
First I want to reveal what the minutes disclose regarding the authority to
renovate the building. Mr. Gandy made the decision, which later received
unanimous support from the Board that the Police Department would stay in this
building along with the Board of Aldermen Chambers. That Code Enforcement,
Finance, Planning and Administration would occupy the 1st floor of the 1029
building. Ref. 4.6.13 & 9.12.13 BOA Minutes.
When Mr. Gandy elected not to take the City Managers position that the Board
had offered him, the Board asked the Space Planning Committee to move the
project forward. Ref 9.12.13 & 10.10.13 BOA Minutes
The issues raised are dealt with in state statutes NCGA143-129 & NCGA 143-131.
The statutes require informal bids for contracts from $30k to $500k, then
formal bids for contracts in excess of $500k. If the project is $30k or less
then bidding is not required and the City is free to establish its own
procedure.
∙   The total cost of the construction portion of the project is $66,266.00
which I believe is some 40% less than projected. Only one contract required
informal bids.
∙   Turner Contracting, Inc. who provided construction labor and tools was paid
$35,997.46.
∙   Architectural Service and space planning were $16,495.64.
∙   All other Contracts were significantly less.
Results:
∙   Unexpectedly the labor portion of the job exceeded $30k. We should have
obtained and documented informal bids for this one Contract.
∙   Turner Contracting has an employee who is Alderman Powell’s son-in-law.
∙   Mr. Powell’s son-in-law has never been awarded a contract individually; as
stated above the Company he works for did contract labor and providing tools
for the 1029 Building upfit. The only project he or Turner have been involved
regarding City projects.
∙   While using a Company that employs an Alderman’s family member is not
illegal it presents the wrong perception.
∙   There are no outstanding commitments to any person or Company for work
under consideration by the City. Mr. McDuffie assumed responsibility for all
projects when he joined the staff; he clearly understands the statutes and
perceptions.
In order to assure full transparency we will take this concern to the next
step. I am asking Mr. Minton Padgett of Berry, Padgett and Chandler, whose firm
has the audit contract for the City this year and the City Attorney to examine
the minutes, documentation and financial records together with any other
documents they deem appropriate regarding this issue; then report their
findings and results to the Board of Aldermen in open session.
The fact is that during the transition of City Managers, the Board asked the

mistakes during this time are my sole responsibility, no one on this Board, Mr.

any consequences for any errors or misjudgments.
If any infractions are found during the investigation and audit, then and in
that event I will assume full responsibility.”

4.   Resolution of Support for International Peace Day
Alderman Poole recognized the event coordinators and commended them for their
efforts organizing the first Southport “Peace Day.” She pointed out that
through the Parks and Recreation Department, children would be doing peace
poles which will be placed at the Caswell Avenue Community Garden and City
Hall. She added that an information display case had been set up at the
Visitors’ Center and Ms. Margorie Jones, present in the audience, had
brochures.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Coring to adopt the Resolution in
Support of International Day of Peace. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Aldermen Poole read the Resolution:
RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF INTERNATIONAL DAY OF PEACE
WHEREAS, The United Nations in 1981 established a yearly International Day of
Peace, a day devoted to strengthening the ideals of peace both within and among
all nations and people; and
WHEREAS, The International Day of Peace is now observed around the world each
year on September 21 to put aside all that separates us and to experience
peace; and
WHEREAS, the theme of the 2014 International Day of Peace is “The Right of
Peoples to Peace”; and
WHEREAS, Southport residents are coordinating a celebration of the
International Day of Peace on a local level and encouraging other communities
to create their own events; and
WHEREAS, the Celebration of Peace will be held and will include songs, dances,
informational booths, a Peace board for participants to leave peace thoughts,
and children’s activities creating peace doves, cranes and pinwheels; and
WHEREAS, Peace poles will be installed at the Caswell Avenue Community Garden
and at City Hall; and
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Mayor and Southport Board of Aldermen
on this the 11th day of September 2014, hereby proclaim Sunday, September 21,
2014 as “Peace Day” in the City of Southport and urge all citizens to join in
the festivities of this day and promote peace among all peoples.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

10.   Utility Adjustment Policy
Mayor Howard pointed out that Alderman Childs would not be participating in the
discussion and vote.
City Manager McDuffie discussed recent large leaks of water customers and his
subsequent review of the city’s utility rate structure. He identified that the
water rates are based on two functions; the cost to purchase the water from the
County and Operation and Maintenance (O&M) of the distribution system. He noted
when a large leak is found, it is not practical to collect O&M costs. He stated
that historically the City has adjusted the sewer charge for a large water
leak. He indicated staff is recommending, retro-active to July 1, 2014, that
customers experiencing a large water leak only be charged with the purchase
cost of the water. Responding to queries by Mayor Howard and Aldermen Poole,
Adams and Powell, City Manager McDuffie stated that moving forward, when a
customer receives a large bill, a leak is discovered and verified by a plumber
or city staff, the city will charge for a six-month historical usage rate by
the customer and the customer would be issued a credit for the overage.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to approve the Utility
Adjustment Policy as presented by the City Manager.
Discussion
Alderman Adams indicated he had met with the city’s meter reader and the
equipment used to read the meters notifies the meter reader of a reading that
is above the normal usage. City Manager McDuffie pointed out the meter reader
reads approximately 100 water meters and 124 electric meters per day.
Alderman Coring suggested researching further technological capabilities for
indication of abnormal usage prior to issuance of the utility bill.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

12.   Parking on Davis Street
City Manager McDuffie reported he had received a request from citizens that
live on N. Davis Street to change parking from parallel to diagonal for easier
and safer access to their driveways. He stated there are currently 11 parking
spaces and changing to diagonal parking would allow for a total of 14 spaces.
He presented a proposal from Southern Asphalt, Inc. in the amount of $4,050 to
do asphalt work and stripe the spaces.
Alderman Adams suggested deferring consideration of the request to explore what
issues the parking change would address and what complications could be
created. Alderman Coring agreed and pointed out a raised concrete wall on the
east side of Davis Street that would be problematic. Alderman Barnes asked
about the proposed length of the parking spaces and he discussed the
possibility of trucks extending into the street.
Item deferred to a future meeting.

City Manager McDuffie stated that the North Carolina Department of
