additional parking spaces could be realized on Moore and Howe Streets, during
the upcoming repaving and marking, had concluded that the existing parking
spaces are the maximum allowable.
14.   Speed Limit on Howe and Moore in Downtown
City Manager McDuffie provided a staff recommendation to decrease the speed
limit to 25 mph on Moore Street between Rhett and Howe and on Howe Street
between Moore and Leonard.
Police Chief Dove reported that NCDOT had twice turned down a request from the
City to reduce the speed limit from 35 mph to 25 mph along Moore and Howe
Streets. He stated he had contacted NCDOT and they would review the accident
rate and perform a radar check of vehicular speeds. Chief Dove pointed out that
the 35 mph speed is rarely exceeded along Moore and Howe Streets and most
accidents occur in the Wal-Mart parking lot.
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to adopt a resolution
requesting NCDOT lower the speed limit from 35 mph to 25 mph on Moore Street
between Rhett and Howe and from Howe Street between Moore and Brown Street.
Discussion
Alderman Adams stated his opposition noting that the area has a very low
occurrence of auto accidents and the reduction will create a speed trap.
Ayes:   Aldermen Powell, Barnes, Childs, Coring, Poole
Nay:   Alderman Adams
Motion carried 5-1
RESOLUTION REQUESTING ACTION BY THE NCDOT DIVISION OF HIGHWAYS
WHEREAS, the safe use of State roads and highways is of utmost importance to
not only the citizens of Southport, but also to our visitors from this great
State and other states and countries; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport have been concerned
with the safety of motor vehicles, bicyclists and pedestrians on Highway 211,
Howe and Moore Streets, through the downtown area of the City; and
WHEREAS, the speed limit on Highway 211, unless otherwise posted, is typically
35 mile per hour, which the Board is concerned is too high for specific areas
of downtown; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen respectfully request that the North Carolina
Department of Transportation perform an analysis of traffic speeds between
Rhett Street and Brown Street on NC 211.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Southport Board of Aldermen requests
that the North Carolina Department of Transportation assist the Board in
reducing the posted speed limit between Rhett and Brown Streets (SR 211) to 25
miles per hour.
This the 11th day of September, 2014.

RESOLUTION REQUESTING REPLACEMENT OF THE NC 211 DUTCHMAN CREEK BRIDGE
WHEREAS, the safe use of State roads and highways is of utmost importance to
not only the citizens of Southport, but also to our visitors from this great
State and other states and countries; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport have been concerned
with the safety of motor vehicles, bicyclists and pedestrians on Highway 211;
and
WHEREAS, the Dutchman Creek Bridge on Highway 211 is a narrow two-lane bridge;
and
WHEREAS, safety would be improved if the bridge and approaches were widened to
accept four lanes of traffic and bicycle paths.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Southport Board of Aldermen requests
that the North Carolina Department of Transportation widen the NC 211 Dutchman
Creek Bridge and its approaches to accept four lanes of traffic and bicycle
paths.
This the 11th day of September, 2014.

2.   Board Action on Zoning of 88 Acres
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Childs to adopt the Ordinance
granting the initial zoning classifications of Highway Commercial (HC) and
Planned Unit Development (PUD) for the 88 acres, consistent with the CAMA Core
Land Use Plan Future Land Use Map. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
RESOLUTION GRANTING APPLICATION FOR THE INITIAL ASSIGNMENT OF ZONING
CLASSIFICATIONS
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other
land use ordinances and a zoning map that control land development within both
the City’s incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s zoning map; and
   WHEREAS, Oak Island Building Supply, Inc., as owner of the hereinafter
described property, petitioned the City for non-contiguous annexation of said
property and said property has now been annexed by the City; and
   WHEREAS, Wakefield Associates, Inc., on behalf of the owner, has filed an
application for initial zoning classification assignments for said 88.89 acres
of property located on the north side of NC 211 requesting that 33.25 acres be
zoned for Highway Commercial and the remaining acreage be zoned for Planned
Unit Development; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and has
recommended that the application for the requested zoning classifications be
granted; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on September 16, 2014, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds the application for the initial
assignment of Highway Commercial and Planned Unit Development zoning for the
property as requested by Wakefield Associates, Inc. in the application is
consistent with the Southport Unified Development Ordinance, the Southport CAMA
Core Land Use Plan and the City of Southport Transmission Facilities Agreement
mutually adopted by the City and the County of Brunswick; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the granting of this
application is reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) the location
and the size of the tract in question lends itself to the nature of the split
zoning requested and (ii) the character of the mixture of existing commercial
and residentially developed properties in the vicinity of the property suggest
a compatibility with development that may be anticipated within the zoning
classifications to be assigned.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
assignment of the zoning map designations as requested by Wakefield Associates,
Inc. is hereby granted.
      This 16th day of September, 2014.
                     City of Southport
                     By: /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

4.   Tour Commission Recommendation of Ordinance Update
Ms. Cindy Brochure, Tourism Director, gave an overview of the proposed
revisions to Chapter 10, Article VII For-Hire Tours of the Southport Code of
Ordinances. She reported that the requests to operate tours in Southport had
increased and there is no provision in the ordinance to regulate the number of
tours. She indicated there are currently three (3) driving tours, one (1) horse
and buggy tour, two (2) walking tours and one (1) bicycle tour. She emphasized
the safety considerations for the residents of Southport and visitors to the
city. She stated the recommendation of the Tourism Commission is to:
∙   Permit no more than 3 walking tours, 4 low-speed vehicle tours and 1 animal
drawn vehicle tour at any one time
∙   Require a valid driver’s license
∙   Conduct a criminal record check
∙   $50 application fee
∙   Each tour guide permit granted will be valid for one year and must be
renewed annually
∙   Tour must operate for 90 consecutive days or permit will be revoked
Alderman Barnes stated his opinion that the number of tours should be self-
regulating by the demand.
Alderman Adams stated he had received complaints about the number of tours and
the disruption to travel around the city.
Responding to Alderman Coring, Ms. Brochure reported the recently adopted
regulations for time and location of advertising signs for the tours had been
well received by tour operators and is being strictly enforced. She pointed out
that the Tourism Commission is charged with making recommendations and
reporting annually to the Board.
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Powell to adopt the Ordinance
Amending Chapter 10, Article VII. Unanimous vote by an uplift of hands; motion
carried. (Ordinance on file in the Clerk’s office)
5.   Parking on Davis Street
City Manager McDuffie reported that a demonstration of the proposed diagonal
parking on Davis Street had been viewed by the Board. Concerns were raised that
the travel lane would be too close to the sidewalk. He stated that one of the
residents of Davis Street had withdrawn support for the parking change.
Consideration of the staff recommendation died for lack of a motion.
6.   Request DOT Install Crosswalks on Howe and Moore Streets in Downtown
City Manager McDuffie discussed aspects of street intersection bulb outs
proposed in the recently adopted Southport Comprehensive Pedestrian
Transportation Plan. He reported that North Carolina Department of
Transportation (NCDOT) will be resurfacing Moore and Howe Street with
completion expected prior to Memorial Day 2015. He suggested including
construction of the bulb outs along the resurfacing route. He indicated he did
not have a cost to include the bulb outs but anticipated it would deplete the
entire budget of Powell Bill funds.
Alderman Powell pointed out the need to coordinate with NCDOT to change the
truck route to Rob Gandy Boulevard to eliminate trucks using Howe and Moore
Streets. He noted that intersections with bulb outs would not accommodate the
turning radius for trucks.
Alderman Adams spoke against depletion of Powell Bill funds.
Mayor Howard acknowledged that synchronizing with NCDOT, during their
resurfacing project would be ideal. He stated his opinion that an informed
decision could not be made at this time.
Alderman Barnes stated his support for future installation of bulb outs,
pointing out that former City Planner, Amy Nelson, had proposed similar
intersection improvements.
Alderman Adams emphasized the need to prioritize street and sidewalk projects.
Alderman Coring requested marking and placement of signs identifying crosswalks
on Bay Street.
City Manager McDuffie was directed to coordinate with NCDOT for striping of
crosswalks during the resurfacing project. Too, he will obtain costs for
installation of bulb outs.
7.   Discussion & Consideration of Action on Community Building Charges

departments would be required to pay rental fees for use of the Community
Building and he stated his belief that was not the intention of the Board when
adopting the Community Building rental rates.

internal departmental usage of the Community Building.
Discussion

Community Building by city departments.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT
WHEREAS, recognitions and citations are extended to CPT Bryan K. Anderson for
directing and extending Combat Life Saver Skills to a World War II Veteran; and
WHEREAS, on the 4th of July 2014 CPT Anderson responded to the excessive
bleeding of a World War II Veteran during the North Carolina Celebration
Parade, and
WHEREAS, the Veteran’s health was maintained and ensured due to quick and
skillful response to the emergency and knowledge of Life Saver Skills; and
WHEREAS, his professionalism, calming execution and direction and providing of
assistance allowed for higher level of medical care by preventing degradation
of vital signs and stopping loss of blood; and
WHEREAS, this act of heroism deserves special recognition and commendation by
the governing board of the City of Southport.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Southport Board of Aldermen and the
citizens of this community extend sincere appreciation and special thanks to
CPT Bryan K. Anderson for his heroic actions in directing and providing Life
Saver Care to a World War II Veteran.
DULY RESOLVED THIS THE 9th Day of October 2014.

Vision Awareness Month
Proclamation
Southport Lions Club
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club is working to increase vision awareness,
especially among the youth through vision screening at local schools; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club collects over 1,500 pairs of glasses each
year and provides assistance to those needing, but unable to afford, eye exams
and the purchase of glasses; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club conducts vision screenings on the fourth
Thursday of each month at the New Hope Clinic, and at the Brunswick County
Health Festival in September; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club has covered the expense of cataract surgery
for 8 needy individuals over the past 2 years; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club continues to keep with the challenge Helen
Keller issued to the association in 1929 to become “knights of the blind in the
crusade against darkness;” and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club, established in 1945 is composed of men and
women volunteers who dedicate their time to the betterment of our community and
aiding those in need; and
NOW THEREFORE, I, Robert Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC and the
Board of Aldermen in recognition of this important service sponsored by the
Southport Lions Club, do hereby proclaim October as Vision Awareness Month.
ADOPTED, this 9th day of October 2014 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
                     /s/ Robert Howard, Mayor      
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

CERTIFICATE OF SUFFICIENCY
To the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport, North Carolina:
I, Michele Windham, City Clerk, do hereby certify that I have investigated the
attached petition and hereby find that said petition is signed by all owners of
real property lying in the area described therein in accordance with G.S. 160A-
58.1.
I further find that the area meets the standards for a noncontiguous area as
specified in G.S. 160A-58.1(b), in that:
1.   The petition includes a metes and bounds description of the area proposed
for annexation and has attached a map showing the proposed satellite area in
relation to the primary corporate limits of the City of Southport.
2.   The petition includes the names and addresses of all owners of real
property lying in the area described therein.
3.   The petition includes the signatures of all owners of real property lying
in the area described therein, except those not required to sign by G.S. 160A-
58.1(a).
4.   The nearest point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is no more
than three (3) miles from the primary corporate limits of the City of
Southport.
5.   No point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is closer to the
primary corporate limits of any municipality other than the City of Southport.
6.   The satellite area is so situated that the City of Southport will be able
to provide the same services as are provided within its primary corporate
limits;
7.   To the extent that the proposed satellite area contains any portion of a
subdivision, the entire subdivision is included;
8.   By Act of the North Carolina General Assembly, the City of Southport is
not subject to the 10% limitation of G.S. 160A-58.1(b)(5).
9.   The petitioner has not declared vested rights.
In witness whereof, I have hereunto set my hand and affixed the seal of the
City of Southport, this   9th  day of October, 2014.
/s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk

AGENDA
8.   Resolution Supporting Lion’s Club October Vision Awareness Month
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Adams to adopt the Resolution
Supporting Lion’s Club October Vision Awareness Month. Unanimous vote; motion
carried.
9.   Update on the Audit of the 1029 Building
City Attorney Mike Isenberg presented a report on his examination of Board
meeting minutes and other documents pertaining to the renovation of City Hall.
He discussed the adoption of the plan for use, expenditure approval, role of
the Space Planning Committee, and the company contracted to do the work. He
stated that the hiring of Turner Contracting Company, who employs Alderman
Powell’s son-in-law, was not prohibited as a conflict of interest. Attorney
Isenberg pointed out that the renovation cost exceeded $30,000, that informal
bids should have been obtained and a contract should have been executed before
work commenced. He added that the auditing company Berry, Padgett and Chandler
would be providing a financial audit report on the project with the annual
audit.
10.   Load Management Switches on New Construction
Elle Pittenger, Load Management Coordinator, presented a load management
comparison of communities with mandated load management switches for new
construction and the associated cost.  (Comparison included as Attachment #1)
City Manager McDuffie pointed out that those communities that mandate the
switches on new construction have lower electric retail costs. He recommended
adoption of an amendment to Chapter 19, Article V of the Code of Ordinances to
mandate placement of load management switches on electric water heaters, heat
pumps and HVAC units installed in new residential construction.
Alderman Adams spoke against mandating the switches and he advocated better
educating Southport electric customers to the Load Management Program.
Alderman Barnes shared his experiences with load management and spoke in favor
of requiring the switches during construction.
Mayor Howard spoke in support of amending the Ordinance.
Alderman Powell stated his load management switches have never interfered with
his electric demands and his bills are lower than that of a neighbor who does
not make use of the switches.
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Powell to amend Chapter 19,
Article V Electrical Service as presented by staff.
Discussion
Alderman Adams repeated his opposition.
Alderman Poole agreed with Alderman Adams and she stressed informing new
construction applicants of the option.
Alderman Powell stated his opinion that mandating the switches would be a step
toward reducing the overall electric rate.
Alderman Childs emphasized the need to improve getting the benefits of
participating in the Load Management Program out to customers.
Vote   Aye:   Aldermen Barnes, Powell
   Nay:   Aldermen Adams, Poole, Childs, Coring
Motion Failed 4 – 2
11.   Consideration of Time Extension for Transient Boaters at the City Pier
Alderman Barnes presented a proposal to amend the current 24 hour stay policy
for transient boaters at the Yacht Basin City Dock. He contended that
permitting a stay of 48 hours would allow boaters to enjoy the amenities of
Southport. He noted that boaters would continue to check in at time of arrival
with the Police Department.
Alderman Barnes moved, second by Alderman Powell to amend the policy and allow
transient boaters to stay for 48 hours at the City Dock. Unanimous vote by a
show of hands; motion carried.
12.   Budget Amendment #8 to move a part-time position to full-time Community
Development Specialist
City Manager McDuffie explained the request for Budget Amendment #8 to expand
the part-time planning position vacated by Bob Grant to a full-time position
with additional duties to include special projects. He indicated the salary
proposed would be $45,000 annually. Responding to a query by Alderman Coring,
City Manager McDuffie stated that funding for the position would be 50%
Planning/Code Enforcement/Inspections and 50% divided equally into General
Fund, Water and Sewer funds. He pointed out that there are multiple city
projects underway simultaneously and the city is experiencing an annual growth
rate of 6% in development.
Alderman Coring opposed creating an unbudgeted position. He talked about the
cost for benefits and he recommended keeping the position part-time or using
someone from the League of Municipalities.
Alderman Adams expressed his opposition to a full-time position citing the
Board’s conservative stance at budget time and the recent staff restructuring
aimed at assisting the city manager. He raised concerns that long time
employees’ salaries had not been adjusted.
Mayor Howard spoke in support of the full-time position noting the demands the
Board has put on the manager and staff.
Alderman Poole discussed the surge in annexations, development and the
incomparable skill set Mr. Grant possessed that will be difficult to replace
with a new hire.
Responding to a query from Alderman Powell, City Manager McDuffie explained
that the part-time salary for the position had been budgeted for fiscal year
2014-2015
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Childs to approve Budget Amendment
#8.
Aye:   Aldermen Poole, Childs, Powell
Nay:   Aldermen Adams, Coring, Barnes
Aye:   Mayor Howard to break tie
Motion Carries 4-3

…………………………………………
Mayor Howard made comments about the recent water rate increase. He pointed out
that the city purchases water from Brunswick County and the County raises the
rate the city pays by 2 – 3% annually; i.e., to purchase 3,000 gallons of water
in 2005 was $16.50, 2007 - $19.15 and 2014 - $23.95. He discussed the switch
from drawing water from city wells to the purchase of water from the County due
to an abundance of iron and minerals in the well water. He expressed regret
that the City water rates had not been incrementally raised to keep up with the
cost.
Alderman Barnes noted that a city water rate increase had not been done since
2006. He recommended reviewing the rates on an annual basis.
Aldermen Childs and Coring emphasized the need to better notify customers of
rate increases.
Mayor Howard reported that the audit would not be completed by the October 31
due date. The Board tasked the city manager with determining why the audit was
going to be late and to put procedures in place to assure that future audits
would be completed on time.
City Manager McDuffie reported that the former Building Inspections/Code
Enforcement building was scheduled for demolition during the week of October
13. He indicated construction bids for the new public restrooms would be
obtained in November, construction would begin in January 2015 and the
restrooms would open to the public in April or May. He stated the cost for the
facility is anticipated to be under the formal bid threshold. He added that he
expects construction on the Rescue Squad renovation project to begin in May or
June 2015 and construction of the Police Department renovation project to begin
in July 2015.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Adams to adopt the Resolutions In
Recognition of Capt. Bryan K. Anderson and Sgt. Alisha Espinoza. Unanimous
vote; motion carried.

is privileged or confidential under state law and G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for
discussion of personnel issues. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

   The Board discussed the orientation and configuration of the Aldermen’s dais

E)   Public Comment
   Ms. Roberta Dosher, 210 W. Moore Street, asked for consideration of a 4-way
stop at W. Moore Street and Caswell Avenue and a 3-way stop at Bay Street and
Caswell Avenue. She expressed her concerns about pedestrian safety and sight
distances at the intersections, noting an increase in traffic and excessive
speed in the area. Ms. Dosher presented a petition to the Board with 32
signatures in support of the request.
   Mr. Gary Claussen, 102 S. Fodale Avenue, requested consideration of reducing
the speed limit from 45 to 35 on an approximately 3/10th of a mile section of
North Howe Street between River Road and Tidewater Plaza. He stated the
reduction would permit golf carts to travel to the many businesses on that
portion of Howe Street; 7 restaurants, 10 retail businesses, 15 service
facilities, 3 medical centers. He contended that the speed limit reduction
would reduce emissions and residents’ fuel costs. Mr. Claussen presented a
petition with 17 signatures in support of the speed limit reduction.
Mayor Howard referred Ms. Dosher and Mr. Claussen’s concerns to the Police
Department and the Traffic & Transportation Committee for study and
recommendation to the Board.

CITY OF SOUTHPORT
PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, on Friday, November 14, the City of Southport will host a wine and
cheese reception to welcome the Sail 2014 Snowbird Rally; and
WHEREAS, the Snowbird Rally is an annual journey south along the Intracoastal
Waterway (ICW) by longtime and aspiring “cruisers”; and
WHEREAS, this year’s rally launched November 1 in Hampton, Virginia and will
conclude December 15 in Miami, Florida; and
WHEREAS, the “cruisers” make major and intermediate stops along the way; and
WHEREAS, Southport, North Carolina is a 2014 intermediate stop.
NOW  THEREFORE, by virtue of authority vested in me, as Mayor of Southport and
on behalf of our citizens, I do hereby extend to the Snowbird Rally, a most
cordial and sincere welcome to our City.

AGENDA
2.   Public Hearing: CAMA Core Land Use Plan
Alderman Childs motioned, second by Alderman Poole to go into Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Jacob Vares, Cape Fear Council of Government (COG), presented an overview of
the process to update the Plan. He stated he worked closely with Mr. Bob Grant
and city staff, public engagement was pursued via on-line questionnaires with
over 100 responses, brochures were placed throughout the city and public
engagement sessions were held. He stated the Plan is a play book for land use
decisions and used heavily by planning boards. He indicated the Plan, upon
adoption by the City, would be presented to the Coastal Resource Commission
(CRC) for adoption. (Plan available for review in the Clerk’s office).
There were no public comments.
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Childs to come out of Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
3.   Consideration of Adoption of the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan
Alderman Barnes, a Planning Board liaison and former Planning Board member,
stated his appreciation of the efforts put into the update of the Plan by city
staff, the Planning Board and COG. Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman
Powell to adopt the Resolution of Adoption of the 2015 CAMA Core Land Use Plan.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
RESOLUTION OF ADOPTION OF THE 2015 CAMA CORE LAND USE PLAN
WHEREAS, beginning in January of 2013 and culminating in September of 2014, the
City of Southport Planning Board, with the assistance of the Cape Fear Council
of Governments, conducted an open, thorough, conscientious and methodical
review and update of the City of Southport’s 2007 CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, having finalized the task it was charged with by the Southport Board
of Aldermen to guide, direct and complete the CAMA Core Land Use Plan update
process, the Southport Planning Board, a meeting conducted September 18, 2014,
approved a Resolution recommending adoption of the 2015 CAMA Core Land Use Plan
and forwarded it to the Board of Aldermen for consideration and appropriate
action; and
WHEREAS, following a Public Hearing conducted at a regular meeting of the Board
of Aldermen on November 13, 2014, the Southport Board of Aldermen found the
policies and maps contained within the draft 2015 CAMA Core Land Use Plan to be
consistent with the City’s desired vision for the future and officially adopted
said plan as presented; and
WHEREAS, the adopted plan will now be submitted as required by state law to the
Wilmington District Planner for the Division of Coastal Management under the
North Carolina Department of Environmental and Natural Resources and forwarded
to the Coastal Resources Commission (CRC) for consideration and appropriate
action; and
WHEREAS, following ratification by the Coastal Resources Commission (CRC), a
certified copy of the 2015 City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan shall be
forwarded to the Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management (OCRM) for
federal approval.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
hereby adopts the 2015 City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and it is
further resolved that the City Manager or his designee is hereby authorized to
submit the adopted Plan to the State for certification as described above.
DULY ADOPTED, this the 13th day of November,
2014.                                                /s/ Robert D. Howard,
Mayor

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE
            CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has been petitioned under G.S. 160A-58.1 to
annex the area described below; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at the Rivermist
Amenity Center, 5020 J. Swain Boulevard, Southport, NC 28461 at 6:00 pm on
November 13, 2014, after due notice by publication on October 29, 2014; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the area described therein meets the
standards of G.S. 160A-58.1(b), to wit:
a.   The nearest point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is not more
than three
(3) miles from the primary corporate limits of the City of Southport;
b.   No point on the proposed satellite corporate limits is closer to the
primary corporate limits of any other city than to the City of Southport;
c.   The area described is so situated that the City of Southport will be able
to
provide the same services within the proposed satellite corporate limits that
it
provides within the primary corporate limits;
d.   No subdivision, as defined in G.S. 160A-376, will be fragmented by this
proposed
annexation;
e.   By Act of the North Carolina General Assembly, the City of Southport is
not subject to the 10% limitation of G.S. 160A-58.1(b)(5); and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the petition has been signed
by all the owners of real property in the area who are required by law to sign;
and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the petition is otherwise
valid, and that the public health, safety and welfare of the City and of the
area proposed for annexation will be best served by annexing the area
described;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina that:
Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-58.2, the following
described non-contiguous territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City
of Southport as of November 13, 2014:
Being all of that certain parcel or tract of land lying and being in Smithville
Township, Brunswick County, North Carolina and being more particularly
described as follows:
Beginning at an Iron Pipe found in the western right of way of North Carolina
Highway 211 (150 ft. R/W), said Iron Pipe being the Northeast corner of the
lands claimed in Deedbook 2721, Page 69; thence leaving aforesaid right of way
and with the northern line of the above referenced deed, S 70°02'59"W, 199.78
feet to a Rebar Found, the northwest corner of the lands claimed in the above
referenced deed and the northeast corner of the City of Southport as claimed in
Deedbook 252, Page 50, thence continuing, S 70°02'59"W, 99.94 feet and with the
northern line of the City of Southport to an Iron Pipe found in the eastern
line of Southport Tidewater WMS, LLC; thence with aforesaid eastern line, N
23°10'01"W,199.93 feet to an Iron Pipe Found, the southwest corner of the lands
of James F. & Sarah Faircloth as claimed in Deedbook 368, Page 661; thence with
the southern line of Faircloth, N 70°00'00"E, 299.86 feet to an Iron Pipe found
in the western right of way of North Carolina Highway 211; thence with said
right of way, S 23° 07'23"E, 200.18 feet to the place and point of beginning,
containing 1.37 acres according to a survey by Norris & Ward Land Surveyors,
P.A. dated July 25th, 2014 to which reference is made for a more full and
accurate description.
Section 2. Upon and after November 13, 2014, the above described territory and
its citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the   City of Southport and shall be entitled to the
same privileges and  benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said
territory  shall be subject to municipal taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10.
Section 3. The Mayor of the City of Southport shall   cause to be recorded in
the office of the Register of Deeds of Brunswick County and in  the office of
the Secretary of State at Raleigh, North Carolina, an accurate map of the
annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the Brunswick
County Board of Elections, as required by G.S. 163-288.1.
Adopted this 13th day of November, 2014.

of Southport

the NC211 Dutchman Creek Bridge;
   The referenced bridge is Brunswick 24. Current statistics are as follows:
   Sufficiency Rating – 52.19 (out of 100). Must be < 50 to qualify for federal
replacement.
   Functionally Obsolete, not structurally deficient.
   Originally built in 1922, rehabilitated in 1952.
   Deck, Superstructure and Substructure ratings are all “5” which is fair.
   The bridge is not posted less than legal load.
This project is included in R-5021, widening of NC 211. Under this project, the
current 37.5’ long bridge is scheduled to be replaced with 140’ long dual
bridges. Project is currently on track for let in 2021.
If this bridge required widening prior to the widening of NC 211, I would
estimate a replacement cost in the range of $3-4M.
Another point is that once the Long Beach Road Extension Project is completed,
traffic will not be as heavy on this section of roadway.

    Mayor Howard listed the agenda items to be considered:
∙   Duke Progress Energy request for sewer service
∙   Brunswick County Proposed Sewer Service Agreements Amendment
∙   Discussion of sewer capacity issues
∙   Christmas bonus for city employees
∙   Closed Session for a personnel matter
1.   Duke Progress Energy
   City Manager McDuffie explained a request made by Duke Progress Energy for
sewer service outside the City’s corporate limits to Duke Energy’s Brunswick
Nuclear Plant (BNP). He pointed out that City policy requires annexation unless
the Board waives the requirement, in order to receive city services but Duke
Progress Energy lobbies that annexation of the BNP is not practical. City
Manager McDuffie discussed the advantages of providing the BNP with sewer
service. He indicated the land and building values of approximately $44M are
set by the State. At the city’s current tax rate Duke Progress Energy would pay
$109,000 annually for property taxes if annexed into the city. He stated that
staff recommends negotiating an agreement with Duke Progress Energy to provide
sewer without annexation and, in lieu of property taxes, an amount equal to the
amount of taxes be charged to Duke Progress Energy for as long as the BNP
receives the service. City Manager McDuffie indicated Duke Progress Energy
would be required to pay impact fees in the amount of $3M and incur the cost of
connecting to the sewer system.
   Responding to questions, City Attorney Isenberg indicated the City is not
obligated to provide sewer service and any agreement in lieu of annexation
would be treated like a contract for services.   
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to authorize the Utility
Committee and the City Manager to negotiate a contract with Duke Progress
Energy and bring the proposed contract to the Board for consideration.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
2.   Brunswick County Proposed Sewer Service Agreements Amendment
   City Manager McDuffie explained a proposed sewer service agreements
amendment from Brunswick County;
∙   The County would assume remaining debt on Sandy Lane pump station and 16”
force main; approximately $596,000
∙   Upon assumption of debt, City would deed and dedicate pump station and
force main to County
∙   City would agree to amend the limits of the Sewer Service Area to the
limits of the City of Southport ETJ (extra-territorial jurisdiction)
   The City Manager stated staff could not recommend amending the current Sewer
Service Agreements with Brunswick County.
   Alderman Powell pointed out that the proposed amendment would inhibit
Southport’s growth.
   No action taken on the proposal.
3.   Sewer Capacity
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the city’s sewer capacity limit of
500,000 gallons would be taxed if Duke Progress Energy was provided sewer
service. He suggested the Utility Committee and staff examine alternatives for
increasing the sewer capacity. Board consensus to accept the City Manager’s
recommendation.
4.   Christmas Bonus for City Employees
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Poole to give Christmas bonuses
to city employees; $175 for full-time employees and $125 for part-time
employees. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
5.   Closed Session – 4:27 p.m.
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Powell to go into Closed
Session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for discussion of personnel issues.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

4.   Lease Agreement with Historic Society for Old Jail
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Poole to approve the lease

to adopt the Resolution Authorizing Lease of City Property for a term of 10
years for the sum of $1 per year. Unanimous vote; motion carried.   
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING LEASE OF CITY PROPERTY
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport owns the old Brunswick County jail site
located at 318 E. Nash Street, which site the Board finds is currently surplus
to the city’s needs; and
   WHEREAS, the City and the Southport Historical Society have agreed upon a
lease under which the Southport Historical Society will lease the City’s
property described above for a term of 10 years beginning December 10, 2014;
and
   WHEREAS, in consideration of leasing this property, the Southport Historical
Society has agreed to pay the sum of $1 per year and to make all necessary
improvements, additions and alterations to the property and be responsible for
all repairs, maintenance, insurance and expenses; and
   WHEREAS, N. C. G. S. 160A-272 authorizes the City to enter into leases of up
to 10 years upon resolution of the Board of Aldermen adopted at a regular
meeting after 10 days public
notice; and
   WHEREAS, the required notice has been published and the Board is convened in
a regular meeting;
   NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN RESOLVES that the Board hereby
approves the lease of the city property described above to the Southport
Historical Society for 10 years and directs the City Manager to execute any
instruments necessary to the lease.
   Adopted December 11, 2014.         City of Southport

8.   Approval of Agreement for Lord Street Gym
City Attorney Isenberg reviewed the details and terms of the Memorandum of
Understanding Between City of Southport and Brunswick Community College for
acquisition by the City of the Lord Street Gym:
∙   The boundary of the property to be conveyed
∙   Fee simple warranty deed
∙   If city fails to renovate and open the facility within seven (7) years or
ceases to use the building for public recreational purposes, the title could
revert back to the College
∙   City agrees to paint the exterior and replace the roof within two (2) years
from the date of the recording of the deed
∙   City agrees to renovate the interior of the building within seven (7) years
from the date of the recording of the deed
∙   The College may use the facility without fee at such times as the facility
is not being used by the City
Alderman Adams stated his support for the agreement and shared his vision and
expectations of how the facility can serve the community. He discussed applying
for a grant to get the project started and he emphasized the “can do” spirit of
Southport government and citizens to raise funds to improve the quality of life
for all.
City Manager McDuffie discussed a new Department of Commerce grant program and
he explained that Ms. Heather Hemphill, Director of Parks and Recreation, had
prepared a grant application for $50,000 towards the Lord Street Gym project.
He stated an additional $150,000 for replacement of the roof and $11,000 for
exterior painting would need to be raised within two years in order to be in
compliance with the Memorandum of Understanding.
Alderman Powell recounted a previous Board pledge not to commit any taxpayer
dollars to the renovation of the gym. He suggested giving the Lord Street Gym
Committee time to determine if donations can be raised for the project.
Alderman Adams noted that an in-house campaign to raise the needed funding is
being planned. He emphasized the importance of the City owning the building
prior to asking people to pledge.
Alderman Barnes stated his support for the project and pointed out the
consideration before the Board was for an acquisition agreement and not for
expenditure of funds.

AGENDA
1.   Police Department/Board Chambers & EMS Headquarters
City Manager McDuffie updated the Board:
∙   The Emergency Services Committee had met,
∙   Contracts in place with Cape Fear Architecture, PA and Norris & Tunstall
Consulting Engineers for architectural and engineering services,
∙   The basic design plans are being presented to the Board
∙   Project Estimate: EMS with addition - $500,000
Police/Board Chambers - $1M
The Board reviewed full size drawings of the design plans for the renovation of
the Police Department/Board Chambers & EMS Headquarters.
Mayor Howard discussed the lengthy time the projects are taking. He emphasized
the objective of upgrading the city’s deteriorating buildings and the
considerations critical for the best way to accomplish that within an
established budget. He questioned when the projects could go out for bids. City
Manager McDuffie estimated the EMS building could be ready for bids in either
June or July and the Police Department could go out for bids in July or August.
2.   Public Restrooms
The Board reviewed the plans for public restrooms to be constructed at 107 E.
Nash Street. Aldermen Powell reported the bid came in at $264,000, was
negotiated down to three (3) construction options; $193,000, $175,000 and
$165,000.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Childs to authorize the Building
Committee and City Manager to finalize negotiations for Option 3 and to realize
the operation of the facility by June 1. Unanimous vote by an uplift of hands;
motion carried.
3.   Street Lights
City Manager McDuffie presented recommendations and pricing from Brunswick
Electric Membership Corp (BEMC) for street light fixtures. The Board discussed
the options with emphasis on providing a safe environment for pedestrians.
Decorative fixtures and placement locations were considered along with lighting
type; high pressure sodium vs. LED, life expectancy of the different material
types of poles and candlepower.
Alderman Adams motioned, second by Alderman Poole to make aluminum poles the
standard City of Southport street light pole at a cost of $1,070 per pole.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Adams to adopt 1.5 candlepower as
the standard for all City of Southport street lights. Unanimous vote; motion
carried.
4.   Outside City Limits Sewer Rate for Existing Industry
Alderman Barnes presented the Rate Committee’s recommendation for sewer service
rates for customers outside the city limits.
City Manager McDuffie pointed out that the rates are based on the size of the
water tap. He noted also that three (3) businesses outside the city are
currently receiving sewer service at an inside city rate and with the adoption
of the proposed rates, their rates would change.
Board consensus to adopt the sewer rates as recommended by the Rate Committee
for sewer customers outside the city limits. Rates will be effective at the end

5.   Duke Progress Energy
City Manager McDuffie advised that, now that the Outside City Limit Sewer Rates
have been adopted, the Utility Committee would continue negotiations with Duke
Progress Energy for the City to provide sewer service to the Brunswick Nuclear
Plant (BNP).
6.   Amendment to Section 19-138 of the Code of Ordinances
Mayor Howard proposed for consideration, an amendment to Section 19-138 of the
Code of Ordinances entitled “Initiation of water and/or sewer projects outside
corporate limits” which allows for the Board to waive the annexation
requirement in order for industry outside the city limits to be provided sewer
service by the City of Southport. The amendment would waive the requirement of
annexation for any industrial entity which:
1.   Was in business prior to January 1, 2014;
2.   Employs 200 or more employees, and
3.   Is located within the city’s sewer service area
Aldermen Poole, Childs and Barnes spoke in support of the proposed amendment.
Consideration of the proposed amendment will be made in the January 8 regular
meeting.

Committee and City Manager to negotiate with ADM to reach a mutual agreement to
provide sewer service to ADM by the City of Southport per the following:
∙   ADM to pay a one-time fee; $64,000
∙   $53.25 Base Rate
∙   ADM required to connect to city’s pump station on Moore Street
∙   ADM required to furnish a flow meter and vault
∙   ADM required to upgrade the pumping station when the flow increases
 Unanimous vote; motion carried.

Mayor Howard spoke about the City’s impending need for additional sewer
allocation, the County’s inability to provide the allocation and that the Town
of Oak Island may consider selling one (1) million gallon capacity to the City.
He noted that in August 2014, the City went over its current 500,000 gallon
capacity.

12.   Request to add Southport to State Health Plan
Mayor Howard talked about the increased cost for employee health care citing
the cost of $150,000 annually 10 years ago compared to $648,000 currently and
the expected increase going forward. He noted an option for municipalities to
consider is going on the State Employee Health Insurance Plan. To do so would
require a local bill authorizing the city’s eligibility.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to ask local delegation to
make Southport eligible for the State Employee Health Care Plan. Unanimous
vote; motion carried.
13.   Moving Start of Pay Period from Thursday to Tuesday
Mayor Howard explained that employee payroll is processed on Thursday with pay
on Friday which leaves no time to process payroll if there is a power failure
or the Human Resources Technician is ill.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to authorize staff to back
up processing of payroll to Tuesday without any impact to employees
compensation. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 19 OF THE CODE OF ORDINANCES
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Section
19-138 of the Code of Ordinances entitled “Initiation of water and/or sewer
projects outside corporate limits” is hereby amended to read as follows:
(a)   It shall be the general policy of the city to permit extensions of water
and sewer service outside the city’s corporate limits only when those areas or
developments simultaneously with the request for service petition the city for
annexation (including non-contiguous annexation) where practical. Service shall
not be considered prior to annexation.
(b)   The application for service shall contain a valid petition from the
applicant requesting annexation or, if annexation is not practical, a written
statement setting forth the reasons why annexation would not be practical, or a
written statement setting forth the request for waiver and documentation
verifying that the standards set forth in subsection (c) below are met.
(c)   The Board of Aldermen shall have the authority to waive the requirement
of annexation when it determines that annexation would not be practical,
legally possible or would not be in the best interest of the City. In addition,
the Board may waive the requirement of annexation for any industrial entity
which (i) was in business prior to January 1, 2014, (ii) employs 200 or more
employees, and (iii) is located within the city’s sewer service area. In this
event, the city manager shall prepare an extension agreement providing for
service without annexation, which agreement must be approved by the Board of
Aldermen in order to be effective.
(d)   The application for service shall contain written statements agreeing to
the city’s water and sewer extension policy, particularly Section 19-136.
Furthermore, the applicant shall be responsible for one hundred (100) percent
of the cost of the improvements, other related facilities and rights of way or
easements necessary to construct the improvements.
This the 8th day of January, 2015.         City of Southport
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

RESOLUTION FOR THE CLOSING OF CAPITAL PROJECT BUDGET ORDINANCE FOR THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT SAFE ROUTES TO SCHOOLS
WHEREAS, the Aldermen for the City of Southport pursuant to Section 13.2 of
Chapter 159 of the General Statutes of North Carolina created a Capital Project
Ordinance adopted on the 10 th day of January, 2013 for the Safe Routes to
Schools funded by a federal grant from the NC Department of Transportation; and
WHEREAS, the funds for the Southport Safe Routes to Schools, at a projected
cost of $125,000, were appropriated from the Capital Reserve Fund in accordance
with the Ordinances for the City of Southport and Section 22 of Chapter 159 of
the General Statutes of North Carolina; and
WHEREAS, the actual expenditure of funds for Southport Safe Routes to Schools
totaled $121,357.81 leaving a balance of $3,642.19 with all costs of the
project being accounted for;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, that
the Capital Project Ordinance for the Southport Safe Routes to Schools be
closed and the $3,642.19 balance of appropriated funds be unappropriated and
made readily available in the City of Southport’s general fund.
THE FOREGOING RESOLUTION WAS ADOPTED BY THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT ON JANUARY 31,

allocation from the Town of Oak Island through an agreement with Brunswick
County to transfer 750,000 – 1M gallon to Southport from Oak Island at a
projected cost of $970,000 annually through 2031 at which time Southport would
own the capacity.

Board Comments
   Alderman Barnes opened a discussion regarding the recent time change of the
regular Board meetings. He indicated he had received many e-mails about it and
he felt the reason for the change was unclear to many Southport citizens.
   Mayor Howard stated the Board strives to get people to attend meetings and
members have been told that citizens that do not get out a night and retirees
are unable to attend the night meetings. So in an effort to attract more
people, the meeting time was changed to 1:00 p.m.
   Alderman Poole, Adams and Powell echoed the Mayor’s comments.
   Alderman Coring indicated he had been overrun with calls, comments and
messages and speculated that if meeting attendance did not improve, the Board
may want to reconsider the meeting time.
   Alderman Childs stated she had received calls supporting the time change.
   Alderman Coring suggested that the Emergency Services Committee look at the
recommendation to have Animal Control services placed under law enforcement.
   Alderman Childs raised concerns that city staff would not be able to attend
the 1:00 p.m. Board meetings. Additionally, she requested periodic reports on
the progress of the Lord Street Gym Renovation Project.

4.   Arbor Day Proclamation
City Clerk Windham read the Arbor Day Proclamation into the record.
Alderman Childs motioned, second by Alderman Poole to approve the Arbor Day
Proclamation. Unanimous vote; motioned carried.
ARBOR DAY PROCLAMATION
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/199f40a54a06f19a9324bf64df539e216304d812/
IMAGES/0-0-0-1620_1366x1395.jpg]
 
WHEREAS, in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of
Agriculture that a special day be set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS, this holiday called Arbor Day, was first observed with the planting of
more than a million trees in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS, Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS, trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and
water, cut heating and cooling costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air,
produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for wildlife, and
WHEREAS, trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes,
fuel for our fires, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic
vitality of business areas, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual
renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE, I Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC, do
hereby proclaim February 12, 2015 as ARBOR DAY in the City and urge all
citizens to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees and woodlands,
and
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote
the well-being of this and future generations.
DATED, this 12th day of February, 2015.
                        By: /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk

6.   Consideration of Rezoning
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to approve the Ordinance
Granting Application for Zoning Map Amendment to rezone 254 E. 11th Street from
Residential (R-10) to Office/Institutional (O/I) and 250 & 252 E. 11th Street
from Business District (BD) to O/I. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
ORDINANCE GRANTING APPLICATION FOR ZONING MAP AMENDMENT
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other land
use ordinances and a zoning map that control land development within both the
City’s incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
       WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general
welfare and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is
necessary for the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider
appropriate revisions, modifications and additions to the city’s zoning map;
and
       WHEREAS, the city staff has filed an application for a zoning map
amendment requesting that 254 East 11th Street be rezoned from Residential (R-
10) to Office/Institutional (O/I) and 250 and 252 East 11th Street be rezoned
from Business District (BD) to O/I; and
       WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and
has recommended that the application for zoning map amendment be approved; and
       WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a
public hearing, properly noticed, was held on February 12th, 2015, before the
Board of Aldermen regarding this issue; and
        WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that the recommendation of
the Planning Board that the property be rezoned from R-10 and BD to O/I is
consistent with the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
       WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the granting of this
application is reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) the tract at
254 East 11th Street is a non-conforming commercial use in residential zoning,
(ii) the tracts at 250 and 252 East 11th Street are not contiguous to other BD
zoning, (iii) the current use of the properties is allowable under O/I zoning;
       NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that
254 East 11th Street be rezoned from R-10 to O/I and 250 and 252 East 11th
Street be rezoned from BD to O/I.
    This 12th day of February, 2015             City of Southport
                                          BY: /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

7.   Public Hearing; Taxi Cab Application
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Childs to go into Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Attorney Isenberg explained that the applicant has the burden of proof to
satisfy the Board regarding the following factors:
   (1)   Whether or not the public convenience and necessity require such
proposed or additional taxicab service within the city.
   (2)   The financial responsibility of the applicant and the likelihood of
the proposed service being permanent, responsible and satisfactory.
   (3)   The number and condition of equipment.
   (4)   The schedule of proposed rates, if required by the board to be
charged.
   (5)   The number of taxicabs now operated and the demand for increased
service, if any, and whether or not the safe use of the streets by the public,
both vehicular and pedestrian, will be preserved and whether or not adequate
provision has been made for off-street parking of such taxicabs.
   (6)   The experience of applicant in the taxicab business.
   (7)   Such other relative facts as may be deemed necessary and advisable.
Mr. Robert Edge and his wife explained to the Board their desire to start a
clean, reliable taxi cab service to benefit the community. Mr. Edge, responding
to Attorney Isenberg’s concerns relating to the status of Mr. Edge’s driver’s
license, stated he had applied to have his license renewed.
Mr. Robert Gainer, 415 W. West Street, stated his appreciation of
entrepreneurs.
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Childs to come out of Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

10.   Request by Rebecca B. Smith to Become BEMC Customer
Mrs. Rebecca B. Smith, 5215 Southport-Supply Road presented her request for a
release from Southport Utilities in order to become a member of Brunswick
Electric Membership Corporation.
Introduction Remarks
a.   My name is Rebecca B. Smith
b.   I am a lifelong citizen of Brunswick County.
c.   I thank the Southport Board of Aldermen for this opportunity to petition
government for redress, which is my Constitutional right.
2.   The Situation
A.   I asked Brunswick Electric Cooperative to become a member and to begin
receiving its services.
B.   I was advised that I need to seek a release from the Southport Utilities
because the Southport Utilities could block my membership.
C.   I sought a release through the Mayor of Southport, He denied my request.
D.   I am left with this option of seeking an appeal through the City of
Southport Board of Aldermen
E.   Today, I am seeking an appeal to the Mayor’s decision to deny my right to
be released from the Southport Utilities jurisdiction.
F.   I have 3 point to make in support of my request.
3.   First Point is about Fair Representation
A.   I do not live in the City of Southport city limits.
B.   I am not afforded an opportunity to vote for the mayor, Board of Alderman
or other City officials.
C.   As a result, I fail to see the fairness of being subject to a government
agency where I have no voice.
D.   The City of Southport does not provide any municipal services to me. Not
fire, not police, not trash, not water, not sewage.
E.   It seems unreasonable to me to have a government where I have no
representation deny me a legal right to choose a utility of my choice.
F.   The Mayor’s decision should be reversed because the unilateral control of
my services resembles taxation with representation.
G.   On its face, this is fundamentally unfair.
4.   The Second Point is About Equal Protection
A.   As a US, NC, and Brunswick County citizen, I deserve equal protection
under the law.
B.   To me, this means that I should be treated like everyone else.
C.   Equal treatment means equal opportunities to pursue legal choices.
D.   The reason given to me by the Mayor when I sought a release was that if I
were released, others might also seek a release.
E.   It seems to me that government should have a set of standards that apply
to all citizens.
F.   No standards were offered by the Mayor.
G.   Without standards, the Mayor’s decision seems vague, arbitrary and
capricious.
H.   This is further aggravated then I have learned that my neighbors have been
given the option to become members of Brunswick Electric Cooperative.
I.   This is a fairness issue.
J.   I am not treated equal to other similarly situation citizens.
K.   The Mayor’s decision should be reversed because I deserve equal protection
under the law.
5.   My Final Point if About Public Policy.
A.   While I am the plaintiff for this request, the Southport Board of Alderman
should consider the public policy implications of your decision.
B.   This subject should be a matter of much interest to the community and the
press.
C.   If government of any kind can make decisions that unfairly affect a single
person, then other citizens are at risk of unfair treatment.
D.   I am not taking a stand for benefit of the community.
E.   I am but one person who believes her rights as a citizen have been
violated.
F.   But as you ponder how you will treat me as an individual, you should
consider the impression you leave with the community on how any persons will be
treated.
G.   For this reason, the Mayor’s decision to deny my release from the
Southport Utility should be reversed because his position is not a good public
policy.
6.   Summary
a.   Thank you again for hearing my complaint.
b.   I respectfully ask that the Mayor’s decision be reversed and that I be
granted a release from the Southport Utilities.
Mayor Howard remarked that the request is not a governmental action but a
utility provider action. He noted that the City has funded infrastructure that
is required to provide electricity in the city’s franchise area as designated
by the Utilities Commission. He stated his position that the city has an
obligation to serve the service area.
City Manager McDuffie explained the location of Ms. Smith’s residence, that the
electric service territories were established in the 1960’s by the N.C. General
Assembly, and the City purchases generation capacity based on the size of its
service area.
Alderman Coring pointed out that Ms. Smith’s residence is in the Southport Fire
Department district.
Alderman Powell noted that Ms. Smith lives 1.5 miles out of the city limits and
several neighboring properties, i.e. Rivermist Subdivision, Newbridge Bank and
Bella Cucina shopping center are within the city limits.
City Manager McDuffie and Attorney Isenberg verified that to their knowledge, a
release has never been made.
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Childs to table the item in order
to get more information.
Discussion
Alderman Adams raised concerns about setting a precedent for release requests.
Alderman Coring requested staff provide a map of the service area.
Ayes:   Aldermen Coring, Childs, Powell, Adams
Nay:   Alderman Poole
Motion Carried 4-1

Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Powell to go into Public Hearing.

   Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Coring to adopt the Ordinance

ORDINANCE GRANTING APPLICATION FOR ZONING MAP AMENDMENT
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other land
use ordinances and a zoning map that control land development within both the
City’s incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
      WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general
welfare and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is
necessary for the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider
appropriate revisions, modifications and additions to the city’s zoning map;
and
      WHEREAS, the property owner has filed an application for a zoning map
amendment requesting that 621 N. Fodale Avenue be rezoned from Multi-Family
(MF) to Office/Institutional (O/I); and
      WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and
finds the proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance to be
consistent with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommend
their approval; and
      WHEREAS, pursuant to North Carolina General Statutes and city ordinances,
a public hearing, properly noticed, was held on March 12th, 2015, before the
Board of Aldermen regarding this issue; and
       WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that the recommendation of
the Planning Board that the property be rezoned from MF to O/I is consistent
with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
      WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that the granting of this
application is reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) the tract at
621 N. Fodale Avenue is a non-conforming commercial use in residential zoning,
(ii) the current use of the property is allowable under O/I zoning, and (iii)
the use of the property is compatible with adjoining properties;
      NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that
621 N. Fodale Avenue be rezoned from MF to O/I.
This, the 12th day of March, 2015
                                          City of Southport

4.   Public Hearing; Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Childs to go into Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.   
Mr. Allen explained that the newly enacted North Carolina Statute, G.S. 160A-
383.5 required zoning approval of “temporary health care structures” in single-
family areas provided there is a qualifying need, the structure qualifies and a
set of regulatory requirements are met;
Temporary Healthcare Structure. A temporary structure no more than 300 gross
square feet that will house a single mentally or physically impaired person.
Structure must be assembled off-site and meet the standards of the State
Building Code. It must not be placed on a permanent foundation and may be
required to connect to water, sewer and electric utilities. Only one such
structure is permitted per lot. Subject to all requirements of North Carolina
General Statute 160A-383.5.
Mr. Allen pointed out that an annual permit must be obtained for the structure
and once the need no longer exists, the structure has to be removed. Noting the
high cost of the structures, Mr. Allen stated he did not foresee a demand for
them. He indicated the Planning Board had found that meeting the requirements
of G.S. 160A-383.5 was consistent with the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan
and recommended that the Board of Aldermen adopt amendments to Article 2 & 10
of the Unified Development Ordinance.
No one from the public spoke.
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Adams to come out of Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
5.   Consideration of UDO Text Amendment
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Childs to adopt the Ordinance and
approve the UDO Text Amendments as presented. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   AN ORDINANCE APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENTS TO THE UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
      WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general
welfare and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is
necessary for the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider
appropriate revisions, modifications and additions to the city’s land use
ordinances; and
   WHERAS, City Staff, in conjunction with the Planning Board, has prepared
proposed amendments to Article 2 and Article 10 of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and find
the proposed amendments to the Unified Development ordinance to be consistent
with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommend their
approval; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N.C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on March 12, 2015, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby find that these
proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with
the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHERAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest in that they are necessary in order to
ensure consistency with recent changes to North Carolina General Statutes
related to temporary health care structures.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments to Articles 2 and 10 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted.
   This, the 12th day of March, 2015.               City of Southport

that staff did not foresee any potential use of the property by the City. He

recent sales of similar lots have sold for $8,000 - $9,000, and there are no

Resolution
In Memory of
Mary Louise Herring Childs
WHEREAS, the City of Southport Mayor, Board of Aldermen and employees mark with
sympathy the passing of Mary Louise Herring Childs; and
WHEREAS, Mary Childs served as Alderman of the City of Southport, and exercised
sound judgment and a wise and kindly counsel, endearing herself to her
associates; and
WHEREAS, Meezie, as she was affectionately known, dedicated her life to
community service, family, church, and rendering efficient, faithful and
invaluable service in all she undertook as social worker, florist, and local
business owner; and
WHEREAS, we mourn her loss and extend to the Child’s family this expression of
our condolences and with knowledge that her passing will leave an unfilled void
in the minds and hearts of all those who knew her personally; and
WHEREAS, we sincerely hope that you will be comforted by the memories of your
loved one and her life, and all who mourn with you; and
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that Mayor Robert D. Howard and the Southport
Board of Aldermen convey to the Child’s family this Resolution in Memory of
Meezie, evidencing our deepest grief and sympathy; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that we urge all citizens to join with the Southport

Alderman Powell reported that he and Alderman Barnes had met and reviewed the
sewer impact rates. He stated they focused on the allocation and related impact
fees with a recommendation of $20/gallon for single family dwelling (sfd)
development on over two (2) acres. Alderman Barnes noted the rate would not
change for development on less than 2 acres.
The Board reviewed examples provided of the proposed rates vs the rates of
Brunswick County and discussed the need to set the rates at an amount that
would be competitive and reasonable.
Alderman Barnes motioned to adopt an amendment to Appendix A, Wastewater
Allocation Impact Fee Schedule to change the single family dwelling (SFD)
development wastewater impact fee from $30/gallon to $20/gallon and to amend
the third paragraph to read;
“For proposed new subdivided development on less than 2 acres (including the
division of existing lots
plated at the time of the initiation of this schedule), duplex or multi-family
development, or any other
development where a wastewater utility system extension permit is required
where plans are approved
by the City subsequent to the adoption of this schedule, the following shall
apply:”
There was no second to the motion.
The Board further evaluated the rate differential between the city and county
to arrive at an equitable rate.
Alderman Barnes amended his motion to adopt an amendment to Appendix A,
Wastewater Allocation Impact Fee Schedule to change the single family dwelling
(SFD) development wastewater impact fee from $30/gallon to $16.50/gallon, and
amend paragraph three. Second by Alderman Powell. Unanimous vote; motion
carried.
Operation & Maintenance of Sewer Operating System
   City Manager McDuffie reported he had a discussion with Brunswick County
Manager Ann Hardy, regarding the county doing operation and maintenance (O&M)
of the city’s sewer operating system. He stated Ms. Hardy indicated the county
had taken ownership of the Sunset Beach system, including debt, cash and
associated assets, and would prefer a similar deal with the city. She advised
him that the first step would be for county employees to do an assessment of
the city’s system.
   City Manager McDuffie advised the Board that, after his meeting with Ms.
Hardy, it came to his attention that city employees had been informed that the
County was taking over O&M for the city. He indicated he had met with city
employees, this date, to help alleviate their anxiety and render them more
comfortable with the events that had occurred.
   Mayor Howard pointed out that the Board had no intention of relinquishing
ownership of the city’s sewer system.

A RESOLUTION RECOGNIZING THE NATIONAL DAY OF PRAYER
WHEREAS, civic prayers and national days of prayer have a long and venerable
history in our constitutional republic, dating back to the First Continental
Congress in 1775; and
WHEREAS, the Declaration of Independence, our first statement as Americans of
national purpose and identity, made “the Laws of Nature and Nature’s God” the
foundation of our United States of America and asserted that people have
inalienable rights that are God-given; and
WHEREAS, the Supreme Court has affirmed the right of state legislatures to open
their sessions with prayer and the Supreme Court and the U.S. Congress
themselves begin each day with prayer; and
WHEREAS, in 1988 legislation setting aside the first Thursday of May in each
year as a National Day of Prayer was passed unanimously by both Houses of
Congress and signed by President Ronald Reagan; and
WHEREAS, the National Day of Prayer is an opportunity for Americans of all
faiths to join in united prayer to acknowledge our dependence on God, to give
thanks for blessings received, to request healing for wounds endured, and to
ask God to guide our leaders and bring wholeness to the United States and her
citizens; and
WHEREAS, it is fitting and proper to give thanks to God by observing a day of
prayer in the City of Southport when all may acknowledge our blessings and
express gratitude for them, while recognizing the needs for strengthening
religious and moral values in our State and Nation; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of
Southport, and Board of Aldermen do hereby proclaim May 7, 2015 as “A DAY OF
PRAYER IN SOUTHPORT” and urge all citizens of Southport to observe the day in
ways appropriate to its importance and significance.
This 9th day of April 2015.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
City of Southport
2015 Earth Day Proclamation
WHEREAS, our home, this planet Earth, is adversely affected by population
growth and rapid depletion of resources; and
WHEREAS, since the first Earth Day in 1970, the Clean Air Act has made the
nation’s air cleaner, the Clean Water Act has improved water quality, and the
Endangered Species Act has attempted to preserve ecosystems to maintain the
variety of species; and
WHEREAS, following the principles of reduce, repair, reuse and recycle,
residents can improve their environment; and
WHEREAS, preservation is easier and less expensive than restoration; and
WHEREAS, Earth Day provides an opportunity for members of the community to
study, learn and teach local activities which will contribute to protecting our
planet’s ecosystem; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of
Southport, do hereby proclaim Wednesday, April 22, 2015, as
EARTH DAY
to be observed by all citizens in ways to better understand, appreciate, and
preserve the resources of our earth, and especially the resources of this area.
This 9th day of April 2015.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
AGENDA
4.   Adopt Proclamation in Support of National Safe Boating Week
Alderman Barnes read the Proclamation into the record.
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Coring to approve the Resolution
in Support of National Safe Boating Week. Unanimous vote; motioned carried.
Proclamation
Recreational boating is fun and enjoyable, and we are fortunate that we have
sufficient resources to accommodate the wide variety of pleasure boating
demands. However, our waterways can become crowded at times and be a place of
chaos and confusion. While being a marvelous source of recreation, boating, to
the unprepared, can be a risky sport. Not knowing or obeying the Navigation
Rules or the nautical “Rules of the Road,” drinking alcohol or taking drugs
while operating a boat, or choosing not to wear your life jacket when doing so
is clearly NOT the smart thing to do, are all examples of human error or a lack
of proper judgment. One particular behavior that can reduce the number of
boaters who lose their lives by drowning each year by is the wearing of a life
jacket. It is a simple task that has the potential to reduce terrible loss in
lives.
Knowledge and skills are important in reducing human error and improving
judgment. If people are aware of the risk, they are likely to take the
precautionary measures to protect themselves and their friends and family. That
is why we must continue to spread the messages of boating safety not only
during National Safe Boating Week but also throughout the entire year.
Whereas, on average, 700 people die each year in boating-related accidents in
the U.S.; approximately 71% of these are fatalities caused by drowning; and
Whereas, the vast majority of these accidents are caused by human error or poor
judgment and not by the boat, equipment, or environmental factors; and
Whereas, a significant number of boaters who lose their lives by drowning each
year would be alive today had they worn their life jackets; and
Whereas, today’s life jackets are more comfortable, more attractive, and more
wearable than styles of years past and deserve a fresh look by today’s boating
public.
Therefore, I, Robert D. Howard, do hereby support the goals of the North
American Safe Boating Campaign, the United States Coast Guard and the Coast
Guard Auxiliary and proclaim May 16 – 22, 2015, as National Safe Boating Week
and the start of the year-round effort to promote safe boating.
In Witness Thereof, I urge all those who boat to Wear It! and practice safe
boating habits.
Given under my signature and the seal of

5.   Presentation by Gordon Walker & Judy Gordon Regarding John Smith Cemetery
Ms. Judy Gordon, Chairperson of The John N. Smith Restoration and Preservation
Committee and Mr. Gordon Walker spoke to the Board about the efforts of the
Committee and the establishment of the Friends of the John N. Smith Cemetery,
to make improvements and ensure regular maintenance of the cemetery. Ms. Gordon
discussed the history of the 1880 cemetery that is the site of more than 800
interments of many local black citizens who contributed to the growth and
development of Southport; slaves, farmers, teachers, businessmen, laborers,
domestic servants, homemakers and veterans from the Civil War and subsequent
military campaigns.
Ms. Gordon pointed out that contributions are needed to fund publication of
narrative and pictorial history, ground radar penetration to locate unmarked
graves, upgrading and installing markers, design and implement a landscaping
plan and install an attractive perimeter fence. She stated the Committee is
reaching out to the community to recruit volunteers and raise the funds needed
to ensure the cemetery’s future as a unique and respected site for celebrating
an honorable past.
Ms. Gordon and Mr. Walker thanked the City for its’ continued assistance
keeping the cemetery in a respectful condition.
