10.   Street Lights
City Manager McDuffie reported that Brunswick Electric Membership Corporation
(BEMC) had reduced the price of concrete street light poles to be comparable to
the price for aluminum poles and had provided five (5) options of arms and
light fixtures for the Board’s consideration.
Alderman Barnes stated his opinion that decorative poles and light fixtures
should be used in the downtown area and on the waterfront. He stated his
support for a concrete pole with Option 2; decorative 8’ arm with bell shaped
LED fixture.
Responding to a query by Alderman Coring, City Manager McDuffie explained that
the candlepower of Option 2 was 1.5 per sq. ft. and meets State requirements
and North Carolina Department of Transportation (NDCOT) recommendation.
Mayor Howard read the request submitted by the Waterfront Steering Committee:
“We ask the Board of Aldermen only consider attractive lighting that is in
keeping with the beauty of Southport.”
Waterfront Steering Committee member, Harley Lemons, stated the Committee voted
on the options via e-mail and 5 of the 9 members preferred Option 2.
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to accept Option 2 with a
concrete pole.
Discussion
Alderman Poole stated her opinion that the Board had always thought the lights
should be decorative.
Confusion ensued about the shape, color, cost and order quantity of the poles.
Staff directed to confer with BEMC representatives present and return with a
firm recommendation by the end of the meeting. Motion withdrawn; no action
taken.
11.   Approval of Sign Design for City Hall
After a brief discussion about the type of construction material for the sign,
the City Manager was directed by Board consensus to obtain pricing for a
sandblasted sign and have the lettering displayed in the City of Southport
print font.
12.   Use of City Vehicles by City Hall Employees
Alderman Coring pointed out that there had been discussion previously about
parking overcrowding at City Hall and vehicles subsequently being parked on the
grass. He indicated that he had asked the City Manager to provide the formula
used by the Police Department allowing Police Department personnel to drive
city vehicles home. Alderman Coring requested the Board consider allowing two
(2) City Hall employees to drive their city vehicles to and from work to help
reduce the number of vehicles in the City Hall parking lot.
City Manager McDuffie explained that police officers living further than 12
miles from the Police Department pay, $144 per mile per year, for the privilege
of driving a city vehicle to their home.
Mayor Howard raised concerns about preferential treatment unless the option was
provided to all city employees.
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to permit the Animal
Control Officer and Building Inspector to drive their city vehicles home.
Discussion
City Attorney Isenberg indicated that permitting city employees other than
police officers to drive city vehicles home could result in tax consequences
for the employees.
Alderman Barnes withdrew his second. No action was taken.
Aldermen Barnes and Adams requested the city manager to provide the Board with
a listing of city employees on call and to prepare a policy for consideration.
13.   Board of Aldermen Vacancy
   Mayor Howard pointed out that the Board has the authority to fill the vacant
seat on the Board until the November election at which time the position will
be filled for the remaining portion of the term.
   Alderman Barnes nominated Ms. Emily Humphreys.
   Alderman Coring nominated Ms. Regina Alexander.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to close the nominations.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Mayor Howard called for a vote.
   Ms. Humphreys:   Aldermen Barnes, Poole, Adams
   Ms. Alexander:   Alderman Coring
   Alderman Powell did not cast a vote. By a 3-1 vote, Ms. Humphreys was
appointed to fill the Alderman seat for Ward 1 through the election.
14.   Update; 2015 Regional Risk Management Services Meeting
Ms. Mosley gave an overview of the 2015 Regional Risk Management Services
Meeting attended by herself and the city manager. She stated the meeting,
presented by the North Carolina League of Municipalities, entitled “More Than
Insurance,” encompassed employment practices, health insurance renewal
percentages, and risk management initiatives. She noted it was emphasized that
municipalities should have job descriptions for every employee. She pointed out
that the League offers a classification study for providing job descriptions
which for Southport would be approximately $8,700. She stated the funding for a
study will be submitted in the FY 2015-2016 budget. Ms. Mosley explained the
benefits of “Tel-A-Doc,” a new service provided by the League.
Recess - 3:20 – 3:24 p.m.

City Manager McDuffie explained that he had received a request from the Fire
Department to designate a portion of 10 th Street as a No Parking Area.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to designate the north side
of the 100 block of 10 th Street as a No Parking Area. Unanimous vote; motion
carried.

round concrete pole. Unanimous vote by an uplift of hands; motion passed.

Mayor Howard talked about the feasibility and possibility of putting Southport
utilities underground at an estimated expenditure of $18M. He spoke about the
upcoming sale of the North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency (NCEMPA)
generating assets to Duke Energy Progress and the opportunity to consider
issuing bonds up to an amount that would be funded through the cost savings. He
indicated that the Board would be conducting Town Hall meetings to make a
comprehensive presentation to the citizens when specifics of the savings are
known.

Board Comments
Mayor Howard made the following statement:
Democracy demands at least two things of power … that power not be held in too
few hands and that it never be held in the same hands for too long ….
I have been Southport Mayor since December 2009, when the current term ends
during December of this year I will have enjoyed serving the Citizens of this
community as Mayor for six years; the time is right to step aside from this
phase of my inspiration; serving our community. During the upcoming filing
period, I will not file for reelection. I have been honored by the opportunity
to serve my fellow citizens and to help shape the future our city for three
full terms.
As a courtesy to any others who may wish to seek the position, it is important
that I make my intentions known at this time. However, we still have a lot of
work to do in the next seven months and I am confident that our Board of
Aldermen team will remain focused on following through on our plans and the
many projects that are underway.
I arrived at this decision some weeks ago and reconsidered it over this past
weekend and the days leading up to this meeting to be sure I felt comfortable
following through with this decision and making this announcement today.
All I’m really interested in; is doing things that help people. I really care
about the lives of people in Southport. The greatest professional job I could
have is to serve my hometown. Southport and its people have been very kind to
me and my family during my entire life.
For the past four of my six years as Mayor, we have enjoyed Boards that have
been the perfect formula for Southport – such a motivated, disciplined and
decisive group focused on progress, efficiency and streamlining city processes.
In addition to the members service now, I acknowledge and thank Juanita Frink,
Donnie and Vickie Potter, Ken Karn who all worked hard for the harmony of this
Board and its accomplishments for our citizens. Of course my love and respect
for Meezie Herring Childs and her life is well known.
We really have a collective vision that we’re going to move opportunities
forward and to make sure our citizens are engaged early in the decision making
process. I am most proud of the team effort to move the city forward and I am
especially proud of the state the city is in.
Southport has had success because this Board seeks to listen to all
stakeholders before reacting or making decisions that will affect our
Community. The magic is including people in meaningful times and places. Get
people involved in a decision before you make it.
I entered this office knowing that electrical rates is the single largest
concern to our citizens and businesses; now through the efforts of this Board
and the other 31 Cities in our coalition which make up the Eastern Power
Agency, we are on the threshold of making major announcements that will provide
for opportunities in this regard for our citizens.
We understand that healthy citizens need a healthy downtown; this Board has
moved from those days (during the first two years of my tenure) where signs and
benches in addition to confusion, disagreement and division was reality to
creating and supporting efforts to enhance our town for tourist, commercial and
residential appeal.
In recent years I’ve found gratification in our progress in building stronger,
respectful relationships with Brunswick County, Brunswick Community College and
the surrounding Communities. And, more generally, embracing the importance of
diversity for our community.
We have been advocating for the widening of the Dutchman Creek Bridge, of
course our River Front restoration, placing our utilities underground and
completing the renovation and retrofit project to City facilities. We have
completed a portion of the fix needed to relieve traffic congestion by working
towards a private public partnership with the completion of Rob Gandy
extension.
Additionally and most importantly we have been advocating for the paving of
Howe and Moore Streets through our City, and I think we now have the ear of our
legislative delegation and the DOT – because this work has begun and will be
completed during the fall of this year.
Of course we have our Sewer capacity situation which is well underway to being
resolved through the acquisition of capacity rather than short term lease we
inherited. Through our Sewer District and with the flexibility of this Board we
are expanding our corporate limits and increasing service more efficiently and
effectively; all of which are initiatives that are ongoing.
As I leave office we have the comfort of knowing the dye is cast on a number of
important projects that will be completed during the next term of this Board of
Aldermen. Some of those project include protecting and retrofitting our
Riverfront, continuing to make changes to developing our downtown for easier
use and accessibility for our tourists.
We have a wonderful and effective staff; sometimes we are a Board create
concerns in that we involve ourselves in the responsibilities of the City
Manager as he manages his staff. We have a capable and effective City Manager.
Our goal of management should be to put the right people in the right spots
then let them do their jobs. Again, our City Manager is doing an above average
job; he knows and understands his duties and responsibilities. I am very proud
that I was a part of the team effort to bring him to our community.
I hope the next mayor and Board of Aldermen doesn’t try to micro-manage our
City Manager. Just allow he and his staff to run their departments, they really
are good at what they do.
Southport people are truly extraordinary. From the bottom of my heart to the
very fiber of my soul, I want you to know what an honor it has been to be a
part of the team that is Southport!
I look forward to the next seven months as we continue the initiatives we as a
Board have undertaken.
Adjournment- 4:35 p.m.
Alderman Powell moved to adjourn the meeting, second by Alderman Coring.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
                        /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:   /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

Health Insurance Workshop
   Ms. Lisa Kinsey and Ms. Julie Hall of the North Carolina League of
Municipalities provided the Board and city employees with a handout of multiple
health insurance options detailing plans with various deductibles, out-of-
pocket limits, and optional health savings accounts (HSA).
   Responding to inquiries from several employees, Mayor Howard indicated it
was the Board’s intention to maintain health insurance for active and retired
employees with no intention of reducing the general fund contribution,
currently $833 per active employee. He stated the purpose of the workshop was
to review options and hear from the employees before the Board makes a
decision.
   Mr. Charles Drew suggested narrowing the options down to a smaller number
for consideration and he shared his assessment of, and opposition to a HSA.
Several employees agreed and shared their recent experiences with out-of-pocket
expenses for surgeries, medications, etc.
   20 year employee and current retiree, Mr. Johnny Faulk, expressed
appreciation for the health care coverage provided over the years and for the
opportunity to provide input to the Board for their decision process. Ms.
Kinsey pointed out it was very rare for employees to be involved.
   Responding to an inquiry from Mr. Drew regarding how to reduce claims, Ms.
Hall talked about League initiatives that are helping to reduce claims, such as
the wellness requirements and a new grant program. She discussed “Tel-A-Doc”
which is available 24-hours a day via phone for diagnostic and prescription
services by North Carolina Board certified doctors. Additionally, Ms. Hall
stated that per the Affordable Care Act, in 2018, an excise tax will be added
to each plan over $850 per person per month. The responsibility for payment of
the tax may be that of the employer.
   Ms. Hall explained how the annual rate adjustment is determined based on the
amount of claims, noting that 10% of the city’s employees are driving 90% of
the claims. She also explained why the premiums are higher for retirees.
   Ms. Trexler asked the Board to consider offering a high deductible plan
(HDHP) with an HSA, allowing for the difference in the current premium to go
into the HSA. She offered assistance to any employee who would like to
determine what their yearly costs are. Ms. Hall emphasized that a HDHP with an
HSA is an individual decision and not appropriate for everyone.
   Mr. Elle Pittinger requested the Board consider a plan with an option for
employees to pay additional for an upgraded plan.
   Retiree, Mr. Bob Grant, pointed out that employees had forfeited a cost of
living increase last year in order to keep their current health care coverage.
   Mayor Howard thanked employees for attending. He emphasized that employees
are an important and vital part of the City and he stated the Board is
sensitive to their needs
Recess: 1:45 – 1:51p.m.
   Rob Gandy Boulevard
   Mayor Howard spoke about the 2 year public/private partnership to construct
Rob Gandy Boulevard. He expressed frustration that acceptance in the State road
system and opening of the road has been delayed for nearly eight weeks and
through a Duke Energy Progress Outage which adds 4,500 extra employees and
overstresses the area roads. He noted the gridlock situation experienced daily
on Southport’s roads and he emphasized the necessity of opening the road to
assure the safety of Southport citizens and visitors. Mayor Howard suggested
submitting a resolution to NCDOT regarding the situation.
   Alderman Powell pointed out that Memorial Day is within four (4) weeks and
traffic will increase. He supported sending a resolution to NCDOT.
   Alderman Poole supported sending a resolution to NCDOT.
   Alderman Coring supported sending a resolution to NCDOT and he stated that
traffic congestion during a recent accident at Jabbertown and River Roads could
have been avoided had Rob Gandy Boulevard been open.
   Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Powell to send a Resolution to
North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT) Secretary of Transportation
Anthony Tata, Ms. Karen Fussell Division 3 Engineer, NCDOT and Southport
legislative delegates Bill Rabon and Frank Iler requesting the expedited
opening of Rob Gandy Boulevard. Unanimous vote; motion carried. (Resolution on
file in the Clerk’s office)
   Sewer Rates
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Powell to amend Appendix A
Wastewater Allocation Impact Fee Schedule to change the non-residential
wastewater impact fee to $16.50/gallon. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Consideration of Contract with Brunswick County for Sewer Allocation
Mayor Howard reported that the Brunswick County Commissioners had approved an
agreement to lease up to 750,000 gallons per day of sewer capacity to the City
with the understanding that the County will undertake a study of the West
Brunswick Regional Wastewater Treatment plant to evaluate capacity levels and
come back to the City in late September or October with a plan for Southport to
purchase allocation. He added that as part of the agreement the Southport sewer
district and several operating agreements are reaffirmed.
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Poole to authorize the Mayor to
execute a contract between Brunswick County and The City of Southport for sewer
capacity up to 750,000 gallons per day. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
(Contract on file in the Clerk’s office.)
Adjournment- 2:10 p.m.
Alderman Powell moved to adjourn the meeting, second by Alderman Poole.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
                        /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:   /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

Resolution for Municipal Clerks Week May 3 – 9, 2015
Whereas, May 3 – 9, 2015 is the 46th Annual Municipal Clerks Week, and
Whereas, The Office of the Municipal Clerk, a time honored and vital part of
local government exists throughout the world, and
Whereas, The Office of the Municipal Clerk is the oldest among public servants,
and
Whereas, The Office of the Municipal Clerk provides the professional link
between the citizens, the local governing bodies and agencies of government at
other levels, and
Whereas, Municipal Clerks have pledged to be ever mindful of their neutrality
and impartiality, rendering equal service to all, and
Whereas, The Municipal Clerk serves as the information center on functions of
local government and community, and
Whereas, Michele Windham serves as City of Southport Clerk and has been
employed by the City of Southport since December 12, 2003, and
Whereas, Gayle Jones services as City of Southport Deputy City Clerk and has
been employed by the City of Southport since May 3, 2010, and
Whereas, it is most appropriate that we recognize the accomplishments of the
Office of the Municipal Clerk.
Now, Therefore, be it resolved that the Southport Board of Aldermen, recognize
the week of May 3 – 9, 2015, as Municipal Clerks Week, and further extend
appreciation to our Municipal Clerk, Michele Windham and Deputy Clerk Gayle
Jones for their vital services performed and exemplary dedication to the City
of Southport.
Dated this 6th day of May, 2015
                        /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Kerry McDuffie, City Manager

Municipal Clerks Week May 3 – 9, 2015. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

W.K. Dickson
   City Manager McDuffie advised that the contract for services with W.K.

renovation of the existing Lord Street Gym had been received. He indicated that
staff would execute the contract to begin the process. There were no objections

Health Insurance
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that a decision had to be made within 23
days on the 2015-2016 Health Insurance Plan. He stated that the NC Senate had
passed a bill to allow 10,000 municipal employees to join the State health
insurance plan, the bill is currently in the NC House of Representatives and is
expected to pass. He noted that the city’s current plan is based on a fiscal
year of July 1 through June 30th while the deductible is a calendar year. He
stated that the State plan is calendar year and if a six (6) month plan, July 1
through December 31, 2015, could be purchased from the city’s current health
insurance carrier, a 90 day notice would be submitted to the State requesting
Southport be added to the State’s plan January, 2016. City Manager McDuffie
noted that the State has three (3) plans to choice from and the best State plan
is very comparable to what the City currently provides.
    Aldermen Coring and Powell pointed out that employees had shared their
thoughts at a previous meeting and had sacrificed a cost of living allowance in
the 2014 - 2015 budget in order to retain their current health care coverage.
   City Manager McDuffie stated the State does not provide a plan for retirees
so the City would have to purchase a separate plan for the eight (8) pre-65 and
ten (10) post 65 retirees.
   The Board discussed spousal coverage, options for retirees and directed the
City Manager to follow up on joining the State’s plan and to submit a
recommendation to the Board at a future budget workshop.
Adjournment- 6:00 p.m.
Alderman Powell moved to adjourn the meeting, second by Alderman Barnes.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF THE CITY OF BOILING SPRING LAKES’ PLANNED SPILLWAY
PROJECT
WHEREAS, the City of Boiling Spring Lakes is seeking grant funding to help fund
a new spillway project for N.C. 87; and
WHEREAS, heavy rains from thunderstorms and tropical storms often causes
flooding on N.C. 87; and
WHEREAS, the City of Boiling Spring Lakes has a plan to install a new spillway
aimed at correcting the flooding problem on this important thoroughfare; and
WHEREAS, travel on N.C. 87 is important to many in southeastern Brunswick
County, not just the residents of Boiling Spring Lakes; and
WHEREAS, N.C. 87 is one of the few evacuation routes available to Southport
residents and visitors in the event an evacuation is mandated ahead of a
hurricane; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport appreciates the opportunity to lend its support
to this much-needed project which has the potential to help thousands of people
travel away from the coast and to safer areas before a hurricane makes
landfall; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport joins the City of Boiling Spring Lakes in
requesting funding for this project.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport hereby officially
supports the spillway project and requests that grant funding be allocated as
the City of Boiling Spring Lakes requests.
Adopted this the 14th day of May, 2015.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor                              
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

3.   Adopt Resolution Recognizing National Police Week and Peace Officers
Memorial Day
The City Clerk read the Resolution into the record.
A RESOLUTION RECOGNIZING NATIONAL POLICE WEEK AND PEACE OFFICER’S MEMORIAL DAY
WHEREAS,  the Congress and the President of the United States has designated
that there be a National Peace Officers Memorial Day, and the week in which
Peace Officers Memorial Day falls as Police Week; and
WHEREAS, the members of the law enforcement agencies of North Carolina play an
essential role in safeguarding the rights and freedom of the citizens of the
State; and
WHEREAS, it is important that all citizens know and understand the problems,
duties and responsibilities of their law enforcement officers and agencies, and
that members of those agencies recognize their duty to serve the people by
safeguarding life and property, by protecting them against violence or
disorder, and by protecting the innocent against deception and the weak against
oppression or intimidation; and
WHEREAS, the citizens of Southport recognize and appreciate the contributions
made by law enforcement officers at all levels of government.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that I, Robert D. Howard, Mayor of the City of
Southport, and Board of Aldermen do hereby proclaim May 15, 2015 as “PEACE
OFFICER’S MEMORIAL DAY,” and May 10 – 16, 2015 as “NATIONAL POLICE WEEK” in
Southport, North Carolina, and that, all of our people join in commemorating
law enforcement officers, past and present, which by their faithful and loyal
devotion to their responsibilities have rendered a dedicated service to their
communities. In so doing, they have established for themselves an enviable and
enduring reputation for preserving the rights and security of all citizens.
This 14th day of May 2015.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

MAY 26, 2015
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN  PUBLIC HEARING MINUTES
COMMUNITY BUILDING MAY 26, 2015
223 E. BAY STREET  SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Mayor Robert D. Howard
            Aldermen Mary Ellen Poole, Nelson Adams, Todd Coring,
            Jim Powell, Buddy Barnes, Emily Humphreys
 
STAFF PRESENT:      Kerry McDuffie, City Manager
   Michele Windham, City Clerk
   B. Wayne Strickland, Building Inspector
   John Allen, Community Development Specialist
A)   Call to Order - 6:30 p.m.
Mayor Howard called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.
B)   Invocation
Alderman Powell welcomed everyone and Alderman Coring gave the invocation.
C)   Pledge of Allegiance
   Alderman Powell led the assemblage in the Pledge of Allegiance.
D)   Announcements
Mayor Howard announced that the special meeting was scheduled to discuss the
possibility and feasibility of putting Southport's electric system underground.
He urged those attending to participate in the discussion.
Mayor Howard announced that the Board would be holding a 2015 - 2016 Budget
Workshop on Wednesday, May 27, 6:30 p.m. at Fire Headquarters, 1011 N. Howe
Street.
Mayor Howard directed staff and the Traffic & Transportation Committee to look
at limiting access to Moore and Howe Streets from Memorial Day to Labor Day for
the horse and buggy tour. He pointed out that traffic is backing up behind the
tour and could create an unsafe situation during the summer months. He
encouraged everyone to share their thoughts on the issue during the Board's
June 11 regular meeting.
Mayor Howard directed the City Manager and two members of the Board to review
the policy for allowing music to be played outdoors at the Community Building.
He shared his understanding that music via bands or DJ were restricted to
inside the building and he pointed out that he and several Aldermen had
received calls over the past weekend about the outdoor music. He asked staff to
report to the Board in June who is responsible for enforcing the policy and who
citizens should call with a complaint.
Electric Underground
Mayor Howard spoke about the proposed sale of the electric generating assets by
the North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency (NCEMPA) to Duke Energy
Progress. He explained that Southport is one of 32 cities forming the NCEMPA
and the sale would reduce Southport's current portion of debt from $12.3M to
$3.5M. Additionally, he pointed out that there will be a decrease in the cost
to obtain electricity. He stated the Board is seeking input from the citizens
to determine their willingness to allow a major portion of the decrease in cost
to be used towards putting the city's electric system underground, currently
estimated at $18M. He indicated that, pending support from the citizens, the
city would expend approximately $20,000 for a feasibility study.
City Manager McDuffie presented a PowerPoint presentation depicting the assets
being sold, the projected cost of electric after the sale, an average Southport
electric customer's monthly bill, the anticipated monthly savings, and scenes
of Southport with and without overhead electric lines. He explained three
financing options and timelines for installing the electric system underground.
Mayor Howard announced that a representative of NCEMPA would be attending the
Board's June 11 regular meeting to present details of the proposed asset sale.
Mr. Al Willis, 6150 Riversound Circle, spoke about the current electric rates
and his belief that people do not move to Southport because the electric rates
are high. He doubted that proof exists that outages are reduced by putting
electric underground, and he questioned if the homeowner would have to pay for
any part of the project.
Resident, Ms. Jean Brit, shared her experiences being without power due to a
storm and she supported putting the electric service underground.
Ms. Jean Parker, 315 W. 8th Street, a resident for 75 years, urged the Board to
reduce the high rates customers have been paying for the last 25 - 30 years.
Mr. Hank Singley, 113 W. West Street, spoke in support of going underground. He
emphasized the protection from storm damage and the aesthetic quality.
Mr. Richard Sloan, 509 E. Moore Street, questioned what cost, if any, the
homeowner would incur to put their service underground.
Alderman Powell pointed out that there were still many questions that needed to
be addressed. He suggested getting a system survey and cost estimates of how
much it would cost residents to move the lines at their residence underground.
Alderman Adams stated his concerns about the proposal focusing on the
commercial area. He pointed out that his constituents live 8-10 blocks away and
they would suffer a financial burden to connect their homes to the service at
the right-of-way. He noted that his electric panel box is 200 feet from the
right-of-way. He stated his support for giving customers a break on their
electric bills.
Mayor Howard announced that another public hearing would be held for further
public input.
Adjournment - 7:25 p.m.
Mayor Howard declared the meeting adjourned.
                        /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:   /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 17, TRAFFIC AND MOTOR VEHICLES,
ARTICLE III, OPERATION OF VEHICLES
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Section
17-79 of the Code of Ordinances is hereby amended to read as follows:
Sec. 17-79, Prohibition of certain vehicles on light traffic roads.
(a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to drive or operate a truck or other
motor vehicle having a gross weight in excess of thirteen thousand (13,000)
pounds upon the following light-traffic roads within the city which are hereby
designated as light-traffic roads:
(1)   Fodale Avenue from Howe Street to Moore Street
(2)   Stuart Avenue from Howe Street to Moore Street
(3)   Park Avenue from Leonard Street to Moore Street
(4)   Willis Avenue from Leonard Street to Moore Street
(5)   Turtlewood Drive between E. Moore Street and Leonard Street
(6)   Grey Squirrel Path between Turtlewood Drive and Canvasback Court
(7)   Canvasback Court between Grey Squirrel Path and E. Leonard Street
(8)   Brunswick Street
(9)   Yacht Basin Drive between W. Moore Street and Brunswick Street
(10)   I Am Street
(b)   The following trucks or motor vehicles are hereby exempted from the above
light-traffic road limitations:
(1)   A truck or other motor vehicle when owned, operated by or under contract
to a public utility, electric or telephone membership corporation or
municipality and such motor vehicle is used in connection with the
installation, restoration or emergency maintenance of utility services on said
light-traffic road.
(2)   A firefighting vehicle operated by any member of a municipal or volunteer
fire department in the performance of his duties and any vehicle of a voluntary
lifesaving organization when operated by a member of that organization while
answering an official call.
(3)   A fully enclosed motor vehicle designed specifically for collecting,
compacting or hauling garbage from residences or garbage dumpsters located on
said light-traffic roads.
(4)   A truck or motor vehicle when transporting heating fuel for on-premises
use at a destination located o the light-traffic road.
(5)   A truck or other motor vehicle when transporting and delivering materials
for on-premises use at a destination located on the light-traffic road or a
truck or other motor vehicle when performing contractual work at a destination
located on the light-traffic road.
(6)   Buses operated by a school or other educational institution for the
purposes of transporting students between home and school.
(c)   This ordinance shall be effective whenever appropriate signs are erected
indicating the contents hereof.
Adopted this 11th day of June, 2015               City of Southport
                        By: /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

4.   Budget Workshop
The Board heard from the city manager regarding the cost to continue the
employee and retiree health care plan with the North Carolina League of
Municipality. He indicated the city hopes to join the state’s health care plan
in 2016. The League plan most comparable to the state’s plan is $896/ month/
employee. He stated that changes in coverage should be minor but if an employee
chooses to keep the city’s current plan, the employee would pay an additional
$62/month. He pointed out that the proposed budget has $833 month allocated and
to fund the $896/month plan, an additional $37,420 will need to be allocated in
the budget.
City Manager McDuffie recommended the $896/month/employee plan with option for
employee to pay an additional $62/month and to help offset the cost, he
recommended the city no longer pay 30% of the cost for employee dependents, no
longer allow spouses to be covered under the city plan and ask department heads
to make cuts to their respective budgets.
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Poole to accept the recommendation
of the city manager. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

the rare opportunity to consider relocating the electric lines underground and
he discussed the city’s goal to provide reliable, clean electricity free of
disruptions. He pointed out some of the advantages of pursuing the endeavor:
less storm damage, aesthetically pleasing, less vulnerable to wind and ice and
reduced butchering of Southport’s prized Live Oaks. He explained the
opportunity comes about through the sale of assets of the North Carolina
Eastern Municipal Agency (NCEMPA), of which the city is one of 32 municipality
members, to Duke Progress Energy. The sale will result in considerable savings
for Southport’s wholesale power cost allowing for realization of the project
without assessments, increased taxes or increased electric fees for Southport
residents. He stated the project is estimated to cost $14 - $22 million and a
bond initiative would be presented to the citizens of Southport.
City Manager McDuffie led a presentation of how the sale would affect overhead
lines and power bills. (Presentation included as Attachment #1)
Mr. Ellie Pittenger, Load Management Coordinator, discussed the Load Management
Program that can save 4 cents per kilowatt hour which equates to $80 monthly if
the customer participates in the R-12 level of the program. He stated Southport
is the only city in the state that offers a discount instead of a credit.
Ms. Julie Canny, 6241 Navigator Way, spoke to the Board in favor of giving
customers relief on their utility bills. She stated she is a retired Manager of
the North Carolina Utility Commission. She stated her opinion that underground
is not perfect, it will go out during storms just not as much as overhead
lines. She referenced a 2003 report, precipitated by a 2002 major ice storm, by
the North Carolina Natural Disaster Preparedness Task Force entitled
Feasibility of Placing Electric Distribution Facilities Underground. She
questioned the projected completion time for the project, estimating it would
be as ten years instead of five.
Mr. John Simmons, 315 W. Brown Street, former 40 year employee of Duke Energy,
stated his property on Oak Island with underground electric experiences nearly
as many outages as his home in Southport. He asked about the cost of the load
management devices. Mr. Pittenger advised him of the costs.
Mr. Al Willis, 6150 Riversound Circle, quoted aspects of the NC Task Force
Feasibility Study and spoke in favor of utility bill relief. He stated his
opinion that electric usage would decline dramatically with the increased usage
of natural gas.
Mr. Ed Boguskie, 502 W. Brown Street, questioned if natural gas usage would
effectively reduce the customer base. He stated his opinion that hooking up
underground should be required, noting that his home has underground services
but the transformer is on the ground and is affected by storms. He supported
pursuing a feasibility study and stated it is important not to do anything that
would turn people away from coming to Southport.
Ms. Harriet Davis, 605 N. Clarendon Avenue, stated her frustration with the 30
years with ElectriCities and the associated costs. She spoke in favor of
utility bill relief.
Ms. Betty Timberlake, 118 N. Atlantic Avenue, stated her support for the
underground proposal. She talked about her love of Southport and its majestic
trees. She discussed the rights of electric utility to cut the trees and the
resultant damage.
Mr. Paul Fisher, 110 River Drive, supported the underground proposal. He added
that the existing system would have to be in peak condition for the proposal to
work. He suggested keeping electric rates in place until December 2015 when the
full impact of the sale will be known. He talked about his personal savings by
utilizing the Load Management Program.
Ms. Sandy Spencer, 410 W. Brunswick Street, supported the underground proposal
encouraging city officials to investigate the costs to the citizens and doing
it in a reasoned manner with as little affect as possible. She commended former
Alderman Paul Fisher for his work on the NCEMPA Commission.
Cherie Oliver, 613 E. Leonard spoke in support of the underground proposal and
offered her opinion that the above ground system could use some attention.
Responding to an inquiry from Ms. Jean Parker, 315 W. 8th Street and a Park
Avenue resident pertaining to possible assistance for homeowners to hook up
underground to their homes, Mayor Howard responded that the feasibility study
would include that aspect of the project and the related costs. 
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to come out of Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Mayor Howard thanked everyone for attending and announced that the Board would
meet next in regular session on June 11. He stated the Board would be
considering returning to their 6:00 p.m. time slot.
Adjournment- 7:27 p.m.
Alderman Poole moved to adjourn the meeting, second by Alderman Powell.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
                     /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
Attest:   /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

4.   ElectriCities; Ordinance Approving Sale of Assets
Mr. Paul Fisher, Commissioner, North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency
(NCEMPA), introduced Mr. Roy Jones, Chief Operating Officer of NCEMPA.
Mr. Roy Jones presented to the Board and audience a detailed presentation of
the specifics and impacts of the asset sale between North Carolina Eastern
Municipal Power Agency (NCEMPA) and Duke Energy Progress. He pointed out that
the sale would not impact Southport’s electrical distribution system or
physical infrastructure, Southport’s debt will be reduced by 77 percent, there
will be a 14 percent reduction in the wholesale power costs, and Southport and
the other 31 municipalities of the Power Agency will shed their ownership and
liabilities in two nuclear and two coal-fired plants.
Mr. Jones explained the three contracts before the Board for consideration:
∙   Power Sales Agreements Termination Agreement which terminated all pre-
existing contracts
∙   Debt Service Support Contract
∙   Full Requirements Power Sales Agreement which is a new 20 or 30 year
contract by which the City agrees to purchase electricity from Duke Energy
Progress
Alderman Adams motioned, second by Alderman Powell to approve the Ordinance
determining that it is in the best interests of the City of Southport to
approve the Asset Purchase Agreement and the Full Requirements Power Purchase
Agreement between North Carolina Eastern Municipal Agency and Duke Energy
Progress, Inc., to consent to the transactions contemplated thereby, and to
approve and authorize the execution and delivery of the Debt Service Support
Contract, the Full Requirements Power Sales Agreement and the Power Sales
Agreements Termination Agreement between the City of Southport and North
Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency as corrected. (Ordinance, Agreements &
Contracts included as Attachment #1)
Discussion
Alderman Barnes stated for the record that he would vote for the Ordinance but
he felt “like we are going from the frying pan into the fire. Just like 30
years ago, we don’t know what is going to happen in the future, so there is a
big risk in passing this.”
Roll Call Vote:    Alderman Adams     Aye
     Alderman Barnes     Aye
     Alderman Coring    Aye
     Alderman Humphreys    Aye
     Alderman Poole    Aye
     Alderman Powell    Aye
 Motion Carried:   6-0 
5.   Consideration of Load Management Ordinance
Mr. Paul Fisher spoke in support of the Load Management Program and the savings
benefits. He gave an example of the potential savings referencing a monthly
bill of $104.30, $43.20/month savings using load management for an annual
savings of $518. He pointed out that the City saves $150,000 annually utilizing
load management.
Mr. Ellie Pittenger, Load Management Coordinator, talked about the need to shed
the electric load for the city, noting that approximately 100 new homes are
being built annually and increasing the demand. He outlined a proposed policy
for requiring all new construction to install load management switches.
City Manager McDuffie indicated that staff is requesting adoption of an
Ordinance to require all new construction to install the load management
switches. He pointed out that customers would not be required to use them.
Alderman Adams repeated his position taken in August 2014, when the issue was
previously considered, stating he would not support requiring the switches.
Stating her support for the load management program, Alderman Poole agreed with
Alderman Adams that the decision to participate in the program be at the
discretion of the individual.
Alderman Coring stated appreciation for the information provided by staff,
stated he could see the benefits of load management but agreed with Aldermen
Adams and Poole that the switches should not be mandatory.
Item died for lack of a motion.

8.   Transportation Committee Recommendation for Limiting Time of Parking in
Yacht Basin
Mr. Allen explained that the Transportation Committee met and discussed ways to
curb the practice of parking all day in the Yacht Basin area by individuals
working on Bald Head Island. He indicated the committee considered a proposal
to place a four (4) hour time limit and unanimously decided to recommend to the
Board of Aldermen not to add a parking limitation.
Alderman Barnes commented that he sees the same cars parked daily in the Yacht
Basin area by 7:00 a.m., people boarding boats traveling to Bald Head Island
for work and he stated his opinion it is not fair to the citizens of Southport
and that a time limit is justifiable and needed. He commented that Bald Head
Island provides parking at Deep Point Marina.
Chief Dove pointed out that the parking in the Yacht Basin area is public
parking and available for anyone to use. He spoke about the difficulty
enforcing a parking time limit and he suggested issuing courtesy/warning
letters and working with Bald Head Island officials to find a remedy to the
problem.
Alderman Poole raised concerns for those homeowners using the public spaces
because they do not have on-site parking.
Alderman Coring spoke in support of the courtesy letters and suggested Alderman
Barnes work with Chief Dove to identify the vehicles parking in the area for
the entire day.
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Poole to give the Police Chief 60
days to try to work out an amicable solution for the ongoing problem. Unanimous
vote; motion carried.
9.   Input on Community Building Noise
City Manager McDuffie requested input from the Board regarding the concerns
from neighbors of the community building that music played on the outside deck
until 10:00 p.m. was too loud. He pointed out that the current contract for
rental of the facility allows music outside until 10:00 p.m and inside until
11:00 p.m.
Mayor Howard stated his concern for the citizens living in the neighborhood,
noting he had received complaints about the music.
Alderman Poole indicated she had received complaints as well.
Alderman Barnes remarked that the city’s noise ordinance allows for bands to
play anywhere until 10:00 p.m. and a band or DJ is common with rental of the
Community Building.
Attorney Isenberg advised that the city’s rental agreement can include any
terms the Board chooses and there is no requirement that music be permitted for
any particular period of time.
Alderman Adams suggested reducing the time playing music outside is allowed. He
pointed out that the city’s Parks and Recreation Department hosts movies and
bands on the lawn of Fort Johnston which is next door to the Community
Building.
Alderman Adams motioned, second by Alderman Poole to lower the permitted time
for outside music at the Community Building from 10:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
10.   Input on Horse and Carriage on Howe and Moore Streets
Alderman Poole reported that she and Alderman Humphreys reviewed the operation
and route of the horse drawn carriage tours with emphasis on the placement of
the carriage on Howe Street for loading and the route’s impact on Moore and
Howe Streets vehicular traffic and pedestrian safety.
Tourism Director, Cindy Brochure, told the Board that the carriage company is
willing to work with the city.
Staff was directed to get a reasonable solution worked out for the tour company
and Southport citizens.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Southport proposes to undertake
the Project as described below, to incur the related and necessary project
expenditures, and to finance the cost of the Project with the proceeds of debt
to be issued by the City for the project all as described below:
1.   Expenditures to be Incurred. The City of Southport anticipates incurring
estimated expenditures of $1,000,000 for renovations to the municipal building
201 E. Moore St. Southport, NC.
2.   Plan of Finance. The Issuer intends to finance the costs of the Project
with the proceeds of financing or other suitable form of debt, to be issued by
the City (the “Borrowing”), the interest on which is to be excluded from gross
income for Federal income tax purposes.
3.   Maximum Principal Amount of Debt to be Issued. The estimated principal
amount of the Borrowing to be incurred by the Issuer to finance the project is
$1,000,000.
4.   Declaration of Official Intent to Reimburse. The Issuer, City of
Southport, NC, hereby declares its official intent to reimburse itself with the
proceeds of the Borrowing for any of the Expenditures incurred by it prior to
the issuance of the Borrowing.
Adopted this 11th day of June 2015.            City of Southport
                         /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor

SECTION IV. TAX RATE
There is hereby levied, for fiscal year 2015-2016, a tax at the rate of $0.2456
on each one hundred dollars ($100) of assessed valuation of property located
within the City of Southport for the purpose of raising revenue in the General
Fund.
SECTION V. BUDGET OFFICER AUTHORITY
The city manager (budget officer) is hereby authorized to transfer
appropriations within a fund and between funds under the following terms:
A.   He may transfer amounts between objects of expenditures (line items)
within a departmental appropriation.
B.   He may transfer amounts between appropriations within the same fund,
provided that a report of such transfers shall be made no later than the next
regular financial report to the Board of Aldermen. He may approve un-budgeted
inter-fund transfers, up to $5,000, provided that a report of such transfers
shall be made no later than the next regular financial report to the Board of
Aldermen.
C.   He may transfer and/or utilize appropriations contained in contingency
appropriations within a fund (except for contingency amounts within the
governing board appropriation) or in emergency fund appropriations.
D.   He may authorize temporary transfers of cash among funds as necessary to
meet cash flow needs.
E.   He may transfer funds from capital reserve funds, up to $20,000 per
purpose, to meet current needs for the purpose for which such funds are being
held in reserve, provided that a report of such transfers shall be made no
later than the next regular financial report to the Board of Aldermen.
All other transfers of funds between appropriations or budget funds shall be
accomplished by Board amendment of this ordinance.
SECTION VIII. CONTINUING AUTHORIZATION
Previously-adopted capital project budgets, grant project budgets, and special
reserve funds are hereby re-authorized, and revenues and appropriations made
for all such funds shall remain authorized on an ongoing basis until such
projects are completed and/or all funds are utilized. At the conclusion of such
capital projects or grant projects, any residual, unexpended local funds shall
be transferred to the general government or enterprise fund with which the
project is associated.
SECTION IX. BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION
This ordinance and the supporting budget document shall be the basis of the
financial plan for the City of Southport municipal government for the 2015-2016
fiscal year. The budget officer shall administer the budget and shall insure
the finance officer and department heads of the city are provided with
sufficient guidance to properly implement this plan. Copies of the budget
ordinance shall be furnished to the city manager and the finance officer for
their use and direction in the disbursement of funds and to the city clerk for
the official records of the city.
SECTION X. ADOPTION
This ordinance has been adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen in regular
session on June 11, 2015, upon the motion of Alderman Powell and the second of
Alderman Poole, with a vote of  6  ayes and  0 noes, and shall be effective
July 1, 2015.

(3) quotations for auditing services:
∙   Berry, Padgett & Chandler            $ 46,400 revised to $36,000

∙   Thompson, Price, Scott, Adams & Co., P.A.      $ 23,950
Mayor Howard noted the sensitivity of the issue and emphasized the Board’s
ethical and fiduciary responsibility to the citizens of Southport. He noted
that the three firms were equally qualified and acceptable to the Local
Government Commission (LGC).
Alderman Adams reported that he and Alderman Powell had met with Menton Padgett
to discuss all aspects of past audits performed by Berry, Padgett & Chandler
and the additional work the firm had to accomplish which resulted in higher
fees. Alderman Adams provided Board members with a 55 item checklist of
financial reports, schedules and other records that would need to be provided
to Berry, Padgett & Chandler in a timely manner in order to complete the audit
for a revised cost of not to exceed $36,000. Alderman Adams emphasized the
quality of work provided by Berry, Padgett & Chandler, pointing out that the
firm has been doing the city’s audits since 1973 and has saved the city a lot
of headaches. He and Alderman Powell stated their opinions that the City’s
audit should be performed by the local firm.
Alderman Barnes stated his respect for Berry, Padgett & Chandler. He stated it
is his responsibility to the tax paying citizens to get the best price for
services and he could not justify spending over $10,000 more for the same work,
comparing the services quoted by all three firms as “apples to apples.”
Alderman Poole stated her opinion that changing firms and going in a different
direction could be a good thing for the city.
Alderman Coring pointed out that Berry, Padgett & Chandler have been loyal to
Southport, are very familiar with the city and he is nervous bringing in a new
firm that would not know the city and how it operates.
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Adams to retain Berry, Padgett &
Chandler for auditing services at a cost not to exceed $36,000.

Nay:   Aldermen Poole, Barnes

“America’s Happiest Seaside Town” and city employees and their families will be

states; “If a holiday, other than Christmas falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the

2.   Consideration of Amendment to Code of Ordinances, Chapter 10, Article III,

Item removed from agenda.
3.   Consideration of Resolution Recognizing Exception to Chapter 143, Article
VIII, Public Contracts, for Purchase Pursuant to G.S. 143-129(e)(6)
Mayor Howard explained that in order to upgrade electric meters and the
substation, the city would need to purchase equipment and apparatus compatible
with Brunswick Electric Membership Corps’ (BEMC) system. He stated that doing
so would save a tremendous amount of money on the meters and would avert any
difficulties using a different system. He indicated that after a meeting with
the city manager, city attorney and BEMC, it was determined that State Statute
G.S. 143-129(e)(6) provides for an exception to the bidding requirements when
compatibility is the overriding consideration.
Responding to a question from Alderman Powell, City Manager McDuffie stated
that BEMC will sell the meters to the city at a cost of $10 each, saving $117
per meter, nearly $370,000 for 2,450 meters. He added that replacement of the
meters will be included at no additional charge to the maintenance and
operation portion of the current contract with BEMC.
RESOLUTION RECOGNIZING EXCEPTION TO CHAPTER 143, ARTICLE VIII, PUBLIC
CONTRACTS, FOR PURCHASE PURSUANT TO G.S. 143-129(e)(6)
                                                               WITNESSETH:
THAT WHEREAS, the City of Southport currently has an Operation and Maintenance
Contract with Brunswick Electric Membership Corporation for operation and
maintenance of its’ electric system; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has determined that it is in the best
interests of the City to now contract with Brunswick Electric Membership
Corporation for BEMC to read its’ electric meters; and
   WHEREAS, in order to do so, it is necessary for the City to purchase certain
apparatus and equipment to enable BEMC to provide said service; and
   WHEREAS, it is necessary for said apparatus and equipment to be compatible
with the BEMC system and equipment; and
   WHEREAS, standardization and compatibility is the overriding consideration
in the purchase of the necessary apparatus and equipment;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport as follows:
(1)   That the Board hereby determines that standardization and compatibility
with the existing BEMC system is the overriding consideration in the purchase
of the necessary apparatus and equipment to enable BEMC to provide meter
reading services to the City.
(2)   That G. S. 143-129 (e)(6) provides an exception to the bidding
requirements of Chapter 143, Article 8, of the General Statutes when
standardization or compatibility is the overriding consideration in the
purchase of apparatus and equipment.
(3)   That in order to assure said compatibility it is necessary for the City
to purchase said apparatus and equipment directly from BEMC.
(4)   That the purchase of said apparatus and equipment directly from BEMC is
hereby approved.
       This the 24th day of June, 2015.
               CITY OF SOUTHPORT
               BY: /s/ Robert Howard, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk
Board Comments
City Manager McDuffie reported that the new concrete street light poles would
be delivered June 25 and would be stored at the former wastewater treatment
plant site.
Alderman Powell reported he had spoken with the contract for the public
restrooms and a final inspection is expected by July 1. He noted that 21 rain
days had delayed the project.
Alderman Barnes asked if the Beautification Committee could put in landscape
plantings, likely in September. Mayor Howard directed a design and proposal be
submitted to the Board for consideration.
Alderman Barnes announced that the $30,000 goal for purchase of sailboat
Christmas wreaths had nearly been met.
Alderman Barnes announced that N.C. House Bill 97 will add a new tax to all
boaters.
Mayor Howard asked Jason Tyson, State Port Pilot reporter, to explain the
proposed New Inlet Dam project currently before the state legislature. Ms.
Tyson stated that Senate Bill 160, submitted by Representative Michael Lee,
proposes to remove the rock dam walls installed in 1870 just south of Fort
Fisher. The walls have created their own ecosystem and it is uncertain why
removing the walls is being considered. Mr. Tyson said that Bald Head Island
had commissioned a study by Mr. Erik Olsen, engineer, which shows the
ramifications for Southport would be severe. Bald Head Island officials have
asked the Southport Board of Aldermen to consideration a resolution opposing
the project.
Mayor Howard requested comments from the Board.
Alderman Poole indicated she had received several calls about the project, she
had read the engineering report and feels a resolution opposing it would be
appropriate. Alderman Barnes agreed.
Alderman Adams stated he was not prepared to support a resolution until he
would review the engineering study. Alderman Powell noted he had not yet read
the report.

   Mr. Harley Lemons, 6228 Navigator Way, and member of the Lions Club, stated
his appreciation to the 4th of July Committee, Chamber of Commerce, City of
Southport, citizens, merchants and all those involved in the 4th of July
Festival.
   Mr. Edward Quinn, 114 N. Caswell Avenue, presented a drawing depicting
parking and for cars traveling south on Caswell Avenue line of sight at the

   Ms. Karen Mosteller, 310 N. Atlantic Avenue, read comments pertaining to the
proposed legislative bill to remove the rocks known as the New Inlet Dam at
Zeke's Island:
   As a concerned citizen, I'm speaking to you this evening about the proposed
legislation regarding the removal of rocks known as the New Inlet Dam at Zeke's
Island. And please forgive me if I repeat information that you are already
aware of.
   This Bill was originally introduced as N.C. Legislative proposal (SB160) and
when it did not receive any traction the Bill was added to the proposed budget
as a line item within Budget Bill 97.
   The stated purpose in the Bill is to remove the historical New Inlet Dam's
Southern Component in order to reestablish the natural hydrodynamic flow of
water between the Cape Fear River and the Atlantic Ocean that occurred prior to
emplacement of the dam, much of which was built circa 1879.
   The physical and environmental consequences of reintroducing a second tidal
inlet to the Cape Fear River would be significant.
   Any inlet related erosion - after inlet opening - could threaten portions of
the historical Ft. Fisher complex.
   Not accounting for future erosion, at the onset of removing the dam…the
boundary of Zeke's Island Reserve would be shifted 200 feet eastward loosing
critical habitat. According to the NC Department of Environmental and Natural
Resources, Zeke's Island is one of the three original National Estuarine
Research Reserve components dedicated by the National Oceanic Atmospheric
Administration and the Division of Coastal Management in 1985.
   And the unusual characteristics of the site have created a variety of
habitats, including tidal flats, salt marshes, shrub thicket, maritime forest,
sand dunes, ocean beach, and the hard surface of the rocks. Fish, shrimp,
crabs, clams, and oysters use the estuary as a nursery ground and again, the NC
Department of Environmental and Natural Resources has identified the expanse of
intertidal flats in the Zeke's Island vicinity as the single most important
shorebird habitat in southeastern North Carolina.
   The entire geomorphology of the entrance to the Cape Fear River as it
currently exists - with its congressionally authorized and routinely maintained
federal navigation channel, is dependent upon a no-flow condition at New Inlet.
Prior to its closure, New Islet was a relatively robust flowing tidal inlet.
With dam removal, the driving forces which influence tidal inlet creation and
stability would be expected again to foster a large flowing inlet.
   The re-opening of New Inlet would immediately service to decrease tidal flow
through the Cape Fear River mouth. Subsequently, shoal configurations would be
subject to significant change. The latter would substantially influence
littoral processes and sediment transport on both Oak Island and Bald Head
Island. Federal navigation channel shoaling would be expected to increase
significantly thereby requiring more frequent and larger dredging operations.
   According to the bill, the reason for removing the rocks would be "for eco-
system restoration and protection of navigational safely."
   NC State Senator Lee, one of the bill's primary sponsors said that,
"removing the Rocks would simply help restore the areas equilibrium." Mr. Lee
further stated that, "The general idea is that they don't need to be there, so
let's see if we can get them removed."
   Clearly Senator Lee's observations are not based on science. You have the
science in the White Paper written by Coastal Engineer, Eric Olsen. These
findings are echoed by Spencer Rogers, a coastal engineering expert with NC Sea
Grant and other Coastal Engineers.
   The White Paper report sheds light on more resulting changes and risks than
I have stated here tonight.
   I stand before you, asking you to please consider passing a Resolution
against the proposed legislation in House Bill 97, Section 14.6, requesting the
removal of the rocks at Zeke's Island, New Inlet Dam.
   Thank you for your thoughtful consideration of this issue and thank you for
changing the meeting time to 6:00 in the evening. The last time I attended an
Aldermen meeting, I had to take a half day off from work…..so I am looking
forward to being able to attend the meetings. Thank you.
   Ms. Roberta Dosher, 210 W. Moore Street, reiterated her plea of November 14,
2014 to improve safety at the W. Moore Street and Caswell Avenue intersection
via a 4-way stop, overhead flasher, parking reconfiguration or traffic camera
for issuance of speeding citations. She emphasized that the visibility is so

   Mr. Bill Van, 506 W. St. George Street, and President of the Cape Fear

event and asked if they could be placed closer to the venue at the end of S.

7.   Adoption of Resolution Requesting NCDOT Incur the Cost of Placing Electric
Power Lines Underground in the Howe Street/Highway 211 Widening Project Area
City Manager McDuffie explained that NCDOT will be widening Howe Street/
Southport-Supply Road/Hwy NC 211to four (4) lanes from 12th Street to Hwy NC
17. He pointed out that the electric poles will have to be relocated and it is
the policy of Southport to place electric lines underground whenever lines are
moved. He stated that questions had been raised whether Southport or NCDOT
would be responsible for the estimated $600,000 cost to move the lines. He
noted that Southport has been in the business of providing electrical power
since 1917 which predates NCDOT assuming maintenance of the county roads in
1932. Based on the prior right of the City, City Manager McDuffie stated it is
staff's belief that NCDOT should assume the cost of relocating the electric
lines underground in the Howe Street/Highway 211 widening project.
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Poole to adopt the Resolution
Requesting Assistance from the North Carolina Department of Transportation. By
an uplift of hands, unanimous vote; motion carried.
The clerk read the resolution into the record.
CITY OF SOUTHPORT
RESOLUTION REQUESTING ASSISTANCE FROM THE NORTH CAROLINA DEPARTMENT OF
TRANSPORTATION
   THAT WHEREAS, the North Carolina Department of Transportation (DOT) intends
to widen Howe Street/Highway 211 in the City of Southport (Southport); and
   WHEREAS, Southport has electric power lines and poles within the right of
way of Howe Street/Highway 211 which must be moved to accommodate the widening
project; and
   WHEREAS, it is currently the policy of Southport to place electric power
lines underground whenever such lines are moved; and
   WHEREAS, the estimated cost of placing the electric power lines in the
project area underground is $600,000, the cost of which would be an
unreasonable burden on Southport; and
   WHEREAS, Southport has been in the business of providing electrical power to
its' residents and customers since 1917; and
   WHEREAS, DOT took over the maintenance of county roads in 1932, 15 years
after Southport began providing electric power; and
   WHEREAS, it is logical and reasonable to assume that Southport's electric
power poles and power lines pre-existed DOT's takeover of county road
maintenance, including Howe Street/Hwy 211; and
   WHEREAS, if Southport's power poles pre-existed DOT's takeover of the
maintenance of county roads then it should be the responsibility of DOT to bear
the cost of placing the power lines underground;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that a formal
request is hereby made of DOT to pay the cost of relocating the electric power
lines in the Howe Street/Highway 211 widening project underground.
This, the 9th day of July, 2015.   
City of Southport
                     BY: /s/ Robert D. Howard, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
8.   Consideration of Amending Code of Ordinances Chapter 10, Article III,
Peddlers, Itinerant Merchants and Vendors
Attorney Isenberg explained the proposed provisions, as requested by the Board,
to Chapter 10, Article III of the Southport City Code, to regulate peddlers and
itinerant merchants. He explained that a peddler is someone that moves around
with a push cart, wagon or vehicle and it is common practice to limit the time
a peddler can stay in one location to thirty (30) minutes.
Alderman Barnes talked about the growing trend of food trucks. He stated his
opinion that the proposed amendments do not do enough to protect the local
merchants and restaurants.
Alderman Poole noted that some municipalities limit peddlers and itinerant
merchants to those that have a brick and mortar business.
Attorney Isenberg pointed out that federal law allows regulating peddling but
not prohibiting it. He added that some communities differentiate between
regular peddling and food peddling.
Alderman Coring suggested taking more time to research the issue.
Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Humphreys to accept the amendments
to the ordinance with the changes discussed.
Mayor Howard stated that a majority vote of the whole board (4) would be
required to amend an ordinance.
Ayes:   Aldermen Barnes, Humphreys, Poole
Nay: Alderman Coring
Motion Failed
Board consensus that further consideration of the issue to be included in the
August Board agenda.
Mayor Howard announced that staff had, due to safety concerns, directed an ice
cream vendor to set up in the Waterfront Park parking lot. Board consensus for
the ice cream vendor to remain at the park location until resolution of the
issue.

11.   Consideration of Resolution in Opposition to Removal of New Inlet Dam
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to adopt the Resolution
opposing the removal of New Inlet Dam.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
A RESOLUTION EXPRESSING THE SOUTHPORT BOARD OF ALDERMENS'
OPPOSITION OF THE NORTH CAROLINA GENERAL ASSEMBLY'S PROPOSAL
TO REMOVE THE HISTORICAL NEW INLET DAM SO AS TO ALLOW FOR OR
ENCOURAGE THE REOPENING OF NEW INLET WHICH HAS BEEN CLOSED SINCE 1879
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport is committed to recognizing and being a sound
steward of the unique coastal environment, including estuaries, marshes,
barrier islands and pristine beaches on and around Southport; and
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport Aldermen recognize that the City of Southport
and her sister coastal municipalities' economic survival solely depends on the
sustainability of the existing environment and this proposed legislation calls
for a strong response by Southport and surrounding coastal communities,
environmental conservation organizations, and all interested persons and
businesses to stand firmly in opposition to this serious economic and
environmental threat; and
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport Aldermen understands that, based on the
analysis (included in this document) of Erik Olsen, P.E., if the Southern half
of New Inlet Dam is removed, serious negative consequences will occur. Mr.
Olsen has decades of experience with coastal North Carolina and these issues
and his opinions are shared by other coastal engineers that have reviewed this
issue.
   WHEREAS, the negative effects may include but are not limited to major
alterations to the Cape Fear River's salinity regime, essential fish habitat
and entire eco-system-as they exist today- would be inevitable with the
introduction of a second tidal inlet. Additionally, hydraulic condition changes
would substantially influence littoral processes and sediment transport on both
Oak Island and Bald Head Island jeopardizing the barrier island protection they
provide Southport; and
   WHEREAS, changes in tidal flows through the mouth of the Cape Fear River
could create alterations within the AIWW and in the vicinity of Southport,
creating associated water quality changes because of reductions in water
exchange and in particular within the canalized (manmade) segment of the
Intracoastal Waterway; and
   WHEREAS, the reintroduction of a major inlet connecting the Cape Fear River
with the Atlantic Ocean, would allow increased flooding due to storm surges
associated with major storm events and result in possible flood insurance
elevations at Southport and other adjacent communities causing higher flooding
risks and insurance rates for existing habitable structures built to today's
100-year storm elevations, as established by FEMA; and
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, the City of Southport Aldermen are opposed
to SECTION 14.6(h) OF THE CURRENT VERSION OF HOUSE BILL 97 which proposes to
remove the historical New Inlet Dam so as to allow for or encourage the
reopening of new inlet which has been closed since 1879; and
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED the City of Southport Aldermen stand in solidarity
with our regional coastal communities who may suffer long-term social, economic
and environmental impacts of removing the New Inlet Dam.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED the City of Southport Aldermen call upon all North
Carolina municipal and county governing bodies of North Carolina to pass
similar resolutions to this one and that the League of Municipalities join in
this effort.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED the City of Southport Aldermen urge Governor McCrory
and the entire North Carolina General Assembly to oppose policies that risk the
health, safety and sound environmental stewardship of North Carolina's
coastline whose natural beauty attracts a proven tourism-driven economy.
On Behalf of the City of Southport Aldermen:         July 9, 2015
/s/ Robert D. Howard
                            City of Southport Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

ideal location but they needed to be placed where the crowds are. He suggested
the 4th of July Committee look at other possible locations.

Alderman Poole moved to adjourn the meeting, second by Alderman Barnes.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
