9.   Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Code of Ordinances, Chapter 10,
Article V. Taxicabs
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Barnes to amend Chapter 10,
Article V. Taxicabs, of the City of Southport Code of Ordinances. Unanimous
vote; motion carried.
BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that Chapter
10, Article V, of the Code of Ordinances is hereby amended to read as follows:
Sec. 10-111. Definitions.
The following definitions apply in this article:
(a)   Driver. A person who actually drives or operates a vehicle for hire on
the streets or roads within the City of Southport.
(b)   Limousine. A for-hire motor vehicle engaged in the on-call or on-demand
business of carrying and transporting people but does not solicit passengers
indiscriminately between points along streets and highways. The driver or
operator may not leave the vehicle for the purpose of soliciting passengers.
(c)   Taxicab. Any motor vehicle seating fifteen (15) or fewer passengers,
other than a limousine, operated upon any street or highway within the city on
call or on demand, accepting or soliciting passengers indiscriminately for hire
between such points along streets or highways as may be directed by the
passenger so being transported.which is or is intended to be used for the
purpose of carrying or transporting or conveying one or more persons from one
place to another, for which services a charge or fee is made or accepted. Any
taxicab parked or traveling on the streets of the city shall be subject to the
provisions of this article.
Sec. 10-112. Unlawful to operate without certificate.
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a taxicab engage in the business
of operating a taxicab or taxicab business upon and over the streets of the
city without first having applied for and secured from the board of aldermen a
certificate of convenience and necessity as hereinafter set forth.
Sec. 10-113. Application required.
Every person desiring to operate a taxicab business upon and over the streets
of the city must hold a certificate of convenience and necessity issued by the
City. Each person shall file on forms supplied by the city clerk an application
for certificate of convenience and necessity which shall be accompanied by the
fee adopted by the board of aldermen.
Sec. 10-114. Issuance of certificates.
The board of aldermen shall have power, and it will be its duty, to order
certain certificates of convenience and necessity issued under this article, or
refuse to issue certain such certificates, or to issue certificates for partial
exercise only of the rights granted herein, only such certificate shall be
issued under such terms and conditions as in its judgment the public
convenience and necessity may require.
Sec. 10-115. Duration of certificate.
A certificate shall constitute a franchise from the city for the operation of
taxicabs a taxicab business within the city subject to the provisions of this
article for one (1) year, unless a shorter period of time is specified in the
certificate. Applications for renewal shall be filed annually and hearing
conducted as herein provided. but if there have been no formal written
complaints from the public received during the previous year regarding the
certificate holder, and with the provision of certificates of insurance,
drivers’ licenses and other required elements, a renewed certificate may be
issued by the city manager for the same period as originally issued. Should any
formal written complaints have been received, the renewal shall follow the same
process as an original application, including public notice and hearing.
Sec. 10-116. Determination of convenience and necessity.
(a) In determining whether the public convenience and necessity require the
franchising of a taxicab, the board of aldermen shall, among other things, take
into consideration the following factors:
(1)    Whether or not the public convenience and necessity require such
proposed or will be favorably affected by additional taxicab service within the
city.
(2)    The financial responsibility of the applicant and the likelihood of the
proposed service being permanent responsible and satisfactory.
(3)    The number and condition of equipment.
(4)   The schedule of proposed rates, if required by the board, to be charged.
(5)   The number of taxicabs now operated and the demand for increased service,
if any, and whether or not the safe use of the streets by the public, both
vehicular and pedestrian, will be preserved and whether or not adequate
provision has been made for off-street parking of such taxicabs.
(6)    The experience of applicant in the taxicab business.
(7)    Such other relative facts as may be deemed necessary and advisable.
(b) Before making any decision with respect to the issuance of a certificate of
convenience and necessity, the board, or a committee thereof appointed by the
board, shall make a full and complete investigation of all facts, if it so
desires, subpoena witnesses and utilize the services of the chief of police or
any other officer or employee of the city.
Sec. 10-117. Insurance.
   No certificate of public convenience and necessity shall be issued or
continue in effect unless (i) there is in full force and effect common carrier
insurance, if available, and if not, automobile liability insurance for all
vehicles used in the taxicab business in the minimum amount required by North
Carolina law, and (ii) a certificate of insurance is on file with the city
clerk. If the automobile insurance expires without a new certificate being
filed with the city clerk, the city clerk shall notify the Chief of Police and
the holder’s certificate shall be immediately null and void.
Sec.10·118. Hearing, notices.
Each application for a certificate of convenience and necessity under this
article shall be scheduled for a hearing not later than forty-five (45) days
after the same is filed, and the applicant shall be notified by the city clerk
by mail to the business address set forth in the application of the date and
time of such hearing, such notification to be sent at least ten (10) days
before the date set for the hearing. The city clerk shall also, within the same
time, notify all persons who at the time hold certificates of convenience and
necessity for the operation of taxicabs within the municipality, of the date
and time for such hearing and the name of the applicant. In addition, the city
clerk shall cause to be published at least once in a newspaper of general
circulation at least ten (10) days before the hearing a notice setting forth
the name of the applicant and the date and time of hearing. The cost of such
publication shall be paid by the applicant.
Sec.10·119. Burden of proof.
The burden of proof shall be upon the applicant to establish the existence of
public convenience and necessity for the operation of the taxicab business
specified in his application, and all other facts required for the granting of
a certificate.
Sec. 10·120. Failure to begin operations.
If a certificate is granted under this article to an applicant, and such
applicant shall fail, in accordance with the provisions of the certificate, to
begin operations within sixty (60) days after the date of such certificate,
then such certificate shall become null and void, and no refund of any amount
paid by the applicant will be made by the city.
Sec. 10·121. Transfer.
A certificate granted under this article is not transferable. without the
consent and approval of the board of aldermen. Applications for a permit to
transfer shall be filed in the same manner as an application for a certificate
of convenience and necessity. The proceedings upon such application for
transfer shall be the same as those prescribed for the issuance of a
certificate, except that the question of public convenience and necessity need
not be proved.

Sec. 10-122. Revocation of certificate.
(a) The board of aldermen may at any time after a public hearing revoke any
certificate of convenience and necessity issued by authority of this article
for any one (1) or more of the following causes:
   (1)    Failure to operate the taxicab specified in the certificate in such
manner as to serve the public adequately and efficiently.
   (2)    Failure to maintain motor equipment the taxicabs in good repair.
   (3)    Failure to carry liability insurance or bond as required by law or
failure to file proof of financial responsibility with the city clerk.
   (4)   Failure to pay to the city the current taxes or license fees imposed
upon such taxicabs.
   (5)    Repeated and persistent violation by the holder or taxicab drivers of
traffic ordinances or state laws relating to alcoholic beverages or
prostitution.
   (6)    Failure to report accidents within 24 hours from the time of
occurrence.
   (7)    Willful failure to comply with any provision of this article or other
ordinances or state laws relating to the operation of taxicabs, whether such
ordinances and laws be now in force or hereafter enacted into ordinances and
into laws.
   (8)   Making any false or erroneous statement with reference to (i) the
ownership of the taxicabs or the names of those financially interested therein,
(ii) the name of the person in charge of the business, or (iii) the application
for the certificate.
       (9) Employment of any driver whose license has been suspended or revoked
within 3 years prior to the time of his employment.
      (10) The employment of a driver who shall not have a driver’s permit
issued by the city.
      (11) Failure to comply with any provision of this article or other state
or federal law relating to the operation of taxicabs.
(b) No certificate shall be revoked until the owner has had at least five (5)
days' notice by personal service or registered mail of the charges against him,
and of the time and place of the hearing. If, after the hearing, it is found
that the owner is guilty of one (1) or more of the offenses listed herein, the
board shall have the power to revoke the certificate, or to condition a non-
revocation upon compliance of its order within any time fixed by it.
Sec. 10-123. Substitution of vehicles.
The person to whom a certificate has been issued under this article may, by
proper endorsement thereon by the city clerk substitute another vehicle for the
vehicle for which certificate was granted. In such instance, the liability
insurance or bonds shall also be transferred to such substitute vehicle.
Sec. 10-124. Number of certificates limited.
The board of aldermen reserves the right to issue only one (1) such certificate
to anyone (1) person or entity, and the person or entity holding such
certificate shall be required to operate his taxicab business himself and shall
have no power or authority by virtue of his certificate to delegate the
operation of such taxicab business to any person.
Sec. 10-125. Driver’s Permit.
   (a) No person shall transport passengers in a taxi or other vehicle for hire
(except limousine) within the City of Southport unless such person shall have
first applied for and secured a driver’s permit from the Chief of Police or his
designee. Permits shall be valid for one year from the date of issuance.
Renewal applications must be submitted not less than 30 days prior to
expiration of each annual permit. All permits not presented for renewal in
accordance with this section shall become null and void.
   (b) Each application for a driving permit hereunder shall be on a form
prescribed by the city and shall be accompanied by a nonrefundable fee payable
to the City to defray the costs of processing the application. It shall
contain:
(1)    the applicant's name, address, age, and date of birth;
(2)    the applicant’s sex, weight, height, race, color of hair and eyes, and
description of tattoos;
(3)    the length of time the applicant has lived in the city and state and
whether or not the applicant is a citizen of the United States. Non-citizens
must provide a valid alien registration card;
(4)    the applicant’s employment for the previous 5 years and his or her
experience in driving taxicabs;
(5)    the name of the applicant’s prospective employer;
(6)   the number and date of issuance of the applicant’s North Carolina’s
driver’s license;
(7)   A list of all places where he or she has resided in the previous 10
years;
(8)   such other information as the Chief of Police or his designee may
require.
(c) Upon filing of an application for a permit, the applicant shall provide two
passport-sized photographs showing the applicant's face and shall proceed to
the Brunswick County Sheriff’s Office for taking of fingerprints and a
photograph. The photograph and fingerprinting are required for completion of
the application process.
(d) Any false statement of material fact made in an application for a permit
shall invalidate the permit issued thereon, and it shall be unlawful for any
applicant knowingly to make any such false statement.
Sec. 10-126. Investigation.
   The applicant's criminal history shall be investigated by the Chief of
Police or his designee prior to the issuance of a permit. Pursuant to G.S.
160A-304(a), The Department of Public Safety may provide a criminal record
check to the city for a person who has applied for a license or permit through
the city. The city shall provide to the Department of Public Safety, along with
the request, the fingerprints of the applicant, any additional information
required by the Department of Public Safety, and a form signed by the applicant
consenting to the check of the criminal record and to the use of the
fingerprints and other identifying information required by the State or
national repositories. The applicant's fingerprints shall be forwarded to the
State Bureau of Investigation for a search of the State's criminal history
record file, and the State Bureau of Investigation shall forward a set of the
fingerprints to the Federal Bureau of Investigation for a national criminal
history check. The city shall keep all information pursuant to this subsection
privileged, in accordance with applicable State law and federal guidelines, and
the information shall be confidential and shall not be a public record under
Chapter 132 of the General Statutes.
Sec. 10-127. Denial of Permit.
    The following factors shall be deemed sufficient grounds for refusing to
issue a permit or for revoking a permit already issued:
(1)    Conviction of a felony against this State, or conviction of any offense
against another state which would have been a felony if committed in this
State;
(2) Violation of any federal or State law relating to the use, possession, or
sale of alcoholic beverages or narcotic or barbiturate drugs;
(3) Addiction to or habitual use of alcoholic beverages or narcotic or
barbiturate drugs;
(4) Violation of any federal or State law relating to prostitution;
(5) Noncitizenship in the United States;
(6) Habitual violation of traffic laws or ordinances.
(7)   Conviction of a DWI/DUI when the actual date of offense was within five
years of the application.
(8)   Conviction of more than one careless and reckless driving offense.    
(9)   Conviction of any offense involving the driving of an automobile
resulting in death to any person.
(10)   Conviction of any offense which would require the applicant to be
registered as a sex offender.
(11)   Failure to pay the fees set forth herein for processing the application.
(12)   Suspension of a state driver’s license within 5 years of the application
filing.
(13)   False statement in the application and supporting documents.
Sec. 10-128. Revocation of driver’s permit.
A driver’s permit may be revoked by the Chief of Police or his designee for any
reason which would have been sufficient for refusing to issue a permit.
Sec. 10-129. Display of permit.
The driver of every vehicle for hire shall at all times while operating such
vehicle for hire, prominently post and display in such vehicle for hire, so as
to be visible to the passengers therein, the issued permit to drive a vehicle
for hire along with a photograph of the permit holder.
Sec. 10-130. Appeal.
Any person who is denied a permit or whose driver’s permit is revoked by the
Chief of Police or his designee may appeal such decision to the city manager
provided that he or she files with the city clerk a written notice of appeal
within 10 days following receipt of notice of the decision. The written notice
of appeal must include the appellant’s name, phone number, driver’s license
number, driver’s permit number if issued and basis for the appeal. Upon receipt
of a proper notice of appeal, the city manager shall schedule a hearing to be
held not more than 15 calendar days from the receipt thereof. Appellant may be
represented by an attorney provided that he or she gives the city clerk 5 days’
notice prior to the hearing of his or her intent to do so. The city manager
shall notify the appellant of his decision either by personal delivery or
certified mail to the address furnished by applicant within 10 days from the
hearing. The decision of the city manager shall be final.

   Mayor Howard reported that the Board had met with Brunswick Community

Street Annex and include the City deeded gym property in the proposed study. He
pointed out that the College wishes to proceed with the project through the
School of Government. Mayor Howard stated that the School of Government can
only act through a municipality. He asked the Board to support the Community
College project to the extent the School of Government can work with the
College via the city. Board consensus to table consideration of financial
obligation on the part of the city and to support the College partnership with
the School of Government.

Waterfront Improvements and Erosion Control; Mike McIntyre and Glenn Dunn,
Partner, Poyner & Spruill LLP
   Mayor Howard spoke about the Waterfront Improvement Plan D recently adopted
by the Board with emphasis on stabilization and erosion control of the
riverfront. He stated the Board recognized the process would involve multiple
regulatory agencies and pursuit of federal and state funding. He pointed out
that the Board had voted to ask Mike McIntyre to considering working with the
city on the project.
   Mr. Mike McIntyre, former 7th District Congressman and current director of
governmental relations with law firm Poyner and Spruill LLP, which specializes
in coastal legal matters, presented a proposal for consulting services relating
to Southport’s proposed waterfront project. He talked about the numerous ways
federal government programs can assist the city in developing a financial plan
for undertaking the project, i.e. low interest loans and grants from the U.S.
Department of Agriculture Rural Development and the U.S. Department of
Transportation. Mr. McIntyre praised the proposed plan prepared by Criser
Troutman & Tanner Consulting Engineers and thanked the Board for the
opportunity to assist the City.
   Mr. McIntyre was joined by Mr. Glenn Dunn, a partner in the firm with
extensive experience in regulatory matters. Mr. Dunn outlined a variety of
state level funding options through Coastal Area Management Act (CAMA), N.C.
Parks Service, Division of Water Resources and N.C. Department of
Transportation.
   Mayor Howard made an observation that beach communities can designate a
portion of their occupancy tax for beach renourishment. He suggested pursuing,
on a State level, a similar opportunity for Southport to designate occupancy
tax funds towards riverfront renourishment and maintenance.
   Alderman Barnes motioned, second by Alderman Poole to authorize the city
manager and staff to seek a request for proposal (RFP) from Poyner and Spruill
LLP for consideration by the Board at the November regularly scheduled meeting.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

Resolution
Southport Lions Club 70th Anniversary
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club was established 70 years ago (1945) by some
of the most prominent citizens in our community; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club continues to honor the challenge Helen Keller
issued to the Club in 1929 to become “knights of the blind in the crusade
against darkness”; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club conducts vision screenings every month at the
New Hope Clinic, each year at numerous local schools, and at the Brunswick
County Health Festival; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club has covered the expense of cataract surgery
for 10 needy individuals over the past 3 years; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club collects over 1,700 pairs of glasses each
year and provides assistance to those needing, but unable to afford, eye exams
and the purchase of glasses; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club contributes financial and volunteer support
to over 20 local charities and youth programs; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club is composed of men and women who dedicate
their time to the betterment of our community and aiding those in need; and
NOW THEREFORE, I, Robert Howard, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC and the
Board of Aldermen, hereby congratulate the Southport Lions Club on 70 years of
service to our City and the surrounding communities.
ADOPTED, this 12th day of November 2015 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
                     /s/ Robert Howard, Mayor

11.   Tourism Department Discussion
   Alderman Coring talked about issues people had expressed to him during his
recent campaign for re-election. He stated that concerns about the Tourism
Department were frequently mentioned. He pointed out that many accolades for
the Tourism Department had been shared during public comment. He questioned why
it is perceived that the department is not fully supported by the Board and
city staff, why the full-time assistant position is being eliminated and what
were the reasons for placing the department under the Parks & Recreation
Director when his research could not find anywhere that tourism is under Parks
and Recreation. He stated his opinion that the city organizational chart needs
to be revised and the vision of the Tourism Department defined.
   Mayor Howard stated his respect for the Tourism Department. He insisted that
a false perception had prevailed in part because the press had not been
objective. He challenged finding another community in the area with the
percentage of revenue support as Southport for tourism. He spoke about the
organizing of five (5) groupings within the city administration and that the
Tourism Department was on the same level as the Parks & Recreation Department.
   City Manager McDuffie emphasized the importance of the Tourism Department
and noted that the Board has demonstrated its willingness to fund the
department with approval of all budget requests. He pointed out that the
reorganization occurred a month after Ms. Brochure filed for office. He stated
it was unfortunate that both staff members were leaving and he indicated that
job descriptions would be updated and advertised.
   Aldermen Powell and Adams noted that the Tourism Department annual budget is
$230,000, of which $80,000 is collected from occupancy taxes and the remainder
from taxpayers.

December 10.

RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE PURCHASE OF LOAD MANAGEMENT SWITCHES FROM NEXGRID
FOR $109,860.00 THROUGH THE ELECTRICITIES NORTH CAROLINA, INC., PURCHASING
PROGRAM AS AUTHORIZED UNDER NORTH CAROLINA GENERAL STATUTE §143-129(e)(3)
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport Board of Aldermen has determined that it is
in the best interests of the City to purchase load management switches for its
electrical system; and
   WHEREAS, N.C. General Statute §143-129(e)(3) provides an exception to the
requirements of Chapter 143, Article 8, for purchases made through a
competitive bidding group purchasing program which is a formally organized
program that offers competitively obtained purchase services at discount prices
to two or more public agencies; and
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport has contacted ELECTRICITIES NORTH CAROLINA,
INC., a competitive purchasing program as authorized under General Statute
§143-129(e)(3), seeking their assistance in acquiring said load management
switches using specifications to meet the City’s needs; and
   WHEREAS, ELECTRICITIES NORTH CAROLINA, INC., has completed the bidding
process with manufacturers and Nexgrid is offering said load management
switches for $109,860.00 meeting the City’s submitted specifications with a 90
days’ delivery date; and
   WHEREAS, the Southport Board of Aldermen has determined that it is in the
best interest of the City of Southport to waive the normal bidding requirements
of N.C.G.S. 143-129 in order to purchase said Equipment in accordance with this
cooperative purchase program.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen,
that:
   1.   The City waives the formal bidding provision of N.C.G.S. 143-129; and
   2.   The Board authorized the City Manager to execute documents required to
purchase 700 load management switches per submitted specifications from Nexgrid
through THE ELECTRICITIES NORTH CAROLINA, INC., Purchasing Program in the
amount of $109,860.00 pursuant to N.C.G.S. §143-129(e)(3)
   Adopted this 24th day of November, 2015.            CITY OF SOUTHPORT

8.   Sewer Update
   Mayor Howard updated the Board on the status of sewer capacity. He reported
that expansion of the West Brunswick wastewater treatment plant would be
required in order for Southport to purchase 1M gallon of capacity in lieu of
leasing. He stated that the cost to expand the plant was estimated at $20M and
would be the sole responsibility of the city. Mayor Howard indicated that the
city had begun negotiations with the Town of Oak Island to purchase a portion
of capacity the town owns at a cost of $14 – 15 million. He added that
Brunswick County had given the city its blessing to negotiate with the Town of
Oak Island. He personally thanked the Brunswick County Commissioners and County
Manager who have been sympathetic to Southport’s needs and have worked to find
additional capacity.   
9.   Lord Street Gym Update
   Mayor Howard discussed the donation from Brunswick Community College (BCC)
to the City of the Lord Street gymnasium; the City agreed to do yard
maintenance for ten (10) years and paint the exterior and put a new roof on
within two (2) years of acquisition (July 2015). He stated the Board had
authorized an engineering study which revealed the steel beam trusses of the
roof would have to be removed which would not be cost efficient for the City.
Mayor Howard reported that Alderman Adams was working to obtain an additional
quote to test the structural integrity of the trusses.
   Alderman Adams added that the condition of the trusses would dictate what
direction the City could take on the project.
   Projects Status Update by Mayor
   Mayor Howard reported that BCC had dedicated the Southport Campus. He
expressed gratitude that the campus is functioning and commended president
Adams for making the project happen through multiple setbacks and delays.
   Ball Field Project
   Mayor Howard spoke about the status of the 9 th Street Park Ballfield,
noting the setback from heavy rains. He pointed out that Bald Head Island
Limited owned 50% of the park, have leased the property to the City for two (2)
years and will continue to permit City use as long as they have no development
plans for the area. Mayor Howard announced that the Parks and Recreation
Director had advised him that the fields would be ready for play in the summer.
   Riverwalk
   Mayor Howard talked about the lease with the State Port Authority for the
Riverwalk, set to expire in 2017. He stated that through the assistance of
Senator Bill Rabon, himself, Alderman Powell, City Manager and Mayor-Elect Dove
had met with state officials and it is believed that the City of Southport will
gain ownership of the property.
   211 Widening
   Mayor Howard reported that the North Carolina Department of Transportation
(NCDOT) had notified the city that the city would be financially responsible
for removal of power poles in the right-of-way of NC 211 for the widening of
the road. He stated it was DOT’s contention that Southport had not been
providing electric service along the route prior to 1952 and DOT had requested
the city provide proof to the contrary to avoid financial responsibility. Mayor
Howard reported that the city attorney had obtained affidavits from older
residents stating that the city was providing electric service prior to 1952 as
far out 211 as to the current day location of the Verizon Store.
   Electricities
   Mayor Howard thanked Paul fisher, Jim Powell and the City Manager for their
efforts to reduce Southport’s high electrical costs, noting that with the sale
of the power plants, the citizens of Southport have electric rates lower than
Duke Energy and Brunswick Electric Membership Corp. (BEMC) Additionally he
pointed out that new automated meters will provide customers with access to
electric usage, payment kiosks and prepay accounts.
   Water Meters
   Mayor Howard pointed out that new automated water meters will be read
electronically and provide better service to the customer.
   BEMC Contract
   Mayor Howard reported that the operation and maintenance (O&M) contract with
BEMC would expire June, 2016. He indicated that negotiations are on-going for a
conclusive contract for meter reading and O&M.
   Walk of Honor
   Mayor Howard deferred consideration of the Walk of Honor in Franklin Square
Park to the new board.

resolutions of recognition. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

10.   Public Hearing: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment,
Article 15, Section 15-8: Small Lot Cluster Development
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to open Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Mr. Nick Kern, 415 N. Burrington Avenue, a former Washington, D.C.
developer, stated he had reviewed the proposed text amendment and had concerns
that he had discussed with city staff.
   Mr. Allen thanked Mr. Kern for his interest, his review of the proposed
amendment and for sharing his concerns. Mr. Allen explained that the proposed
amendment specifically was designed to create a small lot cottage home
development of 10 acres or less and zoned multi-family (MF). He added that the
amendment would allow a development on lots of 5,000 sq. ft. with a maximum
footprint of 1,400 sq. ft. and with reduced setbacks where houses are close
together with pedestrian access and geared towards social interaction. Mr.
Allen noted that concerns raised by Mr. Kern, such as a garage in front of the
house, were addressed in other articles of the UDO.
   Mr. Kern reiterated his concerns relating to lot size, house size, driveway,
garage, impervious coverage, off street parking and he suggested footnotes
should be added to refer to other articles within the UDO
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to close Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
11.   Consideration of Text Amendment
   Responding to a query by Aldermen Adams and Powell, Mr. Allen stated that
the houses would be a story and a half, with setbacks: front 10’, side 6’, rear
5’; for an unattached accessory structure, 20’ from principal structure.
   Mr. Allen noted that stormwater management plans for developments must be
submitted to NC Department of Environmental & Natural Resources (DENR), parking
requirements were covered in Article 16, and the amendment was not designed
with a specific project in mind.
   Alderman Powell pointed out that when the UDO was crafted, a stormwater
ordinance was developed first and all proposed developments are required to
meet those requirements.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Coring to defer consideration of
the text amendment to the January regular meeting. Unanimous vote by an uplift
of hands; motion carried.

A RESOLUTION HONORING THE 100TH BIRTHDAY OF

Resolution Honoring the 40th Anniversary of the Southport Historical Society
WHEREAS, the Southport Historical Society was established 40 years ago (1976)
by founders Eleanor Smith and Susie Carson; and
WHEREAS, the mission of the Historical Society is to bring together persons
interested in the history of Southport, promote a better appreciation of our
heritage and to discover and collect materials which illustrate the history of
the area; and
WHEREAS, the Society cooperates with city officials in the preservation of the
city’s records and archives and encourages the preservation of historic
buildings, monuments and markers; and
WHEREAS, the present membership of the Southport Historical Society is 170 with
plans to add at least 40 more members during the anniversary year; and
WHEREAS, the Society distributes a quarterly newsletter, “The Whittler’s
Bench”; and
WHEREAS, the Society has developed a museum at the Old Brunswick County Jail
and has cooperated on displays in the City Museum; and
WHEREAS, the Society funds annual scholarships to high school seniors; and
WHEREAS, the Society provides critical assistance in the preservation of the
18th Century Old Smithville Burial Grounds; and
WHEREAS, the Society conducts an annual Christmas Tour of Homes; and
NOW THEREFORE, I, J.V. Dove, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC and the Board
of Aldermen, hereby congratulate the Southport Historical Society on 40 years
of service to our City and the surrounding communities.
ADOPTED, this 14th day of January 2016 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.

AN ORDINANCE APPROVING A TEXT AMENDMENT TO THE
UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, City Staff, in conjunction with the Planning Board, has prepared
the proposed amendment to Section 15 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and finds
the proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance to be consistent
with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommend its approval;
and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on December 15, 2015, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby find that this
proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the
Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) this type of use is not
addressed in the Unified Development Ordinance and should be, (ii) this
amendment is necessary to promote orderly growth and development in the Multi-
Family District, and (iii) will meet the needs of a population diverse in age,
income, household composition and individual needs through encouraging a
variety of housing types and price points, innovation and variety in housing
design and site development.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment to Section 15 of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This, the 14th day of January, 2016               City of Southport
                     BY: /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
Section 15-8: Small Lot Cluster Development
Small lot cluster development is a type of detached housing providing small
residences for smaller households. Such “cottage” housing is provided as part
of the city’s overall housing strategy, which seeks to meet the needs of a
population diverse in age, income, household composition, and individual needs
through encouraging a variety of housing types and price points, innovation and
variety in housing design and site development.
Small lot cluster development standards are intended to create a small
community of cottages that is pedestrian- friendly, provides for pedestrian
amenities, minimizes impervious surfaces, and takes advantage of natural
features on the site. The development standards are intended to maintain
traditional cottage amenities and proportions while ensuring that small lot
cluster developments contribute to the overall community character. Small lot
cluster developments are encouraged to use low-impact development techniques to
the greatest extent possible.
   (A)   This section shall apply only to parcels less than 10 acres that are
zoned Multi-Family (MF).
   (B)   The minimum lot size is 5,000 square feet.
   (C)   The following minimum set back restrictions shall apply:
      (1)   Front Yard: 10 feet
      (2)   Side Yard: 6 feet
      (3)   Rear Yard: 5 feet from an unattached accessory structure; 20 feet
from principal structure
   (D)   No principal structure shall have a total “footprint” greater than
fourteen hundred (1,400) square feet. No principle structure shall have a
maximum heated square footage greater than eighteen hundred (1,800) square
feet. Open covered walkways, open covered porches on the front elevation and
first floor covered open or screen porches on the rear elevation shall not be
included in the calculation of either heated square footage or “footprint”. An
unattached accessory structure shall not be included in either the calculation
of the total heated square footage nor the “footprint”; however, the total
“footprint” of an unattached accessory structure shall not exceed five hundred
and thirty (530) square feet.
   (E)   No principal structure shall include an attached garage or accessory
structure.
   (F)   Unattached accessory structures shall be limited to a maximum area
above the first floor of three hundred and fifty (350) square feet.
Additionally, a Conditional Use Permit shall be required in order to install
plumbing lines or fixtures in an unattached accessory structure.
   (G)   Dimensional and Orientation Requirements
      (1)   Maximum building height of a principle structure shall be thirty-
five (35) feet. Structures shall be designed to be single-story, single-story
plus a loft, story and a half or two-story. Maximum building height of an
unattached accessory building shall be twenty-five (25) feet.
      (2)   All principle structures shall be provided with a covered porch
oriented towards the front yard to create a private outdoor space protected
from the weather and provide a transition from the interior private residential
space to the semi-public outdoor space. Covered porches shall be usable in both
design and dimension.
      (3)   Principal structures shall have a covered main entry porch with a
floor area measuring at least seventy-five (75) square feet in area.
      (4)   The floor of the covered main entry porch shall have minimum
dimensions of not less than eight (8) feet in any direction (length or width).
      (5)   All principle structures shall be oriented to avoid blank walls or
appear to have a “back” towards streets.
   (D)   Small lot cluster development housing may be developed on individual
lots or with a common form of ownership (townhouse or condominium-style), with
all units within a development on a single lot.
   (E)   In order to minimize impervious surface area, driveways shall be
shared whenever possible.
   Small lot cluster developments shall be designed to incorporate existing
trees and natural features into the site design, to the extent possible.
Structures shall be located so as to minimize the removal of existing trees,
especially large “specimen” trees, and to maximize natural stormwater
functions. As soils allow, small lot cluster developments shall be designed to
take advantage of open space, landscaped features, and natural areas to utilize
low-impact development techniques, including natural filtration and on-site
infiltration of stormwater.

JANUARY 16, 2016
FACILITIES TOUR SESSION MINUTES
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN FACILITIES TOUR SESSION MINUTES
                 JANUARY 16, 2016
                 SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Mayor J.V. Dove
            Aldermen Mary Ellen Poole, Karen Mosteller, Todd Coring,
            Jim Powell, Rick Pukenas
ABSENT:         Alderman Nelson Adams
STAFF PRESENT:      Kerry McDuffie, City Manager
   Michele Windham, City Clerk
   Randy Jones, Interim Tourism Director
   David Fox, Public Services Director
   Heather Hemphill, Parks & Recreation Director
   Maureen Moore, Parks & Recreation Program Supervisor
Call to Order – 9:00 a.m.
   Mayor Dove called the meeting to order at 9:00 a.m.
   By means of the Parks and Recreation Department bus, the Board toured
municipal properties.
Fire/Rescue Substation - 111 E. Nash Street
   Assistant Fire Chief, Todd Coring, guided the tour of the Fire Department
substation on E. Nash Street which formerly housed the Southport Rescue Squad.
He explained that with the recent merger of the fire and rescue departments to
Fire Headquarters at 1011 N. Howe Street, the renovations needed to the
substation would be approximately $25,000 for interior paint, carpet, restroom
upgrades, replacement of bay light fixtures, exterior doors painted, roof
repairs and electrical work. He indicated that the work had been quoted with a
local contractor. He pointed out that the substation would house three (3)
support vehicles for a presence in the downtown area. He added that a security
system with card access would be installed.
Bill Pay Terminal
   The Board looked at two (2) possible locations for a drive up electric bill
pay terminal. City Manager McDuffie suggested an area in the parking lot at the
rear of 201 E. Moore Street or along the Dry Street side of the Police
Department.
Police Department – 201 E. Moore Street
   Joined by Police Chief Gary Smith, the Board toured the first floor of the
former city hall. Chief Smith pointed out water damaged areas and pointed out
the need for a new door on the evidence room (former vault) due to safety
concerns. Responding to Alderman Mosteller, Chief Smith stated he currently had
two (2) vacancies in the department and would have enough space for staff if
the area was redesigned.
   City Manager McDuffie showed the Board the termite damage to the front porch
which has resulted in closure of the area for public access. Mayor Dove
emphasized the need for the Police Department to have a top quality facility.
   City Manager McDuffie advised the Board that he had received verbal notice
from the tenants of the second floor of City Hall, 1029 N. Howe Street, that
they may want to negotiate a reduced lease for one half of the floor area when
the lease is due for renewal December 31, 2016.
   Alderman Pukenas questioned if city facilities were under contract for
termite treatments. Public Works Director Fox to research and respond.
Community Building – 223 E. Bay Street
   The Board stopped briefly at the Community Building and members asked about
establishing a schedule for painting the facility.
Fort Johnston Garrison – 203 E. Bay Street
   Interim Tourism Director, Randy Jones, emphasized to the Board the condition
of the 200+ year old bricks and the pressing need for them to be sealed and
pointed. He stated the last seal and point of the bricks was performed in the
1980’s and the maintenance is supposed to be performed every 15 years. He noted
the expense of such a project and suggested a capital campaign. He indicated
the interior floors are scheduled to be refinished in 2016, the front door
needs to be replaced, he is proposing sunlight filters on the windows in the
2016-2017 budget along with a rearrangement of the welcome area and a reduction
in retail merchandise. Mr. Jones also suggested up lighting the front exterior
of the building.
Parks & Recreation – 209 N. Atlantic Avenue
   Parks & Recreation Director, Heather Hemphill, gave the Board a tour of the
central office for the department. She spoke about the After School Program
which accommodates 40 participants, Summer Camp and recent repairs to the
building. The Board joined Ms. Hemphill in the gym and heard that it is the
only indoor public gym in the County with 230 participating in the Youth
Basketball League.
Jaycees Building & Senior Building - 311 N. Fodale Avenue
   Ms. Moore explained to board members that the facility was used for city
sponsored activities such as aerobics, dance, cha-cha fitness and rented out
for event. It was noted that the Senior Building was also a rental and used
specifically for senior activities. Ms. Hemphill pointed out that maintenance
of the facilities was funded by the Parks & Recreation budget.
City Dock – Yacht Basin
   The Board inspected the City Dock and heard a report from Ms. Hemphill to
the projected cost for dredging in order to use the 8 – 10 boat slips currently
unusable during low tide. Ms. Hemphill discussed the recent submittal of a
grant, explaining that the grant was denied because the proposal to add three
(3) transient slips was not enough to satisfy the provisions of the grant.
Former Wastewater Treatment Facility - 901 W. West Street
   Board members toured the former site of the wastewater treatment plant.
Public Works Director, David Fox, explained the former treatment process and
why the State ordered the plant decommissioned. He showed members the areas of
the site continuing to be used for storage; i.e. Christmas wreaths and new
utility poles.
Central Pump Station – W. Leonard Street & Burrington Avenue
   Aldermen Mosteller and Pukenas, along with City Manager McDuffie and Mr.
Jones were given a comprehensive description of the components and operation of
the central pump station by Mr. Fox.
Lunch – 12:20 p.m.
   City Manager McDuffie asked the Board to consider a sidewalk and crosswalks
project from 9th Street to 12th Street in the 2016-2017 budget.
Bill Payment Terminal - 720 N. Fodale Avenue
   Board members viewed the proposed location of a drive thru bill payment
terminal on Fodale Avenue next to the city’s electric substation and across the
street from Dosher Hospital. City Manager McDuffie stated that staff recommends
the location which is better for pedestrian traffic than other proposed sites,
along with availability of required fiber optic cables.
   Aldermen Mosteller, Coring, Powell & Pukenas voiced their opinions that the
site was the best and safest location. Alderman Coring motioned, second by
Alderman Pukenas to install the bill payment terminal on the Fodale Avenue
site. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
441 Acres – Sunny Point Road
   The Board was driven to the city owned property along the Military Ocean
Terminal Sunny Point access road. During the drive, Alderman Powell pointed out
the city’s sewer district. He explained that four (4) basins had been dug on
the city’s site to provide dirt to the North Carolina Department of
Transportation (NCDOT) for the newest Oak Island bridge. The Board discussed
the cost and timeframe for building a wastewater treatment facility.
Public Works – 1010 N. Howe Street
   Garage
   Mr. Fox provided a tour of the vehicles and equipment used by the department
of 16 employees. He explained that he oversees the operation and maintenance of
the city’s infrastructure, i.e. water, sewer, streets, city buildings,
cemeteries, grounds and electric system. Alderman Powell suggested a
replacement program for the department’s vehicles.
   Load Management
   Mr. Ellie Pittenger, Load Management Coordinator, presented an overview of
the load management program, emphasizing the four levels of rates available
depending on the number of switches installed. He pointed out that a customer
can get an 8.5¢ per kWh rate with implementation of all switches. Mr. Pittenger
explained that 50% of the city’s electric cost happens at peak and the highest
peak ever experienced was in January 2015. Mr. Pittenger added that he has had
123 requests for the new highly efficient two-way load management switches that
are expected to arrive in March. Alderman Powell and Mosteller suggested
increased public outreach. Mr. Pittenger indicated a review of switches
currently in use was performed in 2012:
   *   612 hot water heater
    *   73 pending
   *   379 heat strips
   *   359 HVAC cycling
   *   103 HVAC total control
Mr. Pittenger encouraged upgrading to LED lighting on the street lights.
   AMI Project
   Mr. Paul Woodall, Utilities Specialist, reported that the contract had been
signed, purchase orders cut and water meters would be ordered for the automated
metering infrastructure (AMI) project. He stated it is anticipated that the
infrastructure will be set up mid-March with 100% of the project completed in
May. He indicated that 200 remote disconnect meters are ordered along with
additional stock parts. He noted that technology is not yet available for pre-
pay water similar to pre-pay electric. He added that updates to the system are
on the annual contract.
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out there is a 10 year warranty on the
batteries and a suggested 20 year replacement of batteries and meters. Mr.
Woodall stated the system will allow easy access to actual usage and
notification of a possible leak.
   City Manager McDuffie reminded the Board that replacement of all water
meters will start in early March, replacement of all electric meters will begin
in March and the city’s financial software will be implemented in February. He
emphasized that notices will go out on utility bills, special mailings and
information will be posted on the city’s web page.
Board Comments
   Alderman Coring requested replacement of the “no parking” signs on the fence
along the Dry Street side of the water tank. Alderman Coring motioned, second
by Alderman Poole to direct staff to put up the no parking signs. Unanimous
vote; motion carried.
Recess - 4:00 p.m.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to recess the meeting to
Saturday, January 23, 2016, 8:45 a.m. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
                        /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor
Attest:   /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS
(Complete reports on file in the Clerk's office)
Tourism Department - Randy Jones
   Mr. Jones thanked the Board, city staff and citizens for making him feel
welcome, the support and encouragement, and the assurances that Tourism is
important for Southport. He emphasized the Tourism Department Vision Statement:
City of Southport envisions our town being a premier tourist destination,
retaining and showcasing the values, heritage, culture and the natural beauty
Southport has to offer and Mission Statement: The Department of Tourism has a
mission to foster, develop and promote a sustainable tourism industry for
Southport.
   Mr. Jones discussed working with other local historical organizations in
planning and developing exhibits, partnering/networking with community groups
on ongoing and new events and outreach activities, develop a "branding
campaign" to attract a sustainable flow of tourists by concentrating on a day
trip tourist base within a 100 mile radius and implementing monthly tourism
roundtable meetings.
   Mr. Jones reviewed proposed options for the Museum Store, Garrison House
repairs and maintenance, supporting filming activities and development of a new
City of Southport Website.
   Mr. Jones praised the Visitor's Center volunteers noting that they were
Southport's best ambassadors.
Fire Department - Chief Drew
   Chief Drew provided a handout of the department's accomplishments for 2015.
He emphasized the training and certifications achieved through classes held at
the station and at Brunswick Community College. He discussed the health of
volunteerism in Southport with 26 new volunteers; (13 firefighters, 13 EMS
division). He reviewed the number of calls responded to, response time and
pointed out that 15-18 members respond on each call with an average 4-6 minute
response time.
   Chief Drew discussed the goal of equipping the department for industrial
calls noting there are four (4) industrial plants in the area. To that end, the
department was awarded a $10,000 grant to help purchase equipment specific to
industrial responses.
   Chief Drew pointed out that the department is in the process of updating
Automated External Defibrillators (AED) stations and had received $40,000 worth
of equipment from a local company for that purpose. He stated a map of AED
locations will be produced for distribution and advertisement.
   Chief Drew reported that the department's fleet was in good shape and it is
not anticipated any requests will be made for upgrades in the next fiscal year.
   Chief Drew indicated the department had tested and serviced 450 hydrants and
13,000 feet of fire hose.
   Goals/Project
   Chief Drew emphasized the department's preparation for the ISO inspection,
the first in 15 years. He reported that the renovations to the former rescue
squad station had been quoted at $25,000 vs. the once quoted half million
dollars. He stated that Deputy Chief Johnson is in the process of getting
quotes for replacement of cardiac monitors.
   Chief Drew stated that getting the EMS division uniformed is a departmental
goal. He indicated that the EMS Division is talking with Dosher Memorial
Hospital about doing patient transfers which will bolster revenue.
   Chief Drew pointed out that the majority of the department's budget is based
on fire fees collected but some changes will be realized with the Fire/Rescue
merger. He stated that part-time assistance will be added in Fire Inspections
and secretarial help is needed along with staffing of the station when squads
are responding to calls. He stated that a small increase to the call stipend
(likely $5) will be proposed in the FY 2016-2017 budget.
   Chief Drew stated there is interest in the department to start a small scale
water rescue program.
   Long Range Goals
   Chief Drew stated that long range goals of the department are getting the
EMS division certified at a paramedic level and securing property in the
Rivermist subdivision to establish a future substation for better coverage of
the area.
Planning - John Allen
   Mr. John Allen reviewed the 2015 accomplishments of the Community
Development/Planning Department, pointing out his support to the Waterfront
Steering Committee and representation of the City on the Regional Hazard
Mitigation Committee and the Oak Island Area Economic Development Committee. He
indicated that the Southport-Oak Island Chamber of Commerce started the
economic development committee to assist in recruitment and retention of
retailers. Mr. Allen stated he had sold $22,243.52 worth of surplus vehicles
and equipment and had obtained a grant from Electricities to have a Phase I
environmental assessment conducted on the old wastewater treatment plant. Mr.
Allen outlined the 2016-2017 goals, emphasizing a planned review and update of
the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) and the rezoning of parcels zoned
business district (BD) behind the parcels fronting the Howe Street business
district. He explained that the BD zoning encompasses properties beyond those
fronting Howe Street that are residential. He cited instances where parcels and
houses have split zoning.
Inspections-Wayne Strickland
   Mr. Strickland presented an annual report for the Building Inspections
Department. He reported that the Rivermist subdivision is built out and the
Cades Cove subdivision will be in the near future. He reviewed the permitting
and valuation of 93 single family residences, 20 commercial structures, 703
electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits, and 4,012 corresponding
inspections. He highlighted the updates of the Zoning Map and permitting fees
and certification of the Community Rating System (CRS). Mr. Strickland stated
he anticipates completion of an appeal to Federal Emergency Management Act
(FEMA) pertaining to Letters of Map Amendments (LOMA) for Rivermist and
adjustments to Bonnet's Creek floodway. He outlined the department's goals for
2016, specifically the purchase of a wide format printer/copier and long term
goals to digitize permitting files and update software programs.
   Mr. Strickland announced that he is nearing retirement age and encouraged
consideration of hiring a trainee replacement.
City Clerk - Michele Windham
   Ms. Windham presented a report of the 2015 accomplishments of the City
Clerk's Office, emphasizing the completed preservation of one large volume
minutes book dated 1925 through 1954 and 14 Code of Ordinance updates. She
pointed out that additional books are scheduled to be preserved in 2016. She
noted that she and the Deputy City Clerk were participating in North Carolina
Association of Municipal Clerks (NCAMC) and School of Government training
opportunities. She highlighted future goals of the department to improve
meeting recording equipment and electronic management of all records. Ms.
Windham shared plans to host a regional NCAMC conference in the upcoming years.
Human Resources - Michele Windham
   Ms. Windham reported that Human Resources Technician, Teresa Parker-Mosley

integrates the employee time clock system. Ms. Windham pointed out that Human
Resources endeavors to develop a uniform pay plan classification and job

Community Building - Vickie Potter
   Ms. Potter presented a list of 13 needed repairs and maintenance totaling
$41,170. She also proposed a new day-rate fee adjustment to rent the building,
six-hour block min. $1,800 ($300 per hour), 12-hour block $3,900 ($325 per
hour) for non-residents and $1,800 ($150 per hour) for 12 hours for residents
and city employees. She stated she proposed the new rates to keep the building
profitable. She pointed out that the building is booked every Saturday until

Parks and Recreation - Heather Hemphill

noted the renovations to the Lord Street Gym are dependent on the

   Ms. Hemphill stated long term goals include construction of a recreation and
athletic complex at the 9th Street property or a recreation center at Lord
Street Gym and an athletic complex at 9th street property.
Finance Department - Melanie Trexler
   Ms. Trexler presented an update on the installation of the city's new
financial software; payroll live for the first payroll in February, purchase
orders and accounts payable live March 1, utility billing target date live July
1. She provided an analysis of the 2015 fire fees and expenditures, general
funds & enterprise funds operating cash balances, governmental funds balance

   Ms. Trexler stated she expects the city auditors to deliver a report at the

   6.   Audit Presentation
   Auditor Menton Padgett of the accounting firm Berry, Padgett and Chandler
presented the June 30, 2015 audit report. Noting that the Board had just
received it, he advised them on how to read it and encouraged them to come to
his office with questions. He referred the Board to the management's discussion
and analysis as a positive summary of the city's financial condition. He
highlighted the accounting policies used, reviewed fund balances, budgetary
statements and explained new pension reporting requirements. He emphasized that
revenues and expenditures continued to increase along with cash-on-hand in the
electric, water and sewer funds which were up over previous reporting periods.
Additionally, he pointed out that the city had no bonded debt. (Report on file
in the Clerk's office)
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Poole to accept the audit.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to amend the auditor
contract to February 28. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Poole to adopt a resolution
requesting certain action by the NCDOT. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
A RESOLUTION REQUESTING THE NORTH CAROLINA
DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION TO PLACE CERTAIN
TRAFFIC LIGHTS IN FLASHING MODE
WHEREAS, the citizens of the City of Southport and all those who visit,
appreciate and enjoy the unique history, charm and appeal that the Southport
area offers; and
WHEREAS, the safe use of roads and highways is of upmost importance to not only
the citizens of Southport, but also to our visitors from this great State and
other states and countries; and
WHEREAS, Howe and Moore Streets are state-maintained roads; and
WHEREAS, there are traffic signals at the intersections of Howe and Moore
Streets and Howe and 9th Streets; and
WHEREAS, between 11:00 PM and 5:00 AM, traffic volumes are very low in
Southport and the normal operation of the traffic signals is therefore
unnecessary for public safety; and
WHEREAS, if the traffic signals were set to a red/yellow flashing pattern, it
would allow the few vehicles on the road to move about more easily.
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport,
North Carolina, that the City of Southport requests that the North Carolina
Department of Transportation place the traffic signals at Moore and Howe
Streets and at Howe and 9th Streets on a red/yellow flashing pattern between
the hours of 11:00 PM and 5:00 AM.
Adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen in regular session, February 22,
2016.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: s/s Michele Windham, City Clerk

AGENDA
   1.   Whittler’s Bench Parking
   City Manager McDuffie presented a staff recommendation and a variation on
the adopted Waterfront Plan to address the parking issues at the Whittlers
Bench parking area. He outlined the proposed plan to install a concrete
planting median in the parking area with six (6) to eight (8) diagonal parking
spaces. He indicated that a catch basin would be replaced to tackle drainage
problems.
   The Board discussed the availability of water for care of the plantings in
the median and the required handicapped parking spaces.
   Alderman Pukenas suggested coordinating the paving with the contractor
tasked with the repaving of the Yacht Basin area.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to proceed with paving
of the Whittlers Bench parking area, installing a landscape median
approximately 10’ wide x 40’ long, replacing the catch basin, lining of parking
spaces in conformance with the NCDOT Uniform Traffic Control Manual and to
coordinate the work with the Yacht Basin paving project.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.  
   2.   Lord Street Gymnasium
   Pointing out that the Board had seen the engineering assessment on the steel
roof trusses, Alderman Adams asked the Board to make a decision on the Lord
Street Gymnasium renovation project. He noted that the fundraising effort was
behind, but he said one reason was the uncertainty of the structural integrity
and the city’s commitment. He emphasized the opportunity to have a civic
center, theater and larger recreational facility. He challenged the Board to
have a long range vision as previous Boards did when rebuilding the USO
(Community) Building.
   Aldermen Poole and Pukenas agreed that the building should be saved.
   Alderman Powell contended that the structure could be torn down and a new
one built for half of the cost quoted to renovate it. He pointed out that water
and sewer infrastructure throughout the city is also in need of upgrading.
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that the college expects a new roof to be
on the building by July, 2017. He also said that building permits have to be
filed and approved by December 2018 prior to State building code changes that
would prohibit the rehabilitation due to the building’s structural make-up.
   Alderman Coring declared that he had continually supported the project. He
stated concerns that the city has multiple projects underway and he stressed
the need to prioritize. He stated his opinion that the city has already
committed to rehabilitating the gym as has the gym committee to raising money
for the project. He added that tearing down the building would go against the
historic significance of the structure.
   Mr. Donnie Joyner, gym committee member, stated he had commitments from the
community but many were hesitant to give money until the project moves forward.
He stated a facility that could host trade shows and events would draw people
to Southport.
   Mayor Dove recalled partnering with citizens of the city to rebuild the USO
Building when it was destroyed by fire in 1995. He spoke about the theory of
diminishing returns while encouraging the Board to make a decision and
afterwards to have a maintenance plan to ensure that city buildings do not fall
into disrepair in the future.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Coring to authorize $48,000 to
do the preliminaries (cleaning, scraping, structural assessment) on the Lord
Street Gymnasium roof trusses.
   Discussion
   Alderman Powell asked if the motion could include instructions to staff to
research the deed to determine if the city could build on the site.
   Alderman Poole did not modify her motion.
   Ayes:   Aldermen Poole, Coring, Adams, Mosteller, Pukenas
   Nay:   Alderman Powell
   Motion Carried 5-1
   3.   201 E. Moore Street
   City Manager McDuffie reported that an account of the February 29th Town
Hall public meeting regarding the future of the former City Hall had not been
submitted from the facilitator of the meeting, Chris May, Cape Fear Council of
Government.
   Alderman Mosteller stated her assessment of the comments from the meeting
that expressed a clear mandate for a commitment to put a roof on the building
to halt further decline and deterioration and to relocate the Police
Department.
   Mayor Dove stated he took copious notes of what citizens stated with most
wanting the structure preserved as part of the city’s historic history. He
noted that the building was never designed to be a police department.
   Alderman Adams expressed support for relocating the police department,
putting a new roof on and taking time to consider the direction to proceed with
the building.
   Alderman Poole pointed out that the Board had previously authorized
replacement of the roof but issues arose that delayed the work. She fully
supported putting on a new roof.
   Alderman Pukenas stated his opinion that the police department needs to get
out of the building as quickly as possible and that replacement of the roof is
of vital importance to stop decline.
   Aldermen Coring and Powell agreed.
   City Manager McDuffie explained that the bid received from a Wilmington
based contractor was less than one year old and he would contact them to
determine if they would still honor it.
   Alderman Mosteller motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to proceed with the
roof replacement at 201 E. Moore Street in an amount not to exceed $225,000.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

   5.   Wells Fargo Lease of 1029 N. Howe Street
   City Manager McDuffie explained that the lease for the second floor of City

   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell for all or nothing, with

   6.   Electrical Underground Priorities

   7.   City Boat Dock
   Parks & Recreation Director, Heather Hemphill, told the Board that the
condition of the City Boat Dock had reached a point where a decision had to be
made. She stated she had applied for a boating infrastructure grant that was
not awarded because not enough slips were dedicated to transient boaters. She
stressed the need to dredge, noting that many slips were not useable at low
tide. She discussed three options:
   1.   Do nothing.
   2.   Reapply for the grant with dedication of the majority of slips to
transient boaters.
   3.   Pay for dredging and renovations with a loan to be paid back with boat
slip rentals.
   Ms. Hemphill pointed out that in order to meet the requirements for the
grant, and reach the minimum 6 foot depth for slips 5 - 26 at low tide, 1,600
cu. yds. would have to be dredged and hauled to a spoil site. She estimated the
cost at $37,000 - $47,000 with a total cost up to $70,000 to include removal to
a spoil site.
   City Manager McDuffie stated that the city would have to charge $1,800 per
year, per slip to recoup the costs. He pointed out that the current annual
income is $24,000. He noted that Southport Marina charged by the linear foot.
   After hearing Alderman Adams’ position, Board consensus to re-apply for the
grant with the understanding that a larger ratio of boat slips would have to be
converted to transient slips.
   8.   Consideration of Request from Brunswick County for Sewer Service at
Smithville Park
   City Manager McDuffie stated that Brunswick County had asked to provide
their own sewer service in the City’s sewer territory at Smithville Park and to
become a city customer.
   Alderman Powell said he didn’t see a problem with the County tapping into
the 12” force main as long as the tap was not considered the city’s allocation
per the current sewer agreement with them.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Poole to provide metered sewer
service to Smithville Park, making the County a city customer and the tap would
not be considered a city tap.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   9.   Subdivision Maintenance Guarantee
   Alderman Adams stated that he had requested consideration of extending the
maintenance guarantee from one (1) year to eighteen (18) months to ensure more
protection for the city when accepting infrastructure in a subdivision. He
cited occurrences in the past when problems with the infrastructure surfaced
after the one year period.
   Alderman Powell contended that a performance bond would better serve the
city, noting that in the past 30 years there had been just one or two
subdivisions that had resulted in problems for the city.
   Alderman Adams indicated he would withdraw the request for consideration
while reserving the right to bring it before the board in the future if a
subdivision caused problems for the city.
   10.   Set Priorities   
   Mayor Dove stated one of his priorities would be to see sidewalks in the

   Alderman Poole asked about the status of correcting the erosion on the

   Alderman Mosteller inquired about additional odor control filtration at the

   Alderman Adams stated he would like to see the deteriorating valve station

   Citing safety concerns, Alderman Adams requested a meeting be arranged with

   Commenting on witnessing an individual with a dog in a wheelchair while in
the middle of N. Howe Street, Alderman Mosteller asked about a safe pedestrian

right-of-way at The Ridge Subdivision and is pursuing an easement from
adjoining landowner, Roy Daniels.
   Referring to the Parks, Recreation and Open Space Master Plan and the
unprecedented amount of work the Parks and Recreation Department does, Alderman
Mosteller suggested analyzing the need for another position in the department
and ways to implement the Plan. Additionally, she proposed a summit meeting of
various civic leaders, i.e. Downtown Southport Inc. (DSI), Historical Society,
Garden Club, Beautification Committee, etc. to focus on working together on
citywide projects. She noted that the Tourism Department has planned a local
businesses summit in April. Board consensus was to see what results come out of
the Tourism summit before setting a date for an additional summit.
   Alderman Mosteller shared her opinion that the proposal to adjust the rental
rates for the Community Building as presented at the January 23rd Retreat
seemed reasonable and would provide for the much needed repairs and continued
maintenance of the facility. She pointed out that in 2014 there were 54 City
sponsored events, 60 non-profit events, 45 citizens rented the building in
addition to wedding and other event rentals.
   Alderman Poole stated she could not support raising the Community Building
rates to a level that a majority of citizens could not afford to pay. She
emphasized that the citizens, businesses and organizations paid to rebuild the
building when it burned in 1995. She noted that the rental agreement prohibits
subletting.
   Responding to Alderman Coring, City Manager McDuffie told the Board that in
order to enforce two (2) hour parking in the city, a sign stating the
limitation must be in front of the parking slip. He stated options would be to
add signs or modify the ordinance to reflect what is currently posted. He added
that a parking schedule is maintained in the Police Department. Board consensus
to modify the ordinance and place on the April consent agenda for approval.
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the fire substation renovation would go
slightly over the $25,000 budget because replacement ceiling grids could not be
purchased and the electrical contractor quoted the work without looking in the
electrical box. There were no objections from the Board.

Resolution Requesting the North Carolina Department of Transportation to Set a
Speed Limit of 45 miles per hour on Rob Gandy Boulevard
WHEREAS, a portion of Rob Gandy Boulevard, a state road, is located within the
municipal limits of the City of Southport; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has determined pursuant to G. S. 20-141(f) that
a higher maximum speed than that set forth in G.S. 20-141(b) is reasonable and
safe; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Board of Aldermen hereby determines and declares that 45
mph is a safe and reasonable speed limit on said road;
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the speed
limit on Rob Gandy Boulevard within the City of Southport be set at 45 mph and
that the State enact a concurring ordinance.
This the 10th day of March, 2016.
                  City of Southport
/s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
AGENDA
   7.   Request to Sponsor the Military Appreciation Day Event
Mr. Hank Pomeranz, a Southport resident, small business owner, retired Navy,
and President of the Southport Chapter of Military Appreciation Day, Inc., a
non-profit 501C3 organization, introduced an initiative to declare one day a
year as Military Appreciation Day. He explained that the event would be held on
September 10th and geared towards thanking active duty troops and their
families with a day of fishing provided by local fishermen. He stated the event
would showcase at Southport Marina with games included for children and a lunch
provided by volunteers. He pointed out that Southport has helped the
organization in the past and he asked for a donation to assist with the cost of
a banner.
The Board took no action on the request.
   8.   Piedmont Natural Gas Presentation
   Ms. Kathy Pleasant, Piedmont Natural Gas, spoke to the Board about the
challenges in bringing natural gas to the community. She pointed out that
additional infrastructure is required to provide gas to existing commercial and
neighborhood areas of the city versus installing infrastructure in a new
development. She stated that since first providing gas to Dosher Hospital and
the Southport Elementary School in 2011, the service has been expanded to
Indigo Plantation, Harbor Oaks, Smithville Woods, Cades Cove and The Landing.
She said the company is currently working on projects on the west and east side
of Howe Street and hopes to eventually provide natural gas to restaurants along
the waterfront. She asked for patience through the process, noting that most
Southport projects have taken two years to become feasible for the company to
undertake.
   Responding to a query by Alderman Mosteller, Ms. Pleasant stated that
typically a 40% commitment of households in a neighborhood is needed to obtain
project feasibility.
   In response to a question by City Manager McDuffie, Ms. Pleasant indicated a
gas line could not be included in joint trenching. She added that Piedmont
Natural Gas does not do fracking. She stated that the increased availability of
natural gas will drive the price lower.
   9.   Consideration of Franklin Square Park “Walk of Honor”
   Mr. Stanley Mandel discussed establishing a Walk of Honor in Franklin Square
Park with first honoree P.D. Midget, a 30 year resident, musician and pastor.
Mr. Mandel stated his vision of a committee of citizens and Aldermen to decide
others to be honored.
   Alderman Mosteller pointed out that the Old Southport Jail on E. Nash Street
has a brick paver path that honors citizens.
   Mr. Mandel indicated that Franklin Square Park had been chosen because P.D.
had performed there and had his art displayed at the Franklin Square Art
Gallery.
   Alderman Pukenas motioned, second by Alderman Powell to establish a
committee to set criteria and to recommend where done.
   Discussion
   Alderman Adams questioned locating the memorial in Franklin Square Park and
he cautioned against fragmenting memorials throughout the city.
   Alderman Poole concurred with Alderman Adams and reminded the Board that
other groups had submitted similar requests and they had been denied. She
stated that such proposals should be launched by an outside source and not
established by the Board.
   Both Alderman Adams and Poole went on record stating their respect for P.D.
Midgett.
   Alderman Coring agreed with Alderman Adams while noting that a memorial for
firefighters had been proposed at the former location of the Fire Station on E.
Nash Street.
   Aye:   Aldermen Pukenas and Powell
   Nay:   Aldermen Mosteller, Poole, Coring, Nelson
   Motion Failed.
   10.   Update on Waterfront Improvement Project
   Mr. Allen updated the Board on the status of the Waterfront Improvement
Project. He reminded the Board that the project is two parts: shoreline
stabilization and waterfront park and area improvements. He stated the current
focus is on the erosion control. He indicated he had been in frequent
communication with Mike McIntyre and Glenn Dunn of Poyner & Spruill who have
contacted the following entities on the city’s behalf:
United Stated Department of Agriculture, Rural Development
US Army Corp of Engineers
NC Division of Coastal Management
Duke Energy
Golden Leaf Foundation
   Mr. Allen stated that he has submitted the “Request for Environmental
Scoping” to the NC Department of Administration, has provided information
regarding the project to The Golden Leaf Foundation, is preparing a preliminary
grant application for submittal to the NC Division of Coastal Management’s
“Public Beach and Coastal Waterfront Access Program Grant”, and has met with
the US Department of Agriculture’s Rural Development staff in regard to a
possible loan. He indicated he plans to contact Duke Energy about a possible
grant from their foundation.
   11.   Request to Accept Infrastructure: Norseman Loop in Rivermist
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the Public Works Department had
evaluated the street and recommends acceptance pending submittal of a one year
warranty bond.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Coring to accept the
infrastructure of Phase IV, Norseman Loop, upon submittal of a one year
warranty bond, as recommended by staff. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

   Ms. Shirley Snyder, Chair of the Beautification Committee, presented a brief

towards purchase of additional wreaths for display in the Yacht Basin Area and
on Bay Street. She reviewed calculations of the value of the volunteers’
service. Ms. Snyder submitted a $5,795 budget request for FY 2016/2017.

Alderman Mosteller thanked everyone for participating in the recent Town Hall
meeting. She thanked the Beautification Committee for all they do for the city.
Alderman Coring stated the Fire Department had completed the Insurance Service
