Alderman Powell talked about the two (2) hour parking limit on W. Moore Street

Responding to a query from Alderman Pukenas, Mr. Isenberg gave an example to

RESOLUTION IN RECOGNITION OF J. ARTHUR DOSHER MEMORIAL HOSPITAL NURSES
WHEREAS, the nearly 3.1 million registered nurses in the United States comprise
our nation’s largest health care profession; and
WHEREAS, the depth and breadth of the nursing profession meets the different
and emergency health care needs of the American population in a wide range of
settings; and
WHEREAS, the cost-effective, safe and quality health care services provided by
nurses will be an ever more important component of the U.S. health care
delivery system in the future; and
WHEREAS, the American Nurses Association has declared the week of May 6 - 12 as
NATIONAL NURSES WEEK with the theme Delivering Quality and Innovation in
Patient Care; and
WHEREAS, the nurses of J. Arthur Dosher Memorial Hospital have provided
essential lifesaving medical service to the citizens of Southport and the
surrounding communities since the opening of the hospital in 1928; and
WHEREAS, the nurses of J. Arthur Dosher Memorial Hospital are an integral part
of our health care system providing unselfish care to the citizens of Southport
and the surrounding area of Brunswick County; and
WHEREAS, the nurses of J. Arthur Dosher Memorial Hospital have a long history
of dedicated service to the citizens of Southport;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that J. V. Dove, Mayor of the City of
Southport, and Board of Aldermen recognize the importance of their contribution
to the health and well-being of all citizens and do hereby proclaim May 6, 2016
as
 “J. ARTHUR DOSHER MEMORIAL HOSPITAL NURSES DAY”
This 14th day of April 2016
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

Resolution
Municipal Clerks Week
May 1 – 7, 2016
Whereas, Municipal Clerks week is May 1 – 7, 2016, and
Whereas, The Office of the Municipal Clerk, a time honored and vital part of
local government exists throughout the world, and
Whereas, The Office of the Municipal Clerk is the oldest among public servants,
and
Whereas, The Office of the Municipal Clerk provides the professional link
between the citizens, the local governing bodies and agencies of government at
other levels, and
Whereas, Municipal Clerks have pledged to be ever mindful of their neutrality
and impartiality, rendering equal service to all.
Whereas, The Municipal Clerk serves as the information center on functions of
local government and community.
Whereas, Michele Windham serves as City of Southport Clerk and has been
employed by the City of Southport since December 12, 2003, and
Whereas, It is most appropriate that we recognize the accomplishments of the
Office of the Municipal Clerk.
Now, Therefore, be it resolved that the Southport Board of Aldermen, do
Recognize the week of May 1 through May 7, 2016, as Municipal Clerks Week, and
further extend appreciation to our Municipal Clerk, Michele Windham for the
vital services performed and exemplary dedication to the City of Southport.
Dated this 14th day of April, 2016

A RESOLUTION RECOGNIZING THE NATIONAL DAY OF PRAYER
WHEREAS, civic prayers and national days of prayer have a long and venerable
history in our constitutional republic, dating back to the First Continental
Congress in 1775; and
WHEREAS, the Declaration of Independence, our first statement as Americans of
national purpose and identity, made “the Laws of Nature and Nature’s God” the
foundation of our United States of America and asserted that people have
inalienable rights that are God-given; and
WHEREAS, the Supreme Court has affirmed the right of state legislatures to open
their sessions with prayer and the Supreme Court and the U.S. Congress
themselves begin each day with prayer; and
WHEREAS, in 1988 legislation setting aside the first Thursday of May in each
year as a National Day of Prayer was passed unanimously by both Houses of
Congress and signed by President Ronald Reagan; and
WHEREAS, the National Day of Prayer is an opportunity for Americans of all
faiths to join in united prayer to acknowledge our dependence on God, to give
thanks for blessings received, to request healing for wounds endured, and to
ask God to guide our leaders and bring wholeness to the United States and her
citizens; and
WHEREAS, it is fitting and proper to give thanks to God by observing a day of
prayer in the City of Southport when all may acknowledge our blessings and
express gratitude for them, while recognizing the needs for strengthening
religious and moral values in our State and Nation; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that I, J.V. Dove, Mayor of the City of
Southport, and Board of Aldermen do hereby proclaim May 5, 2016 as “A DAY OF
PRAYER IN SOUTHPORT” and urge all citizens of Southport to observe the day in
ways appropriate to its importance and significance.
This 14th day of April 2016.
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
City of Southport
2016 Earth Day Proclamation
WHEREAS, our home, this planet Earth, is adversely affected by population
growth and rapid depletion of resources; and
WHEREAS, since the first Earth Day in 1970, the Clean Air Act has made the
nation’s air cleaner, the Clean Water Act has improved water quality, and the
Endangered Species Act has attempted to preserve ecosystems to maintain the
variety of species; and
WHEREAS, following the principles of reduce, repair, reuse and recycle,
residents can improve their environment; and
WHEREAS, preservation is easier and less expensive than restoration; and
WHEREAS, Earth Day provides an opportunity for members of the community to
study, learn and teach local activities which will contribute to protecting our
planet’s ecosystem; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that I, J. V. Dove, Mayor of the City of
Southport, do hereby proclaim Friday, April 22, 2016, as
EARTH DAY
to be observed by all citizens in ways to better understand, appreciate, and
preserve the resources of our earth, and especially the resources of this area.
This 14th day of April 2016.
                                               /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
/s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk
AGENDA
10.   Public Hearing: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment,    
Article 11, Section 11-1 (I) Rear Yard Abutting Side Yard
Mr. Allen pointed out that the Board had asked the Planning Board to review
setback requirements for accessory structures. He stated that the proposed
amendment would require a 20 foot setback for an accessory structure that is
over 15 foot tall, when the back yard of the lot containing the accessory
structure is adjacent to the side yard of a neighboring lot.
Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to go into Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Mr. Richard Bandera, 309 Clarendon Avenue, stated his concerns that the
proposed amendment would hinder the building of an accessory structure within
the historic district. He cited several properties in the city that would be
impacted, including one owned by him and his wife.
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Powell to close Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
11.   Consideration of Text Amendment
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Coring to send the
recommendation back to the Planning Board for further review.
Discussion
   Alderman Adams backed Alderman Poole, noting that he had raised the issue.
He supported the reduction in height.
   Alderman Mosteller questioned if a moratorium on accessory structures should
be considered.
   Attorney Isenberg explained the difficulty in adopting a moratorium due to
legislative changes.
   Unanimous vote; motion carried.

AN ORDINANCE APPROVING A TEXT AMENDMENT TO THE
UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, City Staff, in conjunction with the Planning Board, has prepared
the proposed amendment to Section 15.8 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and finds
the proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance to be consistent
with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommend its approval;
and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on April 14, 2016, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby find that this
proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the
Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that narrower street rights of way are
appropriate for Small Lot Cluster Developments.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment to Section 15.8 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance is hereby approved and adopted.
This, the 14th day of April, 2016                  City of Southport
                     BY: /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor

Section 25-9: Subdivision Infrastructure Acceptance and Maintenance Guarantee
After construction of streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, drainage facilities,
and water and sewer lines is complete, the developer or owner of a subdivision
approved under the process set forth in this Article may request that the City
take over ownership of said streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, drainage
facilities located within rights of way, and water and sewer lines. Prior to
such acceptance by the Board of Aldermen, the developer or owner shall provide
a security guaranteeing streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, drainage
facilities, and water and sewer lines against defects for one year. This
security shall be in the amount of 75% of the costs of the infrastructure
accepted by the City and shall be in cash, letter of credit, or bond made by a
surety company authorized to do business in North Carolina.
The developer or owner shall also provide a letter or statement in which said
developer or owner shall agree to maintain the backfill and any improvements
located thereon and therein and any ditch which has been dug in connection with
the installation of such improvements. Such letter or statement shall be
binding on the developer or owner for a period of one year after the acceptance
of such improvements by the City of Southport.
This section shall be effective April 14, 2016, except that the 75% maintenance
guarantee shall not apply to any subdivision for which the preliminary plat has
been approved prior to said date.

17.   Consideration of Whittlers Bench Parking Lot Resurfacing
   Mr. David Fox presented two (2) options for repair of the Whittlers Bench
parking lot: Option 1 would remove the existing asphalt, Option 2 would do a
crack fill.
   Alderman Powell pointed out that the pavement area could be ripped out in
approximately five (5) years with implementation of the Waterfront Project.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to accept Option 2.
   Discussion
   Alderman Poole expressed concerns about the current parking lines bleeding
through as had happened in the past causing confusion and the inability to
drive around the Whittlers Bench.
   Alderman Adams acknowledged Alderman Poole’s concerns. He supported Alderman
Powell with an added mandate to beginning the Waterfront Project within two
years.
   Mr. Fox noted that with the crack fill and overlay, a better product should
be realized and bleed through would be minimal.
   City Manager McDuffie recommended using thermal line marking.
   Alderman Pukenas emphasized that the fix is temporary and not a long term
solution.
   Alderman Coring pointed out that the Board had committed to doing the
Waterfront Project and the area needs to be something everyone can be proud of.
He stated his opinion that resurfacing would make a big difference.
   City Manager McDuffie explained that with a 1-1/2” asphalt layer, there
should be no bleed through. He stated that two contractors had highly
recommended removing all asphalt and installing a stone base. He said that
without a base, within three to four years, the asphalt would crack as is now
seen on West Moore Street.
   Mayor Dove asked about the longevity of Option 2. Mr. Fox responded that the
asphalt would last for an indefinite period but would crack. He added that he
would provide a sketch of the project before proceeding.
   Unanimous vote; motion carried.

7.   Proclamation Recognizing May 21-27, 2016 as National Safe Boating Week
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to adopt the
Proclamation Recognizing May 21-27, 2016 as National Safe Boating Week.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Alderman Poole read the Proclamation into the record and the Board joined
her in presenting it to members of the USCG Station Oak Island and USCG
Auxiliary Flotilla 10-05 in attendance.
ProclamationA Sample Proclamation
Recreational boating is fun and enjoyable, and we are fortunate that we have
sufficient resources to accommodate the wide variety of pleasure boating
demands. However, our waterways can become crowded at times and be a place of
chaos and confusion. While being a marvelous source of recreation, boating, to
the unprepared, can be a risky sport. Not knowing or obeying the Navigation
Rules or the nautical “Rules of the Road,” drinking alcohol or taking drugs
while operating a boat, or choosing not to wear your life jacket when doing so
is clearly NOT the smart thing to do, are all examples of human error or a lack
of proper judgment. One particular behavior that can reduce the number of
boaters who lose their lives by drowning each year by is the wearing of a life
jacket. It is a simple task that has the potential to reduce terrible loss in
lives.
Knowledge and skills are important in reducing human error and improving
judgment. If people are aware of the risk, they are likely to take the
precautionary measures to protect themselves and their friends and family. That
is why we must continue to spread the messages of boating safety not only
during National Safe Boating Week but also throughout the entire year.
Whereas, on average, 700 people die each year in boating-related accidents in
the U.S.; approximately 71% of these are fatalities caused by drowning; and
Whereas, the vast majority of these accidents are caused by human error or poor
judgment and not by the boat, equipment, or environmental factors; and
Whereas, a significant number of boaters who lose their lives by drowning each
year would be alive today had they worn their life jackets; and
Whereas, today’s life jackets are more comfortable, more attractive, and more
wearable than styles of years past and deserve a fresh look by today’s boating
public.
Therefore, I, JV Dove, do hereby support the goals of the North American Safe
Boating Campaign, the United States Coast Guard and the Coast Guard Auxiliary
and proclaim May 21 – 27, 2016, as National Safe Boating Week and the start of
the year-round effort to promote safe boating.
In Witness Thereof, I urge all those who boat to Wear It! and practice safe
boating habits.
Given under my signature and the seal of
/s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor, Southport, North Carolina
/s/ Todd Murray “as directed”, Officer-in-Charge USCG Station Oak Island
/s/ Jack Gordon, Flotilla Commander, USCG Auxiliary Flotilla 10-05
at the city of Southport, North Carolina
this 12th day of May, 2016.

9.   Consideration of Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment,
Article 11, Section 11-1 (I) Rear Yard Abutting Side Yard
Mr. Allen gave the following report. (April 29, 2016 memo presented in its
entirety)
   In February, the Board of Aldermen requested that the Planning Board review
the setback requirements for accessory structures. A Planning Board review
committee met with staff to review the existing setback requirements and
discuss potential changes. At its March meeting the Planning Board approved a
recommendation to amend Section 11-1 of the UDO and require a 20 foot setback
for an accessory structure that is over 15 feet tall, when the back yard of the
lot containing the accessory structure is adjacent to the side yard of a
neighboring lot.
   After hearing public comment at its April meeting, the Board of Aldermen
sent the item back to the Planning Board for further study. The original review
committee met with Richard Bandera, a local architect, on April 20 and after
discussing the issue extensively, came to the conclusion that the previous
recommendation was not viable; nor could the committee determine a way to
modify the recommendation in such a way as to make it viable. The committee
voted to recommend to the Planning Board that the original recommendation be
withdrawn.
   At its meeting on April 21, after a presentation by the committee and much
discussion, the Planning Board voted to withdraw its previous recommendation
and leave Section 11-1 of the UDO unchanged.
   While stating her appreciation for the committee’s recommendation to not go
forward with a revision, Alderman Mosteller shared her opinion that the entire
accessory building regulations throughout the UDO should be reviewed.
   Alderman Mosteller motioned, second by Alderman Poole to ask the Planning
Board to revisit all of the accessory building regulations throughout the UDO.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

BUDGET WORKSHOP
1.   General Overview

2017 budget as presented to the Board at the May 12 regular meeting.
Budget numbers are balanced
Water, Sewer and Electric funds on solid footing
General Fund is the tightest
$500,000 was cut from departmental requests
1.9% COLA included for employees
$96,000 saved with change of insurance proposed to fund a salary study

accounts front loaded with $1,500 and $57/month for eleven months to ease the
transition from a PPO.
Standard health plan for new hires will be an HSA
2.   Revenue
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the proposed budget keeps the tax rate
the same as FY 2015/2016. He noted there was a slight increase to the tax base,
the Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV) tax was an estimated, the ABC Store
revenues are expected to be lower due to the recent remodel, and the Southport
Marina property taxes first collection will be realized during the FY 2017/2018
budget year.
   Alderman Powell questioned if the City was taxing the boats at Bald Head
Marina. City Manager McDuffie stated he would have the Tax Collector look into
it.
   Mayor Dove noted that a 1.9% COLA was proposed for all city employees. He
stated his opinion that many employees have dedicated many years to the city
and he suggested additional salary increases be considered. City Manager
McDuffie indicated that he is doing a salary study for all city positions as
previously requested by the Board and he anticipates having it completed by the
end of June. Mayor Dove asked if the Cape Fear Council of Government (COG)
could do a study free of charge. City Manager McDuffie stated he would contact
Chris May. Alderman Coring asked for a listing of pay increases made within the
last year.
   Mayor Dove thanked the City Manager for a wonderful job on health insurance
costs and communicating the options to the employees.

total cost, possible grants, 20 year financing projections and potential

rental rates for 22 slips useable, consideration of selling, leasing, or re-
applying for a grant with emphasis on transient boaters. Alderman Adams noted
that the boat docks are a sensitive, controversial and political issue to the
community. Board consensus to direct the city manager to ascertain the value of
the boat dock and lease opportunities.
   Garrison
   Tourism Director Jones advised the Board of the first assessment received on
the Garrison structure and mortar. He stated a 4-year project is planned to
perform the necessary point work at an estimated total cost of $388,000. He
indicated he would pursue grants and have a “Save A Brick” campaign. He pointed
out that the last pointing done on the building was in the late 1970’s.
Alderman Poole concurred that when the property was given to the City, the
needed pointing was identified at that time.
   Lord Street Gym
   Parks & Recreation Director Hemphill reported that the gymnasium roof
trusses could be repaired and used. Responding to a question by Alderman Poole,
Director Hemphill stated it would cost $321,000 to put a roof on the structure
and paint the exterior.
   Alderman Mosteller cited past Board minutes relating to a public/private
partnership to restore the building.
   Alderman Adams emphasized that the City had negotiated with Brunswick
Community College (BCC) to obtain ownership of the gym. He stressed doing the
roof and pursuing outside interests, i.e. Duke and ADM to assist with the 5-
year mandate for having the building back in use.
   City Manager McDuffie recommended the city set aside a portion of the
$321,000, with the other portion to be raised via donations.
   Alderman Adams motioned, second by Alderman Poole that the city will budget
$160,000, fundraising will have until December 31, 2016 to get pledges for the
remaining $160,000, the pledges must to be collected by January 31, 2017 and if
the money is not raised, the project will not move forward.
   Alderman Powell stated his concerns about spending the estimated $2.9M on
renovation of the structure when a new building could be built for much less.
   Unanimous vote; motion carried.
4.   Surplus Property
   City Manager McDuffie talked about five (5) city owned properties that could
be surplused and sold:
Residential Building Lot in Boiling Spring Lakes (BSL)
Former Wastewater Treatment Plant Site
Rhett Street 1971 Jail
9th Street Well Site
City Boat Dock
   Noting the former WWTP side is a valuable asset, Alderman Mosteller shared
her hope that the property could be retained as green space.
   Aldermen Powell and Adams suggested testing the market to determine if the
property could bring $2M.
   City Manager McDuffie stated that Preston Development (Southport Marina) may
be approaching the city about the property after they complete a Water
Delineation Study. He suggested not advertising the property for sale.
   1971 Jail
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the 1971 jail is currently being used as
a storage building which is not the best use for the property. He stated the ¼
acre property is a buildable residential parcel in a desirable location.
   Alderman Mosteller favored selling the property as it appeared there was no
apparent municipal use for it.
   Alderman Adams suggested putting it out for lease.
   All Board members thanked the City Manager and Police Chief Smith for moving
the Police Department to the former visitor center at 113 W. Moore Street. It
was pointed out that the general public likes the downtown location and there
is room for expansion.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to list the Boiling
Spring Lakes property and 9th Street well site, with a real estate agent at the
discretion of the City Manager. Unanimous vote, motion carried.
5.   Tourism
   Tourism Director Jones reported that as of July 1, the Historical Society
would be taking over the operation of the Ft. Johnston retail store with all
proceeds going into the maintenance of the building. Mr. Jones noted that the
Tourism budget reflects revenue from a donation box which during the tourist
season averages $700/week, money of which goes into the Ft. Johnston
maintenance fund. Mr. Jones pointed out that the departmental budget went down
over the previous years.
   Responding to a query by Alderman Coring, Mr. Jones stated the Community
Events line item is for ticket sales for the annual Tour of Homes and the
Marketing line item is for printing brochures and maps.
   Mayor Dove asked about potential filming coming to the area. Mr. Jones
reported that he is in contact with location managers from “Six” and “Good
Behavior.”
   Mr. Jones stated that Mr. Strickland and the Building Superintendent are in
the process of installing new security cameras at the entry to Ft. Johnston and
at the restrooms.
6.   Parks & Recreation
   Parks & Recreation Director Hemphill explained her request for a 12
passenger van to be used for smaller group trips and for hauling equipment to
events. She stated that most of the Parks & Recreation budget was contingent on
capital projects, i.e. Lord Street Gym and Boat Dock.
      Community Building
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that a private contractor had been hired
to do 33 cleanings a year at $300/week. He noted that the building looked much
better during the last Board meeting.
   Community Building Coordinator Potter talked about the needed repairs and
maintenance:
Paint and repair interior
Power wash exterior
Sand and apply polyurethane to hard wood floors
Replace warming cabinets
Replace ice machine
Replace deck and deck step LED lights
Replace light fixtures in restrooms
Add electrical outlets in office
Redo walls in storage room with FRP boards
Paint porch ceiling and top of hand rails
   She emphasized the need to power wash and stain the deck and steps to
alleviate wet and slippery conditions from algae build up.
7.   Fire/EMS
   City Manager McDuffie praised Chief Drew for presenting a good solid budget
for the merged Fire and Rescue Department. He noted that the budget was tight
with two (2) full-time employees.
   Chief Drew stated it was a challenge merging the budgets. He stated the
department received nearly $629,000 in fire fees and total revenue of just over
$1M. He indicated that non-emergency transports within the city limits are
being added at $450 a trip. He stated there is one final payment of $84,000 on
the tower truck, and the department is in the process of specing out a tanker/
pumper to replace the 1995 vehicle. Chief Drew pointed out that more Insurance
Services Officer, Inc. (ISO) points can be realized by reclassifying vehicles
as was done with the old ladder truck.
   City Manager McDuffie noted that the shift honorarium line item was
increased in anticipation of increased revenue from transports.\
   Chief Drew stated that $25,000 was budgeted for the substation with $20,000
in reserve. He said it is hoped a substation can be established in the
Rivermist Subdivision area, which could potentially lower the ISO rating to a
2. He added that Pender County had recently put up three (3) substations for
approximately $300,000 and he plans to have a look at them.
   Responding to Alderman Powell, Chief Drew indicated there is $250,000 in the
Fire Department Reserve Fund.
   Mayor Dove thanked the department for lowering the ISO rating.
8.   Police
   City Manager McDuffie stated he is recommending $80,000 for additional
personnel in the Police Department: 1 full-time position July 1 and adding a
12th officer April 1. He stated the hope is to cut overtime to 50 hours per
officer. Also, he stated that Chief Smith wanted to add part-time officers at
$15/hour but that request had been cut from the budget.
   City Manager McDuffie noted that the Police Department has 12 vehicles and
the 2016-2017 budget includes purchase of two (2) vehicles. He stated the Chief
budgeted for an SUV and a car. The City Manager stated his recommendation would
be for either two (2) cars or a car and a truck for animal control.
   Alderman Adams supported purchase of an SUV. He stated his displeasure that
the department closes at 6:00 p.m. He suggested keeping the department open
until 12 midnight.
   City Manager McDuffie discussed the added expense to man the station an
additional 54 hours a week. Chief Smith stated his wish to have the station
open until midnight. He added that the additional hours could be covered by
three (3) new part-time personnel.
   Alderman Poole cautioned that the part-time positions did not evolve into
full-time positions with benefits.
   Closed Session – 12:10 p.m.
Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Powell to go into closed session
pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a) (6) for discussion of personnel issues.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.  
Return to Open Session – 12:33 p.m.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Adams to come out of Closed
Session. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
9.   Public Services
      Electrical
   City Manager McDuffie reported that no electrical rate change is proposed,
additional Load Management switches are included, $800,000 is budgeted for
underground services, and 10% of the Finance Department salaries are being
budgeted in the fund, a reduction from FY 2015/2016.
   Responding to Alderman Powell, Electrical Superintendent Pittenger stated
that there has been increased participation in the Load Management Program. He
added that he approves the proposed electrical budget.
   City Manager McDuffie stated his recommendation to budget $300,000 in the
Water, Sewer and Electric Funds for potential purchase of six to eight acres
for relocation of the Public Services Department. He noted that the
department’s current location has no room for storage or growth.
   Alderman Adams shared his concerns about Brunswick Electric Membership

charges will be reduced.
Lunch: 1:00 p.m.
Return to Session – 1:45 p.m.
   Water
   City Manager McDuffie reported that replacement of the mechanical water
meters with the Automated Metering Infrastructure (AMI) will increase revenue.
He stated 1,200 of the new meters have been installed to date and he cited an
instance where a leak was quickly detected by the reporting equipment. Public
Services Director Fox stated his satisfaction with the proposed water budget.
   Buildings & Grounds
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that two new part-time positions were
requested but that only one position had been included in the budget.
Additionally, he stated a walk behind brush cutter and additional parking at
City Hall was removed from the budget request. Included in the budget is
funding for storm drainage work at the Atlantic Avenue gym and Parks &
Recreation offices, tree maintenance in Northwood Cemetery and a carport at
Public Services to store equipment under.
   Alderman Mosteller emphasized setting aside funding for city wide tree
maintenance and arborist evaluations. She volunteered to make contact with the
NC Cooperative Extension Office at Brunswick County to determine what
assistance they could provide.
   Garage
   City Manager McDuffie stated a request for a new tire mounting machine had
been cut from the budget. Mr. Fox agreed with the cut and the proposed budget.
   Street   
   City Manager McDuffie reported that line item 5500 was cut $10,000, funding
was included to fix Caswell Avenue/Bay Street drainage problems and
installation of a walkway from N. Caswell Avenue to the Senior Center at
Smithville Crossing. The Board discussed funding and specifics of a connector
to WalMart for wheelchairs and golf carts.
   Solid Waste
   City Manager McDuffie commended the Finance Department for finding an
overbilling discrepancy from Waste Industries. He discussed the current 5-year
contract through June 2018, the problems encountered getting Waste Industries
to replace carts. He suggested future consideration of assuming the service in
house, noting he receives more complaints on this service than any other.
Currently there are 96 carts in use. He suggested purchase of a one-man grapple
truck which would be efficient and citizens would not have to bundle. Alderman
Mosteller recommended a cost analysis.
   Powell Bill
   City Manager McDuffie stated the budget included $12,000 for design work and
North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT) approvals of Howe Street
sidewalks/crosswalks from 9th Street to 11th Street.
   Alderman Adams asked about the status of an additional traffic light on N.
Howe Street. City Manager McDuffie stated he was waiting a response from
Senator Rabon.
   The Board discussed the NCDOT Route 211 widening project and what, if any,
impact it would have on the commercial development planned at the recently
annexed 88 acres.
10.   Community Building Rates
   At the request of Alderman Mosteller, the Board discussed a proposed rental
rate change for the Community Building.
   Alderman Poole stated her opinion that the Tourism Department budget had for
many years subsidized the building through taxpayers. She pointed out that the
building used to be rented multiple times a day and not in 12 hour intervals.
   Mayor Dove noted that the building operated in the past without a full-time
employee and was not rented as often which resulted in less utility usage.
   Alderman Mosteller explained that she had put the information provided by
the Community Building Coordinator into a format for clear rate comparison. She
stated her opinion that the proposed rental rates would provide better savings
for citizens and employees than the current rates. She viewed the proposal as
an opportunity to make the building a self-sustaining community asset.
   Aldermen, Coring, Powell and Pukenas stated their support for the operation
of the facility to be self-sustaining.
   Aldermen Adams and Poole stated their opinions that the current and proposed
rates were unaffordable for many Southport citizens.
   Alderman Mosteller motioned, second by Alderman Powell to adopt the rates
effective July 1, 2016.
   Aye:   Aldermen Mosteller, Powell, Coring, Pukenas
   Nay:   Aldermen Adams & Poole
   Motion passed 4-2

BUDGET REVIEW
   City Manager McDuffie provided the Board with a copy of the proposed budget
with the revisions as discussed at the May 14 Budget Workshop. He pointed out
the need for a discussion about funding for roof replacements on the Lord
Street Gym and 201 E. Moore Street, estimated amount $410,000. He stated the
funding could be realized via fund balance, a loan, or property taxes. He
indicated that by removing those capital projects, the budget is $8,250 from
being balanced.
   Powell Bill
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the currently approved paving projects
will encumber the entire $108,000 received in Powell Bill funds. He indicated
the projects may not be completed by the end of the fiscal year but will be by
the end of the calendar year.
   Electric Fund
   City Manager McDuffie stated there were no changes made to the Electric
Fund.
   General Fund – Board
   City Manager McDuffie noted that the Board budget will be the same as FY
2015-2016 with the exception that it is anticipated the audit will cost more.
   General Fund - Administration
   City Manager McDuffie discussed the past practice of leasing copiers. He
stated the fee quoted for FY 2016-17 would be $5,000 for leasing six (6)
copiers which would not include maintenance. He stated he had researched State
Contract pricing and he recommended a $20,000 capital equipment purchase of new
copiers.
   Alderman Adams queried if fewer copiers would be adequate.
   Alderman Poole noted that most desk top printers function as copiers.
   Alderman Coring stated his opinion that copiers have frequent problems and
he did not feel comfortable getting away from a lease.
   Mayor Dove asked about a centralized location. City Manager McDuffie stated
that a centralized location would likely increase cost due to employee travel
time.
   Alderman Adams suggested revisiting the issue after determination is made to
the exact number of copiers needed.
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that the copier expenditure was the only
change in the Administration budget.
   Finance
   City Manager McDuffie discussed a proposed reconfiguration of the City Hall
east lobby for better customer experience and employee safety. He estimated the
redesign of two (2) teller stations would cost approximately $7,000, would
allow for more customer privacy and alleviate the crowding Angie and Rose are
experiencing.
   Alderman Adams stated his opinion he would like to see it remain as it is
and a privacy board installed on the existing counter.
   Finance Director Trexler indicated the current counter is not large enough
for installation of a privacy board.
   Alderman Adams asked for a drawing of what is being proposed.
   Streets
   City Manager McDuffie stated that $20,000 had been added to the Street
budget for installation of a golf cart/bicycle connector between Southport Way
Subdivision and Wal-Mart.
   Police
   City Manager McDuffie indicated money had been added to the budget for part-
time salaries for the additional manning hours of the station and funding for
two (2) vehicles.
   Alderman Adams stated his understanding that a consensus had been made at
the previous budget workshop to purchase an SUV and a car for the Police
Department.
   Board members discussed the pros and cons of a truck vs. an SUV.
   Alderman Adams motioned, second by Alderman Coring to purchase a 2-wheel SUV
and a car for the Police Department.
Ayes: Aldermen Adams, Coring, Poole, Mosteller, Pukenas
Nay:   Alderman Powell
Motion Passed 5-1
   Mayor Dove and Alderman Adams talked about the different functions of the
Police and Fire Departments. They suggested re-examining the role of the Public
Safety Director/Police Chief as the overall department head.
   Planning & Inspections
   City Manager McDuffie reported that Mr. Strickland, the Building Inspector,
would be retiring in March, 2018 with over 20 years with the City. He pointed
out that four (4) months of salary for a full-time building inspector trainee
had been included in the proposed budget to aid in a seamless transition. He
stated that a Level I inspection certification would be required at the time of
hire and acquiring a Level 3 certification in all disciplines within 2 years.
He said the position would be advertised in January or February of 2017.    The
Board discussed the possibility of an employment agreement.
   Responding to a query from Alderman Coring, City Manager McDuffie explained
the $7,500 proposed expenditure for a share of the $21,500 cost for a wide
format printer.
   Street
   City Manager McDuffie explained the proposed 6 foot wide asphalt Maple Leaf
Drive/Wal- Mart connector for wheelchair, bicycle and golf cart access.
   Parks & Recreation
   City Manager McDuffie explained the Parks & Recreation departmental capital
requests:
Van - $31,000
Jaycee Building Roof - $3,000
Lord Street Gym Roof - $320,000
   Community Building
   Aldermen Poole and Adams questioned the $10,000 contract services for
cleaning of the Community Building. The Board emphasized the need for the
bidding process to include local and minority vendors.
   Tourism
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the Tourism Department budget had not
changed from the previous budget workshop. He pointed out the $50,000 entry for
brick pointing and restoration, noting that the funds would be raised through
donations.
   Alderman Poole commented on the improved look of the Garrison with the
recently installed new entry door.
   Electrical
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that the cost of streets lights had been
under budgeted by $63,000. He stated that Brunswick Electric Membership Corp.
(BEMC) had mapped the 600 lights throughout the city and is billing $93,000. He
recommended performing an audit of all lights and accounts to clean up the
discrepancy. He noted that previously the charge was paid to the city.
   Discussion
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that State statutes require a certain
amount of money must be kept in fund balance; the equivalent of one (1) month
operating capital, 8% for the City of Southport. He noted that any money over
that amount is available for emergencies. While he stated the funding of
capital projects proposed in the budget could be realized with fund balance he
instead recommended securing a loan for the 201 E. Moore Street and Lord Street
Gym roof replacements or a tax increase.
   Board consensus to not raise taxes or use fund balance for capital projects.
They discussed the potential sale of various city properties; 9th street
abandoned well site, residential lot in Boiling Spring Lakes, Rhett Street
storage building, former site of the Wastewater Treatment Plant.
   Alderman Adams recommended selling property and securing a loan to fund the
capital projects. City Manager McDuffie reviewed the loan process through a bid
for work in hand, receipt of a bank proposal and approval by the Local
Government Commission (LGC) which takes up to 60 days, delays commencement of
the work and potentially increases the cost.
   Board consensus for departments to further review their budgets and make
additional cuts.
Recess – 8:30 p.m.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to recess the meeting
to Tuesday, May 31, 6:00 p.m. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

AGENDA
5.   Presentation by Owen Garner with Brunswick County Airport Commission
   Mr. Owen Gardner, Southport’s representative on the Brunswick County Airport
Commission since 1988, outlined the background of the Cape Fear Regional
Jetport. He noted that it competes with 82 other airports for FAA funding.
   Mr. Howie Franklin, Director of the State chartered airport for the past 22
years, spoke about the economic impact the airport has on the area. He cited
specifics of past and recent NC State studies performed at the request of NCDOT
Aviation Division: 1995 impact $4M; with initial extension of runway, $21M;
runway extension to 5,005 feet resulted in current impact of $215M.
   Mr. Franklin pointed out that the airport is a fueling stop, is operating in
the black, attracts people from all over the country, sits on 197 acres, is
used by the military, Coast Guard, and could accommodate a C17 in the event of
an emergency. He stated the airport has a low environmental impact, its
maintenance shops are successful and various flight schools and flights are
provided. He added that the airport has one of the state’s largest Civil Air
Patrol (CAP) and a chapter of the Experimental Aircraft Association (EAA).
   Mayor Dove asked if an apprentice program is available for young people. Mr.
Franklin responded that an apprentice program is not currently in place but the
airport commissioners and Brunswick Community College would like to develop a
mechanics school and an air traffic control school. He stated that high school
students work at the airport and he mentors them.
6.   Public Hearing: FY 2016-2017 Operating Budget
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to go into Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   No one from the public spoke.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to close Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
7.   Adopting of FY 2016-2017 Operating Budget
   City Manager McDuffie indicated that the tax rate for the proposed FY 2016-
2017 Operating Budget would stay the same and there is no increase in electric,
water or sewer rates. He pointed out that purchase of one police vehicle was
removed from the police department budget and $13,000 was put into part-time
salaries to facilitate extended operating hours of the police station to 12
midnight. He stated that $10,000 of the vehicle cost was placed in Board
discretionary funds.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Poole to accept the budget.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

There is hereby levied, for fiscal year 2016-2017, a tax at the rate of $0.2456
on each one hundred dollars ($100) of assessed valuation of property located
within the City of Southport for the purpose of raising revenue in the General
Fund.
SECTION V. BUDGET OFFICER AUTHORITY
The city manager (budget officer) is hereby authorized to transfer
appropriations within a fund and between funds under the following terms:
He may transfer amounts between appropriations within the same fund, provided
that a report of such transfers shall be made no later than the next regular
financial report to the Board of Aldermen.
He may authorize temporary transfers of cash among funds as necessary to meet
cash flow needs.
All other transfers of funds between appropriations or budget funds shall be
accomplished by Board amendment of this ordinance.
SECTION VIII. CONTINUING AUTHORIZATION
Prior year Capital Reserve Fund is no longer a restriction of Fund Balance.
Previously-adopted capital project budgets, grant project budgets, and special
reserve funds are hereby un-authorized as all such projects have been completed
and all monies shall be returned to the associated funds upon adoption of the
Budget ordinance.
SECTION IX. BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION
This ordinance and the supporting budget document shall be the basis of the
financial plan for the City of Southport municipal government for the 2016-
2017fiscal year. The budget officer shall administer the budget and shall
insure the finance officer and department heads of the city are provided with
sufficient guidance to properly implement this plan. Copies of the budget
ordinance shall be furnished to the city manager and the finance officer for
their use and direction in the disbursement of funds and to the city clerk for
the official records of the city.
SECTION X. ADOPTION
This ordinance has been adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen in regular
session on June 9, 2016, upon the motion of Alderman Powell and the second of
Alderman Poole, with a vote of 6 ayes and 0 noes, and shall be effective July
1, 2016.

JULY 6, 2016
SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN            SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
FIRE DEPARTMENT HEADQUARTERS JULY 6, 2016
1011 N. HOWE STREET          SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Mayor J.V. Dove
            Aldermen Mary Ellen Poole, Karen Mosteller, Nelson Adams,
            Todd Coring, Rick Pukenas
ABSENT:         Alderman Jim Powell
STAFF PRESENT:      Kerry McDuffie, City Manager
   Michele Windham, City Clerk
   Charles Drew, Fire Chief
   Tyler Johnston, Deputy Chief
   Gary Smith, Police Chief
   Heather Hemphill, Parks & Recreation Director
A)   Call to Order – 4:30 p.m.
Mayor Dove called the meeting to order at 4:30
   Chief Drew gave the invocation.
   Mayor Dove stated the purpose of the special meeting was to discuss a Salary
Study.
   City Manager McDuffie explained that he had been requested by the Board to
do a salary study. He stated he used the 2015 North Carolina League of
Municipalities salary publication of actual salaries paid across the state. He
also worked with the Cape Fear Council of Government (COG) on a regional
average starting salary to draft a study. He indicated he had met with
department heads, received their recommendations and then individually met with
each Board member.
   City Manager McDuffie emphasized the need to do performance evaluations. He
stated that at the request of Alderman Mosteller, he had contacted the MAPS
Group about performing a salary study. The MAPS Group, which works with the
League of Municipalities, indicated the earliest they could work for the City
would be October with the process taking four (4) months. City Manager McDuffie
stated the considerations before the Board are:
   1. Adoption of the salary recommendations as presented by the city manager
and contracting for a salary study in July, 2017
   2. Granting a 1.9% COLA across the board and contracting for a salary study.
   Alderman Adams spoke in opposition to bringing in a company to do a salary
study, contending that an outside company would not know the individual. He
stated his confidence in the city manager to evaluate the employees and bring
the salaries in line as he had accomplished with the Police Department.
   Alderman Pukenas stated his support for an independent review by an outside
company and development of job descriptions.
   Alderman Mosteller talked about the importance of a methodically to the
city’s salary structure and she supported an outside agency. She noted that the
study would be a management tool and she emphasized that an outside agency that
works with the School of Government has the experience and access to in-depth
relevant data across the state.
   Alderman Coring stated his appreciation for the city manager’s work and he
supported a professional salary study. He pointed out that performance
evaluations had not been performed in many years, there seemed to be no
consistency in awarding pay adjustments and having a professional salary study
performed would show the employees a true justice. He noted that because of
health care savings, funding was available for a study.
   Alderman Adams voiced his concerns that too many studies are done that then
sit on a shelf and cannot be implemented. He shared his opinion that a “not in
my job description” attitude could result from the study and undermine the
current successful team effort.
   Mayor Dove recalled performing two (2) salary studies for the police
department during his tenure as chief. He stated his practice was to contact
local departments in order to do position comparisons.
   Alderman Poole emphasized the importance of job descriptions and a plan for
implementation of a study’s recommendations. She pointed out that the city
manager, directors and supervisors would need to work very closely with an
outside agency. She questioned if another company could do a study sooner than
the fall. She emphasized getting a company that understands municipalities. She
stated her position that the employees be given the 1.9% COLA. She explained
that a performance for pay process would require rating levels, performance
appraisal system, levels of performance and mandatory percentage tied with
them.
   City Manager McDuffie spoke about the MAPS Group assisting with performance
evaluations with the most important element being training of all supervisors
on how to do an and evaluation. He stated the MAPS Group would provide a
training course. He reported that department heads would be viewing a
Performance Evaluation Webinar at an upcoming staff meeting.
   Mayor Dove emphasized that many city employees are dedicated to serving the
city and its citizens and he cautioned not taking the human factor out of
evaluations.
   Alderman Coring shared that Brunswick County had contracted a salary study
and had implemented a 4 point system for grading.
   Responding to a concern from Alderman Adams, City Manager McDuffie stated
that no city employee’s salary would decrease from the results of a study.
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to give a 1.9% COLA to
all employees, ask for a professional salary study and the Board commit to
following through with the recommendations.
   Discussion
   Alderman Adams stated he would not vote for the salary study, noting that
many city employees, as shown by the city manager’s pay recommendations, could
not afford to wait seven (7) months.
   City Manager McDuffie answered specific funding questions posed by Alderman
Poole.
   Vote:   Aye:   Aldermen Coring, Pukenas Mosteller
    Nay:   Alderman Adams, Poole
   Motion Carried 3 – 2
Adjourn – 5:11 p.m.
   Alderman Adams motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to adjourn the
meeting. Unanimous vote; motion carried.  
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

   9.   Public Hearing: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment,
Article 2, Section 2-2 (282) Definition of Residential Hotel  
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to go into public
hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Mr. Strickland explained that the amendment proposed by the Planning Board
would reduce the number of rooms permitted for a Residential Hotel to 10.
   Mr. Johnstone contended that a change to the definition alone would not
prohibit a hotel with 70 rooms in other commercial zoning districts.
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Powell to close the public
hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   10.   Consideration of An Ordinance Approving a Text Amendment to the UDO
   City Attorney Isenberg recommended a revision to the following sentence in
the proposed text amendment: Kitchen area separate from the living or sleeping
areas shall may be provided and cooking may be done only in the kitchen area.
Additionally, he pointed out that the word “suites” involves one or more rooms
and he asked if the intent of limiting the residential hotel to ten (10) rooms
should actually be ten rental units.
   Alderman Powell stated his understanding that the Board had agreed to
conduct a review of the UDO prior to making any revisions.
   Noting the proposed amendment was made by the Planning Board and was a stop
gap measure to prevent another residential hotel adjoining residential zoning,
Alderman Mosteller concurred that areas of the UDO did need to be addressed.
   Attorney Isenberg presented an amended Ordinance incorporating four (4)
specific finding.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to adopt An Ordinance
Approving a Text Amendment to the UDO, Article 2, Section 2-2 (282) Definition
of Residential Hotel, incorporating Attorney Isenberg’s wording change, four
specific findings, and limiting the number of total rooms to 10.
Ayes:   Aldermen Poole, Pukenas, Coring, Mosteller
Nay:   Alderman Powell
Motion carried 4-1
AN ORDINANCE APPROVING A TEXT AMENDMENT TO THE UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, City Staff, in conjunction with the Planning Board, has prepared
the attached proposed amendment to Section 2 of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and finds
the proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance to be consistent
with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommend its approval;
and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on July 14, 2016, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby find that this
proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the
Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable
and in the public interest in that (i) this amendment defines “residential
hotel” to be on a smaller scale than a “hotel” so as to protect the property
values of nearby property owners and protect the character of the neighborhood
and secure the public safety, (ii) the UDO already provides for “hotels” within
the City’s jurisdiction in zones more appropriate for larger scale
construction, (iii) it would not be appropriate and in the public interest to
allow larger scale hotels in areas near residential zones and (iv) this
amendment is more consistent with the spirit, purpose and intent of the city’s
CAMA Core Land Use Plan than allowing large scale hotels in the applicable
zones.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment to Section 2 of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This, the 14th day of July, 2016       City of Southport
                     BY: /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
Residential Hotel. A building or group of buildings, limited to a maximum of 10
rooms total, providing lodging for persons, with or without meals, and intended
and used for the accommodation of transient lodgers in suites designed in such
a fashion that reflects the intended use for transient lodgers and not for
permanent residential accommodation. Suites may have one or more rooms in
addition to bathrooms, water closet compartments, laundry, pantry, foyer,
communicating corridor, closets, or any dining alcove. Kitchen area separate
from the living or sleeping areas may be provided and cooking may be done only
in the kitchen area. The definition of residential hotels shall not include
housing units defined in this section, but may include services ordinarily
provided by hotels, such as maid, desk, and laundry services.

10.   Arbor Day Resolution
   Alderman Mosteller read the Arbor Day Resolution into the record:
ARBOR DAY RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, in 1972, J. Sterling Morton proposed to the Nebraska Board of
Agriculture that a special day be set aside for the planting of trees, and
WHEREAS, this holiday called Arbor Day, was first observed with the planting of
more than a million trees in Nebraska, and
WHEREAS, Arbor Day is now observed throughout the nation and the world, and
WHEREAS, trees can reduce the erosion of our precious topsoil by wind and
water, cut heating and cooling costs, moderate the temperature, clean the air,
produce life-giving oxygen, and provide habitat for wildlife, and
WHEREAS, trees are a renewable resource giving us paper, wood for our homes,
fuel for our fires, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees in our city increase property values, enhance the economic
vitality of business areas, and beautify our community, and
WHEREAS, trees wherever they are planted are a source of joy and spiritual
renewal.
NOW, THEREFORE, I J.V. Dove, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC, and the Board
of Aldermen, do hereby proclaim September 9, 2016 as ARBOR DAY in the City and
urge all citizens to celebrate and support efforts to protect our trees and
woodlands, and
FURTHER, I urge all citizens to plant trees to gladden the heart and promote
the well-being of this and future generations.
DATED, this 11th day of August, 2016.
                     /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA
COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK
RESOLUTION TO ESTABLISH A NO-WAKE ZONE IN THE INTRACOASTAL WATERWAY IN
BRUNSWICK COUNTY, NORTH CAROLINA
WHEREAS, the area of the Intracoastal Waterway between Waterway Marker 1A and
Waterway Marker 2A in the area abutting the City of Southport, is an area of
extremely high boating traffic, and includes marinas where vessels are docked
and fueled;
WHEREAS, boating traffic creates hazardous and dangerous conditions in the
above described area, due to boating congestion, appreciable wakes that result
in damage to vessels, fuel spills, and personal injuries due to falls, when
vessels are traveling at speeds substantially above idle speed.
WHEREAS, this has been a long established and recognized problem, resulting in
the North Carolina Legislature in North Carolina Session Law 1993-67, declaring
it unlawful under North Carolina state law to operate a vessel at greater than
a no-wake speed in the Intracoastal Waterway between Waterway Marker 1A and
Waterway Marker 2A in the area abutting the City of Southport.
WHEREAS, subsequent to the enactment of Session Law 1993-67, the United States
Corps of Engineers notified state and local authorities that because the
Intracoastal Waterway was constructed for the purpose of facilitating
commercial boating traffic, and is under the authority of the United States
Corps of Engineers, that the North Carolina State Law is pre-empted by federal
authority.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT NORTH CAROLINA BOARD OF
ALDERMEN THAT:
1.   The governing body of the City of Southport, North Carolina hereby
requests that the United States Corps of Engineers, the United States
Department of Commerce, or such other authority or entity establish such
federal law, United States Code, or Code of Federal Regulations as necessary
that it is unlawful to operate a vessel at greater than a no-wake speed in the
Intracoastal Waterway between Waterway Marker 1A and Waterway Marker 2A in the
area abutting the City of Southport, North Carolina.
2.   Such federal law or regulation authorize enforcement of the above
described no-wake zone by law enforcement personnel of the State of North
Carolina and Brunswick County.
Alderman Powell moved for the adoption of the forgoing resolution.
Alderman Coring seconded the motion and, upon vote, the same was adopted.
This the 8th day of September, 2016.
   /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

9.   Resolution Authorizing Submittal for a Loan and Grant for Construction of
a Wastewater Treatment Plant
   City Manager McDuffie explained to the Board that the city is currently
leasing wastewater capacity from Brunswick County. He stated that staff had met
with the County and the County proposed to sell the city one (1) million
gallons of capacity for $28 million. He said that a cost-analysis for
construction of a wastewater treatment plant on city-owned property near Sunny
Point Military Ocean Terminal was requested from engineering firm Norris &
Tunstall. City Manager McDuffie reported that the cost-analysis showed that the
city could construct a million-gallon-per-day wastewater treatment plant for
$18.3 million which would make construction of a facility the most cost
effective option for the city. He further explained staff’s recommendation to
apply for grants and interest-free loans, as a recent state bond made added
money available, and the city would likely qualify for a zero-percent interest
loan which could potentially save the city upwards to $8 million.
   Responding to a query by Alderman Pukenas, City Manager McDuffie explained
that the state mandated closure of the former wastewater treatment plant. He
talked about the purchase of 430 acres near Sunny Point and the suitability of
the land for a wastewater treatment facility.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to adopt a resolution
authorizing staff to submit an application for a state loan and grant for
construction of a wastewater treatment plant. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
RESOLUTION BY GOVERNING BODY OF APPLICANT
WHEREAS,   The Federal Clean Water Act Amendments of 1987 and the North
Carolina Water Infrastructure Act of 2005 (NCGS 159G) have authorized the
making of loans and grants to aid eligible units of government in financing the
cost of construction of a wastewater treatment works project, and
WHEREAS,   The City of Southport has need for and intends to construct a
wastewater treatment works project described as a new wastewater treatment
plant, and
WHEREAS,   The City of Southport intends to request state loan and grant (if
available) assistance for the project,
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, BY THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT:
That the City of Southport, the Applicant, will arrange financing for all
remaining costs of the project, if approved for a State (loan or grant) award.
That the Applicant will adopt and place into effect on or before completion of
the project a schedule of fees and charges and other available funds which will
provide adequate funds for proper operation, maintenance, and administration of
the system and the repayment of all principal and interest on the debt.
That the governing body of the Applicant agrees to include in the loan
agreement a provision authorizing the State Treasurer, upon failure of the City
of Southport to make scheduled repayment of the loan, to withhold from the City
of Southport any State funds that would otherwise be distributed to the local
government unit in an amount sufficient to pay all sums then due and payable to
the State as a repayment of the loan.
That the Applicant will provide for efficient operation and maintenance of the
project on completion of construction thereof.
That Kerry McDuffie, City Manager, the Authorized Official, and successors so
titled, is hereby authorized to execute and file an application on behalf of
the Applicant with the State of North Carolina for a (loan or grant) to aid in
the construction of the project described above.
That the Authorized Official, and successors so titled, is hereby authorized
and directed to furnish such information as the appropriate State agency may
request in connection with such application or the project: to make the
assurances as contained above; and to execute such other documents as may be
required in connection with the application.
That the Applicant has substantially complied or will substantially comply with
all Federal, State, and local laws, rules, regulations, and ordinances
applicable to the project and to Federal and State grants and loans pertaining
thereto.
Adopted this the 8th day of September, 2016 at Southport, North Carolina.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

WHEREAS,   The Federal Clean Water Act Amendments of 1987 and the North
Carolina Water Infrastructure Act of 2005 (NCGS 159G) have authorized the
making of loans and grants to aid eligible units of government in financing the
cost of a wastewater collection system project, and
WHEREAS,   The City of Southport has need for and intends to complete a
wastewater collection system project described as facilities assessment of the
City’s wastewater collection system to include system mapping, and
WHEREAS,   The City of Southport intends to request state loan and grant (if
available) assistance for the project,
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, BY THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT:
That the City of Southport, the Applicant, will arrange financing for all
remaining costs of the project, if approved for a State (loan or grant) award.
That the Applicant will adopt and place into effect on or before completion of
the project a schedule of fees and charges and other available funds which will
provide adequate funds for proper operation, maintenance, and administration of
the system and the repayment of all principal and interest on the debt.
That the governing body of the Applicant agrees to include in the loan
agreement a provision authorizing the State Treasurer, upon failure of the City
of Southport to make scheduled repayment of the loan, to withhold from the City
of Southport any State funds that would otherwise be distributed to the local
government unit in an amount sufficient to pay all sums then due and payable to
the State as a repayment of the loan.
That the Applicant will provide for efficient operation and maintenance of the
project on completion of construction thereof.
That Kerry McDuffie, City Manager, the Authorized Official, and successors so
titled, is hereby authorized to execute and file an application on behalf of
the Applicant with the State of North Carolina for a (loan or grant) to aid in
the construction of the project described above.
That the Authorized Official, and successors so titled, is hereby authorized
and directed to furnish such information as the appropriate State agency may
request in connection with such application or the project: to make the
assurances as contained above; and to execute such other documents as may be
required in connection with the application.
That the Applicant has substantially complied or will substantially comply with
all Federal, State, and local laws, rules, regulations, and ordinances
applicable to the project and to Federal and State grants and loans pertaining
thereto.
Adopted this the 8th day of September, 2016 at Southport, North Carolina.
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

12.   Presentation by Chad Kimes, NCDOT, 211 Widening
   Mr. Chad Kimes, deputy engineer for Highway Division 3, North Carolina
Department of Transportation (NCDOT) presented an alternate plan for the
widening of N.C. 211 to four lanes as it approaches the city. He stated that
DOT revised the plan at the request of the city to preserve 11 live oak trees
and to lessen the impact on affected businesses. Mr. Kimes stated that the
project would go out for bid in June 2018. He indicated that the revised plan
eliminated a turn lane at the Robert Ruark intersection and would lessen the
level of service expected with the original widening plan. Mr. Kimes stated
that the average daily traffic on N.C. 211 between Southport and Long Beach
Road is 35,000 – 50,000 vehicles and ranks at the top of the division, which
covers six counties.
   Alderman Powell voiced opposition to the plan and the vehicle count. He
emphasized alleviating truck traffic from Howe Street by rerouting an estimated
200 trucks a day to Rob Gandy Boulevard which was built as a truck route to ADM
and Capital Power. Alderman Powell pointed out that Southport’s traffic hold-up
was due to bridges at the Duke Energy Progress canal and Dutchman Creek and he
stressed DOT re-working the bridges. He stated his opinion that the four lanes
should be stopped before reaching the city limits.
   Alderman Adams, noting that the NC 211 widening would address the city’s
future needs, stated he appreciated DOT revising the plan to lessen the impact
on property owners and he felt it was in the city’s best interest to accept the
revised plan.
   Alderman Coring stated his appreciation for the state protecting the trees.
He added that there had been a dramatic drop in the number of wrecks that the
Southport Fire/Rescue Department had responded to since the new road opened at
NC 211 and Long Beach Road.
   Alderman Mosteller expressed concerns about the four lanes extending so far
into the city. She stated she would like to see the road be more pedestrian and
bike friendly.
   Mr. Kimes stated that DOT would need a resolution from the Board in support
of the revised plan or the project would proceed with the original design.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Adams to adopt a resolution to
support the redesign as presented by NCDOT.
Ayes:   Aldermen Poole, Adams, Coring
Nays:   Aldermen Powell, Pukenas, Mosteller
Discussion
   At the request of Alderman Mosteller, City Attorney Isenberg explained that
the consideration before the Board was whether to endorse the original plan
that came further into town and eliminated eleven trees or to favor the
redesign. He pointed out that not voting for the redesign meant that the Board
was in favor of the original plan.
   Mayor Dove called for a show of hands.
   Ayes:   Aldermen Poole, Adams, Coring, Mosteller, Pukenas
   Nay:   Alderman Powell
   Motion Passed 5-1
RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, the North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT) is proposing
to widen NC Highway 211 from Midway Road to 14th Street in Southport; and
WHEREAS, the widening would require the removal of 11 Live Oak Trees on the
entry corridor into Southport; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Board of Aldermen wish to preserve the Live Oak Trees;
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the Mayor and Southport Board of Aldermen
that the City of Southport is in support of the NCDOT redesign to stop the
four-lane project at Robert Ruark Drive.
Adopted this 8th day of September, 2016
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor      
/s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk
13.   East Bay Street Buildable Lot
   Building Inspector Strickland addressed the Board regarding 240 E. Bay
Street and the specific regulations within the Unified Development Ordinance
(UDO) which he must follow to determine if a structure can be built upon a
parcel. He stated that through review of documentation provided by multiple
owners of 240 E. Bay Street, i.e. a survey, he was able to determine that a
structure could be built on the property. Mr. Strickland noted that during his
20 year tenure with the city, he has been through five mayors, five city
managers, six public service directors, 17 aldermen, 12 planners, 18 board of
adjustment members and 46 planning board members. He addressed recent questions
about whether the UDO lacks vision, pointing out that the UDO “is the vision,”
has been continually worked on since its adoption in 2004 and has undergone 48
amendments. He added that the UDO ensured that consistency was maintained
throughout the city. Mr. Strickland addressed claims about transparency noting
that an agenda packet for the planning board is available every month at city
hall, the library and at the State Port Pilot. He encouraged people to get
involved by applying to serve on the planning board and board of adjustment.
Additionally, Mr. Strickland praised the professionalism of city staff and
their genuine care about the city.

AGENDA
   Fire Substation
   Chief Drew advised the Board of the Fire Department’s efforts to find a
suitable location for a substation in the vicinity of Long Beach Road. He
indicated that there is a possibility of property being donated for a
substation in the future; however, in the interim, a building at 4884 Long
Beach Road has been located. Chief Drew stated the property was formerly used
as a car wash and would need minimal modifications to utilize as a substation.
He provided a proposed 2-year lease with two (2) one-year extensions for $1,200
a month beginning October 1. He said the property owner would be responsible
for paying property taxes and the fire department would be responsible for
building liability insurance and maintenance of the lot. He reported that the
Fire Insurance Service Office (ISO) wants a substation within 1.5 miles of fire
headquarters. He stated that the fire department budget had $20,000 that had
been appropriated towards a substation and would cover the rental fee and
needed modifications. Chief Drew asked the Board for endorsement of the lease.
   Alderman Powell asked about the percentage of activity that the fire
department responds to in the area of the proposed substation. Chief Drew
stated his estimate is 50%.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Poole to accept the lease of
the building as a fire/rescue substation upon review of the lease by the city
attorney. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Lord Street Gym
   Mr. Donnie Joyner, chair of the Lord Street Gym Committee, updated the Board
on the status to raise $160,000 towards putting a roof on the historic
building. He stated that pledges were coming in and he would have an accurate
account by the next regular Board meeting. He expressed his confidence that the
goal would be met. Mr. Joyner indicated that several churches were involved in
collecting pledges and he was also soliciting pledges from members of the
Brunswick County Training School Alumni. He explained that promoting the
facility as a civic center would garner more interest, along with naming it in
tribute to Harry O’rie Gore, veteran, educator and prominent figure in
Southport history. Mr. Joyner stated it is planned to establish a 501c3
organization to continue the renovation project.
   201 E. Moore Street
   City Manager McDuffie reported that Engineer Phil Norris was working on the
design for the replacement of the roof on the 201 E. Moore Street building. He
indicated that staff would like feedback from the Board on the projected use of
the building. He stated that ElectriCities has offered to do a proposal on the
building for a public/private partnership which would require a long term
lease.
   With the absence of two aldermen and the importance of the project, Alderman
Poole and Powell recommended scheduling a workshop.
   The city manager was directed to obtain a timeline for the roofing aspect of
the project.
   Waterfront
   City Planner Lloyd reported that the Duke Energy Water Resource Fund Program
has grant awards ranging from $10,000 - $100,000 available which, if awarded to
the City could be used for engineer designed plans for the shoreline
stabilization portion of the waterfront project. He stated that Duke Energy is
accepting only 50 letters of intent, to be narrowed to 30 by December 1 for an
invitation to submit a full proposal. Mr. Lloyd indicated that he had also been
in contact with the U.S. Army Corps. of Engineers who responded they would make
a site visit and determine how they could assist the city on the project.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Powell to proceed with the
letter of intent with Duke Energy and to work with the Corps. of Engineers.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
