SEPTEMBER 22, 2016
RECESSED MEETING MINUTES
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN   RECESSED MEETING MINUTES
1011 N. HOWE STREET SEPTEMBER 22, 2016
SOUTHPORT, N.C.      
 
PRESENT:         Mayor J.V. Dove
            Aldermen Mary Ellen Poole, Karen Mosteller, Rick Pukenas,
            Todd Coring, Jim Powell
ABSENT:         Alderman Nelson Adams            
STAFF PRESENT:      Kerry McDuffie, City Manager   
         Michele Windham, City Clerk
Call to Order – 5:30 p.m.
Mayor Dove called the meeting back to order at 5:30 p.m.
AGENDA
   NCDOT – 211 Widening
   Mr. Chad Kimes, deputy engineer with NC Department of Transportation’s
Highway Division 3, presented a modified plan of the NC 211 widening. DOT
representatives accompanying Mr. Kimes displayed a map of the modified plan
which changed the shoulder feature to a curb and gutter section which lessens
the impact to businesses in the area. Mr. Kimes said that because of the curb
and gutter section it would allow for five foot wide sidewalks from Robert
Ruark Drive/NC 87 to the northern most entrance to Walmart. Mr. Kimes stated
that in order to include the sidewalks, DOT would require a cost share of 20%
from the city, estimated at $25,000. He stated that the project has an expected
bid date of June 2018 at which time DOT would need the cost share for the
sidewalks from the city.
   City Manager McDuffie inquired if sidewalks could be continued to 9th Street
to tie into existing sidewalks. Mr. Kimes responded that additional sidewalks
would be outside the project limits and the right of way had not been purchased
to continue the sidewalks beyond Robert Ruark Drive/NC 87.
   Alderman Powell inquired about where water would run for the curb and gutter
section. Acknowledging that the area had drainage issues, Mr. Kimes assured the
Board that improvements would be made.
   Responding to a question from the city manager, Mr. Kimes stated that
putting crosswalks with actuator buttons at the stoplights would be considered.
   Board consensus to submit a letter of commitment for the cost share
($25,000) for the sidewalks.
   Alderman Mosteller asked if there would be shoulders for bikes. Mr. Kimes
stated that the project will have four to five foot shoulders and he will be
asking other DOT units about bike lanes. He added that at a minimum, Share the
Road signs could be posted and at the most, symbols on the roadway. He noted
that there is a lot of engineering that goes into it and dependent on the
number of turn lanes.
   NCDOT – Long Beach Road
   Responding to a request from City Manager McDuffie as to the status of the
proposed interchange at NC 211 and the Long Beach Road, Mr. Kimes, discussed
the design for the project. Mr. Kimes cited a 20-year traffic forecast that
indicates as many as 50,000 vehicles daily will pass through the intersection.
He told the Board that an intersection with that volume triggers NCDOT to look
at an interchange. Mr. Kimes displayed the chosen design noting that 15 to 20
acres of high ground on the NW corner of the intersection would be needed. He
noted the addition to the current intersection of an off-ramp towards St. James
and a critical free-flow ramp to Oak Island.
   Mayor Dove remarked that the area of the planned overpass is within the city
limits and a proposed commercial development.
   Mr. Kimes stated that meetings had been held with Mr. Rick Rowe, Wakefield
Associates, developer of the Southport Crossing retail center and
Representative Frank Iler. Mr. Kimes indicated that meetings would continue
with Mr. Rowe who had also brought in an engineer to look at possibilities.
   Alderman Powell pointed out that 15 to 20 acres for an interchange would
seriously impact the proposed commercial development. He questioned if the
interchange could be located on the SE corner of the intersection with a
potential relocation of businesses in the Live Oak Plaza. Mr. Kimes responded
that the SE corner was on the wrong side of the road, DOT was trying to stay
away from existing businesses, construction would be less disruptive to traffic
with the chosen location and it was a cheaper land wise option. Alderman
Powell, noting the design of the diamond interchange in Leland, encouraged
rethinking the design for another way to make it work.
   City Manager McDuffie asked about a possible “flower” structure with an
elevated road which would require less land, equating to a savings on the
purchase of right of way. Mr. Kimes stated that the flower structure would
present constructability issues along with being more expensive.
   Alderman Coring asked if enough time had passed to judge the impact of the
recently completed Long Beach Road extension. He expressed concern about the
significant impact the interchange will have on the commercial development and
Southport and confusion about the research showing 50,000 cars daily. He
questioned where support for the project came from and pointed out that the
announcement about the interchange was made at a St. James meeting. Mr. Kimes
explained that funding became available, a local Council of Mayors supported
the project and it was purely a coincidence that the announcement was made at
St. James.
   Responding to a query from City Manager McDuffie, Mr. Kimes, noting that the
design had been chosen just the day before, September 21, and he indicated that
the Division design team had approved the interchange design based on impacts,
traffic count projections and benefits vs. cost.
   Alderman Powell emphasized the need for truck route signs on NC 211 to
reroute trucks across the Long Beach Road Extension to NC 87 and Rob Gandy
Boulevard. It was noted that the County GIS mapping needed to be updated. Mr.
Kimes stated that a member of his team would follow up on Alderman Powell’s
request.   
   Other
   At the request of the City Manager, Mr. Kimes updated the Board on drainage
issues in the 1100 block of E. Moore Street and a dip in the 300 block of Howe
Street.
   Mayor Dove and the City Manager asked about the process for adding
crosswalks at Howe and West Streets and Moore and Davis Streets. Ms. Leonard
stated that a municipality submits a request to DOT and a site visit is made.
She indicated that the cost is absorbed by the municipality and each crosswalk
is typically $2,500 each. She said that she would provide an estimate for the
locations.
   Board consensus to pursue crosswalks at Howe and West Streets and Moore and
Davis Streets.
   City Manager McDuffie announced that Brunswick Electric Membership Corp.
(BEMC) accidentally notified 483 city electric customers that they were invited
to the upcoming BEMC membership meeting. He pointed out that city electric
customers are not considered members per the city’s agreement with BEMC. BEMC
was contacting each customer.
   City Manager McDuffie announced that he and Public Works Director David Fox
are scheduled to meet in Raleigh with the NC Division of Water Quality (DWQ)
regarding a loan for construction of a wastewater treatment plant.
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the MAPS Group had completed interviews
of all city employees. He provided a listing of communities the Maps Group will
use to make comparisons which included Leland and Brunswick County. He pointed
out that Southport has lost employees to both Leland and Brunswick County.
   Mayor Dove announced that the 7th Annual Wooden Boat Show would be held
Saturday, September 24th.
   Mayor Dove announced that the Mt. Carmel AME Church would be celebrating 126
years of service on Sunday, September 25, 4:00 p.m.
   Mayor Dove thanked Beautification Committee chair Shirley Snyder for the
committee’s continued efforts and recent clean-up at the Waterfront.
   Alderman Poole thanked the Board for voting for the new substation location.
She indicated that the Emergency Services Committee had endorsed it as well.
She noted that the combined fire/rescue operations were working well together
as one entity.   
Recess – 6:30 p.m.
   Alderman Mosteller motioned, second by Alderman Coring to recess the meeting
to Wednesday, September 28, 2016, 5:30 p.m. in the Fire Department EOC, 1011 N.
Howe Street. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

12.   Use of 1029 Building
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the N.C. Department of Motor Vehicles

temporarily operate Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of the first week of the
month at Fire Headquarters.
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that Wells Fargo will be vacating the
second floor of City Hall and he suggested providing DMV permanent space on the
first floor, move Administration and Inspections to the second floor and
reconfigure Finance to allow for better use. He indicated that $50,000 remained
in the budget from a land purchase allocation and could be used to do
improvements needed to move offices and to purchase furniture.
   Alderman Coring, noting that the Police Department was originally planned to
be strategically located in the 1029 building, asked to look at the original
floor plan. He stated his opinion that the current police station at 113 W.
Moore Street would be a better location for CMV and an after-hours dispatch.
   Aldermen Adams and Powell agreed with Alderman Coring with Alderman Adams
recalling a building committee had been in place when the building was
purchased and he suggested a workshop.
   Aldermen Coring and Powell expressed concerns about DMV using fire
headquarters and interfering with emergency response personnel.
   City Manager McDuffie explained the connectivity difficulty of the CMF’s
equipment at the Nash Street substation. Board consensus to work towards
boosting the signal at the substation and, if unable, to relocate DMV to the
Parks and Recreation Department building on Fodale Avenue, and to schedule a
workshop at their October meeting to discuss options for the 1029 building.
13.   Fuel Needs
   The Board discussed fuel options such as providing generators to gas
stations with Southport electric service in order to provide fuel for the city
and citizens during an electrical outage. City Manager McDuffie pointed out
that Load Management would pay for the cost of generators. Advantage and
disadvantages of the city having its own fuel tanks was discussed. Alderman
Adams endorsed the city having fuel tanks and being independent. He cautioned
against providing generators to service stations. Mayor Dove pointed out that
the city removed the fuel tanks because they were leaking and were no longer
permitted underground.
Break – 6:53 p.m.
14.   Mosquito Spraying
   City Manager McDuffie advised that mosquito spraying will be performed in
the evenings in addition to the morning spraying.
15.   Credit Card Processing for Utility Bills
   City Manager McDuffie updated the Board on the processing of credit card
payments through provided CivicPay. He stated credit cards would be interacting
with the city’s software in real time which would save approximately 10 hours
of employee time a month for doing manual entry. City Manager McDuffie
discussed staff’s efforts to encourage the no cost ACH transfers to reduce the
$2.40 per transaction fee for credit card payments. He stated 580 ACH transfers
are currently in place. He added that the city does not accept American Express
or Discover. He stated that the city is currently paying $21,000 a year in
credit card bills or 1% of everyone’s utility bill. He reported that a voice
interactive phone service will also be implemented for credit card payments.
16.   Rope at Garrison
   Tourism Director Jones reported that staff, Beautification Committee,
Forestry Committee, Garden Club, Downtown Southport Inc. (DSI) and the
Historical Society were putting together standards and practices using
information contained in city adopted plans for the Board to review. He
indicated that Joe Medlin is working with the Parks and Recreation Director for
remaking the tops on the poles holding the rope at the Garrison.
17.   AMI
   City Manager McDuffie reported that all the new water meters are installed.
He stated he would be sending Board members information to interface with their
meters. He said customers, especially absentee homeowners, would benefit from
the new system that allows real time monitoring of water usage.
18.   Schedule Workshop for 201 Building
   City Manager McDuffie reported that it is expected that the proposals will
go out on the roofing project of the 201 building at the end of October with a
potential contract award date in December. He stated that construction time is
anticipated to be 90 days. Board consensus to schedule a workshop when the
roofing project is closer to completion.
19.   Other
   Alderman Poole requested an update on the status of the sale of property on
9th street (abandoned well site) and in Boiling Spring Lakes at the Board’s
October meeting.
   Mayor Dove announced that the annual Captain Charlies Kids’ Fishing
Tournament would be held Saturday, October 1, 9:00 – 12:00.
   City Manager McDuffie announced that Piedmont gas has run a gas line to the
City Hall generator. He stated that the tie in to the gas main trunk line and
connection to the generator should be made within a week.
   Tourism Director Jones announced that the Beautification Committee would
have a clean-up on Saturday, October 1.          
Recess – 7:20 p.m.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to adjourn the meeting.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.  
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

RESOLUTION
HONORING CECIL RHODES
ON HIS RETIREMENT
WHEREAS, Cecil Rhodes started his employment with ElectriCities in February
1987; and
WHEREAS, since joining ElectriCities, Mr. Rhodes has played many important
roles in making public power in North Carolina a monumental success; and
WHEREAS, Mr. Rhodes has set an example of dedication to principle which has
been an inspiration to his fellow employees; and
WHEREAS, Mr. Rhodes has served as North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency
Vice President for the past ten years; and
WHEREAS, Mr. Rhodes’ leadership has spanned from holding the position of
Supervisor of Load Management Operations, Manager of Power Operations, NCEMPA
Division Director and Vice President of NCEMPA; and
WHEREAS, his years of service have been marked by exemplary dedication to the
best interests of our community; and
WHEREAS, he was instrumental in establishing the Load Management Program for
the City of Southport; and
WHEREAS, Mr. Rhodes assisted city staff with refurbishing the EMS Substation to
the useful building that it is now; and
WHEREAS, he helped the City of Southport secure a contract with Brunswick
Electric Membership Corporation that will not only benefit the City but also
the residents of Southport; and
WHEREAS, Mr. Rhodes has aided the City of Southport in a number of projects
over the years, his knowledge has been immeasurable for the success of numerous
endeavors; and
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Mayor and the Board of Aldermen wish to
express their gratitude for all the assistance and friendship Mr. Cecil Rhodes
has shown the City of Southport over his 30 year working career with
ElectriCities.
Adopted this 13th day of October 2016.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Gayle A. Jones, Deputy Clerk

Resolution
Proclaiming October 9 - 15, 2016
Fire Prevention Week
WHEREAS, the Southport Fire Department is committed to ensuring the safety and
security of all those living in and visiting our Fire District; and
WHEREAS, fire is a serious public safety concern both locally and nationally,
and homes are the locations where people are at the greatest risk of fire; and
WHEREAS, the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) has documented through
its research a significant increase in home fires, and due to this fact, it is
important that everyone know two ways out of your home in case of a fire; and
WHEREAS, the Firefighters of the Southport Fire Department are dedicated to
reducing the occurrence of residential and commercial structural fires and fire
related injuries through prevention and protection education; and
WHEREAS, the residents of the Southport Fire District are responsive to public
education measures and are able to take personal steps to increase their safety
from fire; and
WHEREAS, being prepared in the event of a home fire will have a positive effect
on the home fire problem; and
WHEREAS, each home fire that is prevented in the Southport Fire District is an
opportunity to prevent painful injury and costly property damage; and
WHEREAS, the 2016 Fire Prevention Week theme, Don’t Wait Check the Date –
Replace Smoke Alarms every 10 years, effectively serves to remind us all of the
simple actions we can take to stay safer from fire every day.
THEREFORE, I Jerry V. Dove, Mayor of the City of Southport do hereby proclaim
October 9-15, 2016 as Fire Prevention Week throughout this City, and I urge all
the citizens of Southport to heed the important safety messages from the
Southport Fire Prevention Team, and the Office of the City Fire Marshal and to
support the many public safety activities and efforts of the Southport Fire
Department.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

AGENDA
   1029 N. Howe Street
   Noting that the request to review the original floor plan for the 1029 N.
Howe Street building had been brought up in a previous Board workshop, City
Manager McDuffie stated his concerns about implementing the layout after Wells
Fargo vacates the second floor at the end of the year. He pointed out that in
three (3) years the city’s population had grown from 2,800 to 3,304 and, as
evidenced by the current construction projects, population will continue to
grow resulting in an increase of city staff. He noted that the original plan
did not allow for growth or expansion. Additionally, he expressed concerns
about locating the utility billing collections function on the second floor.
   Alderman Adams, member of the original building committee for the 1029
building, stated his opinion that city operations are currently flowing well
and it would not be appropriate to service the general public from the second
floor. He stated his position that it was not the proper time to take on
another project in the midst of current projects. He suggested consideration of
utilizing the second floor at budget time.
   Board members concurred that the city is involved in many costly projects in
addition to recent property damage from Hurricane Matthew.
   Alderman Pukenas stated his opinion that relocating the Finance Department
to the second floor would be a disadvantage for the elderly.
   Agreeing with Alderman Adams, Alderman Powell emphasized determining what
direction to take on the 201 E. Moore Street building and to move slowly on
relocating city departments to the second floor of the 1029 N. Howe Street
building.
   Alderman Coring agreed that moving the Finance Department to the second
floor would not be in the best interest of customers. He suggested relocating
the Building Inspections & Planning Department to the second floor in order to
keep Finance on the first floor and to move the Police Department to the
building. He discussed the time and effort that went into developing the floor
plan at the time of purchase of the building.
   Alderman Mosteller agreed with all comments and favored taking time to
determine the best use of the second floor.
   Mayor Dove concurred with all that the Finance Department not be relocated
to the second floor. He stated his opinion that he prefers the Police
Department remain in downtown, he shared comments he has heard from citizens
supporting the Police Department being downtown and he speculated about adding
on to the building. He talked about the possibility of having a Fire/Rescue/
Police substation in the Long Beach Road area and stated his opinion that at
some point the city would need to be divided into precincts.
   Alderman Powell stated he had heard positive remarks from the neighbors of
the Moore Street Police Department.
   City Manager McDuffie pointed out that the W. Moore Street location of the
Police Department was intended to be a temporary location.
   City Manager McDuffie stated that after the second floor of 1029 is vacated,
he would bring information to the Board about what would be needed for a
conference room and an office for the Mayor.
   Alderman Poole pointed out that the former jail on Rhett Street is being
used for storage. She emphasized relocation of the stored items and listing the
property for sale and using the proceeds for pending projects.
   Mayor Dove asked about the status of the lot in Boiling Spring Lakes. City
Manager McDuffie responded that he planned to accept proposals from local real
estate agents for listing that lot and the 9th Street property.
   201 E. Moore Street
   Responding to a query by Alderman Pukenas, City Manager McDuffie reported
that Norris & Tunstall Consulting Engineers are nearing completion of the plans
and specifications for the roof replacement of 201 E. Moore Street. He stated
that bids would be let by December and construction should be completed by
March.
   Alderman Adams stated he had recently been in the 201 E. Moore Street
building and noticed a large amount of stored files. Remarking that the records
pose a fire hazard, he emphasized disposing of the records. City Manager
McDuffie pointed out that due to a recent public records request, records
dating back 10 years must be retained.
   Stating that if a decision is made not to move the Police Department to the
1029 building, Alderman Coring advocated moving the Police Department back into
the 201 E. Moore Street building after it is renovated.
   Alderman Mosteller talked about the public meeting regarding the old City
Hall and her perception that a task force would be established to develop
criteria for proposals.
   Alderman Adams emphasized the Board’s responsibility to make the tough
decisions.
   Mayor Dove, stating he had met with potential businesses considering the
building, and he remarked that the building is not suitable for retail sales.
   Storm Damage
   City Manager McDuffie reported that estimates for repair to damages at the
waterfront ranged from $200,000 - $300,000. He stated that FEMA had declared
disaster category A (storm debris removal) and category B (storm preplanning)
for disaster assistance. He said it is expected that FEMA will declare
additional categories which would include the waterfront. He indicated that
shoreline stabilization is moving forward on the damage to E. Bay Street, an
engineer assessment of the city pier is being obtained and to date, one quote
has been received for repairs of the waterfront bulkhead and the city boat
dock.
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Poole to contact the district
office of the Coast Guard to request declaration of a lower speed for boat
traffic on the river in view of hurricane damage to the bulkhead. Unanimous
vote; motion carried.
Board Comments
   Mayor Dove announced that the annual Warrior Ride would be held Wednesday,
October 19, 10:00 a.m. at the Waterfront.
Adjourn – 6:10 p.m.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to adjourn the meeting.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

   3.   Resolution in Opposition of NCDOT Interchange at NC 211 and Long Beach

Alderman Coring read into the record the Resolution in Opposition of NCDOT
Interchange at NC 211 and Long Beach Road Extension.
[Image]
RESOLUTION IN OPPOSITION OF NCDOT PROPOSED INTERCHANGE AT NC 211 AND LONG BEACH
ROAD EXTENSION
WHEREAS, On September 22, 2016, the North Carolina Department of
Transportation, Division 3, presented to the Southport Board of Aldermen a
proposal for planned improvements at the NC 211 and Long Beach Road Extension;
and
WHEREAS, the majority of the area for the proposed interchange will fall within
property voluntarily annexed into the City of Southport September, 2014; and
WHEREAS, the Aldermen of the City of Southport recognize that Southport’s
economic survival depends on continued development; and
WHEREAS, the Aldermen believe that the plan presented September 22, 2016 is not
the best plan for the economic prosperity and transportation needs of the City
of Southport
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, the Aldermen of the City of Southport are in
opposition to the proposed design of the interchange at NC 211 and Long Beach
Road Extension.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to adopt the Resolution.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   4.   Consideration of Painting Franklin Square Gallery
   City Manager McDuffie explained that the Associated Artists of Southport had
requested the exterior of Franklin Square Gallery be painted during the winter
closing of the gallery, December 18 through February 16. He said that the
building was in need of repairs to the wood siding and painting but funds had
not been allocated in the current year’s budget. He stated an estimate of
$25,000 had been obtained and funds would have to be used from fund balance to
proceed with the project. He pointed out that the lease of the building would
expire the end of December, 2017 and the lease stipulated that the city was
responsible for upkeep of the exterior of the building.
   Alderman Adams suggested consideration of the project during budget review.
   Alderman Mosteller asked about the condition of the wood. Public Works
Director Fox responded that the Facilities Maintenance Coordinator had spoken
to contractors and the wood damage repair would not entail total replacement.
   Board consensus to evaluate the project during budget consideration.
   City Manager McDuffie to look into the urgency of repairs and report back to
the Board if warranted.

   7.   Tree Trimming
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the Fire Department had brought it to
his attention that tree limbs throughout the city are below the 14 ft. required
height above the street surface to allow for safe passage of trucks and
emergency vehicles. He stated that the Forestry Committee had been apprised of
the situation, the trimming was advertised in the local newspaper and a
contractor with decades of experience was scheduled to begin trimming November
14 at a cost of $5,400 for four (4) days’ work. He added that Alderman
Mosteller had requested use of a certified arborist. City Manager McDuffie
requested direction from the Board.
   Alderman Adams questioned if the contractor had been used before and if any
problems had been experienced with the company. City Manager McDuffie replied
that the contractor had been used for tree trimming by the city on several
occasions and no problems had occurred.
   Responding to Alderman Adams query, City Manager McDuffie stated that the
last arborist used by the City, charged $2,800 a day for a full crew.
   Aldermen Adams and Poole cautioned against incurring the additional expense
for an arborist.
   Alderman Mosteller, referring to a map depicting the area in which trimming
needs to be done, pointed out that some of the trimming would be severe cutting
of leader branches which could jeopardize the health of the tree if incorrectly
cut. She spoke about the monetary value of the trees and stressed erroring on
the side of caution.
   Alderman Coring noted that money had been budgeted for an arborist and the
city would not be doing its due diligence to protect the trees if an arborist
was not consulted. He suggested having an arborist view the trees and provide a
recommendation.
   Alderman Pukenas questioned if, in the future, an arborist could be under
contract to the city. City Manager McDuffie stated an arborist could be put on
retainer. Additionally, he stated there is a possibility that someone on staff
could be trained as a certified arborist.
   There was no objection from the Board for the City Manager to retain a
certified arborist to ride the tree trimming route with the Public Works
Director and for the arborist to provide the Director with guidance and
information on where and how to trim the trees.   
   8.   Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for consideration
of a personnel matter.
Closed Session – 6:53 p.m.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to go into Closed
Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for consideration of a personnel
matter. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Out of Closed Session – 7:15 p.m.
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to come out of Closed
Session. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Board Comments

efforts performed by city staff.

   City Manager McDuffie reported that funds originally budgeted for contracted

AN ORDINANCE APPROVING TEXT AMENDMENTS TO THE UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, City Staff, in conjunction with the Planning Board, has prepared
proposed amendments to Article 2 and Article 10 of the Southport Unified
Development Ordinance; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and find
the proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance to be consistent
with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommend their
approval; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on December 8, 2016, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby find that these
proposed amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance are consistent with
the Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that these amendments are
reasonable and in the public interest because they will create standards and
put rules in place for portable storage containers. This directly aligns with
one of the City’s Core Values of the 2014 CAMA Core Land Use Plan, to “preserve
the city’s residential areas.” Without regulation, portable storage containers
could change the character of residential neighborhoods and hurt property
values. Furthermore, an absence of standards for public storage containers
could become a safety issue if they were used as habitable structures.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendments to Articles 2 and 10 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance are hereby approved and adopted.
This, the 8th day of December, 2016.      City of Southport
                     BY: /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk      
AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
TEXT AMENDMENT # 16-0824-01
AMEND BY ADDITION:
1) ARTICLE 2: BASIC DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS   
Section 2-2 “Definitions of Basic Terms” is hereby amended by adding the
following definition in alphabetical sequence:
Portable Storage Containers: A container designed to store personal property
which are typically rented and intended to be delivered and removed by truck.
Portable storage containers shall not be used as a dwelling and shall not
impede public vehicular or pedestrian access or create a public safety hazard.
This definition includes shipping containers and other portable self-storage
units.
   (a)   Temporary. A portable storage container that is used for less than a
year.
(b)   Permanent. A portable storage container for commercial use.
2) ARTICLE 10: TABLE OF PERMITTED USES
Section 10-1 “Notes to the Table of Permitted Uses” is here by amended by
adding the following as Note 16.
Note 16. Portable Storage Containers. Portable storage containers are permitted
when the following conditions are met:
   (1)    A temporary portable storage container may be placed for thirty (30)
or less consecutive days in any twelve month period without issuance of a
permit in all zoning districts upon notification of the Building Inspector.
   (2)    Temporary portable storage containers being used for over thirty (30)
days shall apply for and obtain a permit from the Building Inspector. A maximum
of one (1) portable storage container shall be allowed per lot in residential
areas for up to a twelve (12) month period if the following conditions are met:
(a)   The principal structure is damaged and is undergoing repairs,
constructions, reconstruction, or renovation.
      (b)   A building permit has been issued for the repairs, constructions,
reconstruction, or renovation, if required, and is valid.
      (c)   After a twelve (12) month period, an extension may be granted for
up to thirty (30) additional days as approved by the Building Inspector.
      (d)   Temporary portable storage containers used by developers for
construction of a subdivision shall renew their permit with the Building
Inspector every twelve (12) months. Portable storage containers must be removed
upon completion of the subdivision.
   (3)   Permanent portable storage containers may be permitted for commercial
use as storage. Permanent portable storage containers may be permitted in the
business, highway commercial, light industrial, and heavy commercial districts
per approval of the Building Inspector. Permanent portable storage containers
shall submit a site plan for review by the Building Inspector.
   (4)   Permanent portable storage containers in commercial areas shall be
screened from view of any public right-of-way, private street or access
easements and any residential use or residential zoning district. Screening
shall be accomplished by a combination of fencing or landscaping, which is
contiguous and at least 1 foot higher than the height of the container.
Screening plans shall be included in the site plan submitted to the Building
Inspector for review.
   (5)   Permanent portable storage containers shall not be permitted as
accessory structures or habitable structures in residential districts.   
   (6)   Portable storage containers shall not be located in an area that
displaces required parking standards.
   (7)   Setback requirements for portable storage containers shall be the same
as setback requirements for accessory structures in their respective zoning
districts according to Article 11 of the Unified Development Ordinance.
   (8)   Portable storage containers shall meet the following appearance
standards:
      (a)   Portable storage containers shall not exceed the dimensions of
forty (40) feet in length, eight (8) feet in width and ten (10) feet in height.
Stacking of portable storage containers shall not be permitted
      (b)   No sign shall be attached to a portable storage container other
than the provider’s contact information.
      (c)    The structure of a portable storage container shall be maintained
in good condition free from structural damage, rust and deterioration.
   (9)   All portable storage containers located in the City of Southport and
its
      Extraterritorial jurisdiction prior to this text amendment which do not
comply with the terms hereof shall be designated as non-conforming and shall be
removed or brought into compliance with the terms hereof within twelve (12)
months from the date of approval of this ordinance.
7.   Set dates for January workshops

two (2) workshops, one for departmental feedback for preparation of the FY

CITY OF SOUTHPORT
RESOLUTION REQUESTING SUPPORT OF A PREPARED MEALS TAX
WHEREAS, the City of Southport waterfront is in need of improvements that will
require significant infrastructure expenditure; and
WHEREAS, people from many areas come to enjoy the Southport waterfront; and
WHEREAS, all individuals who enjoy the waterfront should participate in the
needed infrastructure improvements instead of only being funded from taxes of
property owners; and
NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved, that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
request the NC General Assembly to establish a Prepared Meals Tax of one-half
percent (0.5%) and dedicate the funds to infrastructure in Southport.
This the 12th day of January, 2017            By: /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

AMENDMENT TO CITY OF SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
TEXT AMENDMENT # 16-1208-01
An Ordinance Amending the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance, With
Respect to the Basic Definitions and Interpretations and the Table of Permitted
Uses
AMEND BY ADDITION:
1) ARTICLE 2: BASIC DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS
Section 2-2 “Definitions of Basic Terms” is hereby amended by modifying the
following definition in alphabetical sequence:
(112) Family Care Home. An adult care home having two to six residents. The
structure of a family care home may be no more than two stories high and none
of the aged or physically disabled persons being served there may be housed in
the upper without provision for two direct exterior ground level accesses to
the upper story. A home licensed pursuant to G.S. 131D, Article 1 or G.S
Chapter 122C, Article 2 for adults and children with support and supervisory
personnel that provides room and board, personal care, and habilitation
services in a family environment for not more than six (6) resident handicapped
persons as defined in G.S 168-21. Handicapped persons are defined as such
persons that have a temporary or permanent physical, emotional, or mental
disability including but not limited to mental retardation, cerebral palsy,
epilepsy, autism, hearing or sight impairments. This does not include mentally
ill persons who are dangerous to others as defined in NC G.S 122C-3 (11) (b).
2) ARTICLE 10: TABLE OF PERMITTED USES
Section 10-1 “Notes to the Table of Permitted Uses” is here by amended by
adding the following as Note 17.
Note 17. Family Care Homes.
   (A)   A proposed family care home or group home shall be located no closer
than a one-half mile radius from any existing permitted family care home or
group home within any zoning district whether contiguous or not.
   (B)   With respect to the distance between the proposed use and the
existing, permitted uses described in subsection (a) above, the distance shall
be measured by following a straight line from the nearest point of the lot line
of the proposed use to the nearest point of the lot line of the lot on which
the existing facility is located.    
   (C)   The Board of Adjustments may grant a variance from the separation
requirement if shown to be a reasonable accommodation under the Fair Housing
Act.
   (D)   The structure of a family care home may be no more than two stories
high and none of the aged or physically disabled persons being served there may
be housed in the upper story without provision for two direct exterior ground
level accesses to the upper story.

11.   Consideration of Acceptance of right-of-way
   City Planner Lloyd reported that Mr. Michael Bellany had approached city
staff about donating a portion of the Hankinsville Road entrance off 9th
Street, in the form of a 20 foot easement. Mr. Bellamy expressed to Mr. Lloyd
that he thought the donation would be the first step for the city in working
towards gaining access and maintaining Hankinsville Road.
   City Planner Lloyd presented issues and options for consideration:
   Considerations
   ∙   Width of the Easement: The first consideration is whether the width of
the easement is large enough. In order to be eligible for inclusion in the
Powell Bill, the average width of the road must be 16 feet. To my knowledge,
the City has never accepted a 20 foot easement for a road.
   ∙   Liability and Maintenance: If we accept this, we will be legally
required to maintain this road to DOT standards and will also be liable for it.
   ∙   Emergency Vehicles: Although we are already able to get in and out with
certain vehicles, some of our larger vehicles would not be able to access
Hankinsville Road with only a 20 foot easement.
   ∙   Road Improvements: Currently, this portion of the road is unimproved. If
the deed of easement is accepted, the City would be responsible for improving
this portion of the road.
   Options
∙   Option 1: Accept the 20 foot easement and improve and maintain the road. If
we could ensure the road has a 16 foot width and bring it up to DOT standards,
we could claim it as a Powell Bill road. It is estimated that a 16 foot wide
paved asphalt road on this portion of Hankinsville with a length of 165 feet
would cost roughly $12,000. We could also gravel this portion. Once the first
portion is accepted, we would need to work towards obtaining easements for the
rest of it.
∙   Option 2: Offer to accept the easement if we can get a larger right-of-way.
For example, in subdivisions our UDO requires at least a 60 foot right-of-way
and a 20 foot road. Rough estimates put a 20 foot wide paved asphalt road with
a length of 165 for this portion at $15,000. This portion could also be
graveled. Based on the size right-of-way that the Board would want, we could
work with remaining property owners towards obtaining approximately sized
easements to improve and maintain the road.
   Attorney Isenberg spoke about other instances when the city had accepted a
reduced right-of-way of 30’.
   Alderman Powell asked the Building Inspector if he knew of any city
developments with a right-of-way less than 60’. Mr. Strickland indicated that
The Landing and Cottages at Prices Creek subdivisions had 50’ rights-of-way.
   Alderman Powell expressed appreciation for the donation but said the
proposed 20’ right-of-way was not enough. Aldermen Mosteller, Coring and
Pukenas agreed.
   Alderman Mosteller stated her opinion that the right-of-way should be 60’
with a 20’ wide road surface.
   Attorney Isenberg stated that the road has been a neighborhood road and
never dedicated to the public. He said that the other property owners could be
approached to determine interest in dedicating an easement to the city.
   Board consensus for the City Planner to contact Mr. Bellamy and advise him
of the Board’s position.

Former Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP)
   Director Hemphill provided the Board with estimated costs to demolish the
former WWTP including costs to dispose of debris and solids. Depending on the
design for demolition, Director Hemphill estimated $400,000 for the project.
She indicated storage units would also need to be purchased for Christmas
decorations and other items currently stored at the location.
   Director Hemphill also provided estimates for turning the property into open
space/nature park and kayak launch. She estimated $20,000 – $100,000 depending
on the type of materials used, design of park and permitting. She pointed out
that the launch would have to be ADA compliant and a CAMA permitting process
would be involved due to the wetlands.
   Director Hemphill asked if the Board wanted to demolish the WWTP, sell the
property or turn it into a nature park with kayak launch.
   Alderman Adams shared his recollection that the Board had previously reached
a consensus to sell the property and use the revenue to offset other projects.
   Noting that citizens had expressed an interest in a park in that area,
Alderman Mosteller pointed out that the CAMA Core Land Use Plan supports
designating the area as Open Space and a park. She stated that the 2015-2020
Parks, Recreation and Open Space Master Plan indicates that Southport is
lacking the amount of water access facilities for the community and should have
two access points. She stated her opinion that it is important to explore
options and she suggested asking the Parks & Recreation Board to form a
committee to delve into possible options.
   Alderman Powell agreed with Alderman Adams. He cited pending projects, i.e.
sewer, old city hall and specifically the waterfront, noting that the latter is
the drawing card for tourism.
   Alderman Poole, commenting that she sees plans as conceptual, and that the
Board had approved many plans which she wished could all be done, stated that
the issue is how to pay for all of the projects. She emphasized that the Board
needs to address the city’s basic needs first.
   Alderman Coring stated he agreed with both sides of the discussion. He said
he did not recall a consensus to sell the property. He pointed out that the
property is unique. He remarked that interest in kayaking has grown around the
world. Acknowledging that many outstanding projects are underway, he stated his
opinion that he does not see a problem with the park option being looked at.
   Alderman Coring read the following letter into the record:
   February 1, 2017
Southport citizens ask the Board of Aldermen to retain the former waste water
property on W. West Street for future use as a nature park. We believe the
creation of a nature park on land currently owned by Southport would provide a
tourism asset, support the goals of the Southport Parks and Recreation Master
Plan and would help maintain clean water in our environment.
To accomplish the repurposing of the old water treatment site to a nature park
we propose the formation of a nonpolitical, nonprofit citizens group, Friends
of The Southport Nature Park. This type of nonprofit organization is
instrumental in the protection of historical landmarks, fundraising,
facilitating maintenance and operating venues. “Friends” organizations work
together with local government agencies to accomplish strategic goals.
There are several of examples of local “Friends” groups here. These groups
provide leadership and financial support to enhance citizens’ quality of life
as well as contributing to the tourism attractions in our locality.
   Friends of the Southport Maritime Museum
   Friends of the Southport and Oak Island Libraries
   Friends of the Oak Island Lighthouse
To move forward we ask the Board of Aldermen to commit to retain the wastewater
treatment property on W. West Street. If this is agreed, the citizens
submitting this request will formally organize a Friends of The Southport
Nature Park as a 501c3 organization. It would be open to all interested
residents of Southport. This group would undertake the task of exploring what
is possible to repurpose the site and how it can be funded through grants and
donations.

Load Management Coordinator, Ellie Pittenger
1159 N. Caswell Avenue Electric Service
   Mr. Pittenger, Load Management Coordinator, advised the Board that City
Ordinance 19-184. Electric line extensions states: (b) Normally, the city will
make single-phase electric overhead line extensions to residential customers
without cost to such customers except that the customer may be required to
secure right-of-way on private property without cost to the city or to assist
the city in obtaining rights-of-way. The city shall be under no obligation to
construct such single-phase electric overhead extensions unless rights-of-way
are so obtained. Mr. Pittinger added that BEMC estimates the cost of $12,000 -
$15,000 to rerun a direct bury cable from 12th street.
   City Manager McDuffie explained that the North Caswell area between 12th and
14th Streets was subdivided in 1910, prior to electric service. Additionally,
he explained that the property owner is requesting annexation into the city and
city services. He stated there are five (5) separate property owners in the
area and the street has been accepted as a public easement and would need to be
annexed into the city limits in order to be accepted by the City.
   City Manager McDuffie stated that establishing electric service to the area
would encourage further development.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Adams to provide the electric
service to the parcel.

RESOLUTION SUPPORTING THE DEVELOPMENT OF A JOINT LAND USE STUDY (JLUS) FOR THE
MILITARY OCEAN TERMINAL SUNNY POINT (MOTSU) AND SURROUNDING LOCAL GOVERNMENTS
THAT WHEREAS, the City of Southport recognizes that the continued operation of
MOTSU is important to the economy of the area and region; and that its future
operational capacity as an important asset for our nation’s defense that should
be protected; and
WHEREAS, MOTSU is interested in participating in a JLUS to coordinate future
planning efforts of is operations with surrounding local governments; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport recognizes that participation in and development
of a JLUS will preserve and enhance the health, safety and general welfare of
the residents of the community and surrounding areas by improving communication
between MOTSU and surrounding local governments and by developing
recommendations for coordinating compatible land uses in area.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport
that:
The Board of Aldermen agrees to participate in the development of a JLUS for
MOTSU and the surrounding local governments.
The Board of Aldermen agrees to appoint a representative(s) to the JLUS policy
committee.
The Board of Aldermen agrees to consider funding their local matching shares of
the cost of the JLUS, either in cash or in-kind or a combination thereof, once
determined by the policy committee.
The Board of Aldermen commits to a good faith effort to implement any
recommendations included in the JLUS.
The Board of Aldermen supports the appointment of the Cape Fear Council of
Governments as the sponsoring entity for the JLUS.
This, the 9th day of February, 2017.         City of
Southport                                                           
                     BY: /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

ORDINANCE APPROVING A ZONING TO OS (OPEN SPACE) FOR 2.47 ACRES BRUNSWICK COUNTY
PARCEL ID – 221KC001
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other
land use ordinances, and a zoning map that control land development within both
the City’s incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s zoning map; and
   WHEREAS, the City Planner has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board a
favorable staff recommendation to zone parcel 221KC002 to Open Space (OS); and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended
that this proposed zoning be approved; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to the NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on February 9, 2017, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that this proposed zoning is
consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is
reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) the proposed zoning is
consistent with the CAMA Core Land Use Plan, (ii) the impact to the adjacent
property owners and the surrounding community is reasonable, and (iii) the
zoning of this parcel to open space will act as a buffer between the
residential Planned Unit Development (PUD) zoning district and the Highway
Commercial (HC) district;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
zoning request for city-owned parcel # 221KC001 and alteration to the Southport
Zoning Map is hereby approved and adopted.
This, the 9th day of February, 2017.         City of Southport

MARCH 8, 2017
SPECIAL SESSION MINUTES
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN          SPECIAL SESSION MINUTES
FIRE DEPARTMENT SUBSTATION MARCH 8, 2017
111 E. NASH STREET         SOUTHPORT, N.C.
PRESENT:         Mayor J.V. Dove
            Aldermen Mary Ellen Poole, Karen Mosteller, Jim Powell,
            Todd Coring, Rick Pukenas, Nelson Adams
STAFF PRESENT:      Kerry McDuffie, City Manager
   Michele Windham, City Clerk
   David Fox, Public Works Director
   Heather Hemphill, Parks & Recreation Director
   Gary Smith, Police Chief
   Charles Drew, Fire Chief
   Randy Jones, Tourism Director
   Thomas Lloyd, Planner
   Mike Simmons, Police Lieutenant   
   Brannon Gray, Code Enforcement Officer
   Vicky Potter, Community Building Coordinator
   Cheryl Metcalf, Accounting Technician
A)   Call to Order – 5:30 p.m.
   Mayor Dove called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.
   Salary Study
      Ms. Becky Veasey, The MAPS Group, addressed the Board. She stated the
study before the Board for consideration was comprised of updated
classifications, job descriptions, creates a pay plan, salary range and revised
the Personnel Policy. She added that the job descriptions were based on job
duties and no personalities or people.
      Ms. Veasey pointed out that the most useful ways to approach adoption of
the study is in three (3) pieces; Job Titles, Classification Plan and Personnel
Policy.
      Noting that staff had reviewed the study and provided their input to her,
Ms. Veasey made herself available to questions from the Board. Alderman Coring
asked about the recommendation to change the job title of the Human Resources
Technician to Payroll and Benefits Specialist. Ms. Veasey explained that the
City’s HR Technician does more than a typical HR Tech., and as the city does
not have an HR Director, the duties of which are spread between the City
Manager, Finance Director and the existing HR Technician. Ms. Veasey pointed
out that with new HR regulations, it is common to find communities adding an HR
Director once the number of employees reaches 65 – 80.
      Alderman Coring asked about the Finance Specialist position. Ms. Veasey
explained that the position is recommended for the current Tax Collector
position as tax collection only makes up approximately 5% of the job duties.
She added that the position would act as backup for the Finance Director.
      Alderman Adams asked if the city was far out of line with what employees
should be paid. Ms. Veasey indicated that Southport was better off than most of
her clients and the average employee would receive roughly a 4% increase if the
study is adopted. She emphasized that the pay plan would need market
adjustments in the future (COLA), and continued range adjustments so good
employees are not lost to other communities.
      Ms. Veasey stated that City staff had started a process of developing a
performance pay and policy. She indicated that once policies are in good draft
form, employees input will be sought, supervisor training will begin to gain
the fundamental skills of conducting performance reviews and employees will be
trained to participate and gain benefits of the system. Responding to Alderman
Mosteller, Ms. Veasey stated the supervisor training is scheduled for May and
she anticipates employee training to be the end of May, first of June, followed
by a pilot period.
      Ms. Veasey explained the benefits of simultaneously posting a job vacancy
internally and externally.
      Noting the recommendation to drop Personal Leave, Alderman Coring
supported keeping it. He added that Brunswick County provides Personal Leave
and it keeps abuse of sick leave down. Alderman Powell agreed. Ms. Veasey noted
that employees had recommended phasing out Personal Leave for new hires as new
employees would receive ten (10) vacation days the first year instead of the
current five (5) days. Alderman Adams stated his opinion that all employees
should be treated the same. Alderman Coring added that Personal Leave should be
kept as it is, a benefit, and taking it away could cause morale problems.
   Board consensus to keep Personal Leave.
      Alderman Powell questioned, if the study is adopted, how it would be
funded without having to raise taxes. City Manager McDuffie explained that
changes to medical insurance resulted in a savings to fund the study and
implement the results.
      Mayor Dove asked about how an employee would be affected by the
Performance Pay once they reached the top of their range. Ms. Veasey explained
that the performance pay allows for a good performer at the top of their range
to get an increase as a lump sum check.
      Alderman Coring supported the change to Political Activity. Ms. Veasey
stated that employees have a right to be involved politically and run for any
office except the Board of Aldermen. Alderman Powell recommended adding
language to prohibit an employee from serving on the Board of Adjustment.
      There was a discussion about Policies with Ms. Veasey stating the
recommendation to keep some policies separate from the Personnel Policy is due
to the frequent changes, i.e. social media, and the ability of the City Manager
to keep the policies updated.
      Alderman Powell pointed out that there are three (3) employees that work
for the Board and would not be under the Personnel Policy: City Clerk, City
Attorney, and City Manager. Ms. Veasey pointed out that City Clerks, especially
in small towns where they have more responsibility, are considered under the
authority and daily supervision of the City Manager. Alderman Adams questioned
if the Clerk should have other duties. Ms. Veasey stated that most cities,
until the population reaches 20,000, have Clerks doing more and it is a good
use of resources. Alderman Pukenas asked who would review the Clerk’s job
performance. Ms. Veasey responded that the Board and City Manager would review
the Clerk.
      Alderman Mosteller asked about when the size of Southport would warrant a
separate HR Officer. Ms. Veasey stated that 65 – 85 employees are the trend and
depends on the growth of the community and additional needed personnel to
provide services. Ms. Veasey pointed out that the current Human Resources
Technician has too much and also does payroll which is a Finance function.
      Alderman Coring asked how the job descriptions were developed. Ms. Veasey
reported that employees completed a position description questionnaire,
interviews were conducted with each employee, and supervisors and management
clarified duties and responsibilities.
      Alderman Adams asked what the cost of the study was. City Manager
McDuffie indicated that the cost was $25,000, including multiple levels of
training.
      The Board discussed compensatory time, overtime, standby/call out pay and
longevity. Alderman Adams stated his opinion that $100 per week for standby/
call out pay was insufficient.
      Alderman Poole stated her opinion that the study was very detailed, will
put together and reviewed well. Alderman Powell stated that the Board needs
more time to review the study.
      Alderman Coring pointed out the absence of a Police Corporal job
description and pay grade.
      Ms. Veasey pointed out that the best time to put the study results into
effect is at the beginning of the fiscal year.
   City Managers Contract
      Alderman Adams motioned, second by Alderman Coring, to take action on the
City Manager’s employment contract at the Thursday, March 9 regular meeting.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Personnel Matter
      City Manager McDuffie reported that an employee in Building Maintenance
would be out on a Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) for at least 12 weeks and
potentially the employee may not come back. He stated that Building Maintenance
currently has two (2) positions and staff was going to ask for a third position
at budget time in order to keep the buildings better. He pointed out that one
custodian cannot handle the work load. City Manager McDuffie stated that staff
would like to advertise for a permanent position instead of a temporary in
order to get a better group of candidates. Alderman Adams asked for a cost
analysis of contracting the work for 12 weeks versus hiring an employee.
      City Manager McDuffie reported that in response to the Board’s February
4th direction, the city had contracted with Booth & Associates to obtain a
quote for the city to provide electrical service to the recently annexed
property at Long Beach Road Extension and NC 211, proposed development
Southport Crossing. He stated that Booth & Associates would be making a site
visit Tuesday, March 14, He added that Brunswick Electric Membership Corps.
(BEMC) is also interested in providing electric service to the area.
      Alderman Powell stated that Southport had gotten out of the electrical
business and did not need to get back into it. He added that the site was in
BEMC’s area and they have multiple back-ups in case of an outage. He pointed
out that the city does not need to hold up the developer of the property.
Alderman Powell talked about a 2003 agreement between the City of Southport and
BEMC for Operation & Maintenance (O&M) by BEMC and the city’s substantial
savings. He stated his relief that no one was killed when Southport had its own
electric crew. He discussed the service the city receives from BEMC and stated
his opinion that the expense for Southport to provide electric to Southport
Crossing would take 20 years to recoup and the $800,000 currently in the
electric fund should be designated to the current city customers.
       Alderman Adams agreed with Alderman Powell. He stated his opinion that
the first priority is to maintain what the city already has. He added that the
O&M contract would increase with additional service area.
      Responding to a query from Alderman Adams, City Manager McDuffie stated
that the cost for Booth & Associates to do a site visit and provide a report is
$3,800.
      Alderman Mosteller asked if ElectriCities could provide an analysis of
the cost for servicing the area. City Manager McDuffie stated that
ElectriCities had estimated build out at a cost of $700,000 with a $100,000
annual revenue. Additionally, he stated that ElectriCities had referred Booth &
Associates.
      City Manager McDuffie said that State Law states that any customer that
is inside the city limits, the city has a right to service unless on the day of
annexation, the Co-op (BEMC) had electric in the area within 300 feet. If the
customer is partially within the 300 foot, it becomes customer choice. City
Manager McDuffie pointed out that the contract the city has with BEMC
specifically says that any customer within the city of Southport city limits,
is the City’s customer.
      Alderman Mosteller emphasized the importance of getting an official cost
for providing the service in order to make an informed decision.
   Budget Amendment #2; Hurricane Matthew
      City Manager McDuffie provided the Board with Budget Amendment #2 for
unbudgeted expenses incurred during Hurricane Matthew. He stated that it is
anticipated that FEMA will be reimbursing the city but likely not before the
end of the current budget year. He stated that if the Budget Amendment is not
adopted, there will not be enough money for operating expenses in May/June.
Item to be considered during the March 9 regular meeting.
      Stating his concerns about the city’s fund balance and the potential
ramifications to the $19.8M loan for construction of a wastewater treatment
plant, Alderman Powell suggested looking at department budgets to find the
$300,000 for Hurricane Matthew expenses.
      Mayor Dove stated his goal to get the fund balance up to 30% over the
next 24 – 30 months.
   201 E. Moore Street Building
      Responding to a question from Mayor Dove, City Manager McDuffie explained
that the discrepancy between the low and high bids for the roof replacement on
the 201 E. Moore Street building was due to the unknown conditions that may
appear when the current roof is torn off.
   Greenway
      City Manager McDuffie reported that he anticipates people will again be
at the Board’s regular meeting to address the greenway access to Walmart. He
stated that he had spoken with Roy Pender, Landscape Architect, and had
received some useful ideas to enhance the greenway. He stated that Walmart had
indicated it would sign off on the greenway being built and may pay for
amenities, such as lighting, trash cans, benches, privacy fences, plantings and
entranceway if citizens would agree to it. City manager McDuffie indicated that
he is waiting to hear back from Walmart and preparation of a drawing to report
back to the Board. He stated that a public meeting may be considered.

meeting. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

City of Southport
RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF
THE JOHN SMITH CEMETERY
Whereas, the John N Smith Cemetery is an African American cemetery , created in
the 1870’s and located on Leonard Street in the City of Southport and consists
of 3.6 surveyed acres, and
Whereas, the John N Smith Cemetery Restoration and Preservation, Inc. is an
established non-profit, North Carolina corporation and has been granted 501c3
status by the IRS, and it plans to pursue designation of the Cemetery on the
National Register of Historic Places, and
Whereas, this Cemetery can stand as a testament to the relevant role African
American citizens have played in the development of Southport and it can
nurture a living legacy and honored the memory of African American history
while promoting public awareness thereof, and
Whereas, this Cemetery should be maintained and sustained in safe and sound
condition, and
Whereas, improvements to the Cemetery, including construction of a perimeter
fence, will help to advance the Cemetery’s public visibility , its physical
integrity, prevent vandalism, provide for pedestrian safety and discourage
inappropriate vehicle access;
Be it hereby resolved that the Southport Board of Aldermen supports the
activities of John N Smith Cemetery Restoration and Preservation, Inc. to
enhance, maintain and preserve the John N Smith Cemetery by means of a
perimeter fence and other improvements, and
Be it further resolved that the City recognizes the Cemetery for its historical
significance as a distinguishable Southport landmark and community asset.
                     By: /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

Resolution In Support of the John Smith Cemetery. Unanimous vote; motion
carried.

AGENDA
   7.   Shoreline Stabilization 
   Noting that a “band aid” had been put on the damage sustained during
Hurricane Matthew, Building Inspector, B. Wayne Strickland, reported that he
had been in contact with Jim McKee Site Manager, Brunswick Town/Fort Anderson,
regarding their method of shoreline stabilization that has been proven to
revitalize the shoreline, promote growth of oysters and improve the health of
the river. He introduced Mr. Randy Boyd with Atlantic Reefmaker.
   Mr. Randy Boyd, Atlantic Reefmaker, gave an abbreviated overview of his
involvement with the Brunswick Town stabilization project. He noted that the
Brunswick Town shoreline is along a shipping channel on the Cape Fear River
with large wave action. Noting that Southport’s greatest asset is the
waterfront, Mr. Boyd pointed out that the rip rap the city has along its
shoreline would float away with a long duration storm. A pictorial packet of
Atlantic Reefmaker projects was provided (on file in the Clerk’s office).
   Mr. Dave Hancock, Atlantic Reefmaker, addressed the Board. He stated that he
had been in the industry 40 years. He talked about Atlantic Reefmarker’s team
work on waterfront communities’ redevelopment and shoreline protection. He
stated that Atlantic Reefmaker designs around the community needs and wants
while taking into consideration what happens during a major storm. He said
Atlantic Reefmaker can offer a system along with amenities, i.e., boardwalks,
piers, esplanades, easy waterfront access while providing protection for
erosion. He stated that Atlantic Reefmaker understands the aspects of storm
water runoff, their systems are environmentally friendly, attract fish life,
and the materials are composites that do not breakdown over time. He offered to
give an alternate presentation on projects Atlantic Reefmaker is working on.
   Responding to a query by Alderman Powell, Mr. Hancock indicated the
Brunswick Town project is expected to start within a month and May would be a
good time to visit the site.

AN ORDINANCE TO EXTEND THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH
CAROLINA
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport has been petitioned under G.S.160A-31 to
annex the area described below; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has by resolution directed the City Clerk to
investigate the sufficiency of the petition; and
   WHEREAS, the City Clerk has certified the sufficiency of the petition and a
public hearing on the question of this annexation was held at the Southport
Community Building at 6:00 p.m. on March 9, 2017, after due notice by
publication on February 22, 2017; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen finds that the petition meets the
requirements of G.S. 160A-31;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina that:
   Section 1. By virtue of the authority granted by G.S. 160A-31, the following
described territory is hereby annexed and made part of the City of Southport as
of March 9, 2017:
   BEGINNING at a new iron pipe in the Western right of way of Caswell Avenue,
which said iron pipe is located South 22 degrees 52 minutes 19 seconds East 200
feet from the intersection of the Western right of way of Caswell Avenue and
the Southern right of way of 13 th Street, City of Southport. From said point
of beginning South 22 degrees 52 minutes 19 seconds East with the Western
right-of-way of Caswell Avenue 50 feet to a new iron pipe; runs thence South 67
degrees 07 minutes 41 seconds West 122.77 feet to a new iron pipe; Runs thence
North 22 degrees 52 minutes 19 seconds West 50 feet to a new iron pipe; runs
thence North 67 degrees 07 minutes 41 seconds East 122.77 feet to the place end
point of beginning and being Lot 15, Block 9 of Southport Heights as per plat
of survey for Patrick S. Lynch and Cheryl L. Serra by Tide Water Land
Surveying, dated May 13, 2015.
   Section 2. Upon and after March 9, 2017, the above described territory and
its citizens and property shall be subject to all debts, laws, ordinances and
regulations in force in the City of Southport and shall be entitled to the same
privileges and benefits as other parts of the City of Southport. Said territory
shall be subject to municipal taxes according to G.S. 160A-58.10.
   Section 3. The Mayor of the City of Southport shall cause to be recorded in
the office of the Register of Deeds of Brunswick County, and in the office of
the Secretary of State at Raleigh, North Carolina, an accurate map of the
annexed territory, described in Section 1 above, together with a duly certified
copy of this ordinance. Such a map shall also be delivered to the County Board
of Elections, as required by G.S. 163-288.1.
Adopted this the 9th day of March, 2017.      City of Southport
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

ORDINANCE APPROVING A ZONING MAP AMENDMENT REZONING THREE PARCELS FROM SPLIT
ZONED R-10, CBD TO R-10
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance, other
land use ordinances, and a zoning map that control land development within both
the City’s incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s zoning map; and
   WHEREAS, the City Planner has prepared and submitted to the Planning Board a
favorable staff recommendation to rezone parcels 237LG006, 237LG046, and
237LG042 from R-10, CBD to R-10; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered this matter and has recommended
that this proposed zoning be approved; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to the NC General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on March 9, 2017, before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen hereby finds that the proposed zoning map
amendment is consistent with the Southport CAMA Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this zoning map amendment
is reasonable and in the public interest in that (i) the proposed rezoning of
the above properties preserves residential areas, (ii) the proposed rezoning of
the above properties resolves the issue of split zoning, (iii) and the impact
to the adjacent property owners and the surrounding community is reasonable;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
that The Official Zoning Map of the City of Southport, an element of the
Unified Development Ordinance of the City, is amended by changing the zoning
classification of the below-described properties from a split zoning of R-10,
CBD to R-10: Tax Parcel ID Numbers of properties to be rezoned: 237LG006,
237LG046, and 237LG042.
This ordinance shall be effective upon its adoption, and the Official Zoning
Map of the City of Southport shall be revised accordingly.
This, the 9th day of March, 2017            City of Southport
                     BY: /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk

   13.   Sewer Plant Construction Method
   City Manager McDuffie reported that the city was approved for a subsidized
loan for construction of a wastewater treatment plant. He stated he and the
Mayor had spent time with people from the State regarding a traditional bid
build process vs. a design/build process. Noting the size of the project, City
Manager McDuffie asked for guidance and suggested having a workshop.
   Alderman Powell discussed the design build method and the benefits of
obtaining qualifications, the project gets completed faster and the city is not
required to accept the low bid.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to use Design/Build for
construction of a wastewater treatment facility.
   Discussion
   Alderman Mosteller questioned if the process was approved by the grant
entity and would allow the Board to compare using the County for solid waste
services. City Manager McDuffie stated the design build process allows the city
a better sense of direction, saves money and helps provide clear information.
He noted that the project would come before the Board many times in the next
couple years while all aspects and options are considered.
   Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   14.   Setting Date for Workshop  
   The Board set Monday, April 3, 5:00 p.m. for a workshop to further discuss
the wastewater treatment plant project and consider uses for the 2nd floor of
City Hall.
   15.   Budget Amendment # 2; Hurricane Matthew Expenses
   City Manager McDuffie explained that Budget Amendment #2 is for expenses
incurred during preparation for Hurricane Matthew, overtime of personnel, clean
up and rip rap installation along the waterfront in front of Ft. Johnston. He
pointed out that if the approximately $125,000 of the budget amendment was not
adopted, general operating expenses could not be covered to the end of the
year.
   City Manager McDuffie stated that $180,000 in the budget amendment was for
the estimated cost to repair the Bay Street CAMA water access, waterfront
bulkhead and city boat dock. He added that the repairs have been submitted to
FEMA and it is anticipated FEMA will reimburse the expenditure. He noted that
tourist and hurricane seasons are approaching and it would be detrimental not
to have the waterfront bulkhead repaired before another storm season.
   Mayor Dove commented that the waterfront is Southport’s calling card and
needs to be ready for tourist season. He added that it does not look good with
cones everywhere and busted up sidewalks.
   Alderman Powell expressed concerns that FEMA had not provided a guarantee of
reimbursement nor how much they would reimburse. He recommended putting a
hiatus on all outside spending. He argued that continued fund balance spending
would jeopardize the loan for construction of a wastewater treatment plant.
   Mayor Dove pointed out that the General Fund is for the unexpected expenses
from storms.
   City Manager McDuffie stated that he would contact FEMA and ask for a time
line.
   Alderman Mosteller pointed out that the $125,000 had already been spent.
   Alderman Adams agreed with Alderman Powell to cut spending until there is a
guarantee from FEMA.
   Noting that Southport specifically had extra money in the general fund
because it is a waterfront town, Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman
Mosteller to approve the Budget Amendment as written, minus the $180,000 line
item.
   Discussion
   While endorsing Alderman Powell’s position, Alderman Adams encouraged
Alderman Powell to support the budget amendment for $125,000, noting that the
money had to be spent.
   Alderman Powell stated his opinion that the money could be found elsewhere
in the budget.
   Aye:   Aldermen Poole, Mosteller, Pukenas, Adams
   Nay:   Aldermen Powell, Coring
   Motion Carried 4 – 2

Nay:   Aldermen Powell, Coring, Adams

   17.   Salary Study
   City Manager McDuffie talked about the funding, realized from health care
savings, for the salary study as presented February 4 to the Board. He
suggested continued review of the proposed Personnel Policy after the revisions
requested March 8 are incorporated.
   Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to approve the job
descriptions as presented and the salary study, effective March 14, 2017.
   Discussion
   Alderman Powell stated his impression that the Board was not satisfied with
the study and he stated that he did not go along with the recommendations in
the Personnel Policy. He expressed his views that employees in Category 9 are
underpaid in the recommended salary study and he would not endorse it until the
discrepancy was corrected. Additionally, he pointed out that the organizational
chart, chain of command was incorrect.
   Alderman Adams suggested a stipulation in the motion to endorse the study
when the particular issues expressed by Alderman Powell were straightened out
and implement the salary results retroactive to March 14. Alderman Adams
emphasized the need to let employees know the Board supports them.
   Stating his support for the study, Alderman Coring indicated he was not in a
position to vote on the study after just having a workshop the previous night.
He contended that he did not have all the facts, there was a missing job
description and pay scales.
   Alderman Coring raised a question about travel & training monies being used
to pay for the study. Finance Director Trexler could not attend the meeting and
City Manager McDuffie indicated he did not have the specifics about budget line
item transfers.

decision.

weeks. He stated that a dollar amount to build the system to the property would
be provided by Booth & Associates. He added that Electricities calculated the
return on investment at roughly $100,000 annually.

would be a large figure and the city’s underground service in the area had not
had any improvements in over 10 years and would incur additional expense.
   Responding to Mayor Dove, City Manager McDuffie explained that there was
$800,000 in the electric fund allocated for underground projects that could be
used to fund the project.

   Nay:   Aldermen Poole, Adams, Mosteller, Coring
