representatives about lowering the speed limit on NC211 to Walmart for use by

A)   Call to Order – 6:00 p.m.
Mayor Dove called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
B)   Invocation
Alderman Pukenas welcomed everyone and Mayor Dove gave the invocation.
C)   Pledge of Allegiance
   Alderman Pukenas led the assemblage in the Pledge of Allegiance.
D)   Public Comment
   Ms. Joni Christmas, 4455 Willow Moss Way, spoke in opposition to the
proposed pedestrian pathway to Tidewater Plaza through the Southport Way
Subdivision.
   Ms. Regina Napolitano, 3103 Spring Oak Lane, spoke in opposition to the
proposed pedestrian pathway to Tidewater Plaza through the Southport Way
Subdivision.
   Mr. James Rankin, 4457 Willow Moss Way, expressed his understanding that the
proposed Greenway was originally planned to provide safe passage for those
individuals in wheelchairs and he shared his perception that the greenway was
now planned for golf cart usage. He spoke about instances he had witnessed of
drug use and indigents camped behind the development.
   Mr. Robert Creech, 426 W. Brunswick Street, stated that he was on a campaign
to re-open the city dock in the Yacht Basin that was damaged by Hurricane
Matthew. He pointed out that he had read in the board agenda that consideration
was being made to demolish the structure. He asked the Board to consider re-

SOUTHPORT
RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF INTERNATIONAL DAY OF PEACE
WHEREAS, The United Nations in 1981 established a yearly International Day of
Peace, a day devoted to commemorating and strengthening the ideals of peace
both within and among all nations and people; and
WHEREAS, The International Day of Peace is now observed around the world each
year on September 21 to put aside all that separates us and to experience
peace; and
WHEREAS, the theme of the 2017 International Day of Peace is “Together for
Peace: Respect, Safety & Dignity for All”; and
WHEREAS, Southport residents are coordinating a celebration of the
International Day of Peace on a local level; and
WHEREAS, Peace Day Southport promotes world peace, local peace and inner peace
through education, art and celebration; and
WHEREAS, the Celebration of Peace will be held in Franklin Square Park and will
include songs, dances, art, peace information and literature, and children’s
crafts; and
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Mayor and Southport Board of Aldermen
on this the 3rd day of August 2017, hereby proclaim Saturday, September 16,
2017 as “Peace Day” in the City of Southport and urge all citizens to join in
the festivities of this day and promote peace among all peoples.
                           /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

local government experience.
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Mr. Bruce Oakley is appointed the City
Manager of Southport, NC effective September 1, 2017, and that the Employment
Agreement between the City and Mr. Oakley is hereby approved.

CITY OF SOUTHPORT
AN ORDINANCE TO ALLOW THE SALE OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES
BEFORE NOON ON SUNDAYS AT LICENSED PREMISES
WHEREAS, on June 29, 2017, the North Carolina General Assembly enacted Senate
Bill 155, entitled “An Act to Make Various Changes to the Alcoholic Beverage
Control Commission Laws”; and
WHEREAS, Section 4 of Ratified Senate Bill 155 authorizes city and county
governments to adopt an ordinance to allow alcohol sales beginning at 10 am on
Sundays; and
WHEREAS, Ratified Senate Bill 155 was signed into law by Governor Roy Cooper on
the 30th day of June, 2017 and became effective on that date (Session Law 2017,
Chapter 87); and
WHEREAS, by enacting Senate Bill 155, North Carolina joins 47 other States in
allowing alcohol service before noon on Sunday; and
WHEREAS, Sunday morning alcohol service will allow the hospitality community
and retail merchants in our community to meet the needs of their customers; and
WHEREAS, Sunday morning alcohol service will benefit our small business
community, bring people into business districts earlier in the day, and
generate increased tax revenues; and
WHEREAS, our community has a diverse and growing population with different
religious beliefs, each of which has various times and multiple days for
worship;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of Southport, North
Carolina that:
Section 1. Pursuant to the authority granted by S.L. 2017-87 any establishment
located in the corporate limits of and holding an ABC permit issued pursuant to
G.S. 18B - 1001 is permitted to sell beverages allowed by its permit beginning
at 10 A.M. on Sundays.
Section 2. All laws and clauses of law in conflict herewith are repealed to the
extent of any such conflict.
Section 3. This ordinance is effective on the 4th day of August, 2017. Adopted
this 3rd day of August, 2017.
8.   First Reading: Golf Cart Ordinance Revisions
   Mayor Dove questioned the size and seating restrictions. City Planner Lloyd
responded that the Committee recommendation is to permit up to 3 seater golf
carts. He spoke about the differences between golf carts and low speed
vehicles.
   Alderman Powell suggested changing the seating restrictions to 4 seats.
   City Attorney Isenberg stated that low speed vehicles are licensed by the
State and travel more than 20 mph. He added that the city cannot regulate low
speed vehicles.
   Alderman Adams questioned the 18 years old age requirement and asked the
Committee to revisit the requirement. He pointed out that 16 year olds can
obtain State issued Driver’s Licenses and should be permitted to drive golf
carts. He expressed caution about making the Ordinance too restrictive.
   Alderman Coring stated he had received queries about the age limit, required
equipment such as mirrors and headlights and tagging the vehicles already
licensed by the State. He suggested providing an educational session for the
public.
   City Planner Lloyd stated that the Committee had reviewed other
municipalities’ ordinances.
   Attorney Isenberg stated that State Law prohibits anyone under 16 from
driving a golf cart. He pointed out that until the city had adopted an
ordinance, it was illegal to operate a golf cart on city roadways.
   Mayor Dove asked if provisions had been included in the draft ordinance for
handicapped operation. City Planner Lloyd responded that the ordinance allows
for operation by those with a handicap.
   Mayor Dove asked if it would be possible to tag carts for use only during
daylight hours. Attorney Isenberg advised the Board to consider the duties that
will be placed on the Police Department and the effectiveness of enforcement.
   Alderman Pukenas stated that an informational brochure would be created.
   Alderman Poole pointed out that once an ordinance is approved, the
information will be available to the public in City Hall, on the city’s web
page and each cart owner that gets a sticker would be required to read and sign
an affidavit that they have read the ordinance.
   Alderman Pukenas noted that the stickers would cost $25.
   Mr. Steve Simon, 6211 Pebble Shore Lane, golf cart owner since 2007, tour
operator for past four (4) years shared his concerns for Board consideration.
Referencing a newspaper article, Mr. Simon noted that the proposed ordinance
did not address gasoline carts or mopeds. He stated there was public confusion
about the regulations for state roads vs. city streets, low speed vehicles vs.
golf carts, what low speed vehicles can and cannot do and the proposed age
requirement of 18. He stated that golf carts typically go 12 – 13 mph and
operating them on 35 mph streets would put people at risk. He surmised that,
with additional rules, enforcement of the ordinance by the Police Department
would be difficult.
   Alderman Poole pointed out that the Board’s agendas, with all attachments,
are available at the library and City Hall. She recommended having the Golf
Cart Committee revisit the Ordinance taking into consideration all comments,
prepare another draft and bring back to the Board.
   Interim City Manager Bauer indicated that the draft ordinance is on the
city’s web page and copies are available at City Hall.

with the FY 2018-2019 budget.

Mayor Pro Tem Coring called the meeting back to order at 5:30 p.m.
   Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 160A-683(b) Alderman Poole motioned, second by Alderman
Powell to go into Public Hearing regarding the creation of the Bald Head Island
Transportation Authority. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Mr. Robert Creech, 426 W. Brunswick Street, asked for justification as to
why the establishment of and inclusion in the Bald Head Island (BHI)
Transportation Authority is a good idea for the City of Southport. He talked
about the loss of taxes, potential liability and what entity would be
responsible if the Authority defaulted. Mr. Creech recalled a large boating
accident of a passenger ferry in years past, with litigation still in process.
   There were no further public comments.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to close Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Board Comments
   Attorney Isenberg advised that Alderman Mosteller is not legally required to
abstain from voting for a conflict of interest. He stated that Alderman
Mosteller informed him that she did not want to have the appearance of a
conflict of interest due to her employment with Bald Head Limited.
   Alderman Mosteller commented on her understanding of the franchise fee as a
way to compensate for fire, police and emergency services similar to mutual aid
agreements.
   Alderman Powell stated his understanding that the Authority, which is
modeled after the Douglas Airport Authority in Charlotte, will be incorporated
through the Secretary of State who will have jurisdiction over the Authority.
He indicated that the franchise fees would be determined by mirroring the
current taxes collected. He stated that as property taxes increased, so would
the franchise fee which would be controlled by the eleven members of the Board
of Trustees as appointed by the Governor (1), General Assembly (2), North
Carolina Department of Transportation (3), Mayor & Mayor Pro Tempore of the
Village of Bald Head + 1, Southport (1), and Brunswick County (1). Alderman
Powell reported that the BHI Transportation Authority will operate just like
the State Ports Authority. He added that if a boating accident should occur, it
would be addressed by the State Authority.
   City Attorney Isenberg stated that per the legislation, there was no
liability to the City and the City would not be responsible for any debts.
   Alderman Poole pointed out that the financial reports for upcoming years had
been reviewed and a 2- 2-1/2% annual increase in franchise fees was estimated.
Additionally, she pointed out that 5 – 6 acres of property will be pulled out
of the Authority and will remain as taxable property for the City.
   Alderman Pukenas commented that he had reviewed the legislation and
determined that the franchise fees would be comparable to the property tax and
the State would assume responsibility for the ferry system, not the City.
   It was noted that appointments by the Governor, Legislature and County could
be individuals from Southport. Attorney Isenberg pointed out that the only
stipulation for the appointment made by the Board was that it be a citizen of
Southport.
   Alderman Mosteller asked to be recused. Alderman Poole motioned, second by
Alderman Powell to recuse Alderman Mosteller. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Powell to adopt A Concurrent
Resolution Whereby The Village Of Bald Head Island, The City Of Southport, And
The County Of Brunswick Signify Their Determination To Organize The Bald Head
Island Transportation Authority & Articles Of Incorporation Of Bald Head Island
Transportation Authority.
   Ayes:      Aldermen Coring, Powell, Poole, Pukenas
   Recused:   Alderman Mosteller
   Motion Carried 4-0
A CONCURRENT RESOLUTION WHEREBY THE VILLAGE OF BALD HEAD ISLAND, THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT, AND THE COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK SIGNIFY THEIR DETERMINATION TO ORGANIZE
THE BALD HEAD ISLAND TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY
WHEREAS, on July 18, 2017, the Governor of the State of North Carolina signed
the Ferry Transportation Authority Act, as ratified by the North General
Assembly, 2017 Session Law 120, codified at North Carolina General Statutes,
Chapter 160A, Article 29 (the “Act”);
WHEREAS, the Village of Bald Head Island (the “Village”) is a municipal
corporation that is only accessible by watercraft vessel;
WHEREAS, the Village is dependent upon a reliable, safe, and affordable ferry
system (including passenger and barge transportation services, terminal
facilities and vehicle parking) that operates on the Cape Fear River between
Deep Point Marina in the City of Southport and Bald Head Island Marina in the
Village;
WHEREAS, the City of Southport (“Southport”) is a municipal corporation where
the mainland ferry terminal, the mainland barge terminal, and vehicle parking
for access to Bald Head Island are located;
WHEREAS, many Southport and other Brunswick County residents are employed on
and/or regularly visit Bald Head Island and depend upon the ferry services and
parking facilities, and many residents living on and visitors to Bald Head
Island regularly transact business in Southport and Brunswick County;
WHEREAS, the Village and Southport are both municipalities located in Brunswick
County, North Carolina in which all of the ferry terminal and barge facilities
and vehicle parking for access to Bald Head Island are located;
WHEREAS, the ferry system, barge system, on-island tram system, terminals, and
parking facilities are presently owned and operated by a number of privately
held corporations;
WHEREAS, the Act permits the purchase of those assets of those privately held
corporations used in the operations of the ferry system, barge system, on-
island tram system, terminals, and parking facilities, and the consolidation of
those operations in, by a single ferry transportation authority as defined in
G.S. 160A-681 and with the powers set forth in G.S. 160A-685 (“the Authority”);
WHEREAS, pursuant to G.S. 160A-683, the Village Council of the Village of Bald
Head Island, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport, and the Board of
Commissioners of the County of Brunswick are the proper entities to adopt a
resolution to create the Authority pursuant to the Act;
WHEREAS, the Village, Southport, and Brunswick County are engaging to
coordinate and plan for the Authority that will operate a reliable and safe
ferry and barge transportation system to transport passengers and freight
between Southport and the Village, to provide parking facilities for those
passengers on the mainland, and to provide tram service on the island; to
enhance the quality of life, mobility, and circumstances of residents of the
Village, Southport, and Brunswick County; and to promote economic development
and tourism throughout the Cape Fear region, while protecting and preserving
the environment;
WHEREAS, the Village, Southport, and Brunswick County have duly afforded the
general public, and other interested parties, both public and private, the
opportunity to participate in public hearings regarding the formation of the
Authority, which public hearings were noticed as required by G.S. 160A-683 and
properly conducted pursuant to all applicable laws;
WHEREAS, the creation of an Authority, pursuant to the Act, appears to be in
the best long-term interest of the Village, Southport, and Brunswick County,
and their residents and businesses;
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport, NC, desires by this
Concurrent Resolution to signify its determination to organize an Authority
under the applicable provisions of the Act; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, NC:
That the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport, NC, signifies its
determination to organize an Authority under the Act.
That the articles of incorporation of such Authority are included herein by
reference, and that, pursuant to G.S. 160A-683, these articles of incorporation
set forth all of the following:
that the “Bald Head Island Transportation Authority” is the official name of
such Authority;
that such Authority is organized under the Act; and
that the names of the organizing entities for the Authority are the Village of
Bald Head Island, the City of Southport, and Brunswick County
that the registered agent for service of process shall be the Chairman of the
Board of Trustees or such other agent as the Board of Trustees may designate
and whose name and address is provided to the North Carolina Secretary of
State.
That the purpose of the Authority shall be to operate a reliable and safe ferry
and barge transportation system to transport passengers and freight between
Southport and the Village, provide parking facilities for those passengers on
the mainland, and to provide tram service on the island; to enhance the quality
of life, mobility, and circumstances of residents of the Village, Southport,
and Brunswick County; and to promote economic development and tourism
throughout the Cape Fear region, while protecting and preserving the
environment, in accordance with the provisions of, and with all such powers as
provided in, the Act.
That pursuant to G.S. 160A-683, public hearings were duly conducted concerning
the matter of organizing an Authority under the provisions of the Act prior to
adoption of this Concurrent Resolution.
This resolution shall become effective if and when concurrent counterparts are
adopted by the Village Council of the Village of Bald Head Island, NC and the
Board of Commissioners of Brunswick County. 
ADOPTED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport, NC, this the 7th day
of August, 2017.
                      CITY OF SOUTHPORT
                      /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION
OF
BALD HEAD ISLAND TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY
In compliance with the Ferry Transportation Authority Act, Article 29 of
Chapter 160A of the North Carolina General Statutes, the Village Council of the
Village of Bald Head Island, North Carolina, the Board of Aldermen of the City
of Southport, North Carolina, and the Board of Commissioners of Brunswick
County, North Carolina, each pursuant to a resolution signifying its
determination to organize an Authority pursuant to G.S. 160A-683, which
Authority shall be a public body and body politic and corporate of the State of
North Carolina, hereby certify that:
The name of the Authority is the Bald Head Island Transportation Authority.
The Authority is organized under Article 29 of Chapter 160A of the North
Carolina General Statues.
The names of the organizing entities for the Authority are the Village of Bald
Head Island, the City of Southport, and Brunswick County.
The Authority shall be governed by a Board of Trustees consisting of eleven
(11) members selected and serving in accordance with Article 29 of Chapter 160A
of the North Carolina General Statutes.
The registered agent for service of process shall be the Chairman of the Board
of Trustees or such other agent as the Board of Trustees may designate and
whose name and address is provided to the North Carolina Secretary of State.
IN WITNESS THEREOF, the City of Southport, NC, has caused these Articles of
Incorporation to be executed by the Mayor and an official seal to be affixed
hereto and attested by the City Clerk, this the 7th day of August, 2017.
                     CITY OF SOUTHPORT
                      /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

Resolution
Proclaiming October 8 – 14, 2017
Fire Prevention Week
WHEREAS, the Southport Fire Department is committed to ensuring the safety and
security of all those living in and visiting our Fire District; and
WHEREAS, fire is a serious public safety concern both locally and nationally,
and homes are the locations where people are at the greatest risk of fire; and
WHEREAS, the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) has documented through
its research a significant increase in home fires, and due to this fact, it is
important that everyone know two ways out of your home in case of a fire; and
WHEREAS, the Firefighters of the Southport Fire Department are dedicated to
reducing the occurrence of residential and commercial structural fires and fire
related injuries through prevention and protection education; and
WHEREAS, the residents of the Southport Fire District are responsive to public
education measures and are able to take personal steps to increase their safety
from fire; and
WHEREAS, being prepared in the event of a home fire will have a positive effect
on the home fire problem; and
WHEREAS, each home fire that is prevented in the Southport Fire District is an
opportunity to prevent painful injury and costly property damage; and
WHEREAS, the 2017 Fire Prevention Week theme, Every Second Counts – Know 2 Ways
Out, effectively serves to remind us all of the simple actions we can take to
stay safer from fire every day.
THEREFORE, I, J. V. Dove, Mayor of the City of Southport do hereby proclaim
October 8-14, 2017 as Fire Prevention Week throughout this City, and I urge all
the citizens of Southport to heed the important safety messages from the
Southport Fire Prevention Team, and the Office of the City Fire Marshal and to
support the many public safety activities and efforts of the Southport Fire
Department.
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

A RESOLUTION REQUESTING THE NORTH CAROLINA DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION
UNDERTAKE A STUDY OF AN ADDITIONAL TRAFFIC LIGHT ON NORTH HOWE STREET
WHEREAS, the citizens of the City of Southport and all those who visit,
appreciate and enjoy the unique history, charm and appeal that the Southport
area offers; and
WHEREAS, the safe use of roads and highways is of utmost importance to not only
the citizens of Southport, but also to our visitors from this great State and
other states and countries; and
WHEREAS, at the September 8, 2016 Board of Aldermen meeting, a representative
of NCDOT stated that the average daily traffic on N.C. 211 between Southport
and the Long Beach Road is 35,000 – 50,000 vehicles and ranks at the top of
NCDOT Division 3; and
WHEREAS, much of this traffic is traveling through the City of Southport; and
WHEREAS, Howe Street is a State-maintained road and has only three signalized
intersections and thirteen unsignalized intersections; and
WHEREAS, this creates a dangerous situation for drivers attempting to turn left
onto Howe Street due to the high traffic count Howe Street experiences and the
numerous unsignalized intersections.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport, North Carolina, that the City of Southport requests that the North
Carolina Department of Transportation undertake a feasibility study for
installing a traffic light on N. Howe Street in the area of 12th and 14th
Streets.
Adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen in regular session, September 14,
2017.

AGENDA
11.   Second Reading: Golf Cart Ordinance Revisions
   Alderman Mosteller reported that the Golf Cart Committee comprised of
Alderman Poole, Alderman Pukenas, City Planner Lloyd, Building Inspector
Strickland, Police Chief Smith, and herself, had reviewed the concerns voiced
by the Board of Aldermen during the first reading of the proposed ordinance
revisions.
   Alderman Mosteller stated that the Committee recommends that the City
request low speed vehicles, which are regulated by the State, register with the
City and get a sticker free of charge so the City can maintain an accurate
count of low speed vehicles in Southport. She indicated that the Committee also
recommends that golf carts be required to have front headlights and/or
equivalent light bar.
   Referencing the NC Drive Manual, Alderman Mosteller indicated the Committee
revisited the 18 years of age requirement for operation of a golf cart and
recommended retaining 18 due to the fact that a valid NC driver’s license
issued at age 15 – 18 is a provisional license with specific restrictions and
statistics show that younger drivers have more accidents.
   Alderman Powell stated his opinion that golf carts should be inspected once
a year as are low speed vehicles, i.e. lights, turn signals, wear on the tires.
Alderman Mosteller stated that a sticker from the City would be required
annually following an inspection by the Police Department.
   Alderman Mosteller motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to adopt the Golf
Cart Ordinance Revisions. Unanimous vote; motion carried. 
 City of Southport Golf Cart Ordinance
Sec. 17-80. - Golf carts.
(a) DEFINITIONS
(1) GOLF CART.  A vehicle designed and manufactured for operation on a golf
course for sporting or recreational purposes and that is not capable of
exceeding speeds of 20 mph.
(2) OPERATE.  To drive, or be in physical control of a golf cart that is moving
or has its key inserted and in the on position.
(b) REGISTRATION AND PERMIT REQUIREMENTS
(1) Registration and Permit required. In order to operate a golf cart in the
corporate limits of the City of Southport under this section, the golf cart
must be registered annually with the City of Southport using an application
furnished by the city. A twenty-five dollar ($25.00) per year registration fee,
from July 1 through June 30, must be paid to the City before a registration
sticker is issued. The registration sticker must be displayed on the left rear
fender of the golf cart. Low speed vehicles subject to state regulation and
licenses will be exempt from a permit and inspection, but the City of Southport
requests low speed vehicle owners to register with the City and obtain a
sticker free of charge so the City can maintain an accurate count of low speed
vehicles in Southport.
(2) Basic requirements. In order to register a golf cart and secure an annual
permit, the owner and golf cart must meet the following basic requirements:
a. All golf cart operators must be 18 years of age or older and possess a full
valid driver's license, except any driver or operator 18 years of age or older
with a medical or physical condition that prevents that individual from being
able to obtain a valid North Carolina driver’s license. Any driver or operator
with such a medical or physical condition must have certification from an
appropriate medical professional that they can safely operate a golf cart. Any
driver or operator that is exempt from the requirement of a valid North
Carolina license must still present and have a valid North Carolina
Identification card on record and while operating a golf cart.
b. The owner must possess and maintain liability insurance in an amount not
less than required by North Carolina law for traditional motor vehicles
operated on a public street or highway.
c. The golf cart must have an identifiable vehicle identification number.
(3) Required safety features. In order to register a golf cart and secure an
annual permit, a golf cart must have the following safety features installed:
a. Two operating LED front headlights or an equivalent light bar, visible from
a distance of at least 250 feet;
b. Two operating tail lights, with brake lights and turn signals, visible from
a distance of at least 250 feet
c. A rear vision mirror;
d. An air horn
e. Stop lamps
f. At least one reflector per side;
g. A parking brake;
h. A Type 1 or Type 2 seat belt assembly conforming to section 571.209 of the
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 209 installed at each designated
seating position.
i. A windshield; and
j. Must be limited to a maximum of three rows of seats.
k. Any modification to the golf cart must comply with all safety requirements
of this section and must be inspected by the appropriate City staff prior to
operation.
(4) Unobstructed views. No golf cart shall be registered, approved for use, or
operated on the city’s streets if the operator’s view is materially obstructed,
obscured, or impaired by any sign, poster, sticker, or other non- transparent
material placed upon any front windshield, or side or rear window.
(5) Dimension and weight limits. No golf cart shall be registered or approved
for use, or operated on the city’s streets if the overall dimensions and/or
weight of the vehicle exceed any of the following dimensions:
a. Length: 160.00 inches; 13 feet 4 inches
b. Height: 84.00 inches 7 feet
c. Width: 60.00 inches 5 feet
d. Weight: 1,600.00 pounds. Weight shall be determined by the manufacturer’s
published data or, if none is available, then by the vehicle’s curb weight.
Curb weight, for purposes hereof, is defined as the weight of the vehicle in an
operational status with all fluids and components, including batteries, but
without driver, passengers or cargo.
(6) Inspection. Prior to the issuance of a permit, designated city staff shall
inspect the golf cart for compliance with the requirements of this section. No
golf cart shall be registered and permitted unless it is in compliance with all
requirements.
(7) Acknowledgment. Prior to issuance of a permit, the owner shall sign an
acknowledgment that he or she has read and understands the provisions of this
section.
(8) Disqualified vehicles. All-terrain vehicles, 4-wheel utility vehicles, go-
karts, and other similar utility vehicles which are not manufactured for
operation on a golf course, and/or a golf cart which has been modified so that
it no longer meets the definition of golf cart may not be registered as a golf
cart under this section or shall such vehicles be operated on the public roads,
streets and highways within the city, unless such vehicles are registered and
permitted under the motor vehicle laws of North Carolina.
(9) Exceptions:
a. The operation of golf carts on private property, with the consent of the
owner
b. The operation of golf carts within private, gated, or limited access
communities, unless the streets of the community are dedicated for public use
and maintained by the city;
c. The use of a golf cart in connection with a parade, a festival, or other
special event provided the consent of the sponsor is obtained, the police
department is notified, and provided the golf cart is only used during such
event; and
d. The use of city vehicles by city personnel, or other governmental agencies
and/or public service agencies on official business.
(c) OPERATION ON PUBLIC STREETS AND ROADS. It is unlawful to operate a golf
cart on any public street or road within the City except in accordance with the
following regulations:
(1) The golf cart may only be operated on streets and roads that have a posted
speed limit of 35 miles per hour or less.
(2) A golf cart must display a valid city-issued golf cart annual registration
sticker.
(3) All golf cart operators must be 18 years of age or older and possess a full
valid driver's license, except any driver or operator 18 years of age or older
with a medical or physical condition that prevents that individual from being
able to obtain a valid North Carolina driver’s license. Any driver or operator
with such a medical or physical condition must have certification from an
appropriate medical professional that they can safely operate a golf cart. Any
driver or operator that is exempt from the requirement of a valid North
Carolina license must still present and have a valid North Carolina
Identification card on record and while operating a golf cart.
(4) No golf cart may be operated at a speed greater than reasonable and prudent
for the existing conditions, and in no instance at a speed greater than 20
miles per hour.
(5) No golf cart may be operated in a careless or reckless manner
(6) The driver and passengers must be properly seated while the golf cart is in
motion, the seating capacity with seat belts shall not be exceeded.
(7) Golf carts must be operated to the extreme right of the roadway and must
yield to all vehicular and pedestrian traffic
(8) Golf carts may not be operated or parked on any sidewalk or in any city
park, except for golf carts operated by governmental or public service agencies
for official purposes.
(9) Golf carts must be operated in accordance with all applicable state and
local laws and ordinances, including all laws, regulations and ordinances
pertaining to the possession and use of alcoholic beverages and other impairing
substances.
(10) Golf carts may only be parked in the same manner and at the same places
designated for the parking of motor vehicles or in parking spaces specifically
dedicated for golf cart parking.
(11) Golf carts may only park in handicapped parking spaces if the driver has a
valid handicapped placard or sticker and the same is clearly posted or
displayed in the golf cart.
(12) Golf carts may not be used for the purpose of towing another cart, trailer
or vehicle of any kind, including a person on roller skates, skateboard, or
bicycle.
(13) The possession of open containers of alcohol and/or consumption of alcohol
by the driver and/or passengers of a golf cart is prohibited.
(14) Golf carts may not be used as a taxicab or bus or for the commercial
carrying of passengers or the hauling of freight.
(15) All golf carts are required to maintain liability insurance at the same
level as required for automobiles.
(16) Golf carts shall not be operated on or across any public or private
properties without the permission of the property owner.
(17) During an emergency situation or at a special event, any police officer
supervising or controlling traffic may direct that golf carts be operated only
on or upon certain streets or locations as directed by the officer.
(d) PENALTIES
(1) In addition to constituting a misdemeanor or infraction as provided by G.S.
14-4, violation of any provision of this ordinance shall subject the offender
to a civil penalty in the amount of $ 50 for each separate of distinct offense
to be recovered by the city in an action in the nature of debt if not paid by
the offender within 72 hours after being cited for the violation.
(2) Operating a golf cart under the influence of an impairing substance (i.e.,
alcohol or drugs) on a public street or road is a violation of state law, and
is punishable as provided therein. The charging officer does not have
discretion to issue a civil citation for violation of this subsection.
(3) The city may refuse to register and issue a permit for the operation of a
golf cart, or may revoke a previously issued permit, if the registered golf
cart and/or the owner of the golf cart is involved in three or more violations
of this section and/or violations of state law pertaining to within a three-
year time period. Said revocation and/or denial of a permit shall be effective
for one year.
(e) LIABILITY DISCLAIMER
(1) This section is adopted to address the interest of public safety. Golf
carts are not designed or manufactured to be used on the public streets and the
city is no way advocates or endorses their operation on public streets or
roads. The City, by regulating this operation, is addressing obvious safety
issues, and adoption of this section is not to be relied upon as determination
that operation on public streets is safe or advisable if done in accordance
with this section. All persons who operate or ride upon golf carts on public
streets or roads do so at their own risk and peril, and must be observant of
and attentive to the safety of themselves and others, including their
passengers, other motorists, bicyclists and pedestrians. The City has no
liability under any theory of liability and the city assumes no liability, for
permitting golf carts to be operated on the public streets and roads under the
special legislation granted by the state legislature.

14.   Fire Pumper Financing Award to BB&T in Amount Not to Exceed $450,000 &
Adoption of Resolution Approving Financing Terms
   Fire Chief Drew explained that the purchase of a new fire pumper was put out
to bids with three (3) bids received. He stated that staff recommends award to
BB&T which came in as the low bidder on a five (5) year term at a 1.97%
interest rate.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to award the financing
of a fire pumper vehicle to BB&T for not to exceed $450,000 and to adopt the
Resolution Approving Financing Terms. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Resolution Approving Financing Terms
   WHEREAS: The City of Southport (“City”) has previously determined to
undertake a project for the financing of a fire truck, (the “Project”), and the
Finance Officer has now presented a proposal for the financing of such Project.
   BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED, as follows:
   1.   The City hereby determines to finance the Project through Branch
Banking and Trust Company (“BB&T”), in accordance with the proposal dated
September 1, 2017. The amount financed shall not exceed $450,000.00, and the
annual interest rate (in the absence of default or change in tax status) shall
not exceed 1.97%, and the financing term shall not exceed sixty (60) months
from closing.
   2.   All financing contracts and all related documents for the closing of
the financing (the “Financing Documents”) shall be consistent with the
foregoing terms. The Mayor, City Manager, and Finance Director of the City are
hereby authorized and directed to execute and deliver any Financing Documents,
and to take all such further action as they may consider necessary or
desirable, to carry out the financing of the Project as contemplated by the
proposal and this resolution.
   3.   The Finance Director is hereby authorized and directed to hold executed
copies of the Financing Documents until the conditions for the delivery of the
Financing Documents have been completed to such officer's satisfaction. The
Finance Director is authorized to approve changes to any Financing Documents
previously signed by City officers or employees, provided that such changes
shall not substantially alter the intent of such documents or certificates from
the intent expressed in the forms executed by such officers. The Financing
Documents shall be in such final forms as the Finance Officer shall approve,
with the Finance Officer’s release of any Financing Document for delivery
constituting conclusive evidence of such officer's final approval of the
Document’s final form.
   4.   The City shall not take or omit to take any action the taking or
omission of which shall cause its interest payments on this financing to be
includable in the gross income for federal income tax purposes of the
registered owners of the interest payment obligations. The City hereby
designates its obligations to make principal and interest payments under the
Financing Documents as "qualified tax-exempt obligations" for the purpose of
Internal Revenue Code Section 265(b)(3).   
   5.   The City intends that the adoption of this resolution will be a
declaration of the City’s official intent to reimburse expenditures for the
project that is to be financed from the proceeds of the BB&T financing
described above. The City intends that funds that have been advanced, or that
may be advanced, from the City’s general fund, or any other City fund related
to the project, for project costs may be reimbursed from the financing
proceeds.
   6.   All prior actions of City officers in furtherance of the purposes of
this resolution are hereby ratified, approved and confirmed. All other
resolutions (or parts thereof) in conflict with this resolution are hereby
repealed, to the extent of the conflict. This resolution shall take effect
immediately.
Approved this 14th day of September, 2017.
      By: /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor   
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

16.   Resolution Requesting State Grant for a Water Distribution System Asset
Inventory and Assessment Project
   City Planner Lloyd explained that staff plans to resubmit for a $52,000
grant from North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (NCDEQ), Division
of Water Infrastructure in order to assess and digitally map the City’s water
distribution system. He pointed out that the City would be required to match
$13,000 which he indicated is funded in the current budget.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to adopt a Resolution
Requesting State Grant for a Water Distribution System Asset Inventory and
Assessment Project. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
RESOLUTION BY GOVERNING BODY OF APPLICANT
WHEREAS,   The Federal Clean Water Act Amendments of 1987 and the North
Carolina Water Infrastructure Act of 2005 (NCGS 159G) have authorized the
making of loans and grants to aid eligible units of government in financing the
cost of a water distribution system project, and
WHEREAS,   The City of Southport has need for and intends to complete a water
distribution system project described as facilities assessment of the City’s
water distribution system to include system mapping, and
WHEREAS,   The City of Southport intends to request state loan and grant (if
available) assistance for the project,
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, BY THE BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT:
That the City of Southport, the Applicant, will arrange financing for all
remaining costs of the project, if approved for a State (loan or grant) award.
That the Applicant will adopt and place into effect on or before completion of
the project a schedule of fees and charges and other available funds which will
provide adequate funds for proper operation, maintenance, and administration of
the system and the repayment of all principal and interest on the debt.
That the governing body of the Applicant agrees to include in the loan
agreement a provision authorizing the State Treasurer, upon failure of the City
of Southport to make scheduled repayment of the loan, to withhold from the City
of Southport any State funds that would otherwise be distributed to the local
government unit in an amount sufficient to pay all sums then due and payable to
the State as a repayment of the loan.
That the Applicant will provide for efficient operation and maintenance of the
project on completion of construction thereof.
That Bruce Oakley, City Manager, the Authorized Official, and successors so
titled, is hereby authorized to execute and file an application on behalf of
the Applicant with the State of North Carolina for a (loan or grant) to aid in
the construction of the project described above.
That the Authorized Official, and successors so titled, is hereby authorized
and directed to furnish such information as the appropriate State agency may
request in connection with such application or the project: to make the
assurances as contained above; and to execute such other documents as may be
required in connection with the application.
That the Applicant has substantially complied or will substantially comply with
all Federal, State, and local laws, rules, regulations, and ordinances
applicable to the project and to Federal and State grants and loans pertaining
thereto.
Adopted this the 14th day of September, 2017 at Southport, North Carolina.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

D)   Public Comment
   Mr. Jack Palmer, President of the Rivermist POA, on behalf of the residents,
welcomed the Mayor, Board and city officials to the Rivermist Amenity Center.
   Mr. Nick Kern, 415 Burrington Avenue, shared his concerns about The Haven
subdivision, i.e. dead end streets, inadequate turn arounds at the end of
streets, parking space, shared driveways, hardwood trees to be removed, and
proximity to sanitary pump station. He suggested sending the preliminary plat
back to the Planning Board for further review.
   Ms. Gloria Jones, speaking on behalf of Friends of Southport Feral Cats,
recognized approximately 12 members of the group present in the audience and
she read the following:
   “My name is Gloria Jones and I am a lifetime resident of Southport. I am
making this presentation on behalf of the Friends of Southport Ferals. We are
an advocacy organization dedicated to protecting and caring for the Southport
feral cats.
   We would like to make you aware of our organization and solicit your support
of our effort in the TNR program in the Southport Community. The Friends of
Southport Ferals is a non-profit community service organization staffed by
volunteers and funded by donations. We are an action group formed to accomplish
the following goals:
   1.   Identify all feral cat colonies in the Southport area
   2.   Rescue stray/homeless cats and relocate them to a colony
   3.   Recruit volunteers for the following needs:
      maintain/care for colonies
      help with trapping/transporting to Vet
      care for after surgery (usually 24 hours)
      foster/tame/train kittens to be adopted out
   4.   Plan/organize/participate in fundraising
   5.   Educate the community to the need/importance of cats in the community
   6.   Seek low cost vet care
   7.   Establish a 501©3 corporation and apply for grants
   Feral cats (aka, community cats) are the same species as pet cats, but feral
cats are not adoptable. “feral” means that the cats are not socialized to
people and generally avoid contact with humans. Under TNR, these unadoptable
cats are neutered and vaccinated. As a result, the feral cat population
stabilizes and decreases. TNR makes feral cats healthier and ends the breeding
cycle, which means no more kittens. It also ends mating behaviors including
yowling, fighting, spraying, and roaming. Feral cats in TNR programs are just
as healthy as pet cats. They receive vaccinations and ongoing management from
generous volunteers. Under the TNR, cats are humanely trapped, neutered,
vaccinated, ear tipped for identification, and returned to their outdoor homes.
   More and more communities are embracing TNR. Our neighbors in Oak Island
have a well-established society. Humanely trapping, spaying or neutering,
vaccinating and returning cats to their outdoor homes are not only good for the
cats, but it also balances the needs and concerns of the human communities in
which many feral cats live. We want to see the cat population stabilized and
mating behaviors curbed. TNR makes great public policy. It is a purposeful and
balanced approach that helps improve the coexistence of outdoor cats and humans
in their shared communities. This is why so many communities are adopting it.
   The Friends of Southport Ferals meets the 4th Thursday of each month at 4
p.m. at the Southport Library. We extend an invitation to you to attend our
meetings.
   Thank you for your time and consideration.”
   Alderman Mosteller thanked Ms. Jones for bringing the topic to the Board and
a public forum.
   Alderman Poole thanked Ms. Jones for her leadership and establishing the
group. Alderman Poole suggested preparing a resolution in support of the
endeavor for consideration at the Board’s next meeting.
    Per a citizen’s request, Mayor Dove read the following comments into the
record:
   I would like to thank the Southport Board of Aldermen for the resolution
supporting the Lions Vision Month. You are all aware of the many good works
that the Lions Clubs do. The Southport Lions Club has carried the work of
helping to another step. The Southport Lions Club helps with cataract surgeries
for many of our local citizens that need help. The Southport Lions Club has
accepted the challenge that Helen Keller gave to the Lions many years ago to
become, "Knights of the blind in the crusade against darkness".
Thank you board for your support.
Ed Boguskie

Resolution
Southport Lions Celebrating October as Vision Awareness Month
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club was established 72 years ago (1945) by some
of the most prominent citizens in our community; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club continues honor the challenge Helen Keller
issued to the Club in 1929 to become “knights of the blind in the crusade
against darkness”; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club conducts vision screenings every month at the
New Hope Clinic, each year at numerous local schools, and at the Brunswick
County Health Festival; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club has covered the expense of cataract surgery
for needy individuals over the past 5 years; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club collects over 1,700 pairs of glasses each
year and provides assistance to those needing, but unable to afford, eye exams
and the purchase of glasses; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club contributes financial and volunteer support
to over 20 local charities and youth programs; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Lions Club is composed of men and women who dedicate
their time to the betterment of our community and aiding those in need; and
NOW THEREFORE, I, J. V. Dove, Mayor of the City of Southport, NC and the Board
of Aldermen, hereby join the Southport Lions in celebrating October as Vision
Awareness Month.
ADOPTED, this 12th day of October 2017 by the Southport Board of Aldermen.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

CITY OF SOUTHPORT
RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF THE
FRIENDS OF SOUTHPORT FERAL CATS
WHEREAS, there are feral cats (aka, community cats) in the Southport area; and
WHEREAS, “feral” means that the cats are not socialized to people and generally
avoid contact with humans; and 
WHEREAS, the Friends of Southport Feral Cats is an advocacy organization
dedicated to protecting and caring for the Southport feral cats; and
WHEREAS, the Friends of Southport Feral Cats is staffed by volunteers and
funded by donations; and
WHEREAS, the Friends of Southport Feral Cats embrace the Trap/Neuter/Release
(TNR) program that stabilizes the feral cat population and curbs mating
behaviors; and
WHEREAS, the TNR program is being adopted in more and more communities,
including our neighbors in Oak Island.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
goes on record in support of the Friends of Southport Feral Cats.  
DULY RESOLVED THIS THE 9TH DAY OF NOVEMBER 2017.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

Minutes of October 12, 2017 Regular Meeting – approved
2.   Resolution in Support of Cape Fear Regional Bicycle Plan – approved
A RESOLUTION BY THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT ADOPTING THE CAPE FEAR REGIONAL BICYCLE
PLAN
   WHEREAS, The Cape Fear Council of Governments, along with representatives of
the City of Wilmington, and the Towns of Carolina Beach, Kure Beach,
Wrightsville Beach, Belville, Leland, Oak Island, Navassa, New Hanover County,
Brunswick County, Pender County, Cape Fear Public Transportation Authority, the
Wilmington Urban Area MPO, Cape Fear RPO, and the North Carolina Board of
Transportation worked cooperatively for over a year to create the Cape Fear
Regional Bicycle Plan; and
   WHEREAS, cities, towns, and regions around the country are increasingly
recognizing the benefits that bicycle-friendly communities offer in terms of
quality of life to residents and visitors; and
   WHEREAS, there were 487 reported bicycle crashes from 2007-2012 that have
resulted in 254 or more injuries and eight fatalities in the region; and
   WHEREAS, the Plan will improve the quality and safety of bicycling through
new and improved infrastructure, policies and programs, for all types of
bicyclists; and
   WHEREAS, the Plan will increase transportation choices by improving
connectivity of the bicycle network while increasing accessibility to transit
and key destinations through the region; and
   WHEREAS, BlueCross BlueShield North Carolina has stated that every $1
investment in trails for physical activity can save about $3 in medical
expenses; and
   WHEREAS, the Plan will improve health and wellness by increasing access to
bikeways, thereby offering more opportunities for recreation, active
transportation, and physical activity; and
   WHEREAS, a NCDOT study in the neighboring coastal region of the Outer Banks
has demonstrated the annual return on bicycle facility development is
approximately nine times higher than the initial investment; and
   WHEREAS, the Plan promotes bicycle-related tourism and economic development
for communities in Brunswick, Columbus, New Hanover, and Pender Counties as
well as southern Bladen, western Onslow, and southern Sampson Counties; and
   WHEREAS, this Plan included an open and participatory process, with over 500
online mapping and public survey comments, with outreach at dozens of public
events; and
   WHEREAS, 97% of survey respondents said they would bike more often if more
bicycle lanes, trails, and safe roadway crossings were provided for bicyclists;
and
   WHEREAS, it is envisioned that a more bicycle-friendly Cape Fear region
would offer multiple quality of life benefits to residents and visitors by
increasing public safety, supporting health and the environment, expanding
choices for mobility, and diversifying the strength of tourism in local
communities throughout the region; and
   WHEREAS, supporting this resolution does not replace any local plans nor
dedicate any funding, but rather indicates a willingness to support the Plan’s
recommended bicycle projects and programs.
   THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:
   THAT, the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport hereby adopts the Cape
Fear Regional Bicycle Plan.
   This, the 9th day of November, 2017
                           /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk

AGENDA
Discussion of Animal Control Policies
   Alderman Coring stated he had requested the Special Meeting as a fact-
finding mission so the Board could hear and discuss any problems with animal
control practices and procedures within the Police Department. He reported that
he had staff research Board minutes and no reference was found to any past or
current problems. He stated he was shocked by a newspaper article concerning
the recent handling of animals. He added that he had received calls from
citizens and did not know how to address their concerns as he had not been made
aware of the specific incident.
   Alderman Mosteller concurred with Alderman Coring that she was not aware of
recent events. She stated her opinion that the current animal control
procedures are not working and she recommended a thorough review and possible
adjustments to the policies and procedures.
   Alderman Powell stated his understanding that when the animal control/code
enforcement responsibilities were moved under the Police Department
supervision, the position would be an 8:00 – 5:00, 5 days a week job with sole
responsibility to animal control/code enforcement and not running radar and
issuing tickets. He agreed with Alderman Mosteller that changes need to be
made.
   Alderman Adams stated that he has been of the opinion for many years that a
sworn Police Officer assigned as an Animal Control Officer is a misuse of
resources. He contended that the Police Department was delegated responsibility
for animal control in order to get another position in the department. He added
that an Animal Control Officer should be hired on a part-time/on call basis,
and properly trained.
   Alderman Poole expressed appreciation to Alderman Coring for calling the
meeting. She stated she was also unaware of any issues. She recalled an
Emergency Services Committee meeting when there was discussion and a request
made for an estimate to have Brunswick County take over the animal control
function. She added that the Board had authorized the position and budget be
reassigned to the Police Department.
   Alderman Pukenas thanked Alderman Coring for bringing the issue to the
Board’s attention. He stated his opinion that the code, policies and
enforcement needed to be revamped.
   Mayor Dove recalled a time when the Animal Control/Code Enforcement Officer
had been trained and the city provided a holding shelter. He suggested the City
Manager meet with the County to get an estimate for the service and to allocate
training funds for two officers.
   City Manager Oakley indicated had been in contact with the County Manager
and per her suggestion, he was making arrangements to meet with the County
Sheriff. He added that he would find funding for training of two officers and
will compile an operating manual for Animal Control.
   Alderman Adams cautioned going with the County for the services, stating his
viewpoint that the City would lose control. He suggested hiring young retirees
on a part-time basis.
   Alderman Coring questioned where the information had been obtained for the
newspaper article and he questioned if someone had spoken to the press. Chief
Smith stated he had not given any interviews.
Other Administrative Business
   Board consensus to consider employee Christmas bonuses at the December
regular meeting.
   Alderman Powell raised concerns brought to him by citizens of Police
vehicles sighted in the vicinity of Lowe’s Home Improvement, on Long Beach Road
Extension, and NC 87. Mayor Dove pointed out that the city limits reach
Rivermist Subdivision and commercial areas at Dutchman Village and Walgreens
beyond the Duke Energy Progress canal.

   Thomas Lloyd, Planner

A)   Call to Order – 6:00 p.m.
Mayor Dove called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
B)   Invocation
Alderman Powell welcomed everyone and Mayor Dove gave the invocation.
C)   Pledge of Allegiance
   Alderman Powell led the assemblage in the Pledge of Allegiance.
D)   Public Comment
   Mr. John Losch, 310 N. Fodale Avenue, spoke about the old Yacht Basin boat
dock and the monies received from FEMA for repairs of damages incurred from
Hurricane Matthew. He suggested involving Southport Marina and raising rental
rates to facilitate the repairs. He stated his dismay that dredging and repairs
would not come to fruition until October 2018. He also spoke about the city’s
animal control policy.
   Ms. Francesca Slaughter, 6243 Cottage Creek Road, board member for Rescue
Animals Community Effort (R.A.C.E.) spoke to the Board about an issue raised in
a recent State Port Pilot editorial alleging cruel treatment of stray, injured
and lost animals picked up by members of the Southport Police Department. Ms.
Slaughter spoke of her efforts to get answers regarding the truth of the
allegations and her ultimate review of requested police reports. She talked
about the results of her inquiry, pointed out that Southport is an animal-
friendly town, and her opinion that the city’s animal control program is flawed
and being carried out by untrained individuals. Ms. Slaughter implored the
Board to allow Brunswick County Sheriff’s Office Animal Protection Services to
take over the city’s operation. By a show of hands, most of those in attendance
agreed with Ms. Slaughter.
   Mr. Buddy Barnes, 425 W. West Street, expressed pride and appreciation to
have served as an Alderman alongside Aldermen Poole and Adams. He thanked the
outgoing Aldermen for their service.
   Ms. Jill Denmon, 610 Caswell Avenue, Secretary of Friends of the Southport
Feral Cats, spoke. She pointed out that the city’s animal regulations are
“unclear as to the well-being of a feral or a stray” cat. She noted that
Southport does not have a holding facility or shelter so officers have to
transport an animal to the Brunswick County Animal Shelter which requires more
time than an officer can spend. Ms. Denmon suggested a partnership between the
County and City along with having a veterinarian who could treat and board
injured or sick animals until they could be taken to the shelter.
   Mr. Jason Robbins, 506 W. Brunswick, expressed his dismay upon hearing the
allegations of cruelty to animals. He urged the Board to stop any cruelty and
to pursue public help if fundraising is needed.
   Rev. J. Lowe Davis, 504 W. Brunswick Street, spoke on the animal control
issue and referenced scripture.
   Mr. Peter MacQueen III, Willow Moss Way, spoke about his previous
involvement with a committee designated to revise the Animal Control Ordinance.
He noted that the revisions were never adopted and suggested revisiting the
work.

   Alderman Pukenas read the resolution into the record
A RESOLUTION HONORING THE 102nd BIRTHDAY
OF ROBERT C. RUARK, JR.
WHEREAS, Robert C. Ruark,, Jr. was born in Wilmington on December 29, 1915; and
WHEREAS, Ruark achieved international success as a newspaper and magazine
columnist and author; and
WHEREAS, Ruark spent a great deal of his childhood visiting his maternal
grandparents, Capt. Ned and Lottie Adkins at their home in Southport; and
WHEREAS, Among Ruark’s works were the beloved book, The Old Man and the Boy; a
semi-autographical work defined by the philosophical musings of his
grandfather; and
WHEREAS, Ruark’s success brought much attention to Southport which continues to
this day.
BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport, North
Carolina, that the City of Southport hereby designates December 29, 2017 as
“Robert C. Ruark, Jr.” day in his honor.
Adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen in regular session, December 14,
2017.
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

Call to Order - 9:00 a.m.
   Mayor Dove called the meeting to order.
Invocation
   Fire Chief Drew gave the invocation.
Introduction of Chris May
   Chris May, Executive Director, Cape Fear Council of Governments gave a brief
synopsis of his background and experience.
Process and Ground Rules
   Mr. May explained his approach to guiding the Board through exercises that
will pinpoint their five (5) priority projects to pursue. He pointed out that
Board members are representatives and stewards for the people.
Expectation of Roles Exercise
   Mr. May guided the Board through an exercise which highlighted the desired
attributes of a Mayor, an Alderman and City Manager.
Mayor Attributes
   Knowledge of City and Municipal Government      Connected to People
   Accessible                  Team Leader
   Communicator (both ways)            Understanding
   Responsive & Transparent            Delegation      
   Brings all viewpoints to the table for discussion
   Spokesperson for the City
Alderman Attributes
    Patience         Good Listener      Responsive
   Work for Common Good   Open-Minded      Strive to Understand Issues
   Negotiator – Compromise            Honesty & Integrity
   Ability to Communicate Vision
   Working Knowledge of City Regulations, Policies, etc.   
City Manager Attributes
   Educated in Municipal Government         Team Leader & Motivator (Coach)
   Supportive – Helpful – Advocate            Organized – Organizational Skills
   Good Communicator – Listener            Resourceful
   Honesty & Integrity               Visionary
   Being Able to Bring People to the Table         Accessible & Visable

   Fire Chief Drew provided the following update on the Brunswick County Fire
Commission:
   The Brunswick County Fire Commission is comprised of 19 members that were
appointed by the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners. I am currently the
Southport appointee, until July 2019. At that time the Mayor or Mayor Pro Tem
will take my spot on the Board. Currently, the Board is meeting every other
month, unless a special meeting is called. The Organizational meeting was held
in the month of October 2017. At that meeting a Chairman & Co Chair was elected
by the members of the commission.
   This group is an advisory board. Its mission is to make advisory
recommendations to the Brunswick County Board of Commissioner on fire
protection and emergency services. They can recommend funding mechanisms
including fees and or tax rates, and develop and provide overview of all
service operations regulations and guidelines for all Brunswick County Fire
Protection services.
   At the last 2 meetings, the main discussion has been performance standards
for fire departments. The commission set a sub-committee that has drafted a set
of performance standards on how fire departments are to respond and train
members. The draft was presented at last month’s meeting, and has not been
presented to the County Fire Chief’s for review. A special meeting will be held
this month to discuss the standards, making revisions or changes, vote on them
and send them to the Commissioners for approval. It has been alluded to in the
meeting, that fire departments that do not meet these standards, would not be
able to receive their fire fee funding.
   At the last 2 meetings, the main discussion has been performance standards
for fire departments. The commission set a sub-committee that has drafted a set
of performance standards on how fire departments are to respond and train
members. The draft was presented at last month’s meeting, and has not been
presented to the County Fire Chief’s for review. A special meeting will be held
this month to discuss the standards, making revisions or changes, vote on them
and send them to the Commissioners for approval. It has been alluded to in the
meeting, that fire departments that do not meet these standards, would not be
able to receive their fire fee funding.
   I have been contacted this week alone, by 8 County Fire Chiefs in regards to
these standards, and their response has been in a negative manner. As a
representative of the commission I have voiced my concerns publically at the
commission meetings and by email as requested by the commission. I am staying
very aware of the happenings of this committee. There has been some rumored
talk of a County Fire Department, but majority of the fire chiefs are not in
favor of this talk. A meet of fire chiefs has been called, and is scheduled for
late this month. The commission will meet again this month to discuss the
performance standard, and I will keep the city manager and the Board updated
with any new information. I will entertain any questions, or comments that you
may have.

Resolution of Continued Opposition of Seismic Surveying and Stated Opposition
to Oil and Gas Offshore Exploration and Drilling Off the Coast of North
Carolina
Whereas, the City of Southport is committed to being a sound steward of the
unique coastal environment, recognizing the value of the maritime forest,
estuaries, marshes and pristine waterfronts in Southport and other Brunswick
County coastal communities; and
Whereas, North Carolina waters provide some of the finest fish and shellfish
products in the world and seismic oil and gas exploration along the US Mid-
Atlantic and South Atlantic coasts is viewed by the marine science community to
pose an unacceptable risk of serious harm to marine life at the species and
population levels. Particularly at risk is the North Atlantic right whale, one
of the most endangered whales on Earth. Scientists warn the full extent of
impact by proposed seismic air gun activities will not be understood until long
after the harm occurs; and
Whereas, the Aldermen of the City of Southport have evaluated the validity of
job and revenue claims by the offshore drilling industry against the 2016
statistics of $543 million in tourism revenue for Brunswick County and the
41,000 plus tourists that visited the Southport Visitor Center, proving that
tourism has and continues to be the backbone of the City of Southport and
Brunswick County economies; and
Whereas, in 2016, the Aldermen of the City of Southport reaffirmed its earlier
opposition to seismic surveying and opposed the proposal by the U.S. Department
of the Interior to allow exploration and drilling of oil/gas resources in the
Mid and South Atlantic Ocean regions, such opposition resulted in the Atlantic
Ocean Outer Continental Shelf of the United States being withdrawn from federal
energy leasing program; and
Whereas, Presidential Executive Order 13795, “Implementing an America-First
Offshore Energy Strategy”, issued in April 2017 intends to reverse limits on
offshore seismic exploration and drilling in the Atlantic Ocean and reduce
environmental protection regulations related to offshore drilling, it is
critical the Aldermen of the City of Southport express continued opposition to
any proposals that would permit seismic surveying and offshore drilling for
oil/gas resources off the coast of North Carolina.
Be it Resolved the Aldermen of the City of Southport stand united with North
Carolina Governor Roy Cooper, governors of neighboring coastal states,
communities, residents, and visitors who oppose seismic air gun activities and
offshore drilling for oil/gas resources in the Atlantic Ocean.
Be it Further Resolved the Aldermen of the City of Southport call upon the U.S.
Secretary of the Interior to exempt the coastal zone and Outer Continental
Shelf of North Carolina from seismic oil/gas exploration and offshore drilling.
Adopted this 8th day of February, 2018
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk

5.   Public Hearing; Zoning Text Amendment ZA 17-1214-01, Planned Residential
Development (PRD) 50 Foot Setbacks
   Alderman Sharkey motioned, second by Alderman Powell to go into Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   City Planner Lloyd explained the proposed zoning text amendment. He stated
that he had received numerous complaints about the 50 ft. PRD setback line in
Forest Oaks, The Ridge and Southport Way. He pointed out that the setback
requirement made one vacant lot unbuildable and other lots unable to build
accessory structures. He stated that the proposed text amendment would clear up
the issue; the Planning Board reviewed the amendment and found it consistent
with the CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommends that the Board of Aldermen
approve the text amendment.
   No one from the public spoke.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to close Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
6.   Consideration of Text Amendment ZA 17-1214-01, PRD 50 Foot setbacks
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to approve the text
amendment. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
AN ORDINANCE APPROVING A TEXT AMENDMENT TO THE UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modification and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, City Staff, in conjunction with the Planning Board, has prepared
the proposed amendment to Article 11 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly considered this matter and find
the proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance to be consistent
with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommend its approval;
and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on February 8, 2018 before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby find that the
proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with the
Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is
reasonable and in the public interest in that it will make the setbacks more
uniform with similarly zoned land and it will increase the enjoyment and use of
the properties; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
attached amendment to Article 11 of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby approved and adopted.
This, the 8th day of February, 2018                  City of Southport
                           /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

7.   Public Hearing; Zoning Text Amendment ZA 17-0809-01, Tree Preservation
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Spencer to go into Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   City Planner Lloyd explained the proposed zoning text amendment. Planner
Lloyd’s agenda packet memorandum included in its entirety:
   Background
   “For some time, the Forestry Committee has worked on creating a text
amendment for adding tree preservation    standards to the Unified Development
Ordinance (UDO), primarily to be used during the development process. The goal
of    the text amendment is to have an Article in the UDO that would manage and
preserve the City’s tree canopy during the    development process. This
management will take the form of tree preservation on properties when possible,
and mitigation    through the replanting of trees when others are removed. The
Committee went to the Planning Board at the August 17th    meeting. Over the
next few months, they received feedback from staff, the Planning Board, as well
as some comments    from builders, developers and concerned citizens at two
Public Workshops (held at the October 19th and November 16th    Planning Board
meetings). At the November 16th meeting, the Planning Board voted to forward
the text amendment on to    the Board of Aldermen for review. Due to the
holidays, Alderman Mosteller and staff thought it would be best to hold the
   text amendment and review it at the February meeting. The public hearing for
this text amendment has been duly    advertised as required by NC    General
Statutes.
   Request
   The Forestry Committee is requesting a text amendment to amend the Unified
Development Ordinance by adding an    additional article in the UDO for Tree
Preservation.
   Article 27. Tree Preservation
   Amend:
   Add the amendment attached.
   Staff Recommendation
   Staff advises that the Board of Aldermen thoroughly review this addition to
the Unified Development Ordinance and gain feedback from the public. This is a
significant amendment and should be thoroughly considered. Staff also
recommends that    the Board of Aldermen have the City Attorney review the
ordinance to make sure that there are no potential legal issues that could
arise.”
   Alderman Mosteller thanked the Forestry Committee and City Planner for their
efforts creating the proposed tree preservation ordinance. She gave a brief
overview of the 15 month process preparing the draft proposed ordinance. Noting
that the first ordinance protecting the city’s trees was passed in 1890, she
emphasized that the trees are a valuable and important asset in the city and
Southport has a rich history recognizing that importance. She pointed out that
the city enjoys a 50 – 55% canopy coverage and the ordinance’s goal is to
establish a minimum standard of 40% canopy coverage. She talked about recent
housing developments and that the UDO did not have tree protection measures in
place for building projects. She noted that the proposed ordinance had been
presented to “subject matter experts” including the UNC School of Government,
city attorney and Urban Forestry Specialist Sam Marshall with NC Cooperative
Extension Brunswick County office.
   City Attorney Isenberg stated he had reviewed the proposed Ordinance and
made minor changes relating to penalties and property notice. He asked the City
Planner if a consistency statement had been made by the Planning Board. City
Planner Lloyd responded that the Planning Board did not make a consistency
statement.
   Noting the Ordinance would encourage smart design consistent with the
character of Southport, Mr. Fred Fiss, 206 N. Atlantic Avenue, and a
residential builder, stated his support for the proposed Tree Ordinance.
   Ms. Suzanne Hunt, 316 W. St. George Street, shared her experience with a
neighbor clearing their lot of all trees. She supported the proposed Tree
Ordinance to prevent clear cutting of lots.
   Stating she had attended several Forestry Committee meetings, Ms. Mary Ellen
Poole, 217 Willis Drive, thanked the Forestry Committee for their work on the
proposed Tree Ordinance and she expressed her support of it.
   Mr. Larry McCracken, 4004 Norseman Loop, spoke about multiple Live Oak trees
in the undeveloped parcel next to the Rivermist entrance. He stated his hope
that an ordinance could be put in place to protect the trees and that the area
could be city park.
   Ms. Betty Timberlake, 118 N. Atlantic, lifelong member of the Southport
Forestry Committee reminded everyone that the Committee has planted over 300
Live Oak trees along Southport streets. She provided a letter from her neighbor
and asked that the comments be a part of the official minutes.
   “To the members of the Committee for Trees in Southport:
   First off, thank you for serving and having the interest in our community!
   As a resident here for 30+ years, and a homeowner in the old section, I have
been a “proud steward” of 3 giant oaks since 1983. Passers-by often pause/or
stop and point and admire their stately beauty. I have been honored – twice! To
have my home on the Christmas Tour – and I give the trees in the front “huge
credit”!
   It has been brought to my attention that this Committee in considering some
revision in the local ordinance for trees that now    exists. May I please make
a comment or suggestion?
   We know and recognize that the beauty of our community would be severely
diminished if we didn’t have our ancient oaks! If you as Committee are seeking
to protect and preserve these local trees on city and private properties alike,
may I suggest the following for discussion?:
Choosing a qualified arborist for a (twice) yearly inspection of “city-wide”
oaks to monitor them and prescribe pruning/care as necessary.
Revision of cutting/removal permits to not allow any further damage or over
development where trees are located (this may point to architectural revision
in some cases)
Establishing a “Celebration of Oaks” to involve our citizens (especially our
young people and new comers) to educate them and inform them of our
irreplaceable assets we have in our magnificent trees. (written information and
field trips?)
You are serving Southport as you are on this committee. You were chosen or
appointed because of your awareness of the need to protect our unique natural
assets here in Southport. Surely this lovely coastal community deserves its
heritage and beauty to be valued and continue into the future!
Respectfully requested,
Elizabeth (Betsy) Isley
111 N. Atlantic Avenue
Southport, NC 28461
