      ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk
AGENDA
10.   Consideration; Solid Waste Collection, Transportation and Disposal
Agreement with Waste Industries, LLC
   City Manager Oakley stated that the renewal of the contract with Waste
Industries was the same as past contracts with one change; yard waste pick-up
is not included and would be privately contracted out. He indicated he would
bring a yard waste contract to the Board for consideration at a future meeting.
   Alderman Sharkey asked if Waste Industries would provide receptacles for
recycling at those city locations that did not already have them.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to approve the Solid
Waste Collection, Transportation and Disposal Agreement with Waste Industries,
Inc. Unanimous vote; motion carried.   
11.   Consideration; Southport Marina, Inc. Letter of Intent, Southport Yacht
Basin – Dock Extension
   City Manager Oakley gave a brief status overview of the positions of various
regulatory entities regarding the rebuilding of the City Boat Dock;
Working through review with Coastal Area Management Act (CAMA) Army Corps of
Engineers will not permit removal of pilings and rebuild as is – prefers a
floating dock which CAMA has denied CAMA may grant a variance
Marsh owned by Southport Marina who would have Riparian Rights Ongoing
discussions with Southport Marina about potential partnering on the project.
   City Manager Oakley referenced the Letter of Intent (LOI) provided in the
agenda packet that sets a mutual understanding between the City of Southport
and Southport Marina with respect to the potential demolition, dredging and
reconstruction of the City Boat Dock. He emphasized that the LOI was not
binding.
   City Attorney Isenberg pointed out revisions suggested by Alderman Pukenas;
   First sentence, addition of language: “to negotiate in good faith and
agreement….”
   Item #14, Confidentiality; Exclusivity of Dealing.
       Addition of language:   “until such time as a final decision is rendered
by the                   CAMA permit and applicable government agencies”
   City Manager Oakley stated that if a partnership was made with Southport
Marina, the CAMA application would be a joint effort.
   Alderman Pukenas asked what benefits the City would get from a partnership
with Southport Marina. City Manager Oakley stated that parking and Southport
Marina amenities would be available, a walkway from the Marina to the dock
would be built and maintenance and management would be performed by Marina
staff.
   Alderman Pukenas asked why the LOI needed to be considered by the Board at
this time. City Manager Oakley stated the LOI needed to be considered due to
the schedule for dredging in November, the 90 day permitting process that CAMA
has indicated it would deny the permit, a 90 day period to apply for a CAMA
Variance and the hope to have the permit in place prior to dredging.
   City Manager Oakley pointed out that the City had received funds from FEMA,
for damages incurred during Hurricane Matthew, towards construction of a
floating dock.
   Based on feedback received from citizens, Alderman Sharkey stated her hope
that the LOI could be simplified without reference to reimbursement of cost,
income and management.    
   Alderman Powell emphasized the urgency of getting the project permitted, the
potential to lose the dredging and having to absorb the entire cost of dredging
vs. 95% of the cost being absorbed by the Corps of Engineers.
   Noting that a lot of the city’s infrastructure has fallen by the wayside and
the city is now trying to catch up, Alderman Coring expressed his opinion that
a partnership with Southport Marina could be mutually beneficial. He stated he
wants to assure continued public use of the City’s L dock and he believes a
detailed plan can be worked out.
   Acknowledging that Southport Marina has been a good corporate citizen in
Southport, Alderman Mosteller pointed out that the LOI obligates the City to
reimburse the Marina for construction of the dock, including interest; that the
Marina will manage the City Dock and when the loan is paid in full, the City
will receive 50% of the slip rental fees based on Marina rates. She stated her
opinion that the City could obtain a loan, collect rents to pay for the loan
and she asked the Board to consider creating a water infrastructure fund
dedicated for maintenance. Emphasizing that Southport is a historical
waterfront town, she stressed that the Dock belongs to the citizens of
Southport and needs to remain accessible to all citizens.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to approve the Letter of
Intent with Southport Marina.
   Discussion
   Responding to a query by Alderman Spencer, City Manager Oakley stated that
the existing structure could not be removed until the CAMA permit is in place.
   City Attorney Isenberg pointed out that approving the LOI begins
negotiations of a potential contract and the City is obligated to negotiate in
good faith.
   Alderman Spencer stated that the City needs to move forward with the LOI in
the interest of getting the Yacht Basin dredged.
   Alderman Mosteller raised concerns about filing for a CAMA permit without a
contract for reconstruction. City Manager Oakley stated that having a
construction contract had no effect on the permit.
   Alderman Pukenas emphasized LOI Item 15 which stipulates the LOI shall not
be deemed or constitute a legally binding obligation.
   Vote:   Ayes:   Aldermen Powell, Coring, Sharkey, Spencer, Pukenas
      Nay:   Alderman Mosteller
   Motion carried 5-1
12.   Consideration; Agreement with NCDOT for Ownership of Common Sewer Lines
Along NC 211 Widening Project
   Public Works Director Fox reported that staff had met with NCDOT regarding
the NC 211 widening project and the relocation of nine (9) private pump
stations. He stated that NCDOT has agreed to bear all costs of design and
relocation of the stations per the Utility Relocation Agreement approved on the
Consent Agenda. Director Fox stated the Agreement requires the City to accept
the gravity lines after completion of the NC 211 widening project.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to accept the
wastewater gravity lines per Transportation Improvement Program (TIP) R-5021,
Element #41582.2.1 after completion of the project. Unanimous vote; motion
carried.    
13.   Side by Side Utility Cart for Right-of-Way, Cemetery & Parks Maintenance
   
   Director Fox explained a request to purchase a utility cart to be used for
right-of-way, cemeteries and parks maintenance. He stated that a gasoline model
is quoted vs. electric as representatives were unable to guarantee a battery

   Responding to a query from Alderman Mosteller, Director Fox stated he would
find out what the warranty period on the vehicle would be.
   Alderman Pukenas motioned, second by Alderman Sharkey to approve the
purchase. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
14.   Consideration; Mandatory Load Management Switches on New Construction
   Ellie Pittenger, Electrical Superintendent, reviewed a comparative and
factual study of the City‘s Load Management program (complete report on file in
the Clerk’s office). He emphasized that the “peak” one hour period of one day
during each month is charged at a rate of $18.80/kW and scheduled to increase
to $21.94/kW. That charge for January, 2018 was $305,780.58. Mr. Pittenger
pointed out that of 2,922 commercial and residential Southport electrical
customers, only 803 are on some form of load management. He stated his opinion
that additional participation in the program and mandatory load management
switches on new construction would greatly reduce the City’s energy charges.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to adopt an Ordinance
Amending Chapter 19, Article V, Section 19-186. Load Management.
   Discussion
   Noting that a 100% participation in load management would save a customer
32% on their energy usage, Alderman Mosteller suggested distributing an
informational flier and holding workshops to promote participation.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 19, ARTICLE V, OF THE SOUTHPORT CITY CODE
   BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of Southport that
Chapter 19, Article V, of the Southport City Code, is hereby amended by adding
the following section:
ARTICLE V. ELECTRICAL SERVICE
Sec. 19-186.   Load Management.
(a)   The building contractor or his plumbing or electrical sub-contractor
shall place a Load Management switch purchased from the City on all Electric
water heaters 40 gallons or larger, as long as they are no more than 9kW,
installed in new residential structures before a Certificate of Occupancy is
issued.
(b)   The building contractor or his HVAC or electrical sub-contractor shall
place Load Management switches purchased from the City on all compressor and
heat strip circuits on all standard 240V Electric Heat Pumps or HVAC units
installed in new residential structures (“mini-split” heat pump units are
exempt) before a Certificate of Occupancy is issued.
   This the 12th day of April, 2018.            City of Southport
                     
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

NATIONAL SAFE BOATING WEEK
PROCLAMATION
For nearly 90 million Americans, boating continues to be a popular recreational
activity. From coast to coast, and everywhere in between, people are taking to
the water and enjoying time together boating, sailing, paddling and fishing.
During National Safe Boating Week, the U.S. Coast Guard and its federal, state,
and local safe boating partners encourage all boaters to explore and enjoy
America’s beautiful waters responsibly.
Safe boating begins with preparation. The Coast Guard estimates that human
error accounts for 70 percent of all boating accidents and that life jacket
could prevent more than 80 percent of boating fatalities. Through basic boating
safety procedures – carrying lifesaving emergency distress and communications
equipment, wearing life jackets, attending safe boating courses, participating
in free boat safety checks, and staying sober when navigating – we can help
ensure boaters on America’s coastal, inland, and offshore waters stay safe
throughout the season.
National Safe Boating Week is observed to bring attention to important life-
saving tips for recreational boaters so that they can have a safer, more fun
experience out on the water throughout the year.
•Whereas, on average, 650 people die each year in boating-related accidents in
the U.S.; approximately 80 percent of these are fatalities caused by drowning;
and
•Whereas, the vast majority of these accidents are caused by human error or
poor judgment and not by the boat, equipment or environmental factors; and
•Whereas, a significant number of boaters who lose their lives by drowning each
year would be alive today had they worn their life jackets.
Therefore, I, J. V. Dove, Mayor, do hereby support the goals of the Safe
Boating Campaign and proclaim May 19-25, 2018 as National Safe Boating Week and
the start of the year-round effort to promote safe boating
Given under my signature and the seal of:            /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor,
Southport, North Carolina
Patrick Ford, USCG: Boatswain’s Mate Second Class
Kim Curry, Flotilla Commander, USCG Auxiliary Flotilla 10-05
at the City of: Southport, North Carolina
this day of: May 10, 2018

AGENDA 
5.   Report: Cape Fear Regional Jetport
   Airport Commission Member Flick Guerrina thanked the Board for appointing
him to the Commission and he introduced Howie Franklin, Chief of the Cape Fear
Regional Jetport.
   Mr. Franklin gave a history of the airport and spoke about the economic
impact for the area. Noting that the area is the 2nd fastest growing location
in the country, he stated that the airport has more air traffic than Hilton
Head, $5M in funded projects to improve the airport, eight (8) active
businesses on the airport, largest amount of executive jets in the state, and
4th busiest airport in the state per FAA. He displayed the plans for a new
multi-use environmentally friendly terminal building and examples of aircraft
using the airport. He emphasized that the economic impact for 2016 was $215M
and that for every $1 put in aviation there is a $19 return.
6.   Public Hearing; Water & Wastewater System Development Fee Analysis
   Mr. Jim Bourey, McGill Associates, summarized House Bill 436 amendment to
G.S. 162A Article 8, System Development Fees (SDF), to provide for uniform
authority to implement system development fees for public water and sewer
systems in North Carolina. He stated the legislature established a defined
methodology on how system development fees can be calculated and the City
retained McGill Associates to complete a system development fee analysis. Mr.
Bourey indicated the study, website posting and public hearing had to be
completed by June 30.
   Mr. Mike Ballard, McGill Associates, explained the methodology used for
determining SDF and he walked the Board through the study and the resultant
development fee ceiling of $17,547.20 for a three-bedroom single-family
dwelling. (Complete study on file in the Clerk’s office).
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to Open Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Mr. Bourey responded to a citizen’s query about the $17,547.20 maximum fee
and if that fee would be paid by developers. He explained that the larger a
single family dwelling, the larger the fee to provide water and sewer services
which would be paid at time of subdivision review, building permit issuance or
at Certificate of Occupancy.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to close Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
7.   Public Hearing; Flood Maps
   City Planner Lloyd explained that in order to comply with the minimum
criteria of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and per notification by
the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the city is required to move
forward with adoption of the new Flood Insurance Study (FIS) and the associated
Flood Insurance Risk Maps (FIRM) effective August 28, 2018. Mr. Lloyd reported
that the Planning Board had found that the adoption of the FIS and FIRM is
consistent with the 2015 CAMA Core Land Use Plan and along with staff,
recommends adoption of the FIS and FIRM by the Board of Aldermen.
   Alderman Coring motioned, second by Alderman Sharkey to Open Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   There was no public comment.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to close Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
8.   Consideration; Adopt Flood Maps
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to adopt the Flood
Insurance Study (FIS) and the Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRM). Unanimous vote;
motion carried.
ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA, TO ADOPT THE EFFECTIVE
FLOOD INSURANCE STUDY (FIS) AND ITS ACCOMPANYING FLOOD INSURANCE RATE MAPS
(FIRM)
WHEREAS, the City of Southport has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance with
a Flood Damage Prevention Article to control land development within the
Special Flood Hazard Area; and
WHEREAS, in order to comply with the minimum criteria of the National Flood
Insurance Program (NFIP) [44 CFR 60.3(d) and (e)] and NC Session Law 2000-150,
Senate Bill 1341 [NCGS 143.- 215.51-.61] the City of Southport must adopt the
effective Flood Insurance Study (FIS) and its accompanying Flood Insurance Rate
Maps (FIRM); and
WHEREAS, at the duly held meeting on April 19, 2018 the Planning Board found
the new flood maps to be consistent with the CAMA Land Use Plan and recommended
approval of the proposed adoption of the new flood maps; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport conducted a duly advertised public hearing on
the draft amendment to the effective Flood Insurance Study (FIS) and its
accompanying Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRM) at the Regular Meeting of the
Board of Aldermen on May 10, 2018.
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing response
and recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby finds that the proposed
adoption of the effective Flood Insurance Study (FIS) and its accompanying
Flood Insurance Rate Maps is consistent with the Southport 2015 CAMA Core Land
Use Plan and is reasonable and in the public interest because they will (i)
promote public health, safety, and general welfare in the community by
establishing provisions to minimize public and private losses due to flood
conditions within flood prone areas; (ii) they are consistent with Management
Goal 2A of the CAMA Land Use Plan, (iii) they are consistent with Policies 51
and 52 of the CAMA Land Use Plan, and (iv) the adoption of the new flood maps
is necessary to comply with the minimum criteria of the National Flood
Insurance Program (NFIP); and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen that the effective
Flood Insurance Study (FIS) and its accompanying Flood Insurance Rate Maps
(FIRM) is hereby approved and adopted.
Adopted this the 10th day of May 2018
                        City of Southport
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk

ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF SOUTHPORT, NORTH CAROLINA, TO AMEND ARTICLE 21 OF THE
UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance with a Flood
Damage Prevention Article to control land development within the Special Flood
Hazard Area within both the City’s incorporated areas and within its
extraterritorial area; and
WHEREAS, in order to comply with the minimum criteria of the National Flood
Insurance Program (NFIP) [44 CFR 60.3(d) and (e)] and NC Session Law 2000-150,
Senate Bill 1341 [NCGS 143.- 215.51-.61] the City of Southport must amend
Article 21 of the Unified Development Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, at the duly held meeting on April 19, 2018 the Planning Board found
this proposed amendment to be consistent with the CAMA Land Use Plan and
recommended approval of the proposed amendment to Article 21 of the Unified
Development Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, the City of Southport conducted a duly advertised public hearing on
the proposed amendment to Article 21 of the Unified Development Ordinance at
the Regular Meeting of the Board of Aldermen on May 10, 2018.
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing response
and recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby finds that the proposed text
amendment of Article 21 of the Unified Development Ordinance is consistent with
the Southport 2015 CAMA Core Land Use Plan and is reasonable and in the public
interest because the amendment will (i) promote public health, safety, and
general welfare in the community by establishing provisions to minimize public
and private losses due to flood conditions within flood prone areas; (ii) the
amendment is consistent with Management Goal 2A of the CAMA Land Use Plan,
(iii) the amendment is consistent with Policies 51 and 52 of the CAMA Land Use
Plan, and (iv) the amendment is necessary to comply with the minimum criteria
of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP); and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the City of Southport Board of Aldermen that
Article 21 of the City of Southport Unified Development Ordinance is hereby
amended as follows on Exhibit A attached.

A RESOLUTION AFFIRMING SUPPORT OF A TOLL RATE INCREASE FOR THE SOUTHPORT-FORT
FISHER FERRY
WHEREAS ,  the Southport-Fort Fisher Ferry is in need of additional revenue to
pay for capital improvements to vessels on its route; and
WHEREAS, in 2013, the North Carolina General Assembly mandated that new capital
improvements to the ferry system be funded through the Strategic Transportation
Initiative (STI) or by revenue-raising initiatives such as tolling,
advertising, and concessions; and
WHEREAS ,  the North Carolina Board of Transportation approved a tolling
methodology but has taken no action to increase fares on the Southport-Fort
Fisher Ferry; and
WHEREAS ,  the Southport-Fort Fisher Ferry is currently tolled and all fares
collected fund new ferry vessels and ferry improvements that directly benefit
the Southport-Fort Fisher Ferry; and
WHEREAS ,  in 2014, the NCDOT proposed to retain the same fares for
pedestrians, bicycles, and motorcycles but increase the fares for vehicles less
than 20 feet from $5 to $7, between 20 feet and 40 feet from $10 to $14 and
greater than 40 feet from $15 to $28; and
WHEREAS ,  there is no proposed change in the price of a Commuter Pass, thereby
protecting regular users from increased costs; and
WHEREAS, all fares will be deposited in an account designated for ferry
replacement vessels on the Southport-Fort Fisher Ferry route, per NCGS §136-82
(d); and
WHEREAS ,  public comments at a February 18, 2014 meeting at Southport City
Hall were supportive of the increase; and
WHEREAS ,  on March 22, 2014, May 20, 2016, and August 18, 2017 the Cape Fear
Rural Planning Organization RTAC adopted a resolution in support of increasing
the fares on the Southport-Fort Fisher Ferry; and
NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that the City of Southport Board of Aldermen
hereby affirms its support for the proposed ferry toll increase for the
Southport-Fort Fisher Ferry.
Adopted this, the 14th of June 2018.                City of Southport
                           /s/ J.V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk
STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA
COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK
CONTRACT AND AGREEMENT
THIS Contract and Agreement made and entered into this first day of September,
2018 by and between The County of Brunswick, a North Carolina body corporate
and politic, hereinafter called County, and the City of Southport, a political
subdivision of the State of North Carolina, Brunswick County, North
Carolina, hereinafter called Fire Department;
WITNESSETH
THAT WHEREAS, N.C.G.S. Chapter 153A authorizes Counties to enter into
contracts, and to make annual appropriations of funds; and
WHEREAS, N.C.G.S. Chapter 160A authorizes Municipalities to enter into
contracts; and
WHEREAS, the County collects Fire Fees from its citizens in order to provide
fire protection services to those citizens; and
WHEREAS, the County chooses to contract with Fire Department in order to
provide those fire protection services, and for mutual assistance in fire
protection services in order to increase fire defenses and to provide reserves
needed to assure the community of adequate protection;
NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the mutual promises and agreements
herein contained, and pursuant to the general power and authority of the Fire
Department to furnish firefighting services, and the general power and
authority of the County to provide fire protection for its inhabitants and
owners of property, the parties hereto mutually contract and agree as follows:
GENERAL DUTIES
The Fire Department agrees to furnish and provide continuing fire protection
and related services to all properties lying within its designated
fire response territorial limits, upon the call of any resident,
property owner, other person, or agency. The City shall serve the area
including the Southport Fire District as well as the Yaupon Beach Fire
District.
All firefighting equipment, related services equipment, and personnel
necessary and proper for the performance of this contract and Agreement
shall be provided by the Fire Department at its sole cost and expense, and all
persons engaged in fighting fires or in related
services pursuant to the provisions of this Contract and Agreement shall be
subject to the exclusive control, direction and supervision, of the Fire
Department. Except as noted herein below, the County shall not have any right
or power with respect to the employment, control, direction, supervision,
suspension or discharge of any person who may engage in firefighting or related
services imposed by the provisions of the Contract and Agreement upon the Fire
Department in furnishing firefighting and related services to the County for
the benefit of its residents and property owners.
MUTUAL AID
THAT WHEREAS, the General Assembly of North Carolina did enact into law an
act to authorize mutual aid assistance between fire departments
whereby full authority may be exercised for fire departments to send
firefighters and apparatus beyond the territorial limits which they normally
serve, said act having been codified as G.S. 58-83-1;
WHEREAS, the purpose of this agreement is to provide each
department within the county through this contract, a pre-determined plan by
which each of the departments might render automatic aid or mutual aid
to the other in the case of conflagration, holocaust, civil disorder, or
natural disaster, any of which demand fire services to a degree beyond
the existing capabilities of a department;
WHEREAS, it is deemed to be in the public interest
for the departments within the county to enter into an agreement for mutual
assistance in fire protection and in order to increase fire defenses and
to assure proper fire control, as well as providing reserves needed
to assure the community of adequate protection;
WHEREAS, by action of the (Governing Body) of the Department this agreement for
automatic aid or mutual aid assistance was duly authorized;
NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein by the
COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK and the CITY OF SOUTHPORT , it is hereby agreed as follows:
Upon notification by another fire department, Emergency Management Department,
Fire Marshal, or other agency that an emergency does in fact exist and Fire
Department's automatic aid or mutual aid is needed, the Chief  (hereafter  also
including any other fire officer or person delegated that authority by said
Chief) shall have the implicit authority to order such available apparatus,
equipment, and personnel as may be required to respond to assist the requesting
agency. After determining that the automatic aid or mutual aid request may be
honored without impairing the Fire Department’s capacity to provide protection
within its own jurisdiction, the Chief may take such steps, as he/she deems
appropriate to furnish the requested aid.
It shall be the responsibility of the Fire Department to assure that all
personnel responding to the request for automatic aid or mutual aid
are trained, responsible persons. The conduct and actions of said responding
personnel shall remain the obligation and responsibility of the responding Fire
Department. In addition, it shall be the responsibility of the Chief of the
Fire Department to assure that each piece of responding apparatus and equipment
is operational and capable of functioning properly for that type of apparatus
or equipment.
Fire Department shall assume all liability and responsibility for the death
or injury to any of its own personnel while responding to the request for
automatic or mutual aid.
Fire Department shall assume all liability and responsibility for damage to, or
caused by, its own apparatus and equipment while en route to or from an
automatic or mutual aid request.
Agency requesting automatic or mutual aid shall have
no liability nor responsibility for the personal property of Fire Department
personnel if said property is lost, stolen, damaged, or destroyed while those
personnel are performing their duties under the automatic or mutual aid
response terms contained herein.
Fire Department shall assume no liability or responsibility for property
damaged or destroyed at the actual scene or any automatic or mutual aid
response due to the fire fighting and/or rescue operations, fire control
tactics, and strategy or other operations as may be required or ordered; all
such liability and responsibility shall rest solely with the requesting agency
and within whose boundaries the property shall exist, or the incident occurred.
Fire Department shall assume all costs of salaries, wages, bonuses, or other
compensation for its own personnel that respond to a automatic or mutual aid
dispatch under the terms of this Contract and Agreement, and Fire Department
shall also assume all costs involving the use of apparatus, equipment, and
tools used specifically in response to the request for automatic or mutual aid,
and Fire Department shall make no charge for such use to the agency requesting
the automatic or mutual aid assistance. However, any special extinguishing
agents, other than water, provided by the Fire Department
from its own supply shall be paid for by the requesting agency, upon receipt of
an itemized statement of costs for such extinguishing agents.
The Chief of the agency requesting assistance shall in all instances be  in
command  of the emergency as to the aspects of strategy, fire control tactics,
and/or overall direction of the operations. All orders or directions regarding
the operations and personnel of the automatic aid or mutual aid Fire Department
shall be relayed to the Officer of the Fire Department present at that incident
and in command of that department.
When Fire Department personnel are sent to another district pursuant to this
Contract and Agreement, the jurisdiction, rights, authority, privileges, and
immunities, including coverage under Workman's Compensation Laws, which said
personnel have in the Fire Department, shall be extended to the areas outside
the normal response territorial limits, when said personnel are acting within
the scope of the authority conferred by this Contract and Agreement.
In Fire Department where their districts have been extended to a six mile
district, the Fire Department that joins that district will automatically be
dispatched under the automatic aid agreement of this Contract and Agreement.
Upon dispatch, that Fire Department who is providing automatic aid will send a
minimum of one engine with 1,000 gallons of water and adequate personnel.
CONDITIONS TO RECEIVE FUNDS
A roster of personnel, including their fire and rescue certifications, shall be
provided quarterly.
The Fire Department will submit promptly to the County Manager any information
requested related to any services which use County fire fees.
The Fire Department shall conduct pre-fire plans on all structures other than
one and two- family dwellings within their response districts.
Each Fire Department shall have an adopted standard operating guideline that
addresses the appropriate number of firefighters needed on all types of fire
calls. The Fire Department shall adhere to the response criteria set forth by
the North Carolina Department of Insurance and associated 9S rating criteria.
Should the Brunswick County Fire Commission and/or Board of Commissioners adopt
new standards, those standards shall control to the extent they are more
stringent than the 9S rating criteria. The Fire Department shall provide a copy
of its standard operating guidelines and any amendments thereto.
The Fire Department officer in charge at all fire scenes shall attempt to
determine the origin and cause of every fire. When the officer cannot determine
the origin and cause of the fire or if the cause of the fire is suspected to be
arson in nature, the officer in charge shall request the appropriate agency
having jurisdiction to assist. The Fire Department should provide whatever
assistance is needed to assist the agency having jurisdiction at the fire
scene.
The Fire Department shall be NIMS compliant and adhere to any local, state or
federal guidelines regarding Incident Command.
The Fire Department shall take under advisement any recommendations of the
Brunswick County Fire Protection Oversight Committee.
The Fire Department shall prepare an annual budget based on anticipated
revenues and shall submit the budget to the county for processing and approval
according to the county’s regular budget calendar. The budget and recommended
fire fees shall have the approval of the department’s Board of Aldermen prior
to submission to the County.
The County may audit the Fire Department’s financial records upon reasonable
notice to the Fire Department. Any fees collected by the county will be
withheld until all fiscal issues are resolved to the satisfaction of the County
Finance Officer.
The Fire Department will use the County supplied “Emergency Reporting” software
for NFIRS incident reporting and will allow County access to their records via
Emergency Reporting login.
The Fire Department that chooses to operate a Medical Responder program shall
adhere to EMS system guidelines established for the operation of Medical
Responder programs in Brunswick County and shall adhere to the Brunswick County
EMS System Continuing Education Program.
The Fire Department shall maintain an up to date membership with the North
Carolina State Firemen’s Association and shall ensure that all members have
acquired the mandated minimum training hours as required per year to remain on
the roster.
The County shall have the right to inspect, examine, and make copies of such
operational records it requests as may assist the County in its evaluation of
the effectiveness of the department and the provision of fire services to the
County generally. Such operational information may include, but is not limited
to, Emergency Reporting Access, call volumes, staffing on duty, staffing on
scene, response time, rosters of employees and volunteers, and information the
County deems necessary to conduct a study of fire service delivery methods in
the County.
COMPENSATION AND AUDIT
As full compensation from Brunswick County for services to be rendered by Fire
Department as herein provided, the County agrees to make payments to Fire
Department in the sum as set by the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners for
each fiscal year to be advanced in quarterly payments beginning with the first
quarter after July 1, 2018.
FIRE FEE EXPENDITURES AND PROPERTY DISPOSAL
All Fire Fees shall be utilized strictly for the operation, maintenance and
capital outlay needs of the Fire Department. Any item acquired using Fire Fees
by the Fire Department shall become the property of that Fire Department (and
titled to that Fire Department when applicable).
No Fire Department resources procured with fire fees may be used for personal
purposes or for the benefit of any board members, paid staff, or volunteer
staff. In the event the Fire Department deems a piece of equipment necessary to
sell or dispose of, the department shall offer it for sale to other Brunswick
County fire departments or to the County prior to offering the equipment to
outside agencies. Any proceeds obtained from the sale of surplus property
acquired with any Fire Fees shall be used only for the same purpose as Fire
Fees.
A breach of this section shall result in the withholding of fire fees in an
amount equal to the value of the breach as determined by the County Finance
Director.
TERM
   This Contract and Agreement shall be valid until June 30, 2019 and shall
automatically renew for terms of one year following the County fiscal year
cycle until notice of termination is provided pursuant to this contract.
TERMINATION OF CONTRACT
Each party shall have the right to terminate this contract at the end of the
term without cause by giving the other party one hundred twenty (120) days
written notice of termination.
Each party shall have the right to terminate this contract with cause by giving
the other party sixty (60) days written notice of termination.
EVENT OF A BREACH
    Unless otherwise stated herein, in the event of a breach of any provision
of this contract by the Fire Department, the department shall be notified and
provided thirty (30) days to cure the breach. Failure to cure within thirty
(30) days shall result in the immediate suspension of funding.
NOTIFICATIONS
   Notifications pursuant to this agreement shall be in writing to the
following:
   Brunswick County            City of Southport
   c/o County Manager            c/o City Manager
   P.O. Box 248               1029 N. Howe Street
   Bolivia, NC 28422            Southport, NC 28461

   Entire Agreement. This writing contains the entire agreement between the
parties. No representations were made or relied upon by either party other than
those that are expressly set forth. This agreement may not be amended or
modified except in a subsequent written agreement duly executed by each of the
parties.
   Controlling Law. The validity, interpretation, and performance of this
agreement shall be controlled by and construed under the laws of the State of
North Carolina. The parties hereby submit to jurisdiction and venue in the
courts of Brunswick County, North Carolina.
   E-Verify. Pursuant to G.S. 143-48.5 and G.S. 147-33.95(g), the undersigned
hereby certifies that the Contractor named below, and the Contractor’s
subcontractors, complies with the requirements of Article 2 of Chapter 64 of
the NC General Statutes, including the requirement for each employer with more
than 25 employees in North Carolina to verify the work authorization of its
employees through the federal E-Verify system." E-Verify System Link:
www.uscis.gov.
   Non-Waiver of Rights. It is agreed that either party’s failure to insist
upon the strict performance of any provision of this contract or to exercise
any right based upon a breach, shall not constitute a waiver of any rights
under this contract.

STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA
COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK AGREEMENT      
THIS AGREEMENT ("Agreement") made and entered into this the 14th day of June,
2018, by and between the City of Southport, a North Carolina municipal
corporation, party of the first part (“Southport”), and Brush Bandit Hauling,
LLC, a North Carolina limited liability company of Brunswick County, North
Carolina, party of the second part (“Contractor”);
   W I T N E S S E T H :
   THAT WHEREAS, Southport desires to contract for the removal of yard debris
from the residential properties located within the city limits; and
   WHEREAS, Contractor desires to provide said service to Southport upon the
terms and conditions hereinafter set forth;
   NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises and covenants
contained herein, and other valuable consideration, the receipt of which is
acknowledged by both parties hereto, it is hereby agreed as follows:
   1. This agreement shall be for a term of one year and shall take effect on
July 1, 2018, and run through June 30, 2019. This agreement shall automatically
renew each year for additional one year terms unless either party gives the
other party a 60 day written notice of termination prior to the end of the
current term.
   2. As compensation for the services provided herein by Contractor, Southport
shall pay to Contractor the sum of $ 1.00 per residential home per week. New
residential homes shall be added quarterly at the same price per year. In the
event that diesel price rises above $ 3.50 per gallon, the parties agree to
negotiate in good faith a fuel surcharge to be added to the above compensation.
In the event that the parties cannot agree regarding said adjustment to the
compensation, either party may terminate this contract upon 60 days written
notice.
   3. Yard debris will be picked up by Contractor on each Wednesday of the year
unless July 4 or Christmas falls on a Wednesday in which event an alternate
date will be chosen to ensure timely service.  
   4. Yard debris shall be serviced by Contractor provide that (i) it has been
placed in a 95 gallon rollout cart designated “Yard Waste”, or (ii ) it is in
biodegradable paper bags, or (iii) it consists of bundles of brush and limbs
securely tied in 5 foot lengths of no more than 50 pounds in weight. All
rollout carts are the property of the homeowner and Contractor is not
responsible for the maintenance or repair of said carts.
   5. Yard debris pickup shall be for residential homes only and pickup is not
included for vacant lots, businesses, parks and other public areas. In
addition, yard debris will not be picked up if mixed with trash or recycle.
   6. Contractor shall not be required to pick up yard debris above normal
tonnage following a named storm unless the parties reach an agreement related
thereto. Contractor shall, however, if conditions permit, make its regular
pickup pursuant to this agreement of the amount of debris contracted for
herein.
   7. Contractor agrees and covenants to comply with all local, state and
federal laws and regulations in performing the services hereunder.
   8. Contractor shall maintain general liability insurance coverage in at
least the amount of $2,000,000 automobile insurance coverage in at least the
amount of $1,000,000 and workmen-s compensation and other insurances as
required by law. Contractor does hereby agree to indemnify and save harmless
Southport and its employees, officers and officials from and against any and
all claims, causes of action, loss, costs, damages, charges, liability or
expenses, including court costs and attorney fees, which it may sustain or be
put to by reason of the services provided herein by Contractor.
   9. If Southport shall fail to pay any payment within seven days after the
same is due, or fail to perform any other obligations, duties or
responsibilities for which it is liable or responsible hereunder, after ten
(10) days’ notice in writing to pay or perform, Contractor may terminate this
agreement upon 10 days’ written notice without further obligation hereunder.
    If Contractor shall fail to perform its work, obligations, duties or
responsibilities in accordance with this agreement, after ten (10) days’ notice
in writing to perform, or in the event of Contractor’s bankruptcy, insolvency,
receivership or assignment for the benefit of creditors, then in any of said
events Southport may terminate this agreement upon 10 days’ written notice
without further obligation to Contractor other than to pay for the services
rendered to the date of termination.
   10. Contractor may not assign this agreement to another party without the
written consent of the City of Southport.
   IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement the day and
year first above written.

RESOLUTION ADOPTING SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT FEES REPORT
   THAT WHEREAS, Session Law 2017-138 (House Bill 436) known as the “Public
Water and Sewer System Development Fee Act” sets certain standards and
limitations before a city may adopt a system development fee for water and
sewer service; and
   WHEREAS, said Act requires that a system development fee be established only
after written analysis prepared by a qualified financial professional or
qualified licensed professional engineer in a manner as set forth in said Act;
and
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport has retained McGill Associates, a qualified
and licensed professional engineer and consulting firm, to perform said
analysis in accordance with said Act; and
   WHEREAS, McGill Associates has performed said analysis and delivered a
written report to the City of Southport pursuant to said Act; and
   WHEREAS, the analysis has been posted on the City’s website as required in
said Act and a public hearing has been held as required in said Act and all
comments have been considered; and
WHEREAS, all other conditions, standards and requirements of said Act have been
satisfied;
    NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that the City hereby adopts and approves the Cost-Justified Water and
Wastewater System Development Fees Report dated March, 2018, by McGill
Associates.

15.   Consideration; Caswell Beach Fire Protection Contract & Lease
   Referencing a handout provided to each Board member, Fire Chief Drew
explained the proposal for Southport to provide fire services for Caswell Beach
and the former Yaupon Beach Fire District. He reviewed how Brunswick County,
since 1999, had funded fire service through fire fees and how the County had
chosen not to continue funding the Yaupon Beach department, which served the
smallest district in the County with annual calls of 15 per year. Chief Drew
talked of the solid 30 years working relationship the Southport Fire Department
has had with Yaupon Beach Fire Department and that as a mutual aid response
agency, Southport Fire has been responding to that district every time there
has been a call.
   Chief Drew stated that when the County decided to cut supplemental funding,
the Town of Caswell Beach reached out to Southport to provide fire protection
services. He added that the details have been worked out and the resulting
contract has been presented to the Board of Aldermen for consideration along
with a lease agreement to use the Caswell Beach Fire Station at no cost.
   Chief Drew presented a cost analysis:
Southport to receive $121,000 annually in fire fees from properties within
Caswell Beach town limits.
Southport to obtain all Yaupon Beach Fire Department assets, equipment,
apparatus and capital funds.
The new area will receive a lower ISO rating and an increased level of coverage
at a reduced cost.
The district will be covered with volunteers that will receive a stipend in
lieu of part-time employees.
   Chief Drew noted that there would be challenges but he felt confident the
challenges could be overcome with teamwork and he cited the past merger of
Southport Fire and Rescue Departments as an example.
   Chief Drew talked about the upcoming closure of the G.V. Barbee Bridge for
repair. He indicated that the Caswell Beach station would be manned with two or
three personnel and there are commitments from two Caswell Beach Public Works
employees that they will respond to any calls during working hours. Chief Drew
pointed out that some members of the Southport Fire Department live on Oak
Island.
   Responding to a query from Alderman Powell, Chief Drew stated that fire
protection services would also be provided to the N. C. Baptist Assembly.
   Chief Drew discussed the request to eliminate the ordinance that limits the
fire department membership to 50 members. He stated that there are currently 45
firefighters on the roster, 40 EMS members and 20 firefighters of Yaupon Beach
Fire Department that will be joining the Southport Fire Department.
   Alderman Sharkey asked if the Southport Fire Department would be doing fire
inspections for Caswell Beach. Chief Drew responded that fire inspections are
currently contracted out by Caswell Beach. He added that the prospect of
Southport doing the inspections could be considered in the future.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to approve the Contract
and Lease with Caswell Beach. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA
COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK          CONTRACT
   THIS CONTRACT is made and entered into this the 14th day of June, 2018 by
and between the TOWN OF CASWELL BEACH, a municipal corporation of the State of
North Carolina, hereafter called the “Town”, and the CITY OF SOUTHPORT, a
municipal corporation of the State of North Carolina , (through it’s fire
department) hereafter called the “Department”. This Contract and Agreement
shall commence on the first day of July, 2018, and run through June 30, 2019.
This contract shall automatically renew each year for an additional one year
term unless either party gives the other party a 120 day written notice of
termination.
WITNESSETH:
   In consideration of the mutual promises and covenants herein contained and
pursuant to the authority of North Carolina law, Town and Department do hereby
agree as follows:
   1.   The Department agrees to provide continuing fire protection services to
all citizens in the Town and to all real and personal property lying within the
boundaries of the Town to the extent possible within the boundaries of the
Department's manpower and equipment.
   2.   The Department agrees to dispatch, upon call of any person within the
corporate limits of the Town, the equipment necessary to answer the call with
adequate personnel to operate such equipment.
   3.   The Department and the Town jointly agree to strive to maintain a Class
six (6) insurance rating, based on the current ratings standards.
   4.   The Department shall render aid in the event of any fire within the
Town limits. If an alarm is sounded, the Department shall respond and shall not
be obligated to secure the permission of any Town Official. It shall be the
responsibility of the officer in charge of the Department to assure that all
personnel responding to the request for assistance are responsible persons, and
the conduct and actions of said personnel shall be the responsibility of the
Department. Each party to this agreement shall assume all liability and
responsibility for the death or injury to any personnel of their own command
responding to the request for aid.
   5.   All vehicles responding to a fire call shall be operated and equipped
as provided by law.
   6.   The Department shall not be bound to dispatch apparatus, equipment or
personnel to the assistance of the Town Police or the Town Emergency
Coordinator but every effort should be made to furnish such assistance if, in
the judgment of the officer in charge of the Department, such dispatch can be
made without impairing Department’s capacity to provide protection within its
own jurisdiction.
   7.   The Department shall maintain at all times adequate insurance coverage
for automobile liability, workmen’s compensation and general liability
coverage. 
   8.   The Department and the Town will cooperate at all times to see that
adequate inspection, planning, safeguards and insurance coverage are maintained
so as to the minimize the risk of liability to both the Department and the
Town.
   9.   This writing contains the entire agreement of the parties. No
representations were made or relied upon except as set forth herein. Any
amendment, addition or modification to this contract must be in writing and
signed by both parties.
   10.   Town acknowledges that it currently owns and maintains a fire station
within it’s corporate limits which it will lease to Department under a separate
lease agreement between the parties.
   11.   Town acknowledges that all fire fees collected by Brunswick County for
property lying within the corporate limits of Town will be distributed to
Department pursuant to a separate agreement between Brunswick County and City
of Southport.
   IN WITNESS WHEREOF the Town of Caswell Beach has caused this instrument to
be signed in its corporate name by its Town mayor, attested to by its Town
Clerk with its corporate seal affixed, and the City of Southport has likewise
caused this instrument to be signed in its corporate name by its City mayor,
attested to by its City Clerk with its corporate seal affixed, all on the day,
month and year first above written.
   Town of Caswell Beach            City of Southport
   BY: /s/ Deborah Ahlers, Mayor            BY: /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

STATE OF NORTH CAROLINA             LEASE
COUNTY OF BRUNSWICK
    THIS LEASE, made and entered into this 14th day of June, 2018, by and
between Town of Caswell Beach, a North Carolina municipal corporation of
Brunswick County, hereinafter called "Owner", and City of Southport, a North
Carolina municipal corporation of Brunswick County, hereinafter called
"Tenant".
W I T N E S S E T H   T H A T:
Owner hereby leases to Tenant and Tenant hereby leases from Owner the property
described below, on the terms and conditions herein set forth.
   I.   Property. The leased property, herein called "Property", is located at
1100A Caswell Beach Road, Caswell Beach, North Carolina, as more particularly
described as “Leased Premises” on Exhibit A-1 attached hereto and located
within the building depicted on Exhibit A-2 attached hereto. Excluded from the
leased Property are all other parts of the building and all other buildings,
fixtures and structures located on the land.
   II.   Term. The term of this lease begins on the first day of July, 2018,
and runs through June 30, 2019. This lease shall automatically renew each year
for additional one year terms unless either party gives the other party a 120
day written notice of termination prior to the end of the current term.
        III.   Rent. Tenant shall pay no rent, since the consideration is the
undertaking of Tenant as set forth in a separate Contract between the parties
dated June 14, 2018.
    III.    Improvements, Etc. Tenant shall make no changes, remodeling,
improvements, alterations, renovations or additions to the Property without the
Owner's prior written consent and then only in accordance with plans and
specifications previously approved in writing by Owner. Except to the extent
otherwise approved in writing by Owner, all changes, remodeling, improvements,
alterations, renovations and additions shall be at Tenant’s expense and shall
become a permanent part of the real estate (excluding Tenant’s trade fixtures)
and the property of Owner. Tenant shall pay all costs and expenses of repairing
damage to the Property caused by any installation or removal of signs and/or
trade fixtures.
   IV.    Owner's Inspection. Owner, during the term of this lease, at
reasonable times and upon reasonable notice, may enter the Property to view and
inspect it.
    V.    Use. Tenant shall use the Property as a Fire Substation to provide
fire protection services, including services to Owner pursuant to that certain
Contract between the parties dated June 14, 2018, and for no other purposes.
   VI.   Condition of Property. Tenant has inspected the Property and is
familiar with its condition and agrees that Owner has made no representation as
to condition or repair of the Property. Tenant hereby accepts the Property in
its present condition and, upon termination of this lease, will surrender the
Property in as good condition as the same now exists, ordinary wear and tear
excepted.
    VII.   Maintenance. Tenant shall maintain the leased Property and the
improvements located thereon in good order and repair, in at least as good a
condition as the same existed on the date that Tenant took possession. Tenant,
at its expense, shall perform and be responsible for (a) all routine
maintenance and repairs to said leased Property and its fixtures and personal
property located thereon and (b) all repairs to the leased Property and to
Owner’s property excluded from the leased Property (i) caused by the
installation and removal of Tenant’s fixtures and personal property or (ii)
necessary due to acts or omissions of Tenant or any of its agents, employees,
members, contractors or invitees. Tenant shall promptly make such repairs.
    VIII. Utilities. Owner shall be responsible for all utilities used in
connection with said Property including water, sewerage, garbage, electricity,
trash and telephone services.
   IX.    Insurance and Indemnity. Tenant covenants and agrees to maintain at
all times, during the term of this Lease, municipal general liability
insurance, on an "occurrence" basis (and not on a "claims made" basis), with
minimum limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $5,000,000 in aggregate, or be
a member of a local government pooled insurance group. Tenant agrees to
indemnify and save harmless Owner from any loss or expense arising out of any
claims asserted or actions brought against Owner based upon acts or omissions
of Tenant (but not the acts or omissions of Owner), its agents, employees,
members, contractors and invitees, in connection with Tenant's use and
occupancy of the Property, including but not limited to any claim that Tenant
is or was an agent of Owner. Owner agrees to keep and maintain fire and hazard
insurance on the Property.
X.    Fire or Casualty. If the Property is destroyed or damaged by fire, flood,
casualty or other happening so as to render the Property unfit for Tenant's use
as described herein, this Lease may be terminated by either party.
XI.    Owner's Covenant. Owner covenants that it is seized of the Property in
fee simple and has the right to execute this lease, and that Tenant, upon
fulfilling all covenants and agreements herein contained, shall peacefully and
quietly have, hold and enjoy the Property for the term of this lease.
XII.    Tenant's Covenants. Tenant shall procure all licenses and permits
required for Tenant's use and occupancy of the Property and shall comply with
all laws, regulations, and ordinances relating to the Property and its use and
shall not permit any noxious or offensive sights, odors or activities on the
Property and shall not conduct or permit any nuisances thereon. Tenant also
covenants that it will keep the inside and outside of the Property clean at all
times.
XIII. Assignment. Tenant shall not have the right to assign this lease in whole
or in part or to sublet any portion of the Property.
XIV. Default. If Tenant shall fail to perform any obligations, duties or
responsibilities for which it is liable hereunder, after fifteen days’ notice
in writing to perform such obligation then in any of said events, Owner may
terminate this lease.
XV.    Remedies on Termination; Tenant Holding Over.
      (a)    Upon expiration or termination of this lease for any reason (i)
the estate hereby granted and all rights of Tenant hereunder shall expire and
terminate, (ii) all obligations of Tenant hereunder shall continue until fully
discharged, except if Tenant terminates this lease due to Owner’s breach, then
Tenant’s obligations for maintenance under Section VII, to insure the Property
under Section IX and to procure licenses under Section XII shall terminate
(iii) Owner immediately may reenter and resume possession of the Property and
remove all persons and other property therefrom, (iv) Owner may take any other
legal action or pursue any other remedy against Tenant (including but not
limited to terminating the lease and proceeding with other remedies
concurrently) and (v) Tenant shall (A) immediately surrender and deliver
possession of the Property to Owner in the same condition in which it was at
the start of this lease, ordinary wear and tear excepted, and (B) remove within
30 days after the expiration or termination of the lease from the Property all
property (including trade fixtures and personal property) owned by Tenant and
repair any damage caused by such removal. Property not so removed shall become
the property of Owner, and Owner may thereafter cause such property to be
removed from the Property. The cost of removing and disposing of such property
and repairing any damage to the Property caused by such removal shall be paid
by Tenant to Owner on demand.
      (b)    If Tenant fails to vacate and surrender possession of the Property
at the expiration or termination of this lease, such holdover by Tenant shall
create no more than a month-to month tenancy during the period that begins on
the date this lease expires or is terminated and ends on the date on which
Tenant shall have vacated and surrendered possession in full compliance with
all terms of this lease.
      XVI. Binding Effect. This lease shall be binding upon and inure to the
benefit of all parties, their heirs, executors and administrators, successors
and assigns.
   XVII.   Notices, Consents and Waivers. All notices and other communications
given in connection with this lease must be in writing and shall be deemed
given when delivered: if to the Owner, addressed to the Town of Caswell Beach,
1100 Caswell Beach Road, Caswell Beach, NC 28465, Attention: Town Administrator
or, if to Tenant, addressed to the City of Southport, 1029 North Howe Street,
Southport, NC 28461, Attention: City Manager. This lease may not be amended,
supplemented or otherwise modified except by a written agreement executed by
the party to be charged, and the failure of either party to exercise any right
or power hereunder and the grant of any extension of time or any other
indulgence to the other party shall not constitute or be regarded as a waiver
of any of that party’s rights, powers or remedies.
   XVIII. No Agency; Limited Recourse; Miscellaneous.  
   (a)   Tenant is completely independent of Owner, is not an agent of Owner,
has no authority whatsoever to act on behalf of Owner for any purpose and is
not subject to Owner’s control in its operations as a fire department or
   otherwise. Tenant agrees it will not represent to any other entity that
Tenant is an agent of Owner.
   (b)   Any claim based on or in respect of any liability of Owner shall be
limited to actual damages and shall be enforced only against Owner and not
against its mayor or any of its commissioners, officials, employees or agents.
   (c)   This lease supersedes all prior agreements, whether written or oral,
between the parties with respect to its subject matter and constitutes a
complete and exclusive statement of the terms of the agreement between the
parties with    respect to its subject matter.
    IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this lease in duplicate
originals as of the day and year first above written.

Call to Order - 5:00 p.m.
   Mayor Dove called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m. and stated an informal
discussion would be held regarding water and sewer rates.
   City Manager Oakley stated that the System Development Report is being
further analyzed and is not ready to be adopted. He indicated that the water
and sewer development rates will significantly increase over the next two (2)
years and then will level off with a 2% annual increase.
   Mayor Dove asked members of the Rate Review Committee for their reports.
   Alderman Mosteller talked about the current residential sewer rate of
$46.50, the proposed 17% reduction and, rate increases for commercial and
residential outside the city limits. She added that there is a proposed 35%
increase to adjust the base rate in 2019, 2020 and stabilizing in 2021. She
pointed out that the rate adjustments are required in order for the City to
fund a Brunswick County Wastewater Treatment Plant expansion estimated at $25M
paid over 20 years. She noted that the City has obtained a 1.5% interest rate
on the debt.
   Mayor Dove stated that he gets questions regarding the 3,000 gallon base
minimum charged each customer. City Manager Oakley responded that the base rate
is charged for access to the system.
   Alderman Mosteller stated that the Rate Committee worked with the School of
Government (SOG) to create the proposed rate structure and be as equitable as
possible. She added that utility rates are reviewed annually.
   Alderman Powell asked the City Manager to research if the loan could be for
25 years instead of 20 years.
   Alderman Spencer asked how many customers the city serves. Alderman Pukenas
stated that there are a total of 2,516 customers which includes 280 commercial
customers.
   Alderman Sharkey, member of the Rate Review Committee, stated that the
formula applied to establish proper water and sewer rates was based on three
(3) things:
      Fixed Operating Costs
      Variable Operating Costs
      Capital Costs
   She pointed out that the City’s water and sewer lines are currently being
mapped, are very old, and will have to be replaced before they fail. She stated
that as Southport has grown, the financing of a waste water treatment plant
expansion has become a reality, all customers are paying for it, the Board is
making it as equitable as possible, and the rates will allow the city to pay
for current assets, repay the loan and accommodate growth.
   Alderman Powell talked about line repair techniques.
   Mayor Dove stated he has heard concerns about water and sewer development
(impact) fees. He asked to hear Board comments and comments of builders.
   Mr. Cameron Smith, developer, stated appreciation for further discussion
regarding the development rates. He expressed concerns about the maximum, by
law, the City is permitted to charge. He encouraged the Board to set a fair
impact fee.
   Alderman Powell emphasized the need to promote growth that will add value.
   Mr. Richard Bandera, architect, questioned irrigation rates and if the water
used for irrigation is potable water and treated the same. He contended that
irrigation usage of 10,000 gallons is charged at a lesser rate than a resident
using 3,000 gallons.
   A woman in the audience asked about the quality of the City’s water and if
the City is comfortable with the County’s treatment level and the cost.
Aldermen Powell and Sharkey pointed out that 75% of the city’s water comes from
an aquifer and 25% from the Cape Fear River. Alderman Sharkey noted that with
the discovery of GenX in the river, the County is doing a lot of testing and
plans to purchase a reserve osmosis system. The unidentified woman asked if the
rate structure would create more conservation of water useage.
   Mr. Robert Creech, 426 W. Brunswick Street, stated the proposed rates would
not promote conservation. He stated that if he used 2,000 gallons of water a
month, he should only be charged for 2,000, not the 3,000 base.
   Mr. Steve Simon, 6211 Pebble Shore Lane, agreed with Mr. Creech and he added
that his rate went up 25% when the City went to a simplified water and sewer
charge in 2017. He asked the Board to set the base rate for what is actually
used.
   Alderman Mosteller stated that the City went to a 3,000 gallon/month base
rate for water in part because of the number of second homes and that
volumetrics are trending downward.
   Mr. Creech contended that per his review of the proposed rate structure,
customers who use more water pay less. He suggested asking the Golden Leaf
Foundation for funding for the plant expansion.
   There being no further discussion, Mayor Dove adjourned the meeting at 6:00
p.m.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove,    Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

SECTION V. TAX RATE
There is hereby levied, for fiscal year 2018-2019, a tax at the rate of $0.2956
on each one hundred dollars ($100) of assessed valuation of property located
within the City of Southport for the purpose of raising revenue in the General
Fund. The assessed value of property is $784,569,252.
SECTION VI. BUDGET OFFICER AUTHORITY
The city manager (budget officer) is hereby authorized to transfer
appropriations within a fund and between funds under the following terms:
He may transfer amounts between appropriations within the same fund, provided
that a report of such transfers shall be made no later than the next regular
financial report to the Board of Aldermen.
He may authorize temporary transfers of cash among funds as necessary to meet
cash flow needs.
All other transfers of funds between appropriations or budget funds shall be
accomplished by Board amendment of this ordinance.
SECTION IX. CONTINUING AUTHORIZATION
Prior year Capital Reserve Fund is no longer a restriction of Fund Balance.
Previously-adopted capital project budgets, grant project budgets, and special
reserve funds are hereby un-authorized as all such projects have been completed
and all monies shall be returned to the associated funds upon adoption of the
Budget ordinance.
SECTION X. BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION
This ordinance and the supporting budget document shall be the basis of the
financial plan for the City of Southport municipal government for the 2018-2019
fiscal year. The budget officer shall administer the budget and shall insure
the finance officer and department heads of the city are provided with
sufficient guidance to properly implement this plan. Copies of the budget
ordinance shall be furnished to the city manager and the finance officer for
their use and direction in the disbursement of funds and to the city clerk for
the official records of the city.
SECTION XI. ADOPTION
This ordinance has been adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen in special
session on June 27, 2018, upon the motion of Alderman Powell and the second of
Alderman Sharkey, with a vote of six (6) ayes and 0 noes, and shall be
effective July 1, 2018.

RESOLUTION ADOPTING SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT FEES REPORT
   THAT WHEREAS, Session Law 2017-138 (House Bill 436) known as the “Public
Water and Sewer System Development Fee Act” sets certain standards and
limitations before a city may adopt a system development fee for water and
sewer service; and
   WHEREAS, said Act requires that a system development fee be established only
after written analysis prepared by a qualified financial professional or
qualified licensed professional engineer in a manner as set forth in said Act;
and
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport has retained McGill Associates, a qualified
and licensed professional engineer and consulting firm, to perform said
analysis in accordance with said Act; and
   WHEREAS, McGill Associates has performed said analysis and delivered a
written report dated March, 2018, to the City of Southport pursuant to said
Act; and
   WHEREAS, the analysis was posted on the City’s website as required in said
Act and a public hearing was held as required by said Act and all comments were
considered; and
WHEREAS, all other conditions, standards and requirements of said Act were
satisfied; and
WHEREAS, on June 14, 2018, in accordance with said Act, the Board of Aldermen
adopted a Resolution approving the Cost-Justified Water and Wastewater System
Development Fees Report dated March, 2018, by McGill Associates; and
WHEREAS, it has now come to the attention of the Board of Aldermen that there
was an error in the calculations set forth in the Cost-Justified Water and
Wastewater System Development Fees Report dated March, 2018, and the Report has
now been revised by McGill Associates to correct said error; and
WHEREAS, it is necessary for the Board of Aldermen to rescind the prior
resolution and approve the Report as now revised;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that the City hereby rescinds the Resolution dated June 14, 2018,
approving the Cost-Justified Water and Wastewater System Development Fees
Report dated March, 2018, by McGill Associates, and the Board hereby now adopts
and approves the Revised Cost-Justified Water and Wastewater System Development
Fees Report dated June, 2018, by McGill Associates .
   This the 27th day of June, 2018.         City of Southport
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

ORDINANCE ADOPTING SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT FEES
   City Manager Oakley explained that the City is required by the State to
adopt system development fees by July 1. He indicated that reinstating the pre-
recession development fee rates would be a starting point, is equitable and a
review of the rates could be revisited at any time.
   Alderman Powell stated that during the recession, the Board cut impact
(development) fees to the current rates. He pointed out that the area is
experiencing growth again and he felt returning to the prior fees would be
affordable. He recommended setting the sewer development fee for a 3-bedroom
house at $7,200.
   Alderman Mosteller agreed with Alderman Powell that the $7,200 per 3
bedrooms is a good place to start with the development fee as there is history
of operating at that level.
   Noting she was relying on the people that were here before her and that the
fees were set and used consistently vs. using something arbitrarily, Alderman
Sharkey endorsed the $7,200 rate.
   Alderman Spencer stated he wanted a moderate number to sustain growth. He
added that the $7,200 proposed rate should be reviewed in the future to ensure
it is enough to cover the City’s costs and is not having a negative impact on
building.
   Alderman Pukenas agreed and stated his opinion that $7,200 is an equitable
number for everyone.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to adopt the Ordinance
Adopting System Development Fees and setting the sewer development fee for a
residential unit (3 bedroom home with 360 gallons per day flow) at $7,200.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
ORDINANCE ADOPTING SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT FEES
   THAT WHEREAS, the North Carolina General Assembly amended Chapter 162A of
the General Statutes by adding Article 8 entitled “Public Water and Sewer
System Development Fee Act”; and
   WHEREAS, this Article established a uniform approach and associated
methodology required for local governments to calculate and implement system
development fees for public water and sewer systems; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Article 8 of Chapter 162A of the General Statutes, the
City of Southport hired McGill Associates, a qualified and licensed
professional engineer and consulting firm, to perform the analysis in
accordance with said Article and the City has adopted and approved the Revised
Cost-Justified Water and Wastewater System Development Fees Report dated June,
2018, by McGill Associates; and
WHEREAS, the City has complied with all conditions, standards and requirements
set forth in said Article and now desires to set a system development fee for
water and sewer service in accordance with Article 8 of Chapter 162A; and
WHEREAS, in accordance with said Article, the Revised Cost-Justified Water and
Wastewater System Development Fees Report calculated the development fee for
water and sewer for an Equivalent Residential Unit (3 bedroom single family
residence) to be $ 16,452.80 based upon a $ 4.25 GPD cost of capacity for water
and $ 40.98 GPD cost of capacity for sewer; and
WHEREAS, after careful review and consideration, the Board of Aldermen has
determined that the development fees should be established as hereinafter set
forth:
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport as follows:
That the City of Southport hereby sets a system development fee for its water
system for a Residential Equivalent Unit (3 bedroom home with 400 gallons per
day flow) at $744.00 based upon a $1.86 GPD cost of capacity .
That the City of Southport hereby sets a system development fee for its sewer
system for a Residential Equivalent Unit (3 bedroom home with 360 gallons per
day flow) at $6458.40 based upon a $17.94 GPD cost of capacity.
That the water and sewer development fees for other types of development be
calculated by applying the calculated cost of capacity per gallon of flow per
day set forth above to the water and wastewater demands for various uses
determined in accordance with the North Carolina Administrative Code flow rate
tables.
That a Capital Reserve Fund shall be established pursuant to Part 2 of Article
3 of Chapter 159 of the General Statutes and limited as to expenditure of funds
in accordance with G.S. 162A-211.
That the System Development Fee shall be collected in accordance with G.S.
162A-213.
That all ordinances in conflict with this ordinance are hereby repealed and
rescinded.
This the 27th day of June, 2018.            City of Southport
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
