RESOLUTION ADOPTING PROCUREMENT POLICIES
   City Manager Oakley stated that the proposed Procurement Policies were
requested by the City’s Auditor and will codify current procedures.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Sharkey to adopt the Uniform
Guidance Procurement Policy and Uniform Guidance Conflict of Interest Policy.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
City of Southport
Uniform Guidance Procurement Policy (UGPP)
Effective July 1, 2018
I. Purpose
The purpose of this Policy is to establish guidelines that meet or exceed the
procurement requirements for purchases of goods (apparatus, supplies,
materials, and equipment), services, and construction or repair projects when
federal funds are being used in whole or in part to pay for the cost of the
contract.
II. Policy
Application of Policy. This policy applies to contracts for purchases,
services, and construction or repair work funded with federal financial
assistance (direct or reimbursed). The requirements of this Policy also apply
to any subrecipient of the funds.
All federally funded projects, loans, grants, and sub-grants, whether funded in
part or wholly, are subject to the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost
Principles, and Audit Requirements for federal awards (Uniform Guidance)
codified at 2 C.F.R. Part 200 unless otherwise directed in writing by the
federal agency or state pass-through agency that awarded the funds.
Compliance with Federal Law. All procurement activities involving the
expenditure of federal funds must be conducted in compliance with the
Procurement Standards codified in 2 C.F.R. § 200.317 through § 200-326 unless
otherwise directed in writing by the federal agency or state pass-through
agency that awarded the funds. City of Southport will follow all applicable
local, state, and federal procurement requirements when expending federal
funds. Should the City of Southport have more stringent requirements, the most
restrictive requirement shall apply so long as it is consistent with state and
federal law.
Contract Award. All contracts shall be awarded only to the lowest responsive
responsible bidder possessing the ability to perform successfully under the
terms and conditions of the contract.
No Evasion. No contract may be divided to bring the cost under bid thresholds
or to evade any requirements under this Policy or state and federal law.
Contract Requirements. All contracts paid for in whole or in part with federal
funds shall be in writing. The written contract must include or incorporate by
reference the provisions required under 2 C.F.R § 200.326 and as provided for
under 2 C.F.R. Part 200, Appendix II.
Contractors’ Conflict of Interest. Designers, suppliers, and contractors that
assist in the development or drafting of specifications, requirements,
statements of work, invitation for bids or requests for proposals shall be
excluded from competing for such requirements.
Approval and Modification. The administrative procedures contained in this
Policy are administrative and may be changed as necessary at the staff level to
comply with state and federal law.
III. General Procurement Standards and Procedures:
Either the Purchasing Department or the Requesting Department shall procure all
contracts in accordance with the requirements of this Section of the Policy.
Necessity. Purchases must be necessary to perform the scope of work and must
avoid acquisition of unnecessary or duplicative items. The Purchasing
Department and/or the Requesting Department should check with the federal
surplus property agency prior to buying new items when feasible and less
expensive. Strategic sourcing should be considered with other departments and/
or agencies who have similar needs to consolidate procurements and services to
obtain better pricing.
Clear Specifications. All solicitations must incorporate a clear and accurate
description of the technical requirements for the materials, products, or
services to be procured, and shall include all other requirements which bidders
must fulfill and all other factors to be used in evaluating bids or proposals.
Technical requirements must not contain features that restrict competition.
Notice of Federal Funding. All bid solicitations must acknowledge the use of
federal funding for the contract. In addition, all prospective bidders or
offerors must acknowledge that funding is contingent upon compliance with all
terms and conditions of the funding award.
Compliance by Contractors. All solicitations shall inform prospective
contractors that they must comply with all applicable federal laws,
regulations, executive orders, and terms and conditions of the funding award.
Fixed Price. Solicitations must state that bidders shall submit bids on a fixed
price basis and that the contract shall be awarded on this basis unless
otherwise provided for in this Policy. Cost plus percentage of cost contracts
are prohibited. Time and materials contracts are prohibited in most
circumstances. Time and materials contracts will not be used unless no other
form of contract is suitable and the contract includes a “Not to Exceed”
amount. A time and materials contract shall not be awarded without express
written permission of the federal agency or state pass-through agency that
awarded the funds.
Use of Brand Names. When possible, performance or functional specifications are
preferred to allow for more competition leaving the determination of how the
reach the required result to the contractor. Brand names may be used only when
it is impractical or uneconomical to write a clear and accurate description of
the requirement(s). When a brand name is listed, it is used as reference only
and “or equal” must be included in the description.
Lease versus Purchase. Under certain circumstances, it may be necessary to
perform an analysis of lease versus purchase alternatives to determine the most
economical approach.
Dividing Contract for M/WBE Participation. If economically feasible,
procurements may be divided into smaller components to allow maximum
participation of small and minority businesses and women business enterprises.
The procurement cannot be divided to bring the cost under bid thresholds or to
evade any requirements under this Policy.
Documentation. Documentation must be maintained by the Purchasing Department
and/or the Requesting Department detailing the history of all procurements. The
documentation should include the procurement method used, contract type, basis
for contractor selection, price, sources solicited, public notices, cost
analysis, bid documents, addenda, amendments, contractor’s responsiveness,
notice of award, copies of notices to unsuccessful bidders or offerors, record
of protests or disputes, bond documents, notice to proceed, purchase order, and
contract. All documentation relating to the award of any contract must be made
available to the granting agency upon request.
Cost Estimate. For all procurements costing $150,000 or more, the Purchasing
Department and/or Requesting Department shall develop an estimate of the cost
of the procurement prior to soliciting bids. Cost estimates may be developed by
reviewing prior contract costs, online review of similar products or services,
or other means by which a good faith cost estimate may be obtained. Cost
estimates for construction and repair contracts may be developed by the project
designer.
Contract Requirements. The Requesting Department must prepare a written
contract incorporating the provisions referenced in Section II.C of this
Policy.
Debarment. No contract shall be awarded to a contractor included on the
federally debarred bidder’s list.
Contractor Oversight. The Requesting Department receiving the federal funding
must maintain oversight of the contract to ensure that contractor is performing
in accordance with the contract terms, conditions, and specifications.
Open Competition. Solicitations shall be prepared in a way to be fair and
provide open competition. The procurement process shall not restrict
competition by imposing unreasonable requirements on bidders, including but not
limited to unnecessary supplier experience, excessive or unnecessary bonding,
specifying a brand name without allowing for “or equal” products, or other
unnecessary requirements that have the effect of restricting competition.
Geographic Preference. No contract shall be awarded on the basis of a
geographic preference.
IV. Specific Procurement Procedures  
Either the Purchasing Department or the Requesting Department shall solicit
bids in accordance with the requirements under this Section of the Policy based
on the type and cost of the contract.
Service Contracts (except for A/E professional services) and Purchase
Contracts  costing less than $3,500 shall be procured using the Uniform
Guidance “micro-purchase” procedure (2 C.F.R. § 200.320(a)) as follows:
The contract may be awarded without soliciting pricing or bids if the price of
the goods or services is considered to be fair and reasonable.
To the extent practicable, purchases must be distributed among qualified
suppliers.
Service Contracts (except for A/E professional services) and Purchase
Contracts  costing $3,500 up to $90,000 shall be procured using the Uniform
Guidance “small purchase” procedure (2 C.F.R. § 200.320(b)) as follows:
Obtain price or rate quotes from an “adequate number” of qualified sources (a
federal grantor agency might issue guidance interpreting “adequate number,” so
the Requesting Department should review the terms and conditions of the grant
award documents to confirm whether specific guidance has been issued).
Take affirmative steps to solicit price quotes from M/WBE vendors and suppliers
as required under 2 C.F.R. § 200.321.
Cost or price analysis is not required prior to soliciting bids.
Award the contract on a fixed-price basis (a not-to-exceed basis is permissible
for service contracts where obtaining a fixed price is not feasible).
Award the contract to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder.
Service Contracts (except for A/E professional services) and Purchase
Contracts  costing $90,000 and above shall be procured using a combination of
the most restrictive requirements of the Uniform Guidance “sealed bid”
procedure (2 C.F.R. § 200.320(c)) and state formal bidding procedures (G.S.
143-129) as follows:
Cost or price analysis is required prior to soliciting bids.
Complete specifications or purchase description must be made available to all
bidders.
The bid must be formally advertised in a newspaper of general circulation for
at least seven full days between the date of the advertisement and the date of
the public bid opening. Electronic-only advertising must be authorized by the
governing board. The advertisement must state the date, time, and location of
the public bid opening, indicate where specifications may be obtained, and
reserve to the governing board the right to reject any or all bids only for
“sound documented reasons.”
Take affirmative steps to solicit price quotes from M/WBE vendors and suppliers
as required under 2 C.F.R. § 200.321.
Open bids at the public bid opening on the date, time, and at the location
noticed in the public advertisement. All bids must be submitted sealed. A
minimum of 2 bids must be received in order to open all bids.
Award the contract to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder on a fixed-
price basis. Governing board approval is required for purchase contracts unless
the governing board has delegated award authority to an individual official or
employee. Any and all bids may be rejected only for “sound documented reasons.”
Service Contracts (except for A/E professional services) costing $150,000 and
above may be procured using the Uniform Guidance “competitive proposal”
procedure (2 C.F.R. § 200.320(d)) when the “sealed bid” procedure is not
appropriate for the particular type of service being sought. The procedures are
as follows:
A Request for Proposals (RFP) must be publicly advertised. Formal advertisement
in a newspaper is not required so long as the method of advertisement will
solicit proposals from an “adequate number” of qualified firms.
Take affirmative steps to solicit price quotes from M/WBE vendors and suppliers
as provided under 2 C.F.R. § 200.321.
Identify evaluation criteria and relative importance of each criteria (criteria
weight) in the RFP.
Consider all responses to the publicized RFP to the maximum extent practical.
Must have a written method for conducting technical evaluations of proposals
and selecting the winning firm.
Award the contract to the responsible firm with most advantageous proposal
taking into account price and other factors identified in the RFP. Governing
board approval is not required.
Award the contract on a fixed-price or cost-reimbursement basis.
Construction and repair contracts costing less than $3,500 shall be procured
using the Uniform Guidance “micro-purchase” procedure (2 C.F.R. § 200.320(a))
as follows:
The contract may be awarded without soliciting pricing or bids if the price of
the goods or services is considered to be fair and reasonable.
To the extent practicable, contracts must be distributed among qualified
suppliers.
Construction and repair contracts costing $3,500 up to $150,000 shall be
procured using the Uniform Guidance “small purchase” procedure (2 C.F.R. §
200.320(b)) as follows:
Obtain price or rate quotes from an “adequate number” of qualified sources (a
federal grantor agency might issue guidance interpreting “adequate number,” so
the requesting department should review the terms and conditions of the grant
award documents to confirm whether specific guidance has been issued).
Take affirmative steps to solicit price quotes from M/WBE vendors and suppliers
as required under 2 C.F.R. § 200.321.
Cost or price analysis is not required prior to soliciting bids, although price
estimates may be provided by the project designer.
Award the contract on a fixed-price or not-to-exceed basis.
Award the contract to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder. Governing
board approval is not required.
Construction and repair contracts costing $150,000 up to $500,000 shall be
procured using the Uniform Guidance “sealed bid” procedure (2 C.F.R. § 200.320
(c)) as follows:
Cost or price analysis is required prior to soliciting bids (this cost estimate
may be provided by the project designer).
Complete specifications must be made available to all bidders.
Publically advertise the bid solicitation for a period of time sufficient to
give bidders notice of opportunity to submit bids (formal advertisement in a
newspaper is not required so long as other means of advertising will provide
sufficient notice of the opportunity to bid). The advertisement must state the
date, time, and location of the public bid opening, and indicate where
specifications may be obtained.
Take affirmative steps to solicit price quotes from M/WBE vendors and suppliers
as provided under 2 C.F.R. § 200.321.
Open the bids at the public bid opening on the date, time, and at the location
noticed in the public advertisement. All bids must be submitted sealed. A
minimum of 2 bids must be received in order to open all bids.
A 5% bid bond is required of all bidders. Performance and payment bonds of 100%
of the contract price is required of the winning bidder.
Award the contract on a firm fixed-price basis.
Award the contract to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder. Governing
board approval is not required. Any and all bids may be rejected only for
“sound documented reasons.”
Construction and repair contracts  costing $500,000 and above shall be procured
using a combination of the most restrictive requirements of the Uniform
Guidance “sealed bid” procedure (2 C.F.R. § 200.320(c)) and state formal
bidding procedures (G.S. 143-129) as follows:
Cost or price analysis is required prior to soliciting bids (this cost estimate
should be provided by the project designer).
Complete specifications must be made available to all bidders.
Formally advertise the bid in a newspaper of general circulation for at least
seven full days between the date of the advertisement and the date of the
public bid opening. Electronic-only advertising must be authorized by the
governing board. The advertisement must state the date, time, and location of
the public bid opening, indicate where specifications may be obtained, and
reserve to the governing board the right to reject any or all bids only for
“sound documented reasons.”
Take affirmative steps to solicit price quotes from M/WBE vendors and suppliers
as provided under 2 C.F.R. § 200.321.
Open the bids at the public bid opening on the date, time, and at the location
noticed in the public advertisement. All bids must be submitted sealed and in
paper form. A minimum of 3 bids must be received in order to open all bids.
A 5% bid bond is required of all bidders (a bid that does not include a bid
bond cannot be counted toward the 3-bid minimum requirement). Performance and
payment bonds of 100% of the contract price is required of the winning bidder.
Award the contract on a firm fixed-price basis.
Award the contract to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder. Governing
board approval is required and cannot be delegated. The governing board may
reject and all bids only for “sound documented reasons.”
Construction or repair contracts involving a building costing $300,000 and
above must comply with the following additional requirements under state law:
Formal HUB (historically underutilized business) participation required under
G.S. 143-128.2, including local government outreach efforts and bidder good
faith efforts, shall apply.
Separate specifications shall be drawn for the HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and
general construction work as required under G.S. 143-128(a).
The project shall be bid using a statutorily authorized bidding method
(separate-prime, single-prime, or dual bidding) as required under G.S. 143-129
(a1).
Contracts for Architectural and Engineering Services costing under $150,000
shall be procured using the state “Mini-Brooks Act” requirements (G.S. 143-
64.31) as follows:
Issue a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to solicit qualifications from
qualified firms (formal advertisement in a newspaper is not required). Price
(other than unit cost) shall not be solicited in the RFQ.
Take affirmative steps to solicit price quotes from M/WBE vendors and suppliers
as provided for under 2 C.F.R. § 200.321.
Evaluate the qualifications of respondents based on the evaluation criteria
developed by the Purchasing Department and/or Requesting Department.
Rank respondents based on qualifications and select the best qualified firm.
Price cannot be a factor in the evaluation. Preference may be given to in-state
(but not local) firms.
Negotiate fair and reasonable compensation with the best qualified firm. If
negotiations are not successfully, repeat negotiations with the second-best
qualified firm.
Award the contract to best qualified firm with whom fair and reasonable
compensation has been successfully negotiated. Governing board approval is not
required.
Contracts for Architectural and Engineering Services costing $150,000 or more
shall be procured using the Uniform Guidance “competitive proposal” procedure
(2 C.F.R. § 200.320(d)(5)) as follows:
Publically advertise a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to solicit
qualifications from qualified firms (formal advertisement in a newspaper is not
required). Price (other than unit cost) shall not be solicited in the RFQ.
Take affirmative steps to solicit price quotes from M/WBE vendors and suppliers
as provided under 2 C.F.R. § 200.321.
Identify the evaluation criteria and relative importance of each criteria (the
criteria weight) in the RFQ.
Proposals must be solicited from an “adequate number of qualified sources” (an
individual federal grantor agency may issue guidance interpreting “adequate
number”).
Must have a written method for conducting technical evaluations of proposals
and selecting the best qualified firm.
Consider all responses to the publicized RFQ to the maximum extent practical.
Evaluate qualifications of respondents to rank respondents and select the most
qualified firm. Preference may be given to in-state (but not local) firms
provided that granting the preference leaves an appropriate number of qualified
firms to compete for the contract given the nature and size of the project.
Price cannot be a factor in the initial selection of the most qualified firm.
Once the most qualified firm is selected, negotiate fair and reasonable
compensation. If negotiations are not successfully, repeat negotiations with
the second-best qualified firm.
Award the contract to best qualified firm with whom fair and reasonable
compensation has been successfully negotiated. Governing board approval is not
required.
V. Exceptions
Non-competitive contracts are allowed only  under the following conditions and
with the written approval of the federal agency or state pass-through agency
that awarded the federal funds:
Sole Source. A contract may be awarded without competitive bidding when the
item is available from only one source. The Purchasing Department and/or
Requesting Department shall document the justification for and lack of
available competition for the item. A sole source contract must be approved by
the governing board.
Public Exigency. A contract may be awarded without competitive bidding when
there is a public exigency. A public exigency exists when there is an imminent
or actual threat to public health, safety, and welfare, and the need for the
item will not permit the delay resulting from a competitive bidding.
Inadequate Competition. A contract may be awarded without competitive bidding
when competition is determined to be inadequate after attempts to solicit bids
from a number of sources as required under this Policy does not result in a
qualified winning bidder.
Federal Contract. A contract may be awarded without competitive bidding when
the purchase is made from a federal contract available on the U.S. General
Services Administration schedules of contracts. 
Awarding Agency Approval.  A contract may be awarded without competitive
bidding with the express written authorization of the federal agency or state
pass-through agency that awarded the federal funds so long as awarding the
contract without competition is consistent with state law.
City of Southport
Uniform Guidance Conflict of Interst Policy
Effective July 1, 2018
Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to establish conflicts of interest guidelines
that meet or exceed the requirements under state law and local policy when
procuring goods (apparatus, supplies, materials, and equipment), services, and
construction or repair projects paid for in part or whole by federal funds and
required under 2 C.F.R. § 200.318(c)(1).
Policy
This policy applies when procuring goods (apparatus, supplies, materials, and
equipment), services, and construction or repair projects funded in part or
whole with federal financial assistance (direct or reimbursed). This policy
also applies to any subrecipient of the funds.
The employee responsible for managing the federal financial assistance award
shall review the notice of award to identify any additional conflicts of
interest prohibitions or requirements associated with the award, and shall
notify all employees, officers, and agents, including subrecipients, of the
requirements of this policy and any additional prohibitions or requirements.
Conflicts of Interest. In addition to the prohibition against self-benefiting
from a public contract under G.S. 14-234, no officer, employee, or agent of the
City of Southport may participate directly or indirectly in the selection,
award, or administration of a contract supported by a federal award if he or
she has a real or apparent conflict of interest. A real or apparent conflict
exists when any of the following parties has a financial or other interest in
or receives a tangible personal benefit from a firm considered for award of a
contract:
   the employee, officer, or agent involved in the selection, award, or
administration of a contract;
   any member of his or her immediate family;
   his or her partner; or
   an organization which employs or is about to employ any of these parties.
Any officer, employee, or agent with an actual, apparent, or potential conflict
of interest as defined in this policy shall report the conflict to his or her
immediate supervisor. Any such conflict shall be disclosed in writing to the
federal award agency or pass-through entity in accordance with applicable
Federal awarding agency policy.
Gifts. In addition to the prohibition against accepting gifts and favors from
vendors and contractors under G.S. 133-32, officers, employees, and agents of
the City of Southport are prohibited from accepting or soliciting gifts,
gratuities, favors, or anything of monetary value from contractors, suppliers,
or parties to subcontracts. Items of nominal value valued at less than $100
which fall into one of the following categories may be accepted:
   promotional items;
   honorariums for participation in meetings; or
   meals furnished at banquets.
Any officer, employee or agent who knowingly accepts an item of nominal value
allowed under this policy shall report the item to his or her immediate
supervisor.
Violation
Employees violating this policy will be subject to discipline up to and
including termination. Contractors violating this policy will result in
termination of the contract and may not be eligible for future contract awards.

shown on MB 78 PG 98 of the Brunswick County Records.
Thence with the south line of said Cades Cove Subdivision, N79°08’16”E, 144.36’
to the PRINCIPAL PLACE OF BEGINNING FOR THIS SURVEY.
Thence leaving said south line of and into said Cades Cove Subdivision,
N19°28’04”E, 281.37’ to a point;
Thence S70°27’07”E, 479.78’ to a point on the south line of said Cades Cove
Subdivision;
Thence with said south line of Cades Cove Subdivision, S79°08’16”W, 555.86’ to
the PRINCIPAL PLACE OF BEGINNING.

of Elections, as required by G.S. 163A-1594.

   5.   Public Hearing; Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment; Article
17 Signs, Section 2 and Section 5 (ZA 18-0412-01)
   City Planner Lloyd explained the specifics of a proposed text amendment to
permit billboards in a section of the Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district.
He stated that the Board of Aldermen were required to hold a public hearing and
adopt a statement of consistency and adopt an ordinance accepting the text
amendment, or a resolution denying the request. He reported that the Planning
Board considered the amendment and found it not consistent with the CAMA Core
Land Use Plan, not in the public interest, not a public necessity, and
permitting the billboards would set a precedent for allowing them in other
areas of the city. Planner Lloyd stated that the Planning Board recommended
that the Board of Aldermen not adopt the text amendment.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to open Public Hearing.
   Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Mr. Brian Keesee, agent to the applicant, stated his position that the
request permitting billboards in the HC zoning district would not affect
downtown and would be a good use of the 5 acre property formerly a part of the
Southport Crossing development at NC 211 and Long Beach Road Extension. Mr.
Keesee noted that there are currently two “grandfathered” billboards nearer to
the city’s business center.
   Mr. Gray Vick, a sign contractor, stated that the proposed text amendment
would allow multiple billboards in one area and would set a precedent for more
and more similar requests. He pointed out that the proposed 500’ spacing
between signs was not consistent with the County’s 2,000’ spacing requirement
and the height limit of 40’ would be more suitable to an interstate.
   Mr. Patrick Newton, a sign contractor, agreed with Mr. Vick’s observations.
Mr. Newton suggested that an approved text amendment be consistent with the
County’s regulations for billboards; 2,000’ spacing, 30 sq. ft. maximum size,
25’ maximum height and a 15’ setback.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Sharkey to close Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Pointing out that the Planning Board had made its findings, Attorney
Isenberg advised the Board that they were not bound by the Planning Board
findings and could find that the proposed text amendment is consistent with the
CAMA Core Land Use Plan and in the public interest.
   Noting that the NC 211 improvements and construction of an overpass are to
start soon in the area, Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Sharkey to
deny the proposed text amendment, and adopt the Resolution and a Statement of
Inconsistency. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
RESOLUTION DENYING APPLICATION FOR AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE 17 OF THE CITY OF
SOUTHPORT UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE
THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City’s
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city’s land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, the applicant, Brian Kessee, has submitted in a proposed amendment
to Sections 3 and 5 in Article 17 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance to allow billboards in a certain area of the Highway Commercial
District; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly reviewed this matter and found
that the proposed amendment to Article 17 of the Unified Development Ordinance
to be inconsistent with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and does
not recommend its approval; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on July 12, 2018 before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby finds that the
proposed text amendment is not consistent with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan for
the reasons stated in its Statement of Plan Consistency attached hereto; and;
WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is not
reasonable and in the public interest for the reasons stated in the Statement
of Plan Consistency attached hereto;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
proposed amendment to Article 17 of the Southport Unified Development Ordinance
is hereby denied.
This, the 12th day of July, 2018.               City of Southport

City of Southport Board of Aldermen               Statement of Plan Consistency
                              (as per NC General Statute 160A-383)
Zoning regulations shall be made in accordance with a comprehensive plan. Prior
to adopting or rejecting any zoning amendment, the governing board shall adopt
one of the following statements which shall not be subject to judicial review;
1) A statement approving the zoning amendment and describing its consistency
with an adopted comprehensive plan and explaining why the action taken is
reasonable and in the public interest. 2) A statement rejecting the zoning
amendment and describing its inconsistency with an adopted comprehensive plan
and explaining why the action taken is reasonable and in the public interest.
3) A statement approving the zoning amendment and containing at least all of
the following: A declaration that the approval is also deemed an amendment to
the comprehensive plan. The governing board shall not require any additional
request or application for amendment to the comprehensive plan, an explanation
of the change in conditions the governing board took into account in amending
the zoning ordinance to meet the development needs of the community, why the
action was reasonable and in the public interest.
                        (NCGS 160A-383)
TEXT AMENDMENT:      ZA-18-0412-01
STATEMENT OF CONSISTENCY AND RECCOMENDATION:
The City of Southport Board of Aldermen hereby find that the proposed text
amendment is not consistent with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan adopted November
13, 2014 because it goes against Policy 90 in the CAMA Land Use Plan. Policy 90
states that the City will encourage development that will protect its resources
and preserve its atmosphere, and simultaneously promote industrial and retail
growth. The Board of Aldermen feels that the addition of Billboards would not
protect and preserve the atmosphere of Southport. Furthermore, the Board of
Aldermen finds that the proposed text amendment is not reasonable and in the
public interest because allowing Billboards in this area would not be uniform
with other areas in the City zoned Highway Commercial, allowing Billboards is
not a public necessity, and allowing billboards in one area of highway
commercial would start a precedent of allowing them in certain areas. At their
meeting on July 12, 2018, the Board of Aldermen found the proposed amendment to
be INCONSISTENT with the goals, objectives, and policies, of the CAMA Land Use
Plan.
The statement and motion was seconded and passed July 12, 2018.
                              /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk   
   6.   Unified Development Ordinance Update Phase 1
   City Planner Lloyd reported that city staff had been negotiating with the
Cape Fear Council of Governments (COG) for an update of the CAMA Core Land Use
Plan and a review and audit of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). He
stated that the Planning Board would be the advisory committee working with the
consultants. Planner Lloyd stated that the fee for Phase I of the project is
not-to-exceed $12,000 and staff would proceed with the COG at the pleasure of
the Board.
   Responding to a query by Alderman Powell, Planner Lloyd estimated the
project would take one (1) to two (2) years to complete and the cost stretched
over two budget cycles.
   Alderman Mosteller motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to approve
contracting with The Cape Fear Council of Governments to complete Phase 1 of
the Land Use Plan & UDO update. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

SOUTHPORT
RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF INTERNATIONAL DAY OF PEACE

WHEREAS, The United Nations in 1981 established a yearly International Day of
Peace, a day devoted to strengthening the ideals of peace both within and among
all nations and people; and
WHEREAS, The International Day of Peace is now observed around the world each
year on September 20 to put aside all that separates us and to experience
peace; and
WHEREAS, in 1984, the General Assembly adopted the Declaration on the Right of
Peoples to Peace; and
WHEREAS, the theme of the 2018 International Day of Peace is "The Right to
Peace"; and
WHEREAS, Southport residents are coordinating a celebration of the
International Day of Peace on a local level; and
WHEREAS, the Celebration of Peace will be held and will include songs, dances,
art, informational booths and exhibits, a Peace Circle discussion, children
crafts, and a Peace Pilgrim film; and
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Mayor and Southport Board of Aldermen
on this the 9th day of August 2018, hereby proclaim Saturday, September 15,
2018 as "Peace Day" in the City of Southport and urge all citizens to join in
the festivities of this day and promote peace among all peoples.
                         /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

EQUIPMENT TRANSFER
This Equipment Transfer ("Transfer") has occurred between the Town of Shallotte
("Shallotte"), a North Carolina municipality, located at 106 Cheers Street,
Post Office Box 2287, Shallotte, North Carolina 28459, and the City of
Southport ("Southport"), a North Carolina municipality located at 1029 N. Howe
Street, Southport, North Carolina 28461,who may hereinafter be referred to
individually as "Party" and jointly as "Parties."
WHEREAS, "Shallotte" and "Southport" have forged a partnership to protect and
serve the public safety interests within Brunswick County;
WHEREAS, "Southport" has expressed an interest in acquiring a 1987 Ford C-8000
FMC 50' TeleSquirt ladder truck holding the vehicle identification number of
VIN IFDYD8OU6HVA64644,("Equipment") which was previously used by the Town of
Shallotte Fire/Rescue Department, to be used by the City of Southport Fire
Department in support of its current aerial apparatus fleet;
WHEREAS, the Town of Shallotte Board of Aldermen authorized the "Transfer" of
the aforementioned asset on August 7, 2018, as a gesture of good faith in
wanting and willingness to continue to support protecting and serving the
public safety interests within the Brunswick County and Southport's
jurisdiction;
WHEREAS, the Town of Shallotte, under G.S. 160A-280, may donate to another
governmental unit within the US, a sister city, or nonprofit organization
incorporated by the United States, the District of Columbia, or one of the
United States, any personal property, including supplies, materials, and
equipment, that the governing board deems to be surplus, obsolete, or unused;
NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements
contained in this "Transfer", and for good and valuable consideration, the
receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the "Parties" agree
to the "Transfer" as follows:
1. "Shallotte" hereby transfers to "Southport" all rights, title and interest
in the Equipment, and "Southport" accepts all rights, title and interest in the
Equipment.
2. "Shallotte" warrants that title to the Equipment as transferred to
"Southport" shall be free and clear of any liens or encumbrances.
3. "Southport" hereby assumes all risk of loss of the Equipment and accepts the
Equipment AS IS, WHERE-IS, AND WITH ALL FAULTS, known or unknown.
4. "Shallotte" DISCLAIMS AND MAKES NO WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, WITH REGARD
TO THE EQUIPMENT, INCLUDING WARRANTIES OF OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
5. "Southport" shall hereby defend, indemnify and hold harmless "Shallotte",
its affiliates, and each of their officers, agents, employees, assigns and
successors in interest from and against any and all liability, damages, losses,
claims, demands, actions, causes of action, costs (including attorney's fees
and expenses), or any of them, arising out of Southport's ownership or use of
the Equipment.
6. This "Transfer" contains the entire agreement and understanding between the
Parties regarding the Equipment and merges and supersedes all prior
representations and discussions pertaining to the subject matter herein.
7. This "Transfer" shall be interpreted, governed and construed under the laws
of the State of North Carolina.
9. The person signing this Agreement represents that he or she is duly
authorized to execute this "Transfer" on behalf of the Party for whom he or she
signs, and to fully bind such Party to this "Transfer".

AGENDA
7.   Public Hearing; Zoning Map Amendment Residential (R-10) to Multi-Family
(MF) for Parcel ID's: 221MA006, 221MA00802, 221MA00804, 221MA00805, 221MA00803,
221MA00801 (RZ 18-0613-01)
   Building Inspector Strickland explained that developer RHH Land Investors
has requested a zoning map amendment for six parcels in the vicinity of 11th
Street for a proposed 38 unit multi-family townhome complex. Mr. Strickland
indicated that the parcels are currently zoned R-10 (residential) and are
surrounded by multi-family zoning. He stated that the Planning Board had
reviewed the request, found the properties highly suitable for development; the
zoning map amendment was consistent with the CAMA Core Land Use Plan and
recommend that the Board of Aldermen approves it.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Coring to Open Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Ms. Lena Tobler, 215 W. 11th Street, asked about the location on 11th
Street. Mr. Strickland explained where the area was located.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to Close Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
8.   Consideration of Zoning Map Amendment
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to approve the zoning
map amendment. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
STATEMENT OF CONSISTENCY AND RECCOMENDATION:
The City of Southport Board of Aldermen hereby finds that the proposed zoning
map amendment is consistent with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan adopted November
13, 2014. The Board of Aldermen feels that the proposed amendment is consistent
with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan because it is shown as highly suitable for
development on the Land Suitability Analysis map and it is surrounded by
properties currently zoned multifamily. Further, the Board of Aldermen believes
it is reasonable and in the public interest because additional land zoned
multifamily is needed in the City. At their meeting on August 9, 2018, the
Board of Aldermen stated that the proposed amendment is CONSISTENT with the
goals, objectives, and policies, of the Land Use Plan.
AN ORDINANCE APPROVING A ZONING MAP AMENDMENT REZONING PARCELS
221MA006, 221MA00801, 221MA00802, 221MA00803, 221MA00804, AND 221MA00805
FROM R-10 TO MF
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances, and a zoning map that control land development within both
the City's incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city's zoning map; and
   WHEREAS, the applicant, RHH Land Investors, has prepared and submitted an
application for a zoning map amendment to rezone the above mentioned parcels;
and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has thoroughly reviewed this matter and found
that the proposed zoning map to be consistent with the City of Southport CAMA
Core Land Use Plan and recommends its approval; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on August 9, 2018 before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, hereby finds that the
proposed text amendment is consistent with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan for the
reasons stated in its consistency statement attached hereto and incorporated
herein; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is
reasonable and in the public interest because additional land zoned multifamily
is needed in the City;
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that the
Official Zoning Map of the City of Southport, an element of the Unified
Development Ordinance of the City, is amended by changing the zoning
classification of the below described property from R-10 to MF:
Tax Parcel ID's of properties to be rezoned:
221MA006, 221MA00801, 221MA00802, 221MA00803, 221MA00804, and 221MA00805
This ordinance shall be effective upon its adoption, and the Official Zoning
Map of the City of Southport shall be revised accordingly.
This, the 9th day of August, 2018.

amendment is consistent with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan. The Board of Aldermen
feels that the allowance of one sign per street frontage in multiple tenant
developments larger than 5 acres in areas zoned highway commercial is
consistent with CAMA Land Use Plan because it adheres with Policy 90. Further
the Board of Aldermen finds that the proposed text amendment is reasonable and
in the public interest because it will promote economic development in the city
and it will allow larger multi-tenant developments to have adequate signage. At
their meeting on August 9th, 2018, the Board of Aldermen stated that the
proposed amendment is CONSISTENT with the goals, objectives, and policies, of
the Land Use Plan

11.   Public Hearing; Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment, Article 15
Residential Cluster Development (ZA 18-0613-01)
   Building Inspector Strickland explained that RHH Land Investors have
requested a zoning text amendment to allow a 50 foot right-of-way in
residential cluster developments in order to further preserve the natural
character of the site. Mr. Strickland stated that the 50 feet is an adequate
amount of space to install all utilities and infrastructure. Mr. Strickland
reported that the Planning Board had thoroughly considered the proposed text
amendment and found it reasonable because NCDOT's minimum right-of-way for
local roads in their design criteria is 40 feet and the amendment is consistent
with the CAMA Core Land Use Plan. Mr. Strickland stated that the Planning Board
and staff recommend that the Board of Aldermen adopt the text amendment.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to Open Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   There were no public comments.
   Alderman Powell motioned second by Alderman Coring to close Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
12.   Consideration of UDO Text Amendment
   Alderman Pukenas motioned, second by Alderman Spencer to approve the UDO
Text Amendment. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
STATEMENT OF CONSISTENCY AND RECCOMENDATION:
The City of Board of Aldermen hereby finds that the proposed text amendment is
consistent with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan. The Board of Aldermen feels that
the allowance of a 50 foot ROW is Consistent with the CAMA Land Use Plan
because it adheres with Policies 25, 45, and 90. Further the Board of Aldermen
finds that the proposed text amendment is reasonable and in the public interest
because it will allow developers to better preserve the natural character of
cluster development sites while having adequate room for the installation of
infrastructure. At their meeting on August 9th, 2018, the Board of Aldermen
stated that the proposed amendment is CONSISTENT with the goals, objectives,
and policies, of the Land Use Plan.

AUGUST 29, 2018
SPECIAL SESSION MINUTES
 
BOARD OF ALDERMEN     SPECIAL SESSION MINUTES
COMMUNITY BUILDING  AUGUST 29, 2018
223 E. BAY STREET     SOUTHPORT, N.C.
 
PRESENT:         Mayor J.V. Dove
            Aldermen Karen Mosteller, Jim Powell, Todd Coring,
            Marc Spencer, Rick Pukenas
ABSENT:         Alderman Lora Sharkey
STAFF PRESENT:      Bruce Oakley, City Manager
   Michele Windham, City Clerk
   David Fox, Public Works Director
   Heather Hemphill, Parks & Recreation Director
   Randy Jones, Tourism Director
   B. Wayne Strickland, Building Inspector
   Thomas Lloyd, Planner
A)   Call to Order - 5:30 p.m.
Mayor Dove called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.
B)   Invocation
Alderman Coring welcomed everyone and gave the invocation.
C)   Pledge of Allegiance
   Alderman Coring led the assemblage in the Pledge of Allegiance.
……………………………….
   Mayor Dove stated that over the past six (6) months, the Board of Aldermen
had been considering and discussing the course of action to take with the City
Boat Dock. He noted that special meetings had been held to provide information
to the public and to receive comments, concerns and suggestions. He declared
that the purpose of the meeting was for the Board to gather information from
CAMA and the Army Corps of Engineers in order to make a wise and informed
decision.
   Mayor Dove introduced Ms. Debbie Wilson, District Manager for the N.C.
Division of Coastal Management (CAMA) and Mr. Todd Horton, Chief of Geospatial
Services for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. Mayor Dove recognized Thad
Moore, vice-president of finance for Preston Development Company and Hank
Whitley, Manager of Southport Marina.
   City Manager Oakley gave a brief update on the status of the Police
Department audit:
   ∙   The audit has been ongoing for the past two weeks
   ∙   Policies and procedures are being audited
   ∙   Findings will result in a stronger, better department
   City Manager Oakley expressed appreciation to the Sheriff's Office for
providing law enforcement coverage.
   City Manager Oakley pointed out that during the Board's annual retreat, the
#1 priority was to get the City Dock back into a safe, accessible, and
functional condition with the Mayor and Aldermen Powell and Sharkey appointed
to a committee to oversee the project. City Manager Oakley stated that the
Committee was included in meetings with NCDOT, CAMA, The Corps and Land
Management. He pointed out that a partnership with Southport Marina was the
best option after discussions of limitations with permitting organizations. At
an April special meeting, the Board directed the City Manager to proceed with a
Letter of Intent (LOI) with Southport Marina and at the April regular meeting,
the Board approved the LOI. He displayed a slide showing the area of limitation
for building in the city owned portion of the Yacht Basin.
   Referencing meeting highlights prepared by Steve Morrison of Land
Management, from a March 1, 2018 interagency scoping meeting, Alderman
Mosteller asked about the Corps denying the rebuilding of the "L" portion of
the city dock. Ms. Wilson explained the Corps navigational channel, required
setbacks and riparian rights.
   Alderman Mosteller asked if the City rebuilt the dock in the same footprint
and stopped at the navigational line, would the dock comply with the CAMA non-
conforming structure rules. Ms. Wilson stated that CAMA would consider
permitting the rebuilding of the dock if it was put back exactly as it is now,
or shortened. She pointed out that anything outside the footprint would be
denied and then a variance with the Coastal Resource Commission (CRC) would
have to be pursued. She added that the same procedure would apply if the City
partnered with the Marina.
   Alderman Mosteller asked if it would be required for the dock to be stick
built. Ms. Wilson stated a stick built or floating dock would be acceptable
based on the non-conforming structure regulations.
   Alderman Mosteller asked Mr. Horton if the Corps would permit rebuilding to
the navigational line and into the setback. Mr. Horton responded that it would
be a tight fit and he pointed out that the setback is 15 feet.
   Mayor Dove asked if there would be impediments with other property owners'
riparian rights. Noting the structure would be "grandfathered", Ms. Wilson
stated a riparian rights objection could affect the permitting decision.
   Referencing a handout listing six (6) options, Alderman Mosteller cited:
   Option 1    Replace City Dock with new fixed dock, in the same footprint as
the existing dock, stopping short at the Federal Navigational Channel Line;
Would allow for approximately 200 feet of dock, approximately 11 to 15 20' boat
slips. She estimated that a rental fee of $200/mo./slip would pay for the
maintenance of the dock. Mr. Horton emphasized that nothing can go into the
channel.
   Alderman Mosteller stated her understanding that $124,000 in reimbursable
funds available from Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) could be used
for a stick built or floating dock. She commented that the leasing of slips
could be executed as a lottery to make it fair and equitable.
   Alderman Pukenas asked for clarification that the dock could be rebuilt as a
fixed or floating structure and he asked if permission was required from
adjacent property owners with riparian rights. Ms. Wilson responded that the
City should be able to do either type structure and would be required to notify
persons with riparian rights.
   Alderman Pukenas asked if CAMA or the Corps had any concerns about dredging
the Yacht Basin. Mr. Horton stated that he foresaw no issues as long as the
structure is removed in order to do the dredging.
   Alderman Spencer asked about removal of the existing pilings. Ms. Wilson
stated that the City would have to go through the permitting process.
   City Manager Oakley stated his understanding from the scoping meetings, that
the structure was deemed 50% damaged and the new structure rules would apply
for replacement. Ms. Wilson responded that the non-conforming regulations
provided some allowances.
   Option 2   Same as Option 1 utilizing floating dock. Replace existing City
Dock with new floating dock, in the same footprint as the existing dock,
stopping short at the Federal Navigational Channel line.
   Alderman Coring asked Ms. Wilson to expand on "riparian rights." Ms. Wilson
explained that riparian rights refer to allocation of water space among those
who possess land along its path. Additionally, she stated that there is a 15
ft. setback requirement and a waiver from each riparian rights holder would be
needed to encroach into those setbacks.
   Alderman Powell asked for clarification that the dock is "grandfathered" and
the main line of the structure could be rebuilt. Ms. Wilson stated that the
structure is grandfathered for the structure out to the L section. She pointed
out that reconstructing the L would not be allowable.
   Alderman Powell asked if a pump out station would be required and what
agency would need to permit it. Ms. Wilson stated that a pump out station would
be required when a facility had more than 10 slips. She added that a portable
station one could be used and permitting of a station was not under the
oversight of CAMA. She did not indicate which agency to contact.
   Option 3   The Corps suggested footprint dated November 9, 2017. This
footprint extends beyond existing first section of the dock and allows for an
"L" section to be in the Corps setback but not in the navigational channel. The
Corps will not allow pilings in the Federal Navigational Channel.
   Ms. Wilson explained that Option 3 was the option that would trigger a
denial and the need to pursue a variance as it would expand the footprint, be
considered new construction and would have to conform to current regulations.
   Responding to a query from Alderman Spencer, Ms. Wilson stated that tearing
off the L portion of the dock does not require a CAMA permit as long as no
digging occurs.
   Option 4   Small dock with no slips extending a maximum of ¼ of the water
body distance.
   Alderman Pukenas asked if consent from adjacent property owners would be
required for Option 4. Ms. Wilson stated that those properties with riparian
rights would only need to be notified of the project. City Manager Oakley noted
that Option 4 would allow for two (2) or three (3) slips only.
   Option 5   The City of Southport Basin Expansion project; creates a dock
approximately 800 feet long, portions owned by the Southport Marina and City of
Southport. The City of Southport would provide a perpetual easement to the
Southport Marina and the dock would be managed by the Southport Marina.
   Alderman Mosteller asked if Option 5 would require a new permit, which would
be turned down, and then have to go through the variance process. Ms. Wilson
concurred.
   Alderman Mosteller asked if a joint permit was submitted by the City and
Southport Marina and one party wanted to withdraw, would both parties have to
withdraw. Ms. Wilson responded that both parties would have to withdraw.
   Speaking about Option 5, Alderman Mosteller stated that the increased size
and scale of the proposed project would include nearly 800 feet of dock wrapped
around the marsh, have 50 slips, Marina section would include 40 ft. slips that
are contrary to everything currently in the Yacht Basin and the investment for
taxpayers would be larger than what can be grandfathered in.
   Alderman Pukenas asked Mr. Whitley if any restrictions would be in place on
the 40 ft. slips to prohibit extension into the navigational channel. Mr.
Whitley stated that the Marina's goal would be to have boats that fit into the
slips and do not extend into the channel.
   Alderman Spencer asked if the Marina would allow public access on their
dock. Speaking to the potential partnership with the City, Mr. Whitley stated
that access would be open on the city portion of the dock and controlled on the
Marina's portion. Alderman Spencer stated appreciation for and thanked
Southport Marina for being a good neighbor.
   Alderman Mosteller noted that objections and concerns were received from the
Cape Fear Pilots Association regarding navigation within the Yacht Basin and
that larger working fish boats are not as maneuverable as the Pilot boats. She
added that business owners submitted letters about the potential negative
impacts. She commented that the Board had reached a crossroad and had a duty to
protect the Yacht Basin, the heart of the community, its history. She stated
her opinion that it was never envisioned that the Yacht Basin would become part
of the Marina which would be counter to the CAMA Core Land Use Plan and the
City's vision and core value - historic preservation.
   Mayor Dove asked if the Marina would have objections to the City rebuilding
the dock in the current footprint and if the Marina would continue with their
plans to build boat slips along the marsh. Mr. Moore replied that the Marina
would have to explore its options.
   Option 6   Do nothing.
   Alderman Pukenas thanked Ms. Wilson and Mr. Horton for attending the meeting
and helping the Board work through the issue.
   Alderman Coring stated appreciation for the information and said that his
questions and concerns had been addressed.
    Alderman Mosteller thanked Mr. Moore and Mr. Whitley for attending the
meeting. She stated her hope that the Marina would join with the City in
preserving the marsh and maintaining the Yacht Basin as a working dock.
   Mayor Dove thanked CAMA, the Corps, Marina and citizens for attending the
meeting.
   Alderman Pukenas shared a statement he found in a historical book about
Southport, written by Mr. Curtis, Editor of the Southport Herald in 1909, and
which he felt still applied: "Southport is already a naturally beautiful city
and could be more so but growth to a larger and greater city is inevitable.
When the growth does come, it shouldn't be sacrificed to commercialism.
Destroying the natural beauty and charm of the town to enhance commercial
development or preserve its unique qualities through development sensitive to
these values."
   Alderman Pukenas motioned, second by Alderman Powell to wait until the
September regular meeting to vote on the City Dock. Unanimous vote; motion
carried.
ADJOURN
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Spencer to adjourn the meeting.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

   Ms. Susan Rice, 203 Stuart Avenue, presented the following petition signed
by 32 citizens:
Petition for Additional Storm Drains for the City of Southport, NC
We, the residents of the City of Southport, petition the city to install
additional storm drains due to the severe flooding that occurs in the 100
through 300-Blk ranges of Stuart Avenue as well as the intersection of E.
Leonard Street. This is insufficient storm drainage for the city properties of
residents who suffer great flood issues during heavy rainstorms and
catastrophic weather events. Due to the city not being able to assist the
citizens with pumping as well as the lack of storm drains, citizens’ property
values are left to suffer in these exigent, reoccurring circumstances. What’s
more, since the construction of the new development ‘The Hammocks’ located off
of the 100-Blk of Stuart Avenue; flooding has become devastating to properties,
city streets and local roadways. This is creating additional issues within the
city such as sewage run-off and mosquito ridden standing water which not only
affects the property value but the health and welfare of the residents of this
area. The Brunswick County Health Department has issued dire warning of the
toxicity of this run-off which is a grave health concern to citizens and
animals alike. We have been made aware that there is existing storm water
pipeline that runs in the block ranges of the affected area of concern. We, the
below signed petitioners, have voiced our concerns and are seeking for the City
of Southport officials to not just recognize the issue as has been done in the

RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, on Saturday, November 3, 2018 the Southport Wooden Boat Show will be
held at the Old Southport Yacht Basin; and
WHEREAS, the 9th Annual Southport Wooden Boat Show, a 501(c) 3 organization
will be held from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m.; and
WHEREAS, this year’s show is expected to be bigger and better than the previous
events with more boats, demonstrators, nautical/maritime exhibits and children
events; and
WHEREAS, boats will be displayed in and around the historic Old Yacht Basin;
and
WHEREAS, visitors can meet and talk with wooden boat makers and owners; and
WHEREAS, visitors will be able to vote for their favorite boat entrant for the
People’s Choice Award, and
WHEREAS, other awards will be given in various categories; and
WHEREAS, wooden boat shows across the country are popular with boat builders
and restorers; and
WHEREAS, the Southport Wooden Boat Show Committee encourages people to preserve
the wooden boat and nautical history for which Southport is known.
NOW  THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Mayor and Southport Board of Aldermen
on this the 15th day of October, hereby proclaim November 3, 2018 as Southport
Wooden Boat Show Day in the City of Southport and invite citizens and
surrounding communities to help make this day a success.
                      /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor

CITY OF SOUTHPORT
DOMESTIC VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, Domestic Violence Awareness Month, also known as DVAM originated from
the “Day of Unity” that was held in October of 1981 and was conceived by the
National Coalition Against Domestic Violence. This single day quickly evolved
into an entire week and in 1987 the first Domestic Violence Awareness Month was
observed; and
WHEREAS, Domestic Violence Awareness Month founders began this initiative to
connect advocates across the nation who were already working to end violence
against women and their children. The goal was to bring together the
individuals in a group effort to have a stronger voice against violence; and
WHEREAS, The, now month, of awareness is full of activities to make it known to
each participating community the serious issue that our nation is undergoing.
It is also an opportunity to let them know the resources available to them in
the case that they were to need help; and
WHEREAS, The advocates and staff here at Hope Harbor Home take great pride in
this month of activities and see it as an opportunity to reach more people in
Brunswick County who may be looking for help. HHH has been in operation for
over 30 years and in those years has served thousands of women, men, and
children. Domestic Violence Awareness Month sends a clear, much needed, message
that Brunswick County, North Carolina is united against violence.
NOW THEREFORE, I, J. V. Dove, Mayor of the City of Southport, North Carolina,
and the Board of Aldermen, do hereby proclaim October as Domestic Violence
Awareness Month in the City and urge all citizens of Southport to show your
support for ending domestic violence.
This 15th day of October 2018.
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
Resolution
Proclaiming October 8 – 14, 2018
Fire Prevention Week
WHEREAS, the Southport Fire Department is committed to ensuring the safety and
security of all those living in and visiting our Fire District; and
WHEREAS, fire is a serious public safety concern both locally and nationally,
and homes are the locations where people are at the greatest risk of fire; and
WHEREAS, the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) has documented through
its research a significant increase in home fires, and due to this fact, it is
important that everyone know two ways out of your home in case of a fire; and
WHEREAS, the Firefighters of the Southport Fire Department are dedicated to
reducing the occurrence of residential and commercial structural fires and fire
related injuries through prevention and protection education; and
WHEREAS, the residents of the Southport Fire District are responsive to public
education measures and are able to take personal steps to increase their safety
from fire; and
WHEREAS, being prepared in the event of a home fire will have a positive effect
on the home fire problem; and
WHEREAS, each home fire that is prevented in the Southport Fire District is an
opportunity to prevent painful injury and costly property damage; and
WHEREAS, the 2018 Fire Prevention Week theme, Hot Things Burn, effectively
serves to remind us all of the simple actions we can take to stay safer from
fire every day.
THEREFORE, I J. V. Dove, Mayor of the City of Southport do hereby proclaim
October 8-14, 2018 as Fire Prevention Week throughout this City, and I urge all
the citizens of Southport to heed the important safety messages from the
Southport Fire Prevention Team, and the Office of the City Fire Marshal and to
support the many public safety activities and efforts of the Southport Fire
Department.
                     /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
Attest: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

12.   Burial In Old Smithville Burying Ground
   Building Inspector Strickland explained a request from Mr. Samual Watts for
permission to place a cremation vault in a family plot in Old Smithville
Burying Ground. Mr. Strickland stated that the burying grounds were closed to
burials for all except those who had permits issued prior to August 31, 2000.
Mr. Strickland indicated that Mr. Watts did not have a permit and in order to
get an exception to the Ordinance, he would have to petition the Board of
Aldermen. Mr. Strickland stated that many years ago an archaeologist from
Raleigh was hired by a group of plot owners to do a survey and determine if
burials could be allowed. Those plots that the survey showed was clear were
issued permits. Responding to a query by Alderman Sharkey, Mr. Strickland
stated that a 2 x 2 area would hold a cremation vault.
   Alderman Sharkey motioned, second by Alderman Spencer to authorize Mr. Watts
to explore the possibility of having cremains put in cemetery plot as long as
he pays for a permit and pays for the archaeological survey to be performed to
the satisfaction of the Cemetery Superintendent.
Discussion
   Alderman Pukenas noted that the 2000 Ordinance requires a 3 x 8 plot.
   Alderman Mosteller stated her reluctance to permit an exception to the
Ordinance that she feels is well thought out and complete.
   Alderman Coring asked how Mr. Watts could obtain a permit and if many
requests of this type were made. Mr. Strickland stated that an archaeological
survey showing no evidence of burial would be required for issuance of a burial
permit and the last request was made by Joe Mintz.
   AYES:    Aldermen Sharkey, Spencer, Coring
   NAYS:    Aldermen Powell, Mosteller, Pukenas
   NAY:    Mayor Dove
   Motion fails 4-3
13.   Board Consideration of Replacing the City Dock in the Original Footprint
(outside the Army Corps of Engineers Navigational Channel)
   Noting that Southport Marina had withdrawn their interest in the city dock
project, Alderman Pukenas motioned, second by Alderman Mosteller to direct
staff to pursue a design plan for a floating dock system, fixed dock system, or
a combination of the two in the original footprint and to expedite this as soon
as possible.
   Discussion
   Alderman Powell pointed out that the issue of a pump out station needed to
be addressed. Alderman Pukenas stated that a pump out station could be included
in the design plan.
   Alderman Sharkey emphasized that dredging of the entire Yacht Basin would be
required before a dock could be built. She pointed out that funding had not
been budgeted for dredging and the approval process is nine months to a year.
   Alderman Mosteller stated that the State has a 66/33 matching grant program
that the City could pursue and she felt it short sighted not to use the FEMA
reimbursement funds approved for Hurricane Matthew damage to the city dock. She
added that the time required for permitting would allow for people to donate
towards the project. She contended that rentals of boat slips would pay for
dock maintenance and upkeep.
   Alderman Powell agreed with Alderman Sharkey that dredging should be the
highest priority along with permission for a spoil site. He estimated the cost
could be upwards to $350,000.
   Alderman Pukenas shared his understanding that a design plan needs to be in
place before any approvals can be obtained from the permitting agencies. He
noted that citizens are interested in helping with funding. He agreed with
Alderman Mosteller that FEMA funds from Hurricane Matthew should be utilized.
   Alderman Sharkey asked how a design plan would be funded. She stated the
City has an obligation to clean up the old dock. She proposed going through a
Capital Improvement Plan and she questioned the investment of money for so few
slips.
   Alderman Mosteller voiced her understanding that the old dock could not be
removed until CAMA and the Army Corps of Engineers approved a replacement plan.
She suggested the slips could be awarded via a lottery with a three year
rental.
   AYES:    Aldermen Pukenas, Mosteller, Spencer, Coring
   NAYS: Aldermen Powell, Sharkey
   Motion carried 4-2   
14.   Adoption of Pay Policy for Aldermen
   Alderman Sharkey motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to discontinue the per
diem payments of $25 per meeting for each Alderman, excluding the Mayor and to
adopt the following policy:
   Aldermen compensation will consist of one monthly payment. This amount will
be the same for each of the Aldermen, regardless of committee assignments or
extra duties. Effective immediately, Aldermen will no longer receive extra
meeting pay. Funding for training and travel may be available depending on
money appropriated in the adopted City of Southport Budget. This policy applies
only to the position of Aldermen, it does not include the position of Mayor.
   Discussion
   Alderman Powell asked for a definition of a meeting. City Attorney Isenberg
responded that any duly called meeting of the Board of Aldermen with a quorum
is a meeting. He verified that every town/city is required by law to have a
regular monthly meeting and attendance as a liaison to other board or committee
meetings is not considered a meeting of the Board of Aldermen.
   Responding to a query by Alderman Coring, Alderman Sharkey stated that her
intent is to eliminate any payments for attending outside meetings and to
receive a flat monthly fee.
   Attorney Isenberg stated he had no issues with the proposed policy.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

   1.   Resolution Approving Contract for Emergency Repairs
   Alderman Powell asked to be recused. Alderman Pukenas motioned, second by
Alderman Sharkey to recuse Alderman Powell. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   City Manager Oakley explained that Ellixson & Sons, Inc. were retained to
make emergency repairs to the drainage and sewer systems of the City due to
Hurricane Florence. He stated that Ellixson was the only contractor in the area
at the time. Responding to a query by Alderman Sharkey, City Manager Oakley
reported that the majority of the repairs have been completed.
   Alderman Sharkey motioned, second by Alderman Spencer to adopt the
Resolution Approving and Ratifying Emergency Contract for emergency repairs
with Ellixson & Sons, Inc. Unanimous vote; motion carried.    (Contract on file
in the Clerk’s Office)
RESOLUTION APPROVING AND RATIFYING EMERGENCY CONTRACT
   THAT WHEREAS, G. S. 143-129 (e)(2) permits cities to enter into contracts
without going through the required bidding process in cases of special
emergency involving the health and safety of the people or their property; and
   WHEREAS, on or about September 14, 2018, Hurricane Florence struck the City
of Southport causing widespread damage and destruction; and
   WHEREAS, Hurricane Florence impacted the drainage and sewer systems of the
City necessitating immediate action by City staff in order to protect the
health and safety of the people; and
   WHEREAS, city staff immediately retained the services of Ellixson & Sons,
Inc., to perform emergency repairs as follows:
Storm drain repair on West 11th Street
Storm drain repair on Herring Drive
Storm drain repair on Park Avenue Extension
Storm drain repair on Atlantic Avenue
Storm drain repair on Caswell Avenue
Storm drain repair at Willis and Moore Streets
Sewer main repair at Howe and Brown Streets ; and
              WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen has determined and hereby finds
this to be a case of special emergency involving the health and safety of the
people or their property and that it was necessary for city staff to contract
with said contractor for immediate repairs to the drainage and sewer systems of
the city;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Southport that the contract dated September 16, 2018, between the City of
Southport and Ellixson & Sons, Inc., for the above-described work was entered
into as a result of a special emergency involving the health and safety of the
people and said contract is hereby approved and ratified.
   This the 23rd day of October, 2018.            City of Southport
                        /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk
   2.   Amendment to Personnel Policy – Section 3. Retirement Insurance
   City Manager Oakley explained that the proposed amendment to the Personnel
Policy would allow for employees hired after March 14, 2013 to receive benefits
after 20 years of service. He added that the benefit would help the City
recruit and retain good employees.
   Alderman Mosteller noted that neighboring communities provide the benefit.
Alderman Pukenas pointed out that Southport has been losing employees. Alderman
Sharkey emphasized that the proposed amendment would also provide a family
option for the employee which is not provided by Brunswick County.
   Alderman Powell motioned, second by Alderman Pukenas to approve the
amendment. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
A RESOLUTION AMENDING THE PERSONNEL POLICY
WITH REGARD TO RETIREE HEALTH INSURANCE
   WHEREAS the City of Southport Personnel Policy, Article IX, Section 3,
provides for certain health, life, and dental insurance benefits to be paid to
retirees, and
   WHEREAS the Board of Aldermen desires to amend such benefits for persons who
are hired or become creditable service employees going forward, but to leave
unchanged such benefits as they may apply to current retirees or creditable
service employees;
   BE IT RESOLVED that the Personnel Policy of the City of Southport, Article
IX, Section 3 is amended by the language shown below:
   The second and third paragraphs of this section, relating to the payment of
health, life, and dental insurance coverage for retired employees, shall not
apply to any employee who begins creditable service in the retirement system as
a City of Southport employee after March 14, 2013 or who is hired as a City
employee after March 14, 2013.
Retiring employees must make an election to continue or terminate coverage at
the time of their retirement. It they waive the right to continue at the date
of retirement, they may not elect coverage at a future date.
Employees hired after March 14, 2013 who retire with twenty (20) years of
creditable service with the City and are at least 55 years of age or have at
least thirty (30) years of creditable service as defined and accepted by the
North Carolina Local Government Employee’s Retirement System of which at least
(5) five of the years are with the City may continue in the City’s group health
and dental plans with the City paying 100% of the premium for the employee’s
coverage and the employee paying 100% of the premium for family or spouse
coverage. When the employee becomes eligible for Medicare, such coverage in the
City’s group plans will be the Medicare supplement, if offered by the plan
provider.
This the 23rd day of October, 2018.         City of Southport
   /s/ J. V. Dove, Mayor
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, City Clerk
