MAY 6 AND 8, 2020
City of Southport
Special Work Session-Manager Interviews
The Mayor and Southport Board of Aldermen met Wednesday May 6, 2020 at the
Southport Community Center to interview candidates for the position of City
Manager. Mayor Joe Pat Hatem presided. Mayor ProTem Mosteller, Aldermen
Spencer, Sharkey, Davis, Lombardi, and Interim Manager May attended. Alderman
Allen participated via teleconference. Interim Manager May recorded the
minutes. The meeting as called to order at 9:15 AM by Mayor Hatem who called
for a motion to enter Executive Session to consider qualifications and
interview candidates for Southport City Manager. Mayor ProTem Mosteller so
moved, seconded by Alderman Davis, and the motion carried unanimously.
Following interviews and subsequent consideration of qualifications, Mayor
ProTem moved to come out of Executive Session at 4:50 PM, seconded by Alderman
Allen. The motion carried unanimously. With all in agreement that they needed
an opportunity to consider all they heard; Mayor Hatem called for a motion to
recess until Friday May 8th at 10:00 AM at the Indian Trail Meeting Hall.
Alderman Davis so moved, seconded by Alderman Lombardi. The motion carried
unanimously. The meeting recessed at 5:05 PM.
The Mayor and Southport Board of Aldermen reconvened in special work session on
Friday May 8, 2020 at 10:00 AM at the Indian Trail Meeting Hall to continue
review and consideration of qualifications of City Manager candidates. Mayor
Hatem presided. Mayor ProTem Mosteller, Aldermen Spencer, Sharkey, Davis,
Lombardi, Allen, and Interim Manager May attended. Interim Manager May recorded
the minutes. Mayor Hatem called the meeting to order at 10:05 AM and called for
a motion to enter executive session to consider qualifications for manager
candidates. Alderman Davis so moved, and Alderman Spencer seconded. The motion
carried unanimously.
Following robust and extensive discussion, the Mayor entertained a motion to
close the executive session at 12:50. Mayor ProTem Mosteller so moved and
Alderman Davis seconded. The motion passed unanimously.
Mayor ProTem Mosteller moved to direct the Mayor and the Interim Manager to
contact the top candidate with an offer of employment. Alderman Allen seconded.
The motion carried unanimously. Alderman Davis moved to adjourn at 12:55. The
motion carried unanimously.

To the Aldermen of Southport,
It is with serious deep concern that I type this email. I look forward to the
opportunity to join with others who would like to physically be present and
speak on behalf of the concerns of Osprey Landing development planning further
progressing. This meeting being held without residents being able to physically
voice concerns is quite frustrating given we have numerous residents who are
lacking in the social media availability to see or hear the meeting conducted.
My name is Lauren Broadwell, I am a lifelong resident of the Southport-Oak
Island Area a current resident in the Smithville Woods neighborhood. Given the
circumstances an email is required as I personally would prefer to stand before
you and speak to all who hold the decisions of the development of Osprey
Landing and its effects in their hands. I will do my best to keep this email
brief and to the point, many have shared their frustrations and concerns with
me but I would like to specifically take a moment to highlight just a couple of
the many effects that will most certainly be felt should development be allowed
to follow. My family resides at 2007 Robert Ruark Dr., just across the street
from that would POSSIBLY be the Egress/Ingress of Osprey Landing. I was
informed that the DOT conducted their traffic study and an estimated 914
trips...., yes 914 trips would be made up and down this narrow road. My husband
and I have 2 young boys. We along with a large number of our fellow friends and
neighbors bike, walk, run and walk their dogs with us in this same stretch of
road. If 914 trips are being made with trucks, cars etc, this will no longer be
safe to anyone, drivers and pedestrians alike. Southport promotes a small
friendly quiet town, this volume of traffic does not seem to echo that
sentiment. If an estimate of 914 trips will be made daily I shudder to think
what number it would possibly reach, upwards of 1,000? I urge that Bill Clark
homes (the developer) place an entrance off of 211 as I understand they can do.
It is my understanding that this was in the original plan, that the residents’
access via this avenue.
In the event of any emergency for those in that neighborhood, be it hurricane
evacuation or emergency vehicles reaching someone in distress hwy 211 will be a
much more direct route. A direct entrance off hwy 211 seems much more fitting
specifically for the number of people who are expected to access Osprey
Landing, which is expected to be much larger than Smithville Woods, and would
be safer for all who will be traveling these areas. In closing I must question
that if development of Osprey Landing and its Ingress/Egress do connect
directly to Robert Ruark Dr. does this align with the Mission Statement set
forth of Southport and its goal of "controlled" development? I look forward to
the opportunity to speak with you in person and it is my hope that further
development access on Robert Ruark Dr is not permitted until adequate meeting
and awareness is made of what is to come. Given the current status of the town
and following guidance and advisement from our Mayor and governing bodies to
remain at distance and not gather I hope you view the wise decision the
planning board members saw, in line with what Bill Clark previously stated to
use Hwy 211 for their access to their development of property. I look forward
to a proper meeting to address with subject at a later date. Thank you for your
time.
Blessings to each of the Alderman at this difficult time.
Lauren Broadwell
910-367-2863
"Work like you don't need the money, love like you've never been hurt and dance
like nobody's watching."

Good afternoon,
I understand tomorrow night the Southport City Aldermen Committee will hold a
virtual meeting to discuss the future plans of development Osprey Landing.
While I completely understand the meeting being virtual due to the current
global pandemic, it is extremely unfortunate that concerned citizens cannot be
physically present to have our faces seen and voices heard. I sincerely hope
that no major decisions will be finalized at this time due to the uncertain
nature of our country and community.
That being said, I would ask that each of you read and digest the words in this
email. Please read them as if your children and grandchildren live in this
neighborhood.
My husband and I have 2 boys, ages 10 and 7. We were drawn to this neighborhood
for many reasons. It's tranquil nature, well-established estates, safe streets,
and loving neighbors. It's close proximity to the downtown area and waterfront
is only accentuated by the richness added by being able to ride bikes together
as a family to these treasured places. When the weather is nice, I cannot keep
my boys inside! They love playing basketball, climbing trees, walking the dogs,
and especially love riding bikes to the waterfront. We do this almost every
single day. If this development's plans continue as they are at this time, the
daily lives of my family and each of the 160+ residents of Smithville Woods
will change. The traffic study completed by the NC DOT and reviewed by
consulting firm, Kittleson & Associates, predicted 914 daily weekday trips
coming from Osprey Landing. Let that sink in... 914 more trips.
I so appreciate your commitment to advocating for our sweet town, which is
articulated so perfectly in the City of Southport Mission Statement:
“To strive for excellence in our government, project a positive attitude,
involve our community and protect our citizens by ensuring a safe, secure and
tranquil quality of life with controlled and orderly growth.”
The development of Osprey Landing does not feel like controlled and orderly
growth and it certainly does not preserve the safe, secure, and tranquil life
of residents of Smithville Woods. Please advocate for us! Please require Bill
Clark Homes to create a second, full-functioning ingress/egress access to
connect to NC 211 north of Robert Ruark Drive, as suggested by Kittleson &
Associates.

My name is Jennifer Skadeland, I live at 1131 N. Atlantic Ave. Unit B in
Southport. I am writing this email with regard to the business, All In Bloom
that is located right across the street from my home. I would like this to be
included in the board meeting that is going to be held tonight, May 14th at 6
P.M. I understand that the meeting is closed to the public due to Covid-19, but
I would still like my voice as a citizen of Southport heard. I'm hoping that
all of you can give myself and my neighbors, some solutions, resolution and/or
guidance with the following issues we are having in our neighborhood.
I have lived at my address for 7 years and have never had issues with any of my
neighbors, until All In Bloom moved in across the street. I do support local
business and was very excited that they were moving in next door. I went over
and introduced myself when they started preparing the lot and let them know how
happy I was that there would finally be something beautiful next door to look
at instead of an empty lot. Once they moved in everything about our peaceful
little neighborhood has changed. It is no longer peaceful and quiet. I can no
longer sleep in or enjoy a few moments of tranquility, whether it's in my home
or on my balcony.
The music starts at 6:30 A.M., every morning, the backpack blowers start at 7:
00 A.M, they are both every day occurrences. Their business hours are 9:00 A.M
Monday thru Saturday and 10:00 A.M on Sunday. I have an app on my phone that
can tell me the name of a song and the artists who sings the song just by
tapping a button. I can use it in my bedroom, bathroom, kitchen and patio and
pick up the music they are blaring from their business generally any time of
the day. This occurs on a daily basis. I have been documenting every day for
the past week what time they start the music, which has been 6:30 A.M.
consistently and the music is on all day long and sometimes goes on for an hour
or more after they close. I have the names of the songs and who sings them
throughout the day as well. I have also documented when the blowers start which
is 7:00 A.M consistently and the blowers last anywhere from half an hour to an
hour on some days, this is also on a daily basis. I have called the Southport
Police department and one officer told me to put a box fan on in my house so I
couldn't hear it. He did ask them eventually to turn it down after I told him
he wasn't addressing my concern. They did not turn it down. He did tell me to
call 911 if I was having an issue with them. I did call 911 on May 12th. Two
officers arrived and went over and spoke with the owner, this was after their
business closed and the music was still blaring. She did turn the music down
initially and when she thought the officers left, she cranked it back up even
louder. The officers went back over and said it was up to them if they were
going to issue her a citation. The officers were Mayner and Jeffrie, reference
# 20-057878. On May 13th I called Police Chief Coring because the music was
once again blaring at 7:00 A.M from their business. I left him a message and he
called me back at 1:43 P.M. he said he would stop over to their business and
talk to them regarding the music, but the music continued.
All in Bloom has a very small parking lot, maybe 15 spaces. They have placed no
parking signs all along the outside of their lot. The customers park all over
my lawn and in my parking lot as well as my neighbor’s lawns and sometimes just
in the street. The traffic is terrible and it's an accident waiting to happen.
The delivery trucks come in sometimes very early in the morning and sit idling
in the street all night. Which means we get no sleep that night. When they do
have deliveries, the trucks are parked on the street usually blocking traffic
and it's almost impassable.
I initially spoke with them asking them to please not use the blowers so early
in the morning because it wakes me every morning to which I was told no. I
asked them to maybe blow the leaves at closing time to which I was told no. I
feel as if I have made attempts to come to an agreement and let them know how I
feel and have come to the conclusion that they don't care about their neighbors
or being good neighbors. I don't know why they feel they can do whatever they
want and I have no rights. I do not feel as if the police have taken my
concerns as a tax paying citizen seriously and they don't want to deal with it.
I don't care that they have music, but I don't want to hear it every minute of
my day in my home. Do they even have a permit to play outside music and what
are the limits and restrictions they have to abide by? Why is their parking lot
so small for such a large business? Where are our rights as citizens who have
lived in this neighborhood peacefully before All In Bloom arrived.
The following are statements from a few of my neighbors. They have given me
permission to include them with my email.
Thomas and Elizabeth Caudill

Dear City of Southport,
This letter is to voice our disapproval of the new All In Boom Gardening Center
location. We feel as residents located next door to this business we were not
informed or considered. It seems that the local residents within the proximity
of the business are now second-class citizens and do not matter. We feel that
their business should conduct their business on their property grounds and not
the surrounding area/properties. The high volume of the business has caused
multiple concerns and issues for us which include:
High volume traffic continuously up and down the street with speeding.
Parking of their service and delivery trucks up and down the street (N.
Atlantic Ext) at times making the road unpassable.
Loud music throughout the day which can be heard in multiple rooms throughout
our residence.
The use of leaf blowers and machinery every morning at 7:00 A.M. which makes
for uncomfortable sleeping conditions on our days off.
The arrival of delivery trucks between 2:00 A.M. - 3:00 A.M. also provides
uncomfortable sleeping conditions.
Excessive customer parking on property that is not part of the business which
adds congestion on our side street. N. Atlantic Ext.
As residents of Southport for 25+ years and residents of this address for 10+
years we understand the growth of our community. We also understand that All in
Bloom has a right to run their business but we feel they should operate their
business on their business grounds during business hours and follow noise
ordinances as respect to the nearby homes. We also feel our side street (N.
Atlantic Ext) should not be a parking lot for their customers and service
vehicles or to be an unloading dock for their delivery trucks.
We hope that you consider our issues and concerns and that changes will be made
to address this. Thank You for your time.
The letters above were just a few of my neighbors that I could reach out to
before I realized that the meeting was taking place today. I truly hope that I
get a response from one or all of you regarding the concerns of our
neighborhood and I hope we can come up with some solutions that work for
everyone. Please reach out to me via email or by phone. I also saw a form I
could fill out requesting a meeting with the city council which I will be
taking advantage of as well. I'm hoping that this will be read as a part of the
minutes of the city council meeting since it is closed to the public. I will be
purchasing and putting up no parking signs along our property and parking lot
for the restaurant. I feel as if every day is now the Fourth of July in my
neighborhood due to the noise, parking issues and traffic volume. One day a
year is enough to deal with all of the issues we are having now on a daily
basis. Please consider how it would feel to be constantly listening to your
neighbor’s music inside or outside of your house every day up to 10 hours a
day. How it feels to be woken up every morning by backpack blowers every
morning even though you just want to sleep in a little. I just want to sleep in
every once in a while and to have some peaceful quiet time without hearing
their music.
Sincerely,
A tired and frustrated resident of Southport
Jennifer Skadeland
910-599-6405
jennifer27_68@yahoo.com

and National Police Week into the record.
Proclamation
RECOGNIZING PEACE OFFICERS’ MEMORIAL DAY AND NATIONAL POLICE WEEK (May 10-16,
2020)
WHEREAS, the Congress and President of the United States have designated May
15th as Peace Officers' Memorial Day, and the week in which May 15th falls as
National Police Week; and
WHEREAS, the members of the Southport Police Department play an essential role
in safeguarding the rights and freedoms of our community; and
WHEREAS, it is important that all citizens know and understand the duties,
responsibilities, hazards, and sacrifices of their law enforcement agency, and
that members of our law enforcement agency recognize their duty to serve the
people by safeguarding life and property, by protecting them against violence
and disorder, and by protecting the innocent against deception and the weak
against oppression; and
WHEREAS, the men and women of the Southport Police Department unceasingly
provide a vital public service; and
NOW, THEREFORE, I, Joseph P. Hatem, Mayor of the City of Southport do hereby
proclaim that the week of May 10-16, 2020, be recognized as “National Police
Week”. Citizens in the Southport area are encouraged to recognize National
Police Week with appropriate ceremonies and observances in which all people may
join in commemorating law enforcement officers, past and present, who, by their
faithful and loyal devotion to their responsibilities, have rendered a
dedicated service to their communities and, in so doing, have established for
themselves an enviable and enduring reputation for preserving the rights and
security of all citizens.
Further, I call upon all citizens to observe Friday, May 15, 2020, as Peace
Officers' Memorial Day in honor of those law enforcement officers who, through
their courageous deeds, have made the ultimate sacrifice in service to their
community or have become disabled in the performance of duty, and let us
recognize and pay respect to the survivors of our fallen heroes.
 
This the 14 th day of May 2020.          /s/ Joseph P. Hatem, Mayor
                     City of Southport
ATTEST: /s/ Michele Windham, Clerk

Howe St. Sewer Replacement Project
WHEREAS, the City of Southport is committed to repairing the City’s sewer
infrastructure: and

4.   Planned Unit Development (PUD) Land Use Plan Application, Osprey Landing,
Submitted by Bill Clark Homes
City Planner Lloyd presented an overview of the Land Use Plan for a 196-unit
PUD located off Robert Ruark Drive on 68 acres:
   •   Zoned for PUD in December 2018
   •   Land Use Plan submitted December 2, 2019
   •   Site is in the extra-territorial jurisdiction (ETJ)
   •   PUD can modify setbacks for additional flexibility
   •   Developer proposing 10’ minimum front yard setbacks, 5’ side yard
setbacks, and 10’ rear yard setbacks
   •   Minimum lot width is 50’
   •   3 lot types of varying sizes; Type A – 50’ x 120’; Type B – 52’ x 130’;
Type C – 65’ x 140’
   •   PUD’s are allowed up to 6 dwelling units per acre
   •   Proposed density, 2.88 dwelling per acre
   •   Project will have an amenity center and a pool
   •   10.2 acres of open green space; equivalent to 15%
   •   1,185,000 sq. ft. of tree canopy
   •   After development, there will be 320 oaks, 7 magnolias, 1 sweet fun, and
409 pines
   •   Traffic Impact Analysis approved by NCDOT (Robert Ruark a State road)
   •   Primary entrance off Robert Ruark Drive
   •   Secondary emergency only access on Maple Leaf Drive to comply with Fire
Code
   •   City selected engineering firm reviewed the TIA and included a traffic
diversion analysis of Maple Leaf Drive if it were opened
   •   Planning Board thoroughly reviewed the project for three (3) months
   •   Planning Board recommended that the Board of Aldermen approve the
development plans with the condition that Bill Clark Homes include a secondary
access that extends along their easement all the way to Highway 211
   •   Planning Board recommended amending the individual lot setback
requirements to 10’ in the front yard, 8’ in the side yard, and 15’ in the rear
yard
 
Mr. Lloyd’s complete, detailed project overview and corresponding exhibits,
reports, etc. on file in the Planning Department.
The following representatives of Bill Clark Homes, Paramount Engineering,
Davenport Engineering, and Ward & Smith were in attendance:
   •   Landon Weaver, Bill Clark Homes
   •   Sam Franck, Ward & Smith
   •   Rob Balland, Paramounte Engineering
   •   Mike Nichols, Paramounte Engineering
   •   Robert Gey, Davenport Engineering
Attorney Sam Franck, Landon Weaver and Mike Nichols spoke about the proposed
project, addressed specific requirements, and answered Board questions.
At 8:04 p.m., Alderman Allen moved, with a second by Alderman Mosteller to go
into Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the
City attorney. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Open Session resumed at 8:31 p.m. by motion from Alderman Sharkey, with a
second by Alderman Mosteller. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   Alderman Allen asked City Attorney Isenberg to provide the legal options
pertaining to the Land Use Plan submittal.
   Noting that the site was zoned to Planned Unit Development (PUD) in 2018,
City Attorney Isenberg explained that the developer is entitled to approval of
its application if the application and plans meet the criteria in the Unified
Development Ordinance. He pointed out that, under state law and the current
UDO, the Aldermen did not have the authority to require the developer to build
a secondary access outside of their property as was recommended by the Planning
Board.
Alderman Mosteller moved, with a second by Alderman Spencer to approve the Land
Use Plan application as submitted by the applicant.
Discussion
   Pointing out that the UDO was being updated, Alderman Mosteller stated that
the City would not be in a similar situation in the future.
   Alderman Allen stated his dismay that there was no legal basis to require
the applicant to access NC 211 by building a new road outside their
development.
   Alderman Spencer stated his hope that the discussed second access from NC
211 could be installed at a future date.
   Alderman Davis stated her reluctance to vote on the land use plan without
first hearing from the Planning Board, Fire Chief and having the public
present.
   Alderman Lombardi shared his hesitancy, that he would prefer an access to NC
211, and he stated his hope that the revision of the UDO would assure the
situation did not happen again.
   Alderman Mosteller asked that the gated Maple Leaf Drive emergency access be
landscaped to resemble a park setting.
   Vote:   Ayes:   Aldermen Mosteller, Spencer, Sharkey, Allen, Lombardi
      Nay:   Alderman Davis
   Motion carried 5-1 (Entire audio discussion on file in the Clerk’s office.)

1.   Review and Approval of Proposed Capital Project Ordinance to Disperse
NCDOT Proceeds to BEMC as agreed
   Finance Director Trexler explained that the City had entered into an
agreement with the North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT)
regarding utility relocation during the NC 211 expansion, in the amount of
$2.4M. Per the agreement, NCDOT would reimburse the City for charges incurred
by Brunswick Electric Membership Corp (BEMC) for relocation of the electric
lines. She reported that BEMC had submitted invoices for payment, NCDOT had
paid the City, and a Capital Project Fund needs to be adopted by the Board for
revenues and expenditures associated with the project.
   Alderman Sharkey moved, with a second by Alderman Lombardi to establish a
Capital Project Fund for the NCDOT Route 211 Utility Relocation Project.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.

2.   Continued Discussions on FY 2020-2021 Operating Budget
   Finance Director Trexler presented revised Community Building proposed FY
2020/2021 Operating Budget pages to the Board. She reported that $13,110 for
group health insurance had been incorrectly posted to the department and those
funds needed to be specifically allocated by the Board. Additionally, Director
Trexler asked the Board if they wanted to roll over unused 2019/2020
appropriations for the Forestry Committee and the Neighbors to Neighbors
Program to the FY 2020/2021 Budget.
   The Board considered revising the current pay plan to include incremental
steps of 2-1/2% each in all grades and a 5% increase between grades. City
Manager May shared his experience developing Step Pay Plan systems and he
recommended adding steps to the current Southport Pay Plan.
   The Board discussed the amount of funding for the Neighbors-to-Neighbors
program. Board consensus to roll over $6,000 from FY 2019/2020 Operating Budget
to FY 2020/2021 Operating Budget and add $4,000 to start FY 2020/2021 with a
total of $10,000 for that program.
   Alderman Spencer suggested allocating $7,000 in the Board Supplies line item
and $2,000 in the Board Travel line item.
   Alderman Allen expressed his concern that the budget did not have enough
designated maintenance funds for the many City buildings. He suggested re-
examining the budget in three (3) months to determined if there is any money to
address deferred maintenance costs.
   Alderman Davis moved, with a second by Alderman Spencer to defer salary
increases proposed in the FY 2020/2021 Operating Budget until November 2020 or
such time that incoming City Manager Hargrove can present a salary study to the
Board. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
ADJOURN

special meeting at 4:57 p.m.

D)   Public Comment
   Mr. Bob Tolle, 2136 Maple Leaf Drive stated the following:
“On behalf of the HOA’s of both Southport Way and The Ridge
We are appealing to your common sense, and request that you do what needs to be
done to correct what should never have been in the first place.
What we are referring to is the Right of Way on the grassy and berm area at the
end of Maple Leaf Dr.
Just to be clear, this piece of property is approximately 50 feet wide and 150
feet long, located between a townhome in The Ridge and a single-family home in
Southport Way, where Maple Leaf Dr. dead ends.
It is somewhat obvious the original developer intended for this to have been a
continuation of the road at some point for whatever reason, but it never
happened, so was there a Right of Way? It may have been the original
developer’s plan, but it has never been the desire of the residents of The
Ridge or Southport Way.
The residents of our two communities have used this property for years as a
common area, for socializing, dog walking and parking, since we have no on
street parking. We even made it clear several years ago that we were not even
interested in having a pathway through the property for security reasons.
The streets within Southport Way were turned over to the City in June of 2014,
but not until the HOA had to make improvements to bring them up to city
standards, for which money had to be borrowed to make the improvements. It’s
obvious that if the roads had not been paved, the City would not have approved
it. So, where this perceived Right of Way is, has never been paved, nor are
there curbs. So, it would seem apparent there would be no reason for a Right of
Way, since there is no road.
So, the question is; Why does the City have a Right Away here? It was not a
developed road by the original or second developer, nor when the City took over
the roads in 2014.
This Right of Way has no benefit to the residents and it’s hard to see a
benefit for the City.
So, we are requesting the City do the right thing and remove this Right of
Way.”
 
   Mr. Charlie Hess, 4459 Willow Moss Way, echoed Mr. Tolle’s comments and
spoke in opposition to the Osprey Landing subdivision. He shared his
disappointment that the development had been approved by the Aldermen and he
stated his safety concerns for the elderly residents of neighboring
communities.
   Mr. Jim Lightbourne, 316 W. West Street, indicated that he had heard a rumor
that Southport Marina was seeking a CAMA permit to install boat lifts in the
Yacht Basin marsh area. He questioned if the City was aware of the CAMA permit,
if the City has been in discussions with the Marina, what the CAMA permit
approval process was, if the City has input into the CAMA permit process and
does the CAMA permit process include comments from the public?
   City Clerk Windham read the following public comment into the record:
Mayor Hatem and aldermen, just a few questions concerning your 5-1 vote in
favor of the Osprey Landing development. I've been informed that, because
Osprey Landing is not located within the city limits, in order to connect to

developers??

developers that they must downsize before any annex.

representatives into a meeting that was closed to the citizens of Southport??
If your answer is that you closed the meeting because of a health risk, then
why did you allow them to go without protective masks. Poor excuse!
Last comment and question. Alderman Allen, Aldermen Davis, one other aldermen
and Mayor Hatem came to the Southport Way HOA during their campaign and
promised us that you understood that we did not want anything to do with Osprey
landing. You further stated that you would vote to disapprove the development.
Then all of you with the exception of Aldermen Davis turned your back on us,
your planning board and all the citizens of Southport who researched and
reported the negative aspects of your decision.
I viewed the online meeting and heard nothing concerning a master plan, dog
park or a review of who actually owns the property at the end of Maple Leaf dr.
Again, Thank You for attempting to do your share. I know it’s not an easy task.

   Juneteenth Proclamation
   Mayor Hatem read the proclamation into the record.
CITY OF SOUTHPORT PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, President Abraham Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation on
January 1, 1863, formally abolishing slavery in the United States of America;
and
WHEREAS, word about the signing of the Emancipation Proclamation was delayed
some two- and one-half years, to June 19, 1865, in reaching authorities and
African Americans in the South and Southwestern United States; and
WHEREAS, Emancipation Day observations are held on different days in different
states in the South and Southwest, and in other parts of the nation; and
WHEREAS, June 19th has a special meaning to African Americans, and is called
"JUNETEENTH" combining the words June and Nineteenth, and has been celebrated
by the African American community for over 150 years; and
NOW, THEREFORE, I, Joseph P. Hatem, Mayor together with the Board of Aldermen
of the City of Southport, North Carolina, do hereby declare June 19, 2020, as
JUNETEENTH
in the City of Southport, North Carolina, and urge all citizens to become more
aware of the significance of this celebration in African American History and
in the heritage of our nation and City.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, we have hereunto set our hand and caused the seal of the
City of Southport, North Carolina to be affixed this 11th day of June 2020.
         
                     /s/ Joseph P. Hatem, Mayor
 
/s/ Karen Mosteller, Mayor Pro Tem          /s/ Lora Sharkey, Alderman
/s/ Lowe Davis, Alderman             /s/ Marc Spencer, Alderman
/s/ Thomas Lombardi, Alderman            /s/ John Allen, Alderman
 
Dosher Memorial Hospital 90 th Anniversary
CITY OF SOUTHPORTPROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, Dosher Memorial Hospital began serving the Southport community as
Brunswick County Hospital on June 2, 1930; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Memorial Hospital is a full accredited, comprehensive
healthcare facility providing diagnosis, treatment, acute care, skilled care,
wellness and education in hospital, outpatient, and community settings; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Memorial Hospital’s mission is to improve the health and well-
being of the entire community; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Memorial Hospital serves more than 13,000 outpatient visits
each year; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Memorial Hospital employs more than 300 North Carolinians in
high quality, professional jobs; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Memorial Hospital is the only critical access hospital in North
Carolina that is owned by a township, Smithville Township, and to support their
beloved hospital, voted for a Hospital Tax, in the 1970s and most recently in
2000; and
WHEREAS, Dosher Memorial Hospital will celebrate its 90th Anniversary on June
2, 2020.
NOW, THEREFORE, I, Joseph P. Hatem, Mayor together with the Board of Aldermen
of the City of Southport, North Carolina, do hereby proclaim June 2, 2020, as
DOSHER MEMORIAL HOSPITAL
90TH ANNIVERSARY DAY
in the City of Southport, North Carolina, and encourage all citizens to join me
in this worthy observance.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, we have hereunto set our hand and caused the seal of the
City of Southport, North Carolina to be affixed this 11th day of June 2020.

City of Southport
Budget Message FY 20-21
 
The past fiscal year may best be characterized as a year of change; a new
Mayor, three new Aldermen, and a new City Manager. By mid-year, the economy was
robust, unemployment lowest in over 50 years, and the future was bright! One
month later came the worst pandemic since the 1917 Spanish Flu outbreak. The
economy sputtered to a stop with the world being shutdown to “stay home”
sequestered away from the virus. While our businesses languished, Southport
City Government was ramped up to protect our citizens and keep the spread of
the virus at bay. However, life as we had known it changed overnight to the new
normal; masks, gloves, hand sanitizer, take-out food only, social distancing,
no groups over 10. The impact felt world-wide resulted in economic collapse
felt immediately here locally with reduced retail sales and sales tax revenues.
The future suddenly became uncertain.
 
We are now two months into the pandemic and are beginning to slowly phase back
into a more relaxed but still restrained economy. As we tally the costs, we are
pleased to report that we may be over the worst of it and remain hopeful for a
stronger third quarter followed by a recovery by January 2021, The local
government experts agree and our numbers reflect the collective thought of the
NC League of Municipalities, the UNC School of Government, the NC Local
Government Commission, as well as our local government colleagues. No one has a
crystal ball, but we can with certainty predict growth on the horizon.
Thankfully, our reductions were not near as dire as initially thought. That
said, we are solvent, secure, and confident with prudent fiscal conservatism,
the budget presented for FY 20-21 is balanced with appropriations for
necessities, no lost positions, and service levels at or above last year.
 
As we summarize the Budget Ordinance, it is important to understand the process
that got us here. Melanie Trexler, CPA - Finance Director and her staff have
been working on this budget since the first of the year. In February they began
compiling year to date balances and projecting March through June estimates. At
the same time the Department Heads were given worksheets to use in calculating
what they needed for the upcoming Fiscal Year. Those estimates where turned in
to Finance in late March so Finance could prepare draft budget numbers to
review with each Department Head during April. By the end of April, I had the
Department numbers and Finance recommendations to review for the final
revisions leading to the balanced budget given to the Aldermen at their May
meeting.
 
The proposed Budget is 5.4% less than last FY. We propose no new positions,
modest increases in salaries of a one percent cost of living and the
possibility of up to two percent merit based on employee evaluations. We are
recommending no tax increase with the rate remaining 29.56 per $100.00 of tax
value. The General Fund is $7,946,120 which is 4.0% below last year. The Water
and Sewer Fund is $3,754,002 which is (8%) below last year. The W/S Capital
Reserve account is set at $300,000 for Water and $80,000 for sewer. The
Electric Fund is projected at $6,856,231 which represents a decrease of (13.9%)
below last year. Three capital projects funds added this year, Howe St. Sewer
Replacement Project funded by Golden Leaf and W/S funds of $1,148,550, NCDOT
Improvement Program / Utility Relocation Agreement 41582.2.2 funded by NCDOT
reimbursements and the Electric fund for $2,486,727.54, Taylor Field Part F
Grant of $842,448 funded by grant and donated property. The grand total for all
funds is $23,414,078.54, which represents an increase of 13% over last year.
 
Each Department Head provided explanations and defense for their budgets by
line item. That sheet in your budget package follows each Departmental page as
the next tab. The explanations are detailed, sufficient to understand what they
are asking for, and will have some inserts from me and Finance in red where
there is a difference which may occasionally need to be addressed by the BOA.
 
I am optimistic that next year will see a return to previous levels as we
slowly come out of this pandemic. FY 19/20 was a challenging and historic time.
As always, the citizens, the Staff, and the leadership of Southport have
answered the challenge with determination, faith, and optimism. Better times
are coming.
 
Respectfully submitted
 
Chris May
Chris May,
Interim City Manager
   Alderman Mosteller pointed out that proposed salary adjustments would be

SECTION IX. TAX RATE
 
There is hereby levied, for fiscal year 2020-2021, a tax at the rate of $0.2956
on each one hundred dollars ($100) of assessed valuation of property located
within the City of Southport for the purpose of raising revenue in the General
Fund. The assessed value of property is $917,971,341.
SECTION X. BUDGET OFFICER AUTHORITY
 
The city manager (budget officer) is hereby authorized to transfer
appropriations within a fund and between funds under the following terms:
 
He may transfer amounts between appropriations within the same fund, provided
that a report of such transfers shall be made no later than the next regular
financial report to the Board of Aldermen.
He may authorize temporary transfers of cash among funds as necessary to meet
cash flow needs.
 
All other transfers of funds between appropriations or budget funds shall be
accomplished by Board amendment of this ordinance.
 
SECTION XI. BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION
 
This ordinance and the supporting budget document shall be the basis of the
financial plan for the City of Southport municipal government for the 2020-2021
fiscal year. The budget officer shall administer the budget and shall insure
the finance officer and department heads of the city are provided with
sufficient guidance to properly implement this plan. Copies of the budget
ordinance shall be furnished to the city manager and the finance officer for
their use and direction in the disbursement of funds and to the city clerk for
the official records of the city.
 
SECTION XII. ADOPTION
This ordinance has been adopted by the Southport Board of Aldermen in regular
session on June 11, 2020, upon the motion of Alderman Spencer and the second of
Alderman Sharkey, with a vote of _6__ ayes and  0_ noes, and shall be effective
July 1, 2020.

5.   Presentation of DRAFT Unified Development Ordinance
City Planner Lloyd presented a copy of the proposed revised Unified Development
Ordinance (UDO) to each Board member. He indicated that the draft would be
posted on-line, and an e-mail would be established for citizens to post their
concerns and questions. He added that a joint Board of Aldermen/Planning Board
meeting would be scheduled. Planner Lloyd introduced Mr. Wes MacLeod with the
Cape Fear Council of Governments, who has been working with the Planning Board
and staff on the UDO update.
Mr. MacLeod addressed the Board and spoke about the process. He highlighted
some of the revisions:
The process has been on-going since July 2018
Over a dozen meetings held
A comprehensive audit was performed, reduction in overall text and
clarification of many ambiguous, conflicting, and unclear provisions
Document reduced from 27 Articles to 8 Articles
Consolidation of approval procedures, roles, responsibilities, and
administrative items into one article
Clarification of development approval processes and responsibilities for major/
minor site plans, major/minor subdivisions, exempt/final plats, and planned
unit developments
Conditional Zoning procedure included
Building design standards for CBD and BD zoning district included
Off-street parking requirements reduced and simplified
Tree canopy standards updated
Modification of sign requirements
All legislative updates included
Established roles and responsibilities for the UDO Administrator
 
Responding to a query from Alderman Sharkey, Mr. MacLeod explained that the
bonding or financial guarantees for the installation of required infrastructure
was removed. Developers will have to have all improvements finished, inspected,
and certified prior to final plat approval.
 
Board members stated appreciation to all those involved in the UDO update.

7.   Discussion; Amending Southport Code of Ordinance Article #19 Load
Management
Electrical Superintendent Pittenger presented a proposed amendment to Article
19 of the Code of Ordinances relating to Load Management. He spoke about
participation by residents in the Load Management program, the cost of the peak
load hour, the savings to customers and the City, and expanding participation
in the program by mandating installation of Load Management switches on all new
electric service accounts. He pointed out that Load Management switches are
mandated on all new construction.
Alderman Davis stated she had received comments from residents objecting to
Load Management switches because the savings was minimal, and they did not want
to get hot. Mr. Pittenger stated that a customer could get up to $176 in
savings with full participation in the program. Noting that she does not notice
her house getting hot, Alderman Mosteller shared her experiences with full load
management.
Alderman Allen suggested adding hot water heaters to the proposed amendment.
Alderman Sharkey moved, with a second by Alderman Mosteller to Amend Section
19-186 of the Code of Ordinances by adding subsection (c) thereto as presented
in the agenda with the addition of electric water heaters to said subsection.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
(c)   Property owners, when making application for electrical service to an
existing residential property, shall permit installation of load management
switches if not already installed and functioning on all compressor and heat
strip circuits, on all standard two hundred forty volt (240V) electric heat
pumps or HFAC units (“Mini-split” heat pump units and geothermal systems are
exempt) and on all electric water heaters forty (40) gallons or larger provided
they are no more than nine (9) kilowatts before an electrical service account
will be granted.

10.   Discussion; State of Emergency
Alderman Spencer asked his fellow Aldermen to share their opinions on the
continuance of a State of Emergency, i.e. the pros/cons, duration, plans for
moving forward, what to advise the public.
Alderman Lombardi pointed out that many tourists are coming into the City, are
not wearing facial covering, and are holding hands and hugging. He stated his
opinion that the businesses should require customers to wear facial covering.
He stated support for continuation of the State of Emergency.
Responding to Alderman Davis, Mayor Hatem acknowledged that Dosher Hospital is
seeing patients with COVID-19. She expressed her impression that people do not
believe the pandemic is real until it affects someone they know. She shared her
experiences suffering with polio.
Responding to a query by Alderman Davis, Attorney Isenberg pointed out that the
cancellation of the 4 th of July Festival differed from the recent peaceful
protests that are protected by the First Amendment of the Constitution.
Emphasizing the need to remain under a State of Emergency, Mayor Hatem noted
that new cases of COVID-19 are rising and are putting Southport’s over 65
population at risk. He added that numerous cities and towns throughout North
Carolina and the U.S. had cancelled 4 th of July celebrations.
Alderman Mosteller expressed gratitude for Mayor Hatem’s physician expertise
and having a Master of Public Health.

   Per request by Alderman Mosteller, her comments are included verbatim:
“The Southport City Dock has been in the Yacht Basin since the late 1950’s. As
a result of the damage sustained during Hurricane Matthew in 2016, the City was
given FEMA funds and a grant from the Golden Leaf foundation to rebuild the
dock. After several starts and stops, the City has been waiting on CAMA permit
approval since November of 2019 to rebuild the dock.
The City was made aware about a month ago, that Preston Development, owners of
the Southport Marina, had submitted a preliminary CAMA permit application to
build 86 boat lift type slips in the ICW in front of the marshes and build
adjoining walkways and docks in the marsh and around in the Yacht Basin. The
City then reached out to the regional office of the NC Division of Coastal
Management for clarification of the Marina’s proposed project and was informed
that the completed application had yet to be submitted to CAMA and the City of
Southport would be contacted for comment once Preston Development’s application
was complete.
Last Thursday, June 4th, on behalf of Preston Development, Mr. Rose, the Vice
President of Land Acquisitions and Construction for Preston Development
contacted the Southport City Manager Mr. May, to advise the city that Preston
Development’s recent submittal for a CAMA permit to build additional new docks
in the marsh areas adjacent to the Marina was being withheld by CAMA due to the
City of Southport’s existing Open Space District zoning.
According to the City Manager, Mr. Rose, indicated that because Southport’s
current zoning does not allow the Marina’s business use in Open Space, the
Preston Development Company, would be withholding the riparian line agreement
between the current City Dock project and their property. Further, Mr. Rose
indicated that Preston Development is now claiming that their riparian line
intersects with the Southport City Dock.
In part, because of Preston Development’s new objection to the City’s riparian
line, CAMA has placed the Southport City Dock permit application on hold
pending resolution and riparian line agreements.
The City Manager also indicated that during the call, Mr. Rose offered to
discuss what he called a compromise whereby Preston Development would be
allowed to build new docks onto the marsh that is zoned Open Space District.
This would require the City of Southport to change the current zoning ordinance
in order to give Preston Development the right to build commercial docks in an
area zoned Open Space.
Current Southport zoning defines Open Space District as areas of special
interest that should be placed in a zone protected from any development other
than improvements or uses undertaken by the City of Southport.
Based on records, in recognition of its value to our community, the marsh areas
beside the Yacht Basin may have been zoned Open Space for over 35 years. The
city dock has been in the Yacht Basin for over 60 years.
In 2007, the City of Southport gave Preston Development a zoning variance to
build the existing 50-foot dry stack storage building. Last year, in 2019, a
majority of the Board of Aldermen voted to sell to Preston Development two and
a half acres of water access land at the end of West West Street for $650,000.
Then, against the recommendation of the Planning Board, a majority of the Board
of Aldermen voted to change the zoning for Preston Development to maximize
their investment and build a second 50-foot-high dry stack storage building.
The city has always worked with Preston Development and has been more than
reasonable and accommodating.…
Now, they want to claim the very heartbeat of Southport for more profit.
Preston Development is in the business of making money… but their short-term
gain would be at the expense of Southport’s future. I say to Preston
Development…We do live here; we do know that the marsh is zoned Open Space for
a reason, we do know that Southport, in part, is defined by the Yacht Basin and
the marshes.
The CAMA Core Land Use Plan, our city’s strategic long-range planning document
includes policies, regulations, land use goals and planning objectives for the
future of the City of Southport and its citizens.
In the plan, under Southport’s Vision and Core Values, the first two named
priorities are:
Preserve Southport’s historic character
Protect Southport’s Shoreline Vista
Let me repeat that … our Vision and Core Values…
Preserve the city’s historic character.
Protect the city’s shoreline vista.
Am I to understand if Southport does not give Preston Development a zoning
change to allow them to ruin the open space zoned marsh, then Preston
Development will make the claim that their riparian line should prevent the
City of Southport from rebuilding the City Dock that was originally built in
the late 1950’s? Our city manager said yes, from the conversation, this is what
he understood was being offered.
It’s a sad day in Southport. Sounds like the Board has been asked to choose
between changing the definition of Open Space zoning and giving up rebuilding
Southport’s City Dock for our citizens and the public to enjoy.
In this year’s budget, the City of Southport has $255,000 available from FEMA
and grant money to rebuild the City Dock. And now, if Preston Development stops
the City from getting a CAMA permit because they will not agree with our
riparian line, the opportunity will expire, and the City will lose the money to
rebuild the dock.
I would like to believe that the owners of Preston Development, would
reconsider their demand to build in the Open Space zoned marsh in trade for
allowing Southport to rebuild our historic City Dock. I have to wonder if they
have ever looked across the Yacht Basin to see the marsh …the unparalleled
vista that is the heartbeat of our community.
I say to Preston Development, that Southport has helped the Marina be
successful… now, we ask you to help us preserve and protect our historic
character and our shoreline vista… Preston Development… please dance with the
one that brung ya… honor Southport and what makes our city this very special
place. Please let the citizens of Southport rebuild our dock and preserve the
heartbeat of our community.”

   6.   Public Hearing ZA 20-051-01: Zoning Amendments; Unified Development
Ordinance (UDO), Article 2: Definitions, Article 10: Table of Permitted Uses,
and Article 12: Zoning & Conditional Use Permit Approval Concerning
Transitional Housing Facilities
City Planner Lloyd presented a proposed zoning amendment to approve
Transitional Housing Facilities as a Conditional Use in the Office &
Institutional zoning district. Memorandum of Jun 29, 2020 included in its
entirety:
BACKGROUND
At the May 21st Planning Board meeting, Brunswick Partnership for Housing (BPH)
requested that the Planning Board consider amending the ordinance to add
language for transitional housing facilities to the UDO. BPH described
transitional housing as a project that is designed to provide housing and
appropriate services to families in order to facilitate movement to independent
living within an average of nine months. These facilities would provide
services such as educational programs, counseling, and other social services to
assist residents in their transition to permanent housing. She explained that
these types of facilities are not licensed by State or National programs. The
current language in the ordinance does not have a provision for this type of
facility. The Planning Board established a committee to draft language for
transitional housing facilities. The committee proposed adding a definition for
transitional housing facilities and proposed allowing them as a conditional use
in the 0/1 district in the table of permitted uses. They also proposed
supplemental standards that would screen the property from other adjacent
residential uses, added parking standards specific to these facilities, and
limited the number of units to 5. See the preliminary minutes that are attached
from the June 18 th Planning Board meeting for more information.
REQUEST
To amend Article 2: Definitions to add a definition and supplemental standards
for transitional housing facilities, Article 10: Table of Permitted Uses to
make Transitional Housing Facilities a Conditional Use in 0/1, and Article 12:
Zoning & Conditional Use Permit Approval to add supplemental standards. It is
important to note that this is a zoning amendment that would allow this type of
facility in all of the office/institutional zoning district. This is about the
ordinance as a whole and not the project that BPH is proposing. The Board of
Aldermen must adopt a statement of plan consistency (whether the proposed
amendment is consistent with the CAMA Land Use Plan and amending the CAMA Land
Use Plan if it is not) and then vote on the proposed text am endment .
PLANNING BOARD RECOMMENDATION
At the May 21st and June 18th Planning Board meeting, the Planning Board
reviewed this text amendment. The committee that came up with the language
thought it would be best for transitional housing facilities to be a
conditional use permit so any potential facilities would go through both the
Planning Board and the Board of Adjustment for review. The Board of Adjustment
would have a quasi-judicial hearing and would do a finding of facts to ensure
(a) that the use will not materially endanger the public health, safety, or
general welfare if located where proposed and developed according to the plan
as submitted and approved; (b) that the use meets all required conditions and
specifications; (c) that the use will not adversely affect the use or any
physical attribute of adjoining or abutting property, or that the use is a
public necessity; and (d) that the location and character of the use, if
developed according to the plan as submitted and approved, will be in harmony
with the area in which it is to be located and in general conformity with the
City of Southport Land Use Plan. The burden would be on the applicant to prove
all 4 of those statements. The Board of Adjustment would also be able to place
reasonable conditions on the Conditional Use Permit that would run with the
property. The committee also thought that since this would be similar to a mf
use, Office Institutional would be an appropriate area because it allows things
like duplexes, triplexes, quadraplexes, townhomes, and apartments on the basis
of obtaining a conditional use permit . The rest of the Planning Board agreed.
At the June 22nd Special Planning Board meeting, the Planning Board found that
the proposed text amendment was consistent with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan and
voted to recommend approval.
Alderman Davis questioned if there was language in the amendment that would
prevent the use from evolving into an emergency overnight shelter. At Alderman
Davis' request, City Planner Lloyd stated that the definition of Transitional
Housing Facilities could include, "this definition shall not include emergency
overnight shelter."
Alderman Spencer moved, with a second by Alderman Davis to open Public Hearing.
Unanimous vote; motion carried.
Ms. Beth LeBlanc, 224 E. 11th Street, spoke in support of the text amendment
concerning Transitional Housing Facilities.
Giving examples of people in need, Ms. Becky Felton 230 N. Caswell Avenue,
member of Brunswick Partnership for Housing, spoke about the need for a
transitional housing facility to help "our neighbors who need our help."
Ms. Sage Seeley, 255 E. 11 th Street, resident of Brunswick Village, stated her
stance in support of transitional housing. She related her experience of loss
during Hurricane Irma and her journey to Southport.
Ms. Sally Learned, Brunswick Partnership for Housing, spoke about the
organization's endeavors towards requesting the proposed text amendment. She
indicated that there is a real need for families with children. She emphasized
that the scope of the housing is very definitive, not for emergency housing,
and there are multiple layers of review and safeguards to protect the community
and enhance the program.
Expressing appreciation for Brunswick Partnership for Housing's outreach to the
community, Mr. Cliff Pender, 230 E. 11th Street, expressed his concerns about
the proposed location for transitional housing. He urged the City to find a
better location outside the city limits than in dense residential
neighborhoods.
Mr. Stephen Dillow, 3445 St. James Drive, vice-chairman of Brunswick
Partnership for Housing, spoke of his 40-year career in Family Services. He
empathized with the safety concerns and assured the Board that any families
making use of the transitional housing program would be vetted by other
agencies, thoroughly screened, and there would be strict rules about behavior.
He spoke about the sobering number of homeless families with children.
Praising the remarkable job Brunswick Partnership for Housing is doing, Mr. Roy
Pender, 7766 Skipjack Circle, stated his opinion that the proposed text
amendment was being requested in the Office & Institutional (O&I) zoning
district because there is currently a building available in that zoning
district for the proposed use. He emphasized considering closely the areas that
are O&I and the uses permitted.
Ms. Dawn Coleman, 233 E. 11th Street, a paint contractor by trade, offered her
assistance and shared her experience with homelessness. She begged the Board to
consider a better location.
Mr. Joel Clary, 120 NE 38th Street, Oak Island, spoke about the lostjobs due to
COVID-19 in the service industries and the lack of affordable housing for those
displaced. He noted that area churches are doing all they can with limited
resources, and he urged the Board to approve the proposal.
Mr. Gary Pethe, 221 E. 11th Street, speaking on behalf of himself, Ms. Martha
Johnson who was unable to attend and residents at 217 & 225 E. 11th Street,
endorsed the proposed amendment and spoke about living in a neighborhood with a
similar program and never experiencing any problems.
City Clerk Windham read the following public comments into the record:
Dear Mr. Lloyd,
Our names are John and Susan DeLaney. We live at 304 W. West Street and have
been citizens of Southport since 2015.
It has come to our attention that a zoning text amendment is being considered
that would change the current regulations regarding transitional housing
facilities within the city limits of Southport. We would like to voice our
concern with this proposal. Although we understand the need for transitional
housing, we are concerned with allowing these facilities within our city
limits. We do not believe it is best for our community and do not believe it
would be the best for the residents of the facility.
Southport is a small, primarily residential community. As with many of the
residents, we chose to live in Southport because of its safe, friendly
environment. We believe that a transitional housing facility in Southpmt would
detract from the safety and peace of mind that our community has come to enjoy.
Secondly, we do not believe that a transitional housing facility within
Southport would be the best for their residents. We have members of our own
family that have lived in transitional housing units. The times when they have
benefited the most have been when these facilities were located in very rural
areas. Being away from bars and liquor stores and live music venues has helped
to remove the temptations that led them to make poor decisions in the past.
Brunswick county is blessed with an abundance of beautiful, quiet, rural areas
that would provide a much better environment for these individuals as they work
to put their lives back together.
For the sake of the residents of Southport, and for the betterment of the
transitioning residents, we ask the leadership of our community to reject the
proposed zoning amendment.
Best regards,
John and Susan DeLaney

   7.   Consideration of Zoning Amendment; UDO Article 2, 10 & 12
Following the public hearing and before discussion of the proposed text
amendment, Attorney Isenberg advised the board (i) that this was not a rezoning
of particular property; (ii) that this was also not a decision regarding a
particular project as the proposal was to add this as a conditional use to the
entire 0/1 District and that the decision whether or not to allow a particular
project would be handled thru the conditional use process by the Board of
Adjustment; and (iii) that the decision was to determine whether there is a
need for transitional housing in our zoning jurisdiction and if so, whether the
O/I District was the proper district in which to place this condition use.
Responding to Alderman Sharkey, Planner Lloyd provided examples of uses by
right and conditional uses in the 0/1 zoning district, i.e. hospitals, doctor
offices, nursing homes, multi-family, duplex/triplexes, apartments, townhomes.
Alderman Davis stressed including language in the amendment to prohibit
emergency overnight housing. Alderman Sharkey stated her opinion that the
amendment as presented would not permit those types of facilities. Planner
Lloyd pointed out that a Conditional Use Permit for the use would be presented
to the Board of Adjustment and they could include additional conditions on the
project.
Alderman Davis, with the assistance of Attorney Isenberg, with a second by
Alderman Mosteller made the following motion:
   1.   To modify the proposed definition of Transitional Housing Facility by
adding the following sentence at the end of the definition: "This shall not
include emergency overnight housing".
   2.   That the Board find that the proposed text amendment as modified herein
is consistent with the 2015 CAMA Land Use Plan for the reasons stated in the
Statement of Plan Consistency submitted by the Planning Board in the agenda
package.
   3.   That the Board find that the text amendment as modified herein is
reasonable and in the public interest for the reasons set forth in the proposed
ordinance prepared by staff; and
   4.   That the Board adopt, enact and approve the Ordinance contained in the
agenda packet amending Article 2: Definitions, Article10: Table of Permitted
Uses, and Article 12: Zoning and Conditional Use Permit Approval, with the
addition of the above-referenced sentence to the definition of Transitional
Housing Facility.
   Discussion
   Alderman Spencer stated his thankfulness to Southport forefathers for
permitting low income housing at Brunswick Village and Fiddler's Creek
Apartments and he stated he was proud to be on a Board that voted on a
mechanism that can truly help someone.
   Alderman Sharkey supported adoption of the text amendment because the
concerns have been addressed , the use is distinctly defined, and it is another
example of how the City and Boards have provided assistance to those in need.
   Alderman Davis praised Brunswick Partnership for Housing (BPH) for bringing
forth one of the seven acts of loving kindness.
   Alderman Lombardi fully supported the amendment and stated he had received
overwhelming calls and e-mails in favor of the measure.
   Unanimous vote; motion carried.
AN ORDINANCE AMENDING ARTICLE 2 DEFINITIONS, ARTICLE 10 TABLE OF PERMITTED
USES, AND ARTICLE 12: ZONING & CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT APPROVAL CONCERNING
TRANSITIONAL HOUSING FACILITIES
   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City's
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city's land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, Brunswick Partnership for Housing has requested UDO text amendment
to amend Article 2 Definitions, Article 10 Table of Permitted Uses, and Article
12: Zoning & Conditional Use Permit Approval in order to incorporate
transitional housing facilities into the UDO; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has reviewed this matter and found that the
proposed amendment to Article 2, Article 10, and Article 12 of the Unified
Development Ordinance to be consistent with the City of Southport CAMA Core
Land Use Plan and recommends its approval; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on July 09, 2020 before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, together with the
comments of staff, hereby finds that this text amendment is consistent with the
2015 CAMA Land Use Plan for the reasons stated in its Statement of Plan
Consistency attached hereto and incorporated herein; and
   WHEREAS, the current UDO does not have a provision for this type of facility
and the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is reasonable and
in the public interest because the CAMA Land Use Plan supports quality
development reflecting the spectrum of housing needs, Section 6 :Plan for the
Future identifies affordable housing as an important need that needs to be
addressed by the City, the CAMA Land Use Plan also encourages uniformity in the
types of uses that are allowed in zoning districts.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that
Article 2, Article 10, and Article 12 of the Southport Unified Development
Ordinance is hereby amended as follows on Exhibit A attached.
This, the 9th day of July 2020         City of Southport

EXHIBIT A
Zoning Text Amendment: ZA 20-0521-01
Additions Highlighted
ARTICLE 2. BASIC DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS
Transitional Housing Facility. A facility configured as a multifamily
development but operated and funded by a nonprofit, charitable, religious, or
governmental organization to provide temporary housing and appropriate
supportive services to families or individuals to facilitate movement to
independent living over a 3 to 24-month period. A transitional housing facility
may provide social services, counseling, and other programs to assist residents
in the transition to permanent housing. This classification shall not be
construed to include uses licensed or supervised by any federal, state, or
county health/welfare agency, such as group homes, halfway houses, boarding
homes for children, and convalescent nursing homes. This shall not include
emergency overnight housing.

   8. Public Hearing ZA 20-0521-02: Zoning Amendment; Unified Development
Ordinance (UDO) Article 11: Table of Area, Yard, Density and Height
Memorandum from Planner Lloyd to the Board of Aldermen dated June 29, 2020
included in its entirety:
BACKGROUND
At the May 14th Board of Aldermen meeting, Alderman Davis brought up some
concerns about how the 50-foot height text amendment for dry storage buildings
was still present in the current ordinance. It was mentioned that the language
was proposed to be removed as part of the UDO Update process. Alderman Davis
was concerned because if someone with a 40 wet slip marina in Business District
were to apply for such a structure prior to the ordinance being updated, they
would have the right to be approved under the existing ordinance at the time of
their application being submitted. The Board of Aldermen instructed the
Planning Board to come up with a proposed amendment that would remove the SO-
foot Marina Height provision in the Table of Area Yard & Density.
To be clear, this would not affect the approved site plan by Southport Marina
for their SO-foot structure. The commercial site plan approval for Southport
Marina is subject to the vested rights provisions as referenced in GS 160A-
335.1. Once a site-specific development plan is approved, a right which has
been vested shall remain vested for a period of two years from the date of
approval. Such vested right shall confer upon the landowner the right to
undertake and complete the development and use of said property under the terms
and conditions of the approved site-specific development plan. Their commercial
site plan for that project was approved on October 17, 2019.
The planning board established a review committee met on June 2, 2020 to
discuss the amendment. It was the consensus of the committee to delete the
superscript and language that allows Marina's with 40 or more wet boat slips in
Business district to have dry storage buildings with a maximum height of 50
feet. To be clear, the proposal is for the language that was added last year to
be removed from the UDO.
REQUEST
To amend Article 11: Table of Area, Yard, Density, and Height to delete the
superscript and language that allows Marina's with 40 or more wet boat slips in
Business district to have dry storage buildings with a maximum height of 50
fee. The Board of Aldermen must adopt a statement of plan consistency (whether
the proposed amendment is consistent with the CAMA Land Use Plan and amending
the CAMA Land Use Plan if it is not) and then vote on the proposed text
amendment.
PLANNING BOARD RECOMMENDATION
At the June 13 th Planning Board meeting, the Planning Board reviewed this text
amendment. The Planning Board supported the proposed language because they did
not recommend that the original amendment be approved in the first place. At
the June 13th meeting of the Planning Board, the Planning Board found that the
proposed text amendment was consistent with the 2015 CAMA Core Lane Use Plan
and voted to recommend approval.
Alderman Spencer moved, with a second by Alderman Mosteller to open Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
No one from the public spoke.
Alderman Lombardi moved , with a second by Alderman Mosteller to close Public
Hearing. Unanimous vote; motion carried.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING ARTICLE 11 TABLE OF AREA YARD & DENSITY OF THE CITY OF

   THAT WHEREAS, the City has enacted a Unified Development Ordinance and other
land use ordinances that control land development within both the City's
incorporated areas and within its extraterritorial area; and
   WHEREAS, in order to promote the public health, safety and general welfare
and to promote the best interest of the city and community, it is necessary for
the City Board of Aldermen from time to time to consider appropriate revisions,
modifications and additions to the city's land use ordinances; and
   WHEREAS, the City of Southport Board of Aldermen directed the Planning Board
to review and propose language to amend Article 11 of the Unified Development
Ordinance to remove a footnote to the Article 11 Table of Yard, Area, Density
and Height Requirements that allows Marina dry storage buildings to have a
height of 50 feet in the BO District; and
   WHEREAS, the Planning Board has reviewed this matter and found that the
proposed amendment to Article 11 of the Unified Development Ordinance to be
consistent with the City of Southport CAMA Core Land Use Plan and recommends
its approval; and
   WHEREAS, pursuant to N. C. General Statutes and city ordinances, a public
hearing, properly noticed, was held on July 09, 2020 before the Board of
Aldermen regarding this issue; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen, after considering the public hearing
response and the recommendation of the Planning Board, together with the
comments of staff, hereby finds that this text amendment is consistent with the
2015 CAMA Land Use Plan for the reasons stated in its Statement of Plan
Consistency attached hereto and incorporated herein; and
   WHEREAS, the Board of Aldermen further finds that this amendment is
reasonable and in the public interest because the CAMA Land Use Plan encourages
protecting the City's shoreline vista. The CAMA Land Use Plan also encourages
uniformity in zoning ordinances and decisions. Reducing the height of Dry
Storage Buildings in Business District to 40 feet make these types of
structures more uniform and consistent with the City of Southport's 40-foot
maximum height standard throughout all zoning districts.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Southport Board of Aldermen that
Article 11 the Southport Unified Development Ordinance is hereby amended as
follows on Exhibit A attached.

beginning at Caswell Avenue past the Yacht Basin businesses.

be accommodated.

Street. Aldermen Allen and Spencer agreed that there is a blind spot at W. West
Street when traveling up the current direction of Short Street and it was their
contention that by changing the direction of Short Street, only residents that
live on the street would use it.
   Alderman Sharkey moved, with a second by Alderman Spencer to adopt the
pedestrian one- way plan as presented and request the Police Department to
report at the next regular meeting on incorporating Short Street and Brunswick
Street to be pedestrian friendly.
   Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   12. Final Plat; Preserve at Fisher Landing
   Memorandum from Planner Lloyd to the Board of Aldermen dated June 30, 2020
included in its entirety:
BACKGROUND
Hoosier Daddy LLC has filed for Final Plat Approval of the Preserve at Fisher
Landing. The Preliminary Plat was approved on January 10 of 2019 The Preserve
at Fisher Landing is a Major Subdivision between W 9th and W. 11th street. This
subdivision was developed using the Residential Cluster Development standards
found in Article 15 of the UDO. In cluster developments conventional zoning
standards are relaxed in order to provide an alternative development option
that promotes more efficient use of land resources, to better preserve the
site, and to provide desirable and useable open space .
This subdivision consists of 48 single family lots on a total of 15 acres. The
average lot size is 7813 sf. The open space requirement is 1:1 per lots less
than 10,000 sf. The total requirement is 2.46 acres. This property provides
2.46 acres of open space with 1.23 of that being contiguous. The setbacks will
be 15' in the front, 12' in the rear, 6' in the side. They are also including a
25' periphery boundary.
Prior to the recording of a Final Plat, there must either be infrastructure
already in place or there must be performance guarantees (such as a bond or
letter of credit.) According to the Public Works Director David Fox, the
developer has completed the required wastewater infrastructure, water
infrastructure, and road infrastructure to our construction standards. The
Public Works Department has received as-builts as well as certifications from
the Engineer in charge of the project. The City also required asphalt core
testing for the roads and tests for the water and sewer. The Public Works
Department has all of these on file. There is not sidewalk infrastructure yet,
but the developer will be submitting a performance guarantee equal to $63,350
(125% the cost of the infrastructure.)
REQUEST
Motion to approve the Final Plat for the Preserve at Fisher Landing.
STAFF RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Board of Aldermen approve the Final Plat for the
Preserve at Fisher Landing with the condition that the performance guarantee
for the sidewalk infrastructure be executed prior to the recording of the plat.
The Final Plat matches the Preliminary Plat and is in compliance with our
Subdivision regulations.
   Alderman Lombardi moved, with a second by Alderman Allen to approve the
Preserve at Fisher Landing Final Plat. Unanimous vote; motion carried.
   13. Preserve at Fisher Landing Deed of Dedication & Acceptance of Water and
Sewer Infrastructure
   Memorandum from Planner Lloyd to the Board of Aldermen dated June 30, 2020
included in its entirety:
BACKGROUND
The developer of the Preserve at Fisher Landing is asking that the City accept
and take over maintenance of the water, sewer, and road infrastructure. The
stormwater infrastructure will still be private and maintained by the HOA.
According to the Public Works Director David Fox, the developer has completed
the required wastewater infrastructure, water infrastructure, and road
infrastructure to our construction standards. The sidewalk is to be constructed
as houses are built to prevent damage. The Public Works Department has received
as-builts as well as certifications from the Engineer in charge of the project.
The City also required asphalt core testing for the roads and additional tests
for the water and se wer. The Public Works Department has all of these on file.
REQUEST
Motion to accept the wastewater, water, and road infrastructure.
   Noting that the streets would be damaged during construction, Alderman
Lombardi questioned acceptance of the street infrastructure before the project
was built out. Planner Lloyd indicated that the City is under no obligation to
accept the streets prior to the industry standard of 60% built out. He
emphasized that the developer would have to bring the streets up to standards
prior to the City accepting them.
   Alderman Mosteller moved, with a second by Alderman Sharkey to accept water
and sewer infrastructure at the Preserve at Fisher Landing. Unanimous vote;
motion carried.

simply say nothing can be built there. While there are obviously some positives

possible development outcome of the entire city of Southport, and that is what

One misconceptions about Project Indigo is that it has been under review by the
City for some time. This is not correct. The project came to my attention on
Friday July 5th when I received the agenda packet for our meeting on July 11th.
The developer has not submitted a development application to the City, and no
steps have been taken towards consideration, much less approval, of the
project. The preliminary information that the developer presented at our July
meeting has been posted on the City’s website so that all citizens can see it.
We all have the same information. The consideration of this project will be
done thoughtfully, publicly, and in the accordance with the requirements of our
UDO and the public will have multiple opportunities to inform themselves of the
details of the project and provide their input.
In regard to the City’s response to the Project Indigo, I propose that we hire
a consultant to help the City analyze and evaluate the project including
potential issues such as the impact on the City services, infrastructure and
conduct an impact analysis. I have spoken about this to the City Manager, Staff
and some of my fellow Aldermen, and the response has been positive. I believe
this will help us create a better outcome and I hope we will do this,
Moving on the recent storm as we experienced. I’d like to commend and thank the
City Manager, Police chief and Fire Chief, as well as our employees fir their
hard work and excellent response to the storm. There is obviously a lot of work
left to do, but I know it will be handled in the same professional
conscientious manner.”
