A) Call to Order
Mayor Hatem called the special workshop to order at 9:04 a.m. He mentioned all
the events that took place the weekend before including Arbor Day, Naturefest
and a car show.
B) Invocation
Alderman Lowe Davis provided the invocation.
C) Pledge of Allegiance
Mayor Hatem led everyone in the Pledge of Allegiance.
D) 
Alderman Lombardi made a motion to approve the agenda. Alderman Carroll
seconded the motion. All ayes. Motion carried. Mayor Hatem said the Board was
planning to prioritize goals, consider the personnel that is needed, and think
of ways to be more environmentally conscious. He added that the Board strives
to preserve Southport’s character.
E) Agenda
   1.
   Human Resources Director, Patti Fortuna, said she wanted to go over some of
the information that was requested and let the Board know what she had
accomplished during her first six months with the City.
She explained that she compared the City’s benefits plan with other
municipalities including Oak Island, Sunset Beach, Shallotte, and Brunswick
County. Shallotte gives more vacation (96 hours). Oak Island pays 90% of health
insurance coverage for employees, and 40% for dependents. Shallotte offers
longevity pay, too. Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller stated that she had been
considering whether we need longevity pay anymore, since we are including merit
raises. City Manager Therrien said that a government should never remove
benefits. Instead, they could consider a moratorium starting July 1st, so that
no new employees would receive it. Eventually, it would stop. Alderman Allen
and Alderman Alt both agreed that the City should do something to help provide
some assistance for dependent insurance coverage. Alderman Allen said there are
only a couple of people who would take advantage of the dependent coverage
assistance, so the City wouldn’t be contributing a whole lot. Alderman Carroll
said that the Board is so far removed from staff; that staff wants more money.
People who make $40,000 a year are worried about making their payments on time.
Alderman Davis said that she understands that, but a benefits survey would be
helpful. Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller asked to know the overall impact on the cost
of the benefit; would the cost increase if more people have claims? City
Manager Therrien said that the more claims, and the higher amount of claims,
the rates would increase the next year. She also reiterated that City staff
unanimously said they preferred more money. Alderman Carroll said that out of
(74) employees, only three are not on individual coverage. There is no point of
including coverage if only three employees will use it.
Ms. Fortuna moved on to say that she had also made a salary comparison,
particularly with the public sector averages. The payroll study and
classification is about 4-6 months from being completed once the project
begins.
The Human Resources Director said that over the last six months, she has
updated employee files, started engagement surveys, exit interviews,
performance evaluations, job competencies, training on writing and delivering
performance reviews, performance coaching, employee recognition, and NeoGov
implementation is at 50%. Also, the career page is built out on
governmentjobs.com, and she has completed a public employment law course.
Alderman Lombardi stated that he prefers a more competitive salary and leaving
insurance assistance out. Alderman Alt reiterated that a competitive salary is
important, but kids need insurance coverage. He said that young folks are all
about money, but health insurance is still very important.
   2.
   Heather Hemphill thanked the Board and staff for their kindness, sympathy,
and grace they extended to her with the loss of her mother.
She said that a lot of her requests are more capital oriented. She reviewed her
operating expenses including vehicle leasing, fuel costs and departmental
supplies. She said that she would like to have two employees in the parks and
recreation department to focus on park maintenance and upkeep. The positions
would include tasks like pruning the azaleas, irrigation installation, mowing
the grass, etc. The Parks and Recreation Master Plan recommends staff devoted
to these tasks. Alderman Lombardi said that he supported this, as long as two
new employees can be hired for the Parks and Recreation department, and the
positions are not taken from the public services department. Alderman Alt asked
how many man hours were used currently to maintain the parks. Alderman Davis
said she thinks that they are overreaching when it comes to reorganizing
departments. Some of the parks do need a lot of work, but it is not because
staff is slacking off. Can the City afford to hire two new people? Alderman
Lombardi also asked the Board to consider the equipment that would be needed
for the Parks. City Manager Therrien said that it is a mixed bag. She
recommends moving one person and leaving coordination to Heather and Tom
Stanley. Ms. Hemphill added that she would like to move the position in-house,
based on the recommendation of the master plan. City Manager Therrien also
recommends hiring a parks and recreation assistant.
Next, Ms. Hemphill added that the cross-bracing at the City pier took another
hit during Hurricane Ian. There is already $25,000 allocated for the repairs/
replacement, but the estimated cost to repair it is $87,000. We are not sure if
we will get any funding from FEMA. Ms. Hemphill said that FEMA has allocated
$215,000 towards Kingsley Pier repairs. The Board approved the recommendation
of hiring McPherson Marine. The Kayak launch project is being funded by the
efforts of the Morningstar Marina, the City, and a CAMA grant. The shoreline
stabilization project is ongoing, and Ms. Therrien found out that the City can
use the funding on private or publicly owned property. The Yacht Basin dredging
project is at the early stages, and there is no estimates yet. The City is
trying to work with the marina to dredge in January or February. It is more
beneficial to work together.
Mayor Hatem announced there would be a short break. The meeting resumed at 10:
41 a.m.
   3.
   The City Manager asked the Board to review the list that was in their
packets. She reminded the Board that those were items that the Board needed to
make a decision about. Alderman Allen asked if they could have that information
in a more streamlined document. There was some discussion about adding the
items back into the budget and how much the tax rate would increase for each
item. Some items are already included in the Capital Improvement Plan. Ms.
Therrien explained that all personnel requests would affect the budget.
Alderman Alt asked about digitizing the records. The Board discussed the ABC
revenue, and ad valorem taxes that are collected. Alderman Carroll said there
were two non-negotiables; the two paramedic positions. Alderman Allen asked the
City Manager to prioritize the positions. Ms. Therrien stated the building
inspector, permitting technician, and fire inspector are easy because they are
funded by the departments already. Ms. Therrien asked about the 5% COLA that
she included, and the merit raise. She added that the pay study is equally
important. Mayor Hatem summarized that the City Manager will bring that list
back to them and help them make some decisions. They discussed dates for a
future workshop. The decided on Wednesday, May 10th at 1:00 p.m. in the
Community Building.
F)  Mayor’s Comments
Mayor Hatem thanked staff for their work on the budget.

There were no Board comments.

   Alderman Alt asked if benefits were included in this breakdown. Mr. Stevens
said yes. Alderman Alt    asked why the IT and paver positions are similar in
percentage to the tax rate when the IT position is a more significant expense.
Alderman Allen noted that at the bottom of the document that part of the
   expense was covered due to already being budgeted for an IT contract. Mr.
Stevens said that was correct.
   Alderman Alt said that the City has gone out for bids on the Cemetery care
for two years, and only a few    have been received. He said the work is time-
consuming and must be done carefully to protect the    gravestones, and time is
money. He noted that it might be more efficient to contract someone to do the
linear parks that could be completed very quickly. City Manager Therrien said
that she had looked at both    options to have Building and Grounds continue to
maintain or subcontract out. She said that if contracting out for grounds work
was the option, they would have to be supervised often, and more time would be
spent trying to ensure that they are working and doing the best quality.
Alderman Lombardi questioned why the revenue-neutral number was published. He
said that everybody was calling and telling him thank you before, and now it
will jump back up. Ms. Therrien noted that by state law, it has to be
published. Alderman Lombardi said he doesn’t think people will accept the fact
that it is going way back up.
Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller questioned the budget sheet, where stated the revenue
2023 actuals and what is collected for that tax year. Ms. Therrien said the
estimated actuals are estimated to be what the end of this fiscal year would
be. Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller asked why the FY 23-24 was $195,000 less than what
the estimated actual going to be from the previous year when there is more

the estimated actuals. He stated that is less than what is being requested. Mr.

received as income. Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller stated that would be less. Alderman
Carroll said that the value went up, and the point of neutral is that it stays
the same. Mr. Stevens said that they would have to go back and review this
information.
There was a discussion on the proposed new positions for one permit technician,
one building inspector, one fire inspector, and two paramedics. There was
clarification that these positions would be revenue based. That Department
would need to be budgeted prior to the revenue that was generated and put back
into the fund balance. Ms. Therrien said that any money generated from the
Inspections Department must be put back into that Department by law. Alderman
Alt’s concern is that when hiring these new positions, taxes will be raised to
accommodate. Mayor Pro Tem said it could come from the fund balance. City
Manager Therrien did not recommend that. Alderman Alt said he is trying to
figure out how to hire new employees without raising taxes. He said if we can
prove that getting through the first year that it is revenue neutral would go
over better with the citizens than saying that the City is hiring many new
positions on top of the ones hired last year.
Mayor Hatem noted that the City should be getting every dime out of the ad
valorum tax. That it should not be less. Ms. Therrien said that the finance
director is reviewing that again right now. He said that he believes that if
the Citizens knew that the money was going to new positions, such as the two
paramedics and a Planning Director for the Historic Preservation Commission,
etc., they would understand that they are gaining beneficial services.
Alderman Lombardi questioned why the departments don’t include their requested
new positions when submitting their budget. Ms. Therrien said it was not the
Staff that did it this way. She said she has always worked on budgets this way.
She noted that the Board would have the final approval on what positions they
feel are beneficial and needed for the City.
Ms. Therrien said that if you look at the budget, there is approximately $1.2 M
that is sitting in the contingency that should not be just sitting in there.
She said that it was way too much money that could be earning interest. She
said to look at the increased revenue amount that was not projected correctly,
and the Departments did a great job keeping their budget under control. She
said a lot of positions were approved last year but were never hired before
July 1st, even though they were budgeted for before July 1st. Alderman Alt said
that sometimes there is credit for turnover and that Department gets to keep
the money that was not used, and other jurisdictions turn that money back to
the general fund. Ms. Therrien said that 90% of that unused money goes back to
the General Fund except for the electric and water because it has to. Alderman
Carroll asked what the current fund balance is. Ms. Therrien gave the
description of the funds. Ms. Therrien had the general fund totals but was
looking for the fund balances. Alderman Carroll asked because it appears that
around $1.1M is needed to proceed, so some of the funds could come from the
general fund balance. Ms. Therrien said she would recommend using the capital
funds but not for recurring expenses. The fund balance needs to cover
hurricanes and other potential storms, etc. This could wipe out the fund
balance. She said this could mean laying people off or raising taxes to make up
the difference. That’s why she recommended using it for one-time expenses and
took a lot out of the fund balance to pay for capital.
Alderman Carroll reiterated that there needs to be more discussion on the ad
valorem tax. Alderman Allen asks what is the $1.2 M in contingency. Ms.
Therrien said that is excess revenues. All the revenue has come in beyond or
above what was proposed as adopted last year. She also said the departments
kept their budget under control, the new positions that were approved on July
1st but were hired in October. The merits were budgeted for the entire year,
but they weren’t supposed to go into effect until this month. So, that’s
creating a part of the excess money. Alderman Allen asked if that money could
be applied to the new positions. Ms. Therrien did not recommend it because she
said it’s a one-time expense and should not be recurring. Alderman Allen asked
if the $1.2M in contingency is just a placeholder and where it comes from. Ms.
Therrien said that she had never seen it done this way in her 30-year
experience. Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller noted that she has seen in past budgets
that there had been money in contingency. Manager Therrien said that she knows
that the former finance director had this money in contingency, but she does
not think it should be just sitting in a contingency account. Alderman wanted
clarification on how this could be used as a reoccurring expense if it is only
used once. Manager Therrien said that if those revenues go down and suddenly
you don’t have those revenues coming in, and you use it, then people will have
to be laid off. Alderman Alt said that with the banking system being unstable
and not having guarantees, he would be against reoccurring expenses. Alderman
Carroll’s recommendation was to agree on what positions on the list would be
agreed on and use the general fund to pay for it.
Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller asked about the water/sewer budget calculation and the
three oversized ticket items that were listed as capital improvements, but they
actually factored into the water/sewer budget. She said it was like counting

Capital Improvements later in the discussion. Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller noted
that with the trucks requested for the Public Services Department, there is a

it will be kept in the fleet but will also be used for other things. Mayor Pro

the old truck. She said if they are leasing a new truck, why not keep the old
truck? Alderman Lombardi stated that he believes the new truck would be used to
haul things such as asphalt for road repairs. He said the old truck was not
worth much, and he suggested keeping it.
Alderman Carroll and Alderman Allen wanted more clarification on the
contingency in the surplus. He asked where is this money going. Manager
Therrien said that it would go into the interest bearings. Alderman Carroll
asked why it did not go back into the fund balance. Manager Therrien said that
it goes back into investments. Alderman Carroll stated that instead of going

Alderman Carroll suggested the best answer would be to keep a revenue neutral
tax rate, and it would accomplish everything. Alderman Davis asked if the $1.2M

rates go down, it was projected to reach $700,000 but would possibly not get
$700,000. She said somehow, we would have to make up the $700,000 or lay people
off. Alderman Allen said there is always that possibility that the rates could
go up or down. He doesn’t agree with the $1.2M sitting in contingency when it
could be used in the budget.
Alderman Alt asked how many people were hired last year. It was estimated
between 8-12 were employed. He said there are 11 new positions being requested
for this year, and with the cumulative inflations going up, citizens will be

Mr. Stevens said that the ad valorem taxes are based on last year’s 39.39 tax
rate. This year is from the preliminary scroll from the county, and as of

account for growth. Mayor Hatem asked if that was the same as the estimated
actual that was projected in 2023. Mr. Stevens said that was correct.
Alderman Lombardi asked if it was the 50% dependent coverage was still being
considered. Alderman Allen said that he believes the consensus of the Board is

H)   Agenda
   1.   Social Media Policy
   The City Attorney Mr. Brady Herman stated that Staff approached him along
with the City Manager to help them put together the social media policy. He
said this is a policy decision by the Board and they are free to adjust what is
presented, and to delete anything they want or choose not to adopt. He said the
intent is not to infringe on the First Amendment right to free speech. He said
it does set forth some requirements not only for the Board but also the other
appointed boards and committees of the City and as well as to establish a way
for the different boards to go about and create a social media account through
the City. He explained a couple of the highlights on the important items. He
said a lot of what's in the proposed policy regardless of social media are
standards that you all must adhere to anyway for example privileged
confidential information record retention and some other requirements that
otherwise in the City Board of Ethics policy. He said one of the key things
here is this policy can fit in one of 2 scenarios where it doesn't apply is if
you or another board have a personal social media account and you don't discuss
any sort of city business this policy does not apply in that scenario. The
other scenario is if you have a personal social media account and use it some
for personal and discuss city business then this would go and apply. He said if
you want to have a social media account and add your platform as a public
official use this board as an example then you can get that registered through
the City. Attorney Brady said what that does is it's goes to help with record
retention. If you discuss City business, no matter what sort of platform it
comes from that is a public record. He said one of the things that is key to
this policy is putting the disclaimer on your social media account when you're
speaking about city business that it's coming from your personal opinion it's
not coming from the board as a whole unless the board approved it.
   Alderman Davis made a Motion to deny the proposed Social Media Policy.
Alderman Alt seconded    the Motion. Mayor Hatem asked if there was any
discussion from the Board before a vote was    taken.
   Alderman Davis said that there is the law and the spirit of the law. She
thinks this proposed social    media policy is unnecessary and infringes on
free speech. She believes that it is overreaching and    redundant.
   Alderman Alt said he does understand why the federal government can put
minimal restrictions    on using social media. He said in the past year they
have opined several things like record    retention and detention of comments.
His objection was that the city’s policy had several illegal    sentences such
as the city would allow one to have a social account, the city was forbidding
the    use of social media for re-elections or backing other candidates.
Additionally elected officials had    opined in public actions they thought
were improper which are clearly protected speech.
   ChyAnn Ketchup/ PIO said this policy is not telling you what you can and
cannot post but how to    post it safely. Attorney Herman said this policy can
be redrafted and the language revised. He said    for example in the authorized
right that could just say elected appointed officials have the right    to
operate a personal social media account.
   Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller noted that an updated social media policy is needed.
She recommended    having ChyAnn and Attorney Herman revisit the language,
address the concerns, and bring it back    to the Board in a Workshop to work
out the details. Alderman Alt said that he would like to    continue the
discussion so that Attorney Herman can address these concerns and continue with
   the specifics on how the language should be revised and regarding the
accounts and how they are    retained. Attorney Brady said that it he would
have to review the Administration process of    retention, but the City
Business accounts would have to be retained. Alderman Alt said that the
   language needs to be more defined.
   It was the consensus of the Board to review the policy in a workshop to
address concerns.    Alderman Davis amended the original motion to not approve
the Social Media policy but to table    the Social Media Policy for further
work and discussion at a workshop, seconded by Mayor Pro    Tem Mosteller.
Unanimous Vote; Motion Carried.
   2.    Budget Summary Presentation by City Manager Bonnie Therrien
   City Manager Therrien gave a presentation on her proposed 2023-2034 Budget.
She said that with the Department Staff they have been putting a budget
together so the Mayor and the Board can devise a strategic plan to reduce that
tax rate so that it does not incur a huge expense with the increased values.
She said she wanted to make sure we continued with the increase of capital
items as well as the fund balance and using that to pay for those onetime
expenses of capital. She said she wants to make sure that our fixed costs are
adequate and not just putting enough money so that you would have to go back to
the fund balance or contingency. She said to keep in mind all future mandates
from the federal and state government, and we have one that we have to complete
fairly quickly which is federal mandate to inspect all of our lead pipes and we
have to come up with a complete report on which ones have led in them which
don't I'm sure we're going to have to replace those that do and that's going to
be very costly. Also, is proposed 11 new positions that were provided in the
agenda packet that are listed in priority order. She provided highlights of the
proposed Budget on PowerPoint.

   7.   Oakton Preliminary Plat
    City Attorney Brady Herman stated as a benefit to the public and The Board
he would go over the standards for preliminary plat decisions. This decision
from this Board is administrative decision which means this board needs to
decide based upon the objective standards and criteria in the UDO whether the
preliminary plat meets the standards. He said if the preliminary plat meets the
standards of the ordinance, it should be approved. He said if it doesn't meet
the standards than it can be denied. But he said if that's the case there would
need to be a statement for which sections of the ordinance did that plat not
meet those standards. City Planner Meehan gave an overview of the project. She
said Greg Wayne for Stanley Martin homes is seeking approval for a major
subdivision preliminary plat known as Oakton. The approval would authorize
construction of the required improvements to the site, so this is an
approximately 20 acre site between Stuart and Fodale Avenues and adjacent to
the Hammocks subdivision. It is zoned R-10 which requires a minimum 10,000
square foot lot with a 75 foot width setbacks and height will be confirmed with
the permit stage. There will be almost 3 acres of open space with walking
trails around the stormwater pond and that exceeds the 2% open space for a
standard subdivision. It is a 42 lot single family subdivision and per Section
4 of the UDO requires interconnectivity to the streets and this one does
connect with Sand Dollar Lane with the Hammocks. There are 2 entrances on
Fodale Avenue and a one way entrance off of Stuart avenue and they have a 60
foot right away that would be dedicated to the City. The planning board has
composed a committee and the committee meetings that were concerns from the
neighbors of the entrance from Stuart as a two way and so it was requested that
the entrance become a trail or a bike or walking paths only or a consideration
of a one way only. After considerations the applicant was willing to do a one
way off of Stuart avenue with the signage added so that people would know that
it is a one way street. There were some questions about the landscape plan and
the tree mitigation in this application. It is using what is called permit
choice it's an option in the UDO and it's also in 160 D of the planning
enabling statutes that allows an applicant when they apply to rules change,
they are able to choose which rules they want to use for their application. The
application was originally brought in in July of 21, they are only allowed
they're to mitigate the regulated trees or specimen in the setbacks only or
specimen trees anywhere on site. Then in September 2022 there was a change to
the tree ordinance that would allow an infrastructure drainage and utility
provision which would allow that the subdivision to remove the trees without
mitigation except for Live Oak trees. This will be taken care of after homes
are built because they can't plant the trees where they are needed. There was a
lot of questions over the drainage and storm water retention. They do have a
stormwater pond system and all of the water will be designed and engineered to
drain into that pond. They are designing it to meet the 100th year 24 hour
event and the final design will be reviewed and approved by the city engineers
and the public services department prior to any work starting on site. The
planning board at their March 16th meeting made a unanimous recommendation to
the board of Alderman for approval of this major subdivision preliminary plat.
It meets the requirements of the UDO and is eligible to be approved. The
applicant was there to answer any questions. Mr. Worth Mills with Long Leaf Law
partners on behalf of Stanley Martin Homes, the subdivision applicant, came to
the podium. He said that he appreciates the explanation from the town Attorney
and the Planning Department. He said State law requires that subdivision plat
decisions are based on the clear explicit standards that are set forward in
Southport’s UDO. He said the City’s Planning Department has done a great job
with the process. He said that they exceed the minimum standards of the UDO.
Mr. Mills said that they appreciate the opportunity, and Stanley Martin Homes
looks forward to being a part of this community.

   9.   Prices Creek Townhomes Preliminary Plat Phase II
   City Planner Meehan explained that Cameron Smith is the applicant/owner and
is requesting approval of Phase 2 of the Prices Creek major subdivision
preliminary plat. It is a planned unit zoned planned unit development and it
was approved in 2004 for 3 phases the first phase is where the cottages or the
single family home portion of the development and then there were 2 other
multifamily phases, and this is the second phase with the multifamily located
some off of Rob Gandy Boulevard and also E. Leonard St. It has connectivity
with green Meadow Way onto East Leonard. It is 48 units or townhomes. It is a
little over 17 acres with almost 4 acres of open space which exceeds the 20%
required and they have 40 foot right away that would have 24 inch or 4,024’
dedicated public streets. There will be space for sidewalks, and this was
specifically permitted by the fire Marshall and the Fire Chief which is allowed
by the UDO. They have met their landscape and mitigations and there are no
buffer requirements. They are putting a lot of their mitigation along the top
near rob Gandy to because it is the property across the street is light
industrial. This is a low density stormwater project so they will not have a
stormwater retention pond it is designed to be less than 24% impervious
surfaces and is permitted through the North Carolina Department of
Environmental quality. The city engineers will work with DEQ for the final
plans prior to installation for compliance with the city standards on the
system. They will be using a system of vegetated swales and curb outlets that
will disperse the flow so it's going to help protect the stream hydrology
remove pollutants and then prevent erosion through infiltration. The planning
board at the regular scheduled meeting on April 20th recommended unanimous
approval for recommendation to the board of Alderman for the major subdivision
plat. It meets the requirements of the UDO and is eligible for to be approved
by as a major subdivision for a preliminary plat. Mr. Cameron Smith was in
attendance to answer any questions. Alderman Alt asked if he knew how far away
the water table is from the bottom of the swale. Mr. Cameron Smith said overall
it is very sandy and has a good elevation and not as far as the stormwater
swales. He did know where the groundwater would be. He said Phase I has
stormwater ponds.

   8.   Osprey Landing Phase 1 and 2 Final Plat:
   Director Henley presented the Major Subdivision Final Plat for phases 1 and
2 of Osprey Landing located to the north of Robert Ruark and West of Howe
Street. Osprey Landing was approved as a Planned Unit Development with a
Development Agreement in May of 2020. The preliminary plat for the entire 196
unit subdivision was approved by the Aldermen in June of 2021. The roadways
within the entirety of the project are private. The water and sewer is to be
handled by Brunswick County the electric system is the only system that would
be help handled by the city of Southport and the electric infrastructure
they've installed is in accordance with all applicable with the City of
Southport standards. Phase one includes the main entrance off of Robert Ruark
and includes the amenity site located to the left. The amenity site received
major site plan approval from the planning board in June 2022. There are 45
single family lots located along 3 private roadways that includes the amenity
site. Based on the preliminary plat they did show a few areas for tree
retention and a few areas for tree planting based on the multiple site visits.
Mr. Henley said he has done his own review and walking the site with the
applicant they've actually both been able to retain more trees than they had
proposed and have planted more than they said they were going to plant. There
are a number of conditions of approval that staff are recommending be included.
Director Henley said these are all pretty standard conditions that would look
familiar based on the other final plats that have been brought before this
board. These are all to be done prior to plat recordation including DEQ
approval of the water and sewer systems and Brunswick County utilities signing
the plat prior to the City signing the plat. He said that is standard for any
project that involves Brunswick County utilities. He said the purpose of
putting these conditions on with approval should come in any day now. He said
with the plat recordation the applicant will provide a performance guarantee
with associated financial instrument and engineer cost estimate with 25%
contingency for the construction of sidewalks in accordance with the
preliminary plat. Mr. Henley said you can put the sidewalks under a performance
guarantee in order not to have them installed and then torn up through the
construction process and then 3 prior to plat recordation the applicant will
provide certification from NC dot that all required improvements dictated by
the approved traffic impact study for the project have been installed or
otherwise satisfied. Another one of their requirements was a financial
commitment to the City for a long term signal upgrades at the Robert Ruark 87
to 11 intersection and with all the construction happening right there they
were not going to make the applicant make any signal changes that are just
going to get removed in a few months. He said has already happened and they are
just waiting on certification of the turn lane from Robert Ruark into the
neighborhood which should per the applicant come soon. With those conditions
staff respectfully recommends approval. Alderman Alt clarified that City will
not be responsible for any of the streets. He stated there is no intention of
the City ever taking them over. He said the engineer will certify that they are
designed and constructed to the standards that they committed to. Director
Henley all the roads are platted as private and there is permanent recordation
of that.

Call to Order
Mayor Hatem called the meeting to order at 9:01 a.m.
Invocation
Alderman Lowe Davis provided the invocation.
Pledge of Allegiance
Mayor Hatem led everyone in reciting the Pledge of Allegiance.
Approval of Agenda
Mayor Hatem gave a quick overview of the agenda and said that one item would be
added. A presentation on the American Flood Coalition would be added as the
second item on the agenda. Alderman Allen made a motion to approve the agenda,
with the additional presentation. The motion was seconded by Alderman Lombardi.
All ayes. Motion carried.
Agenda
   1.
   Ms. Dutton made sure the Board could hear the audio from Mr. Clark Harris.
Mayor Hatem welcomed him to the meeting and thanked him for attending. Mr.
Harris explained the Unique Places to Save program and described the Boiling
Springs Wilderness Conservation Project. That project is a potential land
acquisition of approximately 950 acres between Southport and Boiling Springs
Lakes. The property connects to existing conservation land. The property is
home to several vital species including the Red-cockaded woodpecker and the
Venus Fly Trap. It is also beneficial to the water quality of the region
because it is connected to the headwaters of Orton Creek and the Castle Hayne
Aquifer. Mr. Harris said that he wasn’t speaking to the Board to gain monetary
donations, he was simply requesting a Letter of Support for the project. The
Board directed Ms. Dutton to draft a letter and add it to the Consent Agenda at
the June 8, 2023 Board meeting. Alderman Carroll asked what other
municipalities had shown support? Mr. Harris said that he started with
Southport. After that, he would likely reach out to Boiling Springs Lakes. Mr.
Harris thanked the Board for offering the Letter of Support and said he is
available for any questions that might come up later. Mayor Hatem thanked him
again for attending and the virtual meeting ended.
   2.
   Mr. Tony McEwen, with the American Flood Coalition addressed the Board next.
He explained that the AFC was a national organization that focused on solutions
to flooding and sea level rise. They advocate for smarter, more resilient
planning in all communities. Their mission includes four pillars that includes
economy, communities, rebuilding, and military. He invited the City of
Southport to join the organization for free and take advantage of all the
benefits including advocacy, technical assistance and help acquiring funds to
work on projects pertaining to flooding. Mr. McEwen explained that the AFC is a
great organization because it crosses the political party lines, and both
Republicans and Democrats are members. They have been able to secure funding
for many projects including a transportation flood resilience grant. Ms. Dutton
explained that there was a Resolution in Support of Joining the AFC as an item
on the Regular agenda for June 8, 2023.
   3.
   Travis Henley, the Development Services Director, approached the Board with
more discussion about rights- of-way. He said that he needs direction from the
Board on two items: surfacing and grandfathering. Alderman Davis stated that
before the Board makes a decision, a public meeting should be held, to get
feedback from the public. She added that most driveways are dirt or gravel, and
she thinks it is a mistake to require impervious surfacing. Mayor Pro-tem said
she thinks it is better to have something on paper to discuss, and then adjust
after public comment. Mayor Hatem agreed that it’s best to discuss things
first. He further added that with regards to grandfathering, safety issues
should be addressed right away. But other issues can be managed over time. If
plants in the right of way need to be removed for utility work, they would not
be allowed to be planted back. Mr. Henley suggested a collaborative approach in
which property owners would apply for vested rights of existing encroachments.
But also, egregious offenses should be removed immediately following the
adoption of the amendment. Alderman Carroll questioned who would decide what is
safe? Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller said she prefers an approach that is less severe;
if it interferes with vehicular, pedestrian or bicycle traffic, it should be
removed. She also supports special considerations for corners. She stated that
she feels that hardened structures could have six months to comply with the
ordinance, but vegetation and existing trees should be allowed to stay at the
City’s discretion. Alderman Carroll said he doesn’t feel like the Board or
staff should pick and choose; it should be all or nothing. Alderman Allen added
that he doesn’t understand how some things can be justified, but not others.
   Alderman Lombardi asked about what types of gravel would be required?
Alderman Allen said it would be better to list what is not allowed. There was
some discussion about parking pads, including the driveway in part of the pad,
and also who would maintain the gravel area. Mayor Hatem said that our
Engineer’s would help us determine what kind of gravel/surfacing would be
required. Mr. Henley said that the next time the Board saw the right of way
information, it would be in ordinance format. He would provide both options
regarding grandfathering for the Board’s consideration.
   4.
   Heather Hemphill and Bob Jarvis approached the Board to give an update on
the dredging project. Ms. Hemphill explained that there are two possibilities
to consider. The first dredging area is the area of the federal channel, which
is 50,400 cubic yards. The Board can have just that area dredged, or they can
include an additional area near the City dock. The total for both areas is
55,800 cubic yards. If that additional area is dredged, the boat slips can be
put back at the City dock. The Board agreed that the larger dredging project
would be best.
   5.
   The next item was also regarding the dredging project. TI Coastal Services
had completed the work from the first contract with the City. The next process
is to do the permitting packet. There will be a scoping meeting first for all
the groups involved; and then putting together the permitting packet. The
contract currently being considered is based on an hourly rate, not to exceed
$7,000, including contingency. Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller said she was thankful
for the assistance with the permitting process. Mayor Hatem said that it was an
exciting project.
   6.
   ChyAnn Ketchum, the Public Information Officer and Communications staff
addressed the Board and said that the Board’s Symposium session was
approaching. City staff thought it might be better to provide a list of topics
for the Board, so they can narrow down their subject matter and it doesn’t get
too personal. After some discussion, it was decided that Mayor Hatem would talk
about the duties of the Mayor and the Board; Alderman Lombardi would speak to
the Board’s goals and objectives; Alderman Allen would go through the budgeting
process; Alderman Davis would discuss Boards, Committees, and Commissions and
how to volunteer; Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller would discuss ordinances and how they
are created and voted on. Alderman Carroll would discuss the ways the public
can participate in government. At the end of their presentations, the public
will be able to ask questions. Ms. Dutton offered to send the Board various
articles and PowerPoint presentations that might help them with their
presentations.
   7.
   Next, the Board reviewed the Agenda for the June 8, 2023 Board meeting.
There were no questions about the Consent agenda items. Mayor Hatem read
through the agenda items, and when he got to Rescinding the Waiver of the
Credit Card processing fees, the Board had some questions. Teresa Jones, the
Finance Specialist, approached the Board to answer any questions. She explained
that prior to the Covid-19 pandemic, a flat $5.00 fee was added to each
transaction. But the Board waived the fee to encourage more people to pay
remotely instead of coming to the office. The City is usually charged between
1.5-2.5% of the charge. The City also pays $225.00 a month for the subscription
that allows card payments, and $540 as a transaction fee. So far this year, the
City has paid $13,000 in fees for card payments. Alderman Allen asked about
fees for debit versus credit cards. Ms. Jones explained that it was fairer to
charge 2.5% of the amount of the transaction. There was more discussion about
charging all card users the fee instead of only the phone or online payments.
Ms. Jones also stated that they all encourage people to pay using a draft
process through their bank, because there is no fee. Ms. Jones also stated that
Dropbox is available to customers. Dropbox payments are applied like an ACH
transaction and are automatically processed on the 15th of each month.
   There was some discussion about the speed limit in the Yacht Basin area.
Alderman Davis is requesting to make the speed limit 10mph. The other Board
members said there wouldn’t be much difference because everyone has to go so
slowly at the Yacht Basin already.
   Next, was the discussion about the proposed Noise Ordinance amendment.
Several Board members were in support of an exemption for City work and the
City’s contractors, such as the trash collection contractors. The Board asked
Ms. Dutton to review other municipalities to see how they manage their own
workers and equipment. Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller also asked for information about
when Public Services is most successful and productive at completing their
jobs?
   Interim Finance Director, Paul Gross, approached the Board to review the
Finance Policies being considered at the Board meeting. He said that since his
appointment, it was apparent that the City did not have important finance
policies in place. The first policy for consideration is the Fund Balance
Policy. After reviewing the Town of Bluffton’s fund balance policy, he
recommends changing his draft policy from 25% to 35%. The Town of Bluffton won
an award for their Fund Balance Policy, and their recommended fund balance is
35%. Mr. Gross added that the City is in good shape; our total fund balance is
62%. Alderman Allen suggested 50% unassigned fund balance. Mayor Pro-tem
Mosteller said that she researched the Town of Bluffton, and they are a larger
area than Southport. The Town of Bluffton is 55 square miles, and they have
other sources of revenue. The Board thanked Mr. Gross for attending the meeting
and also for accepting the Interim Finance Officer position.
F.) There were no Board comments.
G.)
   Mayor Hatem stated that the meeting was excellent. He thanked everyone for
attending, and those watching from home.
H.)
   Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller made a motion to adjourn the meeting, which was
seconded by the full Board. All ayes. Motion carried. Mayor Hatem adjourned the
meeting at 11:12 a.m.

A)   Call to Order
Mayor Hatem called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m.
B)   Invocation
Alderman Lowe Davis gave the invocation.
C)   Pledge of Allegiance
Mayor Hatem led everyone in the Pledge of Allegiance.
Mayor Hatem read the Ethics Statement.
D)   Approval of Agenda
Mayor Hatem said the order of the agenda was changing so that the overview was
first, then the public hearing and lastly, the fee schedule discussion.
Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller made a motion to approve the agenda with the
recommended changes. Alderman Lombardi seconded the motion. All ayes. Motion
carried.
E)   Agenda
Mayor Hatem stated that the proposed budget was great for many reasons; it
lowers the tax rate, provides for the City staff, includes many new positions,
and indicates our enterprise funds are solid. He added that the City is working
toward regionalization. He asked the City Manager to provide an overview of the
budget, and Ms. Therrien approached the podium.
   1.
   Ms. Therrien explained that the budget being presented is the Board of
Aldermen’s consensus budget that they have worked through over the last few
months. At the beginning of the process, the Board began to review the
strategic plan and decide on priorities. This year was Brunswick County’s
revaluation of property. The average increase in Southport was 44%, but there
were some that the value increased 60%, and others than only increased 16%.
   The Board included a 5% cost of living increase for all employees, as well
as a 5% merit increase. The Board stressed the importance of decent wages and
benefits for all employees. We have to retain and attract employees. We have to
address fixed costs and look ahead at state/federal mandates. There are ten new
positions included. In addition, there is a 15.9% increase in revenues and the
fund balances are very healthy.
   There are many capital projects included in the budget: a new comprehensive
plan, a survey and assessment of all the City-owned buildings, stormwater
planning, cross bracing at the City pier, decking for the Community Building, a
parking study, new roofs for the gazebos, and a storage shed for the Parks and
Recreation department. A new dump truck will be paid for partly by Powell Bill
funds and partly with Capital funds.
   The ten positions approved include an additional Building Inspector,
Permitting Tech, an additional Fire/ISO Inspector, Recreation Assistant, two
Full-time paramedics, a promotion for one Public Services staff positions, two
new Public Services positions, make a part-time Community Building Facilitator
position to full-time, a downtown-historic planner position, a part-time plant
waterer, and either a Code Enforcement Officer, or making Alliance Code
Enforcement contracted for full-time hours.
   Ms. Therrien stated that public input is crucial to the budget process. She
encouraged people who were not able to attend this Public Hearing to reach out
to her, or the Board with any questions and concerns.
   Ms. Therrien added that the solutions to reduce taxes in the future would be
to reduce services, gain approval for local option taxes, and find a way to
capitalize on the dollars raised by tourism. The City can also collaborate with
other municipalities to save money on certain projects by regionalizing.
   2.
   Mayor Hatem clapped after the presentation and said that it was excellent.
Ms. Therrien said again that she was disappointed there was no one else there.
A motion was made by the Board to open the Public Hearing at 6:25 p.m. Ms.
Dutton stated that one person had signed up to speak, but there may be others
in the audience. She called Ms. Pat Kirkman to the podium for her comments.
   Ms. Pat Kirkman said that she was very impressed and congratulatory towards
Ms. Therrien and the City staff. There are still a couple of areas for concern,
primarily the cemeteries. Ms. Kirkman said that she came across a document from
the Historical Society that was thirty-two years ago. She read the letter, that
stated the cemeteries were not a priority back then, either. The Old Smithville
Burying Ground was assigned to the Buildings and Grounds department and the
Recreation department. The document stated that no additional monies were
allocated to the maintenance of the cemeteries. Ms. Kirkman then said that
during the last budget cycle, she was told by the Mayor that there would be a
line item for the cemeteries; but there never was. The only relevant item was
for tree removal in the cemeteries. She continued adding that some of the
“asks” in this year’s budget were fairly large, including $1000 for a trash bin
at Northwood Cemetery. Ms. Kirkman added that Ms. Therrien was always very
quick to respond and very helpful. The proposed budget also includes $15,000
for a survey. There was a survey done in the past to mark the corners and
alleyways, but the former City Manager, Gordon Hargrove, requested the markers
be removed for some reason. Now, it is very difficult to find the graves.
$70,670 was requested for a repair and maintenance contract to maintain the
cemeteries. Ms. Kirkman asked if the Board would have to vote on the contract
for maintenance. Does the proposed maintenance contract include the John Smith
cemetery, too? But Ms. Kirkman added that there was still no line item for the
cemetery committee. Ms. Therrien explained to Ms. Kirkman that once the
Cemetery Committee go farther along with their mission and goals, they are
welcome to ask the Board for funds. Mr. Kirkman also asked if it was feasible
to create a new line in the budget for burial permits and plot sales.
   Mayor Hatem stated that if the public compares what is in the budget and all
the work that Public Services can accomplish in the cemeteries, it is a HUGE
improvement. We are making progress and he appreciated her bringing the topic
forward.
   There was no one else interested in speaking.
Alderman Allen made a motion to leave the Public Hearing, which was seconded by
Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller. The Mayor closed the Public Hearing at 6:42 p.m. All
ayes.
   3.
   City Manager Therrien asked Ms. Dutton to review the Fee Schedule and any
proposed changes. Ms. Dutton explained that she had worked with the various
Department Heads to make any appropriate changes to the fee schedule. Some of
the changes included the addition of a $35.00 fee for checking a meter at the
request of the property owner when the problem was on the owner’s side. The
Fire fees had increased as high as they are allowed, at the recommendation of
the Fire Association. Some of the building permit and inspection fees were
updated and some changes were made to the fees to rent a park or facility.
There was some discussion about rescinding the waiver from the 2.5% processing
fee for credit card payments in the Utilities department.
F) Board Comments

He said that if he only made enough income to cover his bills, what would he do

   Director Henley gave a recap on the Subdivision. Greg Wayne, on behalf of
Stanley Martin Homes,    is seeking approval of Oakton Subdivision Preliminary
Plat consisting of 42 single family home lots.    The property is located
between Fodale Avenue and Stuart Avenue and is adjacent to the    Hammocks
subdivision. He said there have been no changes to the plat since the Aldermen
last    reviewed it at the May 11th Regular Meeting. This project was first
introduced as a sketch plan at    the July 15, 2021 Planning Board Meeting. The

Board of Aldermen for approval at their March 16, 2023 meeting.

    5.    American Flood Coalition
   City Manager Therrien discovered an Article in the Brunswick Beacon
regarding from the    American Flood Coalition and found that it would be a
useful program for Southport to be a part    of. She stated that joining will
provide support to address flooding and provide access to the best    practices
and support to develop response to flooding issues and keeping the public
informed.    She said many of the communities in Brunswick County as well as
New Hanover and Pender    Counties have been members for years. She recommended
joining the program not only for the    information that could assist us with
funding but for grant opportunities as well. Mayor Hatem    noted that in the
information guide it states that every $1 spend on pre-disaster mitigation
saves    $4-7 in disaster relief funds.
   Alderman Carroll made a Motion to approve the resolution by the Board of
Aldermen for the City    of Southport to become a member of the American Flood
Coalition and seconded by Alderman    Davis. Unanimous Vote; Motion Carried.
    6.    Adoption of a Fund Balance Policy
   Mr. Paul Gross, Interim Finance Director came to the podium and gave an
overview of the fund    balance policy. He said that a fund balance policy is
essential to the preservation of the financial    integrity of the City and is
fiscally advantageous to both the City and the taxpayer. He said this    policy
establishes objectives; it provides guidance concerning the desired level of
fund balance    that is maintained by the City to mitigate financial risk. He
said that it is proposed to offer an    accessible fund balance of 35% and a
total fund balance of 40%. Mayor Hatem noted that it’s    about the risk that
Southport faces with respect to Natural Disasters such as Hurricanes that other
   municipalities may not have to face. The municipalities on the coast have to
make sure that the    fund balance is adequate. He thanked Mr. Gross for his
presentation. Alderman Allen questioned    if accessible fund balance is the
same as unrestricted fund balance. Mr. Gross said that he defines    accessible
fund balance as the assigned fund balance as well as the unassigned fund bund
balance.    He said he tend to be more conservative in his recommendation and
he excluded the committed    fund balances. Alderman Allen asked what if the
fund balance policy succeeds the amount and    percentages. Manager Therrien
said there would be no issue with that and more could be added.    Alderman Alt
agreed with Alderman Allen with a 35% minimum. He said sometimes it tale 2-
4    years to get a FEMA reimbursement and he said he would be inclined to be
more on the upward    of 50%. Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller stated that she reviewed
the Bluffton policy and they do a 15%    emergency recovery fund within that
unrestricted fund. She said that with not having a 15%    emergency fund she
would prefer to have a 50% fund balance. Mayor Hatem said to consider the
   cost of damages from the most devasting hurricane and relate that cost to
the amount of funds    that need to be available for that recovery.
   A Motion was made by Alderman Alt to adopt the Fund Balance Policy that
states a 50% accessible    fund balance and a total fund balance of 55% and
seconded by Alderman Carroll.
   Unanimous Vote; Motion Carried.
    7.     Adoption of Write Off Policy for Uncollectible Accounts
   Manager Therrien explained that it has come to her attention by Teresa
Jones, Utility Director,    that there have been accounts that have been
sitting on the books for fifteen years that have    been uncollectible. She
said that the City continues to try to collect but maybe the customer has
   died or there are unknown reasons. She said they do not need to stay on the
books    because it is giving a false sense of what the City is worth. She is
recommending a policy that a    list of those accounts be bought to the Board
to be approved to be removed off the balance sheet.    She said there will
still be continuation of attempts to collect on those accounts.
   Alderman Allen made a Motion to adopt the Write Off Policy for Uncollectable
Accounts and    seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller. Unanimous vote; Motion
Carried.
   8.   Ordinance Rescinding the Waiver of the Credit Card Processing Fee
   Manager Therrien said that before Covid there was a credit card fee that was
added if you used    credit cards to pay utility bills, then when Covid hit the
credit fee charges were waived. She    said that now that Covid cases have
subsided it may be a good idea to come back to the Board to    rescind that
Ordinance and return to charging the credit card use fee. Ms. Therrien said the
reason    for this addition is because the credit card companies charge fees
and the City should not be    responsible for paying these fees. She asked for
approval to rescind this waiver so that credit card    processing fees will go
back into effect. Utility Director Teresa Jones was available to answer
   questions. Alderman Lombardi asked if this fee will be included in walk-in
payments. Ms. Jones    that prior to the waiver there was a $5 convenience fee
charged for taking a payment by phone    or online. That fee was not charged
when making a card payment in person. She said what is being    proposed is
instead of a $5 flat fee is doing a 2.5% fee. Ms. Jones does not recommend
charging    the fees for in person payment because there is a challenge with
the processing system so that    they can charge for credit card processing
fees but not charge fees for using a debit card.    Alderman Davis asked how to
encourage more people to use the automatic draft system. Ms.    Jones said that
this is a very good system, it is free to use for the customers and the City.
There    was discussion on software that could help calculate with the
processing fees for credit card    payments when paid in person or the option
to just allow cash or check payments for in person    payments. It was
discussed that it should be fair across the board and not to just charge
customers    that pay by phone or online since there is a fee for every credit
card transaction. Manager Therrien    said that she preferred to look into
software after a new Finance Director was in position.
   Alderman Allen made a Motion to adopt the Ordinance Rescinding the Waiver of
the Credit Card    Processing Fee and adding the 2.5% processing fee back to
the fee schedule, with the provision    for no fees charged for in person cash
or check payments, effective August 1, 2023. Mayor Pro    Tem Mosteller
seconded the Motion. Unanimous Vote; Motion Carried.
   10 minute break 7:56 p.m.
    9.     Dredging Area
   Parks and Recreation Director Heather Hemphill gave an overview of the
proposed Yacht Basin    Dredging Limits. She said that this will determine the
dredging limits outside of the usage    authorized channel and also the volume
of dredge material in cubic yards that Board would like    included in this
project. She explained that the dredge limits need to be approved in order for
the    project to move forward. If the Board does not approve there will be no
dredging around the city    dock. Dredging is needed to develop the 10
transient and emergency boat slips that have    been previously discussed. She
said TI Coastal Services needs an answer from the Board on    the limitations
of the dredging.
   A Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller to authorize TI Coastal
Services to include the    City Dock along with the Federal Channel in the
dredging area and seconded by Alderman Allen.    Unanimous Vote; Motion
Carried.
   10.   Approval of Contract for Dredging Project and Submit Dredging Permit
Application
   Director Hemphill explained that T1 coastal services completed their
original task of surveying the    volume of dredge material. She said now there
will need to be a contract for them to continue    with the permitting process,
coordination for spoil material, meet with the regulatory    stakeholders to go
over plan, generate meeting files and presentation, and prepare/submit the
   full permit application. She said it is recommended to enter into the
contract with Tl Coastal    Services to allow them to coordinate with CAMA. Ms.
Hemphill said that the biggest challenge is    coordinating with the Audubon
Society but they have been in great communication and they will    ensure that
no wildlife will be disrupted.
   Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller made a Motion to authorize the contract with TI
Coastal Services to    continue the work for preparation for full permit
application for dredging the yacht basin at the    cost, but not to exceed
$7,000 and seconded by Alderman Lombardi.
Unanimous Vote; Motion Carried.
    11.    Request to Schedule the Public Hearing: Conditional Zoning Text
Amendment

Alderman Carroll. Unanimous    Vote; Motion Carried.
   12.   Petition for Contiguous Annexation
   Director Henley gave an overview of the request. He said Ms. Gayla
Armstrong, property owner,    has petitioned the City of Southport for
voluntary contiguous annexation of two parcels on    Lookout Point Drive. The
subject properties include Lot 1 (0.793 acres) and Lot 2 (1.515 acres).    The
property recently received final plat approval from the Board of Aldermen to
create the two    lots in question, with the division being recorded with the
Brunswick County Register of Deeds.    The properties are located at the
physical addresses of 6240 and 6245 Lookout Point Drive. He    said that Staff
has determined that this request includes property reflected on the     adopted
Resolution of Consideration and that annexation of this property supports the
town's     long-term objectives. The property is currently located within the
City's Extraterritorial    Jurisdiction and in the Fire Department's
jurisdiction. Annexation is a requirement for the    provision of City sewer
and water service.
   A Motion was made by Alderman Allen to accept the petition for annexation,
accept the City    Clerk to Investigate the Sufficiency of the Petition, accept
the City Clerk's Certificate of     Sufficiency and to set the Public Hearing
on July 13, 2023, and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem     Mosteller. Unanimous Vote;
Motion Carried.
    13.    Noise Ordinance Amendment
   Director Henley presented the Draft Noise Ordinance Amendment to provide a
proposed update    to the City's Noise Ordinance. These amendments are intended
to provide more clarity to the    purpose and intent of the City's noise
regulations, provide definitions to certain terms to remove    elements of
subjectiveness, and provide more certainty to the process for violations of the
City's    noise regulations. Mr. Henley went over each of the proposed
amendments. He did note that any    noise clearly audible at a distance of 100
feet was revised to 500 feet from the property line. Mr.    Henley stated that
this section was updated following Board feedback from their April 11, 2023
   workshop. He also said that in regard to the six items listed in Section 9-
94 for Noises Generally    Exempt there was some discussion at the workshop and
comments from the public regarding    private refuse collection. He said that
draft language has been prepared for consideration of an    additional
subsection G “Private Refuse    Collection and the noise that sounds generated
by    vehicles and other operations engaged in trash and refuse pick up”.
Alderman Carroll stated in    reference to the proposed Section 9-94 subsection
G that he would like to include language    regarding private refuse collection
(dumpsters) that says as long as it is more than 100 ft from a    residential
structure. There was clarification on the term “private pick up”, and it is
dumpsters    that are used by commercial businesses that contract and pay for
pickup to the trash companies    and that is separate than residential trash
services. City Manager Therrien wanted to get    more information on what the
Board was trying to achieve with the language and said that the    language may
need to be revised again. It was the consensus of the Board to table the
   proposed amendment. A Motion was made to Table the proposed Noise Ordinance
Amendment    by Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller and seconded by Alderman Carroll.
   Unanimous Vote; Motion Carried.   
   14.   Yacht Basin Speed Limit
   Alderman Davis said that there should be consideration for lower speed
limits around the yacht    basin as well as other streets particularly Eighth
Street. She said there are a lot of complaints    about speeding on eighth St.
She said the speed calming devices were put on Stuart Ave and Park    Avenue
but there are other streets where speeding has become a big problem. She would
like    consideration of lowering the speed limits on other streets as well.
Alderman Davis said that as    far as the Yacht Basin speed limit where there
is high vehicular and pedestrian traffic 10 mph is    best. Alderman Alt
recommended to confer with the State Department of Transportation so that
   they can provide on how to proceed with any reduction on the speed limits.
Manager Therrien    said that she asked the risk manager accessor to come and
review liability and safety concerns    and that he did recommend 10 mph.
Alderman Allen agreed with reducing the speed limit to 10    mph and reducing
the sign pollution down at the yacht basin.
   Alderman Davis made a motion to reduce the speed limit to 10 mph around the

   showing the designated areas that would be included for speed reduction.

reduction location(s). Alderman Davis    made a Motion    to reduce the speed
limit to 10 mph from W. Moore St to Yacht Basin Dr, and    from N. Caswell to
Yacht Basin Dr., from Yacht Basin Dr. to W. Bay St, and from W. Bay to S.
   Caswell. Motion failed for lack of second. Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller suggested
conferring with    Chief of Police Todd Coring and get feedback on his
recommendations to what area(s) to include    in the reduction. It was the
consensus of the Board to table the proposed Yacht Basin Speed Limit
   reduction, get a recommendation from Chief Coring, and have the City Manager
bring back to the    Board.
   15.   Code of Ordinance Amendment and By-law Adoption: Cemetery Committee

JUNE 21, 2023
SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
BOARD OF ALDERMEN
SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
COMMUNITY BUILING
JUNE 21, 2023
PRESENT:
Mayor Pro-tem Karen Mosteller, Alderman Alt, Alderman Carroll, Alderman Davis,
and Alderman Lombardi. Alderman Allen joined by telephone because of some
trouble with his return flight.
ABSENT:
Mayor Hatem was unable to attend.
STAFF PRESENT:
Bonnie Therrien, City Manager
Dorothy Dutton, Assistant City Manager/City Clerk
Paul Gross, Interim Finance Officer
Brandon Stevens, Deputy Finance Officer
Randy Jones, Community Relations Director
ChyAnn Ketchum, Communications/PIO
Sydney Heil, Community Building Administrator
OTHERS PRESENT:
Just a few citizens were in attendance.
A) Call to Order
Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller called the special meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. She
announced that she would preside over the meeting in the Mayor’s absence.
B) Alderman Lowe Davis provided the invocation.
C) Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller led everyone in the Pledge of Allegiance.
D) Alderman Carroll made a motion to approve the agenda. Alderman Lombardi
seconded the motion. All ayes. Motion carried. 
E) Agenda
   1.
   Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller explained that first on the agenda was the adoption
of the budget and budget ordinance. She thanked the City Manager and the
Interim Finance Director for all of their hard word. She also thanked the
Department Heads.
   Alderman Carroll made a motion to approve the FY 23-24 Budget and Budget
Ordinance with the tax rate of 0.275, the neutral tax rate. Alderman Carroll
explained that he would like to see the extra $459,000 in the Capital Projects
Fund. He added that this tax rate allows the City to maintain a robust capital
improvement fund to accomplish projects without relying too much on outside
sources. The City can allocate funds strategically.
   Alderman Alt countered by stating that last year, the tax rate was raised by
ten cents. The City hired eleven new employees. He added that the workforce
study was still not completed, and he doesn’t feel like any of the positions
are justified besides the paramedics. In addition, he added that the budget
that Alderman Carroll has motioned to adopt is not the same one that the public
has been considering for the past two weeks. He said he understands where
Alderman Carroll is coming from, but he would oppose it, because he doesn’t
think the positions are justified. Alderman Alt added that the sale of the
Sunny Point property can be used for capital projects. In fact, Alderman Alt
stated that he is going to vote against both proposed budgets, because he
doesn’t feel the positions are justified.
   Alderman Davis stated that she also agrees with the goals and objectives
that Alderman Carroll described. But she does not believe that the tax rate of
0.2485 would prevent the City from doing those same projects. She explained
that if the City has a higher tax rate in conjunction with the County tax rate,
it creates an unnecessary hardship for our citizens.
   Alderman Lombardi agreed with Alderman Carroll. The City has kicked the can
down the road so much that we are now in a bad position with our
infrastructure. A tax rate of 0.275 will allow the City to save 459,000 that
can be applied towards projects. He added that the Board can act now or have to
raise the tax rate more next year and the projects will likely be more
expensive.
   Alderman Carroll said it is easier to eat the elephant one bit at a time. He
wants to be responsible to the citizens of Southport, but he feels like this is
the responsible thing to do. He added that he understands Alderman Davis’s view
point, too. The Board must keep in mind those in the City who are less
fortunate.
   Alderman Davis asked for clarification as to what the Board was giving up
with the 0.2485 tax rate. City Manager Therrien explained that everything would
be the same, except for the additional $459,000 in tax revenue.
   Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller provided the definition of tax neutral. She also
explained that Brunswick County increased their taxes by one-half cent above
the neutral tax rate, which equals approximately $10.00 on a $200,000 home.
Alderman Carroll restated his motion. There was no other discussion. Alderman
Carroll, Alderman Allen, Alderman Lombardi, and Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller were
all ayes. Alderman Alt and Davis were noes.
F) Mayor Pro-tem
commented that in January, the Board held their strategic planning meeting.
Staff was the first asset identified, and it was important to conduct the
salary study. The beauty and history of Southport was identified as two of the
external strengths. The proposed budget includes funding for Capital
Improvement projects, dredging, a Yacht Basin comprehensive plan, sidewalks,
and stormwater projects. The City is taking big steps.
G) Alderman Allen
and Alderman Carroll had no comments. Alderman Alt added that while they do not
all agree with the outcome, they are not all mad at each other; this is a
democracy.
Alderman Davis reminded the public of the flag lowering ceremony that is taking
place every evening at the waterfront.
Alderman Lombardi had no comments.
H) Mayor Pro-tem Mosteller
stated that the Board had included a Closed session on the agenda per N.C.G.S.
143-318.11 (a) (5). After a motion by Alderman Lombardi and seconded by
Alderman Carroll, the Board went into Closed Session at 6:26 p.m.
I) Adjourn
The Board moved back to open session at 6:48 p.m., after a motion made by
Alderman Allen, who had arrived in person at the beginning of the closed
session. Alderman Davis seconded the motion. All ayes. Mayor pro-tem adjourned
the meeting at 6:49 p.m., after a motion by Alderman Allen and seconded by
Alderman Lombardi.

JUNE 28, 2023
SPECIAL PUBLIC MEETING
Board of Aldermen
Special Public Meeting
Community Building 223 E. Bay Street
June 28, 2023
6:00 P.M.
Present:
Mayor Pro Tem Karen Mosteller, Aldermen Thomas Lombardi, Lowe Davis, Robert
Carroll, John Allen, and Rich Alt.
Absent:
Mayor Joseph P. Hatem
Staff Present:
Bonnie Therrien, City Manager
Dorothy Dutton, Assistant Manager/ City Clerk
Maureen Meehan, City Planner
Tanya Shannon, Deputy Clerk
ChyAnn Ketchum, Public Information Director
Sydney Heil, Community Building Administrator
Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller called the meeting to order at 6:02 P.M. and welcomed
everyone.
Reverend Alderman Lowe Davis gave the Invocation.
The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller.
Agenda
Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller gave thanks and appreciation to the Planning Staff and
the Planning Board for all the work that they have done to bring forward the
proposed text amendment to update the Conditional Zoning language in the UDO.
City Manager Bonnie Therrien came to the podium and said that she will be
acting as moderator this evening and went over some of the guidelines on how to
respectfully provide public comments.
   3.
   Mayor Pro tem Mosteller provided an introduction of Dorothy Dutton Assistant
City Manager/City Clerk and Maureen Meehan City Planner for the presentation
and explanation of Conditional Zoning.
   Ms. Dutton presented a review of the proposed amendment. She explained the
differences    between Conditional Zoning versus Conventional Zoning, and the
benefits of Conditional Zoning.
E.   Board Comments and Questions
   Alderman Allen asked if Conditional Zoning project was approved could it be
modified. Ms. Dutton said that it could, but it would have to go back through
the same process for approval again. He asked about the non-contiguous open
space provisions and if it was allowable in CZ. Ms. Dutton stated that it is
discouraged in the current UDO, but she believes that developers could request
it if applying for CZ.
   Alderman Carroll thanked Staff for the presentations and explaining the
process and use of CZ in    a simplified matter, and how it would work for the
City.
   Alderman Davis thanked everyone for attending and said that she was here to
listen to the Public    and help address some of the concerns.
   Alderman Lombardi said that many citizens have requested to hear the pros of
CZ and he said that Ms. Dutton did a great job on providing that information.
   Mayor Pro Tem Mosteller asked for consideration to amend the process and
make the pre- application conference a required step instead of an optional
step. That will allow staff to provide additional guidance regarding the
application and then require the community input meeting. Ms. Dutton explained
that having the public input meeting prior to presenting to the Planning Board
allows the Planning Board to hear concerns from the public and for the
applicant to take suggestions and comments back to review for recommended
revisions. Alderman Mosteller said that CZ is a voluntary application, and the
process is more stringent. She believes that it would be better if staff had a
conference with the developers before it is presented to the public for input.
   Alderman Lombardi asked if CZ would eliminate PUD. Planner Meehan said that
as it written now it does not remove PUD from the ordinance. Alderman Allen
asked if CZ would replace PUD. Ms. Meehan said that mostly it would. Ms. Meehan
said that it would be more beneficial for the land owner to use the CZ process.
Alderman Allen stated that it may be redundant to have both. Ms. Dutton said
that it would be up to the Board to make that decision and to decide which
suits the best needs of the City.
   Alderman Alt stated that he understands that with CZ there will be input
from the citizens. However, he said after going through a lengthy three year
PUD process where many citizens voiced concerns, but only a few citizens wanted
to work through an agreement. He said that if there was that much input from
the citizens and it did not change the outcome, how would CZ be able to do
that. Ms. Dutton explained the legislative PUD process and that projects can be
denied without legal consequences though CZ.
F)   Public Comment :
   1.
   Ginny Prunty; 5906 Dutchman Creek Road; stated that she was pleased to that
the approved budget included an update on the Comprehensive Plan. She said this
plan is a guide to the future of the City. She asked the Board not to approve
the proposed Conditional Zoning Text Amendment until after the Comprehensive
Plan has been updated.
   2.
   Francesca Slaughter; 6272 Cattail Court; said that developers are only
concerned about profits. She questioned how CZ could be safeguarded from
decisions that are made between the Boards and the developers. She would like
to see that the UDO and the Comprehensive Plan are updated and revised to
prevent the mistakes made from the past.
   3.
   Shirley Sullivan; 5002 Seaward Court; is opposed to CZ for all of Southport.
She asked if this type of zoning would be spot zoning or contract zoning and
would that not be illegal. Manager Therrien said that the City Attorney will be
consulted regarding this question. She states the amendment is contradictory
and allows to much flexibility.
   4.
    Rebecca Kelly; 5971 Dutchman Creek Road; she stated that with the current
process she has seen    the City and the Public work through a large
development process. She questioned, instead of    adding    a CZ text
amendment to the UDO why not consider revising the UDO and updating the
   Comprehensive Land Use Plan. Alderman Allen said that updating the
Comprehensive Land Use    Plan will take approximately two years and CZ would
allow for protection and a better     outcome for the City. She said that
without revisions in the UDO and an updated Plan    developers will find holes
in the Ordinance.
   5.
    June McWhorter; 126 Park Avenue; has recently moved to Southport and said
that she is concerned about major development and would like to ensure that
trees are protected and preserved.
   6.
   Marcus & Marty Younts; 285 Lord Thomas Avenue; are concerned about
development and the protection of wildlife and the conservation of land.
   7.
    Jack Gordon; 5920 Dutchman Creek Road; wanted clarification on why the
proposed Conditional Zoning    Amendment would be any different than the
Traditional Zoning process in the UDO. Alderman Allen replied that Conditional
Zoning would be part of the UDO and it would be another process that developers
can request to help achieve the best outcome for the community and the
developer. Mr. Gordon asked if CZ was adopted how could it be implemented and
controlled when arguments of precedence have already been established. Alderman
Allen replied that every application for CZ is different and reviewed on merit.
   The Board had a discussion about how the property would be affected if
property was sold. Ms. Dutton explained that after the submittal of the
application the property owner at the time has vested rights and there are
statues of limitations to complete the process. After approval and an agreement
has been made the conditions of the rezoning would be recorded with the
Register of Deeds that would follow the property and not the owner.
   8.
   Karin Rife; 5980 Dutchman Creek Road; questioned why a developer would
choose to go through the CZ process when the PUD process is not as lengthy or
complicated. Alderman Mosteller explained that CZ would offer the developer the

desirable for the community. She stated that CZ would be a process that
developers can apply for to request specific amendments to allow for
negotiations and compromises. This process would allow conditions to be placed
on the zoning approval that would be appealing for the community and agreeable
to the developer. Ms. Rife questioned what happens when the vested rights
period expires. Ms. Dutton stated that once the vested rights have expired the
process will have to start over. Ms. Rife said that she has heard different.
Ms. Dutton said they would have to consult with the City Attorney.

almost any additional feature/condition, including amount or types of open
space, neighborhood design, housing types, or community amenities, the
